543223|2026-06.headline: Max India Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 66% YoY to INR68.6 crore, but EBITDA loss widened to INR25 crore; AGEasy breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.
543223|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR68.6 crore versus INR41.3 crore a year ago, though it fell sequentially on lumpy DM fee income. The EBITDA loss was INR25 crore, against INR23.2 crore a year ago and INR6.8 crore in Q4 FY26, because Q4 included an exceptional DM fee. Antara Noida (340 units) received possession offers in June 2026, with about 75% of dues collected by the call date, though revenue recognition is deferred to Q2 on possession. Management said care home occupancy is improving at 5 of 8 homes and AGEasy's ARR is trending up toward INR120-150 crore, and it reiterated AGEasy profitability by around Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Antara Senior Living (residences)
segments.commentary: Dehradun is profitable and fully occupied; Estate 360 Gurgaon is fully sold out. E361 has sold 154 of 360 units by June end, with 27 sold in Q1 and about 34 in July. Noida possession offers went to 340 residents in June, with INR169 crore demanded and about 75% collected.

segments.name: Antara Assisted Care (Care Homes)
segments.commentary: 485 beds across 8 Care Homes in NCR, Bengaluru and Chennai; occupied bed days up 23% QoQ. Occupancy rose at Bannerghatta to 41% (from 37%), Gurugram to 41% (from 33%), Whitefield to 18% (from 8%) and OMR to 12% (from 3%). Four homes reached ARPOB above INR7,000 in June.

segments.name: AGEasy (consumer products)
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR19 crore in Q1, below INR23 crore in Q4 on post-peak moderation. Online gross margin held at 45% (vs 46%). Marketplace ROAS 3.8 and D2C exit ROAS 2.6; marketplace CM2 improved to minus 17% in July from roughly minus 70-80% historically. Monthly revenue run-rate about INR10 crore in July.

segments.name: Antara Integrated Wellness Clinic
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR15.75 lakh in Q1 with negative contribution margin; average revenue per client INR4,000, client satisfaction 96%, sessions rose from 199 to 307 in June. Will be built into residences and Care Homes, not as a standalone business.

guidance_outlook: AGEasy expected to reach contribution and EBITDA breakeven around Q4 FY27 (management: 'by January or last quarter of this year'), with CM2 improving as ROAS rises.
AGEasy revenue doubling target for FY27 (from INR77 crore to about INR150 crore) reiterated; management expects significant Q2-Q4 top-line improvement.
Management said it will report a smaller EBITDA loss next quarter versus the 63% figure cited for FY26 (loss to revenue ratio).

Two new projects, Bangalore (about 300 units, potential sales value about INR900 crore, in final diligence) and Dehradun (under 150 units, sales value INR850-900 crore), are expected to help meet the 1.5 million sq ft / INR1,800 crore annual sales ambition for the year; definitive documents pending.
Care Home expansion decision timed for October-November 2026, subject to occupancy trends; no new beds added at present.
Incremental capital requirement of about USD20 million over the next two years (reduced from about USD25 million), with the second fund raise deferred.
capex_capacity: Antara Noida (340 units): possession offers issued June 2026; residents expected to move in over 30-45 days; Phase II approval is the next step, with rates cited at INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft versus INR7,000-10,000 earlier.
Care Homes: 485 beds across 8 homes; all 8 operational after DLF Phase II Gurgaon relaunch in July 2026; each new bed costs about INR10-12 lakh including operating losses.
Chandigarh project unwound after height clearance denial near flight paths post Operation Sindoor.
Second tranche of preference issue of INR40 crore received in July 2026; management says the total capital need is unchanged but working-capital credit lines are being used to bridge timing.
demand_pricing: Gurgaon E361 sales velocity slowed in April-June amid geopolitical uncertainty but recovered in July (34 units) and August; management says it has not seen DLF's senior-living entry affect sales.
AGEasy ROAS improved to 2.0 at Q1 exit from 1.8 in Q4; conversion rate rose from 2% to 3.5% after brand spend (Anupam Kher as ambassador).
AGEasy repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); management's directional target is 20%+.
Management noted that logistics and China-sourcing disruption raised COGS and forced some airlifting, depressing margins.
Competition: management said real-estate developers and hospital chains can replicate infrastructure but not services IP; DLF's launch plans in Gurgaon are reportedly small and tied to Medanta.

542580|2026-06.headline: Aartech Solonics Q1 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 728 lakh from Rs 433 lakh YoY (~68%), with PBT up to Rs 119 lakh from Rs 73 lakh.
542580|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 728 lakh versus Rs 433 lakh a year earlier, which it attributed to an order book of about Rs 7 crore carried over from FY26 and executed in the quarter. Material cost was about Rs 3.36 crore, employee cost about Rs 119 lakh, and PBT rose from Rs 73 lakh to Rs 119 lakh with no exceptional items. Management said Q1 is seasonally subdued and that Q3 and Q4 are heavier, and expects healthy revenue and margins in the coming quarters. Management described the balance sheet as near debt-free, with only non-fund-based liabilities. The Q&A focused on pipeline conversion, ultracapacitors and defence approvals, CRP margins versus peers, R&D spend, and new customer segments.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 433 lakh in Q1 FY26 (about 1.7x)
marginally up YoY; includes annual increments and performance bonus paid in Q1
vs Rs 469 lakh a year earlier; management said expense ratio is broadly flat as % of revenue
vs Rs 73 lakh in Q1 FY26

segments.name: CRP (control and relay panels)
segments.commentary: Described as the bread-and-butter product; management said pricing carries a margin of around 100% plus. Peers in higher-rated relay segments earn higher margins. Management is pursuing OEM tie-ups to move into 415 kV to 750 kV ratings.

segments.name: Defence projects
segments.commentary: Revenue of about Rs 156 lakh in Q1 per management. Ultracapacitor and energy storage programmes for the Army, with technical evaluation taking about 18 to 24 months.

segments.name: Other diversified segments (electrical engineering services, plastic enclosures, lubricant-related)
segments.commentary: Management cited about Rs 40 lakh from the plastic enclosure segment and about Rs 181 lakh from the trading segment, which totalled about Rs 7 crore on its own basis. The description of these segments was partly unclear in the transcript.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the next quarters to be very healthy in terms of both revenue and margins.

Management said inquiries worth around Rs 100 crore are in the pipeline and expects a near-about number by this financial year or around the same time next year, while being conservative on project delays.
Management said the roadmap to 415 kV and above depends on OEM or manufacturing partners and on possible in-house relay manufacturing in future.
No specific revenue or margin numerical guidance was given.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, or utilisation figures were discussed in the call.
Management said it is working on partnerships with relay manufacturers to move from 220 kV to 415 kV and above, with own manufacturing possible later.
Type-test certification from PGCIL, CPRI or similar bodies is required for new products; no timeline was given.
demand_pricing: Management said data centres are beginning to develop in India and that its energy storage products (flywheels, ultracapacitors, rectifiers) are being positioned for them.
Bus Transfer System demand is widening from GENs to refineries, process industries and cement; oil and refinery was named as a sunrise opportunity.
Management said the supply chain for some newer EPC-linked business segments is slightly stagnant, with unclear delivery timelines, though margins are good.
Management said the stock price has not reflected the improved performance, and that the market will eventually price it in.

qa_highlights.question: How will ultracapacitors and defence products such as Faradyne/AAPM be industrialised, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product details, citing proprietary work and customer commitments. It said ultracapacitor work spans more than 15 years, with applications in railway locos, Army tank engine starting and missile nano-ultracapacitors.

qa_highlights.question: Is CRP pricing lower than peers, and are margins being cross-subsidised?
qa_highlights.answer: CRP is the core product with pricing around 100% plus margin. Competitors in higher-rated segments earn more, and the company's long-term aim is 415 kV to 750 kV via OEM partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 100 crore pipeline convert into orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inquiries are still active and are long-gestation projects. It expects good numbers this financial year, or around the same time next year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the approval timelines for ultracapacitors and who gives approval?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical evaluation typically takes about 18 to 24 months, and the approval involves the Army and other agencies. Breaking into the market takes much longer.

qa_highlights.question: How is R&D spend low relative to development activity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it runs R&D on a frugal basis, excludes most overheads from R&D, and capitalises most R&D spend into assets. The FY25 R&D figure cited by the analyst was about Rs 45 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: Are Indian Railways and oil and gas target markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said oil and refineries are a process industry where the Bus Transfer System fits. It cited prior supply to Dangote and Reliance and said Indian Railways was not addressed in detail.

risks_watch: Revenue is seasonal, with Q1 typically subdued. Q1 profit in absolute terms is small, so Q3 and Q4 execution matters.
The Rs 100 crore inquiry pipeline is long-gestation and may slip because of policy and ecosystem changes.
Ultracapacitor and defence commercialisation has long approval cycles (about 18 to 24 months for technical evaluation), with uncertain timing and no disclosed revenue visibility.
Expansion into 415 kV and above depends on partners and certifications (PGCIL, CPRI). Supply chain for some EPC-linked segments is described as stagnant.
R&D expense disclosure is low relative to the claimed product development. Investors should watch the FY26 annual report for disclosures.
542580|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top-line growth and near-term outlook, but reticent on product details, citing proprietary and customer-confidentiality constraints. Answers on pipeline conversion and timelines were hedged and general.

500410|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Cements Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA INR1,589 crore (16.7% margin, +331 bps), net cost INR4,241/t (down INR206/t QoQ), trade volumes down 2% YoY.
500410|2026-06.overview: Ambuja reported revenue of about INR9,500 crore, operating EBITDA of INR1,589 crore and PAT of INR660 crore for Q1 FY27, with EBITDA per ton at INR931. Management prioritised value over volume: total volumes fell about 7% YoY, with trade down 2% and non-trade down 21%, and about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume in South was cut. Net operating cost fell INR206/t QoQ to INR4,241/t, which management says already absorbs about INR110/t of West Asia-related cost pressure. Management guides to 8% full-year volume growth (July trade volumes up 8% YoY) and FY27 cost of INR4,250/t, and expects some sequential cost pressure in Q2 that it says it can offset.

financial_highlights.value: ~70 million tonnes (implied from cost arithmetic on analyst question)

financial_highlights.change: margin ~7% vs 14-15% in prior four quarters per analyst

financial_highlights.value: ~INR24 crore (VRS at a South India plant)

segments.name: Trade / non-trade
segments.commentary: Trade volumes fell 2% YoY and non-trade fell 21% YoY; trade share rose to 78% from 74% QoQ. Management says trade will be upwards of 75% of sales going forward.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Trade volumes grew 2% YoY, and management called North the highest-EBITDA cluster. North, West, Central and East together are about 80% of volume, with South about 10%.

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Grew both trade and non-trade, per management, with Mumbai and Gujarat margin-accretive. West is about 30% of volume.

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Highest degrowth cluster as about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume was curtailed; channel build-out to take one to two quarters more.

segments.name: Central
segments.commentary: Volumes declined as the company shifted to blended cement offerings to improve margins.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume growth guidance of 8%; management says July trade volumes were up 8% YoY, implying a steep ramp needed for the rest of the year.
FY27 net operating cost target of INR4,250/t, with Q1 at INR4,241/t; a further INR250/t reduction targeted in FY28 to about INR4,000/t.
Identified savings of INR130-150/t from lead distance (INR35/t), fly ash and BCFC logistics (INR30/t), green power and heat rate (~INR50/t), and other items (INR10-15/t).
Q2 expected to see geopolitical-driven cost pressure of about INR100/t if conditions persist, which management says is mitigated by inventory (about 1 month clinker, about 3 months coal).
Capex of about INR6,500 crore in FY27 (about 25%, or INR1,500-1,600 crore, spent in Q1); FY28 capex run-rate of INR6,000-7,000 crore; capacity additions of 8-10 mtpa per year.

Capacity to reach 119 mtpa by end FY27 (Dahej, Salai Banwa, Bhatinda, Jodhpur already commissioned or in trials; Kalamboli and Warisaliganj expected Q2; Maratha clinker in Q1 FY28; Mundra in about 2029).
Green power target of 60% share by FY28 (48% on a revenue-plus-consumption basis versus 34% consumption-based today); RE capacity 973 MW, target 1,122 MW.
Targeted utilisation of 70-75% on a value-focused basis.
AFR (alternative fuel) share targeted at 12-15% in FY27 (currently about 7%) and 25% in the longer term.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity of 109 mtpa today, targeted at 119 mtpa by end FY27 after adding about 10.2 mt.
RE capacity 973 MW (up about 500 MW over the year), with about 75 MW more commissioning; WHRS capacity 228 MW rising to about 376 MW by FY28.
Around 3.5 mtpa of old ACC plants temporarily suspended for about six months (Chaibasa, Marwar, Wadi, Lakheri cited by analysts); management says not permanent closures and no impairment expected.
Sanghi jetty expansion of about INR600 crore for clinker utilisation; Penna AFR and WHRS investments of INR100-150 crore.
Three coal blocks in pipeline, the first to be operational in about 30 months; investment payback 5-6 years.
demand_pricing: Management said cement demand was stable in Q1, with infrastructure and housing support, but input cost and monsoon risks in the near term.

Net sales realisation (NSP) is down YoY and rose only about 1% QoQ per analysts; management attributed the gap to accounting netting of expenses and Ex-works Incoterm shifts, and said NSP is market-driven.
Management cited Q1 disruptions from diesel shortages, packing material availability and geopolitical tensions as reasons for the YoY volume decline.
Brand pull and channel momentum in North, West, Central and East; South channel needs investment.
Capacity utilisation about 65% overall; management says value-focused utilisation target is 70-75%.

523367|2026-06.headline: DCM Shriram Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 9% to INR3,564 crore and PBDIT 12% to INR364 crore; reported PAT of INR693 crore includes INR474 crore one-time tax credit.
523367|2026-06.overview: Consolidated net revenue grew 9% YoY to INR3,564 crore and PBDIT rose 12% to INR364 crore, led by Chemicals (revenue +33%, PBDIT +24%). Vinyl PBDIT nearly doubled on price gains despite a 25% fall in PVC volumes, while Bioseed swung to a loss on delayed monsoon. Reported PAT of INR693 crore includes a INR474 crore one-time tax adjustment and INR79 crore of other one-time gains; underlying PAT was INR147 crore, up 28%. Management flagged weak rural demand, soft Q2 vinyl offtake and a 15-20% Kharif sowing shortfall as near-term headwinds.

financial_highlights.change: Includes INR474 crore one-time tax adjustment and INR79 crore one-time gains
vs INR236 crore a year ago

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue +33% YoY and PBDIT +24% to INR274 crore; ECU prices firmed 7% with caustic volumes flat. Capacity utilisation 82% for caustic, ~85% for hydrogen peroxide, ~70% each for epichlorohydrin and epoxy.

segments.name: Vinyl
segments.commentary: Revenue -10% YoY on PVC volumes -25% despite prices +22%; utilisation 100% vs 98%. PBDIT +88% to INR43 crore; carbide volumes and prices each +15%.

segments.name: Sugar and Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue -2% YoY; domestic sugar volumes -8%, realisations +2%. PBDIT INR22 crore vs negative INR7 crore last year, which included a ~INR36 crore one-time ethanol duty provision. Sugar inventory 20.8 lakh quintals vs 27.7 lakh a year ago.

segments.name: Fenesta Building Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue +22% YoY; PBDIT +13% to INR40 crore, diluted by product mix and fixed costs for new platforms. Order book up 4%, roughly INR1,000 crore.

segments.name: Shriram Farm Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue +2% to INR357 crore; PBDIT +22% to INR30 crore on better margins in crop protection and specialty plant nutrition despite muted volumes.

segments.name: Fertilizer (Urea)
segments.commentary: Revenue +11% with realisations +19% and flat volumes; PBDIT fell to INR23 crore from INR38 crore, as the year-ago quarter had a INR24 crore one-time gain.

segments.name: Bioseed
segments.commentary: Revenue -26% YoY; PBDIT negative INR9 crore vs INR42 crore last year on lower corn and paddy volumes and weaker cotton margins.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give forward caustic price guidance, but said ECU is just below INR30,000/t and expects prices in that range or higher; chlorine is at minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000/t.
Bharuch aluminium chloride and calcium chloride projects expected to start commercial production in Q2 FY27.

Kota 68 MW peak hybrid renewable project under commissioning, with average injection of 25 MW in July; Serentica 58 MW hybrid agreement signed to take peak renewable capacity at Bharuch and Kota to about 176 MW.
Cash tax outgo expected at about 19% for at least five years through MAT credit utilisation of INR376 crore, while P&L tax rate stays at 25%.
Net borrowings at FY27 end expected to be similar to current levels, with a reduction of about INR200 crore possible; capex of about INR1,000 crore planned this year.
Demolition of the group demerger: application to government targeted within FY27, timeline uncertain.
Vinyl demand expected soft in Q2 FY27; government reinstated basic customs duty on PVC imports and DGFT set minimum import price of US$766/t for six months.
Bioseed: large part of Kharif volume lost; no firm recovery guided for Q2.
capex_capacity: Caustic soda utilisation 82% in Q1; expected to improve as downstream projects commission. New flaker facility lets part of caustic output be exported.
Vinyl utilisation 100% in Q1 FY27.
Epichlorohydrin and epoxy plants running at ~70% utilisation with ramp-up ongoing; epoxy plant in Gujarat acquired October 2025.
Grain-based ethanol capacity can be run up to 260 KLD; management said it does not plan to add ethanol capacity.
Chlorine: after current projects, ~50% captively consumed; with pipeline and regional customer tie-ups, ~85% tied up.
Fenesta setting up a wooden door manufacturing facility; two acquisitions worth ~INR450 crore completed in the 12 months to June 2026.
demand_pricing: Domestic caustic demand steady from alumina, soaps and detergents, and textiles; hydrogen peroxide oversupplied in Asia.
PVC: imports surged after temporary customs duty waiver and Chinese imports; offtake weak on labour shortages, heatwave and cautious buying.
Sugar: global deficit of ~0.7 mt expected in 2026-27; domestic sugar price around INR4,450/quintal, expected to stay firm for a couple of months.
Ethanol: installed capacity ~2,000 crore litres vs OMC allocation ~1,060 crore litres; sugarcane feedstock only 28%.
Kharif sowing shortfall of 15-20% all-India and much higher in Bioseed markets; rainfall patchy after July.
Urea: subsidy regime governed by FICC; management says government is paying domestic makers on time, and gas-price spikes are a pass-through.
Fenesta order intake only up 4%; management attributes slowdown to customers deferring decisions amid West Asia crisis.

544223|2026-06.headline: Ceigall Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 10.2% YoY to INR901 crore, with EBITDA margin at 13.4% and order book at INR18,568 crore.
544223|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 10.2% YoY to INR901 crore and PAT rose to INR75 crore (8.4% margin) from INR56 crore. Consolidated revenue grew 15.7% to INR970 crore. The company completed its first HAM divestment (Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali) and started three new projects, while management kept FY27 margin guidance of 11-12.5% and raised revenue growth guidance to at least 15%. Q1 order inflow was modest at about INR600 crore against a INR6,000 crore full-year target.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR94 crore in Q1 FY26; margin 13.4% vs 11.4%
vs INR56 crore; PAT margin 8.4% vs 6.8%
down from around INR13 crore in prior quarter
down from INR15-odd crore a year earlier
mainly a launcher purchased at Danapur

financial_highlights.metric: Equity invested in HAM and solar (Q1 and YTD)

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: 19 EPC projects, 10 HAM projects, 1 DBFOT project and 9 tariff-based renewable and transmission projects. Diversification extends to metro rail, renewable energy, T&D and industrial infrastructure.

segments.name: Renewable energy (Solar plus BESS)
segments.commentary: Signed a PPA for a Solar BESS at Morena and emerged L1 for a standalone battery storage project. Maharashtra solar projects MH1 and MH2 started in Q1. Rewa solar awaits a transmission line tender before start.

segments.name: HAM and highways
segments.commentary: Divested Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali, the first HAM asset monetised. Signed concession for Ambala-Chandigarh-Zirakpur HAM. Received appointed dates for VRK 11, VRK 12 and Indore-Ujjain HAM after quarter end. Northern Ayodhya bypass execution was about INR42 crore in Q1.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 11% to 12.5% for FY27 maintained, per CFO.
Revenue growth guidance raised to minimum 15% for FY27, from earlier 10-15%.
Order inflow target of about INR6,000 crore for FY27; close to INR600 crore secured so far. Order inflow typically concentrated in Q3 and Q4 (about 45% of the order book came in Q4 last year).
Full-year capex guidance of INR30-35 crore.
Balance equity commitment of INR859 crore in FY27 (INR310 crore solar, INR550 crore HAM) and INR744 crore in FY28 (INR296 crore solar, INR444 crore HAM).
Execution targets: VRK 11 and VRK 12 at least 20-25% in FY27; Southern Ludhiana at least 15% due to only 62% land availability.
Working capital intensity expected to improve in FY27 and further in FY28, citing government relaxation.
Commercial paper of about INR100 crore on private placement, carved out of working capital limits at about 6.8-7% versus WCDL at 7.5-7.8%.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex about INR14 crore, mainly a launcher bought at Danapur; more than INR100 crore of machinery already paid from IPO proceeds.
Full-year FY27 capex guidance INR30-35 crore; specialised machinery to be bought only as required.
Three new projects started in Q1 (MH1, MH2 solar and Indore-Ujjain HAM); three more to start from July after appointed dates.
Two HAM projects (Bihar and Punjab) await appointed dates: Bihar FC expected next month, Punjab around November; work to start 2-3 months after FC.

Equity infusion by project for FY27 includes VRK 11 INR97 crore, VRK 12 INR139 crore, Northern Ayodhya INR61 crore, Southern Ayodhya INR53 crore, Ludhiana-Bhatinda INR53 crore, Southern Ludhiana INR38 crore, Indore-Ujjain INR60 crore, Bihar Sahebganj INR50 crore and Zirakpur INR16 crore.
demand_pricing: Management cited a Q1 seasonal slowdown from monsoon; order inflow was modest in Q1 with the bulk expected in Q3 and Q4.
International: bids in Romania and Dubai; management is taking a conservative approach given the war situation, with focus on India.
Management says the company targets 25% project-level IRR and will sell completed projects, citing Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali returns above guidance.
Renewable margins guided in line with EPC margins, with an aim to do better.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Northern Ayodhya bypass execution fall to about INR42 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said progress is steady and milestones are being met early; payment is only received on milestone achievement, and rain over the last 1.5 months affected timing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rewa solar project timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: PPA and land are in place; the transmission line tender has been floated and the company expects it soon, after which the project can start quickly.

qa_highlights.question: What equity will be invested in HAM and solar in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 balance commitment INR859 crore (INR310 crore solar, INR550 crore HAM); FY28 INR744 crore (INR296 crore solar, INR444 crore HAM). Initial equity at IPO was INR253 crore; total now INR692 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was margin higher than guidance and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Three new projects started in Q1 and more are starting; the CFO said FY27 margin guidance of 11-12.5% is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation and other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation fell due to assets sold in the prior year on WDV method; other income fell as royalty is no longer charged and IPO-linked FD interest ended. About INR320 crore in FDs now earn interest, and management expects this run rate to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of the commercial paper issuance?
qa_highlights.answer: CP of about INR100 crore is carved out of working capital limits, at about 6.8-7% versus WCDL at 7.5-7.8%, to reduce finance cost and access the market.

540701|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% to INR 6,776 mn and EBITDA to INR 600 mn, mainly from an INR 10 mn order deferred to H2.
540701|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 6,776 mn versus INR 7,080 mn a year earlier, a 4% decline, which management attributed mainly to an order pushed from Q1 into the latter half of FY27. EBITDA fell to INR 600 mn from INR 1,406 mn, and the company posted a loss before tax of about INR 512 mn after finance costs of about INR 370 mn and an FX loss of about INR 117.3 mn. The CDMO segment revenue fell to INR 5,343 mn while Marketable Molecules rose to INR 1,432 mn. Management guided to single-digit group revenue growth for FY27 with EBITDA margin similar to or slightly above FY26, and said a promoter-level ECB of up to CHF 200 mn is expected to close in 60-90 days.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 5,343 mn, down from INR 6,112 mn; EBITDA margin 6.3% vs 17.9%, hit by deferred order and FX loss.

segments.name: Marketable Molecules (cholesterol, Vitamin D and analogues)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,432 mn, up from INR 968 mn; margin normalised as cholesterol sales outweighed analogues versus a high analogue quarter last year. Vitamin D and analogues sales and margin reportedly rose.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue growth guided to single digits; France and Swiss CDMO growth slower than planned.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected similar to FY26, possibly slightly higher.
Indian entity revenue guided to grow 25-35% in FY27 with operating margin near 10% (analyst's characterisation, not explicitly confirmed by management).
FY28-29: at least double-digit growth in France and India; group revenue growth above 10% YoY; EBITDA margin closer to 25-26% seen before EDQM issues.
No quarterly guidance; management said Q2 is difficult to guide. Net debt expected CHF 140-150 mn (excluding promoter infusion), reducing by about CHF 8-9 mn.
Interest expense guided at about INR 130-140 crores for the full year (about INR 35-40 crores per quarter).
Promoter ECB up to CHF 200 mn at 4% all-inclusive, 10-year tenor, to prepay high-cost India debt; expected in 60-90 days. RBI approval reportedly received.
capex_capacity: Two tech transfers from Carbogen Amcis Switzerland to India: one commercial contract signed with a US company (Switzerland to Bavla, to complete within FY27); a second legacy project approved by a Swiss MNC and already initiated; three more in advanced discussion.
Second co-investment with the Japanese ADC customer is in progress, with operations expected in calendar 2027.
Naroda and Bavla hold certifications from all major international health authorities; Naroda passed a Korea MFDS inspection and is under US FDA observation; two CEPs granted by EDQM.
Restarting some API production at the Netherlands entity.
Inspections scheduled for later in 2026 at Carbogen Amcis sites (no details given).
demand_pricing: New commercial leadership: Angela Ameriks joined as Global CCO; new India sales leadership; hiring in UK, Central Europe and US West Coast (start 1 Sept).
SPRINT early-phase acquisition initiative reported as successful; over 13 late-phase projects in drug substance portfolio, including PPQ campaigns.
Drug product (Saint-Beauzire, France): RFP volumes up and quotation rates raised, though market is challenging; big pharma audits had positive outcomes.
Naroda: CDMO RFPs rising steeply, several in final negotiation; semiconductor and fine-chemical projects in progress.

504614|2026-06.headline: Sarda Energy Q1 FY27 total income INR 1,717 cr, EBITDA INR 762 cr and PAT INR 478 cr (+9.4% YoY), helped by a one-time INR 110 cr net benefit.

Net profit included a one-time net benefit of INR 110 cr from regulatory approval of the final project cost of the 113 MW Sikkim hydro plant, which management said was worth about INR 162.6 cr of revenue and INR 18 cr of interest income. 530813|2026-06.headline: KRBL Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR261 crores (16.7% margin) on price hikes and investment gains, while exports fell about 50% on Middle East disruption.

qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Bansal cited enterprise customer forward projections and visibility, plus new D2C and quick commerce customers (Amazon Now); he said the company is fairly confident in the numbers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 capex is for the growth upgrade versus beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex is front-loaded before the peak season and the product mix is unchanged, with 77% in network and automation; the assets last 5+ years.

qa_highlights.question: Can the margin bridge be explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Praveen Kumar KJ said transport cost rose 0.1 pp to 18.8%, consumables rose 0.1 pp, and other costs rose 0.1 pp; lost-shipment cost fell 0.6 pp to 5.5%. Efficiency work offset larger cost increases; management says most of the cost impact is already in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the minimum wage hike?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2-2.5 crore per month across four states; management said much of the delta does not hit P&L because many staff earn incentives above minimum wage.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 dark store contribution disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined store-wise revenue but said all stores together contribute 10-12% of other logistics services revenue; it will provide more detail as the vertical matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is there cannibalisation between vertical dark-store quick commerce and SDD for D2C?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Bansal said SKU width differs (about 1 million SKUs for same-day vs up to 10,000 for dark-store delivery), so the models serve different needs in the same cities.

risks_watch: Diesel and crude-linked cost pressure; management absorbed a 5-day diesel pass-through lag.
Labour supply squeeze and minimum wage increases (INR2-2.5 crore per month).
Pricing pressure from listed anchor customers, which management says is managed through rate cards with volume-linked discounts.
Dependence on two large Express 3PL networks and on Amazon Now ramp-up.
Dark store economics still unproven at store level; 47 live of 100 target by year-end.
Upside growth guidance depends on new customer acquisition and sales-season volumes.
544685|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive. Management was assertive on raising guidance and on market-share gains, but gave limited numbers on dark stores, realisation and the margin bridge, and deflected some questions on pricing and realisation to external factors.
key_quotes: Through all of it, our performance effectively showed zero volatility.
We were not going to let the external environment decide our margins.

502090|2026-06.headline: Sagar Cements Q1 FY27: volumes up ~13% YoY but loss after tax of ₹28 crore and EBITDA of ₹451/tonne on West Asia-driven cost inflation.
502090|2026-06.overview: Volumes grew about 13% YoY and revenue rose 5% YoY, with realisations broadly stable. Profitability moderated as energy, fuel and packaging costs rose amid West Asia tensions, leaving EBITDA at ₹451 per tonne and a loss after tax of ₹28 crore. Management maintained a 7 million tonne volume target for FY27 (excluding clinker) and reiterated FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, down from the earlier ~₹600 reference raised by an analyst. Capex completed in the quarter includes Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne expansion and the remaining 1.55 MW of Gudipadu waste heat recovery; the 0.75 million tonne Andhra Cements expansion is expected by quarter-end.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, driven by volumes; realisations broadly stable
Moderated in Q1 on higher energy, fuel and packaging costs
vs ₹1,450 per tonne in Q1 FY26
vs ₹860 per tonne in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Mattampally (Telangana)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 65% in Q1; debt-free per management and carries waste heat recovery, which keeps its grid power cost lower.

segments.name: Gudipadu (AP)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 79% in Q1; remaining 1.55 MW of the 4.35 MW waste heat recovery commissioned, with ~₹25/tonne consolidated saving expected.

segments.name: Bayyavaram (AP)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 67% in Q1.

segments.name: Jeerabad (MP)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 96% in Q1; 0.5 million tonne expansion completed, with ramp-up expected as soon as possible and some clinker still sold until volumes stabilise.

segments.name: Jajpur (Odisha)
segments.commentary: Utilisation 50% in Q1.

segments.name: Dachepalli
segments.commentary: Utilisation 42% in Q1.

segments.name: Andhra Cements
segments.commentary: Utilisation near 50%, targeted at ~60% by end-FY27 and 60–70% thereafter; variable cost ~₹100–125/tonne above Mattampally due to grid power with no waste heat recovery; new cement mill due end-September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of ~7 million tonnes, excluding clinker sales; management sees FY28 volume growth in double digits.
FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, assuming prices stay flat; management said ₹550 is 'definitely doable'.
Q2 FY27 to see cost increase from maintenance shutdowns at three plants (Mattampally, Jeerabad among them) and inventory cost adjustment; management expects recovery in Q3 and Q4.
Management pencilled in ~₹100/tonne cost inflation (₹50 power and fuel, ₹50 miscellaneous), offset by efficiency gains; inventory covers operations up to mid-October.
No capex plans beyond ~₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028, apart from ~₹240 crore of ongoing capex spread over FY27 and FY28.
Vizag land monetisation of ₹150 crore pencilled for FY27 and ~₹200 crore for FY28, pending a generic Government GO.
capex_capacity: Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne capacity expansion completed in Q1; Madhya Pradesh volumes expected to rise after this.
Gudipadu 1.55 MW waste heat recovery commissioned, completing 4.35 MW total installed capacity.
Andhra Cements 0.75 million tonne cement capacity expansion expected to complete before end of Q2 FY27.
New cement mill at Andhra due for commissioning end-September 2026.
Andhra waste heat recovery planned in the next couple of years, expected to deliver savings similar to Gudipadu's.
Super fine building material work has started; operational plan to be shared by end of Q2.
demand_pricing: South footprint ~80% of volumes; AP and Telangana combined Q1 demand up ~11% YoY, Tamil Nadu ~4% (April negative, June ~20%), Kerala ~12%, Karnataka flat; South demand ~6–6.5% YTD, expected at 8–10% for FY27.
Madhya Pradesh demand grew ~9–10%; Maharashtra and Odisha described as healthy.
July demand expected to track Q1 trend, with labour availability back.
Prices rose early in Q1 but moderated late in the quarter; flat from March exit to July, with a ₹50–60/tonne realisation gain cited.
Management expects price hikes eventually, citing flat cement inflation over 10 years against substantial cost inflation; timing and size uncertain amid competitive intensity.
Tamil Nadu ban on transport of rough stones and aggregates to other states: management sees no impact.
Heat waves and election-related labour shortages in Eastern and Southern India disrupted Q1 execution.

500660|2026-06.headline: GSK Pharma Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 15% to INR924 crore and PAT 24% to INR253 crore, with growth led by innovation at 7% of sales.
500660|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales grew 15% YoY to INR924 crore, with EBITDA up 17% and EBITDA margin up 50 bps, and PAT up 24% to INR253 crore (27.6% margin). Management said about 4-5 percentage points of headline growth came from a soft base after last year's CMO supply disruption, so underlying growth was about 9-10%. Innovation products (IP-protected) reached 7% of sales versus about 4% a year ago, contributing about 4 points of growth. PAT growth included a one-off dividend from subsidiary Biddle Sawyer; excluding it, PAT growth was about 17%. Spend-to-sales rose about 1 percentage point on front-loaded promotional investment ahead of the September quarter.

financial_highlights.value: improved ~50 bps YoY (management expects ~34% range for year)

financial_highlights.change: driven by pricing and product mix
vs ~4% last year; ~4 pts of headline growth
opex up ~36% YoY per analyst question; management confirmed deliberate front-loading

segments.name: General medicines (Gen Med)
segments.commentary: Grew in double digits and most brands outgrew the market per IQVIA, with EIs of 105-106. About 44-45% of the Gen Med portfolio is under price control. Gen Med is about 2,000 field staff.

segments.name: Vaccines
segments.commentary: Held private-segment leadership in pediatric vaccines. Shingrix grew about 65% in Q1, sells about 45,000-50,000 doses per quarter, and crossed INR100 crore on a MAT basis. A phasing issue in availability for a couple of vaccines is to be corrected in Q2.

segments.name: Specialty (respiratory, oncology)
segments.commentary: Nucala has about 600 active patients, with new patient starts roughly doubling YoY to about 100-120 a month. Trelegy Ellipta holds about 10,000-12,000 units a month despite about 10-12 generic launches of umeclidinium. Zejula and Jemperli together treat about 250-300 patients a quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; the stated objective is sustaining double-digit growth.
Opex/investment ratios expected to moderate in following quarters; S&A ratio to normalise toward historical levels through the year.
EBITDA margin expected to be roughly in the 34% range, similar to last year.
Q2 seasonal acute trends were said to be tracking in line with expectations, with June and July data supportive.
Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin, second-line RRMM) launch expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27 after DCGI approval.
Bepirovirsen (Hibsago) launch in India expected within three to four quarters.
Arexvy launch and upcoming Ojjaara expected within roughly 18-24 months.
Long-term ambition of INR8,000 crore top line in four to five years; established portfolio to grow 8-10%, with new launches providing the rest of the ~13% CAGR.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing is local-for-local: own plant at Nashik (MIDC) plus about 20 contract manufacturers; all Gen Med products are made locally. Management sees no need for further local manufacturing beyond the current portfolio.

Field force of about 2,000 in Gen Med and 200 in established vaccines; about 40-45 people in oncology (medical oncology and hematology), with new hiring focused on areas of little or no presence such as liver disease.
Blended productivity about INR15-16 lakh per rep, up 5-6% this quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry Q1 growth was about 13.5%, with volume growth around 2%; oncology was the fastest-growing Indian pharma segment at about 27%.
GSK Q1 blended volume growth was about 3-3.5%, price about 6%, and the balance from new introductions.
Acute therapies are about 60% of the Indian pharma market; Q2 (July-September) is the seasonal peak.
Supply chain: management said the worst is behind, after the CMO disruption, and that cost hardening on imported inputs from rupee depreciation has not yet hit margins.
Zejula is among the top five PARP inhibitors; Jemperli is the only approved immunotherapy in first-line endometrial cancer, which has about 17,000-19,000 new diagnoses a year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the parent's restructuring focused on specialty hurt growth and India investment, given the Gen Med-heavy portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gen Med still grows in double digits and the parent's cost programme is a simplification effort; India was already restructured, and global trials are being brought to India to shorten launch lags.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the CMO-related lost Calpol sales have been recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the worst is behind, the supply chain has been stress-tested, and business continuity plans are being strengthened. It did not quantify recovery.

qa_highlights.question: How is reach into Tier 3/4 and rural areas ensured, given peers' distributor models?
qa_highlights.answer: A super-distributor manages some tail-end brands to reach mofussil interiors; no new operating model details were given beyond this.

qa_highlights.question: What are trends for the seasonal acute Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Trends since June are tracking in line with expectations; management expects Q2 broadly in line with its plan.

qa_highlights.question: Is the opex spike a one-off, and how should EBITDA margins be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Spend was deliberately front-loaded ahead of the September quarter (about 3,800 HCP events); ratios should moderate, and EBITDA margins are expected around 34%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on Blenrep and Bepirovirsen commercialisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Blenrep approved by DCGI for second-line RRMM, launch Q2 or Q3 FY27 (about 7,000-8,000 second-line patients). Bepirovirsen launch in three to four quarters; pricing model still being worked out.

risks_watch: Opex intensity and S&A ratio normalisation: the Q1 spend spike must moderate in coming quarters to hold a ~34% EBITDA margin.
Imported input cost hardening from rupee depreciation, and post-West Asia cost pressure, could erode gross margin gains.
Sustainability of underlying growth, which was about 9-10% after the base effect, versus the 13-14% CAGR implied by the INR8,000 crore target.
Launch timing of Blenrep (Q2/Q3 FY27) and Bepirovirsen, and their commercial model for a functional cure in chronic hepatitis B.
Q1 PAT growth included a one-off dividend from Biddle Sawyer, so the underlying growth rate is about 17%.
Trelegy Ellipta and Nucala face generic and competitive pressure; monitor Trelegy units and Nucala patient growth.

544120|2026-06.headline: Capital SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 41.3 crore, with NIM at 4.21% and GNPA down to 2.47%.
544120|2026-06.overview: Gross advances reached INR 9,074 crore, up 22% YoY and 4.5% QoQ, while deposits grew 16% YoY to INR 10,596 crore with CASA at 36.7%. NIM improved to 4.21% from 4.06% a year ago, helped by deposit repricing and a higher average CD ratio of 83%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.47% and NNPA at 1.14%, as the bank raised PCR to 54.5%. Management guided to stable NIM near 4.2% for FY27, ROA of 1.35-1.4% for FY27, and 22% advance growth.

financial_highlights.change: from 4.06% in Q4 FY26 and 4.06% in Q1 FY26
GNPA -28 bps YoY, -7 bps QoQ; NNPA from 1.39% YoY and 1.24% QoQ
broadly in line with last year

segments.name: Business loans (MSME and other)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 27% of book (22% a year ago) and 35% of incremental disbursements; MSME grew 49% YoY and 11% QoQ, with average ticket INR 28 lakh and yield on business loans at 10.5%.

segments.name: Mortgage
segments.commentary: Stable at 25% of book (around 26% a year ago); grew 3% QoQ and 10% YoY, with housing yield at 9.87% vs 9.85% in Q4 FY26; average housing ticket INR 20-25 lakh.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Share fell to about 27% from 30% a year ago; target ticket INR 5-35 lakh (average INR 30 lakh), with yields of 12-12.5% over the last 7-9 quarters and 50% LTV collateral.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Stable at 14% of book; calibrated lending to well-rated corporates.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: Yield of 12.27%; grew 5% QoQ and 18% YoY.

segments.name: Consumption loans
segments.commentary: Stable at around 7% of book, mostly top-up loans; 2-3% of the book is loan against deposits or securities.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Advances outside Punjab grew over 30% YoY and are 25% of the book (24% in Q4 FY26, 21% a year ago).

guidance_outlook: FY27 advance growth guided at 22%; FY29 loan book target of INR 16,000 crore plus.
NIM expected to hold around 4.2% through FY27, with expansion in FY28 and FY29 as average CD ratio rises from 83% toward mid-to-high 80s.
ROA targeted at 1.35-1.4% in FY27 and 1.6% plus by FY29; ROE targeted at 15% plus by FY29.
Medium-term net NPA target of around 1% (below 1% per Vision 2029); management expects stable PCR from here.
Opex to see some improvement in FY27 (currently 2.95-2.98% of assets) after Q1 salary increments; larger opex growth expected in FY29.
Around INR 1,597 crore of term deposits reprice in Q2 FY27, with a 10-12 bps benefit that management expects to be offset by higher incremental deposit costs.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 216 branches across 5 states and 2 union territories as of June 2026; 74% of branches are semi-urban and rural.

Average CD ratio at 83% (vs 80.9% in Q1 FY26); management targets mid-to-high 80s, implying an incremental 3-6% from deployment of investments and interbank balances (yielding about 7-7.5%) into advances at about 10.5-11%.
Liquidity coverage ratio averaged 184.18%; capital adequacy at 21.6%.
demand_pricing: Competition in housing loans from PSU banks has eased due to deposit repricing, with mortgage growth recovering to 10% YoY; housing yields held at about 9.87%.
Private universal banks focus above INR 1 crore tickets, leaving the INR 10-50 lakh MSME band to the bank; management says it prices slightly above market for service and turnaround time.
Agri yields are priced 25-35 bps above PSB rates for INR 5-25 lakh tickets; management cites industry-wide risk premium rather than bank-specific pricing.
Cost of deposits fell to 5.6%; the spread target of cost of deposits vs advance yield is 5.05-5.3%. Advance yield fell to 10.9% from 11.1% a year ago.
Management said 50% of advances are fixed-rate and 50% floating-rate; 48.67% of the book resets annually, mainly MCLR-linked; MCLR was raised by 10 bps in the quarter.

513228|2026-06.headline: Pennar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 3.6% to INR884.55 crore while PBT grew 16% to INR46.8 crore, with PBT margin at 5.38%.
513228|2026-06.overview: Revenue growth was moderate as legacy steel, railways and diversified businesses shrank, but EBITDA rose 13.3% to INR106.8 crore and PBT rose 16% to INR46.8 crore. Management attributed margin gains to mix shift toward PEB US and engineering services, though PEB India margins dropped for a month or two due to delayed steel pass-through. Order books are at record levels in PEB India (INR1,008 crore), PEB US (above USD100 million) and boilers (INR150.75 crore), while Hydraulics orders softened on US tariff uncertainty. Management guided to double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth in Q2 and reiterated a 7% PBT margin target over about three years. Questions on segment EBITDA, employee cost growth, other income and the promoter warrant issue drew deferred or defensive answers.

financial_highlights.value: INR884.55 crore (transcript also cites INR870.4 crore vs INR845.7 crore, +2.9%)

financial_highlights.change: Depressed by INR1.75 crore tax adjustment relating to a prior quarter, per management
from 27.14%; INR252.12 crore from INR231.81 crore
from INR92.5 crore, +16%; US employee cost +37% (INR16.24 crore increase)

financial_highlights.value: Interest INR2.26 crore, gain on investments INR2.16 crore, rental and export incentives INR3.05 crore, write-backs remainder

financial_highlights.change: management said slightly above internal target; long-term guide ~4%
from INR450 crore; down about 15% YoY

segments.name: PEB India
segments.commentary: Order book at record INR1,008 crore; execution hit by engineering clearance and delivery issues, and PEB margins fell over 200 bps for a month or two until steel price increases were passed through. Management expects margins to recover from Q2.

segments.name: PEB US (Ascent)
segments.commentary: Order backlog crossed USD100 million (about USD70 million cited in one answer as the prior-quarter level), revenue running ahead of plan; US revenue stream described as the highest-margin unit with operating margins above 15%.

segments.name: Engineering Services (structural engineering, BIM)
segments.commentary: Structured engineering grew 26.3%; annual revenue about INR70 crore, mainly US and Europe. Management says productivity gains of 30-35% are being used against AI-driven automation risk.

segments.name: Boilers
segments.commentary: Order backlog at record INR150.75 crore; first industrial power boiler achieved as pre-qualification reference, and first pharmaceutical-sector orders won.

segments.name: Hydraulics
segments.commentary: Order backlog about INR30 crore; US activity slowed on tariff uncertainty while Europe performed well. Management is in wait-and-watch mode; the business is about INR100 crore a year.

segments.name: Tech Pennar
segments.commentary: Named as the weak spot: thin order book and execution issues at some customers; a new sales team is in place with improvement expected from Q2.

segments.name: BIW (body-in-white)
segments.commentary: Hyundai plant commissioned in August 2026 with three programmes; management expects revenue to double over the next three months on a scheduled order basis.

segments.name: Legacy businesses (steel, railways/Cadnum, tubing)
segments.commentary: About INR1,300 crore annual revenue, now about 25% of group revenue and declining; capital is no longer being deployed and management is seeking a value-realisation structure similar to the solar JV with Zetwerk.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27: double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth expected; PEB margins expected to return to prior levels from Q2.
FY27: management says 20% PAT growth is the stated goal for the year; ROCE target about 25-30% for the year (Q2 above 20%).
Debt-to-equity target about 0.7 by year-end FY27; management says anything above 0.7 is unacceptable, with INR20 crore of the promoter's INR50 crore commitment already in.
Over three years PBT margin target of about 7%, from 5.38% now.
Management said it expects the combined entity to grow at double-digit rates from Q2 as higher-growth units scale, while legacy units decline.
capex_capacity: PEB India capacity is available, but execution was hit by engineering clearance delays and labour constraints, which management says are resolved.
PEB US and India advance payments fell to about 25% from 5-10% earlier, as the company moved to reduce working capital.
BIW Hyundai plant commissioned in August 2026; three programmes in place.
Management is deliberately building raw-material inventory ahead of expected PEB revenue, which weighed on working capital.
Management is not deploying capital into legacy businesses (steel, railways, Cadnum aerospace); no material capex.
demand_pricing: Record order books across PEB India, PEB US and boilers; the company says the larger backlog is now ready to execute.
Hydraulics bookings below expectations on US tariff uncertainty; Europe performed well.
Steel price pass-through was delayed for about 1-2 months, which compressed PEB margins.
Management says it has about 6-7% share of an addressable market of INR2.25-2.3 lakh crore, and an obtainable market of about INR80,000 crore.
Solar JV with Zetwerk: Pennar holds 45% of a 2 GW capacity entity with potential revenue of about INR4,000 crore; no current revenue numbers were disclosed.

544430|2026-06.headline: Sambhv Q1 FY27 revenue INR732 crore (+31% YoY), EBITDA INR100 crore, PAT INR56 crore; FY27 EBITDA/ton guided INR7,500-8,500.
544430|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the highest-ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with revenue up 31%, EBITDA up 31% and PAT up 70% YoY. Sales volume rose 16% YoY and value-added volume rose 27%, with EBITDA per ton of about INR10,000 excluding sponge iron. The Kuthrel stainless CR coil debottlenecking doubled capacity to 116,000 tpa, and the Kesda greenfield project is guided for Q4 FY27 commissioning. Management guided FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of 10-15% over FY26, and flagged softer MS pricing and stainless steel import competition as the main headwinds.

segments.name: MS ERW pipes and tubes
segments.commentary: Q1 net realisation about INR60,000/ton, guided to about INR58,000/ton in Q2. Capacity utilisation above 65% against a market norm of about 70%.

segments.name: GP pipe and coil
segments.commentary: Q1 net realisation about INR75,000/ton, guided to INR72,000-73,000/ton in Q2. Operating above 90% utilisation.

segments.name: Stainless steel (SS 200 / SS 300)
segments.commentary: Q1 realisation about INR1,40,000/ton for SS 200 and INR2,00,000-2,10,000/ton for SS 300; Q2 guided to INR1,30,000 and about INR2,00,000. Stainless CR coil margin guided at INR15,000-16,000/ton; utilisation about 60% after the Kuthrel doubling to 116,000 tpa.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA per ton guided at INR7,500-8,500 (weighted average), and Q2 FY27 at INR7,500-8,500.
FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of 10-15% over FY26; FY26 operating EBITDA base cited as about INR270 crore.
FY27 sales volume guided at 10-15% above FY26; segment volumes: MS pipes 230,000-240,000 t, GP pipe and coil about 90,000 t, stainless CR coil about 60,000 t (about 400,000 t total value-added).
FY27 margin guided at about 12% with a 1-2% standard deviation; PAT margin guided at about 6% with a 1% standard deviation.
FY28 EBITDA per ton guided above INR8,000; FY28 revenue cited at about INR4,500 crore.
MS pipe prices expected to fall a further 3-5% this financial year; stainless steel pricing expected to soften as QCO relaxation lets in imports.
capex_capacity: Kesda greenfield (Phase 1, 360,000 tpa stainless CR coil) at INR930 crore, targeted for trial run and production in Q4 FY27; total stainless capacity to reach 476,000 tpa by Q4 2027.
Kuthrel Unit 2 stainless CR coil debottlenecking completed; capacity doubled from 58,000 to 116,000 tpa, with consent to operate now in place.
Captive power plant of INR200 crore plus DFT pipe mill (150,000 t) with INR100 crore spend in FY27 and INR100 crore in FY28; DFT mill expected to lift MS capacity to about 500,000 t by Q2 2028.
8 MW rooftop solar at Kuthrel for INR25 crore (INR10-12 crore in FY27, balance in FY28), expected to reduce power cost.

Total captive power to reach about 88-90 MW from 25 MW today, with a 2030 target of about 150 MW; estimated power cost saving of INR180-200 crore. Finished capacity target of over 2 million tpa by 2030.
Peak debt by end FY27 cited as INR800-850 crore term debt and INR200-300 crore working capital; cost of debt 7.5-8%.
Working capital need of about INR200 crore in FY28 (about 35% utilisation) rising to INR300 crore in FY29 (60-65% utilisation) for Kesda.
demand_pricing: Management expects MS pipe prices to stabilise after a further 3-5% decline this financial year; cited a lackluster demand environment elsewhere but said Sambhv's volume of about 20,000-24,000 t/month is not much affected.

Stainless steel: QCO framework relaxed and shipping delays from the war situation; Chinese stainless cost now broadly at par with Indian cost, so pricing competition expected to rise once shipments normalise.
Nickel exposure limited: about 90% of production is 200-series, sourced from nickel scrap and alloys.
Stainless co-branding: 28 MoU partners (18 added in Q1); about 1,200 t supplied currently, targeted at about 2,500 t by year end.
Net realisations for Q1 and Q2 guided as above; management said segment-wise realisation is not rising much, with overall realisation rising from the SS mix shift.
Engineers India Limited and Chennai Metro Rail approvals received during the quarter, supporting institutional sales.

qa_highlights.question: What will peak debt, finance cost and cost of debt look like after Kesda?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt by end FY27 of about INR800-850 crore term debt and INR200-300 crore working capital; cost of debt currently 7.5-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kesda Q4 FY27 timeline achievable through monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is optimistic on trial run and production by Q4 FY27; substructure is done and superstructure is advanced, with machinery installation proceeding in monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the INR100 crore warrant issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Funds for capex at the holding company and the wholly owned subsidiary Sambhv Tubes, working capital for Kesda, and promoter contribution toward the solar, DFT mill and captive power projects; promoters and management to participate.

qa_highlights.question: Why co-branding for stainless pipes instead of direct sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 800-900 small pipe makers sell regionally, so co-branding with 28 partners builds Sambhv awareness; Sambhv sells only CR coil, not pipe.

qa_highlights.question: Stainless CR coil margin and HR coil margin?
qa_highlights.answer: CR coil margin about INR15,000-16,000/ton; HR coil expected at INR12,000-13,000/ton once Kesda starts, and lower initially.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA growth guided at only 10-15% given the stainless ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Stainless production has peaked, so volume looks flat; management expects pricing softness in stainless as QCO relaxation allows imports, and is guiding conservatively.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital needs and capex schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital of about INR200 crore in FY28 and INR300 crore in FY29 for Kesda; Kesda INR930 crore mostly in FY27, with power plant and DFT mill spread over FY27 and FY28.

544578|2026-06.headline: Rubicon Q1 FY27 revenue rose 52% YoY to INR5,343 million and operating EBITDA margin hit 24.2%; FY27 EBITDA margin guide raised to 23%.

Gross margin rose about 140 bps QoQ to 67.7% as management gave up lower-margin US business and reduced reliance on contract manufacturing. USD revenue was USD55 million, up 32% YoY but slightly down QoQ. Operating cash flow was weak at INR285 million due to delayed GST refunds, which management expects to normalise in Q2. Arinna Lifesciences (acquired April 2026) contributed about INR12 crore of revenue and immaterial EBITDA. Management said it ranks number one across the six IPO-showcased products; market shares are broadly stable to up.

500645|2026-06.headline: Deepak Fertilisers Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA hit record INR845 crore (+65% YoY) at 26% margin; PAT INR490 crore (+101% YoY).
500645|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose 22% YoY to INR3,256 crore, with operating EBITDA up 65% YoY and 139% QoQ to a record INR845 crore. Margin expanded to 26% from 19% a year ago and about 12% in Q4 FY26, driven by stronger TAN, nitric acid and IPA realisations plus early benefits of Equinor LNG supply, which began with the first cargo in May. Net debt fell to INR4,719 crore and debt/EBITDA improved to 1.4x despite over INR500 crore of quarterly capex. Gopalpur TAN (about 96% complete) and Dahej nitric acid (about 93% complete) are expected to start operations in Q2 FY27, within the approved capex envelope of about INR3,850 crore spent to date.

segments.name: Mining chemicals (TAN)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR911 crore (+37% YoY) on volume of 130 KT, which was lower due to a few days of supply-chain disruption from new PESO guidelines. B2C revenue grew 42% to INR151 crore, 17% of segment revenue.

segments.name: Industrial chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR490 crore. Merchant nitric acid sales flat at around 80 KT YoY. IPA volumes hit by propylene availability constraints, though pharma-grade demand and realisations supported profit.

segments.name: Crop nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,367 crore (+9% YoY) despite delayed monsoon, high input costs and subsidy misalignment. Manufactured NPK sales +4%; specialty and Croptek products are 43% of segment revenue.

guidance_outlook: Gopalpur TAN and Dahej nitric acid projects expected to commence operations in Q2 FY27; management said they should be operational around end of the quarter.
Management expects faster ramp-up for the new plants (same chemistry, not new technology); analyst's ~80% utilisation for Q4 FY27 was not explicitly confirmed.
Equinor LNG savings described as sizable; a figure of around INR300 crore was cited by an analyst, and management said current conditions support that level but it could rise or fall.
Phase-out of legacy gas contracts to complete by Q4 FY27, after which Equinor supply is expected to be sufficient for all requirements.
Management declined to guide full-year EBITDA margin, calling it too early; said the new capacities and gas benefits will lift the base by year-end.
Q2 expected to see a seasonal slowdown in mining from monsoon, with a pick-up in crop nutrition demand after good rains.
Ammonia prices expected to stay elevated for at least some more quarters; ammonia FOB Middle East around USD600/t.
Net debt expected to peak near current levels (about INR4,700-4,800 crore) before deleveraging begins this year.
capex_capacity: Gopalpur TAN project about 96% complete; Dahej nitric acid project about 93% complete; both expected to start operations in Q2 FY27.
Total capex spent till Q1 about INR3,850 crore, within approved envelope.

Ammonia plant averaged 94% utilisation in Q1; April had gas constraints, but supply normalised after May with Equinor. Debottlenecking yielded about 10% capacity improvement, with the plant running at about 5 lakh tonnes.
Ammonia for Gopalpur to be bought externally; the other three captive businesses at Taloja use captive ammonia. About 80% of ammonia is captive consumption.
New plants to be depreciated over 25 years.
Explosives acquisition (DMSL) completed in May 2026; facility being upgraded with new explosives plants planned.
demand_pricing: TAN and ammonia prices remain elevated due to the Middle East conflict but have softened from war peaks, which management said was factored in.
Analyst flagged possible Russian FGAN export ban from October 2026, per global analysts; management did not confirm.
Management sees market growing 6-7% p.a.; even with new capacity, the market is expected to stay roughly balanced to short over the medium term.
Nitric acid pricing improved on supply tightness and lower imports; merchant nitric acid volumes flat YoY.
Raw-material pressure expected in crop nutrition (phos acid, sulphur) with the need for faster government subsidy corrections.
Management said elevated margins in TAN are expected to persist near term, with medium-to-long-term margins returning to a consistent level.

qa_highlights.question: What was ammonia plant capacity utilisation in Q1 given gas issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Average 94% for the quarter; April had gas constraints, but post-May supply from Equinor resolved them. Debottlenecking gave about 10% capacity improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TAN volumes fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a raw material, production or demand issue; a few days of logistics disruption from new PESO guidelines. Management expects normal volumes YoY from Q2 onward, with the monsoon seasonal slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DMSL listing going to be an IPO or demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Committed in principle to list DMSL; form (IPO or demerger) not yet decided, with communication to the market later.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Equinor gas contract phasing in and what are the savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy contracts phase out through Q4 FY27; Equinor to be sufficient for full requirement afterward. Savings described as sizable; an analyst cited around INR300 crore, which management said is broadly in line under current conditions but could move with crude, Henry Hub and international prices.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 EBITDA margins match Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit; said it is too early to estimate, though new capacity and full-quarter gas benefits will raise the base by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt near peak at around INR4,700-4,800 crore with some more debt possible during final project leg; deleveraging expected from this year as new capex contributes. Working capital needs are low, as the businesses are B2B.

Priorities for next year: residual technology modernisation, automation, resilience and customer-experience enhancements.

544225|2026-06.headline: Ola Electric Q1 FY27 deliveries nearly doubled QoQ to ~39,200 units, Auto revenue ₹455 crore (+72% QoQ), Auto gross margin 30.5%.
544225|2026-06.overview: Ola returned to volume growth in Q1 FY27, with deliveries of ~39,200 units (nearly 2x QoQ) and orders of ~44,000, while electric two-wheeler registrations grew 97% against a market up ~17% QoQ, lifting share from 5.1% to 8.4%. Auto revenue rose 72% QoQ to ₹455 crore with gross profit of ₹139 crore and Auto gross margin held at 30.5%. Consolidated opex fell 22% QoQ to ₹333 crore (including a ~₹55 crore one-time reversal of a Cell ACC PLI penalty provision), and adjusted operating EBITDA improved to –₹195 crore from –₹326 crore in Q4 FY26. Management pivoted Auto distribution from company-owned to a multi-channel model with dealers, with the first batch slated to go live on Janmashtami (4 September), and reiterated a Cell gigafactory ramp to 6 GWh.

Capex beyond Cell project about ₹30-50 crore; ₹50 crore used as target number.
Pending 4680-cell Roadster deliveries to be completed over Q2 and Q3 FY27.

Depreciation policy aligned to industry norms, causing ~₹10-20 crore delta.

Shakti to be sold through company stores, automotive dealers and industry-specific inverter/battery channels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ASP decline sharply sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 90% to product mix; ASP guided at ~₹1.25 lakh ±5%.

qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; management expects steady growth but declined quarter-on-quarter numbers.

qa_highlights.answer: A few thousand own-cell vehicles on road; about 3 of ~9-10 SKUs use 4680 cells. Shakti Gen 1 (NMC) had no meaningful revenue; Gen 2 (LFP) on 15 August.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Beyond the Cell project, capex ~₹30-50 crore, with ₹50 crore as target; Auto needs hardly any capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy aligned to industry norms after aggressive depreciation; delta ~₹10-20 crore, no write-off mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: LFP vs NMC mix and 20 GWh expansion timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all Auto to move to LFP over time, ~20% of Auto stays NMC; Shakti/Mahashakti all LFP. 20 GWh expansion (prismatic) in FY27 with separate Cell-company equity; yields high-70s to ~80% at pause.

qa_highlights.question: Scale of energy storage opportunity and Axis Energy MoU?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites CEA estimate of ~400 GWh needed over 5-6 years, which it views as an underestimate; Mahashakti expected to have round-trip efficiency a few points above peers and safety above standard 5 MWh containers.

qa_highlights.question: Roadster contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Small minority of sales; deliveries slightly below orders in Q1 due to 4680 cell shortage.

Management reiterated 2 million tons capacity by FY29, with 6.5-7 lakh tons of FY27 sales guidance.

Monsoon and geopolitical conditions cited as near-term volume headwinds; July-August volumes described as similar to Q1.
Export focus on Europe, America, Canada and Australia; repeat orders reported.

qa_highlights.question: How is the demand outlook across infrastructure, construction, water, solar and industrial for the rest of FY27?

qa_highlights.question: What is the end-use mix, and which new industries are emerging?

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for EBITDA per ton to reach INR3,750-4,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to exceed INR4,000/t once the three new plants reach critical mass and extra dealer rebates are withdrawn; the target is for FY28 per later comments.

544239|2026-06.headline: ECOS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,113.7 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% and FY27 margin guidance was cut to ~10%.

Guidance credibility: an investor criticised the sudden guidance change within one quarter, and management said competitive behaviour is hard to predict.
Other expenses fell only because a prior-year one-time provision did not recur, so the base is not a structural saving.
