Q1 openings: 3 Bangalore stores (2 Varthur, 1 Mysore Road). Closures: 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai); management said 2 of the Bangalore closures had already been relocated.
New stores: Stanley Boutique Colombo, Sri Lanka (July 2026, JV with Singer Sri Lanka PLC) and Sofas & More Jaipur (first Rajasthan store).
demand_pricing: Demand demand: customer inquiries and footfall encouraging, but conversions slowed as residential handovers were delayed 12 to 18 months in several projects; West Asia supply chain issues constrained construction material availability.
Stanley Superlative Living targets buyers with budgets of INR 3 to 5 crores and above, aiming for average ticket size up to about 10x current levels with full home design, build and install.
Management said 6 COCO cities (Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, Chennai and one other) account for about 80% of India's luxury housing, per company claim.
Sofas & More: about 95% of customers are direct buyers without designers or specifiers; Stanley relies more on specifiers and design-led purchases.
Export exposure is small; management said the business is mainly domestic and US tariffs have stalled talks with large US buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation about INR 15 crores per quarter (above INR 50 crores a year)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Sudhir Iyer attributed it to Ind AS accounting; IGAAP depreciation would be lower, and the charge is front-loaded in the earlier years of asset lives. He did not give asset-class detail.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report pre-Ind AS margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said only Ind AS numbers will be published, but pre-Ind AS figures are available offline. Management then gave pre-Ind AS averages: gross margin 56% to 60%, EBITDA margin 11% to 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the order book and B2B billing?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book stood at INR 68 crores on 30 June 2026, up from INR 62 crores at March 2026. Products are produced but cannot be invoiced until logistics clear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stanley Superlative Living format?
qa_highlights.answer: A large-format store in mature markets, replacing smaller Stanley stores. Management said Hyderabad is the proof of concept; the format consolidates Boutique and Level Next. Sofas & More becomes the value-premium brand.

qa_highlights.question: How many COCO stores are store-level EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: 35 of 42 mature COCO stores are EBITDA positive, after cash rent (the answer refers to 42 stores out of 47 total). Break-even takes 6 to 12 months and ROI 24 to 36 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are same-store sales growth and mature store revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 mature-store SSSG was slightly negative due to format changes; target is 15% to 20% YoY. Average annual revenue: Sofas & More about INR 5 crores, Boutique INR 4 to 5 crores, Level Next about INR 10 crores plus.

544306|2026-06.headline: Sai Life Sciences Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR553 crore, with CRO up 26% and CDMO up 6%; management guides to a stronger H2.
544306|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR553 crore against INR496 crore a year earlier, up about 12% YoY. CRO (about 40% of revenue) grew about 26% YoY, while CDMO (about 60%) grew about 6%. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations and reiterated a stronger H2 as new capacity comes online, with the Discovery facility already commissioned and sold out and Bidar production block 1 due in H2/Q3. Management reaffirmed the mid-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin of 28-30%, and FY27 capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore.

financial_highlights.change: about +12% YoY vs INR496 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: CRO / Discovery
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 26% YoY. About 65% of customers now use integrated discovery services, mainly biotech; a pilot with a large pharma converted to a long-term high-volume discovery chemistry partnership. Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 and is already sold out.

segments.name: CDMO / CMC
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 6% YoY, described as lumpy. Portfolio is 33 active commercial molecules and 14 late-phase molecules. Three of the four commercial contracts expected this year were added in Q1; management said three are commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three (anecdotal).

guidance_outlook: Mid-term (3-5 year) revenue growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management said guidance should be viewed over a longer horizon, not quarterly.
EBITDA margin range of 28-30% reiterated.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with capacity coming on stream by end-Q2 or early Q3; management referenced a 40/60 historical H1/H2 split, with FY26 at about 48/52.
FY27 capex guidance INR1,100-1,300 crore unchanged; no FY28 capex guidance yet.
Target of about 1,150 KL capacity by FY27 reconfirmed.
Expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27.
Formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2) expected to be operational in about six months, within the current fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 FY27 and is sold out, ahead of the one-to-1.5-year fill timeline management had assumed.
Bidar: two production blocks of 225 KL each (450 KL total); first block due for completion and operation in H2/Q3 FY27, on track.
First dedicated peptide development lab coming online shortly for a top-tier pharma company; GMP pilot-scale peptide facility coming online soon for clinical supply.
Commercial peptide manufacturing at a new greenfield site near Hyderabad expected to be operational in 2028; groundbreaking planned. Peptide spend to end-2028 likely below INR300 crore.
XDC Center of Excellence close to opening; ADC pilot-scale space under build.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian outsourcing demand is strengthened by geopolitical concerns and IP worries, with customers using India for diversification.

FTE (dedicated team) model: one top-tier pharma FTE relationship expanded from small scale to a sizable dedicated contract running end-to-end from discovery to commercial; another large pharma process development FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2, with work from Q3.

Pipeline sourced via three routes: biotech molecules acquired by pharma partners, molecules transferred from acquirers, and FTE-led progression. Five of six late-phase molecules added in 15 months came via large pharma FTE relationships.
Phase 3 pipeline: one customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, one expected Q2 FY28.
Modalities: about 4-5% of revenue from new modalities, all in development and discovery, none in commercial. Peptide work is mainly early-stage discovery.
Sai works with 19 of the top 25 pharma companies. Five FDA-approved molecules in calendar 2025 involved Sai in discovery, development or commercial manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Has the shift to integrated CRDMO and big pharma FTE engagements accelerated this calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still early, with relationships growing from one service at a time; FTE model started about 15 months ago and acceleration is seen mainly in scale and scope.

qa_highlights.question: Is the H2-weighted FY27 guidance due to capacity, given the historical split?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said FY26 was about 48/52 H1/H2 versus a historical 40/60, and capacity additions are behind the stronger H2 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex threshold and what would cause a slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal hurdle rates are set above the company's ROCE/ROE targets. Capacity-addition capex can be slowed if demand slows; capability-building capex is harder to defer absent severe circumstances.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 15-20% when the pipeline is large and recent quarters slowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is framed over 3-5 years given lumpiness; management said it is not constraining growth and FY26 grew close to 30%, with quarterly revenue driven by delivery timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI initiative the same as the high-throughput experimentation platform?
qa_highlights.answer: No. HTE generates more data points per experiment; the AI initiative targets non-value-added chemist and operator work, with an update expected before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial profile of the four new commercial contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Three of four are commercial supplies, described as decently sized by value; one is a lower-volume product. Primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotally.

risks_watch: CDMO growth of about 6% YoY and quarterly lumpiness; H2 recovery depends on Bidar block 1 and formulation start-up timelines.
Capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore is heavy; FY28 capex guidance not yet given.
Formulation entry (oral solids to Phase 2, China+1 driven) is new; management says it is not yet commercial and profitability was questioned.
Management did not disclose revenue at the individual molecule or customer level, and declined to discuss mAb strategy or fermentation capex.
Commercial peptide capacity not due until 2028.
544306|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FTE model, with a long-term framing; cautious and evasive on quarterly guidance, customer-level revenue, and capex phasing beyond FY27. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations.
key_quotes: We remain confident in our ability to sustain our longer-term revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20%, and the EBITDA range of 28% to 30%.
Generally, we don't quantify what we're doing with each customer.

544814|2026-06.headline: Knack Packaging Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40.5% YoY to INR2,647.7 million, with EBITDA up 53.1% and margin at 22.35%.
544814|2026-06.overview: Knack Packaging reported Q1 FY27 as its first earnings call after listing on NSE and BSE. Consolidated revenue grew 40.5% YoY on 20.9% higher volume (10,940 MT), with EBITDA up 53.1% and PAT up 47.96%. Management attributed margin gains to operating leverage, cost discipline, solar power and a rising share of pinch-bottom bags. Capacity utilisation is about 91%, with a rented plant added to bridge until the IPO-funded plant, targeted for October 2027, takes installed capacity to about 70,000 MT.

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Management said about 55-56% of sales are export and about 45% domestic; export margins are about 5-6% gross profit higher than domestic. Operations span 74 countries, up from 71 in FY26.

segments.name: PLWPP and pinch-bottom bags
segments.commentary: Pinch-bottom share of sales rose from 19-20% in prior-year quarters to a current 22.5-23%. Management says about 70% of sales are PLWPP bags. Two pinch-bottom machines (about INR20 crore each) were installed in the last quarter of FY26.

guidance_outlook: New IPO-funded plant targeted for commissioning in October 2027, taking installed capacity to about 70,000 MT from about 43,300 MT at listing.
Management expects Q1 FY27 sales levels to be maintained until the new plant starts, using the rented facilities.
Another rented plant of about 5,040 MT annual capacity was added about a month before the call; trials are under way.
Main construction of the new plant is expected to pick up after the monsoon; machinery finalisation is ongoing.
No explicit FY27 volume or EBITDA per kg guidance was given.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 43,300 MT at listing; operating above 48,000 MT including rented facilities, at about 91% utilisation.
Target installed capacity about 70,000 MT once the new plant is commissioned (October 2027).
Management said it is running at 90-92% utilisation and has no spare space to expand existing sites.
11 MW solar farm at Khedbrahma started in the last quarter; electricity cost fell about 1.1% of revenue YoY from solar.
Gross block rose to INR416 crore, with INR141 crore added over the year; the IPO proceeds are about INR320 crore.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR130 crore cited by management.
Customer retention is about 90%; more than 2,000 customers and over 13,000 SKUs.
Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue (figures varied on the call), with about 600 SKUs and a contract of 2 years plus a 1-year extension, priced as polymer cost plus conversion.
About 45-50% of customers are on fixed conversion-cost pricing with raw material pass-through; the rest are small buyers with pass-through pricing on the day of change.
Management said it passes polymer price changes through to customers on the same day, and that about 50% of input cost changes are passed on, with about 60% retained in some cases.

Management claims about 10% market share in the Indian bag segment (per a Technopack report), and says it is the leader in pinch-bottom bags in India. Management named Polytex (USA) as its only direct listed peer.

qa_highlights.question: Why are ROCE and asset turnover so high versus peers, and how is margin sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset turn is 2.53x on gross block and 4.12x on net block as of 30 June 2026, versus peer averages of about 1.5-2x. It attributed this to specialised machinery and a shift to higher-margin pinch-bottom bags. ROCE is supported by ongoing profits and IPO proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: How is the polymer price rise being managed, and how fast is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a SAP S/4HANA forecasting system, buys in cash and in bulk, and passes price changes to customers the same day. It said conversion-cost contracts cover 45-50% of customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Cargill relationship and the FX gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Cargill (USA) business grew from INR4 crore in 2020 to about INR140 crore; it is on a 2+1-year contract and buys finished bags. Management cited the cost of packaging below 1% of product value. FX gain in Q1 FY27 was INR1.6 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How does EBITDA per kg look, and how fast will pinch-bottom volumes move?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited EBITDA per kg of about INR54 in Q1 and INR45 in FY26. Pinch-bottom share is 22.5-23% and is rising; the call did not give a 70,000 MT utilisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth be sustained in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 sales levels to hold as the rented plants run until the new plant starts in October 2027. It said the onboarding process for new products is long, so marketing is being increased through rented capacity.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude volatility; management said the situation is fully volatile, and pass-through on fixed-conversion contracts shifts cost to the company.
Commissioning timing of the October 2027 plant; construction main phase is after the monsoon.
Dependence on rented plants for interim capacity and on rented facilities until the new plant starts.
Customer concentration: Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue, and figures on the call were inconsistent.
Several figures and facts on the call were inconsistent or corrected (ROCE corrected from 57.73% to 54.73%; Cargill share stated as 12%, 16-17%); verify in filings.
Export share of about 55% and FX exposure; the company reported only INR1.6 crore FX gain in the quarter.
Gross block growth to INR416 crore; management did not commit to maintaining asset turn of 2.5x+ on INR380 crore expansion.
544814|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, margins and customer relationships, with a strong emphasis on the 30-year history and first-mover position. Less precise on peer benchmarking, competitor data and volume guidance, where answers were loose and some figures were corrected during the call.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR273 crore a year earlier; INR30.75 crore added in Q1 FY27

544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.

segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR50 crores from INR28 crores in the first three months of FY26. Mumbai was the largest market in FY26 GMV at INR205 crores.

segments.name: Delhi (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

539551|2026-06.headline: Narayana Health Q1 FY27 call: India hospital EBITDA margin ~24% with footfalls up; insurance and UK losses weigh on consolidated margins.
539551|2026-06.overview: Management said India hospital growth came from both volumes and realisations, helped by high-end and robotic procedures and clinic-driven footfalls. Insurance losses rose sharply in the quarter on a small book, though management said the July renewal cycle went through at 100% acceptance and Cayman insurance losses fell to about USD 3.7 million from USD 5.2 million quarter-on-quarter. UK business was hit by a severe heat wave and a longer software certification timeline, and it remains about 95% NHS by value. Management guided that margins should trend upward over the medium term but gave no numeric targets.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited 40% EBITDA growth; margin expansion stated as 400 bps YoY for India business net of clinic losses

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR 15 crore in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.change: down from approx. USD 5.2 million in Q4 FY26 (QoQ)

financial_highlights.value: about 6% in USD terms (analyst figure, not disputed)
about 5% YoY growth on pre-acquisition comparable basis
INR 327 crore in Q1 FY27 vs INR 244 crore in Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.change: Q4 figure reflected a Cayman reclass; management said underlying cost flat QoQ

segments.name: India hospitals
segments.commentary: Growth from both ARPOB and footfalls, supported by high-end procedures, robotics and clinic referrals; no meaningful bed addition expected for 2-3 years. Management said margin expansion will continue, with the leverage benefit partly reinvested in integrated care.

segments.name: India clinics
segments.commentary: OP consultations about 66,000 in the quarter, up about 30% YoY; clinic footfall about 30% of hospital OPD footfall. Clinic losses about INR 15 crore in Q1 FY27; two more clinics opening this quarter.

segments.name: India insurance (Narayana Health Insurance)
segments.commentary: Loss ratio spiked in Q1 on a small book with a few large claims; expense ratio fell substantially. Management is focused on SME and retail, AI-led claims review, and in-housing claims; no numeric loss or breakeven guidance.

segments.name: Cayman hospitals
segments.commentary: Sequentially soft quarter, but management cited healthy double-digit YoY growth in discharges and OP footfall. Cayman margins back to earlier levels after ramp-up, per management.

segments.name: Cayman insurance
segments.commentary: Quarterly losses fell to about USD 3.7 million from about USD 5.2 million QoQ. July renewals had 100% acceptance; book about USD 60 million annualised.

segments.name: UK hospitals
segments.commentary: Acquired business was about 95% NHS by value, against a peer at about 70%; private share at an all-time high but still low. Heat wave disrupted chillers and HVAC; software certification adds about 4 to 6 months.

guidance_outlook: Management expects core operating margin to expand over time given leverage benefit, but declined to give a numeric projection.
Insurance book expected to moderate its loss ratio over time; management would not give a timeline for profitability.
Management said worst of Cayman insurance losses is behind on a rolling two-to-three-quarter basis, barring large-claim swings.
Management committed INR 3,000 crore of projects over the next two years, funded partly by internal cash and partly by borrowing.
Net debt to EBITDA expected to decline by FY30 after debt rises during the 2-3 year build-out.
ALOS target of 3.9 to 4 days (currently 4.3).
capex_capacity: Southwest Bangalore project of about 100 beds: construction at end stage; start targeted by end of Q2 FY27.

Three projects slipped from FY28 to FY29 (two) and FY30 (one), mainly asset-light partner projects with licensing delays expected to clear in about a month; management said the slips are within the 6-month acceptable window.
No meaningful bed additions expected for the next 2-3 years.
North Bangalore expansion already announced for the first round; future expansion priority in Bangalore.
Expansion to new states such as UP and Bihar deferred until Phase 1 of capital deployment progresses.
demand_pricing: India hospital volume growth across all regions, alongside realisation gains; management declined to give volume or price numbers.
Analyst questioned the 24% EBITDA margin versus peers' lower ARPOB; management said further margin expansion is possible.
UK private revenue share at an all-time high but still very low versus peers; NHS dependence to fall over 4 to 5 years.
Cayman insurance renewals in July had 100% acceptance of repriced premiums; January cycle expected to be similar.
Management said it does not disclose the share of insurance-originated admissions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India hospital footfalls rise alongside ARPOB, and is margin expansion still possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Venkatesh cited high-end and robotic procedures and clinic-driven brand strength (clinic footfall about 30% of OPD). Sandhya said margin expansion will continue because no beds are being added, but the split between cash flow and affordable pricing is an ongoing choice.

qa_highlights.question: Why did insurance losses spike and will they persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Ravi said the book is small, so a few large claims distort loss ratios; expense ratio fell substantially. Actions include AI-led claims review, in-housing claims, and a shift toward SME and retail, with no timeline for normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UK ROCE and the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandhya said it is too early to measure and reporting may start in about four quarters. Anesh said there is no defined ROCE target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Cayman hospital growth soft and when will Cayman insurance break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Anesh said Q1 is seasonally weak and volumes grew at a healthy double-digit rate YoY; insurance losses fell QoQ to about USD 3.7 million, and July renewals were fully accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Why did UK losses rise sequentially and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Anesh cited a severe heat wave that disrupted HVAC and chillers, and software certification taking 4 to 6 months longer than expected. Cost measures include standardising consumables and automating admin, with private payer mix still early.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the jump in professional fees to doctors QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandhya said Q4 included a reclass of Cayman doctor fees out of the professional fees line, so the Q4 base was distorted; underlying cost was flat.

540762|2026-06.headline: TII Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18% to Rs 2,366 Cr, but PBT fell to Rs 213 Cr on steel cost lag; management expects full recovery.
540762|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew to Rs 2,366 Cr from Rs 2,007 Cr, while standalone PBT declined to Rs 213 Cr from Rs 222 Cr, with management attributing margin pressure to steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 that pass through to customers with a 2-3 quarter lag. Engineering revenue rose 21% to Rs 1,566 Cr with flat PBIT at Rs 153 Cr, and Metal Formed Products PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr despite 11.5% revenue growth. The e-mobility (Clean Mobility) business posted its highest-ever quarterly turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr and management said losses likely peaked, with volumes up about 64% QoQ. Management said steel price recovery, including Q1 under-recovery, will be fully recovered, while non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery talks with OEMs are ongoing.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated PBT before JV share, exceptionals and tax
CG Power and Industrial Solutions (56.29%) revenue
CG Power and Industrial Solutions PBT

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,566 Cr vs Rs 1,298 Cr YoY; PBIT flat at Rs 153 Cr. Volume grew about 17%, and margins were hit by steel cost inflation.

segments.name: Metal Formed Products (MFP)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 408 Cr vs Rs 366 Cr YoY (about 11.5%), but PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr. Growth was volume-led, with railways a drag and a Hyundai-linked unit weak; a western region greenfield plant is delayed by six months.

segments.name: Mobility (Clean Mobility / e-mobility)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 250 Cr vs Rs 198 Cr YoY; PBIT Rs 9 Cr vs Rs 7 Cr. Management cited highest-ever turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr (the call figure), with negative EBIT narrowing by about Rs 40-50 Cr per analyst, and three-wheeler billing of 1,924 units.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 256 Cr vs Rs 236 Cr YoY; PBIT Rs 21 Cr vs Rs 17 Cr. Includes TI Medical, CDMO (3xper) and Orange Koi, the newly acquired metal injection moulding start-up.

Management declined to quantify the Q1 under-recovery but reiterated guidance for double-digit EBIT margin growth.

530367|2026-06.headline: NRB Bearings Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR370 crore and PAT 15% to INR38 crore; management guides to a long-term INR2,700-3,000 crore FY31 vision.

Standalone sales grew 14.7% YoY, standalone PAT 31.7% and standalone EBITDA 21.7%. Management focused on diversification into aerospace (via the Mahant Tool Room/MTR acquisition), electrification, off-highway and robotics, plus a first US Corvette planet-pin production order. Management declined to give quarterly or FY27 growth guidance and repeatedly redirected questions to the trailing 12-month baseline.

508814|2026-06.headline: Cosmo First Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 46% to Rs 1,166 crore and EBITDA 26% to Rs 147 crore, though margin fell to 12.6%.
508814|2026-06.overview: Revenue growth was driven mainly by raw material pass-through after the West Asia conflict, with volume up only 9%. EBITDA rose 26% to Rs 147 crore, helped by better per-kg contribution across base, semi-specialty and specialty films, and management says all B2B businesses are now profitable. Export volumes fell 13% due to port congestion and a line maintenance outage, and BOPET margins compressed sharply sequentially. Net debt was flat at Rs 1,166 crore (2.3x EBITDA), and management targets below 2x within 12 months.

segments.name: BOPP films (base, semi-specialty, specialty)
segments.commentary: Specialty sales volume up 12% YoY; specialty mix at 61%, highest in five quarters, with target of 70%. Gross margin Rs 30/kg including non-repeating stock gain; management said base BOPP margin ex-stock gain was broadly flat.

segments.name: BOPET films
segments.commentary: Gross margin fell to Rs 9/kg from Rs 18/kg in Q4 FY26. Capacity is 30,000 tonnes against 277,000 tonnes of BOPP. Management expects margins to recover after recently levied anti-dumping duty.

segments.name: US film business
segments.commentary: Export volumes down 13% due to port congestion and in-transit shipments. US subsidiary received about USD 7 million duty refund in July 2026, not yet appropriated. Management expects US revenue to grow 25-30% in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 34% YoY with 25% EBITDA margin, improved 2 percentage points QoQ. About 80% of business is backward integration into group films. FY27 growth guided at about 50%; Rs 400-500 crore FY30 target may be reached by FY29.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue up over 58% YoY and turned EBITDA positive. FY26 revenue about Rs 100 crore; FY27 guided Rs 150-160 crore and Rs 200+ crore next year, with capacity up 50% at minimal capex over next two quarters.

segments.name: Zigly (petcare)
segments.commentary: Monthly GMV run rate about Rs 100 crore (annualised Rs 100 crore, per the call). Gross margin 47%, services 64% of sales mix, private label revenue up 105% YoY, 47 centres, 29,000 customers in the quarter. Management estimates breakeven at about Rs 250 crore revenue, a couple of years away.

segments.name: Cosmo Consumer (window films, PPF, ceramic coatings)
segments.commentary: Near EBITDA breakeven in Q1. Revenue grew 4.5x last year and management expects more than 3x this year. Margin about 25% (EBIT per management, up from 15-17% at launch); gross margin target 35-40%. TV advertising began July 2026; 150 dealers in 100+ cities.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated topline to grow about 20% in FY27, with commensurate bottom-line growth.
New businesses to grow about 60% in FY27; specialty chemicals about 50%.
ROCE targeted at 15-20% within 12-24 months, from about 11% in the last financial year.
Net debt/EBITDA to fall below 2x within 12 months; Rs 400-500 crore debt reduction over two years with minimal capex.
Specialty mix target of 67-68% next year if 10% volume growth is achieved; management also cited 70% as an objective.
Renewable power savings of about Rs 25 crore per year not yet in Q1; one PPA from Q3 FY27, another from Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Film capacity utilisation at 85% in Q1 FY27; about 15% spare capacity expected to be filled over the next two quarters.
Specialty chemicals has 15-20% spare capacity.
Plastech capacity to rise 50% over the next two quarters at minimal capex; revenue capacity of Rs 250+ crore.
Management says capex cycle is largely complete; Rs 1,200 crore strategic capex over the last three years. Future incremental capex directed to specialty assets.
BOPP capacity 277,000 tonnes; BOPET 30,000 tonnes. A line under maintenance in Q4 FY26 lost a couple of thousand tonnes of volume.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices rose sharply after the West Asia conflict; pass-through inflated revenue and working capital (Rs 85 crore).
Management said the spread on BOPP fluctuates daily; July spreads were broadly in line with Q1. Demand described as quite strong.
India is slightly over capacity in BOPET, which management expects to correct; anti-dumping duty recently levied.
Specialty film margins above Rs 60/kg for five consecutive quarters; semi-specialty about Rs 15-20/kg above base film margins.
PPF penetration in India about 2%, growing 30%; pet care market growing 22% a year.

544028|2026-06.headline: Tata Technologies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.3% QoQ in constant currency to $175.4M (25.2% YoY), with management reiterating double-digit FY27 organic growth.
544028|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was $175.4M, up 4.3% QoQ and 25.2% YoY in constant currency, with Services at $136.6M (approximately 78% of revenue). Operating EBITDA was about $28M, a 16.1% margin, up 10 bps QoQ, while PBT fell to INR 252 crores from INR 283 crores because Q4 included a one-time Labour Code provision reversal. Management highlighted the $100M Tenneco engagement and a Japanese OEM full-vehicle program, and reiterated double-digit FY27 organic growth with growth expected to be much greater in H2 than H1. Near-term margin expansion may moderate due to upfront ramp-up investments and a Germany wage increase in Q2.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Revenue $136.6M (approx. 78% of total), +4.3% QoQ cc and +24.4% YoY cc. Anchor-account share fell to 48.9%, down 150 bps QoQ; embedded and software grew 8.5% QoQ in USD.

segments.name: Technology Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue $38.8M, +4.2% QoQ cc and +27.9% YoY cc. Education grew 9.1% QoQ while product business declined 2.6% (seasonality); margin fell 250 bps on mix toward education.

segments.name: Automotive non-anchor
segments.commentary: Revenue $43.9M, +6.7% QoQ and +56.3% YoY. Non-anchor is about 49% of services revenue and about 36% of total automotive, per CFO.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Revenue about $10.2M, +6.4% QoQ and +38.1% YoY. Management sees a path to a $100M target in the next two to three years.

segments.name: IHM
segments.commentary: Revenue about $15M; no growth rate was disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Europe (geography)
segments.commentary: Revenue about $67.9M, +10.1% QoQ, supported by Es-Tec integration; Germany saw an uptick, but some customers are under restructuring.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: strong double-digit organic revenue growth, with services as the primary growth engine; management reiterated this on the call.
Growth is expected to be much greater in H2 than H1 FY27, with the ramp-up of closed deals as the main driver; quarterly phasing depends on team mobilisation and customer readiness.
Management said it would not focus on a specific margin milestone; it expects QoQ margin expansion to continue in Q2 despite the annual wage increase in Q2.
Tenneco ($100M, 5-year deal) begins execution in Q2, scales toward calendar year-end, and will require incremental headcount and cost.
Management said Germany wage increases in Q2 will be absorbed, which may moderate the pace of margin expansion near term.
capex_capacity: Several large strategic engagements and full-vehicle programs entered mobilisation in Q1, requiring upfront investment in talent, ramp-up, transition and delivery readiness ahead of steady-state revenue.
BMW TechWorks crossed 2,000 engineers; it is a JV and not consolidated into revenue.
Headcount optimised to 12,579 with a balanced FTE vs outsourced mix; hiring is selective and focused on strategic skill areas.
Development cycles of 18 to 24 months for full vehicles, versus 36 to 48 months at many Western OEMs, per management.
demand_pricing: Tenneco: $100M multiyear transformation engagement spanning engineering, digital, AI-enabled processes and operational modernisation; described as mostly new business with a small renewal element.
A North American industrial equipment manufacturer engagement covering systems, software and embedded software, using AI-enabled methodologies.
A leading global OEM Range Extender Vehicle program; a leading off-highway manufacturer selected Tata Technologies as preferred partner.
A Japanese OEM full-vehicle development program, which management described as a first-time relationship in this space and a path into Japan.
Management said deal momentum continued into Q2 and that additional large deals have closed beyond those disclosed; no customer names or sizes were given.
Management said tariffs and EV tapering had held back demand over the past ~18 months, and that clarity is now returning and investment is resuming.
On AI pricing, management said AI is a force multiplier on productivity and that it sees the work volume as expanding, not shrinking.

Management guided to a recovery from Q3 and reiterated the FY27 revenue target of INR1,200 crores, while net debt rose to about INR152 crores.

capex_capacity: Land: a legally binding contract for more than 50 acres of contiguous land in a prime Lucknow location was executed in Q1; about 15 acres of land aggregation was also completed.
Latitude 27: completed towers targeted for revenue recognition within FY27 or by April-May 2027; completion certificate scheduled for November 2027.
Eldeco Trinity: third and last tower (Faith) launched in mid-June 2026.
Eldeco City Courtyard: a small commercial component of the Eldeco City integrated township, a very small share of salable area in forthcoming projects.
Management is pursuing a land-banking strategy aimed at bringing land to development quickly rather than holding it on the books.
demand_pricing: Q1 bookings normalised after the exceptional launch-led Q4 FY26 performance; management says customer engagement remains healthy.
Management says the strategy is to sell most inventory in the initial launch period; tail inventory is now being sold at current market prices.
Lucknow commercial rates described as steady with an upward trend, but management declined to quote figures.
Management says the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway is driving inbound migration and housing interest in Lucknow.
Management declined to give FY27 sales or booking guidance; it pointed to presentation data on average realisation for estimation.

qa_highlights.question: Why diversify into projects like Eldeco City Courtyard, and is commercial/mixed-use a larger opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Courtyard is a small commercial component of the integrated Eldeco City township, needed to meet development control norms; it is a very small share of salable area and Imperia Avenue shows good reception.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 37% EBITDA margin in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue mix shifted to Imperia Phase 2, a high-margin horizontal project (about 60% gross margin), while Q1 FY26 was dominated by a lower-margin vertical project; management expects horizontal projects to keep margins higher.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Imperia Phase 2 revenue is recognised, and how much is left?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 170-180 crores of the roughly INR 300 crores GDV is still to be recognised, predominantly in FY27 but timing depends on sales and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy ready inventory remains and how much can be sold in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 75 crores of legacy inventory remains; management expects 40-60% to be liquidated in the current year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Latitude 27 can be recognised in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Towers are targeted for revenue recognition within FY27 or by April-May 2027; management estimates 15-20% of GDV (about INR 275-300 crores) between March and May 2027, depending on execution and RERA extensions.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Faith tower bookings traction weak, and how is the booking figure reconciled with area?
qa_highlights.answer: Faith launched mid-June after war-related delays; the sample flat was ready 10-15 June, with 2-3 bookings and 20-25 in pipeline. Rajiv Khurana said the slides now show area allotted rather than area booked, since allotment follows booking, and the two are not directly comparable.

514448|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY (about 10% volume, 7% price) while EBITDA margin fell to about 14.4% on raw material spike.
514448|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 17% YoY in Q1 FY27, with roughly 10% from volumes and about 7% from price increases taken in April and mid-May. EBITDA margin compressed to about 14.4%, which management attributed to 6-7 percentage points of raw material cost inflation (VAM spike linked to West Asia tensions) plus about 3-4 points of aggressive dealer-meet and sales promotion spend. Management guided back to a 22-25% EBITDA range longer term and said it is too early to commit to 28-29% in Q2. Working capital weakened, with receivables around INR 145-150 crore (debtor days above 150) and inventory higher, and management targets 120 days over the next two to three quarters.

financial_highlights.change: hit by 6-7 pts raw material cost and 3-4 pts promotion spend

financial_highlights.value: about INR 360 crore annualised (cited by analyst; ~INR 90 crore per quarter)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 INR 314 crore, FY25 INR 285 crore, FY24 INR 258-260 crore
debtor days above 150 vs target of 120
vs about INR 2 crore for ~30 meets last year

segments.name: Wood adhesives (Euro brand)
segments.commentary: Core business; management cites brand strength, distribution reach and carpenter trust. Registered carpenters rose to 210,000, about 10,000 added in the quarter.

segments.name: OEM / modular kitchens and furniture
segments.commentary: About 6% of revenue currently; management targets 10-12% over time, with team build-out in Bangalore, Telangana and Delhi.

guidance_outlook: Brownfield expansion from 2,000 to 3,500 tonnes per month expected operational within one to two months; management says it can support INR 600-650 crore revenue from the existing plant.
Longer-term target of INR 500 crore revenue by end FY29 at 23-25% EBITDA margin, requiring 15-20% volume growth; management also refers to a INR 1,000 crore vision.
EBITDA margin guided at 22-25% longer term; management said it is too early to say whether Q2 can reach 28-29%.
Sales promotion expense for FY27 expected at about 10% above last year's INR 45-50 crore, scaling with volume.
Advertising and branding targeted at 6-7% of revenue for the year (currently about 4%).
Employee cost expected to settle at 11-13% of revenue per management.
Greenfield plant: initial capex INR 45-50 crore, funded from internal accruals, to add 1,500 tpm in phases; timing not specified.
Debtor days target of about 120 within two to three quarters.
NSE listing said to be in process and expected within the quarter; buyback discussed internally but no decision.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion from 2,000 to 3,500 tonnes per month; management said about 80% of work is done and capacity is ready within one to two months.
Q1 utilisation about 65-70% (earlier stated as about 60%); average monthly volume about 1,300 tonnes, March peak about 2,400 tonnes.
Brownfield capex about INR 7 crore, described as asset-light.
Greenfield: INR 45-50 crore initial capex (about 50% land, 50% construction, balance machinery), adds 1,500 tpm in phases.
Raw material inventory was about 30 days; management has contracted 90-day supply for Q2.
demand_pricing: VAM (key raw material) averaged about INR 75-78/kg, spiked to INR 170-180/kg in late March, eased to INR 135-150, and is now about INR 100/kg.
Price hikes: about 4% in April and about 11% in mid-May; management says about 7% realised for Q1 and no further hike in Q2.
Volume response: customers delayed projects in late May; demand recovered from June and July described as good; volume growth of about 10% maintained.
Retailer margin passed on is 7-13% (about 11-12% average); about 13,000 retailers served directly via 54 branches across about 15 states.
Competition: management said market leaders also raised prices and maintained EBITDA, which it read as rational pricing.
Bad debt historically below 0.5% per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue plan before Greenfield expansion, and what margins are expected by FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the brownfield 3,500 tpm can generate INR 600-650 crore revenue and the Greenfield is a longer-term step; EBITDA guidance remains 22-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sales promotion and employee costs rise sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales force raised from 520 to 562, new hires and April appraisals; about INR 4.5 crore spent on 54 dealer meets in 45 days (vs about INR 2 crore for 30 meets last year).

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 margins rebound to 28-29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say; management is targeting the 22-25% range longer term and said raw material cooling has begun but not returned to earlier levels.

qa_highlights.question: What share of growth came from volume vs price?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% from volume and about 7% from price in Q1; management expects price contribution may not persist if realisations normalise, and aims for 15-20% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth weak in FY24-FY26 after the COVID-era surge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a consolidation phase after an 80% jump to INR 181 crore; it cited FY25 and FY26 growth of about 9-10% and two quarters above 15% in the last four.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and debtor days outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables about INR 145-150 crore; target 120 days in two to three quarters, with slower push to protect retailer relationships in newer states; cited bad debt below 0.5%.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from VAM volatility; the 90-day supply contracts were only signed for Q2, and the EBITDA recovery depends on them.
Receivable days above 150 versus 120 target, concentrated in newer states; working capital and inventory build-up.
Demand elasticity after 7% price hike; management said some projects were held in late May and June.
Whether volumes ramp into the 3,500 tpm capacity; Q1 utilisation about 65-70%, with the 600-650 crore revenue claim not yet tested.
Sustained high employee and promotion spend without commensurate volume gains.
Possible price rollback if realisations normalise, which management said it may need to take.
NSE listing and buyback decision still pending.
514448|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, but noticeably cautious and sometimes evasive on near-term margin (declined to commit to Q2 28-29%) and on receivables timing. Answers on revenue capacity conversion and the INR 500 crore target were loosely framed and required clarification from analysts.

506222|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 133.9% to INR201.4 crore (26.1% margin) even as sales volume fell 26% to 38.9 KT.
506222|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income grew 6.6% to INR770.5 crore and PAT rose 150.3% to INR137.3 crore, driven by a sharp margin jump, while volumes dropped 26% as non-OEM buyers held back amid Middle East-driven raw material price volatility. Consolidated (India plus Thailand) volume was 50.8 KT, EBITDA INR223.6 crore at 22% margin. Management described the margin gain as a snapshot of a volatile quarter, not a sustainable run rate, and gave no volume guidance. The ABS capacity expansion is said to be on track for completion in FY27 without a firm commissioning month, and Thailand volumes remain subdued.

segments.name: ABS (India)
segments.commentary: Demand fell in the quarter, with a smaller drop than polystyrene; OEM is about 70% or more of ABS sales. Management did not give a segment volume split.

segments.name: Polystyrene (India)
segments.commentary: Hit harder than ABS, mainly in the non-OEM/unorganised segment; OEM is about 50% of PS sales. Management did not give volume numbers.

segments.name: SAN
segments.commentary: Merchant sales run at about 15,000-20,000 tonnes a year against roughly 100,000 tonnes of capacity; most output is used captively, and merchant sales will continue after the ABS expansion.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Running at low utilisation on specific products; volumes were broadly maintained quarter on quarter, but new business has not yet translated into meaningful volume growth. Validation cycles run 12-24 months.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance given; management said it is 'virtually impossible' to forecast given the current environment.
Management said Q1 margins are not indicative of sustainable performance; for modelling, assume margins similar to the existing business, with the expansion adding volume.
ABS expansion (about 50,000 tonnes in the chemical plant) to be completed in FY27; exact commissioning month not given.
Thailand: management expects volumes to improve over about three years, and margins to be much stronger once volumes arrive.
No new capex or capital allocation changes beyond the ABS expansion; polystyrene expansion to be decided when the business case is clearer.
capex_capacity: ABS expansion is a brownfield project at a running site, so commissioning is complex; management expects completion within FY27.
SAN capacity of about 100,000 tonnes against merchant sales of 15-20 KT a year; expansions planned across rubber, SAN and compounding sites.
Thailand cost base is described as higher than India's; no reduction timeline was given.
demand_pricing: Demand fell in Q1 due to a Middle East-driven price spike from March and high volatility; buyers in the non-OEM/unorganised segment held back. Management put the volume decline at about 15-25% on total polymer.

Styrene monomer went from about $1,000/t pre-war to $1,600-1,700, then about $1,200, and has since traded in a $1,100-1,400 range. Acrylonitrile moved from $1,200 to about $1,800-1,900 and is now $1,400-1,600. Butadiene (bought locally) went from $1,000 to above $2,500 and has since eased.
Styrene monomer is now sourced from alternate suppliers with 10-15 days longer lead times; management said it is 'fully covered' and carried slightly higher raw material inventory at quarter end.
Price pass-through is handled through short-term mechanisms and global price markers; management said previous-quarter pricing was significantly higher and moderated toward quarter end.
Imports: management said it has seen no significant change in import volumes, with some Asian exporters constrained by energy and naphtha shortages. Official import data is not available.

qa_highlights.question: How much did demand fall in India for ABS and PS, and was it driven by non-OEM buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the volume decline was in line across ABS and PS, roughly 15-25% on total polymer. The non-OEM segment was hit harder than OEM, which was affected only muted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin once the Q1 benefit reverses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was a snapshot of an unusual event and is not indicative of sustainable earnings; pre-event performance is the right base. It did not give a number.

qa_highlights.question: Will SAN merchant sales stop after ABS expansion, and what is the capex timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: SAN merchant sales will continue. The ABS expansion will be completed in FY27, but exact timing was not disclosed because the project runs alongside an operating plant.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any new capital allocation plan given extra cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new plan; cash will go to planned capex with the rest returned to shareholders in line with existing policy. No specific dividend or buyback was announced.

qa_highlights.question: What are Thailand's volume and sales plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Thailand sales strategy is to win validations in China, Japan, Vietnam, Korea and others; validations take 12-24 months. No volume guidance was given.

risks_watch: Sustainability of Q1 margins once the price gap and volatility normalise; the company declined to give a normalised margin figure.
Recovery of non-OEM volumes and whether destocking or channel stock effects reverse in the next nine months.
ABS expansion timing (within FY27) and execution risk on a brownfield site.
Thailand utilisation and validation progress; cost base still above India's.
Raw material lead times and alternate sourcing for styrene monomer and acrylonitrile; freight and energy disruptions.
Limited import data availability, which makes competitive import pressure hard to track.
506222|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the strategy and balance sheet, but guarded on numbers: management declined to give volume guidance, timeline precision, margin normalisation or current-quarter pricing, citing volatility.
key_quotes: I think it's about a few hundred tonnes.
So it will happen in this year, like I mentioned, exact month will not be possible to give at this stage.

540710|2026-06.headline: Capacite Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7% to INR629 crore, but EBITDA fell 3% to INR99 crore after a INR10 crore commodity provision.
540710|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY to INR629 crore while EBITDA moderated 3% to INR99 crore, with margin down to 15.7% from 17.2%. PAT fell to INR40 crore (6.2% margin) from INR47 crore, impacted by an additional INR10 crore provision for non-ferrous commodity price escalation not yet covered by government indices. Management attributed the weak execution to labour shortages (workforce fell to about 7,000 in June, roughly 30% short) and a delayed IIT Bombay start, and said labour is now fully in place. Order book stood at INR13,535 crore, with FY27 inflow guidance of INR4,500-5,000 crore and INR1,071 crore booked so far.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26 had a similar INR10 crore provision
Up on ~INR150 crore receipts shifted by 10 days

segments.name: MHADA BDD Worli (via TCC, 35% stake)
segments.commentary: Total TCC order about INR17,000 crore incl. escalation; Capacite share of 34 rehab buildings backlog estimated at INR7,500-8,000 crore x 35%. Management targets about INR20 crore per month in Q2, with about INR60 crore for the quarter and INR75 crore+ in each of Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: CIDCO Maha Awas housing
segments.commentary: Handed over 2 of 7 locations; balance 50% of 16.2m sq ft expected to be handed over Q2-Q3. Remaining backlog about INR2,000-2,500 crore incl. escalation, with FY27 revenue target about INR600 crore; revenue expected to step up from Q3. Extension to March 2028 received.

segments.name: NBCC
segments.commentary: Revenue ramp from under INR15 crore per month last year to about INR60 crore per month from the current quarter; certified bills about INR300 crore, and profit recognition has started after crossing the 20% threshold.

segments.commentary: Start delayed from Q4 FY26 to Q2 FY27 due to tree-cutting permissions; cost about INR65-70 crore of Q1-Q2 revenue. First building handed over and execution started.

segments.name: Signature Global
segments.commentary: Target about INR22 crore monthly revenue; Q1 dipped on labour shortage, now more than 1,000 workers on site, with improvement expected from July-August.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 20% YoY, reiterated; management says Q2 July was strong and needs about INR850 crore+ quarterly run rate in Q3 and Q4.
FY27 order inflow target INR4,500-5,000 crore; management expects to exceed 50% of the upper end in Q2 alone.
Additional INR10 crore provision not expected in Q2; Q3 provision reversal possible if escalation indices catch up, though management gave a disclaimer.
Net debt-free target within 8 quarters reiterated; working capital days expected to fall 25-30 in FY27 after 43-day reduction in FY26.
Term loan repayments of INR102 crore in FY27; debt may rise by INR45-50 crore net due to equipment purchases.
Promoter share pledge reduced from 85.5 lakh shares (31 March 2026) to 50 lakh; full release targeted by fiscal year-end.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex target INR193 crore: INR121 crore aluminium formwork and extrusions, INR56 crore plant and machinery (high-speed lifts, heavier cranes for composite buildings), INR5.43 crore IT including SAP go-live in Q3 FY27.
Q1 FY27 capex was INR52.2 crore.
Management says more than 15 super-high-rise buildings are under execution.
demand_pricing: Order book INR13,535 crore; 62% of book is 40-plus-storey towers per analyst; public 55%, private 45%.
Q1 FY27 order inflow was entirely private; Q2 expected to be equal public and private. Identified public pipeline of INR22,000 crore and private pipeline of INR5,000 crore for Q2-Q3.
Non-ferrous commodity inflation (aluminium up 35-40%) not yet reflected in CPWD/government price variation indices; CPWD DSR escalation about 14% vs raw material up about 40%.
Price variation on order book about 28% per management; NBCC escalation about 6%.
Contract assets plus debtors about 78% of revenue as of 31 March 2026 vs peers 56-65 days; down from about 120% post-COVID.
Working capital days cut 43 in FY26; cash from operations rose from about INR50 crore to about INR250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order book not converting into revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited IIT Bombay delay (INR65-70 crore Q1-Q2 revenue lost), NBCC ramp, and labour shortage; said execution had been about INR8,000-9,000 crore of the INR13,500 crore book and expects revenue to peak in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR20 crore provision reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a substantial portion could reverse in Q3-Q4 if inflation indices catch up, but disclaimed that it depends on indices, not market prices; no further provision expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Status of L1 positions (CIDCO Maha Awas, Chennai Metro commercial complex)?
qa_highlights.answer: Company does not declare L1 positions; said it hopes to convert both into orders within the current month, citing public-domain information.

qa_highlights.question: Contract assets versus peers and exit target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contract assets plus debtors are about 78% of revenue vs peers 56-65 days; aims for leadership by March 2028 and a positive surprise by March 2027. Absolute contract asset figures to be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Capex increase from INR165 crore to INR193 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase is driven by expected orders in Q2, including more formwork, high-speed lifts and cranes for composite projects; term debt may rise by INR45-50 crore net.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt rise to INR522 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase due to about INR150 crore of receipts shifted by 10 days, collected in the current month; management says annual gross and net debt will decline.

544402|2026-06.headline: Jash Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 17% YoY to Rs156 crore and PAT turned positive at about Rs5 crore; FY27 target Rs875 crore reiterated.
544402|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs156 crore, up about 17% YoY, with PAT moving from about minus Rs5 crore to plus Rs5 crore and gross and EBITDA margins both higher YoY. Management said shipments to Qatar, Singapore and other Middle East customers were held back (about Rs15 crore in total), so the quarter was below what management expected. Consolidated order book stands at Rs932 crore (India Rs293 crore, outside India Rs639 crore). Management reiterated FY27 revenue of Rs875 crore and PAT of about Rs100-105 crore, and said Rs1,500 crore revenue is targeted by 2031.

financial_highlights.change: from about minus Rs5 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: India Rs70 crore; outside India Rs80 crore

financial_highlights.change: PAT up significantly; standalone PAT margin about 13% in Q1

financial_highlights.value: Rs932 crore (India Rs293 crore; outside India Rs639 crore)
Jash Engineering Rs559 crore; Rodney Hunt Rs369 crore; Jash Process Equipment Rs29 crore; Waterfront Rs34 crore

segments.commentary: Revenue up about 21% YoY with significantly higher PAT; order book Rs559 crore. Management says standalone PAT margin is about 13% in Q1.

segments.name: Rodney Hunt (US)
segments.commentary: Order book Rs369 crore; management targets over $35-36 million revenue in FY27 with profitability, and expects an 8-9% PAT margin. Management called Q1 a 'first quarter blues' quarter. Management also said the order book is close to $40 million.

segments.name: Jash Process Equipment (ex-WesTech)
segments.commentary: Order book only Rs29 crore; management said Rs150-200 crore of orders were lost in the last three to four months and a full review is under way. Management called this entity a concern.

segments.name: Waterfront
segments.commentary: Revenue up marginally YoY but profit up on high-margin executed orders; management reiterated Rs5 million-plus revenue target with significant profit. Order book Rs34 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs875 crore (India Rs320 crore; outside India Rs555 crore), reiterated; management said there is potential to go beyond this but size is premature until Q2 or Q3 results.
FY27 PAT of about Rs100-105 crore stated in closing remarks; separately, PAT margin of 13-14% described as achievable for the year, depending on geopolitics.
Rs1,500 crore revenue targeted by 2031; FY28 revenue guidance of about Rs1,025 crore mentioned.
Further tariff refund of about Rs7.5 crore pending, expected to be filed and resolved in FY27 after legal vetting.
Saudi Arabia plant: land expected by end of CY2026, plant ready by December 2027, operations by March 2028. US (Houston/Orange) plant: land already acquired, contractor being finalised.
capex_capacity: Foundry expansion and gate and valve manufacturing expansion commissioned in Q1 FY27; management says capacity is up about 30%.

Capex estimates of about $12 million for the US plant and $4 million for Saudi Arabia; about $3 million already held as deposits in the US; the rest from internal accruals and debt (management expects debt of about $3-4 million); US banks reportedly willing to fund.
Data-centre pressure vessels: capacity of about 75-80 vessels a year in the existing Indore setup; management says a new plant may be needed if order flow is sustained.
Chennai plant ramp-up is still in progress; new production head moved there two weeks before the call.
demand_pricing: Pipeline: orders worth Rs72 crore already negotiated; a further Rs60 crore under negotiation; management expects about Rs72 crore more to be added in the current month.

Data-centre vessels: first order for 4 units; a 32-unit order under negotiation; more than 600 vessels quoted. Management says per-vessel value is Rs30-60 lakh and margins will be similar to other business.
US tariff: 15.6% currently (10% special tariff plus 5.6%); management is budgeting for 25% and says it will not price for 100%.
About 70% of US orders are to be made in America and 30% in India; management is cautious on new US order booking. A few large orders above $7 million each are under negotiation but not being pushed.
Mahr Maschinenbau (Austria): taking orders now, with manufacturing in UK and India; first jobs are 16 screens (2 for UK, 14 for Iraq); expected revenue about Rs15 crore per the presentation.
Competition in domestic water control gates and industrial process equipment: Tega, Delkor, Metso Minerals named as main competitors.

Singapore: a Rs6,000 crore figure discussed earlier was for project reports, not a bid; management says the overall Singapore investment is around Rs50,000-60,000 crore, spread over 15-20 years, and Jash's equipment is about 10% of project cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was product-wise and region-wise breakup dropped from the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IR team concluded order mix changes too much quarter to quarter, so data will be shown year-on-year going forward; a Q1 split of Rs70 crore India and Rs80 crore outside India was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 margin gain is from tariff refund versus manufacturing benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination; the Rs5.6 crore tariff refund was booked in consumption. Dharmendra Jain also said the revenue reversal for deferred March recognition (Rs27-28 crore) was offset in June, leaving about Rs10 crore positive.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt margin profile and path to 10% PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 40% of revenue is from old orders and 60% from new orders; expected PAT margin is 8-9%; 10% may be reached by FY28 if things go well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Russia-sanctions/tariff risk and bidding in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bidding continues but aggressive order-chasing has slowed; it will review after the next US visit, and a US Senate bill was cited as a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Saudi and US plant timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi: approvals received, land application submitted, plant ready by December 2027 and operational by March 2028. US: land acquired, contractor to be finalised; both targeted in operation by March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs875 crore FY27 target expected to be exceeded and what is executable?
