qa_highlights.question: Why did Jash Process Equipment (WesTech) underperform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costing systems differed from what was expected at acquisition and marketing was not aggressive; a two-to-three-quarter transition is needed to set a clear direction.

543064|2026-06.headline: Cohance Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 23% YoY to INR4,223 million and adjusted EBITDA margin dropped to 2.2%, with management guiding to a Q2 sequential rebound.
543064|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was management's stated lowest quarter ever, driven by shipment phasing in Pharma CDMO (down 38.7% YoY), a weak agrochemicals quarter, low formulation revenue and NJ Bio underperformance. Sapala grew 2.5x YoY and the standalone business delivered a 9.2% adjusted EBITDA margin, but NJ Bio's INR328 million adjusted EBITDA loss weighed on the consolidated numbers. Management guided to sequential improvement in Q2 FY27, YoY growth from H2 FY27, and margin recovery weighted to H2. Adjusted EBITDA of INR92 million and gross margin of 71.5% (vs 73%) reflected negative operating leverage. Management also laid out an integrated nucleic acid business under Dr. P.Y. Reddy with a path to full Sapala ownership by FY30, and disclosed a USFDA Form 483 with five observations at Pashamylaram.

segments.name: Pharma CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 38.7% YoY on shipment phasing; commercial OTIF near 100% YTD and commercial vs development mix 57:43. Restocking order received for one molecule that destocked last year, with visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28.

segments.name: API+ (API and formulations)
segments.commentary: API performed slightly ahead of internal expectations on favourable pricing and mix. Formulations were below expectations on an API production delay, lower demand for a mature product and a pack configuration change; Nacharam supplies have resumed but remediation continues.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 34.7% YoY, led by H2-skewed AgChem phasing; Performance materials grew and were in line with plan. Two Japanese innovator qualification campaigns are scheduled in FY27.

segments.name: ADC / NJ Bio
segments.commentary: Revenue INR350 million with adjusted EBITDA loss of INR328 million. Some payload deliveries moved from Q1 into later quarters; FTE renewals are at risk from biotech funding conditions.

segments.name: Sapala (oligonucleotides)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR274 million, 2.5x YoY, after supply began on a specialised nucleic acid building blocks programme; EBITDA margin described as strong.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 to show sequential improvement in revenue and EBITDA, with movement toward YoY comparability by end of H1 and YoY growth from H2 FY27.
Margin recovery weighted to H2 FY27; CFO expects Q2 FY27 margin in line with prior-year margin percentage for the current year, accelerating from FY28.
Pharma CDMO: two molecules moved into commercial supply, with six intermediates scheduled for delivery across Q2 and Q3 FY27; customized ADC payload order on schedule for Q2 FY27.
API+: targeting seven new API filings in FY27 and around 10 formulation launches this fiscal year, with two in Q2 FY27.
Management views the USD 1 billion FY30 revenue target as an aspiration; will provide an update by December.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR598 million in Q1 FY27 to support future growth.
Commercial flow reactor at Jaggayyapet expected to be ready next quarter.
New effluent treatment facility commissioned at Ankleshwar; several API debottlenecking projects completed.
Commercialising the new amidites facility and operationalising Sapala's GMP oligonucleotide facility, with validation of priority amidites in progress.
Additional GMP manufacturing laboratory operationalised at Princeton for NJ Bio; another GMP ADC batch released.
Evaluating targeted capacity additions across small molecules, ADCs, API+ and specialty chemicals; Specialty Chemicals R&D, manufacturing and asset strategy being finalised.
demand_pricing: Pharma CDMO RFQ pipeline strengthened, with Phase 3 KSM commercial inquiries from a large pharma company; clients typically have one or two existing sources, which slows conversion.
Ten molecules in Phase 3 pipeline per management; more than 50% are expected to get approval.
Two commercial molecules face patent expiry, but the intermediates supplied are for post-expiry products and revenue impact was already seen in the past two fiscal years.
API+ price increases passed through a major part of raw material escalations, largely in Q4 FY26; API order book described as robust.
Customers in ADC payloads show positive response to MMAE and Exatecan, which are gaining traction as alternatives to Chinese suppliers.
Two CEP approvals obtained and two Korean DMFs filed during the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Growth ranges by segment over 2-3 years and beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Umang Vohra said nucleic acid CDMO could roughly double within 3-4 years, API+ could be a CAGR business and perhaps only 30-40% of its potential, and most growth becomes visible from H2 FY27. He stressed these were directional, not strategic plan targets.

qa_highlights.name: Macro and Indian CDMO RFQ trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Yann D'Herve said geopolitical diversification and US de-risking are increasing late-stage RFQs, but conversion is slow because clients already have one or two sources.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook beyond FY27 after NJ Bio and Sapala changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Agarwal said margins should rise steadily YoY with operating leverage; whether they reach 35% is hard to say. Later, he guided Q2 FY27 margin close to the prior-year level and acceleration from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Restocking contribution from the INR260 crore destocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Agarwal said it is too early to quantify the restocking, since the order for one molecule is spread over two years; clarity is expected by the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses trend and merger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Agarwal said there were no merger-related or one-off costs in Q1; the expenses are administrative and recurring and should be assumed to continue through the year.

544367|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue INR256.4 crore with reported PAT INR46.7 crore; gross margin rose to 47.2% and order book stood at INR1,945 crore.
544367|2026-06.overview: Revenue was INR256.4 crore and reported EBITDA INR64.7 crore (25.2% margin). Excluding a INR7.82 crore non-cash Ind AS 29 hyperinflation loss on Turkish operations, management cited adjusted EBITDA of INR72.5 crore (28.3%) and PAT of INR54.5 crore. The order book closed at INR1,945 crore, about 1.9x last year's revenue. Sangli machinery installation is under way with trial production targeted this month, but customer audits mean meaningful volume is guided for Q3-Q4. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20% and standalone EBITDA of around 20% or high teens, and flagged likely temporary margin moderation in Q3 from new capacity fixed costs and aluminium pass-through.

financial_highlights.change: Year-on-year growth not stated for group; Quality Power standalone rose from INR37 crore to INR69 crore per management
Increased; to rise as Sangli and Endoks capacity is capitalised

financial_highlights.value: INR1,945 crore (Endoks INR801 crore, Mehru INR585 crore, Quality Power standalone INR553 crore)

segments.name: Quality Power standalone
segments.commentary: Order book INR553 crore; standalone revenue INR69 crore per management, up from INR37 crore. Management expects standalone EBITDA of around 20% and flagged Q3 margin moderation from Sangli fixed costs and aluminium cost lag.

segments.name: Mehru
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR83 crore, up from about INR60 crore. Q1 EBITDA about 18% versus internal target of 22-23%, hit by copper and oil price spikes in April; revised guidance to around 18%. Order book INR585 crore; capacity near 100% utilisation.

segments.name: Endoks (Turkey, power electronics / BESS)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR107 crore revenue; Turkish revenue dipped slightly due to Eid holidays. Order book INR801 crore. Power conversion system facility civil works complete, operations expected Q3 FY27. Pipeline about USD60 million BESS PCS orders, with USD40 million more expected in 12 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20%; management declined to raise it before Q3, saying revision may come then.
Margin guidance: model around 20% or high-teens EBITDA; coil products stable guidance about 20%, with most recent orders booked above 25%.
Q3 FY27 standalone margin moderation expected from new Sangli fixed costs and aluminium cost pass-through; margins expected to normalise as utilisation rises over the next 15 months.
Sangli coil facility: trial production targeted this month; commercial revenue to trickle in from Q3, meaningful from Q4. Peak revenue potential about INR1,500-1,800 crore.
HVDC magnet wire facility: full production targeted by Q4 FY27 after three to five months of stabilisation.

WS Insulators acquisition: consolidation expected from Q4 FY27 after SEZ approvals; EV about INR315 crore. Insulator order target of about INR200 crore over next nine months; standalone potential INR250-300 crore without capex, INR450-500 crore with capex.
Management indicated FY28 growth guidance of 50%, pending order book and delivery timelines.
Order book slated for completion in about 15 months.
Interim dividend of INR0.25 per share declared.
capex_capacity: Sangli new facility: machinery installation in progress; last-mile issues around sequencing, utilities and statutory approvals; building completion certificate pending. Approvals and about 60 global customer audits expected to take about six months; initial ISO/OHSAS audits about one month.
HVDC CTC magnet wire facility at Sangli: machinery installation commencing; full production targeted Q4 FY27.

Endoks PCS facility: civil complete; interiors and power electronics fit-out in progress; facility estimated at about USD70-80 million revenue capacity for about USD2 million capex plus about USD1 million further spend.
Winwin Speciality (Vizag, SEZ): about 40 acres of land; planned INR50 crore capex for capacity; about 120 people on site.
Possible second facility decision (Turkey or Vizag for European and export markets) in 6-7 months.
Fundraise of less than INR500 crore planned, including Winwin acquisition funding, INR50 crore capex and US sales entry; roadshows from 20 August and raise targeted before AGM.
demand_pricing: Demand strong across businesses; energy storage at Endoks has inquiry levels ahead of expectations. Data-centre bids of about USD100 million seen, but 12-month delivery periods limit participation for now.
Two large HVDC programmes expected: one partly awarded (expected Q3-Q4) and Barmer tender close to award. About half a dozen STATCOM projects in talks across US, Europe and Australia.
Management said order acceptance is not the constraint; capacity ramp is. Factories sit on close to two years of order book at current capacity.
Every executable order in the book was booked above the margin guidance communicated to the market; pricing discipline maintained.
Group procurement consolidation (CPO appointed) expected to lower aluminium casting and other input costs; about INR3 crore of volume discounts benefited Q1.
Chinese HVDC bidders: management views the four Chinese entities allowed to bid as non-operational with limited near-term threat; local content norms unchanged at 60-70%.

527001|2026-06.headline: Ashapura Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19.2% to INR1,616 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR188.9 crore and margin fell to 11.7%.
527001|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations rose about 19% YoY to INR1,616 crore, while reported EBITDA was broadly flat at INR188.9 crore as higher fuel, marine freight and input costs absorbed the gain. PBT declined about 1.4% YoY to INR130.03 crore and EPS rose to INR12.07 from INR11.5. Guinea bauxite volumes fell to 2.34 million tons from 3.16 million tons in Q4, with bauxite EBITDA per ton rising to USD6.3 from USD5.9. India businesses were hit by fuel, freight and sulphuric acid costs, with the bleaching clay JV under the most pressure.

financial_highlights.change: vs 3.16 mt in Q4 and 2.05 mt in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Guinea bauxite and iron ore
segments.commentary: Turnover about INR1,360 crore (84% of group) and EBITDA INR163 crore; volumes 2.34 mt, EBITDA USD6.3/t. Iron ore is in trial production with revenue not disclosed and EBITDA reported is bauxite-only.

segments.name: India bentonite and allied minerals / white performance minerals
segments.commentary: Wholly owned; bentonite broadly stable with domestic growth offsetting weaker exports, while white performance minerals profitability was hit by higher sales and distribution costs. No segment figures given.

segments.name: Bleaching clay (Ashapura Perfoclay, 50% JV)
segments.commentary: Sulphuric acid, a key raw material, rose about five-fold over the past year to above INR30/kg, adversely affecting the business. No figures given.

segments.name: Advanced ceramics (Orient Ceratech, 32%)
segments.commentary: Management said segment EBITDA more than doubled on premium product mix, oil and gas demand and steel-industry materials. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bauxite volume target of 10-12 million tons retained with a potential variance of ±10% (about 9-11 mt); Q2 is seasonally weakest, with most sales in late Q3 and Q4.
Bauxite EBITDA per ton expected near USD6 (USD5.5-6 range) for the next one or two quarters; return toward ~USD10 is a medium to long-term expectation, timing not predicted.
Iron ore: 15 million ton target by FY28 reaffirmed ("achieve or even cross"), but long-term iron ore guidance needs a couple more quarters.
Guinea export quota system expected before end of CY2026, seen as supportive of realisations and freight.
Management expects bauxite revenue near USD1 billion (about INR10,000 crore) at 15 mt once conditions normalise.
India capex of close to INR200 crore planned across projects and verticals.
capex_capacity: Boffa port fully operational with capacity raised from 5 mtpa to 8 mtpa; no further expansion to 10-12 mt planned near-term, to be decided as volumes ramp.
GSM second port new jetty under construction, expected operational by Q4 FY27, raising capacity from 6 mtpa to 10 mtpa; combined port capacity about 23 mt.
Total bauxite export capacity stated at 18 million tons.
Bauxite washing plant set up with ~20,000 tons/day capacity, on an operate-and-transfer model; a comparable plant would cost about USD15 million and take about one year to build if expanded.
Ashapura has over 1 million tons of bentonite grinding capacity, which management described as the world's largest.
demand_pricing: Freight remains highly volatile and elevated; management expects volatility through 2027 and freight is the main margin overhang.
Chinese index bauxite price around USD72/t, up from ~USD61, mostly due to ocean freight rather than FOB Guinea price.
Alumina prices under pressure; management is positive on medium-term demand, citing four new Chinese refineries adding 20-30 mt of bauxite demand.
Middle East and Europe customer demand impacted by geopolitics and freight; company focusing on India, Asia and Africa.
Customer demand volatile; customers may take time to absorb market and cost changes.

qa_highlights.question: Status and timing of Guinea bauxite export quota system and expected realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the quota system before end of 2026 and sees realisations flat until then; margins also flat with freight overhang. FY28 15 mt target described as on track.

qa_highlights.question: Response to new entrants such as Nimba selling bauxite via monthly tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a new development with slow materialisation and will not significantly disrupt the market, with volumes likely going to other traders; Ashapura may participate in tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Impact and expansion of the washing plant on EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant is roughly EBITDA neutral and mainly a sustainability and throughput tool; no EBITDA quantification given; expansion would take about one year.

qa_highlights.question: Boffa port expansion beyond 8 mt to 10 mt by Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: No near-term plan; 8 mt is seen as reasonable for now, with expansion to 10-12 mt to follow volume ramp-up without a fixed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Fako deposit and China Railway arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Only an MOU; details under study and little progress to report, with possible update next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why no iron ore revenue disclosure, and is the 10 mt guidance achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore is in trial production with low revenue, so it is not split out; EBITDA disclosed is bauxite only. Guidance is 10-12 mt with ±10% variance, and management said it is broadly on track.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA per ton outlook for Q2, FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term USD5.5-6/t; a return toward USD10/t is expected over the medium to longer term, timing uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of Orient Ceratech's EBITDA doubling and India growth levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are oil and gas product demand with debottlenecking and steel-industry materials replacing imports; India growth from cat litter, foundry, oil and gas, and kaolin for paper and paint.

544614|2026-06.headline: Capillary Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43% YoY to INR256 crore and adjusted EBITDA to INR44 crore (~17%), with organic growth at 17%.
544614|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR256 crore, up 43% YoY, with two months of SessionM (acquired May 1, 2026) contributing; organic growth was 17% and currency added about 6%. Adjusted EBITDA was INR44 crore (about 17-18% margin) versus INR19 crore a year earlier, and reported PAT was -INR9.5 crore, or INR25 crore normalised after excluding a cyber-fraud loss and a one-time deferred tax charge. ARR reached INR1,026 crore (+34% YoY), and trailing-12-month new ACV excluding one large healthcare win was about INR92 crore (+75%). Management kept FY27 guidance of INR1,065 crore revenue and INR172 crore EBITDA unchanged, saying it expects to beat both.

financial_highlights.change: +132% YoY; from INR19 crore; organic EBITDA margin ~23%
Includes cyber-fraud exceptional loss and one-time deferred tax liability
Up from INR19 crore in Q4 FY26
+34% YoY; from INR765 crore in FY26 and INR608 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Trailing-12-month new ACV (ex one healthcare win)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR17 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Loyalty stack
segments.commentary: Over 90% of revenue; core product and the business's main monetisation layer. Contracts are typically 3-7 year subscriptions.

segments.name: Engage (Engage+)
segments.commentary: About 5% of revenue; one-to-one personalised customer communication platform.

segments.name: Rewards
segments.commentary: About 5-7% of revenue; mainly banks and telcos.

segments.name: aiRA (AI analytics and action agents)
segments.commentary: About USD2.5 million ARR (~26 customers live, under 10 paying); management targets 5-10% of revenue from aiRA in FY27. Gross margin above 80%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged at INR1,065 crore revenue and INR172 crore EBITDA; management expects to beat both but did not quantify.
Organic growth expected at about 17% for FY27 (about 20-23% including FX and inorganic); management described 15-20% as the organic run-rate.
Kognitiv: first customer migration to go live September 1, 2026; ~16-17 customers in total; migration of the full base targeted by September 2027, with ~INR15-20 crore EBITDA uplift from Kognitiv.

SessionM: management expects EBITDA margin to move from break-even to ~15% within a year and to 35-40% over a further year; server cost savings of USD6-8 million over 3-4 quarters, with a payback possibly within FY27.
ESOP expense guided at INR12-15 crore for FY27, kept at 1-2% of revenue.
New ACV expected to grow at least 30-40% YoY in FY27 (not the 75% trailing figure).
capex_capacity: SessionM acquired from Mastercard effective May 1, 2026; enterprise value USD20 million, net cost about INR17 crore after net-debt true-up on April 30; entities debt-free; SessionM ARR about USD32 million, all contracts agreed to move to Capillary paper.
Kognitiv (closed May 1, 2025): ~16-17 customers; AI-led migration tool; first customer live Sept 1, 2026.
Migration of SessionM customers not expected to start until end-2026 / early 2027; 3-4 of ~45 SessionM customers are being fast-tracked.
Cloud-native platform across four colos; product uptime of nearly 5 nines in Q1.
CustomerGlu tuck-in (rebranded Experiences+) bought for less than a few hundred thousand dollars; acqui-hire IP deal.
demand_pricing: Win rates on large new deals above 35%, which management attributes partly to aiRA.
Existing-customer NRR of 111% split roughly: 4-5% from price escalators and overages, ~10% from upsell and new cohorts, net of ~5% churn.
Management frames loyalty as a red ocean; about 90 loyalty companies have revenue of USD10-100 million and are the M&A pool.
Acquired agency-model businesses run at ~30% gross margin; moving them onto the platform lifts gross margin to 65-75%.
Management says fewer than 10% of loyalty revenue sits with software vendors versus agencies; named competitors include Epsilon, Merkle, Kobie and Salesforce.

qa_highlights.question: What share of SessionM clients have migrated and what is the FY27 run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: No SessionM migrations before end-2026/early 2027; the full base is expected to take 2-3 years. 3-4 of ~45 customers are being fast-tracked; margins will improve through server cost cuts (SessionM server costs are ~50% of revenue vs ~7-9% at Capillary).

qa_highlights.question: Organic vs inorganic growth split and FX effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 organic growth was 17%; FX contributed about 6%; the rest is SessionM's two months. Cash is about half USD and half INR, which gives a natural hedge with the US at ~60% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cyber-fraud loss covered by insurance?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the bank-account fraud at a subsidiary is insured, but the amount and timing of recovery are not yet clear. No customer or employee data was exposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic NRR breakdown and churn?
qa_highlights.answer: Price escalators and overage are 4-5% of NRR; upsell and new cohorts add ~10%; churn is ~5%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the aiRA figures net of cannibalisation and what are the economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ARR is ~USD2.5 million with no cannibalisation so far; gross and contribution margins are above 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the SessionM purchase price INR17 crore when the deal was USD20 million?
qa_highlights.answer: The USD20 million enterprise value was adjusted for net debt at closing; the final true-up on April 30 brought the value to about INR17 crore; the entities are debt-free.

risks_watch: Q1 organic NRR excluding the healthcare account was 116%, but reported 111%; one large healthcare customer did not grow, which weighs on the quarter.
Enterprise budget cycles and ~9-month average deal cycles make quarterly new ACV lumpy (trailing-12-month metric).
Kognitiv migration milestone on September 1, 2026 is the first test of the AI-led upgrade approach; success is needed for the INR15-20 crore EBITDA uplift.
Reported PAT is negative; the insurance recovery on the fraud loss is still uncertain.
aiRA is early: under 10 of ~26 live customers are paying, and the 5-10% revenue target depends on enterprise budget timing.

544203|2026-06.headline: ABD Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.8% to ₹984 crore and reported EBITDA was flat at ₹120 crore, as ₹24 crore of supply-chain disruption cost offset gross margin gains.
544203|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations grew 5.8% YoY to ₹984 crore on 6.2% volume growth to 9 million cases, with Prestige and Above (P&A) volumes up 10.7%. Gross margin expanded 277 bps to 46%, but a ₹24 crore global supply-chain disruption hit profitability, leaving reported EBITDA at ₹120 crore (12.2% margin) versus ₹119 crore and PAT at ₹45 crore versus ₹56 crore. Management presented like-to-like EBITDA of ₹144 crore (14.7% margin, +21.4% YoY) excluding the disruption. Net debt fell ₹33 crore QoQ to ₹947 crore, with net debt to EBITDA at 1.7x.

financial_highlights.change: down ₹33 crore from ₹981 crore at March 2026

segments.name: ICONiQ White
segments.commentary: Volume 3.1 million cases vs 2.3 million in Q1 FY26 (+33.8%); monthly average above 1 million cases. Management targets close to 15 million cases in FY27 from 10.7 million in FY26.

segments.name: Prestige & Above (P&A)
segments.commentary: Volume share 48.2% (vs 46.2%) and value share 59.3% (vs 55.8%); segment volume grew 10.7% YoY. Management said ABD outgrew an industry where P&A grew low single digits.

segments.name: Mass Premium & others
segments.commentary: Volume grew 2.3% YoY, led by Northern and Southern regions in whisky and brandy.

segments.name: ABD Maestro (super premium/luxury)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about ₹40 crore, guided to double in FY27. Portfolio of 10 brands, about 5,500 premium touchpoints, sold in 6 international markets and 4 travel retail locations.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Present in 39 countries (36 in Q4 FY26); ICONiQ White available in 10 international markets. Management describes exports as asset-light, high-margin and working-capital efficient.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth guided at mid-teens; management said it may be reviewed upward toward high-teens over the two-year horizon.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided broadly in line with FY26, with pressure expected to be concentrated through Q2 FY27.
Expected margin benefit from backward integration of about 300 bps by FY28 and a further 100 bps by FY29.
India-UK FTA expected to add about 70-80 bps to FY27 margins (benefit from H2) and 130-140 bps in FY28.
Malt distillery at Rangapur expected operational in H1 FY27. Management said captive ENA capacity (Maharashtra and Telangana) should cover requirements for the next four years.
Two-year guidance (EBITDA margin 18% target) reiterated and described as potentially stepped up; Telangana price-increase talks ongoing and not included as certain.
capex_capacity: Capex across Telangana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh to deepen in-house ENA, malt, PET and bottling capacity; funded by internal accruals and debt.
PET bottle plant at Rangapur, Telangana commissioned in FY26 and described as EBITDA accretive.
Malt distillery at Rangapur expected operational in H1 FY27.
Mid-FY27 launches planned: deluxe vodka (addresses a 15-18 million case vodka segment) and a premium whisky, both in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Industry: P&A grew low single digits and Mass Premium & others broadly flat in Q1, per management; ABD outgrew both.
Supply-chain disruption (global, linked to a war) cost ₹24 crore in Q1; management expects pressure to last through Q2 and recover in Q3-Q4.
Telangana: dialogue ongoing for a price increase; management has built guardrails in case it does not come through. Management also said 1-2 other states may grant price increases.
Telangana government overdue about ₹400 crore; management said pre-2024 dues are largely cleared and recent supplies are paid within agreed timelines.
Packaging: vendor evaluation underway in a buyers' market and value-engineering initiatives being undertaken.

qa_highlights.question: What are ABD Maestro's manpower, advertising and salary cost trajectory, and any long-term revenue or profit targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expenses will not rise further and will be subsidised by distribution support. FY26 turnover was about ₹40 crore, expected to double in FY27. Management called it at least a three-year gestation luxury business and declined to give longer-term numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance building in a Telangana price hike and a resolution to supply-chain and glass inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the two-year guidance and said it could be stepped up. Telangana price hike talks are ongoing with guardrails built in. Management expects the war-related pressure to last until Q2 and then ease.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Telangana overdue and how much is from prior years?
qa_highlights.answer: Overdue is about ₹400 crore. Pre-2024 overdue has been paid, and recent supplies are paid on time, but some older overdue is still awaiting government clearance.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Officer's Choice Blue, Sterling Reserve B7 and B10 declining, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed cash-flow constraints before the 2024 listing and said ICONiQ is the growth engine. OC Blue is being relaunched with new packaging in UP first; B7 gets a new look in H2 FY27 (packaging rollout targeted Q4 FY27). B10 was named as losing ground.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reach mid-teens growth given weak non-ICONiQ brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ABD P&A growth of 11.6% vs industry mid-single digits, the full-year benefit of ICONiQ, brandy push in AP, OC volume in Telangana and AP, and vodka and premium whisky launches in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does ENA capacity suffice for backward integration needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said captive ENA capacity in Maharashtra and Telangana, plus planned Maharashtra expansion, covers requirements. Its ENA expansion plan is designed to meet needs from captive sources for the next four years.

541302|2026-06.headline: Dhruv Consultancy Q1 FY27 net sales fell to INR15.55 crore with an operating loss of about INR3 crore, while Q1 order inflow reached about INR90-100 crore.
541302|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 net sales were INR15.55 crore and total income INR15.95 crore, with management attributing the operating loss to estimate corrections, tax reversals and a fixed-cost base ahead of revenue conversion. Management said Q1 order inflow was about INR90-100 crore, including a INR40.92 crore OBCC order, the largest ticket the company has booked. Unexecuted order book is stated at INR300 crore, with the company also citing a total order book of INR600 crore in a later answer. Management guided that billing on new orders starts around Q3 and that the company is entering wayside amenities through a 55% SPV. Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance, citing SEBI LODR constraints.

financial_highlights.change: Management said operating loss reduced more than 50% vs Q4

financial_highlights.metric: Total expenditure (Q1 FY27, as reported by management)

financial_highlights.change: Management also cited total order book of INR600 crore in a later answer

financial_highlights.value: 60-90 days typical; up to 120 days in Northeast/difficult-access states

segments.commentary: Q1 orders of about INR90 crore included INR19.34 crore Rowghat-Jagdalpur railway authority engineer and PMC work (140 km), INR8.34 crore MPRDC Ujjain-Jaora IE, and INR40.92 crore from OBCC. Company is executing 65-70 assignments.

segments.name: Wayside Amenities (new vertical)
segments.commentary: Formed SPV Verul Drivehub Private Limited with 55% stake; first 15-year lease-based development and O&M agreement signed 4 August 2026, with revenue expected from around February 2027. Three further LOAs expected in September 2026.

Management said bids are being submitted at better margins; the company has no specific margin target.
Management targets 10-15% of order book from international markets (Ghana preferred bidder, Mozambique empanelment, Saudi Arabia bids).
Wayside Amenities: first site revenue expected around February 2027, 7-8 months after possession for subsequent projects.
capex_capacity: Railway project (Rowghat-Jagdalpur) requires 108 manpower; management said about 60-70% already deployed and project commencement expected in about a month.

Wayside Amenities site: fuel pump installation (4-5 months) is the critical path; sites are 50-60% constructed by NHAI and concessionaires.
demand_pricing: Q1 order inflow of about INR90-100 crore, compared with about INR90-100 crore for full FY26 per management.
Q2 to date additional orders of about INR60-65 crore cited.

Price discounting may return in Q2-Q4, particularly festive H2, where management expects better ROI.
Women's wear could reach 2x to 3x current revenue in about a year, with gradual scaling rather than sudden growth.
Insurance claim (fire incident, about INR 21 crore of stock insured) expected to settle soon; debt and interest cost expected to normalise after realisation.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity is fully utilised for the last few quarters; the company uses job work and rented capacity to meet demand.
Manufacturing footprint across Sholapur, Bangalore and Gurgaon, with fulfilment centres across India.

demand_pricing: Price elasticity was subdued in Q1; management says demand exists but price cuts did not earn adequate ROI, so it chose performance marketing over discounts.

Q1 is an end-of-season sale quarter in which the company chose not to discount heavily.

qa_highlights.question: How do women's wear unit economics and repeat purchases compare with men's wear, and what share is targeted?

qa_highlights.question: Quick commerce strategy and economics?

qa_highlights.question: Bangalore store performance and expansion?

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth slow in ROI for licensed and own brands?

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for prior revenue run-rate and margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets unchanged: same growth rate as the last few years and healthy margins, with margin improvement sought while reserving margin for growth investment.

qa_highlights.question: Fire insurance claim and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance claim (about INR 21 crore of stock, fully insured) is in process; elevated working-capital loans raised to fund inventory are expected to fall once the claim is realised. Exception provisions are small (INR 3-4 lakh).

qa_highlights.question: Dockers deal: B2B or B2C, and effect on premiumisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Dockers agreement is B2C-focused; B2B is used for long-run sourcing orders. More than 94% of revenue is B2C. Dockers fits the premiumisation strategy.

risks_watch: Finance cost rising sharply on working capital; normalisation depends on timing of the insurance claim settlement, which is still in process.
Revenue growth is dependent on the timing of price reinvestment in H2 festive; if festive demand is weak, the growth catch-up may not happen.
Rising other expenses (marketing) and a higher CAC in Q1; watch whether gross margin gains hold as marketing spend rises.
Aggregator/wholesale channel share (about 40% of brand revenue) and its effect on reported revenue vs. NSV; the company reports B2B value, which understates headline sales.
Women's wear is still in a test-and-scale phase; scaling could strain returns and inventory.
Capacity is fully utilised, so growth depends on job-work and rented capacity.
533941|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the platform and long-term ambition, but defensive on Q1 growth, which management framed as a deliberate trade-off to protect price and margin. Evasive on specific CAC, payback, and insurance claim timing, citing process constraints.

financial_highlights.value: about INR 10 crore (approx. 40% of Thomas Scott revenue)

541403|2026-06.headline: Dollar Industries Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA up 11.4% to INR 48 crore at 11.8% margin, on price hikes and no discounting, while volume fell 1.6%.

544058|2026-06.headline: Credo Brands (Mufti) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5% YoY to INR125.3 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR26.6 crore (21.2% margin) on higher marketing spend.

Competition from both Indian and foreign apparel brands, with some competitors spending above 15% of revenue on advertising.
Inventory days at 74; management expects a reduction but said levels are cyclical.
Same-store revenue target of mid-single-digit growth against a flat store-count trend and a recent 3-year growth slowdown.

516072|2026-06.headline: Vishnu Chemicals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.9% YoY to INR433.4 crores, but EBITDA margin slipped to 15.1% from 16.1%.
516072|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue grew 24.9% YoY to INR433.4 crores and PAT rose 23% to INR39.6 crores, while EBITDA margin fell to 15.1% from 16.1%. Management expects freight costs to stay elevated in Q2 because of West Asia tensions and gave no quarterly or full-year margin guidance, while reiterating a 20% long-term EBITDA margin target. Chromium mix shift, strontium ramp-up and the South Africa chrome mine restart are the main levers cited for H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any impact from the Vizag maintenance shutdown?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the South Africa mine and chrome ore benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Production expected around end-July, with volumes to India from H2 FY27; standalone gross margin of 44-45% expected to move toward 50% by end of FY27, but management declined to quantify the timing precisely.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt is on the books and what is the capex plan?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% margin achievable next year and is the chrome metal decision linked to the EU contract?
