capex_capacity: 16,500-tonne forging press due for production by Q4 FY27; 4,000-tonne press commissioned in the last few weeks.
Management says all machining and forging cells ran at full capability from June; remaining 7-10% constraint is technical, with debottlenecking targeted to lift output by 15-20%.
Cumulative machining investment about INR1,100 crore, of which INR625 crore in the last 5 years and ~INR1,000 crore in the last 10 years.
Automation spend about INR7.5-10 crore to date; expected to rise to INR30-50 crore by end of FY27.
Management could not quantify machining capacity in tonnes; said it will come back with a method. Gross block ~INR2,100 crore; CNC machine count described as 'hundreds' without a figure.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as strong across domestic and export markets, with US commercial vehicle (Class 8 truck) demand moving strongly and Indian CV, tractor and passenger car markets running hot.
Realisation per tonne up to INR2.02 lakh from INR1.93 lakh; management attributed the ~350 bps sequential gross margin improvement to higher realisation and machining/export mix.
New orders are mostly machined parts, which management says raise capital requirements.
Hyperscaler-linked business is filtering into domestic forging demand; management said it is moving into businesses that support hyperscalers.
Freight costs rose sharply on routes around the Strait of Hormuz, and fuel costs spiked in Q1 due to the West Asia conflict, which has since stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year growth outlook by market, and reason for higher machining mix?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 turnover expected at INR1,800-1,900 crore (~18% growth). Machining mix expected at 65-68%, reflecting ~3 years of machining investment.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost increase QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Increment was given from 1 April 2026 rather than in the subsequent quarter, plus some headcount additions; management expects current cost levels to hold through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt held at ~INR750 crore; ~INR170 crore repaid and redrawn; capex ~INR150 crore. Land sale proceeds to go to working capital, capex and borrowings. No plan to raise debt beyond INR750-800 crore until turnover and EBITDA grow.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses up 35% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Export freight is the main driver (about INR4 crore of a INR4.2 crore increase), due to routing around the Strait of Hormuz; base overheads rose about 10% (INR8 crore to INR9 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Europe revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe is stable and moves with customer demand, volume-wise de-grown, with no business lost.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting lower working capital; AI tools are being used to identify slow inventory, with a rapid action team to clear stock and WIP cut to about one week.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margin headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees scope for improvement; target 20%-plus, with 1-2% visible and 2-3% as the stretch goal.

qa_highlights.question: Tractor/axle suspension entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Not at this moment; management cited margin dilution and focus on current growth and cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: QIP status?
qa_highlights.answer: QIP is on the cards and under consideration; to be pursued at an appropriate time linked to market opportunity.

risks_watch: Working capital and inventory build-up; management says it is actively trying to reduce it, and the timing of the reduction is not yet quantified.
Cost pressure from freight, power and fuel, and rising personnel costs following increments; management flagged cost challenges.
Labour availability: April and May volumes were hit by shortages; June recovered with hires.
Mix shift toward machined parts raises capital needs; management said most new orders are now machined.
Machining capacity remains unquantified; management promised a method at a later date.
Unresolved status of the enabling QIP resolution.
Europe revenue trend: Q2 FY26 INR82 crore, then INR89 crore, INR68 crore, and INR59 crore in Q1 FY27 per analyst's figures.

542919|2026-06.headline: Artemis Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12.7% to INR 287.32 crore, PAT up 48.3% to INR 31.44 crore, EBITDA margin 21.5%.
542919|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 287.32 crore (+12.7% YoY), with Gurugram standalone up 15.4%, and EBITDA of INR 61.82 crore at a 21.5% margin. PAT rose 48.3% YoY to INR 31.44 crore. Gurugram occupancy was 65.7% and ARPOB-linked ARPOB (average revenue per occupied bed) was INR 85,690. Artemis Shanti Hospital in Raipur (300 beds) went live in July 2026, with OPD from 9 July and theatres/cath labs from 27 July. Management also announced a 200+ bed Tower IV in Gurugram and an INR 700 crore enabling resolution for a QIP, which is expected 6-8 months out.

segments.name: Gurugram flagship (tertiary/quaternary)
segments.commentary: Contributes 95-97% of revenue per management. Occupancy 65.7% and ARPOB INR 85,690 in Q1; management expects margin to reach 20-21% in FY27 and 23-24% over 2-3 years.

segments.name: Artemis Shanti Hospital, Raipur (300 beds)
segments.commentary: Newly operational: OPD from 9 July 2026, theatres and cath labs from 27 July. Capex INR 120 crore, about 80% spent; breakeven expected in 15-18 months with operating loss of around INR 20 crore.

segments.name: Smaller centres (Artemis Lite, Cardiac Care, Daffodils)
segments.commentary: Management described performance as muted due to capacity constraints in small units. Segment revenue and margin were not disclosed on the call; the analyst was asked to request them offline from the CFO.

segments.name: International patients
segments.commentary: Close to 27% of revenue in Q1 despite West Asia disruption; management guides to 30% or more in Q2 and adds 2-3 new country fronts a year.

guidance_outlook: Gurugram margin expected at 20-21% in FY27 and 23-24% over the next 2-3 years; management said upwards of 23% at the 900-1,000 bed scale.
Gurugram occupancy targeted at 70% by Q2 FY27, with management saying it is on track.
Tower IV (200+ beds, Gurugram) expected to be operational in 18-22 months; breakeven in 8-10 months and 50% utilisation in the first six months after launch, per management.
Raipur expected to break even in 15-18 months with about INR 20 crore operating loss; direct insurance empanelment expected in 8-10 weeks.

Total capex of about INR 800 crore over three years (FY27-FY29) including Raipur, Tower IV, VIMHANS and parking, with INR 250 crore VIMHANS deposit additional; INR 700 crore QIP enabling resolution expected 6-8 months out.
Target of about 2,000 operational beds by 2029-30 across Gurugram Tower IV, Raipur and planned South Delhi / VIMHANS projects.
capex_capacity: Tower IV Gurugram: 200+ beds plus multi-level parking, capex about INR 55 lakh per bed (INR 50-55 lakh range), total about INR 120 crore for the tower.
Multi-level parking INR 70-80 crore; replacement capex INR 100-120 crore over three years, per management's breakdown of the INR 800 crore plan.

Raipur: 300 beds, total capex INR 120 crore, 80% spent; PET-CT installation and radiotherapy unit (about six months to transport) pending, with services going live between 10 August and end-August 2026.
VIMHANS (650 beds) pure capex INR 350-360 crore plus about INR 250 crore deposit, of which INR 130 crore already paid; remaining IFC-raised money to be deposited to VIMHANS by year-end.
demand_pricing: Gurugram ARPOB is among the highest in Delhi NCR; growth attributed to case-mix shift toward quaternary procedures and fewer average length-of-stay days.
Management cited economies of scale (cost base steady while admitting more patients) and case mix as margin drivers; smaller centres a relatively small contributor.
International business held up despite the West Asia war: 27% share of patients in Q1, with the top line up 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the international patient mix come off, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said international share was close to 27% in Q1 despite West Asia flight disruption; it sees Q2 at 30% or better, with 2-3 new country fronts added each year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 200-bed FAR expansion a function of new height/FAR rules, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Tower IV combines 130-150 free beds from Platinum green-building FAR with about 70 beds of purchased FAR; full operationalisation in 18-22 months.

qa_highlights.question: Can Gurugram margins reach 20-21% in FY27 and 23-24% over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management answered yes to both; it expects the Gurugram margin to exceed 21% after the 200-bed addition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Raipur ramp-up and the expected breakeven and loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven in 15-18 months with about INR 20 crore operating loss; all services launched together, with insurance empanelment expected in 8-10 weeks and an interim cashless intermediary in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will the QIP be postponed given only half of the IFC money is spent?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 700 crore is an enabling resolution; the remaining IFC money will be deposited to VIMHANS by year-end, and the QIP is 6-8 months out depending on brownfield asset finalisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is Tower IV capex per bed and the FY27-FY29 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 55 lakh per bed including parking; total FY27-FY29 capex including Raipur is about INR 800 crore, excluding the VIMHANS deposit.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 800 crore capex is attributable to each project?
qa_highlights.answer: Raipur INR 120 crore, VIMHANS INR 350-360 crore, Tower IV about INR 120 crore, parking INR 70-80 crore, replacement capex INR 100-120 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Daffodils and Artemis Lite muted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small units face capacity constraints; some centres (e.g., New Friends Colony) are being consolidated, and the model will be hub-and-spoke for new cities.

500031|2026-06.headline: Bajaj Electricals Q1 FY27: revenue up 2.3% YoY while EBIT margin rose to 6.6% from 2.5%, led by consumer products margin recovery to 3.9%.
500031|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 2.3% YoY in Q1 FY27, with consumer products up 1.7% (after multiple quarters of decline) and lighting solutions up 4.4%. Consolidated EBIT margin expanded to 6.6% from 2.5%, with consumer products EBIT margin at 3.9% versus negative 1.7% a year earlier, driven by gross margin gains and operating leverage. Fans remained the weak spot, with management attributing share loss to operational issues including gas and PCB shortages. Management guided to 8-10% growth on a blended basis (described as a non-binding aspiration) and a 6-7% margin stabilisation for the next two years before a move toward 10% in consumer products. Cash flow from operations was negative in the quarter, mainly due to tax payments linked to the Morphy Richards acquisition.

financial_highlights.change: consumer products gross margin up 220 bps
debtors improved, inventory slightly up seasonally
due to tax and TDS/GST payments on Morphy Richards acquisition; ex these, described as healthy

segments.name: Consumer products
segments.commentary: Revenue +1.7% YoY with a split: cooling (fans, coolers) contracted while non-summer categories grew double digits; Morphy Richards grew double digits post acquisition. EBIT margin 3.9% vs -1.7% a year ago. Fans lost share; management plans to claw back in two to three quarters.

segments.name: Lighting solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue +4.4% YoY, with double-digit growth in consumer lighting. EBIT margin about 7% as legacy professional lighting contracts signed before commodity inflation limited pass-through; management expects a return to double-digit margin after exiting these over a quarter or two.

guidance_outlook: Blended company growth of 8-10% per year targeted (management said this is not a forward-looking commitment); industry assumed to grow 6-7%.
Consumer products EBIT margin expected to stabilise at 6-7% over the next two years, with a longer-term target of about 10%; management said it would not come in the next two years.
Lighting EBIT margin expected to return to double digits once legacy professional lighting contracts roll off.
No major price increases expected for the rest of FY27 at this stage, but management said this could change within two months given volatility.
Fan share expected to be recovered over the next two to three quarters.
capex_capacity: Wires entry progressing better than expected; management did not disclose current-quarter contribution. Wires sit within lighting and switchgears.
Management is evaluating adjacent opportunities including solar, cables, and professional lighting; no timelines given, described as early stage.
BLDC fans: industry BLDC penetration estimated at 30-35%; Bajaj is slightly under-indexed but growing faster.
demand_pricing: Cost inflation across categories ranged from about 6% to 11-12%, with coolers as high as 13%. Part was recovered through selective price increases and part through savings.

Fan volumes declined due to supply constraints (gas shortage during the war period and PCB shortages as BLDC demand exceeded plans), plus operational issues; gas supply restored, PCB supply being covered on longer cycles.
Overall market share mixed: stable in most categories, gaining in iron and mixer grinders, losing in fans.
E-commerce about 15-20% of consumer business, growing double digits; quick commerce 8-10% of e-commerce. Alternate channels about 45% of business, modern/general split about 55:45.
Exports almost doubled. Weak in South, strongest in East (per management).
Competition increasing as new players enter; management expects the market to expand as a result.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fans lag, and what are the BLDC and premiumisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Vishal Chadha said fans declined, and price increases kept pace with commodity inflation. BLDC is estimated at 30-35% of industry, with Bajaj slightly under-indexed but growing faster.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly can lighting margins return toward double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Sachdeva said legacy professional lighting contracts signed before the war limited price pass-through, a temporary blip. Margins should recover within a quarter or two as these exit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consumer products margin path and timeline to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Sachdeva said margins should stabilise at 6-7% for the next two years, with a steady path toward 10% thereafter, timing dependent on brand investment and scale.

qa_highlights.question: Market share trend and rural performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Share stable or growing in most categories except fans, which is losing share; management has no separate rural share data but assumes rural share is intact.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors improved, inventory slightly up for the season; working capital days in the 50-60 range. Operating cash flow negative due to Morphy Richards-related tax and TDS/GST payments.

qa_highlights.question: Cost inflation and pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost inflation of 6-11% (coolers up to 13%), partly recovered through pricing and partly through savings. No major price increases seen as needed for the rest of the year, subject to commodity movement.

risks_watch: Fan recovery: whether share loss reverses within two to three quarters, given PCB and supply constraints.
Commodity inflation and the possibility of further price actions, which management says could change within two months.
Lighting margin recovery depends on exit timing of legacy professional lighting contracts.
Working capital and operating cash flow normalisation after Morphy Richards-related payments.
Competitive intensity increasing with new entrants, especially in consumer categories.
500031|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margin recovery and the consumer products turnaround, though guarded on forward growth and pricing, which management repeatedly qualified as volatile. Evasive on specifics for wires contribution and on distribution-level detail.
key_quotes: We delivered overall revenue growth of 2.3%. However, our EBIT margin improved to 6.6% from 2.5%.
But this is not a forward-looking commitment. But this is the kind of targets which we are looking at.

544293|2026-06.headline: Suraksha Diagnostic Q1 FY27 total income rose 21% YoY to INR 887 million, with PAT up 40% to INR 128 million and EBITDA margin at 36%.
544293|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 21% YoY to INR 887 million and EBITDA rose 28% to INR 315 million, with margin expanding about 200 bps to 36%. PAT grew 40% to INR 128 million (14.7% margin). The network reached 72 centres after one hub and three spokes were added in Q1, with three more hubs/spokes opened in July-August and a hub commissioned in Jharkhand. Management reiterated 100 centres by FY28 and guided EBITDA margin of at least 34% for FY27. Analysts pressed on the slowdown in test volume growth (about 10-11% vs ~20% in prior two quarters), repeat-patient decline, and the conservative 15% revenue guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Centres under 2 years old EBITDA margin
financial_highlights.change: from -5.5% last quarter; first profitable quarter
+136% YoY; fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth

segments.name: Mature centres (>2 years, ~42-45 centres)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 12-12.5% YoY (management cited QoQ and YoY figures interchangeably); EBITDA margin 40.9%, attributed to volume, genomics contribution and lower COGS after biochemistry shift from Siemens to Roche.

segments.name: Centres under 2 years (27 centres)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 85 million (Rs 8.5 crore) of INR 880 million quarterly sales per management; turned EBITDA positive at 6.5%.

segments.name: Genomics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 13.7 million (+136% YoY); mix 80% B2C and 20% B2B; genomic margins estimated at 15-20%; Rs 22 crore invested over three years.

segments.name: Wellness / corporate
segments.commentary: Wellness contribution about 4-5% of revenue; CGHS rate revision from mid-October 2025 added about 1.5% to top line per management, with public-sector corporate contributing around 15%.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin to be not below 34% for FY27; management expects more by FY29 (analyst cited 33-34% by FY28-29).
Q2 expected strong (seasonal disease season), Q3 muted (festivities and winter), Q4 strong; July-August trends described as robust.
Genomics growth expected at about 20% per quarter through FY27.
Capex of about Rs 70-80 crore in FY27; on track for 100 centres by FY28.
Plan to add 4 hubs and 7 spokes for the rest of FY27 (corrected from 3 hubs and 6 spokes after clarification, with 3 hubs and 6 spokes stated in one answer).
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27: one hub and three spoke centres commissioned; July-August added two hubs and three spokes; network at 72 centres at quarter end.
Hub capex about Rs 10-10.5 crore; spoke capex about Rs 1.5-2 crore; spoke centre-level breakeven 3-4 months, HO-level breakeven 8-9 months.
Genexus rapid genome sequencer acquired, in final validation; turnaround for oncology genomic study cut from 14-17 days to 48 hours.
No major additional genomics capex expected in next 2-3 years per CSO.

Kolkata proper: 5 hubs and 6 spokes, with room for 3 more hubs and at least 6 spokes; Greater Kolkata has 9 hubs with scope to double. Jharkhand hub commissioned, another planned with 5 spokes; Assam hub operating with spoke commissioned and another under construction; Agartala (Tripura) hub to follow.
demand_pricing: Like-for-like mature centre revenue growth about 12% YoY; test volume growth about 10-11%; growth attributed to test mix change, with no price increases taken per management.
Patient footfall for consultation up about 11% YoY in June 2026; patient volume up 12.4% QoQ per management.
Repeat patient share down to about 40% (from 52% in FY22-23), which management attributed to new patient additions from expansion, not absolute decline.
B2B carries a margin challenge but volume offsets it; B2C seen as margin-stable with no deep discounting.
Franchisee-run collection centres number 214; these are used as feeder points before spokes are opened.
Organised share of diagnostics in East India is lower than the national 15-20%; Suraksha claimed to be the largest organised player in the region.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ~400 bps margin expansion and can margins reach 33-34% by FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage as revenue scales against largely fixed costs; management said it expects margins to be higher than 33-34% by FY29 and that mature-centre margins are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin outlook given the seasonal pattern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overall EBITDA will not go below 34% for the year, with Q2 and Q4 strong and Q3 muted.

qa_highlights.question: Why has test volume growth slowed to about 10-11% from around 20% in prior quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was nothing specific and that the company would evaluate it; it did not give a reason.

qa_highlights.question: What is the genomics market size and B2B/B2C split?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is 80% B2C and 20% B2B, with B2B expected to grow as a share. Indian genomics market cited at about Rs 450 million by 2030 (figure as stated; unit unclear). Average realisation not given, since genomic test prices range from Rs 4,000-5,000 to over Rs 50,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ROCE/ROE below national peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the young centre base (27 of 45 mature centres under 2 years old); lower only against three or four players.

qa_highlights.question: Are franchisee collection centres affected by new spokes?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; when a collection centre area proves strong, a spoke is opened and the franchisee is relocated to a further location.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance only 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: CSO said the company has been conservative as it is a relatively new organisation; no dearth of effort.

533023|2026-06.headline: ZF CV India Q1 FY27: Total income up 5.7% to ₹1,101.8 cr; PAT fell 14.7% to ₹104.5 cr on a high base FX gain, while aftermarket rose 15.6% to ₹158.4 cr.

543996|2026-06.headline: Updater Services Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR764 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR42 crore (5.5% margin) and PAT of INR30.3 crore.
543996|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 9% YoY to INR764 crore, with IFM up 11% to INR525 crore and BSS up 7% to INR253 crore. Consolidated EBITDA was INR42 crore at a 5.5% margin, with IFM at 4.5% (about INR24 crore) and BSS at 7.5% (about INR19 crore). Management declared an interim dividend of INR1 per share, about INR7 crore of cash outflow, and said it remains a net cash company. Management gave no formal guidance and pointed to Q1 as the indicator.

financial_highlights.change: +9% YoY vs INR700 crore in Q1 FY26
IFM PAT INR20.7 crore vs INR19.9 crore a year ago

segments.name: IFM (Integrated Facility Management, incl. Global and Avon)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR525 crore, up 11% YoY, with 6 new significant logos added. EBITDA about INR24 crore at 4.5% margin, with management noting this is stable and it does not expect further decline. Global reported its highest-ever EBITDA margin of 9% (vs 5% last year), and all 23 airports are operational. Avon core mailroom revenue grew 10% YoY after the transport business was fully shut off.

segments.name: BSS: Denave (sales enablement)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR161 crore, up 18% YoY, with EBITDA INR7 crore at 4.3% margin. Margin pressure came from a mix shift toward low-margin field marketing and budget timing at one large customer.

segments.name: BSS: Athena (BFSI customer engagement)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28 crore with EBITDA INR5 crore, an 18% margin. Won 2 new clients that started in July on 2-year tenures, and started its first agentic AI engagement in May-June.

segments.name: BSS: Matrix (Audit & Assurance and EBGC)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 2% YoY and was flat QoQ. EBITDA rose about 76%, and margin improved to 13.1% from 7.6% (EBITDA INR4.2 crore vs INR2.4 crore). EBGC revenue grew 9% YoY to INR12.5 crore with gross margin about 21%. Audit & Assurance revenue fell about 2% as large audits slipped from May into June and July.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; management said Q1 numbers can serve as an indicator.
Management expects IFM and BSS each to grow low double digits, roughly 9-12%, so the 67:33 IFM:BSS mix should hold.
Matrix Audit & Assurance results are expected in H2 FY27 as deferred audits land.
EBGC volumes and margins are expected to be sustainable through this year.
Cash of upwards of INR300 crore to be deployed across inorganic growth, brownfield organic investment and shareholder returns.
capex_capacity: Global: all 23 airports operational and generating revenue; expanding into training and aviation support services, including security training and regulatory certification.
Athena: another agentic AI project has customer approval and is expected to go live in August 2026.
Matrix: a dedicated sales team was built for Audit & Assurance to target large multinational audits and food and automobile sectors.
Acquisition: a pending deal is on hold over valuation differences; management said it is also reviewing a wider pipeline.
Labour: recruitment teams in Eastern and Northeast India redeploy workers to labour-short states such as Gujarat, parts of Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and NCR.
demand_pricing: IFM demand: strong commercial real estate, GCC expansion and enterprise outsourcing; management sees clients favouring single strategic partners. Management says its GCC exposure is limited (low commercial, no residential).
BSS demand: clients are prioritising projects with faster ROI and sales productivity; spending is selective in some global markets.
EBGC: volumes are recovering after subdued banking and BPO hiring; the company describes margins as volume-driven with a flat cost base.
Contracts are largely pass-through, and labour shortages in several states did not visibly hit Q1 results.
Seasonality: Q1 is seasonally weak for catering; Q2 and Q3 are festive peaks for consumer-linked IFM and BSS work.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Matrix margin improvement sustainable, and has IFM margin moderation from headcount additions ended?
qa_highlights.answer: EBGC revenue went from INR11.4 crore (Q1 FY26) to INR11.7 crore (Q4 FY26) to INR12.5 crore (Q1 FY27), and gross margin from about 12% to 21%. Management says cost structure is flat, so volume drives margin, and it expects this to hold. IFM EBITDA was INR23.6 crore vs INR23.1 crore YoY, with some cost and contract front-loading.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash balance be used, and are buybacks planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is above INR300 crore across three buckets: inorganic growth, brownfield organic investment, and shareholder rewards. The INR1 interim dividend is the first step. There is no buyback proposal before the Board, though management did not rule one out.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IFM:BSS mix change over 2-3 years, and can agentic AI matter for Athena?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the 67:33 mix to hold, since both segments can grow 9-12%. Agentic AI is in use for outbound lead qualification and inbound repetitive queries. Management said it does not see wholesale replacement of human agents in BFSI near term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSS margin fall from 11.5% in Q4 to 7.5% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to a Q4 FY26 Avon restatement that added revenue to last year's Q4. Excluding it, Q4 BSS EBITDA was INR19.1 crore vs INR18.9 crore in Q1, so margins are similar.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the rise in other expenses and the tax-expense swing quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose because of restructuring costs and transport provisions taken in FY26. Tax fell on a manpower-linked tax benefit in a couple of group entities, and the mix is also a factor because Matrix gets no such benefit. Management said the full-year effective tax rate is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the SIS share purchases and the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no discussion with SIS beyond public knowledge; it reads the purchases as a treasury investment. The promoter family holds 59.1%. The acquisition is on hold over valuation.

533282|2026-06.headline: Gravita Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR1,475 crore and PAT 14% to INR106.39 crore, but lead volumes fell on Gulf supply disruption.
533282|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 42% YoY to INR1,475 crore, adjusted EBITDA rose 29% to INR145 crore (margin over 9.8%), and PAT rose 14% to INR106.39 crore, with total volumes up only 4% to 55,455 MT. Lead volumes declined YoY because Middle East war disruptions cut scrap imports, with 15-20% of imports routed via the Gulf. The copper subsidiary (Rashtriya Metal Industries) ran at 50% utilisation and contributed INR376 crore revenue. Management guided that copper plus a higher value-added mix (63% of revenue) will drive growth while lead margins are protected, and that the Phagi lead expansion of 40,500 MT was commissioned with INR30 crore of internal accruals.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA per ton: lead / aluminium / plastic / copper

financial_highlights.change: raised by copper inventory and goods in transit

financial_highlights.value: INR47 crore (INR35 crore operational, INR13 crore non-operational)

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: Volumes fell YoY due to scrap shortage from Gulf disruption; Mundra expansion ran at about 50% utilisation and Phagi (Jaipur) at about 45%. Management guided similar EBITDA margins for lead next quarter despite lower top-line.

segments.name: Copper (Rashtriya Metal Industries subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Ran at 50% utilisation, contributing INR376 crore revenue and EBITDA of about INR55,151 per ton. Management expects about 60%+ utilisation by year-end, with a 29,400 MT Gujarat copper plant (INR160 crore capex) due within 12 months.

segments.name: Aluminium and plastic
segments.commentary: Q1 per-ton EBITDA of INR25,175 (aluminium) and INR10,197 (plastic) included price gains; management's sustainable range is INR15-17/kg aluminium (overseas operations) and INR10-12/kg plastic.

guidance_outlook: Lead volumes likely to stay under pressure in Q2 FY27 from Gulf logistics; management expects lead EBITDA margins similar to Q1.
Copper EBITDA per ton expected to stay around INR55,000 near term, rising to about INR60,000 by year-end and INR65,000-75,000 over 2-3 years.

Copper capacity to double to about 60,000 MT per annum within 3 years; Phagi and Gujarat lead capacity expected to reach about 70% utilisation once scrap normalises, with about INR50 crore extra monthly revenue at optimal utilisation.
Installed capacity 4.97 lakh MT per annum; target over 8 lakh MT per annum by FY29. Total capex of INR1,680 crore through FY29, of which INR850 crore for existing businesses.
Management reiterated PAT growth target of 25-30% CAGR and copper business ROCE reaching about 25% in roughly 2.5-3 years; group ROCE currently about 20%.
capex_capacity: Phagi (Jaipur) lead plant expanded by 40,500 MT per annum at about INR30 crore, funded internally; total plant capacity now 75,819 MT per annum.
Copper: 29,400 MT per annum recycling plant in Gujarat, estimated INR160 crore, on track for commissioning within 12 months; bottleneck debottlenecking expected to finish by end of FY27.
Rubber capacity (Eastern Europe plant machinery) put on hold; copper expansion fast-tracked in that area.
Kathua manufacturing unit operations to be consolidated into Jaipur.
Own scrap yards being set up in the US and developed economies for copper, lead, aluminium and plastic, to be in place by end of FY27.
demand_pricing: Scrap shortage in India and demand-supply mismatch let management lift lead margins despite lower volumes.

Copper alloy realisations priced off monthly or fortnightly LME averages and hedged metal-by-metal (e.g. 70% copper / 30% zinc for brass); management said Gravita remains 100% hedged, so copper price rises do not flow through to profit.
Average LME copper about $13,500/t in Q1 FY27 versus about $9,000 a year earlier, diluting margin percentage.
Domestic sourcing about 35% for India plants.
Lead brand GRAVITA M listed on the London Metal Exchange (lead from Mundra); management said no LME sales yet, and the listing is aimed at new OEM approvals.
MCX inclusion of ADC12 aluminium alloy still pending with the exchange; management expects it within this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lead volumes decline YoY, and what is the FY27/FY28 lead volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed Middle East war supply disruption; 15-20% of imports come via the Gulf. Volume guidance was not given; growth is expected from copper and the Phagi/Mundra expansion once scrap normalises.

qa_highlights.question: When will copper reach 100% utilisation and how does margin bridge from 5.2% vs about 8% last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is at 50%, expected 60%+ by year-end; EBITDA per ton is seen at about INR55,000 with gradual increases. Management said last year's margin included copper price gains and that the margin percentage is diluted by higher LME prices.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt and working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is close to INR150 crore; working capital cycle is about 95 days, higher due to copper inventory and goods in transit.

qa_highlights.question: Plastic and aluminium sustainable EBITDA per kg?
qa_highlights.answer: Plastic sustainable INR10-12/kg; aluminium INR15-17/kg when only overseas operations run (INR13-14 when Indian operations run). Q1 figures included price gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company setting up its own copper yards and is there a cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is moving away from arbitrage agents to its own yards in developed economies (US), which it expects to lower procurement cost; lead yards were not viable earlier at lead-only scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is Mundra's new lead capacity utilisation, and is pyrolysis oil replacement contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mundra ran at about 50% including the February expansion; management said pyrolysis oil was already in use at Mundra and the Eastern European plant is not supplying India.

qa_highlights.question: Is ROCE below 20%, and where is it heading?
qa_highlights.answer: ROCE is about 20% currently, held back by lead capacity under-utilisation and copper premium paid on acquisition; management expects a rise toward 25% over about 3 years.

517214|2026-06.headline: DiGiSPICE Q1 FY27: continuing-business PAT of INR 9 crore; EBITDA INR 8.6 crore; AePS market share dipped to 17.93%.
517214|2026-06.overview: Management framed DiGiSPICE as a holding company whose only continuing business is Spice Money, a banking-agent fintech serving Tier-3 to Tier-5 India. Revenue was flat on a product-mix shift, but gross margin held at INR 48.1 crore as financial product distribution offset seasonal CICO weakness. EBITDA rose to INR 8.6 crore (about 6.5x QoQ) and PAT to INR 6.6 crore from INR 2.8 crore in Q4. The NCLT merger is in its second motion, with completion targeted by March 2027. Management said there are no formal fundraising plans and it is funding growth from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.metric: PAT (continuing business, as stated by Chairman)

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 2.8 crore in previous quarter
up 87% QoQ; up 25% YoY on a like-for-like basis excluding one-time items
BBPS grew 14.2% YoY; share of GTV 15% vs 9% a year ago

segments.name: Payments (AePS / CICO / UPI Cash Point)
segments.commentary: AePS market share fell to 17.93% in Q1 on lower withdrawals in stronger regions, recovering to 18.3% in July; AePS GTV about INR 13,300 crore. UPI Cash Point GTV INR 276 crore; management targets about INR 500 crore exit in Q2. Around 47% of AePS GTV came from agents on subscription packs.

segments.name: Collections (CMS / BBPS)
segments.commentary: Traditional CMS faces commoditisation and price sensitivity; BBPS GTV about INR 1,500 crore, up 14.2% YoY, with share of GTV rising to 15% from 9%. Three new BBPS clients added. Collections are about 10-12% of revenue.

segments.name: Financial product distribution (CASA, credit cards, insurance, lending)
segments.commentary: Management says this is the growth engine: GTV up 16.3% QoQ and margin up 50.7% QoQ. Grahak loan disbursals INR 167.7 crore; 17.8 lakh CASA accounts sold; five new secured card categories; two-wheeler insurance launched in July. Insurance sales moderated in Q1.

segments.name: Credit (own book, Adhikaris and Vyapar MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Disbursed INR 30.8 crore, up 55% QoQ and 2.8x YoY. Breakeven reported in the credit business. Seven lending partners; third-party capital, with first-loss model discussed. No stress reported so far.

guidance_outlook: NCLT merger in second motion; DiGiSPICE to convert into Spice Money as a pure-play listed fintech by March 2027.
Management expects gross margin growth in coming quarters from new products (financial product distribution, UPI Cash Point).
UPI Cash Point exit run-rate of close to INR 500 crore in Q2 FY27 (Rohit Sood).
Management expects 50% or more of margin from financial products and credit in five years; credit AUM and margin to contribute significantly around year five.
Discontinued-business structures to be closed by FY27 year-end; discontinued-business costs described as minimal.
No formal fundraising plans; growth funded from internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Agent network at 16.85 lakh agents at end Q1, 12.9% CAGR over five years; 13.3 lakh Adhikaris in Tier-4/5/6 towns.
Push into adjacent micro-urban clusters for financial product distribution.
Asset-light model; company described as zero-debt.
Insurance distribution operating model being changed, with portfolio expansion planned for the coming quarter.
Two own apps planned: a banking-agent app and a consumer app; SPICE UPI account in development; FDRT savings product in beta.
demand_pricing: AePS market share 17.93% in Q1 (down), 18.3% in July; management says share loss was driven by DBT disbursement skew toward South, where share is lower.
UPI Cash Point is positioned under the BC agent framework; management estimates about 40% share informally.
Collections market highly commoditised and price sensitive; growth shifting to higher-margin BBPS.
Management said the company is not seeing stress in agent lending or early open-market lending.
Cash-in/cash-out corridor products from the regulator (AePS third-party money transfer) cited as possible tailwind for South and West expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning any fundraising?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Modi said there are no formal fundraising plans; growth is through internal accruals, with capital raising possible later for new engines or customer acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in insurance policy sales, and how will it be accelerated?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Sood said insurance is sold mainly to captive Adhikaris (shopkeeper insurance), which saturated quickly; the company is expanding the product portfolio and changing the distribution construct next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Any early signs of stress in credit repayments or transaction volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Akash Bafna said agent lending shows no stress because agent cash flows are visible; open-market lending is underwritten cautiously on business vintage and model.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AePS market share fall to 17.93%, and can share gains be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Sood attributed the dip to DBT disbursement skew in southern markets where share is lower; share recovered to 18.3% in July.

qa_highlights.question: Can UPI Cash Point reach 50% of AePS, and how is advantage sustained as entry barriers fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 50% a hopeful target and said Q2 exit could be near INR 500 crore; the BC-agent onboarding requirement was cited as a moat for players with large agent networks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected timeline for the merger and listing, and are there residual costs from discontinued businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kapoor said the merger is expected by end of FY27; discontinued-business losses are minimal and reported separately, with structures being closed by year-end.

534309|2026-06.headline: NBCC standalone Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore (8.77% margin) on 10% revenue growth to INR 1,823 crore.
534309|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR 1,823 crore, while EBITDA rose 62% to INR 160 crore and PAT rose 32% to INR 151 crore, helped by marketing fees from the Bharat Business Park sale. Consolidated revenue was INR 2,260 crore, with a consolidated order book of INR 1,27,000 crore and INR 1,600 crore of orders secured in the quarter. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore and expects INR 18,000-20,000 crore of new awards over the next 2-3 quarters, but several large awards (GPRA 5 colonies, J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) have slipped repeatedly. Management also announced the HSCC merger into NBCC and an SPV for a proposed CPSE REIT.

segments.name: PMC / redevelopment (standalone order book)
segments.commentary: Standalone order book split is about 60% redevelopment and 40% PMC. Management says redevelopment and Amrapali contribute more than 60% of total revenue, and PMC fees are 8% plus 1% marketing on Amrapali.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Management expects about INR 500 crore of real estate revenue this year from land, completed inventory and WIP sales. Bharat Business Park was fully sold, raising about INR 10,000 crore across three auctions.

segments.name: HSCC (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue dipped because HSCC foreclosed a Maharashtra health project quoted at about 2% margin, which management says cost about INR 300 crore of top line. Management is merging HSCC into NBCC.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 15,000-17,000 crore reiterated; management referred to INR 16,000-17,000 crore in parts of the call.
Standalone FY27 revenue guided at INR 13,000-14,000 crore; FY28 revenue around INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore (consolidated basis per management).
PAT guidance of INR 1,100-1,200 crore for FY27, INR 1,300-1,400 crore for FY28 and about INR 2,000 crore for FY29, on a consolidated basis.
Margin guidance: EBITDA at least 6.5-7% and PAT 6-6.5%.

Awards guided at INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year (including Supertech about INR 10,000 crore, J&K about INR 3,500 crore, Rajasthan Mandapam about INR 3,500 crore), against an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore target.
GPRA 5 colonies (Lodhi Colony, Andrews Ganj, DIZ, Lakshmi Bai Nagar) order of about INR 30,000 crore expected; management says cabinet approval is pending.
Redevelopment fund generation of INR 30,000-35,000 crore expected this year, sale-linked and construction-linked, with cash collected over about two years.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 Amrapali is awarded and in execution, with one tower at the 20th floor using Mivan shuttering and others at the 13th floor; Phase 1 has 23 of 24 projects completed.
Standalone order book: about INR 10,000 crore of balance work across GPRA 7 packages, to be completed within about 18-24 months.
Gurugram Sector 37-D: contractor mobilised and test piles done; revised plan and EC approval pending, with sales expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Ghitorni: final lease agreement in process; consultant tender expected to be finalised this quarter; revenue after handover in about two years.
Business Park Tower purchase is construction-linked; only 10% first instalment paid so far, with the balance tied to construction milestones over about two years.
Dubai: 66 housing units under construction on a purchased land parcel; developer licence in hand; construction tender expected in October.
Goa redevelopment: four packages ordered, site mobilised and work started; two more packages pending tender.
demand_pricing: Africa Avenue auction for 262 residential units drew about 2,900 participants; auction postponed on a technical issue and expected in August. Vinayak Mandir auction targeted for September and Palanji area for September-October. Management expects INR 5,000-6,000 crore from Africa Avenue sales.
Amrapali: about 8,800 units in total, with roughly 4,000-4,500 sold; management expects to sell about INR 4,000-5,000 crore of inventory.

Pipeline: Supertech tender to be floated this quarter (16 projects in Noida and Greater Noida, about INR 10,000 crore); J&K infrastructure tender of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore to be floated this month after an initial INR 100 crore package drew about 15 bidders; MAHAPREIT (about INR 25,000 crore) expected in Q3; Naveen Nagpur infrastructure tender after DPR approval.

Recent wins: Odisha schools INR 253 crore, J&K campus INR 171 crore, New AP Bhavan INR 106 crore (Q1); Seychelles housing about INR 620 crore, RBI Amravati about INR 780 crore, Rajasthan science labs about INR 431 crore (July-August).
International: Seychelles has awarded a further 1,000 houses after about 2,000 in Maldives; management cites prospects in Australia, Saudi Arabia and Fiji, none included in projections.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited INR 6,500 crore last quarter; management did not reconcile the comparison

543983|2026-06.headline: EMS Ltd Q1 FY27 standalone operating income rose about 50% QoQ to Rs 125.72 crore, with PAT of Rs 15.03 crore and Rs 317 crore of new work orders.
543983|2026-06.overview: Management reported standalone operating income of Rs 125.72 crore, up about 50% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 25.53% and PAT of Rs 15.03 crore. Consolidated operating income was Rs 157.24 crore, up about 30%, with consolidated PAT of Rs 15.49 crore. Management attributed the weak prior quarters to monsoon disruption in Uttarakhand and election-related restrictions in West Bengal (Kolkata), which left fixed establishment costs uncovered. Management guided FY27 revenue back to roughly Rs 900-950 crore, with Q2 about 30-35% above Q1 and Q4 the strongest quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: PAT margin (Q1 FY27, as stated by H.K. Kansal)

segments.name: Kolkata / West Bengal sewerage project
segments.commentary: Execution was hit by election-related restrictions. Management said the Rs 70-80 crore run rate is not expected before Q3, as sewer line revenue cannot be booked quickly; Q3 and Q4 are expected to be stronger.

segments.name: Uttarakhand
segments.commentary: Heavy monsoon rains and a state directive halting sewerage work delayed execution in prior quarters; ramp-up started in Q3/Q4 FY26. Management stated about 61% of revenue came from Uttarakhand in the current period (as stated on the call).

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Management stated about 42% of revenue came from Uttar Pradesh in the current period (as stated on the call).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue targeted at roughly Rs 900-950 crore, similar to FY25 levels; management said this is 'at par' with FY25 by year-end.
Q2 FY27 revenue expected about 30-35% above Q1; Q3 and Q4 expected to grow more than 50% QoQ, with Q4 the strongest and Q2 the weakest of the remaining three quarters.
Management said margins should return to around 25% EBITDA and 15% PAT, citing margin-accretive order book; it noted margins may settle slightly below FY24 levels due to rising competition.
Management said FY27 would grow at least 50% over FY26 (about Rs 125 crore already achieved in Q1, per Ashish Tomar).
No capex plan as of now, per management.
capex_capacity: No capex or investment plan for FY27 as of now, per Ashish Tomar.
Fixed costs (establishment, labour, machinery rent) mean margins compress when revenue dips, per H.K. Kansal.
demand_pricing: Work orders of about Rs 317 crore converted in Q1 FY27 from the Delhi and Maharashtra bidding pipeline (cited as Rs 2,500-3,000 crore).
About Rs 158 crore of additional work orders received in Q2 to date; L1 position on a Banaras project above Rs 100 crore.
Bidding in Bihar and Madhya Pradesh; exploring Maharashtra and Karnataka.
Management said competition is increasing, so margins may not return fully to FY24 levels.
Management said current order book was bid at margins similar to target levels.

qa_highlights.question: Has West Bengal execution reached the Rs 70-80 crore run rate after election restrictions were lifted?
qa_highlights.answer: Restrictions are lifted, but the run rate will only be achieved from Q3 because sewer line revenue cannot be booked quickly; Q3 and Q4 Kolkata numbers expected to be much better.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 2,500-3,000 crore pipeline has reached award?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 317 crore converted to work orders in Q1, Rs 158 crore more received in Q2 to date, and L1 on a Banaras project above Rs 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of margin compression and how will it be reversed?
qa_highlights.answer: Monsoon disruptions and government restrictions reduced revenue while fixed establishment, labour and machinery costs stayed; margins rise with revenue. Management said PAT margin went from 6.3% in Q4 FY26 to 11.95% in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital stretched and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Government payment delays slow work, which delays billing; management said working capital needs are about 120 days of turnover (about Rs 300-350 crore on Rs 1,000 crore turnover).

qa_highlights.question: How long does conversion from order to revenue take?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineering and approvals take about six months after work order; site revenue starts around 8-9 months after award, with total timelines of 18-24 months of revenue conversion on two-to-three-year projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue split and how much will the Rs 2,329 crore order book execute this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 50% growth over FY26 and said Rs 125 crore is already achieved in Q1, with the balance in the remaining quarters; it stated Rs 300 crore of revenue in Q3-Q4 is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue concentration by state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 42% of revenue from Uttar Pradesh and about 61% from Uttarakhand for the current period, which together exceed 100%, so the basis needs clarification.

risks_watch: Monsoon and government restrictions (Uttarakhand, West Bengal) have repeatedly stalled execution; Q2 is the rainy season and management expects only 30-35% QoQ growth.
Working capital cycle around 120 days; delayed government payments are slowing work and billing.
Revenue target of Rs 900-950 crore needs roughly Rs 250-300 crore in each of the remaining quarters, with about Rs 300 crore in Q3-Q4 combined per the analyst's math, which management confirmed.
Margin recovery to 25% EBITDA and 15% PAT is management's target, not yet demonstrated; rising competition may cap margins below FY24 levels.
High state concentration (Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand); the disclosed percentages need confirmation.
Management said Q1 numbers were partly seasonal; the analyst pushed for YoY comparisons rather than QoQ.
543983|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the recovery and the FY27 revenue target, but defensive on margin compression and execution delays, which management attributed to weather, government restrictions and fixed costs. Answers on working capital and state-wise revenue were loose and some figures were restated during the call.

543985|2026-06.headline: Zaggle Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR423 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% from 10.1% on DICE costs and expensed capitalisation.
543985|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to about INR423 crore, while stand-alone revenue grew 18% to about INR390 crore against a soft seasonal Q1. Adjusted EBITDA was about INR34.7 crore (8.2% margin vs 10.1% a year ago), pressured by DICE integration and relocation costs (about INR3 crore in the last two months of the quarter, before any DICE revenue), one-time expenses, a moderation of capitalisation, annual increments and Zagg.Money costs. Management said DICE revenue starts from July 1 (Q2 FY27), reiterated the 40% consolidated growth guidance and a 25% stand-alone target, and pivoted the stated focus to cash flow and calibrated capitalisation. Analysts pressed on the sharp growth slowdown, margin volatility and the lack of explicit EBITDA guidance.

financial_highlights.change: about 10% YoY per analyst calculation, not stated by management

financial_highlights.metric: Cash back as % of program fees
financial_highlights.change: vs 65.7% in Q1 FY26 and about 69% in Q4 FY26
from INR17 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Save and Zoyer (stand-alone SaaS and programs)
segments.commentary: Post new income tax regime, wallet additions and per-user wallet increases for new and existing corporates; 73% of new users came from existing corporates. Large retail chain Zoyer rollout: about 2,000 of roughly 19,000 stores onboarded.

segments.name: Propel
segments.commentary: Consolidated Propel margin 7.1%, stand-alone about 5%, including spillover of overriding commissions realised in Q1. Signed Saint Gobain, Supreme Pipes and Phoenix India during the quarter.

segments.name: Fleet (CDG)
segments.commentary: Transactions up 43% YoY and transaction value up 5.8% YoY; annualised spend run-rate about INR100 crore. First contract with an OMC (HPCL, 5-year aggregator agreement for DT Plus).

segments.name: Zagg.Money (Rio.Money)
segments.commentary: Annualised new card acquisition run-rate raised to about 84,000 from 36,000 a quarter earlier; management cited about INR2.5 crore loss on the business. Co-brand launches with PNB and AU Small Finance Bank.

segments.name: DICE (acquired, spend management)
segments.commentary: Acquired as asset purchase for about INR68 crore excl. GST (from INR123 crore initial valuation). About 100 staff relocated from Pune to Hyderabad; revenue from novated contracts only from Q2 FY27. FY26 DICE revenue about INR12 crore; FY27 target INR15-16 crore at 90%+ gross margin.

segments.name: TaxSpanner (rebranding to Z.tax)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR80 lakh, +65% YoY; B2B business expected to grow about 120%. Management says on track to breakeven this financial year.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: About INR8 crore invested in Unobanc (moneyHOP), which holds an RBI Authorised Dealer Category-II licence for cross-border payments and forex cards.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated revenue growth guidance of about 40% for FY27 reiterated; stand-alone growth target about 25% retained, despite Q1 at 18%.
No explicit EBITDA margin guidance; management said it will guide on margin in coming quarters once DICE revenue kicks in. Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 14-15% framed over 5-7 years.
Stand-alone employee costs to rise in Q2 FY27 with DICE staff; other expenses expected to taper from Q2.
Program fee growth expected to improve in coming quarters; management says 10% growth is 'by design' as cash flow optimisation takes priority.
Novation of about 85-plus DICE clients to complete by end of Q2 FY27; full DICE pickup expected from Q3 FY27.
ADGM (Abu Dhabi) subsidiary to be opened in Q2 FY27; Investors Day planned in the coming quarter.
Expects cash flow turnaround to take about 15-18 months.
capex_capacity: Capitalisation moderated in Q1 FY27 ahead of a full policy review, which is being done with auditors and advisers; more clarity promised in coming quarters.
About INR6 crore of product development cost expensed in Q1 for an immediate client-required product; policy to expense more than capitalise over time.
Relocation of about 100 DICE AI professionals from Pune to Hyderabad completed in May-June; final payment-rail integration into DICE software due by Aug 31 or Sept 10.
Project Shiva (Zaggle Brain) to be filed with the exchange in coming months; patent planned.
Fleet rollouts accelerating in CDG programs; HPCL go-live and monetisation expected in later quarters.
demand_pricing: Stand-alone growth of 18% against soft Q1 seasonality; management attributes the slowdown partly to moving high working-capital-cycle banks' customers to other banks (re-carding takes time).
Geopolitical tailwinds for travel cited, but management said spend growth is not the primary focus; cash back share of program fees is.
Revenue per customer about INR10.6 lakh (INR423 crore / about 4,000 customers, management's rough figure).
Marquee wins: Radisson Hotels, SCA, Bikaji Foods, Nuvama Wealth (Save); Diesel Fashion, Navi, Dezerv (Zoyer); DICE clients Hindalco, Bajel, Trident, IDFC First Bank, Lenskart, XpressBees (novated).
86400 signed LankaPay (first international partner), Union Bank of India (Bharat Bill Payment) and Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank.
Management cites a possible limited MDR on high-value merchant transactions under the proposed Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill 2026 as a UPI monetisation tailwind.

500241|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Brothers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million, but EBITDA grew only 2% at an 11.8% margin.
500241|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to Rs.1,306 million, a margin of 11.8%. Standalone domestic revenue grew 9% to Rs.6,738 million, EBITDA 16% to Rs.920 million, and PAT 15% to Rs.540 million. International revenue grew 19%, but international EBITDA margin fell to 5.1% on lower high-margin services revenue at SPP UK and weak Rodelta execution. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 on both standalone and consolidated bases, while acknowledging that a large order slipped and foundry modernisation delayed some dispatches.

financial_highlights.change: driven by SPP USA and Kirloskar Brothers Thailand
moderated due to lower services contribution

segments.name: International (overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue +19% YoY, led by SPP USA and KBT Thailand. EBITDA Rs.207 million at 5.1% margin. Overseas pending order book Rs.15,045 million.

segments.name: SPP USA
segments.commentary: Growing 20-plus% in the quarter, driven by data centers, fire and HVAC projects; a multi-year framework with a large US data center operator is near signing (under NDA).

segments.name: SPP UK / Rodelta (Netherlands)
segments.commentary: SPP UK margin pressure from lower services revenue as chemical/petrochemical service contracts idled; management expects services recovery from Q2 FY27 for SPP UK and Q3 for KBL. Rodelta losses widened on delayed execution; improvement expected over the next two quarters.

segments.name: KPML (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Margin fell from 12.5% to 7.3% after merger of loss-making TKSL (steel castings) into KPML; management expects TKSL to turn profitable.

Services business expected to recover from Q2 FY27 at SPP UK and from Q3 at KBL, lifting blended overseas margins.
Rodelta execution expected to improve over the next two quarters; all entities expected to be profitable with better-than-prior-year numbers.
About two-thirds of the domestic order board (~Rs.2,500 crore) expected to execute in FY27.
Capex expected to be roughly equal to depreciation, focused on modernisation, debottlenecking and quality.
Management asks investors to assess performance half-yearly or annually rather than quarterly.

Capex guided at roughly equal to depreciation for FY27, mainly modernisation, debottlenecking and quality.
Nuclear primary circuit pump development is close to order placement; metallurgical trials in European and Indian foundries expected to conclude by mid-to-late August.

532699|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36% YoY to about INR 107 crore, with EBITDA up 39% to about INR 33 crore and margin at roughly 30.7% versus 30%. Reported PAT declined to about INR 6.4 crore from INR 10.9 crore, which management attributed to higher finance costs, depreciation and Ind AS effects, and ramp-up of leased properties. On a non-Ind AS basis, management said Q1 FY27 PAT was about INR 9.8 crore versus about INR 12 crore a year earlier. Five managed/franchised hotels with 237 keys were added, contributing negligibly to the quarter; management also flagged about INR 2.5 crore of GST input credit loss from a change in GST treatment and an April-June demand hit from the Middle East flight disruption.

segments.commentary: Occupancy about 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 vs INR 4,031 a year earlier. Management fee income is the revenue line here; fees grew about 14% last year on 7,700 keys.

segments.commentary: Management said Q1 occupancy was hit by April-June travel disruption (April about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%) versus about 80% in Feb-March. Breakeven estimated at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; target INR 100 crore.

Management declined to give a revenue growth rate for the next 2-3 years and said it is not assuring any date for INR 150 crore management fees; Vision 2030 target not specified as revenue or fees.
Keshav Baljee expects employee cost to stabilise within range over about another year as new properties open.
capex_capacity: Added five hotels with 237 keys in Q1 FY27, all managed or franchised, with no capex by the company.

Lakshminarayan Palace in Vadodara opened, branded under an ICONIQA collection brand, positioned upper upscale.
demand_pricing: April-June demand hit by flight cancellations linked to the war; management said about 50% of India inbound travel runs through three Middle Eastern carriers, which went to zero.
Business hotels seasonally weakest in Q1 (April-June); management said Q3-Q4 are the strongest quarters.
Leisure destinations performed well while business and airport hotels were hit.
Rain in Mumbai in July and August has weighed on ICONIQA occupancy.

ICONIQA missed the corporate RFP season, so management is relying on online travel portals and repeat guests.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q1 growth came from the 237 new keys, and what is the growth of the existing base?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said the five new hotels are managed/franchised and contributed very negligibly, as only management or franchise fees are earned; growth came from JLO hotels.

qa_highlights.question: What are occupancy and ARR for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: JLO occupancy about 70% and ADR INR 6,233 (vs INR 5,488). Managed portfolio occupancy 60.8% and ADR INR 4,300 (vs INR 4,031).

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue grow 25% or 30% over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; managed-segment fees will grow, and JLO growth depends on ICONIQA stabilising over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will profit growth come through, and what is the ex-ICONIQA, ex-Ind AS trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE is about 17-18% and targeting 20%+ in about a year. Amit Jaiswal said he was not very happy with ex-ICONIQA performance and cited high tax cost; Arjun Baljee said the hotel is about a year from turning the corner.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ICONIQA's top line decline, and what was occupancy in April-June and August?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jaiswal said April was about 79%, May about 60%, June about 70%; Q4 about 80%. Q1 is seasonally weak and the war hit inbound travel. August occupancy was hit by heavy Mumbai rains.

qa_highlights.question: What is ICONIQA's breakeven and incremental margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven at about INR 85 crore annualised revenue; management said about 60-65% of revenue above that flows to the bottom line, with a target of INR 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why has employee cost risen from 19-20% to about 23% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee cited the new wage code, annual increments, new leases and management team additions; Amit Jaiswal said the average through the year is about 20-23%.

qa_highlights.question: When can the company build a INR 100-150 crore annual management fee business?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee said no date is committed for INR 150 crore; fees grew about 14% last year, and the company aims to double fees as quickly as possible.

544501|2026-06.headline: Sugs Lloyd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR78.4 crore with EBITDA margin 15.3%; order book INR807 crore; FY28 INR1,000 crore target reaffirmed.

Management attributed the slower quarter to Patna project teething issues and supplier material shortages that pushed some June billing into Q2. Order book stood at INR807 crore (ex-GST) as of 30 June, and management reaffirmed the INR600 crore FY27 and INR1,000 crore FY28 revenue targets. Receivables fell by about INR10 crore to INR149 crore, while borrowings rose from INR68 crore to INR91 crore to fund Patna working capital.

524342|2026-06.headline: Indo Borax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.3% to Rs 70.36 crore and PAT rose 59.3% to Rs 16.25 crore, but management guided Q2 to be softer.
524342|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue was Rs 70.36 crore (+31.34% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 19.8 crore (+62.16%) at a 28.1% margin and PAT of Rs 16.25 crore (+59.31%) at a 22.3% margin, with EPS of Rs 5.07. Management attributed the quarter to improved capacity utilisation, higher realisations and new leadership after the Zenrock promoter change. The call was dominated by the proposed acquisition of a 64.26% stake in Kronox Lab Sciences from its promoters for about Rs 250 crore, funded partly by internal accruals, asset sales and a term loan. Management said Q2 margins will fall versus Q1 because of raw material inflation from the war and the monsoon-weak quarter, and reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 250-260 crore revenue at about 20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Boric acid (technical and IP grade)
segments.commentary: Management says about 80% of revenue comes from boric acid; IP grade is 7-8% of boric acid volume (about 100 tonnes vs 1,500 tonnes technical, per the speaker). Capacity utilisation expected at 96-98% of practical capacity, with output rising to about 18,000 tonnes this year from 15,917 tonnes last year.

segments.name: DOT (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume about 900 tonnes; FY27 target 1,500 tonnes against 6,000 tonnes nameplate. Contributes about 9% of revenue this year vs 7% last year. Margin expected broadly in line with boric acid.

segments.name: Kronox Lab Sciences (proposed acquisition)
segments.commentary: Vadodara-based listed specialty chemicals company with 185 products across excipients, reagents, API and nutraceuticals. Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore planned in phases over 18-24 months, with benefits from FY29 and full impact in FY30-31; management expects 3-3.5x current revenue post-capex.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance Rs 250-260 crore vs Rs 215 crore in FY26, with EBITDA margin about 20% and absolute EBITDA growth of about 11-12%.
Q2 expected to be softer on monsoon-weak volumes and raw material inflation from the ongoing war; margins not expected to match Q1's 28.1%.
Q3 expected to pick up again.
Boron oxide and boric acid capacity additions planned; management expects these to lift margins in FY28.
Capex of about Rs 50 crore over the next two to three years (Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore, boric acid Rs 20-25 crore, plus contingency); the Rs 50 crore figure is a business-plan rounding.
capex_capacity: Nameplate capacity about 26,000 tonnes per year at Pithampur: about 20,000 tpa boric acid and 6,000 tpa DOT.
Practical output expected at about 18,000 tonnes this year vs 15,917 tonnes last year, after planned maintenance days.
Boron oxide capex about Rs 20 crore; boric acid capex Rs 20-25 crore, with plant size flexible between 5,000 and 20,000 tpa.
Kronox Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore in phases: first phase about Rs 55-60 crore; benefits from FY29, full impact FY30-31; execution 18-24 months.
Management says there is capacity upside of 15-20% at existing Indo Borax plants through process changes.
demand_pricing: Indian boric acid market estimated at about 40,000 tpa, projected to grow about 8% CAGR to about 53,000 tpa by 2030; steel and refractory is 55-60% of demand.

Boric acid prices moved from about Rs 127/kg early in FY27 to about Rs 155-160/kg, per management, as costs rose during the war; some pass-through still pending and spot prices were soft in Q2 seasonally.
Management says Indo Borax prices at a premium to market (market plus), citing specifications.
DOT: management cites about 8,500 tonnes of imports and about 10,000 tonnes total market; Indo Borax targets 1,500 tonnes.
Kronox's Indian market growing about 11% CAGR per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kronox's previous promoter exit, and what is the status of the Dahej capex delayed by environmental clearances?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on the promoter's reasons. It said the Dahej land and design are ready, audits and studies are complete, and customers have been approached; the capex is to be executed as a first priority once the deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kronox to be merged into Indo Borax, and what is the group acquisition strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision yet on merger; both entities will continue as separate listed companies for now. Future acquisitions by Zenrock will be evaluated case by case; Indo Borax will focus on integration.

qa_highlights.question: How will the acquisition be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 250 crore to promoters. Rs 134-135 crore from internal accruals plus Rs 48-50 crore from sale of two Mumbai office properties. A term loan is expected in a couple of weeks to fund the open offer (Rs 151 crore) and the remaining gap. Promoter group committed Rs 25 crore contingency; total funding Rs 432 crore vs about Rs 400 crore required.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 50 crore capex plan consistent with the individual product items?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore and boric acid Rs 20-25 crore total about Rs 45 crore, rounded to Rs 50 crore including inflation and contingency.

qa_highlights.question: Will the open offer be tendered, and when does control transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not wait for the open offer to complete; it is using the expedited SEBI route to take control, with the open offer running in parallel. The SEBI holding period currently applies.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for unpledging Indo Borax shares pledged for the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific timeline; the pledge is standard for acquisition financing and is a work in progress.

511034|2026-06.headline: Jindal Drilling Q1 FY27: ONGC awarded a rig contract at ~INR45 lakh/day fixed; order book INR1,310 crore, with three rigs to dehire later in FY27.
511034|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as fairly good and broadly in line with expectations, with total revenue flat over the previous couple of quarters. EBITDA was stable; the variation in other expenses was driven by forex, which was more pronounced in Q4 FY26 and less so in Q1 FY27. The key development was a new ONGC contract for Jindal Pioneer, which is under refurbishment in UAE with deployment targeted for October 2026. The order book stands at INR1,310 crore, and three rigs are expected to dehire within FY27, which management said will reduce H2 revenue. The call also disclosed a JV loss tied to Pioneer refurbishment and an update on a long-running ONGC legal dispute.

segments.name: Rig contracting (offshore jack-up)
segments.commentary: Five rigs on long-term ONGC contracts, with the sixth rig (Pioneer) newly contracted. Most EBITDA comes from owned rigs and rigs on good day rates. Fixed-rate contract for Pioneer at about INR45 lakh/day, INR-denominated, versus a bid of USD62,000/day that was pushed to about USD47,800/day.

guidance_outlook: Three rigs (Discovery-I, Virtue-I, Jindal Star) expected to dehire in later part of FY27; H2 FY27 revenue expected to decline, with EBITDA declining less than proportionally and margin possibly rising.
Blended EBITDA margin target of 35% reiterated as earlier guidance.
Post-dehire refurbishment of 4-6 months with no revenue; INR90-110 crore estimated refurbishment cost per rig.
Pioneer refurbishment expected to finish by first week of September 2026, with deployment in October 2026.
Company expects cash position to improve; no acquisitions planned, focus on redeploying the three dehiring rigs.
Discovery-I and Jindal Star contracts had a slight extension in duration (per presentation).
capex_capacity: Jindal Pioneer refurbishment carried out in UAE through a joint venture; spend not disclosed. Completion by first week of September 2026 and deployment in October 2026.
Three rigs dehiring in later FY27 will need 4-6 months refurbishment each, at an estimated INR90-110 crore per rig.
Company acquired one rig in FY25 and refurbished it; cash conserved for upcoming refurbishments.
Tenders must be submitted separately for each rig owned, though multi-rig tenders are possible.
demand_pricing: Pioneer contract awarded at fixed INR45 lakh/day (approx.), INR-denominated; management said the rate was pushed down from its USD62,000/day bid to about USD47,800/day.

Redeployment of dehired rigs has been difficult for all drillers over the past two years; management expects the three dehiring rigs to be re-hired, citing the Government of India's Samudra Manthan exercise.
Day rates for the next three rigs expected to improve, though management declined to guide on rates; order book shows wide day-rate variation.
Focus is domestic (ONGC); international deployment considered only if opportunities arise, given existing-participant preference and counterparty and country risk.
Management could not say how many competing rigs are available in the market.

qa_highlights.question: Likelihood, timing and rates for renewal of the three rigs expiring in 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: After dehire there is a 4-6 month refurbishment with no revenue. Redeployment is fairly likely, though subject to tender nuances; management declined to comment on rates.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 FY27 revenue fall materially with three of six rigs out of contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, revenue will decline in H2. EBITDA is expected to decline less than revenue because the dehiring rigs include Discovery-I (owned), Virtue-I and Jindal Star, and the decline in earnings comes mainly from two rigs; margin may rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR denomination of the new contract fixed, and will INR or USD apply going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed day rate of about INR45 lakh, INR-denominated. Management will update on whether future tenders are in USD or INR next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a loss in the JV, and will it return to profit?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV was the seller of Pioneer and is funding refurbishment to bring the rig to contracted condition, which is causing the loss in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Any acquisitions planned given improved cash and lower debt?
qa_highlights.answer: No acquisitions planned. Focus is on redeploying three dehiring rigs, and cash is needed for refurbishments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ONGC dispute status and potential exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: No material update; the case has run 14-15 years and is in Supreme Court on appeal by ONGC. Company has received funds; if it loses (considered remote), it would repay about INR163 crore (INR63 crore USD receivable plus interest and forex).

risks_watch: Three rigs dehiring in later FY27 with 4-6 months of no revenue each; H2 FY27 revenue to decline.
Redeployment uncertainty: industry has struggled to re-hire rigs for two years; tender-based award process for each rig.
Pricing pressure: Pioneer bid cut from USD62,000 to about USD47,800/day; rate on renewals not guided.
Refurbishment capex of INR90-110 crore per rig may pressure cash; company says cash will improve.
ONGC legal dispute unresolved after 14-15 years; exposure about INR163 crore if lost (considered remote).
JV loss from Pioneer refurbishment; expected to be temporary per management's refurbishment explanation.

543954|2026-06.headline: Allcargo Terminals Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR47 crore (vs INR35 crore YoY) on 7.2% TEU growth to 1,76,499 TEUs.

EBITDA excluding other income was INR47 crore, with management citing yield management, technology-led efficiencies and higher transhipment share. Standalone revenue grew about 7.3% YoY to INR 110.4 crore, but standalone EBITDA margin was 11.64%. The expanded Palghar facility only became fully operational on 21 May 2026, so the quarter carried ramp-up costs and lower lead-free PVC offtake. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% and kept Egypt commercial production targeted before 31 December 2026.

Egypt revenue for FY27 cut to INR 30-35 crore from an earlier INR 50-60 crore estimate.
EBITDA margin guidance of 13-15% and PAT margin of 11-12% for coming months, reaffirmed from the previous call.
Egypt plant (60,000 tpa, about INR 67-68 crore capex) to start commercial production before 31 December 2026; Egypt top line of INR 250-300 crore over three years.
Palghar expansion peak potential of INR 700-800 crore over three years; top-line CAGR of about 35% over three years.
