Sales-related expenses fell sharply as the company skipped exhibitions in Q1; ECL provisions were also lower.

544060|2026-06.headline: RBZ Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 60% YoY to INR121 crores, with EBITDA up 39% to INR18 crores at a 14.9% margin.
544060|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR121 crores, up 60% YoY, in line with prior guidance, led by retail at INR78 crores (+70% YoY). EBITDA rose 39% to INR18 crores (14.9% margin) and PAT rose 28% to INR9 crores (7.5% margin). Management attributed margin pressure to muted gold price inventory gains, lease amortisation of INR76 lakhs, lease liabilities of INR115 lakhs, and pre-opening costs for the Surat store. The call focused on the store rollout (four stores this fiscal), a shift toward a gold metal loan (GML) based hedging model, and a long-term target of 75:25 retail to B2B mix.

segments.name: Retail (Harit Zaveri Jewellers)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78 crores, up 70% YoY. Ahmedabad store grew from INR24 crores turnover in FY21 to INR408 crores in FY26. Share of retail in B2B/B2C mix targeted at 50:50 in one to two years and 75:25 long term.

segments.name: Wholesale (B2B)
segments.commentary: Revenue reported as 42 (unit not clear, likely INR crores), up 47% YoY. Management says order book is strong for the coming quarter and B2B volumes grew.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Revenue approximately INR1.2 crores. Job work is 54% of mix per management, and management is seeking customer gold advances to reduce working capital.

guidance_outlook: Surat store (large format, ~10,000 sq ft) to open around late September 2026, ahead of Navratri (11 October); capex about INR10 crores; 52-60 staff hired.
Rajkot large-format store to open before October/early Q3; Maninagar and Gandhinagar mid-format stores in Q3 (possibly November).
Management expects Q2 performance in line with earlier projections, supported by IIJS order book; July and August order books described as full.
Capex break-even targeted within about one year per store; large-format inventory deployment INR125-150 crores, small-format around INR50 crores.
Debt-to-equity expected below 1:1 (about 0.8 debt to 1 equity) by fiscal year end; medium-term target 1.5-2:1 via GML.
Sanctioned debt of about INR300 crores, not yet fully utilised.
Inventory valued at about INR400 crores; market value about 18% above book.
Employee costs expected to keep rising as store and senior hiring continues; marketing spend to rise.
capex_capacity: Total factory capacity 1.8-2 tonnes a year; current consumption about 900-1,000 kg, around 50% utilisation.
Seasonal utilisation reaches 70-85%, sometimes near 90%, in peak months (July-September).
Surat store capex about INR10 crores; large-format inventory INR125-150 crores; small-format about INR50 crores (plus or minus 10-15%).
Plan to roll out about seven stores in total; four are in this fiscal year, and a few more have leases signed, some in Gujarat.
Retail inventory around 350 kg per an analyst question, not confirmed by management.
demand_pricing: IIJS show described as strong, with good buyer growth and order book; corporate design appreciation noted.
18-karat share of corporate sales: 0% before December, targeted at least 20% by year end.
Management says gold in USD fell about 30% from peak; INR gold has been flat, leaving negligible inventory gain in Q1.
Management says it does not expect 18-karat occasion wear demand to rise across India; 22-karat remains dominant.
Retail Q1 volume about 49 kg versus B2B about 125 kg; own production about 15-20% of retail volume.

qa_highlights.question: Expected timeline, investment and break-even for new stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat in Q2, Rajkot early Q3, Maninagar and Gandhinagar in Q3. Large-format capex break-even within a year or less.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term retail vs wholesale mix and debt-equity target?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B:B2C targeted at 50:50 in one to two years and 75:25 long term. Debt-equity below 1:1 by year end, rising to 1.5-2:1 via GML at about 3-3.5% cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: Negligible inventory gain as gold rate was flat, INR76 lakh lease amortisation, INR115 lakh lease liabilities, and pre-opening staff and marketing costs for Surat. Management estimated the total impact at about INR9 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How will the GML hedging work and what share of inventory will be hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Gradual move toward hedging, with about 50% in year two and 75% in year three. Retail cash flows will repay GML sub-limits. Bank negotiations are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the company shifted to GML from cash credit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a 30% USD gold correction, rising custom duty and a stronger balance sheet, with better ratings and banking relationships. GML is a natural hedge and is cheaper than the roughly 9% cost of the current borrowings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the franchise route planned and what is the long-term business split?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchising is premature. Current brand investment is meant to make the brand franchisable later. B2B will remain, and B2C profit share is expected to rise over three to four years.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from pre-opening costs, lease accounting and muted gold price gains; quarterly EBITDA margin trend as stores open.
Store ramp-up in Surat and Rajkot against the one-year capex break-even target.
Gold price volatility on about INR400 crore inventory; hedging transition depends on bank GML sub-limits still under negotiation.
Rising debt as borrowings grow; target D/E of 1.5-2:1 depends on GML availability and rating upgrade.
Job work share (54%) and working capital cycle; customers must provide gold advances.
Shift toward 18-karat jewellery; management says its contribution is still small.

We are utilizing factory at around 50% of capacity.
Right now we are not sharing it because of competitive reasons.

544853|2026-06.headline: Juniper Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79% YoY to INR 324 crore and EBITDA 86% to INR 294 crore, with 601 MWp commissioned in the quarter.

Fleet CUF rose to 30.2% from 28.2% and generation grew 72% to 944 million units. Management reported record commissioning of 601 MWp in the quarter and won new SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic and GUVNL wind tenders after quarter end. Net debt-to-equity was 3.24x before IPO proceeds of INR 1,800 crore; net worth is now stated at INR 5,200 crore.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Target ~4.5 GWh installed by June 2027 and ~10 GWh by March 2028; ~4 GWh additional orders placed with Envision. Round-trip efficiency ~91%, state of health ~99.6%.

segments.name: Portfolio
segments.commentary: Total portfolio ~11,200 MW plus ~9 GWh BESS; operational plus PPA-signed capacity above 6.2 GW. FDRE and wind-solar hybrid are 84% of the portfolio at blended weighted average tariff of INR 3.7/unit.

guidance_outlook: FY27: ~2 GW of renewable capacity additions targeted; 250-300 MW planned in Q2 FY27; ~4 GW total capacity by FY27 with run-rate EBITDA ~INR 2,750 crore for the 2 GW added.

Transmission: remaining ~1 GW substations largely operational; one ~300 MW substation expected to complete by December 2026.
Bikaner 50 MW merchant plant curtailment ~2-2.5%; 100 MWh battery doubling to 200 MWh expected within a month.
capex_capacity: 601 MWp commissioned in Q1 FY27 (458 MWp solar, 143 MW wind), the highest quarterly commissioning; ~400 MWh BESS also commissioned.
Surplus connectivity above 4.5 GW over the full pipeline; connectivity for more than 20 GWh of further BESS; over 14,000 acres of land banked and 200+ identified wind locations.
Module procurement closed at INR 12.1-12.2/Wp non-DCR; DCR modules assumed at ~INR 17/Wp for the thermal-mimic tender.
BESS sourced fully integrated from Envision (containers with AESC cells, PCS, EMS via Universe); container prices ~USD 58-60/kWh for early batches, ~USD 65-68 for later, all-in ~USD 100-110/kWh.
Thermal-mimic tender (SECI, 870 MW / 2,200 MWh, Rajasthan) has grid connectivity available; COD timing to follow PPA signing.
demand_pricing: Two tenders won after quarter end: SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic (870 MW, 2,200 MWh BESS against 230 MW contracted, tariff INR 5.26/unit; letter of award received) and a 50 MW GUVNL wind project at INR 3.51/unit.
Signed a 50 MW PPA with SJVN under FDRE at INR 4.25/unit; 550 MW FDRE capacity remains unsigned, with 350 MW in advanced discussions and a further 150 MW hybrid in very advanced discussions.
98% of contracted capacity is with off-takers rated A and above; 98% of portfolio under long-term PPAs, typically 25 years.
Merchant BESS: ~1.5 GWh of capacity not yet linked to projects will run merchant; some power sold on HPDAM at up to INR 20/unit; charging cost ~INR 1-1.50/unit.
Standalone BESS not pursued as returns are low; new tenders target higher-teens returns on an overall basis.

US: wholly-owned subsidiary set up in Greenville, SC at the International Center for Automotive Research; greenfield plant planned, initial investment directionally ~$5 million.

Service revenue growth was similar to Q4 FY26, while AMC bookings softened after price increases of roughly 3% to 12%. Management guided to a clear step-up in full-year growth and to FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26.

financial_highlights.change: +44% YoY; includes one-time INR19.5 crore gratuity reversal gain

segments.name: Water purifiers
segments.commentary: Grew high-teens on double-digit volume growth, with market share gains driven by economy range, stainless steel range, and premium Hot/UTC/IoT models. Management says growth was ahead of the category.

segments.name: Product business (overall)
segments.commentary: Grew late teens, broad-based across retail, direct and e-commerce, each with strong double-digit growth.

segments.name: Emerging categories (robotics, softeners, air purifiers)
segments.commentary: Strong growth across all emerging categories; robotics driven by premium mix (fully automatic cleaning station), softeners by volume. Robotics campaign launched with Shraddha Kapoor.

segments.name: Service (AMC and filters)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth similar to Q4 FY26 levels, but AMC bookings growth moderated after price increases; filter portfolio grew well. Filter gross margin is slightly below AMC but still high.

guidance_outlook: Clear step-up in FY27 full-year growth expected, supported by strong Q1 start.
FY27 full-year EBITDA margin aimed to be broadly in line with FY26 (FY26 exited with ~55 bps expansion).
Service revenue growth in Q2 FY27 expected to be similar to Q1; beyond that depends on AMC bookings and filter scale-up.
A&SP spend expected to grow ahead of revenue growth in FY27, focused on in-store presence and consumer finance.
ESOP expense expected at INR25-26 crore for FY27.
FY30 ambition reiterated: 2x revenue vs FY25 and 3x EBITDA; robotics targeted at INR1,000 crore by FY30.
Price increases to be calibrated; no plan for further consumer price hikes while momentum holds.
demand_pricing: Water purifier category penetration about 7%; high perceived cost of ownership cited as key barrier.
Price increases in products taken at start of quarter; peers followed with about a 30-day lag, and price parity now restored.
AMC price increases in the 3% to 12% band (single-year vs multi-year) led to deferred AMC renewals and softer bookings.
Four-year filter-life water purifiers (Glow 4X at ~INR22,000, Ritz Pro 4X at ~INR25,000) launched in e-commerce about 45 days before the call; competitors followed more recently.
Simplified filter range cut from ~65 SKUs to five universal filters; filter awareness campaigns stepped up.
Management says no supply-side help from competitors' disruptions; market share gains attributed to own initiatives and point-of-sale investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is service growth not picking up despite pricing, and when will it reach double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said service revenue grew in line with Q4 FY26 levels; AMC bookings were deferred by customers after the 3-12% price hike, with an 18-month AMC tenure creating a lag into revenue. Filters are being used to offset.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 15% growth came from pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly volume-led for water and softeners, while robotics growth came from premium mix. Pricing had some impact in water; management did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the service liability (deferred revenue) help FY27 service growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it helps FY27 revenue. However, in-year bookings must sustain growth, and the softness in AMC bookings is expected to show more in the later part of the year. Q2 service growth is expected to be similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins be maintained in FY27 with A&SP rising faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 margin decline reflects upfronted growth investment. Management cited COGS and opex efficiency workstreams and operating leverage, with the aim to hold FY26 margins; it noted FY26 ended with ~55 bps expansion after a similar Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Could the company reverse price hikes if commodity costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that if costs correct, it would pass benefits to consumers to stay competitive and grow share, rather than retain them.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2x revenue ambition by FY30 hold for products vs services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects products and emerging categories to grow faster than services, with filters growing ahead of AMC. It reaffirmed 2x revenue vs FY25 (about 17-18% CAGR) and 3x EBITDA by FY30.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from commodity and forex; management says no meaningful input cost relief yet.
AMC bookings softness after price hike may weigh on service revenue in H2 FY27.
A&SP rising ahead of revenue growth; margin hold depends on cost programmes.
Increasing competition from new entrants and 3-4 year filter-life offers from peers.
Ongoing geopolitical crisis and currency volatility.
Q1 PAT growth of 44% is flattered by INR19.5 crore one-time gratuity reversal; underlying PAT grew 6.1%.
543482|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on product growth and market share, but cautious on margins and service bookings. Management repeatedly flagged the year as "extremely unusual" due to commodity, forex and geopolitical pressure, and was evasive on the exact A&SP split and service growth targets.

we expect full year EBITDA margins to be broadly in line with last year.

544777|2026-06.headline: CMR Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore and PAT 22% to INR68 crore, with EBITDA/kg at about INR12.40 but operating cash flow negative.
544777|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore, EBITDA rose 27% to INR139 crore and PAT rose 22% to over INR68 crore, with aluminium volumes up 25% YoY. Management stressed EBITDA per kg (about INR12.40) over percentage margin because aluminium is largely a pass-through. Operating cash flow was negative due to a roughly 40% rise in average realisation (from about INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg), which raised working capital; inventory days fell to 40 from 45 and the cash conversion cycle to 65 days from 69. Management kept INR12/kg EBITDA and 25% FY27 volume growth as internal targets, while the Odisha plant ramps up.

financial_highlights.change: slightly up; management says per-kg is the right measure
+25% YoY total sales volume; aluminium +32% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Gross profit per kg (CFO's per-kg figure)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR26,000/ton in FY26 per management
cash flow hedge accounting entry, not a hedging cost per management

segments.name: Aluminium (recycled alloys/ingots and liquid metal)
segments.commentary: Aluminium volumes grew 32% YoY in Q1; liquid aluminium now exceeds 50% of aluminium sales, and management expects liquid metal growth to outpace ingot growth. Liquid metal margins are higher but management did not quantify the gap.

segments.name: Recycled billets and UBC
segments.commentary: Billets volume +149% YoY and UBC volume +333% YoY, both in ramp-up mode. Management cites construction, renewables, electrical and industrial demand beyond automotive.

segments.name: Non-ferrous (other metals) mix
segments.commentary: Aluminium to other non-ferrous sales mix held at about 80:20. FY26 volume mix was 66% automotive alloys, 10% non-automotive and 24% other metals; target rebalancing to 60:20:20 over the coming year.

guidance_outlook: Internal target of 25% volume growth in FY27, which management says is based on Tirupati and Odisha ramp-up, brownfield expansion and existing auto customers.
EBITDA guidance held at INR12/kg on a sustainable basis; management said it could do better but is not guiding above that.
Installed recycling capacity to exceed 7 lakh tons per annum by end FY27 (about 6.15 lakh tons currently), per management.
Expects to reach full utilisation at the Odisha (Hindalco) plant within FY27; current run-rate about 6,000 tons for the quarter, targeting about 4,000 tons a month.
Expects to return to positive operating cash flow once aluminium prices stabilise; debt to fall as inventory days and working capital cycle reduce.
Plans to bring debt-equity back toward its historical 0.5 ratio; currently about 0.86.
capex_capacity: INR53 crore invested in the quarter in greenfield projects at Shoolagiri and Bawal, with brownfield and technology projects at Tirupati and other locations progressing as planned.
Odisha plant (48,000 tpa capacity, built for Hindalco) is ramping up.
Capacity utilisation is about 65%; traditional range of 70-75%.
Hindustan Zinc: MoU signed, nothing definitive, and no construction started; management says it will take a while.
demand_pricing: Passenger vehicle and two-wheeler sales grew about 26% and 20% YoY in Q1 FY27; EV penetration was 8.26% of registrations in FY26. Ather Energy is a new customer.
Auto customers are on cost-plus pricing; management says hedging is used to manage the balance on the un-passed-through portion.
Exports were about 3.4% of FY26 turnover, focused on niche products to Japan, Europe, Southeast Asia and some China.
Management says volumes are independent of aluminium price movements; scrap availability is not price-dependent.
Management says scrap sourcing is getting harder as some countries restrict scrap exports; the company is widening its sourcing base and buying more domestically.

Regulatory tailwinds: proposed EPR framework to lift minimum recycled aluminium content from 5% in FY28 to 10% over time; EU CBAM cited; India's aluminium extrusion industry expected to grow at 12% CAGR through FY29.
Recycled aluminium is about 40% of India's aluminium consumption, growing about 13% a year versus about 7-8% for primary, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How does hedging work for secondary aluminium given peers say it cannot be hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said secondary prices follow primary with a lag and auto customers pay cost-plus, so part of exposure is left to cost-plus pricing and part is hedged on LME. The CFO added that operating cash flow is negative because average realisation rose about 40%, from INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR36 crore was loaded for a cash flow hedge entry under accounting standards, not a hedging cost; other expenses were broadly flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive and what will debt be by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects positive operating cash flow once prices stabilise. The CFO said D/E is about 0.86 against a historical 0.5 target, which should fall as prices stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Why does reported EBITDA differ from the earlier presentation for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company reclassified foreign exchange gains and the ineffective portion of commodity hedging from other income into EBITDA as they are operating in nature, though accounting standards require other-income classification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% FY27 volume growth still on track after Q1 aluminium volume growth of about 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25% is an internal target, not guidance; Q1 volume grew 25%, and growth is expected from the Tirupati and Odisha plants and existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Do GP and EBITDA per kg move with utilisation, and how should hedging costs be treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held INR12/kg EBITDA as guidance despite utilisation of about 65% versus 70-75% historical. It said hedging costs are minimal (broker and LME fees) and that hedging works against physical profit or loss.

544550|2026-06.headline: Pace Digitek Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51.3% YoY to Rs.555 crore; FY27 guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated on Rs.10,803 crore executable order book.
544550|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.555 crore (up 51.3% YoY) but down sharply from Rs.1,097 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition and a high Q4 base. EBITDA was Rs.86.1 crore (15.5% margin vs 14.9% in Q4) and PAT was Rs.63 crore (11.3% margin vs Rs.55 crore in Q1 FY26). Order inflow in the quarter was about Rs.1,677 crore, with two energy EPC wins (NLC, DVC, ~Rs.1,412 crore) and a BSNL OFC project (~Rs.265 crore). Management said the 5 GWh BESS line is operational, with a further 5 GWh line due to be commissioned by December 2026, and reiterated the FY27 revenue guidance.

segments.name: Energy (BESS, renewable EPC, BOO)
segments.commentary: Contributed 79.5% of Q1 revenue and is the main growth driver; energy executable order book Rs.8,453 crore, split Rs.4,074 crore BOO and Rs.4,367 crore EPC. Management expects energy to be about 65-70% of the order book by year end.

segments.name: Telecom & ICT (BharatNet, Railway Kavach, BSNL OFC)
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.5% of Q1 revenue; executable order book Rs.2,350 crore. Kavach about 30% complete; BSNL OFC (~Rs.265 crore) to execute over about 2.5 years. Management said telecom has better margins but lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated; management said it sees no concern in achieving it, with most revenue expected from the existing order book.
H1 FY27 targeted at 40-45% of full-year revenue vs 35% in H1 FY26.
Q2 container supply planned at 210 units; management expects about 125+ containers per month in the next calendar year.
FY27 PAT margin guidance of 10.5-11% for BESS, with the lithium-ion cell cost increase said to be factored in.
Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive by March 2027; inventory and receivables expected to stabilise between December and March.
Energy-to-telecom order book mix expected to move to about 65:35 or 70:30 by year end.
capex_capacity: BESS capacity is 5 GWh operational (two 2.5 GWh lines); a third 5 GWh line is due for installation in October 2026, targeting 10 GWh by early December 2026 as India's largest operational BESS facility.
Total capex of about Rs.300 crore for the 5 GWh expansion phase, the container fabrication unit, and related setup, mainly land cost, funded from the earlier private placement.
In-house container manufacturing started with trials this month; batch production from next month. Over 300 containers supplied to date.

BOO projects: 975 MWh commissioned to date (MSEDCL standalone BESS, about Rs.900 crore recognised in P&L); four BOO projects expected to add about Rs.750 crore annual revenue once all are commissioned.
Pune R&D centre inaugurated about three weeks ago; cell manufacturing planning under way. Applying for 4 GWh under the government cell PLI scheme (10 GWh total scheme).
demand_pricing: Bidding for about 27 GWh of tenders; NTPC Renewable Energy and NTPC Green tenders noted, with NTPC Green tenders drawing only 7-8 bidders versus 32-51 in earlier state tenders.
Management said bidding aggression has eased after a 4 GWh Maharashtra project was cancelled and a Punjab tender saw a single bid at higher prices.
Management said cell cost is about 60% of total BESS cost, unchanged; recent tenders include price variation clauses while older tenders do not. Stock was built in March to lower Q1 cell costs.

C&I BESS (below 5 MWh) received product approval from large Indian customers; first trial order of about 25 units, with management referring to potential for thousands per year. Management guided C&I EBITDA margin about 4-5 points above grid-scale product margin of 13-15%.
Container unit value about Rs.4-4.5 crore; about 70 containers per month currently.
Early exports: small container supply to a Saudi company in Q1 and an MoU signed in Saudi Arabia.
MEGMEET tie-up for AI data-centre power solutions in India; demo equipment planned; management said a concrete revenue plan could come in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Telecom & ICT order inflow break-up and execution timeline for the Rs.2,350 crore telecom book?
qa_highlights.answer: Of Rs.1,677 crore inflow, NLC and DVC EPC wins were about Rs.1,412 crore and BSNL OFC about Rs.265 crore. EPC projects run about one year; OFC about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance not higher given the energy order book visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: BOO solar-plus-BESS capex is capitalised as a fixed asset and not recognised as revenue, so physical execution will exceed reported revenue. Revenue recognition comes from EPC and standalone BESS in BOO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow and working-capital profile by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom net working capital is about 5 months (~150 days); energy is expected at 90-100 days. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue path needed from Q2 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the remaining Rs.2,700 crore should come from the existing order book, with Q1 seasonally low due to government funding and approval cycles.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising lithium-ion cell prices affect EPC and BOO margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 10.5-11% margin already includes anticipated cell price increases; price variation clauses in new tenders and stock built in March mitigate impact.

500280|2026-06.headline: Century Enka Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 554 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.46%, helped by a Rs 46.24 crore one-time inventory gain.
500280|2026-06.overview: Revenue of Rs 554 crore grew 38% YoY and 15% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 86 crore (up 331% YoY) and PAT of about Rs 62 crore (up 301% YoY). Management attributed the margin jump partly to a one-time inventory gain from low-cost opening stock (Rs 46.24 crore as reported) and partly to GST-cut-driven auto and tyre demand, pass-through pricing and a higher renewable power share above 40%. Management said margins are expected to normalise, and it kept its normalised operating margin range at 7-10%.

financial_highlights.change: Per management, as reported in the results filing

segments.name: Tyre cord fabric (NTCF/PTCF)
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 306 crore, up 69% YoY. Demand is described as robust after GST cuts on tyres and autos. PTCF approvals are progressing, with commercial sales expected from H2 FY27.

segments.name: Filament yarn
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 230 crore, up 20% YoY, with healthy demand and better mix from valuated and mother yarn products. Cheap Chinese commodity imports persist, and anti-dumping duty was not notified despite favourable DGTR findings.

guidance_outlook: Margins expected to normalise over the next few quarters as higher-cost inventory is consumed. Normalised operating margin range maintained at 7-10%; management said it would revise this only once it is confident the range has moved up.
Renewable power share is over 40% in Q1; expected to reach about 50% once the Bharuch group captive expansion (about 10-10.5 MW capacity) commissions, most likely in Q3 FY27 or H2.
PTCF commercial sales expected to start in H2 FY27, possibly Q3 or Q4.
No significant capacity addition in FY27. Mother yarn capacity addition to commission in FY28, adding about 3-4 thousand tonnes per annum.
Capex of over Rs 100 crore planned for FY27, covering value-added yarn products, power-cost reduction and safety upgrades.
No forward guidance on realisations, volumes or the quantum of margin impact from raw material costs.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is 92,000 MTPA; utilisation normally runs at 85-90%, varying by product.
Capex of over Rs 100 crore in FY27, including value-added filament yarn products (adds to margins, not capacity) and power-cost reduction.
Bharuch group captive renewable scheme adds about 10-10.5 MW; Century Enka's equity contribution is about 26%, with about Rs 8.5 crore spent so far.
Mother yarn capacity addition to commission in FY28; PTCF plant is under approval, and the company is selling some yarn in the meantime, which affects capacity.
Management said new investments must clear board-approved hurdle rates, typically a minimum 12-15% IRR.
demand_pricing: Tyre-cord demand is robust after the September 2025 GST cuts on tyres and autos; management could not quantify the GST contribution to the 38% growth, but said Q3 onwards showed a stark improvement.
Management flagged geopolitical events, volatile crude, inflation and cheap imports as risks to domestic demand. Exports are very small.
Caprolactam and chips prices spiked after the Iran war and have since eased but remain volatile. A sharp move within one to two months affects gross margin.
Realisations are not guided because pricing changes month to month.

Raw material inventory is about 25-30 days for imports (including in transit) and about 10-15 days (around 15) for domestic sourcing. Management does not see raw material availability as a constraint.
Volumes have been broadly flat over the past four years per an analyst; management said FY27 volume depends on market conditions and import competition.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the inventory gain add to the bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the Rs 46.24 crore inventory impact already in the results filing and declined to say whether it applies at EBITDA level or to give any further breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is the renewable power share and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable power was over 40% of consumption in Q1. It is expected to rise to about 50% after the Bharuch expansion commissions, and management did not quantify the value impact.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 38% growth came from GST-cut-led demand, and is there a risk of air-pocketing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not quantify the GST effect. It said auto sales across segments kept growing quarter-on-quarter, and that how long the effect lasts depends on financing and the economy.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gross margin stayed at 58-59% for three quarters, and what is the normalised EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked gross margin to volume growth and to inventory timing on sharp raw material moves. It reiterated a normalised operating margin of 7-10% and said anything above that may not be permanent.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin range move to 10% or double digits on a sustainable basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide. It said the range would be revised only once it is confident the improvement is durable, and it would not be breached at least in normal circumstances.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned capex, and what is the capacity outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is over Rs 100 crore in FY27. Capacity is not expected to rise in FY27, with about 3-4 thousand tonnes per annum added in FY28 from mother yarn.

risks_watch: Reversal of the one-time inventory gain and normalisation of margins as higher-cost caprolactam and chips inventory is consumed. Management did not quantify either.
Demand softening after the GST-driven tyre and auto boost, plus crude, geopolitical and inflation risks.
Cheap Chinese filament yarn imports, with anti-dumping duty still not notified.
PTCF commercial sales timing (H2 FY27) and whether the approvals hold.
Renewable power share rising to about 50% and the Bharuch commissioning timing (Q3 FY27 expected).
Volume growth has been flat over four years per an analyst, and FY27 capacity is not expanding.
500280|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's headline numbers, but guarded on forward margins, realisations and volumes, which management repeatedly declined to guide. It stressed that the 7-10% normalised range is unchanged while also saying margins will normalise, and it was evasive on the inventory gain quantum and the GST demand split.

511144|2026-06.headline: Axis Solutions Q1 FY27 revenue rose 78% YoY to ₹48.98 crore, with EBITDA up 122% to ₹6.21 crore and PAT up 77% to ₹3.09 crore.

PAT rose 77% to ₹3.09 crore, but PAT margin was flat at about 6.3% as tax was provided for the first time this year. Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance, only qualitative comments that growth and profit would be "very, very good". Emerging segments (hydrogen storage, Kavach, EV charging) are still pre-revenue, and the company said hydrogen margins are not yet in the financials.

financial_highlights.value: ₹6.21 crore (stated as ₹6.22 crore in one place)

financial_highlights.change: Nil in Q1 FY26; some carried-forward tax provision

segments.name: Industrial engineering and systems
segments.commentary: 59% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs 28.6% in Q1 FY26, the largest vertical now. Management attributed the mix shift to lumpy timing in the first quarter.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: 26% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs 55.8% in Q1 FY26. Water share fell as the mix moved toward industrial engineering.

segments.name: Automation and digitalisation
segments.commentary: About 15% of Q1 FY27 revenue vs 15.6% in Q1 FY26, broadly flat share.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance. Management said growth would be 'very, very good' compared with last year and profit 'really very good', and referred to the quarterly results for projections.
Most of the ₹365 crore open order book is expected to be executed in FY27, with some orders running 1-2 years.

Green hydrogen, Kavach and EV charging are described as emerging. No revenue timing was committed; management said commercialisation activities are ongoing and no hydrogen margins are in the financials yet.
MRO/AMC/warranty recurring revenue is about 5-6% of total revenue and is expected to increase over one to two years.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing is in Ahmedabad only, across five purpose-built facilities totalling about 1,40,000 sq ft, with end-to-end manufacturing under one roof.

demand_pricing: Management said it does not compromise on price against competition and credited product life cycles, registrations and in-house R&D for growth.
ATEX and IECEx certifications allow supply to the Middle East, Southeast Asia and Europe. Import substitutes for European and Chinese products were cited.
Named clients include IOC, HPCL, NTPC, Tata Chemicals, BHEL, L&T, Reliance, Adani, Petronas, ADNOC and KAFCO. Customer names were given without order values.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see growth in the coming years and where will FY27 end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, saying projections are in the quarterly results. It said growth and profit will be 'very, very good' versus last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹365 crore order book be executed this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of it is expected in FY27, with some orders closing in the following year. New large orders would be announced.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for NSE listing, promoter stake reduction and fundraising?
qa_highlights.answer: NSE listing depends on first meeting minimum public shareholding (MPS) norms, and there is time to do so. No instrument, amount or dilution has been decided and nothing is pending with the board.

qa_highlights.question: What is the green hydrogen product, its patents and when will it generate revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a solid-state hydrogen storage technology, described as a first in India. Management holds both design and technology patents. No revenue timing was confirmed, and commercialisation is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kavach work and are there orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Axis is in proof-of-concept with several companies and got approval for Kavach. No Kavach orders were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins low despite about 13 granted patents?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hydrogen revenue and margins are not yet in the financials. It said one industrial engineering and systems patent is in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: MRO, AMC and warranty revenue is about 5-6% of total revenue and is expected to rise over one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and peak revenue capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give utilisation or peak revenue. It said products are customised rather than batch-produced, and the facilities would not constrain the top line.

533339|2026-06.headline: Zen Technologies Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to Rs.141.6 Cr (vs Rs.158.2 Cr YoY) and operational EBITDA margin to 27.3%, with management guiding to mid-30s for FY27.
533339|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs.141.6 Cr, down from Rs.178.1 Cr in Q4 FY26 and Rs.158.2 Cr in Q1 FY26, which management attributed to order execution timing. Operational EBITDA was Rs.38.7 Cr at a 27.3% margin versus 40.9% a year ago and 28.6% in Q4, with management citing negative operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base and a Rs.7.65 Cr provision release in the prior-year quarter. Reported PAT was Rs.34.5 Cr after a Rs.3.4 Cr exceptional fire-related loss at a subsidiary; adjusted PAT is about Rs.37 Cr (26.1% margin). Order book stood at Rs.1,239 Cr, with a Rs.177.5 Cr Ministry of Defence simulator order received after quarter end; the group remains debt free with about Rs.1,217 Cr cash.

segments.name: Simulators (army, navy, air force)
segments.commentary: Management calls simulators and anti-drone systems the two matured franchises; a Rs.177.5 Cr MoD order for tank and crew gunnery simulator upgradation came after quarter end. Management expects Rs.700-800 Cr of simulator orders in the pipeline, with some possibly within months.

segments.name: Anti-drone / counter-drone systems
segments.commentary: Demand is tender-gated: management says no anti-drone or simulator tenders have been floated recently, though a fast-track process is expected to bring them. Management cited about Rs.800 Cr of anti-drone orders after Operation Sindoor and expects anti-drone opportunities of at least Rs.2,000 Cr.

segments.name: Vector Technics (drone propulsion)
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded to about 300,000 units. Management said drone segment orders have slowed; it estimates Rs.300 Cr potential revenue if orders at Rs.10,000 per unit materialise, with about 50% of enquiries from overseas.

segments.name: Robotics / new products
segments.commentary: Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle has completed internal trials; customer trials pending. Management expects robotics, autonomous vehicles and related products to take at least two to three years to mature.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year operational EBITDA margin expected in the mid-30s, as revenue scales and operating leverage works in the company's favour; Q1 margin was below the 35% guidance.
Order book expected to end FY27 at about Rs.2,500 Cr after FY27 execution, per management's earlier investor-meeting communication.
Revenue for FY27 expected to be weighted toward Q2 and Q3, given that much of the order book was secured in H2 FY26 with roughly 12-month execution cycles.
Management referenced a cumulative Rs.4,000 Cr revenue target for FY27 and FY28 combined; the simulator share was put at about Rs.2,000 Cr.
Management said it is actively looking to acquire companies, with funds remaining from QIP plus accumulated cash.
capex_capacity: Vector Technics propulsion capacity expanded to about 300,000 units.
Working capital build-up in supplier advances and inventory to execute order book deliveries through FY27.

Air Force: first flight simulator (C295 referred to on the call as C195 in one answer) developed in-house; full motion simulator capability available; company shortlisted for future Air Force simulators.
demand_pricing: Q1 order intake was Rs.44.6 Cr against Rs.141.6 Cr executed, so the order book declined from March 2026.

Management attributes softness to demand, not supply: no tenders for anti-drone or simulator systems had been issued recently; prior tenders were single-vendor because competitors were disqualified on technical grounds.
Management expects some competition and says Zen will not win every requirement.

Export push: targeting Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia and CIS; also North America and EU via prime contractors (FOCI and ITAR clearances in progress). Management says US target is about $100 Mn in year three.
Government is moving more orders to 12-month fast-track procurement (FTP) cycles, though large orders still go through regular procurement.

financial_highlights.change: -11% YoY vs Rs.158.2 Cr; -20% QoQ vs Rs.178.1 Cr
vs 40.9% in Q1 FY26 and 28.6% in Q4 FY26
vs Rs.47.8 Cr in Q1 FY26 and Rs.31.5 Cr in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax (adjusted for Rs.3.4 Cr exceptional fire loss)
financial_highlights.value: about Rs.37 Cr at about 26.1% margin

financial_highlights.change: net reduction vs March 2026 (Rs.44.6 Cr secured vs Rs.141.6 Cr executed in quarter)
up vs year-end, driven by supplier advances and inventory

financial_highlights.value: about Rs.1,217 Cr; group debt free

540879|2026-06.headline: Apollo Micro Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 17% YoY to INR156 crores, while consolidated revenue jumped 88% to INR251 crores; standalone PAT up 43% to INR28 crores.
540879|2026-06.overview: Management reported its best June quarter, with standalone revenue of INR156 crores (+17% YoY), EBITDA incl. other income of about INR48 crores, and PAT of INR28 crores, giving record EBITDA and PAT margins of 31% and 18%. Consolidated revenue was INR251 crores (+88% YoY) and consolidated EBITDA excluding other income was INR54 crores (+31%). Management pointed to a standalone order book of INR1,224 crores and a consolidated order book of INR1,704 crores as of 8 August 2026. The company also signed to acquire a 41.33% promoter stake in Premier Explosives for about INR1,550 crores in cash, and reiterated 40-45% growth guidance.

segments.name: Standalone Apollo Micro Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue INR156 crores (+17% YoY) with PAT of INR28 crores and 18% PAT margin, the highest June-quarter PAT. Export revenue is nil.

segments.name: Ideal Explosives (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Turned PAT positive in Q1 FY27 after being EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26, but margins are thin. Management expects full positive contribution from FY28 after 3-4 quarters of restructuring; order book is INR480 crores.

segments.name: Premier Explosives (proposed)
segments.commentary: Acquisition of 41.33% promoter stake for about INR1,550 crores, all cash; open offer timing is with the regulator. Not yet consolidated.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 40-45% continues to be guided for FY27, on both consolidated and standalone bases; management declined to give EBITDA margin guidance.
FY28 guidance to be given at the end of FY27.
Consolidated order book expected to reach INR3,500-4,000 crores by end FY27 on the back of a single order of INR2,500-3,000 crores (understood to be MIGM/QRSAM-linked, not confirmed).
Ideal Explosives expected to be fully positive from FY28.
Export orders expected to be meaningful in FY27 but not guided; next FY seen as sizable. Export revenue is excluded from guidance.
Promoter pledge expected to be fully cleared in about one year (around Q1 FY28).
capex_capacity: Unit III is a large facility; first phase production has started and full production is expected before March 2027. Management says operational readiness is expected in the next couple of quarters.
Plans for new production plants at Ideal and Premier are to be announced in the next 2-3 months, with the broader plan to follow once Unit III is fully operational (around December).
Autonomy segment investment to be heavy in FY27 and FY28 across land, air and sea.
Aerial bombs (1 kg to 25 kg) established, with 9 variants tested and acceptance received.
Management plans to acquire 2-3 more companies; MoUs to be signed before announcements.
demand_pricing: QRSAM: BEL to take the order soon, with a missile portion to BDL. BDL order value expected at INR11,000-12,000 crores; first phase 1,000 numbers. Apollo content is more than INR1 crore per missile across about 5 sub-systems. Execution starts in FY28.

MIGM: DAC approval received; Navy inquiry expected end of next month; purchase order expected December-January. Total budget about INR3,500 crores, 20% advance, and management expects about 70% share. Execution over about 3 years, with production starting FY28.
Pinaka: 2,000 numbers under negotiation; Apollo component about INR85 lakhs per Pinaka.
Akash-NG: 1,000 numbers cleared by MoD; component value similar to QRSAM (more than INR1 crore).
HAL: current orders about INR100-150 crores, with another INR150 crores expected.
Moored mines: combat trials done; DCP and contract expected; orders expected next FY. Limpet mines: trials complete, orders possible from Q4 FY27.
Kusha: 150 km version tested; Apollo supplied about 7 critical sub-systems. Conversion to orders expected in 2-3 years.
Anti-drone Make-II: trials not yet started; TAM guidance expected around December quarter.
SAVIOR ASW: Make-II prototype sanction; customer expects completion in 18 months, with orders about a year later.
IPREC (IAF Make-II): Apollo is prime development agency; conversion of dumb bombs to precision guided bombs.

qa_highlights.question: How will Premier Explosives be integrated and what synergies arise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Premier gives backward integration into propulsion and explosives, removing dependence on third parties (e.g. MIL) and enabling Apollo to become a prime OEM for weapons. Operations will remain separate for now; Ideal will not merge with Premier.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ideal's losses be resolved, and when will it integrate into defence?
qa_highlights.answer: Ideal is PAT positive in Q1 but margins are low. Bulk explosives volumes are weak; GOCL accessories manufacturing starts in a couple of quarters. Full positivity expected from FY28. Integration plan to come in 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any FY27 or FY28 revenue or EBITDA margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth guidance of 40-45% is reaffirmed for FY27. No EBITDA margin guidance; management said the momentum will continue, with FY28 guidance at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Order book trajectory for three years including Premier?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated order book is INR1,700 crores; a single order of INR2,500-3,000 crores expected by FY27-end could take it to INR3,500-4,000 crores. Premier's own order book was not disclosed as it is in the CCI process.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR2,500 crore acquisition funding deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR2,500 crores for the acquisition, around INR500 crores for working capital debt, with the rest for general corporate purposes.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D as a percentage of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management initially said about 4% for FY26, then corrected it: FY26 R&D was INR72.53 crores on INR764 crores revenue, around 9.5%, with a 6-8% average over the last 3-4 years.

financial_highlights.change: Includes INR480 crores at Ideal Explosives
Management corrected an earlier ~4% figure on call

543275|2026-06.headline: Anupam Rasayan Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR655 crore (TI +36% YoY), EBITDA INR175 crore at 26% margin, PAT up only 6% to INR51 crore.
543275|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 36% YoY to INR667.5 crore, with EBITDA up 35% to INR174.9 crore and margin steady at about 26%. PAT grew 6% to INR51.2 crore as higher depreciation (partly Jayhawk's older depreciation policy) and interest absorbed the EBITDA gain. Management said the major capex cycle is complete and Jayhawk contributed roughly 20-22% of revenue at a 19-20% EBITDA margin. The Bliss GVS Pharma open offer closed on August 10, with completion expected by the first half of September 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR62.9 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR56 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Jayhawk Fine Chemicals (US)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 20-22% of Q1 revenue (around INR145 crore), with EBITDA margin of 19-20% (around INR30 crore) and PAT of about INR9 crore after heavy depreciation. Management said Jayhawk is unlevered and well capitalised.

segments.name: Standalone performance materials / polymers
segments.commentary: Standalone polymer share guided at 20-25%, and 30-35% on a consolidated basis. Agro contribution was lower this quarter due to seasonal demand. Standalone gross margin was about 58%, driven mainly by performance materials.

segments.name: Agro
segments.commentary: Management said demand recovery is visible in existing agro products and that agro should be stable, with its share declining as other segments grow faster.

guidance_outlook: Organic revenue growth guided at about 25% plus or minus a few points for FY27, with Jayhawk adding another 10-15% inorganically.
Standalone EBITDA margin guided at 24-26%; consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.
Interest cost expected to stay at the current run rate; no major further capitalisation expected, so depreciation should not rise sharply from new capex.
Standalone capex guided at INR70-80 crore for now (repair, maintenance and repurposing).

Bliss GVS Pharma completion expected in the first half of September 2026, with integration to start after completion. Management targets 60-70% utilisation at Bliss over 2-3 years, versus about 30% currently.
Working capital expected to be stable and then improve, reaching the guided range by year-end FY27.
capex_capacity: Major capex cycle complete; all major planned projects commissioned and operational. Incremental capex to be selective and based on customer visibility.
Standalone capex guided at INR70-80 crore for now, mainly maintenance and repurposing.
ETFA commercialised via flow chemistry, claimed as a first globally; management says it is the only player doing this in flow.
Bliss utilisation about 30% today, targeted at 60-70% over 2-3 years. Bliss has a pipeline of 62 molecules over 2 years, including 48+ aimed at regulated markets (per the CEO's opening remarks).
demand_pricing: ETFA addressable market estimated at about USD0.5 billion across the two molecules; management said initial share of 5-10% and possibly up to 15-30%, without a firm number.
BASQUEVOLT LoI covers a potential long-term supply opportunity of about USD300 million over 10 years, with commercialisation expected in H2 FY27 and meaningful revenue in 2-3 years.
Cumulative signed LOIs and contracts represent roughly INR18,000 crore of potential business over their tenures.
Management expects order-book-linked revenue to be about 25% of revenue this year and about 30% going forward.
Semiconductor revenue is growing fast per management, with Jayhawk's semicon and defence products cited as a contributor. No quantified figures were given.
Bain & Co is supporting the PMO and IMO for Jayhawk-Anupam synergies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the API plant acquisition flagged in the last call?
qa_highlights.answer: Still exploratory with nothing to share. Management will work with Bliss management on any acquisitions once Bliss completes.

qa_highlights.question: Bliss completion timeline and pending approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: SEBI approval received and open offer closed on August 10. Procedural steps remain; completion expected by the first half of September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Jayhawk contribution and margin this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20-22% of revenue (around INR145 crore), with EBITDA margin of 19-20% (around INR30 crore) and PAT of about INR9 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone EBITDA margin 24-26%; consolidated 22-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Anupam fund Jayhawk capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No requirement is foreseen; Jayhawk is well capitalised and unlevered, with only limited repurposing or replacement capex.

qa_highlights.question: How is Bliss funded?
qa_highlights.answer: A fully owned subsidiary will take about INR300 crore of debt, with the balance funded through an equity-linked instrument that Anupam can buy out at any time. Management said Bliss has over INR200 crore of cash flow and no debt, so no large external capital is needed for later API acquisitions.

risks_watch: PAT growth (6%) lagged EBITDA growth (35%) because of depreciation and interest. Jayhawk's depreciation policy is under review and may change the run rate.
Q1 is seasonally weak, and organic growth ex-Jayhawk was single digit this quarter, so the 25% organic guidance needs a strong H2.
Bliss completion depends on procedural steps, and management declined to give Bliss-specific numbers or CDMO timelines before consummation.
HFC-32 quota status for Tanfac was deferred to Tanfac management; no confirmation given on Anupam's side.
Working capital was described as stable and not improving; management expects it to reach the guided range by year-end.
Open-offer acceptance was very small, so the Bliss stake cost is largely fixed.
543275|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, new products and the Bliss and BASQUEVOLT opportunities. Guarded and deferential on Bliss-specific numbers, CDMO and Tanfac HFC-32 quota, citing listed-company constraints until the deal closes. Margin and capex guidance was given with clear numbers.
key_quotes: And to our knowledge, we are the only ones who are able to do it in flow today.
We expect commercialization to begin during FY27 and we'll gradually scale the opportunity based on customer requirement.
So we continue to believe that we should be able to improve the utilization of the company's assets to 60% to 70%, and that would translate to the kind of numbers that are there, that would be there.

532482|2026-09.headline: Granules pivots to four growth engines; plans ~2,000 crore organic capex over 3-4 years after warrant-funded move to net cash.
532482|2026-09.overview: Management, at an IIFL-hosted "Granules India 2.0" webinar, framed FY27 onward as a shift from building capabilities to scaling them, after a return to growth in FY26. Four growth engines were named: controlled substances, complex generics/early market entry, oncology, and peptide CDMO (Senn Tides). The CFO said the company is now in a consolidated net cash position following September 2026 preferential warrant proceeds, and plans about 2,000 crore of organic capex over three to four years. Management was candid that gross margin gains (about 15 pp over four years) have not yet fully flowed to EBITDA, and that the peptide business is currently loss-making. No quarterly financial figures for Q2 FY27 were given in the call.

segments.name: US (anchor market)
segments.commentary: About 75% of overall revenue; currently retail-focused across OTC and Rx, with first specialty/institutional launch expected in FY29 and a B2C division in Canada next year.

segments.name: Controlled substances (US Rx)
segments.commentary: Now the third-largest US controlled substance manufacturer by value per IQVIA (eighth in July 2025). Top-three position in six of seven ADHD products marketed; Adderall XR share rose from 5% (2024) to 29%.

segments.name: Complex generics / first-to-file
segments.commentary: Two sole first-to-file ANDAs filed (generic Lumryz and generic Dyanavel, combined US market above $350 million, potential 180-day exclusivity); four to five further first-to-files planned for FY30-34 commercialisation.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: Shifted from broad conventional oncology generics to selected molecules; two products filed, one extended to about 15 countries; about six more filings planned this year and early next year. Commercialisation begins FY29.

segments.name: Peptide CDMO (Senn Tides India / Senn Chemicals, Switzerland)
segments.commentary: Acquired about 18 months ago; currently EBITDA-negative with target to turn profitable in FY27. Targets about $50 million revenue run-rate in three years and above $100 million in five years. About one-third of about $20 million revenue is development-based.

segments.name: Europe and ROW (API and PFI-led)
segments.commentary: Management plans a meaningful Latin America and other international presence by FY30 using B2B and B2C channels.

up about 3 pp over four years
up from about 3% a few years ago
up about 1 pp YoY; Q1 vs Q1 up about 2 pp

financial_highlights.value: about 4,100-4,200 crore in FY26 (analyst's figure, not disputed)

financial_highlights.metric: One-off costs over last full year
financial_highlights.value: about 100 crore total (about 60 crore USFDA remediation consultancy plus failure-to-supply and air freight)

540497|2026-06.headline: S Chand Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs1,145m, but EBITDA loss of Rs97m and PAT loss of Rs187m widened the reported loss.
540497|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs1,145m, up 12% YoY, with gross margin improved. EBITDA turned to a loss of Rs97m and PAT to a loss of Rs187m, hit by marketing costs pulled into Q1 from Q2 and a one-time tax rate adjustment. Management pre-bought paper ahead of expected price rises, lifting inventory and slightly raising net working capital days. Net cash reached a record Rs1,182m after Rs141m dividend, and FY27 guidance of 10-15% operating revenue growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin was reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Wider loss YoY due to one-time tax rate adjustment
vs Rs1,160m in Q4FY26, after Rs141m dividend

segments.name: School Education (K-12)
segments.commentary: Refreshed curriculum brands Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK and Solid Steps received repeat adoptions; Mylestone (650+ schools) and My Zen (about 500 schools) together generated about Rs55-60 crore in FY26. New partnerships with Allied, Jump Maths, Penguin and Speedlabs added to the offering.

segments.name: Content Licensing
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue of about Rs9 crore (Rs91m); about Rs14 crore booked to date. Target is above Rs40 crore for FY27 and growing active clients from 5 to 10.

segments.name: International (CPD Singapore, acquired)
segments.commentary: Q1 contribution about Rs1 crore; target of SGD 1m (about Rs7.5 crore) by year end. Management says it was profitable earlier, currently investing in content and marketing with limited burn; India and Middle East K-12 expansion will take 1-2 academic cycles.

guidance_outlook: Operating revenue growth of 10-15% for FY27.
EBITDA margin guidance of 17-19% for FY27, stated to include a 10-12% paper price increase assumption.
Content licensing revenue target above Rs40 crore in FY27.
Market buyback under consideration; management expects a decision by October 2026, contingent on acquisitions progressing.
Acquisitions under discussion in test prep and school spaces, total size about Rs40-50 crore at most.
Steady-state growth for core business of 10-12% over the next 2-3 years, excluding acquisitions and new segments.
Full adoption of NCERT new-syllabus books expected in FY27; West Bengal new syllabus expected to support growth for about 2 years from next year.
capex_capacity: New printing and binding facility: half to be completed in FY27, full completion in FY28; partial binding and printing to start from the following week, with operations in September-October 2026.
Management says the facility covers requirements for 10-15 years and should improve productivity, quality and output speed.
demand_pricing: Dollar rate cited at about Rs95 versus about Rs85 a year earlier, raising imported paper cost along with logistics and Middle East tensions.
Paper availability is not a constraint; management says the issue is price. About 20-25% of annual paper requirement purchased so far, roughly 3-4 months earlier than usual.
Receivable days stable; collections from the Middle East are being hit by geopolitical instability and are expected to normalise.
Management is cautious on paper inventory due to space and cash limits, so it will not buy the full annual requirement.
Regional board growth (Chhaya Prakashani) was lumpy in FY26 due to West Bengal elections shifting sales into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company buy paper early and where are paper prices heading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pre-bought to hedge against higher USD-linked import costs, logistics and Middle East tensions; paper prices may firm up next quarter. About 25% of annual consumption bought, versus the usual August-October purchase window.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 17-19% margin guidance inclusive of paper price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Guidance assumes a 10-12% paper price increase; management said a 40% rise would be a different case.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of buyback and acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: A market buyback is being considered, with a decision targeted by October once acquisitions progress. Two acquisition discussions in test prep and school space, total size Rs40-50 crore at most.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state growth outlook beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Core business steady state is 10-12%, built from 3-4% student growth, 4-5% volume and 4-5% pricing; acquisitions or new segments would add to this.

qa_highlights.question: Will goodwill be revalued or impaired?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not impair now because the acquired investments have intrinsic value. Impairment may be considered in a year with exceptional income, such as a real estate sale or Smartivity listing.

risks_watch: Paper cost inflation versus the 10-12% assumed in the 17-19% margin guidance; further USD-INR weakness or freight disruption would pressure margins.
Working capital: higher inventory from early paper purchases and Middle East collection delays; cash deployment on paper versus buyback.
Q1 EBITDA loss partly reflects marketing timing (Q2 costs in Q1), so the Q2 margin needs watching.
Content licensing must scale from about Rs14 crore to above Rs40 crore; contracts not yet signed.
Large goodwill on the balance sheet weighs on return ratios; no impairment or revaluation planned near term.
Buyback decision and acquisition progress, targeted for October 2026.
540497|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the core K-12 franchise and content licensing, but cautious on paper prices and working capital. Management was non-committal on the timing of the buyback and on content licensing contracts, and deflected goodwill questions.
key_quotes: We took a conscious decision to advance Paper purchases since we are pre -empting higher paper prices, supply disruptions and elongated shipping timelines for imported paper.
The steady state is again 10% to 12%, for the core business.

523642|2026-06.headline: PI Industries Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 17,023 million with 57% gross margin and 22% EBITDA margin; FY27 growth guided to lower single digit.
523642|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 17,023 million with gross margin of 57% and EBITDA of Rs 3,693 million (22% margin), amid soft exports and cyclical domestic headwinds. Exports saw volume down 8% and value down 12% YoY, while domestic volume grew 12% but revenue only 3%. Subsidiary losses, driven by global biologicals and pharma ramp-up, were about Rs 100 crore at EBITDA level in the quarter. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth in the lower single digits and expects FY27 to beat FY26 on an export recovery in the second half.

financial_highlights.value: Reduced by 19 days, releasing Rs 300 crore cash

segments.name: Agchem exports (CSM)
segments.commentary: Export volume down 8% and value down 12% YoY; new products contributed 16-18% of CSM revenue in Q1. Management cited soft commodity prices, genericization and tariffs as pressures.

segments.name: Domestic agri
segments.commentary: Volume up 12% but revenue up only 3%, reflecting price pressure; management said it prioritised market share over price. Flagship brands include Nominee Gold, Brofreya and Biovita.

segments.name: Biologicals
segments.commentary: Grew 50% with a three-year CAGR of 15%; global biologicals are loss-making due to market development spend (1,000+ grower engagements, 500+ field trials).

segments.name: Pharma / CRDMO
segments.commentary: Platform across Jaipur, Hyderabad and Lodi (Italy); some orders delayed to later quarters. Management described a long J-curve; company does not disclose molecule names.

segments.name: Electronic and specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: A commercial plant is operational and commercial supplies have started; management said the segment is not yet substantial in revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to lower single digit, contingent on cycle.
FY27 expected to be better than FY26, driven by export recovery in H2, new launches and scale-up of pharma and global biologicals.
FY27 capex guidance of Rs 700-800 crore; Q1 capex about Rs 250 crore.
ETR for FY27 around 24%.
R&D spend kept at 3-4% of revenue.
Pioxaniliprole (first NCE) expected domestic launch within FY27 pending regulatory approval; other geographies in later years.
Gross margin target to be maintained via optimisation; management gave no explicit EBITDA margin guidance.
capex_capacity: Capex for Q1 about Rs 250-260 crore, spread across existing manufacturing, new verticals and innovation-led geographies/products.
Commissioned one of the world's largest flow chemistry plants.
Commercial plant for electronic chemicals is operational.
QC lab commissioned at Italy (Lodi) site, approved by regulators.
Centre of excellence for drug discovery at Hyderabad CRO facility.
demand_pricing: Management said global crop protection demand is showing early signs of stabilisation, but pricing pressure remains from weak demand and high input costs.
Domestic sowing said to be at par with last year after delays; chemical pre-placement and sales were affected.
Management said price escalation was mainly in generics, while PI focused on market share.
Export pricing and growth pressured by soft commodity prices, genericization pressures and tariffs.
Brazil nematicide market about USD 750 million; company aims for double-digit share over 5-10 years.
Global biologicals market about USD 10 billion, growing double digits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated lower single-digit growth and a positive trajectory, depending on the cycle.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be viewed through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to sustain gross margins at the best possible levels through optimisation; it did not give an EBITDA margin figure.

qa_highlights.question: When will Pioxaniliprole launch?
qa_highlights.answer: Early start expected this year and India launch within the year, subject to regulatory approvals; other geographies planned for next year and the year after.

qa_highlights.question: Why did currency benefits not reflect in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said currency benefits are shared with customers under a pass-through model, with some currency risk management, and margins are managed at an optimal level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidiary loss and when does it break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses reflect front-loaded investment in pharma and global biologicals (market development, human resources); management gave no breakeven timeline and said it would try to provide quarterly biologicals numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the pharma guidance intact after order delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said delays are sequential timing shifts from new customers and products; it did not quantify the delay.

risks_watch: Export volume decline (-8%) and value decline (-12%) despite rupee depreciation of around 13% YoY, with management giving limited explanation of the gap.
Subsidiary losses of around Rs 100 crore EBITDA in Q1 from biologicals and pharma; no breakeven timeline given.
Pricing pressure in domestic agri and exports, plus input cost and inventory overhangs.
Pharma order delays and high volatility in CRDMO revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 PAT margin meet the 16-18% guidance?

544418|2026-06.headline: Oswal Pumps Q1 FY27 revenue fell 7.9% YoY to INR474 crore and operating EBITDA margin dropped to 15.7%, while FY27 guidance of 20-25% growth was maintained.

vs ~40,400 in Q4 FY26 and ~56,000 in Q1 FY26

segments.commentary: Order book ~72 MW with 359 MW pipeline. Dedicated PM Surya Ghar vertical formed; internal target of ~2 lakh installations in FY27, implying INR800-1,000 crore revenue per management. Negligible contribution in Q1; expected to start from Q2.

segments.commentary: Management expects INR70-100 crore revenue from wires and cables this year, using existing in-house spare capacity with no significant capex; margins expected to be below KUSUM pumps.

Raw material and copper price volatility; management said any rise would affect the whole industry.
Execution of PM Surya Ghar 2 lakh installation target and inverter in-house timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-30% revenue growth guidance range, and what is the trend in new customers?

qa_highlights.question: Is the PTL yield increase seasonal or sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Why does the NBFC (asset-light lending) plan matter?

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT difference between the press release and reported figures (Rs.62 Cr vs Rs.32 Cr vs Rs.17 Cr)?

qa_highlights.question: Why did SCS margins decline and what is the new-contract economics?

qa_highlights.question: Is Delhivery exposed to competition from in-house or 3PL consolidation?

540203|2026-06.headline: Sheela Foam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA 45% to INR109 crore, with margin at 10.6%.
540203|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA rose 45% to INR109 crore, with margin up 139 bps to 10.6%. Management reiterated a 15% EBITDA margin target for next year and expects volumes to recover in the festive quarters.

segments.name: India mattresses

segments.name: India foam
segments.commentary: Value up 26% and volume up 4% YoY; faster foam growth diluted gross margin but was cash-accretive as competitors lacked raw material.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand.com sales up 69% YoY, platforms up 19%; overall category up 30% with volumes up 23%.

segments.name: Staqo (IT)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 67% YoY with EBITDA margin around 28-30%; Presence 360 crossed 3.2 lakh users.

segments.name: Furlenco (associate)
segments.commentary: Operating profit roughly INR9 crore per quarter; Q1 PAT share reflects 35% stake and no deferred tax asset recognition (DTA only booked at year end, likely Q4).

guidance_outlook: Reiterated 15% EBITDA margin target for next year; management said there is no change to this stance, though Rachna Kukreja's question suggested earlier 11-12% FY27 guidance.
Expects more than 15% revenue growth for the full year and double-digit volume growth in both foam and mattresses for FY27.

International operations to grow about 5% in local currency with 10-12% EBITDA margins; for FY27, management is confident of crossing INR1,000 crore revenue and about INR120 crore EBITDA for overseas operations.
Synergy benefit of about INR40 crore still pending; machine under installation, with full impact expected in Q3.

Standalone synergy-related machine under installation, expected to deliver full impact in Q3.
Operating units reduced from 21 to 12 as part of Kurlon integration.
demand_pricing: Standalone India volume growth about 6%; management views sub-10% as satisfactory and says industry grew close to 5%.

Organised mattress market combined share of Sleepwell and Kurlon close to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone volume growth slow to single digits and margins fall?

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% EBITDA margin target and 13-14% FY28 guidance hold?

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and rollout of company-owned stores?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kurlon integration status and synergy realisation?

544865|2026-06.headline: LEAP India Q1 FY27 total income rose 19% to INR2,134 million, EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million at a 53.5% margin.

PAT rose 30% to INR247 million (12% margin) and cash PAT rose 23% to about INR812 million. Management reported 48 new customers in the quarter against a normal 15-20, asset count of 14.9 million, and utilisation up to 89.2%. Capex slowed to INR76 million-equivalent (stated as INR76 crores) from INR110 crores a year earlier as raw-material inflation made new crate and pallet purchases less attractive.

qa_highlights.question: Asset growth was 9% but revenue rose 19%; how is the growth split between asset growth and throughput?

qa_highlights.question: Can you guide to EBITDA margins for the rest of the year?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ revenue growth on a YoY basis and is Middle East additive?

539889|2026-06.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR945 crores (record Q1), but EBITDA margin slipped to 7.4% from 7.7% and PAT fell 20%.
539889|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached a record INR945 crores, up 11% YoY in value and 3% in volume. EBITDA grew 6% to INR70 crores, with margin down 30 bps to 7.4%; PBT was broadly flat and PAT fell 20% on higher current tax. Gross profit rose 11% to INR258 crores with gross margin stable at about 27.3%, which management attributed to calibrated pricing and mix. Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi; 61% of revenue) saw volume fall 2% YoY, with B2C growing and B2B declining modestly; new-age business (Pride of Cows and Avvatar) grew 59% and reached about 13% of revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY; gross margin stable (27.3% vs 28% in Q4 FY26 per call)

segments.name: Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi)

segments.name: New-age business (Pride of Cows, Avvatar)
segments.commentary: Grew 59% YoY, about 13% of revenue vs 9% a year earlier. Portfolio expanded into protein bars, ready-to-drink (RTD) coffee with 15 g protein per serving (launched Q1), creatine. Management said new-age margins are roughly double the company average, without giving a figure.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Down 46% YoY per analyst question; management said this reflects PSI and state incentive income falling after GST cut on ghee and cheese from 12% to 5% in September 2025, plus dahi moving into flagship. UHT and beverages performed reasonably well.

Calibrated price increases will continue in response to commodity costs; ghee prices were raised late in Q1 and new-age prices were revisited recently.
Milk prices described as stable; slight increase possible in coming months due to monsoon-linked seasonality and festive demand.
Distribution target of more than 1.5 million outlets within three years.

demand_pricing: Whey protein prices reportedly moved from about INR2,500/kg to about INR3,400/kg recently; management said global whey demand is structural, not temporary.
Management said Avvatar retail prices rose only in stages, not 100% as an analyst suggested; consumers switch between protein formats as prices change.
Q1 B2B volumes were deliberately forgone where customers negotiated hard on pricing, to protect margins.
Avvatar sales are 75% via quick commerce, e-commerce and website, and 25% via traditional retail and specialised protein outlets.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth break the roughly 10% sales growth band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will exceed 10%, with Q2 and Q3 festive quarters expected to drive it; Q1 is seasonally weak.

qa_highlights.question: How is Avvatar up 59% when retail prices reportedly doubled?

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin flat despite mix improvement and price hikes?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Samay Raina / India's Got Latent deal's cost and ROI?

qa_highlights.question: Is Avvatar's whey price rise a margin hit given backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost of production per kg or margin impact by product, saying margins are reported on a blended basis.

Milk price stability versus monsoon and festive demand pressure, and dependence on price hikes for pass-through.

532662|2026-06.headline: HT Media Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR 497 crore and EBITDA nearly tripled to INR 90 crore, while a preferential issue drew shareholder pushback.
532662|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY to INR 497 crore, with EBITDA up nearly 3x to INR 90 crore (margin up about 12 points) and PAT of INR 47 crore (9% margin). Print drove growth, with advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, and management credited yield improvement. Digital operating revenue fell about 28% with EBITDA of negative INR 3 crore, as the portfolio was deliberately reset, and Radio was flat with negative INR 3 crore EBITDA after surrendering licences for non-viable stations. The board approved a preferential issue of equity to HT Media and Digicontent Ltd (not HMVL), priced at the SEBI formula (around INR 24-25 per share), which drew sharp objections from minority shareholders on dilution and pricing.

segments.name: Hindi Print
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue rose YoY to INR 139 crore; circulation revenue flat.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Topline flat YoY; operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore. Licences surrendered for certain non-viable stations.

segments.name: Digital

Newsprint (25-40% of print bill of materials) at about USD 650-700 per tonne is the highest since COVID; management believes prices have peaked and will plateau before easing, but acknowledged no forward market exists.
Q2 newsprint expected slightly higher than Q1; Q1 Print margin of about 13% offered as a modelling baseline, with downside if dollar and newsprint rise further.
Preferential issue proceeds to retire 30-50% of the debt at HT Media and Digicontent; management says it is EPS-accretive and will improve interest coverage and credit rating.

capex_capacity: Preferential issue at HT Media and Digicontent Ltd (DCL), priced on the SEBI formula (higher of 10-day or 90-day VWAP); promoters subscribing on the same terms, up to their regulatory maximum; ongoing vote, with a shareholder voting against.
Radio footprint reduced by surrendering licences for non-viable stations.
