HMVL cash (where most of the INR 922 crore net cash sits) to be deployed at HMVL board's discretion; no preferential issue at HMVL.
demand_pricing: Commercial print revenue held on volume with yield improvement as the main driver; government revenue grew on both volume and the November 2025 rate increase.

Cover price hikes seen as difficult: Hindi papers are already well priced and prior commodity-driven hikes were taken.
Circulation held steady market by market to protect copy share in English markets.
Other operating income at HMVL roughly doubled to about INR 20 crore (from about INR 10 crore), mainly job work and scrap sales.
Competitive environment described as likely to remain as is for circulation.

qa_highlights.question: Why use a preferential issue at about INR 24 per share, below book value of about INR 70, rather than a rights issue, given INR 922 crore net cash and a 15% dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all the net cash sits in HMVL, while HT Media and DCL are net debt companies. Preferential issue is faster (2-3 months), gives more certainty of raising the amount and avoids underwriter risk; pricing follows the SEBI formula with no premium. Proceeds will retire 30-50% of debt.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 15% dilution, the valuation and the moral/reputational issue, will the company withdraw the preferential issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not agree to withdraw. It said price-to-book is below 0.5x, the promoters are subscribing on the same terms, and it is raising capital to retire debt and improve EPS. A shareholder said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the debt position consistent with earlier statements that the company was debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt has built up at HT Media over the last 3-4 years post-COVID (Print English and Radio); the combined net cash figure hides this, and the number is not new.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of HMVL's other income jump, and is it MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury gains from mutual funds (NAV-based) plus realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on investments. Treasury gains depend on yield curve movements and are not predictable.

qa_highlights.question: How will newsprint costs affect Print margins, and can prices be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Newsprint is 25-40% of the bill of materials. Management expects a plateau at current levels, so Q1 Print margin of about 13% can be used as a baseline if prices don't rise further; cover price increases are difficult.

qa_highlights.question: What drove ad revenue growth at Print, and what share is government revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly commercial yield improvement with volumes holding; government revenue grew on volume and pricing. Management did not disclose the government share and called it 'substantial' but smaller than commercial.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR323 crore (+7%), EBIT INR27 crore (+19%), EBIT margin 8.4%; management also cited EBITDA margin of 10.8% (+250 bps).

segments.name: Chemicals (India Glycols)
segments.commentary: Chemicals revenue INR332 crore (+25%) at 11.4% EBITDA margin; small gases INR13 crore at 23.1% margin. Glycols value up 83%; green solvents and glycol ethers volume +6%, value +13%, gross margin close to 50%. Performance chemicals grew 40%, below target.

segments.name: Ennature Bio Pharma
segments.commentary: Best-ever quarter at INR83 crore revenue (per call) / INR90 crore net revenue under new structure, up 53-65%; EBITDA up ~188% per the prepared remarks. Nicotine sales doubled QoQ on European customer conversions; thiocolchicoside up 26% QoQ.

segments.name: Clariant JV (Kashipur)
segments.commentary: JV net revenue up 21% QoQ with EBITDA up in high double digits QoQ; JV profit cited at about INR21 crore versus about INR19 crore a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: IGL Spirits: EBITDA above INR500 crore for FY27 (INR120 crore already delivered in Q1); IMFL volume to roughly double versus FY26 (FY26 IMFL volume 3.4 million cases).
Spirits: management expects healthy double-digit growth in FY28 and aims to be debt-free from FY28; target EBITDA above INR1,000 crore in four to five years.

Chemicals aspiration (explicitly not a projection): EBITDA about INR400 crore and revenue about INR2,500 crore in four to five years; FY27 revenue aspiration INR150 crore-plus for the new performance chemicals business; margin targeted to rise toward 30% gross margin.
Ennature aspiration: EBITDA INR130-150 crore over the next four to five years.
Capex in chemicals expected to be small: INR5-20 crore incremental in the current year; no INR400-500 crore plant expected for at least two years.
capex_capacity: Chemicals capex plans: incremental INR5-10 crore, possibly up to INR15-20 crore this year, via modular expansion; new plant additions to date about INR50-60 crore.
Ennature started nicotine crude processing at its Kashipur plant, adding capacity.
Spirits: captive ENA capacity described as sufficient, supporting cost advantage in UP, Uttarakhand and Delhi.

Demerger: after effectiveness, Spirits, Bio-Fuel and Bio Pharma undertakings transfer to dedicated resulting companies; IGL Spirits will hold potable spirits, Bio-Fuel and biopolymers; Ennature retains nutraceuticals and APIs. Effective date not yet communicated.
demand_pricing: Spirits: management says the industry grew at a 4-5% CAGR over the last one to two years; IMFL growth attributed to launches in deluxe whisky, semi-premium vodka and white spirits. Prestige & Above volume ~0.5 million cases, roughly double last year.
Mix: revenue lagged volume in Spirits because of state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium grew faster).

Chemicals: ethylene oxide became similar to or slightly cheaper than Reliance's EO for a few months, increasing specialty chemicals off-take. Oil and gas and Middle East exports were hit by propylene oxide shortages and freight volatility (westbound freight up 5-20x).
Ennature: raw material availability and pricing volatile and a challenge in Q2 as well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guidance for potable spirits for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA above INR500 crore, with INR120 crore delivered in Q1; volume to double versus last year, with healthy double-digit growth expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the NSU (chemicals) business and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex limited to about INR5-20 crore this year; cumulative new plant investment about INR50-60 crore. Aspiration of INR150 crore-plus revenue this year and INR600-700 crore in 4-5 years, with margins improving over time.

qa_highlights.question: Are JV profits sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a fair assumption; JV PAT about INR19 crore a year ago versus INR21 crore now, with the improvement linked to narrower EO cost disadvantage.

qa_highlights.question: Prestige & Above volumes and IMFL revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: P&A about 0.5 million cases, roughly double last year. FY26 IMFL volume was 3.4 million cases; FY26 IMFL revenue was not disclosed and will be sent later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes grow faster than revenue in Spirits?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium growing faster); revenue growth expected to exceed volume growth as premium mix rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IMFL margin versus country liquor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins in deluxe and semi-premium whisky are almost the same as in P&A and did not give separate EBITDA margins.

544748|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 129% YoY to INR 158.3 crore, driven by first full quarter of Netcom BCC, with EBITDA margin at 24.9%.
544748|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full reporting period consolidating Netcom BCC, lifting consolidated revenue to INR 158.3 crore (up 64.6% QoQ, 129% YoY) and EBITDA to INR 39.4 crore (24.9% margin). Profit for the period rose to INR 16.3 crore, with basic EPS of 0.62 versus 0.36 a year ago. Finance cost rose to INR 8.1 crore from INR 1.9 crore, tied to acquisition borrowing. Management positioned the company as moving from capacity-led outsourcing toward outcome-based AI orchestration through its ResolX platform, while the standalone base business grew 11.6% YoY.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1.9 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.value: ~50% of revenue and ~50% of EBITDA; Netcom margin ~24-25%

segments.name: Global human service engine (incl. Netcom BCC)
segments.commentary: Netcom fully consolidated this quarter, deepening Americas presence; contributes roughly half of consolidated revenue and EBITDA at ~24-25% margin.

segments.name: Base business (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue INR 61.1 crore, up 11.6% YoY, at 30.4% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Agentic AI engine (ResolX)
segments.commentary: Launched May 2026; 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients. Revenue described as only just starting to catch up; management expects meaningful revenue in 12-18 months or slightly more.

guidance_outlook: Management said the company should be able to roughly double revenue this year, while acknowledging this was not a one-off quarter.
Management expects EBITDA margins to improve progressively over the coming year as the revenue mix shifts to AI orchestration and outcome-linked models.
Cash generation expected to rise in coming quarters, making debt servicing easier; no equity raise indicated.
Management intends to acquire two more companies over the next three years, targeting firms with Fortune 500 clients in North America.
AI-led revenue expected to show up in quarterly numbers over the coming 12-18 months.
capex_capacity: Netcom BCC acquisition debt carries an effective cost of around 9%; management said total debt is about INR 220 crore and a repayment schedule is planned.

ResolX platform: 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients (insurance, aviation, banking, automotive, digital assets), including two Central American banks; management said about 6-7 of 12 projects were deployed as of the call.
Management plans roughly 40-plus bots for one Indian insurance client across languages and its 7-8 products.
Management said capacity is not a constraint, with AI expected to free room in accounts for additional work.
demand_pricing: Management expects growth from India and LATAM, with the Americas growing on dollar arbitrage; banking is the leading vertical, with some insurance, healthcare, travel and hospitality.
AI deflection to humans reported at roughly 30-40% depending on use case; one airline deployment cited about 30% of employee-size benefit.
Management claims the company is the only Indian BPO with in-house domain, tech stack and Agentic AI capabilities; other BPOs described as relying on third-party AI.
Conversion rate on active deal pipeline stated at around 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the current quarter's run rate one-off or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not one-off, as this is the first quarter with full Netcom consolidation, and it expects revenue to roughly double this year.

qa_highlights.question: Split of revenue and EBITDA between Netcom and base business, and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Netcom contributes about 50% of revenue and about 50% of EBITDA, with margins of 24-25%, similar to group margin.

qa_highlights.question: Plan for INR 220 crore debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash earnings will rise, debt servicing will get easier, and repayment is planned; the company is described as debt-free apart from Netcom acquisition borrowing at about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Does ResolX/Agentic AI generate savings or margin lift yet?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin benefit is visible in a few projects but is too small to be noticeable yet; deflection to humans is about 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Singapore acquisition and revenue there?
qa_highlights.answer: The Singapore company acquired in 2025 served as the platform later relaunched as ResolX; there is no current revenue in Singapore, with small revenues in the Middle East, Europe, LATAM and India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended cost of debt, and acquisition criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt sits mainly with Netcom at about 9%. Acquisition screen is EPS accretion first, then North American customer access; management said margin accretion is immediate.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and monetisation of resolution-based model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said resolution cost is measured by time and motion across channels, and that single-owner end-to-end handling shortens interactions (e.g. 5 minutes to 2 minutes).

risks_watch: Margin progression: consolidated EBITDA margin 24.9% is below standalone 30.4%, due to Netcom mix; AI-driven margin uplift is still small.
AI revenue timing: management guided to 12-18 months or longer before AI revenue is meaningful.
Debt of about INR 220 crore at ~9% cost on Netcom acquisition; finance cost rose to INR 8.1 crore.
Management's claim of unique positioning and high 10-12% deal conversion has not been independently verified.
Revenue doubling target for FY27 relies on Netcom consolidation plus new customer ramp-ups.
544748|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the ResolX/Agentic AI narrative and growth trajectory, but vague or evasive on AI-driven margin and revenue quantification, which management repeatedly deferred to future quarters. Some answers on competition and differentiation were assertive without supporting data.
key_quotes: Today, I can say that we are the only ones who exist in India who have the domain plus tech stack plus Agentic AI capabilities, which is truly born within the organization.
We are not in the business of creating LLMs, which is your Large Language Models. What we are in the business is on what sits on top of an LLM.

524494|2026-06.headline: Ipca Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 21% to INR2,788 crores and EBITDA margin reached 22.88%; FY27 growth guidance raised to 14-16%.
524494|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 21% YoY to INR2,788 crores, with consolidated EBITDA of INR638 crores (22.88% margin) versus INR425 crores (18.39%) a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA rose about 34% to INR557 crores. Management raised FY27 guidance: revenue growth to 14-16% (from 12-13%) and consolidated EBITDA margin to around 23% (from around 22%). Exports (+34%), domestic formulations (+13%) and institutional generics (+107%, helped by about INR40 crores of shipments slipping from March to April) drove the quarter. Management said margin gains came mainly from lower personnel and manufacturing costs as a share of sales, not material savings.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR425 crores, 18.39% in Q1 FY26 (+4.49 pp)

financial_highlights.value: about INR193 crores; zero short-term borrowings
financial_highlights.change: Dollar loans of about USD50 million fully repaid

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,082 crores, +13%; IQVIA-tracked growth about 11.7%, chronic +17.2% and acute +8.9%. Market share about 2.08%, rank about 16. Antimalarials fell about 24% and are now about 1% of business.

segments.name: Exports / ROW branded
segments.commentary: Export business about INR603 crores (+34%). Promotional branded ROW about INR143 crores (+16%from INR124 crores).

segments.name: Europe / UK generics
segments.commentary: European business up about 70%, from INR33 crores to INR137 crores, the main growth driver. US shipments up about 8%; Canada saw a minor decline.

segments.name: Unichem (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: US business up about 27%, with Ipca-portfolio sales to Unichem up about 37% and Unichem's own portfolio up about 9%. Brazil up about 52%. Unichem API rose from about INR33-34 crores to about INR58 crores.

segments.name: Lyka Labs (associate)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat and EBITDA reported negative. Management cited animal health, critical care and IVF as growth areas, with some divisions still below breakeven.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth raised to 14-16% from 12-13%.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin raised to around 23% from around 22%.
Institutional business to grow in single digits, with annual sales of about INR260-300 crores.
Unichem guidance (10% portfolio growth, 13% EBITDA margin) not revised yet; to be reviewed after more quarters.
FY28 guidance to be given with Q4 results.
Medium term: Ipca standalone margin could reach about 30% and consolidated margin about 25-26% in 2-3 years.
Long-run US growth of about 15-17% seen as possible.
FY27 capex of about INR700-800 crores; about INR100 crores extra for biotech pilot facilities and R&D.
capex_capacity: Pithampur: capacity additions for controlled-release and extended-release formulations under way.
API: new plants at Dewas and Wardha (intermediates) as Ratlam runs out of capacity; continuous-process conversions of existing intermediates.
Biotech: about 7 candidates in pipeline and capacity for 3-4 products a year; 2 products at engineering-batch stage, with results in line with expectations.
Sales force of about 7,000 medical reps; about 200 more to be added mid-year for new divisions.
demand_pricing: Domestic growth split: volume about 5%, price about 4.5-5%, new launches about 2%.
Management said there are no price renegotiations downward; prices are rising because costs are rising.

Freight costs rose sharply: South America containers from about USD3,000 to USD9,000-10,000; US from about 7,000-7,500 to 12,500-13,000; Europe from 3,000 to about 5,500. Container availability is also constrained.
Rupee depreciation (dollar up about 11% YoY) added about 5 pp to the 21% revenue growth; about 25% of that benefit was offset by higher material cost.
Materials cost moved up about 21%, in line with sales; management said material cost to sales would fall slightly relative to sales growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did acute underperform, and what is the India outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed underperformance, citing IPM growth of 4.5% vs Ipca's 8.9% acute growth. Antimalarials fell about 24%. Pain management grew about 13%, CV and diabetes about 17%, CNS about 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 12-13% guidance hold, and what is the institutional outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was raised to 14-16%. Institutional growth is expected to be single digit, since the Q1 spike was largely about INR40 crores of delayed shipments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the US launch plans, and can growth reach 20-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3-4 Ipca launches and 7-8 combined Ipca and Unichem launches a year. Mid-teens growth (15-17%) is possible; source-change approvals are progressing.

qa_highlights.question: Will material cost pressure hit margins in the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: No margin pressure expected; material cost should fall slightly relative to sales. Q1 margin gains came mainly from personnel and manufacturing cost ratios.

qa_highlights.question: Is rupee depreciation or price renegotiation affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices are rising, not being renegotiated down. FX adds to revenue and is partly offset by dollar-linked costs such as freight, testing, salaries and non-trading offices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and interest position?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt about INR193 crores with a INR70 crore term loan at year-end, repaid next year. No short-term borrowings. Interest cost to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: Where will margins settle over 2-3 years, and what are the biotech plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated margin about 25-26% in 2-3 years, with Ipca standalone up to about 30%. About 7 biosimilar candidates, mostly off-patent. Clinical revenue expected in FY29-30.

risks_watch: Freight and container availability: rates up about 3x and still rising in July-August; South America is hardest hit.
Malaria decline (about 24%) and institutional shipment timing, which can swing quarterly growth.
Unichem margin and guidance are not yet revised; Europe approvals take about 1.5 years after filing.
Biotech and biosimilar spending (about INR100 crores this year) could weigh on EBITDA before revenue arrives in FY29-30.
FY28 guidance is pending until Q4; rupee moves affect both revenue and dollar-linked costs.

542857|2026-06.headline: Greenpanel Q1 FY27 combined revenue rose 8.5% to INR350 crore and EBITDA turned positive at INR32.5 crore, but exports fell to zero and OEM volumes degrew 14%.
542857|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 8.5% YoY to INR350 crore on a combined basis, with MDF operating EBITDA margin at 10.3% versus 4.4% a year earlier. Price hikes of around 15% taken in April were largely rolled back by peers through May to July, so realisations are now close to pre-hike levels. Exports fell to zero and OEM sales degrew 14%, while domestic MDF volumes grew 12% YoY and retail MDF grew about 20%. Management declined to give margin or utilisation guidance, citing daily chemical cost and discount volatility.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated operating EBITDA (ex-euro ECB currency impact)

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR12.4 crore in Q1 FY26
from INR353 crore at start of quarter

financial_highlights.value: INR2.5 crore overall, INR1.8 crore on ECB

segments.name: MDF (retail)
segments.commentary: Retail MDF grew about 20% YoY and domestic MDF volumes grew 12% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of domestic volume growth. Retail is about 75-80% of the mix.

segments.name: MDF (OEM)
segments.commentary: OEM sales degrew 14% YoY after management chose not to supply at discounted prices during the chemical shortage; OEM is about 20-25% of mix.

segments.name: MDF (exports)
segments.commentary: Exports fell to zero in Q1 as freight rose from about $400-500 to $5,500-6,000 per container; Middle East made up about 80-85% of past exports and remains effectively shut, with July and August exports negligible.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Volumes +10.4% YoY and revenue +5% YoY; around 5% price hike taken in Q1, with only a small part passed on as schemes. Management said QoQ plywood margin fell from 7.5% to 2.7% on product mix and higher fixed costs.

guidance_outlook: No quantitative margin or capacity utilisation guidance given; management cited chemical cost and discount volatility.
Management aims to ramp domestic volumes over the remaining nine months to improve full-year market share versus peers.
Management said the objective is to maintain Q1 margins, with possible lag in passing on any future price hikes.
Management expects pricing and demand pressure to persist through FY27, with improvement hoped for in FY28.
Management said double-digit MDF margins are not a very tough ask if volumes and utilisation rise; current utilisation is about 50-60%.
No MDF growth capex needed for 18-24 months beyond maintenance; plywood capacity to rise 30-40% via minimal debottlenecking investment.
capex_capacity: MDF utilisation is around 50-60% (cited as about 51% in Q&A); management intends to enhance utilisation this year, subject to market volumes and exports.
Action has a new line coming in South India and another continuous press is coming up in Madhya Pradesh.
Plywood: plan to fully utilise current capacity, then add machinery in existing facility at minimal investment to lift output 30-40%.
Maintenance shutdown: 5-7 day line shutdown taken this quarter due to lack of orders; management prefers splitting maintenance into short shutdowns rather than a 15-day stop.
Working capital up 4 days QoQ on higher finished goods and timber inventory for seasonality, but still 5 days leaner YoY.
demand_pricing: Peers rolled back the approximately 15% April price hike in phases through May, June and July; management said almost all of the hike is now rolled back, with 1-2% retained in some segments and markets.
Management said the company now prices OEMs at par with peers rather than at a premium to Century, to regain OEM volumes.
Channel partners are holding inventory on a hand-to-mouth basis, with destocking in Q1 and expected to persist given volatile prices.

Management estimates industry growth at mid-teens in the prior quarter; Arun Baid noted Greenpanel had the lowest industry growth in India this quarter and Century has out-volumed Greenpanel for two quarters.
Chemical costs are about 4-5% above pre-war levels and rising again; timber costs are stable, and mixed wood is being used in place of eucalyptus.
Q1 cost savings from timber and efficiencies were about 6-7% combined, and low-cost inventory from last fiscal helped gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company diversify export markets given the drop in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is exploring other markets, but freight volatility and foreign manufacturing make it hard to compete; alternative markets cannot replace lost Middle East volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7.4% ASP increase due to channel mix shift to retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly. A large part came from removing OEM discounts, so OEM sales came through at near retail prices, shifting mix toward retail price levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not the price maker as market leader?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids undercutting and does not lead on rollbacks, but takes the lead on hikes; averaging out export pricing into the domestic market would have triggered further price cuts.

qa_highlights.question: Why has market share been lost and what is the game plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 OEM sales were intentionally held back during chemical shortage; the company now plans to price at par with peers and focus on volume and utilisation, with the aim of regaining share from Q2 FY27 on a smaller base.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained if raw material costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to maintain Q1 margins; if chemical costs rise again, the industry may take another price hike, with some lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth capex planned over the next 18-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: No MDF capex beyond maintenance; a small plywood debottlenecking investment to add 30-40% output.

risks_watch: Export recovery depends on Middle East normalisation and freight rates, currently $5,500-6,000 per container versus $400-500 before.
Chemical cost volatility and competitor discounting could force further price rollbacks or hikes; the Q1 margin gain may not persist.
Market share loss versus Century and rising capacity from Action (South India) and a new Madhya Pradesh line could keep pricing under pressure through FY27.
Channel destocking and hand-to-mouth buying may keep Q2 volumes below run-rate.
Forex loss of INR2.5 crore on the euro ECB, and plywood margin decline to 2.7% QoQ.
542857|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term guidance, citing daily chemical and discount volatility, but confident on the structural case for margin recovery through volume and utilisation. Management was defensive when pressed on market share loss and on why it did not act as price leader.

522163|2026-06.headline: Diamond Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 129% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT rose 191% to INR58.5 crores, with FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crores.
522163|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR690 crores (up 129% YoY), EBITDA INR85 crores (12.3% margin, up ~200 bps) and PAT INR58.5 crores (8.5% margin). Management attributed the quarter's softness versus a normal Q1 to early, heavy monsoon flooding in Gujarat that hit medium and extra high voltage cable laying. The company completed a INR1,640 crore QIP (net INR1,614 crore), turning net worth positive at INR691 crore post-QIP from negative INR922 crore at June 30, 2026. Order book stood at INR3,688 crore as on August 11, 2026, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,300–4,500 crore and FY28 of INR7,500 crore.

financial_highlights.value: Negative INR922 crore at 30 Jun 2026; positive INR691 crore post-QIP
INR1,640 crore gross (INR1,614 crore net per Q&A)
INR3,688 crore as on 11 Aug 2026 (~$445 mn), across 12 product lines
financial_highlights.change: ~2x FY26 revenue; >INR1,000 crore fresh wins since April

financial_highlights.value: Negligible in Q1 due to carried-forward losses; benefit expected for at least two years

segments.name: Medium voltage (11–66 kV) and EHV (132 kV+) cables
segments.commentary: Largest order-book block; management targets moving mix up the voltage curve, with 66 kV and above EBITDA guided at 18–22%. A INR435 crore data center order sits in this band.

segments.name: Low voltage (1.1 kV) cables
segments.commentary: Q1 mix skewed toward LV and conductors because MV/EHV cannot be laid in flood conditions; LV EBITDA guided at 8–9%. New copper LV facility (brownfield, ~42,000 km capacity, revenue potential ~INR1,880 crore) targeted for FY28 commercial production.

segments.name: Conductors (incl. HTLS, AL-59)
segments.commentary: Conductor EBITDA guided at 9–10%. Management says AL-59 is now ~70% of the market and Diamond has stopped producing ACSR.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Currently negligible. Team being built; certifications for Europe and US in progress. Internal target of INR500 crore export order book by year-end.

543252|2026-06.headline: Fairchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34.4% YoY to Rs 176 crore and EBITDA margin reached 10.14%, driven by price realisation.
543252|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 176 crore, up 34.4% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 18 crore (10.14% margin) and net profit of Rs 10 crore. Management attributed the gain mainly to higher price realisation, linked to elevated raw material costs, lower imports amid Middle East supply disruption, and reduced Chinese dumping. Sales volume was 13,500 tonnes versus 13,000 tonnes in Q1 FY26, while utilisation is near 60% against a target exit of 70-75% for FY27. Isostearic acid remains small (4% of revenue) with slow customer qualification.

segments.name: Dimer acid
segments.commentary: Approximately 30% of Q1 FY27 revenue; key export product alongside Isostearic acid.

segments.name: Linoleic acid
segments.commentary: Approximately 42% of Q1 revenue and about 40% of volume; goes into the paint industry.

segments.name: Isostearic acid
segments.commentary: About 4% of Q1 revenue; sold into cosmetics, qualification slow as only three global manufacturers exist.

segments.name: Other by-products
segments.commentary: Approximately 24% of Q1 revenue.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2-Q4 revenue and margin run rate to be maintained at current levels.
Capacity utilisation to rise by about 5% per quarter, to about 70-75% exit FY27 from roughly 60% now (on 80,000 tonne capacity).
A new oleochemical product is to start trial runs from Q2 FY27 on a 40,000 tonne capacity; ramp-up only after stabilisation; management says margins should be better than current.
Isostearic acid expected to exceed 80% capacity utilisation in 1-2 years; management indicated a positive outcome by end FY27 at some customers.
Export share currently 7-8% of revenue; management expects export growth from dimer and Isostearic acid, aided by India-UK and India-EU FTAs and rupee depreciation.
Management is not planning debt-funded or aggressive expansion given business risk.
capex_capacity: Current capacity is 80,000 tonnes; utilisation near 60% now, targeting 70-75% exit FY27.
A new 40,000 tonne oleochemical capacity is slated to begin trial runs in Q2; any capacity beyond 80,000 tonnes depends on this.
Energy conservation last year cut power consumption by more than 30% and solid fuel consumption by more than 35%.
Bypass fat plant and Isostearic acid (green route, third globally) are recent commissioned products.
demand_pricing: Price realisation up ~30% vs Q1 FY26 and ~25% vs Q4 FY26; management says raw material cost increases were passed through due to Middle East supply constraints and lower imports.
Management attributes improvement to reduced Chinese dumping, which it says may return and cannot be controlled.
Management says 7-8 large customers have enquired about alternative supply due to diversification.
Management declined to commit to long-term volume contracts with fixed pricing given volatility.
Paint industry is about 40% of revenue; management does not intend to reduce this dependence.
Duty inversion: raw material duty 16.5% (earlier 27.5% from 2024) vs finished product 7.5%, a roughly 9-point margin drag per management.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the revenue impact of the inverted duty structure versus dumping on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 9-point duty differential (16.5% on raw material vs 7.5% on finished product) is the margin loss; it declined to size the dumping effect and said the company is too small to influence duty policy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement sustainable if supply constraints ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company cannot control renewed dumping; it called sustainability uncertain and cited business risk as the reason for avoiding debt-funded expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D spend as a percentage of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 50 lakh is spent on revenue R&D, with the CFO stating 1-1.5% of sales; the company will check the annual report disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Isostearic acid outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals from cosmetics buyers in Europe and Japan are slow; the company is at step 3 or beyond everywhere and expects a possible positive outcome by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation change and sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation up about 25% from Q4 FY26 and about 30% from Q1 FY26; management hopes it holds as long as the West Asia crisis continues.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company sell at maximum utilisation now?

segments.commentary: Non-module revenue was 4-5% of total, with a target of 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1 and the transformer market is about INR 30,000 crore, targeted at INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp YoY EBITDA margin compression despite a strong order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a crowded module market, higher commodity, freight and forex costs from the geopolitical situation, and weak customer demand. qa_highlights.question: When does cell manufacturing start and what utilisation is expected?

qa_highlights.question: Debt peak and capex needs for FY27-28?

qa_highlights.question: Why did demand slow in Q1 when the ALMM transition was expected to pull volumes forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said developers waited because input costs rose after the Iran war began on 20 February, and force majeure notices and expected DCR extensions pushed projects out. Two tariff regimes (before and after 30 June) also encouraged waiting, which left demand subdued in May and June.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give the FY28 outlook?

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-module business plan and transformer opportunity?

540575|2026-06.headline: Star Cement Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR203 crore (INR1,497/t) from INR230 crore, with PAT at INR74 crore versus INR98 crore on subsidy cuts and fuel costs.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said stock is held on demand rather than pushed into channels, so no negative impact is expected; lower prices should help secondary demand.

qa_highlights.question: Will plywood reach EBITDA breakeven, and in which quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven is targeted within FY27, but management said it would be a single quarter, not the full year; PAT breakeven may follow in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the laminate volume decline not reflected in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-12% guidance is on revenue; adding back about INR30 crore of deferred exports brings volume close to the target, and it still stands by the range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR135 crore net (INR70 crore laminate, INR40 crore maintenance, INR10-20 crore past payments), with debt expected to fall about INR100 crore; FY28 repayments are above INR150 crore per schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Is chipboard capacity enough, and when is more needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is sufficient; management will move toward pre-laminate mix and will decide on new capacity once utilisation nears 80-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Plywood target of about INR20 per sq m EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR20 per sq m equals about 8-8.5% EBITDA, achievable only at 80-90% utilisation over time; current realisation is about INR270-275 per sq m.

544634|2026-06.headline: Aequs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR3,955 million, while operational EBITDA rose about 3.5x QoQ to INR148 million.
544634|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 55% YoY and 8% QoQ to INR3,955 million, led by aerospace (+40% YoY) and consumer (+190% YoY). Reported EBITDA fell QoQ to INR215 million because other income dropped from INR279 million to INR67 million, but operational EBITDA (excluding other income) rose from INR42 million to INR148 million. Consumer EBITDA loss narrowed by INR112 million QoQ to INR361 million. PAT loss was INR532 million, and the aerospace order book crossed USD1 billion after Farnborough wins including an A320 wheels contract with Safran Landing Systems. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 45-50% revenue growth and doubled operational EBITDA, with consumer EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,222 million (+40% YoY, +6% QoQ) with segment EBITDA INR731 million (about 23% margin). Order book USD1,004 million, up 13% QoQ from USD889 million; 86 parts added, taking portfolio to 5,740 parts.

segments.name: Consumer (electronics, toys, durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR734 million (+190% YoY, +16% QoQ) at roughly 22-23% capacity utilisation, similar to Q4. EBITDA loss INR361 million, narrowed by INR112 million QoQ; breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27 with utilisation at 40-50%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 45-50%, implying roughly INR1,700-1,800 crore; aerospace growth 25-30% and consumer growth 125-150% over FY26.
Operational EBITDA to double vs FY26 in FY27, weighted to the second half; aerospace segment EBITDA margin above 20%.
Consumer EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27; consumer utilisation expected to reach 40-50% by Q4.
PAT milestones: PAT breakeven by H1 FY28, consumer PAT breakeven by FY30, decent PAT in FY31 with about 20% steady-state ROCE.
Steady-state EBITDA margin guidance 18-22% (aerospace 18-22%, consumer 18-20%); ROCE target 18-20% steady state.

FY27 capex about INR660 crore (originally INR500 crore consumer, INR160 crore aerospace); aerospace capex may be accelerated. Five-year capex of USD350-400 million over FY27-FY31; about USD150 million equity raise expected, not planned this year unless capex pulled in or inorganic opportunity arises.
capex_capacity: Hosur ecosystem: about INR1,900 crore total investment over 10 years including JVs; first machining facility to commence in H2 FY27 (Sept to March window), with revenue from FY29 and vertical integration largely complete by 2030.
Aerospace capacity being added continuously (about one machine per week); management says aerospace utilisation can comfortably reach 75%.
Management is evaluating accelerating aerospace capex to meet new Farnborough wins; additional INR2,800 crore planned across consumer and aerospace in Karnataka.
Consumer capex (around INR400-500 crore) is for capacity augmentation and new programmes; part of it would not be committed if utilisation ramp fails.
Consumer asset turns about 1.5x, stable.
demand_pricing: Farnborough: long-term agreements with two new aerostructure Tier-1 customers and first contract for fully integrated A320 wheels with Safran Landing Systems (single source, about 15-year agreement, contract value not disclosed). New wins not yet in the Q1 order book; expected to reflect next quarter.
Management reports no specific demand change from tariffs or trade policy; customer allocations are being committed.
Consumer demand described as customer-driven; all production is being shipped.
Raw materials about 99% imported; limited qualified Indian sources for super alloys, titanium and aerospace aluminium (only two grades qualified, for forging).
Named consumer customers: Mattel (toys, strategic, scaling up) and Tramontina (consumer durables); a large consumer electronics brand is unnamed.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR399 million in Q1 FY26 and INR321 million in Q4 FY26
vs INR42 million in Q4 FY26, ~3.5x QoQ
down from INR279 million in Q4 FY26
+35% YoY, down QoQ due to high Q4 FX gain
vs loss of INR74 million in Q1 FY26; loss narrowed from INR473 million in Q4 FY26 (about 24%)
vs INR246 million in Q1 FY26; broadly flat vs INR455 million in Q4 FY26
down from INR358 million in Q4 FY26
vs adjusted Q4 FY26 loss of INR631 million (reported Q4 loss INR541 million incl. INR90 million exceptional gain)
plus INR537 million other bank balances
from 127 days at end FY26 (quarterly annualised)

543972|2026-06.headline: Aeroflex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72.4% YoY to INR145.97 crore, with EBITDA margin at 23.04% and SFN skid assemblies contributing INR32.4 crore (~23%).
543972|2026-06.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR145.97 crore (+72.4% YoY), with EBITDA up 116% to INR33.5 crore and margin up 468 bps to 23.04%. PAT rose 162% to INR18.79 crore (about 13% margin). Growth came from flexible hoses (+41% YoY), assemblies and value-added products (faster), and the new SFN liquid-cooling skid assemblies for data centres. Management said sequential margin dipped due to ramp-up manpower costs for Taloja and Chakan facilities and West Asia-related logistics costs.

financial_highlights.change: more than +100% YoY; margin +278 bps YoY

segments.name: Flexible hoses and assemblies
segments.commentary: Hoses grew 41% YoY and assemblies grew faster. Mix was 63% fittings/assemblies and 37% plain hose; hose-only margins are 16-20% and assembly margins 22-26%.

segments.name: SFN skid assemblies (data centre liquid cooling)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.4 crore on 1,040 units in Q1, about 23% of revenue. Capacity expanded from 6,000 to 9,000 units/yr; target 15,000 units/yr by start of Q3 FY27. Management says skid margin is in line with company average.

segments.name: Metal bellows
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR3 crore in Q1. Management expects an uptick over the next two quarters; bellows utilisation is not yet at optimum.

segments.name: Hyd-Air
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR7 crore in Q1. Used internally for hose-assembly components, not sold to third parties; capex plan under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Company EBITDA margin target of 25% over the next few years; management says it is on track, but gave no quarterly margin guidance.
Flexible hose capacity to rise from 17.5 million m/yr to 20 million m/yr, to be completed by Q3 FY27; hose-related capex budget ~INR54 crore, with the remainder spent in FY27.
SFN skid capacity to reach 15,000 units/yr by expected Q3 FY27 (October-November, dependent on machine supplier delays); total skid capex budgeted at INR48 crore.
Q4 FY27 skid exit run-rate guided at ~60-65% utilisation on the 15,000-unit capacity (about 750 skids/month per analyst), which management said remains intact.
Optimal skid utilisation of ~80% expected in FY28, after a full year at 15,000 units.
Management cited a peak-utilisation potential of INR650-675 crore top line for flexible hose plus assemblies, assuming 70% of sales from assemblies.
Management said the SFN share of revenue would be discussed at year end, not quarterly; it did not reiterate the 25% share target.
capex_capacity: Flexible hoses: 17.5 to 20 million m/yr by Q3 FY27; current utilisation 65-66%.
SFN skids: 9,000 units/yr now, targeting 15,000 units/yr by start of Q3 FY27; some machines already commissioned, others arriving Q2 and Q3.
New Chakan (Pune) plant under setup; a new facility for hose assemblies for an international customer was also set up.
Hyd-Air capex plan for FY27 under discussion; to be announced once finalised.
Skid machines are largely fungible and can be redeployed to bellows or other flow-control applications (HVAC, ports, terminals).
demand_pricing: Export growth was 43% YoY; Europe (Italy, Spain, France, UK) and the US grew, including hose assemblies for European data-centre applications.
Skid assembly pricing varies by design. Management said the average value per skid is not a valid price metric and that margins are costed per design.
International skid competitors named: Senior and Parker, plus local players in the US and Europe. Management declined to name domestic competitors.
Largest US customer is the source of the fire-hose assembly for data centres, expected to be commercialised by end-Q1 FY28 with international supply; margin 23-26%.
Management said about 40-odd skids go into 1 MW of liquid-cooled IT load.
Customer dispatch schedules come about 2 months ahead; tentative Q3 project lists are also shared.
Logistics costs rose sharply due to the West Asia crisis, which began in mid-March and worsened through Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin on the flexible hose assembly business, and is it on track for 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Hose-only margins are 16-20% and assemblies 22-26%. The 25% target is for the whole company's blended EBITDA margin, not hose alone. Mix is 63% assemblies and 37% hose, so blended is about 22-23%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SFN average price per skid decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price per skid depends on design (piping length and content), so per-unit value is not a valid metric. It said margins are unaffected because each skid is costed separately.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the skid expansion from 9,000 to 15,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Total budgeted skid capex is INR48 crore for the expansion from 2,000 to 15,000. Some machines have arrived, others are planned for Q1 and Q2 FY28, and ancillary machines are used from day one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 exit run-rate of about 750 skids a month still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60-65% utilisation guidance on the 15,000-unit capacity remains intact, but the final Q4 plan depends on Q3 visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall 80 bps QoQ when skid volumes doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to added skid-team headcount, the new hose-assembly facility for an international customer, and higher logistics costs from the West Asia crisis. It asked to be judged on a YoY basis.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 employee-cost deleverage is one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the costs relate to ramp-up manpower at Taloja (SFN) and Chakan, and that bellows utilisation is still below optimum, so margins should improve as those ramp up.

544124|2026-06.headline: Vibhor Steel guides ~20% Q1 revenue growth, driven by Jharsuguda; Q1 pipe dispatch only 1,500 t against 1,800 t pipe order book.
544124|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 20% YoY, with growth coming almost entirely from the Jharsuguda (Odisha) plant, while Mumbai and Hyderabad were broadly flat versus last year. Order books for pipe, crash barrier, transmission line towers (TLT) and poles were described as well above normal, but the second galvanizing tank at Jharsuguda (expected around 1 September) is the binding constraint. Management said new-product contribution would start in Q2 and smooth out in Q3 and Q4. Figures on EBITDA, PAT and margins were not quantified in the call; the company also said it is planning a North India plant via a newly incorporated subsidiary, starting with crash barrier.

segments.name: Pipe (ERW black/galvanized)
segments.commentary: 83% of revenue. Jharsuguda pipe order book 1,800 t vs ~1,500 t dispatched in Q1; Mumbai order book 6,500 t (1,000 t on hold, ~5,000 t sold); Hyderabad pipe/galv orders ~2,000 t vs 1,000-1,200 t historical average.

segments.name: Crash barrier / highway guardrail
segments.commentary: 12% of revenue. Jharsuguda order book ~600 t and Hyderabad ~850-1,000 t; Jharsuguda crash barrier line is at maximum installed capacity, with another crash barrier line being installed.

segments.name: Transmission line towers (TLT)
segments.commentary: Order book ~2,000 t (MP ~1,500 t, Chhattisgarh 200-250 t, Maharashtra 50-60 t, plus Sikkim, Chennai). Installed capacity ~600-700 t/month; dispatch of 300-400 t expected in the current month. Power Grid approval (~2 months) pending.

segments.name: Poles (octagonal, high-mast)
segments.commentary: Order book ~250 t, equal to ~75-80% of pole installed capacity of 300 t/month. Last 3 months' max sales 80 t; targets 100 t this month, 200 t next month, 300 t by October.

segments.name: Other / RSJ pole / Monopole
segments.commentary: RSJ pole first order ~500 t, processed as job work with ~Rs 1 crore revenue; Monopole certification pending, expected Q3. Monopole has highest margin per management.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27: management expects ~20% revenue growth to continue plus incremental ~1,000 t/month (~Rs 10 crore/month, ~30%) from TLT, poles and crash barrier; said 20-25% growth expected through the year, with the new products yet to contribute meaningfully.

Second galvanizing tank at Jharsuguda expected to be operational around 1 September; management said it would add at least 1,000-1,500 t of galvanizing capacity and roughly Rs 100-150 crore of revenue (rough estimate, as stated).
Growth from new products expected to start in Q2 and smooth out in Q3 and Q4.
North India plant: land purchase in talks; new subsidiary created for the plant, first phase crash barrier; management did not give capex amount or commissioning date.
Capex: management said further capex depends on utilisation; no FY27 capex quantum given.
capex_capacity: Jharsuguda: second galvanizing tank expected to be commissioned around 1 September 2026 (monsoon delay of ~2 weeks); one more crash barrier line being installed (bought last year).
Jharsuguda pole capacity ~300 t/month, effectively maxed out; TLT installed capacity ~600-700 t/month, could rise to ~2,000 t with Power Grid orders.
Sundargarh total capacity 1,56,000 t per annum (~40,000 t per quarter per management); utilisation ~18% overall.
North India plant under planning via new subsidiary; land purchase under discussion, not finalised.
Future Jharsuguda galvanizing tanks to be dedicated by product (pipe, crash barrier, TLT, RSJ, poles); timing not fixed.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong during monsoon; management cites government infrastructure push, high freight costs for imports and steel makers focusing on domestic sales.
Management is turning away export orders (EN10255/EN10217 galvanized), 1161/3601 BIS orders and hollow section orders because galvanizing tanks are full and margins are thin.
Product margin ranking per management: Monopole > TLT > pole > crash barrier (~3%) > pipe; some TLT and pole orders reportedly gave ~10% margin, overall ~2%.
Pipe orders arriving at ~100 t/day in Mumbai per management; dealer-MOU based allocation prioritised over end users.
Management said competition in TLT and poles is limited for 2-3 years due to engineering and certification requirements.

financial_highlights.change: Stated as ~20% increase; growth attributed mainly to Jharsuguda

financial_highlights.metric: Jharsuguda pipe dispatch in July-Aug to date
financial_highlights.value: ~1,500 t this month with 11-12 days left
~18% (7,500 t against ~40,000 t quarterly capacity; annual 1,56,000 t)

financial_highlights.change: Management said could rise to 24-30% from Sept/Oct

financial_highlights.value: Overall margins ~2%, per management on product margin discussion
financial_highlights.change: Not a reported Q1 EBITDA figure
Target to reduce to ~70% over time, no timeline

540173|2026-06.headline: PNB Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA 2.37% and ROE 11.44%, while NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to 3.50%.
540173|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT grew 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA of 2.37% and ROE of 11.44%. Disbursements moved to a cheque-realisation basis this quarter, so reported disbursement grew 18% YoY to INR 5,882 crore against 56% on the old cheque-handover basis. Loan book grew 15% YoY to INR 89,670 crore, NIM moderated to 3.50% and gross NPA was 0.95%. Management says margin and yield have bottomed and expects Q2 to be much better than Q1, especially in Affordable.

financial_highlights.change: -19 bps QoQ (12 bps leverage, 7 bps Q4 true-up)

financial_highlights.metric: Spread / portfolio yield / cost of borrowing
financial_highlights.change: Spread stable QoQ; yield +1 bp; cost of borrowing +1 bp

financial_highlights.value: Negative 12 bps (recoveries INR 67 crore from written-off pool)

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 3,083 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; Prime yield up about 8 bps QoQ, which management attributes mostly to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 2,029 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; INR 71 crore disbursed under the new Emerging Developer Finance programme.

segments.name: Affordable / Emerging (retail)
segments.commentary: Affordable and Emerging book grew 27% YoY and is 41% of retail portfolio (target 45% by FY27-end). Affordable net disbursement only INR 555 crore, below target; management cites about 11% YoY growth on a like-for-like basis.

segments.name: Corporate loan book
segments.commentary: INR 493 crore outstanding at 30 June 2026, with about INR 215 crore disbursed in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Written-off pool (retail)
segments.commentary: About INR 340 crore remaining; INR 67 crore recovered in Q1. One legacy account of about INR 420 crore was classified as fraud, already fully provided in FY23, so no incremental P&L impact.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 overall loan book growth guidance of 18% to 20% maintained; management says it expects to beat it.
Affordable loan book growth guidance of 50% to 60% maintained for FY27.
Construction finance capped at about 3% of the overall book in FY27.
Affordable and Emerging share to reach 45% of book by FY27-end and about 50% in FY28.
FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 ROA around 2.3% as credit cost normalises. Long-term ROA 2.3% to 2.35%.
NIM expected to have bottomed; gradual improvement from H2 FY27. Yield expected to keep improving on mix.
Credit cost expected to stay negative through FY27 on continued recoveries.
Q2 FY27 disbursement (net) expected 60% to 70% above Q1 overall and 2.5x to 2.6x in Affordable; management says July was promising.
Rating upgrades (CARE done; ICRA and CRISIL pending) expected to cut cost of borrowing by at least about 10 bps.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded by 12 in the quarter to 404 branches.
Affordable business launched from selected Prime and Emerging branches; about INR 30 crore disbursed in June, and 15% to 18% of Affordable business in July.
Management does not plan to open more branches; plans to use existing branches to contain opex.
Micro-housing policy formulated and rolled out in Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution expected from H2 FY27.
Full buyout transactions started; loan assets of INR 146 crore acquired in Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management cites steady housing demand across retail mortgage segments, particularly Affordable and Emerging Markets; RBI repo unchanged at 5.25%.
Gross disbursement YoY growth of 56% on cheque-handover basis vs 18% on the new net basis; the gap reflects the accounting change, not lost demand.
Incremental disbursement yield is above the 9.48% book yield, per management.
Incremental cost of borrowing rose about 18 bps in Q1 on tighter liquidity and market volatility; management says it has eased somewhat but remains elevated.
BT-in share of sourcing fell to 4.4% from 5% a year ago; Affordable BT-in fell to 3.4% from 10.5%.
Prime yield mix benefit about 10 to 15 bps; Affordable yield up about 50 bps QoQ per management.

544133|2026-06.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.
544133|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 57% YoY to INR236.8 crore, with Critical Power up 80% to INR176 crore and EV up 15% to INR61 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR20.9 crore (8.8% margin), helped by operating leverage and richer mix. Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

segments.name: Critical Power (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR176-177 crore, up 73-80% YoY and down ~11% QoQ; BharatNet is among the largest contributors, with a 60% share in that project per management. Export sales about INR15 crore (~8% of Critical Power).

segments.name: EV Charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR61 crore, up 15% YoY but down QoQ from Q4 DC-charger pull-forward; consolidated EV grew 50%. FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of total.

segments.name: Tritium (consolidated, US DC fast charging)
segments.commentary: Revenue about USD10-10.5 million in Q1, second consecutive quarter above USD10 million; bookings about USD20.8-21 million, roughly double the usual ~USD10 million per quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven expected within the next two quarters (management could not specify Q2 or Q3).
Tritium EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27, with 3x revenue growth versus last year targeted.
Standalone Critical Power exports targeted to rise from ~8% to ~15% of Critical Power sales within FY27.
AC charger monthly run rate expected to rise ~50% over the next three months.
Parallel-run fixed costs (~INR8.7 crore in Q1) expected to phase out as Gurgaon transition completes over coming quarters.
Tritium large strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX from hyperscaler) contingent on trial success.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and fully in production in Q1 FY27; management says it gives 3x production capability versus Gurgaon.
Standalone depreciation rose ~67% YoY, and management said standalone D&A increase was INR10-12 crore.
Management said DC charger utilisation is ~65% (90-100% for DC power system lines), AC charger ~100%, and PCBA and battery lines ~100%.
Ordered an additional AC charger line; management said the Hyderabad plant was built for ~2x AC capacity.
Tritium US factory capacity is about USD100 million a year versus ~USD10 million current quarterly revenue run rate (about one-quarter utilised).
demand_pricing: Critical Power order book ~INR1,000 crore; consolidated order book INR1,400 crore-plus as of 30 June 2026.
Large DC power system order of INR85 crore from a leading Indian telco; supply agreement with a large tower company for power systems and batteries.
BharatNet: INR700 crore open orders plus ~INR800 crore of service orders over 10 years; BSNL Phase 2 expected ~2,000 sites at INR90-100 crore.
BESS (commercial and industrial, mostly under 0.5 MWh): ~15 MWh orders worth ~INR20 crore in hand and ~34 MWh (INR45 crore) in advanced pipeline.
EV charger order book about INR200 crore for AC/DC chargers in India plus ~USD2 million export orders; 10 new export countries won; 15 new network operators added in Q1.
Margins on some large orders were hit by forex and commodity price increases, partly offset by volumes.
Supply disruptions in semiconductors, plastics and copper were cited as the main constraint, not capacity.

541233|2026-06.headline: Lemon Tree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs 346.8 crore, but net EBITDA margin fell 99 bps to 43.8% on GST and SAR provision.
541233|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 346.8 crore and PAT rose 19% to Rs 57.3 crore, while occupancy rose 314 bps to 75.7% as the company shifted to a volume-led retail strategy. Gross ARR rose only 2% to Rs 6,361 because retail business carries lower net ARR after commissions, and management called Q1 an aberration driven by West Asia-related corporate travel softness. Margin compression came from a GST input-credit loss and stock appreciation rights provision, worth 3.1% of revenue combined. Management expects Q2 to be better, with July described as strong and August as solid. The call also covered the planned demerger of Fleur Hotels and Warburg's Rs 960 crore investment in Fleur.

segments.name: Owned hotels (Lemon Tree)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 320 crore of network revenue, 56% of network revenue. Net EBITDA margin hit by GST input-credit loss and renovation spend of about Rs 9.8 crore (2.25-2.3% of revenue).

segments.name: Managed and franchised (asset-light)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 256 crore of network revenue. Opened 6 hotels with 334 rooms and signed 13 hotels with 1,020 rooms in Q1. Same-store managed revenue grew 9-10%.

segments.name: Keys portfolio (Fleur)
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 19% YoY to Rs 2,885, with occupancy up 350 bps to 67% and ARR up 13% to Rs 4,311. Renovation is about two-thirds complete across 7 hotels.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (pro forma)
segments.commentary: FY27 revenue Rs 311.4 crore (+7%), net EBITDA ex-GST Rs 125.1 crore (+10%, margin 40.2%), PAT Rs 34.7 crore (+23%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 net EBITDA margin to be better than the ~47% analyst estimate, and sees a path to at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops and ARR improves.
Management targets a long-term Lemon Tree EBITDA margin of 75-80% as fee income doubles and corporate costs fall as a share of revenue.
Management targets Keys EBITDA of Rs 60 crore on revenue of Rs 115-120 crore, implying Rs 6.5 lakh per key EBITDA.
Target of about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27; management says it is broadly confident, with Q1 at 334 rooms.
Renovation spend is expected to fall to about 1% of revenue from FY28. GST impact is about 2% of net revenue and expected to decline gradually.
Demerger of Fleur expected to complete in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in late second half of calendar 2027 after SEBI, shareholder, creditor and GST approvals.
Fleur's long-term plan is to keep debt-to-EBITDA around 2x; Fleur targets roughly 15% ROCE after renovations are complete.
capex_capacity: Aurika Shimla (owned, 90 rooms): about Rs 108 crore deployed as of 30 June 2026; opening shortly as finishing and licences are in final stage.
Aurika Shillong (leased, 165 rooms): about Rs 33 crore deployed; opening expected H2 FY28.
Aurika Varanasi (leased heritage, 47 rooms): work begun; opening expected FY29.
Aurika Nehru Place Delhi: approvals pending; opening on or after FY30; DDA letter of award validity extended by one year.
Renovation: 300 rooms renovated in Q1 at about Rs 10 crore; similar number expected in Q2. Management expects 600-700 rooms in H1 and refurbishments of about 800 rooms in H2.

Fleur plans capital deployment of about Rs 2,500-3,000 crore, funded by Warburg's Rs 960 crore and about Rs 200-300 crore of balance-sheet cash. Management targets about 2,500 rooms of operating and under-development acquisitions.
Asset-light pipeline: 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels, of which 11,946 rooms across 135 hotels are operational.
demand_pricing: Q1 ARR growth was driven by a retail-led volume strategy, which lowered net ARR after commissions. Management calls this temporary and says the mix is returning to balance in July and August.

Corporate demand softened in high-density CBD markets such as Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru during the West Asia conflict, with lower travel, hiring and relocations. Delhi, Bengaluru and Hyderabad still outperformed; Mumbai and Gurgaon did not.
Mumbai airport micro-market absorbed about 2,000 new rooms over the last two years, creating a temporary supply mismatch. Aurika Mumbai pricing is being reset, with the stated aim of higher ARR.
Around 52% of company room sales are below Rs 7,500 (the GST threshold) and 48% above. Management is repricing demand-dense hotels to reduce GST drag.
OTA share of business is in the mid-30s%, and direct channels rose in Q1 with the retail push. Management expects a better negotiated versus non-negotiated mix from Q2.
Management says July was strong and August solid; Q2 demand is significantly better than Q1.
