540544|2026-06.headline: PSP Projects Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR853 crores, with order book at INR13,245 crores (up 103% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 6.42%.
540544|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 65% YoY to INR853 crores and EBITDA rose 121% to INR55 crores, with margin expanding to 6.42% from 4.79%. Net profit reached INR18 crores versus INR37 lakhs a year earlier. Management attributed the margin shortfall versus its 7-8% target to weak April-May billing against labour-heavy costs, with employee cost at 5.4% of sales. Management reiterated FY27 revenue of INR4,400-4,500 crores and a 7-8% EBITDA margin for the full year, with the bulk of improvement expected in the second half.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR35 crores; ~5.39% of sales; headcount ~2,400 to ~2,600

segments.name: Adani Group projects
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 45% of Q1 revenue came from Adani Group projects, including RVNL and SMC. Within the order book, group projects are about 70% (61% of the INR6,200 crore bid pipeline).

segments.name: Order book by sector
segments.commentary: Industrial 39%, residential 37%, government 23%, institutional about 1%. Q1 order inflow was INR630 crores, 93% from Adani Group.

segments.name: Precast
segments.commentary: No separate revenue disclosed. Management indicated plant capacity of about INR200 crores, with INR150-200 crores executed per year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue of INR4,400-4,500 crores reaffirmed; management expects average growth of more than 25% going forward.
EBITDA margin of 7-8% for the full year; management said the bulk of the improvement comes in the second half, and could go beyond 7-8% as execution speeds up.
Employee cost expected to normalise to 4-4.5% of sales once sales pick up and labour availability improves.
Capex guided at 3-4% of revenue; larger projects could push it higher.
Order inflow of INR400-500 crores above prior expectations is not assumed; management expects FY27 inflows in the INR4,000-5,000 crore range, with more projects expected to click in Q2 and Q3.
Management expects finance costs to fall further and says the company could become net debt-free within two to three quarters.
Guidance is on a consolidated basis, and government orders are excluded from inflow guidance until they are firm.
Expects end-FY27 order book of about INR1,000 crores above the INR5,000-6,000 crore range if more than INR4,000 crores is executed.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of INR28 crores; guided to 3-4% of revenue on average.

Workforce of 16,000+ labourers deployed in Q1; management expects requirement of 16,000-17,000 at peak, with a further 3,000-4,000 to be added over the next one to two quarters as finishing and MEP work starts.
Mahim project: first two blocks raft foundation complete, now in first basement work. Matunga: piling under way, sheet piling before excavation.
SMC high-rise: core and shell complete, MEP, interiors and facade under way; completion expected by June 2027.
RVNL: two of three buildings to be handed over soon, hospital building RCC complete; project expected to complete by October 2026.
Ahmedabad Airport cityside: RCC work in full swing. Ambaji Mata Temple: excavation stage, some buildings at footing level.
demand_pricing: Order book INR13,245 crores as of 30 June 2026. Largest projects: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple INR962 crores, SMC High-Rise INR693 crores, GIFT City FinTech building INR259 crores, Science City gallery INR248 crores.
Bid pipeline of INR6,200+ crores, 61% group and 39% external.

Dharavi: about INR3,000 crores of the order book across two projects, which management equated to roughly 30,000-32,000 of the 2 lakh houses planned. Right of first refusal on further Dharavi work depends on performance over the next 1-2 years.

Cost escalation: aluminium and copper price increases hit some SMC and RVNL activities. Adani projects are pass-through, so management sees little impact there. Cost-plus contracts target about 7% EBITDA; Adani projects 6-7%, non-Adani 8-9%.

Management said the company will concentrate on Gujarat and Mumbai and aims for a 70-75% Adani / 25% non-Adani mix. Government order inflows are excluded until firm, and the Commonwealth Games project tender has not yet been issued.
UP medical project receivables: about INR40 crores receivable and INR60 crores unbilled; management expects EOTs to be signed and collections to close by end-August or mid-September 2026.
SDB receivables outstanding: INR90 crores; management plans a meeting with the counterparty's board.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR4,500 crore FY27 revenue target and 20-25% growth still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed INR4,400-4,500 crores and said average growth would exceed 25%.

qa_highlights.question: When does the 7%+ margin start, Q2 or H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 7%+ range comes from H2. Q1 margin was hit by about 1% from low April-May billing against labour cost. Q1 billing was INR319 crores in June versus INR270 crores in each of April and May.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be net debt-free within two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this could happen as working capital use falls and surplus FDs build.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a Dharavi opportunity beyond the current two projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds the first right of refusal. Further projects depend on performance on the current two. Redevelopment of about 2 lakh houses over roughly five to six years is planned, with separate development of cleared land after that.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 tax rate was 35%. Management expects the full-year rate to be slightly above 25% because some expenses are non-deductible.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin on cost-plus projects tightly controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-plus contracts work out to about 7% EBITDA, with a 1-2% gap depending on location (Mumbai about 3%, Mundra about 1.5%).

543232|2026-06.headline: CAMS Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 18% YoY to a record INR183 crore, with margin up 270bps to 46.4% despite muted MF AUM growth.
543232|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue grew 11.5% YoY to INR395 crore and EBITDA grew over 18% to INR183 crore, the highest ever, with PAT up 17%. MF revenue grew under 10% while non-MF revenue grew over 28%, led by Pay (up ~67-70%) and AIF (up ~25%), while KRA declined after the April 2026 pricing reset. Management said July AUM recovered strongly and expects FY27 blended revenue growth of about 13% and EBITDA growth of about 16%. Non-MF margin fell to about 13% in Q1 from over 17% last quarter, which management attributed mainly to the KRA dip.

financial_highlights.change: just under +15% YoY; market share about 67.2%

segments.name: Mutual fund (asset-based)
segments.commentary: MF revenue grew about 11% on asset-based revenue, with absolute MF revenue up under 10%; management sees no quarter-on-quarter yield decline. Equity AUM grew 17.6% and equity net sales and live SIP counts grew ahead of industry.

segments.name: Pay (payments)
segments.commentary: Grew just short of 70% YoY, driven mainly by credit card transactions after the PA licence; management said cards will be grown step by step given low margins.

segments.name: AIF / Alternatives
segments.commentary: AUM crossed INR3.2 lakh crore, grew mid-20s (about 25%), with 50 new mandates won in the quarter.

segments.name: KRA
segments.commentary: Revenue fell YoY after the April 2026 pricing reset (rates down about 29-30%); management expects recovery from Q2.

segments.name: SIF and GIFT City
segments.commentary: SIF: 11 unique SIFs launched, about INR12,000 crore accumulated and about INR1,000 crore net sales per month, nearly 50,000 investors. GIFT City retail: about INR750 crore AUM from first 10,000 investors.

segments.name: CAMS Repository, AA, pension
segments.commentary: Not yet EBITDA positive; management expects CAMSRep to turn EBITDA positive on a Q4 basis. Think Analytics is near breakeven.

guidance_outlook: FY27 blended non-MF revenue growth of about 20%, possibly 22-23%; MF revenue growth of at least 12%; blended revenue growth about 13% and EBITDA growth about 16%.
Non-MF margin expected to recover to about 17% for the year, 'close to 20%' by year-end, per management's varying comments.
Employee cost growth target about 5% YoY for FY27; total cost growth target below 10% per year for the next two to three years.
Enterprise headcount to fall about 5% in FY27; net employee cost benefit expected to be about 3-3.5% rather than 5%.
Operating margin expansion of about 1% a year, with possibility of 1.5%.
PAT margin expected to stay at about 30-31%; FY27 PAT growth about 31% if EBITDA growth is about 45%, per Ram Charan's answer.

On-prem capex about INR75 crore in the coming year, declining later; re-architecture total cost about INR500 crore, of which about INR290 crore capex, with about INR40 crore capitalised in Q1 and at least another INR80 crore in the rest of FY27.
Depreciation expected to rise, not fall, for the rest of FY27 by INR4-5 crore, due to re-architecture capitalisation.
capex_capacity: On-prem capex about INR75 crore in the coming year, falling in later years as cloud migration progresses.
Re-architecture project cost about INR500 crore, of which INR123 crore spent so far; about INR290 crore to be capex on a 10-year amortisation.
About INR40 crore re-architecture capitalised in Q1 FY27; at least INR80 crore more expected in the rest of FY27.
Transaction acceptance module of new platform going live Aug-Sep; full transaction acceptance concept by year-end. Four of eight transaction types live; all expected by November.
About 10% of gross payload converted to AI-based acceptance at maker level, to scale to 100% in 12 months.
demand_pricing: Market conditions muted in April-June; July materially better, AUM close to INR60 lakh crore but not yet there.
SIP collections held at just under INR60,000 crore in Q1; SIP collections and unique investor base grew faster than industry.

Yields: no quarter-on-quarter decline in Q1; compression from 4Q FY26 and 1Q FY26 is now in the base; residual compression for the next 3-4 quarters expected to be small. Historical 2.5-3% annual yield decline cited as likely.
KRA: pricing reset from 1 April 2026 cut rates about 29-30%; some fetch services that were free are now priced. Management says pricing is uniform across KRAs.
Mid-size AMC renewals: a couple concluded and two in discussion; impact on pricing expected to be very muted and already in Q1 pricing.
Non-asset MF revenue down YoY on lower NFO activity, the NSE arrangement winding down and application fees; QoQ also hit by MF Central and OPE.

540750|2026-06.headline: IEX Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose about 12% to Rs 134.8 crore on Rs 202.8 crore revenue, with electricity volume up 16% to 37.5 billion units.
540750|2026-06.overview: IEX reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 202.8 crore and PAT of Rs 134.8 crore, up about 12% YoY, on electricity volume of 37.5 billion units (+16%). Real-Time Market growth was the main driver, with RTM up about 25% in Q1 and its share of mix reaching about 34% last year. Management used the analyst meet to push a set of new products (Green RTM, peak contracts, 11-month TAM, carbon trading, coal exchange) while pushing back on CERC's proposed market coupling and the Day-Ahead Market pilot, which it has challenged at APTEL and the Supreme Court. The call was mostly a policy and product narrative; no formal FY27 guidance was given.

segments.name: Electricity (DAM / RTM / TAM)
segments.commentary: RTM is now roughly the size of DAM; DAM share of mix fell from 95% in FY16 to about 39%, RTM rose to about 34% in FY26, and RTM is up about 25% in Q1 FY27. Term-Ahead Market and Green Market are about 7-8% of the mix.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange, associate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 42 crore; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 16 crore. DRHP filed for IPO of a 22.3% stake to bring IEX's 47.3% holding down to 25% under PNGRB rules, after a one-year extension.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC / environmental)
segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.name: Indian Coal Exchange (new)
segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. Market size cited at about 120 million tonnes today, with a target of at least 100 million tonnes in year one.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or revenue guidance given; management expects RTM volumes to grow about 25-30% a year.
Management expects carbon credit trading to begin in FY27, with BEE targeting 1 October 2026.

Management expects the Green RTM, peak-power contracts (DAM and RTM) and 11-month TAM products to be approved by CERC; timing was not committed, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending for over two years.
Management sees the exchange-routed share of electricity rising to about 25% over five to six years, against about 14-15% short-term market today.
Management said it would consider a buyback in future, citing SEBI's revised market-buyback rules.
Management said the coal exchange's fee should exceed those of MSTC and M-Junction, since exchanges perform price discovery, clearing and settlement.
capex_capacity: Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity in the pipeline, 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW awarded, and 16 GW in planning; most is expected in FY31-FY33.
Management said it has built a hot standby for RTM and a DC-to-DR switch; both were positioned as ready for the proposed 5-minute bidding window.

BESS merchant capacity cited: ACME about 3,200 MWh, Juniper about 500 MWh, Adani about 3,400 MWh, with more than Rs 9,000 crore of BESS VGF support. Management said the arbitrage window may last 3-5 years.
The SECI 500 MW CfD pilot for peak power was cited as launched; it is a peak-power product, not solar.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand growth of about 5-5.5% a year, versus 11% in Q1 FY27 on heat and delayed monsoon. Peak demand touched about 271 GW in May and July.
Management said exchanges as a group grew 18% in FY26 against 1% demand growth.

On market coupling, CERC proposed Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, with DAM first. Management said it has challenged the July 2025 order at APTEL (order dated 13 February 2026) and is now before the Supreme Court; a second hearing was held on 27 July 2026.
Management said that even after coupling, DAM share could fall 20-40%, but said business impact would not be significant. The market-share loss figure is management's own estimate.
Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side and the top-buyer concentration is 50-60%, with 800-900 participants daily.

Management cited an RTM realisation issue in a Q&A: an analyst's per-unit realisation calculation (about 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa a year earlier) was not reconciled; management pointed to incentives in REC and TAM.

financial_highlights.change: about 11% QoQ per management; YoY not stated

544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.
544911|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR137.1 crore, up 103.5% YoY, with transformers at 84.9% and EPC at 14.81% of revenue. EBITDA rose 152.2% to INR38.8 crore (28.3% margin, up 550 bps) and PAT rose 140% to INR27.3 crore (19.9% margin). Consolidated order book stood at about INR2,026 crore on June 30, 2026, up 11% from March 31, 2026, after incremental orders of INR332.2 crore in Q1 and INR867.3 crore in Q2 to date. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR950 crore with EBITDA margin similar to FY26, with H2 as the main execution period.

financial_highlights.value: Q1: INR332.2 crore; Q2 to date: INR867.3 crore

segments.name: Power Transformers / 400 kV
segments.commentary: 400 kV transformers contributed 70.16% of Q1 revenue (52% in FY26, 10.3% in FY24). Management said 400 kV, Scott-connected and shunt reactor products carry similar gross margins; about 70% of order book is power transformers, mostly 400 kV.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: EPC contributed 14.81% of Q1 revenue. Management does not disclose EBITDA separately; directionally lower than transformer margins.

segments.name: By end-user
segments.commentary: Power Transmission 85.18%, Railways 11.53%, Renewable Energy 2.84%, Power Distribution 0.23% of Q1 revenue. Shunt reactors were about 13.1% of order book at June 30.

segments.name: Voltage mix (other)
segments.commentary: 132 kV to below 220 kV at 11.38%, 220 kV to below 400 kV at 3.19%, below 132 kV at 0.23% of Q1 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR950 crore, with EBITDA margin broadly similar to FY26.
FY28 revenue growth expected to be similar to FY27 guidance (about 40-45% per analyst's read, not confirmed by management).
Brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol, targeted to be in place by end-FY28 / FY29; existing capacity seen sufficient through FY28.
Net working capital guided at 110-120 days.
Order book at end-FY27 may be adequate to cover FY28 and FY29 revenue, per management; no specific FY27 closing order book number given.
Shunt reactors expected to be about 10-15% of revenue on average over time.
capex_capacity: Existing capacity about 19,200 MVA across Rithani and Gangol (Meerut); Gangol about 18,000 MVA.
Q1 FY27 executed about 1,725 MVA, implying roughly 36-46% utilisation depending on base used.
Planned brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol; part funded from IPO proceeds.
765 kV: technology developed in-house; capacity to be suitable for 765 kV; management estimates 3-4 years to become eligible for regular 765 kV tenders.
About 2,500 kW solar plant planned, partly funded from IPO proceeds; savings not quantified.
demand_pricing: Management estimates India 400 kV transformer market at about 60,000-70,000 MVA last year, growing 10-15% industry-wide; analyst's INR4,000-6,000 crore 400 kV market size was confirmed as 'in that range'.
Railways envisages about 1,000 traction substations for high-speed rail over 5-10 years (about 2,000 transformers), implying about INR20,000 crore opportunity.
Most contracts have price variation clauses (IEEMA PVC), which management says offsets raw material swings; order book margins said to be similar to FY26.
Industry lead times are 18-24 months; tenders being bid are mainly for FY29-FY30 execution.
Revenue per MVA about INR6.1 lakh last year; may have risen slightly due to raw material costs.
Management said there were no new entrants in the last 3-6 months that it is aware of, but expects new entrants over time.

qa_highlights.question: How were transformer margins protected in Q1 given input cost increases and fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts carry price variation linked to the IEEMA clause, which passes through raw material moves in both directions.

qa_highlights.question: Will GEC-III drive a multi-year order tailwind for 400 kV and 500 MVA transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a multi-decadal structural tailwind; intra-state transmission is mostly 400 kV, but no split of GEC-III capacity by voltage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can order book reach INR3,000 crore by FY27 end, and 40-45% YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to confirm; said Q2 execution will reduce the order book slightly, and end-FY27 book may cover FY28-FY29 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1H-weak, 2H-heavy revenue pattern a continuing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said H1 is typically softer and H2 heavier, an industry trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will new 400 kV capacity pressure margins beyond 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visibility for 3-4 years from current order book and tenders; beyond that, short-term supply-demand mismatch and margin pressure are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY24 a revenue decline and why is utilisation low; are exports planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY24 focus went to obtaining 400 kV and Scott certifications; ramp-up takes time. Exports are not the current focus; a re-look may come in 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Supply chain and raw material availability, which management named as the key risk; geopolitical sourcing issues were raised.
Margin pressure from new 400 kV entrants and added capacity beyond the 3-4 year visibility window.
Execution timing: H2-weighted revenue and 18-24 month execution cycles.
Capacity addition: brownfield 18,000 MVA must come on stream by FY28-FY29 to support growth.
Order book lumpiness toward power transformers, with large CPSU orders (INR250 crore+) in Q2.
Working capital intensity of 110-120 net days.
Management did not disclose bid pipeline, EBITDA by segment, or the MVA-based breakdown beyond Q1 execution.
544911|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and qualifications, with a clear long-term structural narrative. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to confirm order book targets, FY28 growth, bid pipeline, and solar savings, and deferred several answers to later follow-up.

544645|2026-06.headline: Park Medi World Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs.476 crore, PAT up 35% to Rs.89 crore; FY27 guided to Rs.2,080 crore revenue.
544645|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.476 crore (+19% YoY) with EBITDA excluding other income of Rs.126 crore (26.5% margin) and PAT of Rs.89 crore (18.6% margin, +220 bps). PAT growth was attributed mainly to lower interest outgo after term debt repayment. Occupancy fell to 56% from 68% as 960 new beds (Bhatinda, Agra, Panchkula) entered the denominator. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs.2,080 crore, EBITDA Rs.530 crore and PAT Rs.360 crore, and announced two acquisitions (Rudrapur, commissioned 2 August 2026; Zirakpur/Mehar, Rs.107 crore valuation).

vs 68% in Q1 FY26; FY26 was 64%

segments.name: Newer hospitals (Agra, Panchkula, Bhatinda)
segments.commentary: Agra (commissioned Feb 2026) and Panchkula (commissioned Apr 2026) are ramping in line with plan; management expects no EBITDA loss, with first-year margins of about 10-12%. Mohali, the mature comparable, is at about 26% margin.

EBITDA margin expected at 26.7-27% for FY27; PAT margin 17-18%.
ARPOB growth guided at 10-12% annualised for the next two years.
FY27 occupancy expected to moderate from FY26's 64% due to new capacity.

CGHS rate revision (12-15% headline, about 7-7.5% net benefit to ARPOB, 70% of patients on CGHS) to flow fully from Q2 FY27; management says limited EBITDA benefit as it is redeployed into equipment and maintenance.
Payer mix target of 70:30 (government schemes vs cash/TPA) over 12-18 months.
Debtor days target of 125-130 days over the medium term.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 beds: 3,960 (up 32% YoY), including Panchkula's 350 beds; 960 beds added in last 12 months across Bhatinda (250), Agra (360), Panchkula (350).
Rudrapur (The Medicity, 330 beds, NABH) acquired for about Rs.177 crore all-cash; commissioned 2 August 2026. Additional capex of Rs.10-12 crore planned.
Mehar Hospital, Zirakpur (150 beds) acquisition at about Rs.107 crore valuation announced 3 August 2026; commissioning targeted November 2026.
Palam Vihar 'Park Platinum' 100-bed extension in Gurgaon (Rs.25 crore capex, about Rs.25 lakh/bed), taking Gurgaon to 750 beds; Naraela 200-bed insolvency acquisition on track for commissioning.
Agra: Rs.245 crore acquisition cost plus about Rs.7.5 crore equipment/upgrade.
Capex per bed about Rs.37 lakh currently; ongoing projects of Rs.767 crore for 2,130 beds over FY27-FY28 imply about Rs.36 lakh/bed blended, including acquisitions.
Ambala adding 200 beds, largely oncology-dedicated; LINAC planned at Bhatinda and Rudrapur.
demand_pricing: ARPOB rose 12% YoY to Rs.30,444; management says trend growth is 10-12%, versus 3-5% in the past.
Mature hospitals are growing 18-20% per management.
Management says patient footfall at the Park brand was about 9 lakh last year and about 2.5 lakh in Q1 FY27.
Patient mix at new acquisitions (Rudrapur, Zirakpur) expected at 75-80% government and 20-25% cash/TPA.
Management says doctor attrition at consultant level is among the lowest in the industry; no comparative data was given.
Management said it has not faced any CGHS-related pressure in oncology, citing vendor relationships.

532163|2026-06.headline: Saregama Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to Rs 263.6 crore and adjusted EBITDA 69% to Rs 112.4 crore; music vertical grew 39%.
532163|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 263.6 crore (+27% YoY), adjusted EBITDA Rs 112.4 crore (+69% YoY) and operational PBT Rs 70.5 crore (+38% YoY). The music vertical (licensing, artiste management, retail) delivered Rs 230.6 crore revenue (+39%), EBITDA Rs 139.8 crore (+36%) and net margin Rs 99.6 crore (+31%). Video revenue fell 52% to about Rs 17 crore as the company winds down its films business in favour of Bhansali Productions. Management reiterated 20-23% music growth and 60-65% music EBITDA margin guidance, and asked analysts to judge performance on a rolling 12-month basis.

financial_highlights.change: +36% YoY (analyst noted music EBITDA margin down ~1% YoY on mix)
Rs 40 crore per quarter run rate over last three quarters

segments.name: Music (Licensing, Artiste Management, Retail)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 230.6 crore (+39% YoY), EBITDA Rs 139.8 crore (+36%), net margin Rs 99.6 crore (+31%); management attributed part of the growth to a low base in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Video
segments.commentary: Revenue fell 52% to about Rs 17 crore as films business is being wound down; remaining film releases expected to clear over the next three to four quarters.

segments.name: Artiste Management
segments.commentary: Running at about Rs 40 crore per quarter for three quarters, roughly 10% EBITDA margin per analyst; 309 artistes represented with more than 440 million followers across Instagram and YouTube.

segments.name: Live Events
segments.commentary: 23 Carvaan Live shows, 22 devotional-format shows and 48 standard packs in Q1; Ilaiyaraaja US tour underway; Arjan Dhillon tour planned for September.

segments.name: Pocket Aces (partner company)
segments.commentary: Reached breakeven in FY26 and is moving towards profitability in FY27; no revenue figure disclosed.

segments.name: Bhansali Productions (partner company)
segments.commentary: No releases in Q1; next releases planned in Q4 FY27.

New music content spend for FY27 expected at Rs 300-350 crore, mostly already committed; AI-related investments to sit within this envelope.

Brand and direct-to-customer revenue split to be updated annually, not quarterly.
capex_capacity: New music content spend of Rs 300-350 crore in FY27, with large releases lined up including Love and War (January), Dharman, Paradise, Naagzilla and a Tiger Shroff Bhansali Productions film.
UN40 music festival next season set for 13-14 February 2027 in Bangalore.
Krishna show with Manoj Muntashir: 25-30 more shows planned; Carvaan Live targets a minimum of four shows per month in each city.

543389|2026-06.headline: Sigachi Q1 FY27 revenue INR121.27 cr with EBITDA margin 13.6%; management reiterates FY27 guidance of INR650-675 cr revenue and ~18% EBITDA despite run-rate gap.
543389|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 total operating income was INR121.27 crore, with EBITDA of INR16.5 crore (13.6% margin) and PAT of INR8.14 crore (6.76% margin). MCC contributed INR82.74 crore, API INR21.68 crore and O&M INR13.06 crore. Average MCC realisation rose to INR241.36/kg from INR216/kg in Q4, while capacity utilisation was 76.8% across plants. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR650-675 crore revenue and ~18% full-year EBITDA margin, but the Q1 run-rate of ~INR121 crore implies a steep H2 ramp that the call did not fully reconcile.

segments.name: MCC (microcrystalline cellulose)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR82.74 crore, about 70% of Q1 sales per analyst math; realisation INR241.36/kg. Management attributed share loss to a ~6,000 TPA capacity reduction after a Hyderabad incident, and expects to regain share as capacity returns.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21.68 crore in Q1; management expects quarter-on-quarter improvement and cited Sparsentan, Bempedoic acid and other higher-margin molecules. Mgmt expects INR100-110 crore for the year, below the INR90-100 crore Q4 target framing for FY27 quarterly pace was not clarified.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Revenue INR13.06 crore in Q1; described as a steady, scalable contributor with no further quantification.

segments.name: CCS (croscarmellose sodium)
segments.commentary: 1,800 TPA facility at Dahej SEZ under construction; management says it will be operational only in FY28. Indian CCS market estimated at ~$100 million, with realisation INR1,200-1,500/kg per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance unchanged at INR650-675 crore; management says H2 ramp will deliver it, but Q1 was ~INR121 crore versus ~INR160-170 crore per quarter needed.
Full-year EBITDA margin target ~18%, reiterated; management attributes margin expansion to fixed-cost leverage as revenue rises.
Dahej-2 12,000 TPA MCC expansion now targeted for Q2 FY28, delayed from earlier Q1 FY28/Q4 FY27 timelines; total cellulose-based excipient capacity to reach 30,000 TPA on commissioning.
FY27 capex more than INR100 crore; FY28 INR150-200 crore; funding via bank borrowing and a possible preferential equity issue (not finalised).

Insurance (business interruption) claim expected to be settled in full with some discount, or an ad hoc amount, by about September 2026; eligible amount INR16.5 crore against INR25 crore policy, with a further 3-4 months expected for receipt.
capex_capacity: Current cellulose-based excipient capacity 18,000 TPA, exports over 53.5% of production; debottlenecking (extra shifter/blender) to add about 1,600 TPA per management.
Dahej-2 MCC expansion of 12,000 TPA (INR106 crore cost per Q4 call) targeted Q2 FY28; total capacity to reach 30,000 TPA.
CCS facility 1,800 TPA at Dahej SEZ (INR93 crore), operational in FY28; primarily export-oriented, with export inquiries already received.
Management plans further unspecified capacity expansion of about INR50 crore beyond MCC and CCS projects.
Company is debt-free with no term loans currently; bankers ready to lend.
demand_pricing: Management says MCC demand is strong given regulatory approvals and quality; cited Asia Pacific MCC CAGR of 7-8% and market size ~$1.4 billion by 2035.
Realisation rose ~12% QoQ to INR241.36/kg; management attributed this to product mix shift toward higher-grade MCC used in formulations (cheaper grades declining).
Smokeless tobacco (snuff) MCC demand described as nascent; management declined to give a growth number.
CMC (key CCS raw material) to be bought from China rather than made in-house; management says in-house CMC would be costlier at the ~couple-thousand-ton scale.
Management said CCS margins would be well above MCC margins; analyst's 25%+ margin figure was confirmed as correct, though no official target was set.

qa_highlights.question: Is oversupply a risk with many Indian MCC players expanding capacity, and what is the pricing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said regulatory approval and quality matter for export markets; realisation rose to INR241.36/kg from INR216/kg in Q4, attributed to quality-driven customer preference.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q1 revenue (~INR120 crore) well short of the INR650-675 crore run-rate, and is guidance changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no change in guidance; Q1 was on plan with only small variations, and revenue will rise in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How does ~76.8% utilisation reconcile with the 30,000 TPA expansion and FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant needs shutdown/cleaning validation on product-mix changes; it expects run-rate above 95-96% by year-end on 18,000 TPA declared capacity (about 4,500 TPA per quarter).

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge to INR650 crore revenue given MCC capacity limits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 19,600 TPA available capacity at INR241/kg plus API and O&M contributing more than INR200 crore; analysts found the math difficult to reconcile and management asked them to recalculate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and funding for the capex and insurance claim?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance settlement or ad hoc amount expected by about September; capex funded via borrowing or a preferential equity issue, not yet finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MCC margins rise structurally since 2019?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited industry consolidation (world number one changed hands twice; an Indian player bought by a European firm) and a shift in formulator demand toward higher-grade, innovative MCC grades.

financial_highlights.change: Mgmt quoted ~INR21 crore in Q&A; Q4 call target was INR90-100 crore for API

543667|2026-06.headline: INOX Green Q1 FY27 PAT rose 86% YoY to INR41 crore; Wind World India acquisition completion expected in Q2 FY27.
543667|2026-06.overview: INOX Green reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR101 crore (+17% YoY), EBITDA of INR57 crore (+19%), PBT of INR54 crore (+74%) and PAT of INR41 crore (+86%). Management said the power evacuation business was demerged into INOX Renewable Solutions effective August 1, 2026 (record date), leaving INOX Green as an asset-light O&M player. NCLT Ahmedabad approved the Wind World India acquisition, with completion expected in Q2 FY27. Management reiterated full-year guidance but declined to quantify quarterly trajectory, and the call was largely about the parent's (INOX Wind) revenue and receivables questions.

Blended revenue of INR9-10 lakh per MW excluding GST on the about 4 GW base.

segments.name: Wind World India (acquisition pending)
segments.commentary: O&M portfolio of about 4.5 GW; FY26 revenue about INR580 crore with contracted annual price escalation of about 5%. Completion expected in Q2 FY27, after which line-by-line consolidation follows.

segments.name: INOX Wind (group parent, equipment/EPC)
segments.commentary: Equipment supply share of third-party order book about 59% (41% turnkey) as of July 2026; order book about 4.4 GW. Q1 revenue flat YoY per management.

segments.name: INOX Renewable Solutions (demerged EPC/power evacuation)
segments.commentary: Power evacuation infrastructure business demerged from INOX Green effective August 1, 2026; listing expected in about 2-3 months, subject to regulatory approvals.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% YoY maintained (INOX Wind, per management).
Full-year FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin of 20% to 22% maintained; H2 expected to carry about 70-75% of annual business.
INOX Green EBITDA guidance of INR600 crore on an annualised basis from Q3/Q4 FY27 post consolidation; management clarified it is an annual, not quarterly, figure.
INOX Green wind O&M EBITDA margin guidance of about 50% on the existing portfolio, excluding treasury income; management said one-off costs and life-extension spend cause quarterly variation.
Working capital guidance maintained on an annualised basis; receivable days expected to fall over the next 3-4 quarters.
4X wind turbine: prototype installation in August 2026, commercial launch about a month later; ALMM-driven indigenisation targeted near 100% by calendar year-end.
Wind World India acquisition formalities expected in Q2 FY27; other investments expected to be completed and consolidated in FY27.
capex_capacity: INOX Wind signed a 1.5 GW MOU with INOX Clean in June 2026; firm orders for 500 MW signed so far, balance 1 GW pending.
INOX Wind received a 200 MW LOA from NLC India in Q1 FY27 (repeat order); order book about 4.4 GW as of July 2026, visibility 24-36 months.

Expansion at INOX Renewable Solutions: transformer capacity to 4.9 MVA for 4X series, plans for 8-20 MVA and 100 MVA+ transformers, 4 cranes in operation with more this fiscal, unit substation (USS) commercial launch in FY27.
demand_pricing: Wind industry added 1.4 GW in India in Q1 FY27; cumulative installed wind capacity 57.4 GW; management expects 8-10 GW annual additions over the next few years.
Of 9.34 GW renewable capacity awarded through tenders in Q1, 2.35 GW (25%) was standalone wind.
Blended O&M realisation INR9-10 lakh per MW on the about 4 GW own base; acquired portfolios expected to be substantially higher per management.
INOX Clean plans 3 GW+ annual IPP capacity; management expects roughly 25-30% of that to flow to INOX Wind and the O&M portion to INOX Green.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise funds for the Wind World acquisition when prior preferential issue funded it, and why not debt against cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said these were enabling resolutions and declined further comment citing the silent period.

qa_highlights.question: Is INOX Clean business on the same terms as third-party business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inter-entity contracts are arm's length, INOX Clean is treated as a customer, and there is no preferential pricing for any customer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INOX Green portfolio's revenue per MW and how much of the acquired portfolio is consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended INR9-10 lakh per MW excluding GST on about 4 GW own turbines; the two acquired portfolios (about 6.5 GW) remain investments and are not consolidated until shares are acquired.

qa_highlights.question: Why is legacy O&M EBITDA well below the 50% guided margin, and what about the deferred INR400 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to one-off, infrastructure and life-extension costs, plus value-added services previously not billed separately, which will be billed from this year. On the deferred revenue, management said part was recognised in Q1 and the rest would be covered over FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR600 crore EBITDA guidance for FY27 and does it start from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR600 crore is an annual figure on an annualised basis from Q3/Q4 post consolidation, not a quarterly target, and gave no FY28 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 75% FY27 revenue growth guidance still achievable given flat Q1 at INOX Wind?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 75% growth target, citing H2-weighting (70-75% of business) and a shift to equipment supply that it expects to show results from Q2-end and predominantly in Q3.

507552|2026-06.headline: Foods & Inns Q1 FY27: export dispatches slowed by vessel shortage and freight spikes, though frozen segment grew ~20% and no order cancellations were reported.
507552|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 mango production was good in quality and price, but export dispatches slowed due to vessel non-availability and sharply higher ocean freight, with customers delaying call-offs rather than cancelling. Exports are 35-40% of sales and domestic about 55%; management expects domestic demand, aided by an El Nino-driven juice and drinks season, to offset export softness. Frozen food is the growth engine: about USD3 million in Q1 (up ~20%) and USD12 million last year, with a target of USD30-plus million in three years. Realisations fell ~18.5% YoY in the quarter, and management flagged working-capital blockage from delayed shipments, with a CFO resignation pending replacement.

financial_highlights.metric: Frozen food segment revenue (last full year)
financial_highlights.change: Frozen grew ~30% CAGR over last 2 years (stated)

financial_highlights.value: Down 18.5% YoY (as cited by analyst, not disputed)
Growth of 14.7% YoY (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Frozen food (pulp, vegetables, snacks)
segments.commentary: About USD3 million in Q1 with ~20% growth; ~USD12 million last year. Target USD30-plus million in 3 years. Absorbing higher freight better than other segments; capacity expansion in process.

segments.name: Pectin
segments.commentary: Commercial production started; audits ongoing. Brand consumer testing underway, with opportunity expected from October/November (H2 FY27).

segments.commentary: Kusum showed better Q1 performance; focus on HORECA, with slow retail build-out. Spray line and spice division run 24x365.

segments.commentary: Vegetables have steady demand but depend on raw material cost. Tomato is the largest non-mango pulping utilisation, followed by guava.

guidance_outlook: Management expects lost export volume to be caught up over the remaining nine months, assuming freight normalises within a couple of months.

Frozen pulp: trial runs completed for West Asia opening; order booking described as very encouraging.

Frozen food demand in US, UK and Canada remains strong; company says frozen is the only segment absorbing high freight.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of loss for perishable products because of shipping delays, and how should the next nine months be guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said finished goods are processed foods with a 2-year shelf life in drums or cans, so no loss risk; delays are expected but no cancellations. It expects domestic demand to offset export softness and sees pent-up export demand later.

qa_highlights.question: How big is frozen food and what is the scale target?
qa_highlights.answer: Frozen was ~USD12 million last year and ~USD3 million in Q1 with 20%-plus growth expected. The target is USD30-plus million in 3 years, across frozen pulp, vegetables and snacks.

qa_highlights.question: Overdue export shipments: what is the clearance timeline and working-capital impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Clearance is slow; management estimated 45-50 days but would not commit. Working capital is blocked, adding interest cost. Air freight is about 30x ocean and ruled out.

qa_highlights.question: Pectin growth and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production started and audits are underway. Brand consumer testing is needed before procurement orders, with opportunity expected from October/November.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 20% volume guidance be met, and is value growth possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic volume growth of ~20% is seen as achievable; export depends on freight. Value growth may not come in Q1 given lower realisations; the company expects +/-10% from September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is top line stagnant, and will promoter holding rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line fell because mango raw material prices dropped (cost-plus model). Promoter says holding is just over 25%, plans to look at market purchases or a preferential issue to raise stake and reduce debt, with no decision yet.

risks_watch: Freight normalisation timing: export dispatch recovery depends on it; management hopes for improvement within a couple of months.
Working capital is blocked by delayed export shipments, adding interest cost; watch overdue shipment clearance.

CFO position vacant after Anand Krishnan's resignation (last day 11 August 2026); replacement to be announced.
Pectin commercialisation depends on customer consumer testing, with no firm timeline beyond H2 FY27.

507717|2026-06.headline: Dhanuka Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12.56% YoY to Rs 461.93 crore; EBITDA Rs 55.01 crore and PAT Rs 36.30 crore, with FY27 growth guided to small single digits.
507717|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined about 12.56% YoY to Rs 461.93 crore from Rs 528.29 crore, with volume down about 12.7% and value down 12.56%, per management. Management attributed the quarter to delayed monsoon onset, a June rainfall deficit of about 40% (narrowing to 15% by end-July), weak herbicide demand in soybean and cotton states, and price erosion after a short-lived price hike. Management now expects a small single-digit growth in FY27 crop protection, versus the earlier guidance that was cut in the presentation. Biologicals, Bayer-acquired molecules and the Nagpur formulation plant (Rs 200 crore outlay, 23,000 MT) are the main forward-looking items.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from last three years' launches

segments.commentary: North 36%, West 37%, South 18%, East 9% of Q1 turnover.

segments.commentary: Herbicides 42% (down about 25% YoY per analyst), Insecticides 25%, Fungicides 14% (up about 11% YoY per analyst; management did not dispute it, but confirmed the 14% share), Others 19%.

segments.name: Dahej chemical synthesis site
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 26 crore in Q1 vs Rs 16 crore last year; FY27 revenue guidance about Rs 65 crore; FY27 EBITDA expected at about negative Rs 4-5 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crop protection growth guided at a small single-digit rate (Rs 100-150 crore swing cited by analyst; management said small single-digit growth).
Management expects growth in Q2 and Q3 but said Q2 so far has not shown larger growth.
Five new launches planned in coming months: one liquid fertiliser, three fungicides, one herbicide.
Three biological products: two launched, third expected by end-August 2026; two more nutrition biologicals planned in FY27.
Bayer-acquired Iprovalicarb major revenue expected in September (grape season); not significant in FY27 balance sheet for overseas Bayer products.
Dahej EBITDA breakeven seen as difficult; expected negative Rs 4-5 crore for FY27.
Nagpur plant commissioning targeted Q4 FY28 (April 2028); capex about Rs 100 crore-plus in FY27-28 per CFO, with overall outlay up to Rs 200 crore.
Management expects no channel stocking or destocking by end of Q2.
Management said no Bayer-acquired product revenue booked in Q1 for overseas markets; company will address FY27 Bayer contribution separately.
Final dividend Rs 2 per share (100% of face value) approved at 41st AGM; record date and payment not stated.
capex_capacity: Nagpur (Butibori, Maharashtra): land acquired for a formulation plant, 23,000 MT per annum, outlay up to Rs 200 crore, operational by April 2028 (Q4 FY28 per later remark); CGST benefits from Maharashtra government.
Nagpur plant to be significantly automated; CFO indicated capex of about Rs 100 crore-plus in FY27-28; Dahej capex to be communicated later.
Dahej is a chemical synthesis facility in GIDC notified zone; management does not want formulation overlapping with synthesis, hence Nagpur is separate.
Company has four manufacturing facilities and 41 warehouses; reaches 10 million-plus farmers via about 6,500 distributors and 80,000-plus retailers.
Asset-turn assumption (7x-8x raised by analyst) not confirmed; management to revisit around late Q4 when project details are finalised.
Buyback of 5 lakh shares at Rs 1,400 per share absorbed Rs 70 crore; company described as debt-free.
demand_pricing: June rainfall deficit about 40%, narrowing to about 15% by end-July; management said even 1% deficit affects sowing areas.
Herbicide-heavy Q1 hit in Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra (cotton/soybean) with some resowing; South also weak in June and July.
Price hike in April not sustained; prices declined from May, sharply in June and further in July per CFO, described as artificial due to war-related shortage.
Fungicide growth in Q1 attributed to a Japanese fungicide (Nissodium and Conika) on horticulture crops with high vegetable prices.
Management expects no stocking or destocking through end-Q2; channel inventory described as normal rotation after front-loading at end-FY26.
Biologicals: regulation seen favouring organised players as state governments tighten product approvals; prior-year base quarter had a ban with no sales.
Management benchmarks a minimum 20% margin on new launches; 9(3) and nutrition products carry materially higher margins.
Other expenses flat YoY despite 12.56% revenue decline; CFO said expenses are planned ahead of season.

qa_highlights.question: Why such a steep guidance cut, especially on top-line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is giving a realistic picture given monsoon movement; still hopeful of Q2 and Q3 growth, and the outlook was reset to small single-digit growth for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 200 crore Nagpur capex high for a formulation plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant is designed to be significantly automated for safety and efficiency, so higher initial capex; asset turns to be addressed later (late Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Dahej split: revenue, EBITDA, Bayer revenue and royalty?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej revenue Rs 26 crore vs Rs 16 crore, EBITDA under Rs 1 crore vs Rs (-3) crore; Bayer product revenue not booked in Q1; royalty about Rs 4 crore, significantly lower YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory trend for Q1-Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees neither stocking nor destocking; inventory rotating normally with market demand; no change expected by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs price split for the revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said value -12.56% and volume about -12.7%, with price effect negligible; denied a 12% price growth in the books.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 crop protection flattish given biologicals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small single-digit growth overall, after accounting for biologicals rebuilding in the year.

534618|2026-06.headline: Waaree Renewable Q1 FY27 revenue rose 53.23% YoY to INR924.25 crore, with PAT of INR118.97 crore (+37.7%) and unexecuted order book of INR5,300 crore.

The quarter included completion of a 55% stake acquisition in Associated Power Structures Private Limited (APSPL), a Vadodara T&D EPC and tower maker, which consolidated for about 12 days; management said consolidated margin dipped on lower-margin T&D while standalone EPC margin improved. segments.name: APSPL (T&D, 55% stake)
segments.commentary: Integrated substation and transmission EPC plus fabrication and galvanisation, capacity 108,000 MT per annum, executed over 10,461 circuit km of transmission line. Consolidated margin dilution attributed to this business; T&D pipeline cited at about INR20,000 crore, with typical execution of 18-24 months.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: Order of about 1.5 GWh (reported as roughly 300 MW / 1,400-1,520 MWh across combined orders); unexecuted BESS value about INR200 crore. Margin to be in line with company average at order intake.

segments.name: IPP
segments.commentary: 82 MWp of IPP assets in financials; pipeline of about 198 MWp of small plants (20-25 MW each), for Waaree Renewable Technologies itself.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance given; management said it is not giving margin guidance.

Management indicated it would try to maintain around 15% EBITDA margin for FY27 on a consolidated basis, with APSPL likely not in line with the 19% standalone EPC level; to be updated with Q2 results.
Unexecuted INR5,300 crore order book expected to execute over roughly 12-15 months (or 12-18 months), not within the current fiscal year alone.
Management expects further orders during the remaining nine months of FY27 from the pipeline.

IPP pipeline of about 198 MWp of small plants (20-25 MW each); 82 MWp already in financials, some added in Q1.

Building capability for data center EPC; no data center order received yet.
demand_pricing: Standalone EPC margin improved QoQ and stable over two years; consolidated margin fell in percentage terms due to T&D consolidation, while absolute EBITDA rose.
Management said it bids only on projects meeting its risk/reward thresholds despite new entrants in solar EPC.
Working capital cycle cited at 60-90 days on progressive billing with customer advances.

qa_highlights.question: How was the APSPL acquisition financed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 75% debt was used for the acquisition, with the rest self-funded; interest cost will weigh on coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical T&D execution timeline and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: T&D timelines of about 18-24 months, sometimes 9-12 months for shorter lines; T&D pipeline about INR20,000 crore under active pursuit.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and cash flow after APSPL?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle around 60-90 days on progressive billing; management expects operating cash flow to continue, with funding costs rising.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book comes from group entities?

535693|2026-06.headline: Brahmaputra Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.24% YoY to Rs 110.79 crore, with PAT up 9.57% to Rs 16.48 crore.
