qa_highlights.question: Why was net sales of about Rs 329 crore weak when absorption was healthy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to cancellations and terminations for non-payment, mainly at Niyaara, with no launches in the quarter. Gross sales were above Rs 700 crore, and cancelled units were being rebooked at higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 9,600 crore FY27 launch plan on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was largely on track, with most launches planned for Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Vashi margins and structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Economic interest is 90% with a 10% partner, who handles society negotiations and approvals. Margins are expected at 25–30%, with sales at Rs 38,000–40,000 per sq ft on about 1 million sq ft saleable area.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Rs 283 crore cash outflows on the cash flow statement?
qa_highlights.answer: Land payment about Rs 125 crore (Thane), net deposit outflow about Rs 151 crore (including a Noida auction EMD and a Khar redevelopment deposit), and capex about Rs 7 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much construction spend is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah said FY27 construction cost would be about Rs 1,200–1,300 crore, against Rs 226 crore construction cost in Q1 out of Rs 437 crore total spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why has BD lagged peers over the past 1.5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a robust risk framework, due diligence, pricing, title and competitive bidding, and said deals negotiated for 18–24 months are close to closing. It described its stance as prudent rather than conservative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax impact on the ITC proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax outflow is expected on the proceeds, but the amount is still being worked out. The balance about 5% of consideration is subject to conditions and working capital adjustments.

543270|2026-06.headline: MTAR Q1 FY27 revenue rose 130.4% YoY to INR360.7 crore with a 23.5% EBITDA margin; closing order book stated at INR5,143 crore.
543270|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR360.7 crore, up 130.4% YoY from INR156.6 crore, with EBITDA of INR85.1 crore (23.54% margin) and PAT of INR50.2 crore. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 80% revenue growth and a 24% ±100 bps EBITDA margin, and said it expects to do better. Working capital days fell sharply to 59 from 172 days for FY26, and management said debt is near nil after investments. Management highlighted civil nuclear order inflows, fuel cell capacity expansion in three phases, and a new data centre infrastructure product line.

segments.name: Civil nuclear
segments.commentary: Highest-ever order inflow in the quarter for Kaiga 5 & 6; current nuclear order book about INR684 crore, with INR130-140 crore refurbishment orders expected in Q1 FY28 and about INR800 crore total nuclear book targeted. Execution of Kaiga 5 & 6 runs 1-3.5 years; refurbishment orders within 2 years; ramp-up starts H2 FY27.

segments.name: Clean Energy (fuel cells)
segments.commentary: Record order inflows in the quarter. Phase 1 capacity commissioned; Phase 2 due Sept-Oct 2026; Phase 3 (multifold expansion) due March 2027. Data centre infrastructure products entered; first batch of about INR45 crore for export due by March 2027.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: Management expects to double aerospace and defence revenue in FY27, with a 3-4 year ramp. Domestic defence opportunity above INR250 crore, including Tejas Mk-1A actuator assemblies (about INR140-150 crore program value). Oil & gas facility operational by October 2026.

segments.name: Products and others
segments.commentary: Revenue jumped to about INR100 crore in the quarter, roughly 50% of the Clean Energy run-rate per the analyst's framing; management says it will keep growing and H2 will be stronger than H1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 80%, reiterated; management said it is confident of doing better.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 24% ±100 bps; Q1 margin of 23.54% described as in line.
Closing order book target of about INR5,000 crore by FY27 end; Q1 closing book of INR5,143 crore plus about INR800 crore received after quarter end.
Working capital days target about 100 by FY27 end; ROCE target 23% next year.
Capex of about INR500 crore over FY27 and FY28 (70% Clean Energy, 30% other), with spillover into the next 1-2 quarters; asset turnover target 4-6x. FY28 guidance not given formally.
Aerospace and defence: FY30 potential cited at INR600-700 crore; products division potentially above INR1,000 crore.

financial_highlights.change: +130.4% YoY vs INR156.6 crore; highest-ever quarterly revenue
+199.7% YoY vs INR28.4 crore; margin up from 20.11% in Q4 FY26
vs 47.65% in Q1 FY26; attributed to revenue mix
vs INR191.66 crore in last year period
vs 172 days for full FY26; target about 100 days by year end (previously 150-175)

financial_highlights.value: INR423.6 crore as of 30 June 2026; net debt about INR20-30 crore after investments of INR379 crore

540673|2026-06.headline: SIS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.7% YoY to INR 4,604 crore; consolidated EBITDA up 36.2% to INR 207 crore at 4.5% margin.
540673|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR 4,604 crore, up 29.7% YoY and 2.5% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR 207 crore (4.5% margin), flat QoQ but up 36.2% YoY. PAT was INR 101.7 crore (2.2% margin). India Security crossed INR 2,000 crore in quarterly revenue for the first time, while International Security hit its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR 1,982 crore. Management tied the coming quarters to labour code implementation (rules notified 8-9 May 2026) and minimum wage pass-throughs, and announced an open-market buyback of INR 106 crore at a maximum price of INR 478.50.

segments.name: India Security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,004 crore (+37.3% YoY), first quarter above INR 2,000 crore; EBITDA INR 103 crore at 5.1% margin. Management said the acquired A P Securitas business, with revenue INR 332 crore and EBITDA INR 12.2 crore in the quarter, runs at lower margin and will be integrated over 4 to 8 quarters.

segments.name: Facility Management
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 642 crore (+8% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 5.5%, which management described as a normalised new level. Aspirational target is near 6%.

segments.name: International Security (Australia-led)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,982 crore (+31% YoY, +7% constant currency), highest ever quarterly run rate; EBITDA INR 69.6 crore (+52% YoY) at 3.5% margin, down from Q4 as high-margin events fade in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Management expects labour code implementation to be accretive to EBITDA and PAT over the next 3-4 quarters, with impact more visible in Q2 and Q3.
Minimum wage hikes in several states (Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Uttarakhand) reportedly ranged 20% to 47%; management expects more state-level hikes over the next 6-9 months.
India business margins targeted to move from about 5.3-5.4% blended toward 5.5-6%.
Acquired business margins expected to converge toward the group's original margin profile over 4 to 8 quarters through integration and synergies.
Open-market buyback of INR 106 crore, maximum price INR 478.50, expected to open the week after the call; promoters not participating.
capex_capacity: Acquired 51% stake in an entity (A P Securitas referenced) roughly 20% of SIS's size; remaining 49% to be acquired over the next couple of years, with anniversary in 2028.
Cash business IPO: DRHP filed; management is waiting for a more opportune window given peer de-rating, and declined to share its financials.
Buyback: fifth buyback approved; cumulative capital returned would exceed INR 700 crore after completion.
demand_pricing: Contracts have open-book costing and rise-and-fall clauses; minimum wage hikes are passed through to clients, with a time lag from invoicing and customer payment cycles, not tied to contract renewal.
Australia minimum wage rise of 4.75% was flagged by an analyst; management said contracts pass it through via rise-and-fall clauses.

Management says 30-40% of Indian customers use compliant operators versus about 90% in Australia; the new principal-employer definition in the labour codes is expected to shift the cost arbitrage to clients.
SIS manages more than 16,000 contracts in India; no single contract exceeds 1% of revenue.
No labour shortage beyond the usual April-June pre-monsoon seasonal pattern, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What were the revenue and EBITDA of A P Securitas this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue INR 332 crore and EBITDA INR 12.2 crore (CFO Brajesh Kumar).

qa_highlights.question: Did labour shortage affect the business and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing exceptional; the April-June shortage is seasonal and eases by July, in line with prior years.

qa_highlights.question: How will state minimum wage hikes affect SIS and when will they be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Hikes are passed through to clients as a revenue boost, EBITDA-accretive with little gross-margin impact; the Q1 effect is limited since the process began 8 May, with Q2-Q3 more visible.

qa_highlights.question: Are India margins sustainable and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: India blended margin is about 5.3-5.4% (Security 5.1%, FM 5.5%); management said it is sustainable and aims for 5.5-6%.

qa_highlights.question: Australia: will the 4.75% wage hike be passed on only at contract renewal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rise-and-fall clauses allow immediate pass-through, with only a billing and payment lag, not dependent on renewal dates; the Australia CEO was to follow up separately, and the line was disrupted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Updater Services share purchase a treasury operation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is a treasury operation and that it is the only single stock bought so far.

risks_watch: Pace and extent of state-level minimum wage notifications and whether pass-through lags delay margin benefit beyond Q3.
Working capital: DSO rose 3 days to 66 days; management attributes this to seasonality and it needs to revert in later quarters.
International Security margin at 3.5% is sensitive to the fading of Australian Q4 high-margin events and to currency effects.
Integration of the acquired 51% stake, which runs at lower margin than the core security business.
Smaller-operator cost arbitrage narrowing under the new principal-employer rules is management's view; its actual effect on share and pricing is not yet evident.
540673|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on labour code tailwinds, buyback and return ratios. Evasive on the Cash business IPO financials, the Australia wage-pass-through follow-up (line disrupted), and contract-level detail for the Hyderabad business.
key_quotes: So, it is completely designed for our minority shareholders. Promoters are not participating.
This is a tectonic shift. It has not happened before in this industry.
We want to drive SIS into that box of 100 companies in this country which deliver INR 500 crore plus in PAT

543953|2026-06.headline: Khazanchi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 45% YoY to INR586.36 crore and PAT 84% to INR27.83 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.82%.
543953|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 45% YoY to INR586.36 crore, EBITDA rose 89% to INR39.98 crore and PAT rose 84% to INR27.83 crore, with margins expanding 158 bps (EBITDA) and 99 bps (PAT). Management attributed the quarter to the first full quarter of the new flagship showroom and ERP rollout. The company is migrating from BSE SME to the main boards of BSE and NSE, which management expects to complete in about 2 months, and it reiterated a INR5,000 crore revenue target by FY30 with 25-30% growth and B2C reaching ~40% of revenue. Several answers were vague (volume split, store capex, quantum sold), and the call ran on a mix of expansion plans and operating metrics.

financial_highlights.change: +45% YoY vs INR403.84 crore in Q1 FY26
Management said grams/quantum sold implied by ~15% growth; exact grams to be shared later
Inventory turnover days 73 vs 63 in Q4 FY26
Revenue ~5x and PAT ~10x since FY23 (INR481 crore revenue, INR8 crore PAT)

segments.name: B2B (wholesale)
segments.commentary: Management described B2B as the scale and stability base, with ~1,000 clients, none above 5-6% of revenue, and a targeted 25% growth. Working cycle is ~40-45 days. Higher-margin Kundan Jadau and diamond jewellery were added to B2B.

segments.name: B2C (retail)
segments.commentary: Flagship showroom is targeted at ~INR500 crore annual revenue, with management saying it is achieving 80-85% of that; current monthly run-rate is ~INR30-35 crore. Retail working cycle is ~100-120 days. Target is 40% of revenue by FY30, from a current share the company did not state precisely.

guidance_outlook: Revenue target of ~INR5,000 crore by FY30, with growth of 25-30% per year (management said both revenue and PAT CAGR of 25-30%, clarified in the call).
Management now expects ~30% full-year growth if current pace holds, with B2B growing ~25%.
B2C to reach ~40% of revenue by FY30; plan of 8-10 stores over 3-4 years, initially in Tamil Nadu, company-owned only, with later expansion to other states (Andhra named as next).
Main board migration to BSE and NSE: documents to be submitted shortly; completion expected in about 2 months, subject to regulatory approvals.
Management expects positive operating cash flow in FY27 after a negative FY26, as stock build for new stores normalises.
capex_capacity: 8-10 retail stores planned by FY30, a mix of flagship showrooms and minimal-jewellery boutiques; capex per store not defined until formats and venues are finalised.
Flagship showroom is company-owned; management said the model going forward is asset-light, with leased properties for new stores.
Funding: internal accruals first, with debt or other means if needed. Bank limit of INR100 crore; management said the only borrowing is working-capital, with no long-term debt.
Gold savings scheme app and a B2B product-selection app are live; an e-commerce platform for lightweight, minimal, diamond, rose gold and silver jewellery is due shortly.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is strong into the marriage and festive season, and order books are in execution; it did not quantify advance bookings.
Gold price spikes cause a 2-week slowdown in sales, which management says is normal and digested.
Old gold exchange is 15-20% of total sales, up from last year.
Bridal and wedding jewellery is ~60% of sales (management's broad estimate; no exact split is maintained).
Making charges are protected by design differentiation and direct manufacturing, which management says gives better pricing than peers.
Marketing spend is 5-7% of total earnings (management's figure).
Standard lead times range 7-21 days for customised orders, mainly for handmade designs.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the main board migration and when will listing happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Documentation submission is underway and will be completed shortly. Management expects migration to finish in about 2 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the underlying volume growth and grams sold in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quantum growth was around 15%. It deferred the exact gram figure and asked the analyst to email for it.

qa_highlights.question: How is the new flagship performing vs target?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is ~INR500 crore annual revenue, with management reporting 80-85% achievement. Current monthly run-rate is ~INR30-35 crore. No store EBITDA was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% growth target for revenue or PAT, and what is the path to INR5,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both revenue and PAT are targeted at 25-30% growth, and that 5,000 crore is reachable through B2B and B2C growth plus new showrooms by FY30. The answer was not clear on the split.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days and cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Wholesale cycle ~40-45 days, retail ~100-120 days. Management said FY27 cash flow should be positive, though it gave no quantum.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any long-term debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no long-term debt; the INR100 crore bank limit is used only for working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Store capex and format for the 8-10 new stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex per store and format will be defined once venues are finalised. Capex was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Share of B2B revenue from the top 10 clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no single client exceeds 5-6% of total revenue.

risks_watch: Growth targets are not backed by a stated volume/price split or grams sold; the quantum figure was deferred.
Retail working-capital intensity (100-120 day cycle) and rising inventory (INR460 crore) could keep cash flow negative despite the FY27 positive-cash guidance.
Store-level profitability and capex per store are undisclosed; the flagship's store EBITDA was not given.
Gold price volatility and a 2-week demand slowdown after sharp price moves.
Main board migration is subject to regulatory approvals and has not yet been filed.
Competition from large organised chains and regional jewellers; management gave no quantified pricing data.
543953|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top-line and margin trend, with repeated reference to the INR5,000 crore FY30 target. Answers on store capex, store-level economics, grams sold and the exact growth split were vague or deferred, and the 25-30% target was clarified mid-call (both revenue and PAT).

519126|2026-06.headline: Hindustan Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 33% YoY to INR42.8 crore, a record, while footwear cost pressure of ~INR6 crore weighed; FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed.
519126|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 18% YoY to INR1,207 crore and EBITDA rose 26% to INR106.3 crore, with PBT up 33% to INR56.6 crore. Footwear absorbed about INR6 crore of raw material, freight and minimum-wage cost pressure, with the Haryana wage hike the main driver. Management reaffirmed FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore and announced INR190 crore of new projects, taking FY27 commitments to INR340 crore plus INR150 crore carried forward. A Silvassa plant disruption from July rains is expected to be fully resolved by end-August.

financial_highlights.metric: Footwear cost pressure (raw material, freight, wages)

segments.name: Home & Personal Care
segments.commentary: Running at maximum capacity with a record quarter; Aurangabad personal care integration complete. Silvassa brownfield expected to start in Q2 FY27 and Lucknow greenfield later this year. INR50 crore Lucknow project (bar and liquid lines) announced.

segments.name: Food & Beverages
segments.commentary: Coimbatore, Nashik and Mysuru at record production; beverages had an excellent season. INR210 crore of beverage projects across Coimbatore, Mysuru, Goa, Aurangabad and Hyderabad, expected online by Dec/Jan. Greek yogurt facility being added in Goa.

segments.name: Ice Cream
segments.commentary: Strong summer with record volumes; Panipat facility commissioned in Q1. INR80 crore Panipat expansion announced; Nashik cone and ice cream utilisation improving with new customers.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Q1 utilisation was poor due to imported material and freight disruption, and cost pressure hit margins. Management says utilisation is about 80-90% from August; order book full from Q2 FY27 and the business is expected to pay off in H2 FY27. Price pass-through now being achieved from Q1 onward per management.

segments.name: Healthcare / OTC Pharma
segments.commentary: Baddi site approved; commercial production started for 2 more multinational companies. Management expects Baddi to reach 100% utilisation within 6-12 months. Class III medical device certification started at Chennai.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed; management said it is too early to signal the lower end and will revisit in a couple of quarters.
Capacity commercialisation of more than INR500 crore expected in FY27 including carry-forward projects.
Management expects footwear to return to profitability in coming months and to pay off in H2 FY27.
Profit growth expected to outpace revenue growth because customers increasingly supply raw and packing material, so only conversion cost is booked as revenue.
Continued 1:1 debt-equity funding for projects; growth to rely on internal accruals with ROCE threshold of 18%.
capex_capacity: FY27 new project commitments of INR340 crore (INR190 crore newly authorised), plus INR150 crore carried forward from FY26.
Breakdown: Food & Beverages INR210 crore; Ice Cream INR80 crore (Panipat); Home & Personal Care INR50 crore (Lucknow).
Silvassa flood disruption from July rains: partially restored, fully operational by end-August; management says it is insured and has no material long-term impact.
Lucknow greenfield facility due for commissioning later in FY27; Silvassa brownfield to start in Q2 FY27.
Pipeline of inquiries about INR1,000 crore, not yet confirmed; policy is to announce capex only after signing.
demand_pricing: Footwear raw material prices rose ~50-60% (polymer, fabric) and freight rose up to 4x; footwear pricing is fixed 6-12 months ahead, so costs could not be passed through in Q1.
Haryana/NCR minimum wage hike of ~30% hit footwear and was described as a local, one-off issue; other contracts have pass-through clauses.
Footwear order book full for Q2 FY27 onward, with new domestic and multinational customer wins and some lapsed customers returning.
HPC demand has improved materially over the last three months per management, with liquid home care volumes growing near double digits.
US personal care order is on hold due to tariff ambiguity and freight; product development, trials and mould investment are complete.
Middle East export discussions (UAE, Saudi Arabia) put on hold; Dr. Scholl portfolio exported to UK, EU, Australia, NZ and Japan.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company negotiate better terms with customers given GST inversion and weakening competition, and is there any asset revaluation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said GST inversion is not the main driver of outsourcing and that the company is better placed to handle it. Assets have not been revalued and the business model does not depend on it; the value sits on the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Can footwear raw-material cost increases be built into contracts structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shoe contracts are set 6-8 months ahead with fixed prices, so mid-season changes are not industry practice. Brands have agreed to absorb some cost for the coming season, and pass-through is now being achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the INR340 crore of new projects by segment.
qa_highlights.answer: Food & Beverages INR210 crore across five units, Ice Cream INR80 crore at Panipat, and HPC INR50 crore at Lucknow for a bar and liquid line.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear utilisation and order book quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation was poor; utilisation is about 80-90% from August with a full order book and new logos, with the business expected to pay off in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear employee cost share and profit impact of INR210 crore beverage capex at 18% ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Footwear employee cost is about 35-40% of Q1 total. Beverage units are expected online by Dec/Jan on anchor-tenant basis; the analyst's ROCE maths was corrected to EBIT, with 1:1 debt-equity funding implying interest outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block growth outlook over 3-5 years versus sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross block will grow faster than sales because customer-supplied raw material means only conversion cost is booked as revenue. It expects to fund growth from internal accruals at 1:1 leverage with an 18% ROCE threshold.

risks_watch: Footwear margin recovery depends on brands absorbing cost and on Middle East-driven material and freight costs easing; ~INR6 crore hit in Q1.
Silvassa restoration by end-August and insurance recovery; watch for any Q2 output shortfall.
Execution of INR500 crore capex this year, and whether Lucknow and Silvassa start on time.
US tariff ambiguity keeps personal care export orders on hold.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation for shared sites; footwear ROCE is below the 18% threshold, per management.

539807|2026-06.headline: Gross revenue rose 109% YoY to INR 2,680 crore and PAT rose 45% to INR 85 crore, while net revenue fell 3% to INR 147 crore.
539807|2026-06.overview: AvenuesAI (formerly Infibeam Avenues) reported Q1 FY27 gross revenue of INR 2,680 crore (+109% YoY) and PAT of INR 85 crore (+45% YoY), with EBITDA excluding other income of INR 100 crore (+41% YoY). Net revenue was INR 147 crore, down 3% YoY, and management said take rates have compressed slightly. Management guided FY27 consolidated gross revenue to INR 11,000–13,000 crore (about 35%+ growth) and EPS to INR 8.75–9.50 on the post-split face value of INR 10. The company also announced the merger of its AI subsidiary Neuromind and Phronetic AI into the parent, and a face value change from INR 1 to INR 10.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY (about -1% QoQ per analyst question, not confirmed by management)
vs 47% in Q1 FY26 (as cited by analyst and confirmed by CFO)

segments.name: Payments (CCAvenue, BillAvenue, ResAvenue)
segments.commentary: Core merchant acquiring; transaction volume INR 1,479 billion (+74% YoY) across utilities, government, retail, B2B and hospitality. Management says UPI is about 22% of transactions and online acquiring market share is 8-10%.

segments.name: Consumer (Rediff, RediffPay, RediffOne)
segments.commentary: RediffPay is moving out of CUG into production this month. FY27 guidance assumes no meaningful contribution from RediffPay. RediffOne is being positioned as an enterprise operating platform.

segments.name: Intelligence (Phronetic AI / Neuromind)
segments.commentary: PayCentral, described as an agentic payment platform built on Google's Agent Payments Protocol, is in early days. Neuromind is to be merged into AvenuesAI; on-prem SLM products are in early phases with impact expected 9-18 months out.

segments.name: Credit (asset-light distribution)
segments.commentary: Proposed investment of up to 2.5% in RatnaFin Capital (NBFC) and up to 7% in Online PSB Loans. Lending risk is said to remain with regulated partners; no revenue contribution quantified.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated gross revenue guided at INR 11,000–13,000 crore, about 35% growth and above.
FY27 EPS guided at INR 8.75–9.50, on the post-corporate-action face value of INR 10.
Management says the cost base is front-loaded for AI, international expansion and financial services, and it is not building for a short-term margin spike.
EBITDA margin 'guardrail' of about 15% set by management, described as a floor rather than a target.
Management wants investors to focus on net revenue, not gross revenue, as the better indicator of progress.
Meaningful e-commerce platform/AI rewards results are expected to show up in Q3–Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Management ruled out large data-centre investments (hundreds of MW); it may invest selectively in smaller data-centre capacity.
Focus is on application-layer SLMs and transaction intelligence scores built on the company's transaction graph data.
Licences received: in-principle approval from Central Bank of UAE for Retail Payment Services (Cat III), and RBI authorisation to set up a prepaid payment instrument system in India.
Management said it has US expansion aspirations this year.
demand_pricing: Take rates compressed slightly, which management cited as the main reason net revenue fell 3% YoY.
Management said UPI MDR for businesses is expected on large merchants and high-value transactions, but the Act is still awaiting Rajya Sabha, presidential assent and gazette notification.
Shiprocket Checkout integration gives same-day settlement, international payments, no-cost EMI and payment links to B2C and SME merchants.
Credit distribution through RatnaFin and OPL is expected to bring merchant financing, checkout financing and working capital products to the CCAvenue ecosystem.
Management says Apple Pay and Samsung Pay are enabled on the platform; it operates on the acquiring side.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Neuromind merger and face value change on the Rediff DRHP timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the corporate action has no bearing on the Rediff filing, which it called a separate event. It said the process is at an early stage and some updates are on the SEBI website.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant onboarding traction on PayCentral and whether MDR is an opportunity or a threat given a 8-10% share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PayCentral is early, with the Indian protocol working well and international growth faster. It said MDR is positive but not finalised, and the company sees no consolidation threat on the acquiring side.

qa_highlights.question: Why EBITDA rose while net revenue fell, and should investors focus on net or gross revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investors should focus on net revenue, and the EBITDA increase came from lower expenses. The CFO said EBITDA rose 41% YoY and margin moved from 47% to 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EPS guidance flat when PAT margin is about 57%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will protect core earnings and reinvest incremental accruals into AI, transaction intelligence and new revenue streams. It said the 2027–2029 ambition is a strong earnings base plus a large AI-led business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI infrastructure plan and the expected returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management ruled out large data-centre capex. It is focused on transaction intelligence scores, financial behaviour graphs and SLM application layers, which it said LLMs cannot replicate because they lack the data.

qa_highlights.question: Top-5 client concentration and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the strategy is to go horizontal with a larger merchant base, and that international focus is on larger clients. It did not give a top-5 revenue share.

risks_watch: Net revenue fell 3% YoY, so gross growth is not translating to net revenue; watch take-rate trend.
FY27 EPS guidance (INR 8.75–9.50) is flat in a year where revenue is guided up about 35%; management is reinvesting incremental accruals.
MDR monetisation timing and pricing are uncertain pending the Act's final notification; competitive response from large incumbents is a risk.
Middle East exposure (UAE, Saudi) may be affected by the regional conflict, per management.
Rediff DRHP timing and the merger of AI subsidiaries; promoter stake increase has not been committed to a timeline.
Credit distribution (RatnaFin, OPL) depends on closing; no revenue contribution has been quantified.

543263|2026-06.headline: SMC Global Q1 FY27 consolidated operating income rose 21.2% YoY to ₹515.1 crore and PAT rose 22.3% to ₹36.7 crore.
543263|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating income reached ₹515.1 crore (+21.2% YoY) with EBITDA of ₹107 crore (+6.9% YoY, 20.9% margin) and PAT of ₹36.7 crore versus ₹30 crore in Q1 FY26. Broking, distribution and trading drove growth, with cash-market mix rising and derivatives softer. Insurance broking revenue grew 44.4% but segment EBIT was only ₹1.6 crore due to investment in manpower. The NBFC segment's AUM fell QoQ to ₹1,025 crore, and management is now targeting a lower year-end AUM than earlier guidance implied.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹30 crore in Q1 FY26, +22.3% YoY

segments.name: Broking, distribution & trading
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹316.3 crore (+15.1% YoY) and EBIT ₹74.3 crore (+17.6% YoY); 13.8 lakh client accounts including StoxKart and 92,129 active SIPs. Cash-market brokerage share reportedly rose from 45% to 55%.

segments.name: Insurance broking
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹167.3 crore (+44.4% YoY) with EBIT of ₹1.6 crore; gross premium ₹759 crore, 2.7 lakh policies, 16,747 POS agents. Non-life is about 90% of premium; EBIT moderated on manpower investment.

segments.name: Financing (NBFC, Moneywise)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹46.5 crore and EBIT ₹26.1 crore; AUM ₹1,025 crore across 40 branches in 7 states. Secured book is 75% of AUM; LAP (about ₹50 crore) and unsecured business loans (about ₹40 crore) declined in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: NBFC AUM expected to close FY27 at ₹1,250-1,300 crore, versus the earlier guidance of about 25% growth that management acknowledged was missed.
NBFC AUM longer-term aim is 20-25% CAGR, but management said investors should wait a year or two because of run-off from discontinued products.
Cost of funds fell about 25 bps in the quarter; management expects NIM to rise gradually over coming years on higher-yield retail mix.
Management expects Q2 to be 'much better' and the coming year to be much better than last year, citing market activity.
Long-term target of about 20% revenue CAGR; management cited a five-year revenue range of ₹6,000-8,000 crore and PAT rising from ₹103 crore to about ₹170 crore, but declined to give formal figures.
StoxKart revenue has increased about four times YoY, and management is positive on its subscription model.
capex_capacity: Investment in technology and AI: in-app AI chatbot on a proprietary language model, AI-based algo platform launched; AI insights feature in mobile app in testing with launch expected soon.
Insurance broking spending on manpower in corporate and life insurance, plus distribution capacity and technology ahead of a reinsurance opportunity after composite broker upgrade.
Distribution network: 16,747 POS/cost network, 385 Motor Insurance Service Providers, 40 NBFC branches across 7 states.
demand_pricing: Management attributed broking growth to Nifty and Sensex gains of about 6-7%, DII buying above ₹2 lakh crore against FPI selling of about ₹1.5 lakh crore, and a shift from derivatives to cash market.
MTF and T+5 book rose from ₹760 crore to over ₹900 crore.
StoxKart added about 26,000 subscription clients in the quarter; its revenue was about ₹20 crore in Q1 FY27, per management.
Mutual fund AUM growth came partly from market appreciation and partly from net mobilisation through training, investor awareness and the Easy Invest digital platform.
NBFC: secured retail products (micro LAP, gold loan) are growing; yields are rising as the mix shifts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC AUM miss the earlier ~25% growth guidance, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Gupta said AUM was ₹1,025 crore versus ₹1,118 crore in March 2026. LAP (about ₹50 crore) and unsecured business loans (about ₹40 crore) declined, and management still expects ₹1,250-1,300 crore by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What drove broking revenue growth despite a weaker derivatives environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Garg cited index gains of about 6-7%, DII inflows, lower crude and easing geopolitics, which shifted activity to cash and delivery. He said the cash brokerage share rose from 45% to 55%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove mutual fund AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Anurag Bansal said MF AUM rose from ₹4,294 crore to ₹4,787 crore (about 11.5%), helped by training, investor awareness and Easy Invest, with part of the gain from market appreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did insurance EBIT moderate while revenue grew?
qa_highlights.answer: Sakshi Mehta said spending was mainly on corporate and life insurance manpower, and operating leverage is expected in future quarters. Non-life is about 90% of premium.

qa_highlights.question: How will NBFC funding cost and NIM trend in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Gupta said weighted cost of funds fell about 25 bps, and NIM is expected to grow gradually as the yield mix improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the five-year outlook and quantitative target?
qa_highlights.answer: Subhash Chand Aggarwal cited 20% CAGR and a ₹6,000-8,000 crore revenue range in five years, and PAT of ₹170 crore versus ₹103 crore last year, but declined to give formal figures.

544088|2026-06.headline: Medi Assist Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 24.1% YoY to INR236.5 crore, with operating EBITDA margin at 20.3% and retention down to 90.2%.
544088|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue grew 24.1% YoY to INR236.5 crore and group revenue grew 25.5%, while operating EBITDA rose 14.3% to INR48 crore at a 20.3% margin. Reported PAT was INR27.6 crore, or INR24.5 crore excluding a one-time INR3.1 crore derivative gain. Retention fell to 90.2% in the quarter, which management attributed to Paramount book transition, portfolio rationalisation and a high base. Management also announced the separation of Chairman and CEO roles, with Dr. Chhatwal moving to Non-Executive Chairman subject to AGM approval on 8 September.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating revenue (revenue from contracts, excl. other income)

financial_highlights.change: Includes one-time INR3.1 crore derivative gain; normative PAT INR24.5 crore

segments.name: Group TPA
segments.commentary: Revenue INR166 crore, up 25.5% YoY, with group market share at 37.6%. Same-store growth averaged about 7-8%, slower in large IT companies and faster elsewhere.

segments.name: Retail TPA
segments.commentary: Retail TPA-model revenue INR23.4 crore, up 13.1% YoY. Management says platform-administered retail premiums reached over INR4,254 crore, about 29% market share, versus INR521 crore TPA-model premiums.

segments.name: Government
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28.5 crore, up 35.3% YoY, now across 16 states; management called it margin accretive and said it serves over 31 crore members across 12 states and 4 UTs under TPA model.

segments.name: International (Mayfair)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR10.1 crore, down 5.2% YoY, hit by softness in student, leisure and marine volumes. Ownership raised to 91.75%; first technology contract went live in Thailand from 1 July 2026.

segments.name: Technology SaaS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR7.8 crore, up 55.5% YoY, 3.3% of consolidated revenue. Fraud savings from MAven Guard exceeded INR183 crore in Q1; 7 insurers contracted across MAven, MAtrix and Magnum stacks.

guidance_outlook: Complete the Paramount integration: over 95% of group claims and over 80% of retail claims were on MAtrix at Q1 end, with the balance targeted for Q2 FY27.
Management expects Paramount-related retention drag to normalise through FY27 and EBITDA margin to return towards the pre-integration 22-23% level by the end of FY27.
Management says group and retail will grow at par with or faster than the market; government growth is opportunistic.
Management expects technology and international to become meaningful contributors to growth and EBITDA margin over time, funded from operating cash flows.
capex_capacity: Company spent about INR24.5 crore on its AI stack over the last six quarters under a Board-approved roadmap, funded from operating cash flows.
MAtrix implementation at Star crossed 90%.
Platform processed over 186,000 pre-authorisations within 5 minutes in Q1; Raksha Prime delivered zero-wait discharge for over 87,000 members across 6,000 hospitals.
Company remains debt-free.
demand_pricing: Retention at 90.2% in Q1, below the historical 93-94%, due to onboarding challenges with a large acquired book, portfolio rationalisation and a higher base.
Management says its PSU group premium growth of 28.9% compares with industry PSU group premiums down about 1.5%, while overall group health industry growth was about 14%.
DSO improved 4.5 percentage points versus the prior-year trend for the quarter, on a higher receivables base.
Revenue per average headcount on non-government contracts was INR13.2 lakh annualised.
Management said international Q1 is not representative, citing softness in student, leisure and marine volumes.

qa_highlights.question: How should retail business trajectory be interpreted, given the traditional TPA model looks plateaued while technology grows fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TPA-model retail line is reported narrowly, so it should be viewed alongside platform and technology revenue, which together indicate market-share gains. Platform-administered retail premiums are over INR4,254 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a margin recovery to 23%, and is FY27 likely to be a record profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the immediate priority is finishing Paramount integration and returning to the 22-23% margin band towards the end of FY27. It did not give a FY27 profit target and does not break out margins by line of business.

qa_highlights.question: Does government business strain working capital, and should revenue from it be capped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government collections are the safest as they come from state and central governments, and it is margin accretive. Consolidated DSOs include government and are improving.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic growth of the legacy group TPA book, and what is the outcome-based contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retention is about 90%, same-store growth is about 7-8%, and new business seasonality distorts quarterly figures. It declined to give the outcome-based contract details beyond saying it is tied to fraud, waste and abuse outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk of PSU TPA in-housing (HITPA) shifting premiums away from Medi Assist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not comment on specific TPAs, that the policyholder-choice regulation supports it, and that its share of wallet has improved in both PSU and private group.

qa_highlights.question: What is NPS Swasthya and what is the opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is the health benefit administrator and technology platform connecting NPS members, CRAs, pension funds, insurers and networks, and that it is at an early stage with potential platform and incremental TPA revenue.

risks_watch: Group retention at 90.2% versus the historical 93-94%; management did not disclose a breakdown of the retention figure.
Paramount integration completion and the target to move the remaining claims to the MAtrix stack in Q2 FY27.
PSU in-housing (HITPA) trend could shift group premiums away from the company.
International revenue fell 5.2% YoY; student, leisure and marine volumes are soft.
Management did not provide a separate depreciation breakdown; this was deferred offline.

532899|2026-06.headline: Kaveri Seed Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 815 crore from Rs 945 crore (about -14%) on a weak El Nino monsoon, with EBITDA margin held near 35%.
532899|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 815 crore against Rs 945 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA at Rs 285 crore (vs Rs 332 crore) and net profit at Rs 271.3 crore (vs Rs 316 crore) as stated on the call. Management attributed the decline to a delayed, deficient monsoon that shortened the sowing window, cutting maize sales in Karnataka and weakening demand in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat. Cotton was flat YoY at Rs 213.43 crore while non-cotton was Rs 601.57 crore, and new products gained share in cotton and maize. Management said the quarter's margin was helped by lower production cost (down 4-5%) and that inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY, prompting lower production next year.

financial_highlights.change: same as last year, management said slightly above
about Rs 265-270 crore as of 30 June

segments.name: Cotton
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 213.43 crore, flat YoY. New cotton products were 37% of cotton sales vs 22% last year; North India (Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) roughly doubled from a small base, while Gujarat and Maharashtra were hit by low rain and illegal Bt seed.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Sales fell sharply (about 40% decline per analyst question, not disputed by management); Karnataka sowing was about one-fifth done by mid-June. New single-cross hybrids are over 20% of maize sales.

segments.name: Hybrid rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 247.07 crore, the largest non-cotton segment. Two new hybrids KRH7344 and KRH7227 launched this season contributed 62% of new-product sales in rice.

segments.name: Selection rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 159.07 crore, marginal YoY growth despite poor rain in rice sowing areas.

segments.name: Bajra
segments.commentary: New hybrids are 65% of Bajra volumes, up from 61%.

segments.name: Vegetables
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 15.08 crore; management called it a small segment with some spillover possible in Q2 if rain improves.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the rest of FY27 quarters to be higher than the prior year's comparable quarters, with Karnataka recovery and Rabi maize supporting H2; the Q1 revenue gap is expected to narrow but no full recovery was committed.
Management said Q2 margins would be lower than Q1 margins, and that the YoY revenue gap would narrow, not turn positive, within FY27.
Karnataka Kharif recovery: about 1,500 tonnes sold this year vs about 2,600 tonnes last year, a gap of 1,100-1,200 tonnes worth about Rs 40-60 crore (figures given inconsistently on the call).
Export target of Rs 100 crore in vegetables and other crops within about 3 years; export margin expected at 25-30%, in line with current levels.
Management reiterated a long-term growth target of 15-18% (earlier referenced as 18-20%) over the next 2-3 years, with growth expected to return to last year's level.
Cash expected to rise only by about Rs 20-30 crore by Q2 to close to Rs 300 crore; any buyback is subject to a Board decision, with no amount decided.
capex_capacity: Inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY because production was taken up on expectations of a good El Nino-era season; management said production will be reduced next year.
Cost of production is down 4-5% YoY while dealer-level realisations are down 2-3%; management said FY28 production will be minimal and cost per unit should stay at last year's level.
Product pipeline described as among the best in 10 years, with Madhya Pradesh hybrids newer and not yet at scale.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit to June 15 shortened the Kharif sowing window and farmers bought fewer premium products; Karnataka tanks now filling after July rains, which management expects to support maize in Q2-Q3.
Maize price rose to about Rs 27-28 from Rs 16-17 at the start of the season, which management expects to support Rabi demand.
Cotton MRP is government-capped; management said Kaveri realises higher prices than many peers in the top three cotton segments.
Competition: illegal Bt cotton and smaller players have grown; management said no new hybrids from peers have taken share in the last 3-4 years, and that Kaveri has lost cotton share over 7-8 years.
Management said subsidiaries (sales of about 10-12 lakh cotton packets this year) operate as separate competitors, and that their revenue is booked independently.

544055|2026-06.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q1 FY27: record Q1 disbursement of INR2,644 crore, cost of funds down to 10.13%, credit cost 2.6%, and AUM growth guidance raised to 20%.
544055|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the start of an execution-led turnaround, with disbursements of INR2,644 crore (about 49% above Q1 FY26) and collection efficiency near 98%. Cost of funds fell 14 bps QoQ to 10.13% before the benefit of the AA- CRISIL upgrade, and credit cost eased to 2.6% from 2.8%. PPOP rose about 43% YoY and 3% QoQ, and AUM grew 18% YoY. Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 20%, ROA to the upper end of 3.3%, and ROE to around 18%, and said NIM expansion would show from Q2.

financial_highlights.change: about 49% above Q1 FY26; highest Q1 ever

financial_highlights.value: Up about 43% YoY and about 3% QoQ
Flat QoQ; management cited about 50 bps YoY expansion in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Full-year FY27 NIM guided 12.3%-12.5%; management said 12.5% upper end is achievable

segments.name: Joint Liability Group (JLG)
segments.commentary: Yield on group loans about 24.85% after a rate hike from 23.5% at end of Q1. Remains one of three priority products.

segments.name: Individual loans
segments.commentary: About INR3,200 crore book with 0.02% 30+ delinquency and no 60+ or 90+. Yield about 23.5%. Built on a creamy layer of about 8.5-9 lakh customers with 700+ scores. Repayments are 100% digital.

segments.name: Gold loans (referral and co-lending)
segments.commentary: Disbursing about INR100 crore per month since April; about INR350-360 crore disbursed to date. Q1 was almost entirely referral business. Co-lending split is 60% on Muthoot Microfin's book and 40% on the parent's book. Referral earns 1.5%.

segments.name: Loan against property and consumer durables
segments.commentary: LAP yield 18%-22%. Consumer durable loans are a pilot of about INR500 crore at 22%-23% yield, funded through CP at about 8.1%-8.2%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance raised to 20% for FY27.
Disbursement plan exceeds INR12,000 crore for FY27, averaging about INR1,000 crore per month.
Cost of funds targeted to reach single digits by end of FY27, with AA- rating benefit still to flow through.
FY27 ROA guided at 3.3% (upper end expected), ROE around 18% (upper end). Management expects 4%-4.5% ROA within about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.
Credit cost guidance of 2.7%-3.5% for FY27, now expected to be better; long-term normalised range 2%-2.25%.
NIM guidance 12.3%-12.5%; NIM expansion expected from Q2 as liquidity drag eases.
Digital collection to reach about 75% by 2030, possibly earlier. Currently about 40%, improving about 6% per quarter.
Branch count to reach 1,740-1,750 by end FY27 from about 1,670 now.
capex_capacity: Branches about 1,670 now, targeted at 1,740-1,750 by end FY27. Expansion focus on Andhra Pradesh and Assam, plus north, east and west geographies.
AUM per branch rose to INR8.65 crore from about INR7 crore a year ago. Management targets INR12-13 crore per branch.
Gold loans use parent Muthoot Finance branches for storage and assessment, so no separate gold branch capex is needed.
Consumer durables pilot of INR500 crore to be expanded depending on results.
demand_pricing: Industry AUM contracted, but quality is improving. Management says larger, well-capitalised players are gaining share. Industry active customers have fallen from about 8 crore at peak to about 6 crore.
Muthoot's active customers fell 0.6% QoQ and declined YoY. Management attributes this to write-offs and closures and says new customer acquisition should lift the base from Q2.
Group yield raised to 24.85% from 23.5% at end of Q1, with no further hike planned for now. Management said the benefit should go to NIM rather than customers.

Liquidity is ample. About INR5,000 crore of sanctions are in hand, plus INR1,000 crore under CGFMU of which only INR200 crore has been drawn. About 20% of AUM is targeted for CGFMU cover; the application is pending.
Management said El Nino rainfall deficit fell from 43% to about 12%. Less than 2% of customers are directly exposed to agri activity in sensitive regions.

qa_highlights.question: Can disbursement return to INR1,000 crore per month, and can AUM growth exceed 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,000 crore per month is achievable, with FY27 disbursement above INR12,000 crore. Q1 at INR2,644 crore was the slowest quarter, and Q2 onward should rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended yield, given that the incremental cost of borrowing fell while NIM stayed flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended portfolio yield is about 23%. Reported yield is diluted by non-performing assets in the denominator. Management said Q1 NIM is up about 50 bps YoY, and yield expansion will follow as collections from NPAs improve.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Assam flood or the broader monsoon risk affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has no exposure to upper Assam, where floods are seasonal, and its lower-Assam portfolio is unaffected so far. Natural calamity insurance covers all customers, including drought.

qa_highlights.question: How do the direct assignment (DA) income and gold referral and co-lending work?
qa_highlights.answer: DA income is booked under net gain on fair value changes, not interest income. Q1 DA was about INR355 crore, and FY26 DA was about INR1,600 crore. Gold co-lending began only at quarter-end, so about 98% of Q1 gold business was referral.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 2.7%-3.5% has been beaten, with Q1 at 2.6%. Management expects FY27 to come in below 2.7%, with a long-term normal of 2%-2.25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and ROA/ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM guidance is 12.3%-12.5%, with the upper end expected. FY27 ROA is guided at 3.3% (upper end) and ROE at about 18%. Management targets 4%-4.5% ROA in about 18 months and about 5% by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What are the MFI vs non-MFI mix targets?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM mix is at 76:24 (JLG to non-JLG) now and is expected to end FY27 at about 70:30. Management's long-term target is 55:45 on AUM and 60:40 on balance sheet after DA.

506194|2026-06.headline: Arihant Superstructures Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 132 crore, with EBITDA margin at 21% and PAT at INR 10 crore.
506194|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 sales bookings were 221 units (2.31 lakh sq ft), up 15% YoY in area and value to INR 173 crore, with average realisation flat at INR 7,500 per sq ft. Consolidated operating revenue reached INR 132 crore (up 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 28 crore (21% margin) and PAT INR 10 crore (7.4% margin). Net debt stood at INR 818 crore against net worth of INR 460 crore, and management reiterated plans to reduce debt from next year while funding hotel and club assets. Management guided to 2,500 unit deliveries by FY27-end and said no new land acquisitions are planned this year.

segments.name: Residential (sales)
segments.commentary: 221 units booked for 2.31 lakh sq ft at a flat average of INR 7,500 per sq ft; average ticket size about INR 78 lakh per unit. Project mix is 41% luxury per management's presentation.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Hotel at World Villas (5-star, Radisson) is concluded; second hotel near Imagicaa is in closing. Hospitality capital deployed so far is INR 35-40 crore (about 7% of capital employed of INR 730 crore), with INR 500 crore total planned over three years for hotels and club.

guidance_outlook: Deliver 2,500 units by end of FY27; expects FY27 numbers a little above FY26, but not exponential growth.
Blended EBITDA margin expected to move towards 30-35% once Town Villas and villa projects contribute largely; management said at least a 10 percentage point rise is achievable over about 12 months.
Blended PAT margin expected to exceed 20% over roughly two years.
Hotels expected to contribute INR 50 crore+ PAT per year from the third or fourth year; hospitality payback projected at 8-9 years.
Debt-to-equity expected to decline gradually as projects mature, with debt repayment focused on Arihant Advika, Vashi once cash flows allow.
Average ticket size expected to rise to INR 95 lakh-1 crore as premium mix grows; target project mix 40-45% premium, 30-35% middle income, 20% affordable.
Pre-sales convert to revenue in about 90 days on average under percentage-of-completion method.
capex_capacity: Occupancy certificates received for Arihant 5 Anaika, Arihant 6 Anaika, Arihant Anant and Arihant Aaradhya Phase 1, with about 1,495 units completed and ready for possession in coming quarters.
No new land acquisition or business development capital planned for FY27; focus on executing the INR 14,000 crore project portfolio, a 6-7 year cycle, with asset-light deals possible.
Hospitality and club program totals about INR 500 crore over three years, funded by debt or internal resources.
Average project timeline is about 4 years (range 3-5 years from start to completion).
demand_pricing: Management says demand is strongest below INR 5 crore; INR 10-30 crore tickets in Mumbai are seeing a slowdown. Overall market is normalising, with sales velocity moderate due to geopolitics, crude and FX moves, and large projects.
Navi Mumbai's share of the MMR market rose from 12% to 17% over three years, with Thane and Kalyan losing share.
Labour and skill shortages and higher construction costs are raising input costs; management says inventory on hand offsets this with no balance-sheet impact.

Blended margin fell to about 9% this quarter from 13-14% in prior years; affordable projects (below INR 5,000 per sq ft) earn single-digit to 9-10% margins, middle income up to 15%, and premium around 20% PAT.
Management is holding price rather than chasing volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much of current industry volume growth is structural, and what indicators are monitored?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a similar behaviour over the next four quarters and a slightly higher than last year performance, but not exponential growth this year. Indirect expenses are being held at roughly the same level.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost saving is captured and what further reduction is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost reduction is not possible as HR costs are held flat year on year. Rising construction costs are offset by existing inventory, and margins should stay steady for the next three to four quarters as older projects roll off.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for converting pre-sales into revenue, given pre-sales of INR 1,731 million vs reported revenue of INR 1,316 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-sales take about 90 days on average to enter revenue recognition under percentage-of-completion, covering owner contribution, agreement, registration and NOCs.

qa_highlights.question: Are new land acquisitions attractive given higher costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No new capital investment programme for business development this year; the INR 14,000 crore project pipeline takes 6-7 years to complete. Only asset-light opportunities may be considered.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the premium share of the project mix reach, and will geography be diversified?
qa_highlights.answer: Target mix is 40-45% premium, 30-35% middle income and 20% affordable. No plans to expand to new cities; management says MMR (including Mumbai 3.0, twice the size of Mumbai city) is large enough.

qa_highlights.question: What drives average realisation, and how do margins and ROCE evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: New premium additions would raise average rates; otherwise, about 10% growth on current mix. Margins are expected to rise toward 30-35% EBITDA with villa projects; ROCE is said to be on an increasing trajectory on a project basis. Capital employed of INR 730 crore is 90-93% residential.

risks_watch: Blended margin compression: the quarter's blended margin fell to about 9% from 13-14% in prior years, and management's margin recovery depends on villa and premium projects ramping up.
Net debt of INR 818 crore against net worth of INR 460 crore; debt reduction depends on completions at Arihant Advika, Vashi, offset by new loans for hotels and club.
Rising construction and labour costs from geopolitical factors and labour shortages; management says inventory offsets this, but no quantification was given.
Sales slowdown above INR 10 crore ticket sizes in Mumbai and moderating market velocity.
Concentration in MMR with no geographic diversification; hospitality execution and operator tie-ups are still ahead.
Management claims of 'no competition' for large hotels in Lonavala, Karjat and Mumbai and of 30-35% EBITDA margins are forward-looking and unquantified in the call.
506194|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand in MMR and project completions, and on margin recovery, but cautious on volume growth ("very exponential growth ... will not be able to witness in this financial year"). Answers on margin and debt timelines were vague and several were given as 'can be' or 'expected' without figures.

505533|2026-06.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 7.36 billion with SSSG of 4.3%, though operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable amid inflation.
505533|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR 7.36 billion, up 12% YoY, with same-store sales growth of 4.3% and positive SSSG in all three months. Growth was guest-count led, with double-digit footfall growth and the South turning SSSG-positive. Operating EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 946 million, but the operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable as over 200 bps of inflation (fuel, food, packaging, utilities, labour) was absorbed. Management said Q1 marks the peak of gross margin pressure and expects improvement from here, while restaurant additions were only 5 in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Positive in all three months; May and June mid-single-digit

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Management described West as continuing to deliver a very strong performance, with growth aided by a rollout of the value platform and expanded store clusters in Gujarat, Pune/rest of Maharashtra and Mumbai (each ~100 restaurants).

segments.name: South

532209|2026-06.headline: J&K Bank Q1 FY27 net profit fell to INR424 crore on margin compression to 3.28% and higher standard-asset provisions, despite 25.44% advances growth.

Operating profit was INR703 crore (+5% YoY), but net profit of INR424 crore was below last year, driven by standard-asset provisions raised on strong credit growth and lower technical write-off recoveries. NIM compressed to 3.28% as cost of deposits stayed high (4.74%) while yield on advances was 8.56%. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged for now, to be reassessed after Q2, but indicated credit growth of 18-20% against the 12% guidance.

segments.name: Rest of India (ROI)
segments.commentary: ROI contributes around 26% of business as on 30 June 2026, versus less than 20% a year ago. Corporate lending in ROI at competitive rates drove the quarter's growth.

segments.name: J&K and Ladakh
segments.commentary: Home-market share of banking business at 61.13% (31 March 2026); deposit market share improved in 19 of 22 districts during FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance kept unchanged for now, to be reassessed only after Q2 results: credit growth ~12%, deposit growth ~10%, CASA ~45%, NIM ~3.5%, ROA around FY26 levels, ROE ~16%, GNPA below 2.25%.
Chairman-level view: actual credit growth 'will not be less than' 18-20% in FY27; J&K growth ~12-13%, ROI growth ~25%.
ROA of 1.25%+ guided for FY27, with management saying it should show from Q2; Q1 ROA was ~0.90%.
NIM expected to return to around 3.5% 'by end of Q3, definitely'; retail yields to be at least 200 bps above corporate book.

Possible one-off gain from sale of stake in MetLife; timing and use not decided, awaiting clearances.
demand_pricing: Corporate credit growth outpaced retail in Q1 as higher bond yields pushed companies back to bank credit; bank chose selective lending to well-rated corporates at competitive rates.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin increase, residual GST effect, and why did solvency stay flat despite protection growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split the ~3-point margin gain as ~30% protection mix and operating leverage, ~70% yield curve. About 80% of the GST effect was taken in Q4 and no further GST impact is expected. Solvency rose to 198% on the Axis infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the structure simplification timeline intact, and how does Axis's potential stake increase affect plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Scheme filing followed by NCLT approval takes 6–12 months and those timelines hold. Management is still doing internal and shareholder consultation; Axis is evaluating going to 30% and both sides will disclose in due course.

qa_highlights.question: Opex-to-GWP improvement despite GST input tax credit loss, and the offline proprietary slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth was held down by productivity gains and cost cuts (travel, advertising, negotiations). Management said some of this will normalise. Offline prop growth was affected by deliberate cancellation of certain sourced policies that did not meet quality standards.

qa_highlights.question: How long can solvency be run before a capital raise is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can stay above its internal threshold for at least two to three quarters comfortably, helped by debt capacity from the Axis equity infusion; RBC and Ind AS 117 clarity expected in the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: Does the annuity push raise any product margin concerns; what is the variable annuity risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Annuity and non-par margins are broadly similar in aggregate. The variable annuity has a fixed return component hedged in line with other products; the equity-linked component is borne by the annuitant, so no additional company risk is claimed.

Gross profit rose 12% to Rs 46.6 crore and gross margin widened to 28%, while EBITDA fell about 4% to Rs 9.6 crore with margin up to 5.7%. PAT fell to Rs 2.4 crore from Rs 3.9 crore as finance costs rose about 19% YoY. Management declined to give FY27 growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Rising finance cost and tax rate outlook?
