qa_highlights.question: How much Publication revenue is loss from curriculum delay and what will Q2 look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 30-35 crore would have been earned in Q1 without curriculum change; this shifts to Q2 plus curriculum-driven growth. Q2 Publication expected at Rs 130+ crore vs Rs 91 crore in Q2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 Publication growth outlook and does competition from coaching and EdTech content threaten it?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance ~10% for FY27 given Q1 uncertainty; management said more than 10% possible. Competition seen mainly in higher grades and is not comparable on price; primary-level changes limit that threat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Export Stationery guidance move from high single-digit growth to about -5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Gulf disruptions after May and US inflation hurt demand; back-to-school orders due before August did not arrive and cannot be recovered. Quantification of lost orders was not possible.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of Rs 330 crore from K-12 stake sale and will PE investments continue?
qa_highlights.answer: No investment thoughts currently; only strategic investments in education tech. Funds kept for organic and possible inorganic Stationery growth; the company does not want to be a financial investor.

qa_highlights.question: Polymer plant underutilisation and expected normalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant at about 30% utilisation; raw material prices rose and orders did not come; expected to normalise in FY27 but dependent on external factors.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic Stationery growth drivers and non-paper plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth driven by paper stationery, brand association, packaging and e-commerce/quick commerce; non-paper product refresh done, new categories by year-end, target 10-15% share in 3 years. Price/volume split not disclosed.

financial_highlights.change: management noted it is majority of business

538882|2026-06.headline: Emerald Finance Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit rose 52.72% YoY to Rs 4.88 Cr; gold loan distribution slowdown dented top line.
538882|2026-06.overview: Management reported consolidated total income up 39.97% YoY to Rs 9.44 Cr and net profit up 52.72% to Rs 4.88 Cr, with diluted EPS at 1.44 versus 0.92. Gold loan distribution fell sharply (Rs 290 Cr in Q1 vs Rs 375 Cr in Q4), which management said pushed distribution income down and made the quarter-on-quarter top line decline. EWA's share of consolidated revenue rose to about 10.5%, and the EWA monthly run rate was stated at Rs 26 Cr. Management reiterated FY27 EPS guidance of about 7 but gave no quarterly bridge, and analysts questioned the pace required.

financial_highlights.change: +52.72% YoY; ~12.5% QoQ per analyst question, not disputed
~Rs 16 Cr from banks incl. SBI; rest from NBFCs
Rs 12.5 Cr EWA, remainder MSME and personal loans

segments.name: EWA (Early Wage Access)
segments.commentary: Monthly run rate of Rs 26 Cr (Rs 12.5 Cr EWA disbursal + Rs 13.5 Cr cross-sell distribution) vs Rs 22 Cr in Q4 (Rs 10 Cr + Rs 12 Cr). Average ticket size Rs 26,000; 32 corporates onboarded in Q1, about 210 active companies at 30 June; ~40,000 registered employees.

segments.name: Gold loan distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution volume fell to Rs 290 Cr in Q1 from Rs 375 Cr in Q4 due to RBI restrictions on banks and NBFCs; distribution fees about 0.9-1% on average (HDFC ~1.25%, ICICI ~0.75%, RBL ~1%). Management expects recovery from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: MSME and personal loans / interest income
segments.commentary: Interest income is primarily MSME working capital loans. Management expects good MSME growth in FY27; home loan, LAP and business loan books described as steady.

segments.name: Education loans (Credila alliance)
segments.commentary: Started during the quarter; about Rs 1 Cr disbursed in the last month.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EPS guidance of about 7 reiterated; management said growth momentum should pick up from Q2 and that Q1 is seasonally slow.
Analyst arithmetic: EPS 7 implies roughly 66% PAT growth YoY, assuming no equity dilution; management said no equity dilution is planned.
Management expects PAT growth of about 40-50% over the next 2-3 years, with PAT margin stabilising at 40-45%.
EWA revenue share expected to stabilise at 30-40% (management wording); a separate remark put it at 12-15%. Management said this was not a firm target.
Management declined to give a March 2027 EWA run-rate target, stating it has no internal number; guided to 10-12% QoQ growth in EWA.
capex_capacity: Borrowing headroom: management says Rs 63 Cr more debt could be raised, keeping debt-equity near 1:1; SBI enhancement proposal under process; ICICI line of Rs 10 Cr announced.
New products (digital gold/silver, small-ticket SIP, pocket insurance) expected to launch within a month via app, web portal and WhatsApp; still in vendor integration.
AU Small Finance Bank partnership for gold loans started this quarter; management is exploring at least one more bank partner.
Management said no capital raise or co-lending is planned for EWA.
demand_pricing: Gold loan distribution slowed sharply; management expects no rebound this quarter and a pick-up from Q3 or Q4 FY27 when banks relax norms.
A single new corporate (BSE-listed, ~11,000 employees) was onboarded; only ~1,000 employees from one plant are live, with six more plants pending.
Repeat usage: management cited ~90% repeat rate for EWA users; seasonal peaks in March and around Diwali (+100-200 bps).
Portfolio-level EWA yield or fee rate was not disclosed beyond ~10-13% range commentary; NPA-related cost remarks included in Q&A below.
Competition: MoneyView (owns Jify), Refyne and Fable named; management expects more fintech entrants and plans LSP/RE partnerships with startups.

qa_highlights.question: Are NPAs rising too fast, and is there a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPAs are about half of provisions, with provisions at about 0.3-0.35% of book. EWA 90+ provisions of about Rs 3 lakh were roughly matched by write-offs; business and personal loans had about Rs 8 lakh provisioned against Rs 6 lakh written off in the quarter, and Rs 4 lakh was recovered on earlier write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Why was EWA onboarding limited to about 30 corporates a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-64 corporates were evaluated to onboard 32, with a rejection rate of about 50-55% due to macro stress, so onboarding is slow and risk-led. Growth expected at 10-12% QoQ, with large corporates as the expected source of a sharp jump.

qa_highlights.question: Will EWA co-lending or a capital raise be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no. Co-lending was described as unsuitable for EWA because it charges no interest and earns only a disbursement fee; debt-equity headroom is ample.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and depreciation costs fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to lower gold-loan incentives paid to employees and DSAs (about 40% of gold-loan business goes to staff or DSAs), with more direct EWA sourcing that carries no commission. Management said it would check the depreciation decline with auditors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fees and commission expenses drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is sourcing more direct business through employees, so it pays fewer outside DSA fees. Fee payments were described as one-time costs per referral.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AUM growth and credit cost target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric AUM growth or credit cost target was given; management cited AUM of Rs 125 Cr at 30 June with headroom to grow EWA and MSME books.

538567|2026-06.headline: Gulf Oil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR 1,320 crore and EBITDA 35% to INR 170 crore, with lubes volume up 17% to 48,000 KL.

533581|2026-06.headline: PG Electroplast Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.2% YoY to INR2,034 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.7% amid commodity and rupee pressure.
533581|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue crossed INR2,000 crore for the first time, up 35.2% YoY, with EBITDA up 12.1% to INR156.2 crore and net profit up 12.9% to INR75.3 crore. Growth came from double-digit volume growth plus a similar ASP increase as copper, aluminium and resin costs and rupee depreciation were partly passed through. Gross margin percentage softened QoQ and YoY, which management attributed to pass-through mechanics rather than per-unit erosion. The company reports a net cash position, and the compressor, refrigerator and washing machine capacity build-out is the main medium-term theme.

segments.name: Room AC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,401 crore, up 38.1% YoY; volume up about 20-22% and ASP up about 10-12% YoY. Management guided roughly 20% plus volume growth for the full year.

segments.name: Washing machine
segments.commentary: Revenue INR211 crore, up 67.2% YoY; fully automatic machines grew about 150% YoY. Resin cost pass-through lagged in the quarter, with management calling the margin impact much larger than 20-30 bps.

segments.name: Coolers
segments.commentary: Revenue almost INR19 crore, up 3.4% YoY.

segments.name: Electronics (EMS)
segments.commentary: 5.3% of revenue, up 65.3% YoY; largely job work with stable margins per management.

segments.name: Plastic moulding and components
segments.commentary: Revenue INR294.6 crore, up 7% YoY; job-work style model where customers specify resin sourcing, so limited margin impact.

segments.name: Goodworth Electronics (JV)
segments.commentary: Sales INR177.3 crore vs INR147.5 crore last year; EBITDA INR6.3 crore vs INR4.3 crore.

segments.name: PG Technoplast (wholly-owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Reported sales of about INR1,600 crore for the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Operating margin aspiration of about 8% for full FY27; management stated this is not guidance and the Q1 operating margin was about 7.3%.
Management expects FY27 earnings to surpass FY25 levels if second-half sales are good.
Full-year volume growth of about 20%+ expected in base case, with 4-5% upside versus industry growth if the compressor plant ramps.
Price increases of roughly 10-15% expected for brands post GST cut, with the next pass-through targeted for the December quarter.
Management expects 25-30% growth in FY27-FY28 and sees no growth challenge for the next 2-3 years; FY29 may be a consolidation year.
AC share of sales expected to fall from 60-65% to 50-55% over 2-3 years.
Management declined to give revenue guidance, quarterly guidance, or FY27 capex detail beyond INR400 crore for the year.
capex_capacity: Washing machine plant in DMIC Greater Noida is online with 1.8 million units annual capacity; total washing machine capacity to reach about 3 million. Target utilisation of 70-80% by FY28.

Refrigerator plant at Sri City (1.2 million units) targeted for commercial production in Q4 FY27; anchor customer tied up with about 30-35% capacity commitment. Phase 1 covers direct-cool and side-by-side models; frost-free and multi-door follow in phase 2.

Compressor plant at Supa: first 2 million-unit line on track for mass production in December-January; commissioning took about 6 months. Second line planned for April-May 2027 decision, with about 3-4 months lead time; the land and building can accommodate 4 lines.
Compressor economics: one line at 80% utilisation is about 1.6-1.7 million units at about INR2,850-2,900 per unit; Indian compressor prices cited at INR2,800-3,000.
FY27 capex about INR400 crore, mainly completing compressor and refrigerator projects, plus a new land parcel at Salarpur to consolidate plastic moulding operations from Greater Noida.
PG Technoplast Rajasthan facility is coming online. Management targets fixed asset turn above 4x.
demand_pricing: Industry RAC primary sales grew about 15% YoY in Q1; with ASP growth of 10-12%, primary value growth was about 20-25%. Secondary sales were reportedly better than primary, with channel and brand inventory near normal (estimated 4.5-5.5 million units).
Management expects RAC outsourcing share to keep rising; brands are using outsourcing to protect margins amid high competition.
Price hikes in July-September have had limited success; some brands took and rolled back increases.

Compressor imports: about 50-60% of India's requirement still imported. Imports capped at 25% of FY25 volumes (about 2.5 million units) until 31 March 2027, then no imports. Management sees possible tightening from January-February 2027.
Copper above $14,000/tonne versus $7,000-8,000 earlier; rupee around INR95.5-96/USD. Management said commodity pass-through remains incomplete.
Imports of inner grooved copper tubing (IGT) to be restricted from November.

qa_highlights.question: What was the RAC volume and ASP split, and how much of the commodity cost increase has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: RAC volume grew about 20-22% and ASP about 10-12%. Management said pass-through was partial, varied by customer, and a further price increase is expected from the December quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company near normal margins, and can it return to 10% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to a 10% margin, saying the business is per-piece priced. It expects per-piece margins to normalise and operating margins ex-PLI to improve significantly, with a reported margin slightly above last year.

qa_highlights.question: How much is compressor capex and what margin will compressors add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex split by segment would be shared offline, and total FY27 capex is about INR400 crore. Compressors are expected to be margin-additive as the first line mainly serves in-house AC needs.

qa_highlights.question: What was washing machine utilisation before the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier capacity ran at about 70% annualised utilisation, with peak months above 100%. Target is 70-80% on the expanded capacity by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of rising inventory values and the working capital build?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5 lakh AC inventory is now about INR940 crore versus about INR700 crore last year, reflecting commodity inflation and strategic stocking of compressors and IGT. Inventory was about INR100 crore lower than planned due to June softness.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book available?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not share order book numbers. The AC season order book is not yet rebuilt and will start building in September-October for the December season; washing machine volume commitments exist but are not disclosed.

financial_highlights.change: Net cash company; modest debt at end-Q1

543386|2026-06.headline: Fino Payments Bank Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 43.1 crore from INR 56 crore in Q4 FY26, while net revenue margin hit a record 42.8% after the UPI P2M B2B pause.
543386|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as one of the toughest quarters in the bank's history, with the UPI P2M B2B business paused for recalibration and relaunch tentatively in Q4 FY27. Fee income was INR 234 crore and made up over 75% of revenue, while CASA's share of revenue rose from 45% to 54% QoQ. Referral loan disbursals rose to INR 628 crore (up 214% YoY). The bank reiterated its small finance bank (SFB) transition timeline, with the readiness submission to RBI targeted for end-Q4 FY27 and the RBI deadline of 5 June 2027. Throughput fell 10% YoY but rose 3% QoQ.

segments.name: B2B CMS
segments.commentary: Throughput grew 26% QoQ to INR 18,000 crore; revenue rose 5% QoQ, though the segment faces pricing pressure.

segments.name: Traditional transactions (remittance, micro ATM, AePS)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell 13% QoQ as cash-to-UPI migration continued to weigh on the segment.

segments.name: UPI P2M B2B
segments.commentary: Paused for strategic recalibration; at least a couple of quarters to relaunch, tentatively Q4 FY27. UPI throughput grew 14% YoY to INR 60,000 crore.

segments.name: Liability franchise / CASA
segments.commentary: Average deposits grew 12% YoY to INR 2,772 crore; CASA share of revenue rose to 54% from 45% in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Referral lending
segments.commentary: Disbursals of INR 628 crore in Q1, focused on gold loan, affordable housing and loan against property.

guidance_outlook: SFB readiness submission to RBI by end-Q4 FY27; RBI's 18-month window ends 5 June 2027.
Senior management expected to join between September and October 2026; technology stack for the loan journey expected ready by Feb 2027.
SFB opex of about INR 10 crore expected in FY27 P&L, including hiring.
SFB target: 90% secured book, blended portfolio yield around 14%, NIM 8-9%, credit-deposit ratio around 70%, CASA around 65%.
Management said the FY30 business plan and the earlier 20%-plus ROE expectation are unchanged; the CEO said it is too early to guide on longer-term ROE and top-line growth.
Plan to open 40 new branches in year 1 of SFB operations.
capex_capacity: Finacle core banking went live in the prior quarter; Q1 focus shifted to stabilisation and Phase 2 (lending, new products).
Lending modules (LOS, LMS and other lending applications) being built with technology partners; PwC appointed for SFB readiness.
Technology investment is largely done; the first three SFB phases expected to complete after FY27.
Operating costs flat YoY despite inflation; continued investment in technology, risk management and AI.
demand_pricing: Total throughput fell 10% YoY but rose 3% QoQ; the decline reflects B2B UPI P2M recalibration, cash-to-UPI migration and a focus on higher-quality merchants.
Net revenue margin improvement is attributed to a shift toward the ownership-led business.
B2B CMS faces pricing challenges.
Newly acquired customers becoming UPI-active within the same quarter: 68%.
Management said it would be a definite positive for the bank if a proposed MDR on B2B transactions above INR 2,000 is implemented; quantification not given.

qa_highlights.question: What rates will the bank charge on gold, LAP and housing loans, and how will the SFB book be priced?
qa_highlights.answer: Referral loans are currently offered through partner NBFCs; post-SFB the bank aims to price better than them. The SFB book is planned at 90% secured with a blended yield of about 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the bank benefit from the proposed MDR changes?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chief Digital and Liabilities Officer said it would be a qualitative yes for the bank; the impact is still being modelled and will be recalibrated with the B2B UPI P2M relaunch.

qa_highlights.question: Would BPCL's stake in the holding company affect the bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the holding company and the listed OpCo are separate, the bank's capital is sufficient, and no holding-company investment activity affects the bank.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 20%-plus ROE guidance hold, and what are the NIM and liability assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO confirmed the 20%-plus ROE guidance holds. The CEO cited liabilities of INR 2,800-3,000 crore, cost of funds 1.4%, current yields of 6-6.5%, and a target SFB NIM of 8-9%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SFB operational step-by-step plan and is there a non-compete on referral customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Senior hires are due September-October; technology partners are engaged; readiness is targeted for end-Q4. There is no non-compete, because referral customers are the bank's own customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the BC business be sold and is a reverse merger required?
qa_highlights.answer: BC activity for other banks is prohibited for an SFB. The BC business needs a different approach, possibly restructuring, with a concrete plan expected in about a quarter. The HoldCo/OpCo structure is unchanged for now.

risks_watch: B2B UPI P2M relaunch timing (tentatively Q4 FY27) depends on the ecosystem and is uncertain.
CEO transition: a new CEO has not been named, and the Board and RBI are handling the process; the candidate is not yet disclosed.
BC business divestment or restructuring plan and its timing are still undefined.
SFB readiness submission by end-Q4 FY27 ahead of the 5 June 2027 deadline, with leadership hires due Sep-Oct and a lag expected before operations start.
Term deposit accretion in rural and low-income segments; management said term deposits will be used for stickiness, not aggressive sourcing.
Net revenue margin and fee-income quality versus the falling traditional transaction revenue and throughput.
543386|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on operations, confident on the SFB roadmap. Management acknowledged a tough quarter and gave no quantified guidance on the MDR impact, the BC divestment, or the new CEO. It was firm that the FY30 plan and the 20%-plus ROE view are unchanged.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR 56 crore in Q4 FY26
+214% YoY; nearly 50% of FY26 total disbursals

500147|2026-06.headline: John Cockerill India Q2 CY26 standalone revenue up 82% YoY to ~INR149 crore; consolidated INR299 crore (+18% YoY), order book ~INR4,500 crore.
500147|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 82% YoY to about INR149 crore and consolidated revenue reached about INR299 crore, up 18% YoY, but both fell sequentially as Q1 benefited from closing older projects. Management attributed weaker Q2 margins to upfront costs on newly started projects, organisation-building spend and one-time consolidation costs after the China, Germany and Belgium entities were brought under the listed company. Order wins of about INR1,200 crore in the quarter lifted the consolidated order book to about INR4,500 crore (standalone about INR2,200 crore). Management expects revenue and margins to build in H2 as new projects ramp, though it gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Expected marginally lower in next two quarters

segments.name: Standalone (India)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR149 crore, up 82% YoY; top customers Tata Steel and JSW. Order book ~INR2,200 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR299 crore, up 18% YoY; ArcelorMittal to be added to top customers after consolidation. Order book ~INR4,500 crore. Top five customers ~80% of revenue.

segments.name: Value-added services
segments.commentary: Service revenue in Q2 about one-third of Q1; management says lower because project progress was slower, not lack of orders, and services margins remain strong.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated INR8,000 crore top-line as the CY30 north-star, to come from organic growth (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions; several acquisitions under evaluation, no timeline given.
Management said consolidated revenue in H2 should improve significantly; did not expect to reach the ~INR2,000 crore CY25 pro-forma figure but 'should not be very far' if US is included.
Execution of new orders to ramp in Q3 and Q4 as engineering and procurement progress; impact on H2.
Employee cost expected to rise as manpower is added on the execution side; other expenses to be marginally lower than Q2 level in the next two quarters.
One-time transaction, forex and notional interest costs expected to stop from H2 after the parent agreed to a share-based payment instead of cash.
Further order wins expected before year-end across Asia, Europe, US and India; a JVD contract in Asia is in advanced discussion, targeted this year.
capex_capacity: Taloja Rolls Coating facility put into operation in June 2026; testing and trial orders underway, production initiation now.
Advanced Coating facility at Taloja, India, inaugurated (value-added services).
Shanghai office opened in China; workshop for assembly of special machines planned to open in Q3 CY26.
Execution timeline on contracts is typically two to three years; management now uses three years as the working assumption for the current book.
Headcount expansion on execution side planned, with employee cost rising.
demand_pricing: Order inflow ~INR1,200 crore in Q2, driven by demand for advanced processing, electrical steel, downstream quality and plant modernisation.
Management cited EU tariff-quota regime (18.3 million tons, 15% duty beyond quota) as supportive for hot-rolling, cold-rolling and processing-line investments.
India per capita steel consumption ~93 kg vs global ~230 kg; India steel production expected at 161.7 million tons this year.

JVD (Jet Vapor Deposition) pitched as a zinc-coating alternative to hot-dip galvanizing; customer savings cited at least INR1,000 per unit, up to 20x that, mainly for automotive and AHSS grades; first contract delayed by customer investment-approval process.
Potential cold-rolling order in the range of EUR50-100 million expected this year.
Competitors named: SMS and Danieli (Tier-1 OEMs), also Primetals; all have downstream portfolios.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore CY30 top-line target still valid, and how will it be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, as a north-star; two streams: organic (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions, which are under investigation. Volteron IP sits with John Cockerill SA, not the listed entity, and is not yet commercial.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the CY25 pro-forma revenue (~INR2,000 crore) far above reported (~INR960 crore), and can the US entity bridge the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2,000 crore was a guideline; US is not a large contributor. Revenue depends on order progress. Management expects significant H2 improvement and said the gap should not be very far if US is included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did John Cockerill SA reduce holding from ~75% to ~70.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to group priorities; SA remains a large shareholder and will get convertible preferential shares that would take it back to 72%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost structure outlook (employee cost ~INR68 crore, other expenses ~INR70 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost to rise with execution hiring; other expenses marginally below current level in next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone and consolidated order book, service revenue, and top-customer concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated ~INR4,500 crore, standalone ~INR2,200 crore. Service revenue ~one-third of Q1. Top five ~80% of revenue; standalone top are Tata Steel and JSW.

qa_highlights.question: Quantum of one-time consolidation costs in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify; said it would come back to the analyst. Costs covered transaction, forex, notional interest, legal, audit and due diligence across Belgium, Germany and China.

risks_watch: Margin pressure in Q2 from upfront costs on new projects; recovery depends on H2 execution ramp.
Revenue lumpiness: sequential decline in Q2 from Q1 project close-outs.
Consolidation and ongoing parent-company cost sharing (R&D, technical development) may persist beyond one-time items.
JVD first commercial contract repeatedly delayed by customer investment validation; Volteron not yet commercial and needs pilot validation.
Gap between INR8,000 crore CY30 target and current run-rate; acquisition plans have no detail or timeline.
Revenue guidance of ~INR2,000 crore CY25 pro-forma was not met; management did not reaffirm a specific figure.
Customer concentration: top five ~80% of revenue.
500147|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on order book and long-term demand, but cautious on near-term profitability, which management called transitional. Evasive on several specifics: the consolidation-cost quantum, regional revenue split, and the reason for delays in the JVD contract and Taloja facility.

532698|2026-06.headline: Nitin Spinners Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR875 crore (+10.3% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose to 17.78%, with PAT up 83.6% to INR75.3 crore.
532698|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR875 crore was the company's highest ever quarter for a second straight quarter, up 10.3% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, driven mainly by yarn realisations. EBITDA before other income was INR155.6 crore (+39.85% YoY), with margin at 17.78% versus 14.02% a year earlier and 15.17% in the prior quarter. Management attributed the margin gain mostly to yarn price realisation outpacing cotton cost, with smaller contributions from power cost savings and efficiency. Management guided that the new capacities (fabric +35 million metres, spinning +74,000 spindles) will add INR200-300 crore revenue in the near term, though the commissioning timeline has since been reset.

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Running at 98% utilisation. Yarn spread (yarn price less cotton) reported at about INR130/kg currently versus about INR110 in the prior quarter. Management said yarn price increases outpaced cotton, and a fall in outside yarn sales was due to higher in-house fabric consumption and stock in transit.

segments.name: Woven fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation above 92%. Fabric margins have not expanded like yarn; pass-through is only of actual cotton increases. Fabric revenue was about INR700 crore plus in FY26 and is about 20-21% of revenue, targeted at about 30% after expansion.

segments.name: Knitted fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation at about 55-60%, below the pre-US-tariff norm of 60-65%, because of US tariff uncertainty; the US had been a major market for knit fabric.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to stay in the company's 16-20% band; management said it aims for the upper end but gave no firm guidance on reaching it. Management said it expects current margins to be maintained, and declined to comment on improvement.

Renewable power capacity expected operational by end Q3 FY27; management estimates about INR50 crore annual EBITDA benefit, with about INR1.2-1.5 crore already in Q1 and an analyst assumption of about INR12.5 crore per quarter from Q4.
Blended power cost expected around INR5.50/unit once solar covers about 60% of requirements.

New capacity: weaving starts in about two months, processing in about 1.5 months later (around Diwali), spinning on stream by about December; utilisation to ramp to 31 March 2027, with fabric 100% ramp taking a quarter or two into FY28.

Expansion adds about INR1,000-1,100 crore of turnover at full run-rate, of which about INR500 crore is fabric (FY28 fabric revenue targeted at INR1,200 crore) and yarn about 40% for external sale; management said incremental fabric revenue is 'not factoring in' the price volatility.
Management said no new capex is planned until after FY28 beyond the announced expansion.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion of 35 million metres (weaving plus finishing; solid and yarn-dyed fabrics; no printing capacity added).
Spinning expansion of 74,000 spindles; about 22,000 metric tons of new yarn capacity, of which 16,000-18,000 MT goes into fabric and some to yarn dyeing.
Capex of about INR1,100 crore; Rajasthan textile scheme incentives apply, with capital subsidy booked in other income.
Renewable power expansion on schedule for end Q3 FY27.
Spinning utilisation 98%; woven fabric utilisation over 92%; knit fabric 55-60%.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices rose about 8-10% in Q1 on lower global output and West Asia-related logistics issues; India removed cotton import duty.
Indian cotton had been priced above the Cotlook index in 2023-24 (about +5-7%); it now trades at about -1 to -2% versus Cotlook, a delta of about 7-8 points.
Indian yarn exports to China rose to about 110-115 million kg in CY26 from 90-100 million kg in 2025; management sees China's import demand continuing.
Management said spinning capacity exits in the last 1-2 years and the post-US-tariff demand slump have rebalanced supply.

Volumes: management said yarn outside sales fell because of in-house consumption by fabric units and about some stock held at quarter-end due to vessel shortages; these were said to have dispatched in July.
Price pass-through: yarn price increases exceeded cotton increases (management cited about 120-125% pass-through on a 100% cotton increase); fabric pass-through is only 1:1 on cotton.
India crop: about 318-320 lakh bales for 2025-26, versus 326-327 lakh bales in 2024-25; 2026-27 acreage about 0.5-1% lower; rainfall over the next month is the key factor.

qa_highlights.question: What are the yarn spreads in Q1 and Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads were about INR110 in the last quarter of FY26 and are now about INR130, and management said this is sustained at current conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Are current margins of 17-18% sustainable for the next one to two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to maintain the current level, with cost savings helping, but declined to comment on any further improvement or on a decline.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 EBITDA expansion is from power savings, realisation, and inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Power savings contributed about 0.5% of EBITDA and a similar amount from solar; the gross margin rise to about 40% came mainly from yarn realisation. Inventory gains were described as very small, and the working capital cycle is broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What share of new capacity revenue goes to fabric, and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: About 600-plus crore of the expansion's turnover is fabric, with yarn ramp-up complete by 31 March 2027 and fabric taking a quarter or two more into FY28; fabric revenue is expected at INR1,200 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, as it is in a growth phase funding capex through internal accruals and loans, so a buyback would not be prudent now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning garmenting or home textiles as the next growth leg?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said garmenting is only an idea with nothing firmed up, and home textiles and garmenting are both seen as equally good opportunities, with Europe the key opening for home textiles after the US slump.

544885|2026-06.headline: Gaja AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR27.2 crores; total income up 26% to INR51.8 crores.
544885|2026-06.overview: First quarterly call as a listed company. Total income rose 26% YoY to INR51.8 crores and PAT rose 35% to INR27.2 crores, with LTM PAT at INR89.1 crores (+38%). Performance income of INR29.7 crores (+17% YoY) drove most of the income, while management fee income of about INR16 crores grew 7%. Cost-to-income improved to 38.4% from 42.3%. Management repeatedly declined to give forward guidance on carry, fund deployment or fundraising timelines.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: About INR16 crores in Q1 FY27, up 7% YoY. Management fee is charged on initial committed capital of Funds III and IV, roughly INR3,200 crores, not on AUM.

segments.name: Performance income
segments.commentary: INR29.7 crores in Q1 FY27, up 17% YoY; LTM INR92.2 crores (INR72 crores sponsor gains and INR20 crores carry per the LTM split given on the call). Carry is booked on a realised basis only. Q1 carry of INR13 crores came from Fund II.

guidance_outlook: Management has a stated policy of not giving future guidance on carry, fund wind-up, deployment or fundraising timelines.
Fund V (flagship) targets INR2,500 crores over a 10-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received. Management said the size may increase a bit.
Eastgate (secondaries) targets INR1,500 crores over a 5-year closed-ended term; SEBI approval received.
Historical trendlines cited: profit about 35% CAGR (Mar-24 to Mar-26) and total income about 24% a year. Not presented as guidance.
Dividend of INR0.75 per share (15%); payout ratio raised to 12.5% from about 10%.
PW (PricewaterhouseCoopers) to be appointed statutory auditor, replacing the previous auditor.
demand_pricing: Fund IV (closed 2023, INR1,775 crores, 7 investments): 75% deployed at 30 June 2026, now 81% after one more investment; gross IRR 29%, gross MOIC 1.8x.
Fund III gross IRR cited at about 9% (analyst figure, from CRISIL cohort data); management says it already earns sponsor gains from Fund III.
Sponsor commitment across funds about INR589 crores, 7.1% of fund size.
Investor base: 298 LPs in existing funds; about 900 investors across India and 20+ countries; little reliance on distributors.
Hurdle rates: 10% for rupee investors, 8% for dollar investors; European (whole-fund) waterfall with full catch-up.

qa_highlights.question: Fund IV dry powder and number of targeted investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 10-12 investments per fund; seven made in Fund IV by June 2026, deployment at 75% rising to 81% since. Fund V will also target 10-12 investments.

qa_highlights.question: Share of carry vs fee income and whether pure fee income will grow faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said performance income becomes more predictable as firms mature, and that fee income does not grow with NAV. Q1 split was about INR16 crores fee and INR30 crores performance; LTM is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of performance income into carry and sponsor gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: INR13 crores carry from Fund II and INR17 crores sponsor gains from Funds III and IV, total INR29.7 crores. LTM performance income INR92.2 crores (INR72 crores sponsor gains, INR20 crores carry). Carry is booked on realised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Fund III carry given low gross IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to say; NAVs are carried conservatively and it expects Fund III performance income trends to continue, with sponsor gains already flowing.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 to Q1 jump of about 594% in carry fee; is it realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 FY26 weakness to low markets and multiple re-rating in March 2026. The Q1 jump reflects fair value gains from the recovery in markets through June, not realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to AI deals such as Fractal and Sarvam and entry valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to discuss underlying fund investments in detail. Said both are mature growth-stage deals, not venture; sector exposure capped at 20-25% of fund capital.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost rise from Q4 to Q1 (INR6.7 crores to INR10.3 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 has seasonal bonus payouts; YoY, Q1 employee costs are in the same range of INR10-plus crores.

qa_highlights.question: Market value of portfolio and LP share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no single portfolio; valuations are done quarterly under SEBI rules and the same valuations are used for the company's holdings.

qa_highlights.question: Fund III and Fund V, Eastgate timelines and first closes?
qa_highlights.answer: Declined to give future guidance on wind-up, deployment or fundraising timing.

risks_watch: Performance income is lumpy quarter to quarter (Q4 FY26 carry sharply lower, Q1 FY27 up about 594% QoQ); management asks investors to judge on LTM.
Fund III gross IRR of about 9% is well below the 10% rupee hurdle and carry depends on returning capital plus hurdle; no carry guidance given.
Carry is booked only on realisations, so timing of fund exits will drive reported earnings.
Fund IV valuation and AI-sector exposure (Fractal, Sarvam) questioned by analysts; management declined detailed disclosure.
Auditor change to PW and fundraising for Fund V (INR2,500 crores) and Eastgate (INR1,500 crores) are pending milestones.
544885|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the franchise and historical numbers, but evasive on forward-looking items. Management repeatedly declined guidance on carry, deployment, fund-raise timing and Fund III outcome, citing board and adviser advice. Explanations of quarterly variance leaned on LTM framing.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR534 crores a year earlier

538836|2026-06.headline: Monte Carlo Q1 FY27 revenue rose 8% to INR149 crores, but a net loss of INR23 crores came from about INR130 crores of B2B sales returns pulled into the quarter.
538836|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR149 crores, up 8% YoY, with EBITDA loss of INR13 crores and net loss of INR23 crores. Management attributed the loss to front-loaded processing of B2B returns (about 65% of the full-period return volume recognised in Q1 versus 50% last year), which it says will even out over Q2 to Q4. Management guided to low double-digit revenue growth for FY27 (cut from an earlier 15-20% view, citing geopolitical tensions, inflation and monsoon risk), SSSG of about 10%, 40-45 new stores, and an EBITDA margin up to 100 bps lower than FY26's ~18%. Most Q&A focused on returns, the solar project, buyback requests and the low valuation.

financial_highlights.metric: Sales returns processed in Q1 FY27
financial_highlights.value: about INR130 crores (INR80 crores extra vs last year per Q&A)
financial_highlights.change: Opening returns provision about INR180 crores for full year

financial_highlights.value: INR305 crores (as stated, transcript reads 'INR30S crores')
Lower by INR36.2 crores YoY (as read by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: Management says full-year guidance ~3% of sales

segments.name: Cotton (basics/T-shirts)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 23% YoY per opening remarks (about 24% per analyst); management says cotton margin is about 100 bps better than winter wear and ~45% of sales, with a target to surpass winter sales in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Home textile
segments.commentary: Volumes up 42% YoY (about 40% per analyst); FY26 revenue about INR170 crores, FY27 guided to about INR215 crores (20-25% growth).

segments.name: Kids wear
segments.commentary: Grew 5% YoY in Q1.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Sales up 38% YoY in Q1; management calls it an emerging category under the lifestyle push.

segments.name: Online / digital
segments.commentary: Online sales up 15% YoY; own website is about 20% of online sales, with quick commerce (Blinkit, Swiggy, Zepto) partnerships. Direct-to-consumer (website plus ~145 company-owned EBOs) is about 3-4% of total sales per management.

segments.name: Solar (new vertical)
segments.commentary: About 50 MW DC project, INR147-150 crores investment, in Madhya Pradesh under a 25-year PPA via a wholly owned SPV; no capex spent so far; commissioning expected in 9-12 months.

guidance_outlook: Revenue: low double-digit growth for FY27 (management declined to quantify further); earlier view of 15-20% was cut because of geopolitical tensions, inflation and monsoon risk.
EBITDA margin: management said it could be up to 100 bps lower than FY26 (about 18%); may be flat or better if input costs ease over the next 3-4 months. Update promised at the Q2 call.
Same-store sales growth target about 10% for FY27 (FY26 was about 11%).
Store addition: 40-45 exclusive brand outlets in FY27, focused on west and south; franchisee ROI 3-4 years; company capex limited to about 10-15% of stores.
Price hikes: about 6-7% taken at winter trade show; another 8-10% planned for summer season.
Capex: about INR30 crores guided for FY28 (warehousing done, machine modernisation INR10-15 crores per year); no major manufacturing capex planned, incremental demand to be outsourced.
Advertising around 3% of sales for the full year; quarterly phasing can shift.
Returns target about 12-13% of sales, versus about 11% company-level return rate cited by management; the aim is 30-50 bps lower than last year.
capex_capacity: Woolen: 15-17 new machines added; cotton plants running at full capacity with no spare capacity, so incremental demand is to be outsourced to third-party vendors.
Returns refinishing capacity doubled (from 5,000 to 10,000 pieces per day) via added warehouse space and manpower.

Solar: about 50 MW DC, INR147-150 crores investment, land being aggregated; PPA signed with Madhya Pradesh government; billing expected from next financial year; management wants to commission and bill before new tenders. Plants are leased land (25-30 year leases), EPC-installed. Exit permitted only 1 year after commissioning.
Cash on books stated as INR305 crores (transcript reads 'INR30S crores'), not yet committed to solar; buyback is 'under Board discussion' with no decision announced.
demand_pricing: Q1 sales were hit by B2B returns (about INR130 crores; 1 lakh extra pieces returned vs last year). Management expects about 70,000 fewer pieces returned in Q2 than last year; combined Q1+Q2 return volume to rise 35,000-45,000 pieces, in line with dispatch growth.
Returns are 100% B2B (retailers), with management able to limit pickups; management says returns run ~11-12% company-wide vs 15-20% industry.
Order book supported growth, but management consciously cut production in view of geopolitical tensions and inflation.
Operating cost pressure from freight, packing and inputs; raw materials are pre-booked, so impact is limited, per management.
Management says ~20% organised share of Indian apparel vs 35-50% in developed markets, citing long-term runway.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue grow under 10% when cotton and home textile volumes rose about 20-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher B2B returns (about INR80 crores more than last year, about INR130 crores in total) absorbed the revenue; returns were pulled forward because of added refinishing capacity. Returns are booked at cost, and the inventory is rebilled later.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the opening provision of about INR180 crores not netting the full Q1 returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns arrive across two financial years, so the INR180 crores provision covers the full year. Q1 consumes part of it, and the rest is spread over Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for revenue, SSSG and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Low double-digit revenue growth, about 10% SSSG, 40-45 stores, and EBITDA margin up to 100 bps lower than last year; management will update in the Q2 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar project's contract structure and exit route?
qa_highlights.answer: Leased land on 25-30 year terms; 25-year PPA with the Madhya Pradesh government; run through a wholly owned SPV; exit allowed one year after commissioning, with buyers available at a cash-flow discount rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company consider a share buyback given the low P/E and the cash on books?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buyback is always under Board discussion, with no decision; a promoter (Diwakar/Gunit-raised) suggestion was noted, and management said 'by next quarter, you should see something'.

qa_highlights.question: Are there exports or FTA benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: No exports at present beyond small Middle East online sales under own brand; the company is an asset-light retailer that outsources most production, so FTA benefits are not expected.

507514|2026-06.headline: Som Distilleries Q1 FY27 hit by Madhya Pradesh suspension: consolidated EBITDA INR15.2 crore on INR268.8 crore total income; FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore.
507514|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was described by management as an extremely difficult quarter, driven by the operational and regulatory disruption in Madhya Pradesh, where the Bhopal brewery remains suspended. Consolidated volume was 45.79 lakh cases, total income INR268.8 crore and EBITDA INR15.2 crore. Karnataka (cases up about 30%) and Odisha (up about 40%) recovered, and the UP brewery (about 10 million cases capacity) began commercial production around June 9, 2026. Gross debt rose only INR10 crore QoQ, with gross D/E moving from 0.3x to 0.31x, and operating cash generation was about INR28 crore. FY27 revenue guidance was lowered to INR1,000-1,100 crore from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore.

financial_highlights.value: 45 lakh cases, about 98.9% of total volume and 93% of revenue

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue lost from MP closure in Q1
Raw material and packaging cost increase (cans, malt, bottles)

segments.name: Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal brewery)
segments.commentary: Operations suspended for about six months; licence restoration is pending in courts and with authorities. Fixed cost run-rate about INR6-7 crore per quarter including interest, salaries and power, of which about INR5 crore is employee cost (standalone). Finished goods stock about INR25 crore, with roughly one month of shelf life left per management.

segments.commentary: Cases sold up about 30% in Q1; plant utilisation about 60%. Sunny Beaches reported as performing well here.

segments.name: Odisha
segments.commentary: Cases sold up about 40% in Q1; plant utilisation about 70%.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh brewery
segments.commentary: Commercial production started around June 9, 2026; about 10 million cases annual beer capacity; about INR300 crore spent on Phase 1 with no pending capex per management. Utilisation not yet meaningful given lean season. Management says peak utilisation is 3-4 years away.

segments.name: IMFL (Mahavat)
segments.commentary: Realisation up about 3% YoY to INR1,047 per case. Mahavat launched in Bhopal, Delhi and UP; supply resumption from Bhopal is a stated focus.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore from earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore; margin guidance deferred to next call.
Management says the MP licence issue should be resolved in the current month, but it is not in management's control and is sub judice.
Andhra Pradesh direct sales expected to start by first week of September 2026, pending export permissions from Karnataka.
Plan to step into the Indian single malt category before end of FY27 (in-house developed).
Phase 2 (distillery) at UP: permissions applied; firmer execution view in three to four months.
capex_capacity: UP brewery Phase 1: about INR300 crore spent, no pending capex; commercial production from around June 9, 2026.
UP brewery capacity about 10 million cases per year; management says peak utilisation is 3-4 years away.
Hassan utilisation about 60%; Odisha about 70%; Bhopal (MP) suspended.
Company has four beer capacities; MP is one of them and is currently suspended.
Management did not give a firm Phase 2 capex figure; said more clarity in three to four months.
demand_pricing: Karnataka and Odisha recovery offsets MP loss; management says market share retained or growing where brands were available, except MP and partly Delhi.
Raw material and packaging costs up about 7.5-8% YoY; cans rely on a single supplier (Ball Corporation) for the industry.
Excise duty paid rose because more volume was sold in Karnataka and Odisha, where excise is paid before dispatch unlike MP.

Beer portfolio: Hunter, Black Fort, Power Cool, Sunny Beaches, Legend (management listed five; analyst cited Woodpecker as well). Management says the multi-brand approach targets different price segments.
Receivables: most sales are to government wholesalers in the states where the company operates, and management sees no material receivable risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost from the MP closure in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR250-260 crore of revenue was lost.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhopal (MP) be restored, and what was the FY27 outlook if it is not?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is in courts and with authorities and is sub judice; it is hopeful of resolution this month. It declined to discuss a plan B or give numbers for a no-approval scenario, and reiterated FY27 revenue of INR1,000-1,100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Could Karnataka or other plants supply Bhopal to lift utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said importing from Odisha or UP to MP would be uneconomic because of MP's very high import fees, potentially leading to a loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Andhra Pradesh entry go live?
qa_highlights.answer: Excise and corporation permissions were delayed until end-July; export permissions from Karnataka are pending, and brands are expected in AP by first week of September.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company use contract manufacturing in states with overcapacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it compares local contract brewing against importing and chooses whichever is better on margin and quality, and that capacity is planned over five to 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Hassan plant not converted into a 100% subsidiary like UP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate and revert soon, with no commitment.

Consumer share loss in MP after a prolonged stock-out; management says recovery will be slow in long-closed markets.
FY27 revenue guidance cut to INR1,000-1,100 crore; margins not guided.
Cost pressure: packaging and raw material inflation of about 7.5-8%; single-supplier dependency for cans.
UP brewery utilisation in off-season and competition from new entrants such as UBL in UP.
Related-party/structure questions (SOM Distilleries Private Limited, Hassan 78% holding) were not answered on the call.

We generated close to INR28 crores of cash from operations during the quarter.
I think I will stay with my guidance of INR1,000 crores of revenue.

544497|2026-06.headline: Anlon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~17% (PAT ₹8.28 cr) on raw-material spikes and Remember India consolidation; management targets 25-27% for FY27.

EBITDA margin moderated to about 17%, which management attributed to a sharp rise in solvent and petrochemical raw-material prices after the geopolitical conflict and to operating costs of the newly acquired Remember India Health links being consolidated. The company completed the 63.98% acquisition of Remember India on 8 May 2026, has acquired Apiqo Organics and Bizotic Lifesciences, and is moving into finished dosage formulations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr and a ~30% three-year revenue CAGR, but gave limited quantitative detail on Remember India.
