Regulatory: two to three more quarters expected for Triacetin approvals.
capex_capacity: Paracetamol capacity tripled from 3,600 MTPA to 10,800 MTPA; operating at about 55%, targeted near 70% by end FY27.
Triacetin plant of 6,000 MTPA commenced production in May 2026; capacity to ramp as market penetration grows. Inputs are acetic acid and glycerol.
Capacity of ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride increased during the period.
Capex of around INR200 crore per year, with INR100-200 crore spent annually over the last four to five years.
R&D spend of INR26 crore in FY26; analytical equipment bought (XRD, LCMS, GCMS).
101-acre land parcel held for future expansion; statutory permissions in process; no project expected to commission in FY27.
demand_pricing: Healthy demand across paracetamol, pantoprazole, metformin, fenofibrate, clopidogrel and levetiracetam. Management said price increases were passed on to customers.

Ethyl acetate and acetic anhydride prices rose sharply in March 2026 after the US-Iran conflict; since then prices have been stable to slightly easing, and management expects the raw-material-to-ethyl-acetate spread to hold.
Energy and logistics costs rose in the quarter; management said most of the increase was passed on.
Sequential gross margin fell as input costs rose before finished-product prices fully caught up. Some prices were pre-agreed with large customers.
Exports: some export customers have agreed quantities, so the export share can move quarter to quarter.

Regulatory: CEP approval for all products; US FDA approval for five products, with two to three more pending ANDA approval by formulators; NMPA China approval for clopidogrel; ibuprofen previously approved in China.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for paracetamol given weak demand in past years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity was tripled to 10,800 MTPA, utilisation is about 55%, and it expects about 70% by year-end. Demand is growing, with domestic traction and exports.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 profit came from one-time inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no material inventory gain this quarter; a 10-15 day benefit existed at the end of Q4 FY26. The improvement was attributed to utilisation, mix, efficiencies and export realisations.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA outperformance came from operating leverage versus mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin gain mainly to internal efficiencies and higher utilisation, with no major product mix change apart from greater export penetration.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a split of pharma growth between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a numerical split. It said the majority came from higher volumes, with higher export realisations also contributing, and most assets at 80-95% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth muted in prior quarters and how long will demand last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher volumes, better pricing on established products and new products, and cost pass-through. It said there is reasonable order-book visibility for the coming quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Triacetin revenue potential and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Production started only after May 2026, so about one month was in Q1. Steady-state revenue potential is about INR120 crore a year from the 6,000 MTPA plant. Management declined to compare its margin with ethyl acetate.

risks_watch: Raw material and energy price volatility (linked to the US-Iran conflict); margin sensitivity to lag in passing through costs.
Export share (28.5% in Q1) may fall back toward the 25-30% guidance band if customer agreed quantities shift.
Paracetamol utilisation at about 55% against the target of 70% by year-end.
Pending US FDA approvals for two to three ANDA-linked products and Triacetin regulatory approvals expected in two to three quarters.
FY28 margin outlook is explicitly conditional on the current scenario; management said it may not hold if conditions change within six months.
Lack of disclosure on the volume versus price split and on the regulated versus non-regulated export mix.
524164|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the diversification story, but guarded on forward numbers: management held guidance, declined to upgrade it, and said FY28 targets depend on current conditions. It was evasive on the pharma volume/price split, the R&D pipeline, CMO opportunities and the regulated-market export mix.

533573|2026-06.headline: Alembic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR2,150 crore; FY27 growth guidance raised to closer to mid-teens on US Generics.
533573|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR2,150 crore, with reported EBITDA up 21% to INR348 crore at a 16% margin. PAT rose 12% to INR173 crore, held back by a higher effective tax rate of about 22% after migrating to the new tax regime. US Generics growth was raised to mid-to-high teens for FY27 from low-to-mid teens, lifting overall company growth outlook to closer to mid-teens from low double digits. Management said the US branded business (Pivya and two smaller UTI-adjacent products) is a drag on margins in the ramp-up phase and is expected to break even around year-end.

segments.name: US Generics
segments.commentary: Grew 49% YoY in INR, driven by volume, new launches and Bosutinib (launched June, one month of sales in Q1). Ex-Bosutinib US business grew close to 25%; FY27 US guidance raised to mid-to-high teens from low-to-mid teens.

segments.name: US Branded Specialty (Pivya + 2 smaller products)
segments.commentary: Soft launch in first three months; a drag on margins. Management expects breakeven around end-FY27 and positive contribution from FY28. No manufacturing capex; cost is field force and marketing, product sourced from a CMO.

segments.name: India Branded
segments.commentary: Grew 7%. Animal Health grew 24% (about 22% of India revenue); acute is about 37% of India revenue. Specialty is about 60% of total revenue; Gynae, Gastro and Ophthal growing in line with market.

segments.name: International Generics (ex-US, ROW)
segments.commentary: Grew 37%. Management guides ROW growth of about 15% in INR for the year; new JV in Saudi Arabia and Canada, new Latin American territories.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Grew 33% in volume-led growth. FY27 guidance was about 10% plus/minus; management now expects to finish above the ~10% level.

guidance_outlook: Overall company FY27 growth now closer to mid-teens, up from low double digits; investment agenda unchanged.
US Generics FY27 growth raised to mid-to-high teens in INR, subject to normal market conditions.
Around 15 more US launches over the remaining nine months of FY27; similar launch count expected next year.

Core-business EBITDA margin expected to improve toward high teens, partly offset by about 150 bps full-year dilution from US branded business; management says FY27 margin broadly flat to slightly better than FY26 (16%).
India business guided to grow close to market growth, roughly high single digits, with gap to market to be bridged.
Gross margin guided at 70-75% range; Q1 was within range but diluted by solvent prices, product mix and under-absorption from Ophthalmic-line debottlenecking shutdown.
Working capital and gross debt expected to unwind in Q2 and Q3; debt to be brought back to at least March 2026 levels and aimed at about 1x EBITDA.
Ex-US business guided to grow about 15% in INR for FY27.
capex_capacity: INR400 crore capex added in the last year (per CFO); debottlenecking and capacity enhancement programmes ongoing in manufacturing.
Ophthalmic-line preventive debottlenecking completed in Q1 FY27, expanding capacity without incremental capex but causing under-absorption in the quarter.
Peptide development programme progressing; R&D at INR186 crore in Q1 for peptide development, exhibit batches and filings.

Depreciation up sharply YoY: intangible assets acquired for US branded business capitalised in Q4 FY26, amortised over 7-8 years; about 70-75% of the QoQ increase in depreciation attributed to intangibles.
demand_pricing: US pricing pressure persists, but Q1 US growth was predominantly volume-driven; management expects erosion to be offset by launches.
Bosutinib: small-volume, high-price indication; exclusivity on 100mg and 500mg strengths runs until November 2026; no incremental competitor seen yet.
Management sees US base run-rate (ex-Bosutinib) potentially holding at a higher level for the next quarter or two, but is uncertain given price erosion.
India human health: management changes under Ramesh Juneja; acute and some divisions dragging, while gastro, ophthalmic and cardio grow in double digits. Azithral and cough/cold traction improving.
Ex-US business is B2B and subject to quarter-to-quarter supply variance; management reiterated 15% INR growth for year.
Management declined to commit on FY28 US growth beyond a stated goal, citing the need to see the branded product trajectory over the next couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 US growth came from Bosutinib and launches, and what is the Pivya investment and breakeven path?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-Bosutinib US business grew about 25% on launches from Q4 and Q1 (six to seven in Q1). Pivya is a soft launch; investment is only field force and marketing; breakeven targeted around end of FY27 with positive contribution in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin guidance given the apparent confusion between flat margins and high-teens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core margin improves to high teens, partly offset by about 150 bps dilution from US branded. CFO said FY27 margin should improve slightly versus FY26's 16%, with breakeven timing determining whether it is better or flattish.

qa_highlights.question: Is the higher US base (about $75-76m per quarter ex-Bosutinib) the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would like it to be, but must balance against price erosion and possible share loss; expects the trend to continue for at least one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India business growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided India business close to market growth, roughly high single digits, with the gap to market expected to narrow versus last year.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify US sales in USD and constant-currency growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a USD figure; it suggested about 10% currency impact, implying roughly 37-38% constant-currency US growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise and what is the debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt about INR1,600 crore, higher than March due to receivables from higher sales; lower interest rates partly offset. Debt expected to unwind in Q2-Q3, returning at least to March levels and aiming near 1x EBITDA.

financial_highlights.change: higher than March 2026 on receivables build-up

543988|2026-06.headline: Nuvama Q1 FY27 record quarter: revenue INR909 crores (+18% YoY) and operating PAT INR306 crores (+16% YoY), with client assets at INR5.36 lakh crores.
543988|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly profit above INR300 crores and revenue of INR909 crores, with ROE near 30%. Client assets crossed INR5 lakh crores, and MPIS plus ARR assets together crossed INR1 lakh crores. Asset services grew about 34% YoY, but management warned that growth will moderate, and part of the fixed income windfall (INR15-20 crores) may not repeat. Cost-to-income was about 55%, and management guided to a full-year opex growth of 15-16% plus an unspecified new office lease charge.

segments.name: Nuvama Wealth (MPIS)
segments.commentary: MPIS revenue up ~20% YoY; assets ~INR42,500-43,000 crores (+32% YoY); Tier 2+ now more than 35% of contribution. Wealth cost-to-income down 160 bps; advisory yield framed at 80-90 bps for ARR.

segments.name: Nuvama Private (ARR)
segments.commentary: ARR assets ~INR58,000 crores (+20-21%); ARR net flows ~INR1,000 crores in Q1 after weeding out low-yield legacy mandates. FY target remains 20-22% growth of opening assets. Private cost-to-income ~70%, guided lower for FY27 vs 66% last year.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: PRIME commercial real estate fund closed at INR4,000 crores (target INR3,000 crores), ~40% deployed. Second CRE fund targeted at INR4,000-5,000 crores by end Q3. Crossover 4 PE fund at INR300-350 crores raised vs INR700-1,000 crores target. Quarterly cost INR30-33 crores, peaking at INR35-36 crores; FY27 cumulative loss INR35-40 crores.

segments.name: Asset Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR260 crores, +34% YoY, with ~20% QoQ growth. Management cautioned against repeating this pace; FY revenue growth guided at 20-25%.

segments.name: Capital Markets (IE + IB)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR180 crores, flat YoY. Fixed income in IB was strong after the 7 June G-Sec tax change; ECM weak with Q1 IPO fundraise down ~60-65%. Full-year cost-to-income guided at 36-40% for this segment.

segments.name: Offshore (Dubai, Singapore)
segments.commentary: Dubai broke even; Singapore expected to break even by end of FY27. Offshore expected to contribute 5-7% of revenue this year.

guidance_outlook: Full-year opex growth 15-16%: about two-thirds inflation and business-linked, one-third new initiatives; new office lease charge (Ind AS 116) to be added on top, not yet finalised.
Full-year consolidated cost-to-income around 55%, with quarterly swings of about +/-1%.
Asset services FY revenue growth of 20-25%, with quarter-on-quarter moderation expected.
Private ARR flow target of 20-22% of opening assets for FY27; private cost-to-income FY27 below FY26 (~66%) and medium-term 60-62% wealth target retained over three years.
Indicative FY27 net flows: wealth and private INR10,000-12,000 crores each; AMC INR3,500-5,500 crores.
Private transactional income FY27 expected at INR350-360 crores vs ~INR300-305 crores in FY26; 20% of transactional income is opportunistic.
Asset management breakeven expected to start after FY27, with revenue inflection from Q4 as new products launch.
Lending cost of debt: blended 40-50 bps could be added to the current ~3.7-3.8% period-end lending margin.
Management expects equity mix in managed products to rise from 30-35% over the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Net RM additions: ~11% (about 15 net) over last 12 months, 6-8 in Q1; target 15-16% a year if markets allow.
Physical offices in top 70-80 locations; presence in 65-70 cities directly and 400-450 pin codes via external wealth managers.
Second CRE fund (INR4,000-5,000 crores) targeted by end Q3 FY27; long-term REIT platform being considered within 24 months.
Private credit fund: team build-out 2-2.5 months; first fund launch around mid-to-end Q3.
RTA and trustee offering rollout expected in about one more quarter; targeted at PMS and AIF clients only.
Office lease renewal under evaluation; costs to be disclosed at quarterly results.
demand_pricing: Private segment RM competition has intensified; management says the company is still adding RMs.
Management says private yields will stay in an 80-90 bps range; can exceed 1% when a blockbuster AIF II/III product is in a quarter. Advisory impact expected to show next year.
Advisory book (ARR) is ~INR13,000 crores of ~INR58,500 crores total; advisory share growing.
Wealth retention fell from ~90 bps to 85 bps, attributed to insurance seasonality and total-yield accounting effects of market mark-to-market.
Venture debt fund fees were waived for three quarters and restarted in Q1, lifting AMC yields.
Public markets had redemptions in absolute return and long-short funds, as clients shift to SIF structures; SIF licence pending.
Q1 IPOs: 8 (vs 15 in Q4 and 14-15 a year ago); IPO fundraise down ~60-65% YoY and QoQ. Pipeline reported to be building.
Fixed income IB activity was strong because of the 7 June G-Sec tax exemption; some INR10-20 crores of income may not recur.
Management flagged STT, intraday financing and bank guarantee collateral rules on derivatives as a monitorable, but does not expect a significant impact.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR1,000 crores net (INR1,800 crores in the prior-year framing used on call)
financial_highlights.change: Soft on net basis due to mandate cleanup

544319|2026-06.headline: Senores Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to INR180 crores and EBITDA 87% to INR54 crores (~30% margin); FY27 guidance is 30-40% revenue and 50-60% PAT growth.
544319|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR180 crores, up 36% YoY, led by regulated markets (up 42%) and emerging markets (up 30%). EBITDA was INR54 crores (up 87%, margin ~30%, up 810 bps) and PAT was INR31 crores (up 56%). Sequentially, absolute EBITDA and PAT dipped versus Q4 FY26, which management attributed mainly to about INR14-15 crores of forex gains in Q4 that did not recur. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and a INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue ambition in three to four years, while the company shifted INR100 crores of IPO proceeds from sterile injectables to oral solids capacity.

segments.name: Regulated markets (US)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 42% YoY in Q1 FY27. ANDA portfolio rose from 30 (June 2025) to about 58 approved (June 2026), with 23 commercialised and 35 planned over the next 18-20 months.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 30% YoY; EBITDA margin was about 14% (mid-teens) against about 20% in Q4 FY26. Management guides 18-20% for the full year and says the business is cash flow positive, with INR18 crores operating cash in Q1.

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR8 crores in Q1 FY27. Management shifted focus to profitability, targeting INR50-60 crores for FY27 at 35-40% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Apnar facility (Baroda, USFDA approved)
segments.commentary: Utilisation is about 80-90% of production capacity, though much of it goes to qualification and launch batches. About six products have been commercialised from Apnar, and about 30 million units were produced in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 30-40% and PAT growth of about 50-60%, with similar growth expected thereafter.
Revenue ambition of INR2,500-3,000 crores in three to four years, based on the current pipeline and excluding NDA products; management said variance of 5-10% is possible in any given year.
FY27 capex of about INR100-120 crores across subsidiaries, with a run rate of INR60-75 crores in the following year.
Emerging market EBITDA margin target of 18-20% on a full-year basis.
Branded generics FY27 revenue target of INR50-60 crores, with 30-40% YoY growth expected.
Zoraya (US front-end) and Amerisyn (US government business) expected to become operational around September-October 2026.
Management expects a 70:30 regulated to emerging market revenue mix to hold for at least the next few years.
Chhatral facility PIC/S approval targeted around Q2-Q3 FY27, opening access to markets such as Vietnam, South Africa and Mexico.
capex_capacity: Apnar (Baroda) facility is at about 80-90% production capacity utilisation, though a large part goes to product qualification and launches. Third production line is under work and a fourth is planned.
Capex is being spent on oral solid capacity in the US and India, plus a scaled-down sterile injectable pilot plant. Shareholder approval for the object change is pending.
Sterile injectable project has about INR100 crores of IPO proceeds left, now pushed to the second half of FY27 with a pilot approach.
Of the 18 products mapped for Apnar, about six are commercialised; portfolio rationalisation between US and India sites is planned from next year.
Management said the Chhatral site in Ahmedabad is PIC/S inspected and makes oral solids, injectables and liquids.

qa_highlights.question: Why did emerging market EBITDA margin fall from about 20% in Q4 FY26 to 14% in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is seasonally weaker than H2, and Q1 is still the strongest first quarter in four years. Management reiterated the full-year 18-20% margin target and cited product mix and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did branded generics decline 2%, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus has moved from sales to profitability after the business rose from INR8 crores to INR40 crores in FY26. It targets INR50-60 crores at 35-40% EBITDA margin for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 'other income' restated for June 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said there is no restatement or policy change. Forex gains were moved from above the operating line into other income, so the presentation changed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sequential EBITDA and PAT decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 included about INR14-15 crores of forex gains that were nil in Q1 FY27. Excluding this, margins are in line sequentially.

qa_highlights.question: Why was IPO proceeds use changed from sterile injectables to oral solids?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Apnar acquisition and oral solid pipeline growth needed capacity sooner, so it reallocated proceeds to oral solid lines in the US and India. A small sterile injectable pilot will follow, and shareholder approval is pending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans, and what is Apnar's utilisation and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR100-120 crores across subsidiaries, and the run rate is INR60-75 crores after that. Apnar utilisation is 80-90% but partly used for qualification; revenue was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 PAT growth be similar to FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a FY28 number and pointed to the INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue goal in three to four years. It said the EBITDA margin of about 30% is the minimum to sustain.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in INR (FY27 expected INR170-180 crores)

financial_highlights.change: Management cited a ~2% decline on the call; no YoY base stated
Down from ~20% in Q4 FY26; lower single digit a year ago

517146|2026-06.headline: Usha Martin Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore and EBITDA grew 44% to INR 208 crore at a 20.1% margin.
517146|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44% to INR 208 crore and margin up 380 bps YoY to 20.1%. Value grew faster than volume, driven by pass-through of input costs, a richer mix of value-added rope and plasticated LRPC, and a higher rope share. Wire rope volumes were marginally down as the Middle East fell about 28%, while India, the US and Europe grew. Operating cash flow was about INR 242 crore (116% of EBITDA), and free cash flow was INR 135 crore after INR 73 crore capex. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 10-12% rope volume growth and about 15% value growth, with a 20% minimum EBITDA margin base.

segments.name: Wire Rope
segments.commentary: Revenue up 18% YoY with value growth of 18% and marginally lower volumes; value-added rope share rose to 73% from 70% in FY26. Domestic rope volume up about 12% and value up about 21%. Middle East volume fell about 28% while realisations rose about 36%, holding revenue broadly flat.

segments.name: Wire and Strand (Wires)
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 19% and revenue up about 32% YoY; largely domestic, with early European supply in automotive and rockfall protection. Wire realisation about INR 85,000 per ton.

segments.name: LRPC (black and plasticated)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 3.9% YoY despite a volume decline; plasticated LRPC posted its highest volume and value to date. First international plasticated LRPC order for stay cable applications. Blended black and plasticated realisation about INR 79,000 per ton; management flagged some realisation softness from monsoon and project slowdowns.

segments.name: Oceanfibre (synthetic slings)
segments.commentary: Revenue has trended up for five consecutive quarters, now about GBP 2-3 million per year with a GBP 10 million target over the next few years. Gross margin 65-70%; estimated TAM INR 1.5-2 billion.

guidance_outlook: Rope volume growth of 10-12% and value growth of about 15% for FY27, conditional on the Middle East situation not worsening; management said it expects the same growth pace in coming years.
EBITDA margin floor of 20%, with quarterly variation within 20-21% and upside from capacity and mix; no margin-per-ton guidance.
Plasticated LRPC FY27 volume target of 3,500-4,000 tons against 6,000 tons annual capacity, versus about 2,500 tons in FY26.
FY27 capex of INR 250-300 crore, which management said is also the annual run-rate needed for 10-12% volume and about 15% value growth.
Thailand and UM Cables plan to be defined within 2-3 quarters; management is evaluating integrating Thailand with India operations.
capex_capacity: Elevator rope capacity expansion of about 6,000 metric tons per annum, commissioning in phases from October 2026, completion by Q1 FY28.
Furnace modernisation and expansion to meet higher demand.
Plasticated LRPC: front-end capacity exists for 6,000 tons; only the plastification line needs additional capex, and management is considering further expansion within 18-24 months.
Management said elevator rope is capacity constrained in India, with the market growing about 20%.
demand_pricing: Middle East volumes fell about 28% (roughly 1,000 tons in the quarter per management) due to the conflict, with project delays in Saudi Arabia and conservative distributor stocking; the region is about 9% of revenue.
Asia Pacific saw project-related delays, which management described as deferred rather than lost demand.
Europe contributed about 27% of revenue, and the US/Americas about 9-10%; US market share is below 5% and Europe about 10-12%.

Steel prices rose about INR 7,000 per ton (about 13% QoQ); wire rod prices were about 7% higher YoY and zinc about 28% higher. Management said 100% of commodity input increases have been passed through.
Realisations: domestic rope about INR 1,90,000 per ton; international rope INR 3,70,000-3,80,000 per ton (mix-dependent).

qa_highlights.question: How much volume loss came from the Middle East, and what is the outlook for rope volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rope volumes were marginally lower, with Middle East down about 28% and Asia Pacific seeing project delays. It reiterated 10-12% volume growth for FY27, conditional on the global situation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and how much did LRPC pricing affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management set a minimum 20% margin base, with quarterly variation in a 20-21% range from product and geographic mix. It said all steel, gas and input cost increases were passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton rise only about 3% QoQ when steel rose about 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the steel increase is about INR 7,000 per ton in absolute terms and is recovered in full; it is not a percentage applied to finished-product prices. EBITDA per ton was INR 40,581.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Oceanfibre TAM and why are margins high?
qa_highlights.answer: The TAM is estimated at INR 1.5-2 billion and gross margins are 65-70%. The products are specialised heavy-lifting slings for oil, offshore and wind, where steel rope cannot be used, and they need approvals and track record.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plasticated LRPC volume outlook and approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: A major domestic-share customer approval was verbally confirmed with paperwork pending. FY27 target is 3,500-4,000 tons against 2,500 tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for UM Cables and Thailand, which are loss-making?
qa_highlights.answer: UM Cables is non-core and may be repurposed for value-added wire and rope; management does not want to remain in cables long term. Thailand margins improved and a plan is expected within 6 months, possibly integrating it with India.

financial_highlights.change: +380 bps YoY; moderated sequentially per management

544540|2026-06.headline: EPACK Prefab Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~25% to INR366 crore, with EBITDA margin down ~100 bps to 9.4% on steel costs and order book at INR1,380 crore.
544540|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 25% YoY to INR366 crore from INR295 crore, and EBITDA rose to nearly INR35 crore from INR30.9 crore. EBITDA margin fell to 9.4% from 10.5%, which management attributed to steel price increases linked to the Middle East conflict, partly offset by fixed-price contract repricing and purchasing policy. Order inflow was INR580 crore versus INR240 crore a year earlier, and the order book stood at about INR1,376-1,380 crore as of 30 June 2026. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-1,950 crore (about 30% growth) and a 10.5-11.5% EBITDA margin from Q2 onwards, and announced a data center subsidiary with INR75 crore planned equity.

financial_highlights.change: ~25% YoY (vs INR295 crore in Q1 FY26)
vs INR30.9 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR240 crore in Q1 FY26 (~150% growth)

segments.name: PEB / prefab (structural steel)
segments.commentary: Order book is 100% PEB per management, with energy sector, logistics (22-25% of book), auto (~10%), cement and steel as main end-users. Management expects ~25% growth in this business; the largest single order is INR165 crore from a renewable company.

segments.name: Sandwich panels
segments.commentary: Order book for sandwich panels is about 3.2 lakh sq m on the Mambattu continuous line, or about 4.7 lakh sq m including Greater Noida and Mambattu, per the Q&A. Utilisation was 44% in Q1, and management expects 70-75%+ for FY27.

segments.name: Ethylene/EPS packaging
segments.commentary: Management said EPS business has returned to normalcy with some price and volume increase. It is run on a monthly rolling plan with no pending order book; about INR180-200 crore of FY27 revenue is expected from it.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR1,900-1,950 crore, about 30% growth; prefab expected to grow ~25%.
FY27 order inflow target of INR2,000 crore; management expects more than 50% achieved in H1.
EBITDA margin to normalise to 10.5-11.5% from Q2 FY27; full-year guidance of ~10.5%.

Ghiloth sandwich panel line to be commissioned by end-Q1 FY27 with commercial production from Q2; Mambattu second AP line starting Q2; Gujarat plant (~50,000 tpa) commissioning in Q4 FY27 with production from April 2027.
Peak revenue potential post-expansion of INR2,700-2,900 crore; management sees INR2,300-2,400 crore possible in FY28 at 80-85% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Ghiloth second sandwich panel line (8 lakh sq m capacity) to be commissioned by end of Q1 FY27; each line implies INR125-140 crore panel revenue, or ~INR250 crore with fabrication.
Mambattu (AP) second line expected to start in Q2 FY27.
Gujarat plant (about 50,000 tpa) to be commissioned in Q4 FY27, production from April 2027.
Analyst-cited PEB capacity of ~1,47,000 tpa rising by ~23,600 tpa in FY27 Q2 (management said operational from Q3); management did not confirm these figures.
EPACK Data Center Solutions subsidiary, with INR75 crore proposed equity; the land and facility location are still to be finalised, with numbers expected by end-Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Most orders are fixed-price; pass-through is not used. Management says steel prices rose 12-15% since the war began, but the balance-sheet impact was ~1% due to repricing new orders and sourcing.
Average order size in the pending book is INR12-13 crore (FY26 average INR6.5 crore); median is somewhat lower.
Win rate is ~20% (management said 10-12% is typical for peers). Existing-client share of order book is 40-45%; win rate from existing clients estimated at 30-40%, not tabulated.
Organised domestic PEB market share ~5-6% in FY26, targeted at 7-7.5% by FY27-end; market leader ~12%.

Data center: 4-5 projects done on sandwich panels, ~4-5% of order book; Adani order for panels won in Q1; two full-structure data center bids lost on design and pricing; typical data-center building ticket INR60-110 crore.
Exports: first sandwich panel export order (~INR2.5 crore) shipped to Africa; PEB exports limited to SAARC nations; railways business nil.

qa_highlights.question: Share of fixed-price vs pass-through orders in the current book?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are fixed-price; management manages risk by booking orders weekly at current prices. Steel rose 12-15% but the balance-sheet impact was about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 10-11% and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects improvement from Q2 and full-year EBITDA margin of ~10.5%. Q1 dip was ~100 bps against an earlier estimate of ~200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Data center revenue potential, working capital, and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify until end-Q1 numbers are available and said the funding plan is undecided, with any debt expected to be modest.

qa_highlights.question: Sandwich panel order book fell from 4 lakh to 3.2 lakh sq m QoQ; is utilisation still rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Correction: 4 lakh sq m covered Greater Noida and Mambattu. Mambattu continuous line alone has 3.2 lakh sq m, and total including Greater Noida is about 4.7 lakh sq m. Even without new orders, the line would reach 70%+ annualised utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Win rate of ~20%: what drives the rate and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it bids on 30-40% of quotes and selects projects, and losses come partly from capacity constraints by region. A 20% win rate is said to be strong against 10-12% peers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company sustain 30% growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited India fabrication demand of 12-19% of steel output, ~36 million tonnes by 2030 in the pessimistic case, and suggested EPACK's 0.3-0.35 million tonnes is a small share.

544545|2026-06.headline: TruAlt Q1 FY27 ethanol revenue INR626.9 crore and PAT INR59.3 crore (vs INR4.7 crore in Q4), on ~60% capacity utilisation.
544545|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong quarter driven by three of five plants running on dual (grain plus sugar) feed, with ethanol sales of about 8.3 crore litres. Ethanol revenue was INR626.9 crore, EBITDA INR147.3 crore (23.5% margin) and PAT INR59.3 crore (9.5% margin). Management guided to 11-12 crore litres of sales in Q2 and about 44 crore litres of orders on hand for FY27, but flagged that maize prices at around INR25.5/kg have compressed margins, so earnings depend on inventory bought at lower prices. Several analyst answers were qualified by poor line quality and some questions went unanswered.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR615.7 crore for the segment; sugar-based feed about 4.37 crore litres (INR277 crore), grain-based about 3.92 crore litres (INR314 crore), roughly a 50:50 split. DDGS revenue INR47.34 crore; ENA INR37.02 crore.

segments.name: Compressed biogas (CBG)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR11.2 crore and PAT about INR4-4.5 crore; plants at about 78% utilisation. Revenue split is about 58-60% gas sales and about 40% FOM/LFOM fertiliser.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 ethanol sales expected at about 11-12 crore litres, with no planned maintenance shutdown.
FY27 ethanol volume of about 44 crore litres from orders on hand (OMC plus private, ENA included); management said it could be higher; realisation about INR67-68/litre.
Capacity utilisation targeted at 80-90%, or 90-95% for the balance of the year if the 15 crore litre court-ordered capacity is implemented; currently about 60%.

CBG: three of four Sumitomo JV plants (20 TPD each) near commissioning, targeted for Q3 with revenue from Q4; GAIL JV six plants (10 TPD each) construction from August; about 72 TPD of additional capacity from Q4.
CBG FY27 run-rate expected at INR10-12 crore per quarter.
SAF: about INR2,000 crore capex; EPC tender pending, construction in 2-3 months; revenue targeted by end-2028 (FY29). About INR150 crore viability gap funding received under PM JI-VAN.
Management said a plan to de-lever the balance sheet would be shared in the next call or within days.
capex_capacity: Ethanol capacity of about 55 crore litres a year; management said no further ethanol capex is planned.

CBG: gross capex about INR760 crore for about 132 TPD across two JVs (51% TruAlt, 49% partner), funded 70:30 debt-to-equity. Sumitomo JV: four plants at INR330 crore; GAIL JV: six plants at INR425 crore.
Pledged shares tied to SBI and IREDA term loans: release requested, expected this quarter.
Plants located within 50-60 km of gas injection points; cascades used for transport to injection points.
demand_pricing: Maize prices rose to about INR25.5/kg from about INR21-22 earlier; management said margin falls to about INR6-7/litre at these prices versus INR15-16 on earlier purchases.
Management said it holds grain inventory bought at INR18,000-21,000/tonne against current prices of about INR25,000/tonne.
Private OMC realisation about INR60.50/litre; about 8 crore litres of unlifted private OMC inventory, of which about 3 crore litres sold and 5 crore litres targeted for Q3.

SAF expected offtake price INR180-190/litre with a 24-25% margin; CBG gas price INR84/kg; FOM prices range from INR2,500/tonne (open market) to about INR8,000/tonne (one large fertiliser company order).

qa_highlights.question: How is the dual-feed shift affecting costs and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said grain-based feed has about 6% better margin than sugar-based feed and a yield of about 450 versus about 317 for sugar-based, plus DDGS income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CBG EBITDA margin dip despite higher revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee costs rose with CBG expansion hiring, and a one-off repairs and maintenance cost was booked; management called the impact minor.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR15 crore spillover included in FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the 44 crore litre guidance excludes the INR15 crore spillover, which management is still pursuing with OMCs with no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ethanol volumes and the next ethanol supply year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects at least 44 crore litres in the next supply year on a conservative base, and more if it can achieve it.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk from sugar companies adding ethanol capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only three or four plants are near commissioning, adding 8-10 crore litres a year; demand and supply are roughly balanced at 20% blending.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation for SAF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expected offtake price is INR180-190/litre with a 24-25% margin; international ATF is about INR210-220/litre.

risks_watch: Maize prices (about INR25.5/kg) could compress ethanol margins once current inventory is consumed.
Court-ordered additional 15 crore litre capacity remains unimplemented; management has no timeline.
Finance cost is about INR180 crore a year; de-leveraging plan not yet disclosed.
Q2 volume of 11-12 crore litres depends on OMC lifting and the unlifted 5 crore litre private OMC inventory.
CBG offtake and government policy (SATAT vs Sampoorna, DPI pipeline scheme changes, FOM/MDA subsidy) remain uncertain.
Middle East crisis has delayed 76 additional fuel retail outlets.
544545|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on volumes, CBG margins and SAF pricing, but evasive on the 15 crore litre court-ordered capacity, the spillover payment, ethanol price revisions and de-leveraging timelines. Several answers were given with little detail.
key_quotes: With the current capacity, we were able to only operate at about 60% of capacity utilization.
So, net-net 1,200 crore litres goes for blending, 300 crore litres for chemical industry and 200 crore litres for AlcoBev.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR4.7 crore in previous quarter

533269|2026-06.headline: VA Tech Wabag Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.8% YoY to INR 887 crore, PAT up ~37% to INR 90 crore, order backlog record INR 19,400 crore.
533269|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 887 crore (+20.8% YoY), EBITDA INR 116 crore (+21.7%, margin just over 13%) and PAT INR 90 crore (+~37%, 10.2% margin). Order intake exceeded INR 3,400 crore, 77% from international markets, taking the order book to a record INR 19,400 crore (over 4x revenue). Management said the company stayed net cash positive for the 14th consecutive quarter, and new wins included a 60 MIGD Kuwait desal plant and the third phase of Ajman STP in the UAE. Management guided 15-20% revenue growth for the year and reiterated a 13-15% medium-term EBITDA margin band, with FY27 more likely at 13-14%.

segments.name: Revenue mix by business
segments.commentary: EPC 82% and O&M 18% of revenue. India 48%, overseas 52%.

segments.name: Order intake
segments.commentary: Q1 order intake over INR 3,400 crore: EPC ~INR 2,960 crore, O&M ~INR 470 crore. International 77%, India 23%.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Record INR 19,400 crore: 66% EPC, 34% O&M; roughly balanced India vs international. Management put Middle East at about 35-40% of backlog. Two framework orders (~INR 600 crore) were removed as not yet effective.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M revenue grew about 7% YoY in the quarter. Management said it will grow in line with project completions moving into O&M phase (Ghaziabad, Digha-Kankarbagh completed; Perur next year).

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guided at 15-20% for the year; management said it expects to meet it and to deliver above guidance.
EBITDA margin: medium-term blended band 13-15%; FY27 expected at 13-14%, with a stated aspiration of 15% by year end.
Working capital guided to stay in the 100-110 day range despite growth; long-term Wriddhi 2.0 strategy to be presented at the May FY27 investor meet.
Backlog expected to execute over about 36 months; international EPC cycles 24-30 months, India about 36 months.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: management said no capex is needed to take orders and there are no capacity constraints.
Perur desal project (Chennai, JICA-funded): about 75% complete, 1 lakh cubic metres of concreting done, marine works finished; commissioning over the next few quarters.
Kodungaiyur: agreement signed, DPR submitted to the PE; refurbishment (1.5 years) to start any time, followed by 18.5 years of operation.
Kuwait 60 MIGD SWRO (with HEISCO) and Kutaisi (Georgia) project started; Ajman STP phase 3 is a design-build sewage biorefinery.
demand_pricing: Order intake was dominated by international wins: Kuwait desal (first project there), Ajman STP phase 3 in UAE, Vienna Water Works high-end drinking water, plus repeat Indian orders in Bengaluru and Delhi (Byramangala, Bellandur, Mitraon/DJB).
Bid pipeline: management cited about USD 2-3 billion across MEA and India (about INR 20,000-25,000 crore), with India about USD 1-1.5 billion. No order inflow target was given.
Management said the Middle East conflict has had no material impact on projects; it has written force majeure letters to customers covering price and time impacts.
Domestic traction is returning in industrial and municipal segments; management still sees larger deal sizes overseas.
Industrial share of backlog is about 12-13%, with an aim of 20-25% over time; traditional industrial is ~90% oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY, and were there one-off provisions in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin differences to project mix (more EPC vs EP). It said other expenses included standard provisions for delay or anticipated default under a tighter policy, which can be reversed on collection. No one-off was described.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share-of-profit from associates (~INR 5.5 crore) and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly from HAM projects that moved from construction to O&M. Management said it includes construction-phase risk releases, so it may not recur at the same level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the forex gain operational and how does it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said forex gains arise from transactions (invoices, collections, payments) and are treated as operational; translation gains go through reserves. It said it has a natural hedge and uses PCFC for residual exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order backlog execute faster outside India?
qa_highlights.answer: International EPC cycles are 24-30 months versus about 36 months in India; the backlog is expected to execute over about 36 months overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub-judice, the Supreme Court verdict is in its favour, and it would not give a timeline.

risks_watch: Forex gains formed a significant part of Q1 profit; management says they are operational, but the standalone operating margin excluding forex fell from 15.8% to 8.9% (as cited by an analyst).
Middle East geopolitical exposure: 35-40% of backlog is in the Middle East; execution risk around logistics, imports and prices, with force majeure notices issued.
Rising provisions for delays or defaults in other expenses under the new, more stringent policy.
O&M growth slowed to about 7% YoY; recurring revenue growth depends on project completions moving into O&M.
TSGENCO receivable (~INR 140 crore) still in arbitration with no timeline; Kodungaiyur refurbishment start awaits PE approval.
533269|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and defensive. Management pushed back repeatedly on margin, forex and geopolitical questions, calling forex operational and the Middle East impact minimal. It was evasive on the Perur revenue recognised and on the EPC/EP split for the quarter.
key_quotes: Importantly, we remained net cash positive for the 14 th consecutive quarter, reinforcing the strength of our balance sheet and our disciplined approach to the growth.
Our order book position reached a historic high of INR 194 billion, that is INR 19,400 crores, almost $1.8 billion, which is over four times of our revenue base
So we have a natural hedge when it comes to it. Whatever is the small component of difference between the revenues and the cost, that is anyway covered through a PCFC.

539876|2026-06.headline: Crompton Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.8% YoY to Rs 2,235 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 20 bps to 10%, despite roughly Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales.
539876|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11.8% YoY to Rs 2,235 crore, with EBITDA up 14.2% to Rs 224 crore and PAT up 15.2% to Rs 143 crore. Management attributed the quarter to commodity cost and availability disruptions, which led to about Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales, mainly in fans and partly in lighting. Pricing actions of high-single to low-double digits covered about 80% of inflation. Management said supply constraints were largely resolved by end-June and Q2 has started well.

financial_highlights.value: +10.6% YoY (ECD revenue not stated in absolute terms)
financial_highlights.change: Management cited ~12% growth on the Rs 200 crore supply-loss basis
+14% YoY; EBIT +19.5% YoY; +18% excluding internal mixer grinder sales to Crompton
Five new BLDC fans launched in the quarter

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue +10.6% YoY; BLDC portfolio grew ~45%; market leader in ceiling fans with share gains; pumps gained share; domestic appliances grew double digits led by water heaters, which now lead General Trade in volume. Management cited ~Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales, mostly fans.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 269 crore, +15.4% YoY, on B2B and B2C growth; EBIT margin 12%. B2C margins expanded while B2B margins contracted because of pre-contracted prices.

segments.name: Butterfly Gandhimathi Appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 214 crore, +14% YoY; EBIT +19.5% with margin 4.2%. Growth +18% excluding internal mixer-grinder sales to Crompton; share gains in mixer grinders, pressure cookers and glass tops.

segments.name: Solar rooftops and solar pumps (renewables)
segments.commentary: Rooftop order book about Rs 500 crore, of which about Rs 450 crore to execute over 6-8 months, mainly Andhra Pradesh (~38,000 rooftops for SC/ST homes). Revenue recognised on installation, expected to pick up in Q2; EBITDA margin said to be similar to company EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: A&P as a percentage of sales over the year expected to be similar to last year, per management.
Q2 started well; management is optimistic as volatility has settled.
Solar rooftop order book expected to see the bulk of execution in Q1 and Q2 FY27.
Management does not give formal forward guidance; no price increases seen as necessary at present, with cost measures and operating leverage expected to help margins.
Greenfield manufacturing plant planned over 2-3 years at about Rs 350 crore including a large warehouse; otherwise regular capex trends to continue.
Brand launch event on 18 August 2026 and capital markets investor event on 20 August 2026.
capex_capacity: Baddi plant capacity was raised by about 50% at a very low investment of about Rs 50 lakh, per management.
Greenfield manufacturing plant planned over the next 2-3 years at about Rs 350 crore, including a large warehousing unit.
No plan currently to manufacture wires; wires are sourced via outsourced manufacturing.
Wires business launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, present in about 14 towns and cities.
demand_pricing: Pricing actions of high-single digits to low-double digits taken across segments, covering about 80% of inflationary pressure; management said the market has accepted them.
Management attributed Q1 slowdown to supply disruption (~Rs 200 crore lost primary sales, mostly fans, also some lighting) and price-induced sticker shock, not demand suppression.
Butterfly core categories grew in line with competition; core channels grew above 20%; induction cooktops not a significant contributor yet. Gas cylinder shortages hit gas stove sales in the quarter.
Management said channel inventory is not a concern; some replenishment from other sources expected.
Competitors did not follow with the same pricing, per management, possibly due to low-cost inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Was volume growth in ECD modest given the price increases, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply disruptions cost about Rs 200 crore or more of sales; the company runs a lean inventory model and prioritised revenue maximisation within available supply.

qa_highlights.question: Will A&P and other expenses normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P is an active investment year for the Crompton brand; management expects A&P as a percentage of sales over the year to be similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: Solar rooftop order book, execution and payment cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 500 crore order book with Rs 450 crore to execute over 6-8 months; government pays 40% upfront on product demonstration, with the balance on installation. B2C solar rooftop revenue has started.

qa_highlights.question: Would the Rs 200 crore loss come back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mix; some channel replenishment will occur, but Crompton expects to claw back share as supply normalises. CFO said some Q1 impact is seasonal and will not recover quarter-on-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further price hikes needed given copper costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no sharp set of additional price increases appears necessary currently; cost measures and operating leverage should help. For solar, panel prices are falling and the company's scale improves negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of Butterfly growth vs competitor TTK's 34%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core category business (about 85% of Butterfly turnover) grew in line with competition; induction cooktops were not a major contributor, and gas stove sales were hit by LPG cylinder shortages.

risks_watch: Recovery of the ~Rs 200 crore lost primary sales and sustainability of supply after the June-end stabilisation.
Copper and other commodity costs remain high; competitors have not matched price increases, which may lead to share shifts or later pressure.
Solar rooftop revenue depends on installation timing (recognised on installation); the Q1 execution gap may extend into Q2.
Solar pumps payment delays from government were seen earlier but reportedly improved; monsoon can delay installations.
Butterfly's EBIT margin of 4.2% is thin; competitive intensity in kitchen appliances is high.
Lighting B2B margins contracted due to pre-contracted prices.
539876|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and Q2 momentum, but defensive when probed on the Rs 200 crore lost sales and channel inventory. Management deflected segment and sub-segment detail, repeatedly citing non-disclosure.

509152|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 26% YoY to INR1,573 million, driven by Pyrova Energy utilisation, export recovery and better realisations. EBITDA grew 60% to INR174 million with margin up 233 bps to 11% despite sharp raw material inflation. Pyrova cleared a 25-day monthly continuous run threshold in July 2026, and the rCB plant is slated for commissioning by October 2026.

segments.name: Others (Engineering Plastics, Repurposed Polyolefin, Windmill, residual polymer composite)
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly flat against a higher base that included polymer composite, which was permanently shut after the tariff hit. Engineering plastics volumes +27%; plastic verticals EBITDA margin up 14 pp YoY on a 10-pp gross margin improvement.

guidance_outlook: FY27: close to 20%+ overall revenue growth, driven by Pyrova, Reclaim capacity and order book, and plastics scaling.
FY27: reclaim rubber volumes to grow close to 20%; management hopes to hold double-digit volume growth for the year.
Reclaim rubber, mid-term: mid-teen volume growth over 3 years, double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin from ~9-10% toward 10-14% after Pyrova synergies.
Pyrova: capacity to 45,000 tons, then +30,000 tons in FY28; EBITDA margin to 18-20% after rCB is mature (later described as 15-20%); FY28 seen as maturity year.
Plastics: over 20% growth in FY27, mid-teen growth through FY30, EBITDA margin 10-15%. Management said current margin is not one-time and should keep improving.

capex_capacity: Pyrova: two more pyrolysis lines to take capacity to 45 KTA; longest continuous reactor run achieved; July 2026 met threshold of 25-day monthly run with 4-day shutdown.
rCB (recovered carbon black) plant: commissioning starts next month (August 2026), target commissioning by October 2026; meaningful contribution expected by Q4 FY27.
Reclaim rubber debottlenecking capex included in FY27 plan.
Long-term: another 30,000 t pyrolysis and 12,000 t rCB capacity in Gujarat; Pyrova stand-alone revenue potential INR250-300 crore.
Renewable energy was ~48% of stand-alone power in FY26 (37% a year earlier); target 50% by FY28, expected to be reached in the current fiscal.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth ~30% YoY vs volume +12%; the balance is price, largely passed through to customers with a lag because contracts reset quarterly, half-yearly or annually.
Management does not expect rubber prices to reverse soon; cited El Nino effects on natural rubber and oil-linked synthetic rubber pricing.
Reclaim is being pitched as a value alternative to virgin rubber given synthetic rubber and carbon black supply-demand mismatches.
US exports recovered (export volumes +20%, mostly North America); Europe and other markets starting to contribute. Non-US indirect tariff-related volumes not fully recovered.
Domestic reclaim market share up ~1% YoY per management; export share flat overall but higher in focus geographies.
Engineering plastics growth driven mainly by automotive OE demand, with early appliance approvals contributing; polyolefin volumes flat as customer selection tightened.

More than doubled; after prior period items
