Employee count 993; about 100 additions expected from the Sharon deal, with the company aiming to stay under 1,000 through churn and partner staffing.
demand_pricing: International funnel is more than 50,000 GPUs; management said customers are waiting for supply.
Domestic order book about INR 3,000 crore over a 3-year duration (per Anmol Garg question); management said domestic demand is growing at 30% to 40% CAGR.
Target lease pricing of about USD 5 to 6 per GPU per hour, in line with industry; management said pricing of B300 contracts is locked, and H100/A100 customers still pay USD 3.5 per hour.
International customers pay 12 to 18 months of advance, and management says the company prefers them for higher prices and larger down-payments.
Management says GPU supply is constrained, with delivery delays of 4 to 9 months from OEMs.
Sharon AI has reportedly leased to direct customers and now demands 50% advance per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Sharon AI go-live delayed from mid-September, and when will revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the date slipped by about 1.5 months, with billing starting now. It targets early Q3 or mid-Q3, and later said November first week go-live, with billing from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quarterly revenue growth (7-8%) inconsistent with a 30-40% order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality with Q3 and Q4 stronger historically; Q1 growth of about 8% was called appropriate given domestic deliverables. Growth is expected QoQ from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GPU pricing locked for the Sharon deal and can its rate be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Sharon GPU purchase cost and the customer revenue are both locked at pre-decided rates, with a 7-year contract.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1,500 GPUs be deployed by Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the target as correct, with deployment by January-February 2027 (mid-to-end Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Are there capex subsidies (PLI) or any client concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not eligible for capex subsidies such as PLI. On concentration, management said advance-funded contracts reduce risk, and it did not name the clients or confirm any China exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be any deal-related guidance for FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to provide forward-looking revenue or profit figures.

533271|2026-06.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 55% YoY to INR292 crores on HAM/BOT monetisation; FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 10-15% from 20%.
533271|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income was flat YoY at INR1,320 crores, with EBITDA down 17% to INR126 crores (9.5% margin) and PAT up 3% to INR31.5 crores. Consolidated total income fell 21% to INR1,534 crores, mainly because of BOT and HAM asset monetisation in Q3 FY26, and consolidated EBITDA fell 55% to INR292 crores (19.0% margin). Management cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10-15% from 20% and EBITDA margin to roughly 9-9.5% from about 10%. Order book stood at INR15,251 crores as of 30 June, with about INR450 crores added after quarter-end, and the company is pivoting to international, railway and power T&D work as domestic highway awarding stays subdued.

segments.name: Road EPC
segments.commentary: Contributed 49.3% of standalone revenue in Q1 FY27. Order book about INR6,780 crores.

segments.name: Road HAM
segments.commentary: Contributed 10.2% of standalone revenue. About INR1,500 crores of HAM order book; six HAM projects had about INR638 crores invested to June.

segments.name: Power T&D
segments.commentary: Contributed 18.4% of standalone revenue. Order book about INR5,066 crores (33.2%), but collections slowed and are expected to normalise by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Railway
segments.commentary: Contributed 11.5% of standalone revenue. Order book about INR1,346 crores.

segments.name: Building EPC and others
segments.commentary: Contributed 10.7% of standalone revenue. Building EPC order book INR536 crores (3.5%).

segments.name: BOT (Jaora-Nayagaon)
segments.commentary: Gross toll collection of INR75 crores in Q1, up 8% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth lowered to 10-15% from 20% earlier, citing a flat Q1 and supply-chain uncertainty.
FY27 EBITDA margin about 0.5 percentage points below the start-of-year target of roughly 10%, i.e. around 9-9.5%; margin recovery expected in H2 as new projects ramp up.
FY27 order inflow guided at INR6,000-8,000 crores: INR800 crores won in Q1, plus about INR1,800 crores where the company is L1 (expected to materialise in Q2), with the rest in Q3-Q4.

Asset monetisation of about INR1,150 crores (quoted as INR1,100 crores later in the call): four assets targeted by September 2026 (about INR700 crores) and two assets by Q4 FY27. Chennai ORR expected by year-end; Jaora-Nayagaon by March 2027 or H1 FY28.
Post-monetisation third-party debt guided at INR500-600 crores; total debt including subsidiary debt about INR1,100-1,200 crores.

FY28 margins expected to improve to 10.5-11% on projects, per management; standalone interest cost guided to about INR200-210 crores for FY28, versus INR225-240 crores for FY26 (INR313 crores was cited for FY26 by an analyst; the management figure for FY25 was INR225-240 crores).
HAM equity requirement: INR179 crores for FY27 on existing HAM projects (including Bowaichandi), then INR72 crores each in FY28 and FY29.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex about INR25 crores (INR7 crores international); FY27 capex target about INR125 crores.
Bowaichandi HAM appointed date expected first week of October 2026; about 15% of work expected this fiscal year.
Mithi River project has started; Guyana work is ongoing; Angola expected to start in about two months.

Guyana four-laning (Versailles-Parika) order valued at USD35.42 million, about INR328-338 crores (figures differ in the transcript); Gems and Jewellery Park PPP (JV, 51% stake) about INR450 crores, with a possible investment of about INR1,000 crores over five years, recovered over the same period.
Purestudy stake diluted from 59% to 39.33%, making it an associate rather than a subsidiary.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded about 5 km of projects in June 2026 versus 102 km in May; construction in June fell 32% YoY to about 274 km; April-May construction about 638 km, down 34% YoY.
Bid pipeline: NHAI/MoRTH about INR1 lakh crore, states about INR25,000 crore, railways about INR50,000 crore; bids submitted but not yet opened about INR8,000 crore.
Order book INR15,251 crores as of 30 June (excluding about INR450 crores won after quarter-end). Road and railway about 63.3% (INR9,648 crores), Power T&D about 33.2%, building EPC about 3.5%.
International presence in 7 countries, with a plan to reach about 10. Margins and competition vary by country.
Management expects good road awarding in Q3-Q4 FY27 and says NHAI is moving to larger packages, which should rationalise competition.

financial_highlights.change: flat vs INR1,339 crores in Q1 FY26
up 3% vs INR30.6 crores in Q1 FY26
down 21% vs INR1,937 crores in Q1 FY26
reduced; management expects around INR50 crores by year-end

544322|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 71% YoY to about INR108 crore, with Hobel Bellows consolidated for two months and a 36.5% EBITDA margin.
544322|2026-06.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was about INR108 crore, up 71% YoY and 32% QoQ, with Hobel Bellows contributing about INR22 crore over two months. PAT was about INR28 crore (24% margin), up 46% YoY, though other income of INR7 crore (vs INR15 crore in Q4 FY26) flatters the quarter less than in the prior quarter. Management guided Q2 to be stronger, with three months of Hobel and a heavier precision component (PCA) contribution in H2. Confirmed order book stood at about INR280 crore including Hobel, slightly lower QoQ, which management attributed to customer pull-ins; the company also signed a USD7.5 million five-year supply agreement with FACC Austria.

segments.name: Aero tooling
segments.commentary: Contributed approx. 76% of Q1 revenue; management said demand visibility is constructive for next quarter and is dominated by aero engine tooling. Tooling orders are largely PO-to-PO.

segments.name: Precision component and assembly (PCA)
segments.commentary: Covers nuclear, semiconductor, aerospace and Hobel Bellows, making up the remaining 24% of revenue. Management expects a much heavier PCA-led contribution in H2 FY27; about 80% of qualified PCA parts are moving into serial production.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows
segments.commentary: Contributed 21% of Q1 revenue (about INR22 crore for two months). Management guides 15-20% growth for this business; AS9100 certification for Vizag facility targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Cumulative nuclear order wins of approx. INR87 crore, with about 50% of the existing order book to execute in FY27, mainly in H2.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be stronger, with higher revenue and robust EBITDA margins, supported by three months of Hobel consolidation.
Blended gross margin of 65% seen as sustainable for FY27.
Consolidated EBITDA margin of about 34-35% expected for FY27, versus a long-run 30-32%+ range.
Other income expected to be roughly half of Q1 level in Q2 onwards.
Working capital days expected to rise gradually to 160+ days by end of FY27.
Gross block by end-FY27 expected to be about double the current level, mainly due to Saudi JV capex.
ROCE of about 15-16% expected to hold for calendar 2026, rising to 20-21%+ with higher utilisation; asset turns of about 2.5x over 2-3 years.
Two new customers (locomotive and power generation) expected to be onboarded by end FY27, subject to qualification.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing facilities at approx. 58% utilisation; about 10% of available capacity committed to new product introduction and qualification programs.
Capacity expansion being advanced earlier than originally planned to serve qualification programs converting into serial production; no significant core business capex was planned for FY27 earlier.
Saudi JV (Dheya/Kanoo venture) capex to proceed as scheduled; approx. USD10 million infusion into the JV expected in August 2026.
Board approved a QIP enabling resolution of up to INR750 crore; management said this is not an immediate fundraise.
Dheya Engineering seeking about USD10 million via equity and debt; Unimech intends to participate, with possible modest dilution.
demand_pricing: FACC Austria long-term supply agreement: initial value USD7.5 million over five years, with scope for expansion; marks entry into recurring aerospace component supply.
Discussions with one leading engine Tier-1 at an advanced stage; qualification and commercial talks ongoing with several airframe and engine Tier-1s.

Confirmed order book about INR280 crore including Hobel as of 30 June 2026; tooling backlog mostly consumed within the quarter, precision parts over about six months, nuclear INR87 crore split across H2 FY27 and FY28.
165 FAIs completed in the quarter; six new prospective customers engaged.
Four new nuclear reactors in the pipeline; management eyeing these opportunities.
Tariff risk: free trade warehousing zone is fully operational; management says it is watchful, with new European and Saudi exposure as hedges.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited 68% in question; management guided 65% as sustainable for FY27
approx. half of Q4 FY26 (about INR15 crore)
broadly in line with FY26 run rate

544606|2026-06.headline: Pine Labs Q1 FY27 revenue grew about 20% YoY, but adjusted EBITDA of Rs.126 Crores fell short of the ~Rs.135-140 Crores management said it would have liked, due to front-loaded investments.
544606|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 revenue grew about 20% YoY, at the lower end of the 21-23.5% full-year guidance, which it described as expected for Q1. Adjusted EBITDA came in at about Rs.126 Crores, below the level management said it wanted, after front-loaded spend on cloud, network and sales headcount (about 500 salespeople added over six months). PAT was close to Rs.20 Crores on PBT of about Rs.38 Crores, with an effective tax rate of about 46% due to losses in international entities that are not tax-recognised. Operating cash flow/working capital was about 16% of revenue against guidance to stay under 15% for the full year. DITP India growth was 20-25%, while the reported 4% DITP GTV growth was driven by bill payments with one client moving transactions in-house.

financial_highlights.change: Full-year guidance 21-23.5%; Q1 guided to lower end
Management said it would have liked about Rs.135-140 Crores
Down from 84.4% in Q1 FY26; management says still about 82%
Full-year guidance to remain under 15% (13-15% tight range cited)
Vs about Rs.130 Crores in prior quarter (per analyst)

segments.name: DITP (distribution, issuing, terminals, processing)
segments.commentary: India DITP growth 20-25%; reported 4% full-year GTV growth attributed to bill payments (per-transaction pricing under Setu) where a client moved volumes in-house. Terminal business grew 12-15% historically.

segments.name: IAP (issuing, acquiring, processing / gift cards)
segments.commentary: India IAP growth reported at 24%, skewed toward distribution per analyst; IAP take rate held at 1.3%. International issuing and acquiring grew 40%+ per analyst, with some Q1 transaction dip in UAE/international. Credit processing business about Rs.100 Crores annualised revenue, present in about 20 countries.

segments.name: Flow-based income / affordability
segments.commentary: Affordability revenue grew close to 20% YoY; flow-based income historically growing about 25%+. Management says MDR/aggregator revenue growing about 60-70%. Flow take rate computed at 28 bps, reduced by mix of UPI growth vs affordability.

segments.name: Online and bill payments
segments.commentary: Online and bill payments historically growing about 50%+; new online clients added include IRCTC, Zepto, Croma, Reliance Digital and Lenskart.com.

guidance_outlook: Full-year revenue growth guidance of 21-23.5% reiterated; Q1 expected at lower end.
Management does not see EBITDA margin going below FY26 level (about 23.5%) for the full year; no EBITDA margin range given.
Contribution margin expected to recover to about 73-74% for full year, with higher margins in H2 from festive-season issuing processing and flow revenue mix.
Full-year ETR guided at about 29-30%.
About 50% of incremental network cost expected to recur; about 25-30% of incremental cloud cost expected to recur.
Operating cash flow guided to stay under 15% of revenue for full year; working capital guidance 13-15% reaffirmed.
OMC contract: about 60-70% of contract value captured so far, with the remainder expected in Q2 and Q3.
Gift card meal and expense card launch planned by October.
International entities (Singapore, Dubai) expected to break even within one to two years.
capex_capacity: About 90,000-100,000 terminals of a planned 125,000-130,000 network deployment (petroleum segment and OMC) completed.
OMC rollout of about 90,000-100,000 terminals; full OMC programme cited at about 200,000 devices in analyst question.
About 50% of terminals are self-healing (AI trust-based services), per management.
Around 25-30% of terminal deployments now sold to merchants upfront (low margin) rather than leased from Pine Labs' balance sheet, to hold depreciation flat for six quarters.
Multi-year cloud contract signed with a leading cloud provider.
demand_pricing: About 70% of offline POS transactions are on UPI; average UPI ticket size on platform above Rs.1,400.
Management sees 10-15% growth in credit card payment transactions in the market; expects Apple Pay entry before end of calendar 2026.
Added about 10 new brands and logos in Q1; signed British Airways gift card programme; signed largest organised restaurant chain for processing in US.
Malaysia: largest instalment payments provider, working with 8-9 banks (all but one large bank). Singapore replicated; Dubai launch imminent.
SignalIQ (AI underwriting product) signed with six banks and NBFCs; J&K Bank live on credit on UPI.
Affordability revenue pressured by mobile phone price increases and supply chain disruptions, per management.
Management states no pricing pressure or market dynamics affecting the business; cost increases are described as proactive investments.
Take rates described as stable; headline take-rate changes attributed to business mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did issuing and acquiring contribution margin dip and will distribution growth keep pressuring margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution-led market entry (e.g., Singapore, US restaurant chain) carries lower margins; contribution margin should be 73-74% for full year with H2 higher from festive processing and flow mix. Lower-margin low-margin device sales (25-30% of deployments) also weighed on margin.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin dip and is the cost recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Cloud costs rose about Rs.10-12 Crores QoQ (25-30% expected to recur) and network costs about Rs.10 Crores (about 50% expected to recur). Management would have liked about Rs.135-140 Crores adjusted EBITDA versus Rs.126 Crores reported.

qa_highlights.question: Will OMC contracts contribute fully and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60-70% of the full-term contract value has been captured; the rest expected in Q2 and Q3. Rollouts of 90,000-100,000 terminals are underway.

qa_highlights.question: What is India DITP GTV growth excluding bill payments?
qa_highlights.answer: India DITP growth around 20-25%; the 4% GTV growth was largely due to bill payments volume moved in-house by one client.

qa_highlights.question: Why did absolute contribution margin not grow more and are there investments above the line?
qa_highlights.answer: No marketing investment above contribution; sub-contribution costs (distribution listing fees, network) and below-line investments were described; management said EBITDA margin in distribution business is expanding year on year.

qa_highlights.question: How big is international losses and when will they break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose per-subsidiary losses. Mature markets like Malaysia are profitable; Singapore and Dubai expected to break even in one to two years. Q1 PBT about Rs.38 Crores, ETR 46%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the issuing/distribution model tie up working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Pine Labs does not pre-purchase inventory or lend against brand inventory; card inventory is created at point of sale. Working capital about 16% in Q1 due to Q1 payouts, with full-year 13-15% guidance reaffirmed.

506687|2026-06.headline: Transpek Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6.5% YoY to INR155.1 crore and EBITDA fell 32.4% to INR24.1 crore, with a 15.6% margin.
506687|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR155.1 crore, down 6.5% YoY, with EBITDA of INR24.1 crore (down 32.4% YoY) and a 15.6% margin, and PAT of INR8.9 crore. Management attributed the decline to aggressive pricing, oversupply and subdued export demand. The company remains net debt-free. Management said it is moving to a more aggressive growth stance, with an Odisha greenfield site (INR250 crore over 5-6 years, subject to board approval) and a multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara. The DuPont contract, now assigned to Arclin, continues on unchanged terms, with renewal talks expected between Q4 CY26 and Q1 CY27.

segments.name: Polymers (end-user application)
segments.commentary: Largest end-user segment at 48.7% of Q1 revenue; down from 60-65% a few years ago to roughly 45-50% over time as the portfolio diversified.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: 22.5% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: 10.11% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 18.7% of Q1 revenue; management cited rising contribution from organic peroxides, dyes and surfactants during the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at least 15% over FY26 (about 15-20% stated), with acid chloride sales to rise from about INR4 crore to about INR15 crore this year.
Target to double business size in 5 years; management said the strategy is finalised.
EBITDA margin guided at 15-20% going forward, with product-wise margins varying.

New products: one product expected to add about INR50 crore annual revenue, with commercialisation near year-end FY27 and revenue from next year; a second product expected to add about INR50 crore annually; several others could add INR50-100 crore each.
Odisha greenfield project: board decision targeted within 25-30 days; construction could start by end-November 2026 if approved; commercial production 1.5-2 years after start; payback 4-5 years.
Multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara: 6-7 months to build, around February 2027.
Management said the company expects to run all four sites at full permitted capacity this quarter.
capex_capacity: Odisha greenfield capex of about INR250 crore over 5-6 years in multiple phases, pending board approval and feasibility study; DuPont-linked capex in the past was about INR110 crore.
Multi-purpose pilot plant (four streams, multi-step chemistry, fluorination, distillation) being built at Ekalbara; about 6-7 months to complete.
Effective capacity utilisation of about 70-75% (best case 80-82%) because capacity is product-specific and permits are 20-30% below the sum of stream capacities.
Expansion blocked at Ekalbara (about 10 years of approvals pending) and Dahej (about 1.5 years for permissions). Of three job-work sites, two are in the same Ekalbara area.
Management said about INR200 crore of capex over the last 5-6 years was largely replacement and captive thionyl chloride capacity, not growth capex.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure from Indian and global competitors; price erosion in some products. Open-market acid chloride pricing is competitive, while Arclin pricing is formula-based cost-plus.

Arclin (ex-DuPont) contract assigned in full with the same terms. Management said Arclin's order volumes are rising this quarter, and the contract is a pass-through for raw materials; rupee depreciation is passed on to the customer.
Management said it is in talks with about 2 customers on sizeable contracts, but decisions are being delayed.
Electronics-grade trimethylbenzoyl chloride (TMBC/246 TMBC, for photoinitiators) is being developed for one large customer; purification work is ongoing.
Management said there were no product discontinuations, though some product demand fell sharply in certain quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Growth has lagged the 10-12% CAGR previously guided (FY19 revenue INR595 crore vs FY26 INR621 crore, EBITDA INR117 crore vs INR80 crore); would the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said estimates are not guaranteed due to cycles, guided at least 15% revenue growth for FY27, and said the board sees buybacks as lower-return than reinvesting in growth.

qa_highlights.question: What happens if the Arclin/DuPont contract is not renewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no reason for non-renewal (nine-year supplier, no rejected kilos, no missed deliveries) but is preparing for a worst case; a non-renewal would be a significant blow to volume and margins, with recovery taking time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the INR300 crore Silox investment not being monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stake is illiquid under the shareholder agreement; the partner has been offered the stake but has not bought it, and no near-term resolution is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US tariff advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no special tariff; Transpek pays the normal 18% rate, and customers receive duty drawbacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand capacity when utilisation is only 70-75%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said permissions at Ekalbara are blocked, product-specific streams require a mix, and Odisha is needed for new products.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex now being committed ahead of demand, and what revenue do the new products add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is investing partly ahead of demand. It said two products could add about INR50 crore each annually, and that the INR150-200 crore guided earlier had not yet materialised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected IRR or payback on the INR250 crore Odisha project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payback would be 4-5 years.

risks_watch: Arclin/DuPont renewal (talks expected Q4 CY26 to Q1 CY27); the contract is a large share of volume and margins.
Margin pressure from competition and from volatile raw material prices (management cited a jump from about $2,600/t to $4,000/t within 10 days).
Odisha board approval and permit timing; the 2 to 1.5 year execution timeline is long.
New product commercialisation has slipped in the past (a battery electrolyte product was stopped after a technology change).
Silox stake (about INR300 crore) remains illiquid with no near-term monetisation.
Management said the West Asia conflict and logistics are a risk to global demand.
506687|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and the balance sheet, but cautious on near-term demand and pricing. Management was evasive on Silox monetisation, contract volumes and product-level margin disclosure, and gave specific but unverified timelines for new products and Odisha.
key_quotes: Transpek has been a consistent 9-year supplier now. Without not a single kilo even rejected by the customer in terms of quality.
Margins, of course, we have to target, and we are targeting 15% to 20% overall margins.
We are looking at almost INR 250 Crores over 5-6 years.
Payback would be 4 to 5 years.

531508|2026-06.headline: Eveready Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR407.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 15.1% and PAT up 22.3%, driven by alkaline batteries and price actions.
531508|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR407.7 crore, up 9% YoY, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth. EBITDA was INR61.5 crore at a 15.1% margin and PAT was INR37 crore, up 22.3%. Management attributed margin protection to calibrated price increases and operational efficiencies, and stated there were no one-off gains. The Jammu alkaline plant began commercial production on 29 May 2026, while flashlights were soft on delayed monsoon and the lighting business reached breakeven.

segments.name: Batteries - Alkaline
segments.commentary: Key growth driver with close to 48% volume growth; premium alkaline market share reached 18%, with management targeting an exit share of 25-30% in two years. Alkaline is about 6-7% of company portfolio.

segments.name: Batteries - Carbon zinc
segments.commentary: Volume growth in line with industry (zinc market volumes roughly flat, -1% to +1%); company holds about 58% share of carbon zinc, described as broadly flattish. Legacy manufacturing costs reduced.

segments.name: Flashlights
segments.commentary: Revenue down 6.7% on delayed monsoon and lower conventional battery-operated volumes; rechargeable flashlights grew over 20%.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue up 13.7%; pricing stabilising after 18-20 months of erosion; company says segment broke even in Q1, with emergency LED bulbs and electrical accessories growing.

segments.name: Electrical accessories / wires
segments.commentary: Insulation tapes growing; wires and MCBs started about 6 months ago, with plans to more than double sales in FY27. Wires are sourced, not manufactured.

guidance_outlook: Management expects roughly 10% gross margin uplift on alkaline products from Jammu plant once fully stabilised (after about one year); operating margin not guided.
Alkaline market share target of 25-30% exit share in two years.
Debt expected to turn positive/like-to-like debt free in 4-5 quarters.
Lighting expected to grow in Q2 and Q3 FY27, with cost softening uncertain.
Management said another round of price or margin corrections may be needed to manage zinc inflation.
Long-term plan and M&A strategy to be presented in 2-3 quarters.
capex_capacity: Jammu alkaline plant commenced commercial production on 29 May 2026; company describes it as the only alkaline battery plant in India.
Jammu plant plant and machinery investment about INR90-95 crore; total Jammu investment INR200 crore-plus, yet to yield results.
Pre-operating expenses of Jammu plant capitalised; expenses after 29 May charged to P&L.
Jammu GST/incentive approval (NCSS scheme, 3x eligible plant and machinery refund over 10 years) still pending formal approval.
Noida plant closed and sold; one plot executed, second expected to close shortly. CCI matter: next hearing around late September 2026.
Solar power installed at Jammu and other plants; company moving toward leasing/rental model for assets.
demand_pricing: Zinc prices around $3,500/ton versus below $3,000 for most of last year; electrolytic manganese dioxide, electrodes, acetylene black and lighting components also inflated.
Alkaline market about INR550 crore (within a battery market of about INR4,100 crore at MRP); alkaline volume growth +19% to +23% over last 7-8 quarters, versus zinc flat.
Alkaline share of dry cell about 13-15%; Duracell is the largest alkaline competitor, Panasonic and Nippo are close followers in zinc.
Digital channels (quick commerce, e-commerce) showed strong growth.
Employee cost up only 2-3% YoY, reflecting the Noida closure.
Management flagged no immediate cannibalisation of zinc by alkaline; may emerge when alkaline exceeds about 20% of the battery market.

qa_highlights.question: Share gains in dry cell (58%) and whether Amazon Basics entry or BIS/EPR compliance is a risk.
qa_highlights.answer: 58% share refers to carbon zinc only. BIS on flashlights is on paper complete, with compliance to be driven across unbranded players over 2-3 quarters. EPR pricing and compliance are under discussion with MoEFCC and the Pollution Control Board, and no cost estimate was given.

qa_highlights.question: What operating margin will Jammu alkaline deliver versus imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 10% gross margin uplift on the product once stabilised, not operating margin. Alkaline is 6-7% of revenue, so the impact is modest for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an one-off in the margin, and how is zinc hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; margin came from calibrated price actions. Zinc is monitored weekly and further price or margin corrections may be needed.

qa_highlights.question: Consultancy fees to a director and timing of the GST subsidy.
qa_highlights.answer: NRC and Board approved a whole-time director's compensation; quantum not disclosed. GST incentive has no formal approval yet, with discussions advancing.

qa_highlights.question: Is there potential for growth above 20%, and what is the H2 ramp-up?

Gland Pharma strategic collaboration covers sterile API manufacturing (aseptic) for niche generic molecules; asset-light arrangement.

qa_highlights.question: Is commercial CMS growth broad-based or driven by a few programs?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said development revenue is product-specific and launch quantities are classified there; the pattern does not correlate with commercial revenue and selection criteria have not changed.

qa_highlights.answer: Gland has sterile (aseptic) manufacturing expertise; Neuland avoids sterile-facility risk. Products are in the niche generic category and the partnership is asset-light, with scope for more products.

Capex step-up and possible ROCE dilution during expansion; possible overseas or M&A moves.

Rail EBITDA per TEU was lower on weaker imports, lower double stacking, higher empty running and fuel and minimum wage costs, with pass-through expected to show in Q2. Snowman Logistics reported 5-7% warehousing price increases and guided 10-15% top-line growth, with about 24,000 additional pallets by end FY27. The call did not disclose quarterly financial figures in the transcript.

segments.commentary: Volumes stagnant YoY; market share intact; rail EBITDA per TEU lower on import-export mix, weaker double stacking (39%), higher underframe and empty running. Domestic business about 500 containers per month.

segments.name: CFS (Gateway Distriparks)
segments.commentary: Management says volume improvements and a pricing increase after fuel and wage hikes could lift margins, possibly visible in Q2. A land-sale exercise about 1.5 years ago failed on valuation; no active sale process.

segments.name: Snowman Logistics
segments.commentary: Warehousing pricing up 5%-7%; 5PL service margin 5%-6%; Pune pallet capacity due in a couple of months, Patna next, about 24,000 additional pallets by end FY27; no new 5PL customers in Q1, possibly by Q3/Q4.

guidance_outlook: Gateway: management hopes to close FY27 with double-digit volume growth, conditional on West Asia conflict easing.

Snowman: 10%-15% top-line growth guided for this year and next, across all segments.
Rail EBITDA: expected to recover to the older range as volumes return; fuel and wage cost impact more visible in Q2.

capex_capacity: Indore ICD: about 26.4 acres after 2.5 acres added; construction slowed by rains, full swing after September; operational by 2028.

Ankleshwar ICD: initial customs permission received; EXIM operations expected to start by end-September 2026 (Q2). Existing ICD there handles about 5,000 TEU (estimate); management expects Ankleshwar to reach a similar level in 3-4 years.
Jaipur ICD: legal matter listed for final arguments in September; no resolution yet.
Snowman: Pune pallet expansion due in a couple of months, Patna next; about 24,000 pallets added by end of this year.
Land bank about 475 acres across India, mostly freehold; Garhi land (85-90 acres) indicated at INR25-30 crore per acre for outright purchase.
demand_pricing: ICD market de-grew in Gateway's markets since April on West Asia war; imports dried up in April-May and improved from June-July.
July volumes hit by weather, port congestion and double-stacking restrictions at Mundra, Pipavav and JNPT.
DFC last connection to JNPT completed; management says cargo shift to JNPT will take a couple of months to be visible; shipping lines may prefer single-dip, about 1-2% annual road-to-rail shift.
JNPT rail haulage about 6 slabs higher than Mundra, making it costlier for North India at current pricing; possible special haulage relief is unconfirmed industry talk.
CONCOR cited as largest competitor in India.

qa_highlights.question: Is the flat ICD volume a market-share loss, and what is the outlook for the rest of FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Why is rail EBITDA per TEU declining while market share holds?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower imports, higher exports, lower double stacking, higher underframe and empty running reduced margins; fuel and Haryana minimum wage hikes (35%) add cost, with pass-through lagging into Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CFS business's future and land-sale option?

qa_highlights.question: Will Ankleshwar and JNPT change volumes and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Ankleshwar EXIM starts by end-September; JNPT is about 5% of rail. Management said JNPT revenue and EBITDA per TEU would be higher on current pricing given distance, but North customers face higher inland cost.

qa_highlights.question: What are contingent liabilities of INR6,000 crore?

qa_highlights.question: What pricing and capacity are planned for Snowman?

risks_watch: West Asia conflict prolonging import weakness and ICD volume stagnation.
Rail margin pressure from low double stacking, empty running and higher fuel and minimum wage costs; Q2 pass-through to be tested.
Ankleshwar EXIM start-up timing (end-September) and Indore (2028) and Jaipur litigation timelines.
Shipping line decisions on JNPT versus Gujarat ports; special haulage relief is unconfirmed.
Tax rate normalisation after MAT credit use over 7-8 years.

Same-store revenue grew about 9.1% and same-store RevPAR grew 9.6%, with occupancy up to 79.3% from 74.2%. Reported EBITDA fell about 4% YoY, which management attributes to a one-time Rs 9.2 crore GST impact and a prior-year one-time item; comparable EBITDA margin was about 12.1%. Management also sought a board enabling resolution for a Rs 750 crore capital raise, which drew heavy analyst questioning.

financial_highlights.change: +7.3% YoY reported; +10.8% comparable (ex Rs 9.3 crore one-time income in base)

segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 13.7% with occupancy at 81.3%, outperforming the broader upscale portfolio in the quarter.

segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew about 3.7-4% YoY against room revenue growth of about 14%, attributed to a shift to domestic guests, a Bangalore restaurant renovation and event cancellations moved into July-August.

guidance_outlook: Long-term same-store revenue growth expectation of 9%-11% reiterated; management says the same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5% sits within this range.

Business plan targets revenue from about Rs 1,200 crore to about Rs 3,000 crore and cumulative free cash flow of over Rs 3,000 crore over FY27-FY31 (the call says Rs 2,000 crore once in error, corrected to Rs 3,000 crore).
Upscale share of revenue expected to rise from about 40%-41% today to about 60% by FY30.
Net debt/EBITDA of about 2.4x expected by FY28, not by end FY27 as an analyst assumed.
GST margin drag to be lower in H2 than H1; YoY GST impact of about Rs 9 crore to be removed from Q3 onward.
Early July trends described as ahead of Q1 exit, with growth split about evenly between rate and occupancy; management cautioned that one month is not representative.

W Hyderabad targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 (or calendar 2027); management flagged possible regulatory delays.
Courtyard Pune: back-office and MEP renovation under way; public area and guest room renovation deferred to about April 2027, taking 5-6 months.
Navi Mumbai (100% SAMHI-owned, outside the GIC JV): on-site start targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build; capex to stay small through FY28 and ramp in FY29-FY30.

Uttarakhand (Binsar, Almora) 8-acre estate Itmenaan acquisition for about Rs 12 crore; total leisure capital including RARE around Rs 60 crore, with management expecting leisure to stay near 10% of capital allocation.
demand_pricing: Office absorption in core markets about 11 million sq ft in Q1, against about 58 million sq ft for FY26; Bangalore, Hyderabad and Pune were over 65% of GCC leasing.
Passenger traffic was roughly flat YoY in Q1 after an early-quarter dip tied to geopolitics and Gulf carrier limits; the latter half recovered.
Domestic guests rose to 82% of room nights sold from 78% a year ago; 36% of days had occupancy above 90%.
Rate growth was soft because international guests, who pay a 10-20% premium, declined; management expects rate to recover in H2 as the mix rebalances.
Upscale and upper upscale hotels earn about 4x the revenue per key of midscale hotels on a same-store basis in FY26.
GST change from 12% with input tax credit to 5% without it cost about Rs 9.2 crore in Q1 and hits midscale rooms priced below Rs 7,500 more than upscale.

530555|2026-06.headline: Paramount Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore; operating margin (ex other income) expanded 320 bps YoY to 6.6%.
530555|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore but fell 7.7% QoQ, which management attributed to the seasonal Q4-to-Q1 pattern. Operating profit excluding other income rose 129.2% YoY to INR 34.7 crore, with margin up 320 bps YoY and 136 bps QoQ to 6.6%. The US export recovery after the IEEPA tariff invalidation drove exports to INR 155 crore (29%+ of revenue, up about 77% QoQ), while domestic revenue reached INR 374 crore. Order book rose to INR 615 crore from INR 583 crore, and a fresh equity raise of about INR 122 crore lifted net worth to INR 894 crore.

segments.name: Power cables
segments.commentary: Accounted for 57.2% of Q1 revenue; power cable order book INR 455 crore (about 74% of total orders), up 27% YoY.

segments.name: Domestic B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 296 crore, up 92% YoY; management cites this higher-margin institutional mix as a margin driver.

segments.name: Exports (US-led)
segments.commentary: INR 155 crore in Q1, 29%+ of revenue; US distributors grew from 2 in FY22 to 8 now. Export order book only INR 97 crore.

segments.name: HTLS conductors
segments.commentary: Management cites INR 100 crore of business in hand; capacity build-out expected to be margin-accretive.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY, constrained by existing plants running at effectively 100% utilisation.
EBITDA margin expected to return to FY25 levels (about 8% pre-tariff, per analyst framing) by Q4 FY27; operating margin of 6.6% is 'on track'.
FY27 US exports targeted at INR 700-800 crore, versus INR 155 crore in Q1.
Narmadapuram plant: partial commissioning in Q1 FY28; ~INR 500 crore revenue expected in FY28 and INR 1,200 crore by FY29 at 75% utilisation.
Long-term target of INR 5,000 crore revenue by FY31; management hopes to exceed it.
Working capital cycle to be kept within 90-100 days.
Debt-equity to stay below 0.3x after Narmadapuram phase 1, with a term loan planned later.

INR 65 crore of the equity raise earmarked for Narmadapuram; no debt drawn yet as of Q1.
Over the past 3-4 years, more than INR 155 crore spent on existing plants (Dharuhera, Khushkhera).

Approved up to 66 kV; 132 kV approvals expected to start within about a year of manufacturing start (one or two possibly in 6-8 months), with all approvals targeted by FY29. E-beam cables are a new product, with major certifications targeted by end-FY29.
Management is evaluating 220 kV and 400 kV products; not officially guided.
demand_pricing: Management describes demand as broad-based across power grid, renewables, data centres, railways/metro and construction; order inflows are firmer than anticipated at the start of the year.
US tariff regime normalised after the US Supreme Court invalidated IEEPA tariffs; management says India is now at par with other exporters.
Export order book is kept deliberately low (INR 97 crore) because firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months delivery and most customers now bear tariff changes.
Key US competitors are South Korea, Vietnam and Cambodia, with Egypt, Ecuador and Turkey emerging. Management says the company faced 25%+ duty last year versus 10-18% for rivals.
Metal throughput up about 4% YoY (absolute figure not disclosed; last year's base cited as roughly 29,000 tons).
New US product: solar cables above 600 V; exports have started, with margins expected similar to current levels.
Existing plants are at effectively 100% utilisation; management says the constraint is manufacturing capacity, not demand.

535602|2026-06.headline: Sharda Motor Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% to INR1,011.1 crores, but gross profit grew only 8% to INR203.9 crores and EBITDA 5% to INR103.2 crores.
535602|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 34% YoY to INR1,011.1 crores, driven by pass-through catalyst sales and product mix, while gross profit grew 8% to INR203.9 crores. Management attributed the weak gross profit growth to a supplier fire at a key customer and one-time premium raw material and freight costs linked to the geopolitical situation in April and May, which it said stabilised in July. EBITDA was INR103.2 crores (10.2% margin, up 5%), and PAT was INR86.5 crores. Management said the lightweighting, export and emission order book is moving into SOPs, but gave no numerical guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items (after JV and associate share)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR107.7 crores last year, which excluded INR22.4 crores exceptional gains

segments.name: Lightweighting (control arms, links, subframes, torsion beams)
segments.commentary: Previously announced control arm and link programmes continue to ramp up. Donghee licence extends the portfolio into subframes and torsion beams, with RFQs generated for multiple platforms. Management sized the broader lightweighting portfolio at INR8,000-9,000 crores in about 5 years, with a target share of mid-teen to high-teen percentage.

segments.name: Emissions and adjacencies
segments.commentary: Multiple WLTP replacement orders secured from leading passenger vehicle OEMs in Q1. The temperature-controlled tube order for an off-highway equipment maker has begun SOP and is ramping up as planned.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Three North American engine and genset orders with combined annual value of about US$10.7 million and lifetime value of about US$58.5 million; SOPs expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27. Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 revenue from these orders.

segments.name: Purem JV (CV above 4 litres)
segments.commentary: Stable and profitable. A new programme started in Q4 FY26 and will ramp up through FY27. Sharda receives 50% of PAT and is not in management control.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given. Management said the exact quarterly trajectory depends on customer production schedules, SOPs and programme ramp-ups.

FY27 growth drivers cited: full-year benefit of lightweighting orders, ramp-up of additional lightweighting programmes, temperature-controlled tube adjacencies, North American export SOPs, and supportive domestic OEM volumes.

Management said it is now ready to be more assertive on acquisitions, subject to filters for strategic fit, valuation, integration and ROCE. Capital will be split between organic growth, technology partnerships, acquisitions and shareholder returns.
Management said it expects the lightweighting market share, last measured at 14% at FY26 end, to rise. The number will be calculated only at FY27 year-end.
capex_capacity: Chakan 3 lightweighting facility has started SOP and is ramping up in line with customer schedules; capacity is modular and tied to confirmed programmes.
New Uttarakhand facility, about INR20 crores investment, is progressing per the customer plan. It will co-locate relocated business first and later serve other North India customers.
Utilisation is expected to rise progressively as the announced control arm and link orders ramp up.
demand_pricing: Management cited industry domestic production up over 22% YoY to 93.6 lakh units. Passenger vehicle production rose 16.8% to 14.53 lakh units and utility vehicles rose 21.2%. LCV production rose 20.8% to 1.91 lakh units.
Management said the addressable market grew 8-10%, and Sharda's gross profit growth of 8% was broadly in line. The company is not present with Japanese OEMs, which it adjusts for.

Substrate (catalyst) prices are customer-directed and passed through without lag. Other direct materials are indexed with a one-to-two-quarter lag. Steel and aluminium impact was said to be immaterial to gross profit.

CAFE III draft (16 July 2026, proposed from 1 April 2027) and BS6.3/WLTP from 1 April 2027 expected to lift emission content. BS7 is not yet notified; Euro-7-aligned content would rise in hot-end aftertreatment, catalyst loading and GPF.
Premium two-wheeler emission opportunity under evaluation for domestic supply (above a particular cc). TREM3 integrated muffler market estimated at INR60-100 crores, which management called small.

qa_highlights.question: Can export orders be converted into FY27 and FY28 top-line, for example about INR100 crores in FY27 and INR200 crores in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, saying revenue depends on customer schedules. It said SOP dates are unchanged and a new platform usually takes one to two years to reach peak volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Gross profit growth of 8% versus steel and aluminium price increases: is there a one-quarter lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said catalyst and substrate are fully pass-through without lag. Other direct materials are indexed on a one-to-two-quarter lag, and one-time premium freight and RM costs were absorbed in Q1. It said the impact was built into the 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth lagging the industry, and when will it converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the serviceable market grew 8-10% after adjusting for the Japanese OEM exposure and a supplier fire at a key customer, and Sharda grew 8%. Growth drivers are existing orders, RFQ conversion and industry growth. No guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Donghee TLA opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Joint showcasing to OEMs has generated RFQs across multiple platforms. Management sized the broader lightweighting portfolio at INR8,000-9,000 crores in about 5 years, and targets a mid-teen to high-teen percentage share.

qa_highlights.question: What content uplift comes from BS6.3, CAFE III and BS7?
qa_highlights.answer: WLTP content uplift may be limited because catalyst efficiency and calibration change rather than a full redesign. BS7 content would rise through hot-end aftertreatment, high catalyst loading and GPF, but depends on Euro-7 adoption. CAFE III supports lightweighting and multi-powertrain engineered emission systems.

qa_highlights.question: What is the emission export pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export focus is CV emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, genset emission components and small agri genset exhaust systems. It pointed to announced orders across emissions, agri and tubes, and said no pipeline figures would be given.

risks_watch: Gross profit growth of 8% against 34% revenue growth shows pass-through dilution; the Q2 gross margin trend needs watching as one-time costs normalise.
The supplier fire at a key customer affected Q1 production; recovery timing was not disclosed.
Management said the one-to-two-quarter raw material indexing lag can shift timing, though it claimed no net vacuum.
Export SOPs for the North American orders are due in Q3 and Q4 FY27, and the timing of revenue ramp was not quantified.
The lightweighting market share gain (from 14%) will only be disclosed at FY27 year-end.
Geopolitical risk and premium raw material procurement costs are flagged as ongoing risks.
Management said it is ready for larger acquisitions, but no target or timeline was given.

500171|2026-06.headline: GHCL Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR233 crore (29.1% margin), which management says is transient and should not be read as run-rate.
500171|2026-06.overview: Revenue was INR798 crore, down from INR808 crore QoQ and INR823 crore YoY, while EBITDA rose to INR233 crore from INR194 crore QoQ and INR225 crore YoY. Management attributed the margin uplift to better realisation, lower-cost raw material and energy inventory, and cost efficiencies, and repeatedly guided investors to judge margins annually rather than quarterly. PAT including a INR40 crore post-tax exceptional item (ESOS Trust settlement) was INR191 crore; PAT before exceptionals was INR151 crore. Vacuum Salt and Bromine projects are commissioning, while the Greenfield soda ash project remains stalled on land acquisition with no timeline given.

segments.name: Soda ash (core, domestic and export)
segments.commentary: Margin lift attributed to realisation, low-cost inventory and efficiencies; management declined to quantify the realisation increase per tonne. Volumes played a smaller role per management.

segments.name: Vacuum Salt and Bromine (new downstream projects)
segments.commentary: Both plants are mechanically commissioned; commercial production of Vacuum Salt expected in Q2 FY27, Bromine output seasonally low in Q2 with production ramping in Q3-Q4. Management guided to INR150-170 crore revenue at 40-45% EBITDA margin at full utilisation, expected in FY28.

Vacuum Salt and Bromine: full utilisation expected in FY28; management said both plants should run at intended capacity during FY27 with gradual, phased scale-up.
FY27 capex guided at roughly INR140-150 crore, mainly for the two downstream projects plus factory infrastructure and regular capex.
Solar glass soda ash demand expected to rise from about 1.5 lakh tonnes to about 3.5 lakh tonnes as new capacity commissions around Jan-Mar 2027.
Dividend payout: last three years about 80-87% of profit distributed via dividend and buyback; management said Board would consider higher payout, with policy around 25%.
capex_capacity: Vacuum Salt project: commissioning checks and production trial completed; commercial production expected Q2 FY27, with gradual phased scale-up.
Bromine project: pre-commissioning complete; output seasonally lower in monsoon (Q2), production expected Q3-Q4 FY27.
Greenfield soda ash project: delayed primarily by land acquisition; no revised timeline, cost or return profile given. Management will update once land clarity is achieved.
No other pipeline projects beyond the two downstream projects and the Greenfield project, per management.
FY27 capex about INR140-150 crore.
demand_pricing: Global soda ash: supply exceeds demand, prices weak for about two to three years; China demand recovery slower than expected and Chinese inventories high. Management believes Chinese synthetic (Solvay) producers are making cash losses.
Some early Chinese capacity rationalisation and a short-term US plant closure noted; meaningful supply reduction still some way off.
India demand soft in Q1 due to conflict and domestic dynamics; management expects this to persist near term into monsoon, with some rise in imports.

Imports: about 80,000-82,000 tonnes/month in Q1 FY26 (about 20% of demand), fell to about 45,000-46,000 tonnes/month in Q4 FY26, and rose to about 73,000-74,000 tonnes/month recently. July data not yet available. Major sources: US, Turkey, and some China.

Landed cost of imported natural soda ash to India cited at about USD 180-190/tonne; base import duty about 7.5%, no anti-dumping duty. Safeguard quantitative restrictions under government consideration, no outcome yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will Vacuum Salt and Bromine reach optimal utilisation in FY28, and what revenue and margin are possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY28 full utilisation; indicated INR150-160 crore revenue (later cited INR160-170 crore) at about 40-45% EBITDA margin for the two projects combined.

qa_highlights.question: Return on capital for the Greenfield soda ash project at current prices, and reasons for delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current prices should not be treated as sustainable and that long-term numbers given in the past still apply. Delay is due to land acquisition; no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify realisation gains versus cost gains in Q1 margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify; said margin gain was a mix of partial price increase, efficiencies and low-cost inventory, and asked analysts to focus on annual margin.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend payout plans given strong cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Payout was about 80-87% over three years via dividend and buyback; Board will consider. Management noted policy around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Imports and trade protection status?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports rose to about 73,000-74,000 tonnes/month from 45,000-46,000 in Q4 FY26; no ADD in place; safeguard QRs still under government consideration.
