segments.commentary: Reached INR624 crore; INR294 crore disbursed across 50 loans in Q1; ~45% of sustainable and emerging businesses portfolio in clean mobility and renewables.

segments.name: Satin Technologies / QTrino Labs
segments.commentary: First paying HRMS customers in Q1; QTrino Labs reached first customer revenue milestone. Core banking platform in customer UAT, go-live targeted Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives
segments.commentary: Progressing toward first close of Category 2 AIF, with first deployment expected in the coming quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated AUM growth of 20-25% in FY27, implying INR18,200-18,900 crore by March 2027.
Standalone reported credit cost of 3-3.5% for FY27, inclusive of any buffer built.
Standalone reported ROA of 3.5-4% for FY27; management expects QoQ ROA improvement from the 3.3% consolidated level.
NIM expected to stay in a 14.35-14.50% steady-state range.
Guidance to be reviewed at the half year depending on monsoon; long-term target INR32,000 crore consolidated AUM by 2030 with 30% from non-MFI.
Non-MFI share of consolidated AUM at 19% vs 14% a year ago; target 30% by 2030.
capex_capacity: Added 41 standalone branches in Q1; total 2,041 branches, 34 lakh clients, 3.9 lakh centres, 18,518 employees.
Commenced operations in Kerala in June 2026, adding to Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
392 branches added in FY26 are seasoning; operating expense ratio improved to 6.33% from 6.98% in Q4.
AUM per loan officer up 29% YoY.
Breakeven rule of thumb for a new branch: about 1,000 customers, typically reached in about 9 months.
INR100 crore promoter infusion approved by shareholders at about a 17% premium to the minimum issue price, to fund subsidiary growth.
demand_pricing: Q1 is seasonally the softest quarter; management called Q1 disbursements the highest first-quarter disbursements in company history.

Assam floods hit 3 districts (Jorhat, Sivasagar, Charaideo): about 44,000 borrowers and INR149.83 crore outstanding affected, of which INR96.95 crore is covered by nat-cat insurance. Management says Assam ex-those districts is 100% on target.
Bank share of outstanding MFI loans fell to 26.4% from 32.6% a year ago; NBFC-MFI share rose to 43.7% from 38.9%.
Marginal cost of borrowing down 37 bps YoY to 10.52%; 77 active lenders; top 10 lenders are 52% of borrowing; INR2,000 crore direct assignment sanction from a public sector bank.
Undrawn sanctions of INR2,600 crore; INR3,000 crore raised in the quarter including INR285 crore subordinated debt (sub-debt total INR497 crore).

qa_highlights.question: How large should the management overlay buffer be built annually or quarterly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not committing to a number; the buffer depends on macro and field conditions and may not be needed. On-book provision is INR250 crore against an RBI requirement of INR152 crore.

qa_highlights.question: DA income trajectory and sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: DA is kept at 20-22% of AUM; Q1 DA was INR94 crore (Q4 was heavier at about INR140 crore). Q2 and Q3 should be in a similar range; Q4 is seasonally heavier.

qa_highlights.question: Gross slippages and write-offs in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages were INR49 crore (vs INR90 crore in Q4). Write-offs were INR127 crore, elevated because GNPA fell by about 90 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Stress from monsoon or Assam?
qa_highlights.answer: Assam is covered largely by nat-cat insurance; only about 5% of the Assam portfolio (INR149 crore) is affected, of which 3.5-4% is insured, leaving about 1% exposed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated AUM guidance lower than last quarter's 25-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says guidance is deliberately conservative; it expects to achieve 20-25% and stable-state growth of 20-25% in FY28 is not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is credit cost up while asset quality improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages halved to INR49 crore and GNPA fell 90 bps, but the overlay rose from a little over INR20 crore to INR36 crore, lifting reported credit cost.

risks_watch: Monsoon impact on rural cash flows over the next 2-3 months; Assam collections in the three flood-hit districts.
Negative carry from surplus liquidity: quarter-end drag about 0.15-0.20%, lower over the full quarter per management.
Forex: INR3 crore net negative impact in Q1 from hedged ECB (INR1,573 crore outstanding) accounting mismatch between servicing income and finance cost.
Subsidiary returns remain dilutive during scale-up; consolidated ROA is in an investment phase.
Credit cost guidance of 3-3.5% reported; further overlay additions would depress reported ROA.

532993|2026-06.headline: Sejal Glass Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR117.95 crore, up 52.88% YoY; management guides FY27 revenue growth of minimum 25%, up to 40%.
532993|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 52.88% YoY to INR117.95 crore, with India up 67.03% to INR36.43 crore and UAE up 47.31% to INR81.52 crore. Consolidated EBITDA grew over 44% YoY to INR18 crore and PAT grew over 63% YoY to INR7.22 crore. Management cited a one-time-like INR1 crore people-cost hit from appraisals and a Taloja labour union agreement, plus UAE logistics and fuel-related cost increases, as drags on Q1 margin. Guidance was framed as a 25% minimum and up to 40% revenue growth for FY27, with EBITDA margin up about 1% and PAT margin of 9-10% targeted, mainly from Q3-Q4.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR52 crore total, of which term loan ~INR38 crore and working capital ~INR14 crore

segments.name: India (Silvassa, Taloja, Erode)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR36.43 crore, up 67.03% YoY; India exports about 6% of sales, domestic 94%. Silvassa utilisation ~77%, Taloja ~55%, Erode ~15%.

segments.name: UAE
segments.commentary: Revenue INR81.52 crore, up 47.31% YoY; utilisation ~71% on tempering base line, with 95% of UAE output sold locally and in GCC, Africa emerging. Order book about AED70-72 million.

segments.name: Railway / fire-safety / bulletproof verticals
segments.commentary: Railway was under 1% of Q1 revenue; fire-rated glass production to start Q3 FY27. Management targets 10% of revenue from these verticals next year, including railway.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at minimum 25%, with upside to around 40% if geopolitical situation stabilises and order inflows continue.
FY27 EBITDA margin to improve by about 1% over upcoming quarters; PAT margin target of around 9% (CFO) to 9-10% (promoter) for FY27, mainly in Q3 and Q4.
Q2 FY27 revenue expected at INR140-145 crore (15-20% QoQ growth from Q1 INR118 crore).
FY28 revenue growth expected at least 25% YoY (early-stage guidance).
UAE monthly revenue on track to AED31 million in Q1 and AED35 million in Q2 per prior commentary; July at AED11.87 million.
Management indicated 25-40% annual growth range over the next 3-4 years.
Expected UAE revenue mix shift to around 60:40 (UAE:India) this year and 50:50 next year.
capex_capacity: UAE third tempering line (capex incl. fire-rated tech total ~AED15 million) installed; commercial production expected Q3 FY27 end, third line utilisation 15-20% initially. UAE total tempering capacity to ~24 lakh sq m per annum.
UAE plant utilisation ~71% now, target 85%; existing two lines expected to reach ~75%.
Silvassa targeted at 85-90% by year end; Taloja 75% in coming quarters; Erode 25-30% in coming quarters.
India capex is maintenance-type, below INR1 crore per item.
Funding: UAE capex from internal accruals plus proposed ~AED7 million long-term bank loan, roughly 50:50 debt-equity.

Management indicated capacity additions across UAE third line and Taloja/Erode could add about INR75 crore revenue capacity on top of ~INR600 crore from existing capacity (analyst-stated, confirmed by promoter).
demand_pricing: UAE order book about AED70-72 million (~INR175 crore), up from ~AED50 million; incremental inflow AED22-27 million; execution from June-July over next two quarters.
India order inflow above INR50 crore from developers including Godrej, L&T, Prestige and Raheja, to be executed over about 6 months.
Customer execution is gated by end-customer site readiness and design approvals, delaying size release; management says July UAE revenue already crossed AED11.87 million.
Bad debts below 0.5% over last three years; top 15 clients currently >70% of India business, ~200 repeat clients.
Management says no listed architectural glass peer in India; Asahi India Glass is mainly automotive and Borosil is solar.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin guidance and what is the closing order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated EBITDA up about 1% and PAT around 9%; order book referenced as India >INR50 crore and UAE ~AED70 million. Promoter said 25% is minimum growth, up to 40% upside, after an earlier TV comment of 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Current and peak capacity utilisation by plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Silvassa ~77%, Taloja ~55%, Erode ~15%, UAE ~71%. Targets: Silvassa 85-90% by year end, Taloja 75%, Erode 25-30%, UAE 85%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there capex planned and how much capacity will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: India capex under INR1 crore per item for maintenance. UAE third tempering line and fire-rated tech total ~AED15 million; commercial production Q3 end; total tempering capacity ~24 lakh sq m per annum.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the Q1 margin squeeze?
qa_highlights.answer: Appraisal and yearly increments plus a Taloja labour union agreement added about INR1 crore people cost; UAE logistics hit by June war disruption; raw material costs up about 1% due to diesel and energy surcharge.

qa_highlights.question: Why has UAE monthly sales stayed near AED10-10.5 million despite a AED60-70 million order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Tailor-made orders are released in size only when end customers are ready, so production timing lags order inflow. July UAE revenue reached AED11.87 million.

qa_highlights.question: How is the UAE capex funded and what are FY28 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded from internal accruals plus a proposed ~AED7 million long-term bank loan. FY28 revenue growth expected at least 25%, too early for margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Railway and new vertical contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway under 1% of Q1 revenue; target 10% of revenue from railway, fire-safety and related verticals next year. Approved vendor for Kapurthala, Raebareli and Chennai railway facilities.

541974|2026-06.headline: Manorama Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore, with PAT margin at 19.5%.
541974|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore, crossing INR 400 crore for the first time, with management attributing growth mainly to volume (about 85% YoY per management). EBITDA rose 42.2% to INR 106 crore at a 26.3% margin, and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore. Management said the QIP of about INR 500 crore has closed and it has lined up a ~INR 460 crore capex plan spanning India and Burkina Faso, with commissioning targeted around Q3 FY28. Several answers were qualitative or deferred, notably on guidance, Brazil revenue, and subsidiary losses.

segments.name: Value-added specialty fats (CBE and stearin)
segments.commentary: Management said CBE is about 30% and stearin about 70% of the contribution from these products; per-ton realisations were not shared, but pricing was described as largely stable.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (consolidated vs standalone)
segments.commentary: Consolidated PAT loss narrowed to about INR 3 crore from about INR 8 crore in Q4 FY26, with negligible subsidiary revenue; West African entities are sourcing vehicles and Brazil is in build-out.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation guidance is about 80% (management internal target 80-85%) on expanded capacity of about 52,000 tonnes per annum after 4,500 t debottlenecking; the company declined to restate the INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue guidance from November, pointing to utilisation metrics instead.
FY27 capex guidance of about INR 225-250 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date and about INR 220 crore more planned in FY27.

Gross margin expected in a 45-50% range, with EBITDA margin the preferred tracking metric; management said margins should hold broadly stable at current range, with quarter-to-quarter movement possible.

Burkina Faso facility (about INR 120-130 crore) has an estimated payback of about 3 years once operational; the remainder of the ~INR 460 crore plan is for India (solvent fractionation 3 and refinery).
Solvent fractionation 3 and refinery targeted for commissioning around Q3 FY28; full impact expected in FY29 as plants ramp up.
Balance sheet: no further equity dilution planned; working capital to be funded via existing banker lines led by SBI, plus ~INR 150 crore FDR outside the QIP proceeds.
capex_capacity: Current fractionation capacity 47,500 t per annum; additional 7,500 t already operational, with a further 4,500 t debottlenecking targeted around Q3 FY27, taking capacity to about 52,000 t.
Debottlenecking cost estimated at INR 5-6 crore.

Burkina Faso: about 10 hectares (24 acres) land acquired for shea nut and mango nut processing with regulatory approvals pending; facility covers extraction and expelling, solvent fractionation and related capacity, about INR 120-130 crore.
Overall proposed capex plan about INR 460 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date; Q1 spend about INR 20 crore across Manorama and subsidiaries.
Brazil (LatAm) partner: trial production started in the last quarter; ramp-up expected gradually over the next 2-4 quarters, with production sourced from the Indian plant.
Asset turn currently about 7x; management would not guide to 7x-9x going forward.
demand_pricing: Demand described as volume-led; management attributed about 85% YoY growth to volume.
Pricing described as largely stable for value-added products, in line with the costing model that passes through raw material inflation.
Raw material mix: about 50-60% imported seeds and butters, the rest domestic seeds (sal, mango) and butters.
Contracts are 9-12 months and renew on a rolling basis; no renewal percentage was disclosed.
Nigeria's temporary shea nut export ban was called non-material given sourcing across about 10 African subsidiaries.
Exports to more than 30 countries; export share about 55-60% in Q1 FY25 and 60% in Q1 FY27 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the 4,500 t debottlenecking and greenfield capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Debottlenecking is due around Q3 FY27; solvent fractionation 3 and refinery are targeted around Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production started; gradual quarter-on-quarter ramp expected over 2-4 quarters; no revenue guidance given yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about 20% QoQ, and is it the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior quarter included a performance incentive provision; run-rate guided at INR 14-15 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline and raw material cost ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin expected at 45-50%; management disputed the 75-80% H1 raw material ratio, saying it has been about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated subsidiary losses and whether they will narrow?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses reflect operating costs of sourcing vehicles and Brazil build-out; drag expected to reduce as entities scale, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation guidance versus the 85-90% cited in the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target 80-85%; 80% advised for stakeholders, with upside to be communicated if achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Funding of working capital for the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded by existing bank lines (SBI lead), the QIP of about INR 500 crore and FDR of about INR 150 crore; no further equity dilution planned.

risks_watch: Supplier dispute: a debit note has been raised for the full claim amount against a foreign manufacturer/supplier, with no recovery timeline or confirmation of liability given.
Geopolitical and freight disruption; management said freight and container costs drove the 16% jump in other expenses.
Utilisation target ambiguity (80% vs 85-90%) and withdrawal of the INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue guidance.
Subsidiary and Brazil losses weigh on consolidated margins; timing of breakeven undisclosed.
Working capital needs for new capacity (analyst estimate INR 900-1,000 crore) and reliance on bank lines.
Hedging policy of 50-60% of net exposure; forex gains formed about INR 13 crore of the INR 16 crore other income, so the earnings quality of other income is a watch item.
541974|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and capacity build-out, but evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify margins, revenue guidance, Brazil contribution, subsidiary breakeven, and per-ton realisations, redirecting to utilisation and "business has risk" framing.

financial_highlights.change: of which ~INR 13 crore forex gain, ~INR 3 crore FDR income
prior quarter elevated by performance incentive provision

543260|2026-06.headline: Stove Kraft Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41.3% YoY to INR480.6 crore, with EBITDA up 50.9% to INR53.8 crore and margin at 11.2%.
543260|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the strongest first quarter since inception, with revenue of INR480.6 crore (up 41.3%), gross profit of INR190.4 crore (up 46%) and PAT of INR17.1 crore (up 63.5%). Induction Cooktops grew 315.9% YoY and were about 27% of revenue, while small appliances and gas cooktops moderated because capacity and people were diverted to induction. Price hikes in domestic and export markets were used to pass on input cost inflation, supporting gross margin expansion of 127 bps. Working capital rose to 45 days on festive inventory build-up, and management guided to Q2 growth despite a high base.

financial_highlights.change: Higher than Q4 FY26; better than Q1 FY26 (69 days)

segments.name: Induction Cooktops (ICT)
segments.commentary: Grew 315.9% YoY and contributed 27% of revenue (about INR130 crore per analyst calculation). Management expects ICT to reach at least 20% of revenue for the year and about 2x last year on an annualised basis.

segments.name: Pressure Cookers
segments.commentary: Grew 41.3% YoY; management says it is the largest by volume at current run rate, with capacity additions under way.

segments.name: Non-stick cookware
segments.commentary: Grew 21.8% YoY and contributed 21% of revenue.

segments.name: Small appliances and gas cooktops
segments.commentary: Moderated temporarily due to capacity diversion to induction; small appliances still make up 27.5% of revenue mix. Management says capacity has since been augmented.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce 31.8% of revenue, general trade 28.6% (up 56.2% YoY, strongest in three years), exports 15.3%, modern retail 13%, and retail 8.7% (up 86.3% YoY). Added 17 franchise stores in the quarter, targeting 500 Pigeon exclusive outlets by end-2027.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 revenue expected to grow YoY over Q2 FY26 (about INR475-480 crore base), though not necessarily at Q1's growth rate.
Gross margin expected to improve at least 1% YoY; management views 40-42% as the sustainable gross margin band.
EBITDA margin targeted to rise at least 1 pp YoY, reaching 14-15% within two to three years.
Long-term PAT margin trajectory of 7-8% over two to three years, per management comments on a TV interview.
Non-induction categories targeted to grow about 15%+ consistently, with a stated aim near 20%; overall growth targeted at 15-20%.
Exports plus IKEA expected to reach about 15% of revenue in the current and next year; IKEA full-scale could be 5-6% of business. IKEA supplies to start in Q2 FY27.
Retail: profitable above INR2.5 lakh sales per store per month; currently about INR4.3 lakh, target at least INR5 lakh.
Triply cookware circle production in China JV expected by December 2026; automated pressure cooker line ready by end Q3.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing facilities set up in the last few quarters are all up and running, per management.
Pressure cooker capacity being added to meet unmet demand; a fully automated pressure cooker line is being set up, ready by end of Q3 FY27.
Small appliance capacity was diverted to induction and infrared products in Q1; management says it has since been augmented.
Triply cookware: JV with a Chinese partner, reportedly among the largest facilities in China; machines being installed; commercial production expected by December 2026.
Chimney range converted from AC to BLDC motors (all but one model); built-in hobs also being pushed.
Outsourced some manufacturing via job work in Q1 to meet demand; management expects this to normalise as in-house capacity comes up.
demand_pricing: Induction cooktop demand remains above pre-war levels; management expects traction to continue but not at the initial spike levels.
Cost-plus pricing model: domestic price increases taken and export buying prices revised upward to pass on input cost inflation.
Gross margin improvement attributed to price corrections and a favourable mix, including stainless steel pressure cookers outgrowing aluminium.
Q1 exchange-offer programme (mainly in EBOs and general trade) cited as a regular seasonal driver; GPOs up about 80% and general trade up about 50%.
Festive calendar spread across Q2 and Q3 (Onam in August, Dussehra in early October, Diwali in November).
South region about 50% of general trade contribution; North and West growing faster from a smaller base.
Working capital: inventory build-up for festive season; management plans straight-line production through the year to smooth working capital.

Other expenses rose to about 18% of sales, driven by job work (+1.2 pp), marketing (+1.2 pp; spend about 3.5-3.6% of sales), franchise commission (about 1% of sales; franchise mix 55-56% vs 43%), and CSR front-loading (about INR94 lakh, about 3% of PBT).

533033|2026-06.headline: ISGEC Q1 FY27 standalone total income up 51% to INR 1,585 crore, but PBT up only 10% to INR 123 crore; FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12%.
533033|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 51% YoY to INR 1,585 crore and EBIT grew 15% to INR 157 crore, with PBT up 10% to INR 123 crore as Q1 FY26 had high forex-driven other income. Manufacturing EBIT margin was 12% and projects EBIT margin 5.25%. Consolidated PBT was INR 53 crore, held back by an INR 83 crore loss at the Philippines ethanol plant, which ran at about 65-70% utilisation. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 10-12% and said it is conservative, citing carry-forward of order execution into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: about 45% higher vs INR 1,374 crore in Q1 FY26
includes INR 37 crore depreciation, INR 20 crore interest, INR 10 crore forex
vs INR 381 crore at 31 Mar 2026 and INR 408 crore at 30 Jun 2025
down INR 170 crore QoQ from INR 476 crore; INR 832 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Industrial Projects (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income up on improved execution per schedule; management expects roughly INR 1,000 crore per quarter in Q2 FY27 and projects EBIT margin of 5-6% for FY27. Export orders booked in Africa and Latin America.

segments.name: Manufacturing (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income lifted by dispatch of a roughly INR 130 crore US order that had been on hold; EBIT margin 12%, guided 12-13%. Steady-state consolidated manufacturing revenue guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter.

segments.name: Isgec Hitachi Zosen
segments.commentary: Orders in hand INR 889 crore. FY26 revenue about INR 670 crore; management expects about 10% growth in revenue and profit in FY27.

segments.name: Saraswati Sugar Mills
segments.commentary: Revenue down due to lower cane availability last season (untimely rain); cane availability improvement steps under way for next season.

segments.name: Philippines ethanol (CBPI)
segments.commentary: Q1 loss INR 83 crore at about 65-70% utilisation; crushed about 84,000 tonnes of cane, sold over 8 million litres of ethanol. Management targets about 90% utilisation by December and a much lower loss in Q2.

segments.name: Eagle Press and Isgec Titan Metal
segments.commentary: Eagle Press about INR 150 crore a year; Isgec Titan Metal expected at about INR 150 crore in FY27 vs INR 102 crore in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at 10-12%; management says the figure is conservative with a bias to realism.
Manufacturing EBIT margin guided at 12-13% for FY27; projects EBIT margin guided to improve slightly within 5-6%.
Isgec Hitachi Zosen revenue and profit guided about 10% higher than FY26.
Manufacturing capacity expansion (approved INR 502 crore) to add up to about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue when fully complete; main benefit from FY28-29.

Bhartauli machine-building phase 1 (INR 73 crore) to complete in early September 2026, with about INR 225 crore annual revenue potential; billing expected only from Q1 FY28 as work-in-progress builds first.
Dahej skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Philippines ethanol depreciation expected about INR 95 crore in FY27 (WDV method); interest about INR 19-20 crore per quarter.
capex_capacity: Bhartauli (Haryana) presses plant: phase 1 INR 70-73 crore completing first week of September 2026; phase 2 (INR 218 crore) completion expected around end-CY2027 or Q1 CY2028.
Dahej (Gujarat) SEZ skids and modules facility expected to complete around 31 May 2027.
Casting factory expansions, tubing and piping shops at Rattangarh and standard mechanical press factory at Bawal are running largely on schedule, with some facilities completing in FY27.
Board-approved manufacturing capex INR 502 crore; separate corporate office building under construction in projects business.
Q1 capex about INR 47 crore, funded from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong across almost all product lines; export inquiry base described as healthy.
Export orders booked in Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia; more than INR 750 crore of export orders booked in Q1.
Standalone orders of about INR 1,200 crore booked in July to date (Q2 FY27).
Management says INR 95/USD rupee improves competitiveness versus other bidders; export logistics costs, freight rates and transit times have risen due to the geopolitical situation.

Commodity prices (steel, copper, aluminium, nickel) stabilised but slightly above pre-war levels; war-related material cost increases have a small adverse effect on profitability, absorbed through contingencies.
Project mix shifting to shorter-duration (max 33-36 months, target 2-2.5 years) technology-intensive orders; avoiding long contract/site-erection-heavy orders.
Sugar machinery export orders up, particularly sugar refineries; management declined to detail the large export orders.

544309|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY (12% constant currency) to INR893 crores, with reported EBITDA of INR294 crores at 33% margin.
544309|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached about INR893 crores, up 21% YoY and 12% in constant currency, with forex gains neutral versus Q4. Reported EBITDA was INR294 crores (33%); management says it was about 35% after adding back roughly INR20 crores of one-time TruBridge acquisition costs. PAT was INR193-194 crores, up about 28% YoY. TruBridge closed on July 10, 2026, so Q1 figures are legacy IKS only; management reset TruBridge's steady-state revenue to about $300 million a year (from $340 million pre-close) while keeping its roughly $68 million EBITDA, and reaffirmed a FY30 EBITDA True North of at least INR3,000 crores without further dilution beyond ESOPs.

~+28% YoY; higher if adjusted for acquisition costs
QoQ decline attributed to acquisition costs and Abridge mark-to-market uplift via OCI
Legacy IKS guided to 22-23% for rest of FY27
Top 10 vintage ~6 years; top 5 vintage ~7 years
Cash flow hit by one-time NEVA customer payment; not reflected in net debt

segments.name: Legacy IKS (urban/semi-urban, large provider groups)
segments.commentary: Run-rate about $97 million a quarter (~$388 million annualised); management aspires to grow it at 12%+ constant currency. About 600 large provider groups served pre-TruBridge.

segments.name: TruBridge (rural and community EHR)
segments.commentary: Run-rate about $75 million a quarter (~$300 million annualised) after reset from $340 million; ~$68 million EBITDA maintained. Two non-profitable IT and early-out service lines (~$8 million a quarter revenue) to be exited; ~$2-3 million a quarter of customer discounts expected during transformation. Revenue growth outlook not yet given.

guidance_outlook: FY30 True North: at least INR3,000 crores EBITDA, targeted with marginal ESOP dilution only and no return to net debt above pre-TruBridge levels.
Blended EBITDA margin expected to return to early-to-mid 30s from a pro forma 26-27% drop over the next couple of years, via technology, offshore human-in-the-loop, and SG&A synergies.
Legacy IKS aspiration: 12%+ constant-currency growth, explicitly not guidance; TruBridge revenue aspiration to be set after two to three quarters.
Integration expenses expected in Q2 at a similar range to Q1 (~INR20 crores); tax rate guided at 22-23% for legacy IKS.
FY27 expected to remain EPS accretive despite the TruBridge revenue reset, per management.

capex_capacity: Headcount inflated above need ahead of TruBridge integration, including investment in TruBridge RCM customers; combined base just over 16,000 employees.
TruBridge acquisition priced at about $550 million for ~$68 million EBITDA, described as accretive.
Five-year lock-in deal signed recently at healthy pricing; no explicit capex figures disclosed.
Patent approved for AAW model (propensity to show/no-show and propensity to pay), deployed in MyCareHub.
demand_pricing: Legacy IKS cross-sell into large health systems showing early land-and-expand wins: Advocate Health Care (top-five US health system, >$35 billion revenue) expanded in RCM and coding; a large California system is moving regions to Epic; a national musculoskeletal aggregator signed a significant RCM deal; StrideCare (vascular) partnership.

Competitive intensity rising; management cites ~30 vendors moving from point solutions to platforms, including Abridge's clinician intelligence launch. Pricing pressure expected but pricing 'not the biggest issue' outside non-deterministic tasks.
Market: total TAM above $260 billion (overall growing ~8%); outsourced TAM ~$35 billion growing ~12%.
Axia Women's Health case study: $12 million cash impact, 96% coding accuracy, reduced denials.
Epic relationship described as strengthening; TruBridge also collaborating with Epic in rural market.

qa_highlights.question: What organic constant-currency growth is healthy over the medium term, and is margin expansion coming from currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin growth is not from currency: revenue grew 12% CC on 4.2% headcount growth; adjusted EBITDA is 35% with neutral forex. Aspiration is 12%+ CC on legacy IKS, not guidance; TruBridge growth to be set in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How does SLM fit with LLMs, and where does glass-box/explainable AI sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Three SLM approaches: standalone SLMs, LLM-distilled SLMs, and hierarchical SLM-plus-LLM. Explainability comes from knowledge graphs acquired via ARAI. Management would not commit to a 60% token-usage reduction, saying it will emerge over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire TruBridge and what criteria govern acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Chosen because the rural market is large, TruBridge holds 30%+ share as one of two dominant rural EHRs, and its service mix resembles ambulatory. Criteria: strategic thesis first, leverage tolerable relative to EBITDA, and accretive price; $68 million EBITDA bought for ~$550 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge's margin of 22-23% fixable, and does the INR3,000 crore target rule out M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers include existing and in-build technology plus offshore human-in-the-loop to restore early-to-mid 30s margins. INR3,000 crores is achievable without another acquisition, but M&A is not ruled out; white space seen as large.

qa_highlights.question: Does Abridge's platform move threaten IKS, and is pricing under pressure in renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management respects Abridge but sees ~30 vendors aspiring to platforms and rising competition. Recent five-year deal signed at healthy price; pricing pressure expected but margin leverage maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge still EPS accretive for FY27 after revenue reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; EBITDA is unchanged, so management says EPS accretion is absolute and possibly a bit higher than previously expected.

532178|2026-06.headline: Engineers India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 55% to INR109 crores, while turnover fell 7% to INR801 crores on Turnkey decline.
532178|2026-06.overview: Standalone PBT rose about 55% YoY to INR145 crores and PAT to INR109 crores, helped by Consultancy growth of about 22% to INR499 crores. Turnkey turnover fell to INR302 crores from INR449 crores as major projects tapered. Order book stood at INR14,424 crores at 30 June 2026, but Q1 order inflow was only INR514 crores. Management kept the INR8,000 crore FY27 order inflow target and the FY27 operating margin guidance of 16%, and said the Middle East new-mega-project pipeline has slowed.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR104 crores, 11.72% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR14,424 crores (Consultancy INR10,498 crores; Turnkey INR3,926 crores)

segments.name: Consultancy & Engineering
segments.commentary: Turnover INR499 crores, up ~22% YoY; segment profit margin rose to ~24% from 17% in Q1 FY26, with management targeting 24-25%.

segments.name: Turnkey (LSTK)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR302 crores, down from INR449 crores as major projects tapered; segment margin ~7.5% in Q1 FY27. New Turnkey orders are in early execution, with turnover expected to rise in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: CEIL subsidiary
segments.commentary: Profit INR6.88 crores vs INR2.69 crores a year earlier.

segments.name: Joint ventures / associates
segments.commentary: Contributed INR42.51 crores to consolidated profit vs a loss of INR7.37 crores in Q1 FY26. RFCL contributed about INR42 crores of revenue-linked profit; management expects some dividend from RFCL this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow target of INR8,000 crores maintained; management said it will try to cross it. Current inflow is about INR2,750 crores (about INR1,100 crores overseas, about INR1,500 crores domestic, of which ~INR1,500 crores domestic is LSTK and the rest consultancy).
FY27 consultancy revenue targeted at more than 50%, possibly around 55%, implying consultancy turnover of INR2,300-2,400 crores.
Total FY27 turnover growth target of at least 10% on last year's INR3,850-4,200 crore base; management said guidance could improve.
FY27 operating margin target held at 16%, same as FY26; upside possible if pending change orders are settled.
FY28 revenue target of INR5,000 crores maintained, with an intent to improve it.
Dividend payout of around 100% for the current financial year referenced.
capex_capacity: Company is setting up a CBG plant with its own investment (non-hydrocarbon).
RFCL plant expected to run about 330 days a year; a 30-35 day regular shutdown in December will carry technical work without hitting profitability.
No specific capex amounts or commissioning dates were given for other projects.
demand_pricing: Middle East: new mega projects on hold or slow; existing jobs continuing. Secured about INR500 crores of Middle East business in Q1, including PMC work of INR400 crores under long-term agreements. Aramco contract in place but no major inquiry yet.
Overseas share of current inflow is about INR1,100 crores out of INR2,750 crores.
Nuclear: environmental studies for 3 private projects and 1 government project; engaged with NPCIL on engineering consultancy; SMR work secured last year.
Coal gasification: government VGF support of INR34,000 crores revived feasibility inquiries; an NTPC gas-to-SNG project is ongoing; results expected in a couple of months.
Domestic pipeline: BPCL Andhra execution tender may come by year-end; IOCL Paradip Phase 2 awaits OMC approval; ONGC petrochemical project only at feasibility stage.
Infrastructure about 45% of business in the current year, mostly LSTK/OBE, with a recent data-centre assignment from PowerTel.
Competition described as high in all segments, with most work won through competitive bidding.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore order inflow target still achievable, and how much would be consultancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is unchanged, with about INR2,750 crores in hand now and about two quarters left. Consultancy is about INR1,100 crores of this, with the rest mainly LSTK domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be write-backs or change orders this year, including HPCL Barmer?
qa_highlights.answer: No exceptional change order is in the current quarter and no provision write-backs are expected; provisions reverse only after the defect liability period ends.

qa_highlights.question: How should consultancy growth and margins be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Consultancy growth target is at least 10%+ overall, with consultancy above 50% of turnover; segment profit is targeted at 24-25%. Operating margin target is 16%, with possible upside from change orders.

qa_highlights.question: Have Middle East clients put projects on hold due to the conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no existing project is stopped; new mega projects are on hold or slow, and routine jobs continue.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue be recognised on the Dangote Nigeria order?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on cost-progress basis, with turnover booked as cost progress is achieved over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan to distribute surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to distribute the full reserves now, as other investment plans are under consideration, and pointed to about 100% dividend this year.

risks_watch: Turnkey turnover fell 33% YoY; management expects recovery in Q3-Q4 but this depends on execution of new projects still in early phase.
Q1 order inflow of INR514 crores is far below the run rate needed for INR8,000 crores; the target depends on a few lumpy domestic and overseas wins.
Middle East (about 12-15% exposure per analyst estimate) faces slow new mega-project awards; Saudi/Aramco work still at initial discussion stage.
Q1 operating margin of ~14% is below the 16% full-year target, so the guidance depends on later quarters and change-order settlements.
Coal gasification and nuclear inquiries remain at feasibility or EOI stage; timing and value of awards unclear.
Management did not confirm the Turnkey-to-consultancy mix beyond ranges given, and gave conflicting statements on the consultancy share (50-60%, around 55%).
532178|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on consultancy margins, growth and dividends, but cautious on the Middle East and on new mega-project awards. Several answers were vague or shifting, notably on the consultancy mix, the margin target and the order-inflow path.

532524|2026-06.headline: PTC India Q1 FY27 standalone PBT fell 32% to Rs 96 crore on 12% higher trading volume of 25.78 BU, as lower surcharge and rebate income offset gains.
532524|2026-06.overview: Trading volume rose 12% to 25.78 billion units at a stated margin of 3.35 paise per unit, and total operating income rose 2% to Rs 113 crore. Standalone PBT fell 32% to Rs 96 crore and PAT fell 33% to Rs 71 crore, which management attributed to lower net surcharge and rebate income as Discoms' liquidity improved. Consolidated PBT fell 48% to Rs 151 crore, also reflecting a Rs 82 crore impairment reversal in the year-ago quarter. Management declared an interim dividend of Rs 23 per share, which it described as one-time, linked to the PTC Energy (PEL) asset sale to ONGC.

segments.name: Power trading
segments.commentary: Volume up 12% to 25.78 BU, with 60% from exchange-traded products and the rest bilateral short, medium and long-term. Management said the volume growth came mainly from exchange trade.

segments.name: Consultancy / C&I services
segments.commentary: Management said the business is steadily growing and is a stable piece, but declined to give projections. No figures were disclosed.

segments.name: Power exchange associates
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 total income Rs 13.98 crore and PAT about Rs 5.16 crore, as disclosed in response to a question.

segments.name: PTC Financial Services (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Management described performance as less than spectacular. Its PBT decline also drove part of the consolidated fall, and the company is now looking to divest it, with SBI Capital engaged as transaction advisor.

guidance_outlook: Management expects power demand to grow 4%-6% annually, with short-term volatility from weather.

Long-term capacity additions: management said no new long-term contracts are expected in FY27 or FY28 because of regulatory constraints. Growth will come from battery storage and time-of-day/seasonal trades.
NTPC Green 1,200 MW long-term solar PPA is expected to come online around FY29.
Teesta Urja (1.2 GW) is under construction; a cofferdam-stage power start is expected around December 2026, with about 40%-50% generation initially.
Interim dividend of Rs 23 per share is a one-time measure and should not be expected annually.
PFS disinvestment: management expects to say more to the market closer to the end of FY27; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Long-term PPA of 1,200 MW signed with NTPC Green for solar power procurement, expected online around FY29.
Teesta Urja 1.2 GW hydro project under construction after the cloudburst-related washout, with staged commissioning.
NLC India JV: DPE approval received; Board has approved investment of up to Rs 500 crore, to be deployed over time.
Battery storage: management said it is in discussions and evaluating whether to own storage assets or contract for storage services, with no tie-up announced.
demand_pricing: Standalone PBT decline was driven by lower net surcharge and rebate income, which management attributed to improved Discom liquidity and Discoms paying on time to capture rebates.
Long-term volume decline YoY was attributed to lower hydro generation under long-term agreements.
Management said pricing is competitive and that some contracts are taken as marketing calls. Trading margins are expected to depend on portfolio mix, with exchange markets providing lower margins.

Management said trading on spot and exchange markets is only about 8,000-9,000 MW against peak demand of about 260,000 MW, and that policy changes such as merchant capacity mandates could deepen the market.
Contracts for difference (SECI pilot) and the futures market were cited as policy developments.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the long-term PPA book expires in the next one to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing is likely to expire in the next three years. It did not give the average remaining tenor and promised data by email.

qa_highlights.question: Why did long-term capacity decline YoY, and will it grow?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline was due to lower hydro generation under long-term agreements. Management said no new long-term contracts are expected in FY27 or FY28 due to regulatory constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Why did rebate income decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Discoms are now paying early and capturing rebates themselves, while PTC pays generators early and then recovers from Discoms later, so PTC's net rebate income fell.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a Rs 17.4 crore provision booked (Note 8)?
qa_highlights.answer: It relates to a generator's claim from a legal dispute over a contract. The adjudicating authority ruled that PTC pay first and recover later. The provision was made on auditor consultation, with no clear visibility on recovery from the counterparty.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash position and who are the top debtors?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone net cash was Rs 2,451 crore at 30 June, before the interim dividend. Top debtors: Punjab (about Rs 860 crore), UP (about Rs 600 crore), Haryana (about Rs 500 crore), Rajasthan (about Rs 400 crore), and Tamil Nadu (about Rs 300 crore). Management said PTC's own exposure is not more than 60 days, as back-to-back pass-through items inflate gross debtors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for PFS and how much stake will PTC keep?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a transaction advisor (SBI Capital) is appointed and the process is under way. No stake or timeline was committed, and the structure depends on advisor input.

qa_highlights.question: Will CERC's HPX rule affect PTC?
qa_highlights.answer: The CERC rule caps shareholding at 5% for trading members. PTC holds more than 22% of HPX, so it cannot be a trading member unless it reduces its stake below 5%, which management said depends on several factors.

544619|2026-06.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore, with EBITDA margin at 34.7% despite an LPG-driven specialty slowdown.
544619|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 27% YoY to INR158.3 crore and EBITDA rose 25% to INR54.9 crore, with margin at 34.7%. PAT increased to INR40.6 crore (PAT margin 25.6%). Pharma, food and nutrition (PFN) grew 31% (management also cited 30% in Q&A), mainly on volume from phosphates. Specialty ingredients grew 19% after LPG shortages in April and first half of May cut utilisation, and NSS (European subsidiary) was weak due to energy costs at a major infant formula customer in Ireland. Management said specialty and PFN momentum should continue into Q2, with price pass-through on phosphates mainly landing in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: +27% YoY from INR124.9 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR31.3 crore in Q1 FY26
below historical growth due to LPG shortage

segments.name: Pharma, food and nutrition (PFN)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 31% YoY, 69% of total; growth mainly volume-driven on phosphates with largest customer, with about 3% from currency. Bisglycinate (Absorbis) Q1 sales already exceed full FY26 sales.

segments.name: Specialty ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue up 19% YoY, 31% of total; utilisation below 50% for half the quarter due to LPG shortage, supplies restored at higher cost. Segment margin 26% including NSS; mid-30s excluding NSS.

segments.name: NSS (European subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Challenging quarter; major infant formula customer in Ireland scaled down and delayed buying. Management expects FY27 flattish to single-digit growth; target similar margins to core specialty by FY28. Five customer approvals and 12 active projects since new business head joined in June.

segments.name: Sudeep Advanced Materials (battery materials, iron phosphate)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 commissioning targeted April 2027; major long-lead equipment deliveries due October 2026. 21 customers at lab validation, 16 at pilot scale, 7 at pre-commercial/commercial validation; 8 customers now qualified. Two MOUs signed with South Korean cathode makers in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Specialty ingredients expected to return to historical growth trajectory from Q2 FY27; core specialty expected to bounce back in Q2.
Price increases on phosphates (phosphoric acid up ~50% in the quarter) expected to largely offset input cost impact in Q2.
EBITDA margin target of 37-38% sustained; management said pre-investment margins were 37-38% and current level is ~35%.

Two significant binding off-take agreements for SAM expected later in calendar 2026; scale-up from 100 to 200 KTPA to be timed after signing, with current target between CY2030 and CY2031.

Greenfield utilisation expected around one-third in FY28, with hockey-stick ramp in year three; optimum utilisation 70-75%.
capex_capacity: Sudeep Advanced Materials Phase 1 commissioning targeted April 2027; Phases 1-3 take planned capacity to 100 KTPA; Dahej site can support 200 KTPA, beyond which a new location is needed.
Greenfield Nandesari facility: approved for food and nutrition, pharma approval pending; five food and nutra customers approving the site (three Indian, two global MNCs).

Asset turns at scale for battery and greenfield expected at about 2.7x to 3x; asset turns at 200 KTPA may exceed that.
Phase 2 HPMC/PVP excipients not expected to be commercialised this financial year.
demand_pricing: Phosphate demand exceeds current manufacturing capacity, giving visibility for the rest of FY27.
Phosphoric acid price up ~50% in the quarter due to logistics costs and sulfur price spike; pass-through mostly reflected in Q2.
Bisglycinate: two large North American customers approved; company behind schedule on deliveries; management expects it to be a top 2-3 PFN product within 2-3 years.
Europe was a key growth contributor for core specialty; NSS weighed by energy costs.
Management said NSS and specialty are not competing with the exited German distributor in existing categories.

qa_highlights.question: How much of PFN's 30% growth came from price vs volume, and what is bisglycinate visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth mainly volume-driven (about 3% from currency); price increases to show up in Q2. Bisglycinate sales are behind schedule on delivery to two US customers; significant growth expected in the next 2-3 years rather than this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is PFN growth sustainable, and what does the greenfield add?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity can add only a couple of percent more; greenfield commissioning in Q3 gives the next leg of growth. Management expects PFN growth to be sustainable at scale in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did specialty margin fall to 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sub-50% utilisation for half the quarter and overhead inefficiency; NSS dragged margin. Core specialty without NSS was in the mid-30s.

qa_highlights.question: Scale-up plans for battery materials and land availability?
qa_highlights.answer: 100 to 200 KTPA scale-up will be timed after binding off-takes; Dahej site can support 200 KTPA; beyond that a new location is required.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of NSS customer issues and the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Largest infant formula customer scaled down Irish operations due to energy crisis; FY27 flattish to single-digit growth. Plan: new sales head expanding outside Ireland and supplying mostly from India; margins similar to core specialty possible in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and steady-state utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up for raw materials and battery business; long-term working capital cycle closer to 150 days. Optimum utilisation 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: Europe distribution and phosphoric acid sourcing for battery business?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales team built to replace the exited German distributor; no overlap in existing products. No phosphoric acid sourced from China for SAM (FEOC compliance); about 3 other countries plus India supply.

543663|2026-06.headline: Five-Star Q1 FY27 disbursements hit a record INR 1,496 crore (+23% QoQ, +16% YoY) while AUM grew 4% QoQ to INR 13,722 crore.

Competition: management cited new competitors entering, requiring more competitive employee compensation.

513519|2026-06.headline: Pitti Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹529 crores, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 16.8% and Lamination FY27 volume target raised to 82,000 tons.

Lamination and assembly volume grew 19% to about 19,200 tons, and management raised its FY27 Lamination target to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons. Incremental LPG costs being passed through to customers per management.

543931|2026-06.headline: Veefin standalone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 128% YoY to Rs 23.14 crore, with EBITDA at Rs 12.83 crore (55.4% margin) and PAT at Rs 6.74 crore.
543931|2026-06.overview: Management reported standalone revenue of Rs 23.14 crore (up 128% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 12.83 crore at a 55.4% margin, and PAT of Rs 6.74 crore (up 151% YoY). Consolidated revenue was Rs 113.97 crore with PAT of Rs 9.5 crore, which management said reflects the group perimeter rather than margin deterioration. Five new clients were signed, including a six-product win with a GCC digital bank, and the qualified pipeline ended the quarter at about $80 million after $15.27 million converted. The amalgamation is at step five of seven, with the NCLT second motion petition being filed. Management also disclosed Rs 50 crore of short-term debt at roughly 14-15%, secured by promoter share pledges, to bridge working capital.

segments.name: Standalone (Veefin Solutions Ltd, product lens)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 23.14 crore, EBITDA Rs 12.83 crore (55.4%), PAT Rs 6.74 crore; management says this is the purest view of product economics. Revenue split roughly 50-50 domestic and international.

segments.name: Consolidated (statutory perimeter, incl. subsidiaries and group entities)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 113.97 crore, EBITDA Rs 22.4 crore (19.7%), PAT Rs 9.5 crore (8.3%). Management attributes the lower margin to subsidiaries' different business profile, not deterioration.

guidance_outlook: Management says FY27 is the year the platform shifts from building to monetising; amalgamation expected to close within the next quarter to quarter and a half, with NCLT final order as the last substantive step.
Revenue from signed deals to be recognised as implementation fees over roughly 9 months, then licence fees from go-live, and AMC from year 2; all five Q1 contracts are five-year terms.
Services EBITDA margin (about 20%) expected to remain similar over the next 3-5 years, per management.
Half-yearly numbers to show TREDX platform revenue, as payment milestones for signed trade and cash deals fall in later periods.
Management plans to retire the short-term debt (2-3 year tenure) earlier than maturity.
capex_capacity: Management said the capex cycle this year is much lower than last year, but working capital needs remain because revenue is lumpy while spend is roughly constant through the year.
PSB Xchange: 3 lenders live, 7 under integration (about half non-PSU), 22 yet to start; 10 lenders now presented deals (3 live plus 7 in progress).
PSB Xchange limits increased to Rs 5,800 crore from Rs 5,400 crore; cumulative requirements rose to Rs 26,000 crore; 94 corporate deals in the pipeline at some stage.
Management sees an inflection point at 10-12 integrated banks, when inter-bank competition starts.
demand_pricing: Qualified pipeline bridge: opened at $79.62 million, added $20.4 million, converted $15.27 million, and removed about $4.5 million deferred on timelines; closed at $80.13 million.
Pipeline mix: about 70% non-supply-chain finance and about 70% outside India; 26 of 52 tracked deals involve more than one product.

Five new clients signed in Q1, including a six-product win with a large GCC digital bank (LOS, LMS, collections, trade finance, supply chain, limits microservice) and a Middle East non-bank lender taking LOS, LMS and collections; a five-country Africa supply chain and LOS rollout.
Pipeline and deal values are stated as five-year contract value (implementation, licence and AMC fees combined).
Management says Veefin wins on technology architecture but falls short against incumbents with 30-40 year histories.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise debt at 15-16% when equity is cheaper, and why is Rs 50 crore needed if capex is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited equity market timing, permanent dilution, and the view that the stock price is not attractive. Promoters pledged shares to secure the debt. The debt is for working capital gaps from lumpy revenue, with plans to retire it over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is pipeline stalling, given it moved only from Rs 79.62 crore to Rs 80.13 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $15.27 million was converted and $20.4 million added, replenishing about 25% of the opening pipeline in one quarter. It acknowledged the replenishment should ideally have been slightly lower.

qa_highlights.question: Why are only 3 of 32 lender integrations live?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed delays to lender IT bandwidth and PSU legacy systems, and said non-PSU lenders make up about half of the 7 integrations in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What triggers invocation of the promoter pledge, and what happens if the NCLT approval slips?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is not price-linked. The covenants are EBITDA at most 3x and DSCR at least 1.25, with headroom described as large. Management does not expect NCLT delay; if it slips by months, it is outside company control.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rs 60 crore subsidiary debts, and did standalone guarantee them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 60 crore sits with subsidiaries Infini and Nityo, and that Veefin (standalone) has provided guarantees for it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PSB Xchange pipeline Rs 26,000 crore while approvals are Rs 5,800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said banks set their own pace; the platform surfaces requests to providers but cannot accelerate bank decisions. Competition among banks is expected once 10-12 are integrated.

~40% higher YoY; ~40% lower QoQ vs Q4

503811|2026-06.headline: Siyaram Silk Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.4% to INR466 crores, EBITDA up 22.3% to INR40 crores at 8.6% margin, PAT INR11 crores.
503811|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income grew 16.4% YoY to INR466 crores, with fabrics at 71% of revenue, garments 19% and yarn & others 10%. EBITDA rose 22.3% to INR40 crores, margin 8.6%, and PAT more than doubled to INR11 crores (PAT margin 2.4%) on operating leverage. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~12% revenue growth and ~14% EBITDA margin including retail, with a ~150 bps EBITDA drag from ZECODE and DEVO. Adhik Maas moderated wedding demand in the quarter, and Diwali is expected to be ~3 weeks later this year.

financial_highlights.change: Mostly recurring (delayed interest, rent); ~30% is mark-to-market gain
FY27 expectation ~INR160 crores vs ~INR70-80 crores in FY26

segments.commentary: Contributed 71% of Q1 FY27 revenue. No separate segment margin or growth figure disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Contributed 19% of Q1 FY27 revenue. No separate growth or margin figure disclosed.

segments.name: Yarn & Others
segments.commentary: Contributed 10% of Q1 FY27 revenue. No separate growth or margin figure disclosed.

segments.name: Retail (ZECODE and DEVO)
segments.commentary: Store count at 30 ZECODE and 19 DEVO after adding 3 and 2 stores in Q1; target ~70 stores across both in FY27. Q1 revenue ~INR30 crores; FY27 revenue target ~INR160 crores; EBITDA drag guided at ~150 bps annually.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance (including retail): ~12% revenue growth and ~14% EBITDA margin, reiterated by management.
Retail drag on annual EBITDA margin guided at ~150 bps; management said it expects to be well within that budget. Stated as a ballpark, including all store costs (rent included per management).
ZECODE store profitability expected in 1.5 to 2 years; some ZECODE stores already EBITDA positive, including some under one year old.
FY27 capex about INR100 crores, of which INR40-50 crores for retail; management expects positive free cash flow to remain this year.
Store expansion to accelerate only after business predictability and proof of mature store model; ~70 stores targeted in FY27, funded by internal accruals.
Real estate project (land development): construction expected to start in Q1 FY27, 24-month completion; no revenue booked yet.
capex_capacity: ZECODE and DEVO network: 30 and 19 stores at quarter end after adding 3 and 2 in Q1; ~25-30 stores in total as of June per management.
Average ZECODE store size moved from ~4,000 sq ft high-street formats to ~7,000 sq ft, which management says performs better.
FY27 capex ~INR100 crores, with INR40-50 crores for retail; management said spend is not a concern given positive surplus cash flow.
Real estate: INR24.6 crores of land development cost passed through P&L with an equal reversal from inventory (net nil); 24-month construction timeline.
Franchise model considered an option later but not pursued; company is using internal capital for stores.
demand_pricing: Demand stable in Q1 but wedding and occasion-led purchases moderated during Adhik Maas; consumers value-conscious and input-cost inflation persisted.
Diwali pushed back about 3 weeks this year, which management expects to delay demand; management said sentiment for the season is positive.
Some price pass-on taken in Q1, and further pass-on planned gradually if raw material costs stay high; management said raw material inflation is volatile and cannot be fully passed through.
ZECODE targets Gen Z in Karnataka/Bangalore first; fast fashion described as a large, faster-growing market with many competitors.
Asset-light, rotating inventory model lets the company shift quickly between categories; working capital build is seasonal ahead of festive and wedding seasons.

qa_highlights.question: How are ZECODE store profitability and breakeven tracking amid competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stores are ~18 months old and profitability is targeted in 1.5-2 years; some stores are EBITDA positive, including some under a year old, but it is too early to conclude.

qa_highlights.question: How much EBITDA loss does retail carry and is the 150 bps drop inclusive of rent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ~150 bps annual EBITDA drop is a ballpark that includes all store operating costs and rent; it is not measured quarterly and the company will not disclose separate ZECODE/DEVO numbers yet.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the Q1 margin improvement, excluding the INR24-25 crore land development cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the land cost was moved from inventory to expenses, so the net effect is nil and EBITDA margins are unchanged; the quarter should not be modelled alone given seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the retail revenue outlook and what would trigger faster store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail revenue was ~INR30 crores in Q1 with FY27 at ~INR160 crores; management will accelerate expansion only after store maturity and scale in infrastructure and technology.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation expected to affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some pass-on was taken in Q1 with more possible if margins compress, and it reiterated the ~14% EBITDA margin guidance including the retail drag.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said other income is mostly recurring (delayed payment interest, rent); management said about 30% is a mark-to-market gain that varies quarter to quarter.

risks_watch: Retail EBITDA drag (~150 bps) depends on store maturity; ZECODE profitability not yet proven and DEVO performance untested beyond the festive season.
Working capital: inventory and receivables built in March; management says March-to-March comparison is the right gauge and extra inventory will rise with store count.
Raw material and chemical cost volatility, with pass-through to customers only partial.
Diwali delayed about 3 weeks, which could shift festive revenue between Q2 and Q3.
Other income includes mark-to-market gains that could reverse in later quarters.
Preference share bonus issue: record date 22 August 2026; tax treatment for investors not settled and listing/sale treatment still to be confirmed.
503811|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the core business and annual guidance, but evasive on retail economics: management declined to quantify store losses or disclose ZECODE/DEVO figures, calling the sample too small. Cautious on quarterly reads, repeatedly pointing to annual and March-to-March comparisons.

544609|2026-06.headline: PhysicsWallah Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,054 crore; pre-Ind AS EBITDA improved to negative INR44 crore, with NEET calendar shift a drag.
544609|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,054 crore, up over 24% YoY, with online up 33% and offline and other up 14-16% (figures differ across the call). Pre-Ind AS EBITDA was negative INR44 crore (margin -4%), a 624 bps improvement from negative INR88 crore last year, while reported EBITDA was positive INR52 crore. Management attributed the enrollment softness to the NEET UG cycle shifting 5-7 weeks, which it said would have added 22-25% to offline growth. Management reiterated full-year FY27 guidance of 30% revenue growth and 100% EBITDA growth, and introduced first-time online/offline segment reporting.

vs negative INR21 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.commentary: Revenue up 14% YoY with bottom line improved about 400 bps; Vidyapeeth is about 70% of offline and ARPU rose 7% in Q1. Management guides offline to near-profitability in FY27 and a steady-state margin of 13-15% for mature centers; Pathshala count fell from 84 to 70 as centers were converted to Vidyapeeth.

segments.commentary: State board enrollments and revenue roughly doubled, state boards operated rose from 7 to 14, and vernacular enrollments and revenue rose about 1.7x (70% enrollment growth per Q&A). Curious Junior enrollments rose 67% and collections 150%, but the category is still expected to reach break-even only this year.

segments.name: NEET PG and competitive exams
segments.commentary: NEET PG enrollments grew about 50% and collections about 100%; CA, CS and ACCA enrollments grew about 30%. NEET PG is described as a big bet but still loss-making.

Online margins expected to improve within FY27 as NEET PG, vernacular and Curious Junior move toward break-even.
Center-level and offline profitability data to be disclosed only at end of FY27.
Divestment of Finzy Fintech expected within about a quarter; two non-binding term sheets signed.
New offline center decisions expected over the next two quarters; expansion to be opportunistic and limited to cohort-economics-fit geographies.
capex_capacity: Offline expansion slowed deliberately to focus on results and unit economics; no aggressive center addition planned.

Capital allocation prioritises new online content and categories, organic and inorganic; personalised AI tutor in beta, to roll out next quarter.
School-integrated programme partner schools grew from 15 to more than 50 last year; asset-light model with admission guarantees from schools.
demand_pricing: NEET UG results on July 16 led to collections about 50% above last year post-results, per management.
Government exam notifications were weak, which reduced enrollments at subsidiary Utkarsh by about 800k in aggregate delta per the call.

Foundation has lower ARPU and teacher cost than NEET; management expects steady-state Foundation margin to exceed flagship categories over a longer horizon.

qa_highlights.question: Adjusted for NEET timing, what would online and offline growth have been, and is the 30% FY27 revenue guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said offline would have grown 22-25% (or 20-25% per one estimate) with on-time NEET; online lost about 1-1.5 lakh enrollments, offset by new categories. FY27 revenue (30%) and EBITDA (100%) guidance were reiterated.

qa_highlights.question: Why is enrollment growth weak even after NEET adjustment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NEET enrollments shifted from Q1 to Q2, and government exam notifications were weak (Utkarsh had about 800k delta). PW itself showed 8-9% enrollment growth in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did offline enrollments not rise with about 63 added centers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to NEET re-examination delaying student decisions by about 1.5 months (exam and results).

qa_highlights.question: How does online margin look and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 online margin was about 27%. Management expects improvement as UPSC, GATE, Foundation and state boards mature and NEET PG, vernacular and Curious Junior reach break-even.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR600 crore quarter-on-quarter rise in cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the negative working capital model (students pay full-year fees upfront) drives a cash build each year from Q4 to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How many offline Vidyapeeth centers are profitable now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a Q1 figure and will disclose center-level profitability at end of FY27.

544479|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.5% QoQ to INR161 crore, but gross margin fell 240 bps to 39.5% and EBITDA margin to 14.3% on polymer cost spikes.

Management says the pass-through is largely complete in domestic and is contracted for most exports, with the largest customer's benefit landing in Q2 FY27. Supply-chain disruption (inbound material, containers, logistics) was the main drag, with about INR5.5 crore of sales slipping into July.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 employee expense a fair run-rate?

qa_highlights.question: Why is volume growth only about 5% QoQ on sales volume, and when does price pass-through show up?

qa_highlights.question: Is the remaining 4,000 MT capacity delayed and what is the domestic growth driver?

544839|2026-06.headline: Lohia Corp Q1 FY27 revenue rose 60% YoY to INR503 crore, EBITDA margin 19.9% and order book about INR1,778 crore.
544839|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR503 crore versus INR315 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR100 crore (19.9% margin vs 11.5%) and PAT of INR66 crore (13% margin). Management attributed margin expansion to higher volumes, operating leverage and efficiencies, and said it targets about 20% EBITDA margin internally without formal guidance. Domestic demand now drives the order book, while management expects exports to recover to around 50% of revenue. This was the company's first earnings call after listing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book rise so steeply from FY24 to about INR1,800 crore, and is this a peak?

qa_highlights.question: Will exports recover to 40-50% of the order book?

Greenfield plants held their prior-quarter run-rate of about INR450 crore and remained at break-even, with no meaningful profit contribution yet. Copper pass-through is still on a 3 to 6 month lag, with the quarter-on-quarter lag delta reduced to about 7% from 17% previously. EVs were 8.5% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the new MFD additions and what is the direct versus indirect AUM split?

qa_highlights.question: How should AUM growth be viewed beyond MTM, and how fast is net sales growth?
