500877|2026-06.headline: Apollo Tyres Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 74bn (+12.8% YoY), EBITDA margin 11.7% (down ~150bp) on ~17% raw material inflation.
500877|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12.8% YoY to INR 74bn but was flat-ish sequentially, with consolidated EBITDA margin down about 150bp YoY to 11.7% on raw material cost pressure. India delivered its highest-ever revenue of INR 54.6bn (+15.6% YoY, +4.3% QoQ), largely volume-led, with India EBITDA margin at 12% versus 13.6%. Europe revenue was EUR147m (+0.5% YoY) with EBITDA of EUR13m (8.9% margin), hit by Enschede closure transition and agri revenue loss. Management said price increases lag raw material inflation and that most of the catch-up flows into Q2 and H2.

financial_highlights.change: India capex INR 500 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material cost increase in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Rubber INR 225/kg, synthetic INR 250, carbon black INR 125, steel cord INR 165 (as quoted)

segments.name: India operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 54.6bn (+15.6% YoY), double-digit growth across all segments; volume growth Replacement 13%, OEM 10%, Exports 15%. TBB was the only category without double-digit growth. Price increases ~3-4% realised in Q1 versus 7-9% taken.

segments.name: Europe operations
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR147m (+0.5% YoY) and EBITDA EUR13m (8.9%). PCR replacement grew double digits; agri revenue fell high-teens QoQ and small single digits YoY. Without Enschede overlap costs, margin would have been ~11%.

segments.name: Reifen
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR43m in Q1 with ~3% EBITDA margin, as disclosed on the call.

guidance_outlook: Raw material inflation of ~8% sequentially expected in Q2 for India; Europe RM basket up 8% in Q1 with hit mainly in Q2.

India needs ~15-16% total price increase to cover commodity inflation; ~11%+ currently in place (9% TBR, 11% other categories); at least 1-2 more hikes needed; July hike 1-2%, similar hike expected in August.
Europe needs ~10% price increase across Q1-Q2; only 3-4% implemented so far.
Europe full-year EBITDA target: high teens margin once manufacturing footprint transition completes.
Net debt/EBITDA expected to rise slightly this year as company becomes a net borrower; capex to rise in Q2 and Q3.
Rubber expected to cool from Q3 as seasonal impact fades; crude-linked cost relief expected with a quarter lag.
capex_capacity: Enschede (Netherlands) plant stopped production in June 2026; ~750,000 tyres/year shifting largely to Hungary, completion Sept-Oct 2026; financial benefits from H2 FY27.
Hungary PCR capacity rising from ~17,000 to ~21,000 car tyres per day, starting H2 FY27; Hungary expanding by 4,000 PCR tyres/day, AP (India) plant expanding double that.
Lower-end 14-15 inch tyres moving from Hungary to India; Spacemaster spare tyre production now in Baroda; India new capacity to start towards end of FY27 and ramp through FY28.
High-end agri (OHT) capacity limited at Kalamassery (Kochi); no economic small-scale alternative; offtake partner identified near Asia-Europe cusp, midterm plan is offtake.
India capex was ~INR 1,200-1,300 crore annually in recent past; FY27 group capex guided above INR 3,000 crore.
Management says India running in the 90s on capacity utilisation and will stay tight through FY27.
demand_pricing: India replacement momentum strong; July started strongly and Q2 YoY growth expected to be good though QoQ muted due to rains and seasonality.
Europe: anti-dumping duty on Chinese tyres expected to help Apollo brand at lower end; Vredestein PCR does not compete with Chinese.
Exports growth driven by Europe; West Asia impacted by war and US underperformed due to dealer inventory issues.
Competition has broadly followed price increases of similar magnitude, per management.
Management market share estimates (internal): TBR replacement upwards of 30% (regained lost share); PCR replacement 21%+.
UHP mix in Europe stayed at around 40%, per management recollection.
Advertising and sales promotion spend cut by roughly 50% QoQ; management said no further reduction expected.

qa_highlights.question: India volume growth by channel and outlook; Europe anti-dumping and capacity shift timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement +13%, OEM +10%, exports +15% volume growth; Q2 seasonal. Enschede-to-Hungary shift to complete Sept-Oct 2026; Spacemaster already in Baroda.

qa_highlights.question: How much India and Europe price hikes have been taken vs needed?
qa_highlights.answer: India: 7-9% implemented in Q1 (only 3-4% flowed into revenue), 11%+ now against 15-16% needed. Europe: 3-4% implemented against ~10% needed.

qa_highlights.question: Europe margin without overlap costs and steady-state target?
qa_highlights.answer: ~11% margin without overlap; full-year Europe target high-teens EBITDA margin after footprint change.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and net debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 consolidated capex INR 650 crore; India INR 500 crore; capex to step up in Q2-Q3; company to become net borrower with slight rise in net debt/EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses and staff cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P cut ~50% QoQ but no further reduction expected; minor increments effective June 1 with full impact from Q2, no further increment planned.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material outlook: rupee, rubber, crude?
qa_highlights.answer: ~7-8% of RM inflation from rupee depreciation (from INR 88); ~50% of RM imported; domestic rubber ~50-50 mix; rubber expected to cool from Q3; crude relief with a quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive pricing behaviour and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition has followed price increases of similar magnitude; TBR share back above 30%, PCR replacement 21%+ (internal estimates).

507789|2026-06.headline: Jagsonpal Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 9% YoY to Rs.82 crores, with operating EBITDA up 21% to nearly Rs.19 crores and PAT up 22% to Rs.13 crores.
507789|2026-06.overview: Management said the growth seen from Q4 FY26 carried into Q1 FY27, with revenue up about 9% YoY and gross margin above 65%. Operating EBITDA margin expanded about 240 bps to above 23% and PAT margin rose 176 bps to 16%. The company completed the Rs.40 crore buyback and acquired 85% of Aequitas Healthcare for Rs.20.8 crores (enterprise value about Rs.25 crores) to enter the hospital segment. Management guided Aequitas to Rs.10 crores EBITDA by year two post-integration, though analysts questioned the step-up from about Rs.50 lakh EBITDA in FY26.

financial_highlights.change: after Rs.40 crore buyback (about half added back to cash)

segments.name: Branded prescription (core)
segments.commentary: Power brand portfolio grew 19% vs market 16%; five brands are #1 in their molecules and 14 are in the top five. Maintane (Pharmarack ~Rs.46 crores: injections Rs.34 crores, tablets Rs.13 crores) is one of the top three brands. Management is shifting mix from acute to semi-chronic and specialty therapies; new brand run-rates have almost doubled.

segments.name: Aequitas Healthcare (hospital pharma, 85% owned)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs.53 crores and EBITDA about Rs.50 lakh per analyst. Portfolio is ICU and perioperative injectables, including latest-generation antibiotics, all branded, sold to corporate hospital chains (no government tenders). Management targets about Rs.100 crores revenue in FY28-FY29 and Rs.10 crores+ EBITDA by year two; gross margins are structurally thinner than JPL's branded business.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow at 1.5x industry growth rate in coming quarters (management reiterated on Pharmarack vs secondary-sales variance question).
Aequitas: about Rs.100 crores business within two and a half years (FY28-FY29) and Rs.10 crores+ EBITDA by year two post-integration; synergies expected over 36 months.
Productivity target of upward of Rs.2,50,000 per-person productivity (PCPM varies by vertical).
Dividend of 200% recommended, including 75% special dividend, subject to AGM approval.
Aequitas expected to contribute meaningfully from second year onwards; numbers expected to show in about the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Aequitas acquired as a subsidiary (not a BTA route); working capital cycle is longer than JPL and will not be aligned with JPL.
Aequitas network: about 49 institutional medical representatives, access to over 1,000 hospitals, around 50 hospitals contribute the majority of top line.
Lean and green productivity programme rolled out company-wide in Q1.
demand_pricing: Secondary (Pharmarack) growth of 18.9% vs reported primary sales growth of about 9%; management attributed the gap to stockist data and geographic statistical correction, and said it is reviewing the variance.
Hospital channel pricing is price-led; management said margins are structurally thinner than in branded prescription business.
Top 10 Aequitas products are over 50% of its sales.
Management reported one first-wave product launch in Q1 and expects one more in the current quarter.
Brand focus for growth: Indocap, Maintane, Endoreg (gynae), Pru and Eukroma (derma).

qa_highlights.question: Why is reported sales growth (about 9%) far below the 18% IPM growth cited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the data is secondary (stockist) sales and the variance is partly statistical correction for geographies; it is reviewing why the gap is so wide and reiterated the 1.5x industry growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aequitas Rs.10 crore EBITDA target achievable from Rs.50 lakh in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited brand equity, lean team, corporate-chain focus, cross-selling of JPL brands and new-age brands with high value per patient; promoters remain with 15% and continue to run the business, so their salaries are not a one-off saving.

qa_highlights.question: Size of Maintane and its impact on portfolio growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Pharmarack value about Rs.46 crores (Rs.34 crores injections, Rs.13 crores tablets); growing ahead of molecule market; one of top three brands, but management did not disclose internal values.

qa_highlights.question: Aequitas gross margin looks low for a branded business; why?
qa_highlights.answer: In hospitals, price comes before brand, so margins are thinner; management plans mix improvement and differentiated innovative launches, but said it is too early to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp working capital improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to inventory control and stricter collections, and said payments now go out on due date; the big step-down was in FY22-FY24 (cash conversion cycle from 59 to 22 days).

qa_highlights.question: Any first-in-India or breakthrough molecule pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it never mentioned such a pipeline; it is targeting first-wave launches (about 5-10 companies) in gynae, ortho and derma, and launched one such product in Q1.

risks_watch: Aequitas execution: hospital working capital is longer and margins thinner; Rs.10 crore EBITDA in year two is an aggressive target from Rs.50 lakh base.
Concentration risk: Maintane and Indocap drive much of recent growth; management acknowledges the portfolio effect depends on a few brands.
Gap between secondary (Pharmarack ~18.9%) and reported primary growth (~9%) needs explanation next quarter.
Attrition and sales-force productivity: management claims improvement but gave no hard numbers.
Board change: Pallavi Dinodia Gupta stepped down; Anil Kumar Matai joined as Independent Director.
507789|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the Aequitas thesis, but evasive on specifics: declined to give Maintane MAT value, exact PCPM, and the reason for the primary-versus-secondary sales gap, and said it is still too early to judge Aequitas margins.
key_quotes: This 9% growth in sales has translated into a 21% growth in operating EBITDA as well as a 22% growth in net profits for the company.
Aequitas alone, we are looking at around Rs.100 crores of business within two and a half years' time, starting from now.
Growth without margins, improvement is hollow.

540401|2026-06.headline: Maximus Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 52% YoY to INR59.91 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.64% from 9.81% on Middle East war input costs.
540401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR59.91 crores versus INR39.52 crores a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 18% to INR4.58 crores. Margin compression, attributed to higher input and freight costs from the ongoing Middle East war, and higher finance costs (INR1.53 crores vs INR0.92 crores) left PAT at INR2.05 crores versus INR2.33 crores a year ago. Management highlighted the proposed associate acquisition of Quebec Petroleum (40% stake), a Kenya grease plant planned for Q3 FY27, and a Tanzania warehousing expansion. Management guided to crossing about INR200 crores revenue in FY27 on a conservative basis.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA margin among the three verticals (manufacturing, toll blending, trading) in Q1 FY27 and historically. Operations in UAE and Kenya.

segments.name: Toll blending
segments.commentary: Management says it is being pursued aggressively; in talks with an East African MNC for toll blending.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Lowest-margin vertical per management. Long-term target split: manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%.

segments.name: Specialty lubricants
segments.commentary: Contribute around 40% of topline, per CFO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to cross about INR200 crores on a conservative basis, with healthy EBITDA margins (stated even under the ongoing war scenario).
Margins expected to hold at current levels or improve over the next couple of quarters if supply disruption persists, through product mix diversification.
Kenya grease manufacturing facility planned for commissioning in Q3 FY27.
Tanzania expansion: initially warehousing and distribution, moving to manufacturing once scale is reached.
Recently launched modernisation programme: automated batch blending, additional storage and warehousing, improved filling lines, and capacity expansion at UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity considered sufficient for next 2-3 years on single-shift basis; additional storage capex needed for full utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined manufacturing capacity of about 50,000 KL across UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity utilisation at about 45% across both units.
Kenya grease plant to cater to East African market, which has few grease manufacturers; also to support toll blending.
Proposed acquisition of an additional manufacturing unit as an associate; process underway, details to be shared later.
Quebec Petroleum: associate investment with initial 40% stake, aimed at entering the Indian domestic market.
demand_pricing: Management says demand for lubricants is supported by industrialisation, infrastructure, vehicle ownership and mining, power and construction; customers are shifting toward premium and specialty products.
Cited Middle East and Africa lubricant market growing from about USD 9.1 billion (2024) to USD 12.4 billion (2034).
Company serves more than 400 customers across 25+ countries and 50+ industries.
Top 10 customers account for roughly 70-75% of revenue, including distributors; company sells mainly through distributors, not B2C.
Product prices and landed costs (freight, insurance) rose due to the Middle East war; company passed on a partial cost increase, which also raised receivables.
Base oil and white oil prices are positively correlated with crude, with a lagged and non-identical impact on lubricant prices.
In Kenya, incumbents Shell and Total have not changed payment terms despite new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: How sensitive are margins to base oil and crude price movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Not directly coupled but positively correlated; raw materials (base oils and white oils) move in the same direction with a lag and not in the same proportion.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the 50,000 KL capacity, and targets over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45% utilised; capacity is sufficient for 2-3 years on a single shift, but full utilisation would need additional storage capex.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical has the highest EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing, both in Q1 FY27 and historically; toll blending is being pursued more aggressively.

qa_highlights.question: Share of premium and specialty versus conventional revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lubricants contribute around 40% of topline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have receivables risen faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher topline (about 50% growth), higher product prices and landed costs from the war, and partial pass-through of cost increases to selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: What if supply disruption lasts more than six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has onboarded new customers and broadened product baskets; margins may dip further but aim to hold or improve through diversification; still expects over INR200 crores revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will Quebec Petroleum contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Associate with 40% stake; its profits will be included in consolidated financials; focus is India domestic market, while Maximus covers Middle East, East and North Africa.

qa_highlights.question: Target revenue split between trading and toll blending over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%; split between manufacturing and toll blending not disclosed as they overlap in co-branding.

qa_highlights.question: Concentration of revenue and B2B versus B2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue (distributors included); no own retail outlets; major revenue comes via distribution channels.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin down about 217 bps YoY to 7.64% due to input and freight costs from the Middle East war.
Working capital: receivables rising faster than revenue; financial cost up about 65% YoY to INR1.53 crores.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue.
Quebec Petroleum associate acquisition and additional manufacturing unit acquisition: terms and financials not yet disclosed.
Competitive response in Kenya from incumbents such as Shell and Total; payment terms unchanged so far.
Management did not split revenue between manufacturing and toll blending; the reported Q1 PAT decline despite revenue growth needs monitoring.

544785|2026-06.headline: Hexagon Nutrition Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 43.2% YoY to INR104.3 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.3% from 13.8%.
544785|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 43.2% YoY to INR104.3 crore, with volume growth of roughly 25-40% across premix and branded segments. EBITDA rose 17.3% to INR11.8 crore, but margin compressed about 250 bps to 11.3% on higher raw material costs (West Asia crisis) and elevated selling, distribution and freight spend. PAT grew 25.1% to INR8.1 crore. Management guided FY27 growth of 20-25%, flagged a INR100 crore order book for Q2-Q3, and said MRP increases of 10-15% on some branded products will help margins from Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Contracted by more than 3 percentage points YoY
financial_highlights.change: Attributed to raw material cost rise

segments.name: Premix (micronutrient)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 62% of Q1 revenue; grew about 55% YoY per CFO. Over 50% of plant capacity utilisation is attributed to premix, and the INR100 crore order book is about 70-75% premix and ESG combined.

segments.name: Branded (clinical/wellness, B2C)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 28% of revenue; grew about 22% YoY (CFO) or about 28% (Dr. Nikhil). Branded share rose from 18% to 20%, 25% and about 30% over recent years. Target of 35% of revenue in the next couple of years; B2C revenue has crossed INR100 crore per an analyst question.

segments.name: Therapeutic nutrition / ESG (RUTF, RUSF, MNP)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 10% of revenue; grew about 42% YoY. Tender-based, so order flows vary quarter to quarter. ESG pipeline cited at INR75-100 crore for the remaining year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 20-25%, same trajectory as last year; management called this the conservative side.
Q2 supported by an order book of about INR100 crore, to be executed in Q2 and partly in Q3.
Seasonality: Q1 and Q2 build momentum, with the main growth in Q3 and Q4 per management.
MRP increases of 10-15% on some branded products will affect margins from Q2; gross margin expected to ease over the next two quarters.
Field force investment (over 50% increase YoY) expected to show productivity in roughly two to three quarters, with operating leverage by end of Q3.
Nashik premix facility redevelopment capex of INR25-30 crore over one to one-and-a-half years; about 70% to be funded by long-term bank borrowing.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 47% (rising from around 30% previously stated); management cautioned segment rates vary, with some lines at 35-40% and others around 65%.
Nashik about 55-60% utilised, Tuticorin about 35-40%, Chennai about 25-30%; Uzbekistan has limited order book for Q2-Q3 and is not material yet.
Nashik premix facility being demolished and rebuilt; capex INR25-30 crore over the next 1-1.5 years.
Management says manufacturing capacity suffices for the next two to three years of growth.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of roughly 25-40% YoY in Q1 across premix and branded; management said price hikes were not the main driver.
Raw material cost pressure: about 25-30% of raw materials are imported; whey protein costs rose sharply, while some vitamins were stable.
Freight costs rose due to the West Asia situation; West Asia is under 20% of exports.
Export concentration: top 3-5 countries make up about 25-40% of exports; growth in Central Asia and Africa, with Europe and North America targeted.
Branded MRP raised 10-15% on some products to pass on raw material costs.
Inventory build partly strategic due to rising product prices and ESG/premix order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a slowdown expected given 43% Q1 growth versus 20-25% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nikhil said Q2 is supported by a INR100 crore order book, with no sign of slowdown; Q1 and Q2 build momentum and Q3-Q4 carry the main growth. CFO called 20-25% the conservative side.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract, and will it normalise from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed a more than 3 percentage point gross margin contraction to West Asia-driven raw material cost increases in premix and branded. Management is passing costs to customers via MRP increases and hopes margins normalise from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly freight costs from the geopolitical situation, plus field force and marketing investment; over 50% more field force versus last year, treated as an investment that will pay off in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and its timing?
qa_highlights.answer: INR100 crore order book, to execute in Q2 and partly Q3; about 70-75% premix and ESG, rest branded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and what is the bottleneck?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended utilisation about 47% (40-47% range cited); premix in 25 kg bags versus branded sachets and tins take different times, so segment-level rates vary widely.

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest constraints to growth over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nikhil said manufacturing capacity and working capital are not constraints; distribution expansion into Tier 2-3 cities is the focus, with operating leverage expected in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression (11.3% vs 13.8%) persists if raw material and freight costs stay high or MRP hikes lag.
Inventory days rose to about 142 from about 130+; strategic stocking may tie up working capital.
Tender-based ESG orders create quarter-to-quarter volatility.
Field force and distribution costs ahead of productivity; leverage expected only by end of Q3.
Branded share target of 35% of revenue in a couple of years; growth needs to keep pace with 20-25% guidance.
West Asia geopolitical risk on freight, raw material costs and exports.
544785|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and order book, but defensive on margin compression, attributing it to temporary raw material and freight costs and promising recovery from Q2 with hedges such as "hopefully". Answers on capacity utilisation were detailed but caveated, and the call had some audio disruptions.

524404|2026-06.headline: Marksans Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.6% YoY to INR841 crore, with record EBITDA of INR213 crore (25.3% margin) and PAT of INR159 crore.
524404|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR840.8 crore grew 35.6% YoY, led by UK and Europe at INR356 crore (+74.7%), which includes INR44 crore from the QliniQ acquisition. Gross margin expanded to 59.1% on product mix, low-cost inventory and favourable FX, and EBITDA margin reached 25.3%. Management said the gross margin is sustainable at around 55-56% as freight and raw material costs from the war normalise, and it reiterated FY27 guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and 20-21% EBITDA margin. Cash rose to INR1,058 crore, with net cash of INR1,031 crore after the QliniQ payment.

Rx price erosion in the US stayed in single digits.

qa_highlights.question: How is QliniQ revenue recognised, and what is the FY27 outlook for Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Effective date was 1 April 2026, so Q1 is consolidated. QliniQ is guided at INR150-175 crore for FY27, and total Europe about INR180 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin sustainable at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 55-56% as the inventory benefit unwinds, and says more upside is unrealistic given freight and crude costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan with over INR1,000 crore of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is earmarked for inorganic growth, mainly in Europe, with nothing concrete yet. Management ruled out riskier instruments such as index investing.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise guidance upward?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Guidance of 15-20% revenue growth and 20-21% EBITDA margin stands, given geopolitical uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US strategy in light of tariff comments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not weight the tariff remarks heavily. US remains an important market, and local manufacturing is an option to keep open.

532891|2026-06.headline: Puravankara Q1 FY27 presales rose 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores and PAT turned positive at INR25 crores; FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crores reiterated.

509675|2026-06.headline: BirlaNu Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.6% to Rs 1,174 crores and EBITDA 35% to Rs 80 crores, with Parador still loss-making at Rs 13 crores.

Pipes revenue fell 11% and volumes fell 27% on a sharp PVC resin price swing, yet EBITDA margin expanded 660 bps on mix and pricing. Parador swung to a Rs 13 crore EBITDA loss, which management attributed mostly to timing items expected to normalise in H2. Gross borrowings fell about Rs 100 crores to Rs 758 crores and working capital was cut by about Rs 100 crores year-on-year.

financial_highlights.change: nearly +70% YoY; margin up over 420 bps
vs profit of Rs 5 crores last year
down from Rs 852 crores at March 2026

segments.name: Roofs

segments.commentary: Revenue up 14% with margin 10.2%, up 270 bps; management says the current portfolio can reach 12-14%.

segments.name: Pipes

segments.name: Construction Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 11% despite raw material prices rising over 50%; tile and project slowdowns hit demand temporarily.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give numeric FY27 targets but said it hopes to keep beating internal targets, which it has done for the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Telangana plant's economics and the Nellore capex status?

536974|2026-06.headline: Captain Polyplast Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.3% YoY to Rs 81.66 crore, with EBITDA margin up 99 bps to 12.07%.
536974|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of Rs 81.66 crore (+16.3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 9.86 crore (+26.7%) and net profit of Rs 4.66 crore with diluted EPS of Rs 0.78. Management said the quarter was hit by geopolitical-driven raw material inflation but revenue growth and margin both improved. Solar EPC order wins of 1,500 pumps in the first four months were highlighted, with 800 already executed and 700 pending. Ahmedabad plant (70,000 sq ft) commenced production, and the company was listed on NSE in July 2026.

segments.name: Micro-irrigation

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Two verticals: solar water pumping (PM-KUSUM, currently only Maharashtra; empanelled in Maharashtra and Gujarat) and rooftop. Management did not quantify segment revenue or growth; said solar revenue was H2-weighted last year. Targets solar EPC contribution of 50% over next 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Blended EBITDA margin expected to improve about 10-15 bps every quarter as Ahmedabad ramps up; volume growth cited as main margin driver.
Micro-irrigation margin uplift of 1-1.5% expected once Ahmedabad is fully operational, over the next 2-3 years.
Raw material (LLDP/HDPE) prices up about 30-35% versus Jan/Feb levels after a ~50% spike at end-March; price revisions expected to be largely complete by end of Q2, with full benefit from Q3.
Central government price revision mechanism expected by end-September.
Expects working capital to improve by year end as micro-irrigation receivables are collected in H2.

Solar EPC is service-only; no in-house manufacturing, so growth constrained by execution rather than capacity.
Dedicated solar execution team already set up; limited incremental manpower needed in states with existing micro-irrigation teams.
demand_pricing: Solar pump orders: 500 pumps from MSEDCL in Q1 and 1,000 more in July 2026; 800 of 1,500 executed, 700 pending, expected to be completed by end of August 2026.
Solar rooftop: 60-70% of rooftop business sourced from existing micro-irrigation dealers; solar pumps largely via dedicated solar dealers.
Replacement demand in mature states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu) currently about 10-20% of micro-irrigation demand.
Export growth said to be in line with domestic growth from a very low base; future growth to come from new customers. Africa and Latin America named as focus markets.
Other states' solar tenders expected to be floated around September; awaiting tender release.

qa_highlights.question: Dealer network and scope for expansion in under-penetrated markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 750 dealers across 16 states; no need for more dealers in existing states. Expansion focus in Northern/Eastern states (Jharkhand, West Bengal, Bihar, UP).

qa_highlights.question: Current status of 1,500 solar pump order execution?
qa_highlights.answer: 800 completed, 700 pending, expected to be completed by end of the current month.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of polymer prices and price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material prices rose about 50% at end-March and are now up 30-35% vs Jan/Feb. Free-pricing markets have passed on increases; Gujarat revised subsidy prices; other southern states expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Solar pump growth outlook and share in business?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects solar EPC to reach 50% of overall business in 3 years; expansion planned to Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Haryana this year.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital cycle for micro-irrigation vs solar pumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation payment cycle 5-6 months (8-10 months in Andhra Pradesh); solar pump receivable cycle 3-4 months. Majority of working capital sits in receivables, not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmedabad facility margin benefit and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation margin benefit of 1-1.5% when fully operational; blended margin uplift of 10-15 bps each quarter during ramp-up. Initial focus on cost efficiency, standalone sales later.

qa_highlights.question: Export growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Export growth similar to domestic, but from a very low base; meaningful growth requires new customers.

risks_watch: Raw material (polymer) cost inflation and pace of state price revisions, especially Tamil Nadu, Andhra and other southern states.
Working capital intensity rising in Q1-Q2; receivable cycles of 5-10 months for micro-irrigation.
Dependence on state tenders for solar pump expansion beyond Maharashtra and Gujarat; tenders expected around September.
Competitive pricing pressure in solar pumps, per management.
Execution bottleneck in solar pump installation as order book scales; export still a small base.

key_quotes: So for the solar rooftop business, I can say that majority of our rooftop business is coming from the existing dealer network.

544867|2026-06.headline: Dhoot Transmission Q1 FY27: revenue up nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue Rs 1,090 crore (+44.6%), EBITDA margin ~15%; FY27 growth guided at 25-30%.
544867|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong first quarter as its first post-listing call, with growth of nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue up 44.6% and non-wiring harness up 67.7%. EV revenue grew 79% and rose to 27% of total revenue from 24% a year earlier. EBITDA margin improved 110 bps QoQ to about 15%, while raw-material (copper, brass) inflation continued and is being passed through to customers with a roughly three-month lag. Management guided to 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin and 25-30% growth for FY27, while flagging a soft comparison in the first half from last year's GST-driven demand.

financial_highlights.change: Ahead of domestic 2W volumes (>20%) and exports (>36%)

Expected to turn to net cash after August IPO proceeds; management indicated ~Rs 1,000 crore net cash around end-August

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,090 crore in Q1 FY27, up 44.6% YoY from Rs 753 crore. Management says localisation has cut imported components from 30-35% to 20-25% of the component base.

segments.name: Non-wiring harness (EV components, battery packs, controllers, sensors, switches)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 358 crore, up 67.7% YoY, with Multilink adding about 10-12 points of that growth. Battery packs are the major portion; a second top customer in the South started supply in the last month of the quarter.

segments.commentary: Contributed ~3% to overall revenue growth for the ~20-day period in Q1. Management expects 25-30% growth and margins in line with the group; full integration in about 3-4 months, adding Hero as a customer plus fuel level sensors and relays.

segments.name: EV vs ICE
segments.commentary: EV revenue +79% YoY, ICE revenue +52.6% YoY. EV content per vehicle is 1.5x-2.5x that of ICE for wiring harness alone, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30% YoY, with soft comparison in H1 noted.

Copper and other key raw materials rose further in July and August (~3-4% per management), so gross margin recovery is not expected in Q2; benefit expected in Q3 if prices stay stable.
EV revenue share expected to exceed 30-32% in the next two to three years.
Multilink expected to grow 25-30% at group-level margins after integration in roughly 3-4 months.

capex_capacity: Expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur plants funded from IPO proceeds, adding ~15-20% to wiring harness capacity this year.

Ride Vision ADAS product: management says it is aimed at two-wheelers first, with regulatory-driven demand expected.
demand_pricing: Management says the EV industry grew ~93% YoY and ICE more than 20% in the quarter, with 2W industry growth of 22.8%.

Management said the Q1 margin was impacted by a hard commodity cycle, not by mix shift toward battery packs.
Wage-hike cost is recovered from customers through annual discussions, per management.
Management says it has not lost ICE market share, despite an analyst comparison suggesting it had.

qa_highlights.question: How much more margin expansion is possible, and when does copper pass-through normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Kalani said most copper inflation is passed through, but prices kept rising for 4-5 months, so there is some impact. Guidance is kept at 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin; Q2 recovery is unlikely and Q3 is the earliest, if prices are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Cash position and FCF at end-June?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was about Rs 220 crore at end-June, after the March Bain infusion and part Multilink impact. Post-IPO money (received in August) should turn the company to net cash, with ~Rs 1,000 crore indicated by end-August.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of non-wiring harness revenue and EBITDA margin expectations for Multilink?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakup by product is not disclosed due to single-customer concentration. Non-wiring harness grew 67.7%, with Multilink adding 10-12 points for its ~20-day contribution. Multilink margins are expected to be in line with group margins.

qa_highlights.question: Wiring harness revenue and prior-year split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: wiring harness Rs 1,090 crore and non-wiring harness Rs 358 crore. Q1 FY26: Rs 753 crore and Rs 213 crore, respectively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity given 75-80% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur adds ~15-20% capacity this year. Management said 75% is the sustainable ceiling because of seasonal peak demand during Diwali.

risks_watch: Copper and other raw-material prices continued to rise into July-August, which could delay margin recovery beyond Q3.
Soft base comparison in H1 FY27, since the GST-cut-driven demand boost came in H2 FY26.
Customer concentration: battery pack business rests on a single customer, and disclosure is limited under customer agreements.
Multilink integration (3-4 months) and cross-selling targets; the Ride Vision JV and passenger-vehicle HV harness JV are not yet finalised.
Management said ADAS demand is partly regulation-dependent; timing is uncertain.
Goodwill and PPA on Multilink still provisional; management estimates goodwill at ~20-25% of the acquisition price.
Q1 employee cost rose ~16% QoQ; management did not quantify the split between wage-hike and organic hires.

Management said some customer inspection and approval delays shifted revenue out of the quarter. Order book was INR920 crore at 30 June 2026, rising to INR2,654 crore including orders received in July and orders negotiated (not yet converted).

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said higher R&M from facility revamp and about INR2 crore additional provision against long-standing receivables drove the increase; otherwise in line with budget.

qa_highlights.question: Quantum of revenue slipped due to customer approval delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing customer confidentiality; said inspection delays are recurring and quarterly revenue is uneven as this is a yearly business.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the negotiated orders to convert into order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some contracts should convert within about 2 months; a customer granted a 2-month extension, and protracted negotiations on other orders are concluding.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin was higher YoY; the EBITDA margin fell because fixed overheads (other expenses, depreciation) were spread over lower quarterly revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the Su-30 jammer pod?
qa_highlights.answer: Qualification expected before December, followed by a few months of flight trials; commercial production after that. Contract expected in about 2 years; value not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the BrahMos seeker orders and HimShakti?
qa_highlights.answer: BrahMos seeker commercial order expected in FY27 after qualification. HimShakti: original products delivered; BEL discussing a new programme but no RFP confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition of ST Advanced and its rationale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a small composites company to support radome and composite requirements for sensors; strategy still being developed, deal finalised the previous day.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for the next two years?

Hardware inventory was built ahead of the price rise, so existing government projects are protected from price escalation.
demand_pricing: Government and PSU customers were about 47% of FY26 revenue; in the order book, 45% is government and 55% non-government.
Order book split: about 45% direct and 55% indirect orders.
Around 50% of the order book is recurring (annuity) revenue over 4-5 years; about 40% of the submitted bids are recurring.
Digital trust market: about 11 licensed CAs in India; XtraTrust competes mainly with eMudhra, with 10,000+ channel partners.
Hardware costs have risen about 3-4x over the past year; management reports no cancellations so far, but is monitoring supply.
Product deployment EBITDA margin is about 6-8%, versus about 20-22% for services end-to-end, per the CFO.
Management now applies year-on-year price escalation clauses in new bids, linked to USD variation and OEM supply costs.

qa_highlights.question: What growth trajectory is expected for data center revenue over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 35-40% annual growth in the segment, keeping it at about 50% of revenue, driven by DC modernization, new DR setups, NOC and cyber SOC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance and its drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is Rs 500+ crore versus FY26 Rs 365 crore (about 35% growth), supported by the Rs 375 crore order book (55-60% executable in FY27) and new bids.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company compete in digital trust and PKI against peers such as eMudhra?
qa_highlights.answer: XtraTrust has about 850,000 subscribers on recurring models, 10,000+ partners, 30-minute issuance, and an in-house PKI engine; eMudhra is the main competitor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle for data center projects?
qa_highlights.answer: End-to-end cycle of 12-15 months; government billing realises in about 120-150 days, and O&M/services billing in 45-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between services and products, and the margin difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Services were about 60% of FY26 revenue, now 65-68% in Q1; product EBITDA margin is about 6-8% versus 20-22% for services.

qa_highlights.question: How do CAPEX and OPEX models and recognition work?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 50-60% of a project is CAPEX billed over 6-18 months; the rest is billed over 4-7 years as O&M. Revenue is recognised on billing with straight-line annuities and no step-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Is hardware price inflation passed through to clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a direct pass-through; prices are locked with OEMs per project after order, and price escalation clauses are now used in new bids and repeat orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical bid-to-order conversion timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Government and PSU orders take about 60-90 days from proposal to order; large enterprise, aviation and BFSI take 30-60 days.

risks_watch: Hardware cost increase of about 3-4x; management says product availability is becoming a challenge, and future orders may face pricing pressure.
Margin dilution during CAPEX-heavy phases of large projects (12-14 months), since product margins are lower.
Management's guidance (Rs 500+ crore FY27) implies a sharp step-up from Q1 run-rate (~Rs 51 crore, +11% YoY), and the call did not clarify Q2-Q4 phasing.
Dependence on government and PSU clients (about 45-47% of revenue) with 60-150 day billing cycles affects working capital.
Inconsistent figures in the call: order book cited as Rs 373 crore and Rs 375 crore; the 55% vs 65% executable share and the 40-45% vs 50% recurring share also vary.
Monitor Q2 FY27 conversion of the Rs 1,200 crore pipeline and the data center capacity expansion at XtraTrust.

500350|2026-06.headline: RSWM Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.7% QoQ to ₹1,161 crore and EBITDA to ₹94 crore (8.0% margin), led by a 39.8% gross margin.

Gross margin expanded to 39.8% from 37.4%, lifting EBITDA to ₹94 crore (+10.1% QoQ, +16.1% YoY) and margin to 8.0%. PAT was ₹17 crore against ₹7 crore a year ago, but lower than Q4 FY26, which included a one-time tax benefit. Management gave no full-year guidance; fabric profitability weakened sharply while yarn held up, and new projects (PET food-grade chips, denim garmenting JV, knitting expansion) were outlined.

financial_highlights.change: +1.7% QoQ vs ₹1,142 crore in Q4 FY26
vs 7.4% in Q4 FY26 and 6.9% in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Yarn (synthetic, cotton, mélange)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 96% for synthetic, 98% for cotton and 92-93% for mélange. Management said yarn demand held up and cotton/mélange spreads were good in Q1; Q2 is running similarly so far.

segments.name: Denim fabric
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was about 90%. Management said the segment faced the same cost and demand pressure as knit, with exports and domestic roughly balanced.

guidance_outlook: No full-year growth or EBITDA margin guidance given; management said all quarters should be similar to or better than Q1.

Power cost savings of about ₹40 crore for FY27 at constant utilisation (from renewables and efficiency), with a stated target of around ₹100 crore; renewable share of power rose from mid-20s% to mid-40s%, and about 60% in the current quarter.
Management expects per-unit power cost to fall by more than ₹1 year-on-year on average.
Knitting expansion expected to add benefits from Q3 FY27, with capacity going from 650 tons to about 900 tons per month, including 150 tons of printing.

Food-grade PET chip plant: completion in Q4 FY27, trials and commercial production in Q1 FY28; 50,000 tpa capacity, ₹500 crore revenue expected, about 15% EBITDA (industry norm per management). Utilisation ramp of 75%, 85%, then 90-91% over three years.
Graphene-based fibre (with Birla Cellulose): management expects commercial traction within FY27.
risks_watch: Crude and polyester price volatility, and a possible reversal of Q1 stocking gains.
Export demand recovery, especially knit fabric and Middle East markets; the company said recent inquiries are improving.
Fabric margins near nil; monitor whether fabric EBIT recovers in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
PET plant execution: food-grade certification and trials, no customer tie-ups yet, and a 15% EBITDA assumption that is management's industry norm.
Garmenting JV: stake and capex undisclosed, new skills needed, and a labour-intensive business that is new to RSWM.
Finance costs rising with working capital needs (₹31 crore).
Management gave no full-year guidance; the company's disclosure is limited on volumes and capex amounts.
Investor-presentation timing: it was uploaded about 15 minutes before the call, which an analyst objected to.

543657|2026-06.headline: Archean Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 14% YoY to INR3,321m and EBITDA margin expanded to 25.3%, but logistics costs and Hajipir road works kept salt volumes down 12%.

544009|2026-06.headline: Blue Jet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% QoQ to INR293 crore and EBITDA hit INR98 crore, with PI/API restart offset by INR30 crore contrast media goods in transit.
544009|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR293 crore, up 25% QoQ, with operating EBITDA margin of 33.5% versus 30.4% in Q4 FY26. Growth came mainly from PI and API, where supply of an intermediate restarted after customer destocking. Contrast media revenue fell sharply (about 40% QoQ per analyst) because roughly INR30 crore of goods were in transit at quarter end, which management says will be recognised next quarter. Raw material inflation from March 2026 weighed on gross margin, which fell about 3 points to 53%. Mahad (Unit 3) is now expected to commission later this calendar year, slightly ahead of the earlier H2 guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR2-3 crore earlier; mainly export incentive and forex gain per management

financial_highlights.value: ~INR30 crore higher at closing vs opening
financial_highlights.change: to be recognised in Q2 FY27

segments.name: PI / API (Bempedoic-acid related intermediate)
segments.commentary: Main driver of QoQ growth after restarting supply hit by customer destocking. Management cites a strong order book and visibility for at least the next 3-4 quarters.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: Revenue declined QoQ because about INR30 crore of goods were in transit at quarter end; plant at ~70% utilisation. Management describes the segment as stable with long-term arrangements.

segments.name: High-intensity sweetener
segments.commentary: Stable contributor per management; new sweetener is in pilot validation at the existing facility, with scale-up planned at Vizag.

segments.name: Iodinated contrast media intermediate (ABA-HCL)
segments.commentary: Commercial batches expected to start shortly; positive trend seen by end Q2 or beginning Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Mahad (Unit 3, contrast media intermediates) to commission later this calendar year, ahead of earlier H2 guidance; about INR210 crore invested with INR40 crore more committed in the next couple of months.
Backward integration project at Unit 3 on track for commercial contribution in H2 FY27.
FY27 capex expected at about INR250 crore; company-level FY27 capex guidance of INR400 crore reiterated as similar.
Vizag Phase 1 investment about INR1,000 crore over the next 3 years; commercialisation expected from end FY29 to FY30, with ramp-up around FY31-FY32.
Management expects to launch 3 contrast media candidates in FY27 and start pilot activities for a new high-intensity sweetener.
Raw material price trend uncertain; price pass-through to customers expected with a few quarters' lag, evaluated case by case.
capex_capacity: Mahad Unit 3: about INR210 crore invested so far, INR40 crore more committed in the next couple of months; still in CWIP and not yet commercial. Adds over INR200 crore to asset block on commercialisation.

Vizag: about 100 acres secured; consent to establish received; engineering and pre-construction under way. Phase 1 covers contrast media expansion, a multipurpose finishing block, sweetener capacity and an intermediate cluster.
Hyderabad R&D centre: first phase expected to be operational in August 2026; scientific talent already onboarded.
Contrast media plant utilisation ~70%; asset turn currently high-ish due to depreciated asset block, expected to align with industry norms after capitalisation.
demand_pricing: PI/API: management cites secular growth in patient consumption and a strong order book; plant running consistently.

Raw material prices rose sharply from March 2026 after the geopolitical situation; partly reflected in Q1 as consumption came from earlier purchases. Price increases partly offset by rupee depreciation; no price escalation clause triggered in Q1.
Contrast media: overall usage rising across geographies; optic requirements stable under long-term contracts.

Pipeline: about 20 high-conviction NCE opportunities tracked; visibility on 4 programmes in chronic therapy areas (oncology, CNS and one undisclosed). Two lateral-entry opportunities (chronic, mature blockbuster products) expected to fructify, with initial quantities small.
Peptides: focus on peptide fragments (liquid phase) rather than generic front-end peptides, where management sees price erosion.

qa_highlights.question: Contrast media revenue fell ~40% QoQ; how much revenue is deferred to Q2 and what is utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing goods in transit were about INR30 crore higher than opening, which will be recognised next quarter. Plant utilisation is ~70% steady; production unchanged and production-to-dispatch at 100%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating income jump to INR16.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the bulk to forex gain and higher interest income, and later clarified the line item is driven mainly by export incentives tied to export levels and byproduct sales; the ratio to exports should remain in a similar range.

qa_highlights.question: Is PI/API growth lumpy or secular, and what visibility exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: secular growth in end-market demand plus a strong order book and consistent production give good visibility for at least 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vizag and cardiovascular-related opportunity translate into sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to speculate, saying it will go by orders on hand; order book described as good and an update to come when more information is available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the peptides strategy and differentiation from other Indian CDMOs?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on peptide fragments first (liquid phase), with selective forward integration into final peptides for large CDMOs or innovators; no participation in generic front-end peptides. Management intends to quantify the peptide-related RFPs in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Do you maintain FY27 capex guidance and what is the asset turn outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR250 crore; company-level FY27 capex of INR400 crore similar. Asset turn to be assessed on commercialisation from end FY29-FY30, with ramp-up around FY31-FY32.

risks_watch: Raw material cost inflation and uncertain trend; pass-through to customers lags by a few quarters and may compress margins in the interim.
Goods-in-transit timing (container shortages, geopolitical transit delays) causing quarter-to-quarter revenue volatility in contrast media.
PI/API concentration on a few molecules; new programmes still in validation, with initial volumes small.
Mahad commissioning and validation timeline; iodinated intermediate commercial batches expected end Q2 or beginning Q3 FY27.
Vizag execution and long gestation (commercialisation FY29-FY30), with asset turnover low until capitalisation.
Management was reticent on customer names, registrations, lateral-entry molecules and competitor developments (Divis, Merck's Lipfendra), so these are unresolved.

500279|2026-06.headline: Onida Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.5% YoY to Rs 182.4 crore, but net loss widened to Rs 14.2 crore from Rs 12.5 crore.
500279|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 29.5% YoY to Rs 182.4 crore, led by LED TV (+56.8%) and AC (+39.2%) in the branded business of Rs 175 crore (+35.8%). Gross margin improved 100 bps to 17.3%, helped by mix and AC/LED realisations, partly offset by washing machine margin pressure from input costs and competitor pricing. Net loss widened to Rs 14.2 crore from Rs 12.5 crore YoY. Management declined to give revenue or EBITDA guidance or timelines, repeatedly pointing to revenue momentum as the first step and profitability only after scale is reached.

segments.name: Air conditioners
segments.commentary: Largest category, about 60% of Q1 turnover per CFO; grew 39.2% YoY on seasonal recovery and better realisations.

segments.name: LED TVs
segments.commentary: About 25-30% of Q1 turnover; grew 56.8% YoY on launches and promotions. 100-inch QD Mini-LED TV launched and going to market.

segments.name: Washing machines
segments.commentary: Low single-digit share of revenue; down 1.8% YoY on mix, with margins hit by input costs and aggressive competitor pricing. Wider semi-auto and fully-automatic top-load range planned for Diwali.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or EBITDA guidance given; management said it would not give forward-looking numbers on this call.
Management said Q1 revenue growth should continue through FY27 and into next year, with bottom line to follow once scale is reached.

Internal target of 800-1,000 retail-excellence outlets by end of FY27; aim to double retail reach in 6-12 months.
Net working capital benchmark of 30-45 days on an annual average basis; expects no pressing funding need over the next 3-6 months.
Investor PPT to accompany Q2 FY27 results; calls planned at quarter-end results.
capex_capacity: Capex limited to small tooling and mould investments, to be funded internally.
Compressor JV or in-house compressor manufacturing not planned currently because scale does not justify it.
Wada plant scaled down in production; management denied immediate closure but said space may be used for other purposes, with no immediate timeline.
Asset monetisation under review; nothing immediately on the table, though not off the table.
Asset-light model: contract manufacturing deprioritised in favour of own branded business; reliance on ODM/OEM partners, with imports largely minimised due to QCO norms.
demand_pricing: Management said it wants to stay competitive on price while protecting margins; product mix is the other lever.
Early customer response to launches described as encouraging, with conversion rising as retail reach and activation expand.
Offline remains the bulk of revenue; e-commerce is in the high single digits.
Presence through distributors and direct dealers estimated at about 4,000+ stores, stronger in Tier-2/3 and in Gujarat, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and West Bengal.
Institutional cooling is a new vertical that management says has a few good inquiries.
Washing machine pricing pressure from competitors; input costs rising continuously, making frequent price changes difficult.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company handle rising input costs: price competitively or protect margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to stay competitive on pricing while managing the value chain to protect margins, with product mix as an added lever.

qa_highlights.question: When can PAT break even and what revenue or EBITDA margins are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. CFO said roughly a further 30% revenue increase would start contributing to bottom line, but that is a ballpark that may shift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment and channel mix?
qa_highlights.answer: AC about 60% of turnover, LED 25-30%, washing machines low single digit. Online is high single digit, offline is the majority.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company shifting to contract manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract manufacturing is now second priority; the branded business is the focus, with own production and some capability maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and cash position and are non-core assets being sold?
qa_highlights.answer: Fund-based limits largely unused as of June; borrowings of about Rs 38 crore to be repaid over 18 months; some surplus parked in mutual funds. Asset monetisation under review, nothing immediate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital benchmark?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30-45 net working capital days on an annual average is a good benchmark, with seasonal elevation expected.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: washing machine margins under competitor pricing; input costs rising with limited ability to pass on.
Loss widened YoY despite revenue growth; the path to PAT breakeven remains undefined.
Balance sheet described as slightly stressed by management; asset monetisation (Andheri office, Wada land and plant) not yet decided.
Execution of retail expansion (double reach in 6-12 months; 800-1,000 excellence outlets) and funding of marketing and GTM spend.
Festive season (Diwali/Dussehra) performance of new TV and washing machine launches.
Service quality and reputation ahead of planned service infrastructure improvements.
Leadership transition: management says the team is fully in place but further changes are expected.

And our objective is to continue this momentum for the rest of the year as well as for the next coming year.

543547|2026-06.headline: Ddev Plastiks Q1 FY27 EBITDA crossed INR100 crore for the first time (INR101 cr, 10% margin), revenue up 29% YoY on export price gains.
543547|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 29% YoY and EBITDA rose 27% to about INR101 crore at a 10% margin, the first quarter above INR100 crore. PAT was about INR64 crore, up 22% YoY. Growth was driven mainly by export pricing (about INR300 crore export revenue, mostly MENA) rather than volume, with export volumes up only single digits and total volume up about 1% YoY. Capacity utilisation averaged about 66% as the new 48,000 t Bhiwadi XLPE plant, commissioned in April 2026, ramps up at roughly 20-25%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% volume growth and a 13-14% revenue target, and said it expects to beat it.

segments.commentary: Low volume but management cites 10-15% EBITDA margin; focus kept on lighting-industry niche (about 4 years of work).

Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) greenfield XLPE plant of 48,000 t commissioned April 2026, running at about 20-25% utilisation; expected to ramp over the next couple of months.
HFFR capacity to be expanded to 20,000 t by FY27 end; new Vapi site for product consolidation; PVC addition of about 25,000 t mentioned.

East India (Bengal) plant for medium-voltage cable compounds being set up; the BESS location is being shifted from West to East, delaying timelines by a couple of quarters, with the state incentive policy expected around end-August.

Management says the company's cable-customer segment grows about 12-13% a year, which is the basis for the 15% volume target, with the extra 2-3% expected to come from market share gains.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q4 export revenue spilled into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 1,000 t moved from late-March shipments; value rose due to freight, so about INR300+ crore export revenue was reported in Q1, partly from Q4 volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA/t sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR19.6/t may not hold each quarter but could last a few months; the long-term target is INR16-17/t or 10-12% margin. The war-risk premium is about INR2.5-3/t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS business model and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Starts as a supply model at 6-8% EBITDA margin, with EPC adding 2-5 points and system integrator another 2-3 points; long-term target 11-15%. BOO/BOOT not planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance (13-14% revenue) below capacity growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance uses FY26 average prices, assumes about 50% Bhiwadi utilisation and 15% volume growth; management says it expects to beat guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will finance costs and cash conversion cycle improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance costs rose from working-capital borrowing after the March raw material spike; they have eased since July. Cash conversion cycle expected to return to 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company gain market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management cites the Bhiwadi plant and importers being displaced by supply-chain disruption. Bhiwadi will serve existing customers, mainly in Rajasthan and Delhi.

540061|2026-06.headline: Bigbloc Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~40% YoY to ~INR 79 crore and EBITDA to ~INR 6 crore (~8% margin), with net loss narrowing to ~INR 70 lakh.
540061|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as an inflection point, with sales volume of 2,21,545 cubic meters (+32% YoY) and plant utilisation of about 69%. Revenue was about INR 79 crore (+~40% YoY) and EBITDA about INR 6 crore versus INR 1 crore a year earlier. The net loss narrowed to about INR 70 lakh from about INR 6 crore. segments.commentary: ~5% of Q1 revenue. Madhya Pradesh plant: construction to begin post-monsoon after a decision over the next couple of quarters; commercial production targeted in FY28.
Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter; Q3 and Q4 expected to be strongest.
Price hikes to be passed through in some markets already and in others in upcoming quarters.

Madhya Pradesh land acquired ~15 months ago with construction permissions and pollution board approvals in hand; construction post-monsoon.
