Management is exploring fleet expansion beyond SUN and is at an initial discussion stage. Financing options: lease structure (fixed lease over 10 years, dollar buyout at year 10), internal accruals, or outright purchase with debt.
Sky lease cost is about USD 16 million per year, treated as an operating cost in management's numbers under Ind AS.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per passenger rose to Rs 13,645 in Q2 FY27 from Rs 10,349, driven by higher ticket price and onboard revenue.
Company started charging a fuel surcharge of USD 15-20 per person per day to offset part of the fuel cost increase.
Sky's per-guest pricing is said to be about 100% higher than Empress, and SUN's about 150% higher, driven by cabin mix (suites: 60/69 on Empress, 260 on Sky, 600 on SUN).

Management said the Indian overnight ocean and coastal cruise market was about Rs 8,301 million in FY25 and is expected to grow 20-25% CAGR over FY26-FY31. India had about 4.8 lakh cruise passenger movements in CY2025, about 89% domestic.
Management cited about 95 wedding dates in FY28 versus a typical 65-70, and plans to grow weddings and celebrations as a revenue stream.
Loyalty programme 'Chairman's Club' is being rolled out.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion from operating leverage, and how will fuel, crew and port costs be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cruise margins globally are 35-40% and the company expects to match or beat that. Shared corporate costs across more ships are expected to lower per-ship operating cost. Fuel is expected to ease, and the company plans to offset it with surcharges, itinerary changes and cost savings.

qa_highlights.question: How will the next fleet addition be financed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the lease structure used for Empress, Sky and SUN (fixed lease over 10 years, then a nominal buyout). It also cited internal accruals (about Rs 220 crore used for Sky and SUN pre-IPO) and possible debt funding for an outright purchase.

qa_highlights.question: Why did short-term borrowings rise by about Rs 344 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the funds were advanced to a subsidiary, which passed them to an intermediary to hold ready for an identified vessel deal. The money is interest-bearing and not yet used.

qa_highlights.question: How much fuel cost is unrecovered and what price increase would neutralise it?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said about Rs 12 crore of fuel cost impact remains after surcharges and savings. Management said full absorption is unlikely and it hopes to return to original forecast by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How does lease cost for Sky and SUN affect earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Sky lease is about USD 16 million per year. Management said it is included in operating costs and pricing, and below EBITDA under Ind AS it is absorbed at PBT and PAT levels.

qa_highlights.question: What are the bookings for H2, including Empress and Sky?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers, citing restrictions on forward-looking statements. It said demand was strong and that near-term bookings were hard to get.

532937|2026-06.headline: Kuantum Q1 FY27 operational income rose 36% YoY to INR304 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR40 crore (13.2% margin) as input costs outran price gains.
532937|2026-06.overview: Paper sales volume grew 35% YoY to 42,922 metric tons, and blended NSR improved about INR3,400/ton QoQ. Cost per ton rose about INR4,200 QoQ on raw material, chemical and fuel inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, so EBITDA stayed broadly flat YoY and PAT was INR6 crore. Management cut its FY27 top-line expectation to INR1,300 crore-plus from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore and pushed the 16-18% EBITDA margin target to the year-end. PM3 rebuild completion, pulp capacity additions and anti-dumping applications were the main operational updates.

segments.name: Paper (writing & printing, copier, maplitho)
segments.commentary: Realisation around INR68,000-69,000/ton per management, targeted to reach INR72,000-75,000 in 4-6 months. Specialty grades are just under 20% of mix (18-19% stated), target 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line revised to INR1,300 crore-plus, versus earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore guidance; management said realisations are running below earlier expected levels.
EBITDA margin at least 16-18% by year-end; management says Q3 onwards is when these margins should be visible, not Q2.
FY28 top line expected INR1,400-1,500 crore; FY29-30 conservatively INR1,500 crore at current pricing, INR1,600-1,650 crore if pricing rises to about INR75,000/ton.
Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; scheduled repayments about INR170-175 crore per year for the next 2-3 years; debt to fall below INR300-350 crore within 3 years.
AI-led opex reduction target of 4-5% by March 2028.
Pulp capacity to rise to about 410-415 TPD from 365 TPD.
capex_capacity: DDS (Double Displacement Digester) for wood pulping commissioned in Q1.
Native starch system commissioned on PM2 and PM3.
Folio ream wrapping machine installed in the finishing house.
PM3 shut for major rebuild; management expects commissioning within about a week of the call (mid-August 2026), completing the upgradation programme.
Pulping capacity of about 200 TPD each for agro and wood, said to be sufficient for all four machines.
EC clearance for PM3 upgrade filed and awaited.
Clonal propagation: record 17.28 lakh saplings in the quarter; plantation area about 19,650 acres after adding about 1,300 acres.
demand_pricing: Demand supported by education, publishing and office consumption; management expects demand to stay supportive.
Chinese imports diminishing, attributed mainly to shipping and container cost issues; imported copier/maplitho price seen at $610-620/ton near port.
Anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty applications filed for writing and printing paper, covering 40-140 GSM; management hopes for a favourable decision, assumed 5-year duration.
Maplitho hit by inverted duty structure after GST change; management says Kuantum is reducing notebook paper exposure and passing GST losses to customers.
Management says pricing held flat QoQ into Q2 with no discounting; dealer channel inventory described as lean.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance maintained, and what EBITDA margin is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is positive with PM3 commissioning, targeting at least 16-18% EBITDA margin by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak debt and the repayment path?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; repayments of about INR170-175 crore a year for 2-3 years, with debt below INR300 crore within 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the revenue guidance fall from INR1,400-1,500 crore to INR1,300 crore-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations are running below earlier expected levels and EBITDA margins are strained by West Asia-driven costs; management says figures are conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall while a competitor's rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Punjab-specific raw material cost increases, mainly wheat straw, which it says is easing; it expects a gradual reduction in procurement cost.

qa_highlights.question: What share of cost increase is due to the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the INR4,200/ton cost increase is attributed to West Asia; INR3,400/ton has been passed through in pricing QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will wheat straw prices come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said procurement prices fell in Q2 versus Q1 after negotiations with suppliers, with further easing expected as rice straw and corn cobs arrive in September-October.

risks_watch: Cost pass-through: about INR800/ton of the INR4,200/ton cost rise was not recovered in Q1 price gains; watch whether Q2 NSR and margins recover.
Execution on PM3 commissioning (mid-August) and full-capacity ramp; Q2 is expected to be weak with machine and boiler shutdowns.
Revenue guidance cut and inconsistency with earlier FY28-30 projections.
Q2 seasonally weak demand; management says October onwards is when the industry picks up.
Pending EC clearance for PM3 and pending anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty decision.
Debt of about INR760-770 crore at peak and interest burden on PAT.
532937|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term capacity and specialty mix, but defensive on the FY27 numbers: management conceded the revenue guidance was revised and that margins are being squeezed by costs outside its control. Answers on the guidance gap and FY30 targets were partly contradictory and hard to reconcile.
key_quotes: We should be reaching closer to about at least between 16% to 18% by the year-end.
Peak debt, we are currently looking at about INR760 crores or INR770 crores maximum.
Nobody could have imagined like a war starting in a part of the world and impacting sort of pricing here in India.
Right now, our contribution from specialty paper is just under 20%.

541578|2026-06.headline: Varroc Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.9% YoY to INR2,634 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.5% from 9.5% on war-related costs and a tooling sale.
541578|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 30% YoY to INR2,634 crore, with India up about 29% and overseas up about 46%. EBITDA margin fell to 8.5% (9.5% a year ago, 9.7% in Q4) on about 0.5% genuine under-recovery of war-related commodity costs, a 0.25% numerator/denominator effect, and about 0.8% from a large low-margin tooling sale (about INR70 crore). PBT before JV and exceptional items was 4.3% of revenue, up 20 bps YoY. Net debt rose to INR527 crore from INR495 crore on front-loaded capex and a INR441 million working-capital build. Management pointed to 20-25% FY27 growth as its ambition, not formal guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before JV and exceptional items
financial_highlights.change: +20 bps YoY (management also cited 4.1% last year)
up from INR495 crore; +INR316 million QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity / net debt to EBITDA
Net new business wins (annual peak revenue)
financial_highlights.change: order book opened FY at INR3,509 crore; close to INR500 crore already moved to SOP

segments.name: India operations
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 29% YoY and 10% QoQ, EBITDA up 22% YoY, PBT up 41% YoY; EBITDA margin 10.6% and PBT margin about 7%.

segments.name: Overseas electronics and lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 46% YoY; losses narrowing sequentially. Romania electronics (E/E architecture, passenger vehicle) is now reported separately. Romania targets EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27; 2-wheeler overseas already profitable.

segments.name: E-mobility (EV)
segments.commentary: EV revenue about 16% of total, up 87% YoY. EV powertrain revenue up about 56% YoY versus industry EV volumes up 80-90%; management attributes gap to lower ASPs (high single-digit decline) from product mix, plus early-quarter labour disruption in April-May.

segments.name: ICE powertrain
segments.commentary: Overseas forging is about 3.3% of revenue (per slide 13) and sits in ICE powertrain. Management said about 70% of the business is powertrain-agnostic, with the balance ICE-specific.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 20-25% seen as an ambition, not guidance; mid-to-high teens was guided earlier.

Around 50 bps of war-related under-recovery expected to be recovered from customers mostly in Q1-Q2; inflation recovery is arithmetic and may take 1-2 quarters. Most other one-time impacts (tooling) not expected to repeat to this extent in Q2.
Long-term target of 10% PBT in 3-4 years; management said medium term 'soon' and declined to give a year-end PBT number.
FY27 capex of INR500-550 crore (India plus overseas), heavier than the last 2-3 years, mainly e-mobility capacity.
Overseas revenue expected to roughly double YoY this year (electronics and lighting); overseas PBT target 10% in 3-4 years.
Revenue ambition: roughly double to INR20,000 crore by FY31 from about INR10,000 crore this year, ~20% overseas, ~10% from inorganic routes.
Zero-debt target for FY28 retained, though management said it will pursue it sooner if possible.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR160 crore, mostly capacity additions; the net debt increase was partly working capital.
FY27 capex INR500-550 crore including overseas, with e-mobility capacity and capacity to service EV models with engine-agnostic products the main drivers.
Traction motor business: one non-Bajaj win to start SOP in Q2 FY27; two further customers in advanced discussions with SOPs expected within FY27.
Eric Hammond appointed CTO for Business Unit I (25 years global automotive technology leadership in electrification, software-defined vehicles, functional safety).
demand_pricing: Net new business wins of about INR600 crore annual peak revenue; about two-thirds e-mobility volume expansion on existing programs, balance mainly a 4-wheeler lighting win for Thailand and smaller wins.
Bajaj share of annual peak revenue in the order book at 75% vs 58% of order-book count (as stated by CFO); management says non-Bajaj wins are growing.
Pricing: management expects no double-digit ASP declines; OEMs are cost-optimised, and component integration into smaller boxes may raise ASP.
PBT margins of ICE and EV are expected to be broadly comparable at PBT level; EBITDA is not a like-for-like metric across product lines given capital intensity.

544174|2026-06.headline: TBO TEK Q1 FY27: EBITDA-to-GTV of 1.3% and operating leverage shown despite Middle East disruption; 24% Europe growth, 15% organic CC growth.
544174|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) as the toughest in two years due to Middle East-driven travel disruption, yet reported top-line and bottom-line growth. Europe grew 24% YoY and Middle East was flat (1% CC growth), with Classic Vacations (acquired about six months ago) adding North America scale. EBITDA margins expanded faster than gross profit, which management cited as evidence of operating leverage. Management began reporting constant-currency numbers because a roughly 11% INR-vs-CC gap in hotel GTV distorted YoY growth. Management declined to give a timeline for Middle East normalisation or a long-term margin target.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 24% YoY in a weak quarter, helped by market development investments made last year; management says Europe and APAC lead growth.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: Analyst cited about 15% growth in APAC alongside 30%+ Europe; management said APAC and Europe are leading the growth charter.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Flat, +1% in constant currency; inbound travel to Middle East is under serious stress, while TBO's outbound business is less exposed.

segments.name: North America (Classic Vacations)
segments.commentary: North America is nearly a quarter of hotel GTV after Classic acquisition; Classic has highest GP profile (about 11%) and is seasonally strongest in Q1 on check-in basis.

segments.name: Airlines
segments.commentary: Airline GTV grew about 15% YoY; airline GP profile is about 1%, so airline mix shifts take rate.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for both QoQ and YoY growth; Q2 expected to be somewhat better than Q1 given July is the heaviest northern hemisphere travel month.
Management expects SG&A growth to be significantly slower than GP growth, though SG&A growth may tick up in Q2 due to increment season and opportunistic market development.
Classic platform integration expected to finish by end of calendar 2026; Classic-to-TBO selling expected to start early next year after platform migration.
Management said margins should expand as top-line normalises, but gave no long-term margin target; said it is not anchoring to 45-60% steady-state platform margins.
Operating leverage expected to continue; Q2 expected to show some margin expansion, Q3 historically lower revenue and margin dip.
Full-year Classic EBITDA margin of about 2.5% described as a fair assessment by management.
capex_capacity: Classic Vacations integration: North America feet-on-street sales hiring largely complete; enterprise CRM being implemented at Classic.
Platform integration (TBO and Classic) expected to be completed by calendar year end 2026.
VOYA AI itinerary tool is experimental; capex minimal and capitalised as intangibles; built in-house by tech team.
AI-based CRM layer launched a few weeks before the call; too early for results.
demand_pricing: Middle East situation described as extremely fluid; management declined to forecast when Middle East returns to growth.
Take rate slightly lower in Q1 as regions fought for business in the crisis; management accepted lower margins to win share.
Airfares very high; Middle East carriers disruption hit East-West travel, affecting India and Europe.
Management claims share gains in APAC and Europe, citing high double-digit growth in a market with no organic growth.
GTV split between retail and B2B/API roughly 50-50, unchanged from last quarter; management will review disclosure.
Management expects bigger players to gain share as smaller and mid-sized players attrite post crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1.3% consolidated EBITDA-to-GTV sustainable and can it grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA-to-GTV is tricky due to airline vs hotel take-rate differences; the right metric is EBITDA-to-GP, at about 26%, which should keep improving.

qa_highlights.question: How should organic growth be modelled once conditions normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a return to the growth profile of Q3 FY26, timing uncertain (Q3 or Q4); Europe and APAC lead, with North America growth expected from October-December on a like-for-like basis.

qa_highlights.question: How will Classic's December-quarter consolidation affect GP growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two opposing forces exist: Classic has not yet delivered standalone enterprise growth (a few quarters away), while pre-war organic growth in Jan-Feb was above 15%.

qa_highlights.question: How long can APAC and Europe growth last before the next investment cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: A key account manager typically shows four to six quarters of growth; no early signs of slowdown, with investments expected to be sticky.

qa_highlights.question: Is the SG&A run-rate of about 4% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A growth may expand a little in the short term due to increment season and market development, but will be range-bound and slower than top line.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 30 bps drop in organic hotels GP/GTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split the drop between lower Middle East saliency and deliberate margin cuts to protect volumes, saying both occurred.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and cross-sell status?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash in bank Rs. 1,980+ crore against USD 70 million loan and EUR 6 million working capital loan; about INR 65 crore of TBO-to-Classic sales, reverse flow not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11% currency impact due to a policy change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no policy change; the gap is purely rupee depreciation, and CC reporting will continue directionally.

financial_highlights.change: Organic growth cited as mid-teens; Jan-Feb pre-war trend was higher than 15%
Strong per analyst; management says tricky metric to track
Management expects this to keep improving

financial_highlights.metric: Classic Vacations EBITDA margin on GTV
financial_highlights.change: Seasonally highest quarter; management indicated ~2.5% full-year as fair assumption
Management says new lower cost baseline

financial_highlights.value: USD 70 million loan and EUR 6 million working capital loan (Jumbo)

financial_highlights.change: Early signs of cross-sell; reverse flow not yet started

financial_highlights.metric: Currency impact on hotel GTV (INR vs CC)
financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY26 vs Q1 FY25 gap was about 3%
Kavish cited 17% for airlines; prior H2 FY26 about 20%

544709|2026-06.headline: Gaudium IVF Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore, while reported EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 29% on expansion and marketing costs.
544709|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore against ₹17.8 crore in Q1 FY26, with management attributing the slow growth to seasonality and pre-launch work. Reported EBITDA fell 52.96% to ₹2.4 crore and PAT from continuing operations fell 42.27% to ₹1.8 crore, which management tied to front-loaded expansion costs and a one-time pan-India marketing push for the SiD and ERICA AI embryology tools. The South Extension (New Delhi) hub became operational on 16 July 2026, with Gurgaon and Nagpur guided to open in about 10 and 25 days. Management reiterated FY27 targets of about 30% revenue growth and 10 new hubs, but the quarter's growth rate is far below that target.

segments.name: IVF (core)
segments.commentary: Anchors the business; management says the Janakpuri (Delhi) flagship is growing about 30% YoY. Pharmacy and hospital services are described as lower-margin and complementary, with no separate figures disclosed.

segments.name: Pharmacy and hospital services
segments.commentary: Supply fertility medications and allied women's health services (gynaecology, obstetrics, minimally invasive procedures). No revenue or margin split given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of about 30% revenue growth for FY27 by year-end, after an analyst challenged whether 40%+ was achievable; it said the growth rate would pick up over Q2 and Q4.
Adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to return to FY26 levels by year-end, per management's answer to a direct question.
Target of 10 new hubs in FY27, then 8 in FY28 and 1 in FY29; South Extension is the first of the 19-centre IPO-funded expansion.
Breakeven for new hubs is said to come in about three months historically, against a six-month industry-type benchmark.
Lucknow Women Hospital project of up to ₹15 crore, funded from internal accruals, with commercialisation expected in FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of about ₹25 crore for 10 new hubs at about ₹2.5 crore per hub (₹1 crore construction, ₹1.5 crore lab machinery), funded from IPO proceeds and internal accruals; described as on track.
South Extension, New Delhi hub operational 16 July 2026, with the Gaudium Signature Lab (AI embryology).
Gurgaon hub expected to be operational about 10 days after the call; Nagpur (Tier 2) about 25 days after the call.
Patna centre relocated to Kankarbagh medical hub and became operational about three days before the call.
Mature hub volume benchmarks: about 30 cycles a year for a Tier 2 hub and about 50 for a metro hub.
demand_pricing: Q1 is seasonally weak (heat) and Q3 is weak (festivals); management said Q2 and Q4 make up for it, and that historically growth has been about 30% YoY against an industry CAGR of 10-12%.
Initial IVF package starts at about ₹2 lakh per patient and can go up to ₹20 lakh for complex cases; per-cycle cost cited as about ₹2 lakh.
International patients are about 25-30% of the patient mix; three international spokes have begun in Paris, Nigeria and Sydney.

Management says the organised segment is about 30% of the market versus 70% unorganised, and expects consolidation as the ART Act is implemented; it also said full implementation may take about another year.
HDFC Bank patient financing tie-up is aimed at Tier 2 and Tier 3 patients.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 growth only 9%, and is 30-40% FY27 growth and FY26-level margins achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 seasonality and build-up work on centres under construction; it said South Extension is already contributing and reiterated 30% growth and FY26-level adjusted margins by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly does a new hub break even, and at what scale is it profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said breakeven historically comes in about three months, and its centres have broken even within that period wherever they have opened.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter hospital business in Lucknow, and is it funded from IPO proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Lucknow was already on the IVF expansion list, that the women's hospital is a step toward women's health beyond IVF, and that it is funded from internal accruals, not IPO money.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics per hub (capex, package size, cycles)?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex averages ₹2.5 crore per centre; initial package ₹2 lakh up to ₹20 lakh; mature Tier 2 hubs target about 30 cycles a year and metro hubs about 50.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin decline from a one-off expense?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin decline mainly to a one-time pan-India marketing push for SiD and ERICA, expected to pay off over the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue growth be split into patient volume and revenue per patient?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a volume versus price split; it repeated the seasonality explanation and did not address the service-mix question directly.

qa_highlights.question: How are the AI tools differentiated and what is the benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SiD (sperm selection) and ERICA (embryo assessment) are the first such tools in India, certified by IVF 2.0, and show early results of about 8% higher first-attempt success; these are early results and not yet validated over a longer period.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 9.1% against a 30% full-year target; delivery depends on Q2 and Q4 recovery and on new hubs ramping.
EBITDA margin of 12.5% versus the guided return to FY26 levels; management calls the drag one-off, but it needs verification next quarter.
Early AI-tool success-rate data (about 8% improvement) is not yet validated over a longer period; management said this would need time.
Competitive intensity and the pace of ART Act implementation across states, which management said could take about another year.
Execution on hub openings (Gurgaon, Nagpur) and on the balance of the 10 FY27 hubs; the Lucknow hospital adds a new business line and capex of up to ₹15 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (ex expansion one-offs, per management)

financial_highlights.value: ₹3.5 lakh (~₹4 lakh excluding low-value services, fresh pickups)

544443|2026-06.headline: Travel Food Services Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT up 35.6% YoY to INR1.3 billion on 20.6% revenue growth, despite flat passenger traffic and 0.8% system-wide LFL.
544443|2026-06.overview: Management reported system-wide sales up 18% YoY to INR8.4 billion and consolidated revenue from operations up 20.6% YoY to INR4.5 billion, with net contract gains of 15.9% system-wide. Passenger traffic was broadly flat YoY, with international traffic hit by the Middle East conflict and May's domestic rebound reversed in June. EBITDA rose 11% to INR1.6 billion, but margin moderated to 35.8% on pre-operating and employee costs for new airports (Noida, Cochin, Delhi). PAT was helped by a INR131 million one-time GST provision write-back in other income.

financial_highlights.change: ex-Mumbai, Guwahati and some South India markets about 7%
Adjusted for INR223 million lounge aggregation cost reclassification: INR3.65 billion, about 81%
+35.6% YoY vs 25.3% margin last year; includes INR131 million GST provision write-back

segments.name: Travel QSR and lounges (system-wide)
segments.commentary: 580 outlets and lounges at June end across 21 airports; 153 brands; 87 travel QSR outlets and two lounges added over last 12 months. Noida International Airport commenced operations in the quarter.

segments.name: JV / associate business
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 15% per management's implied figure as questioned by analysts; drag from Western India airports with Middle East exposure. Management said JV ramp-up continues.

segments.name: Passenger services (Elite Assist)
segments.commentary: Launched at Noida International Airport with meet-and-greet and porter services; to integrate into the EATS platform and expand to more airports.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 passenger traffic bounce-back as airlines restore long-haul international routes from September and October 2026.
About 90 units commissioned over last 12 months expected to normalise over next 12 months; benefits to play out in H2 FY27.
Over 50 outlets under development, mostly to open in FY27; 12-18 months to mature at existing terminals, 18-24 months at greenfield airports.
Pre-operating costs for Cochin, Delhi and Noida ramp-up expected to normalise in about 12 months, returning to traditional cost levels.
Delhi T3 contract runs to 30 September 2026; GHL JV bid result pending. Chennai and Kolkata renewals due end-March 2027 and early Q1 FY28.
Bhogapuram Airport opened 17 August 2026 with multiple outlets under JV GHL.
capex_capacity: Over 50 outlets under construction or about to start construction across airports including Delhi, Navi Mumbai, Bhogapuram and Noida.
Noida International Airport outlets and passenger services commissioned in the quarter.
Asia focus for international expansion; Dubai entity set up for the Middle East and Indonesia entity set up recently to enable local bids.
Highways wayside amenities (WSA) under evaluation, with government plan of about 1,000 wayside amenities; management says medium-to-long term.
demand_pricing: Passenger traffic broadly flat YoY in Q1: April declined, May rebounded to record domestic month, June softened on renewed conflict. Management says traffic in July-August similar to Q1 trend, with international the drag.
LFL growth normally runs 5-7 percentage points above passenger traffic; management did not take significant price increases this year, with growth from premiumisation, bundles and brand changes.
Mumbai and Guwahati hit by traffic migration to new airport infrastructure; South India markets hit by Middle East exposure.
Contract renewal rate moved from about 94% to 92%, attributed to non-renewal of small highway outlets.
Management says bidding discipline stays on cash return; net contract gains are lumpy and not guided.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 4.2% LFL came from higher spend per passenger, and what is sustainable LFL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LFL is typically 5-7 points above passenger traffic; it was 7% ex-affected markets. Growth came from premiumisation, bundles, brand edits and limited pricing, with price increases kept tempered.

qa_highlights.question: Lounge aggregation cost and other expenses rise in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: INR223 million of lounge aggregation cost sits in other expenses; excluding it, other expenses rose 22% YoY. Management expects normalisation within about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why are JV and associate revenues growing slower than consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Some JV contracts are moving to JV structures over time, and Western airports with Middle East exposure, which form a bulk of JV portfolio, were hit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Delhi T3 contract moving to JV in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Delhi T3 contract runs to 30 September 2026; GHL has bid and results are awaited. The new SPV with GMR has 30% TFS shareholding, so it will not be consolidated going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 50 outlets under development in existing airports?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a blend of already-announced airports such as Delhi, Navi Mumbai and Bhogapuram; these were won 3-8 months ago and are in build-out.

qa_highlights.question: Highways strategy: is it accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said highways are a medium-to-long-term opportunity tied to government wayside amenity plans, with a return threshold that must be met; it will be calibrated, not immediate.

risks_watch: International traffic recovery depends on airline route restorations from September-October 2026; Middle East conflict renewed in June.
EBITDA margin (35.8%) under pressure from pre-operating and employee costs at new airports; watch normalisation in next 12 months.
Delhi T3 contract ends 30 September 2026 and the GHL JV bid outcome is unknown; it moves out of consolidation.
Chennai and Kolkata renewals due end-March 2027 and early Q1 FY28 may bring cost resets.
PAT growth flattered by INR131 million one-time GST write-back; underlying growth is lower.
544443|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and balance sheet, but cautious on near-term traffic; management repeatedly attributes weakness to temporary external factors. Evasive on specific numbers such as net contract gain targets and JV economics, and on the Delhi T3 bid outcome.

539658|2026-06.headline: TeamLease Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 6% YoY to INR3,056 crores, but EBITDA fell 31% QoQ on EdTech seasonality and appraisals.
539658|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR3,056 crores, up 6% YoY and 4% QoQ, while PBT and PAT both rose 38% YoY to INR36 crores and INR34 crores. Business EBITDA before corporate costs grew 18% YoY, but group EBITDA fell 31% QoQ as EdTech seasonality and appraisal costs hit. General staffing volume growth slowed sharply, with headcount up only 4,000 QoQ to about 2.91 lakh amid client cost pressure, GST 2.0 exits and a pause in power distribution rollouts. Management kept FY27 confidence based on mix and operating leverage, but gave no firm EBITDA guidance and said the 20% FY27 EBITDA target is uncertain. The company completed a INR238 crore buyback and agreed to exit its 30% stake in Crystal HR at full cost recovery.

financial_highlights.change: Aided by INR38 crores tax refund

financial_highlights.value: INR238 crores (8.8% of pre-buyback paid-up capital)

segments.name: General staffing
segments.commentary: Closed at about 2.91 lakh associates, up 4,000 QoQ; gross joinees about 67,600 with 28 new logos, over 2/3 under variable markup or outcome-linked pricing. Staffing EBITDA is about 1%, expected to stay flat in Q2 and improve in Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Specialised staffing
segments.commentary: Revenue up 13% YoY with headcount at 7,630 (net add of 130 QoQ, +13% YoY); 40 new logos including 15 GCCs. GCCs are 45% of associates and 67% of net revenue; margin dipped on upfront investment in Singapore and Middle East; management sees 8-9% stable EBITDA margin in 4-5 quarters.

segments.name: HR services (EdTech and RegTech)
segments.commentary: EdTech has a structurally weak Q1 and a high Q4 weight; EdTech steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 8-10%, with FY27 margin expansion going up to 8-10%. RegTech expected about 8% EBITDA margin for FY27 and now contributes meaningfully to the bottom line.

segments.name: Degree apprenticeship (DA)
segments.commentary: Net addition of about 2,100 apprentices excluding the planned exit of 5,500 headcount flagged in Q4; 18 new client logos added.

guidance_outlook: Staffing EBITDA margin flat for Q1-Q2 FY27, with margin expansion expected in Q3 and Q4 as sales and hiring investments pay off.
Management said it may or may not achieve the 20% FY27 EBITDA growth guidance, citing business and planned investments in data lake, hiring and adjacencies.
Unallocated corporate costs at the current run rate (new leadership in technology and Managing Director) to continue in future quarters.
Management expects a reasonably decent positive net addition in headcount for FY27 and a bullish outlook for the rest of the year, but gave no volume growth number.
Management expects clients to remain on path through H1 FY27, with 17,500 open positions and a healthy pipeline.
capex_capacity: Investments in sales and hiring engines planned for Q1-Q2 FY27, plus data lake spend that was not budgeted earlier.
Specialised staffing: upfront investment in Singapore and Middle East operations acquired about a year ago; margin recovery expected by Q2-Q3.
Smart meter scheme in power distribution: only about 1/4 of the INR25 crore target installed; scheme extended to March 2028 with a large awarded order book yet to be executed.
Capital allocation: buyback of INR238 crores completed (record date 3 July 2026); exit of 30% Crystal HR stake via put option at full recovery of original cost.
demand_pricing: General staffing volume growth has slowed to mid-single digit or lower; management says demand visibility has shortened from several quarters to one quarter at a time.
BFSI described as rotation rather than expansion; growth came from wallet-share gains at private banks, small finance banks and midsized NBFCs.
GST 2.0 and insurance/FMCG tax changes led some clients to move to in-house frontline models; structural client exits noted.
IT services hiring cautious and concentrated in AI and AI-adjacent skills; over 300 AI professionals deployed in the quarter; over 700 associates hired for GCC customers.
Variable markup or outcome-linked pricing used in over 65% of new logos; management says markups have been constant for many years and no near-term change is expected.
Labour codes: most clients who have implemented have preserved associate net take-home pay and absorbed the statutory cost increase; no P&L impact expected on the associate book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the general staffing volume slowdown and BFSI stress structural, and what is the FY27 EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Balasubramanian said demand has become harder to forecast, with visibility now a quarter at a time, and BFSI setbacks are episodic. Ramani said staffing EBITDA is about 1% and will stay flat for one to two quarters, with margin expansion from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will markups improve as the mix shifts to Tier 2-3 cities, non-BFSI accounts and variable markup contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Suparna said there is no big near-term change; higher-margin opportunities need investment and will play out over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why are specialised staffing margins low and what is the steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramani attributed the dip to front-loaded investment in Singapore and Middle East operations and guided to an 8-9% stable margin in 4-5 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will HR services profitability improve meaningfully in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Suparna said EdTech margin would expand to 8-10% and RegTech to about 8% on a full-year basis, with a good overall improvement in HR services EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unallocated cost increase in the segment results?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramani said it reflects new leadership in technology and a new Managing Director; the current run rate will continue in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term levers to lift margin beyond 1.2-1.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramani said core staffing margin will stay in its current range; the lift will come from portfolio mix, with higher-margin businesses such as specialised staffing and HR services growing faster.

532509|2026-06.headline: Suprajit Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% to INR1,070 crore and operational EBITDA 57% to INR129 crore, while standalone EBITDA was flat at INR60 crore.
532509|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR1,070 crore (up 24% YoY) and operational EBITDA reached INR129 crore (up 57%). Global Cables and Mechatronics (GCM) drove the gain, with EBITDA margin rising from 5.8% to 12.6% after the global restructuring. Standalone margins were squeezed by raw material and wage inflation in ICM (margin ~15% to ~13%) and by delayed price pass-through in PLE (margin 6.7%, down 2.8pp); management calls both timing issues and expects recovery in Q2-Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance from the 25 May 2026 release.

financial_highlights.change: invested in mutual funds and bonds

segments.name: Global Cables and Mechatronics (GCM, formerly SCD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~27-28% reported, ~23% after adjusting for two months of SCS Canada/China tranche not in base; EBITDA margin 12.6% vs 5.8%. Management says 12%-plus is current, guidance 10%-12% retained.

segments.name: India Cables and Mechatronics (ICM, formerly DCD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~21%, broad-based across OEM and aftermarket; EBITDA up 4.2% with margin down from ~15% to ~13% on raw material and wage costs. CBS revenue up 110% and brake shoes/pads up ~80% off a small base.

segments.name: Phoenix Lighting and Electricals (PLE, formerly PLD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 5.4%, EBITDA down 45%, margin 6.7% (down 2.8pp) on delayed aftermarket price increases; new prices now in effect. Ramp-up with a large US retailer; Middle East Trifa sales soft.

segments.name: Sensors, Electronics and Displays (SED)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 48%, EBITDA up 100%, margins close to double digits, led by digital clusters and electronic throttle grips. July was reported as the division's highest-sales month.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance from 25 May 2026 release reiterated: consolidated double-digit revenue growth; consolidated operational EBITDA margin 12%-13.5%.
GCM: double-digit growth and 10%-12% operational EBITDA margin (current margin is above this range).
ICM: EBITDA margin around last year's ~15%; PLE: around 12%; SED: around 10%, in line with last year.
Management expects standalone margin shortfall to recover by Q2-Q3; on full year, standalone margin within ~50bps of last year, with at most ~100bps downside as an extreme case.
Management said it will not change margin guidance until year-end, after the restructuring outcome is visible.
GCM expects strong double-digit growth in Q2 based on July trends; August is a seasonally weak month.
capex_capacity: SED: capacity expansion on a war footing; company is relocating out of current site for about six months into a larger leased premises, then rebuilding the plant as a multistorey electronics facility. Earlier plan was sized for about INR250 crore of business.
New STC R&D building on track for completion in Q3 FY27.

GCM: new product launches in China (one of the largest Chinese EV OEMs, about 25 cable projects won, 5-6 launched) and India (lines for a large US OEM building a resilient supply chain). Business wins across India, Mexico and China.
SED: about six launches in the plant this month and next, across instrument clusters, actuators/sensors and throttle position sensors.
US retailer PLE programme: store count expected to roughly triple or go 4x next year.
demand_pricing: Indian automotive sector grew about 22% in the quarter; passenger vehicle and 2-wheeler both grew at double digits per management.
Global automotive and non-automotive demand described as flat to muted; GCM growth attributed to new contract wins replacing lost business.
Pass-through: raw material increases largely recovered; wage increases (mainly northern region) being negotiated, with some customers agreeing and others still resisting.

Three large GCM contract wins announced about a month earlier: largest EV cable contract (USD 5m annual, USD 37m lifetime); European luxury OEM (USD 2m a year, USD 12m lifetime); Japanese OEM (USD 1.2m a year, USD 6m lifetime).
Management described the business as very competitive globally but consolidating, which may favour stronger players on margin.
Braking: CBS customers include TVS and HMSI; management says validation cycles are long for this safety-critical product.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-offs or FX benefits in GCM margin, and is 12% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no material one-offs; margin gains came from restructuring, leaner operations, cost projects and top-line growth. It is at 12%-plus, but guidance of 10%-12% is retained and depends on product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Can SCS be disclosed separately for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. SCS was disclosed separately only until March 2026; it is now folded into GCM as entities were merged or restructured.

qa_highlights.question: Was the GCM 27% growth flattered by FX or acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reported 27% overstates growth; excluding April-May from the second SCS tranche, growth is about 23%. The USD/INR rate has been stable at about INR95-96 over the period.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's gains came from large favourable currency moves on loans, debtors/creditors and forward covers, plus a Morocco subsidy not repeated. Currency has been stable since March, so the Q1 figure is much smaller.

qa_highlights.question: What drives SED growth and the EV exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is in instrument clusters, actuators/sensors and TPS, across multiple customers, with ICE as well as EV demand. Mahindra throttle ramp-up used a rare-earth-free design. Management expects strong growth for at least 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin shortfall in ICM/PLE temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a timing issue: price pass-through is still being negotiated, with recovery expected in Q2 and Q3 and cost reduction under way.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for PLE run-rate and the European insolvency?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes are declining in the old business; the European insolvency is unresolved. Management expects more clarity in the next quarter and sees opportunities over three to six months, with US retailer business growing.

522249|2026-06.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 20% to INR247.03 crore and PAT 43% to INR58.95 crore, with growth mostly from price and mix, not volume.
522249|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue was INR247.03 crore (up 20% YoY), PBT INR77.79 crore (up 41%) and PAT INR58.95 crore (up 43%). Consolidated revenue was INR269.23 crore (up 25%), PAT INR56.12 crore (up 38%). Management said volume grew only about 2-3%, with the rest from price and mix, led by higher-value export sales. Raw material and freight cost inflation, linked to the West Asia conflict, were not passed on to export OEM customers; the company said it has sent price-increase requests to US customers but has not pushed them hard as markets softened.

financial_highlights.change: Export OEM INR73.56 crore; export general INR30.24 crore
Auto OEM INR56.08 crore; replacement INR36.52 crore; footwear INR41.16 crore; furnishing INR6.08 crore; other INR3.38 crore

segments.name: Export OEM
segments.commentary: INR73.56 crore in Q1 FY27 versus about INR53 crore in Q1 FY26 (analyst figure), roughly 39-40% growth; export volume up about 9% per management. Gross margin did not expand on this growth due to freight and raw material costs.

segments.name: Export general
segments.commentary: INR30.24 crore in Q1 FY27; no separate growth figure given.

segments.name: Domestic auto OEM
segments.commentary: INR56.08 crore; domestic volume growth overall about 1%. Management said four-wheeler volumes from Tata are at an early stage and Mahindra business should rise in coming years.

segments.name: Replacement
segments.commentary: INR36.52 crore in Q1 FY27; no growth figure given.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: INR41.16 crore; management said the segment de-grew as sole prices rose sharply, muting demand.

segments.name: PU (polyurethane) plant
segments.commentary: Underutilised with no change over the last three months; competition from China is intense, no confirmed business from top brands despite sampling, and management would not give a firm recommendation for the PU plant this financial year.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to top-line growth of 10-15% per year over the next 3 years, with strong growth expected in exports and not strong growth in domestic.

Sustainable margin is guided at about 25% plus or minus 1-2%, with the Q4 FY26 margin described as an abnormally high one-time forex benefit; management asked analysts to view margin on a yearly basis.
US automotive business expected to grow substantially over the next 3 years, with Ford and Chrysler wallet share gains cited; management said growth would come from existing clients.
Freight and logistics cost increases expected to ease if the war situation improves, but management did not commit to a timeline.
Price increase for US export OEM customers under consideration; management said it would depend on how the market moves over the next two to three weeks.
capex_capacity: New line ordered for the existing Gujarat plant adds 5 lakh meters of capacity, with production targeted around February-March 2027 (end of FY27).
PVC installed capacity is 3.5 million meters per month (range 3.5-4.2 million depending on mix); utilisation is about 75-78% on current production of 2.7-2.8 million meters per month.
Capex for FY27 is around INR50 crore; a further capex of about INR250 crore over the next two years is possible if an overseas plant is finalised, and not yet confirmed.

Overseas plant location still under evaluation (Mexico, US or other NAFTA locations); management said it will go overseas first and not do both expansions at once. An India expansion is a longer-term option.
Management estimated the new line adds about INR150 crore of annual revenue at INR300 per linear meter; total could reach INR250-400 crore including the additional facility, depending on mix.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 growth of 25% was about 2% volume and the rest price, driven by a higher-value export mix; management said raw material price was not the main cause.
Export volume growth of about 9% and domestic about 1%, with total volume growth about 2.77%.
Raw material prices softened a little in Q1 but remain above their early-March 2026 levels; prices were very volatile after March.
Shipping costs roughly quadrupled, and the company did not take a price increase on export OEM business, partly offset by about a 10% natural hedge from dollar appreciation.
Management said the company received a 10% price increase in US dollar terms on some business, though it said the US market is softening again.
Competition in PU is intense from China. Footwear demand was muted because sole prices rose two to three times.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% growth came from volume versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew about 2%; the rest came from price, mainly due to an export mix shift to higher-priced items rather than raw material pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin fall sequentially from the previous quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the previous quarter was abnormally high due to a one-time forex gain; the sustainable margin is about 25% plus or minus 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't gross margin improved despite a roughly 40% jump in export OEM?
qa_highlights.answer: The Gulf war raised raw material costs and shipping costs (about 4x). The company had requested price increases from export OEM customers but put them on hold when prices fell, and has not taken an increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR9 crore rise in other expenses QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mixed: higher export shipping/freight, travel, legal and professional, and risk coverage costs. Management said some of this will continue and some will ease; part relates to the subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US OEM growth outlook and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects US business to grow substantially over three years, through wallet share gains with Ford and Chrysler and new Europe RFQs. It declined to give an order book figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% margin sustainable as a base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company should look at annual margin, which can move 1-2% either way quarter to quarter; it aims to maintain the margin level guided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is 65-66% on a 48 million meter total capacity basis (PVC 3.5-3.7 million meters per month); the new line lifts capacity to about 4-4.2 million meters per month and gives 25-30% headroom.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the PU plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The PU plant is underutilised with no change in three months. Sampling with top brands has been done but no business is confirmed, and management cannot make a strong recommendation this financial year.

533080|2026-06.headline: Mold-Tek Q1 FY27 per-kg EBITDA rose to INR46.7 (from ~INR40.7 in FY26) on consolidation and mix, while volume grew only ~6% due to a 17% lube drop.
533080|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a record quarter, with turnover crossing INR300 crores and EBITDA per kg at INR46.7 versus INR40.7 for full FY26. The company attributes the margin gain mainly to consolidating Hyderabad units from 5 to 2, lower overheads, wastage and inter-unit transfers, and a higher share of pharma and Food & FMCG. Volume growth was about 6%, held back by a 17% fall in lube volumes linked to base-oil shortages at some clients, while paint grew 10.8% in volume and Food & FMCG and pharma grew 24% and 38%. Revenue growth was inflated by raw-material pass-through (PP copolymer rose from about INR107/kg in Q4 to about INR130/kg in Q1), and working capital and finance cost rose sharply as a result.

financial_highlights.change: Management called it a historical quarter; YoY growth not stated in call
vs INR40.7/kg in FY26 full year; ~INR6/kg higher
Would have been ~9% excluding lube decline
Analyst cited; management attributed mostly to raw-material inflation
from 46.60% in comparison period, per analyst
Management: ~15% from raw-material inflation, remainder from mix
Attributed to higher working capital from raw-material prices, not term loans

segments.name: Paints (decorative)
segments.commentary: Value ~46% of revenue, volume ~50% (management); volume grew 10.8% and value ~31%, with growth from existing clients and rising IML adoption. Management expects paint's share to fall toward ~40% over 3-4 years.

segments.name: Lubes
segments.commentary: Volume fell 17% due to base-oil shortages at some private clients affected by the Iran war; lube EBITDA is about INR35-40/kg. Management expects recovery in the current quarter.

segments.name: Food & FMCG (incl. Qpack)
segments.commentary: Food & FMCG grew 24.2% (26% per analyst); Food is ~24% of sales and ~28-29% including Qpack. Management targets 18-20% CAGR.

segments.name: Qpack
segments.commentary: Growth slowed to ~2% from ~20% in the prior quarter because edible oil and cashew customers were price-sensitive; some customers moved back to tin. Management expects ~10% growth in Q2 and double digits later.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Revenue up 41% (volume up 38%) YoY; FY26 base INR34 crores with FY27 target INR50-55 crores. Pharma is ~3.5% of sales but only ~2% of volume.

segments.name: Vibe (JV)
segments.commentary: Three products have patent applications and further products are at pilot stage; commercial products expected around Q3 FY27, with a couple of crores of revenue possible in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA per kg target raised to INR44-45 (from INR42-43); management says it expects to beat INR42 comfortably.
Volume growth target of 10-12% for FY27; management says ~10% is achievable and paint could grow 10-15%.
FY27 capex cut to ~INR90 crores (from INR130-135 crores), including INR25-30 crores for pharma.
Management expects EBITDA growth of 18-20% with volume growth near 10%, and sees the 19-20% EBITDA growth as sustainable for the rest of the year.
Capacity additions of 10-12% a year; target to lift utilisation from ~75% to 78-80%, plus 8-10% new capacity.
capex_capacity: Total capacity is ~67,000 MTPA across Cheyyar, Panipat and Mahad; management says utilisation is about 75%.
Panipat thin-wall trials on 4 machines sell INR70 lakhs-1 crore a month, doubling from August; Qpack sales from Panipat were INR1-1.5 crores in the last six months.
Ophthalmic range: 25,000 sq ft building under construction at the current facility, due in ~6 months; commercial molds are 5-6 months away. Trial molds are complete.

Medical devices (dosing pens): planned minimum capacity of 1 million pens per month; the new land is reserved for devices, and a plant needs 50,000-60,000 sq ft, INR10 crores building and INR10-15 crores machinery.
Automation and lean-manufacturing study planned with a Chinese partner, with implementation expected in the next couple of quarters.
demand_pricing: Raw-material costs were passed through to clients in the following month; management says the company recovered the full increase while keeping margins.
PP copolymer price peaked near INR155-160/kg in late March/April, was ~INR145-146/kg at the time of the call, and management expects it could fall to INR120-125/kg if the war ends.
Inventory gain in Q1 estimated at INR1-1.5/kg.
Realisation benefit: management said ~INR3/kg came from higher pharma and FMCG realisation and ~INR3/kg from consolidation and efficiencies.
Raw-material availability is better than in March-April, though pricing remains volatile. Company inventory is about 1 month (raw material, SFG and finished goods).

544248|2026-06.headline: Mach Travel Q1 FY27 revenue rose 538% YoY to INR144.33 crore, with EBITDA margin compressing to 6.09% from 7.17%.
544248|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR144.33 crore versus INR22.62 crore a year ago and INR83.25 crore in Q4 FY26, with GMV of about INR252 crore disclosed for the first time. EBITDA rose to INR8.92 crore and PAT to INR6.17 crore, but margins were lower YoY, which management attributed to investment in new verticals, hiring and technology. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR500-plus crore and said it is working on bank overdraft lines because of working capital pressure from payment cycles. Much of the quarter's growth came from a few large government and MICE programmes, and several answers were vague or deferred.

financial_highlights.change: +538% YoY vs INR22.62 crore; +73% QoQ vs INR83.25 crore
+437% YoY vs INR1.66 crore; QoQ up from INR3.81 crore
+307% YoY vs INR1.52 crore; QoQ up from INR1.8 crore
Management described company as debt free

segments.name: MICE (core)
segments.commentary: Management estimated MICE at about INR100 crore of Q1 revenue in one answer, then said INR50-60 crore in another, so the split is unclear. Oceania programmes worth about INR32 crore were completed, covering 950-1,000 delegates.

segments.name: Corporate travel
segments.commentary: Launched in April 2026 with more than 100 corporate clients signed; management put it at about 10-15% of revenue. Billing cycles run 1st-15th payable on the 20th and 16th-30th payable on the 6th-7th of the next month.

segments.name: Government and institutional (Punjab Yatra)
segments.commentary: Punjab Yatra contract worth about INR92 crore covering 1.85 lakh yatris, at about INR4,950 per person for a 2-night, 3-day trip. Management said about 15% of Q1 revenue came from it; about 1.15 lakh travelled to date and the contract runs to about November.

segments.name: IRCTC
segments.commentary: Empanelled as one of four or five A-listed vendors, with a first order of about INR75 lakh to INR1 crore. Empanelment term was stated as two years, extendable, but the executive director was not certain.

segments.name: B2B and B2C OTA / leisure
segments.commentary: B2B tool lets smaller travel agents book tickets. B2C app Machtravel.com is in testing and its launch was pushed from late August to September 2026. Leisure was described as doing very well, with no figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of around INR500-plus crore, reiterated and described as an average-based figure; management expects to surpass it.
Management said quarter-on-quarter growth will not be substantial because October-December is a festival and Christmas lull for corporate travel; Q2 is seasonally heavier than Q1 overall.
Management would not commit to a date for EBITDA margins returning to the roughly 10% level mentioned by an analyst, and would not say margins will be under pressure in Q2.
Markups may be compressed in aggressive pursuit of business, but management said the company will not burn money.
Next milestones named: INR500 crore, then INR1,000 crore revenue, B2C app launch in September, a possible main board move within 12 months, and new southern offices.
capex_capacity: Operating presence expanded to Noida, New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Bhubaneshwar and Ahmedabad; more southern offices planned.
Investment in technology, talent and offices over the past year is cited as the cause of lower margins; no quantified capex figure was given.
Corporate self-booking tool (SBT) covers booking, approval, ticketing, invoicing and reporting; management said it uses the same technology as large players.
Captive audience of about 1.25 lakh travellers a year is to be moved onto the B2C portal and app.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the growth to the transition beyond MICE into corporate, B2B, leisure, government and B2C, and said the policies were implemented from 1 April 2026.
TTV (total ticketed volume) was about INR259-260 crore versus about INR143 crore in revenue; the call did not reconcile TTV with GMV of INR252 crore.
Management said pricing on the B2C app is at par with large B2C players.
Punjab Yatra daily flows are about 1,100 travellers out and 1,100 back, with about 3,300-3,500 people handled at any one time.
Management said it is not clear whether the Punjab yatra will be repeated; three other Punjab yatra programmes were not won. Management is in talks with other state governments.

qa_highlights.question: How did revenue grow from INR22 crore to INR140-plus crore, and what steps were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company spent about 1.5 years building new teams and technology and implemented the policies from April 2026. Revenue now comes from MICE, corporate, leisure, government and B2B; TTV was about INR259-260 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be managed to support growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is debt free with about INR3 crore of debt, but payment-cycle issues have created a working capital need. It is working toward bank overdraft facilities and will update the market if availed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between core MICE and the new verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was unsure of the exact split. It said about INR50-60 crore came from MICE in one answer and about INR100 crore in another, with corporate at 10-15% and the Punjab Yatra at about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margins recover to about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no firm date. It said margins will improve as business scales, buying power rises and markups increase, but that it will be aggressive in the market and may give up some markup.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500 crore guidance conservative given Q1 was about 29-30% of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is an annual average and cited seasonality. It said it hopes to surpass INR500 crore, but expects no substantial quarter-on-quarter growth in Q2 and Q3 because of festival periods.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Punjab Yatra contract repeatable, and how is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract is for 1.85 lakh yatris at about INR4,950 per person and runs to about November. Payment is about 7 days after travel, roughly 15 days in total. It was unsure whether the programme would be repeated.

532683|2026-06.headline: AIA Q1 FY27 volumes rose to 64,644 tons (vs ~60,000 a year ago) with PAT of INR301 crore; management gave no volume or margin guidance.
532683|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was described by management as an uneventful, status-quo quarter, with volumes of 64,644 tons against roughly 60,000 a year earlier, sales of INR1,153 crore and PAT of INR301 crore. EBITDA was INR244 crore (about 21% margin on sales as implied by the reported figures), with reported EBITDA margin near 36% including other income and operating margin near 27.8-27.9%, down from Q4 on lower FX gain (INR25 crore vs INR65 crore), a weaker product mix, and trial and freight costs booked to other expenses. Management kept the NGDS (new generation discharge system) and South America mining conversion trials as the core focus, but declined to share trial outcomes or FY27 volume guidance. Capex guidance was raised to INR350-400 crore for FY27, mainly for a corporate campus land and building.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~60,000 tons in Q1 FY26; down ~5,400 tons QoQ per analyst question (not disputed)
Transcript states 'INR44 crores, INR24 crores' which is garbled; figure as read by analyst context not confirmed
Q4 PAT was higher, aided by a tax refund in Q4; tax rate expected to normalise to 21.5-22% (management also said about 23% for Q1)

financial_highlights.value: Export benefits INR14.78 crore; treasury income INR85.35 crore; FX gain about INR25 crore; total other income about INR124 crore
financial_highlights.change: FX gain down from about INR65 crore in Q4
Reported margin about 36%, down from about 39% in Q4 (per management comparison)
Described by management as its consistent range

segments.name: Grinding media and liners (mining and cement)
segments.commentary: Management said product mix was less favourable in Q1 versus Q4 with fewer high-value castings; grinding media (about 75%) and castings (about 25%) cited as an illustrative mix. High-chrome supply to a Chile order is running at about 3,000-3,500 tons per quarter.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 volume guidance given; management asked investors to wait one more quarter for specific growth guidance, and declined to confirm 280,000-290,000 tons.
No margin guidance; prior operating margin guidance of 20-22% reiterated as the company's stated range, with Q1 said to be above it.
Realisation guidance of INR160-165 per ton was described as indicative, set about a year and a half ago; management declined to revise it.

FY27 capex now expected at minimum INR350-400 crore (up from about INR130 crore), with exact figure to come in Q2: about INR170-200 crore for a new corporate campus plot and INR50-100 crore for additional land for expansion.
Management said it will hold higher cash for at least a few more quarters before considering capital distribution options.
capex_capacity: Current capacity about 430,000-440,000 tons per year; management said current capacity can reach about 300,000-350,000 tons at 70-75% utilisation.
Q1 capex about INR50 crore: about INR30 crore on hybrid solar-wind renewable project (now operational) and about INR20 crore on maintenance and debottlenecking.

Overseas plants: Ghana site identified and government dialogue ongoing; China has a small lab facility and infrastructure plans are in slow mode. India remains the base for now; South America manufacturing not pursued yet.
demand_pricing: South America is the priority market: management cited about 1-1.5 million tons of addressable opportunity across gold, copper and iron, with South America alone potentially 300,000-400,000 tons for AIA.
Chinese players are gaining share in forged grinding media (about 20 forging companies), but management said high-chrome custom solutions remain limited to few companies.
Freight about USD 8,000-9,000 per container, elevated but easing; transshipment port congestion is a current constraint. Raw materials such as ferrochrome are elevated, with pass-through in pricing.

Realisations rose QoQ, which management attributed to a combination of product mix, freight and raw material pass-through, rupee movement and other factors; management said higher realisation does not mean higher margin.

qa_highlights.question: Has the second South America mine trial concluded, and what was the outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share specifics; trials are ongoing and an outcome may take longer than expected due to technicalities.

qa_highlights.question: Is the QoQ volume decline a timing issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes are tracked annually, and the decline reflects timing, product mix and order execution cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 volumes reach 280,000-290,000 tons and what about Peru copper and Ghana gold trials?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance; growth guidance deferred to next quarter. Management said it has no specific answer on crossing 280,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Is NGDS a standalone product and what is its TAM and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: NGDS will be sold only as part of a package with grinding media and liners, priced per kg; no standalone TAM was given. Overall lining-system opportunity is about 2-2.5 million tons, narrowing to about 1-1.5 million tons in gold, copper and iron.

qa_highlights.question: Should realisation guidance be revised above INR165 per ton given Q1 levels near INR180?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to revise; the INR160-165 range was indicative and reflects several moving factors including dollar, ferrochrome, scrap and competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from Q4 to Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Three factors: FX gain fell to INR25 crore from INR65 crore, weaker value-added product mix, and higher trial and freight costs booked in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Will a plant in South America fast-track scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for now; the immediate constraint is customer trial acceptance, not supply. Local manufacturing requires an ecosystem, and India remains the base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Chile high-chrome order?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply is going well at about 3,000-3,500 tons per quarter, with no explicit confirmation of further adjacent-mine enquiries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex raised to INR350-400 crore, including INR170-200 crore for a corporate campus; cash of about INR4,500-5,000 crore is being held for at least a few more quarters.

risks_watch: Outcome of South America mine trials (NGDS and high-chrome conversions) remains undisclosed and timing is uncertain.
Margin pressure from freight, raw material costs and product mix; FX gain has fallen sharply QoQ.
Chinese competition in forged media and potential spread into high-chrome.
Capital allocation: about INR4,500-5,000 crore cash, with no near-term buyback or dividend decision.
Overseas plant plans (Ghana, China) are slowed, with no timeline.
532683|2026-06.management_tone: Confident about long-term strategy but deliberately cautious on near-term numbers: management refused to share trial outcomes, volume guidance, or realisation revisions, and repeatedly deferred specifics to future quarters.

532689|2026-06.headline: PVR INOX Q1 FY27 PAT of INR71 crore vs loss of INR34 crore a year ago; net cash of INR80 crore at June 30, 2026.
532689|2026-06.overview: Revenue on an Ind AS 116 adjusted basis rose 12% YoY to INR1,642 crore, with EBITDA nearly doubling to INR230 crore at a 14% margin. Footfalls rose 8% to 36.6 million, with ATP at INR273 (+8%) and SPH at INR161 (+9%). The company turned net cash of INR80 crore, and management said growth can now be funded from internal cash flows. No new screens opened in Q1 because completed sites were awaiting regulatory licences; openings are expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR34 crore in Q1 FY26
company describes it as debt-free; peak debt cited as INR1,450 crore
up from about 63-64%; convenience fee income +29% YoY

segments.name: Exhibition (cinemas)
segments.commentary: Footfalls 36.6 million (+8%), ATP INR273 (+8%), SPH INR161 (+9%). Premium formats are 16% of the circuit (IMAX, 4DX, ICE, ScreenX, recliners, Insignia, Director's Cut, LUXE).

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Management said ad revenue is still below its post-COVID peak and expects about a year to fully recover. Growth is expected to pick up in Q3 and Q4 with large titles; it did not give a figure.

segments.name: Alternate content and F&B
segments.commentary: Alternate content (live sports, concerts, events) ATP is about INR409; artist cost ranges from 35% to 65-70% of ticket. Food court JV with Devyani has 3 outlets open, with more in the pipeline. Web and app monetisation launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

guidance_outlook: Gross screen additions of 90-100 in FY27 (about 80 net after closures); Q1 had no openings and few closures are expected for the rest of the year.
FY27 capex now about INR350 crore, down from the earlier INR400 crore, including the food court JV and a higher renovation share.
Film hire cost guided at 45% to 45.5% of revenue for full-year FY27; F&B COGS expected to fall YoY.
Near-term target is a return to pre-COVID ROCE levels; no FCF target was given.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 expansion: about 300 cities identified, first opening in Muzaffarpur shortly, with asset-light and FOCO models; growth expected to accelerate from FY28.
Management expects margins of pre-COVID levels even at 27-28% occupancy.
capex_capacity: Screen count about 1,790 today, up from about 1,650 at the merger; about 120 net screens added over the last 4 years.
FY27 screen openings were held back by pending regulatory licences; openings expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.
Closed screens in Q1 were loss-making and more than 18-20 years old; bulk of FY27 closures done in Q1.
Around 600 screens are in South India; southern concentration is about 34%, according to an analyst's estimate.
Asset-light and FOCO models are the main route for new sites; the 15 million sq ft of leased space is being offered for sublease where it is not needed.
demand_pricing: India box office grew 20% YoY in Q1 FY27 across metros, Tier 2 and Tier 3, and across languages.
North America box office was up 14% YoY at $4.8 billion in H1 2026, per management.
Hollywood share of box office is about 60% overall, about 50% for big films, and up to 80-90% for mid and smaller films.
ATP growth was driven by dynamic pricing plus premium mix; discounts are offered on Tuesdays, morning shows and front seats.

Management sees no INR500 crore-plus film so far in the year, but says mid-scale films are performing; it views the upcoming slate (Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic, Avengers: Doomsday, Dune: Part Three) as strong.
Management said the occupancy trend is recovering as release windows return to 8 weeks, but did not disclose a current occupancy figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the screen closures and asset-light mix affecting the FY27 screen and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross screen additions are still 90-100 and net additions about 80. Capex is now about INR350 crore versus INR400 crore earlier, because FOCO and capital-light demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revisit asset-light models now that it is net cash, and is more real estate monetisation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset-light and FOCO will continue and will not limit growth of 100-120 screens a year. Capital will be deployed where needed without borrowing. Real estate monetisation is not planned at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why have footfalls stayed flat at 14-15 crore over rolling 12 months despite southern screen additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the southern skew reflects where opportunities are; 150 million admissions last year was the post-COVID high. It said occupancy is recovering and that margins at 27-28% occupancy can match pre-COVID levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 FCF target and what is the plan for surplus cash, including buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Sharma said there is no FCF target. The immediate goal is pre-COVID ROCE. Shareholder returns, including buyback, are being evaluated and will be disclosed when the Board decides.

qa_highlights.question: What are the unit economics of properties on the capital-light models?
qa_highlights.answer: Properties take 12-18 months to mature. FY24 and FY25 vintages are at margins above company level, and first-vintage performance will be shared by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did online penetration rise and what is the app/web monetisation revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Online penetration rose to about 69% on marketing and content mix. Growth will slow from here. The app/web ad product launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did film hire and COGS fall about 200 bps YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Film hire fell because Dhurandhar was in its lower-rate third and fourth weeks, and there was no mega-blockbuster to trigger bonus payouts. F&B COGS have fallen YoY for two years.

risks_watch: Release calendar: no INR500 crore-plus film so far in FY27; the slate depends on Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic and Hollywood tentpoles.
Licence delays pushed Q1 openings into Q2 and Q3; the 90-100 gross screen target depends on this bunching.
Advertising has not yet recovered to post-COVID levels; management expects about another year.
Online penetration growth is slowing near 70%, so convenience fee growth will depend on ATP and admits.
Capital allocation is undecided: buyback or other shareholder returns may be announced, and the company says it is evaluating all options.
Occupancy is still below pre-COVID levels; management has not disclosed a figure.

544599|2026-06.headline: Studds Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.7% to INR169.7 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% on a styrene-driven raw material spike; management guides 14-15% in Q2.

EBITDA was INR19.6 crores (11.5% margin) and PAT INR12.3 crores (7.2% margin), hit by a sharp rise in styrene-based raw material prices (about 600 bps of margin impact) and manpower costs (about 200 bps, from a Haryana minimum wage hike). Management said effective price realisation was about 5% in Q1, with a full ~9% price increase expected from Q2 as older-price orders roll off. Growth initiatives include 1.5 million helmets of new capacity, Decathlon, an Italian subsidiary and new products.

segments.name: Domestic STUDDS (helmets)
