segments.name: SMK (premium)
segments.commentary: Export EBITDA on SMK was described as about 30-35%. SMK range is INR4,000 to INR15,000 helmets.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 21% of Q1 revenue; target is closer to 30%. Export orders executed in Q1 were contracted before the price rise; new orders are booked at revised prices.

segments.name: Bicycle helmets (Decathlon)
segments.commentary: Bicycle helmet ASPs are about 15-20% below motorcycle helmets. Commercial production expected from October 2026, with Decathlon working like an OEM relationship.

segments.name: Bluetooth and riding jackets (new)
segments.commentary: Management expects INR15-20 crores of revenue from these two categories in FY27. Some products are made in-house and some by contract manufacturers.

segments.name: Italian subsidiary
segments.commentary: Dealer-direct entry planned in Italy, Germany and France. Expected losses of about INR2-3 crores in FY27 and about INR2 crores in FY28; revenue guidance EUR100-125k in FY27 and about EUR1 million in FY28. Management said profits start from year 3, with 10-12% EBITDA margin cited.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 14-15%; normalised 18-20% run rate by Q4 FY27, subject to stable raw material prices.
FY27 revenue growth of mid-teens guided earlier; volume growth now expected at about 10% with 7-8% blended realisation (management said high-teens revenue growth on last call).
Full ~9% price increase (on FY26 base) expected to be reflected from Q2; Q2 realisation expected at 8-9% for OEM/CSD/CPC channels.
Styrene-based raw material cost impact expected to soften to about 300 bps in Q2 from 600 bps in Q1; management expects Q3 and Q4 to improve further.
FY28 standalone guidance: volume growth 13-14% and price realisation 3-4%, implying mid-to-high teens growth (management said this excludes the Italian subsidiary).
At current styrene levels (~INR185 weighted average), PAT margin expected at about 11.5-12%, versus about 13% earlier; management expects a return to FY26 levels by Q4 FY27.
Export mix rising toward 30% could add 200-300 bps to PAT margin, per management's rough estimate.
Total capex of INR76 crores to 30 June 2026 plus INR10 crores of vendor advances; FY27 capex budget INR58 crores (INR7.5 crores spent in Q1); FY28 plan INR31 crores.

financial_highlights.change: volume growth ~8.5% YoY (1.4 lakh units on 17.56 lakh base)

qa_highlights.question: Is EMOSS likely to be wound up, as the earlier Europe subsidiary was?

Execution of the INR1,500 crore order book over four to five years and the new pipeline.

522205|2026-06.headline: Praj Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR 116.1 mn (vs INR 53.4 mn) on INR 7.16 bn revenue, with order intake of INR 10 bn and backlog of INR 45.9 bn.

segments.commentary: 22% of revenue and 28% of order intake. Praj GenX won a hyperscale data-center modular supply framework with a minimum of about USD 50 mn over 2.5 years; management said booking is phased, not the full INR 500 crore headline.

Ethanol-to-SAF detailed engineering order from an international customer, following a completed basic engineering order last quarter.

Dr. Pramod Chaudhari Centre of Excellence for Advanced Bioeconomy inaugurated at SPPU on August 10, 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Collections and execution: why was bioenergy revenue (INR 474 crore) low versus the opening order book?

Collections are lagging because of slow backlog conversion; management is working on it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin expand, and will RM and site expenses weigh on margins?

qa_highlights.question: Praj GenX breakeven timing and order book share?

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports decline YoY while domestic revenue rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export revenue timing depends on order entry and execution cycles; a large export order batch was booked in Q1 with execution starting around Q3 after engineering. International share of orders was 40-43% in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory over the next decade and service mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said services margins are higher than project margins and the mix shift (domestic/international, services/projects, new biofuels) is the route to better margins. Current investments in GenX, R&D and new ventures are absorbing margin.

qa_highlights.question: Bio-isobutanol mandate timing and biomaterials (bio-bitumen, PLA)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the timing of any diesel blending mandate is unknown, but Praj is technology-ready. Lactic acid technology for PLA exists; co-product progress is expected by fiscal year-end.

524332|2026-06.headline: BCL Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore (10.5% margin) despite revenue falling to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore.
524332|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue fell to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore, mainly due to closure of the edible oil unit and exit from packaged oil. EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore, with margin up 370 bps to 10.5%, and PAT rose 6% to INR 36 crore (5.7% margin). Distillery EBITDA margin improved to 12.41%, while ENA realisations fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. A fire at a 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol tank on 19 June 2026 shut that plant temporarily; management said insurance recovery is virtually certain and no net loss was booked. Management also completed the acquisition of the remaining 25% of Svaksha Distillery and reduced working capital borrowings, but deferred the Fatehabad 250 KLPD project and the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 820 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)
from 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Profit on sale of fixed assets (oil exit)

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 12.41% in Q1 FY27 versus 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26. ENA volume rose to 19,376 KL from 7,960 KL YoY, but ENA realisation fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. The 115 TPH paddy straw boiler meets 100% of steam and power needs.

segments.name: Country liquor (PML)
segments.commentary: Sold 6,37,993 boxes, up 42% QoQ and 46% YoY. Punjab Raspberry launched in Q4 FY26 and Jamun Vodka in July 2026. Management targets 30 lakh cases this year out of a market of about 1.25 crore cases per annum in Punjab.

segments.name: Edible oil / packaged oil (exited)
segments.commentary: Exit completed, including closure of the Bathinda oil and vanaspati unit. Soft oil refinery and trading continue as legacy operations. Revenue decline was mainly from this exit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the 200 KLPD Bathinda plant to restart in about 15 days from the call, and that the new 150 KLPD Bathinda unit (commissioned in early July 2026) will substantially offset the lost volume.
Order book described as full for about the next three months, supported by OMC allocation of about 4.5 crore litres from a Supreme Court order covering until November.
Management guided to a sustained distillery/overall margin range of about 10% to 12%, while noting raw material and fuel price volatility.
Working capital limit to be reduced by INR 50 crore in August 2026; management aims to bring working capital utilisation towards zero over about 1.5 years.
No share buyback planned for now. Debt will rise only if a new capex project is started.
capex_capacity: Svaksha Distillery (350 KLPD, Kharagpur, West Bengal) became wholly owned on 30 June 2026 after the remaining 25% stake was acquired.
Newly added 150 KLPD Bathinda unit began commercial trials at end-June 2026 and was commissioned in the first half of July 2026.
200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol plant shut after the 19 June 2026 fire; the tank was holding about 90,000 litres at the time and is under repair.
Fatehabad 250 KLPD grain-based plant: orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash; machinery orders are reportedly finalised and management is waiting before starting construction.
Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project is on hold because biodiesel prices are not remunerative. Goyal Distillery 250 KLPD project is on hold pending industry clarity.
Malt plant is at conceptualisation stage with no timeline. IMFL entry targeted for next year, with the company still working on it.
Bio-CBG is under active evaluation (Haryana policy noted), with paddy straw feedstock seen as tricky. The company is not making biodiesel.
demand_pricing: ENA and private ethanol supply face price pressure from oversupply. Average private ethanol price is about INR 58/litre ex-factory, mainly to Reliance.

Management said maize-based ethanol to OMCs is profitable, while FCI-rice-based ethanol is near cost. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same. Blended average EBITDA is about 12%, roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA.
Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter. Current maize price is about INR 25/kg, and management said ENA prices have been revised upwards.
DDGS prices have eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for both maize and rice based.

544122|2026-06.headline: Entero Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore and EBITDA margin reached 5.0%, already meeting full-year FY27 margin guidance.
544122|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore (40% like-for-like), with organic growth of 17.8% reported and 19.6% like-for-like versus an underlying pharma market growth of 13.8%. Gross margin expanded 147 bps to 11.4% and EBITDA margin expanded 143 bps to 5.0%, with EBITDA up 94% YoY. PAT rose 72% YoY to INR52 crore, but PAT attributable to owners was INR38 crore (up 37%) after INR14 crore of non-controlling interest. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~23% revenue growth ex-acquisitions, 5% EBITDA margin and 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion, and said no major acquisitions are planned in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: entirely calendarisation of prior-year acquisitions; no new acquisitions in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR14 crore (~27% of PBT before minority interest)
financial_highlights.change: Q4 was about INR17 crore per the call

segments.name: Core pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Majority of business is demand fulfilment with lower gross margins; margin gains attributed to scale-driven procurement. Low-margin sub-distribution accounts exited, which reduced reported growth by about 2.5%.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Organic MedTech revenue on track to exceed INR1,000 crore in FY27 and carries higher gross and EBITDA margins than core pharma. Management said the business plays a demand-generation role, not only fulfilment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: consolidated revenue growth of ~23% YoY excluding new acquisitions (about 11-12 points from calendarisation of prior acquisitions, rest organic).
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 5% maintained; management aspires to improve further and said H2 could beat guidance depending on H1 performance.
EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion of 50% on an annual basis; OCF is after working capital changes.
FY27 effective tax rate guidance of 22.5%; FY28 guidance to be given near FY27 close.
Interest cost expected to stay broadly in the same range as Q1 for the rest of the year.
Employee cost increments fell mainly in Q1 (effective 1 April); no major increase expected thereafter.

Medium-term: management said it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and modelling 20% is a safe assumption; ROCE of 25-30% was cited as possible in that period; internal aspiration EBITDA margin above 6%.
No revision to working capital days guidance; management will review after H1.
capex_capacity: Platform: 138 warehouses across 475 districts in 19 states; 72,000+ retail customers, 2,300+ hospital customers, 83,400+ SKUs, 3,000+ manufacturer relationships.
Depreciation: Q1 level expected to be the going-forward run-rate, subject to any major new capex; Q4 included depreciation on certain machines given to customers.
No major acquisitions planned for FY27, though a pipeline exists; a small Andhra Pradesh surgical consumables deal (with Sai Pharma) was completed and is immaterial to revenue.
Around INR200 crore of debt was taken for the last acquisition, disbursed late Jan/early Feb 2026.
demand_pricing: IPM growth has moved to double digits in the last two quarters (earlier 7-9%), driven mainly by volume; management could not isolate a specific cause.
Management said it cannot forecast future IPM growth and built its organic forecast on a lower industry growth assumption.
Growth above market is attributed to wallet share gains from better fill rates, product availability, range and more principal collaborations.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 FY26 through preponed government/diagnostic PPP billing, which made the sequential inorganic contribution look lower.
Management said MedTech has limited distributor competition and offers more scope for demand-generation contracts with higher gross margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for the next 3-5 years without acquisitions, and what ROCE is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and sees ROCE of 25-30% possible at the end of that period.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the minority interest exist and when will the call options on it be exercised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said call options were agreed at deal signing at a valuation multiple matching the original acquisition, with exercise windows of 2-5 years; the minority is reinvested rather than paid out. Not all options fall due this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the sequential inorganic revenue contribution decline from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Q1 government project revenue was billed early in Q4 FY26 because of budget timing, so Q1 had a high base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 one-off items recurring in other opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only part of the INR11.5 crore one-offs sat in other expenses; run-rate other expenses of about INR55 crore are expected to be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 5% EBITDA margin be a floor for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 5% for the full year but said it targets quarter-on-quarter improvement and may revise guidance after H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did minority interest fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minority share depends on subsidiary profit; Q4 had a revenue preponement at one subsidiary that boosted its profit share (INR17 crore in Q4 vs INR14 crore in Q1).

risks_watch: Growth in IPM has been unusually strong for two quarters and management cannot explain the cause, so sustainability is uncertain.
Non-controlling interest is about 27% of PBT and call-option buyouts (2-5 year horizon) will need funding, possibly from parent or subsidiary cash.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 through government billing timing, so quarterly comparisons may be distorted.
Quarterly OCF is not disclosed; balance-sheet items (gross debt, net debt, OCF) will be given only at half-year and full-year, in September and March.
Interest cost is expected to stay at the Q1 run-rate after the INR200 crore debt drawdown.
Further exits of low-margin sub-distribution businesses could reduce reported growth again (about 2.5% impact in Q1).
544122|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top line and margins, and clear on the strategy to consolidate and grow organically. Management was evasive on IPM growth drivers, on the quantum of OCF and net debt, and on non-controlling interest funding.

500730|2026-06.headline: NOCIL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs 403 crore and EBITDA margin hit 11.2%, but volumes fell 3% QoQ on supply constraints.
500730|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 403 crore, up 20% YoY and 22% QoQ, with volumes up 9% YoY but down 3% QoQ. Management attributed the sequential volume dip to utility and logistics constraints linked to the geopolitical situation, which pushed some orders into later quarters. EBITDA rose to Rs 45 crore (11.2% margin) and PAT to Rs 28 crore, though management described several conversion-cost items as one-offs. Anti-dumping duty on Sulphonamides (CBS and NS) was approved on 20 June 2026, while the Pilflex 13 duty awaits Government approval. FY27 guidance was set at revenue of Rs 1,400-1,600 crore and EBITDA around 10%.

financial_highlights.change: +20% YoY (from Rs 336 crore); +22% QoQ (from Rs 330 crore)
+48% YoY (from Rs 31 crore); +115% QoQ (from Rs 21 crore)
+60% YoY (from Rs 23 crore); +77% QoQ (from Rs 21 crore)
+61% YoY (from Rs 17 crore); +63% QoQ (from Rs 17 crore)

segments.name: Tyre chemicals (domestic)
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew double digits YoY, supported by GST 2.0 and healthy tyre replacement and OEM demand. Management said the 9% volume growth skewed towards tyres.

segments.name: Non-tyre chemicals
segments.commentary: Temporary demand contraction in the quarter from lower production at smaller customers due to input cost spikes, contract labour shortages and LPG shortages. Management expects recovery.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export volumes grew single digits YoY on conversion of ongoing customer engagements. Exports were about 33% of Q1 volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at Rs 1,400-1,600 crore, based on current pricing environment.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at around 10%, with some quarterly adjustments expected.
FY27 volume growth assumed at around 10% YoY; management said it has not scaled this down.
Management expects deferred volumes to be recovered in coming quarters.
Realisations expected to moderate from Q1 levels, though not all of the price gains will reverse.

TDQ plant at Dahej: first revenues expected this year, starting with non-tyre customers, with tyre approvals following over the next couple of quarters. Management expects volumes to start trickling in Q4 FY27 and to build more in Q1 FY28.
Export share expected to rise towards 40-45% by FY28-29 (directional).
capex_capacity: New TDQ plant at Dahej in trial production with samples sent to customers; approval cycle typically 6-8 months, sometimes shorter.
Rs 130 crore investment at Dahej progressing on schedule despite war-related disruption.
Specialty segment expansion is expected to add at least 5-10% to the top line over one to two years, from the current ~15% share (per management).
demand_pricing: Anti-dumping duty on Sulphonamides (CBS and NS) notified 20 June 2026; no realisation gain booked in Q1 as the effect depends on how much importers absorb.
DGTR issued a positive final recommendation on Pilflex 13 in June 2026; the Central Government decision is pending, with an outcome expected around end-September.
ADD-covered product lines are about 25-30% of top line excluding TDQ, if Pilflex 13 is also imposed (per management).

Realisation growth implied by guidance is about 30-40%, driven by price increases, product mix, better domestic accelerator pricing and operating leverage. Management flagged moderation from Q1 levels.

Antioxidant imports and dumping remain a concern; management said import influx has not risen significantly after the ADD changes. Chinese yuan and INR movements have had no significant impact so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA run rate sustainable, and what are the one-off conversion cost items?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to around 10% EBITDA for FY27. Conversion cost rose from Rs 110 crore to Rs 130 crore QoQ due to freight, CSR spend, utility cost from gas constraints, plant maintenance, and a Rs 45 crore stock change. Management called some items one-offs, quantified only as 'a few crores' of maintenance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 volume growth guidance (around 10%) below expectations of double-digit export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact has been mainly in non-tyre and not in tyre, and it has not cut the 10% FY27 volume growth outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ADD benefit will flow to EBITDA, and what is the inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to quantify the ADD benefit. It did not provide an inventory gain estimate and will come back on that later.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 9% volume growth came from tyre and non-tyre?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was skewed towards tyres, with a lower contribution from non-tyre.

qa_highlights.question: Will the TDQ plant generate revenue this year, and at what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, revenue is expected this year. Non-tyre customers come first, followed by tyre companies over the next couple of quarters as approvals come through. No utilisation figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why might the Pilflex 13 ADD be approved this time when it was rejected in 2021?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Central Government has discretion, with a decision expected within about 90 days, possibly by end-September. It argued that domestic producers are under more stress now, so the case is stronger.

risks_watch: Central Government decision on Pilflex 13 ADD, expected around end-September; earlier 2021 DGTR recommendation was rejected.
Pass-through and sustainability of price gains: management expects moderation from Q1 realisation levels.
Antioxidant import pressure and falling YoY realisations, with no ADD approved on the antioxidant (TDQ) product.
Utility and gas availability, plus freight costs linked to the Middle East conflict, which may keep conversion costs high.
Pace of TDQ approvals by tyre customers, and whether Q4 FY27 volume reaches the 160-165 index level discussed by an analyst.
Raw material price volatility from the geopolitical situation.
Non-tyre demand recovery after temporary contraction.
500730|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the full-year outlook, but cautious on near-term costs and volumes. Management was evasive on quantifying ADD benefits, inventory gains, one-off costs and the Pilflex 13 outcome, and declined to comment on promoter pledging.

544403|2026-06.headline: ABLBL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore and EBITDA 14% to Rs 327 crore, with margin up 50 bps to 16%.
544403|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with EBITDA up 14% to Rs 327 crore and PAT up 21% to Rs 29 crore. Lifestyle Brands grew 10% to Rs 1,725 crore at an 18.5% EBITDA margin, while Emerging Brands grew 19% to Rs 332 crore at a 4.3% margin. Management attributed a modest demand moderation to adhik maas during the peak wedding period and a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2 that depressed wholesale growth to 5%. Gross margin contracted about 150 bps, which management attributed to channel mix and provisioning rather than raw material costs.

financial_highlights.change: Down ~150 bps YoY per analyst question; management called it marginally lower

segments.name: Lifestyle Brands
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,725 crore (+10% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 319 crore at 18.5% margin. Retail grew 10% with 7% LFL across almost 3,000 stores; e-commerce grew 23% group-wide and over 50% on the company's own platform.

segments.name: Emerging Brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 332 crore (+19% YoY), with retail LFL of 11% and e-commerce growth above 30%. Retail network crossed 400 stores; EBITDA margin 4.3%, up 240 bps.

segments.name: Channels (group)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 10% with 8% LFL, the seventh straight quarter of LFL growth. Wholesale grew 5% on primary billing, though underlying secondary growth was early double-digit.

guidance_outlook: Gross store additions of more than 300 in FY27, with net additions of 150-200 after closures of about 120-140 stores.
Cost inflation of 3-4% expected for Q2-Q3 FY27 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages; mostly to be offset by productivity and cost rationalisation, plus small price hikes.
Management expects Q1+Q2 wholesale primary billing to even out, with the Q1 shortfall moving into Q2.
Small-town retail (about 500 stores) is about 15-16% of retail revenue and is expected to exceed 20% of portfolio over the next three to four years.
Management aims for sustained double-digit growth and margin expansion; it expects retail to grow in early double digits.
Reebok revenue is about Rs 500 crore (from about Rs 250 crore at acquisition); management sees close to 20% long-term growth possible.
capex_capacity: Retail footprint of 3,362 stores (about 5 million sq ft) across more than 800 cities and towns at quarter end; more than 65 gross openings in Q1 (Aditya Bansal's question: 68 gross).
Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha; Karnataka concentration is limited.
Reebok has about 200 stores versus 500-700 for other premium brands, indicating a long retail runway.
Van Heusen Innerwear distribution is about 38,000-40,000 outlets; management expects roughly 20% network addition over the next couple of years.
Two Reebok factories still operate outside India pending BIS annual renewal; domestic sourcing is being built up.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand was broadly consistent with the prior-year trend; adhik maas caused modest moderation in the peak wedding period.
Wholesale grew 5%, with a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2; management says secondary was early double-digit.
Small-town stores grew over 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros; small-town growth has been double-digit for five consecutive quarters.
Price hikes were small and varied by brand and category, taken to offset input-cost increases; management says no meaningful apparel inflation is visible.
Marketing spend was about 3.5% of sales in Q1, down from last year because of IPL spend in the base quarter.
E-commerce profitability is said to be close to retail profitability, with growth now coming without deep discounting.
Quick commerce is small for the company; innerwear is the largest category there.
Casual wear share is rising by 2-3 percentage points a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why the divergence between primary and secondary sales in Lifestyle wholesale, and how will it evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: A 10-15 day festive timing shift moved primary billing into Q2; management expects Q1 and Q2 combined to be as strong as other channels.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 saw marginal to no cost pressure. Management expects 3-4% cost increase in Q2-Q3 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages, offset mainly by productivity and some price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 150 bps gross margin contraction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited channel mix and slightly higher inventory-age provisioning, not raw material costs, and said the effect is not material and will even out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to Karnataka minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Garmenting was never part of the notified hike, which is under High Court challenge. Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

qa_highlights.question: How are the net store adds and LFL growth reconciled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to more than 300 gross and 150-200 net additions in FY27 after 120-140 closures; network growth of 5-6% plus 7-8% LFL supports early double-digit retail growth.

qa_highlights.question: How do small-town and Tier 1 growth compare, and how is Gen-Z targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Tier 3-4 is growing above 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros. Gen-Z is served through sub-brands and collections (for example Peter England's Vybe), with no share figures disclosed.

risks_watch: Wholesale growth of 5% and gross margin contraction of about 150 bps in Q1; watch whether the festive shift reverses in Q2.
3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3 and the wage-regulation outcome in Karnataka at the High Court.
Consumer wallet pressure from inflation; management says it has seen no meaningful demand shift so far but is cautious about H2.
Reebok BIS certification risk on imports from factories outside India, renewed annually.
Net store additions of 150-200 against a gross plan above 300; watch LFL sustainability through closures.

500078|2026-06.headline: Oriental Aromatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to Rs 260 crore and EBITDA margin recovered to 7.62% sequentially, though still below 8.01% a year ago.
500078|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 260 crore, up around 15% YoY but down 8% QoQ, with total sales volume up 22% and production up 18% YoY. EBITDA was Rs 19.8 crore (7.62% margin), up from 6.89% in Q4 FY26 but down from 8.01% in Q1 FY26 on higher raw material costs. PAT was Rs 2.51 crore versus Rs 3.98 crore in Q4 and Rs 0.5 crore a year ago. Mahad (Specialty Aroma Ingredients) remains under-utilised at 50-60% and is still weighing on profitability, with inventory building there. Management guided to 10-15% sales growth over the next year.

segments.name: Fragrance and Flavors (Ambarnath)

segments.name: Specialty Aroma Ingredients (incl. Mahad)
segments.commentary: Healthy YoY growth in production and sales volume, but Asian capacity additions are pressuring selling prices. Mahad utilisation is 50-60%, with target of 75-80% for EBITDA breakeven; Mahad revenue is about Rs 3 crore per quarter per an analyst's calculation (not disputed by management).

segments.name: Camphor and Terpene Chemicals
segments.commentary: Strong YoY volume growth in the quarter, but domestic camphor faces structural overcapacity. Management said Indian camphor prices rose by a substantial double-digit percentage, driven by alpha-pinene up roughly 70-80% over five months.

guidance_outlook: Near-term goal of 10-15% sales growth over the next one year.
Mahad targeted to reach 75-80% utilisation, at which point management expects it to become EBITDA positive; no timeline given beyond 'next few quarters'.
Effective tax rate of about 25% for FY27 (management said same for FY28 was not specified).
Export share expected to stay in the same range (around 33-35%).
No margin guidance given; management said margin outlook is 'very fluid' given raw material and geopolitical uncertainty.
Priority is maximising utilisation of existing assets before major expansion capex.

Fragrance compounding facility has substantial headroom to increase production.

Specialty aroma commercialisation cycles take 500-1,000 days, per management.
demand_pricing: Specialty Aroma Ingredients: buyer's market with Asian (mainly China) capacity additions pressuring prices; pass-through achieved where possible, with step-up pass-through to cover FX and raw material costs.

Alpha-pinene (imported, USD-priced) up roughly 70-80% over five months and still firm; petro-based inputs volatile.
Premiumisation in personal care, home care and fine fragrances cited as intact long-term trend.
R&D spend around 2-2.5% of sales, per CFO.

qa_highlights.question: What is current utilisation for the overall business and Mahad, and what revenue potential exists at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahad is at 50-60% utilisation; most other plants at 85-90%. Management guided to 10-15% sales growth over the next year and did not give a long-term revenue number.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and raw material costs evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast margins, calling the outlook 'fluid'. Alpha-pinene-based raw materials will stay expensive; petro-based inputs are seesawing.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth of 22% versus revenue of 15%: what drove the realisation dip, and where do realisations go?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to raw material-driven price increases and customers pulling forward allocated volumes. It declined to share division-level numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate for FY27 and FY28?

qa_highlights.question: Export contribution this quarter?

qa_highlights.question: Mahad revenue and whether production is being inventorised?

Mahad utilisation at 50-60% with inventory build-up; a meaningful scale-up timeline was not provided.
Asian capacity additions (especially China) keep pressure on Specialty Aroma and camphor pricing.

542752|2026-06.headline: Affle 3i Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.4% y-o-y to INR 7.47 billion with EBITDA of INR 1.68 billion (22.4% margin), though management flagged RMG and FinTech headwinds.

EBITDA rose 20% y-o-y to INR 1.68 billion with margin at 22.4%, and PAT grew 21.7% y-o-y to INR 1.28 billion. Management said over 95% of revenue grew above 25% y-o-y after adjusting for regulatory and macro headwinds in RMG and some FinTech categories. Operating cash flow to PAT was weak in the quarter, which management attributed to timing of collections after a strong March 2026. The company reiterated a 10x growth plan with a larger acquisition targeted to close by early 2027.

financial_highlights.change: +20% y-o-y; +4% q-o-q; margin up from 22.3% in Q4
Up INR 2.3 million q-o-q on business promotion in Developed Markets

financial_highlights.value: About 41% (per analyst question; not disputed by management)
financial_highlights.change: Management expects about 80-85% OCF to PAT by Q3

segments.name: India and Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Grew 20.2% y-o-y and 4% q-o-q, contributing 72.2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management called it the anchor of growth and sees no challenge to sustained growth.

segments.name: Developed Markets
segments.commentary: Grew 20.7% y-o-y and about 1% q-o-q, contributing 27.8% of revenue. Management targets at least 20% growth here and says the ex-currency growth an analyst estimated at 11-12% is not the right read.

guidance_outlook: Management models about 20% organic growth on a medium-term basis, with internal planning at 25%.
Combined entity including the larger M&A is expected to keep growing at least 20%, with accretive EPS and cash flow.
Larger M&A: third-party due diligence under way; closing targeted by early 2027.
AdColony assets: aim to activate over 100,000 mobile apps to reach over 500 million connected devices in Developed Markets within this year, via existing teams and SDK integrations.
Management expects better margin expansion within FY27, especially in Developed Markets.
OCF to PAT expected to normalise in Q2, reaching about 80-85% by Q3 FY27.
10x growth target to be achieved in about five years; next milestone of USD 1 billion revenue cited as a few years away.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed. The business is asset-light, CPCU-based.
AdColony asset acquisition is described as complete; management said it requires no significant new capital.
Management said the company has raised the appropriate funding for the larger M&A, with no amount disclosed.
Bobble investment of INR 136 crore: no impairment taken; management said it will be tested once the NCLT appeal is decided.
demand_pricing: RMG (gaming/category G) remains in a recovery phase after regulatory and macro headwinds; FinTech also saw some impact.
Category E and F are robust; category H (healthcare, hospitality) is seeing momentum. In Developed Markets, categories E and G are currently stronger than F and H.
Average CPCU rate is above INR 60; currency-adjusted pricing passed some benefit to advertisers, weighing on margin in the short term.
Management said no material USD volatility in Q1, unlike Q4, when a steep USD move raised inventory cost. Q1 was flat sequentially on this front.

Direct customers contributed about 79% of revenue in Q1 versus about 74% in FY26; management said it does not prefer direct or agency billing and that 100% of business has direct advertiser integration.

qa_highlights.question: Which markets saw the negative impact, and can growth exceed 25% annualised in a normal environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RMG (no longer a contributor this year) and some FinTech and categories were hit. Adjusted, 95% of revenue grew over 25%; management did not commit to timing for 100% of business.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin trend and recovery timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the pressure to currency-adjusted CPCU pass-through and Developed Markets investment, and pointed to AdColony and margin expansion within FY27. No specific margin figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was OCF to EBITDA weak (about 41%)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kapil Bhutani said about INR 40-45 crore of collections were pulled into March 2026 ahead of year-end, leaving fewer receivables to collect; normalisation expected in Q2 and Q3, with about 80-85% OCF to PAT by Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Currency impact on growth and costs?
qa_highlights.answer: About 72% of business is India and Emerging Markets with cross-currency ROI commitments; only about 20% of US business is USD-to-USD. Q1 USD movement was flat sequentially versus a sharp Q4 spike.

qa_highlights.question: Developed Markets CPCU unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Developed Markets are easier on unit economics than Emerging Markets, with traffic volume about 5x lower for a given revenue. No exact CPCU or margin figures were given.

qa_highlights.question: Bobble write-down risk (INR 136 crore investment)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bobble is a valuable asset with 15-18 million active users, is contesting insolvency with appeals and inspection-rights orders, and will decide on next steps in coming quarters. CFO said no reliable basis for permanent impairment yet; test to follow NCLT appeal ruling.

risks_watch: Regulatory and macro headwinds in RMG and FinTech may persist; management gave no timeline for full recovery.
Gross margin pressure from currency-adjusted CPCU pass-through and Developed Markets investment; no quantified target.
Working-capital and OCF conversion: Q1 OCF to EBITDA was weak; watch for normalisation to 80-85% OCF to PAT by Q3.
Larger M&A (early 2027 close): size, valuation, margin profile and funding not disclosed; management said it will be accretive.
Bobble: INR 136 crore investment is under insolvency; impairment decision deferred pending NCLT appeal.
AdColony rollout: achieving 100,000 app activations and 500 million devices in Developed Markets this year is unquantified in revenue terms.
542752|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term 10x growth, Developed Markets and AI, but cautious and vague on specifics. Management avoided quantifying margin targets, M&A size or CPCU economics, and was defensive on the Bobble write-down question, citing legal proceedings.

532906|2026-06.headline: Maan Aluminium Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR232 crore and EBITDA to INR7 crore, with margin near 3%.
532906|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR232 crore, up 10% YoY from INR211 crore but down from INR255 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA rose to INR7 crore from INR5 crore sequentially, with margin about 3% versus about 2%, and PAT was about INR3 crore (EPS INR0.52 vs INR0.29). Management said exports fell to about 45% of manufacturing revenue (from 60-70% earlier) due to duties, and freight and Middle East shipping disruption continue to weigh on volumes and costs. Capex of about INR166 crore over three years is planned, with Dewas precision tubing and Pithampur Italian press ramp-up the key near-term items.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Q1 manufacturing turnover above INR70 crore with about 40% exports (management also cited ~45% export share of manufacturing revenue in prepared remarks). Production about 1,558 MT against 24,000 MT extrusion capacity. Anodizing utilisation ~45-50% and machining ~55%.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Described as opportunistic and pass-through; the remainder of the INR232 crore revenue (about INR160 crore implied) comes from trading. Management expects trading to decline as manufacturing mix rises.

guidance_outlook: Volumes expected to stay flattish QoQ and for FY27; ramp-up possibly toward end of FY27 or start of FY28.
Manufacturing revenue guided flattish; management would be 'okay' with FY26 level of ~INR300 crore manufacturing top line.
Pithampur Italian press: management targets ~35%/50%/75% ramp in a three-year plan; currently ~25% ramp-up; significant contribution expected by mid-FY28.
Dewas aluminium precision tubing plant: online targeted within 6-8 months, before mid-FY28 (no firm date given); capex mostly in H2 FY27.
Recovery of gas/energy cost increases: about 50% passed to customers over last two quarters, balance expected to be recovered in one to two quarters as contracts renew.
Management said no new debt planned for capex; company is deleveraging and has sufficient cash. Employee expenses expected not to rise materially as technical team is already hired.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity: foundry 12,000 TPA; extrusion 24,000 TPA; anodizing 3,600 TPA; machining 1,400 TPA.
Three-year capex plan of ~INR166 crore cumulative, including Pithampur, new dials and general capex, and new plants under development; ~INR90 crore allocated to new plants.
Dewas precision tubing project: total capex ~INR45 crore, of which ~INR15-20 crore spent to date; aimed at aerospace, defence and automotive; expected asset turn at least 2-3x at peak utilisation.
Capex spend in Q1 FY27 was less than INR5 crore; overseas visit planned to finalise extrusion press and other machinery for Dewas; majority of capex in H2 FY27.
Pithampur capacity was expanded from 1,200 MT to 12,000-24,000 MT near end of last year; Italian press now online.
demand_pricing: Export share has dropped from around 60-70% to about 45% (about 40% in Q1 per call Q&A) because of duties hitting the export business; management aims to shift volume to domestic high-value business, which is slow to convert.
Freight rates up 5-10x on Strait of Hormuz and Middle East disruption; customers in GCC and East Asia holding back orders; delays and backed-up shipping persist.
Conversion margins: plain extrusion 6-10% (management cited 6-8% and 6-10%); value-added processing (powder coating, machining, anodizing) targeted at 15%+.
Commodity exposure: most manufacturing volumes hedged via LME/MCX on order basis; unhedged positions kept under 5%; management says commodity moves impact margins by less than 5%.

Trading is a pass-through business at metal prices; management said EBITDA per ton is reported on a blended basis only, with manufacturing EBITDA per ton not readily available (last quarter's USD340/ton reference not updated).

qa_highlights.question: What was the capacity volume this quarter and EBITDA per ton (last quarter USD340/t)?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA is reported only on a blended basis; manufacturing per-ton figure not available. Total extrusion production was about 1,558 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any ramp-up in volumes sooner than expected?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management reiterated flattish volumes, with any ramp-up toward end FY27 or early FY28. The export loss from duties is being replaced by slow-converting domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: How are aluminium prices hedged and how do margins change with value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging is order-linked on LME/MCX, with under 5% unhedged; plain extrusion margins are 6-10%, rising to 15%+ with value addition. Management said absolute EBITDA per ton is the right metric for conversion.

qa_highlights.question: Dewas project status, timing and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15-20 crore of INR45 crore spent; online targeted within 6-8 months, before mid-FY28, with no firm date. Asset turn at least 2-3x; no margin figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company take on debt for capex, and how will employee costs move?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt planned; management said the company is deleveraging. Employee costs are not expected to rise materially as the technical team is already on payroll.

qa_highlights.question: How has other expenses fallen and how are energy costs being recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell from INR18 crore to INR13 crore over four quarters. About 50% of the gas cost increase was passed to customers, with the rest to follow as contracts renew.

544420|2026-06.headline: Raymond Realty Q1 FY27 booking value rose 129% YoY to INR700 crore; FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin reiterated.
544420|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 booking value of INR700 crore (up 129% YoY), customer collections of INR550 crore (up 47%) and total income of INR536 crore (up 37%). EBITDA rose 70% YoY to INR70 crore, with margin expanding from 11% to 13%, which management attributed to upfront costs from four projects launched in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth, 20%+ revenue growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin and 20%+ ROCE. JDAs now account for about 52% of INR52,000 crore total GDV, and a new Parel JDA with INR8,500 crore GDV was signed.

financial_highlights.change: Gross debt INR1,095 crore; cash INR271 crore
management said FY27 interest INR100-120 crore

segments.name: JDA (asset-light) portfolio
segments.commentary: Eight JDA projects with combined GDV of INR27,000 crore (52% of total GDV); 64% of Q1 presales came from JDAs. Four launched projects (Bandra East, BKC, Wadala, Sion) carry INR11,500 crore revenue potential, INR2,900 crore cumulative sales and about INR692 crore collections.

segments.name: Owned land (Thane, 100 acres)
segments.commentary: 65 acres under active development with 6.7 million sq ft RERA carpet area and INR16,500 crore revenue potential; INR9,400 crore sold and INR7,460 crore collected to date. Contributed 36% of Q1 booking value; 11 towers (about 4,000 homes) delivered. Management expects own-land margins of 25-26%.

532832|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 presales rose 338% YoY to INR868 crore and collections 54% to INR496 crore, but revenue fell to INR217 crore and net loss widened to INR234 crore.
532832|2026-06.overview: Presales of INR868 crore (up 338% YoY) and collections of INR496 crore (up 54% YoY) led the quarter, while no new projects were launched in Q1 by design. Reported revenue from operations fell to INR217 crore from INR681 crore, EBITDA was negative INR106 crore, and net loss widened to INR234 crore from INR166 crore, as revenue is recognised only on completion and handover. Operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore; management expects collections to pick up from Q2 as launches from H2 FY26 hit milestones. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crore owned presales, INR2,000 crore DM presales and about INR3,000 crore collections, and a promoter warrant issue at INR111.51 to repay Embassy Group's INR363 crore shareholder debt.

segments.name: Residential (owned development)
segments.commentary: Presales INR868 crore in Q1; ongoing portfolio of 11 assets about 70% sold by saleable area; OC-received inventory about 98% cumulatively sold. Construction spend INR276 crore, about 56% of collections.

segments.name: Development management (DM)
segments.commentary: Embassy Terazza (Juhu) received RERA approval just before the call and is slated for Q2 launch; FY27 DM presales guidance INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Embassy East Business Park is under excavation and may be held as an annuity asset or sold near completion. Embassy Knowledge Park commercial product is in early planning, with timelines targeted by end-FY27; not included in GDV.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance: INR6,000 crore from owned developments and INR2,000 crore from DM projects, reiterated.
FY27 collections guidance of approximately INR3,000 crore reiterated; management says it could be bettered, with more clarity by Q3.

FY27 launch pipeline: 11 projects, GDV about INR19,400 crore (9 owned, INR13,300 crore; 2 DM, INR6,000-plus crore). Four to launch in Q2 (Embassy One North tower, Embassy Knowledge Park villas and apartments, Juhu DM project); the rest targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.
Management expects a cash-flow inflection around mid-calendar 2027 (April-May) as slab cycles start on Greenshore, Verde and Citadel.
Debt: cost of debt to fall first, with refinancing of the portfolio targeted around March-April 2027; net debt to equity target of 0.3x-0.35x.
Under review: percentage-of-completion accounting, to be assessed over the next couple of quarters.
capex_capacity: Ongoing development of 11 assets about 70% sold by saleable area; Embassy Paradiso and balance towers of Golf City Savroli nearing completion and slated for OC in FY27; Embassy Edge and East Avenue due for completion in FY28.
OC received in Q1 for Embassy One 09 (Gurgaon, Phase 1) and 5 towers at Golf City Savroli.
Embassy Citadel (Mumbai, Worli) has approval for all 81 floors; Leighton appointed as civil contractor; est. INR8,000-9,000 crore of stock to sell over several years.

Beyond 2027: development pipeline of about 20.3 million sq ft, GDV about INR23,470 crore; fully paid land bank of 3,000-plus acres, including 1,400-plus acres at Nashik (MIDC dispute; debonding expected to take 6-9 more months).
Cumulative unsold inventory across launched and under-construction residential and commercial projects: INR13,630 crore.
demand_pricing: Bangalore: about 72% of launch inventory sold within 6 months; management cites this as the cleanest read on demand, with Mumbai's 60% figure skewed by Citadel.
Nearly 60% of inventory launched in FY26 already sold.
Management says Embassy has a pricing premium in Bangalore; Citadel's first tranche priced to build reputation before taking top Mumbai pricing.
Collections-to-presales ratio was about 35% last year; FY27 target implies about 50% (INR3,000 crore vs INR6,000 crore owned presales).
Some Gurgaon landlords have asked about the Indiabulls association; management says the entities are separate and that this is a slow-to-resolve perception issue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Bangalore launch delays (as at Prestige) also affecting Embassy, and can the other 5 Bangalore projects launch within FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q1 non-launch to choice, not approvals; Embassy One North was pushed to Q2 after the Four Seasons branding was dropped. Knowledge Park villas and apartments are targeted for Q2, and Bangalore projects are targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook, given EBITDA of negative INR106 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore because no launches occurred in Q1; collections from Q3-Q4 FY26 launches should accelerate from Q2. Cash balance started FY27 at about INR1,165 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR19,400 crore GDV split between H1 and H2?
qa_highlights.answer: The four Q2 launches (North tower, Knowledge Park, Juhu DM, plus Embassy One already launched) are in H1; the remaining projects are targeted for Q3, possibly Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the average cost of debt and the cost of the Blackstone debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is about 14%. Blackstone debt accrues at 18%, added to the gross debt rather than paid out; management is in talks to convert the Blackstone portion to equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why the promoter warrant issue if the promoter debt is accruing rather than paid in cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it brings no new liquidity; it is a confidence signal, priced at INR111.51 (the earlier pre-merger price), and the Embassy Group debt (growing at over 15%) will be cleared. Warrants will convert within 6 months, versus the 18-month maximum.

qa_highlights.question: Can collections of INR3,000 crore be achieved without new launches, and what is the collection schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Most collections are expected from already-launched projects (Greenshore, Verde, Eden). Launches in Q2 and Q3 are expected to yield 10-20% collected in the quarter; management is confident of the INR3,000 crore.

540678|2026-06.headline: Cochin Shipyard Q1 FY27 PAT fell to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore on turnover of INR 1,094.21 crore; ISRF JV with DP World's Drydocks World valued at INR 1,800 crore.
540678|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover rose about 2.4% YoY to INR 1,094.21 crore, but PBT fell to INR 202.49 crore from INR 249.54 crore and PAT to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore. Management cited EBITDA margin around 24% and PAT margin around 14% for the quarter. The company delivered three vessels in the period, plus three by subsidiary Udupi Cochin Shipyard. Management announced several strategic moves: a 50:50 JV with Drydocks World for the ISRF ship repair facility, a scaled-down block fabrication plan after HD KSOE talks failed, a Tuticorin hybrid yard lease, and a Green Maritime battery JV.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1,068.59 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +2.4%)
vs INR 249.54 crore in Q1 FY26 (about -19%)
vs INR 187.82 crore in Q1 FY26 (about -19%)
Around INR 27,000 crore after NGSV contract (L1, about INR 5,000 crore)

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Management said shipbuilding is about 70% of turnover at 10-12% EBITDA margin. Deliveries in FY27 so far include the third of eight ASW shallow water crafts, a second multipurpose vessel for a German client, and a Ro-Ro ferry for Kochi Municipal Corporation.

segments.name: Ship repair
segments.commentary: Ship repair is about 30% of turnover at roughly 20-24% EBITDA margin. ISRF has a 6,000-ton ship lift, about 1,400 m berthing and annual capacity of up to 82 ships.

segments.name: Udupi Cochin Shipyard (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Delivered three vessels in the period: two 3,800 TDW general cargo vessels to Wilson Group, Norway, and a 70-tonne bollard pull tug to Polestar Maritime (Adani Group). Management said land constraints limit its new order intake.

segments.name: Green Maritime battery JV (with HBL, 40% CSL)
segments.commentary: Incorporated June 2026 for marinized energy storage systems. Target revenue INR 640 crore by year 5 and about 20% EBITDA margin (ballpark, business plan not final). Total capital INR 50 crore; no manufacturing facility, as HBL will manufacture.

guidance_outlook: Turnover growth guidance of about 12% per year, with management saying it could reach 12-15%.
Blended EBITDA margin guided at around 14-15% for the year on a conservative basis, down from prior years' higher margins.

Target to deliver about 10 vessels in FY27 (three delivered so far in Q1): two more ASWs by December 2026, two more multipurpose vessels, a trailing suction hopper dredger next month, and commissioning service vessels and Samskip container vessels through early 2027.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in FY27 as delivery-linked milestone payments come in.
ISRF JV transaction targeted for completion before end of FY27, subject to Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, DIPAM, and CSL shareholder (postal ballot) approvals.
New investments targeted at a return on capital of about 14-15%.
capex_capacity: ISRF JV: INR 1,800 crore slump-sale consideration, 50% in cash and 50% in JV equity. Expected revenue about INR 600 crore over the next 2 years, scaling to INR 1,000-1,200 crore over 5 years. Plan adds 10 workstations.

Block fabrication: Earlier 1 lakh tonne plan with HD KSOE is now a solo facility of about 60,000 tonnes per annum. Current capacity is about 12,000 tonnes per annum, for total throughput near 72,000 tonnes.

Vadinar (Gujarat) ship repair with Deendayal Port Authority: two floating drydocks for ~250 m vessels. CCEA approval received May 2026. Environmental clearance expected shortly; operations targeted within 36 months of EC. Revenue about INR 300-600 crore after 3 years.

Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar Port): won 30-year lease at one-time payment of INR 305.76 crore for about 110 acres land and 17.29 acres waterfront. In DPR stage; revenue of INR 650-700 crore initially, scaling to INR 1,800-2,000 crore over 7-8 years.

Total capex over about 5 years estimated by an analyst at INR 6,000-6,500 crore across the four projects. Funding targeted at about 80:20 debt-equity. Applied for Shipbuilding Development Scheme (25% capex subsidy) and MDF Interest Incentivisation Fund (up to 3% interest subvention).
demand_pricing: Defence pipeline per management: LPD (4 numbers, about INR 32,000 crore), MCMV (12 numbers, about INR 36,000 crore), P-17 Bravo (7 numbers, about INR 49,000 crore). Management said these are RFPs with competition; LPD and MCMV seen as more suitable than P-17 Bravo.
NGSV: CSL is L1 for five next-generation survey vessels worth about INR 5,000 crore; order signing expected around November 2026. Navy procedures are slow (CCS and PNC approvals).

Commercial: Dredging Corporation of India sister dredger (about INR 1,300 crore, nomination basis) expected within about two months. Andaman 4 x 500-passenger vessels under nomination discussion. Government demand aggregation for about 432 vessels over 10 years, with SCI/BCSL tenders in progress. MR tanker technical bid indicative cost about INR 1,700 crore; Aframax EOI indicative cost about INR 2,600 crore.
Export: European commercial vessels from 2023-24 orders are 80-90% complete but only about 30% paid; payment is tail-ended (around 70% on delivery).
Management said the Green Tug Transition Program could create about INR 1,000 crore of battery-led investment over 10 years, with real volume expected in 3-4 years.

514211|2026-06.headline: Sumeet Industries Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 3.24% (EBITDA INR8.85 crore) on raw material volatility, while management guides ~6% margin and 30%+ revenue growth for FY27.
514211|2026-06.overview: Revenue (income) rose over 9% YoY to INR272.74 crore, but EBITDA was INR8.85 crore (3.24% margin) and PAT was INR1.14 crore, which management attributed to crude-driven PTA/MEG volatility, higher freight costs and a 15-day maintenance shutdown. Production fell 17% QoQ, with sales supported by inventory liquidation. Management said the rights issue (INR199.75 crore gross, net ~INR194.90 crore) is being deployed to working capital, the Nakoda CP plant, debt repayment (~INR23 crore) and a 6.5 MW solar plant. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 30%+ revenue growth, ~6% EBITDA margin and 3.5–4% PAT margin, with the Nakoda plant now guided for Q2 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~20%+ in prior three-four quarters per analyst

segments.name: POY / FDY / texturised yarn (value chain)
segments.commentary: Management said value-added yarn is now 30–35% of yarn production. Demand described as good across POY, FDY and texturised yarn, with no demand issue if the Middle East conflict settles.

segments.name: PET chips (CP plant)
segments.commentary: Existing CP capacity cited as 300 tpd, with yarn drawing at 240 tpd. The acquired Nakoda CP plant (140,000 tpa) is expected to roughly double total capacity once commissioned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of more than 30% YoY (management said approximately 30%).
FY27 EBITDA margin of around 6%, expected by end of FY27.
FY27 PAT margin of 3.5% to 4%.
Gross margin expected to exceed 25% and be sustained, per management.
Nakoda CP plant commissioning guided to Q2 of FY28, with optimum utilisation within about 60 days of start.
Power cost benefit of around INR25 crore per annum once renewable power is fully commissioned; remaining solar capacity expected in Q4 FY27.
Finance cost expected to fall significantly as debt is repaid and CC interest is reduced.
capex_capacity: Nakoda CP plant (acquired from Narkoda Ltd under CIRP for INR23.47 crore): 140,000 tpa PET chips capacity; new machinery ordered and restoration underway; commissioning guided for Q2 FY28.
Recent 30 tpd (about 20,000 tpa per analyst's reference) capacity addition: partly commissioned in July, remainder in August 2026; management said it is at optimum within about a month.

Rights issue: 16.84 crore shares at INR11.86, raising INR199.75 crore; net ~INR194.90 crore allocated ~INR100 crore working capital, ~INR50 crore Nakoda operationalisation, ~INR23 crore debt repayment, ~INR22 crore solar captive plant.
Captive solar: 6.5 MW captive solar plant referenced; renewable share of power currently ~30%, rising to 25–30% more after new solar commissions (management wording was inconsistent on the share).
Total capex envelope of ~INR90 crore cited by an analyst; management confirmed the Nakoda INR23 crore payment is included in it.
demand_pricing: Management said end-market demand from apparel, home textiles and industrial applications remained healthy; the margin squeeze was input-cost driven.
Raw material (PTA/MEG) prices have declined from peaks but not back to pre-war levels; management expects normalisation by end of August 2026.
Pass-through lags: order cycle ~15 days; management said prices that moved up and down within 15 days could not be fully passed to customers.
Customer base is largely agents; management said the top 10 agents account for approximately 50% of revenue (analyst later noted 41%).
Export: no exports to date; deemed exports under way and direct exports planned, with no special certification needed.
Receivables: management said no receivable is older than 6 months; collection 30–45 days; supplier credit about 30 days.

qa_highlights.question: Volumes delivered in Q1 between POY and FDY?
qa_highlights.answer: Production fell 17% QoQ due to raw material scarcity and a 15-day maintenance shutdown; sales were maintained by liquidating existing stock. No split by POY and FDY was given.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt post-repayment and finance cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited long-term debt of INR86 crore and short-term borrowings of INR74 crore (pre-repayment). After ~INR23 crore repayment, remaining machine term loan expected around INR30 crore; finance cost expected to fall significantly, with CC interest near negligible.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin 3.24% vs the ~6% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to volatile raw material prices, weekly swings and pass-through lags; it said the 30,000 tpa addition, renewable power in H2 and falling raw material costs should help margins recover.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin path from ~15% to 25%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects gross margins above 25% and sustained, citing normalised operations and falling raw material prices.

qa_highlights.question: Nakoda plant timing and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is guided for Q2 FY28 (first quarter of next financial year cited as Q2); optimum utilisation within about 60 days of commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Tax losses and investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no tax credit remains as past losses were fully utilised. Of INR15 crore investments/loans, INR9 crore is in High Urja, a power company.

qa_highlights.question: Stock price weakness after rights issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on share price, saying selling pressure was expected after the rights issue at INR11.86 versus trading near INR34–35, and expressed confidence in results.

risks_watch: Execution risk on Nakoda CP plant: commissioning timeline (Q2 FY28) and 60-day ramp-up are management estimates.
Margin recovery depends on raw material normalisation; management said pre-war prices have not returned and pass-through to customers was incomplete in Q1.

539300|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 8.18% on raw-material and crude-linked cost pressure.
539300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR276.33 crores, up 120.64% YoY and 39.85% QoQ, with PAT of INR15.04 crores (up 130.67% YoY). EBITDA rose 94.41% YoY to INR22.59 crores, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 9.28% a year earlier and 10.19% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the margin squeeze to dyes, chemicals, boiler fuel, LABSA and PP packaging costs linked to geopolitical crude volatility, which hit the textile business hardest. Installed FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity rose to 20,840 tons per month after a 1,700 MT soap line was commissioned at Roorkee. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR900-1,000 crores and a ~6% profitability level, with a further 0.75-1% improvement in FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 50-55%; another 25-30% expected by FY28; little new capex needed for one to one-and-a-half years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the initial ramp to be slightly below the analyst's INR600-700 crore FY27 estimate; business to treble over three years versus last year's INR400 crores; margins targeted slightly above the historical 15% EBITDA / 8-10% PAT cycle average.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses and employee costs jump sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to advance hiring for Seetharampur and Naidupeta, power costs of Seetharampur built up before July ramp-up, and corporate hiring tied to acquisitions. Per-GW manpower at Seetharampur is expected about 40% lower.

508954|2026-06.headline: Finkurve's Q1 FY27 AUM grew 135% YoY to a 118-branch network, with gross NPA at 0.54% and debt-to-equity up to 2.9x.
508954|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a transition quarter for the gold loan industry, with new RBI norms prompting sector-wide alignment and some near-term drag on customer and channel momentum. Reported AUM rose 135% YoY, revenue about 89% YoY and PAT about 65% YoY, with branches up from 83 to 118. Asset quality was stable (gross NPA 0.54%, net NPA 0.48%), while leverage rose sharply (debt-to-equity 0.7x to 2.9x) and ROA fell to 2.9%. Management reiterated 50-60% AUM growth guidance for FY27 and disclosed the first institutional NCD subscription (Rs 50 crore from Franklin Templeton).

segments.name: Gold loans (consumption and income-generating)
segments.commentary: Average ticket size rose to Rs 1.87 lakh from Rs 1.31 lakh a year earlier; average AUM per branch is Rs 10.3 crore against a target of Rs 12-13 crore. Management attributes roughly 50% of YoY AUM growth to tonnage and 50% to gold price.

segments.name: Co-lending
segments.commentary: Co-lending share is about 3% currently; target is 15-20% of the book by end-FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 50-60% retained; management said Q1 AUM grew about 16% QoQ and that Q3 and Q4 are seasonally stronger.
Target leverage of 4x to 4.5x debt-to-equity; management does not expect to exceed 4x in FY27.
Lending yields expected to stabilise around 20-20.5%, with about 50 bps of yield improvement guided.
Cost of funds expected to fall as co-lending rises to 15-20% and as a re-rating is expected at around Rs 2,000 crore AUM; the company is rated BBB+.
Steady-state ROA target around 3%; over five years, management aspires to 3-3.5% ROA and 18% ROE.
New branches expected to break even in 12-18 months at a breakeven AUM of Rs 5-6 crore.
Rs 30 crore promoter share-warrant infusion expected by November 2026 (deadline), adding roughly Rs 100 crore of leverage headroom.
Expansion limited to current four southern states before moving to Odisha; no plans for distant regions.
capex_capacity: Branch network grew from 83 to 118 as of 30 June 2026; expansion is organic, state by state, within the four current southern states.
Leverage headroom of about Rs 1,600 crore on book plus about Rs 400 crore off book, per management, with a runway of about Rs 800 crore before optimal leverage.
Net worth about Rs 350 crore; management says this supports roughly Rs 350 crore of additional AUM, with co-lending adding Rs 300-400 crore, taking AUM to Rs 1,900-2,000 crore on current capital.
Compliance and risk functions strengthened with a new CRO and Head of Compliance; compliance software investment underway under a year-long plan.
demand_pricing: Management said the industry is seeing smaller ticket sizes, which track gold prices after a correction and higher volatility in Q1.

Competition from banks and PSUs is viewed as targeting a different, lower-yield customer segment; management says pricing is largely the same across lenders and differentiation is on product, service and post-disbursal service.
Management expects growth in new branches to continue on low-base effects, while the existing book is more exposed to gold price declines.
Management said the Q1 AUM growth was achieved despite gold price correction and the regulatory transition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target leverage range and co-lending share for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Target leverage of 4x to 4.5x, with no move beyond 4x in FY27; co-lending target of 15-20% by end-FY27 versus about 3% currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital headroom to grow further?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 1,600 crore on book plus Rs 400 crore off book; with co-lending and promoter warrants, AUM could reach Rs 1,900-2,000 crore on current capital.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company complying with RBI gold loan norms on valuation and LTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Valuation changes are limited to SMS or letter notification on valuation differences and a valuation certificate; LTV is now tiered at 85%, 80% and 75% for consumption loans, with income-generating loans underwritten under a board-approved policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for NIM and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields to stabilise around 20-20.5%, cost of funds to fall with co-lending and re-rating, and opex-to-AUM to decline with scale; ROA is currently depressed by leverage, with a steady-state target of about 3%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 135% AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 50% to tonnage and 50% to gold price; customer additions of about 1,800 per month.

qa_highlights.question: What are the branch economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Average AUM per branch is Rs 10.3 crore, targeting Rs 12-13 crore; breakeven takes 12-18 months at around Rs 5-6 crore AUM.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company compete with banks and PSUs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said banks serve a lower-yield segment, and the company competes on product, service and post-disbursal service rather than price.

risks_watch: Gold price correction and volatility could reduce ticket sizes and slow growth in the existing book, per management.
Leverage at 2.9x debt-to-equity with ROA at 2.9% and pre-tax spread of only 100-200 bps; cost of borrowing 11-11.5% against 20% yield and 6-7% opex.
Co-lending ramp from 3% to 15-20% and cost-of-funds re-rating are both needed for the margin expansion case.
Ongoing regulatory circulars every two to three weeks; management describes compliance as an evolving framework.
Promoter warrant infusion of Rs 30 crore due by November 2026.
Management declined to comment on the share price decline of about 50-55% from highs, which an analyst raised.
508954|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and guidance, but cautious on near-term momentum, which management attributed to the regulatory transition and gold price correction. Answers on competition and regulation were broad, and management declined to comment on the share price.
key_quotes: We have never believed in pursuing short -term growth at the expe nse of long -term franchise quality.
We will continue to scale the business in a manner where systems, technology, governance, and risk management remain ahead of growth.

544342|2026-06.headline: Stallion Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.78% YoY to ₹124.68 crore while PAT jumped 79.15% to ₹18.57 crore; management says margins are partly one-off.
544342|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached ₹124.68 crore (+12.78% YoY), EBITDA rose 75.85% to ₹25.27 crore and PAT rose 79.15% to ₹18.57 crore. Management attributed the margin jump to a mix of better product mix (higher HFO share), earlier logistics planning and inventory gains, splitting EBITDA roughly 50:50 between inventory gains and operations. The high-purity helium plant at Khalapur (1,200 MTPA) is complete with commercial operations expected next quarter, while the 10,000 MT R32 plant at Bhilwara slipped from a July 2026 target to end-December 2026, and Mambattu (HFO blending) is now due by year-end. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR guidance but cut the FY27 contribution expectation from the R32 plant and opened the door to dilution or debt for expansion.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin (analyst-cited, not stated by management)
financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 level as referenced in Q&A

segments.name: Specialty gases - High-purity helium (Khalapur)
segments.commentary: 1,200 MTPA plant ready; commercial operations expected next quarter. Management guides ~5 containers in FY27, rising to 12 in FY28 and 24 thereafter; contribution about 12% of revenue this year per management. Availability of supply, not selling, is the constraint.

segments.name: Refrigerants - R32 (Bhilwara)
segments.commentary: 10,000 MT plant, completion now targeted end-December 2026 (earlier July 2026, then March 2027 startup per funding delay). Current R32 price ~₹800/kg vs ~₹900 peak; guidance based on ₹550/kg.

segments.commentary: Now expected by year-end versus earlier August target; scope expanded to 12 tanks with hydrocarbon and helium capability. Management says immediate turnover uplift may be only ~10%, with margin benefit larger.

segments.commentary: About 50% of business; management says conventional business earns roughly 10% PAT margin, with new businesses at ~24% PAT.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 30-35% maintained over next three years; management says 'the 30-35% is intact'.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 3-4% over the medium term as backward integration and specialty gases scale.
Management described Q1 margins as a 'special quarter' and not sustainable at current levels; FY27 PAT margin ex-R32 expected around 10%.
Peak revenue target above ₹1,100 crore in FY28 with helium, R32 and Mambattu fully operational, at ~15% PAT minimum (per analyst's framing, confirmed by management).
Long-term target of ₹3,000 crore revenue; plan of roughly one new plant per year for three years, with timeline could stretch to six years without external funding.
Capex for proposed HFO plant estimated at ₹350-400 crore for 10,000 tons capacity; management to announce more toward end of year after R32 commissioning.
capex_capacity: Khalapur high-purity helium: 1,200 MTPA installed, commercial ops expected next quarter.
Bhilwara R32: 10,000 MT; target completion end-December 2026 (previously July 2026). Delay attributed to funding: preferential issue abandoned, rights issue funding arrived late (February).
Mambattu (AP): HFO blending plant, expected operational by end-2026; scope enlarged to 12 tanks from 5 with hydrocarbon/helium capability, requiring redesign.

Management says capex is within budget with no overspend.
demand_pricing: Helium: price rose sharply over past 6-7 months and is now stable at ~₹4,000/kg per management (approximate). R32: price ~₹800/kg, down from ~₹900 peak; management says correction is underway. India requirement ~20,000 tons vs 70,000-90,000 tons of capacity coming up; export and China quota reduction (from 2028) cited as demand drivers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion is pricing vs product mix, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combination of better product mix (higher HFO share), earlier logistics planning and high stock-keeping during the Gulf crisis; said inventory gains are roughly 50:50 of EBITDA, and that margins will not necessarily repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30-35% revenue growth guidance still intact after the R32 delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said the 30-35% is intact, while acknowledging the FY27 R32 contribution will change slightly from ₹250 crore; Q4 R32 revenue expected around ₹125 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the R32 plant delayed and what funding was used?
qa_highlights.answer: A planned preferential issue was abandoned after a share-price spike; a rights issue was used instead, reaching the market only by February, so the planned December startup slipped to March-end under the original plan.

qa_highlights.question: What are the helium volumes and how is supply secured given Middle East shipping disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~5 containers in FY27, 12 in FY28, 24 after; utilisation about 20% of 1,200 MTPA next year. Supply secured via Sharjah Oxygen, swap arrangements and multiple sources; price expected to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity or debt for the expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it previously preferred internal accruals, but now sees dilution and debt as likely for faster growth ('some dilution, some debt, not all debt'); no decision made yet.

qa_highlights.question: How much R32 volume is pre-sold under contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose pre-sales, calling existing understandings non-enforceable MOUs; said the company will not commit to take-or-pay contracts ahead of plant readiness.

523796|2026-06.headline: Viceroy Hotels Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 77% to INR44.9 crore and EBITDA rose 144% to INR11.8 crore, with PAT turning positive at INR1.4 crore.
523796|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR44.9 crore against INR25.4 crore a year earlier, and EBITDA margin expanded to 26.3% from 19%. Courtyard reopened with full 168-key inventory after Phase 1 renovation, pushing its occupancy to 83.65% and RevPAR to INR5,006. Combined ADR fell about 12% as lower-paying corporate, army and airline business was added to fill rooms while the Marriott convention centre was offline from April for Phase 2 work. Higher depreciation (INR5 crore) and finance cost (INR5.4 crore, from INR1 crore) absorbed most of the EBITDA, leaving PAT of INR1.4 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT is after interest and depreciation; debt drawn 1 January 2026; combined EBITDA run-rate cited by analyst about INR21.45 crore for the asset.
