543212|2026-06.headline: Borosil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR253.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.6% from 17.8% on a ~INR10 crore West Asia cost hit.
543212|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 9% YoY to INR253.6 crore, with Glassware up 16.8% and Non-glassware up 4.2%, both stated as volume-led. Operating EBITDA fell to INR35.9 crore from INR40.2 crore as fuel and packaging inflation from the West Asia conflict hit margins; management said price increases of 5-7% were taken but realisations lag into Q2 onwards. PBT dropped to INR17.4 crore from INR23.5 crore (last year included a INR7.2 crore one-time stamp duty reversal), and PAT fell to INR12.8 crore from INR17.4 crore. Management reiterated an FY27 EBITDA margin of about 18% excluding other income, and a steady-state ambition of 18% without the conflict impact.

segments.name: Larah Opalware
segments.commentary: Sales INR83.6 crore, up 9.8% YoY from INR76.2 crore, stated as volume-led with hardly any price contribution. Management guides roughly 9% growth going forward.

segments.name: Glassware (borosilicate microwavables, serveware, tumblers, lunch boxes, storage)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR65.6 crore, up 16.8% YoY from INR56.2 crore; management said growth was entirely volume-led with price pass-through lagging. Utilisation about 90%.

segments.name: Non-glassware (small appliances, bottles and flasks, cookware, kitchen essentials)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR98.1 crore, up 4.2% from INR94.2 crore. Hydra (vacuum flasks) remained hit by BIS compliance requirements, offset by domestic appliances and stainless steel cookware.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 18%, excluding other income; management framed 14-15% historically and ~18% as the steady-state level without West Asia impact.
FY27 capex estimated at about INR125 crore, with an overall range of INR125-150 crore including solar and opal furnace rebuild maintenance capex.
FY27 consolidated depreciation expected at about INR92 crore.
Solar Phase 3 savings estimated at INR27-28 crore at EBITDA level in FY27; management declined to say how much would be retained after pass-through.
Price realisation from the 5-7% increases expected to flow in from Q2 FY27 onwards.
Long-term ROCE aspiration of 20-24% (later referenced as 20-22%) on the business; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Stylenest India (subsidiary) Hydra plant in Rajasthan: 2 double-wall lines commenced commercial production on 30 June 2026; third line expected in Q2 FY27.

Third captive solar plant in Bikaner: 20 MWp with battery energy storage, commissioned in Q1 FY27; solar now meets about 61% of energy requirement. Further 6.5 MWp (Borosil) and 3-4 MWp (Stylenest) solar under evaluation.
Bharuch, Gujarat glassware plant: capex INR42 crore, sanctioned in Q4 FY26 to make jugs, jars and bottles currently sourced (~INR100 crore sales) from BSL Bharuch; commissioning by end Q3 FY27.

Jaipur borosilicate pressware blast furnace expansion from 25 to 32 tons per day plus a third forming line; capex INR50 crore; commissioning by end Q4 FY28. Current furnace utilisation about 90%; furnace rebuild due Jan 2028.
Opalware utilisation described as full; Glassware about 90%.
demand_pricing: Price increases of 5-7% by category taken across multiple categories (management says some above that); execution started mid-May and realisation lags into Q2.
West Asia conflict net impact on Q1 FY27 about INR10 crore (INR12 crore cited in Q&A), with price increases compensating only a couple of crore.

Fuel cost run-rate: Opalware fuel impact about INR6 crore in Q1, expected to fall to about INR1.5 crore a quarter; borosilicate fuel impact about INR2.5 crore a quarter, expected to fall to INR60-70 lakh. Fuel at 5.8% of sales vs 2.9% a year ago.
Chinese dumping in borosilicate glassware persists despite rupee depreciation and higher freight; anti-dumping investigation pending with authorities, timing uncertain and not included in guidance.
Whiteware (Opalware sub-category) about 10% of Opalware sales vs under 5% last year; management said margins are well below the regular range, so it will not push that mix up.

Omnichannel presence across 24,000+ retail outlets, e-commerce, quick commerce and B2B/export; first two exclusive Borosil brand stores opened in Pune and Gurugram, Jaipur next, capex INR40-50 lakh per store, no store-count target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Glassware's 16.7% growth was price vs volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was entirely volume-led; price pass-through is lagging and was only a couple of crore in Q1 against about INR12 crore West Asia impact. Price hikes range 5-7% by category.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% EBITDA margin for FY27 excluding other income; capex about INR125 crore, with a range up to INR150 crore including solar and furnace maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Has Chinese dumping eased given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management says dumping continues with no visible difference despite rupee weakness and higher freight. Anti-dumping investigation is ongoing, and no benefit is assumed in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 growth inflated by channel inventory stocking ahead of price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that view, saying price impact arrives only in Q2 and there was no forced sale or retailer stocking. Inventory build is typical ahead of Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in ~18% margin given historical 14-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified that 14-15% is the historical level and ~18% is the steady-state margin without West Asia impact; FY27 target is for 18% on the year, with improvement dependent on price realisation and lower fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to 20-24% ROCE and why is ROCE around 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed low ROCE to heavy capex over three to four years, plus inventory built for BIS challenges. It described 20-24% as a medium-term aspiration; it did not provide a bridge or timeline.

544321|2026-06.headline: Consolidated revenue rose 7% to INR554 crores, but EBITDA fell about INR16 crores as Maldives diesel costs spiked; India grew 16% at INR74 crores.
544321|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY to INR554 crores and consolidated EBITDA was INR205 crores at a 37% margin. The decline in EBITDA was attributed almost entirely to Maldives fuel and ancillary costs, which rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores as diesel prices roughly doubled from pre-war levels in April-May. India delivered 13% revenue growth and 16% EBITDA growth, with occupancy and ADR both up. Reported PAT of INR124 crores was inflated by a INR102 crore deferred tax reversal following the tax regime switch.

financial_highlights.change: YoY decline of about INR16 crores
Broadly flat; about 3% growth adjusted for one-off transaction costs
Includes INR102 crore net deferred tax liability reversal from tax regime change; tax rate cut from 34.94% to 25.17%

financial_highlights.value: INR2,095 crores (India INR1,329 crores; Maldives USD81 million / INR766 crores)

segments.name: India hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue INR203 crores (+13%) and EBITDA INR74 crores (+16%); occupancy rose about 7% to 67% and ADR about 8%, giving RevPAR growth of about 20%. Adjusted for a one-off electricity benefit in the prior year, EBITDA growth would be 18%.

segments.name: Maldives resorts
segments.commentary: Revenue INR218 crores (+5%) but EBITDA INR32 crores (-32%); fuel and ancillary costs rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores. Excluding the fuel spike, management says EBITDA would have grown about 10%.

segments.name: Annuity (commercial/leased assets)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR128 crores (+3%) and EBITDA INR111 crores at 87% margin; committed occupancy 98%. Narmada Estates in Pune was recently added.

segments.name: Hospitality total
segments.commentary: Hospitality EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR106 crores; adjusted hospitality EBITDA growth was about 14%.

532210|2026-06.headline: City Union Bank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 383 crore, a record, with GNPA down to 1.73% and NIM guided to 3.65-3.70%.
532210|2026-06.overview: Advances grew 25% YoY to Rs 67,645 crore and deposits 21% to Rs 79,342 crore, with CD ratio at 85%. Operating profit rose 29% to Rs 581 crore and PAT 25% to Rs 383 crore, both stated as record highs. Asset quality improved further: GNPA 1.73% (from 2.99% a year ago), Net NPA 0.61%, and recoveries exceeded slippages. Management guided to a moderate NIM dip from higher cost of funds, cost-to-income of 47-48% for FY27, and an exit ROA of 1.60-1.65%.

financial_highlights.change: up 25% QoQ as stated; vs Rs 54,020 crore in 1QFY26

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME average disbursement about Rs 3,500 crore per quarter; management targets MSME at 55-60% of book and growth 2-3% above system. Average utilisation fell from 73% to 70%; repayments about Rs 900 crore per month.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Share of book at 30-31%, guided to stay 31-32%. Agri gold yield about 10-10.5% and non-agri 11-11.5%; agri priced 100 bps lower. Average LTV 62.07%. Branches rose from 700 to 1,000.

segments.name: Retail secured (LAP)
segments.commentary: LAP yield about 9.60-9.70%. Management expects retail secured at about 10% of book.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Yield on investments fell to 6.42% from 6.61% in 4QFY26 because Rs 12 crore of mutual fund income (on about Rs 700 crore invested) was classified under other income; 6.67% on an interest-income basis.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guided at 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27; DSA business about 1-2% of book.
NIM expected at 3.65-3.70% over the next few quarters as cost of deposits rises about 5 bps; long-term view 3.70-3.75%.
Cost of deposits guided at 5.60-5.70%; borrowing cost of about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.
Cost-to-income guided at 47-48% for FY27 (currently 45%) because staff hikes start from July; long-term aspiration below 45% in about three years.
Exit ROA guided at 1.60-1.65%; full-year ROA 1.55-1.65%. Steady-state credit cost about 0.40%; FY27 slippages Rs 700-750 crore; slippage ratio 1.20-1.30%.
ECLGS participation: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date; total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provisioning about 0.45% of loan book, CAR consumption capped at 0.65%.
capex_capacity: Branch rollout front-loaded this year; branch count rose from 700 to 1,000 in the gold-loan context.
AI-led automation invested in operations; management expects it to lower cost further.
Liquidity: average LCR at 150%.

Business enterprise (non-MSME, no Udyam registration) loans at Rs 18,827 million; large-industry book fell from Rs 22,500 million (Dec-25) to about Rs 15,000 million then rose to Rs 19,000 million on exits and yield pressure.
demand_pricing: Gold loan rates unchanged; management ruled out raising rates to slow growth, citing agri customer needs and competitiveness in non-agri gold; rates up 20-25 bps over last year.
MSME utilisation fell to 70% from 73-74% norm; management attributes it to cautious borrowers and sees it recovering with textile demand after the European trade agreement.
Term deposit rates expected to rise on high demand; FCNR window brought in fresh deposits of Rs 150 crore.
SMA-0/1/2 at 1.20%/0.70%/0.90% (total 2.85%), down from 7.12% in June 2025 and 10.78% in September 2024. Domestic consumption said to be insulated from West Asia stress.
Fee income fell about 15% YoY and 19% in one comparison per analyst question; management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance.

500245|2026-06.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q1 FY27: castings sales up 18% to 41,345 t, tube sales down 14% to 41,512 t, and power and fuel costs rose about INR58 crore YoY.
500245|2026-06.overview: Pig iron and castings output rose in Q1 FY27, while tube output and sales fell on weaker high-value oil and gas and export orders. Power and fuel costs rose sharply, with about INR58 crore of the INR100 crore YoY jump in other expenses coming from power and fuel, half of it from rate increases. A change in green-power rules (8 hours instead of 17) and the end of power trading (about INR10 crore a year) cut the expected solar and wind savings to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore. Management guided to recovery in pricing and volumes from Q2, and said Q1 EBITDA margin was 12-13%.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY vs 132,392 t; management attributed to higher internal consumption
Company level; steel and tube margins cited at 14-17%

financial_highlights.metric: Power and fuel cost increase in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: INR58 crore of ~INR100 crore YoY jump
financial_highlights.change: About INR50 crore sequential jump in other expenses; about INR30 crore from rate increases

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,345 t, up 18% YoY; pricing passed through to customers, with further price increases still being concluded. Rajpura foundry is fully sold out at about 2,200 t per month.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,512 t, down 14% YoY, with a weaker product mix as more line pipe was sold in place of high-realising export and oil and gas tubes. Management is in a wait-and-watch stance due to Chinese dumping and subdued demand.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Realisation improved YoY and QoQ (about INR42,400/t vs INR39,000/t base, as cited on the call); about 30,000 t exported at slightly better than domestic prices. Pig iron EBITDA is expected to support the company margin.

segments.name: Steel (alloy)
segments.commentary: Management expects external sales of 100,000-110,000 t this year vs about 84,000 t, but cost pass-through is still under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Castings volumes expected to rise to about 162,000 t gross sales and then about 188,000 t, implying roughly 17-20% growth.
Overall volume growth of at least 15% across products in the remaining three quarters, with tube volumes up at least 10% YoY and steel external sales up more than 20%.
Pig iron output close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less.
Price-increase and cost pass-through benefits expected from Q2 and Q3 onward.

Medium term: about INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration with 300,000 t castings, 300,000 t casting sales and 400,000 t tube sales. Management said castings reach 270,000 t realisable capacity in this year plus two more years, with tubes at 350,000 t in 3-4 years.
Capex of INR600-700 crore this year, rising in the following years; about INR3,000-3,500 crore over the next four years.
capex_capacity: 35 MW solar plant in commissioning stage; 12 windmills of 2.1 MW each; both expected to be commissioned between June and September 2026.
Solapur two-part (no-bake) foundry, 15,000 t per annum, with commissioning expected by October 2026. Management said it has capacity of about 1,250 t per month.
Rajpura expansion: first phase to 40,000-50,000 t per annum within about 8 months; second phase to 70,000 t per annum. Total realisable castings capacity across six foundries is 270,000 t per annum.
Koppal oxygen plant and enhanced pulverised coal injection in blast furnaces 1 and 2, expected to complete by February-March 2027. Hiriyur pig iron upgrade to 360,000 t, taking about nine months.
Jejuri rolling capacity to rise from 15,000 t to 25,000 t per month (about 3 lakh t per annum), with about 240,000 t saleable; about 18-month timeline.

Premium couplings plant in Baramati, order expected within weeks. Koppal steel plant (about 2 years) and Baramati expander mill (2 years to build) are at early stages. Iron ore mines and pelletisation at Koppal are in progress.
One blast furnace to move to steelmaking, with government clearances in place; decision expected within 2-3 months, commissioning in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Castings demand described as strong across tractors, automobiles, earthmoving equipment and stationary engines; management expects realisation improvement.
Tube demand subdued by oil and gas slowdown and export disruption; Chinese dumping is pressuring pricing. Management expects the tube market to recover.
Coke dumping into India has reportedly eased, which supports domestic pig iron prices. Pig iron exports are running at about 30,000 t.
Fuel costs rose sharply: LPG cost in Solapur roughly doubled versus pre-war levels. Coking coal cost is expected to peak in June-August because of a three-month coal inventory.
Monthly pig iron sales plan of about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external); foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t of that.

520073|2026-06.headline: RACL Geartech Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose about 22% YoY to ₹132.6 crore, with PBT up about 50% to ₹16.8 crore.
520073|2026-06.overview: Consolidated turnover reached ₹132.6 crore in Q1 FY27 versus ₹108.7 crore a year earlier, with exports at ₹85.06 crore (64%) and domestic at ₹40.54 crore (31%). Management said operating revenue grew about 31.5% on a consolidated basis as non-operating income was negligible this quarter. Consolidated EBITDA rose about 18% to ₹32.19 crore, and PBT rose about 50% to ₹16.82 crore. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of about ₹570 crore (16-17% growth) and a ₹77.4 crore capex plan, mostly for replacing the heat treatment plant.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: ₹85.06 crore in Q1 (64% of consolidated turnover); Europe about 59% of business by region, with KTM as a prime customer served from the Austrian subsidiary.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: ₹40.54 crore in Q1 (31% of turnover); Royal Enfield commercial supplies since January 2026 at about 7,500-8,000 sets per month against a nomination of about 10,000.

segments.name: India and Asia Pacific / North America
segments.commentary: India and Asia Pacific about 36% of business; North America about 5% (new regional split disclosed this quarter).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about ₹570 crore (16-17% growth) retained; management said it is plus or minus 5% and no mid-year revision was made.
Management guided to growth of about 15-20% per year over the medium term and said revenue could double in the next three to four years.
FY27 capex of about ₹77.4 crore: about ₹35-40 crore for heat treatment replacement and about ₹35 crore for capacity expansion, partly in FY27 and partly in FY28.
FY27 blended tax rate guided at 25.62%.
Management said the 2%-type margin swings are normal and it aspires to sustain current margins; no formal margin guidance was given.
Next year's capex to be announced around January 2027.
capex_capacity: Heat treatment plant replacement: foundation laid 21 January 2026; building expected complete by October 2026; equipment arriving September-October 2026; installation and commissioning October-December 2026; trial production targeted January 2027.
Shift from LPG-fired to electric furnaces; the existing equipment is over 30 years old; full switch targeted by end of FY27.
Capacity expansion of about ₹35 crore to come into force partly in FY27 and partly in FY28.
Gajraula (UP) is the mother plant on 100% green energy; Noida unit planned rooftop solar.
Management said the company adds capacity only when demand is secure; the ZF project runs at 50-60% utilisation of installed capacity.
demand_pricing: Royal Enfield: commercial supplies since January 2026; nominated for about 10,000 motorcycle sets per month; currently around 7,500-8,000 sets per month; the engine is 350cc.
BMW: final customer sign-off visit on 24 October 2026; pilot supplies already shipping under conditional approval; SOP expected from October 2026.

ZF: volumes recovering for the X5 SUV program; peak revenue year pushed from 2028 to 2030; customer shifted assembly to Eastern Europe; a possible Chinese OEM project is at an early stage; electric power steering supplies for an American OEM expected end-2027 to mid-2028.
KTM: management said volumes are back to near pre-COVID levels and new models are planned for 2027; a new Duke 790 launched.
Management said it does not disclose domestic pricing or realisation per kit, citing competitive sensitivity; export business is single-source per product for the life of the model.
Customer count about 29-30 active customers; no single customer above 20% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a case to upgrade FY27 revenue guidance given KTM recovery and Royal Enfield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is reviewed once a year and is plus or minus 5%; it declined to revise, and said no single customer exceeds 20% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA margin expansion sustainable, and what explains the low raw material share and higher other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to sustain margins but said 2% swings occur quarter to quarter. Raw material was about 28% of sales; the CFO pointed to the line-item comparison slide, and an analyst noted stock-in-transit consumption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate jump to about 47% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to current tax from depreciation and gratuity differences under the Income Tax Act and deferred tax from a surcharge rate change; full-year blended rate is 25.62%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-auto strategy (aerospace, actuators, robotics)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has identified civil aerospace (Airbus), small micromotors and actuators, and robotics in Europe; these are at an early pilot stage with industrial work for BHEL, and investment so far is mainly human resources.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not fully scale up on Royal Enfield, and is the 20,000-unit potential realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will add capacity only once volumes are proven, since the customer runs a multi-supplier strategy; the relationship is only a few months old.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY28 and FY29 capex will be announced around January; capex is a regular feature of the gear business.

risks_watch: Q1 effective tax rate of about 47% versus a 25.62% full-year guide; watch for normalisation in Q2.

Heat treatment commissioning timeline (October-December 2026 commissioning, January 2027 trial): any slip affects capacity and energy-cost exposure, since the current LPG setup is exposed to the energy crisis that began March 2026.
BMW SOP sign-off on 24 October 2026 and the ZF X5 ramp, where the peak has moved to 2030.
Royal Enfield ramp from about 8,000 sets per month toward the 10,000 nomination, with the multi-supplier risk noted by management.
Scope 2 emissions from the Noida unit and corporate office (321 tonnes in Q1); scope 1 is 73% LPG and 23% DG sets.
Management declined to disclose domestic pricing, realisation per kit and the share of Royal Enfield business it holds.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹108.7 crore in Q1 FY26, about +22%
about +18% YoY; margin cited as 25.11% to 27.29% (about 181-190 bps expansion per analyst)
Management cited current and deferred tax changes; FY27 blended rate guided at 25.62%

544469|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 pre-sales rose 567% YoY to INR409 crores and PAT grew 77% to INR46 crores at a 34.5% margin.
544469|2026-06.overview: Sri Lotus reported strong Q1 FY27 growth: pre-sales INR409 crores, collections INR150 crores (+115% YoY), revenue INR132 crores (+116%), and EBITDA INR48 crores (36.4% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crores pre-sales and 55-60% revenue and PAT growth. A new Juhu commercial redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) was won, and the company reported a net cash balance sheet of INR623 crores. Q&A surfaced some inconsistencies on launch timing and the split of Q1 pre-sales between new and existing launches.

segments.name: Residential redevelopment (Mumbai ultra-luxury)
segments.commentary: Core focus; 17 of 22 pipeline projects are redevelopment-led. Management says micro-market pricing is 10-15% above other developers, with 5-10% price rises seen over the past year.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Two commercial projects in the pipeline; Juhu commercial-cum-retail redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) won, expected to start next year after approvals and take 3-4 years to complete.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance maintained at INR1,800-2,000 crores; management said it will 'easily achieve' INR1,800 crores.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guidance of 55-60% maintained.
EBITDA margin guidance 35-40% and PAT margin 25-30% stated in the prepared remarks; in Q&A the CEO quoted EBITDA margin of 33-36%, a discrepancy.
FY27 cash collections target of about INR1,000 crores, supported by billing on Arcadian and Varun (each about 90% complete) and Amalfi (60-70%) by year-end.

Four further launches in FY27 with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crores: Lotus Sky Plaza (Oshiwara, about INR1,500 crores, H1-end or early Q3), Lotus Odyssey (Bandstand, about INR1,000 crores, Q4), Lotus Portofino (Versova, about INR500 crores, within 3-4 months), Lotus Aurelia (Napean Sea Road, INR600-700 crores).
Gift City project: mixed-use approvals (commercial, retail, residential) expected by end-2026, with construction to start after approvals.
Promoter stake about 82%; management targets dilution to 75% or below within the remaining two years of a three-year window, with no investor discussions yet.
capex_capacity: Two projects launched in Q1 FY27: Lotus Trident (Andheri West) and Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi), together GDV of INR1,350 crores; Aquaria company GDV about INR800 crores (saleable, excluding tenant areas), starting price about INR85,000 per sq ft.
Varun: plinth just completed, about 20 slabs; RCC work targeted by January and 90% of work by March.
Arcadian and Varun targeted at 90% of project cost and Amalfi at 60-70% by end-FY27.

Juhu commercial redevelopment: plot over 5,000 sq m; start next year after plan approvals, 3-4 years to complete. Part of the area to be rehoused for existing tenants, remainder for commercial pipeline; no rental retention decided.
Of the INR550 crores earmarked for subsidiary projects (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun), INR271 crores deployed as of 30 June 2026. Net IPO proceeds about INR732 crores after INR792 crores fresh issue.
demand_pricing: Q1 pre-sales of INR409 crores: management said only about INR25 crores came from the two new launches; the remainder came from projects launched in FY26 and earlier. Trident already reported about INR150 crores of sales within one month, in July-August.
Management said about INR400-plus crores of sales came from Trident, Aquaria and Celestia over the last two quarters.
Sales pace: 20-30% of inventory sold at launch, then about 30% of stock offloaded per year over a roughly three-year build cycle.
Brand campaign across 11 Mumbai coastal projects is ongoing; sales and marketing spend about 1% of pre-sales, which management expects to be offset by lower brokerage.
Management cited Mumbai luxury housing demand growth of more than 11% while the broader market moderated; constrained supply in Worli, Bandra and South Mumbai.
Versova: three existing sea-facing projects with more society talks under way.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR409 crore pre-sales support the INR2,000 crore FY27 guidance, and what supports 55-60% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO Sanjay Jain said the company is confident of easily achieving the INR1,800 crore pre-sales guidance, citing four new launches and strong response to Trident, Aquaria and Celestia.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and GDV of the upcoming launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Sky Plaza (Oshiwara, about INR1,500 crores) at H1-end or start of Q3; Lotus Odyssey (Bandstand, about INR1,000 crores) in Q4; Lotus Portofino (Versova, about INR500 crores) within 3-4 months; Lotus Aurelia (Napean Sea Road, INR600-700 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Juhu project details, margin and rental plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is more than 5,000 sq m plot in middle Juhu with existing shops and offices to be rehoused; no rental retention for this project. EBITDA around 40% and PAT 25-30% expected, which management said it will achieve or beat.

qa_highlights.question: Gap between Q1 pre-sales split and launch-driven sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Rakesh Gupta said about INR25 crores came from the two new launches, with the balance from FY26 and earlier launches. The CEO had earlier cited Trident's INR150 crores within one month, which relates to July-August rather than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Cash collection goal and EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Collection target about INR1,000 crores this year as billing rises on Arcadian, Varun and Amalfi. CEO said EBITDA margin is in the 33-36% range, which differs from the 35-40% guidance in the prepared remarks.

qa_highlights.question: Price increases and premium versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Price rises of 5-10% over the past year. Pricing about 10-15% above other developers in the same micro-markets, per the CEO.

qa_highlights.question: Leverage plans and net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is about 10% of GDV in redevelopment. Management cited total GDV of about INR18,000 crores and net worth of about INR1,900 crores, with annual net worth additions expected.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter stake dilution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter stake about 82%; management said there are three years to reach 75% or below, with two years remaining, but no investor discussions yet.

544469|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 pre-sales rose 83% YoY to INR470 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR107 crore at a 39.9% margin.
544469|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong Q2 and H1 FY27 growth in pre-sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with margins above 38%. Three redevelopment projects were added in the quarter, adding an estimated INR2,700-2,800 crore GDV, taking the pipeline to 24 projects and about INR20,000 crore GDV. Collections were weaker at INR60 crore in Q2 and INR209 crore in H1, which management attributed to construction-linked billing and expects to improve in H2. Analysts focused on collections, the INR300 crore business development outflow, Prabhadevi sales traction and project timeline slippage.

segments.name: Lotus Trident (Andheri West, luxury commercial)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR178 crore pre-sales in its first full quarter after end-June launch, about 35% of sales sold within three months per management. Management guided EBITDA margin of 33-35%.

segments.name: Residential luxury projects
segments.commentary: Celestia reported 36% sales within six months of launch. Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi) reported healthy inquiries, but Lotus Prabhadevi (GDV ~INR800 crore) contributed no pre-sales in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance reiterated at INR1,800-2,000 crore.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guided at 55-60% over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 35-40% and PAT margin at 25-30%.
Four H2 FY27 launches planned: Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino and Lotus Odyssey, combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore; about 90% approvals in place.
Project-level surplus estimated at about INR9,500 crore over the development cycle; projects expected to complete over the next 4-4.5 years.
Management expects H2 collections to be much better than H1 as projects reach plinth level; FY28 collection guidance to be given at the start of FY28.
Amara and Athena expected to receive OC in FY27 (Amara within the quarter or by March; Athena before March).
capex_capacity: Pipeline of 24 ongoing and upcoming projects, aggregate GDV ~INR20,000 crore, of which 19 are redevelopment-led.
Business development: Lotus Impressa (Shivaji Park, Dadar West), Lotus Stellar (Versova) and Lotus Supremus (Juhu) added in Q2.
INR550 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for subsidiary (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun); INR305 crore deployed as of 30 Sep 2026 of INR732 crore net proceeds.
Upfront premium paid to government for new projects in Q2, which management said is to save costs and secure supplier discounts; new projects typically need 8-10% of project cost to start.
GIFT City plot of 5.5 acres on Sabarmati riverfront; expected 1.3-1.5 million sq ft mixed-use development subject to town planning scheme approval.
Lotus Monarch timeline pushed out by one year due to society, trust, Charity Commissioner and government approvals; Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended.
demand_pricing: Management says the luxury segment is less sensitive to RBI's 25 bps repo hike to 5.5% (first hike since early 2023); buyers rely less on home loans.
Mumbai H1 CY2026 sales of homes priced above INR10 crore reached a record INR18,500 crore; prime residential prices up 6.2% YoY per management.
Management says prices have risen across almost all projects in H1 and will rise further as construction progresses if the market supports it.
Management says it is the only suburban player to have completed a commercial redevelopment (Arc One), and has 2-3 more commercial redevelopment projects; about five commercial projects in portfolio.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria) pricing set at a premium, with 270-degree sea view and ~200 m Art Deco tower; management says no pushback, pre-sales expected to show in next two quarters.
Collections as a share of pre-sales: management said completion-stage projects carry 90-95% balance due, and expects 95-100% collection on three projects completing next year.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins above 35% during expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited net debt-free status (no interest burden), minimal marketing spend, a 2.5-3.5 year project cycle that speeds fund deployment, and premium pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for Trident and what is the commercial redevelopment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided Trident EBITDA margin at 33-35%, in line with guidance. Management expects commercial redevelopment to carry sustainable margins and cited 2-3 more projects.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections catch up with pre-sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said collections are construction-linked: about 5-10% at launch and about 25% at plinth. Of about INR800 crore H1 pre-sales, INR200 crore was collected, and H2 should improve as two of three recent projects move past basement.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gives annual guidance only. It pointed to ~INR20,000 crore GDV and ~INR9,500 crore project surplus, with completion over the next 4-4.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did timelines shift for upcoming projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Monarch moved out by one year due to multiple approving bodies. Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended. Management says overall guidance is unchanged and new projects will replace slipped ones.

qa_highlights.question: Why no Prabhadevi pre-sales, and will the business development outflow constrain the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Prabhadevi is a new micromarket with marketing under way and results expected in two quarters. The INR300 crore outflow was upfront government fees and discounted supplier payments; management said cash is sufficient. Operating cash flow will stay negative in launch periods, though Arcadian is working-capital positive.

543331|2026-06.headline: Meghmani Organics Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 42% YoY to ~INR58 crore on revenue down 12% to INR523 crore; TiO2 unit suspended.
543331|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue fell about 12% YoY to nearly INR523 crore on subdued export and domestic offtake, with volumes down about 17% per management. Profitability improved: standalone EBITDA rose 16% to about INR94 crore and consolidated net profit rose 280% to INR48.2 crore, with consolidated EBITDA margin at 18% versus 10.9% a year earlier. Management attributed roughly 5-6 percentage points of the Pigment margin gain to better realisation and the balance to efficiency. The titanium dioxide unit (Kilburn Chemicals) remained suspended because sulfur-linked raw material costs rose sharply and anti-dumping duty was withdrawn; it posted about INR3 crore negative EBITDA in the quarter.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue; revenue INR391 crore, EBITDA INR77.8 crore (19.9% margin); production ~8,880 MT at ~63% capacity utilisation.

segments.name: Pigment
segments.commentary: About 25% of revenue; revenue INR131 crore, EBITDA INR15.9 crore (~12.1% margin); production ~3,233 MT at 39% utilisation. Management guides to INR500-600 crore annualised revenue and ~10% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Crop Nutrition
segments.commentary: Positive contribution to revenue and profitability; no figures disclosed. Nano DAP, Nano NPK and Nano Zinc added to Nano Urea; management targets about INR100 crore from nano fertilisers over 2-3 years.

segments.name: Titanium Dioxide (Kilburn Chemicals)
segments.commentary: Operations suspended for commercial unviability; negative EBITDA of ~INR3 crore in Q1. Management estimates annual losses of ~INR10-12 crore if suspension continues through the year.

guidance_outlook: Pigment revenue expected at INR500-600 crore annualised; utilisation to stay around 40-50%, with EBITDA margin targeted near 10%.
Crop Protection targeted to grow double digit in top line over 2-3 years, with margins at or above the industry 15-17% range.
Peak potential: Crop Protection revenue INR2,500-3,000 crore at 85-90% utilisation (per management, not formal guidance).
Nano fertiliser revenue of about INR100 crore expected over 2-3 years.
Finance cost to fall: about INR130 crore of debt repayment this year at ~7% average cost; no heavy capex planned for 1-2 years, so debt will keep reducing.
Overall FY27 blended EBITDA margin estimated at about 12-13% by management.
capex_capacity: Crop Protection utilisation ~63% and Pigment ~39% in Q1 FY27; management says Pigment demand is weak amid overcapacity, so utilisation will not be pushed higher.
No major capex planned in Pigment; the company is not doing big capex for the next one to two years.
Titanium dioxide plant remains suspended with no restart timeline; restart depends on sulfur/sulfuric acid prices normalising and anti-dumping duty being restored.

Amalgamation of two wholly owned subsidiaries: scheme filed in April 2026, second motion filed, awaiting NCLT hearing date. Pooling-of-interests accounting; benefits expected from closing multiple stock points.
demand_pricing: Customers bought on spot basis with little channel inventory at distributors or customers, per management.
Latin America was the main source of volume decline; pricing pressure from input cost increases led management to avoid pushing volume where realisations were resisted.
Management said it could not reliably predict pricing for Q2 and H2 given volatility, and expects prices to fall only if raw material costs fall.
Pigment industry has seen some capacity cuts by peers due to high costs and weak demand; no consolidation expected.
Pigment demand recovery expected after the prior-year tariff impact faded from 1 April.

qa_highlights.question: Will Pigment utilisation improve from low levels, and what is the revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation may stay around 40-50%; management expects Pigment revenue of INR500-600 crore annualised, with the focus on profitability over volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 margin bridge in Pigment (3% to 12%)?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5-6 percentage points came from better realisation, with the balance from operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: How much EBITDA is lost from the suspended TiO2 plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 negative EBITDA was about INR3 crore; management agreed annual losses would be about INR10-12 crore if the suspension continues through the year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the finance cost reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Shift to INR borrowing at lower rates, no foreign-currency MTM losses, and debt repayment; MTM impact is expected to be minimal going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the 12% revenue decline between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume fell about 17%; management did not give a clear price figure, saying it prioritised margin and product mix over top line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the subsidiary amalgamation and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Scheme filed in April with second motion done after creditor approvals; awaiting NCLT hearing. Expected benefit is cost savings from fewer stock points, not a top-line change.

risks_watch: Pricing volatility: management could not predict Q2 or H2 realisations, and sulfur (over 80% sourced from the Middle East) costs are elevated.
Pigment overcapacity and utilisation at 39% limit volume recovery; the 10% EBITDA margin target is well below the Q1 12.1% level.
Titanium dioxide restart depends on raw material normalisation and anti-dumping duty; no timeline given.
Latin America demand softness and realisation resistance from customers.
Pending NCLT approval for subsidiary amalgamation.
Management's Crop Protection double-digit growth and nano-fertiliser targets are not quantified for the next quarter.
543331|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and margins but cautious on near-term demand, attributing softness to macro uncertainty and volatile input costs. Management was evasive on quarterly pricing and volume outlook, and it corrected an analyst's guidance figures on the call.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR555 crore (ST INR474 crore, LT INR81 crore)
~INR732 crore (ST INR477 crore, LT INR256 crore)

543910|2026-06.headline: AVG Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose 29.98% to INR6.46 crore on revenue growth of 5.97% to INR132.48 crore; FY27 guidance 15-20% revenue growth.
543910|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 5.97% YoY to INR132.48 crore, while PBT grew 24.42% to INR8.71 crore and PAT grew 29.98% to INR6.46 crore, with PBT and PAT margins expanding 98 bps and 89 bps. Management attributed the profit growth to fleet productivity, asset utilisation and cost discipline. The company completed a rights issue raising INR52.93 crore in Q1, secured a 100-vehicle Haldiram contract, and formed a JV (Carbonlite Logistics) with Baidyanath Group for LNG/EV transport. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15-20%, while noting Q1 is seasonally a softer quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: Rights issue proceeds received in Q1

financial_highlights.change: Record date September 18, 2026; AGM book closure Sept 19-25, 2026

segments.name: Dedicated / contract logistics
segments.commentary: Management cited dedicated vehicles, cold chain, reefer trucks and warehousing/factory management as higher-margin segments with less competition. Company is also doing customer warehouse operations.

segments.name: Liquid logistics
segments.commentary: Two tanker trains already purchased; a third to be taken on lease for about one year. Management said liquor freight rates are higher than normal goods, supporting better margins.

segments.name: Green transport (CNG/LNG/EV)
segments.commentary: Management expects lower operating costs versus diesel; LNG contract for 100 vehicles and 30 EV vehicles ordered, with a further 70 EV under discussion. JV Carbonlite Logistics expected to start operations from October 1, 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of approximately 15-20%: management split this as 7-8% from new business and 8-10% from existing customers via expansions and new contracts.
FY27 capex planned at about INR50-60 crore, supplemented by operating leases for additional fleet, particularly EVs.
Management expects margins to improve in FY27 as FY26 H2 capex assets contribute for a full year; depreciation will rise with the new assets.
Target to add about 200 vehicles by March 2027 (CNG 50-60, LNG 100 under Haldiram-related contract, EV 30 ordered plus 70 in discussion) — as stated by management.

Haldiram, Nagpur: 100 dedicated vehicles; 40 deployed as of August 21, 2026, remaining 60 expected within one to two months; customer has asked for another 100 vehicles by December 2026 (not yet contracted).
Operations of Carbonlite Logistics expected to start from October 1, 2026.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR62 crore; FY27 planned capex about INR50-60 crore, with some fleet to be taken on operating lease instead of purchase.
Fleet and warehousing footprint cited: more than 3,000 owned and hired vehicles, over 70 branches, more than 7.4 lakh sq ft warehousing.
Running-kilometre target: minimum 15-20% increase from about 1 lakh km per month, i.e. toward 1.2 lakh km per month; August reportedly saw the incremental growth begin.
Most FY26 capex was in the second half of FY26, so assets contribute for a full year in FY27.
demand_pricing: Haldiram contract indicates large FMCG customer demand; festive season (Ganesh Chaturthi to Diwali/Durga Puja) cited as demand driver.
Management said liquid logistics has strong demand and limited organised competition.
Customers are seeking cleaner transport; steel, metal, cement and FMCG companies cited as LNG/EV prospects.
Fuel escalation clauses in a significant portion of contracts help manage fuel price changes.
Management noted Q4 and Q3 are typically stronger quarters than Q1 and Q2 for volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook after 6% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15-20% growth, with 7-8% from new business and 8-10% from existing customers, and said new fleet added in FY26 will contribute a full year in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental revenue and PAT can the rights issue generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to attribute revenue or PAT to the rights issue alone; proceeds are mainly for working capital, with overall incremental revenue expected from new contracts and fleet utilisation. Depreciation will rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60 crore of capex is planned (also referenced as INR50-60 crore), with leasing evaluated to balance the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Haldiram contract deployment on track and what is next?
qa_highlights.answer: 40 of 100 vehicles deployed on August 21, 2026; remaining 60 within one to two months. Customer has asked for another 100 vehicles by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Are liquid logistics tankers being bought or leased, and will margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Two tanker trains bought; one more on lease for about a year. Management expects margin improvement from FY26 capex and higher utilisation, and says liquid, EV and LNG segments carry higher margins.

qa_highlights.question: What does the in-house real-time tracking software do?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the GPS/dashcam platform gives customers real-time location and ETA, and is aimed at improving asset utilisation; target is 15-20% higher monthly running from about 1 lakh km.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 6% in Q1 versus 15-20% full-year target; back-half weighting is required to meet guidance.
Depreciation will rise with new fleet; margin expansion depends on utilisation and running efficiency.
Capex and fleet targets are inconsistent in the call (INR50 crore vs INR60 crore; ~200 vehicles by March 2027) and need clarification.
Haldiram second 100-vehicle order is not yet contracted.
Carbonlite start-up on October 1, 2026 and leasing-based financing are dependent on third parties.
Net debt of about INR173 crore (March 2026) and the usage of rights-issue proceeds for working capital.
543910|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and margins, with repeated emphasis on disciplined capital deployment. Answers on rights-issue impact and the fleet/capex numbers were less precise and somewhat inconsistent, and the Haldiram answers were repetitive.

544328|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore, driven by tractors (+36.29%) while cranes were flat at ₹52.86 crore.
544328|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore and EBITDA rose 10.84% to ₹13.09 crore. Tractor revenue grew 36.29% to ₹52.08 crore, while crane revenue was flat at ₹52.86 crore, which management attributed to the Tier III to Tier V emission norm transition and full utilisation of the existing crane plant. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 20–25% overall revenue growth and 12.5–13% standalone EBITDA margin. The new Bhud plant is targeted for commercial production by end-November 2026, with tower crane production planned for the new line.

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.08 crore, up 36.29% YoY. Management guides 25–30% FY27 growth; utilisation of ~12,000-unit capacity is about 35–40%, and no capacity addition planned. Dealer network about 225.

segments.name: Cranes
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.86 crore, flat YoY. Existing plant at full capacity (~1,000–1,200 units); guidance 15–20% FY27 growth from existing plant. Dealer network about 25, stagnant for three quarters. New Bhud plant capacity 3,600 units.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth maintained at ~20–25% (existing plant only; new plant contribution mainly assumed in Q4).
Tractor revenue growth ~25–30% in FY27; management says 30%-plus over 3–5 years.
Crane revenue growth ~15–20% in FY27 from existing plant.
Standalone EBITDA margin 12.5–13% for FY27; consolidated margin said to be similar to last year (~14–15% per analyst’s reading).

New Bhud plant: commercial production targeted by end-November 2026; machinery expected in October. First year utilisation ~30% (Q1 of operations), 35–40% next quarter, ~40–45% average in FY28 (1,500–1,800 cranes).
Crane price hike taken; further price hike planned in coming months; management expects cost pass-through from Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: New Bhud crane plant: 3,600-unit capacity; civil work in progress; almost all major machines ready; commercial production targeted by end-November 2026.
Tower crane: first prototype passed testing; first lot of 10 machines targeted within Q2 FY27, subject to imported components; some tower crane numbers to be built at the old factory.
Capex funds: ~₹45 crore still held in bank; management says it will be fully deployed by March, possibly by buying 6–8 of 10 planned machines and deferring the rest by up to three months.
Tractor capacity ~12,000 units; no addition planned. Crane machine shop utilisation ~80–85%; crane assembly ~30–35%.
demand_pricing: Crane dealers ~25 (stagnant for three quarters vs. 50-plus target cited by analyst); management plans ~20–25 more dealers within six to12 months of new plant start; Shubham cited a roadmap of ~60-plus dealers nationally, taking one to one-and-a-half years.
Some existing dealers being replaced to match performance expectations; management says working in only ~20–25% of the addressable area.
Tractor dealers ~225; growth tied to dealer development, retail financing, and village-level demos.
Barota Finance finances ~20% of new Indo Farm tractors; refinances old tractors of all brands.
Crane competitors cited: Escorts Construction (premium pricing) and one Faridabad-based peer at similar pricing. Peer ACE grew more than 20% per analyst.
Management says tractor price hikes will follow industry; crane price hike already taken.

qa_highlights.question: Has the crane input cost increase been passed on, and will margins normalise from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should hold from Q2 as demand improves; the Tier III to V transition took about three quarters to stabilise, and cost increases can now be passed on.

qa_highlights.question: Why is crane dealer count stagnant at 25, and what is the plan to absorb new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Dealers to be added once capacity is in place; some dealers replaced. Roadmap of ~60-plus dealers nationally, taking one to one-and-a-half years. FY28 needs ~20–25 dealers to sell 1,500–1,800 cranes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the crane sales volume and YoY volume growth in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Not provided on the call; management said figures would be shared by email via the Finance Head.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tractor utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Tractor utilisation ~35–40%; assembly ~30–35%; machine shop ~80–85% because many crane components are made in-house.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone guidance 12.5–13%; consolidated said to move on similar lines to last year, which the analyst interpreted as 14–15%; management confirmed the analyst’s reading.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹45 crore capex cash be used by Q3 to start commercialisation by January?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may buy 6–8 of 10 machines and defer up to three months; full deployment by March. Commercial production still targeted for November.

qa_highlights.question: Can crane growth of 15–20% be achieved with existing capacity before the new plant starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management confirmed existing capacity is sufficient for 15–20% growth until the new plant starts.

risks_watch: Crane growth: Q1 flat; FY27 guidance 15–20% depends on July–August demand recovery and dealer additions.
Bhud plant timing: November commercial production depends on machinery arriving in October and on imported tower crane components.
Dealer quality and ramp-up: management says new dealers take 6–18 months; utilisation of new plant guided at 30% in year one.
Tractor volume growth of 25–30% contingent on dealer build-out, financing, and village-level demand; utilisation still ~35–40%.
Price hikes: crane price increase taken; further hikes depend on demand and input costs; tractor pricing follows industry.

500472|2026-06.headline: SKF India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR 5.9 billion, with EBITDA flat YoY and up 540 bps QoQ.
500472|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR 5.9 billion, up 27% YoY and down 1% QoQ, while sales of products were INR 5.5 billion, up about 22% YoY and down 0.7% QoQ. Growth was volume-led (+22% YoY) with price/mix adding 5.6% on a QoQ basis. EBITDA was broadly flat YoY (+7 bps) and up 540 bps QoQ as one-off demerger-related factors in Q4 FY26 faded. Capex of about INR 500 crore is planned, with INR 170-180 crore expected this year.

financial_highlights.change: About 1% lower YoY; about 6.5% higher QoQ

segments.commentary: About 62% of Q1 sales. Within OEM: 2-wheelers ~54%, passenger vehicles ~31%, commercial vehicles ~15%. Management said historical ranges are 48-52%, 28-30% and 11-12% respectively.

segments.name: Vehicle aftermarket (distribution)
segments.commentary: About 20% of sales. Volumes plateaued or declined slightly; discounts given in the last two months are not expected to continue.

Portfolio rationalisation (plants and loss-making businesses) expected to have no major impact on FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines and sizing of EV orders, and how much EV non-wheel revenue is there?

Commodity inflation pass-through timing and amount remain undisclosed, with a 1-2 quarter lag.

EV revenue timing depends on developmental platforms ramping from 2027-2028; no quantified revenue yet.

Capex of INR 500 crore plan with timing slippage risk into FY29.

544305|2026-06.headline: MobiKwik posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR76 million, its third straight profitable quarter, with payments GMV up 50% YoY to INR587 billion.
544305|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as its most profitable quarter yet, with PAT of INR76 million and EBITDA of INR158 million, up INR470 million YoY. Payments gross profit rose 31% YoY to INR777 million and financial services gross profit grew 5.6x to INR433 million. Lending disbursements dipped in Q1, while payments revenue fell as card-linked categories were paused under regulatory pressure and UPI (near-zero take rate) grew. Management targets full-year PAT of about INR400 million and EBITDA of about INR750 million including other income, and is scaling a merchant acquiring business that is still loss-making.

financial_highlights.change: Swing of INR495 million vs Q1 FY26; up from INR45 million in Q4 per management
+50% YoY; 14th straight quarter of payments GMV growth

segments.name: Payments
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR777 million (+31% YoY) on revenue of about INR208 crore versus INR59 crore a year ago on similar revenue; net payments take rate 13-15 bps in recent quarters, guided at 12-14 bps long term. Zaakpay (payment gateway) GMV INR25.6 billion; revenue not disclosed.

segments.name: Financial services (lending)
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR433 million (5.6x YoY). Net financial services margin 4.1% in Q3, 5.4% in Q4 and 5.9% in Q1; management guides 4.5-5.5% long term. About 18% of gross lending revenue came from write-backs on past books (about INR16 crore).

segments.name: Merchant (Zaakpay online + offline acquiring)
segments.commentary: Merchant GMV INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ. Business is loss-making with an expected full-year burn of INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted for FY28. Management expects 10x ramp over two years.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PAT target of about INR40 crore (INR400 million) and EBITDA of about INR75 crore (INR750 million) including other income; management said it is 'fairly confident'.
Lending disbursements to rise from about INR700 crore per quarter to INR1,000 crore per quarter; management says Q2 is already running at that rate.
Consumer payments revenue expected to grow 5-6% QoQ; merchant revenue expected to grow about 25% QoQ.
Merchant business burn for FY27 capped at INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted in FY28.
Long-term net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps; net financial services margin guided at 4.5-5.5%.
Paused card-linked payment categories expected to be relaunched in Q2 FY27.
Digital lending business transfer to wholly-owned subsidiary expected to close in August 2026; own NBFC launch still 'some time away'.
capex_capacity: About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains available for buying more merchant devices (soundboxes, EDC, QR); management does not expect more than this needed for FY27.
Merchant ramp: 10x over two years targeted; merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue not disclosed yet.
Employee benefit expense rose from INR46 crore in Q4 to INR53 crore in Q1, mostly merchant business manpower; expected to rise 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.
Lending partner base: nine major NBFC partners in Q1 (10-15 total); top-three lender concentration cut from about 91% (Q2-Q3 FY26) to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1.
demand_pricing: Payments revenue dipped because high-take-rate card-linked categories (credit and debit) were paused, while low or zero take-rate UPI and merchant volumes grew; management attributes the pause to regulatory guardrail changes on categories such as rent and education.
Wallet transactions up 68% YoY but GMV up only 24%, as users shift to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments on which no PPI MDR is earned.

UPI: MobiKwik's transactions grew 5x faster than the industry; ranked 13th in NPCI UPI stack rankings and described as second fastest-growing TPAP. No MDR on UPI; PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI.

Lending: Q1 disbursements dipped; 60% of loans went to repeat customers and credit quality improved 25%. Cross-sell from about 96 million engaged non-lending users targeted at INR150-250 crore extra disbursement per quarter; AI funnel engine targeted at about INR100 crore per quarter.

543591|2026-06.headline: Dreamfolks Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR39 crore (from INR52.6 crore in Q4) and adjusted EBITDA was negative INR16.4 crore, hit by Middle East war and an MMG payment.
543591|2026-06.overview: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was INR39 crore, down from INR52.6 crore in the previous quarter and well below INR348.9 crore in Q1 FY26. Management attributed the sequential drop mainly to lower global lounge traffic from the Middle East conflict, partly offset by India business. Gross profit was negative INR0.9 crore, reflecting an upfront minimum guarantee payment for global lounge expansion, and PAT was negative INR13.8 crore. Cash rose to INR193.3 crore on collections, and net worth stood at INR300.4 crore. Management guided to adjusted EBITDA breakeven by next year, while holding the earlier H2 FY28 commitment.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR52.6 crore in Q4 FY26; vs INR348.9 crore in Q1 FY26
Impacted by upfront minimum guarantee payment for global lounges
vs negative INR14.4 crore in Q4 FY26; vs INR30.5 crore in Q1 FY26
vs negative INR13 crore in Q4 FY26; vs INR21.3 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR149 crore in previous quarter

financial_highlights.metric: Non-airport lounge services share of top line

segments.name: Global lounges (incl. ETT, Dubai)
segments.commentary: Numbers dropped sharply versus last quarter due to Middle East war impact on traffic. Management expects recovery over a couple of quarters; APAC wins include Singapore, Indonesia (live) and a second Singapore bank (integration underway).

segments.name: Railway lounges (Ten11 Hospitality)
segments.commentary: Network covers 100% of the country's railway stations per management. Capex per lounge quoted at INR1.5 crore to INR5-6 crore, plus security deposits and advances to railways. Management cites INR500 crore opportunity over 4-5 years.

segments.name: Golf
segments.commentary: Access to more than 80 golf outlets in India and over 860 international golf courses; named as a key growth category alongside global lounges.

segments.name: DF Club membership (Club 2.0)
segments.commentary: Early stage; membership sales growing quarter-on-quarter. Average realisation about INR30,000 across three tiers (black tier at INR50,000); contribution described as very small versus total revenue.

guidance_outlook: Adjusted EBITDA breakeven targeted by next year (FY28); management said it would stick to the earlier H2 FY28 commitment and would announce earlier if achieved.
Global lounges, golf and other services expected to grow over a couple of quarters once traffic normalises.
No further minimum guarantee payments expected going forward, so margins should turn positive per CFO.
Margins on ETT global business currently similar to prior India lounge margins; management expects margins to improve over time for global.
Payroll cost in Q1 expected to continue at similar levels in coming quarters; ESOP cost for full year only INR14 lakh.
capex_capacity: Network: more than 1,100 global airport lounges at quarter end, with more than 70 new outlets added in the quarter.
Railway lounges: capex INR1.5 crore to INR5-6 crore per lounge depending on city and size (from about 2,000 sq ft up to 14,000 sq ft), plus security deposits and advances to railways.
Railway lounge opportunity of INR500 crore over 4-5 years, linked by management to government railway modernisation investment plans.
Ten11 Hospitality acquisition gives more direct operational control over railway lounges.
demand_pricing: Revenue decline attributed to lower international traffic from the Middle East war; India outbound-to-Middle East traffic was a large contributor.
India business partially compensating for Middle East shortfall, per CFO.
Management said the Middle East business is down and it cannot expand there currently.
Banking partners shifting to personalised, segment-based benefit bundles; a boarding-pass-linked travel benefit programme launched for a large bank's premium card users.
Several major bank programmes went live in the quarter across global lounges, global meet and assist, airport transfer and premium members-only clubs.
Cost of services moves in line with revenue; management says gross margins are structurally set by the business mix.

qa_highlights.question: Railway lounge unit economics: capex and payback period?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex ranges from INR1.5 crore to INR5-6 crore per lounge depending on city and size, excluding security deposits and advances to railways. No payback period was given.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR500 crore railway lounge opportunity over 4-5 years built up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management tied it to the government's announced railway investment plan over 3-4 years and said it had calculated the figure; no station or per-customer assumptions were shared.

qa_highlights.question: Are ETT margins structurally better than India lounge margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said they are in a similar range today, after advances to lounge operators, and that global margins should improve over time.

qa_highlights.question: Quarters to bottom-line breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said breakeven by next year, with growth from global lounges, golf and other services over a couple of quarters; new bank services need at least a year to build awareness.

qa_highlights.question: Club 2.0 paid membership count, ARPU and retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales are still early, with three tiers (white, orange, black); average price about INR30,000 and black at INR50,000. Numbers not disclosed yet, and management will publish them once material.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cash rise by about INR44 crore and why did revenue fall from INR56 crore to INR39 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited collections of about INR40-plus crore from multiple customers. Revenue fell because of lower Middle East-linked outbound traffic from the war; the CFO said Q1 was better than Q4 on the global mix in some respects.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters increase stake or are strategic investors being sought?
qa_highlights.answer: No promoter stake increase is planned for now; focus is on rebuilding the business first, with strategic investors considered after performance improves.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict continuing to suppress global lounge and outbound traffic.
Gross margin and EBITDA recovery depends on global lounge volumes and removal of minimum guarantee payments.
Receivables: management did not disclose the June 2026 debtor balance or ageing (>90 days) on the call; the company said collections from banks are strong.
Breakeven timing (FY28) and reliance on newer services (Club 2.0, golf, DF Club) that are at an early stage.
Railway lounge capex and deposits required before returns; INR500 crore opportunity is management's estimate, not guidance.
Analyst question on cash and debt movements (INR134 crore figure cited by an analyst) was not directly reconciled by management.
