Management attributed the decline to the Middle East war and repeatedly deferred on specifics such as debtor balances, Club 2.0 membership counts and strategic investors.

500413|2026-06.headline: Thomas Cook Q1 FY27 consolidated total income fell 12% YoY to INR 21,530 million and PBT fell 21% to INR 885 million, driven by Middle East exposure.
500413|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income was INR 21,530 million, down 12% YoY, with PBT of INR 885 million, down 21%, mainly from Desert Adventures and DEI in the Middle East. Excluding the GCC subsidiaries, group EBIT grew 8%, and India businesses (forex, MICE, corporate travel, domestic) were stable to growing. Sterling Holidays reported its best quarter ever, with revenue up 21% and EBITDA up 21%. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, though it said H2 should be better than H1 if conditions hold.

segments.name: Foreign exchange
segments.commentary: Segment revenue +6% YoY, EBIT +8%, EBIT margin 45.3%. Retail turnover +8% YoY vs industry travel forex decline of ~8% (LRS Apr-May); education turnover +36%, digital penetration 23.5% vs 20.4%.

segments.name: Travel (B2B and B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 17,106 million, -14% YoY; EBIT INR 405 million, -50%. Domestic +29%, short-haul +6% (+21% excluding Middle East), long-haul sales -28%. MICE +14% to INR 5,420 million; DMS -31% to INR 5,422 million with Desert Adventures revenue -89%.

segments.name: Sterling Holidays
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1.7 billion (+21%), EBITDA over INR 620 million (37% margin), PBT margin 28% (+200 bps). Occupancy 77% (+700 bps), ARR INR 7,809 (+10%), RevPAR +20%; net debt-free with cash above INR 3.7 billion.

segments.name: DEI (Digital Imaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,307 million vs INR 2,097 million; EBIT swung to INR -152 million from INR 106 million. About 50% of global business is in the Middle East; China site closures and Bahamas contract end added pressure. Net assets employed INR 243 crore.

segments.name: Desert Adventures (GCC)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 89% YoY; management estimated its EBIT impact at roughly INR 8-9 crore (about INR 90 million), not confirmed. Cost base did not flex as fast as volumes.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 guidance given; management said it is too early to forecast full-year outcome and cannot confirm double-digit earnings growth.
Travel EBIT margin working range of about 4-5%; long-term take rates across B2B and B2C around 14-15%.
If conditions remain constant, H2 FY27 expected to be better than H1.
DEI cost optimisation benefits expected in Q2 and Q3 FY27; Middle East recovery sub-20% in Apr-Jun, about 30-35% in July.
DEI long-term target: 20% ROE; normal-year DEI EBIT margin about 6-7% of sales.
Long-haul deficit narrowed from about 28-30% to slightly lower levels in recent weeks; July and early August conversion better than Apr-Jun.
capex_capacity: Sterling: over 78 resorts, hotels and retreats with nearly 3,800 rooms in 65+ destinations; visible pipeline of 35+ properties and more than 2,000 rooms; asset-right model of owned, leased and managed.
DEI: technology upgrade completed in recent years; management said ongoing capex is low and the platform should last 5-10 years; net assets INR 243 crore.
Forex: new counters at Delhi Airport Terminals 1 and 2; branch network being optimised; airports entered opportunistically, not as a strategy.
demand_pricing: Forex travel turnover declined alongside the industry, but education turnover grew 36% with NBFC partnerships and Study Buddy Card launch.
Corporate travel gross turnover above INR 7 billion, +15% YoY; net revenue INR 350 million, +7%; 7 new accounts added.
MICE: over 110 groups; 77% international and 23% domestic; demand deferred from earlier quarters translating into business in June.
Sterling ARR +10% to INR 7,809 and occupancy +700 bps, indicating demand ahead of supply additions.
Short-haul ATV is 20-25% lower than long-haul, creating a mix headwind on revenue.
Management said margins are under pressure from higher airline costs and forex; tactical pricing used to keep capacity engaged.
TCS rate cut to 5% has had no visible impact on pricing; management called it a cash outflow, not a price change.

qa_highlights.question: How did underlying outbound leisure demand trend in July and early August, and do short-haul destinations carry comparable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said July and early August conversion was better than Apr-Jun but too early to call a shift. Short-haul margins are similar to long-haul, though short-haul ticket values are 20-25% lower.

qa_highlights.question: Will Thomas Cook pursue more airport forex counters over branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Airports are opportunistic, not a strategy; entry is made only at commercially rewarding terms, as with Delhi Airport.

qa_highlights.question: DEI: what are capital employed, normalised EBIT and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Net assets INR 243 crore; normal-year EBIT margin 6-7%; target 20% ROE. Major technology upgrade done, with periodic upgrades roughly every 10-12 years.

qa_highlights.question: Travel FY27 topline and EBIT margin outlook, and the TCS impact on pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 guidance. Internal EBIT margin range 4-5%. Management said it saw no clear TCS pricing benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the double-digit earnings growth guidance still achievable, and what is the split of GCC subsidiary impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not confirm double-digit growth. DEI EBIT moved from INR 10 crore profit to INR 15 crore loss (INR 25 crore delta). Detailed numbers to be obtained from Investor Relations.

qa_highlights.question: Will DEI cost optimisation show in Q2 results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visible benefits in Q2 and Q3 FY27; revenue recovery in the Middle East will determine earnings quality.

544889|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR218 crores, while new-business opex drag of INR23 crores left consolidated EBITDA at INR45 crores.
544889|2026-06.overview: Symbiotec's first earnings call after its BSE/NSE listing reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR218 crores (+7% YoY), with API revenue of INR215 crores (+6% YoY, volume-led) and API EBITDA of INR66 crores (+9% YoY). Consolidated EBITDA was INR45 crores and net profit about INR14 crores, which management said understates underlying profitability because of INR23 crores of new-business opex and INR11 crores of depreciation that were previously capitalised as pre-operative expenses. No CDMO or injectable revenue was booked in the quarter, versus about INR33 crores of milestone revenue in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of roughly 20% revenue growth and 25% EBITDA growth, with a plus/minus 5% band, and pinned new-business revenue to milestones in H2 FY27 and commercial CDMO revenue to the next 6 to 12 months.

financial_highlights.change: About INR326 crores after IPO proceeds of INR142 crores and September-quarter capex

segments.name: API (steroid and hormone APIs)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR215 crores, +6% YoY, driven largely by volume; API EBITDA INR66 crores, +9% YoY; gross margin 60%+. Management says more than 90% of FY27 revenue comes from API. Capacity utilisation is about 70-80%.

segments.name: Biotech CDMO (fermentation)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27. Built on about 400 kL of large-scale fermentation at Ujjain, with signed 10-year take-or-pay with a US alternate-protein player and 5-year take-or-pay for insulin drug substance. Small revenues are guided for Q4 FY27 and meaningful revenues for FY28.

segments.name: Complex injectables (dual-chamber vials/bags)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27 (Q4 FY26 had about INR33 crores of milestone revenue across CDMO and injectables). First DCV ANDA filed in September 2026; second molecule ANDA planned for Q4 FY27. Term sheet with a large US pharma multinational; definitive agreement expected early Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% and EBITDA growth of about 25% on a consolidated basis, with a plus/minus 5% band citing global operating uncertainty.
PAT growth will be lower than EBITDA growth because of depreciation drag; cash PAT (PAT plus depreciation) growth is expected to be above 25%.
New-business opex of about INR23 crores and depreciation of about INR11 crores per quarter to run for the next two to three quarters.
Management expects the first couple of quarters to be lumpy, with a strong H2 FY27 from milestone cash flows (Q3/Q4) that management says will offset the new-business opex.
Insulin/biologics revenue expected to start early FY28, pending stability studies and DCGI approval.
Capex of INR200-250 crores per year for the next two to three years, funded by internal accruals and customer contributions.
capex_capacity: Cumulative investment of more than INR1,000 crores in the two new businesses, of which over INR500 crores is in biomanufacturing/biopharma fermentation.
Gross block in API about INR640 crores as of 30 June 2026; management cites INR800-900 crores of API revenue and asset turnover of about 1.5x.

Phase 0: existing 400 kL fermentation capacity, largely booked under current contracts. Phase 1: brownfield expansion of about 600 kL (about 4x the current capacity) with construction starting Q3 FY27 and 15-18 months to build.
DCV: five to six products developed and moving to plant-level validation; a second DCV line may be needed soon due to capacity constraints.
Mhow injectable facility is part of the roughly INR1,000 crores invested in new businesses.
demand_pricing: Management says demand and traction are very strong, with discussions with more than half a dozen potential customers, each seeking about 1 million litres of fermentation capacity.
Take-or-pay contracts are multi-million-dollar per customer; management declined to disclose per-litre pricing, minimum revenue or contract values, citing confidentiality.
Management guides to industry-level margins for complex injectables and CDMO: gross margin above 70% and EBITDA margin above 35%, and expects Symbiotec to be in a similar range.

API gross margin guided at around 60% (currently above 60%), with EBITDA margin near 30%. Management attributes margin strength to backward integration (make vs buy) and mix shift toward regulated markets.
Customer base: over 200 customers in more than 40 countries; about 70% of FY26 revenue from customers served for more than seven years.

qa_highlights.question: How should capacity, revenue and take-or-pay minimums in the fermentation business be framed over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the advanced-stage contracts would require about four times the current capacity (Phase 1, over 2-3 years). It did not give per-litre revenue or minimum revenue numbers, only that each contract is multi-million dollar and asset turnover should exceed 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 600 kL expansion for existing or new customers, and what is the capex?
qa_highlights.answer: The 600 kL Phase 1 is tied to a customer with a signed term sheet, with construction starting Q3 FY27 and taking 15-18 months. Funding combines internal accruals with customer contributions; no specific outlay was given beyond INR200-250 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: What are opex and milestone expectations for the new businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR23 crores quarterly opex run rate should continue for two to three quarters. Management said H2 milestone revenues would offset the full-year new-business opex, without giving amounts.

qa_highlights.question: How long before DCV launches, and how many products follow?
qa_highlights.answer: The first DCV ANDA is filed, the second is due in Q4 FY27, and five to six products are in development. Management said capacity, not product count, is the constraint, and a second line may be needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no revenue from CDMO and injectables in Q1, and what were last year's milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Milestone revenue is periodic, not quarterly. About INR33 crores was recognised in Q4 FY26, and none in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is API capacity utilisation and gross and EBITDA margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: API utilisation is about 70-80%. Management expects gross margin around 60% and EBITDA margin near 30%, with variance from logistics and solvent prices.

qa_highlights.question: Premarin generic timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give timing, saying the partner controls formulation development and FDA submission; Symbiotec's part is the API.

qa_highlights.question: API share of revenue two years out?
qa_highlights.answer: API is over 90% of revenue today. Management expects it to fall below half in 5-6 years as CDMO and DCV scale.

543573|2026-06.headline: Syrma SGS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 67% YoY to Rs 1,604 crore and PAT rose 112% to Rs 106 crore; FY27 guidance of 35%+ growth reaffirmed and possibly exceeded.
543573|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs 1,604 crore (+67% YoY), with operating EBITDA of Rs 162 crore (+69%, 10.1% margin) and PAT of Rs 106 crore (+112%). Growth was led by consumer ramp-ups, exports (+61% to about Rs 387 crore) and ODM (Rs 270 crore, about 115% YoY but down sequentially from Rs 345 crore in Q4). Management attributed the quarter to normal run-rate business rather than one-time items, and said supply-chain constraints (PCB chemicals, component lead times) led to a deliberate build in inventory, pushing net working capital days from 63 to 71. Management reaffirmed 10.5-11% full-year EBITDA margin guidance and said FY27 revenue growth would be 35%+, with a view to exceed guidance.

financial_highlights.change: approx +115% YoY; down from Rs 345 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Rs 122 crore; cash and investments above Rs 800 crore
financial_highlights.change: short-term borrowings up about Rs 340 crore in quarter

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 90 crore (of which about Rs 50 crore on PCB project)

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 34% of business mix; growth from faster customer ramp-ups and front-loaded schedules. Management guides about 30% of annual revenue, with quarterly variation.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: About 25% of business mix (about one-fourth of revenue); growth driven by EV penetration and charging infrastructure. Five new auto clients onboarded in the quarter.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Sequentially moderated; ex-defence/maritime it was about Rs 325 crore vs about Rs 320 crore last quarter (Rs 460 crore total last quarter including about Rs 140 crore defence/maritime). Smart metering slowed, and maritime is second-half loaded.

segments.name: Healthcare / MedTech
segments.commentary: Healthcare order book about Rs 500 crore. Syrma Johari MedTech did about Rs 210 crore last year and is expected to grow about 50%. Target 7-8% of total business.

segments.name: IT and Railways
segments.commentary: Together about 9% of order book; management said IT business is growing at a fast pace, including server motherboard work under a C-DAC approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 35%+, with management expecting to exceed guidance based on Q1.
Full-year operating EBITDA margin guided at 10.5-11%; consumer-mix seasonality may put the full-year figure in the 30-32% range for that segment, per management.
Exports expected to grow 30-40% in FY27, taking exports to about Rs 1,500-1,600 crore (FY26: about Rs 1,200 crore).
ODM share target of 17-19% in the short term, with a long-term aim of 25%.
Growth of 30-35% expected to continue in FY28 and FY29, per management.
Net working capital elevated for at least the next quarter or two as inventory is held as a strategic asset.
New clients onboarded in the quarter may add more than Rs 1,000 crore of revenue at full ramp-up, with volumes starting next year.
capex_capacity: PCB project: building about 65-70% complete; equipment from October onwards; power-on January-March 2027; commercial production expected by April 2027. Phase 1 cost about Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 130 crore funded so far.
PCB economics: asset turn about 1.5x at full utilisation; year-one utilisation 40-50%, rising to 80%+. EBITDA 15-18% at full ramp ex-PLI, and about 10% or lower in the initial year.
Ex-PCB capex guided at Rs 100-150 crore for FY27; about Rs 40 crore spent in Q1.
Current capacity utilisation 65-70%. Expansion underway at Bangalore and Pune, and a new MedTech facility at Jodhpur with plastic injection moulding and SMT lines.
Phase 1 PCB funding: 50-60% debt, plus a 50% government capex subsidy; Phase 2 and 3 expected to start around end-FY27 or early FY28.
Kaga JV (Syrma 60%, Kaga India 40%): initial investment about Rs 24-25 crore combined; opportunity estimated at Rs 300-500 crore over 3-5 years.
demand_pricing: Order book about Rs 6,770 crore at June end (about Rs 6,400 crore at March end); about Rs 5,400 crore to execute in the next 12 months; average execution period about 10-10.5 months. Q1 order intake about Rs 1,781 crore.
Order book mix: automotive about 29%, consumer about 30%, industrial about 24%, healthcare about 7%, IT and railways about 9%.
Customer concentration: top 5 about 38%, top 10 about 51%, top 20 about 66% of revenue.
18 new clients onboarded in Q1 (5 auto, 3 industrial, 2 healthcare, rest telecom, IT and railways).
Pass-through of memory and component cost increases: management said absolute margin rupee amounts are unaffected but percentage margin would dip as there is no markup on pass-through cost.
Exports by geography: USA about 22%, Europe about 40%, rest other countries; North America including Mexico and Canada adds about 15 percentage points.

526263|2026-06.headline: Mold-Tek Q1 FY27 profit rose about 12x YoY with EBITDA margin near 19-23%, though Beryl (US) still contributes nothing to bottom line.
526263|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 profitability was roughly 4x Q4 and 12x Q1 last year, driven by MES downsizing, lower other expenses (including absence of prior-quarter MTM losses) and automation. Beryl, the US residential permitting acquisition, was around break-even and is guided to break even in Q2 and contribute positively from Q3. Civil and structural work on hand was about $4.5 million versus $3.5-3.7 million a year earlier, and MES work on hand was about $1.15 million. Management reiterated FY27 ex-Beryl revenue of Rs 240-250 crore (about Rs 61 crore achieved in Q1) and an indicative Rs 300-350 crore for FY28 together with a structural engineering acquisition.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~15% guided earlier; FY26 EBITDA margin ~11% per management

financial_highlights.metric: Q1 FY27 profit vs prior year
financial_highlights.value: ~12x Q1 FY26 (Q1 FY26 PAT Rs 78 lakh)

financial_highlights.change: vs MTM loss in prior quarter
MES profitable only in FY22-23 and part of FY24 per management

segments.name: Civil & Structural (Mold-Tek Inc.)
segments.commentary: Work on hand about $4.5 million vs $3.5-3.7 million a year ago; project sizes $20k-$500k, lasting 3-12 months. Management treats work on hand as the key leading indicator.

segments.name: MES (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural)
segments.commentary: Work on hand about $1.15 million, flat YoY. Team cut from 125-130 to 50-60 people; EV/automobile design kept at small scale. Power T&D and substation design (poles, towers) now the focus, with a new US power distribution contract (~$1 million per annum, team ramping to 20 by Oct-Nov).

segments.name: Beryl (US residential permitting, Florida; Georgia entry)
segments.commentary: Not yet contributing to bottom line; around break-even, with a marginal loss of $5-10k over 8 months post-acquisition. Received a ~$1 million master purchase order from Hillsborough County; Georgia (Atlanta) listing started.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue ex-Beryl of Rs 240-250 crore reiterated; management says similar Q2 run-rate supports this.
EBITDA margin expected to stay at least 20%, possibly 20-23%, for the current year (management's wording); PAT margin target 15-16% with Beryl adding upside.
Beryl expected to break even in Q2 FY27 and be profitable quarter-on-quarter from Q3-Q4; FY27 Beryl revenue ~$5.5 million at ~8% EBITDA margin; Beryl ceiling ~10% PAT.
FY28 indicative target Rs 300-350 crore, contingent on a structural engineering acquisition.
US data-center-linked power T&D opportunity sized at $5-10 million per annum for Mold-Tek; sector ~$0.5-1 billion.
capex_capacity: MES team cut to 50-60 people from 125-130 a year ago; doubling the power/T&D design team in the last couple of months.
Indian design team for Beryl being built (6-8 people, target 15-20 by Oct-Nov); one PE relocating to Florida from October subject to L1 visa.

Proposed acquisition of a US structural engineering firm (~15 engineers, half PEs/SEs); talks ongoing, CEO to visit US from 16 Aug, chairman late September; decision targeted October and closing possibly within calendar 2026.
Atlanta office (5-6 staff) supports Beryl's Georgia entry; Beryl previously had 38 people at acquisition, lost 2 design staff.
demand_pricing: Civil work on hand $4.5 million (vs $3.7 million last year per one answer; $3.5 million per another), with both existing and new clients.
Power/T&D: new MSA with a US power distribution client; ~10 people billed from July, 20 by Oct-Nov.
Management says Indian rates are very low versus US; focus remains on US work.
Consulting fee model: management aims to charge 2-3% of project cost (vs hourly) once a design firm is integrated.

Beryl's residential/government revenue hit by US government funding shutdown in Jan-May; Florida residential permits reportedly down ~10% YoY (raised by analyst, management attributed partly to demand).

qa_highlights.question: What was the EBITDA per barrel in Q1 and what cost savings are sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Beryl was about break-even; per-barrel EBITDA not given. Savings came from MES downsizing, cut software costs and absence of prior-quarter MTM losses; management called automation and incentive changes long-term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin jump to 19% versus 15% guidance and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited reduced automobile engineering costs, automation and productivity incentives visible for 3-5 months, and a work-on-hand build; described these as long-term, not one-time.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Beryl promoter subscribe to warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6-month window lapsed in April when the 6-month average price (~Rs 165) exceeded market (~Rs 130); promoter did not subscribe and management will not press.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $5-10 million power opportunity sector-wide or company-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-specific opportunity of $5-10 million per annum; sector is ~$0.5-1 billion, with ~$100 million of substation design and detailing outsourced from US.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Indicative Rs 300-350 crore target for FY28 along with a structural engineering acquisition; management said it cannot predict beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: What caused Beryl's sales slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly demand (US government funding shutdown for 4-5 months, affecting government-funded work Jan-May) and partly internal design team disruption after losing 2 design staff in November.

risks_watch: Beryl break-even in Q2 and profitability from Q3 depends on building the India design team; cost arbitrage only after Indian staff start executing.
Structural engineering acquisition not yet identified in terms of size or price; timing repeatedly slipped and could fail (management: 'may either take the deal or drop the deal in October').
Revenue and margin guidance is loosely stated; Q1 EBITDA figure (19% vs 23%) and FY26 margin (11% vs 16%) given inconsistently in the call.
MES EV business remains uncertain; management kept a small team hoping for EV revival in 2-3 years.
Work on hand disclosed as a single number; Beryl's work on hand not tracked; US permitting demand and government funding volatility.
Warrant subscription by Beryl's original promoter has not happened.
526263|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on margins, Beryl's turnaround and the US data-center opportunity, but evasive on acquisition size, price and EBITDA per barrel, and loose with numbers (several corrections during the call).

500008|2026-06.headline: Amara Raja Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose ~24% to ~INR4,215 crore, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 9.6% on input costs and strategic spends.
500008|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 24% to roughly INR4,215 crore, with lead acid up about 22% and new energy up more than 70% to about INR209 crore. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 10.1% and consolidated 9.6%, hit by raw material inflation (alloy, sulfuric acid, poly), brand spends including IPL, Amaron Assist pilot, Factory of the Future costs and higher warranty provisions. Management took ~3% price hikes in June with a further 2-3% planned in the current month, but B2B pass-through lags. Automotive international volumes fell about 20% on Middle East disruption, and management expects recovery in subsequent quarters.

financial_highlights.change: moderated; management attributes ~0.9pp hit to strategic spends
~0.5pp lower, mainly new energy Giga 1 and BESS costs
elevated due to tubular season and inverter/HUPS trading
part of FY27 plan of ~INR1,700 crore

segments.name: Automotive lead acid (aftermarket & OEM)
segments.commentary: Aftermarket 4W and 2W volumes up ~15% YoY; OEM volumes up ~24% in 4W and >35% in 2W. Tubular plant ran at 100% capacity.

segments.name: Automotive international
segments.commentary: Revenue degrew ~20% YoY on ~20% volume drop, mainly lower Middle East shipments due to costly alternative sea routes.

segments.name: Industrial lead acid
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~2% YoY; UPS volumes up ~10%, telecom lead acid degrowing as telecom shifts to lithium-ion. Railways and power control growing 5-6%.

segments.name: Home energy
segments.commentary: Growth of more than 60% in tubular batteries and home EPS.

segments.name: New energy (lithium-ion packs)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR209 crore, up >70%; EV and telecom pack volumes each up >50% YoY. Lithium-ion telecom volumes up ~50%, combined telecom share held above 60%.

guidance_outlook: Additional 2-3% price increases across product segments in the current month (August); B2B pass-through expected to lag, with most recovery likely in Q2 or next quarter.
Other expenses (brand promotion, Amaron Assist, Factory of the Future) expected to normalise over next couple of quarters; freight and warranty costs may recur if fuel and raw material costs persist.
Lead acid revenue growth guided at 9-10% over the medium term (volume-led, industry-level estimate, not formal guidance); 2W aftermarket lower double digits, 4W slightly lower.
FY27 capex of ~INR1,700 crore, of which ~INR1,300 crore for new energy; Giga 1 expected to commercialise in H1 FY28.
BESS 10 GWh factory: initial capex INR250-300 crore; management sees ~5 GWh utilisation within 6-7 months of completion. Working capital cycle of 90-100 days cited as achievable.
R&D spend on cell development of ~INR100-150 crore expected this year.
E Positive research facility expected to start operations in the current quarter; 2 GWh NMC line equipment due for delivery in Q3.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at ~INR1,700 crore (~INR1,300 crore new energy); ~INR450 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Giga 1 cell plant expected to commercialise in H1 FY28; 2 GWh NMC line equipment due in Q3 FY27.
10 GWh LFP BESS factory on track; initial outlay INR250-300 crore; operating margin guided at roughly 5-8%.
Customer qualification plant with multi-form, multi-chemistry capability inaugurated in July 2026; producing 2170 NMC B-samples.
Tubular plant ran at 100% utilisation in Q1; battery breaking (recycling) operations still in trial production.

Long-term 16 GWh target from earlier strategy now under review; management says timing and capacity can change with demand and product mix; strategic share goal of 15-20% of lithium cell potential retained.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation in poly, sulfuric acid and tin/alloys; ~3% price hike taken in June 2026 did not fully offset cost increase.
Warranty provisions raised due to higher raw material costs, applied to the entire unexpired population.
Chinese competition: management estimates a 15-20% price disadvantage versus China for lithium cells; expects 3-4 cell players in India.
Telecom lead acid migrating to lithium-ion; combined telecom share above 60%.
BESS demand visibility from EPC players for power generation projects in India; export opportunities flagged.
Recycling economics: scrap purchase and reprocessing costs roughly equal to or above LME lead currently.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes were taken in Q1 and have cost pressures been recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3% taken in Q1 and a further 2-3% in August; not fully offsetting raw material rises, with poly, sulfuric acid and tin still trending up. B2B hikes delayed, expected to be recovered by Q2 or next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are other expenses non-recurring, and what is the BESS economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Brand and Amaron Assist costs to normalise over a couple of quarters; warranty and freight may recur. BESS: INR250-300 crore capex for 10 GWh, LFP-based, operating margin around 5-8% and asset turns higher than pack business.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the ~0.9% margin hit and how other expenses will trend.
qa_highlights.answer: Hit is from brand promotion, Amaron Assist pilot and Factory of the Future (capitalisation not allowed for throughput initiatives); also warranty and freight. Other expenses should trend lower once projects complete, but freight and warranty stay elevated while input costs are high.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16 GWh lithium plan still on track after the Gotion setback?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity milestones can change with demand; the 15-20% market share strategy holds. ESS cells may be prioritised over standard EV cells. NMC technology gap de-risked by in-house improvements; no broad China tech tie-up feasible.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lead acid growth outlook and is the price hike volume-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Medium-term lead acid revenue growth of 9-10% is an industry-level estimate, mainly volume-led. Aftermarket growth moderating from high base; 2W lower double digits, 4W slightly lower.

qa_highlights.question: How will the holding company fund new energy capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial risk capital of ~INR2,500 crore to complete five facilities; holding company cash generation of INR700-800 crore post-tax and post-dividend. Future debt-to-equity decisions to be made per business case.

540902|2026-06.headline: Amber Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA 28% to INR337 crore, with Electronics EBITDA more than doubling.
540902|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA grew 28% to INR337 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR126 crore (up 19%) before a INR123 crore exceptional loss. Electronics was the standout, with revenue up 29% and EBITDA more than doubling to a 10.8% margin. Railway & Defense EBITDA fell 26% on mix, copper, currency and Haryana minimum wage hikes. Management flagged that PCB margins were compressed by a roughly two-quarter pass-through lag and that cost pressure persists through H1, while Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper. The IL JIN facility incident was a new overhang, with insurance cover and the impact still being assessed.

segments.name: Consumer Durable
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,758 crore (+8%) and EBITDA INR214 crore (+12%) despite commodity and minimum wage headwinds; management attributed the modest growth to a high base. RAC is roughly 55-60% of the division, with the remainder non-RAC.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR985 crore (+29%) and EBITDA INR107 crore (10.8% margin, up from about 6.4%). Bare PCB margin compressed on copper clad laminate (CCL) costs, and the EMS segment grew more slowly as customers destocked and shifted to job work. Management reiterated FY27 growth of about 40%.

segments.name: Railway Sub-systems & Defense
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore (+18%) but EBITDA fell 26% to INR16 crore on product mix, including first trains supplied through a principal, plus copper, currency and a 35% Haryana minimum wage hike. FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% and EBITDA margin at 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: Electronics: FY27 growth of about 40% reiterated; EMS full-year guidance intact per Sanjay Arora.
Railway Sub-systems & Defense: FY27 revenue growth 30-35% and EBITDA margin 15-16%.
Consumer Durable: growth in line with RAC industry, cited as 13-15%; no percentage margin guidance given.
Group margin: earlier 50-100 bps decline guidance for FY27 now moderated, with margins seen normalising if no further currency or commodity disruption.
PCB margin: currently about 12% versus about 16% normal; expected to recover from Q3 FY27 to a 15-16% normalised range, subject to no further CCL price rises.

Oppo mobile: trial production in Q4 FY27, commercial production from Q1 FY28, about 8 million units in year one, rising to 15-16 million in year two; revenue-recognition model to be clarified in 15-20 days.
IL JIN: fundraise enabling resolution up to INR5,000 crore; quantum and form not yet decided. IL JIN production impact being assessed, with guidance expected to be met.
capex_capacity: PCB capex: about INR3,200 crore at Jewar (UP), where construction has started and trial production is about 18 months away; Hosur (Tamil Nadu) about INR1,000 crore, with the plant to be running this financial year; Shogini (Pune) INR500 crore. All three were approved under the ECMS scheme.
Jewar HDI PCB groundbreaking held with Ascent-K / Korea Circuit; air conditioner plant construction planned to start in 2028, with trial production in 2029.
Sidwal greenfield facility in Faridabad (HVAC, pantry, doors, gangways) is now operational.
Asset turn in PCB business about 0.8:1 depending on complexity.
CCL backward integration: Amber in discussion with JV partners; target own CCL plants by 2029-30.
demand_pricing: Consumer Durable: BEE tonnage labelling mandatory from 1 July 2026 has created mixed inventory in the trade; management expects inventory to clear by Diwali, a strong summer from November, and not very high festive demand.
Q1 Consumer Durable margins were helped by pre-buying of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement, and by a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne). Management said this would not be annualised.
PCB: pass-through to customers is progressing, with some customers raising prices in July. Copper clad laminate prices keep rising, driven by AI and data-centre demand and a shortage.
Electronics TAM: management cited $185 billion of electronics consumption, a $16-17 billion addressable market for PCB, PCBA and power electronics today, and an estimated $35-40 billion by FY30.
Power electronics (PLC, HMI, solar inverters, UPS, BESS) expected to grow 35-40%.

financial_highlights.change: +19% YoY (vs INR106 crore); INR141 crore before INR15.35 crore purchase-price-allocation inventory impact
vs around INR510 crore at March 2026

503722|2026-06.headline: Banswara Syntex Q1 FY27 total income rose 4.1% to INR322.4 crores with PAT of INR4.4 crores versus a loss of INR1.4 crores; management reiterates FY27 revenue of INR1,450–1,500 crores.
503722|2026-06.overview: Total income grew 4.1% YoY to INR322.4 crores and EBITDA was INR29.5 crores (about 9% margin), with PAT of INR4.4 crores against a loss a year earlier. Fabric grew 25% YoY while yarn and garment revenues fell, mainly on labour shortages in spinning, higher internal yarn consumption and garment dispatches delayed by West Asia logistics. Management kept FY27 guidance of about INR1,500 crores revenue and 12% EBITDA, relying on a garment order book booked through November/December and a recovery in H2. Analysts pressed hard on the low top-line growth over a decade and on the pace of garment capacity additions.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Revenue INR96 crores (vs INR110 crores YoY); sales volume 36 lakh kg at 70% capacity utilisation. Higher internal transfers to fabric and garments reduced external sales; labour shortage cut output.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Revenue INR147 crores (+25% YoY); volume 59 lakh meters (+18% YoY) at 80% utilisation. Growth driven by value-added bi-stretch and wool blends; Q1 margin was in line with the 12–14% target. Roughly 50:50 export and domestic.

segments.name: Garment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR69 crores (vs INR75 crores YoY); 8 lakh pieces at 69% utilisation. West Asia logistics delayed dispatches; margin below target (8–10% expected) due to container availability. About 60% export, 40% domestic.

segments.name: Jackets (within garment)
segments.commentary: Q1 closed at about 135,000 jackets, soft demand. Run rate now upwards of 75,000 a month; FY27 target 800,000–900,000 jackets versus about 600,000 a year on average.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR1,450–1,500 crores maintained; management expects garment at about INR100 crores per quarter for the next three quarters and about INR375–380 crores for the year plus export incentives.
Consolidated EBITDA target of about 12% for FY27 versus 9% in Q1; segment targets: fabric 12–14%, garment 8–10%, yarn 8–10%.
Yarn expected to normalise progressively as labour availability improves; management expects visible improvement from Q2.
Surat facility targeted for DTA use by November/December 2026 and operations from April 2027; main impact in FY28. Restart seen adding about INR200 crores of runway for about INR50 crores investment.
Garment EU operationalisation with Mango, Celio and C&A targeted by end-December 2026/early January 2027.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR140 crores planned and sanctioned for this year across fabric, garment and common infrastructure.
Management targets about 20–25% garment expansion and about 20% fabric expansion in FY28, with a further 20% in FY28 as stated; yarn to be maintained or marginally grown.
Over the last three years, about INR350 crores invested: about INR150 crores in fabric and about INR130 crores in yarn; management said the modernisation phase is complete.
Surat facility shut to move into DTA; Daman capacity to be fully utilised this year.
demand_pricing: Garment order book fully booked through November and into December; fabric order book shows orders up to November end.
Demand healthy in US and domestic markets; Europe and Middle East softer in fabric.
India-UK FTA effective 15 July 2026; UK fabric exposure about INR70–80 crores a year; UK garment about INR20–25 crores, targeted to double to at least INR50 crores next year.
Two EU anchor garment customers (Mango and Celio) about INR100 crores of revenue; C&A onboarded with trial orders; new UK customers Haggar and NEXT added in fabric.
Domestic yarn realisations improved, partly offsetting lower volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export contribution for fabric and garments, and what are the jacket volumes and segment margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall exports 48%; fabric and garment together about 70% of export turnover. Jackets: about 600,000 a year average, FY27 expected 800,000–900,000. Segment margin targets given (fabric 12–14%, garment and yarn 8–10%).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the sequential drop so sharp in garment and yarn, and is the garment shortfall shipment timing or lost demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to a weak autumn/winter export season and seasonal domestic lull, plus delayed shipments. July garment sales were on target at about INR30 crores, with quarterly run-rate expected to reach about INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 12% EBITDA for FY27 on INR1,500 crores revenue; Q1 was 9%, with the rest expected to average out to 12% over the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth muted despite about INR500 crores of capex over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn capacity was under-used because of labour issues and the investments are now expected to lift top line and bottom line; fabric growth of about 20% a year is expected from its investments.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company different this decade, given flat revenue since FY19 and weak margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the dissolution of the French JV for lost sales a decade ago, said product mix is much better, and cited import substitution of Chinese goods and FTAs. Garment export share rose from about 20% to about 60%, with a target of 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any update on the Surat facility?
qa_highlights.answer: GIDC approvals and no-objection certificate received; customs duty clearance and SEZ debonding pending, expected within 3–5 months. Restart would involve fresh machinery, adding about INR200 crores of capacity for about INR50 crores.

risks_watch: Garment margin recovery (targeted 8–10%) depends on export mix and on timely container availability; Q1 garment EBITDA fell short.
Yarn utilisation (70% in Q1) depends on labour availability; labour shortages recur each festival and marriage season.
FY27 guidance needs about INR1,000 crores or more of revenue in Q2–Q4 at the stated quarterly run rate, with H2 weighted delivery.
Europe and Middle East fabric demand softer; West Asia logistics disruptions continue to delay shipments.
Surat restart timelines (DTA by Nov/Dec 2026, operations April 2027) and capex of about INR140 crores; benefits seen mainly in FY28.
Debt rising to about INR500 crores per analyst estimate; past capex has not yet translated into revenue growth.

543524|2026-06.headline: Rainbow Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR 470 crore and EBITDA 30% to INR 134.6 crore at a 28.6% margin; like-for-like growth was 24%.
543524|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue grew 33% YoY to INR 470 crore, with acquisitions (Guwahati, Warangal) contributing about INR 38 crore. EBITDA rose 30% to INR 134.6 crore at a 28.6% margin, despite losses at newly commissioned hospitals, and PAT rose 16% to INR 62.5 crore. Operating metrics grew: inpatient discharges 28%, outpatient consultations 25%, deliveries 23%, with ARPOB up 6%. Management guided to above 20% revenue growth in Q2 and a return to 24-25% EBITDA margin (pre-Ind AS) by year-end, and set out a plan to add 2,500 beds over five years.

financial_highlights.value: 6% improvement cited; mature hospitals approx. INR 70,000 vs under-5-year hospitals approx. INR 59,000

segments.name: Mature hospitals
segments.commentary: ARPOB approx. INR 70,000 in Q1, about 18% above hospitals less than five years old; management attributed the roughly 10% mature-cluster ARPOB rise to a mix of pricing and case mix.

segments.name: Newer / greenfield hospitals
segments.commentary: Rajahmundry is at roughly breakeven; Electronic City (Bengaluru) expected to break even in 2-3 months. Management guides new Bengaluru hospitals to break even within 12-15 months, all within about 18 months.

segments.name: Acquisitions (Guwahati, Warangal)
segments.commentary: Both are EBITDA-positive. Guwahati is at near company-average margins and grew about 20%; Warangal is ramping toward company-level margins over the next year.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth expected above 20% in Q2 FY27; management expects 20%-plus growth to be sustained, and about 20% annually would double revenue in roughly four years.
Expects to cross INR 2,000 crore revenue by end of FY27.
EBITDA margin expected to return to 24%-25% on a pre-Ind AS basis by year-end.
Plans to add 2,500 beds over five years to reach 5,000 beds, with capex of about INR 2,200 crore; 1,200 beds already in various stages of development.
Mumbai (Malad, 100-bed brownfield) expected to start in Q1 FY28; Management said Mumbai EBITDA margins should eventually exceed 20%, with no precise near-term figure.
Indore to commence Q3 FY27; Coimbatore hub and Gurgaon Sector 56 spoke in Q3 FY28; Gurgaon Sector 44 hub in Q1 FY29; Pune (150 beds) and Bengaluru Seegehalli spoke in FY29.
Nellore (70-bed acquisition, expanding to 100+ beds) and 30-bed maternal block expected in about six months; Guntur 50-bed leased hospital to start in a couple of months.
capex_capacity: Total bed capacity grew 26% YoY to 2,435 beds; operational beds up 22% to 1,862 beds; management said bed capacity reached 500 with recent additions (as stated).

Over next five years: add 2,500 beds to reach 5,000 beds, capex about INR 2,200 crore; approximately 30% of future additions in existing southern markets and 70% in new markets (Delhi NCR, North, Central India, Mumbai).
Capex in Q1 was about INR 56 crore, mainly on existing hospitals and upcoming projects; funded through internal accruals.
Mumbai Malad 100-bed brownfield hospital (definitive agreement signed); Nellore 70-bed Prime Children's Hospital acquired; Guntur 50-bed leased hospital.
Management said it is 'not far' from breakeven at Rajahmundry and Electronic City; Hennur and HRBR are still in investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 revenue growth remain in the mid-20s after the higher base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 revenue growth in the 20% range and above 20%, citing digital initiatives and lead conversion.

qa_highlights.question: Organic growth ex-acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions contributed about INR 38 crore; like-for-like revenue growth was 24%.

qa_highlights.question: Mature-cluster ARPOB up about 10%: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a combination of pricing and case mix.

qa_highlights.question: Mumbai margin expectations and doctor model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise margin, but said EBITDA margins should eventually exceed 20%. Core doctors will stay full-time, with some hybrid models for certain specialists.

qa_highlights.question: Bengaluru hospital breakeven timing and losses?
qa_highlights.answer: New Bengaluru hospitals still incur losses; guidance unchanged at 12-15 months to breakeven, with all within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% growth the medium-term revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sustaining about 20% annual growth would double revenue in about four years; that is the directional view, not a formal target.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from ramp-up of new hospitals (Rajahmundry, Electronic City, Hennur, HRBR); margin recovery to 24%-25% by year-end depends on operating leverage.
Monsoon delay could weaken Q2/Q3 seasonal demand; management has not yet quantified July trends.
Entry into high-cost markets (Mumbai, NCR) with higher employee and doctor costs; Mumbai margins are not yet defined.
Integration of acquired hospitals (Nellore, Guntur, Malad) and the Malad JV structure with three doctor-promoters; ownership and lock-in terms were not disclosed.
Execution across multiple new geographies with management bandwidth and doctor-recruitment constraints, particularly in the Northeast.

543324|2026-06.headline: Gretex Q1 FY27 call gave no financial figures; management cited 3 new advisory mandates and guided to 3-4 IPO listings in the current quarter.

segments.name: Broking and market-making (Gretex Share Broking Ltd)

segments.name: Alternative investments
