509820|2026-06.headline: Huhtamaki India Q2 CY26 net sales rose 23.1% to INR723 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.3%, with PBT up 77%.
509820|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q2 net sales of INR723 crore, up about 23% YoY, with growth split roughly evenly across price, volume and product mix and broad-based across exports and domestic. EBITDA margin expanded to 10.5% from 8.3%, and PBT rose 77% to INR559 crore, with EPS up about 77%. H1 sales grew close to 12% and H1 EBIT margin was hit by a one-time INR8.8 crore prior-period depreciation charge; excluding it, EBIT margin was 7.6%. Management attributed the quarter to pricing pass-through of Middle East-driven raw material inflation, a healthy portfolio mix and productivity, plus some customer inventory build-up that it said would partly reverse.

financial_highlights.value: Growth of ~77.3% YoY (absolute value not stated)

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports grew at roughly the same rate as domestic in Q2; exports are about 30% of sales volume. Management said duty-related challenges are stabilising.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic growth was almost identical to exports at about 23%; volume growth in liquid and home care categories was highlighted.

segments.name: Blueloop (mono-material sustainable packaging)
segments.commentary: Blueloop share of output is below 30% of material volume, up from the prior quarter; the balance of blueloop asset output (>70%) is used for products previously outsourced.

guidance_outlook: No numeric guidance given; management declined to commit to a quarterly EBITDA margin (said it could be 8%, 10% or 15%).
Management would not commit to INR750 crore quarterly revenue run-rate; said it depends on pass-through (single-digit), product mix and customer growth.
Volume growth expected to track market growth (about 4-5%); management said 23% growth should not be expected every quarter.
Festive season expected to support demand in coming months; inventory build-up at customers to be clearer by Q3 CY26 call.
Solar captive plant expected to come online in Q3 and supply ~50% of power for Khopoli plant.
capex_capacity: Volume growth was high single-digit (just short of double digit per management); exact capacity utilisation not disclosed on competitive grounds.
Productivity improvement programme over last 3-4 quarters is said to free capacity enough for growth; management sees no capacity constraint for at least a couple of years.
Modernisation and productivity capex funded from cash on balance sheet; no specific capex amount disclosed.
Solar captive power plant at Khopoli to be commissioned in Q3 CY26, supplying ~50% of Khopoli plant power.
Zero liquid discharge maintained; Taloja implemented mechanical vapour recompression water recycling.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in Q2 described as high single-digit; price, volume and mix each contributed roughly one-third of the 23% sales growth.
Raw material cost pass-through is contract-dependent (quarterly or monthly indexation, or ad hoc); management says most price changes occurred in Q2 and the process is 'never a done story'.
Customers valued supply reliability and contingency during the Middle East crisis; management said this drove share-of-wallet gains with same customer base.
Customer inventory build-up in anticipation of price increases is a tailwind; quantum not known to management.
Home care and liquid categories growing faster than food and beverage in India; late monsoon boosted beverage season.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q2 volume growth and export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was high single-digit, just short of double digit; exports and domestic grew at almost identical rates of about 23%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company pursuing volume growth again after sacrificing volume for profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not moved away from profitable growth; product mix and customer base have largely settled and the focus is share-of-wallet and innovation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR750 crore quarterly revenue run-rate reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit; INR750 crore includes single-digit price pass-through, and outcome depends on product mix and customer growth. It could be INR650 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is working capital and receivables trend (inventory and receivables roughly doubled; receivables ~50% of six-month turnover)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute values are higher due to price increases and higher volume; DSO and DIO are stable, and there are no realisation or ageing challenges.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for acquisitions or monetising land such as Daman?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific non-organic plans disclosed; cash is directed to modernisation and capex. Thane land sale was completed a couple of years ago; other land monetisation will be disclosed in annual reports if it happens.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth rate be sustainable into next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to track market growth (around 3-5%) rather than repeat 23% every quarter.

risks_watch: Customer inventory build-up may reverse, reducing volumes in coming quarters; management will update in Q3.
Raw material volatility from the Middle East crisis; pass-through lags and inventory cost effects on margins.
Working capital: inventory and receivables rose in absolute terms; DIO and DSO said to be stable, to watch next quarter.
Export duty and import tariff regulation uncertainty affecting export growth.
One-time INR8.8 crore prior-period depreciation charge in Q1 affecting reported EBIT; the Q2 and H1 comparison base.
509820|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on results and strategy, citing profitable growth, and cautious on forward numbers, repeatedly declining to quantify volume, margin or revenue run-rate beyond the current quarter. Several answers on inventory build-up, pricing sustainability and acquisitions were deferred to the Q3 call or left undisclosed.
key_quotes: So what that means is we are selective on where we operate. We're selective on which customers we want to grow with.
We don't want to just take volume just for the sake of it, right? It doesn't deliver volume. If it doesn't deliver profit and return on investment, there's no point in doing that.
I would not worry about capacity utilization or amount of growth we can do at least for another couple of years.

532143|2026-06.headline: SKM Egg Products' Q1 FY27 realisation rose to about Rs 770/kg from Rs 722 last quarter, while management flagged feed-cost pressure lasting at least two more quarters.
532143|2026-06.overview: Management said the company is running near full capacity, so volume growth is capped and results depend on international egg product prices, exchange rates and feed costs. Realisation was stated at about Rs 770 per unit against Rs 722 last quarter, mainly helped by the rupee, while margins were hit by a substantial rise in soya-based feed costs. Management said the company is moving into domestic branded eggs, with a business plan due by end-March, and is adding easy-shed capacity with completion targeted for November-December 2028. Capex approval for further expansion is expected at the next board meeting, with a target of October. The call was largely Q&A; no formal presentation was given, and several answers were vague on numbers.

segments.name: Egg powder (export)
segments.commentary: Realisation about Rs 770 per unit this quarter; management guided that the quarterly average will likely stay above Rs 700, with a range of Rs 720-750 cited. Russia shipments run about 150 tons per month.

segments.name: Branded eggs (domestic, new)
segments.commentary: Structure set up after the company took over a brand company; business plan due by end-March. Management said margins are lower than egg products and gave no brand EBITDA or revenue figure beyond the Rs 40-50 crore turnover expected this year.

segments.name: Easy sheds / egg production
segments.commentary: About 20 lakh birds planned; first four sheds completed earlier, all to be complete by November-December 2028. Management said the cost advantage is at least 5% of overall production cost, from higher productivity and feed efficiency.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth limited by capacity for the rest of FY27; the company is running at full capacity.
Feed-cost pressure expected to persist for at least two more quarters, per management.
International egg white prices seen as stable, with possible improvement of 2-3/4 for egg white; inventory positions still high.
Japan office approval delayed one to two months for resubmission; new business expected in the second half of the year.
Next board meeting in October expected to approve a further expansion plan (capex timing, capacity numbers not given).
capex_capacity: Easy sheds: about 20 lakh birds; completion by November-December 2028.
Backward integration and plant expansion referenced; management has not disclosed capacity numbers.
Waste-to-biogas and organic fertiliser: fermentation gas used in the boiler; liquid and solid organic fertiliser to reach commercial sale by September.
Plant at full capacity; next expansion plan to be announced at the October board meeting.
Phased capex to come in FY28 and FY29; capacity by end FY27 or FY28 not disclosed on the call.
demand_pricing: Global egg product prices are set by Europe (egg white) and the US, South America and China (yolk); India and Ukraine are also cited as supply countries.
International prices described as stable; some signs of higher egg white demand but high inventories still with processors.
Pricing is set by competition and market prices, not by the company's cost; management said feed-cost increases cannot be passed on directly.
Russia war reported as not affecting exports; Iran-related shipping disruption led to about 6-7 containers being returned from Dubai and re-airlifted.
Management said Europe's severe summer could support demand toward the end of the financial year.

qa_highlights.question: How are international egg powder prices determined, and which countries set them?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe sets egg white prices and the US, South America and China influence yolk prices; the company said cost structures and historical supply decide prices, which differ by product.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE on the easy-shed and biogas capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate return estimate was given. Management said the biogas gas is burned in the boiler and by-products sold as organic fertiliser, and that the investment is needed for efficiency and sustainability.

qa_highlights.question: What are the realisation and margin drivers this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation was about Rs 770 vs Rs 722 earlier, helped by the exchange rate. The main margin hit was a substantial rise in soya feed cost, which management expects to persist for at least two more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution and margin of branded products?
qa_highlights.answer: Branded eggs were not part of the business historically. Management gave no number and said margins are lower than egg products but volume scale is easier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Japan office status and the Russia export position?
qa_highlights.answer: Japan approval delayed by one to two months; direct contracts already in place. Russia at about 150 tons per month. A second distributor is being sought.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost savings from easy sheds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no figure beyond a minimum 5% reduction in overall production cost, from higher productivity and better feed conversion.

risks_watch: Feed-cost (soya) pressure will keep margins under pressure for at least two quarters and cannot be passed on directly to customers.
Full capacity caps volume growth until new capacity is commissioned (easy sheds targeted by end-2028).
Branded-egg venture has no disclosed margin, capex or revenue split beyond the Rs 40-50 crore turnover expected this year.
Exchange-rate dependence: much of the realisation gain was attributed to the rupee.
Shipping disruption (Iran-related) led to returned containers; management said the stock will be sold in July-August.
532143|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity plans, but vague and evasive on numbers: no capex amounts, branded margins, capacity-by-year figures or ROCE. The chairman said he cannot forecast market prices and deferred several detailed questions offline.
key_quotes: Only the increase in fee cost is the biggest.
We have a strategic goal of 2030. We are working on a strategic goal of 2035.

financial_highlights.metric: Average realisation on dried egg powder
financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 722 last quarter, mainly due to exchange rate

financial_highlights.metric: Branded egg business turnover to be added this year
financial_highlights.change: margin contribution expected only from next financial year

financial_highlights.metric: Easy-shed expansion capex (as stated by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: management said it is for own egg production capacity, not branding

500214|2026-06.headline: Ion Exchange Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 49% YoY to INR 32 crore (4.54% margin) on 20% revenue growth to INR 701 crore, with treatment solutions still loss-making.
500214|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating income rose 20% YoY to INR 701 crore, but EBITDA fell 49% to INR 32 crore and PAT was INR 3 crore (0.44% margin). Management split the former engineering segment into Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products and Lifecycle Services, and reported Specialty Chemicals and Consumer Products separately. Treatment Solutions posted a EBIT loss of INR 17 crore on legacy projects, while Industrial Products margin rose to 11.89%. Management said Roha resin capacity is ramping slower than expected and guidance will be reviewed by end of Q2.

financial_highlights.value: INR 112 crore / loss of INR 34 lakh
financial_highlights.change: +33% revenue YoY; loss was INR 45 lakh
excludes Hyundai win of about USD 52 million

segments.name: Treatment Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 210 crore (+14% YoY) with EBIT loss of INR 17 crore, hit by legacy projects including the UP project. Dispatches to GCC resumed post-quarter; a Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore per Q&A) was won after quarter end.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 105 crore (+14% YoY) and EBIT INR 13 crore, margin 11.89% vs under 6% a year ago, driven by water treatment solutions and membranes. Institutional products moved here from Consumer.

segments.name: Lifecycle Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 72 crore (+28% YoY) and EBIT INR 7 crore (9.92% margin vs 10.55%), with margin pressure from higher input costs. Includes a 20-year O&M concession in Oman with PDO.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 230 crore (+21% YoY) but EBIT INR 22 crore (-52% YoY), impacted by geopolitics and Roha ramp-up costs; Roha cost drag about 6% of segment margin. FX gain in the prior-year quarter also reversed (about 3-4 pts).

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 112 crore (+33% YoY) with a small loss of INR 34 lakh vs INR 45 lakh a year ago; breakeven targeted in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Specialty Chemicals capacity to grow at least 50% over the next couple of years as Roha reaches full capacity over about four years, with asset turnover just under 2x.
Roha utilisation guidance of 25% in year one is still held but described as softer than expected; management will review by end of Q2 FY27.
UP legacy project is not expected to close in FY27 and will spill into FY28, dependent on government fund flows; other large legacy project expected to see significant progress by FY27 end.
Consumer Products targeted to break even in FY27.
Management aims to restore double-digit profitability over time; no timeline given. Input costs expected to moderate if crude stays near USD 80.
capex_capacity: Roha resin plant commissioned and in stabilisation; with Ankleshwar debottlenecking, total resin capacity expected to reach about 5x the pre-Roha level (Phase I doubles capacity, Phase II plus debottlenecking takes it to about 5x).
Pharma resin capacity at Ankleshwar (FDA-approved) to expand 6x, targeted within the next 12 months; described as asset-light, technology-led rather than capex-heavy.
Membrane business: second Goa plant under construction to add UF and MBR capacity; tie-up with MANN+HUMMEL for UF PVDF technology. Management targets 3x business growth over the years.
Standard plants capacity expanded across Hosur, Goa and Wada.
Management would not disclose capital earmarked for BOOT/BOO service projects, saying it will remain asset-light.
demand_pricing: Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore) won post quarter end; supplied to an EPC, FOB Mumbai, kickoff under way.
Bid pipeline stood at INR 9,777 crore as of the call.

Price increases taken across customers and segments, but pass-through lags input cost increases; management sees some moderation in input costs with crude near USD 80 vs over USD 100 in March-April 2026.
Geopolitical situation (West Asia) impacted invoicing and dispatches; Roha volumes expected to lean on overseas markets, including North America after WQA certification.
UP project unexecuted portion is about 11% of June order backlog; receivable exposure said to be broadly unchanged over recent quarters.

532804|2026-06.headline: Technocraft Q1 FY27: Drum Closure EBIT margin near 43% on record volumes and rupee depreciation; management targets sustainable 30% for drums, 15% for scaffolding and engineering services.
532804|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong quarter, with Drum Closure posting its highest-ever revenue and EBIT margin (about 43%) on higher export volumes and a weaker rupee. Scaffolding volumes rose year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter on US demand, with realisations broadly stable. Mach One (aluminium formwork) volumes fell year-on-year but edged up sequentially, which management attributed to site and project readiness rather than competition. Management repeatedly declined to treat the current margins as the new normal and kept its sustainable-margin guidance unchanged. No significant new capex is planned for FY27.

segments.name: Drum Closure
segments.commentary: Almost 100% export. Volumes and rupee depreciation drove record revenue and EBIT. Management targets a sustainable margin of 30% or more. Non-seasonal, not order-book based.

segments.name: Scaffolding (Steel)
segments.commentary: Volumes up year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter on US demand (data centres, semicon, AI chip plants, energy). Operating at about 95% utilisation. Sustainable margin guidance of 15%. Middle East is 2-3% of sales and declining.

segments.name: Mach One (Aluminium Formwork)
segments.commentary: Volumes down year-on-year, up marginally quarter-on-quarter. Utilisation about 75-80%. Order book of 3-5 months. Aluminium extrusion plant at over 95%-100% utilisation and helped EBIT amid higher aluminium prices.

segments.name: Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Growing fast on US outsourcing demand, including AI-based vision, embedded systems and automation. Sustainable margin target about 14-15%, which includes ongoing tech investment.

segments.name: Textile
segments.commentary: Fabric business shut down and machinery sold for Rs 25-30 crore. Yarn business profitable. Garment business loss-making, with breakeven targeted within two quarters. Working capital released about Rs 15-20 crore (figure varied during the call).

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: JT Cooler approved by DRDO and an Israeli sensor maker, with export orders from Israel of about Rs 20 crore at roughly 15% margin. Missile canister repeat orders. Confirmed order book about Rs 20-21 crore.

guidance_outlook: Drum Closure: sustainable margin of 30% or more; similar volumes expected in the immediate quarter.
Scaffolding: volumes expected to be maintained or improved for the next two quarters; beyond that not guided due to volatility. Sustainable margin 15%.
Engineering Services: sustainable margin 14-15%, inclusive of ongoing investment.
Capex: no significant new capacity capex in FY27, only maintenance. Phase 2 of CSN plant and Aurangabad Mach One Phase 2 expected next year.
US tariff refund of close to $3 million expected in the Scaffolding segment, not yet received; timing not stated.
Middle East scaffolding sales expected to stay volatile for one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: No significant new capacity capex planned for FY27; only maintenance capex across divisions. The last major capex (CSN plant, FY25) is fully operational.
Aluminium extrusion plant running at over 95% (management said 100%) utilisation since the March quarter; 100% backward integrated for Mach One.
Mach One utilisation about 75-80%, after a recent Aurangabad capacity expansion. Phase 2 expected sometime next year.
Scaffolding utilisation about 95%. Management says it can add capacity within about 3 months using space in Mumbai and China plants, and is studying options.
Next year: CSN Phase 2 and extra extrusion capacity plus forward integration.
demand_pricing: US scaffolding demand strong since January 2026, driven by AI chip, semicon and energy construction; realisations stable as steel prices did not rise sharply.

US tariff on Chinese scaffolding is 75% (50% Section 232 plus 25% Section 301) vs 50% for India and others. Management says Chinese steel costs are 20%+ lower, but Technocraft is only about 5% higher on cost.
Management says it does not compete on price; it competes on inventory availability, distribution and a 150+ component mix.
Indian project launches strong across 7 major cities; demand also from commercial, GCCs and data centres.
Drum Closure: no price cuts planned; competitive position as the world's second-largest producer. Rupee depreciation lifted realisations.
Europe scaffolding sales started in the last two quarters (CE certification), still small due to weak construction in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mach One volumes decline year-on-year, and how is competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to site and project readiness, not competition or demand. Volumes rose slightly quarter-on-quarter. Focus is on quality customers and profitability, not rapid volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 43% Drum Closure margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the sustainable margin is above 30% and 43% is not the new normal, given volatility in freight, tariffs and geopolitics. Rupee depreciation and volumes drove the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Defence JT Cooler opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Export orders from Israel of about Rs 20 crore at around 15% margin. Management said quantum is hard to estimate because defence procurement is slow and product-specific.

qa_highlights.question: What are the scaffolding tariff and competitive dynamics in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariff is 50% for India, 75% for China. Chinese prices are sometimes lower, but Technocraft does not sell on price. Its US subsidiary and inventory-led distribution are its edge.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant capacity capex this year; only maintenance. Phase 2 of CSN and Mach One expansion next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Textile plan after the fabric exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric shut and machinery sold for Rs 25-30 crore. Yarn profitable; garment loss-making, with breakeven targeted in two quarters. No active plan to sell the rest of the business.

risks_watch: Drum Closure margin normalisation from 43% toward the 30% guidance if the rupee strengthens or freight and tariff costs move.
Scaffolding volume visibility limited to about two quarters; US tariff regime (50%/75%) and Chinese price aggression.
Middle East scaffolding disruption from war and shipping problems.
Garment business breakeven within two quarters; restructuring execution.
Timing of the approximately $3 million US tariff refund.
Defence order timing is slow; JT Cooler export scale is small so far.
Mach One volume recovery depends on site readiness; Y-o-Y decline.

financial_highlights.change: Year-on-year volume growth declined; small sequential increase
Highest ever for the segment, per analyst; management confirmed record revenue and EBIT

financial_highlights.metric: Textile Yarn business EBITDA margin (last quarter)

532796|2026-06.headline: Lumax Auto Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% y-o-y to INR 1,364 crore, with EBITDA up 51% at a 15.1% margin and PAT up 83% to INR 99 crore.
532796|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR 1,364 crore grew 33% y-o-y, with EBITDA of INR 205 crore (up 51%, margin 15.1%, up 190 bps) and PAT of INR 99 crore (up 83%). Management said the margin would hold for the rest of the year, and guidance was kept unchanged: 15% EBITDA margin for FY27 and about 20% revenue CAGR. Growth was helped by a low base and industry production up 22% y-o-y, but management expects growth to slow in Q3 and Q4 after the post-GST-rationalisation base effect. The order book stands at INR 1,600 crore, with about 24% expected in FY27, 56% in FY28 and 20% in FY29.

segments.name: Advanced Plastics (incl. IAC, ~60% share of division)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 47% y-o-y from INR 525 crore to INR 769 crore; order book INR 787 crore. Division is more than half of group revenue; margin band 16-20%.

segments.name: Mechatronics
segments.commentary: Revenue rose ~56% y-o-y from INR 54 crore to INR 84 crore; order book close to INR 500 crore. Management expects ~INR 400 crore FY27 revenue and ~INR 1,000 crore by FY31; currently 6-7% of group.

segments.name: Structure and Control Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 21% y-o-y from INR 180 crore to INR 220 crore; order book INR 130 crore.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 6% y-o-y from INR 98 crore to INR 104 crore, hit by non-lighting products and pricing; management still guides for double-digit growth for the rest of the year.

segments.name: Alternate Fuels (Greenfuel)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 17% y-o-y from INR 95 crore to INR 111 crore; order book INR 200 crore. Q1 EBITDA margin was ~23%, including ~3% one-off tooling revenue; underlying ~20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance is unchanged: about 20% revenue CAGR (FY25-FY31 vision) and EBITDA margin of about 15% for FY27; management expects Q1 margins of 15.1% to be sustained for the rest of the year.

FY27 capex guided at about INR 300 crore, including Mechatronics greenfield and new IAC plants; Q1 capex was INR 23 crore. About 10-12% of capex may be debt-funded at JV or subsidiary level; the rest from internal accruals.

Targets: FY28 EBITDA about INR 1,000 crore, implying 15.5-16% margin (including other income); longer term, move toward 20% EBITDA margin over 5-7 years, with 17-17.5% cited as a satisfactory interim outcome.
Mechatronics JVs to operate at 14-15% EBITDA over the next 12-24 months; Greenfuel margin range 19-20%.
Aftermarket: management expects growth of 15% or more versus 10-12% under the earlier strategy.
Minority interest expected at 11-13% of PAT. Inorganic growth not planned for the current year, but strategic fits are being evaluated.
capex_capacity: New IAC plant at Chakan for Mahindra & Mahindra demand, with some product-line optimisation across facilities.
Mega Mechatronics plant at Manesar, Haryana, expected to commission by Q3 FY27; consolidates Lumax Yokowo, Lumax Alps Alpine, Lumax Ituran and Lumax FAE.
Greenfuel to set up a new facility in Nashik to serve Mahindra (passenger vehicle CNG delivery system).
FY27 capex guidance of INR 300 crore; order book of INR 1,600 crore to be served on this spend for FY28 and FY29 needs. Capex may be revised for FY28 if order book grows.
SHIFT centre in Bangalore for software-defined vehicles and ADAS development.
demand_pricing: Industry: production up 22% y-o-y in Q1 FY27 (PV +17% to 14.5 lakh, CV +15% to ~3 lakh, 2W +23% to 72.5 lakh, 3W +39% to 3.5 lakh); management expects slower growth in Q3-Q4 because of the high FY26 base.
Plastics prices rose ~30-40%; 80-90% of the increase is passed through to OEMs within the same quarter under back-to-back arrangements, with spillover to the next quarter for a few OEMs.
Electronics components rose by more than 30-50% in some cases; the low Mechatronics share limits the margin impact.
Maruti Suzuki revenue grew 48% y-o-y in Q1; Bajaj Auto revenue grew ~64% y-o-y, attributed to wallet-share gains and new models.
Aftermarket growth was held back by pricing: competitors absorbed input-cost increases while Lumax passed them on in non-lighting categories.
Order book: ~one-third sits with IAC, mostly Mahindra. Order book across verticals: Advanced Plastics first, then Mechatronics, Alternate Fuels and Structures and Control Systems.

544733|2026-06.headline: GSP Crop Science Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR386 crore (from INR377 crore) and PAT grew about 16% to INR26.4 crore, helped by a one-off land sale gain.
544733|2026-06.overview: Revenue was broadly stable at INR386 crore versus INR377 crore in the prior-year quarter, with strong domestic momentum partly offset by raw material constraints in international business. Gross margin improved on a richer mix of specialty and patented products, and EBITDA was stated at around 11%. PAT rose almost 16% to INR26.4 crore, but management said about INR5.7 crore of other income came from a land sale, which is a one-off. ICRA upgraded the long-term rating from A to A+ stable, citing IPO-funded debt repayment and performance.

segments.name: Domestic B2C (branded)
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C sales; management aims to roughly double this over 3 years. Recent launches PCT 410 and Fighter are gaining volume.

segments.name: Domestic B2B
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Co-marketing of patented products with B2B partners showed good growth. Management targets B2B at 30-35% of revenue over the next 3 years.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: About 10% of Q1 revenue, seasonally weighted to H2 (Latin America, mainly Brazil). Q1 hit by raw material constraints, order slippage to China, and Brazil credit and liquidity concerns. Expected to be about 20% of mix over 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 15% growth rate, with EBITDA growing 13-14% over the next 2-3 years (earlier in the call, EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% was given).

Management expects the Q2 season to track anticipated growth; PAT in Q2 is expected to be a similar share of full-year PAT as last year (Q2 FY26 was about 60% of full-year PAT), with the absolute number higher.
Management expects Brazil demand to recover from September for H2 ahead of the October season.
Management targets a domestic market share rise from about 3-3.5% to 7-8%.

Management says patented product share of the portfolio will double in 2-3 years, with about 12 products launched in the last 3 years and two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year.
capex_capacity: Technical capacity utilisation is about 70-75%, with room to grow and scope to swap high-value, low-volume products in multi-product plants.
Formulation plant utilisation is about 25-30%; management says formulations are sized for peak season and are not a bottleneck.
Backward-integration technical plant at Dahej and Saykha was capitalised after the prior quarter, raising depreciation.
Technical plant can run 12 months to supply H2 export demand from Latin America.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices were volatile in Q1 due to geopolitical events and petrochemical-linked inputs. Rupee depreciation of about 10-11% also raised input costs. Management said B2B prices can be passed on, while B2C has a lag covered by inventory.
Demand was held back by price volatility, with farmers, channel partners and formulators delaying purchases. Management cited El Nino forecasts and crude volatility.
Monsoon rains from July were good; cotton and soybean acreage is up and chillies are increasing. Management expects insecticide and fungicide demand to benefit.

Brazil demand is weak with customer liquidity and credit issues, and some orders moved to China on logistics. Management is cautious and is focusing on established B2B partners and second-tier distributors in Argentina and Uruguay.
Management says farmers are moving to specialty molecules and preventive spraying. It cited West Bengal as an example.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix between technicals, formulations and branded patented products?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix is about 45% B2C, 45% B2B and 10% export. Formulations are about 75% and technicals about 25%. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C, with a target to double over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of IPO fund utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The loan repayment object has been fully met during the quarter. A small residual amount remains pending bank settlement of brokerage, which may take 2-3 months, before the IPO account can be closed.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material costs affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from product mix. Rupee depreciation of 10-11% and petrochemical-linked price volatility raised input costs. B2B passes costs through, and B2C is covered by inventory for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q1 export business faring and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Brazil orders were delayed by pricing volatility and some shifted to China. Management expects destocking, with demand returning from September for the October season. It is pursuing Argentina and Uruguay via second-tier distributors and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kharif progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: July rains were good and key kharif acreage is up. Management said South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) is still a wait-and-watch situation based on monsoon. No material shortage is seen currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical utilisation is about 70-75% with scope to add high-value products. Formulation utilisation is about 25-30%, which management says is by design for peak-season capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The company plans one or two new technicals a year, with data generation taking 4-5 years, and two to three new patented formulations a year, with a pipeline covering the next 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off nature of other income and the outlook for it?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.7 crore of the INR8.3 crore other income is the land-sale gain. No further other income is planned for the remaining quarters. Management said the land sale is a one-off.

risks_watch: Other income of about INR5.7 crore from a one-off land sale inflated Q1 PAT. Excluding it, management's PAT growth looks much lower, and the analyst cited roughly flat PBT.
Raw material volatility and rupee depreciation of 10-11% could compress B2C margins if pass-through lags.
Brazil credit and liquidity stress, plus loss of orders to China on logistics, puts export recovery at risk. Export is about 10% of Q1 revenue.
South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) depends on monsoon, and the El Nino forecast adds uncertainty.
Management guidance is inconsistent: EBITDA margin 12-13% in one answer, EBITDA growth 13-14% in another, and PAT growth expectations are not quantified. Monitor Q2 delivery against these.
544733|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on domestic patented product growth and the mix shift, but cautious on export, particularly Brazil. Management was less precise on margin and growth figures, sometimes giving different numbers across answers.

500575|2026-06.headline: Voltas Q1 FY27 net profit rose to Rs 213 crore (Rs 141 crore) on revenue of Rs 4,765 crore, with RAC market share at 17.3%.

Segment A (unitary cooling) grew 33%, with RAC volumes up 45% and secondary market share at 17.3% against 15.9% for FY26, widening the lead over the nearest competitor to 4 percentage points. Commodity inflation, rupee depreciation and freight costs were largely passed on (10-12% cost increase, near full pass-through), and UCP EBIT margin improved to 5.3% from 3.7%. Projects (Segment B) was soft on execution issues and delayed new orders in the Middle East, while Commercial Refrigeration and Air Coolers were muted. Management also signed a binding term sheet for a 50-50 compressor JV with Atomberg.

segments.name: Segment A - Unitary Cooling Products (RAC, Commercial AC, Commercial Refrigeration, Air Coolers, Voltbek)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 33% led by RAC; secondary RAC share 17.3% (FY26: 15.9%). Voltbek posted record quarterly sales, with YTD share of 9.4% in washing machines and 7.4% in refrigerators; still loss-making.

segments.name: Segment C - Engineering Products and Services
segments.commentary: High double-digit top-line growth; Mining and Construction Equipment grew strongly on crushing and screening demand and O&M contracts. Textile Machinery grew double digits with early signs of order-book revival.

guidance_outlook: Voltbek EBITDA breakeven, previously targeted for FY27, likely pushed out by a few quarters due to commodity inflation.
UCP margin aspiration of 7%+ (management cited prior quarters above 7%), with improvement targeted year-on-year over the next ~8 quarters; no firm timeline given.
Electromechanical projects: Q2 may not be much better; recovery expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Q2 expected to be seasonally leaner for cooling; channel inventory maintained at around 4 weeks.
No price increase planned unless West Asia-driven costs rise further; any margin upside to come via lower channel schemes.
Projects strategy shifting to shorter-gestation private-sector, data centre, manufacturing and MEP jobs; fewer government projects with payment-delay risk.
capex_capacity: Atomberg 50-50 JV for RAC compressors: planned capacity about 2.8 million units; ramp from under 1 million, to 1-2 million, then 2.5+ million; commercial production about 18 months from start of work.

Outsourcing share stable: Window ACs ~100% OEM (about 10% of peak-quarter AC sales); Split ACs about 75% self-manufactured and 25% OEM.
demand_pricing: Industry RAC secondary sales up about 15% (GfK Nielsen); management estimates primary growth of 20-22% in volume and 25-26% in value.

Cost inflation of 10-12% in FY27 peak: about 7-8% from BEE table change (3-star +5%, 5-star +15%), plus 4-5% from commodities, rupee depreciation, freight and plastics; near-full pass-through achieved.
Commercial Refrigeration costs rose about 10% for freezers, 15% for water coolers and 10% for water dispensers; channel resisted, with traction improving this quarter.
Peer RAC players' EBIT reportedly fell 3-4 percentage points; Voltas says its Q1-on-Q1 EBIT margin improved.
Channel cautious on stock; July-August demand not yet clear, festive season view too early.

qa_highlights.question: Compressor JV: capacity, capex, timeline and split among the three entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity about 2.8 million compressors; total capex still early-stage. Commercial production about 18 months away; the JV was driven by supply security and QCO import limits.

qa_highlights.question: Voltbek EBITDA breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier target for this year; West Asia-driven commodity spike meant brands could not pass through all costs, so breakeven may slip by a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How do QCO norms get met until the JV is operational?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports allowed up to 30% based on FY25 volumes; continued purchases from Highly and GMCC (India capacity blocked), blending with own supply later.

qa_highlights.question: Why UCP margins are 5% in a strong quarter, and what is steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers saw EBIT fall 3-4 pts; Voltas improved YoY on scale, no factory disruption, cost absorption and cost-out. Aspiration of 7%+ over the next ~8 quarters; CFO said margins vary quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Projects margin outlook and order book quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Calibrated order booking to avoid fixed-price contracts without escalation clauses; shifting to shorter-gestation private, data-centre and MEP jobs.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory and July-August demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel cautious; inventory around 4 weeks; too early to judge festive season, with a 4-6 week monitoring window.

qa_highlights.question: Voltbek loss in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Share of JV loss booked at Rs 37 crore; EMP margins to improve in Q3-Q4 after a soft Q2.

526612|2026-06.headline: Blue Dart Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR1,658 crore (from INR1,442 crore) and PAT reached INR87 crore, driven mainly by yield and fuel surcharge rather than volume.
526612|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,658 crore against INR1,442 crore a year earlier, with PAT of INR87 crore. Management attributed growth mainly to pricing: GPI-led increases, targeted repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery after diesel and Brent prices rose from around March–May. Tonnage grew about 7% to 364,430 tons and shipments about 2% to 96.15 million, with air volume up about 2.6% and surface up about 9%. Management declined to quantify yield growth or give forward volume and margin guidance, citing seasonality and H2 resourcing challenges.

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: About 60% of revenue but about 25% of kilos (1:3 air:surface by weight). Volume growth about 2.6%; growth is mainly yield-led. Freighter pallet utilisation 85–90%.

segments.name: Surface / Ground
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue and about 75% of kilos. Volume up about 9%; B2B revenue up about 14%. Management says surface is the faster-growing segment and is approaching air in size.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Revenue up more than 10% YoY. Management says about 50-plus million of the 96.15 million shipments are e-commerce, and Blue Dart holds about 12–13% of outsourced/3PL e-commerce.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 70% B2B and 30% B2C (plus or minus 2%).

segments.name: BFSI (documents and cards)
segments.commentary: BFSI alone is about 10–15% of total revenue; documents plus cards together, including small parcels, about 25–30%. Management says BFSI is no longer a growing segment.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not forecast volumes, citing seasonality, but expects Q2 to reflect the full fuel-surcharge increase from May onward.
Typical GPI realisation is about 4–5%, with extra customer-specific corrections on top.

Standalone annualised capex guided at INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Aviation capex is driven by maintenance and engine cycles, with roughly 20–25% of depreciation as ongoing capex.
H2 is expected to bring higher volumes, but resourcing flex will determine margins; management aims for stable, consistent margin improvement.
No major expansion plans; growth is expected to be organic. Possible consolidation and expansion of southern hubs (Bangalore, Chennai) and Mumbai, a few quarters away.
capex_capacity: Two major hubs added in North and a couple of medium-sized hubs in East in the prior period.
Freighter pallet utilisation at 85–90%; aircraft flown mainly at night and scheduled against available load.
Belly cargo is 30–40% of overall load in a typical month, and can reach 70–80% on lower-volume weekends. Blue Dart flies to 8 stations and carries belly cargo at 25–50 other locations.
The two aircraft acquired earlier are back to pre-acquisition pallet utilisation (as of 2024) and are integrated into the network.
demand_pricing: Growth came mainly from pricing: GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge pass-through. Management said yield was 'directionally' the main driver of revenue growth.
Fuel surcharge on surface is revised monthly based on local diesel prices, which rose in mid-May after about 5–6 years. Air fuel surcharge rose from April as Brent climbed from around mid-March.
Auto is a niche express vertical; management estimates it grows at about high-teens, in line with surface B2B. Market share is hard to quantify.
Management says e-commerce pricing remains competitive, with capacity still available in the market; Blue Dart positions itself as a premium player.
Management says it gained a very small but roughly stable market share in SME clients versus last year (informal assessment).

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue growth mainly from pricing, given volume growth was only about 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed directionally. Pricing came from GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery (fuel surcharge offset fuel cost rises, which also lifted yield).

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-commerce growth lower than the industry, and is it a focus area?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce is a growth driver but not a mass-volume focus. It is prioritising premium, time-critical traffic that fits its capacity, and it is not targeting the largest e-commerce share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and new hubs?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone annualised capex is INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Two major northern hubs and some medium eastern hubs were added, and southern and Mumbai hub consolidation is being considered a few quarters away.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 brings volume opportunity but also resourcing challenges. It aims to keep or improve margins through efficiency and better realisation, without quantifying either.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2 recently acquired aircraft stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said pallet utilisation was restored to pre-acquisition levels by 2024. The aircraft are part of the wider network, and capacity is not a constraint; yield is the main lever.

risks_watch: Growth quality: about 7% tonnage growth against about 15% revenue growth implies most of the increase came from pricing and surcharges, which may not persist.
Fuel: diesel and Brent rises were passed through with a lag; Q2 is expected to show the full surcharge effect, but any fall in fuel prices would reverse it.
Air volume growth of about 2.6% versus surface about 9% suggests air is stagnating in volume.
H2 resourcing: management flagged that peak-season flex will decide margins.
Competition in e-commerce pricing remains intense, with spare capacity in the market.
BFSI (documents and cards) is no longer growing, and the 25–30% documents-plus-parcels exposure needs monitoring.
Management declined to provide e-commerce split by air and surface, D2C share, or yield premium figures, limiting visibility.
526612|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's numbers and direction, but guarded on forward-looking detail: it declined to quantify yield, the e-commerce premium, and market share, and repeatedly deferred to seasonality rather than guiding.

543528|2026-06.headline: Venus Pipes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% to INR320.5 crore and EBITDA hit a record INR51.5 crore, with margin flat at 16.1%.

543426|2026-06.headline: Metro Brands Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 14% and PAT about 13%, with April-May soft and June recovering to mid-teens-plus growth.

April and May were soft on the U.S.-Iran conflict overhang and a shift in wedding dates, while June rebounded to a mid-teen double-digit gain. The e-commerce SOR (3P) channel slowed to 9%, while D2C and marketplace omni each grew about 60%. Management reiterated gross margin near 55-57% (quarter at almost 60%), EBITDA around 30%, and full-year PAT of 13-15%, citing marketing, treasury income, new-store dilution and talent/tech investment as PAT margin drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Why were April and May muted when peers held up, and was June materially stronger?

qa_highlights.question: Why did SOR (3P) e-commerce slow, and will discounting cut growth?
qa_highlights.answer: SOR growth was lumpy from return-swap timing, plus a deliberate reduction in low price points and 3P discounts. Management expects e-com to grow well into double digits, with 20-30% a year as the healthy range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year margin outlook given wage hikes and input cost pressure?

qa_highlights.question: Why not guide to 20% growth when demand is improving?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the PAT margin decline and when does PAT growth return to mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps from top-of-funnel marketing, plus lower treasury income versus last year's teens yields, new-store dilution (about 40 Walkway stores among 140 openings), and talent/tech investment. Management expects a return to 15%-plus PAT growth as these normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Is BIS relief helping FILA launch timelines, and how is FILA inventory being discounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recent QC order allowing imports has no significant impact; ASEAN BIS renewals are the larger constraint. Heavy FILA discounting reflects legacy acquired inventory and 3-4 month sports life cycles with 9-month buying lead times.

risks_watch: BIS certification erraticism for factories, especially ASEAN suppliers and high-end athletic footwear, could constrain FILA and sports launches.

Minimum wage increases in certain states could raise front-end staff costs.
Treasury income normalisation and continued marketing investment may keep PAT margin below prior-year levels in the near term.
Diwali shift into Q3 could weigh on Q2 growth; FILA turnaround timing (late FY27) and MetroActiv and Walkway store productivity are open questions.

505255|2026-06.headline: GMM Pfaudler Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 925 crores, but EBITDA fell 7% YoY to INR 94 crores on pricing pressure and organisation-building costs.
505255|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to INR 925 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR 22 crores, while EBITDA fell 7% YoY to INR 94 crores (up 25% QoQ). Order intake was flat YoY at INR 1,007 crores, and the order backlog reached a record INR 2,289 crores (+20% YoY, +4% QoQ). The company moved to four global technology divisions (CRT, PPT, HET, PST) and disclosed segment results for the first time. Management said debt reduction (about EUR 7 million by end-Q2) and refinancing are under way, with no numeric debt target given.

segments.name: CRT (Corrosion Resistance Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 466 crores (+10% YoY); order intake INR 502 crores (+23% YoY). Glass-lined pharma and chemical demand described as stable; large aftermarket and service base.

segments.name: PPT (Process Performance Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 255 crores (+23% YoY); order intake INR 367 crores (+64% YoY). Covers mixing, filtration, drying, and sealing; pharma and food & beverage adoption cited.

segments.name: HET (Heavy Engineering Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 74 crores (flat YoY); order intake INR 58 crores (up more than 700% YoY). India-led, oil and gas, petrochemicals, with nuclear and power entry and EIL approvals.

segments.name: PST (Process System Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 131 crores (+46% YoY); order intake INR 80 crores vs INR 363 crores in Q1 FY26, which included one large defence order. Skids and engineered systems for semiconductor, defence and pharma.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 15%, described as a minimum target; management said current verticals are roughly around this range, with no timeline given.
Management expects improvement YoY across all businesses but declined to give a specific margin number; quarter-on-quarter margin tracking was framed as the approach.
Debt: about EUR 7 million to be repaid by end of Q2 FY27; further reduction via refinancing over 12 to 18 months. No year-end debt target disclosed.
Tax rate: work with around 30%, possibly slightly lower in the long term, expected within 18 to 24 months after refinancing and entity restructuring.
Most of the Q1 order intake and backlog is in 10 to 12 month execution projects, expected to be largely executed in FY27.
Possible investor day around Q2 FY27 (management said 'hopefully').
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Global engineering centre (GEC) with about 12 people in place; Poland and India being developed as low-cost engineering hubs.
Workforce reductions in UK (prior year) and factory workforce in Germany (last year) expected to flow through to costs in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: India pharma improving, driven by CDMO and API investment in Hyderabad; glass-lined inquiries and conversion rates up vs 12 months ago. Management says Q1 and Q2 look strong for glass-lined.
Chemicals flat in India and remain challenging in Europe; no structural change seen.

International pharma improving in Europe and Americas; US has large glass-lined pharma orders; China back with glass-lined orders; Europe still slow overall though several large glass-lined orders won.
Peptide investment is a new pharma driver, with a large peptide order supplied last year and two large Hyderabad system orders.
Pricing pressure in a shifting business mix cited as a reason for lower YoY EBITDA. Management expects pricing to improve as markets recover.
Opening backlog for FY27 was about 30% higher than a year earlier, which was partly flattered by a large defence order (~EUR 30 million) in the prior-year base.

qa_highlights.question: Are there signs of recovery in chemical and pharma markets, and is competition easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Pharma is improving in India (Hyderabad CDMO), the US and Europe; chemicals remain flat. India traditional markets are better than 12 months ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India standalone margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from HET (lower-margin, longer-cycle project business); a mix shift plus investment in people for the new organisation. Management expects margins to recover over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the target EBITDA margins and debt levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 15% EBITDA as the aspiration and said margins would be tracked quarter-on-quarter. It declined to give a year-end debt target.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book executes within 10 to 12 months, and what is the debt repayment schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Large majority of the roughly INR 1,000 crore Q1 intake is executable in 10 to 12 months. Debt repayment of EUR 7 million now, with a further reduction over 12 to 18 months; no amount was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state tax rate and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 30%, possibly slightly lower long term, achieved in 18 to 24 months after debt refinancing and entity rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there severance cost in Q1, and will employee costs keep rising?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-off severance in Q1. Management aims to lower employee costs over time by shifting non-critical work to low-cost locations, though some sales hires will be added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost and order intake outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Average interest cost of 6% to 7%, mostly hedged SOFR/EURIBOR-linked debt. Order intake is flat YoY but with a different profile, with most Q1 orders at 10 to 12 month cycles.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin recovery depends on three or four underperforming units; management did not give a timeline beyond 'a few quarters'.
Investment in people and organisation raises employee costs ahead of the revenue benefit.
Debt of about INR 835 crores (March 2026) with refinancing and entity clean-up (24 to 25 entities) still incomplete; tax rate depends on this.
Chemicals demand remains weak in India and Europe.
Q1 order intake was flat YoY and the prior-year base contained a large defence order, so the YoY comparison is not like-for-like.
Whether Q2 order intake is strong enough to sustain the backlog and build momentum.
505255|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on strategy and the new divisional structure, but cautious and often non-committal on numbers: no margin timeline, no debt target, and no tax timeline beyond 18 to 24 months. Management repeatedly asked for 'a few quarters' of consistent results before giving more detail.

543936|2026-06.headline: Senco Gold Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 67% YoY and EBITDA margin fell to 7.0% (INR213 crores) on gold-price, discounting and one-off cost effects.
543936|2026-06.overview: Senco crossed INR3,000 crores of sales in a single quarter, with consolidated revenue up about 67% YoY and retail up 50%, same-store sales growth around 39%. April was the strong month (about INR1,500-1,600 crores), while May and June moderated to roughly INR500-600 crores a month amid West Bengal elections, Adhik Maas and heat wave. Reported EBITDA was INR213 crores at 7.0% margin and consolidated PAT INR101 crores at 3.3%, with margin pressure from other expenses (about INR195 crores vs about INR80 crores a year earlier), a gold-price decline, discounting and GML-related finance cost. Management retained FY27 guidance of 20%+ value growth and a 7.5%-7.8% sustainable operational EBITDA margin, and said July and August are running about 25% YoY ahead.

segments.name: Retail / owned and franchise stores
segments.commentary: Retail sales +50% YoY, growth broad-based across zones including newly launched Central region (7 stores) and Delhi NCR; 3 COCO and 4 franchise stores added plus 1 Sennes showroom in Q1.

segments.name: Diamond jewellery
segments.commentary: Value +43% YoY and volume +18%, with management flagging stud-ratio improvement as a margin lever.

segments.name: Factory subsidiary
segments.commentary: Captive design and jewellery supply hub performing well, enabling about 100 designs per day; more than 150,000 designs a year.

segments.name: Sennes / Sennes Fashion / Dubai entity
segments.commentary: Start-up phase (lab-grown diamonds, perfume, leather bags); together weighed on consolidated PAT.

segments.name: Aham (men's titanium-gold-diamond range)
segments.commentary: Newly launched, priced INR20,000 to INR1 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 value growth guidance retained at 20%+, with 25%+ possible depending on the year; implies revenue above INR10,000 crores vs INR8,430 crores in FY26; revisit after Q3.
Sustainable operational EBITDA margin guided at 7.5%-7.8% for the full year, over a normalised 2-3 quarter period; management aims to move toward 8% via higher stud ratio.
PAT margin target of around 4.5%-5%; ROE and ROCE targeted toward the 20% range.
12-15 further store openings planned in the rest of FY27, majority franchise, focused on East and North India.
Q2 expected to be seasonally softer and a planning/inventory-build quarter; July and August running about 25% YoY growth and 8%-10% above May-June level.
Longer term: INR20,000 crores+ revenue and 300+ stores in 4-5 years (currently ~200 stores).
capex_capacity: Store network at around 200 stores; 12-15 more openings planned for the rest of FY27, mainly franchise.
Inventory of roughly INR5,000 crores; inventory per store guided at 15-18 kg to 35-40 kg depending on market.
Management estimates INR8,000-9,000 crores of inventory may be needed to reach INR20,000 crores revenue.
Inventory to be built from September ahead of festive season, then sold through.
Factory subsidiary supports about 100 new designs per day.
demand_pricing: Old gold exchange accounted for ~43% of sales quantity on a blended basis, above 55% at owned stores.
Customers shifted to lightweight, design-led, lower-ticket jewellery (9-carat, 14-carat, lightweight ranges), with grammage down ~1% on a 24-carat-equivalent basis.
Discounting and schemes intensified after the customs-duty increase; management cites competitive intensity as a margin drag.
Monthly mix: April ~55% of quarterly sales; May-June ~45% combined.
Hedging held at about 50% under Board policy; management intends to move toward 75%-80% as gold volatility eases.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance only 20%+ after a strong Q1, and what is July-August trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it has historically guided conservatively; July and August are running about 25% YoY and about 8%-10% above the May-June level, with a stronger build expected in October-November.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses jump to about INR195-229 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to marketing, store renovations in lean season, and customer offers and schemes; it said this run rate is quarter-specific and expected to subside.

qa_highlights.question: Why was GML availability constrained and finance cost up?
qa_highlights.answer: Banks restricted GML in March-April amid duty uncertainty and efforts to curb gold imports; company bought more gold locally and cut GML exposure, and says GML is now more available.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7.5%-7.8% EBITDA range operational and what is the hedge effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the range is operational, assuming a neutral gold-price environment and appropriate hedging; hedge at about 50% is intended to still deliver it.

qa_highlights.question: What was the customs-duty gain in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a gross gain of INR12-15 crores for the roughly 45 days of impact in Q1, partly offset by schemes; benefit expected over 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cash flow from operations expected to look negative and what is inventory strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will disclose CFO with H1; lower GML borrowing may make CFO appear negative on accounting basis. Inventory days ~152, reduced on store-by-store basis.

risks_watch: Margin volatility: Q1 margin at 7.0% vs guided 7.5%-7.8%; hedge ratio at ~50% leaves exposure to gold-price moves.
Other expenses (~INR195 crores) and discounting: management says quarter-specific, watch whether they normalise in Q2.
Inventory days at ~152 and capital efficiency; ROE/ROCE target of 20% depends on inventory productivity.
Cash flow from operations not yet disclosed; management expects it may be negative in Q1 on lower GML borrowing.
Sennes and Dubai subsidiaries weighing on consolidated PAT; 65-70% of business from Eastern India and West Bengal, concentration risk.
Discrepancy: business update reported 62% growth vs 67% in limited review numbers; management attributed gap to accounting adjustments.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY26 reported margin 10.1%, which included 1.5%-2% inventory gains
Q1 FY26 adjusted PAT est. INR70-75 crores
from ~INR80 crores; marketing down 19% from ~INR43 crores to ~INR35 crores
about 45 days of impact in Q1

523301|2026-06.headline: TCPL Packaging Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~79% YoY to INR 40 crore on 16% total income growth, and the company announced a INR 125 crore lithium-ion battery separator film venture.
523301|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 16% YoY to INR 495 crore, EBITDA grew 17% to INR 88 crore, and EBITDA margin improved to 18%. Cash profit rose 56% to INR 76 crore and PAT rose nearly 79% to INR 40 crore, helped partly by a normalised interest cost versus a forex/mark-to-market hit in the prior-year quarter. Growth was domestic-led (good double-digit domestic growth, export growth positive but lower) with volumes up high single digits. Management announced a proposed subsidiary to enter lithium-ion battery separator films (INR 125 crore over 18 months, commercial production targeted Q4 FY28) and a ~30% expansion of flexible packaging capacity (INR 50-60 crore).

financial_highlights.change: improved YoY (exact prior figure not stated)
domestic growth at good double-digit clip

segments.name: Flexible Packaging
segments.commentary: Existing facility at optimal utilisation; growing faster than carton business. Fourth line adding ~30% to existing capacity at INR 50-60 crore, expected operational January/February 2028. Management says flexible EBITDA margins are structurally lower than carton, though returns on capital are similar.

segments.name: Folding Cartons
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 70-plus%, varying by plant; some plants have headroom while others are full. Chennai plant ramping, management says 'getting there' toward ~70%. Expansion can be added within a quarter or 1.5 quarters' notice.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Growth positive YoY but below domestic; prior-year quarter was weak. Management is cautious on near-term global outlook. UK/EU FTAs give slight duty benefit mainly for flexibles.

segments.name: Battery separator films (proposed subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Proposed INR 125 crore investment over 18 months, commercial production targeted Q4 FY28. Phase 1 capacity ~70 million sqm (~6-8 GWh), with a long-term plan of ~500 million sqm (~50 GWh). Phase 1 topline guided at INR 150-200 crore; management expects a 'good double-digit' margin and ROCE above company's 20% hurdle.

guidance_outlook: FY27 non-separator capex budget about INR 100 crore; with separator announcement, total could rise to INR 100-150 crore. Separator spend mostly in next year after land purchase this year.
FY28 capex expected to be at least similar to FY27 levels, possibly higher, depending on carton business.
Management declined to give formal FY27 growth or margin guidance, saying the historic trend is expected to continue and margins follow top line.
Separator revenue at full 500 million sqm scale was estimated at INR 1,100-1,300 crore, with the price environment uncertain.
Separator qualification and scale-up expected to take at least a year, with FY28-29 spent in qualification and early commercial supply.
capex_capacity: Flexible packaging: ~30% capacity addition, INR 50-60 crore, new line operational Jan/Feb 2028; existing facility at optimal utilisation.
Folding cartons: utilisation ~70-plus% overall; new space being developed in some factories for next year's capex; Chennai plant can add 2-3 lines quickly with space and infrastructure ready.
Battery separator: Phase 1 ~70 million sqm/yr (~6-8 GWh), starting with coating and conversion before backward integration into base film; long-term ~500 million sqm (~50 GWh).
Separator land purchase in FY27; majority of spend in FY28. Phase 1 lead times for machinery similar to packaging machinery; base film lines would take longer.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as recovering, with good double-digit domestic growth and improved customer volume growth.
Price increases pass through with a lag of over a quarter due to inventory and order-book timing; management says EBITDA margin could not be held without pass-through.
Competition in separators: no lithium-ion separator capacity online in India; lead-acid separator makers exist. Internationally, China leads with multiple players (SEMCORP cited as largest).
Brand owners' adoption of mono-material recyclable packaging in India is slower than expected because government has not mandated it; export demand for recyclable packaging is growing.
Management says the pan masala plastic ban notification is 'misleading' and the company is not a major supplier to that segment, so impact is marginal in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Flexible packaging capacity addition and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity to rise by ~30% at an investment of INR 50-60 crore; existing capacity is almost fully utilised.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost lower YoY, is it lower debt?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The prior-year quarter included a one-time forex/mark-to-market loss; this quarter is a normalised comparison. Debt figure not given.

qa_highlights.question: Separator Phase 1 topline and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 topline INR 150-200 crore; margin expected to be a good double-digit number; asset turns not comparable because of large land purchase.

qa_highlights.question: Separator technology: in-house or partner?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology developed through a mix of external sources and in-house R&D; management cites group experience across many specialised fields.

qa_highlights.question: Chennai folding carton ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is 'fairly satisfied'; utilisation is 'getting there' toward ~70%; room for 2-3 more lines with space in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will the separator subsidiary be 100% owned, and what is capex per 70 million sqm?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 100% owned. Scaling is not linear; capex will be more than 8x Phase 1 because of base film backward integration.

qa_highlights.question: Opex for the separator business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a top-heavy team would not be a significant drag at the group's INR 1,500-2,000 crore topline; separator opex is already budgeted.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory with flexible mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Flexible has lower EBITDA margins but similar return on capital; no structural margin direction given for the next 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Separator project: execution risk for a new technology in a 'very unforgiving' battery market; qualification and ramp depend on cell makers' factory timelines; PLI support not formalised.
Capex step-up: FY27-28 capex rising to INR 100-150 crore plus separator spend, with the separator's full-scale capex significantly larger than Phase 1.
Export outlook uncertain given geopolitics; management says 'if there is another war somewhere, we do not know'.
Flexible mix growth may dilute EBITDA margins; management did not explain why margins rose despite the mix shift.
Slow adoption of mono-material recyclable packaging by Indian brand owners in the absence of a government mandate.
Price pass-through lag of over a quarter on raw material costs.
523301|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the quarter's numbers, and enthusiastic about the separator venture. On forward guidance, management was cautious and declined to quantify FY27 growth or margins, and it deflected several questions on separator tech, PLI and margin structure.

542830|2026-06.headline: IRCTC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.1% to INR1,370 crore, but EBITDA fell 2.77% to INR386 crore as catering margins and internet ticketing spinoffs weakened.
542830|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 18.1% YoY to INR1,370 crore, led by catering (INR732 crore, +33.8%) and tourism (INR168 crore, +13.5%). EBITDA was INR386 crore (28.17% margin), down 2.77% YoY, and PAT was about INR330 crore. Margins were pressured by a one-time HR/gratuity charge of about INR20 crore, proof-of-concept costs on six trains, a West Asia-driven resin cost spike in Rail Neer, and lower non-convenience fee income in internet ticketing. Management said the catering and HR effects are non-recurring and that the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by November.

segments.name: Internet Ticketing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore (+0.5%); EBIT margin fell to 80.33% from 84.12%, attributed to NGET infra refresh, about INR10 crore maintenance booking, and lower marketing/ad and agent income. About 89% of reserved tickets are booked online.

segments.name: Catering
segments.commentary: Revenue INR732 crore (+33.8%); segment margin 9.29% vs 10.42% in FY26. Management attributed the drop to about INR4 crore proof-of-concept cost on six trains and about INR10 crore HR/gratuity charge; catering onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore.

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR109 crore (+2.83%); margin about 10% vs 14-15% prior, driven by resin/petroleum cost rise (material cost INR55 crore to INR61 crore) linked to West Asia crisis. Management said profit fell only about INR4 crore overall.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168 crore (+13.5%); EBITDA margin improved to 11.31% from 8.78% on better product mix and cost realisation, despite geopolitical disruption. Non-fare revenue from Tejas naming/wrap rights noted as a new lever.

guidance_outlook: Management expects catering margins to return to the traditional 10-12% range; proof-of-concept trains to finish by September (2 trains) and November (2 trains).
The one-time HR cost of about INR20 crore (catering INR10 crore) is not expected to recur in Q2.

Rail Neer augmentation: Ambernath from 2 lakh to 3 lakh bottles/day and Danapur from 1 lakh to 2 lakh bottles/day, targeted for FY27; four new plants (Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi, Bhagalpur) may spill into FY28.
About 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore).
Management aims to bring non-convenience fee back toward INR150 crore over time via iPay, e-wallet loyalty and agent business changes; no quarterly run-rate given.
Active-active disaster recovery planned at Secunderabad, with further investment expected in Q2-Q4.
capex_capacity: Rail Neer installed capacity about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after closure of one plant (from 18.4 lakh); supply about 15.5 lakh bottles/day against higher demand at some stations.
NGET infra refresh: about INR150 crore infused into PRS modernisation; ticketing throughput about 37,000 tickets per minute, targeted to exceed 1 lakh.
E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day in FY27 from 1.05 lakh a year earlier; e-pantry live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100.
Catering services in 81 Vande Bharat trains run by IRCTC; other Vande Bharat catering is outsourced to empanelled licensees via limited tenders.
Payment aggregator (IRCTC Payments Ltd): final RBI application submitted by 4 August 2026 with SAR and MVP; RBI response expected within this financial year; TSP already engaged.
demand_pricing: Average daily tickets 14.58 lakh; Q1 total 13.27 crore (AC 6.92 crore, non-AC 6.35 crore). IRCTC share of railway ticketing rose to 88.92% from 88.78%.
UPI share of tickets 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

Catering revenue bridge: onboard sales INR413 crore (INR301 crore), licence fee from prepaid and other trains INR224 crore (INR192 crore), static units INR33 crore (INR20 crore), e-catering INR22 crore (INR9 crore), election specials INR41 crore (INR5 crore).
Opt-out for catering on prepaid trains estimated at roughly 25-30% (management said unconfirmed); complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals.
Tourism OTA-linked income about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%); internet ticketing about 18% of total revenue excluding convenience fee, 26% including it.
Rail Neer priced at INR14 per bottle; third-party brands visible on non-AC trains and kiosks. Management attributed this to unauthorised vendors filling gaps at non-mandatory stations.

financial_highlights.change: +0.5% YoY; EBITDA margin above 80%, EBIT margin 80.33% vs 84.12%
+33.82% YoY; segment margin 9.29% vs 10.42% in FY26

539301|2026-06.headline: Arvind SmartSpaces Q1 FY27 presales rose 147% YoY to INR432 crores; PAT jumped to INR97 crores on Orchards Phase 1 BU receipt.
539301|2026-06.overview: Presales of INR432 crores grew 147% YoY, with management attributing it to both Aqua City demand and broader core-market strength. Revenue rose to INR318 crores from INR102 crores and adjusted EBITDA to INR150 crores from INR25 crores, mainly from Orchards Phase 1 in Bengaluru receiving BU. Collections grew 76% to INR336 crores and net operating cash flow was INR81 crores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 35-40% bookings growth, INR4,000-5,000 crores BD and 22-25% EBITDA margin on new sales, and India Ratings upgraded the company to AA- (stable).

segments.name: Ahmedabad (Aqua City, horizontal)
segments.commentary: Aqua City named as standout booking performer in Q1; new Vastrapur project planned for launch this year. Management cites leadership in horizontal development in Ahmedabad.

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Orchards Phase 1 BU received, driving the quarter's revenue and profit step-up; Bengaluru stock close to INR3,000 crores. Three launches planned this year, including Sarjapur, which has approvals.

segments.name: Mumbai / MMR
segments.commentary: Mumbai stock of INR4,000 crores-plus GDV; two Goregaon redevelopment-related and BD additions. Goregaon saleable carpet area about 6.7 lakh sq ft, 35-floor-plus, about 4 years to complete; 2 Mumbai launches planned this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bookings growth of 35-40% over FY26, implying about INR2,100-2,200 crores (per Q&A).
FY27 business development of INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV; INR2,600 crores already added in Q1; management leaning to upper band.
EBITDA margin on new sales of 22-25%; management says portfolio average about 25%, JD projects at lower end and outright at higher end.
FY27 operating cash flow target of INR400-500 crores (FY26 about INR400 crores).
Launch pipeline of about INR3,000-3,500 crores booking value across 6 projects (Ahmedabad 1, Bengaluru 3, Mumbai 2) this year.
Land outflow for FY27 of about INR600-900 crores (Q&A), with 4-5 year realisation of INR5,100 crores operating cash flow from existing portfolio.

Medium-term 25-30% CAGR target over 4-5 years; comfort debt-to-equity at 1:1.
capex_capacity: Unrecognised revenue of INR3,825 crores to be recognised over about 4 years: plotted projects 2-3 years, high-rise OC in about 4 years.
Existing portfolio operating cash flow of over INR5,100 crores expected over next 4-5 years.
Construction spend ramped up in Q1; management says larger incremental outflow is construction cost.
Goregaon redevelopment: 200-plus units to be handed to existing members; area for members not yet disclosed.
Pen Khopoli project in Mumbai awaiting approvals; company hopes to launch at least 2 of 3 Mumbai projects this year.
demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand is strong; Aqua City plus broader core-market strength drove bookings.
Sustenance sales improved through sales team build-out across 3 cities, channel partner and marketing reach; sustenance may exceed plan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unrecognised revenue conversion and normalised margin outlook?

qa_highlights.question: How is OCF flattening and what is FY27 OCF guidance?

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and leverage comfort level?

qa_highlights.question: How will BD of INR600-1,000 crores be funded?

530521|2026-06.headline: Virat plans Rs 95 crore primary investment in Brahm Lifestyle for 70.2% stake, pivoting toward lifestyle brands; socks contract sales ~6 million pairs.
