segments.commentary: Sales INR 282 crores, +33% YoY and +12.2% QoQ, mainly volume and export-led with very little price increase; PBIT rose to INR 39 crores from INR 7 crores. Exports rose to about 40% of segment sales from about 35% last year.

segments.name: Ceramics (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 274 crores, +15.2% YoY but -1.6% QoQ on refractories seasonality; PBIT INR 59 crores vs INR 62 crores YoY as IC gains were offset by fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.

segments.name: Abrasives (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 328 crores, +14.7% YoY, volume-driven; PBIT INR 34 crores with margin falling to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY, due to about INR 16 crores cost push (resins, oil, fuel) and INR 8-9 crores volume drop QoQ.

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany, Abrasives)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 15.6 million, +18% YoY and +1.1% QoQ (INR 172 crores, +33.9% YoY); loss after tax EUR 0.7 million vs EUR 1.6 million a year ago. FY27 guidance of about 5% growth and a small PAT loss is maintained.

segments.name: CUMI Awuko Abrasives (Germany, being wound up)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 2.89 million, +11.1% YoY; loss after tax EUR 1.69 million vs EUR 0.9 million a year ago. Voluntary winding up is in progress and management aims to complete it in about a quarter.

segments.name: VAW Russia (Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales RUB 1.58 billion, -14.1% YoY in roubles but INR 201 crores, +3.1% YoY in rupee terms; PAT RUB 52.1 million vs RUB 71.5 million a year ago. Business is domestic-focused.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (51% subsidiary, Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 107 million, -14.7% QoQ; deemed commercially unviable. Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed a INR 17 crore loss; divestment or exit options are being explored, targeted for Q2.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth: FY27 guidance of about 4-4.5% reported, or 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko; management says it could reach about 15% on a comparable basis given the order book.
Consolidated Abrasives sales growth: guidance of 5.5-6% retained; 11-12% excluding Awuko (about INR 108 crores).
Consolidated Ceramics sales growth: raised to 23-25% from 15-15.5%; management expects the Ceramics margin to be at the higher end of the guidance.
Consolidated Electrominerals sales: guidance of a 6.5-7% decline retained (reported basis); 8-9% growth excluding Foskor, and management says this could be 9-10%.

Margins: Abrasives 9.5-10% and Electrominerals 9-9.5% retained, with Ceramics 20.5-21% maintained. Q1 consolidated Abrasives margin was about 2.5% excluding the Sterling gain, which management attributes to Awuko losses.
Capex of about INR 400 crores for FY27 retained. Rhodius guidance of about 5% growth with a small PAT loss is unchanged.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex was INR 53 crores in Q1 FY27 against INR 64 crores a year earlier; the FY27 target of about INR 400 crores is unchanged, and management would not give project-wise splits.

FY27 capex covers expansion in advanced ceramics for power electronics (including substrates), metallized tubes, rings and brazed assemblies, brown-fused alumina expansion, an integrated furnace for thermal spray powders and a zirconia furnace.
Metallized substrate facility is being set up with one anchor customer and a technology tie-up; it should be commissioned in FY27, with revenue from FY28.

Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components: small in FY27, picking up in FY28, with a peak targeted for FY30. Aerospace and defence will improve in FY27 with the main ramp from FY28. Powder purity is moving from 5N to 6N.
Refractories capacity expansion is on track, per management.
demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was volume-driven with very small price increases; management sees early easing of Chinese import competition but says exchange rates and China's export-rebate changes make the trend unclear.
Ceramics: growth was seen across segments; Wear Ceramics returned to growth this quarter after several quarters, and Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics are growing mainly through exports.

Electrominerals: volume-led, with treated-product mix helping margins; little or no price increase. Export share is rising toward 40%, helped by European duties on Chinese imports, with US and Asia efforts under way.

Abrasives cost push: oil-linked inputs such as resins rose sharply in May and June, with oil reaching about $117 a barrel. Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5%. The US-Iran conflict that began end-February 2026 drove the cost pressure.
Management said it will not pass on further price increases until the cost environment is clearer, and will decide one quarter at a time.

538666|2026-06.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs.1,074 crore and EBITDA 25% to Rs.178 crore, but reported PAT of Rs.88 crore was cushioned by lower forex gains.
538666|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs.1,074 crore, with volume down 1.6% and forex contributing 12.7 points. EBITDA margin expanded 220 bps to 16.6% and gross margin rose 120 bps to 36.7%, driven by mix in NAFTA, LATAM and rest of world. Europe revenue softened as distributors cut stock after an unusual heatwave, though Europe gross margin improved to 44.2%. Forex gain fell to Rs.7.5 crore from Rs.73.1 crore, so reported PBT and PAT looked weaker, while management said PBT before forex grew 16% to Rs.111 crore. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 10-15% revenue growth and about 35% gross margin.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Largest market; revenue softened as distributors cut stock after heatwave. Gross margin 44.2% vs 42.9% in Q1 FY26. Management said restocking has largely normalised.

segments.name: NAFTA
segments.commentary: Gross margin 32.8% vs 25.9% a year ago; growth strong and margins improved this quarter.

segments.name: LATAM
segments.commentary: Among the strongest growth engines this quarter, but gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0% a year ago.

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.commentary: Gross margin 30.8% vs 26.8% in Q1 FY26; growth reported as good with better profitability.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 10-15% maintained; volume growth expected at about 5-10%.
FY27 gross margin guided at 35% to 37% (management, in Q&A), and EBITDA margin in the 18-20% range.
Effective tax rate on annualised basis expected at 18-20%, with Q1 running higher.
Amortisation expected to be about Rs.370-375 crore annualised for FY27 vs about Rs.325 crore last year.
Management expects Europe volumes to recover to prior-year levels and the next three quarters to be better than Q1; last month of Q2 said to be better than Q1.
Registration investment of about Rs.450-500 crore per year; FY27 spend to rise further.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex was Rs.273 crore against FY27 guidance of Rs.500 crore; management says guidance not revised and the year could be Rs.480-550 crore.
Q1 capex was elevated by heavy data compensation payments, which management says will not repeat.
Total product registrations at 30 June 2026 were 3,016 (3,011 at 31 March 2026), with 1,027 applications pending.
Registrations by region: Europe 1,682 (up 3), NAFTA 325 (up 2), LATAM 760 (flat), rest of world 249 (flat).
demand_pricing: Volume declined 1.6% YoY; forex added 12.7 points and product mix subtracted 2.1 points.
Management said prices are improving sequentially after a severe decline about two years ago.
Europe revenue fell on distributor destocking linked to heatwave; management attributes this to weather, not molecules.
LATAM and NAFTA growth may partly reflect customer pre-buying ahead of season, per analyst; management said there is no strong trend.
Sourcing is 100% contract manufacturing, mainly from China, and all purchases are in US dollars.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the 9% revenue growth into volume, forex and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume -1.6%, forex +12.7%, product mix -2.1%, total +9%. Management said the mix impact is concentrated in Europe and should improve next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.7.5 crore forex gain and its accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly unrealised, from repricing foreign-currency receivables and payables at each balance sheet date. Q1 FY26 had a Rs.73 crore unrealised gain from a roughly 10% EUR/USD move. EBITDA excludes forex.

qa_highlights.question: Has Europe restocking normalised and what is FY27 EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restocking has improved and is largely normal, and guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex Rs.273 crore in Q1 vs Rs.500 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance not revised; Q1 included heavy data compensation spend that is not expected to recur. Full year could be Rs.480-550 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report PAT excluding forex for like-to-like comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO pointed to the investor presentation, which gives PBT and EBIT excluding forex. He said more clarity will be provided in future presentations.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the NAFTA and LATAM gross margin, and do margins hold for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe mix and price increases drove margins, LATAM volumes grew but margins dipped, and it expects Europe and NAFTA margins to stay in the same range.

risks_watch: Pace of Europe volume recovery after distributor destocking; management guides to a better next three quarters but gave no quantified timing.
LATAM gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0% despite strong volume growth.
Forex volatility: EUR/USD near 1.14 vs about 1.16-1.17 last year; management said it cannot be predicted.
Amortisation rising to about Rs.370-375 crore annualised, which pressures reported profit.
Registration pace: about 100 new registrations over three years versus about 300 in FY21-23, per analyst; no FY27 registration target given.
Capex range wide (Rs.480-550 crore) with no firm guidance revision.
538666|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the full-year outlook and on Europe recovery, but evasive on forex reporting, the capex range and the drivers of regional margins, which management called too detailed for the call. Management often deflected to weather and uncertainty.
key_quotes: It has improved and has reached to normal. In most of the cases, it is reaching the normality.
We don't manufacture anything anywhere in the world, including India.
Between 35% to 37%.
So, on annualized basis, could be around Rs. 370-375 crores.

PBT before forex Rs.111 crore, +16% YoY
vs Rs.702 crore at 31 Mar 2026; debt-free

544695|2026-06.headline: Msafe Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 40% YoY to ₹31.79 crore and PAT rose 44% to ₹7.27 crore, with the rental business up 24%.
544695|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹31.79 crore (up 40% YoY from ₹22.72 crore), PBT of ₹9.73 crore (up 46% from ₹6.65 crore) and net profit of ₹7.27 crore (up 44% from ₹5.04 crore). The Chairman said MS (formwork/scaffolding) volumes grew 7x YoY via temporary premises, while rental grew 24% and now contributes 46% of revenue. The company maintained an operating margin of about 40%, per the Chairman. Capacity remains the binding constraint: the Kosi Kotwan (Mathura) integrated plant targets operations by May 2027, and the formwork line is now targeted for December 2026 after machine delivery delays.

financial_highlights.change: +40% YoY vs ₹22.72 crore in Q1 FY26
Maintained despite inflation and growth investments

financial_highlights.metric: Margin by segment (as stated in Q&A)
financial_highlights.value: Rental about 47%; MS about 38%; aluminium about 10%
financial_highlights.change: Analyst reconciliation; management did not restate these as reported figures

financial_highlights.metric: Q1 expense on new plant/premises (as stated)
financial_highlights.value: ₹7.88 crore on new facility-related spend, later clarified as ₹8 crore
financial_highlights.change: Clarified as a continuous activity; the Q&A also cites ₹3.43 crore for the new plant

segments.name: Rental (scaffolding/access solutions)
segments.commentary: Rental grew 24% YoY and contributes 46% of revenue. Management said rental margins are higher and this is the company's main focus.

segments.name: MS (formwork/scaffolding) manufacturing
segments.commentary: MS volumes grew 7x YoY in Q1 by using temporary premises. Management expects MS share to rise, with formwork (aluminium) targeted for commercial production by December 2026.

segments.name: Aluminium formwork
segments.commentary: Four machines have arrived and are under operation, with five more pending; the company expects to complete installation by September 2026. Management said it is ready to trade at low margins if required.

guidance_outlook: IPO commitment of 50% CAGR reiterated by the Chairman; he said he could not confirm the exact figure cited in an interview.
Kosi Kotwan integrated manufacturing plant (Mathura) targeted to commence operations by May 2027; civil construction has begun.
New 500-ton-per-annum formwork/aluminium facility targeted to commence in December 2026, delayed from an earlier end-June target.
Management said the H1/H2 split for FY27 is roughly 40:60 for the new business, with the new formwork line not contributing materially in H1.
Chairman spoke of a ₹170 crore target and said the gap could be covered by all businesses; he did not provide a formal full-year target.
Initial formwork EBITDA margin may be lower than 20% during trials and ramp-up; no firm guidance given, and the 10-15% range was not confirmed.
capex_capacity: Kosi Kotwan (Mathura) integrated plant: 90 kg per annum augmentation (vs 30 kg already added via temporary premises), commissioning targeted May 2027.
Current MS capacity is almost fully utilised; management said it is at about 40% of its target peak, with peak utilisation of 80-90% expected after the new facility.
Management said the full ramp to 70-80% utilisation at the new facility would take about 6 months after commissioning.
A 30,000 sq m facility in Delhi (temporary premises) is in use; management is considering whether to vacate it after the new plant is running.
Capex: about ₹1 crore for machinery at the new plant, excluding land and civil works; ₹3-4 crore for certain assets was mentioned but not clearly attributed.
demand_pricing: Management said the company is currently about 10% of the Indian market for its products, and MS has not yet reached 10% share.
Competitive edge claimed: organised player, 21 warehouses across India, 24-hour delivery, and an ability to take orders from ₹5 crore upward. PSU orders also cited.
Aluminium market size cited as ₹1,300 crore currently, expected to reach ₹2,400 crore by 2030 (slide figure, as read out in the call).
Tubing is procured externally (no in-house extrusion); management plans an extrusion plant later.
Competitors' formwork EBITDA cited at about 20%; the company's own formwork margin not yet calculated, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue from the expanded capacity (25 kg and 90 kg), and why is the formwork expansion now ₹15 crore vs ₹4 crore earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the peak is not yet reached and the company is at about 40% of its target; the 25 kg/90 kg figures are capacity numbers, and the ₹15 crore figure is for robotic/automatic machines inclusive of rental. Steel and aluminium volumes were discussed in tonnes, not clearly reconciled to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any delay in the formwork timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Delivery of some machines was delayed; four have arrived and five are pending, and commercial production is now targeted for December 2026 versus an earlier end-June target.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 50% CAGR target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chairman reiterated the IPO commitment of 50% CAGR but said he could not recall the specific figure quoted in an interview; he said the company hopes to achieve it.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new formwork business affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial margins may be lower due to trials and ramp-up; management expects them to normalise over time through scale and working-capital use. A 20% EBITDA margin was not confirmed; 10-15% was not confirmed either.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ₹170 crore target be achieved, given a delay in formwork?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chairman said all businesses would contribute and that the delay would be covered by other products; he did not give a segment-level breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ₹8 crore quarterly spend on the new facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the spend is continuous through FY27 and could be more than ₹8 crore per quarter; the split between land, civil works and machinery was not provided.

540025|2026-06.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 1,898 million, but EBITDA fell 10% to INR 510 million as margin dropped to 27%.
540025|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR 1,898 million grew 2% YoY but fell 7% QoQ, held back by an extra INR 100 million sales reversal for export shipments still in transit. EBITDA declined 10% YoY and 19% QoQ to INR 510 million, with margin at 27% versus 30% a year ago, attributed to lower realisation, higher power and fuel costs, and a sales-mix shift. PAT was INR 386 million, down 5% YoY. Management guided to a return to about 30-32% EBITDA margin, double-digit growth for the rest of the year, and announced a INR 697 million buyback and full acquisition of JC Biotech.

B2C USD 1.14 million vs USD 1.12 million a year ago.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 45 million vs INR 44 million in Q4 FY26; management expects stronger growth in H2 FY27.

544558|2026-06.headline: Fabtech Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 74.98 crore and PAT turned to Rs 4.21 crore from a Rs 6.13 crore loss.
544558|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 10.3% YoY to Rs 74.98 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 7.41 crore (9% margin) versus negative Rs 5.27 crore a year ago. Contribution margin expanded about 910 bps to 46.7%, which management attributes to geography mix (Saudi Arabia, Africa) and project mix, with reduced dependence on UAE. UAE FTS faced war-related headwinds, and several large orders slipped (not cancelled) into later quarters. Management reiterated 20-25% organic growth for FY27, with Q2 steady and Q3-Q4 stronger, and guided PAT margin of 9-11%.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 17.14 crore, up 130% YoY. Company incorporated Specialized Contracting Activities LLC with 51% stake to pursue MEP and civil projects; one civil order already secured.

segments.name: Africa (Morocco and Kenya)
segments.commentary: Morocco and Kenya together contributed Rs 27.94 crore, both markets were not material a year ago. Botswana veterinary vaccine facility order of Rs 31.23 crore won in the quarter.

segments.name: UAE FTS
segments.commentary: Faced genuine regional headwinds from the Middle East war; no figure disclosed. Management expects UAE projects to normalise but gave no timeline.

segments.name: Standalone FTL core business
segments.commentary: Management cited a strong standalone turnaround in the core FTL business, without a disclosed figure.

segments.name: India (Fabtech Technologies Cleanrooms)
segments.commentary: Management said Fabtech Technologies Limited is international-focused; India cleanroom business sits in a separate entity. Only one India-specific contract is in the book.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 organic revenue growth guided at 20-25% YoY, with Q2 steady and Q3-Q4 significantly stronger.
PAT margin guidance of 9-11% with around 25% PAT growth; Aman Anavkar framed a 9.5-10% target for the year.
Proposed acquisitions in Italy (Europe) and Saudi Arabia expected to complete before FY27 year-end, subject to approvals; European deal visible in next two to three quarters.
Internal top-line ambition of Rs 1,000 crore-plus by 2030 on an organic basis; Vision 2030/2035 document in preparation.
Contracts being reworked to move toward percentage-of-completion revenue recognition; changes expected over the next few years.
capex_capacity: Up to Rs 24 crore approved as investment into Fabtech Technologies LLC (Saudi), plus additional investment into FT Institutions Private Limited.
In-house manufacturing of process air, water, utilities and process machines supports vaccine and pharma tenders.
Around Rs 400 crore of pre-engineered building (PEB) projects bid in Africa and the Middle East.
Around Rs 20-22 crore of goods lying at port at quarter end due to shipment availability constraints.
Project durations: 12-24 months after civil readiness; 12-36 months for greenfield projects.
demand_pricing: Active inquiries exceed Rs 9,300 crore; hot leads over Rs 3,800 crore. Management cited these as two-year visibility.
Several large ticket orders slipped due to geopolitical conditions and donor/government funding cycles; management said there were no cancellations but investors slowed decisions.
Repeat customers about 10% of the quarter's order intake (about Rs 8 crore); management said the company has deliberately diversified away from repeat clients.
Revenue is 78% from MENA, GCC, ECO and the Persian Gulf region per management.
Price escalation clause: pass-through of raw material cost increases above 5%; offers valid only 2-3 weeks. Management said pass-through is not always full.

qa_highlights.question: Trade receivables rose to about Rs 215 crore; what share is overdue and what are receivable-day expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no open credit, with receivables backed by LCs or CAD. Aging is mostly retention (10-15%, held 1-2 years), and about Rs 120 crore of Saudi receivables sit with a large customer until shipment completes, with Q3 delivery expected. Customer advances total about Rs 110 crore, and working cycle is about 120 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is the UAE weakness cyclical, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UAE demand is focused on high-tech facilities, cell and gene therapy labs and compounding pharmacies, with some projects delayed by geopolitics. It gave no timeline for normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Does the West Asia war affect execution and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said on-site teams kept executing, but conversions slowed as customers delayed decisions. Management said working capital has not been impacted much, and the company is using outsourced labour selectively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company move to percentage-of-completion accounting to smooth quarterly results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is reworking contracts with auditors to define billable milestones tied to percentage completion. Existing contracts stay on shipment/milestone basis, and changes are expected over the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: What progress on the IPO-proceeds acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: The Saudi acquisition (SACE, 51%) is complete. The European acquisition is in due diligence and management expects it in the next two to three quarters, with no value disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the margin expansion come from: gross margin or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both: evaluating procurement from China to lift gross margin, and fixed-cost control with operating leverage visible in Q1.

risks_watch: Revenue is H2-weighted and recognised on shipment/BL basis, so Q1 results are not a run-rate guide; Q3-Q4 must deliver to hit 20-25% growth.
Order slippage from geopolitics: Rs 900 crore+ backlog depends on conversion of delayed large orders.
Around Rs 20-22 crore of goods held at port, and Rs 120 crore Saudi receivable pending delivery in Q3.
Concentration in MENA (78% of revenue) and UAE headwinds.
Shareholder sentiment: stock below IPO price was raised repeatedly; management had no time-bound plan beyond more investor meetings and media strategy.

544515|2026-06.headline: Urban Company Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; Services NTV grew 29% and InstaHelp loss narrowed to ₹(132) crore.
544515|2026-06.overview: Consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore and revenue rose 44% to ₹528 crore, with orders up 79% YoY to 13.2 million. Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

improved from (11.4)% a year ago (410 bps)

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: NTV ₹1,056 crore, growing 29% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration (10%→19%→21%→26%→29%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 6.9% of NTV, up 5.2 pp YoY per the call; management says the 29% base was muted by unseasonal rains and monsoon in the prior year.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

segments.name: InstaHelp
segments.commentary: NTV ₹119 crore (+51% YoY), net revenue ₹95 crore (+60% YoY); adjusted EBITDA loss ₹(132) crore, or (7.3)% of NTV versus (11.4)% a year ago. Largest investment; management expects it to need 2 or more years of investment and aims for adjusted breakeven within about 18 months.

guidance_outlook: Retains guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28.
Retains guidance of ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31.
Long-term Services adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% of NTV; currently at 6.9%. Management said it is not in a rush and sees the target as achievable without trading off growth.
Management said Services will be a cash-generating business going forward and that it intends to keep it profitable; InstaHelp is expected to need 2 years or more of investment.

2030 vision: revenue above INR 100,000 crore and EBITDA above INR 4,000 crore. Steady-state capex assumed at about INR 700 crore per year for modelling.

543398|2026-06.headline: Latent View Q1 FY27 revenue fell 3.5% QoQ to USD 30.3M (INR 287 Cr, +21.6% YoY); FY27 growth guidance held at 12%.
543398|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR 287 crore, up about 21.6% YoY but down 0.6% QoQ in rupee terms; dollar revenue fell about 3.5% QoQ to USD 30.3M, worse than the 1.5-2% decline guided. The drop was driven by CPG (Decision Point one-off projects not extended), a tech account insourcing (about INR 0.5 crore impact this quarter), and a one-time volume discount to a BFSI client (about USD 0.4M). Adjusted EBITDA was INR 58.6 crore (20.4% margin) after wage hikes for about 70% of staff (about 2.7 margin points). Management retained 12% FY27 growth guidance and 20-21% margin guidance, and expects a QoQ bounce-back from Q2. A new CEO, Sonal Ramrakhiani, joined only days before the call.

financial_highlights.change: Average hike about 8%, for ~70% of workforce
vs about USD 7.5M last quarter; FY26 about USD 5M net new, USD 17.5-18M consumption-linked

segments.name: Financial services (BFSI)
segments.commentary: Described as very strong execution this quarter, offsetting CPG softness; a large client grew to a run rate of about USD 10M annually, with a one-time volume discount granted.

segments.name: TMT / Technology
segments.commentary: Grew about 4% QoQ, but one large account was affected by consolidation and insourcing that cost about USD 7-8M of annual business; management expects part of the gap to be plugged in-year.

segments.name: Consumer goods (CPG, Decision Point)
segments.commentary: Key drag this quarter after Q4 one-off projects were not extended; management expects QoQ growth of 25%+ in Q2 and has about USD 2M of extensions and about USD 26M of pipeline. Added one new logo.

segments.name: Rest of World (Europe, LatAm)
segments.commentary: Revenue declined QoQ, linked to CPG one-off projects from these regions.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12% retained; management said confidence is reasonable and upside exists if pipeline converts.
Management expects a strong QoQ bounce-back in Q2 FY27, with CPG QoQ growth of 25%+ cited.
Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 20-21% for Q1 and FY27 held; 21-22% FY27 target not raised, with new Chief Technology and AI Officer and partnership functions offsetting FX benefit.
Further wage-hike impact of about 40-50 bps expected in Q2 FY27.
Long-term target of USD 200M revenue in FY28/FY29 reiterated as a stretch; organic growth needs to accelerate and inorganic deals are being pursued.
Transaction-related expenses end with Q1 FY27; no further such costs expected.
capex_capacity: M&A momentum described as strong, focused on data engineering and life sciences; one or two opportunities in advanced stage, including a letter of intent for a healthcare, life sciences and data engineering target.
New Chief Technology and AI Officer organization to combine AI products, agents, agent foundry, partnerships and service delivery excellence; not yet in the P&L.
Anthropic certification program underway with more than 200 staff enrolled; recognised partner of Anthropic and OpenAI.
Revenue mix: project-led 15-18%, managed services 65-70%, T&M the remainder.
Healtheon (RCM company, investee) is building agents for revenue cycle management.
demand_pricing: AI-led opportunities: about 15+ opportunities generated from AI prototypes; 14+ pursued, each worth about USD 0.5M in-year if won.
AI mix in Q1: about 80% of work has an AI element; about 35% is primary AI (AI solutions delivered directly to clients), versus 28% primary in FY26 and about half of work AI-impacted in FY26.
Productivity gains on completed projects range 30-80%, per management; clients are not yet passing these to tokens cost, as client typically supplies the AI tech stack.
Primary AI work currently less margin-accretive due to forward-deployed engineers and higher on-site mix; expected to become accretive over time with pricing and the agent foundry.
Wallet share: 2-5% at large enterprises with 20-30 partners; 100% at some clients where Latent View is the only partner. Little competition seen on new work or extensions at spending-centre level.
Six new accounts added in Q1 across financial services and auto components; new work for an AI data-centre infrastructure client.

qa_highlights.question: Does 12% FY27 guidance imply a steep QoQ ramp, and does it rely on closing pipeline deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 confirmed numbers give confidence; 12% needs pipeline extensions and new opportunities to come through, and it sees no downside beyond adverse events.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up the 21% of revenue not in direct cost or SG&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Remaining cost is payroll for sales and marketing and corporate management, in addition to SG&A (pure overhead) and direct cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will transaction-related expenses continue?
qa_highlights.answer: No; Q1 FY27 is the last quarter with transaction-related costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin reach 21-22% medium-term target soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to hold 20-21% for FY27, with investments in AI officer and partnership/CDO functions; no upgrade to margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How much FX appreciation flows to margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investments will offset FX benefit; 21-22% guidance still in play but not raised.

qa_highlights.question: How much Databricks revenue was in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Net new Databricks revenue about USD 7.8M this quarter (vs about USD 7.5M last quarter), expected to rise to about USD 8.5M next quarter.

risks_watch: CPG recovery: management needs one-off projects replaced by extensions and new work; Q2 QoQ growth of 25%+ is promised but unproven.
Tech account insourcing and cost-reduction mandate at a large client: about USD 7-8M lost business; plug-gap timing uncertain.
Shift from managed services to fixed-fee, outcome-based models could add lumpiness and slower visibility.
AI productivity may reduce billable effort; token costs and client pushback on AI-led solutions flagged as emerging concerns.
Margin pressure: further 40-50 bps wage impact in Q2, new AI and partnership investments not yet in P&L.
Macro, geopolitical risks (including war) and dollar-rupee moves cited; new CEO setting out long-range plan with details expected in coming weeks.

500215|2026-06.headline: Sundrop Brands Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY (11% QoQ) with EBITDA steady at about 7% of sales, net of ESOP.
500215|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY and 11% QoQ, with B2B up 18% and e-commerce up 32%. Gross margin improved about 110 bps despite commodity and packaging inflation, and EBITDA held at about 7%, the same level as Q4 FY26. A&P was reported about 12% lower YoY, but management says about 5% lower on a like-for-like basis after reclassifying trade spends as contra-revenue. Management reiterated a target of 300 bps annual margin expansion and about 12% EBITDA by FY30, with 200 bps from Del Monte-Sundrop synergies over 18 months.

financial_highlights.value: Up about 110 bps (stated as overall margin improvement)
financial_highlights.change: Material cost efficiency +40 bps; other expenses +70 bps
Same as Q4 FY26; ESOP-burdened about 5.66%

financial_highlights.value: About 12% lower YoY as reported; about 5% lower like-for-like (21.4 vs 22.9 as % of sales)
financial_highlights.change: Reclassification of trade spends to contra-revenue; like-for-like growth about 12% QoQ

financial_highlights.value: About 56% of total business, growing about 16%
About 44-45% of total business, growing about 14%

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26 share of business about 62%

segments.name: Popcorn
segments.commentary: Growing about 18% with about 12% volume growth; Ready-to-Eat growing about 39% (vs 33% last year) while Ready-to-Cook grows about 9%. Management says it holds about 85% category share.

segments.name: Culinary (ketchup, mayo, dressings)
segments.commentary: Growth accelerated to 15% from about 10% last year, with volume growth of about 8%; B2B and exports to Southeast Asia contributing.

segments.name: Premium staples / edible oil
segments.commentary: Value growth about 16% and volume growth about 7%, with about 9% of growth from price pass-through; oil is about 20% of total business. Management targets 4-5% volume growth.

segments.name: Italian (olive oil, pasta, RTE olives)
segments.commentary: Value growth returned to about 8% and volume to 15-17%; olive oil volume grew close to 20%, pasta about 10%. Q1 realisations fell due to prior-year commodity deflation pass-through.

segments.name: Peanut butter / spreads
segments.commentary: Decline narrowed to about 3% in value and volume from 8-10% last year; e-commerce returned to 16% growth. Market is about 85% value-added; company holds about 33% of standard and 3% of value-added peanut butter.

segments.name: Juices
segments.commentary: Investment dropped; management says it was not core and did not show good results.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for mid-teens to high-teens revenue growth, with about 10% volume growth, 4-5% value growth from pricing and 4-5% from innovation as the long-term mix.
EBITDA target of about 12% by FY30 (about three years), from about 7% ESOP-adjusted today; ESOP cost to stay front-loaded for 18-21 months.

Overall ambition of about 300 bps annual margin expansion, split half reinvested in growth and half returned to shareholders; about 100 bps a year from scale, 80-100 bps from premiumisation and about 100 bps a year from synergies over two years.
Del Monte and Sundrop synergies estimated at about 200 bps, delivered over about 18 months; about 8 CFA consolidations targeted by end of this year, leaving 2 of Del Monte's 10 unique CFAs.
Italian business: value growth expected to move closer to 15% if volume growth of 15% is sustained; price stabilisation expected from Q2.
Single ERP for both businesses to be decided soon, with migration expected within about 12 months, before sales-force integration.
capex_capacity: Shift to a capital-efficient model: using third-party manufacturing and outsourced systems in place of own capex; management also says it is actively looking at inorganic opportunities.
Popcorn facilities at Kashipur and Kothur are running at rising utilisation, adding to profitability on instant popcorn.
Ready-to-Eat assorted manufacturing is improving plant utilisation and freight efficiency; direct factory-to-distributor shipping cuts freight and shelf-life packaging cost (4.5-5 month shelf life).
Salesforce automation: about 80% of outlets now billed on the platform, up from about 75% at the end of Q4 FY26.
demand_pricing: Edible oil: volume 7%, value about 15-16%, with about 9% from pass-through of per-kg price increases; management is now growing volume and aims for 4-5% volume growth.
Peanut butter: management says the market has moved to about 85% value-added formats (protein, chocolate, natural) where it has about 3% share; competition includes PE-backed brands.
Popcorn Rs. 10 RTC/RTE packs are expanding into East, West and South; e-commerce growth is led by Rs. 25-50 MRP packs, with bigger packs now about 36% of RTE mix (from about 33%).
Premium staples: management says it has a lower-priced variant (Sundrop Lite and Sundrop Heart Plus) as a safety net if sunflower oil inflation drives consumers down.
Italian realisation down about 6-10% in Q1 due to higher old-price inventory being sold after last year's commodity deflation; not quick-commerce discounting per management.

500165|2026-06.headline: Kansai Nerolac Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew 10.2% with PBDIT up 7.7%; management targets 13-14% margins for FY27 despite input cost pressure.
500165|2026-06.overview: Standalone net revenue grew 10.2% YoY, PBDIT 7.7% and PBT 5.1%; consolidated revenue rose 9.8%, PBDIT 8.3% and PBT 5.8%. Decorative value growth was high single digit with volume growth low single digit, as the company deliberately shed low-margin volume. Industrial coatings grew double digit in value, but price increases lagged, with about 5% realised so far at customer level. Management announced a INR601 crore capacity expansion across automotive, powder coating and resin, spread over about 2 to 2.5 years, and kept its margin ambition intact.

financial_highlights.metric: Industrial price hike achieved so far
financial_highlights.change: Still under negotiation; effective ask from 1 April

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth high single digit; volume growth low single digit as premium mix was prioritised over low-margin, high-volume products. Economy grew mid-single digit and super premium grew double digit. Margins were stable YoY despite higher ad spend.

segments.name: Industrial (Automotive, Performance Coatings, Powder)
segments.commentary: Value growth double digit. Automotive and powder coating saw strong growth; liquid performance coatings led by construction equipment, drums and coil coating. Gross contribution fell about 1.3% as price increases lagged cost inflation.

segments.name: Auto Refinish
segments.commentary: Growth was flat. Management cited notable premium PU body shop wins and a transition from solvent-borne to waterborne systems that is on plan.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and premium wood finish
segments.commentary: Construction chemicals grew double digit; premium wood finish grew high single digit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 margin ambition of 13-14% is retained, subject to the geopolitical situation not worsening.
Q2 decorative price increase of about 3% expected to flow through; industrial price increase of another 3-5% expected in Q2.

Q2 will carry high-cost inventory and a seasonally weaker quarter, but management expects to maintain margins versus last year's same quarter, helped by sourcing, value engineering and formula optimisation.
Medium term, aim to reach the higher end of the 14%+ margin range within 2-3 years through premiumisation, industrial growth and fixed-cost leverage.
Expected ROCE on incremental capex is towards 18%, with per-KL capex on new capacity lower than the current programme.
Management expects a slightly better festive season, with Diwali in November giving October more painting days in Q3.
capex_capacity: INR601 crore capex for automotive, powder coating and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur.
Capacity addition of 66,000 KL per year plus resin capacity of close to 10,000 metric tons per year.
The INR601 crore outlay is spread over about 2 to 2.5 years; normal annual capex is INR150-200 crore.
Part of the spend is front-loaded infrastructure, so future incremental capacity will be cheaper per KL.
Industrial capacity is expected to be full in about 2 years, requiring the addition.
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity in decorative remains high, with new entrants still testing the market; no change in pricing discipline, dealer incentives or scheme intensity versus last year or Q4 exit.
Network expansion: 1,700 dealers added in Q1; network additions targeted at 5-10% a year.
Industrial price hike to date about 5%, with more discussions expected to add in Q2.
Solvent inflation was sharp, but solvent inventory is only about 15 days, which made it hard to hedge.
Some free-product schemes continue in certain markets, not specific to the company's focus towns.
Input cost inflation peaked in June and has since eased slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Is decorative volume growth in line with the market, and is competition easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is not below competitors, but the company is deliberately avoiding low-margin, high-volume products. Competitive intensity remains high and is expected to persist through this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins flat YoY when the market leader expanded margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial price increases lag by 1-2 quarters, so the price-cost gap hit industrial gross contribution by about 1.3%. Ad spend rose in Q1 but was offset by mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value growth split in decorative and industrial?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative value growth is high single digit and industrial is double digit. Q1 mix is heavier on decorative, and the mix changes each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the capex and what returns are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: INR601 crore over about 2-2.5 years on top of normal capex of INR150-200 crore per year. Management expects ROCE towards 18%, with lower per-KL capex on new capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pricing growth in Q1 and Q2 on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated pricing was about 4-5% in Q1. Q2 adds about 3% in decorative and another 3-5% in industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any backward integration plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new resin capacity is backward integration for automotive paint, but raw material integration is not on the card. The Kansai Group's global network can supply intermediates as needed.

risks_watch: Geopolitical escalation (West Asia crisis) could raise crude-linked raw material costs and disrupt supply chains.
Rupee depreciation may lift import costs; industrial price negotiations may still be incomplete in Q2.
Decorative volume growth is low single digit, and the company is ceding share in low-margin segments.
Ad and dealer investment is rising, and margin benefit depends on whether premium mix gains come through.
Whether the INR601 crore capacity delivers the targeted ~18% ROCE.
Auto Refinish growth was flat, and the solvent-to-waterborne transition is still in progress.
500165|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term plan and on margin resilience, but cautious on near-term industrial pricing and the geopolitical outlook. Management was candid that decorative volume is lagging by design and that competition is not easing.
key_quotes: And that is why I guess for this year, at least that intensity will remain and people will test water in terms of this new set equilibrium.
With that, I'm very confident that this year also, our endeavour is to maintain 13% to 14%.
And on the midterm, I think our endeavour is obviously go to higher end of 14% plus kind of a thing.

514043|2026-06.headline: Himatsingka Q1 FY27 consolidated total income fell to INR634 crores from INR661 crores, with EBITDA of INR101 crores (~16% margin).
514043|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income was INR634 crores against INR661 crores, described as range-bound, with shipment deferrals linked to Middle East geopolitical issues and lower capacity utilisation in some divisions. EBITDA came in at INR101 crores, a margin of about 16%, attributed to lower revenue, product mix tweaks and raw material inflation. Management said the call was mainly about the strategic transition to a multi-vertical model using existing assets: Yarn Solutions and Fabric Solutions have started and are ramping up, Apparel Solutions is due a couple of quarters out, and Home Textiles (especially Sheeting) will be rightsized. Net leverage was described as range-bound at about INR2,550 crores.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR661 crores (prior period as stated; decline)
pressured by lower revenue, product mix and raw material inflation
purpose: debt tenor and maturity balancing

segments.name: Home Textile Solutions - Sheeting
segments.commentary: Utilisation at 52% in Q1; revenue expected to taper as capacity is rightsized and reallocated to new verticals.

segments.name: Home Textile Solutions - Terry
segments.commentary: Utilisation at 63%, unchanged from last quarter; management expects Terry to continue growing.

segments.name: Yarn Solutions
segments.commentary: Spinning assets (211,584 spindles, described as world's largest single-roof plant) being converted from captive to independent business; over 90% of capacity to be sold externally. Full-capacity revenue potential about INR1,000 crores.

segments.name: Fabric Solutions
segments.commentary: Uses shared sheeting and knit processing capacity of about 90 million meters by year-end (vs 61 million meters earlier for home textiles, excluding knit). Full-capacity revenue potential about INR1,000 crores; revenue generation has started.

segments.name: Apparel Solutions
segments.commentary: Planned for Phase 2, expected to launch a couple of quarters later; no revenue contribution discussed yet.

guidance_outlook: Transition period of a couple of quarters with expected volatility in numbers before new platforms stabilise.
Management aims to keep revenues range-bound with new verticals offsetting Sheeting decline, but expects Home Textile Solutions revenue to correct somewhat.
Net debt expected to reduce by end of fiscal year; leverage to stay range-bound.
Overall company expected to be transformed in about a year; India may become the largest or top-2 jurisdiction in the medium term.
Capex limited to maintenance and organic requirements; no expansion capex planned.
capex_capacity: Overall utilisation at facilities at 99% (as stated), with Sheeting at 52% and Terry at 63%.
Combined sheeting and knit fabric processing capacity to reach about 90 million meters by year-end, shared between Home Textile and Fabric Solutions.
Yarn spinning capacity of 211,584 spindles; majority to be sold externally.
Capex restricted to maintenance and organic needs; transition uses existing campus and infrastructure.
Apparel Solutions to start in Phase 2 using existing assets, a couple of quarters out.
demand_pricing: US demand affected by policy flip-flops and tariffs, creating inflationary pressure on products; management says tariff situation has stabilised at current levels.
Management expects pricing challenges in home textiles, especially Sheeting, and sees better pricing power in new verticals.
Shipment deferrals in the quarter linked to Middle East geopolitical issues.
UK FTA expected to help in medium term; EU FTA timing uncertain but expected in short term; still under process.
Management cited US market share loss, tariff-driven pricing pressure and client concentration as reasons for the pivot.

qa_highlights.question: What are the positives and negatives this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Negatives were revenue and offtake overhangs; positive is the start of the transition to the new multi-vertical model, which needs no expansion or capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise so much debt and how do tariffs affect the US business?
qa_highlights.answer: The recent NCD raise balances debt tenors and maturities and is not incremental capital. US tariff policy flip-flops created inflation and altered demand; tariff outlook has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: How will fabric capacity of 90 million meters be used versus the 61 million meters home capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The 61 million meters excluded knit platforms; combined 90 million meters will be allocated between Home Textile Sheeting and Fabric Solutions from common infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: How much yarn capacity will be sold externally and is more capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 90% of yarn capacity to be sold externally; capex kept to maintenance and organic needs only.

qa_highlights.question: Will lost Home Textile revenue be replaced in the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for range-bound revenue, but Sheeting will be rightsized; Yarn and Fabric each target about INR1,000 crores at full capacity (about INR2,000 crores combined), with no quarterly split disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Sheeting ramp-down about profitability or US challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: US market share loss, tariff-driven pricing pressure and client concentration led to repositioning the business as Himatsingka 2.0.

risks_watch: Revenue visibility during transition: management warned of volatility over the next couple of quarters.
Sheeting rightsizing and pricing pressure in home textiles, especially US, with utilisation at 52%.
Ramp-up execution of Yarn and Fabric Solutions, with no quarterly revenue split disclosed.
Raw material inflation and margin pressure (EBITDA margin ~16%).
Timing of UK and EU FTAs and Apparel Solutions launch; equity initiatives to be shared later without details.
514043|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the long-term strategic direction but cautious near term, repeatedly flagging volatility and transition for a couple of quarters. Evasive on quarterly vertical revenue split and on the timing and size of equity initiatives.
key_quotes: So our efforts are essentially geared to transforming the Himatsingka model and steering away from U.S. concentration, steering away from client concentration, as we've seen in the Home Textile space, that seems to be a cornerstone of the home textile, let's say, world.
We're keeping our capex limited to just maintenance and organic capex requirements, which is why I keep saying that all of these things are using our existing campus and infrastructure.
So therefore, all in all, we will see a reduction in net debt by the end of fiscal.

542812|2026-06.headline: GFL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 1,588 crore and PAT more than doubled QoQ to INR 219 crore on R32-led fluorochemicals growth.
542812|2026-06.overview: Chemical segment revenue grew 23% YoY to INR 1,574 crore with EBITDA up 29% to INR 458 crore and segment PAT up 33% to INR 261 crore. Fluorochemicals was the standout, with revenue up 52% YoY and 44% QoQ on R32 sales, and existing R32 capacity is already at peak utilisation. Battery materials remain pre-revenue to small (INR 20-30 crore per quarter cited by an analyst), with a ramp promised from Q4 FY27 and a significant step-up in FY28. The Oman battery project has been put on hold and its capex is being moved to India, and the approved sovereign funding for Oman will not transfer.

financial_highlights.change: +24% YoY; +39% QoQ; margin 27% vs 22% in Q4 FY26
+19% YoY; PAT margin 14% vs 7% in Q4 FY26
+29% YoY; +30% QoQ; margin 29% vs 26% in Q4 FY26
-43 days vs 192 days in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Fluoropolymers
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 15% YoY and 8% QoQ, driven by mix shift to higher-value grades and new-age applications (semiconductors, data centres, green hydrogen, batteries). Management guides 15-20% (later 17-20%) annual growth.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (R32 and refrigerants)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 52% YoY and 44% QoQ, mainly R32. Existing R32 capacity is fully utilised; a R32 expansion (about 20,000 t total capacity cited by an analyst) is due in Q2 FY27. R134A is on track for commissioning in FY27.

segments.name: Bulk chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY and 1% QoQ, primarily on better realisations; described as steady.

segments.name: Battery materials
segments.commentary: LiPF6 has nearly completed qualification and is in its growth phase; PVDF qualification is close; LFP and cathode active material revenue expected toward end-FY27. Current revenue is small, with dispatches on CIF terms recognised in the next quarter.

guidance_outlook: R32 capacity expansion to be commissioned in Q2 FY27; management expects full utilisation of the incremental R32 capacity in calendar 2027.
R134A capacity to be commissioned in FY27 (management said it is targeting earlier than year-end); capacity size not yet disclosed.
Battery materials: management says it is on track for a 3-digit INR crore quarterly revenue in Q4 FY27, with significant ramp-up in FY28 and full potential from FY28 onwards.
Gross block of INR 836 crore expected to rise to about INR 1,200 crore by end-FY27 as CWIP is capitalised.
FY27 capex plan held at about INR 2,300 crore in EV/battery and about INR 800 crore in chemicals; total announced plan of INR 6,000 crore over the next two years.
AHF (anhydrous hydrofluoric acid) capacity to come in phases, first set by end-FY27 or Q3, mainly for captive use.
capex_capacity: R32 capacity expansion due Q2 FY27; existing R32 capacity at peak utilisation.
R134A brownfield project at an existing refrigerant site, to be commissioned in FY27; TCE feedstock to be imported, not backward integrated.

Oman battery materials project (about USD 216 million capex) put on hold; capex being redirected to India. Sovereign funding of about INR 1,200 crore approved for Oman will not be available for India.
Land for battery expansion available at the existing Dahej B (Jolva) site; a second Dahej site is being added for FY27-end/FY28.
Fluoropolymer debottlenecking is done continuously, roughly every second quarter; new-age fluoropolymer capex sized in the previous quarter at about INR 250 crore.
demand_pricing: Fluoropolymer price increases were marginal and pass-through of input cost increases (methanol, sulfur, oil-linked inputs since March 2026); management said formula-based contracts protect margins.
R32 is sold globally: about 40-50% under long-term contracts, remainder spot or contract-to-contract. Domestic and export pricing described as 'very close'.
Management said 3M's exit is past and it has taken the impact; AGC's announced UK facility shutdown has begun generating customer enquiries, with traction expected in a quarter or two.
Domestic BESS demand projected at 220-250 GWh by 2030 (versus earlier global ~1,800 GWh view).

qa_highlights.question: Have Chinese peers' fluoropolymer price increases been passed on by GFL, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Malhotra said only a marginal increase was taken to recover input costs; growth is mainly from higher-value grades where competition with Chinese players is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth visible for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said it is absolutely visible; new fluoropolymer capacity is nearly fully utilised and further capacity will be added for semiconductor and battery applications, without disclosing specifics.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Oman funding shortfall require a fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said fundraising is ongoing and project-by-project; he does not see funding as a constraint for India capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How is fluoropolymer growth split between volume, price and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split it precisely, saying growth is primarily mix (higher grades) plus volume from new fluoropolymers, not price.

qa_highlights.question: Will R32 capacity be fully utilised in calendar 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said full utilisation is expected as capacity is commissioned, based on contracts and market understanding.

risks_watch: Oman project shift to India: loss of about INR 1,200 crore sovereign funding for that project and need for new funding of about INR 4,000 crore for battery chemicals.

R32 and R134A quota allocation under the formula (baseline and production over 2024-26) is not yet clear; management declined to say which new players will receive quota. An analyst also raised a question on consumption quota that management could not answer and will follow up on.
Battery materials revenue remains small; ramp is contingent on customer qualification (about 1.5 years stabilisation cited) and CIF-term revenue timing.

532884|2026-06.headline: Refex Q1 FY27 standalone continuing revenue rose 76% YoY to INR619 crore, with EBITDA of INR105 crore (17% margin) and PAT of INR73.6 crore (+123%).
532884|2026-06.overview: Standalone continuing-operations revenue grew 76% YoY to INR619 crore and EBITDA rose to INR105 crore at a 17% margin, while PAT reached INR73.6 crore (11.9% margin). Ash and coal handling remained the largest contributor despite acute diesel shortages and logistics disruptions linked to geopolitical developments. Wind turbine execution started contributing INR295 crore in the quarter at near-zero margin, and the mobility demerger is progressing toward a shareholder meeting next month.

financial_highlights.metric: One-time bank processing charges (loan takeover by Indian Overseas Bank)

segments.name: Ash and coal handling
segments.commentary: Largest contributor to revenue and profit; volume run rate of 65,000-70,000 tonnes per day in Q1, with management targeting close to 90,000 by Q4 FY27 (some remarks cited 75,000-80,000 by Q4). Q2 expected to be slower, Q3-Q4 to scale up. Management guides EBITDA margin of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%.

segments.name: Wind energy
segments.commentary: Q1 execution INR295 crore at near-zero margin; order book INR1,860 crore of which INR525 crore executed and INR1,300 crore remaining. FY27 execution guided at INR1,700-1,800 crore with 5-6% net margin targeted by year-end. Operates as a product supplier (turbine, tower, blades) with a 76-77% stake in the JV.

segments.name: Mobility (Refex Mobility)
segments.commentary: Asset-light premium corporate mobility; being demerged into a separate listed company. NCLT has approved convening shareholder and creditor meetings, with equity shareholder meeting scheduled for next month. Expected to exit discontinued operations by end of Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Refrigerant gas
segments.commentary: Fully discontinued as of the last quarter; part of discontinued operations.

guidance_outlook: Ash and coal handling run rate to reach close to 90,000 tonnes per day in Q4 FY27; Q2 to be slower, Q3-Q4 to pick up; management says the core business will maintain a CAGR at least as good as last year's (~28%).
Wind FY27 execution of INR1,700-1,800 crore; net margin 5-6% by end of FY27 and profitability by year-end; Q3-Q4 margins expected to improve as unbilled material gets billed.
Wind localisation: management expects about 85% of components localised within 12 months, with margins similar to the core business in about 2 years; blades to be made in-house.
Mobility demerger expected to be completed with discontinued operations gone by end of Q3 FY27.
Wind orders in advanced closure expected within 30-60 days; new orders would spill over into FY28.
capex_capacity: Silvassa wind assembly plant is leased; capex to date limited to about INR3.5-4 crore of repairs and maintenance; rated capacity about 1 GW, which management equates to roughly INR5,000-6,000 crore of revenue.
First 5.3 MW turbine erected by a customer at Koppal, Karnataka; management says it is operating as projected and a repeat order is possible.
Blades currently imported; localisation under way, with in-house blade manufacturing planned.
Ash handling capacity not a constraint per management; scaling depends on multiplying fleet and manpower. Working in 42 thermal power plants, about 30-35% of Indian TPPs.
Railway Rail-cum-Road (RCR) initiative started, with freight discounts opening Northeast routes.
demand_pricing: Ash handling realisation varies from INR450 to INR1,200 per tonne-km, driven mainly by distance and volume.
Ash handling order book INR1,635 crore; management says digital tender wins in the past four months should improve the Q4 order book.
Wind order book INR1,860 crore; management says large orders are expected this year, at least as big as last year.
Management welcomes new entrants in ash handling, arguing they expand awareness and market; says Refex is the only organised player.
Wind market tailwinds cited from hybrid renewables (wind, solar, storage) and the 100 GW by 2030 government ambition. Exports ruled out; focus is domestic only.

qa_highlights.question: What was the ash and coal handling volume run rate and the Q4 target?
qa_highlights.answer: 65,000-70,000 tonnes per day in Q1; target close to 90,000 by Q4 FY27 (also cited as crossing 75,000-80,000).

qa_highlights.question: Why is wind margin near zero in Q1 and what is the full-year margin target?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-operating and business development expenses were expensed; part of material is in transit and unbilled. Management targets 5-6% net margin (PAT) for the year, with better margins in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin guidance for ash handling, given conflicting statements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it always guides EBITDA margin of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%; Q1 EBITDA margin was 17%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wind order book and outlook for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: INR1,860 crore in hand, of which INR525 crore executed; INR1,300 crore to be executed in FY27. New orders would spill into FY28; growth expected to be very good, with no quantified figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pledge reduction trajectory for promoter shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pledge was reduced last month, another disclosure due within 15 days, with further releases expected within two weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wind JV structure and technology arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Refex holds about 76-77%, the JV partner 23%; technology was transferred directly for payment, and the partner runs operations. Management did not disclose the partner's equity infusion on the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is the mobility demerger affecting P&L and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Discontinued operations to end by Q3 FY27; the mobility entity will be listed separately via mirror shareholding. Capital allocation will be based on need, with wind capital requirements likely at entity level through working capital or term loans.

risks_watch: Diesel supply shortages and logistics disruptions from geopolitical developments affected operations; management said most of the impact was covered.
Wind segment margin only just breaks even in Q1; delivery of the 5-6% net margin target depends on Q3-Q4 billing of in-transit material.
Q2 FY27 volume seasonality in ash handling; ramp to 90,000 tonnes per day depends on fleet and manpower additions.
Mobility demerger approval steps (equity shareholder meeting next month, NCLT, creditors) and the timing of discontinued operation losses ending by Q3 FY27.
Blade localisation timeline (6-12 months) and the sustainability of margins at the wind plant; no replacement-blade orders yet.
Promoter pledge reduction ongoing; management plans further disclosures in about 15 days.
Management gave inconsistent statements on wind margin basis (net vs PAT) and on Q4 run rate targets, which should be clarified in the next filing.

543300|2026-06.headline: Sona Comstar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 54% YoY to ₹12,310 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 23.1% on input-cost inflation and pass-through lag.
543300|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 54% YoY to ₹12,310 crore, with BEV revenue up 107% to ₹436 crore and BEV share of automotive sales at 44%, both described as the best ever. EBITDA rose 49% to ₹303 crore but margin contracted about 0.7 pp to 23.1%, with April and May weak and June better on pass-through recoveries. PAT grew 45% to ₹181 crore (13.6% margin). Management framed the quarter alongside the Denso JV announcement (two JVs: high-voltage/hybrid for 4W and 2/3W electrification) and a new Robotics and Physical AI vertical with ₹800 crore order book.

financial_highlights.metric: BEV share of automotive product sales

segments.name: Electrification (BEV)
segments.commentary: BEV revenue ₹436 crore, +107% YoY, highest ever BEV mix; EV order book at 69 programmes across 36 customers after 2 new EV and 1 hybrid programme.

segments.name: Traction motors / suspension motors
segments.commentary: Traction motors had the fastest growth in the quarter along with EV suspension motors (management ranked suspension motors fastest in growth); traction motors carry lowest margin and diluted group margin.

segments.name: Driveline / ICE differential gears
segments.commentary: Won ₹2.1 billion ICE differential gear programme from a North American OEM; new hybrid differential assembly order from an existing North American customer.

segments.name: Robotics and Physical AI
segments.commentary: Three new orders adding ₹6 billion, taking the vertical's order book to ₹8 billion; first product (AMR) prototype shown at CES; one SOP in Q1 FY28 per management timing guidance.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Railway acquisition in first year of post-acquisition integration; additional railway business wins noted, no revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Margin recovery expected to become progressively more visible from Q2 FY27 as cost pass-throughs catch up; June showed significant improvement over April-May.
Management said material-cost pass-through lag and revenue/cost arithmetic may keep pressure on margin percentage in the near term.
Expects phenomenal EV growth in India and Europe-led electrification to continue through the year, though US EV demand is weak.
Robotics orders: one SOP this quarter, one next quarter, one within 15 months; management said the market is developing faster than internal assumptions.
JV2 (high voltage) SOP timeline not disclosed due to confidentiality; JV1 expected to kick off faster than JV2.
capex_capacity: Management said it has no capacity constraint; OEM constraints are supply-chain driven, and capacity is built ahead of markets.
Denso JV2 (high voltage 4W/CV electrification) is Denso majority-owned with Denso leading management; JV1 (2/3W) is Sona majority-owned with Sona management control and licenses technology to the JV.
Management cited capex intensity thumb rule of ₹8-9 revenue per ₹1 capex for high-voltage systems, and at least ₹11-12 per ₹1 capex per Sat Mohan Gupta.
Suspension, motor and non-traction motor businesses are outside the Denso JV scope.
Robotics products under commercialisation include short-range radar sensors and advanced robotic components; AMR platform in development.
demand_pricing: Demand healthy across markets: India strong (passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers), Europe growing, US improved through the quarter, China mixed but fastest-growing geography for the company due to suspension motor ramp-up.
Management said EV volumes are constrained by OEM supply chains rather than demand.
Input cost inflation (commodities, labour) was the main margin headwind; April and May were tough, June improved.
Rare earth: heavy rare earth magnets remain restricted from import; company has shifted to light rare earth alternatives with no magnet shortage for traction motors.
Management described high-voltage motor competition as less intense than 2/3W due to technology barriers.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about AI/robotics economics, software share of value, and capital commitment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said metal plus software is now standard across products; suspension motors carry 2 million lines of code. Robotics entry has three revenue streams: components, perception engineering services, and full platforms (AMRs and cobots); no capex guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for JV2 revenue and capacity/TAM sizing for high-voltage JV?
qa_highlights.answer: SOP timelines withheld under confidentiality; JV1 to lead and JV2 to follow. Denso electrification revenue above $8 billion a year; Indian hybrid/EV car and CV addressable market ~2.3 million vehicles, about ₹24,000 crore by 2030 and roughly 3x that by 2035 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why put 2/3W traction motors into JV1 when already growing well?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Denso's interest, access to customers currently not open, export opportunities where Denso is dominant, and a single strategic intent across both JVs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-axle in JV1 but not JV2?
qa_highlights.answer: JV2 makes motors and inverters; e-axle (motor, inverter, gearbox integration) is a tiny market for JV1 and can be sold to e-axle makers, OEMs, or Sona driveline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is VA-to-employee ratio declining QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to product mix shift toward assembly businesses (motors, railways) vs driveline; ratio at 4.5x is still strong and varies quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.question: When do robotics orders start production?
qa_highlights.answer: One starts this quarter, one next quarter, and one within about 15 months; most within 12-15 months.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery: whether EBITDA margin improvement from pass-through shows in Q2 FY27 as management guided.
Traction motor mix: lowest-margin product growing fastest, a continuing dilution to group margin.
Execution risk on Denso JV1 and JV2: SOP timing not disclosed; capex and royalty economics not quantified.
Robotics: early-stage, ₹8 billion order book, product life cycles and generational change unclear to management as well.
Rare earth magnet restriction on heavy rare earths; company relies on light rare earth alternatives.
US EV demand weakness and OEM supply-chain bottlenecks limiting volumes.
543300|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, electrification and new partnerships; cautious on near-term margins, explicitly attributing pressure to input inflation and pass-through lag. Evasive on JV timelines, JV2 revenue sizing and Denso's own India supply, citing confidentiality.

544718|2026-06.headline: PNGS Reva Q1 FY27 revenue rose 119.5% YoY to INR118 crore, with PAT of INR27.21 crore (23.06% margin) and EBITDA margin of 28.76%.
544718|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR118 crore, up 119.5% YoY, driven mainly by diamond caratage volumes, which management said rose more than 50% in quarter. Gross profit was INR41.83 crore (35.46% margin), EBITDA INR33.92 crore (28.76%), and PAT INR27.21 crore (23.06%). Management attributed margin strength to scale and better caratage-based diamond realisations, while flagging that marketing spend, deliberately deferred to Q2-Q4, will dent PAT by 1-2% per quarter for the rest of the year. Network reached 37 stores (3 COCO, 34 SIS) after a Pune COCO opening on 7 July 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR112,000 in Q4 FY26 per management
up from about INR30 lakh, due to interest on parked IPO proceeds

financial_highlights.value: INR27 million, of which INR26.53 million is interest and INR0.95 million is lease liability interest

segments.name: Diamond jewellery (core)
segments.commentary: Growth driven by volume: diamond caratage up more than 50% YoY in the quarter, with ~97% of business in small diamonds (star melee / minus-two). Average order value about INR1 lakh.

segments.name: COCO stores
segments.commentary: 3 COCO stores in operation (Amanora Mall Pune opened 7 July 2026); management says none is over a year old, so no SSSG reported. Two of the planned 15 COCO stores are already operational.

segments.name: SIS (shop-in-shop with PNGS)
segments.commentary: 34 SIS stores; management reported about 50% SSSG across SIS stores and growth across all ~21 cities served. SIS is about 95% of revenue today.

guidance_outlook: FY28 margin view: full-year EBITDA margin expected at 25-27% and PAT margin at 22-23%, after a 2-3 percentage point dent from marketing in Q2-Q4.
Management clarified the 200-300 bps full-year margin impact is mainly marketing-led, not EBO fixed costs; EBO impact is considered immaterial as most open in H2.
Store plan: 9 COCO stores in year one and 7 in year two post IPO, all COCO (no franchise). Breakeven: Maharashtra EBOs in about one year; outside Maharashtra 15-18 months.
Inventory turns expected between 1.1x and 1.4x; management said a 0.75x breakeven and 1.25-1.5x for meaningful profit.
Q1 typically ~15% of annual revenue; H1 ~35% and H2 ~65%. Q2 expected better than Q1.
Guidance unchanged, per Aditya Modak; management says it is more confident in delivering prior commitments.
E-commerce website to launch by end of August 2026.
Short-term WCDL of ~INR166 crore at FY26 end, reduced to about INR120 crore; repayment to continue from profits, with EBO expansion to be funded mainly from internal accruals and IPO proceeds.
capex_capacity: Store network at 37 (3 COCO, 34 SIS) after Amanora Mall Pune COCO opened 7 July 2026.
Plan to open 15 COCO stores from IPO proceeds: 9 in the first year, 7 in the second; 2 already operational.
Store selection uses multi-level approvals, market assessment and feasibility studies; management emphasises payback over speed of rollout.
Gold loan limit available from bank but not yet used; plan to draw in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Demand strong across ~21 cities; management said growth was broad-based, not concentrated in Pune.
Akshaya Tritiya revenue INR12.7 crore, up 268% YoY; monsoon season also contributed in June.

Management views gold price correction as supportive for wedding and festive buying; said diamond jewellery is utility-based and less affected by the government's request to slow gold buying than plain gold.
Lab-grown competition: management says price gap for small diamonds is only 10-15% on a product basis and it is not feeling material pressure.
Marketing spend was modest in Q1 and is to be deployed in Q2-Q4; a brand ambassador is under negotiation with none signed yet.

qa_highlights.question: Are EBITDA and PAT margins sustainable, and what drove them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited scale (turnover roughly doubled) and better caratage-based diamond realisation. Full-year EBITDA expected at 25-27% and PAT at 22-23% after marketing dent.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth in June/July and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Diamond caratage volume up more than 50% in Q1; July not closed, so no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging approach for gold inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: No MCX hedging; relies on natural hedge from periodic gold buying and selling. Gold loan limit available but unused as gold share of inventory is small.

qa_highlights.question: SSSG split between COCO and SIS?
qa_highlights.answer: No COCO SSSG as stores are under one year old; SIS SSSG about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Any upward guidance revision after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in guidance; management says it is more confident in delivering it.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of government request to slow gold buying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said plain gold was hit more; the company saw no impact, with optimism from customers over the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Trade payables fell from INR32 crore to INR20 crore; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Timing of payments, with no change in vendor credit terms, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Average order value trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 about INR112,000 and Q1 FY27 about INR1 lakh; seasonal, with Q2 and Q3 expected higher on festive demand.

risks_watch: Marketing spend ramp in Q2-Q4 will reduce PAT margin by roughly 2-3 percentage points versus Q1 levels.
Inventory turns could fall as COCO stores are added; management expects 1.1-1.4x.
EBO breakeven timelines (one year in Maharashtra, 15-18 months outside) are unproven; only three EBOs are open, one for over six months.
Short-term debt of about INR120 crore outstanding; repayment depends on profit realisation.
Management health: Amit Modak (CEO) was unwell and did not continue the call; the company's sister listed entity PNGS Gargi reportedly slowed sharply in the quarter.
Trade payables fell sharply; management attributed this to payment timing, which should be verified next quarter.
