538734|2026-06.headline: Ceinsys Q1 FY27 revenue flat at INR158 crore (+1% YoY) but EBITDA rose 27% to INR39 crore, margin 24.4%; order book INR990 crore.
538734|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was INR158 crore, up about 1% YoY, while EBITDA grew 27% to INR39 crore and margin expanded 505 bps to 24.4%. PAT was INR31 crore, a marginal decline, with PAT margin at 19.6% (down about 59 bps). Order inflow was INR143 crore against about INR157 crore executed, lifting the order book to INR990 crore from INR880 crore. Management withheld forward guidance throughout, citing policy, and focused on receivables recovery (JJM dues), a proposed AI cloud JV, and undeployed funds from the earlier fundraise.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR880 crore in Q4 FY26
broadly flat vs prior two quarters (162-164 days)

segments.name: Geospatial Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR94 crore, up 30% YoY; majority of the INR143 crore fresh order inflow came from geospatial enterprise solutions. Management said the mix shifts with project execution phase.

segments.name: Technology Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR63 crore, down about 25% YoY. Management aims to take this segment beyond 51% of segment revenue.

segments.name: Mobility (incl. international subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mobility is now a division after the Allygrow merger; management reported improving order book and a top-line increase and margin improvement at the US subsidiary. Mobility is run-rate and not built into the order book.

guidance_outlook: No forward guidance given on revenue, margins or order inflow, citing company policy.
Management said growth should show in the next 2-3 quarters as orders with 3-6 month execution convert, and expects to sustain the growth trend seen over the last 2.5 years.
Management said it is on track with order book milestones and believes margins of around 22-23% are achievable, citing the 24.4% in Q1.
Management expects a better operating cash flow in FY27 than in FY26, without quantifying it.
Expected collection of about INR100 crore of JJM/IoT dues by end of Q3 FY27, with overdues expected to be cleared before 31 March 2027 per the Maharashtra GR.
Management expects one large national-program order (similar to the earlier INR350-400 crore L1 opportunities) possibly in FY27 Q4 or Q1 FY28, and said two L1 positions were pending award.
capex_capacity: Board approved up to INR25 crore investment in a 50:50 JV with AI Fabric USA for a sovereign AI cloud (GPU-as-a-service, model-as-a-service, AI services); first tranche INR5 crore for incorporation, second INR20 crore after due diligence.
JV incorporation expected in about 1-1.5 months; due diligence (technical, market) to take 3-4 months; business model to be frozen after that, with commercial activity indicated for FY28.
Management said it is evaluating acquisitions, aiming for vertical integration and margin-accretive deals; no deal announced. Acquisition multiples cited at 5-10x EBITDA.
Around INR230 crore raised earlier, of which INR130 crore received in March 2026 and INR100 crore in September 2024 (per management clarification).
demand_pricing: Order book INR990 crore; execution timelines range from 3 to 18 months, with some O&M contracts running 2-5 years. Weighted average execution 12-18 months.

Run-rate businesses (mobility, OEM products and services) sit outside the order book; about INR50 crore of Q1 revenue came from these. Management estimated 20-25% of FY26 revenue (of INR660 crore) was outside the order book.

Key Q1/recent wins: INR67 crore Madhya Pradesh PMAY manpower/LoI (over 3 years); INR17 crore Bhandara Municipal Council AMRUT 2.0 smart water meters (12 months); INR4 crore EKS InTec order; INR4 crore US subsidiary order; INR30 crore aggregate T Second purchase orders.

Management said JJM-related bids are being deprioritised in favour of transport (ITMS/ATMS), energy and other geospatial opportunities where budgets are funded. Transport positive developments expected in 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution timeline of the INR990 crore order book and the funnel outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution spans 3 to 18 months, with O&M extending to 5 years; weighted average 12-18 months. Management said the funnel is strong and it will not give a numeric funnel figure or guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order book roll-forward not match inflow minus revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said run-rate businesses (about INR50 crore of Q1 revenue) are not booked in the order book. Net order book increased about INR110 crore after INR157 crore of execution. Reconciliation to be sent via the IR agency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI cloud JV economics and will Ceinsys be an EPC player?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV is 50:50 with AI Fabric USA, targeting defence and government sovereign cloud. Management said it intends to be an AI solutions company, not EPC, with contractors used for construction.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables and JJM dues outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle at 164 days, flat. About INR100 crore of IoT/JJM dues expected by end of Q3 FY27, per the Maharashtra GR. Management said billing is being collected with no new build-up.

qa_highlights.question: Are large orders (INR350-400 crore L1 positions) likely by Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: INR67 crore order already received. Two more in process, with one possibly in Q2. Management declined to commit on timing but said tender pipeline remains strong, and a large national program order could come in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why not a share buyback given idle funds and low valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said buybacks are funded from surplus operating cash, and the raised funds are for growth. Management said it would not invest only to deploy capital; acquisitions must preserve margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is unbilled revenue high and when will it convert?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the large unbilled revenue (about INR320 crore at 31 March, per the analyst) is mainly JJM; it is expected to be billed and reduce over the next 2 quarters as government funds come in.

544742|2026-06.headline: Sai Parenterals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 182 crore, EBITDA margin 14.9%; IPO funds Rs 101.85 crore redeployed to a 60% stake in Saicriti.
544742|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs 182 crore against Rs 201 crore in Q4 FY26, with gross margin up 370 bps QoQ to 41.8% and EBITDA of Rs 27 crore (14.9% margin). PAT was Rs 8 crore (4.3% margin), down from Rs 13.2 crore in Q4 on a normalised tax charge and lower revenue. The Board approved varying IPO objects, moving Rs 83.83 crore from Jeedimetla upgrades to a 60% stake in Saicriti Pharma and Rs 18.02 crore from a greenfield R&D centre to a 60% stake in Prathyak Laboratories (Rs 15 crore), both subject to shareholder approval. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of Rs 750 crore revenue at about 17% EBITDA margin, weighted to H2.

segments.name: Noumed Pharmaceuticals (Australia/NZ)
segments.commentary: Consolidated since 12 Nov 2025; Q1 revenue was hit by West Asia shipping delays, forcing air freight and extra regulatory costs. Renewed EBOS (TerryWhite Chemmart, Pharmacy Choice) OTC contract from 1 July 2026, valued at AUD 202 million (about Rs 1,300 crore) over 7.5 years, roughly AUD 27 million a year.

segments.name: Standalone (India, injectables and exports)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue Rs 56 crore with EBITDA margin about 29%, attributed mainly to operating leverage. Current exports are only oral dosage and cephalosporins; domestic injectables dominate Units 1 and 2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: revenue Rs 750 crore and EBITDA margin about 17%, with a 45:55 H1:H2 split (CFO-era statement also referred to 44:55 in Q&A).
Q1 revenue is said to be about 24% of the full-year Rs 750 crore target, ahead of the phasing needed.
Noumed Australia contribution from the EBOS renewal begins in Q2 FY27.
Management expects the recovery of raw material cost increases to flow through the contract book over Q2 as the 90-120 day price-revision lag unwinds.
FY27 described as a building year; FY28 expected to show the impact. No FY28 number given; management will decide at Q3 call.
Management expects peak debt in FY27 with de-leveraging from FY28.
capex_capacity: Saicriti Pharma (60% stake, Rs 83.83 crore, total project cost about Rs 215-217 crore): critical care injectable facility at Gummadidala, outside the outer ring road, over 15,000 sq yd; completion extended to about April 2027; about 154.66 million units of capacity vs about 105 million under the original Jeedimetla upgrade (about 47% more).
Jeedimetla Units 1 and 2 (about 3,100 sq yd) cannot be expanded and fall within the outer ring road, where upgrades are no longer permitted under HILTP policy.
Prathyak Laboratories (60%, Rs 15 crore): R&D centre at Genome Valley, Hyderabad, expected to complete on or before 30 September 2026; to be renamed Sai Prathyak as a step-down subsidiary.

Australia (Noumed) facility: AUD 53 million total programme funding now complete; physical completion targeted January 2027, TGA inspection by March 2027, Phase 1 manufacturing from April 2027. Packing-line validation through December-February.

Local manufacture is expected to cut Noumed inventory from 9-10 months to about 5-6 months of stock; one Indian container of inputs replaces 8 finished-goods containers. Federal Modern Manufacturing Initiative grant of AUD 20 million cited.
demand_pricing: Noumed holds 5 exclusive long-term contracts and 10 exclusive supply molecule contracts covering 526 SKUs, typically 5+ years.
Wesfarmers Health and EBOS networks together cover over 2,900 of about 5,500 Australian pharmacies.

EBOS contract: about 12 new products per year targeted; first 24 NPD products identified, with 8 to be developed by Sai's R&D (6 started), 4 exclusive supply contracts and the rest via a Catalent soft-gel partnership.
Management said pharmacy-channel growth for some molecules is running at about 8%, and that more order wins of similar size should come over the next year.
Prathyak pipeline: 150 SKUs across 86 molecules (lyophilised, liposomal, nano-based, oncology and critical-care injectables).
Management stated the injectables export plan targets Europe, Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Middle East first, with the US to be reviewed later.
Saicriti existing domestic critical care franchise about Rs 52-53 crore, currently produced via CMOs and to move to the new site.

506401|2026-06.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q1 FY27: record consolidated EBITDA of INR 554 crore (21% margin) and PAT of INR 345 crore, up 207% YoY.
506401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 35% YoY and 22% QoQ to INR 2,592 crore, with EBITDA up 159% YoY to INR 554 crore and margin at 21% versus 11% a year ago. Phenolics delivered record EBIT of INR 418 crore at a 24% margin, while Advanced Intermediates EBIT was INR 67 crore at an 8% margin. Management said April was disrupted by a maintenance shutdown, propylene shortages and gas curtailment, so the phenol run rate of about 1 lakh tonnes applies to parts of the quarter rather than the full period. Debt funding for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project has been closed, and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.27x.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR 1,775 crore and EBIT of INR 418 crore (24% margin), supported by stronger realisations, sustained demand and high utilisation. Management said the business is almost entirely domestic.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates (AI)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR 804 crore and EBIT of INR 67 crore (8% margin), helped by better realisations, higher operating rates and product mix. AI export mix is about 40-50%; raw material costs stayed high for some products.

guidance_outlook: MIBK and MIBC to be commissioned with acetophenone in August 2026; the remaining projects (multipurpose agrochemical intermediates facility, etc.) are due in Q2 FY27, with commercial volumes from January.
Management aims to reach 4 lakh tonnes of phenol in the existing Deepak Phenolics asset in the short to medium term, with about INR 70-odd crore of debottlenecking capex.
Polycarbonate commissioning targeted for H2 FY28-29 and BPA a couple of months later; propylene from the PDH project is expected to support phenol volumes.

Capex: about INR 1,200 crore spent to date, another INR 1,000-1,600 crore in FY27 (figures varied in the call), and about INR 3,000 crore in FY28. Peak debt estimated at INR 8,000-8,500 crore including working capital, with D/E below 1.
capex_capacity: Ammonia-to-amines integration chain (nitric acid plant, nitration and reduction) completed and stabilised; the company says it now runs 8 products simultaneously.

Phenol capacity is about 3.5 lakh tonnes, and management says it is debottlenecking toward 4 lakh tonnes through advanced process controls. Run rate reached about 1 lakh tonnes per quarter in parts of Q1, but was not sustained through the full quarter.
MIBC pre-commissioning runs reportedly exceeded design capacity; management said it can ramp above 100% once demand comes in.
Debt for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project is closed, funded 60:40 debt to equity, with the 25% equity already contributed.
demand_pricing: Management said phenol demand in India is roughly balanced with no new global capacity, and some supply is short. Imports were duty-free for most of Q1 until the government reimposed the duty.
Raw material costs were high in April, but procurement secured feedstock for continuous operations. Management said feedstock costs are competitive domestically and globally.
Freight and insurance costs rose. The company responded with CIF to FOB shifts, larger parcels, and a product reformulation for a Middle East customer that changed its hazard class.
Consolidated export mix is about 20%. AI is roughly 50-50 domestic to export; Phenolics is almost entirely domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Did phenol run rate reach 1 lakh tonnes per quarter, and how is propylene covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 lakh tonnes was a run rate reached in significant periods, not the full quarter, because of raw material sourcing and a short maintenance shutdown. Debottlenecking is aimed at the 4 lakh tonne mark in the short to medium term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Phenolics spread in Q1 and outlook for Q2-Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose spreads and said Deepak buys feedstock below international index levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the phenol capacity now exceed earlier maturity assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main change was confidence. Advanced process controls, costing about INR 80-100 crore cumulatively, enabled higher throughput, with INR 70-odd crore more planned for debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol supply-demand balance sound?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new capacity, China is largely self-sufficient, demand is balanced and India is short of supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt and capex plan for the INR 11,500 crore project?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore has been spent. Peak borrowing is about INR 6,800 crore plus working capital, for total peak debt of INR 8,000-8,500 crore. Management said D/E will stay below 1x.

qa_highlights.question: Could you quantify incremental revenue and EBITDA margin from the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, but said the margin profile of new products is in line with or above the AI average.

risks_watch: Phenol throughput depends on propylene and feedstock availability; April showed how a shutdown and raw material shortage can cut volumes.
Ramp-up timing for the Q2 AI projects and the MIBC run rate; management said the alkylation and multipurpose plants slipped because of manpower and gas shortages.
Polycarbonate and BPA commissioning (H2 FY28-29) and the debt drawdown schedule.
Freight and insurance costs and the reimposed phenol import duty could change domestic realisations.
Management declined to give Phenolics spreads, AI product-level margins, and the MIBK/acetone ratio, so these remain unverified.
506401|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the phenol and integration outlook, but guarded on spreads, margins and specific product economics, which management repeatedly declined to quantify. Timelines for the polycarbonate project and the AI ramp-up were described as on track but were given loosely.

500233|2026-06.headline: Kajaria Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20% to INR1,328 crore and EBITDA margin hit 19.6%, driven mainly by fuel-cost-led price hikes.
500233|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 20% YoY to INR1,328 crore, mainly from selling price increases after gas costs rose following the Middle East conflict, while volume grew 6% despite a weak April. EBITDA margin expanded to 19.6% from 16.72% a year earlier, and PAT rose to INR169 crore from INR109 crore. Management guided to double-digit volume growth over the next nine months, an 18-19% full-year EBITDA margin, and INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA, and announced two new capacity expansions (Srikalahasti and Gailpur). Morbi gas-price dislocation has narrowed the price gap between Kajaria and Morbi peers from about 40% to under 20%.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit before JV share, exceptionals and tax
financial_highlights.change: vs INR149 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR109 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR25 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,162 crore, up 18% YoY; price increases were the main driver and the company is outsourcing part of volume from Morbi to meet demand this year.

segments.name: Bathware (Kerovit)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR122 crore, up 33% YoY; price hikes of about 15-16% and the rest volume. Management expects a tough margin year as restructuring continues, with FY27 value growth of 35-40%.

segments.name: Adhesives
segments.commentary: Revenue INR45 crore vs INR25 crore a year earlier; management says the segment is on track to grow much faster as branded share rises over informal players.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit volume growth expected over the next nine months (no volume guidance was given in the previous two quarters).
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 18-19% for the full year; EBITDA of INR1,000 crore+ targeted (management clarified EBITDA excludes other income).
Expects FY27 revenue growth of around 20%, with value growth of roughly 20% and double-digit volume growth; FY27 tile volume estimated at about 130 MSM vs about 118 MSM in FY26.
FY27 capex of roughly INR400 crore, including maintenance capex; Srikalahasti and Gailpur lines to spill over into next year.
Bathware to remain tough in FY27 with no margin guidance; management expects better value and profit in FY28.
Promoters have said they will not take salary this financial year; timing of future remuneration is undecided.
capex_capacity: Srikalahasti (South) brownfield expansion of 10 MSM at INR210 crore, approved at the last board meeting; about INR80-90 crore of this is a new shed.

Gailpur (Bhiwadi, Rajasthan) expansion of 11 MSM at INR165 crore, to be completed by April 2027; about INR40-50 crore is shed extension. Management expects INR370 crore to yield about 22 MSM in total across both sites, with turnover of INR400-450 crore per plant.
New lines use a 340-metre kiln versus 200 metres previously; machinery is a mix of SACMI and Chinese equipment.
Manufacturing capacity will not rise in FY27, so the company will outsource more from Morbi this year; dependence is expected to fall when the new plants start in Q1 FY28.
Approximately INR12 crore renewable energy acquisition was also mentioned.
demand_pricing: April was soft due to a full Morbi shutdown (March 5 to mid-April), pre-April dealer stocking in March, and labour shortages linked to elections and LPG supply. Management says May, June and July improved, with July growing double digits.

Gas costs in Morbi (GSPC-supplied) rose from about INR48 to INR86-88 per SCM, versus a 10-12% rise in North. Management says Morbi prices rose 40-45%, while Kajaria's North and South plants raised prices 10-13%.
Kajaria's price gap to Morbi narrowed from about 40% to under 20%; management says this shift is driving demand in North and East.

Management says the company is moving into institutional/project sales alongside retail, with two large builders won, and has about 1,800 dealers (450 exclusive), adding about 100 more this year (50 exclusive).
Geographic split: North 35%, South 30%, East 20%, West 15%. Channel: metro 15%, Tier 1 15%, Tier 2 30%, Tier 3 15%.
Exports are under 1% of turnover. Morbi exports fell to about INR1,000 crore per month from a higher pre-war run rate, due to higher freight costs.

Outsourcing: management said about 29-30% outsourcing currently; the FY27 mix is expected to rise before falling when new capacity comes on stream. Gas cost (blended average about INR71 per SCM in Q1; Morbi about INR85; spot about INR85).

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 11% realisation growth came from each segment, and where do price hikes go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Morbi cost increase was 40-45% versus 10-13% for North/South plants. Blended hikes were 13-14%, and non-Morbi plants took about 10%; prices are holding for now, but gas is volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Where will double-digit volume growth come from in the next nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited May-June recovery, July continuing the trend, stronger distribution, project wins with two large builders, and new dealer showrooms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and how much is maintenance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 capex is about INR400 crore, including maintenance capex, with projects spilling over into next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why build in-house capacity now and what is the margin differential versus outsourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new lines are cheaper per MSM and more opex-efficient, and are highly ROC-accretive; outsourcing is used to fill near-term demand and is expected to fall next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA reach INR1,000 crore and when will promoters take remuneration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA and 18-19% margin for the year. The promoters have said they will not take salary this year, and the timing for later is undecided.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Bathware still weak and what margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is a correction year after hiring a new CBO in April. It gave no margin guidance but expects 35-40% value growth in the segment for the year.

544339|2026-06.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.
544339|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR74.7 crore against INR65.6 crore a year earlier. Gross margin was 78.6% and EBITDA rose 20.6% y-o-y to INR14.4 crore at a 19.2% margin, helped by favourable mix and a scanner trading contribution. Dental lab grew 23.5% y-o-y, with international up 37.4%, while aligners grew 28.6%. Management flagged a new US CEO hire, a planned Palghar land purchase to replace rented facilities, and FY27 scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units. The company remains debt-free.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65.6 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +13.9% y-o-y)
vs INR12.5 crore in Q1 FY26; driven by freight, ECL provisions and AI automation
vs INR14.8 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Dental lab
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23.5% y-o-y across domestic and international. Domestic lab excluding scanners grew about 12% y-o-y in Q1, per the analyst's question and management's confirmation.

segments.name: International (within dental lab)
segments.commentary: Grew 37.4% y-o-y. CFO said USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y currency tailwind, so constant-currency growth is lower but still strong.

segments.name: Aligner solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 28.6% y-o-y. Bizdent grew 27.8% and Vedia grew 29.3%. Management linked growth to the iScope at-home monitoring launch and dentist education.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (paediatric)
segments.commentary: Grew 54.4% y-o-y in the quarter. The company holds 60% of its PAT in its adjusted EBITDA calculation.

segments.name: Scanners (trading)
segments.commentary: Sold at about INR3 lakh average to dentists with a trading margin of about 15% to 20%. Scanner mix causes quarter-to-quarter margin swings.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration: 15% to 20% revenue growth and 18% to 20% EBITDA margin. Management said it expects to be in that range, after FY26 margins of about 15.6%.
Domestic lab growth expected to accelerate in Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY27 as satellite labs and scanner-linked customers mature.
Scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units targeted for FY27, with the company saying it is on track.
AI-led automation costs are elevated this year and expected to fall next year as scale rises.
Margin expected to be maintained or improved through the year; gross margin should stay stable excluding scanner mix effects.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 investment in new machinery to modernise and expand manufacturing capacity; no amount disclosed.

Letter of intent executed to acquire land in Palghar, Maharashtra, to replace two rented domestic facilities (Illusion Dental Lab and aligners). Rent is about INR2 crore a year; management said a 3x-size owned facility could otherwise cost INR5 to 6 crore in rent.
No disruption to revenue or productivity expected during the transition, which will be phased. Management cited a 2020 export-unit move from Kandivali to Boisar as precedent.
Aligner capacity utilisation about 70%, with reasonable headroom. Lab utilisation is at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.
Digital penetration in domestic network about 75% to 80% (dental lab and aligner combined); international is mostly digital.
demand_pricing: Domestic lab growth slowed to about 12% y-o-y ex-scanners, which management attributed to scanner-led adoption maturing with a 6-month to 18-month gestation period.
Scanner penetration in the industry estimated at about 7% to 8%, with management saying the adoption curve (J-curve) has not yet clearly started.
Management said competition in aligners persists but declined to detail it, citing counter-strategies such as cross-selling.
Aligners are sold only through dentists, not B2C. Management targets general dentists and orthodontists alike.
Branding push includes a brand ambassador, in-clinic branding and social media. Management described itself as the only branded player in crowns.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates Laxmi Dental products for dentists after the iScan Pro scanner, given no exclusive tie-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 36 years of trust, global quality standards and ISO-certified systems, and innovation, and said it is the only branded crown player.

qa_highlights.question: What is scanner gross margin and how lumpy will margins be?
qa_highlights.answer: Scanners are a trading item with a 15% to 20% margin. Excluding scanners, margins are stable and rising; Q1 margin was 19.2% vs about 15% in the previous quarter and 18% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and utilisation for lab and aligners?
qa_highlights.answer: Aligners at about 70% utilisation. Lab runs at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Palghar land and will there be disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is to move from two rented sites to one owned facility to cut about INR2 crore rent and gain room to expand. Management expects no revenue disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic lab growing only about 12% and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was 12% y-o-y, attributed to satellite labs adding customer proximity, and expects faster growth from Q2 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the international growth is currency?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y, with the rest from existing DSO and retail business. Management expects the tailwind to persist for some quarters but is unsure beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Scanner deployment and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 800 to 1,000 scanner deployments in FY27 and an 18% to 20% margin aspiration; it said Q1 margin supports that range.

risks_watch: Scanner mix drives quarterly gross margin swings; a strong scanner quarter dilutes margin.
Domestic lab growth at about 12% ex-scanners is below the company's 15% to 20% aspiration; Q2 to Q4 acceleration is unproven.
FX tailwind on international growth (USD from about INR85 to INR95) may reverse.
AI-led automation and ECL provisions raised other expenses to INR15.9 crore; cost pressure may persist this year.
Palghar land and facility transition: timing, capex size and rent savings not yet quantified.
Aligner competition, which management declined to detail.
Share price weakness after results drew analyst and retail investor questions; management had no explanation.

532726|2026-06.headline: Gallantt Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 203 crore (18% margin) from INR 254 crore a year ago, though flat sequentially, on coal costs and a pellet plant shutdown.
532726|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 2% year-on-year to INR 1,146 crore but fell from INR 1,205 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA was INR 203 crore (18% margin) versus INR 209 crore in Q4 and INR 254 crore in Q1 FY26, and PAT was INR 124 crore (11% margin). Management attributed the year-on-year decline to higher raw material costs (up 9%), the planned pellet plant shutdown, a seasonal monsoon-driven TMT price correction, and higher employee costs. The 1.23 million tonne capacity expansion and captive iron ore mines remain on schedule for H2 FY27 and FY28 respectively.

segments.name: TMT / long products (Gorakhpur and Gujarat)
segments.commentary: TMT sales volume was flat YoY at about 192,000 tonnes and down about 8% QoQ against a strong Q4 FY26. Gorakhpur rolling mill utilisation is 93%, while Kutch is at about 66%.

segments.name: Pellet and sponge iron
segments.commentary: External sales fell YoY and QoQ due to higher captive consumption for DRI and steelmaking, plus the planned pellet plant shutdown, which is now complete.

segments.name: Billets
segments.commentary: Billet volumes grew 13% YoY and 38% QoQ, running ahead of internal plans for the year.

guidance_outlook: Capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tonnes (0.23 million tonnes) under the INR 3,000 crore capex programme is expected to commission in H2 FY27, with benefits flowing from H2.
Pellet plant returns to normal captive utilisation in the coming quarter now the shutdown is complete; management expects no substantial EBITDA erosion through the year.
Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted because of the monsoon; management expects Q3 and Q4 to pick up.
Domestic steel demand expected to grow 7-9% this year; management referred to 8-9% in the Q&A.
Captive iron ore mines (UP and Rajasthan) are targeted to commence production in FY28; UP exploration expected to finish in 2-3 months and Rajasthan in about six months.
Solar: 18 MW in Gujarat due for Q2 FY27 and 60 MW at Gorakhpur due for Q4 FY27 (the call also cites 67 MW elsewhere, so the split is unclear).
Debottlenecking at Gujarat unit to complete within FY27.
capex_capacity: Total capex programme about INR 3,000 crore, of which about INR 800 crore spent over FY26 and Q1 FY27; INR 137 crore spent in Q1 FY27. Funded by internal accruals with no term loans planned.
Roughly half of capex goes to mining: three iron ore mines (two in UP, one in Rajasthan), with beneficiation plants in UP and a beneficiation-cum-pellet plant in Rajasthan. Production from FY28.
Capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tonnes, commissioning in H2 FY27.
Solar: 7 MW trial plant commissioned in FY26; 18 MW in Gujarat (Q2 FY27); 60 MW at Gorakhpur (Q4 FY27). Total about 85 MW.
Pellet plant installed capacity about 8 lakh tonnes against raw feed need of 9-9.5 lakh tonnes a year.
demand_pricing: TMT and rebar prices corrected meaningfully during the quarter from a firm start; management said the correction was seasonal and sector-wide, with flat products holding up better.
India turned a net steel importer in the quarter, with imports rising under some free trade routes; the industry has sought anti-dumping duties alongside existing safeguard duties.
Management claims a market share above 25% in its addressable UP market and cites brand marketing with celebrity endorsements (Ajay Devgn, and now Janhvi Kapoor).
Export: management said exports are not a focus. Gorakhpur is inland, and Gujarat billet exports happen only occasionally.

Raw material mix: Gorakhpur coal is 100% linkage for power plant; DRI coal is 60-70% Indian and the rest South African, sourced via Itochu. Gujarat uses Indonesian coal for power and South African coal for process.

522113|2026-06.headline: Timken India Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~15% YoY to INR929 crore, with PBT of INR150 crore and PBT margin of 16.2%.
522113|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR929 crore, up almost 15% YoY, after a seasonally strong Q4 FY26 (highest standalone revenue of INR3,147 crore for FY26). PBT rose to INR150 crore from INR130 crore, with PBT margin at 16.2% versus 16.1% a year earlier, and EBITDA margin at 19.6%. Gross margin was 39.9%, up 100 bps YoY and roughly flat QoQ, which management attributed to heavy-truck and off-highway price increases offsetting unfavourable Q1 mix. The Bharuch plant is ramping up quickly, with revenue of about INR50 crore in the quarter and near breakeven.

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: INR200 crore, about 22% of Q1 revenue. Management described government railway buying as slow and sluggish, and said the year started with about 3% growth in rail.

segments.name: Mobile / others
segments.commentary: INR184 crore. Management said mobile (tractors, heavy trucks) is about 20% of the business and is where price increases are sticking.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: INR153.9 crore (about INR154 crore).

segments.name: Process
segments.commentary: INR186 crore, up about 28-30% YoY, driven by metals customers and wind (gearbox exports and domestic wind farms).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR200 crore, including about 1% export incentive. Intercompany push to America rose about 21%; Europe is down, China and ASEAN are down, and the US is up.

segments.name: Bharuch plant (within segments)
segments.commentary: About INR50 crore revenue in Q1, close to breakeven. Spherical roller bearing (SRB) line utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, targeted at about 70% by August-September; CRB line utilisation is lower, with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

guidance_outlook: Bharuch SRB line expected to reach about 70% utilisation in August-September 2026; CRB line ramp toward end of Q2 and Q3.
Rail expansion at Jamshedpur expected to start commercial production by calendar year-end 2026; management said it will ramp up immediately after that.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of sales, with project work described as on track; timing may spill some capex into FY28.
Further cost escalation seen as limited beyond the steel, carbide, coal and grinding increases already in the system; base oil described as the only volatile input.
Management said it will continue to pass on cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew; rail and PSU/ARC contracts are fixed and will reprice only at renewal.
capex_capacity: Bharuch plant ramping up; three manufacturing lines; utilisation cannot be given at plant level but SRB demand is higher than CRB at this stage.
Rail investment at Jamshedpur on track; plain bearings investment at Bharuch on track.
Manufactured vs traded mix roughly 75/25, similar to prior quarters.
Gas conversion from LPG to natural gas completed across supply chain and plants.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth driven by resilient core-segment demand and both export and domestic execution.
Steel producers raised prices by about INR1,500-1,600 per tonne in January and about INR3,500 per tonne by April, around INR5,000 per tonne in total; most customers have started paying the increase.
Price pass-through is working in heavy truck and tractor/off-highway; rail, PSU and cement customers are on fixed annual rate contracts.
Process growth partly from metals projects (mills built in India for export) and wind.
Management said the US market is up, Europe and China are down, and ASEAN and Australia are flat to down.
No direct tariff figure given; management said the US landed tariff has moved over time and it would confirm the current rate.
Management said the parent's 80/20 portfolio review is aimed at performance improvement; no change in Indian strategy was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail INR200 crore (22%), mobile/others INR184 crore, distribution INR153.9 crore, process INR186 crore, exports about INR200 crore including 1% export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of parent's 80/20 strategy and belts divestment on India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80/20 is a Pareto-based performance tool that is being applied globally; it is not yet a change in strategy for India. The India focus stays on off-highway, rail and tractor/heavy-truck, with no two-wheeler, passenger car or washing-machine ball bearings.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch ramp-up and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Bharuch revenue was about INR50 crore, close to breakeven. SRB utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, expected to reach about 70% by August-September; CRB is lower with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of process and export growth and US outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Process grew about 30% YoY, from metals and wind. Exports to the US are growing, Europe is down, and the intercompany push to America is about 21%.

qa_highlights.question: Rail outlook and Jamshedpur ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Government railway procurement is slow due to funds diverted to infrastructure and defence; management expects this to be timing-related. Jamshedpur rail capacity is due to start commercial production by calendar year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation has been passed through to price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to give an exact percentage; heavy truck and tractor customers have largely passed through cost escalation, while rail and PSU contracts will reprice at renewal.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex plan and allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-wise split not given; capex directionally in line with the 8-10% of sales range, with some timing spillover into the next fiscal.

risks_watch: Steel and other input cost inflation: about INR5,000 per tonne of steel price increases; pass-through is incomplete for rail and PSU contracts that are fixed until renewal.
Slow government railway procurement due to fund diversion to infrastructure and defence; it could delay the Jamshedpur ramp-up benefit.
Bharuch ramp-up needs to reach about 70% SRB utilisation by August-September and CRB later; any slippage would weigh on margins.
Parent's 80/20 review and divestments (belts, automotive OE): the Indian implications are unclear, and management said it will review which assets can be used for growth in India.
Export exposure to geopolitics; Europe, China and ASEAN are down; US tariff status was not confirmed on the call.
Base oil price volatility affecting grease costs; the Brent outlook and the Middle East conflict affect energy and gas costs.
NCLT approval of the Timken GGB Technology merger is pending.

544407|2026-06.headline: Aegis Vopak Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, with liquid terminaling up 31% and operating EBITDA up 15.6% to INR179.4 crore.
544407|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, led by liquid terminaling (INR126.5 crore, +31% YoY) while gas terminaling fell 3.5% YoY to INR107.2 crore. Operating EBITDA rose 15.6% YoY to INR179.4 crore (about 76.7% margin) and cash PAT was INR124.9 crore. Management said the board approved a 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA and 49,577 cbm of liquid capacity at Kochi, and that the Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT static) was commissioned. Management framed a $5 billion capex plan through FY2030-31, of which about INR10,000 crore is to be commissioned by March/June 2027.

segments.name: Liquid terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR126.5 crore, up 31% YoY, driven by higher volumes, new capacity and product mix; management cited JNPA plot 1 maturing (about INR6,000 realization per unit vs blended INR3,000) and better-located capacity commissioned last year.

segments.name: Gas terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR107.2 crore, down 3.5% YoY on LPG import disruption from the Middle East; management said volumes held up via diversified sourcing and multi-location distribution. Standard throughput rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow volumes at least 25% YoY every year; management said AVTL delivered 3.9 million MT in the last year and expects more than 25% growth.
Liquid capacity to rise from about 1.7 million cbm to about 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end.
About INR10,000 crore of expansion (JNPA, ammonia, liquid) expected to be commissioned by March 2027 or June 2027 at the latest.
Kochi 49,577 cbm expected by early next financial year; CRL4 at Kandla (about 94,148 cbm) targeted for later next year.

Funding: debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x; about $3 billion of the $5 billion capex to come from debt, with about $2 billion equity net worth target and mandatory dilution to 25% of equity by 2 June 2028.
capex_capacity: JNPA expansion: 318,100 cbm liquid storage, 77,236 MT LPG capacity and a 35,000 MT LPG bottling plant, total outlay INR1,675 crore; first phase of about 100,000 cbm expected in Q3 FY27.
JNPA: board approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank; existing liquid capacity about 101,900 cbm.
Kochi: board sanctioned 49,577 cbm; total liquid capacity to reach 132,122 cbm from 82,545 cbm.

Pipavav: 36,000 MT ammonia storage commissioned; 0.5 million MT/yr 15-year take-or-pay petroleum product agreement to start by year-end via additional liquid rail gantry; VLGC-compliant jetty by APM Terminals expected this year; Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline connection expected in the first half of FY27 (per Q&A, 2-3 months).

Mangalore: 75,000 cbm added last year, total 193,000 cbm; evaluating 60,000 cbm more; LPG rail gantry and bottling investment INR52.5 crore. Haldia: 226,890 cbm liquid storage plus 3 acres of land acquired; Haldia-Panagarh pipeline (HPCL, 60 km) expected October-November 2026.
demand_pricing: LPG throughput is priced per metric ton, not per storage day, and management said there is no escalation; the focus is on volume growth.
Liquid terminaling is charged per cbm capacity, not occupancy, so revenue is not driven by utilization.

Management attributed gas volume resilience to diversified sourcing (ITOCHU partnership, non-Middle East cargoes) and ullage availability; it said domestic LPG shortfall had recovered to about 80-85% of normal by July.
Ammonia realizations described as 2.5-3x LPG realizations; first-year utilization projected at 20-25% of the 36,000 MT static capacity (prorated for an August start).
Pipavav: 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc for part of ammonia capacity for its DAP plant.

qa_highlights.question: Are LPG throughput charges fixed by counterparty and term, and why haven't terminal charges risen while distribution margins did?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals; charges are per MT with no escalation. Management said terminaling is infrastructure usage, while distribution margins reflect sourcing and inventory risk during the geopolitical disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AVTL gain share versus national LPG imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited non-Middle East sourcing (none of its ships were stuck), a partner in ITOCHU, and wider distribution using freed-up ullage across more locations than Mumbai and Kandla.

qa_highlights.question: Is 25% volume growth sustainable, and what is the Haldia pipeline impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for at least 25% YoY growth; four pipelines are due this year (Jamnagar-Loni done; Kandla-Gorakhpur at Kandla and Pipavav in 2-3 months; Haldia-Panagarh in 2-3 months). Haldia-Panagarh is HPCL's 60 km line; the Panagarh bottling plant is 0.5 million MT/yr and currently about 0.25 million MT is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and liquid capacity path to FY28, and what is the Pipavav take-or-pay economics?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10,000 crore to be commissioned by March/June 2027; liquid capacity 1.7 to 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end. The Pipavav 0.5 million MT is higher utilization of existing capacity via rail gantry, not new tankage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth plans beyond the INR10,000 crore phase and the $5 billion program?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing organic and inorganic options, inland depots, strategic storage and industrial terminals, and said binding agreements will be announced as signed. The $5 billion plan through FY2030-31 is reaffirmed, with timing expected to be lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Why did liquid revenue jump when capacity did not change?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity added last year was only partly in the base year and has now matured, JNPA plot 1 is fully running, and product mix has changed, which takes time.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a mix of debt and equity, with debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x, about $3 billion of debt, a $2 billion equity net worth target, and mandatory dilution to 25% by 2 June 2028.

531266|2026-06.headline: VST Tillers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR313.4 crores, but operational EBITDA margin fell about 45 bps to 12.85% on raw material inflation.
531266|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR313.4 crores from INR282.4 crores, and PAT rose to INR48.7 crores from INR44.6 crores. Operational EBITDA margin (excluding other income and fair value gains) was 12.85%, versus 13.3% a year earlier, with management attributing the drop to commodity and raw material inflation. Power tillers grew about 18% and power weeders about 56% in volume, while domestic tractors grew 4.5% and tractor exports were 275 units. Management declined to give a full-year FY27 outlook, saying it would be clearer in about a month, and said the July volume softness reflected a high base.

financial_highlights.metric: Operational EBITDA (excl. other income and fair value gain)

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: Volume grew about 18% in Q1; management cites 16-20% tiller growth over recent quarters and expects 15-20% to continue. Bajaj Finance retail financing volume roughly doubled to about 1,000 units from about 400 a year earlier, but still only 8-9% of retail sales versus a 15-20% target.

segments.name: Power weeders (SFM)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 56% in Q1 and management has been clocking 50-60% growth for several quarters. Retail counters added more than 500 in three months, taking the network toward a target of about 2,000 counters by year-end, on top of 750-800 SFM dealers.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 4.5% in Q1 but supply lagged demand during ramp-up of the new variant, per management. Management expects Q2 growth, with substantial volume increases in Q3 and Q4; 40-50 HP is described as a crowded segment.

segments.name: Tractors (exports)
segments.commentary: 275 tractors sold in Q1. Europe: about 1,400-1,500 tractors per management, with entry into Turkey and the Nordics planned. Africa: 75 HP tractor shipments started. US expansion described as unclear.

segments.name: Reapers
segments.commentary: Seasonal product; volumes expected to pick up in Q2 with the harvest season. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 outlook given; management said it is too early and will comment in about a month, since H2 depends on monsoon and rabi sowing.
Management said demand outlook is positive through September, with the next 15-20 days critical for kharif crop survival.
Long-term target of about 20,000 tractors by FY30 (including 5,000-6,000 international units); revenue vision of INR3,000 crores by 2030.
More than 30 tractor variants planned over the next three years; three global platforms (A, B, C) to launch over 12-36 months.
Tractor dealer additions targeted at 50-60 in FY27, versus 40-50 last year.
capex_capacity: A new production facility will need investment in roughly the next two years, per the CEO.
Tiller-tractor hybrid product (geared, with differential) to roll out from the factory starting this month, with substantial volume in Q3 and Q4.
International distributor logistics infrastructure delayed from Q1 but expected operational in Q3.
Hydrostatic transmission tractor being seeded for export markets, not sold in India.
Bangalore land of about 19 acres; manufacturing already moved out, only administrative office remains; no monetisation decision yet.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand issue in tillers; July volumes declined YoY against a very high base.
Tractor 40-50 HP segment is crowded and highly competitive; company is acquiring market share through product breadth.
Commodity inflation (steel, forgings, castings, aluminium, copper), elevated and volatile natural rubber prices, and high crude and freight costs weighed on margins.

Emission norm: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026, which management says will not create a big cost increase for end customers. Stage 5 for all tractors in 2032 could add 25-30% to tractor technology cost today, though this may fall over time.
Possible 100% US tariff under a bill in Congress is a risk to US expansion plans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is tractor growth lagging the industry despite new launches, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 supply did not fully meet demand during the new-variant ramp-up; management expects Q2 growth and substantial increases in Q3-Q4. Strategy includes more than 30 variants over three years and state-by-state rollout of the FENTM series, starting with Gujarat, then Maharashtra.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the Bajaj Finance tie-up and other financing partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail financing reached about 1,000 units versus about 400 a year earlier, but only 8-9% of retail, against a 15-20% target. Other partners include Chola, TVS and nationalised banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is tiller export viable, and what new products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 300 units last year. A geared tiller with differential for Europe and India and an electric tiller/weeder are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any moderation in demand given July volume decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed July to a high base in tillers. It sees growth continuing at least through September, with tillers at 16-20% growth and weeders at 50-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capital allocation policy and non-core asset plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the policy is to maximise shareholder value and it expects to deploy capital over the next 18-24 months. No development on non-core assets yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are the implications of upcoming emission norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026 is already ready. TREM 3A from April 2028 is covered. Full Stage 5 for tractors in 2032 may add 25-30% to technology cost at current prices.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression from raw material inflation; Q1 margin down about 45 bps YoY.
Tractor market share: domestic tractor growth of 4.5% trails the industry; July volumes were lower YoY.
Monsoon uncertainty over the next 15-20 days affects kharif output and rabi sowing.
Tariff risk to US expansion, and the possible 100% tariff bill in Congress.
Possible capex for a new facility in about two years; capital deployment plans to be disclosed in 18-24 months.
Management has not given a FY27 outlook; next update expected in about one month.
531266|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term tractor and tiller growth targets, but cautious on near-term tractor volumes and on FY27 guidance, which it deferred pending monsoon clarity. Vague on capital deployment and inorganic plans.
key_quotes: And I have in last call also, in the last quarter I have said upwards of 15,000 numbers we will aim to reach, close to 20,000 numbers we will aim to reach in FY '30.
So giving an FY '27 outlook, I think it's a little too early.

500670|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 profit described as second highest in company history after Q1 FY22, driven by better realisations despite lower sales volumes.
500670|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 was shaped by Middle East war escalation and de-escalation, which caused viability-driven shutdowns at acetic acid, ethyl acetate and TDI but lifted realisations. Sales volumes fell well below production, and inventory built up to 30 June was about 15% liquidated by end-July. Fertilizer segment profit rose to about INR85 crores from about INR24 crores, with urea contributing about INR48 crores and ANP about INR12 crores. Management gave no formal quarterly guidance, and several questions on forward realisations and savings went unanswered.

financial_highlights.value: Second highest in company history after Q1 FY22

financial_highlights.change: Up about INR60 crores from about INR24 crores
Held across G-Sec, GSFS and bank

segments.name: Fertilizers (urea, ANP)
segments.commentary: Fertilizer segment result rose to about INR85 crores from about INR24 crores, with urea about INR48 crores and ANP about INR12 crores. Energy norm for urea revised to 6.37 Gcal/MT from 6.20 Gcal/MT, valid for 3 years from FY26.

segments.name: Chemicals (TDI, WNA, CNA, AN Melt, TGU, acetic acid, ethyl acetate)
segments.commentary: Q1 output: TDI 12,800 MT, WNA 113,000 MT (sales 20,800 MT), CNA production 37,500 MT (sales 16,400 MT), AN Melt 55,600 MT, TGU 74,800 MT, formic acid 8,200 MT. Acetic acid and ethyl acetate were shut for part of the quarter; both restarted by 1 August.

guidance_outlook: Management expects TGU output for the rest of FY27 to be broadly at last year's level, against a Q1 run rate it described as about 300,000 MT annualised.

Steam portion of the coal-based Dahej steam and power project is running; power expected in about 45 days. Estimated saving of INR30,000-40,000 per MT of TDI at current gas and coal prices, subject to change.

A.T. Kearney cost-saving quantification is not yet signed off; management expects a clearer P&L picture by end of Q2. Earlier Kearney estimate cited by an analyst was INR250-300 crores, which management confirmed.
Projected incremental revenue of INR1,200-1,500 crores and contribution uplift of INR500-600 crores from the INR2,800 crore project portfolio, given later and subject to price volatility.

Capex for FY27 targeted at INR1,200-1,500 crores more on top of Q1 INR300 crores; most will sit in CWIP, with only partial capitalisation in FY27. Remaining projects commercially operational around mid-2027. Further about INR1,500 crores over the next two years.
capex_capacity: Dahej CCPP (INR613 crores) and other projects are targeted for commercial operation around mid-2027.
Dahej steam portion is online and replacing gas with coal for TDI-II; power portion expected in roughly 45 days.
Weak nitric acid plant running about 3 months behind schedule, to be recouped; AMUGL and AN Melt reported online.
Ammonia output about 173,000 MT, split 54% oil-based and 49% gas-based (as stated, shares sum above 100%). TDI output split 66% Dahej and 34% Bharuch.

Urea and nitric acid ran above rated capacity; CNA ran below design capacity due to weak internal TDI consumption; aniline and nitrobenzene ran above design. Minimum neem coated urea obligation is 637,000 MT.
demand_pricing: TDI: management said global TDI supply exceeds demand, so Covestro and Wanhua maintenance shutdowns will not move global pricing, though Indian TDI shortage will affect local pricing.
Inventory built to 30 June was about 15% liquidated by end-July; realisations were initially lower, then rose, with no single figure given.
Offtake was weak in Q1 even though spreads looked better, causing inventory build-up.
Management declined to give Q2 vs Q1 realisation direction, citing market volatility.
Fuel oil and gas prices rose versus Q4 FY26 on the Middle East crisis; oil prices (per analyst) moved from about INR43-44 to about INR73; easing seen in July-August but not resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Current oil and gas prices and availability versus Q1 averages?
qa_highlights.answer: N.B. Desai said prices eased in July-August but the Middle East crisis is unresolved; gas prices are volatile, though supply has not affected operations.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 realisation direction for chemicals vs Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, citing that Q1 was the reference point and the market is volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej steam and power savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently about INR30,000-40,000 per MT of TDI; the figure moves with the gas-coal price delta, and coal-based operation benefits if coal prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Cash, capex and project pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash about INR4,000 crores; Q1 capex INR300 crores; FY27 capex targeted at INR1,200-1,500 crores more; INR2,800 crore projects on hand plus about INR1,500 crores over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Plant restart status for acetic acid, ethyl acetate and TDI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethyl acetate and acetic acid back on 1 August after July and May shutdowns; Bharuch TDI was down in July, with TDI-I and TDI-II restarting. Methanol sourcing for captive acetic acid has started.

risks_watch: Re-escalation of the Middle East conflict could reopen viability issues and shut plants again, as seen in Q1.
Unsigned Kearney savings estimate; the INR250-300 crore planned saving has not been confirmed by management.
Inventory liquidation and realisation mix in Q2 are unclear; offtake was weak in Q1.
Project timelines: Dahej CCPP and other projects slated for mid-2027; nitric acid plant about 3 months behind.
Gas and coal price volatility drives the Dahej steam and power savings and TDI economics.
Management declined to quantify several forward items (Q2 realisations, project revenue impact), limiting visibility.
500670|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Q1 profitability and project progress, but evasive on forward realisations, guidance and project revenue, repeatedly citing volatility and avoiding numbers.
key_quotes: But overall, the profits for Q1 in our view has been significantly higher , and it is the second highest in the history of the company after the Q1 of '22.
This has been revised for a period from FY25-26, and valid for 3 year s period.
We do not recall, gentlemen, having given any guidance of such nature.
So 1 month shutdown of Covestro and Wanhua will not affect the overall pricing of the TDI.

544004|2026-06.headline: IRM Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 326 crore, with EBITDA ex-other income up 139% YoY to INR 62 crore and PAT of INR 34 crore.
544004|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with volumes at an all-time high of 50.9 MMSCM (up 8% YoY). Margin expansion was attributed to sourcing (HPHT and long-term contracts priced below spot), price realisations, and cost control, with management stating there were no one-time items. Industrial PNG volumes were hit by a 9 March 2026 government notification that cut industrial gas allocation to around 80%. Management guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the remaining three quarters and says the current margin level will likely moderate.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore

segments.name: Banaskantha (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 48% of Q1 volume and about 46% of profitability; CNG is about 51% of vehicle sales here. Station additions limited to 10-15 in FY27 as the GA is nearing saturation.

segments.name: Fatehgarh Sahib (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 38% of profitability. CNG penetration only 6%; volumes hit by the industrial gas cut linked to the NGT order. Plans for 2 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Diu & Gir Somnath (GA)
segments.commentary: CNG is 60% of vehicle sales; contributed about 8-9% of profitability. Entire commercial segment converted to PNG, with commercial connections now on PNG. Plans for about 5 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Namakkal & Trichy (GA)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM, up 102% YoY from 2.84 MMSCM; contributed about 5% of profitability. FY27 volume guidance 25-30 MMSCM (vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26); about 15-17 new stations planned; more than 80 TNSTC buses running, with a target of 200+ buses.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA expected at about INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters; management later indicated overall FY27 around INR 7/SCM and said the 19% EBITDA margin may not be sustained.
Revenue growth of about 25% in FY27 guided; management said a safe range is around 20% or more.
Volume growth of 10-12% in FY27, with total volume targeted at about 250 MMSCM by year-end (FY26: 224 MMSCM).
FY27 capex of about INR 250 crore in total (INR 150 crore for Namakkal and Trichy, INR 50 crore each for Banaskantha and Diu & Gir Somnath / Fatehgarh).
Long-term goal of 20-25% revenue CAGR over the next five years.
Management said same-level performance as Q1 will not be repeated every quarter; performance will be subdued going forward, though it expects QoQ and YoY improvement.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore; cumulative capex about INR 1,090 crore.
FY27 capex plan about INR 250 crore; management said it will not exceed this, of which INR 150 crore is for Namakkal and Trichy.
CNG stations at 153 as of 30 June 2026 (up 37% YoY), with 564 dispensing points across four GAs.
Station model mix: franchisee (DODO), OMC and company-operated; the company is moving away from daughter booster and LNG-based models toward online stations.
Diu & Gir Somnath: tap-off from GSPL pipeline and hookup with IOC and GAIL in progress; currently drawing LNG from HPCL's Chhara terminal.
demand_pricing: Pricing: Realisations up about 15% YoY and QoQ per an analyst's calculation (not disputed by management); management said price hikes are linked to sourcing cost and it will not pass on further hikes now that Brent is cooling.

Sourcing mix in Q1 FY27: APM and NWG about 32-33% (APM 21%, NWG 11%), HPHT about 35%, long-term (Reliance, GAIL and others) about 32%, CBG blending 1%, spot about 1%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%.
HPHT gas at about USD 9/MMBtu versus spot of USD 14-20; industrial volumes benefit from GSPC and Shell long-term contracts running to 2030.
Industrial PNG volumes were hit by the 9 March 2026 notification (about 80% allocation); CNG and domestic/commercial PNG not affected.
Customer base: 86,590 domestic PNG (+13% YoY), 589 commercial (+36% YoY), 228 industrial (+5% YoY).
Management said it is a price taker; competitors and alternative fuel prices are high, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-time items behind the sharp rise in EBITDA per SCM, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-time items; gains came from pricing, gas sourcing and opex optimisation. It guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix and how has it changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: APM+NWG about 32%, HPHT about 35%, long-term about 32%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%; Q4 FY26 APM about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Namakkal and Trichy volumes and FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM (up 102% YoY); FY27 target 25-30 MMSCM, towards the upper end, vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for FY27 and station additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR 250 crore; stations to be added: 10-15 in Banaskantha, 15-17 in Namakkal and Trichy, about 5 in Diu & Gir Somnath, 2 in Fatehgarh Sahib.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the NGT order in Fatehgarh Sahib?
qa_highlights.answer: The NGT order (February 2026) has not been enforced by the Punjab pollution board; supply cuts began 9 March. Management expects ramp-up once enforced and says new industries must use natural gas to get consents.

qa_highlights.question: Is the promoter license fee a concern and how might it change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a 2% license fee disclosed in the IPO document, not profit to promoters, worth about INR 20-25 crore for the year and already included in PAT; it cannot promise the rate will stay unchanged.

532395|2026-06.headline: Axiscades Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 42% YoY to ₹346 crore, but reported PAT loss of ₹14.8 crore; normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore.
532395|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter of the divestment-led transition: Engineering Services is shown as discontinued operations (₹163 crore revenue), leaving continuing operations at ₹183 crore, up 94% YoY. Reported EBITDA for the combined business was ₹27.9 crore, with one-offs of ₹13.1 crore (including ₹9.62 crore receivable provision on an aged defence transaction and ₹3.5 crore hedge provision) and ₹21.81 crore divestment transaction cost below EBITDA. Management says normalized EBITDA was ₹41 crore (11.8% margin) and normalized PAT ₹20.2 crore. Guidance was reaffirmed: FY27 continuing revenue of ₹1,377 crore, EBITDA of ₹270 crore and PAT of about 50% of that, with acquisitions and divestment proceeds central to delivery.

financial_highlights.value: ₹183 crore (₹180.7 crore cited in Q&A segment overview)

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹20.9 crore PAT in Q1 FY26
mainly ADD Solutions (EBITDA -₹4.8 crore, PAT -₹6.7 crore)

segments.name: Defence (continuing)
segments.commentary: Record ₹125 crore revenue, up 112% YoY, with underlying EBITDA of ₹13 crore (up 15% YoY). Reported EBITDA ₹2.6 crore after ~₹9.6 crore one-time costs; management cites underlying 9.7% margin. Assured forecast visibility ₹4,557 crore after 8 wins since April.

segments.name: XiDA (ex-ESAI, US-headquartered)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹49.5 crore, up 63% YoY, at ~33% EBITDA margin (EBITDA ₹14.7 crore cited, ~30% in another remark). Added two large global technology customers via a business transfer.

segments.name: Aerospace manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹6.1 crore in Q1 with negative EBITDA; 30-member leadership team built ahead of acquisitions.

segments.name: Mistral
segments.commentary: Delivered ₹122 crore revenue at ~14.5% EBITDA margin while absorbing its own provisions.

segments.name: ADD Solutions (non-core, European)
segments.commentary: EBITDA loss ₹4.8 crore and PAT loss ₹6.7 crore; exit targeted by Q4 FY27 with a sale process that could realize over FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 continuing operations revenue guidance reaffirmed at ₹1,377 crore on an annualized pro forma basis.
FY27 EBITDA target of ₹270 crore; PAT expected at roughly 50% of EBITDA (~₹135 crore), could be higher with lower interest after debt paydown.
Defence revenue expected to grow over 75% YoY in FY27 and over the following years; ESAI/XiDA expected to grow over 100% this year.
Aerospace manufacturing target: annualized run rate of ₹375 crore revenue and ₹84 crore EBITDA by Q4 FY27, with the platform aiming at ~₹1,000 crore by FY29.
Power 930 targets (FY30 PAT of ₹960 crore) stated as unchanged.
Deferred ~₹140-142 crore revenue: ~40% (over ₹60 crore) recovered in Q1; balance planned across Q2 and Q3.
capex_capacity: Akkodis divestment valued at US$237 million (~₹2,256 crore); Phase 1 targeted by Aug 31 with ~₹190 crore post-tax cash; Phase 2 by Nov 30 (management later said it is trying to pull it to about September) bringing ~₹525 crore cash.
Extraordinary gain of ~₹1,255 crore to be recognised on closing; ~₹200+ crore expected in Q2, the bulk in Q3 (or late Q2).
Aerospace services divestment expected to close in Q2 FY27; combined divestment proceeds ~₹920 crore cited.

Devanahalli AeroLand Complex (DAL) commissioned; Devanahalli Atmanirbhar Complex (DAC) construction ongoing on 20 acres; Missile Atmanirbhar Complex in Hyderabad groundbreaking early July, construction begun; Center for Advanced Manufacturing (240,000 sq ft, 20 acres) being planned.
PP&E rose ₹40 crore in one quarter for Power 930 ramp-up. CapEx to be matched to inflows, with a short-term bridge facility; actual drawdown not more than ₹100-150 crore.
demand_pricing: Defence assured forecast visibility rose to ₹4,557 crore after ~₹332 crore of new wins; management says it converts over ~3 years to FY30. Total pipeline cited at ~₹24,000 crore.

Wins include BrahMos and anti-tank missile onboard electronics (development-cum-production), helicopter ERP, Uttam radar antenna beam control, and a 30 kW laser directed energy weapon technology transfer.
LUH Maritime order visibility of ₹150-170 crore this year, stated as backed by confirmed orders.
MBDA test bench programme: about 5 test benches per year for 3 years; launcher maintenance expanding with a Rafale-linked order.
Aerospace: non-binding offer signed for an AS9100 precision manufacturer; FY27 revenue ~₹180 crore and EBITDA ~₹39 crore (22% margin) annualized, due diligence to complete in Q2.
BrahMos NG seeker: prototype in advanced stage; seeker business expected from next financial year (FY28).

500940|2026-06.headline: Finolex Q1 FY27: volume fell 27% YoY to ~68,000 MT, while EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin widened to 12%.
500940|2026-06.overview: Volumes fell 27% YoY to about 68,000 MT as PVC price volatility triggered channel destocking, with April the weakest month and May and June growing per management. Revenue fell 27% to INR884 crore from INR1,043 crore, but EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin improved from 9% to 12%, which management attributed mainly to top-line realization rather than cost. PAT was about INR107 crore and cash stood at INR2,636 crore. Management said July was the best month of the four, with a minimum price floor from the MIP and customs duty withdrawal, but declined to give full-year volume or margin guidance beyond reiterating the sub-15% margin view.

segments.name: Agri pipes
segments.commentary: Agri was 69% of volume; agri volume fell 27% YoY. Fittings were 5% of agri and 11% of total volume.

segments.name: Non-agri / plumbing
segments.commentary: Non-agri was about 25% of volume (fittings 25% within non-agri per management); volume fell ~24% YoY, versus ~18-20% industry peers per management.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC was about 7% of volume in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 volume guidance; management said it is too early and will revisit after Q2 trends.
Margin: reiterated the Q4 FY26 view of sub-15% EBITDA margin, with no revision.
Management expects a somewhat better Q2 on realizations after the MIP-driven price floor; said it was hopeful H1 volume could be flattish YoY, with a plus possible if July's pace holds.

Capex: capital outlay of INR125-200 crore per year for expansion and debottlenecking, unchanged. Installed capacity 520 (unit as stated), FY26 volume 333, headroom for 10-12% growth over roughly the next 1-1.5 years.
Other income of ~INR75 crore in the quarter is mark-to-market and driven by bond yields, so it is not guaranteed to recur at that level.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity stated as 520 (units not specified); FY26 volume 333. Management says there is headroom to grow 10-12% over the next 1-1.5 years.
Growth is coming through debottlenecking, replacing lower-capacity extruders with higher-capacity ones, rather than large greenfield or brownfield projects.
Capex outlay remains INR125-200 crore, unchanged.

Ratnagiri PVC: EDC-based line running without interruption. VCM-based line does not run during the June-September monsoon months because the Ratnagiri jetty is fair-weather only. VCM availability is constrained by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints.
CPVC extrusion capacity is considered sufficient for near-term CPVC growth, according to management.
demand_pricing: Average PVC price in Q1 was about USD875/MT versus USD707/MT a year earlier (ICIS), carried over from elevated Q4 FY26 levels. A sharp intra-quarter correction in April triggered channel destocking.
Management cited INR96 to INR92 to INR82/kg as the PVC price path through April. Analyst cited a INR12-13/kg hike in the last 15-20 days after the MIP and duty changes.
Customs duty exemption on PVC resin was withdrawn in mid-July, and a minimum import price (MIP) was imposed. Management said these should support price stability and channel inventory.
Pass-through: management said almost all of the recent price increase (barring INR1-2) has been passed to customers.
Demand: July was the best month of the four, with a strong pickup; August to date was described as moving in the right direction.
Channel inventory is near normal, with some room left. A lot of stocking occurred in July in anticipation of price increases. Quantification in days was not given.
PVC-EDC spread was ~USD501/MT in Q1 FY27 versus ~USD522 a year earlier, and ~USD490 currently. PVC-VCM spread was INR122/kg in Q1 FY27 versus INR163 a year earlier.
Pricing: management said Finolex prices ~10-12% above Supreme-type peers in the market (ballpark only).
Market share: management said FY26 share of the top 5-6 reporting companies was about 22%, and it sees no change in Q1. An analyst cited FY23 share of about 27%.
JJM 2.0: management said the outlay is about INR67,000 crore, not higher than JJM 1.0. All sales go through channel partners, so there is no direct correlation to volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realization not rise QoQ when peers reported 7-9% jumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realization per kg was up ~15% vs the same quarter last year and was in line with peers. It said Q4 FY26 was an aberration with a sharp price rise, and that falling PVC prices in April drove the QoQ result. Discounts and incentives also affect net realization.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the volume decline was agri vs non-agri, and what were the monthly trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri fell 27% and non-agri fell ~24% YoY. April was the weakest month, May grew and June was normal. Management did not give monthly figures and said it would reach out separately.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion despite falling volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin was largely top-line driven, with costs range-bound. It cited backward integration and the timing of raw material procurement as a cushion. It did not quantify inventory gains or losses.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year volume decline? Can H1 be flat YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide full-year volume. It said July was a good month and that flattish H1 YoY is possible, with a plus if July's pace holds, while August and September are still to be seen.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy the INR2,636 crore cash into CPVC capacity and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CPVC extrusion capacity is sufficient and CPVC is about 7-8% of the PVC pipe market, which Finolex matches. It said the Board decides on cash deployment or returns and will announce when a decision is made.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin guidance sub-15% when Q1 delivered 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is holding the sub-15% guidance from Q4 because of volatility in Q1 and wants another quarter of data before revising it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM supply situation and the PVC plant utilization outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VCM availability is limited by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints. The VCM line does not run during monsoon months (about June to September) because of the fair-weather jetty. Management said efforts to secure supply are ongoing and H2 is uncertain.

financial_highlights.change: -15% YoY (as stated, decline moderated to ~15%; INR1,043 crore prior year)

financial_highlights.value: Up ~1% QoQ per analyst calculation; management cited +15% in its own comparison
financial_highlights.change: Management did not reconcile the two figures

544344|2026-06.headline: SPR Auto Technologies Q1 FY27: consolidated total income up 51% YoY and EBITDA up 27% YoY, with PAT up 9% after higher finance costs.
544344|2026-06.overview: Management reported 51% YoY growth in consolidated total income and 27% YoY growth in consolidated EBITDA for Q1 FY27. Consolidated PBT rose 7% and PAT rose 9% YoY, with higher finance costs from the debt used to fund the automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin) acquisition. Management attributed a near-term margin squeeze to commodity cost pass-through lagging by about a quarter, which it said it expects to recover next quarter. Standalone legacy growth of about 12% trailed the industry, which management attributed to mix shifts and weak exports.

financial_highlights.value: INR 300 million (per investor presentation, as cited by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Powertrain-agnostic businesses share of consolidated total income

segments.name: Legacy engine components (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said manufacturing growth in the industry was about 12-14% against company growth of over 16%, though the analyst cited ~12% standalone growth. Two-wheelers grew ~19-20%, passenger cars ~11%, CV and tractor ~7-8%, and other segments ~4-5% (per management). Exports were hit by the West Asia situation.

segments.name: Automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin)
segments.commentary: Margins improved from 7-8% to early-to-mid teens after synergies and fixed-cost cuts. Management said the segment won several new customer programs post-acquisition. Ex-Antolin consolidated topline growth was said to be over 16%.

segments.name: Electric motors and controllers (EMFI)
segments.commentary: Management said the business doubled turnover in FY26 after Coimbatore capacity commissioned by end-December 2025, and expects full-year benefit in FY27. Management declined to disclose capacity or market share.

segments.name: High precision injection molded components / plastics (Takahata, TGPEL)
