segments.commentary: Management said the injection-molded business saw very significant growth in Q1 and that plastics revenue grew about 2x last year. Takahata phase-four expansion has started, with new business revenue expected from early next year; TGPEL second Noida plant is filling up.

segments.name: Non-auto components
segments.commentary: Management said non-auto (compressors, marine, defense, railways, snowmobiles, lawn mowers, medical, music keyboards) has grown 15-20% a year over four years, but did not disclose its share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Management expects volume momentum after GST 2.0 to continue through FY27 across two-wheeler, passenger car, CV and tractor segments.
Commodity cost increases are passed to customers with a one-quarter lag; management hopes the gap normalises in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).
Finance costs are expected to be temporary and normalise as acquisition-related debt is repaid.
Management said export markets (US, Europe, Middle East, Turkey, Egypt) have not yet recovered and expects normalisation to take more time.
Management expects to recover the lost margin from commodity inflation and said it will not lose margin.
Management said it targets consolidated EBITDA margins in the high teens and aims for Antolin margins closer to mid-teens.
capex_capacity: Acquired the piston manufacturing plant and machinery from Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Ltd; completed in Q1 FY27, adding piston capacity.
Capacity expansion underway across plastics, EV motors and controllers, interiors and legacy pistons; management did not disclose capacity figures.
Takahata phase-four expansion started, building a new plant adjacent to the existing facility on five acres of additional land; new business revenue expected from early next year.
TGPEL: second Noida plant has full capacity available and is filling up.
EMFI: Coimbatore capacity commissioned around end-December 2025.
Legacy CAFE-compliant piston and ring coating technologies already available at Ghaziabad and Pathredi plants; management said products are under customer testing and validation.
Management said all the tested flex-fuel products up to E85 are ready, requiring different plating with capacity already available.
demand_pricing: Management said realisation may rise to some extent with newer CAFE-compliant technologies, which cost more; management said it is leading the competition on these.
Mix shift toward smaller vehicles post GST 2.0 lowered value realisation per piece, per management.
Management said commodity prices have started to fall from unprecedented levels, and it expects normalisation within the next quarter.
Standalone gross margin was around 56-57% in the past two quarters versus 59-61% historically; management attributed this to product mix and commodity impact.
Management said it has back-to-back pass-through arrangements with customers across legacy, plastics, motors and interiors, with a one-quarter lag.
Management said the Q1 wage hike, effective 1 April, had a small impact on employee cost percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone legacy growth (~12%) trail the industry growth of ~20% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing growth was 12-14% versus company growth over 16%, and that exports were hit by the war situation, so manufacturing shifted toward OE customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin hold while EBITDA margin fell ~200 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of product, market, and volume effects, plus aftermarket lag in Q1 and the commodity pass-through lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is any price increase needed from OEMs to recover the commodity impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said back-to-back contracts exist with a one-quarter lag, so the increase for the prior quarter's average commodity price is recovered the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and what are the leverage thresholds?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated net debt was about INR 550 crore as of June; net debt to equity is 0.2x, and management said it will not cross 1x.

qa_highlights.question: How is the fundraise going to be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funds are fungible and will be split across acquisitions, debt repayment and ongoing investments; no split was given. It said the fundraise is progressing as per target.

risks_watch: Commodity-cost pass-through lag: management expects normalisation in Q2 FY27, so the Q2 margin is a key check.
Export weakness in the US, Europe and Middle East, with no clear recovery timeline per management.
Finance cost burden from acquisition debt, which management said will normalise over time; watch the repayment schedule.
Standalone legacy growth trailing industry manufacturing growth in Q1.
Undisclosed segment breakup: management declined to give plastics, Antolin and EMFI revenue and EBITDA for the quarter.
544344|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, integration and margin recovery, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give segment splits, EMFI capacity, market share, non-auto revenue share and the wage-cost impact. On exports, it was candid that recovery is slow.

532805|2026-06.headline: Redington Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR34,966 crores and PAT 77% to INR486 crores, helped by PC price-led stock-and-sell.
532805|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR34,966 crores (+34% YoY), EBITDA INR751 crores (+67%) and PAT INR486 crores (+77%), with profit growth outpacing revenue. Excluding Arena, revenue grew 41% to INR33,794 crores and profit was INR517 crores, which management called the best ever. India grew 63% on top line and was the strongest geography, while Middle East & Africa grew 15% despite the West Asia crisis, with UAE and Saudi softening. Management attributed a large part of ESG growth to component-shortage-driven price increases and channel stocking, and flagged that large data-center deals will dilute margin percentage. Arena continued to lose money (INR64 crores total, INR31 crores Redington share).

financial_highlights.value: INR64 crores total; INR31 crores Redington share

financial_highlights.change: vs INR31 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Top line grew 63% and PAT 60%; Mobility, Endpoint, Technology and Software Solutions all grew strong double digits. Professional services grew triple digits.

segments.name: Middle East & Africa
segments.commentary: Region grew 15% YoY; GCC and Levant grew 95% and Africa 39%, while UAE declined about 3% and Saudi declined about 7%.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Grew 21% YoY, 35% of top line; growth tied to premium segment and direct retail in India, but supply constrained demand.

segments.name: Endpoint Solutions (ESG)
segments.commentary: Grew 35% YoY, 29% of top line; growth led by component-shortage price increases, with unit growth flat to single digit. AI PCs were 36% of India commercial revenue.

segments.name: Technology Solutions (TSG)
segments.commentary: Grew 50% YoY, 17% of top line; about INR1,000 crores of large deals in the quarter, roughly INR700 crores from India data-center business.

segments.name: Software Solutions (SSG)
segments.commentary: Grew 52% YoY (about 53% cited), 17% of top line vs 15% a year ago; cloud grew 67%, SISA 55%, Rest of World 80%. Services almost doubled and were about 2.5% of revenue.

segments.name: Arena (Turkey)
segments.commentary: Loss of INR64 crores; debt down to $90 million from $120-130 million; interest including factoring INR37 crores vs INR69 crores a year ago. Management expects losses to continue this year.

guidance_outlook: Q2 expected to be a strong quarter, driven by mobility NPI launches, though this depends on the NPI SKU range.
Q3 expected to see good pickup into the festive season; management declined to forecast beyond that.
Management sees at least 2-3 months of channel inventory and expects component shortages to persist for multiple quarters.
Data-center funnel is multiple times the INR1,000 crore Q1 large-deal revenue for the next few quarters; AI hardware not expected to taper for 4-6 quarters.
Large deals will dilute gross and EBITDA margin percentage, but ROCE will not be compromised; large deal profitability will not match normal profitability.
Finance cost run-rate: management said Q1 levels can be taken as steady-state quarterly numbers.
Arena: management expects losses to continue in the current year and is evaluating structural options.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity-expansion figures were discussed on the call.
Mobility growth was constrained by product supply and capacity, per management.
Data-center deal backlog is described as multiple times the quarter's large-deal revenue.
demand_pricing: PC prices have risen an estimated 25-50% over the last 2-3 quarters (some SKUs about 50%); PC unit volume grew flat to single digit.
Channel is stocking up; management estimates about 2-3 months of inventory in the channel, and says inventory build spans distributors and Tier 2 partners.
Apple raised prices last; most PC OEMs and Android vendors have also raised prices. Management says little room for further price rises remains.
UAE and Saudi: government and corporate projects being postponed; supply delays of about 30 days; freight and warehousing costs up, about $3 million extra in the quarter.
Arena: hypercompetitive Turkey market with gross margin compression; revenue roughly halved.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 performance was driven by pre-buying ahead of chip price hikes, and what is channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stock-and-sell effect is largely in ESG PCs; channel holds about 2-3 months of inventory, and the build is across distributors and Tier 2 partners.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on large deals and India mobility growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR700 crores of the INR1,000 crore large deals came from India data centers; funnel is multiple times that. Premium smartphone share gains helped Mobility, but management is unsure if demand holds after price rises.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East demand in UAE and Saudi, and cost pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: UAE was down about 3-4% and Saudi slightly more; some freight and warehousing cost passed on, while about $3 million of extra cost sat in opex.

qa_highlights.question: Why Arena losses persist and what is the end goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue halved, margins compressed and opex inflated by 35-40%; management says structural options are being evaluated and losses may continue this year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days rose industry-wide, but better payable days, especially in Middle East from additional vendor credit, offset it; spikes occurred within the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs rise 74% QoQ, and what was the INR147 crore tax refund?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher revenue and inventory days raised interest, and market rates firmed though central bank rates were unchanged. The refund related to contested past-year demands that the company won.

risks_watch: Channel inventory build and PC price-led demand: management expects consumer demand to weaken as prices rise; watch unit volumes versus value.
Middle East: UAE and Saudi softening, delayed government and corporate projects, about 30-day supply delays, and receivable provisioning (cautious provisioning in Saudi).
Arena: continued losses, debt reduction, and possible structural change.
Finance cost rising with inventory days and firming market interest rates.
Margin dilution from large data-center deals; Q2 and Q3 seasonality is uncertain given higher ASPs.
532805|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on India, TSG and SSG growth and on working capital, but cautious on consumer PC/smartphone demand, Middle East softening and Arena, where management repeatedly said the problem is not easy to solve.

513517|2026-06.headline: Steelcast Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% to INR124.82 crores and PAT 19.26% to INR23.71 crores; management guides 25-30% FY27 volume growth.
513517|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR124.82 crores, up 17% YoY, with EBITDA of INR35.24 crores (28.23% margin vs 28.14%) and PAT of INR23.71 crores (19% margin vs 18.64%). Management said input-cost increases will be passed through via sales price variation formulas, with the bulk of the price correction effective 1 July. Capacity utilisation was 66% in April-June, and a greenfield foundry of 8,500 tonnes (about INR120 crores over two years) was approved, targeted for commissioning by 31 March FY28. The order book stood at INR140 crores, roughly 3-4 months of forward booking.

financial_highlights.change: Export share 60% by tonnage (management also cited 62% by value)
Not quantified vs last year; management said it is higher

segments.name: Sector mix (sales, current year guidance)
segments.commentary: Mining about 27%, earthmoving about 43%, construction about 15%, defense about 1%, with the remainder across other sectors. Ten years ago mining was about 84% of sales, earthmoving near zero and construction 15-16%.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports have historically run at 45-50% of sales; FY27 guided at about 49-50% exports, and the next year at 47% exports and 53% domestic. Sales now go to about 16 countries; the US and Germany together are about 70% of exports.

segments.name: Ground engaging tools (GET)
segments.commentary: Under 1% of revenue today, with FY26 at about 1%; guided to about 3.5% of sales in FY27 and 4.5-5% by FY29 as new parts move into serial supply.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guided at about 25% over FY26; in Q&A the chairman said 30% volume growth is a distinct possibility, and FY27 volume was implied at about 18,000 tons at 63% utilisation.
Long-term growth target of about 20% CAGR over the coming years.
Sequential quarter-on-quarter top-line improvement expected for several quarters.
EBITDA margin guided to stay in range; in Q&A the chairman said a 150-200 bps rise to 28.5-29% for FY27 is theoretically achievable and is the aim. FY27 margin was about 27%.
Price correction for input costs (raw materials and natural gas) effective 1 July, passed through under the sales price variation formula with a one-quarter lag.
Capacity utilisation target of 63% for FY27 and 90% by FY29 on existing capacity; management said above 90% is not advisable.
New facility revenue potential at peak about INR300 crores; commissioning target 31 March FY28.
Two renewable power projects (2.4 MW wind-solar hybrid and 1.4 MW solar) expected to be commissioned before 31 December 2026.
capex_capacity: Greenfield foundry of 8,500 tonnes approved by the Board, steel castings from 5 kg to 1,000 kg, planned investment about INR120 crores over two years, with an internal commissioning target of 31 March FY28.
Land of about 100,000 sq m provided by the Gujarat government; the new site is 12 km from the existing facility.
Existing capacity is about 29,000 tonnes; FY27 utilisation target is 63% and 90% by FY29.
Plan to start recruiting around mid-year for FY28 readiness; staff currently adequate for FY27 targets.
Considering shifting some manufacturing fuel from natural gas to electricity over 2-3 years; natural gas is about 50-55% more expensive than at end-February prices.
demand_pricing: Pricing is pass-through under a sales price variation formula with customers; the chairman said all major raw material increases will be recovered, but declined to give a percentage range.
Over 100 new parts developed in the last 18-24 months; about 20% of revenue expected from new parts over the next 2-3 years, with 80% from existing parts.
Management said US railroad work has been deprioritised in favour of better-priced industrial markets, and defense is a low priority because pricing is better elsewhere.
Rupee movements are shared with customers, not hedged.
Management says all 9 end-user sectors are seeing demand increases, with automobile growing 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the input-cost increase will be passed to customers, and how much is done so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a minimal correction took effect 1 April; most comes from 1 July. All major raw materials are in the formula, so the chairman said all increases will be passed on, without quantifying a range.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 25% growth mean volume or volume plus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 25%, with price increases on top; the chairman later said 30% volume growth is a distinct possibility.

qa_highlights.question: Will utilisation reach 100% by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Target is 90% by FY29 on existing capacity, and new capacity starts adding volume afterwards.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and what is the new facility's peak revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly scale and operating leverage, with minimal price increase so far. Peak revenue potential from the new facility is about INR300 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering a rights issue or bonus issue, and is it focusing on defense?
qa_highlights.answer: Company has about INR120 crores of reserves and will fund the capex from internal accruals; a rights issue is not needed because it would dilute EPS. A bonus issue will be taken to the next Board meeting. Defense is deprioritised because it is a single-customer, higher-risk business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment split and how has it changed over 10 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining, earthmoving and construction together are about 70% of sales. Mining fell from about 84% to about 54% over 10 years, and earthmoving rose from near zero to about 36%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that exports are understated because of Tier 2 supply to OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: The chairman said 98-99% of sales are direct Tier 1 supply to OEMs, and OEMs may export part of what they buy, so total export share may be a little higher.

risks_watch: Realisation of the 1 July price correction, which management says follows a one-quarter lag and has not been quantified.
Inventory build (WIP) during the ramp-up; management described it as a 1-2 month timing effect, to be watched in Q2.
Natural gas and energy cost volatility, with gas about 50-55% higher than end-February prices.
Concentration: the US and Germany account for about 70% of exports, and mining, earthmoving and construction for about 70% of sales.
Tracking of the 25-30% volume guidance and the INR140 crores order book against actual quarterly top line.
Israel defense component trials, which management expects to hear on in coming months.
Recruitment plan from mid-year for FY28 capacity.

540692|2026-06.headline: Apex Frozen Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 138% YoY to INR22 crores on 15% higher shrimp realisation (INR930/kg), despite 13% lower volumes at 2,624 MT.
540692|2026-06.overview: Revenue was flat at INR257 crores against INR258 crores a year earlier, while EBITDA rose 79% to INR33 crores and margin expanded to 12.7% from 7.1%. Shrimp sales volume fell to 2,624 MT from 3,015 MT, hit by April-May labour shortages, container and equipment shortages, and EU shipment clearance delays that spilled into Q2. Management kept full-year production guidance at around 12,000 MT and said Q2 volume should recover, subject to global transport normalising. Realisation was guided to hold near INR900 per kg in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: flat vs INR258 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: Accounted for 70% of shrimp sales in Q1 FY27 vs 54% a year earlier; sales rose 13% YoY and 121% QoQ. Pricing includes a 10% tariff plus ADD/CVD (about 9%).

segments.name: EU and UK
segments.commentary: Contributed 25% of shrimp sales vs 39% in Q1 FY26, hit by war-led transport disruption and origin-side testing and certification requirements; management said EU volumes spilled into Q2.

segments.name: Ready-to-Eat (RTE)
segments.commentary: 16% of Q1 volume vs 15% last year; management targets at least 18-20% of volume in FY27, with RTE margin about USD 0.50/kg above RTC at minimum.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 production guided at around 12,000 MT, reiterated from the start of the year; management said the earlier 14,000 MT figure was not a company guidance.
Q2 volume recovery expected, subject to global transport normalisation; order book covers sales until about mid-Q3 FY27.
Realisation in Q2 expected near INR900/kg, similar to Q1.
Margins expected to stay broadly stable, with partial pressure from higher ocean freight (more than doubled since Q4 FY26) and rising farm-gate prices.
Capacity utilisation targeted at 35-40% through FY27; next growth stage of 14,000-15,000 MT considered for FY28-29, not yet firmly committed.
Japan business initiated; Russia expected to start by end-Q2 or Q3 FY27; Australia still at audit stage.
capex_capacity: Volume capacity utilisation 38% in Q1 FY27 vs 39% in Q1 FY26; management targets sustained 35-40% through the year.
RTE capacity utilisation 16%, similar to prior year.
Labour shortage in April-May due to summer heat was resolved toward end-Q1 per management.
Raw material supply tightness expected to ease as new crop comes in.
No capex plans were announced in the call.
demand_pricing: Realisation of INR930/kg is up about INR80-90/kg YoY, helped by higher USD unit values, a weaker rupee and a higher RTE mix.
US buyers placed more orders after tariff uncertainty eased; the 10% tariff has been stable since the start of the year.
Farm-gate prices rose about 6-7% over the 3-4 weeks before the call; Q1 prices were described as stable.
Management said realisations above a certain level would hurt consumption and volumes, as in FY22-23.
UK-India FTA effective 15 July 2026, but non-tariff barriers such as 50% testing of Indian shipments remain; EU FTA expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 due to war-led disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How are fish meal and feed price increases affecting farmers and the company, and are they temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said feed manufacturing is not part of the business. Farm-gate prices rising gave farmers comfort; margins should stay stable, with freight and farm-gate price increases as partial offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume below the 12,500-14,000 MT run-rate, and what growth is expected for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is about 12,000 MT. Q1 was hit by labour shortage and container shortages, and EU shipments slipped into Q2, which made US volumes look high. The order book is firm to mid-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RTE contribution and its margin premium over RTC?
qa_highlights.answer: RTE was 16% of Q1 volume and is expected to reach at least 18-20% in FY27. The margin premium is at least USD 0.50/kg over RTC, with some products higher.

qa_highlights.question: Will US tariff refunds be received?
qa_highlights.answer: No refunds have been received yet. Timing and outcome are unclear because of ongoing US legal proceedings.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 realisation a new high versus history, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Similar levels were seen in FY22 during COVID phase 2, but those were driven by panic buying and hurt volumes. The company aims for a sustainable level through a richer value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US CVD and ADD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: ADD is at 3.4%, up from 1.35%, with a final determination around September 2026. CVD could fall by about 5.77% in December 2026 if duty drawback and RoDTEP are accepted as non-subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: What new adjacent products are being commercialised?
qa_highlights.answer: Proprietary customer-developed RTE and RTC products are already being shipped, estimated at 3-4% of sales (about 300-400 MT on 12,000 MT), rising to about 500 MT annually.

risks_watch: Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 because of war-led disruption; freight is the main risk to margin stability.
EU and UK volumes dropped to 25% of sales; watch whether shipments normalise in Q2 and whether testing or certification delays persist.
Full-year volume of about 12,000 MT requires roughly 9,000+ MT in the remaining three quarters versus 2,624 MT in Q1 FY27.
Capacity utilisation of 38% is well below the 14,000-15,000 MT next-stage ambition.
Possible US tariff refunds are unclear; the CVD review in December 2026 and the ADD determination in September 2026 could change pricing.
Farm-gate price increases and tight raw material supply could pressure costs.
540692|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on profitability and pricing, but cautious and hedged on volumes, freight and the timing of FTA benefits. Management avoided committing to FY28-29 volume figures and said it was too early to say.

506854|2026-06.headline: TANFAC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.3% YoY to INR187 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.3% on sulphur and power cost spikes; HFC-32 commissioning guided for end-Q3 FY27.
506854|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 6.3% YoY to about INR187 crore, driven by solar grade DHF ramp-up, though it fell about 3% QoQ. Operating EBITDA was INR28.6 crore (15.3% margin) versus INR29 crore a year ago, hit by elevated sulphur prices and higher power and fuel costs linked to West Asia. PAT fell to INR16.8 crore from INR19.4 crore, also weighed by a deferred tax adjustment. The company completed a INR250 crore QIP, is now net debt-free, and has a proposed ~INR100 crore preferential issue and NSE listing application underway.

segments.name: AHF / HF platform
segments.commentary: HF capacity ~30,000 tpa; Q1 HF plant utilisation 73%, AHF segment ~75%, average AHF realisation INR275-280/kg-equivalent as stated; AHF sold monthly or quarterly with no long-term contracts.

segments.name: Sulphuric acid
segments.commentary: Utilisation ~85-88% in Q1 (about 90% by segment); sulphuric acid prices rose from ~INR20 to INR30-35 with management saying spread to sulphur is unchanged.

segments.name: Solar grade DHF
segments.commentary: Both phases commissioned; running at full capacity, 80-85% volume contracted under long-term contracts through FY29 (about 3.5 years); pricing passes through raw material costs.

segments.name: Specialty fluorides
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 50% across 4-5 products in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at at least 30% YoY, driven by HFC-32 launch in Q4 and existing product utilisation ramp-up.
FY28 revenue growth targeted above 60%, driven by HFC-32 ramp-up and inorganic fluorides.
EBITDA margin guided to 16-19% from the next quarter; about 25% for next year once HFC-32 is operational; management also cited ~30% margin on the new project and ~21-22% blended for FY27.
HFC-32 (20,000 tpa) commissioning guided for end-Q3 FY27 / late November; stabilisation December-January, ramp-up from mid-February.
HFC-32 volume assumed at 65-70% in Q4 FY27 and 80-85% in FY28; management said it is confident of 90%+ utilisation in the coming year.
AHF realisation expected stable for next 4-6 months, subject to sulphur prices.

Broad capex plan of INR1,500-1,700 crore over ~4 years; near-term INR300 crore across solar DHF expansion (INR30-40 crore), AHF (~INR120 crore) and electronic grade (~INR150 crore), with +/-10% tolerance.
capex_capacity: HFC-32 (20,000 tpa): ~60% of work complete; remaining 30-35% to finish by November; machines arriving early September, erection 20-25 days; no cost overrun expected; 22% tax rate applies.
Solar grade DHF: management plans to roughly double capacity; decision pending reactor evaluation; work to start after HFC-32 commissioning, about 6 months lead time.
AHF: planned addition of 20,000-30,000 tpa, commissioning expected in FY28 (about 12-15 months lead time).
Electronic grade (semicon) capex ~INR150 crore; technology tie-ups under evaluation, with one MoU-level partner being assessed.
R&D capex INR7-8 crore over last 1.5 years; revenue-nature R&D spend INR5-6 crore.
demand_pricing: Q1 revenue growth split: ~15% pricing and ~6-8% volume, per management.

HFC-32 contracts cover ~65% of 20,000 tpa capacity, 5-7 year terms, ~75% exports; Japanese customer is a firm contract, domestic OEM described as near-contract, and a 5,000 t MoU expected to convert; all take-or-pay per management.
HFC-32 contract price ~$5.5/kg, formula-linked to input costs; management expects prices to soften to $6-7 range in 1-1.5 years versus peer spot prices cited by an analyst at $9-10.
Indian AHF domestic demand estimated at 30,000-35,000 tpa; Chinese AHF imports seen as limited due to export licensing and ISO tank logistics.
Sulphur price moved from ~INR30 to ~INR105 per management; price pass-through lag 30-45 days. Fluorspar sourced from South Africa, Vietnam, Thailand.

qa_highlights.question: Sulphur sourcing and margin range for FY27 with HFC-32 in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sulphur availability is not an issue and cost increases pass through with a 30-45 day lag; EBITDA margin guided 16-19% from next quarter, ~25% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 revenue growth price-led or volume-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 15% pricing and 6-8% volume growth, averaging about 6% overall as stated.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans beyond HFC-32?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term ~INR300 crore: solar DHF INR30-40 crore, AHF ~INR120 crore, electronic grade ~INR150 crore; long-term plan to be decided in 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the HFC-32 contract price ~$5.5 versus peers' spot prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritised speed to market, placed 65% of volume early on formula-based pricing, and expects prices to soften to $6-7; remaining ~30% to be sold spot.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power and fuel costs and employee costs move QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Power costs rose on a one-off basis due to West Asia pricing and captive power plant being down for sulphuric acid maintenance; employee cost fell versus last year's one-off bonuses; expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D/electronic grade strategy and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Evaluating technologies with tie-ups; semicon approval cycle 1-1.5 years; HFOs and high-performance fluoropolymers after 2.5-3 years, with project announcements in FY28 for execution by 2029-30.

financial_highlights.change: +6.3% YoY vs INR176 crore; approx -3% QoQ
vs INR29 crore in Q1 FY26
vs INR19.4 crore in Q1 FY26; deferred tax adjustment impact

financial_highlights.value: INR315 crore of INR395 crore project cost
financial_highlights.change: INR100 crore cash outflow so far

544476|2026-06.headline: Jeena Sikho Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to INR224 crore, with EBITDA of INR92 crore (41% margin) and PAT of INR65 crore (28%).
544476|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR224 crore (up 29% YoY), EBITDA of INR92 crore (up 17% YoY, 41% margin) and PAT of INR65 crore. Government hospital business was cut sharply (INR15 crore to INR5 crore YoY per management), while private Panchakarma and product sales grew. Management attributed part of the cost base to one-off items: about INR4 crore extra advertising, about INR2 crore software implementation and audit fees. Other income of INR14 crore included about INR7 crore one-time gains (warrant valuation and capital gain), per the CFO. Management guided to 30% annual growth and INR3,000 crore turnover within about 3 to 5 years, but gave no quantified FY27 guidance beyond 3,000 to 3,500 operational beds.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY (INR174 crore in Q1 FY26); QoQ growth stated as about 10% on patient/volume basis
Q1 FY27 PAT of INR51 crore was also cited by an analyst and management in the Q&A; treat PAT figure as inconsistent in transcript
Up from INR4 crore in Q4 FY26; about INR7 crore one-time (INR5 crore warrant valuation, INR2.5 crore capital gain)
Panchakarma revenue +13% YoY; private Panchakarma INR78 crore to INR100 crore (about 30% YoY)
Products business grew 47% YoY; INR80 crore in Q1 FY26 per management comparison
Down from INR15 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR15 crore in prior-year Q1 per management

segments.name: Ayurveda healthcare services (Panchakarma, hospitals)
segments.commentary: Panchakarma revenue +13% YoY; IPD patients +33% YoY (about 8,600 to 11,500) and day care volume +31% YoY (day care per-day volume 16,000 to 19,000 per management). Government revenue cut to INR5 crore from INR15 crore as management exited credit-heavy government business.

segments.name: Ayurveda products
segments.commentary: Products grew 47% YoY; medicine sales INR118 crore in Q1, flat vs Q4 FY26. E-commerce orders rose to 2,64,000 from 2,28,000 QoQ; COD patients rose to 18,500 from 14,000.

segments.name: Ultra-luxury wellness (Manali, Jeena Sikho Premium)
segments.commentary: Pre-launch; 108 rooms plus 22 villas, guaranteed 35 rooms under a 3-year lease renewable 3+3+3. Management expects little FY27 contribution, with launch around Sep-Oct 2026 and better season from March; guided year-one EBITDA 35-40%+ and year-two 60% occupancy at ADR INR35,000-37,000.

guidance_outlook: Target of 30% YoY growth annually and INR3,000 crore turnover in about 3 years (maximum 5 years); INR1,000 crore PAT ambition over the longer term.
Operational beds to rise from 2,400 to 3,000-3,500 in FY27; 7,000-10,000 beds targeted in 3-5 years; occupancy target 75-80%.
Plans for 3-4 more luxury wellness centres in India, each guided at INR3-5 crore net profit (management).

Ayushman Bharat/insurance claim inclusion for Ayurveda expected but timing unclear (2-6 months per management); discounted admissions for BPL and Ayushman patients to begin within about 10 days, with 500 beds mentioned.
Entero OTC product listings expected to start across its distributors within about 15 days.
capex_capacity: Operational beds 2,400 as of Q1 FY27, up 100 in the quarter; bed occupancy 59% on 2,400 beds per management.
Panvel hospital currently 49 beds pending OC/fire approvals; to scale to 250 beds, which management says could multiply its revenue 4-5x.
Manali luxury wellness centre: launch around Sep-Oct 2026 after Himachal Pradesh NOC process; 108 rooms and 22 villas, 35 rooms guaranteed under lease.
Management said about INR15 crore revenue from a single Meerut centre.
demand_pricing: Management says patient ecosystem touchpoints rose to 5,34,000 from 4,87,000 QoQ (about 10%); OPD about 1.5 lakh; IPD 10,900 to 11,500 QoQ.
Consultation/COD/OPD-linked patients up 143% YoY and VOPD consultations up 65% YoY per management.
Ticket size fell as discounted admissions were introduced for lower-income patients; management said realisation per patient will be lower on the discount segment.
Government business deliberately shrunk because of receivable risk; management says it will re-engage only once NHA panel payments are reliable (3-6 months).
Advertising expense up about INR4 crore YoY tied to TV integrations (Colors TV shows, Khatron Ke Khiladi), with benefits expected in subsequent quarters; ad budget up 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue flat QoQ and what is the advertising cost run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QoQ patient/volume growth was about 10% and government business was cut to one-third; advertising was up INR4 crore in Q1 with benefits expected in later quarters under a 6-month TV tie-up.

qa_highlights.question: Why do IPD (+33%) and OPD (+22%) volume growth not translate into similar revenue growth (+11-13%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the government-business decline (INR10 crore drop), discounted pricing for lower-income patients, and a lag in OPD-to-Panchakarma conversion; the CFO said incremental ticket size has fallen.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 other income (INR14 crore) is one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR7 crore is one-time (INR5 crore warrant valuation, INR2.5 crore capital gain); recurring other income about INR4-5 crore plus treasury/FD income.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off costs in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly INR4 crore extra advertising, about INR2 crore software implementation instalment, and about INR0.5 crore extra audit fees; management said these expenses will continue.

qa_highlights.question: Manali luxury wellness economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 35 rooms guaranteed under a 3-year lease; year-one occupancy 50% at ADR INR32,000-35,000, year-two 60% at ADR INR35,000-37,000, with 35-40%+ EBITDA in year one. Minimal operating cost since the lessor bears utilities and most staff costs.

qa_highlights.question: Pet Shuddhi price gap versus Pet Saffa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its manufacturing cost is about four times the competitor, citing a multi-shot formulation and liver/spleen/metabolism claims.

544138|2026-06.headline: JG Chemicals posted record Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR315.7 crores (+44.8% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 11.5%, with PAT at INR26.1 crores.
544138|2026-06.overview: Management reported all-time quarterly highs for revenue, EBITDA and PAT in Q1 FY27, with revenue up 10.3% sequentially. Utilisation is in the early 80s (of achievable capacity) and volume growth was in double digits across categories. Management attributed margin gains to operating leverage, higher-priced and specialised orders, cost-reduction initiatives and a small inventory gain that it declined to quantify. The Dahej (Gujarat) greenfield plant is now guided for commissioning around November 2026 (Q3 FY27), later than the earlier first-half target, and guidance was reset to 50-60% utilisation in FY28 and about 14-15% EBITDA margin.

financial_highlights.change: Management said mid-teens for current quarter in a later answer
Rising every quarter/year per management; prior-period figures not given

segments.name: Zinc oxide / rubber and tire (core)
segments.commentary: Tire and rubber remain the largest pillar; company supplies every Indian major tire maker and 9 of the top 10 global tire companies. Tire approvals take about 5 years.

segments.name: Non-rubber (pharma, ceramics, specialty chemicals, agri, cosmetics, electronics)
segments.commentary: Около 18% of revenue this quarter. Ceramics is being seeded for about a year; approval cycle in ceramics estimated at 1-3 months versus about 5 years in tire.

segments.name: Zinc sulphate
segments.commentary: Less than 5-6% of FY26 sales. Southern India is the core market; Western India expansion planned using by-product raw material from Dahej.

segments.name: Recycled rubber (JG TUR) and new products (LabPure zinc oxide, JG-ZRA)
segments.commentary: JG TUR pilot trials well received; commercial launch hoped within about 12 months, capex and revenue not yet disclosed. LabPure and JG-ZRA introduced this quarter as niche, higher-margin grades.

guidance_outlook: Dahej (Gujarat) greenfield Phase 1 of about 15,000-17,000 tpa zinc oxide: commissioning around November 2026 (Q3 FY27); revenue potential INR300-400 crores; EBITDA margin 11-12%; total greenfield capacity about 40,000 tpa.
Dahej utilisation guidance: 50-60% in FY28 (first full year), about 70-80% in FY29; Phase 2 expansion to start around then.
Consolidated EBITDA margin: management now targets about 14-15% (previously 13-14%), with a 14% reference point stated later; current-year margins expected to stay near current level.
Naidupeta brownfield expansion (about 5,000 tpa debottlenecking) expected to commission in Q3 FY27; Naidupeta capex figure to be provided offline.
Management expects higher sales in Q2 FY27 and similar margin profile to continue into the current quarter.
Export share of sales 10-15% today, about 15% expected in FY28-29.
Target payback 3-4 years and ROCE in mid-20s on new capex, per management.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity at West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh facilities close to 70,000 tpa; combined capacity to exceed 115,000 tpa after Dahej phases are on stream.
Dahej greenfield (Gujarat): about INR100 crores investment, civil work advanced, equipment installation underway; commissioning around November 2026.
Naidupeta brownfield: about 5,000 tpa added, expected Q3 FY27. Capex amount not disclosed; to be shared offline.
Q1 FY27 capex and remaining FY27 capex not disclosed on call; management said it would follow up offline.
Naidupeta solar Phase 1 operational; R&D centre at Naidupeta inaugurated.
Proposed UAE subsidiary (BDJ Materials and Metal Trading FZCO) to source raw materials and handle global distribution; not yet incorporated.
demand_pricing: ATMA data cited: Q1 FY27 vehicle volume growth of up to 26.6% for passenger vehicles, 16.5% two-wheelers, 16.5% commercial vehicles and over 11% three-wheelers.
Tire industry capex of about INR25,000 crores announced; about 25% of Indian tire output exported.
Management expects zinc-linked realisations to stay higher ('new normal') as commodity prices have risen; says company is neutral to zinc price levels.

Raw material: zinc dross supply disrupted by geopolitical conflict, but company maintained uninterrupted supply; management said crisis favoured established suppliers and shifted some customers toward JGC.
Around 90% of new sales expected to be direct to customers rather than through distributors.
Dahej customer mix guided at about 60% tire and 40% other segments.

qa_highlights.question: How much of EBITDA came from inventory gains and how much is reversible?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said margin came from operating leverage, higher-priced and specialised orders, and only a small inventory gain; amount not quantified. Margins of 10-12% are structural, with upside from value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Will Dahej commission early or late in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said around November 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will realisations sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said higher realisations are the new normal given higher commodity prices, and he sees no near-term reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY28 Dahej utilisation guidance lowered from 65-70% to 50-60%, and the margin guidance raised from 13-14% to 14-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cut is conservatism because the plant start moved from H1 to Q3 FY27; it still sees close to 60%. The margin rise reflects new products and higher-realisation product launches.

qa_highlights.question: What are the payback and ROCE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Payback of 3-4 years targeted, implying about 20-25% annual returns; ROCE expected in the mid-20s.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth outlook and split between zinc oxide and zinc sulphate?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-teens volume growth in the current quarter. The 15,000-17,000 tpa Dahej Phase 1 is all zinc oxide. Zinc sulphate is less than 5-6% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new products (LabPure, ZRA) carry higher margins and what is their market size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said these are niche, higher-margin products for non-tire customers, slow to ramp; no market size or margin figures given.

544439|2026-06.headline: Crizac Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% YoY to INR2,012 million on adverse university mix; management now guides FY27 flat versus FY26.
544439|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,012 million, down 4% YoY and below the INR3,917 million of Q4 FY26, consistent with Q1 being the seasonal trough. Management attributed the decline to a less favourable university mix (fewer high-fee top-ranked university bonuses and slabs), not lower platform activity, as enrolments rose 15% YoY. EBITDA fell 7.6% YoY to INR600 million, with margin at 29.8% versus 31%, while PAT grew 2.9% to INR471 million. Management moved from earlier growth expectations to a flat FY27 outlook, citing flight disruption and rupee volatility expected to hit Q2, with pent-up demand expected in Q3 and Q4. It also announced a leadership change: Chairman Christopher Nagle stepped down as UK CEO and became Non-Executive Chairman of the Indian holding company, with Eric Wijmenga taking UK and Europe operations.

financial_highlights.change: -4% YoY (constant currency); below Q4 FY26 INR3,917 million
-7.6% YoY from INR649 million; margin 29.8% vs 31% in Q1 FY26; up 585 bps QoQ from 24% in Q4 FY26
vs INR4.0 lakh FY26 and INR3.55 lakh FY24 (analyst's division, not company-stated)

segments.name: UK (largest destination)
segments.commentary: Management says UK share of total student visas granted rose from 3.5% in FY24 to 6% in FY26; UK concentration still around 97% per analyst, with a target to go below 60% within about three years.

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: US share of Indian student visas rose from 9% to 13.9%, though management described the US visa environment as restrictive and its planned expansion as stalled.

segments.name: Acquisitions (acquired businesses)
segments.commentary: Acquired businesses contributed around INR6 crore of revenue in Q1; Innova Consultancy (acquired July 2026) is under INR7 crore in size and adds Mexico source and Netherlands destination.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and performance expected broadly flat versus FY26 ("same line as last year"); earlier informal 15-17% growth view withdrawn.
Q2 FY27 expected to be down, due to flight cancellations (February-June) and rupee volatility affecting April-June intakes.
Recovery expected in Q3 and Q4 from pent-up demand; management said Q3 application flow is healthy.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected in the 25%-27% range, per analyst question and management confirmation.
Value-added services (ForeignAdmits: education financing, visa prep, accommodation, forex loans) expected to add 2-5% to EBITDA and 1-1.5% of revenue over next couple of years.
Consolidated PBT to benefit from UK investments; management expects the effect in Q3.

capex_capacity: Investing in people and infrastructure for technology and AI; management said benefits will build progressively, with upfront cost.
