Recent deals also include Studies Planet (Latin America), Global Tree (India), Medway (New Zealand) and EduMentor (talent acquisition).
demand_pricing: Revenue per student fell in Q1 due to university mix: fewer high-fee top-ranked universities, with missed bonuses and slabs. Management said per-university realisations are unchanged.

Top 3 universities were 41% of Q1 revenue per management's/analyst's figures; management said Q1 is skewed because few universities have April-June intakes, and top 10 universities contribute roughly 60-70% on a full-year basis.
Conversion rate about 10% of unique applicants; TTM blended conversion said to be around 10%.
Unique applicants were about 47,000 in Q1; a student typically applies to 2-2.5 universities.
Platform covers 450+ university partners, 12 destination markets, 85+ source markets; management said it represents more than 95 of 100 UK commercial universities.
Competition: incumbents in other English-speaking markets make expansion slower; management cited US policy changes as blocking planned US expansion.

Visa and currency pressure: UK graduate route cut from 24 to 18 months; US/UK strength in currency raising costs for emerging-market students; demand redirecting to Ireland, Germany and New Zealand per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall QoQ and what is the Q2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency revenue fell about 4% as volume rose 15% but university mix shifted; Q2 expected weaker due to Feb-June flight cancellations and rupee volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be 20-25% or 15-17% as earlier hinted?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management now expects FY27 flat versus FY26, with pent-up demand in Q3 and Q4 offsetting Q1 and Q2 shortfalls.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone PBT above consolidated PBT in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Crizac India standalone recognised some payments as revenue; investments in Crizac UK and subsidiaries should pay off in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a buyback plan given the stock trades around 11x EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has only about 20% public float and SEBI rules do not allow a buyback at this level; the compliance team will look at the suggestion.

qa_highlights.question: Will the UK concentration fall, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the target is to get UK share below 60% within about three years, aided by Innova (Netherlands) and other markets, though policy shifts will slow this.

qa_highlights.question: Will value-added services become material?
qa_highlights.answer: Not initially; they could add 2-5% to EBITDA and 1-1.5% of revenue over the next couple of years, with ForeignAdmits accelerating this.

qa_highlights.question: Is the dividend a one-time payout?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the DRHP commits to a minimum 40% of PAT as dividend for at least three years; FY26 is done, leaving at least two more years.

544485|2026-06.headline: Regaal Q1 FY27 operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr as trading was cut, while value-added margin rose to 39.8% and PAT grew 47% to Rs 13.33 cr.
544485|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a transition quarter: the doubled crushing capacity (825 to 1,650 TPD) was commissioned on 26 May 2026, with operations ramping from early June. Operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr because low-margin trading was deliberately reduced (3.3% of revenue vs 19.5% in Q1 FY26). Value-added revenue grew 30.3% to Rs 80.53 cr and EBITDA rose 26.6% to Rs 30.98 cr, with margin up 540 bps to 15.3%. Capacity utilisation was 71.4%, with management guiding to progressive improvement from Q2 FY27 and a shift to deleveraging after the capex cycle.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Contribution fell to 3.3% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 19.5% in Q1 FY26 as low-margin trading was deliberately cut.

segments.name: Value-added products (liquid glucose, maltodextrin, starches)
segments.commentary: Value-added revenue Rs 80.53 cr (+30.3% YoY) at 39.8% margin. Liquid glucose at about 70% of its capacity; maltodextrin powder still ramping, with 2-3 more months needed to reach target.

segments.name: Maize starch / core crushing
segments.commentary: Crushing of 69,689 MT in Q1, with about 5,500 MT of incremental volume attributed by management to liquid glucose and a small part maltodextrin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crushing expected at about 4 lakh tons (minimum), vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.
Q2 FY27 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons, contingent on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Value-added share of turnover expected at about 20-22% in FY27 (vs about 3% last year); later guided to about 30-35% of turnover on capacity mix.
Management declined to give EBITDA per ton or EBITDA margin guidance, citing maize and product price dependence; said operating leverage and value-add mix should improve margins at constant prices.
Net interest cost (net of subvention) for FY27 expected at about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26.
Total project outlay about Rs 664 crore, of which about Rs 552 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026.
Working capital debt expected to decline in H2; management cited a prior pattern of about 40% reduction by Q4.
Dextrose Anhydrous, Dextrose Monohydrate and Hydrol expected by about Q4 FY27; modified starches (cationic, carboxymethyl, pre-gel, spray) trials to be fully online by September 2026.
No new capex decided; management said focus is on stabilising at 90-95% utilisation and deleveraging before considering next expansion.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity doubled from 825 to 1,650 MT per day, commissioned 26 May 2026; operations started early June; described as largest maize wet milling facility in eastern India.
New liquid glucose facility 180 TPD, maltodextrin powder facility 50 TPD, captive cogeneration expanded from 7.1 MW to 15.8 MW.
Q1 utilisation 71.4%; about 9 shutdown days during April-May integration cost roughly 7,200 MT of output (management estimate).
Planned additions: 50,000 MT storage across two new silos, a 50,000 sq ft maize godown, and a 1.6 MW methane gas-based power plant.
Bihar interest subvention applies to new capex debt; management said the subvention cap was amended to Rs 40 crore but final policy notification was still awaited.
demand_pricing: Management said export share rose to 10.4% and that new markets in South and West India are being developed; no export target given.
Pricing: management said starch margin is a whole-number (per-ton) business rather than percentage-based; a rise in starch prices would not proportionally lift EBITDA per ton.
Maize procurement: about 80% of annual requirement bought in the Rabi season (Apr-Jul), 10-15% from other states; Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg delivered vs market talk of Rs 24.
Liquid glucose sold mainly September to March; big MNC customers now billed directly, and white-labelling customer base has grown.
About 70-80% of new modified starch volumes expected to go to existing paper-mill and food customers.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is the expanded plant running at and when will it reach a comfortable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is rising from the early-June start and expects maximum utilisation within the year; FY27 crushing expected above 4 lakh tons vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 47% PAT jump driven by raw material cost or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to operating leverage and the drop in low-margin trading from about 19% to about 3% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable EBITDA per ton should be expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing maize and product price dependence; it expects per-ton EBITDA to improve with scale and value-add at constant prices (Q1 EBITDA/ton cited as about Rs 4,450 vs Rs 4,742 FY26).

qa_highlights.question: What is the net interest cost for FY27 after Bihar subvention?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26; subvention runs across multiple project loans, with the Rs 40 crore cap still pending final policy.

qa_highlights.question: When will peak debt occur and when will working capital come down?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt is peaking in H1 FY27 because working capital is highest then; debt expected to fall in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What production was lost in Q1 and is the value-added capacity stable?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9 shutdown days (approx. 7,200 MT lost). Liquid glucose at about 70% of capacity; maltodextrin needs 2-3 more months; modified starch trials to be online by September.

qa_highlights.question: Any new capex plans for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management wants to stabilise at 90-95% utilisation and reduce debt before considering the next expansion.

532504|2026-06.headline: Navin Fluorine Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 44% YoY to INR1,044-1,045 crore, with EBITDA up 73% and PAT up 108% to INR243 crore.
532504|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 44% YoY to about INR1,045 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR357 crore (34.2% margin, up 566 bps YoY) and PAT of INR243 crore. All three verticals (HPP, specialty chemicals, CDMO) grew strongly, and the company became net debt free during the quarter. Management announced a new INR90 crore advanced materials adoption capex and a Phase 2 CDMO cGMP capex of INR125 crore. Management guided to a 32-33% EBITDA margin range going forward (plus/minus 1%), while flagging gross margin pressure from higher raw material costs.

segments.name: HPP (HFCs/fluorochemicals)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR540 crore, up 33% YoY on healthy volume growth and improved realisations; management describes HFC pricing as constructive given demand-supply dynamics.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (agchem)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR325 crore, up 48% YoY. Management plans campaign orders for 4-5 agchem molecules this year; LatAm agchem pricing pressure persists, and EBITDA is not expected to return to the old ~30% level.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR180 crore, up 82% YoY. Pipeline of 30-40 molecules, about 10 late stage; 3-4 molecules expected to get FDA readouts in the next 8-12 months. Management targets about $100 million for FY27.

segments.name: Advanced materials (incubating within HPP)
segments.commentary: Not separately reported. Chemours liquid cooling project targeted for completion by end Q2 FY27; Chemours reportedly sold about $1 million of two-phase cooling liquid in the quarter (per analyst). DRDO TDF partnership announced.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected in the 32-33% range (plus/minus 1%) on a normalised basis over the next one to two years, supported by HFC, debottlenecking and Chemours capacity.
CDMO FY27 target of about $100 million reiterated; FY29 asset turn of 3x on INR288 crore cGMP4 capex stated as the near-term view.
Gross margin dipped about 100 bps QoQ from Q4 FY26 on raw material costs; management said price pass-through will lag.
Advanced materials adoption capex (INR90 crore) to be done in two phases, first phase around mid-Q4 FY27 for commercial-scale qualification; not included in any return projections.
Growth visibility beyond FY28 depends on the current capex cycle (cGMP Phase 1, adoption capacity, Chemours).
capex_capacity: New advanced materials adoption capex of INR90 crore, internally funded, to be set up at Surat; creates two core platforms and augments analytical equipment.
CDMO cGMP4 Phase 2 capex of INR125 crore (part of INR288 crore approved Feb 2024), operationalisation expected Q4 FY27; Phase 1 operational in Q3 FY26. Dedicated to European CDMO partner.

HFC capacity addition of up to 15,000 MT of R32 on track for Q3 FY27; company currently has about 9,000-10,000 MT and total would be about 25,000 MT. Revenue band of INR600-825 crore cited from original capex approval.
MPP debottlenecking at Dahej on track for completion by Q3 FY27; management cited 2x asset turn.
AHF capacity of 60,000 MT between Surat and Dahej seen as adequate for the next 4-5 years; AHF commissioned in the subsidiary NFASL.
Renewable project of INR15.73 crore (14.9 MW hybrid) expected to supply more than 60% of energy needs once operational.
demand_pricing: R32: management expects a 35-45% contracted share of capacity over five years; a couple of contracts signed and more at a late stage.
R32 long-term demand said to double over a decade while quota-driven supply shrinks by half; Indian oversupply expected for about five years with exports to global market.
Specialty chemicals: volume recovering, but pricing pressure persists in LatAm; 13-14 new molecules launched last year and 5 new molecules being participated in, of which 3 are patented.
HFO supply to Honeywell: asset commercialised July 2022; original seven-year term with a three-year extension at Honeywell's option, so runway beyond FY29.
Management stated that raw material cost inflation is rising amid global war tensions and supply chain risk.

qa_highlights.question: Advanced materials: end-use applications, and growth beyond FY28 given current capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is to make advanced materials a material business unit by end of decade, modelled on today's CDMO. Focus on data centers, electronics, semiconductors, defence; the adoption capex is phased, with first phase complete around mid-Q4 FY27 to start commercial-scale qualification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR90 crore adoption capex a pilot or commercial scale, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said five products are already lab-approved and this capex takes them to commercial-scale qualification; not a pilot. No asset turn is assumed in numbers for the INR90 crore.

qa_highlights.question: R32 pricing and India capacity additions versus quota start in Jan 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give pricing; said it will stay the lowest-cost R32 producer through its integrated HF chain and renewable power. Expects India oversupply for about five years and exports.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary (NFASL) margin fall about 12 pp QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Campaign mix differs quarter to quarter, and AHF transfers from Dahej to Surat are at arm's-length, so value shows up at Navin Fluorine (NFIL) level; group margin remains solid.

qa_highlights.question: CDMO: is the new capacity dedicated, and is the MSA for an extra molecule with the same customer?
qa_highlights.answer: New capacity dedicated to European CDMO partner; an MSA for an extra molecule in the same supply chain takes Navin to API minus 1. Also working on an early-phase molecule with the same customer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $100 million CDMO target for FY27 still on track, and is INR900 crore cGMP capex math right?
qa_highlights.answer: $100 million target reiterated as on track. Management confirmed the 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29, and that Phase 1 and Phase 2 combined are about INR900 crore is not exactly right; the INR288 crore figure is the approved base (3x = about INR900 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.question: HFC contracts, AHF utilisation, and the reason for the margin mix change YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: A couple of R32 contracts signed, with more near conclusion; balanced approach kept. Margin mix explained by HF price highs in Q1 FY26 and rising RM costs now; gross margin down about 100 bps QoQ, offset by fixed-cost productivity.

544523|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 gross sales rose 5.7% to INR 641.2 crore while PAT jumped 51.7% to INR 15.7 crore on margin recovery.
544523|2026-06.overview: Gross sales were INR 641.2 crore (up 5.7% YoY) and gross margin widened to 8.1% of gross sales from 6.8%, lifting gross margin INR 52 crore (up 26.5%). Operating EBITDA was INR 20.2 crore (up 27.7%) and PAT INR 15.7 crore (up 51.7%), helped by lower finance costs. Cybersecurity grew 8% and DCI grew about 180%, while ILM fell about 60% as customer budgets shifted toward GPU and data-centre spend. Management reiterated 20% growth in gross sales and PAT for FY27 and said H2 is seasonally stronger. The CEO is stepping down, with the Chairman/MD and Executive Director jointly overseeing the role.

segments.name: Cybersecurity
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 44% of gross sales; grew 8% YoY. Management expects it to be about 45-50% of sales on an annualised basis.

segments.name: DCI (Data Centre Infrastructure)
segments.commentary: Grew about 180% YoY (management cited 186% in Q&A) and is the main growth driver; management expects DCI at 18-20% of FY27 revenue.

segments.name: ILM (application lifecycle management)
segments.commentary: Declined about 60% YoY as budgets moved to GPU and data-centre spend; management says it should normalise from Q3 on an annuity basis.

segments.name: Cloud
segments.commentary: Grew around 47% YoY along with ALM, per management (the transcript pairs the two; ILM is later described as falling).

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance of about 20% growth in both gross sales and PAT, with PAT growing faster than top line per CFO.
Management expects H2 to be seasonally stronger, with large deals concentrated in Q3 and Q4.
Q2 faces a hit from the annual appraisal cycle starting 1 July.
DCI expected at 18-20% of total revenue for the full year.
Annuity share expected to hold around 45-46%.
capex_capacity: No incremental capex planned for FY27 versus prior years; Centre of Excellence investment is in line with past years.
Management says supply-chain delays are about 1.5 months for its OEMs, far shorter than some peers' 7-8 months.
Geographic expansion started revenue in Vietnam, the Philippines and the Middle East; numbers still small.
Added about INR 300 crore to the pipeline in the last quarter; the company has 100+ OEM tie-ups and about 67 OEMs in its COE stack.
demand_pricing: Management says customers have prioritised budgets toward GPU and data-centre spend, which shifted demand away from ILM.
Top 15 OEMs contributed about 74% of gross sales; growth seen in more than 12 of them.
Win rate on the pipeline held at 30-35%; the INR 6,150 crore figure is a funnel, not an order book.
Hardware prices rose in parts of the portfolio; management says customers pushed back for discounts and volumes did not fall YoY.
Management guides to about 9-10% annual margins, dependent on value addition rather than vertical.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ILM fall about 60% YoY and is cybersecurity slowing versus peers growing 25-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed ILM's fall to budgets reallocated to GPU and data-centre spend and expects ILM to return from Q3. It said cybersecurity is growing and is expected to be 45-50% of sales annualised.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q1 gross sales soft and why has gross profit growth lagged guidance for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY26 base had a large GSTN deal of about INR 150 crore billed in Q2 and that large deals cluster in H2. It said the Q1 FY26 margin was depressed by rupee depreciation and low-margin deals, so a 10% gross profit growth in FY26 is not the steady-state rate.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 46% annuity share mean net new sales are weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annuity was 43.1% in Q1 FY26 and that the roughly 3-point rise came from upsell and price increases at existing customers, not a hit to net new business.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company benefit from data-centre build-outs such as Reliance-Meta?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishna Raj Sharma said public data centres mostly contract directly with OEMs, so the larger opportunity is private/captive data centres. Sunil Pillai said the TAM will be sized once capacity is online.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CEO be replaced and is inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CEO is leaving for personal reasons and that the Chairman/MD and Executive Director will jointly oversee the role, with new CBO, CRO and CTO appointed. Inorganic growth is being explored, with no material progress announced.

qa_highlights.question: Are OEM acquisitions by Palo Alto, Cisco or IBM a risk to accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Pillai said consolidation has been ongoing for two to three years and that the company has not seen revenue loss from it, and may gain access to acquired products.

risks_watch: ILM decline (about 60% YoY) and whether it normalises from Q3 as management says.
Cybersecurity growth of 8% versus peers reportedly at 25-30%, and whether the 45-50% share target is met.
Gross profit growth (10% in FY26) versus the 20% guidance; the FY26 base is lumpy around large deals.
Q2 margin pressure from the appraisal cycle starting July 1.
CEO transition and leadership changes; three senior executives left recently.
Pipeline conversion (30-35%) and whether the INR 6,150 crore funnel converts to the 20% growth target.
Consolidation among OEMs (Palo Alto, Cisco, IBM acquisitions) and account retention.
Hardware price increases and discount pressure on margins.
544523|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the full-year 20% growth target and annuity stability, but evasive on ILM weakness, the CEO exit, and the INR 6,150 crore pipeline (described as a funnel, not an order book). Management repeatedly deferred quarterly questions to annual and H2 trends.
key_quotes: Though it was referred to as as an order book, it is just a pipeline, it's a funnel.
We believe that our focus on digital and hybrid multi-cloud offerings and expanding our partner ecosystem positions us well for this scale in the coming years.

532834|2026-06.headline: Camlin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR5,199 million, but EBITDA margin collapsed to about 4% from 45% last quarter on raw material costs and vanillin under-utilisation.
532834|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR5,199 million, up about 28% YoY and about INR1,000 million QoQ, but margins fell sharply on raw material, freight and logistics costs tied to the West Asia conflict. The company reorganised reporting into Specialty Ingredients, Aroma and Performance Chemicals, with Aroma and Performance Chemicals both EBITDA-negative or near zero in the quarter. Ethyl vanillin ramp-up ran at low utilisation, and FY27 vanillin volume guidance was cut to about 3,000 tons from 3,600-4,000 tons. Management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 10-12% while keeping revenue guidance, and debt was flat at about INR640 crore gross.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients (blends and straights)
segments.commentary: Revenue above INR4,000 million with blends above INR3,000 million; EBITDA margin 6.35%. Management says about 4-5% of gross margin was lost to raw material costs and Brazil air-freight, with Brazil's shortfall of about INR8 crore expected to correct in Q2.

segments.name: Aroma (vanillin)
segments.commentary: Sold about 560 tons (350 t ethyl, 200 t methyl from channel stock) against 6,000-ton capacity; produced ~400 tons. Quarterly EBITDA negative at INR4-4.5 crore on fixed cost absorption; management expects positive EBITDA in Q2.

segments.name: Performance Chemicals
segments.commentary: Gross segment revenue about INR175 crore, of which ~INR130 crore is internal transfer, leaving ~INR40 crore external sales. EBITDA margin 2.5% with diphenol plant shut; management expects positive EBITDA from Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: INR2,200-2,300 crore, versus earlier INR2,000-2,400 crore; management says top line is secure.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 10-12% (10-11% per CFO/MD), implying about INR220-230 crore EBITDA, versus earlier INR250-280 crore.
Analyst read-back: average run rate of about INR70 crore EBITDA per quarter for remaining quarters; management did not dispute this.
Q3 FY27 expected to return to double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin; H2 margin of 13-15% floated by an analyst, not disputed.
FY28 EBITDA margin in the range of 12-14%.
Vanillin FY27 volume about 3,000 tons (earlier 3,600-4,000); 4 campaigns planned, Q2 volume 500-600 tons, Q3 1,000+ tons. Capacity 6,000 tons, achievable 5,000 tons with 3 campaigns.
Blends growth of at least 20% in FY27; budget assumes 25-30%.
capex_capacity: Vanillin capacity 6,000 tons per year; ethyl vanillin campaign of about 750 tons ran through mid-August, with about 350 tons sold and over 300 tons produced; methyl vanillin campaign to follow after roughly two weeks of changeover.
Diphenol plant shut because phenol and raw material prices are high; hydroquinone secured from China for the next two quarters; decision on alternate use or restart by Q3 FY27.
Working capital cycle about 100 days on a consolidated basis; each INR1 crore of revenue growth needs about one-third as working capital support.
CFS Europe in liquidation with no further cash burn beyond legal costs; China subsidiary liquidation expected to cost INR10-20 million in Q1.
demand_pricing: Channel stocks in the US and China described as cleared; management sees demand picking up and is negotiating quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts with F&F customers.
US and Europe ethyl vanillin realisations stated at about $13-14/kg; methyl vanillin raw material cost $7-8/kg, with conversion cost about INR7 crore/month fixed.
Management sees a supply gap of about 5,000-6,000 tons in US and Europe that must be imported; Syensqo (Solvay) is the market leader; Chinese imports priced around $15 against Solvay's $18.
Pass-through of raw material increases to blends customers is lagging by one quarter; management expects to recover about half of the cost increase in Q2.
Trade financing (dealer finance) on purchase and sales sides costs an estimated 1-1.5% and is hitting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA guidance achievable given Q1 EBITDA of about INR9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated guidance as INR2,200-2,300 crore revenue with 10-11% margin, which it said is within reach on the current cost structure; it expects about 10% margin over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Aroma EBITDA negative and what is its normalised economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low utilisation (about 400 tons produced vs 1,500-ton quarterly capacity) left fixed cost unabsorbed. Management said 70-80% utilisation would make the business profitable and gave about 7% EBITDA at $13/kg on 3,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt reduction and what external funding is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is INR640 crore, down from INR670 crore on 31 March. The CFO said INR100-200 crore of working capital lines are expected within 1-1.5 months, and equity or other capital is being considered without a decision yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 vanillin volume cut from 3,600-4,000 tons to about 3,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The ethyl vanillin ramp-up was slower to secure quality, with 95% customer approval. Each campaign switch costs about a month, and four campaigns are planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: What would Q1 EBITDA have been under normal conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5% of gross margin was lost, which would have lifted EBITDA to roughly INR37-40 crore, an analyst's figure that management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost pressure persist into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects elevated raw material prices to persist through Q2 and guidance assumes about three months of elevated costs, not six or nine months.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~45% in Q4 FY26 as stated by management

financial_highlights.value: More than INR4,000 million (blends >INR3,000 million; straights INR927 million)

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 EBITDA stated as INR255 million (per analyst)
From INR670 crore on 31 March 2026; reduction from IFC/EXIM prepayments

financial_highlights.value: ~560 tons (350 t ethyl vanillin, 200 t methyl vanillin)

544264|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with order book up 20.4% QoQ to INR209 crores.
544264|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with EBITDA excluding other income up 33.76% to INR141.54 million. EBITDA margin eased to 12.85% from 13.12%, which management attributed to higher raw material and employee costs as a share of sales. Standalone PAT fell YoY to INR99.79 million, but this reflects a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend in the year-ago quarter. The order book reached INR209 crores at 30 June 2026, with more than 80% stated as executable in FY27, and a ~INR100 crore capacity expansion is coming on stream in phases at Nagpur.

segments.name: Heavy Engineering
segments.commentary: Order book of INR159 crores at 30 June 2026. Management says ~70% of heavy engineering is new project build and ~30% spare parts for installed base; capacity being raised from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons.

segments.name: Wear Plates and Wear Parts
segments.commentary: Order book of INR26.42 crores. Management said growth in Q1 came across consumables, wear plates/parts and heavy engineering.

segments.name: Welding Consumables
segments.commentary: Order book of INR24.22 crores, described as a strong sequential increase driven by customers consolidating yearly requirements. Management said there was no one-off windfall.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Contributes approximately 1.5% to 2% of revenue. Management said it has not yet won competitive bids for subassemblies; Tejorup (10% stake) is developing a VSHORADS prototype.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Management said domestic drove most of Q1 growth because Q1 FY26 had large export orders; Turkey has turned out of loss, and UAE facility is expected to contribute revenue from Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 20% growth in FY27 and FY28 and continuing for 3-4 years, with an aim to double revenue in about three years.
EBITDA margin expected to rise 100-200 basis points over FY27 and FY28; management said Q1 margin should return to prior-year Q1 levels.
Management expects Q2 FY27 growth at similar levels to Q1, supported by seasonal monsoon-linked maintenance demand.
More than 80% of the INR209 crore order book is executable in FY27; customers are asking to prepone deliveries.
Railway (Vande Bharat, locomotives) revenue expected to convert within 9-12 months after workshop approval; management said new development items are a longer gestation cycle.
No new capex finalised; management wants to start the next expansion once newly installed capacity reaches 70-80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR100 crore expansion program across electrodes, wear plates and heavy engineering, with new strip slitting capability for backward integration.
Heavy engineering capacity being expanded from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons (includes wear parts and flux-cored wires used internally); new Nagpur shop floor coming live in phases since Q1.
New capacity expected to contribute from the next quarter, but management said ramp-up will take 2-3 years; electrode capacity started in Q4 FY26 with similar 2-3 year ramp.
About INR67 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilised; management expects full utilisation by year-end, with savings to be redeployed subject to shareholder approval.
Units 1, 2 and 3 have no capacity change; utilisation there was described as 2-3% in one answer, while management said Units 1 and 3 operate at optimal levels.
demand_pricing: Finished steel production grew ~8.3% in April-June 2026 quarter; cement volume growth expected at 7-8% in FY27.

Named Q1 orders: INR9.88 crore VRM/separator parts (cement), INR8.16 crore roller-press rolls, INR10.63 crore roller assemblies, INR7.49 crore flux-cored wire (defence), INR26.31 crore RAPH rotor assembly (power); aggregate ~INR62.47 crore.
Raw material costs: steel up ~20%, some ferro-alloys like tungsten up several hundred percent; management said gross margin compressed by ~1-1.5% and customers have accepted higher prices.
Heavy engineering payment terms: 10-20% advance, 70-80% post-dispatch, balance after warranty documentation.
Top 10 customer concentration not disclosed on call; management said 60-70% expected, to be confirmed later.

qa_highlights.question: Growth drivers across consumables, wear parts, heavy engineering and trading; domestic vs export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was 30%+ across the three segments, driven by a higher starting order book. Growth was mainly domestic because Q1 FY26 had large export orders that did not repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material volatility and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices remain high but volatility has eased and customers have accepted higher prices. Gross margin contraction was about 1-1.5%, with steel up ~20% and some ferro-alloys up several hundred percent.

qa_highlights.question: Executable portion of the INR210 crore order book in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% is executable in FY27, and customers have asked to prepone some deliveries scheduled for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of profit from associate (LSN Diffusion) of INR4.4 crore: anomaly or steady?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical run-rate is INR1-2 crore per quarter, so management expects INR1-2 crore going forward and treats the rest of the Q1 amount as a one-off extra.

qa_highlights.question: FY27-28 revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~20% growth in FY27-28 and an aim to double in three years, with EBITDA margin up 100-200 bps over FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 standalone PAT included a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend. Management expects margins to return to prior-year Q1 levels and rise 100-200 bps over the next 1-1.5 years.

financial_highlights.change: +35.98% YoY (vs INR122.64 million); includes ~INR4.4 crore share of profit from associate LSN Diffusion

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone EBITDA margin excl. other income

financial_highlights.change: vs INR142.04 million in Q1 FY26, which included ~INR5 crore one-time dividend from wholly owned subsidiary
+20.4% QoQ vs INR174 crores in March 2026

539957|2026-06.headline: MGL Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 31.7% QoQ to INR343 crore and PAT to INR194 crore, but management says margins will be under pressure for 1-2 months.
539957|2026-06.overview: Average sales volume reached 4.766 mmscmd, up 7.01% YoY and 2.01% QoQ, with CNG at 3.496 mmscmd (+9.74% YoY) and domestic PNG at 0.623 mmscmd (+9.09% YoY). Industrial and commercial volume fell 7.15% YoY to 0.648 mmscmd after a 20% government-directed cut. EBITDA from operations was INR343 crore versus INR260 crore in Q4, and PNG realisations on alternate-fuel-linked industrial and commercial pricing rose sharply. Management flagged that West Asia LNG disruption, withdrawal of pooled gas from around the second week of July, and force majeure on RLNG imports make Q2 margins hard to predict. Capex guidance was raised to INR1,500-1,800 crore for FY27.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.496 mmscmd, +9.74% YoY; 26,007 vehicles added in the quarter, taking the base to over 1.31 million; 519 stations after one addition. Management guides 8-9% CNG volume growth if prices hold.

segments.name: Domestic PNG
segments.commentary: Volume 0.623 mmscmd, +9.09% YoY; 97,461 DPNG conversions in the quarter (cumulative 2.17 million); about 95,000 domestic connections added per management. Management says FY27 could reach 8-10 lakh connections if bottlenecks ease.

segments.name: Industrial and commercial
segments.commentary: Volume 0.648 mmscmd, down 7.15% YoY on a 20% government-directed cut; 291 customers added, taking the base to 6,198. Realisations rose INR27-32/scm QoQ (70-80% YoY per management), priced off LPG and FO/LDO.

segments.name: UEPL (Unison Enviro)
segments.commentary: Average volume about 0.322 mmscmd vs 0.224 mmscmd a year earlier (+30-35%); management sees potential of about 1.2 mmscmd.

segments.name: Non-CGD initiatives
segments.commentary: Long-haul LNG has 2 stations at about 5 tonnes/day, roughly breakeven. Battery initiative is on hold. EV 3-wheeler cargo start-up is not yet breakeven. CBG plant of about 350 tonnes MSW/day planned on MCGM land.

guidance_outlook: Long-run EBITDA endeavour of INR8-9/scm, but management says it is not achievable to predict for the current quarter; margins under pressure for at least 1-2 months.
CNG volume growth of 8-9% assumed if prices are maintained; long-run volume growth guided at 8-9%.
Capex for FY27 raised to INR1,500-1,800 crore, subject to manpower and material availability; management calls it preponing rather than raising total capex.
Dividend to be maintained at current level despite higher capex; management said it may borrow, as the company is currently zero-debt.
Q2 gas sourcing and volumes not guided; management says it is 'anybody's guess'. It may restrict supplies to industrial customers to around 80% of DCQ.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of INR350 crore; FY27 capex guided at INR1,500-1,800 crore.
Domestic connections about 95,000 in Q1, the highest ever in a single quarter; daily connection pace could rise from about 1,000 to 2,000-3,000.
Potential of 3.8-4 million households; about 3.3 million already passed and about 2.3 million consumers served.
Cumulative pipeline length over 8,477.01 km after adding 156.57 km in the quarter.
Management said it has about 0.6 mmscmd of HPHT long-term contracts and has used about 0.2 mmscmd via IGX.
demand_pricing: Gas sourcing mix (company level): APM about 30%, NWG and pooled about 21-22%, HPHT about 14-15%, Henry Hub contract about 21-22%, rest Brent, IGX and spot.
Pooled gas priced about $12.5-13/MMBtu, Brent-linked about $13-14/MMBtu, spot touched about $20/MMBtu (spot share very small).
Pooled gas withdrawn from around the second week of July; Henry Hub volumes are under force majeure, so MGL is not receiving full contracted quantities.
CNG is about 40-45% cheaper than petrol and about 12% cheaper than diesel per management; CNG price increase of about INR5/kg taken from February.
Bus CNG demand is about 6,000 buses, roughly 0.14 mmscmd or 4-5% of CNG volume; STU and private fleet programme launched.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company-level gas sourcing mix and blended cost, and how does Q2 look?
qa_highlights.answer: APM about 30%, NWG and pooled about 21-22%, HPHT about 14-15%, HH about 21-22%; pooled $12.5-13, Brent-linked $13-14, spot up to about $20/MMBtu. Q2 supply not guided.

qa_highlights.question: What margin can be assumed if the West Asia conflict persists for three months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very difficult to call; margins will be under pressure for at least 1-2 months until the crisis resolves, and gas cost may spike.

qa_highlights.question: Why was industrial realisation lower than commercial?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is linked to alternate fuels: commercial to bulk LPG, industrial to FO/LDO. Commercial realisation rose 10-15% more than industrial QoQ; MGL also gives large industrial customers a discount. Raigarh has a 10% committed discount for the first 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth guidance changed from the double-digit view given last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier view depended on CNG growth above 8-9% and industrial growth of 12-14%. With supplies curtailed, it may restrict supplies to about 80%, so near-term growth is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Will a debt raise be needed for capex, and will the dividend be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is prepared to raise debt (currently zero-debt), dividend will be maintained, and cash flow is manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Are the battery and EV initiatives a priority?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Battery is on hold, with a restructuring underway. Management expects no sizeable time or money commitment for the next 3-5 years.

500770|2026-06.headline: Tata Chemicals Q1 FY27: standalone EBITDA up 35% on volumes and FX-led soda ash pricing, while consolidated EBITDA fell about INR 100 crore on sharply lower realisations.
500770|2026-06.overview: Tata Chemicals reported Q1 FY27 with consolidated revenue up 14% YoY but EBITDA down about INR 100 crore despite lower realisations, mainly from soda ash pressure in the industrial segment. Standalone performed strongly: revenue up 10%, EBITDA up 35%, and PAT from continuing operations up 12%, helped by higher volumes, an INR 2,000/tonne soda ash price increase in India, and fixed-cost control. The company moved to three reporting segments (Living Essentials, Industrial Essentials, Farm Essentials) to highlight non-cyclical revenue, and net debt fell INR 5,692 crore QoQ on asset monetisation (management later cited about INR 300 crore of debt reduction versus March). Management flagged that cost pressures from the Middle East conflict (Kenya HFO, UK gas, India limestone and coal logistics) could intensify after October.

financial_highlights.value: down about INR 100 crore YoY (absolute figure not stated)
up 35% YoY; India EBITDA margin about 28% per analyst question (not disputed)
INR 5,692 crore lower than previous quarter (per CEO); INR 300 crore reduction vs March (per CFO, in reply to a separate question)
financial_highlights.change: Reduction on land and share sales

financial_highlights.value: About INR 590 crore (per analyst's reading); includes about INR 43 crore one-off, per management
financial_highlights.change: vs about INR 517 crore last year and INR 524 crore in Q4

segments.name: Living Essentials (salt, bicarbonate, prebiotics/FOS, food, feed, pharma)
segments.commentary: Management described demand as stable and growing with premiumisation, with prebiotics expected to grow faster. UK is fully reported in this segment, and bicarbonate faced new competitive capacity in India. No segment revenue or EBITDA figure was given.

segments.name: Industrial Essentials (soda ash, silica, bromine, chlorine, caustic)
segments.commentary: Soda ash faces global oversupply, with Chinese inventories at an all-time high of 1.73 million mt. US and Kenya fall fully here. Management said the outlook is challenging, but India benefited from price increases; no segment figures were given.

segments.name: Farm Essentials (Rallis, Morocco JV)
segments.commentary: Rallis reported revenue growth on higher volumes and pricing, and EBITDA growth from better crop protection volumes and fixed-cost optimisation. Morocco is reported as JV income.

guidance_outlook: Management expects UK to be EBITDA positive and approach PBT breakeven, with breakeven for the full year; the EU ETS loss (part of about GBP 2.4 million one-offs) is expected to reverse by the October quarter.
India sustainable EBITDA margin is around 18%, with GC margin around 32-33%; a marginal pressure is expected as coal inventory gains unwind in Q2.
Annualised capex is to be kept at or below depreciation; the CFO said about INR 1,200 crore (FY26 consolidated depreciation) can be used as FY27 capex.
IMACID did not produce in Q1 due to high sulfur prices, restarted in the quarter, and is expected to be profitable for the full year.
Management expects global soda ash prices to stay subdued, but domestic markets to remain steady; it expects Indian bicarbonate competition to ease as added capacity is absorbed during the year.
Additional non-core land monetisation is planned from after Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Salt plant in India (82.5 KTPA) expected to be operational by end of calendar 2026, with supply to market from Q1 FY28.
210 KTPA salt plant in South India has a 24-month execution timeline; 50 KTPA silica plant also has a 24-month timeline, with operations in 2028.
Mithapur recycling unit for LFP batteries needs no major capex; initial volumes will be small and it will be built on OEM tie-ups.

Sodium-ion battery: first pack built and under testing; piloting expected to take 6-9 months, with lab-to-initial-customer offers by year-end and a full-scale plant about two years after that. Focus is on stationary storage, not mobility.
Capex focus is shifting toward Living Essentials, Farm Essentials and silica, with soda ash capacity maintained.
demand_pricing: India soda ash: spot price increase of about INR 2,000/tonne, partly passed through in quarterly contracts; realisation rise was largely FX-driven (import parity). Freight costs were largely passed on to customers.
Chinese soda ash export prices are USD 160-180 FOB, or USD 170-190 CIF Southeast Asia; management sees USD 160-170 FOB as the floor.

US: volumes up with slightly lower pricing; Southeast Asia exports at breakeven or unremunerative and largely vacated. LATAM exports up (Argentina +53%, Chile +32%). Domestic US pricing stable; logistics cost is the main pressure.
Kenya: volumes up but margins compressed by higher HFO prices, which are hedged through October.
UK: revenue up on volumes, with lower prices in some segments and higher gas costs in EBITDA.
India bicarbonate: one competitor added capacity, and management expects absorption within the year. China has bicarbonate surplus that mainly affects technical grade.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the segment reclassification, and will it change the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is to reshape the portfolio toward non-cyclical, sustainability-led products with stickier customers and lower price volatility, with capital allocation following. Geography-wise P&L will still be disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp India margin expansion despite lower soda ash and bicarbonate volumes (down about 12% and 19% QoQ)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited plant optimisation that shifted production toward higher salt volumes, lower-cost coal inventory that will unwind next quarter, and some bicarbonate tender contracts forgone for pricing reasons. It said about 18% is a sustainable India EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What assets were monetised to reduce debt?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said some land and some shares held were sold in Q1, lowering debt by about INR 300 crore versus March. More non-core land sales are planned after Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What are the status and economics of the sodium-ion battery and recycling businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The first pack is in testing and the strategy is being reviewed. Management is focused on stationary storage, the drone test was only a proof of flight, and soda ash intensity figures will come later.

qa_highlights.question: What capex and maintenance capex should be assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annualised capex will be around depreciation and not above it. The CFO confirmed about INR 1,200 crore (FY26 consolidated depreciation) as the FY27 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why was employee cost higher, and what was IMACID's Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost includes about INR 43 crore of one-off items, with the rest mainly rupee depreciation and Q1 variable pay. IMACID did not run in Q1 due to high sulfur prices and is expected to be profitable for FY27.

543328|2026-06.headline: Krsnaa Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR2,355 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 25% from 27% on Rajasthan ramp-up costs.
543328|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 22% YoY to INR2,355 million, with like-to-like projects up about 12%. EBITDA was INR588 million (25% margin vs 27% in Q1 FY26) and PAT was INR166 million (7% margin). Management attributed margin compression to upfront fixed costs in Rajasthan (about 4,000 manpower onboarded ahead of revenue) and loss-making RPL retail, and guided to EBITDA-positive by Q2 FY27. Retail revenue rose 64% YoY to INR193 million, about 9% of group revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +22% YoY vs INR1,930 million in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Rajasthan PPP revenue booked in quarter

financial_highlights.change: up sharply QoQ and YoY, attributed to Rajasthan, Manipur

segments.name: PPP institutional (pathology/radiology)
segments.commentary: Pathology is the larger contributor at about 59% of mix vs radiology 41%. Like-to-like centres grew about 12%; Rajasthan ramp-up and MRI go-lives are the main volume drivers.

segments.name: Rajasthan PPP
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR26 crore; management guides INR100-150 crore for FY27 (conservative), steady state of INR150-175 crore per quarter-run-rate commentary, below earlier INR200-250 crore aspiration.

segments.name: Retail (RPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR193 million, +64% YoY, ~9% of group revenue, 4,000+ touch points across 7 states. RPL at negative EBITDA in Q1 due to ground fleet and manpower costs; targeted EBITDA breakeven in Q2 FY27. Target retail contribution 10-15% of revenue this FY.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA positive by Q2 FY27 at group level; RPL also targeted EBITDA-positive by Q2.
Margins expected to return to double digits by year-end FY27 once Rajasthan operations mature.
Rajasthan revenue expected to roughly double in Q2; FY27 Rajasthan guidance INR100-150 crore, with earlier INR200-250 crore stated as aspiration.
Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh receivables expected to be collected by Q2 FY27; other projects on track.
Retail contribution targeted at 10-15% of revenue in FY27.
8 MRI centres in Maharashtra operationalised in Q1; balance of pipeline (17 MRI centres total) expected live by end of Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Rajasthan network substantially operational: 31 Mother labs, 62 hub labs and 1,228 collection centres at end of Q1 FY27.
8 MRI centres inaugurated in Maharashtra in Q1; remaining centres expected by end of Q3 FY27.
Himachal Pradesh CT project awarded: 34 CT scans statewide (22 new locations), ~10-year revenue visibility, predominantly cash-paying; revenue and investment details not yet disclosed.
Apulki Hospital, Pune, commenced operations with exclusive radiology and pathology rights, multi-decade partnership.
Warrant issue from promoter; proceeds earmarked for capex and acquisitions.
NABH/NABL/CAP/ACR accreditations at 124 after 12 new NABH additions in Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth attributed to new Rajasthan pathology and MRI centres plus like-to-like activation; value growth from new footfalls and repeat cycles in retail.
Management said margin drag in new projects stems from fixed costs ahead of utilisation, not pricing pressure in the core business.
CGHS rate revisions will not benefit current tenders (contractually at tender rates); only forthcoming tenders may benefit.
Retail customer acquisition, per management, is supported by quality accreditations and pricing; management denied doctor commission arrangements when questioned.
Management said RPL/retail mix shift is still early; retail described as 'just scratching the surface'.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fees to hospital rise to ~INR41 crore in the quarter, and how much Rajasthan revenue was booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Fees to hospital are revenue shares to local partners who run field operations in remote Rajasthan and Manipur; Rajasthan revenue was about INR26 crore, annualising to INR100-150 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR200-250 crore Rajasthan FY27 guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is conservative with clear visibility on INR100-150 crore; the higher figure remains an aspiration. Mitesh Dave indicated steady-state of about INR150-175 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is radiology revenue flat despite centre expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: MRI centres were operationalised in a staggered way over the last three months and are not at full utilisation; some radiology contracts ended their tenure. Radiology is improving QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: How much is RPL dragging EBITDA, and when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: RPL is EBITDA-negative in Q1 due to manpower and ground-fleet costs across 5 states (management said drag is nominal); breakeven targeted in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins expected to improve QoQ as Rajasthan revenue doubles and RPL turns positive; margins to return to double digits by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of receivables from Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: HP has allocated funds and money has started flowing; Karnataka receipts have begun but below expectations. Management expects collection by Q2, with HP, Karnataka and part of Maharashtra being the only delayed states.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on Rajasthan revenue doubling in Q2 and RPL turning EBITDA-positive; slippage would extend the 25% margin trough.
Receivables delays from Karnataka, Himachal Pradesh and Maharashtra government clients; collection timing guided to Q2.
Rajasthan FY27 revenue guidance cut from INR200-250 crore aspiration to INR100-150 crore; watch for further revision.
Fees to hospital (partner revenue share) run-rate of ~INR41 crore; cost sensitivity to partner economics.
Radiology growth has lagged; MRI utilisation and remaining 9 MRI go-lives by Q3 FY27 need to materialise.
Interim CFO in place; questions on retail customer acquisition and doctor relationships went partly unanswered.
543328|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, Rajasthan go-live and retail momentum, but defensive on margins and fees to hospital. Repeatedly framed margin dip as a timing issue, while guidance was softened to 'conservative' and several questions (CGHS, doctor partnerships, HP revenue) were deferred.

532505|2026-06.headline: UCO Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 8% YoY to Rs 656 crore despite a Rs 1,237 crore one-time DTA charge; operating profit up 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore.
532505|2026-06.overview: UCO Bank reported Q1 FY27 with advances up 21.18% YoY to Rs 2,72,768 crore and deposits up 11.28% to Rs 3,32,315 crore. Operating profit rose 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore, helped by Rs 1,018 crore of technical write-off recoveries, of which about Rs 800 crore is from a few accounts management does not expect to recur. Net profit was held to Rs 656 crore by total tax of Rs 1,919 crore, including a one-time Rs 1,237 crore DTA remeasurement on the shift to the new tax regime. Management said most asset-quality and margin metrics were within guidance, and that it would review credit growth guidance only after Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,919 crore (regular ~Rs 625 crore plus one-time DTA Rs 1,237 crore)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -55 bps YoY; NNPA -20 bps YoY
Was 54.06% last year and 52.66% in March; management expects normalised ~50%

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 27.32% YoY. Home loans grew about 20% and vehicle loans about 65% YoY off a low base; management expects roughly 30% vehicle loan growth and 20-25% home loan growth.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 30% YoY; gold loans are cited as a growth driver.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 18.79% YoY; management expects 19-20% growth to continue. ECLGS sanctions stand at Rs 2,150 crore with Rs 1,700 crore disbursed.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 25.27% YoY and make up 64.5% of the book, within the 62-65% guidance; management aims to hold around 65%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 17%, driven by working-capital limit drawdowns. The bank holds no IBPC exposure and is curtailing low-yield PSU and government lending.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth guidance kept at 12-14%, though management says it aims to exceed this; review after Q2 FY27 results. Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline awaiting disbursement.
NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%, with management aiming to stay slightly above 2.9%; yield on advances expected to hold.
Cost-to-income expected at or around 50% or below for FY27, despite Q1's 37.49%.
ROA of 0.68% annualised in Q1; management sees it near 1% by year-end as the DTA charge is a one-time item.
Credit cost to stay below the 0.75% guidance; deposit repricing largely complete, so cost of funds expected to stay stable.
Expected Credit Loss (ECL): about 60% of the estimated transition requirement already provided as buffer; remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before the ECL regime starts.
capex_capacity: Around 400 branches in West Bengal under five zonal offices; pan-India network of 3,421 branches.
GIFT City branch to open in the next month; all approvals in place and IT implementation in progress.
Omni-channel platform and corporate cash management service said to launch 'very soon'.
GST smart product to rise from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 1 crore ticket size; pre-qualified personal loan journey to be extended to the call centre.
Digital balance sheet of about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June, up from Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 31 STP journeys live; about 70% of fixed deposits now booked digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail loan rates held steady, as they are linked to the repo rate; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026 from 8.75%.
Corporate pricing held steady; management sees demand shifting to loans as bond yields are limited.
Yield on advances was stable, moving only about 3 bps QoQ.
Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management did not quantify the split and sees it as market expansion.
Management reports no stress in any sector; corporate pipelines in infrastructure, renewable energy, transmission, steel and cement.

Global advances grew 24.70% to Rs 2,87,690 crore, while deposits grew 14.36% to Rs 3,49,590 crore and CASA ratio slipped to 36.77%. Management said the quarter's slippage rise was mainly agriculture crop-loan marking done half-yearly in September, and that the June quarter had a one-off Rs 785 crore recovery that did not recur.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -60 bps YoY; NNPA -25 bps YoY

Credit cost guidance is below 0.75% for FY27; Q2 is 0.65%.
Cost-to-income expected to be around 50% for the full year and possibly below 50% next year.
ECL transition on 1 April 2027 estimated at about Rs 3,200 crore+ requirement; bank has provided about Rs 2,500 crore over and above existing provisions.

GIFT City IBU opened in Q2; three international branches (Hong Kong, Singapore, GIFT City).
Digital business balance sheet under Project Parivartan above Rs 48,000 crore as of 30 September 2026.
Seven processes automated via RPA; digital marketing solution onboarded; customer 360-degree portal rolled out in branches.
Recruitment of specialist officers (data analysts, CAs, trade finance officers) in FY27; further recruitment of professional officers and customer service associates planned.
demand_pricing: Advances growth came from all segments; RAM share has crossed 65%, and management expects it to hold around 65% with corporate growth also continuing.
Corporate sanctioned pipeline of about Rs 10,000 crore is undisbursed; disbursement depends on corporates' acceptance of lending rates and capex plans.
About 66% of advances are linked to external benchmark (repo/EBLR); a 25 bps repo hike was passed on immediately to these loans.
Deposit rates unchanged for now; management said no immediate need to raise term deposit rates, with any hike applying only to new deposits and renewals.

500238|2026-06.headline: Whirlpool of India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.4% to INR 2,582 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.6% on war-led oil/forex costs and e-waste accounting.
500238|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 11.4% to a record INR 2,582 crore, with management citing record Faridabad output, completed sell-in/sell-out of the new-regulation refrigerator and AC range, and gains in premium categories. Profitability was squeezed: EBITDA was about INR 120 crore at 4.6%, down roughly 377 bps, as oil-linked inputs, a roughly 10% rupee depreciation to 95-96 per dollar, Haryana minimum wage revisions and an e-waste accounting charge were only partly recovered through price. Consolidated revenue rose 12.1% to about INR 2,727 crore with EBITDA at 5.1%. Management guided that July-September will be the weakest quarter and gave no full-year numbers.

financial_highlights.change: +11.4% YoY, highest ever for a quarter

financial_highlights.value: FY25 up 4%, FY26 up 7%, Q1 FY27 up 11%
financial_highlights.change: from declines in Q1 and Q2 FY26
AC receivables collected; 5 of last 8 quarters negative

segments.name: Air conditioners
segments.commentary: Management said AC is about two-thirds of revenue and was the weakest margin category under the new regulations; Q1 AC sales were up about 50% in the company's outlet KPI and AC shipments rose in April-May ahead of the summer.

segments.name: Refrigerators
segments.commentary: Launched the 654-litre Luxuriem side-by-side with triple evaporator and Intelli Crisper, priced against INR 70,000-80,000 competitor side-by-sides; company previously had no presence above 500-600 litres, and Pune plant began shipping in July.

segments.name: Washing machines
segments.commentary: Washer sales grew over 80% in the quarter per management; Dynamix dispenser now on 50% of the range, and 11 kg top-load launched in Juniper Green. Top-load segment described as highly competitive.

segments.name: Kitchen appliances (Elica)
segments.commentary: Elica revenue and profit growth were cited as strong; management said there is no remaining minority stake to buy and the holding sits with Pralhad Bhutada.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management said predicting it is 'close to zero' accuracy.

Management aims for above 10-20% AC growth over the next two years, pacing growth to avoid channel stock build-up.
Management expects war-related and e-waste headwinds to ease if resolved, with an equitable e-waste solution sought from government.
Company aims for 10% share of top-load washers in time; 12-15 months of new product launches planned.
capex_capacity: Pune plant started production in July 2026, shipping Luxuriem refrigerators, with INR 245 crore invested in the facility (as stated).
Faridabad plant delivered record manufacturing output in Q1 FY27 despite war and heat-wave supply constraints.
Current utilisation of about 70-75% on an annual basis; management said no immediate capex need in the next 6-12 months.
Capex is an ongoing process; management said cash is not a constraint and capital goes to projects with strong ROI.
demand_pricing: Price increases taken in April and May 2026 only partly offset war-led and regulatory cost increases, creating a net under-recovery.
Management said the company led hikes only in April and May and avoids unilateral moves that could cost share, citing 2022 experience.
Competition in top-load washers has intensified; the company lost share in that segment while gaining elsewhere.
Distribution is near 10% share in some regions versus about 3% in smaller ones; not present at Croma, Vijay Sales or Reliance Digital (per analyst question).

qa_highlights.question: Parent refinancing and plans for the remaining stake; the cash on the balance sheet.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the parent, Whirlpool Corporation, holds 39.75% and it does not discuss parent matters. The board is examining capital use across manufacturing expansion, automation and inorganic opportunities, with no decision announced.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue growth and margin expectations, including whether OPM could be flat year on year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide; it said the outcome depends on war, forex and regulatory developments, and that margin protection is a focus.

qa_highlights.question: Whether industry can pass on further price hikes, and the elasticity of a 10% increase.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price coordination is illegal and that it decides pricing independently; a 5% price move equals about INR 1,000 per unit, and not all cost inflation will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the about 400 bps margin compression between war, regulation and P4G actions.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the war impact (oil and forex) was larger than the regulatory impact; P4G savings were largely offset as input-supply constraints limited negotiation leverage, and fixed costs were held flat as a percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Sale of services to the parent (INR 250 crore in FY25) and ESOP vesting terms.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the transitional services agreement runs to 2029 on a cost-plus, arm's-length basis; ESOPs were issued at market value with performance-linked vesting and a 3-year cliff.

risks_watch: Oil-linked input costs (MDI, polyol, EPS, plastics) and rupee at about 95-96 per dollar; about 30% of raw materials imported and several Middle East-sourced items are single-sourced.
E-waste accounting provision: management is seeking an equitable industry solution and said the impact is significant.
July-September weakness in AC, which is about two-thirds of revenue.
Price competition in top-load washers and whether the company can hold share while raising prices.
Parent Whirlpool Corporation at 39.75% stake and undisclosed capital-allocation plans.
500238|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and new launches, but cautious on margins; management repeatedly declined to quantify full-year outcomes and attributed the margin squeeze to war, forex and regulation. Evasive on the parent's capital plans and the remaining stake.
key_quotes: Revenue is up 26% and profits are up 22%.

544044|2026-06.headline: India Shelter Q1 FY27: PAT up 23% YoY to INR 143 crore and ROE 17.5%, but Stage 3 rose to 1.5% and reported AUM growth slowed to 24%.
544044|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR 143 crore (23% YoY, 4% QoQ) with ROE of 17.5% and net worth of INR 3,353 crore. Stage 3 rose to 1.5% (up 30 bps) on seasonal and early-bucket delinquency, and management guided Stage 3 to stabilise in Q2 and recover from Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for 25-30% AUM growth, 40-50 bps credit cost, more than 6% spreads and 40-45 branch additions, though analysts questioned the credit trend and the disbursement ask rate.

Stage 3 expected to stay around the Q1 level (about 1.5%) in Q2 and fall from Q3 as SARFAESI actions take effect; 30+ DPD expected to decline from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% AUM growth guidance still achievable given the cheque-realisation disbursement change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change is one-time and disbursement growth above 20% is still expected, supported by July's INR 400 crore; AUM growth of 25-30% is retained.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality and stress in the self-employed, sub-INR 7 lakh ticket cohort (above 2% Stage 3 versus 1.4-1.45% three years ago), and to the cohort's 16%+ yields. It said there was nothing internal, and that April collections were 96.2-96.4% and June slightly above 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company hold credit cost at 50 bps with Stage 2+3 at multi-year highs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of holding 50 bps, citing low LGD on this cohort and management overlays. Stage 3 is expected to stay flat in Q2, with recovery from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no branch addition in Q1 and why is disbursement growth only about 18%?

qa_highlights.answer: The gap is about INR 450 crore of co-lending book, which was not previously included in AUM. From March 2026 it is included, so the correct YoY AUM growth is 24%.

Credit cost guidance of 40-50 bps versus ECL of INR 93 crore, which is above the regulatory threshold of INR 52 crore, and analysts questioned whether buffers will be added.

Seasonal rainy-season effects and the reset of semi-variable home loans starting in Q4 FY27.
