segments.name: Outlets
segments.commentary: Total outlets about 141 (77 showrooms and 64 workshops per analyst's question). Management stopped classifying outlets as new a couple of quarters ago.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a more normalised and consistent demand trajectory through the later part of FY27, with no repeat of the GST-related disruption seen in Q2 FY26.
Management expects cost (employee and other expenses) as a percentage of revenue to fall further as revenue grows; no quantified target given, with a detailed number promised later.
Capex guided at around INR50 crore for the year; Q1 spend below proportionate share, with no commitment for the rest of the year.
Borrowing costs described as stable; surplus cash to be used to repay working capital loans.
Management said it is in talks with OEMs and possible takeover opportunities but will proceed on its own terms; no timeline given.
Asked about FY28 reaching FY23 peak profit levels, management declined to commit, citing macro uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Mumbai (Jogeshwari) workshop of about 50,000 sq ft inaugurated to serve Mercedes-Benz, BYD and Jeep; BYD and Jeep part due to be completed in the next few months.
New Mahindra workshop in Hyderabad to start operations soon; existing Hyderabad Mahindra capacity already exhausted, per management.
BYD outlets in Pune became operational in July 2026; two new BYD outlets opened about 7-10 days before the call.
MG network to reach 17 outlets with an LOI received for an additional Ahmedabad showroom.
Management said workshop capacity will be added in bays rather than workshop count, and smaller workshops will be consolidated into larger sites.
demand_pricing: Management said OEM price hikes (Mercedes-Benz and others) raise absolute gross profit per car, not percentage margin, since Landmark receives a percentage of the hike.
Price contributed roughly 3% of the 22-23% top-line growth; the remainder (about 19%) was volume, per management ballpark.
Mercedes-Benz sold 9,786 units in H1 CY2026, up 9% YoY; Mercedes-Benz plans over 40 new global models from 2027.
MG: new SUV launching in August expected to boost volumes; new Majestor deliveries began last quarter.

Mahindra: strong momentum with more launches to come; BYD: supply to improve through the rest of the year, hybrids later this FY; Kia: Syros EV orders healthy, new Sorento in September; Honda: City facelift, ZRV and Alpha 0 EV later this year.
Management argued that competition such as Audi's share push expands the luxury market (about 50,000 units) rather than cannibalises it.
Premium and mass segments grew faster than luxury in recent months per Aryaman Thakker.

qa_highlights.question: Will OEM price hikes improve Mercedes gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Thakker said price hikes raise absolute margin per car but not the percentage margin, as Landmark receives a percentage of the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Could Audi's share push pressure Mercedes sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants expand the luxury market; the segment has hovered near 50,000 units and luxury penetration fell last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ChargeZone partnership add revenue, and at what economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ChargeZone runs about 16,000 charging points; Landmark onboards EV customers and earns a recurring revenue share with wallet credits for customers. Commercials were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 margin normalisation and Mercedes QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2-Q4 to be normalised, with an EBITDA margin around 1.5% on pro forma new car sales; Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter and Mercedes grew strongly YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV aftersales margin versus ICE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EV margins are similar to the ~15% currently seen and are not expected to be lower; warranty costs (such as batteries) were excluded from the analysis.

qa_highlights.question: Will rental costs and cash conversion change?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said lease amortisation was about INR19 crore, with lease plus interest about INR27 crore; full-year rental cost expected around INR100-110 crore including Ind AS adjustments. EBITDA-to-CFO conversion was about 0.95x last year and expected to be similar.

524348|2026-06.headline: Aarti Drugs Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19% YoY to INR703.6 crore and EBITDA margin hit 13.8%, driven mainly by API price hikes.
524348|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY to INR703.6 crore and EBITDA rose 30% to INR96.9 crore, with margin up 120 bps to 13.8%. PAT fell to INR50.1 crore from INR54.0 crore, but the prior year included a INR15 crore tax refund; ex-refund PAT growth is stated at 29%. Management said API price increases tied to West Asia conflict and raw material volatility drove most growth, while volume grew about 3.5%. Sayakha utilisation rose above 60% for the first time, and the USFDA API block and Baddi formulation expansion are progressing.

financial_highlights.change: +35% YoY (vs INR51.1 crore); PBT margin 9.9%, +120 bps
vs INR54.0 crore in Q1 FY26, which included INR15 crore tax refund; ex-refund growth 29%
+20% YoY (vs INR521.3 crore); about 89% of consolidated
+149% YoY (as stated by analyst; management confirmed)

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Antibiotic 35.0%, antidiabetic 18.2%, antiprotozoal 18.5%, anti-inflammatory 11.9%, antifungal 10.2% and others 6.1% of API sales. Metformin prices are up about 20% versus pre-war levels, though below the March-April peak.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR81.6 crore, up 8% YoY, with about 74% from exports. Baddi brownfield expansion is expected to nearly double oral solid dosage capacity.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR82 crore, up 149% YoY, driven by the Sayakha plant. Methylamine ran at about 64-65% utilisation (about 60 tonnes/day, about 3,500 tonnes in the quarter).

segments.name: Salicylic acid (Tarapur)
segments.commentary: Only 67 tonnes produced in the quarter, as production was kept low. Derivatives plant (methyl salicylate, 350-400 tpm capacity) has started trials at 5-10 tonnes. Anti-dumping duty is expected in about one year.

guidance_outlook: Management says 14% EBITDA margin is achievable and 15% should be easy once the greenfield plants reach higher utilisation; a further 200 bps gain depends on prices normalising.
Volume growth of 10-15% over the next two years is seen as achievable, and about 10% even if the salicylic acid derivatives do not pick up.
Volume growth in the remaining three quarters is expected to be better than June quarter, as demand recovers once prices stabilise.
Specialty Chemicals run-rate of Q1 is expected to repeat in the next three quarters and improve further.
Captive consumption from Sayakha is expected to reach 80-90% by December quarter, adding about 1% to gross contribution at peak utilisation.
Metformin capacity to rise from 1,400 to about 2,200 tpm, including 500-550 tpm USFDA-compliant capacity taking about 10-12 months.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 greenfield assets (Sayakha, Tarapur) cost about INR600 crore and are expected to yield about 1.5x asset turn; Phase 2 brownfield projects are expected at 3-4x.
Sayakha plant utilisation was about 65% in Q1 FY27 (versus 30% in Dec-quarter and 40% in Mar-quarter, per management), with about 50% of capacity used captively for antidiabetic intermediates.
Metformin: 1,400 tpm capacity at mid-80s% utilisation; plan to scale to about 2,200 tpm, with the USFDA block (500-550 tpm) being built at Sarigam, which takes 10-12 months. US DMF already filed.

USFDA API plant (E-22): 2 main lines and 1 small line, around 4-5 active products, mostly supplied to Europe. A quasi-greenfield expansion adds 3 multipurpose lines of about 10 tpm each, more than doubling capacity.
Salicylic acid capacity about 600 tpm, utilisation about 70% per management. Derivatives plant at Tarapur (350-400 tpm) commissioned, in trial batches.
demand_pricing: Metformin pricing up about 15-20% versus pre-war; the March-April peak was higher, and prices have since eased slightly.
Price increases were tied to raw material and ammonia shortages linked to the West Asia conflict. Formulation customers cut purchases, which hit domestic volumes; export demand was less affected.
Management says Chinese competition is not a concern for its product set, though some pressure exists from select players.
Salicylic acid prices were cut sharply by Chinese players, so derivatives (salicylates) are now more profitable than salicylic acid itself.
Europe is still a small, under-tapped market for Metformin; EU CEP approvals were obtained for 9 products.

500674|2026-06.headline: Sanofi India Q1 FY27 PBT before exceptionals rose 19% to INR 112 crore on opex cuts, while diabetes grew ~14% in the quarter and total sales grew only ~2%.
500674|2026-06.overview: Q2 CY2026 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) showed a stronger quarter, with PBT before exceptional items up 19% YoY from INR 94 crore to INR 112 crore and margin rising from 24% to 27% of net sales. Diabetes grew close to 14% in the quarter and 17% in H1, led by Toujeo and Soliqua and aided by public-sector expansion. Partnership-related sales (CV, CNS) remained weak because of a prior-year safety-stock build and one-off return adjustments, and the company said 2026 growth in that business would not reach industry levels. H1 total income was down about 4% and revenue about 2%, with export losses in Australia and other products.

financial_highlights.change: Export losing ground; domestic and export both cited
Q1 partnership transition impact not fully offset

financial_highlights.metric: Profit before tax and exceptional items (Q2)
Overall Company sales growth in Q2 per management (partnership-affected)

segments.name: Diabetes (Lantus, Toujeo, Soliqua)
segments.commentary: Grew close to 14% in Q2 and 17% in H1; Lantus value share ~47%, Toujeo second-generation basal insulin grew 11% in value, basal analog share ~58% by value and ~61% by volume, Soliqua up 16% quarter-on-quarter.

segments.name: Partnership portfolio (CV, CNS, OAD)
segments.commentary: Q2 growth around 2%, below management's expectation; Q1 hit by safety-stock build in Q1 2025 and one-off sales-return adjustments. Amaryl/OAD sales-out via Emcure reportedly tracking market growth.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Down about 2% in Q2; Australia hit by heavy competition in mature products, partly offset by Goa site specialisation and wins in France, Italy, Turkey and Russia.

segments.name: Other operating income (consumer health services)
segments.commentary: Lower because certain services provided to consumer health in the past are no longer provided.

guidance_outlook: Management does not expect partnership business to reach industry growth in 2026; 2027 under evaluation.
Management expects diabetes momentum to continue into H2 but would not commit to 14%, saying it could be 10-15%.
Dividend payout expected to be at least at last year's level, subject to Board decision; no firm commitment.
Opex discipline expected to continue (quarter -5%, H1 -15%) without affecting top line.
No buyback in current strategy; proposals discussed by Board but not in plan.
capex_capacity: Goa site being positioned as specialised manufacturing hub for certain products for worldwide supply; one product already won and other actions pending.
Some products previously outsourced to CMOs are being brought back in-house to increase volume at the site.
Tenders from South Africa awaited.
demand_pricing: Insulin market: management believes insulin demand will hold despite GLP-1 and that analog segment continues at double-digit growth; higher single-digit growth overall expected long-term.
Novo Nordisk's once-weekly Awiqli seen as addressing a different patient profile; management says no major shift expected but will watch for one quarter.
Public sector expansion (CGHS, ESI, Railways, state and Army accounts) has driven close to 70% growth in that channel for Toujeo and Soliqua.
Partnership competition described as aggressive in generic CV/CNS/OAD segments.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the partnership business growing so slowly and when will it catch up with the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to Q1 2025 safety-stock build and one-off sales returns; Q2 at ~2% was below expectation. Industry-level growth not expected in 2026, with 2027 under evaluation. Denied that Emcure or Cipla are sidelining Sanofi products.

qa_highlights.question: Is 14% diabetes growth sustainable and are there new segments beyond diabetes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not commit to 14%, citing 10-15% range; cardiovascular and CNS partnerships remain strategic. Large underdiagnosed patient pool (~100 million cited) gives room for growth. No new parent products identified yet beyond diabetes devices/AI platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Will dividend payout remain healthy post-demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Cannot commit ahead of Board decision; expected payout not lower than last year, supported by cash generation (+34%).

qa_highlights.question: How will Novo's once-weekly insulin affect the franchise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees limited shift as patient profiles differ; once-weekly may bring non-insulin-treated patients into insulin; will assess over the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses in Australia offset by wins in France, Italy, Turkey and Russia; Goa site specialisation and CMO-outsourced products being brought back.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider an open-market buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Not part of current strategy; any such proposal would be discussed by the Board.

risks_watch: Partnership (CV, CNS, OAD) growth remains weak at ~2%, with no firm timeline for industry-level growth.
Export revenue declining; Australia competition in mature products persists.
Whether diabetes growth of ~14-17% holds in H2 as the public-sector channel and Novo's once-weekly entry evolve.
H1 total income and PBT still down YoY, so the margin gains depend on continued opex cuts.
Dividend payout commitment not given; Board decision pending.
500674|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on diabetes and margin expansion, but noticeably defensive on the partnership business, which management conceded was below its own expectations and gave no firm recovery timeline for. Answers on payout and buyback were non-committal.
key_quotes: If you look at the quarter two results, closer to 14% double-digit growth, powered by innovative portfolio, which is both Toujeo and Soliqua.
So, 2% we were expecting...

507205|2026-06.headline: Tilaknagar Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 166% YoY to Rs 1,046 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.1% amid packaging inflation.
507205|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with Imperial Blue (IB) inside the combined business, with volumes up 172% YoY and 9% QoQ, led by IB at 5.4 million cases (+18% QoQ). NSR rose to Rs 1,183 per case (+1.5% QoQ, +5.3% YoY), but glass-led packaging inflation compressed gross margin to 42.1% (adjusted for subsidy) from 45.2% in Q4 FY26. Adjusted-for-subsidy EBITDA was Rs 148 crore at 14.5%, and net debt rose to Rs 2,100 crore on working-capital build. Management reiterated FY27 volume guidance and a net debt target of about Rs 1,700 crore by March 2027.

segments.name: Imperial Blue (IB)
segments.commentary: Volume 5.4 million cases in Q1, up 18% QoQ; June 2026 was the highest ever monthly volume at 3.4 million cases company-wide, with IB the largest-selling deluxe whisky. Reintroduced in Delhi in July 2026.

segments.name: MHB
segments.commentary: Volume grew 7% YoY in Q1 despite April disruptions.

segments.name: Super premium and luxury (House of TI / SSL)
segments.commentary: Spaceman Spirits (SSL) more than doubled sales YoY in Q1; growth led by Samsara Pink and new Indian-flavour launches. House:Pour Picante ready-to-pour launched late in Q1. Monarch Legacy Edition Brandy and Seven Islands Pure Malt are being expanded.

segments.name: Bartisans (associate)
segments.commentary: Stake increased from 36.2% to 41.5% to fund quick-commerce expansion and product innovation.

guidance_outlook: FY27: high single-digit to low double-digit volume growth for the combined business maintained; IB full-year volume expected to grow double digits from the ~21.5 million cases base at acquisition.
Beyond FY27: annual volume growth in mid-teens over the next couple of years; revenue growth at least ~300 bps above volume growth; new launches from FY28 onwards.

EBITDA margin for combined business 16%-18% by FY29 with upward bias; FY27 margin to improve from 15.5% base set in Q4 FY26. Q3 and Q4 expected to show significant margin uptick; Q2 similar to Q1 with extra A&SP spend.
Net debt target about Rs 1,700 crore by March 2027 (reduction of ~Rs 400 crore); net debt/EBITDA below 1.0x by March 2029 (earlier FY29 framing).
Supply chain and packaging optimisation expected to expand acquired-business margins by 250-400 bps and consolidated margins by ~250 bps.
Telangana price increase expected soon; management estimates 150-200 bps incremental annualised margin impact.
capex_capacity: IB manufacturing integration about 90% complete by April 2026; one state (of the TSMA-linked states) still under TSMA, with transition targeted by March 2027.
IB now transitioned from TSMA into Tilaknagar-operated units for 90% of the business.
Prag Distillery: around 60%-70% of the expected bottling-related savings already reflected in the numbers; full benefit not yet visible. Utilisation rate not disclosed.
Sales team scaled from about 350 pre-acquisition to 850+ as of March 31, 2026, across North, West, Central and East India.
demand_pricing: Glass and other packaging inputs inflated due to geopolitical tensions; partly offset by softer ENA prices.
Karnataka: volumes and operating-segment market share improved after price reduction and slab reduction.
Market share of IB improved in all states versus exit levels; South the easiest transition, and share gains in North, East and West (Maharashtra) as well.

Competition intensifying in IB's price segment (ICONiQ White, McDowell's scotch); management expects category activation to help growth. A&SP reinvestment rate being raised; activations in 28,000+ outlets in Q1.
Delhi: IB peak was about 0.5 million cases (around 2019-20); management expects return to those levels in 12-18 months.
Maharashtra-made liquor category around 6-7 lakh cases per month, flat; IB gaining share in the state.
Tamil Nadu business under 0.5 million cases annualised; possible policy change under new state government (imports or market opening) seen as upside.

qa_highlights.question: Karnataka post-reform competition and pricing for IB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reported good volume uptake and significantly improved operating-segment market share since the price reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Which states show more or less IB traction versus average?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined state-level detail; said share improved in every state versus exit levels, with South the smoothest transition.

qa_highlights.question: Are IB-related disruptions in Odisha, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Karnataka TSMA-related?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the disruptions were predominantly IB-specific and TSMA-related; details were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Trade spend and growth in the low-prestige IB segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said segment activity is rising after years of inactivity by leaders; company is increasing A&SP reinvestment and activating in 28,000+ outlets.

qa_highlights.question: Margin recovery timing to 15.5% and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumes inflation status quo; Q3 and Q4 to see significant margin uptick, Q2 similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Quarterly IB run-rate and separate IB NSR?
qa_highlights.answer: No bifurcated NSR given; IB full-year double-digit volume growth expected.

qa_highlights.question: Telangana price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry in talks with government; last increase was three years ago; expected to add 150-200 bps to margin annualised.

qa_highlights.question: Tamil Nadu market size and route-to-market risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Current TN business under 0.5 million cases annualised; upside if imports or market opening allowed under new government.

512573|2026-06.headline: Avanti Feeds Q1 FY27 consolidated PBT fell 37% YoY to INR 157 crore despite 19% higher gross income, as feed raw-material costs squeezed margins.
512573|2026-06.overview: Consolidated gross income rose 30% QoQ to INR 1,966 crore but PBT fell 15% QoQ to INR 157 crore and 37% YoY. The Feed division's gross income rose 27% YoY to INR 1,615 crore on 28,287 MT higher volume, yet PBT dropped 45% YoY to INR 114 crore as fish meal and soya bean meal prices surged. Feed PBT margin fell to 7.06% from about 13% in Q4 FY26 and 17% in Q1 FY26. Shrimp Processing and Export gross income fell 7% YoY to INR 350 crore, while PBT rose to INR 45 crore on better realisations and forex. Management took a roughly 10% feed price hike in June 2026 and said industry and government are working on a raw-material price mechanism.

segments.name: Shrimp Feed (standalone Feed division)
segments.commentary: Gross income INR 1,615 crore and PBT INR 114 crore on 1,93,852 MT of sales; PBT hit by higher fish meal (INR 153/kg avg vs INR 123 in Q4 and INR 93 in Q1 FY26) and soya bean meal (INR 58/kg vs INR 49 and INR 40).

segments.name: Shrimp Processing & Export (Avanti Frozen Foods)
segments.commentary: Gross income INR 350 crore, down 22% QoQ and 7% YoY on 15-16% lower volume; PBT INR 45 crore helped by better selling prices, favourable forex and higher other income. Realisations fell in Q4 after reciprocal tariffs were withdrawn from 24 February 2026.

segments.name: Pet food (Avant Furst, Avanti PetCare)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 180 lakh in Q1 FY27 vs INR 151 lakh in Q4 FY26; distribution in Tier 1 cities expanding to Tier 2/3, available on Amazon and Supertail. Land purchased near Hyderabad for a plant, about INR 25 crore spent of an estimated INR 175 crore.

guidance_outlook: Company feed sales estimated at about 5,85,000 MT in FY27, against 5,62,060 MT in FY26; analyst noted this implies roughly 5-6% annualised growth.
Shrimp exports estimated at about 19,000 MT in FY27, against 16,976 MT in FY26.
Management expects raw-material prices to stabilise in coming months as fresh crops arrive and monsoon eases El Nino effects, but called FY27 a challenging season for aquaculture.
On the Q2 question, management agreed that Q2 could be another weak quarter before the benefit of the price hike and any government intervention plays out.
Shrimp production estimated at 8-9 lakh MT in calendar 2026, with feed consumption estimated at 11-12 lakh MT.
capex_capacity: Pet food plant: land near Hyderabad converted to non-agricultural use; Consent for Establishment application filed and approval pending, construction to start after approval.
Pet food capex estimated at about INR 175 crore in total, of which about INR 25 crore spent on land so far.
No feed capacity, utilisation or new feed plant commentary was given in the call.
demand_pricing: Farm activity described as good: favourable climate and farmers reporting strong culture progress through the second season to December 2026. Management said cost is the only concern.
Feed price hike of around 10% taken on 19 June 2026, effective about 10 July 2026 (speaker's dates were unclear in the transcript).

Government of Andhra Pradesh has formed a committee with a big-four consultant to design a feed price mechanism linked to fish meal, soya bean meal and wheat flour; management said further hikes need affordability balance for farmers.
Wheat flour price fell to INR 28/kg in Q1 FY27 from INR 31/kg; current spot prices are fish meal INR 225/kg, soya bean meal INR 71/kg, wheat flour INR 33/kg.
Frozen shrimp exports FY26 were 7,92,647 MT worth USD 5,624.48 million; USA 33% share, China 21%, EU 17%. US volumes fell 17.9% YoY; China rose 24%, EU 36%, Japan 5%.

542759|2026-06.headline: Spandana Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR12 crore from INR5 crore in Q4, with AUM at INR4,887 crore (+11% QoQ) and marginal cost of borrowing at 11.3%.
542759|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed improvement across growth, asset quality, funding cost and profitability. AUM grew 11% QoQ to INR4,887 crore, and new-book (post-April 2025 sourcing) share rose to 91%. Annualised credit cost fell to 2.1% from 3.2%, with net credit cost negative on recoveries, and NIM widened to 12.5% from 9.9%. Management reiterated FY27 gross credit cost of 2.5-3%, net credit cost near 2%, and an AUM exit of a little over INR6,000 crore for FY27.

vs 3.2% in Q4 FY26; net credit cost negative in Q1

segments.name: Microfinance lending (core)
segments.commentary: AUM INR4,887 crore; top 5-6 states (MP, Bihar, Andhra, Telangana, Odisha, West Bengal) about 60-65% of book. Tamil Nadu share about INR16 crore and Maharashtra about INR288 crore, against industry of INR38,000 crore and INR24,000 crore respectively.

segments.name: Individual loan product (pilot)
segments.commentary: Ready for pilot in 8 MP branches with 8-10 staff over next 3 months, initially for existing customers with eNACH; intended to later extend to new customers and to group company Criss Financial.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross credit cost maintained at 2.5-3%; Q1 was 2.1% and efforts are to retain it.
FY27 net credit cost closer to 2%, with recoveries from 90-plus pool of INR150-200 crore (aim slightly above INR200 crore; current run-rate INR16-18 crore a month).
FY27 business disbursement target INR6,000-6,500 crore; AUM exit FY27 a little above INR6,000 crore; March 2028 AUM about INR10,000 crore (to be firmed up around August-September).
FY27 opex about INR675 crore vs about INR760 crore in FY26; FY28 opex to rise about 10%.
ROA currently about 1%, expected to improve in FY27; 3.5% ROA viewed as feasible for FY28 on business-as-usual basis.
Marginal cost of borrowing expected to decline further as more CGS and PSU bank lines come in; no further lending-rate increases planned (last hike 1 October 2025).
INR200 crore rights issue balance (INR100 crore from promoter, INR100 crore from others) expected before end of Q2 FY27.
Branch count to stay about 1,250 standalone; some branch additions in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu this year.
capex_capacity: About 1,250 standalone branches; no plan for further branch consolidation; 100 underperforming branches carved out for revival by a dedicated task force.
New LOS platform expected in UAT by end of Q2 FY27; migration from Jayam to Perfios platform planned for October-December 2026 across 1,250 branches.
Investments planned in Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra expansion and automation to reduce manual intake; savings to be reinvested.
Liquidity at INR1,316 crore; management says it may optimise liquidity over time but prefers to stay liquid.
demand_pricing: Disbursement and sourcing: new members 1.38 lakh, with 61% new-member share; new book at 91% of AUM under new credit guidelines, targeted to reach about 95% next quarter.
Yield at 24.6% vs ideal disbursement yield of about 25.25%; management expects marginal further improvement, then stabilisation.
Collections: X-bucket 99.5%; July collections in line with prior month, no adverse trend yet despite weak monsoon/El Nino risk; districts likely to be impacted have sourcing controls.
Credit guarantee scheme (CGS) sanctions of about INR545 crore, of which INR200 crore drawn (INR500 crore sanctioned at one point in Q&A) at about 10% or slightly above.
Competition and funding: more banks, including PSU banks, in talks; bank share of borrowings rose to 47%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 credit cost target of 2.5-3% still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes; Q1 annualised credit cost was 2.1% and the aim is to retain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROA target for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ROA about 1%; FY27 expected to improve, with 3.5% considered feasible in FY28 on a business-as-usual basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net credit cost outlook for FY27 including recoveries?
qa_highlights.answer: Closer to 2% net; recoveries from the 90-plus pool expected at INR150-200 crore, with the older pool stopping collections from next year.

qa_highlights.question: How much recovery is expected from the written-off/90-plus pool against cumulative slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: The 90-plus pool is about INR2,500 crore; about INR326 crore collected over the last 18 months; current run-rate INR16-18 crore a month.

qa_highlights.question: Will the yield keep rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Ideal disbursement yield about 25.25% and current yield close to it, so marginal improvement expected before stabilising; last rate increase was October 2025 and no further hikes planned.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any signs of stress from the weak monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: No adverse observation in collection efficiency so far in July; proactive sourcing controls in affected districts.

qa_highlights.question: Stage 1 provisioning looks low at about 40 bps versus peers at 1%+; will it be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed it is a valid point and is working on it; target to raise the 1-30 bucket collections bar to 50%.

543950|2026-06.headline: Yatharth Q1 FY27 revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 3,927 mn with record EBITDA of INR 917 mn; consolidated EBITDA margin 23.3%.
543950|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR 3,927 mn (up 51% YoY, 15% QoQ) and record EBITDA of INR 917 mn, with PAT of INR 454 mn. Newer hospitals (Greater Faridabad, New Delhi Model Town, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra) contributed 27% of revenue. Faridabad Sector 20 reached EBITDA breakeven in about 9 months, while the group margin was diluted by new-hospital losses (adjusted margin ex-New Delhi and Faridabad Sector 20 was 28.1%). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of upwards of 24% EBITDA margin and ARPOB growth of 8-10%, and announced a maiden interim dividend of 5% of face value.

segments.commentary: Contributed INR 2,862 mn, +22% YoY; Noida and Jhansi-Orchha at 90%+ occupancy, Greater Noida 74%, Noida Extension 56%. ARPOB: Noida Extension above INR 50,000, Greater Noida ~INR 43,000, Noida ~INR 35,000, Jhansi ~INR 13,000.

segments.name: Newer hospitals (Greater Faridabad, New Delhi Model Town, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 1,067 mn (27% of revenue). Faridabad Sector 20 at monthly revenue INR 12-13 crore, ARPOB near INR 40,000, EBITDA breakeven in ~9 months. Model Town at INR 8 crore monthly run rate, ARPOB near INR 50,000, breakeven guided to Q3-Q4 FY27. Agra at INR 9-10 crore run rate with 20%+ EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: Contributing close to 10% of group revenue with one LINAC at Noida Extension; additional LINACs being added at Faridabad Sector 20 and then New Delhi.

guidance_outlook: FY27: management says it is on track for guidance on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with upside possible on some parameters; EBITDA margin upwards of 24% (guided 24-25%).
ARPOB growth of 8-10% YoY for FY27 and each year thereafter.

Bed capacity: announced capacity above 3,200 beds (incl. 250-bed Gurugram live in Q1 FY28 and ~450 brownfield beds in Noida cluster over ~15-19 months); target of 5,000 beds now expected in about 2.5 years.
New hospitals expected to reach 25%+ EBITDA margin (~27%) within two years; Faridabad Sector 20 and Model Town to reach 15-20% EBITDA margin about 15-18 months after breakeven.
Depreciation guided at ~INR 29 crore per quarter for the next three quarters; no fresh loans planned in FY27.
Dividend: maiden interim dividend of 5% of face value approved.
capex_capacity: Census beds 1,820 vs 1,655 last quarter; 2,555 total beds in existing network per management.
Gurugram 250-bed hospital under construction, expected to go live in Q1 FY28 with ARPOB potential of INR 50,000+; cost ~INR 1 crore per bed.
Brownfield expansion at Greater Noida and Noida Extension (~450 beds): construction delayed by monsoon; capacity coming live in 15-18 months.
Capex per bed guided at INR 75-80 lakh for the remaining ~1,800 beds (greenfield, brownfield, acquisitions, lease models), up from INR 61.4 lakh cited by an analyst over three years.
Agra: 250 beds installed but only 110 census beds operational; plan to increase census beds.
Funding: acquisition partly debt-funded (~INR 80 crore); management says it is comfortable up to ~2x TTM group EBITDA in debt and will use internal accruals going forward.
demand_pricing: Group ARPOB INR 34,758 (+7% YoY); new NCR premium hospitals (Noida Extension, New Delhi) crossed INR 50,000 for the first time in Q1.

Payer mix: government share ~40% at group level (analyst noted 36% last quarter); attributed to ~2% impact from recent CGHS rate revision, with government volumes declining QoQ. Newer hospitals have under 10% government business and 90%+ cash and private insurance.
Average length of stay fell below 4 days for the first time, attributed to lower government mix and surgical mix in new hospitals.
Doctor attrition ~7% group-wide; senior doctor attrition below 3-4%.
Incremental EBITDA margin on additional occupancy (e.g. Faridabad Sector 20 to 70%) estimated at 22-23%.
Regulatory: a panel recommended capping hospital room rents at 3-star hotel levels; management declined to comment in detail and said no framework has been received yet.

Newer hospitals revenue (Greater Faridabad, New Delhi, Faridabad Sector 20, Agra)

511742|2026-06.headline: UGRO Q1 FY27: total AUM INR 15,013 crore and disbursements INR 2,551 crore (+59% YoY); opex cut to ~INR 119 crore from INR 217 crore in Q4.

Quarterly opex fell 42% QoQ to ~INR 119 crore, and reported PAT was lifted by a one-time deferred tax reversal from the move to the new tax regime (pre-tax ROA 2.6% vs reported 2.8%). Management guided AUM flat for FY27 with on-balance-sheet assets growing, and said growth can be funded without incremental equity through FY29. Q&A focused on runoff, GNPA trajectory, the Profectus merger and the weak share price.

544517|2026-06.headline: Shankara Buildpro Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to Rs 1,890 crore; steel volume grew 10% to 2.5 lakh tons and EBITDA margin was 3.26%.
544517|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 21% YoY to Rs 1,890 crore and PAT rose 12% YoY to Rs 35.8 crore, led by steel volume growth and a recovery in non-steel. Management said April-May were weak due to West Asia-linked energy inflation and steel price volatility, with conditions improving through June and July. EBITDA was Rs 62 crore (3.26% margin), which management said included about Rs 10 crore of inventory erosion (roughly 50 bps) from a price correction in May-June. Management reiterated the 1.2 million-ton steel volume target, 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth, and a 3.5% steady-state EBITDA margin, and proposed a 1:5 stock split.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 35.8 crore (also cited as Rs 35.9 crore)

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Volume of 2.5 lakh tons (+10% YoY) and revenue of Rs 1,725 crore (+21% YoY); pipes, tubes, flats and roofing all grew in volume. Management said the 1.2 million-ton FY27 target is intact.

segments.name: Non-steel
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 165 crore (+15% YoY). Fittings and sanitary ware, the largest category, grew 32%; accessories and electricals grew about 40% on a smaller base; tiles were hit hardest in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 steel volume target of 1.2 million tons, with 20% steel volume growth and 25% non-steel growth reiterated.
Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 3.5%+; management said about 3.8% would have been reached without the Rs 10 crore inventory erosion.
Medium term (FY28 onward): EBITDA margin of around 4%, while maintaining 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth.
Target of 2 million tons in around 4 years; the 20% growth path is the baseline, with new territories and stores as upside.
About 5 more fulfilment centres or stores planned in the coming quarters, taking FY27 additions to roughly 8-9 (3 added in Q1).
Proposed 1:5 stock split (face value Rs 10 to Rs 2), pending shareholder and regulatory approvals; total paid-up capital unchanged.
capex_capacity: Three fulfilment centres/stores added in Q1 FY27 (Mangalore, Mumbai, Thrissur), plus 34 customer touchpoints across 45 towns and cities in 10 states.
About 5 more fulfilment centres planned in the coming quarters.
Planned investment in value-added steel infrastructure (cut-to-length, laser cutting) and warehousing.
Cash use priorities: private-label products (with promotion spend), value-added steel investment, and reducing acceptance-based borrowing. Acquisitions are 'on the table' but none named.
demand_pricing: Steel prices spiked in March-April, then corrected sharply in May-June, causing inventory erosion of about Rs 10 crore; prices have stabilised over July and early August.
Management said the Q4 FY26 inventory gain was about Rs 15 crore.
Volume recovered in June (about 1 lakh MT of rebound cited) and management said the momentum continued into July.
Non-steel tile demand was near zero in April (Morbi gas/energy shock) and recovered in May-June; PVC/UPVC roofing uptake is good.
Competitive intensity from well-funded enterprise-focused players has eased in the last couple of quarters; management is de-prioritising TMT and focusing on flats.
Retail accounts for about 50-55% of total volume. Ticket sizes range from Rs 500 to Rs 1.5 crore across 25 verticals, 75 categories and over 100 brands, with over 2 lakh SKUs.

qa_highlights.question: Can 22-23% volume growth be achieved for the rest of FY27 to reach 1.2 MT, given the high H2 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said June volume growth was very positive and July continued the trend, and he is confident of 1.2 MT barring unforeseen headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What were the margin impacts from fixed-price contracts and inventory, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts carried over from March into April forced supply at high prices, and the May-June price drop eroded about Rs 10 crore (about 50 bps). Ex this, margin would have been about 3.8%; steady state 3.5%+ is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company guiding for 25% non-steel growth when peers are not showing similar optimism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 32% growth in CP and sanitary ware, a tile recovery from May-June, and PVC/UPVC roofing traction; the CP/sanitary segment is expected to drive most of the growth.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the interest cost, given about Rs 75 crore of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Alex Varghese said about Rs 500 crore of acceptances (LCs opened and discounted, with the company bearing interest) bring total borrowings to about Rs 575 crore; the interest cost mainly comes from acceptances.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% revenue growth achievable at a 3.5% EBITDA margin, and is there margin expansion in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhananjay Mirlay Srinivas said the company is on track for 20% volume growth at 3.5% margin, and medium-term aims for about 4% EBITDA margin with 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: How long to reach 2 MT, and what new categories are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is about 4 years to 2 MT via new territories, stores and market share gains; new steel infrastructure for cut-to-length and value-added products, and expanding white-label private labels in retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume/price split of the 21% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said price played little part; steel prices were high and then softened, so the effect was largely neutral. He said a detailed split would be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company guiding for a 3.5% margin when adjusted Q1 margin is about 3.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukumar Srinivas said management is taking a cautious path because steel inventory gains and losses are outside its control, and it prefers to be prudent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel business profitability and outlook for flats?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-steel has an 8-10% EBITDA margin, so steel is trending above 3% overall; diversifying into flats and multiple steel products should help grow EBITDA.

532827|2026-06.headline: Page Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.9% to INR14,204 mn and PAT fell about 4%, as ~3 days of billing slipped into Q2 on logistics disruption.
532827|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 7.9% YoY to INR14,204 mn and volume rose 5.7% to 61.9 mn pieces, but management said quarter-end logistics and manpower disruptions left about three days of billing undelivered. EBITDA fell 1.9% YoY to INR2,890 mn, with margin at 20.3% versus 22.4% a year earlier, as input costs (cotton, nylon, synthetics) spiked from March–May. PAT declined about 4% to INR1,928 mn. Management said most of the delayed billing and the May price increase (about 2.2% weighted average) should show up in Q2, and it reaffirmed double-digit annual volume growth and the 19–21% EBITDA margin range.

segments.commentary: Volume growth of 5.7% was ahead of revenue growth of 7.9%-minus-mix, with lower-ASP accessories and socks gaining share due to scheme design. Schemes are now spread across quarters under the ARS model.

segments.commentary: Launched in June 2026 across close to 500 exclusive brand stores; management said sell-through looks very good.

segments.commentary: Go-to-market planned for end-June; a large portion of revenue expected in Q2.

Full benefit of the mid-May price increase to flow through in Q2 under FIFO billing; difference between volume and value growth expected to widen from Q1 levels.
Annual EBITDA margin outlook retained at 19–21%.
Management intends to hold prices and drive volumes if margins stay within 19–21%; another price action possible if input costs re-escalate.
Marketing spend to remain at 4–5% of revenue.

Odisha and K.R. Pet manufacturing facilities are scaling up progressively.

Management said the May price increase only partially offsets the raw material escalation.
Pricing is uniform across channels with no flash sales or markdowns; quick commerce is on an outright model.
Secondary growth was better than primary in Q1 because of undelivered billing; tertiary and EBO performance was better than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth below the double-digit target flagged in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was affected by a planned scheme phasing change under ARS and about three days of undelivered billing; the full-year double-digit target is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price increase offset input costs and restore margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The May increase only partially covers input costs; the full benefit flows from Q2 and management said prices have eased below April–May levels, so it is a 'waiting game'.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days fall from 73 to 66?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not intend to reduce inventory further, that Q1 had some lost sales from non-availability, and that inventory is now at an optimum level.

qa_highlights.question: What were the logistics and manpower disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party logistics and labour concerns linked to fuel price rumours, fuel availability and a June SAR drive disrupted last-mile delivery to distributors at quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Speedo multi-brand outlets decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline swim consolidation as business moved online; Speedo multi-brand outlets fell to about 700 in Q1, and about 950 counting Q4 and Q1 combined.

qa_highlights.question: Why did A&P spend fall 5% in FY26 and is the company shifting to outright e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included a disproportionate World Cup campaign; marketing will stay at 4–5% of revenue. E-commerce has tilted to outright because of quick commerce, and price governance is maintained through partnerships.

risks_watch: Recovery of about three days of undelivered billing and above-average Q2–Q4 volume growth needed for double-digit annual volume target.
Input cost volatility (cotton, nylon, petroleum-based synthetics) and possible re-escalation requiring another price action.

Karnataka minimum wage: garmenting wage hike applied from April; second announcement affecting third-party support staff was withheld in late July; impact on margins from a garment-level hike not quantified.
Logistics and third-party labour reliability at quarter end.
Speedo multi-brand outlet consolidation and channel shift online.
Shift of e-commerce towards outright model and its implications for pricing control.

500153|2026-09.headline: Ganesh Benzoplast to divest JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms plus Daund rail for INR1,154 crore, with INR500 crore due around January 2027.
500153|2026-09.overview: Management, on an investor call held October 7, 2026, outlined the sale of the LST (liquid storage tank) businesses at JNPA, Goa and Cochin, together with the JNPA-linked Daund rail business, for INR1,154 crore plus an exit-linked consideration. Payment is staged: about INR500 crore by January 2027, about INR300 crore by March 2027, and the balance INR354 crore over 12 to 18 months tied to port approvals and tank commissioning. Of the first INR500 crore, about INR190-200 crore goes to tax and bank-limit closure and about INR200 crore to a buyback and special dividend, with INR100 crore for chemical expansion and EPC book growth. Management guided chemical PAT to about INR18 crore in FY26 rising to INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years, and EPC PAT to about INR150 crore by around FY30. Much of the Q&A probed the rationale for exiting the higher-margin LST business and the lack of quarter-wise numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and target?

qa_highlights.question: Is ₹300 crore FY27 revenue guidance on track?

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital fall from 60–90 days (or 100–120 days) to target levels, and what is the margin cost of invoice discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Shift to railway bogies (30–45 day cycle, payment upfront from wagon builders) and RXIL/Invoice Mart (30–35 days post dispatch). Discounting costs about 5–5.5%. Management said ₹300 crore revenue would need only about ₹50 crore working capital at 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins fall as railway and power fabrication (tender-based) grow?

qa_highlights.question: Is the fundraise sufficient to reach ₹500 crore, and any further borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current fundraise is sufficient for the ₹500 crore projection; further expansion will be funded only from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Green hydrogen DRI project status?
qa_highlights.answer: Project closed. Grant of ~₹160 crore was subject to GST (~₹30–35 crore) because of IP and asset-sharing conditions; the reissued tender required an operating DRI plant, so Simplex did not bid.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term opportunities beyond ₹500 crore?

544290|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR359.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 21.07% from 26.65%, and FY27 guidance was trimmed to 21-22%.
544290|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR359.2 crore (+49% YoY) with EBITDA of INR75.7 crore (+17.9% YoY) and PAT of INR45.2 crore (+6.5% YoY). Management attributed the margin compression to higher raw material costs, a renewables mix, and a step-up in employee cost (about 7% of revenue vs 3-3.5% earlier). Total order book is about INR6,721 crore, split INR3,694 crore water/wastewater and INR3,027 crore renewables and BESS. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,000 crore and PAT of INR260-270 crore, while lowering the EBITDA margin guidance to 21-22% from 22-24%, and later described a blended 19-20% margin.

500405|2026-06.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 1,693 crore and EBITDA margin hit 19.53%, while volumes fell 24.5%.
500405|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR 1,693 crore, up 22% YoY, despite lower volumes, driven by higher raw material prices from the West Asia conflict. Operating EBITDA rose 88% YoY to INR 331 crore (19.53% margin) and PAT was INR 236 crore (13.96% margin), helped by wide global deltas between styrene monomer and downstream products. Manufactured volumes fell 24.5% YoY to 70,842 MT, with exports nearly absent and non-OEM demand down roughly 50%. Management declined to guide on volumes or margins, calling the situation fluid, and announced polystyrene and compounding expansions plus a new 80,000 TPA PS line totaling about INR 450 crore, funded from internal accruals.

Management stated the company does not supply to customers without credit discipline; competitors reportedly give 40-50 days credit.

qa_highlights.answer: Non-OEM demand fell close to 50%; OEM demand was stable to slightly better. Exports were about 10% of normal. Import data is no longer published; unofficial estimate about 20,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 80,000 TPA compounding expansion be absorbed, and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the expanded compounding capacity to be used over 2-3 years after June 2027, with ABS compounds the main growth driver.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the profit improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain came from wider global deltas, not volume; management called the level an aberration that will normalise over time and gave no guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex total and does it include the XPS expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex about INR 900 crore, funded internally, and includes the 150,000 cubic metre wide-width board line.

qa_highlights.answer: India CFR styrene about USD 1,300 currently, versus USD 1,350-1,400 Q1 average. Current GPPS delta about USD 250-275 and HIPS about USD 350.

qa_highlights.question: Are alternate styrene sources structurally more expensive?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; freight rates are higher because Gulf voyages took 4-7 days, while alternate sources involve longer voyages and shipping constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Did the industry de-grow in line with the company?
qa_highlights.answer: In polystyrene, management said the industry de-grew at the same rate; in EPS, the company de-grew less than the fragmented industry.

Non-OEM demand recovery and whether credit discipline costs volume.
Normalisation of GPPS/HIPS deltas from current levels toward historical USD 200-300 range.
Execution of INR 450 crore (and ~INR 900 crore total) capex on schedule by June 2027, December 2028 and March 2029.

531241|2026-06.headline: Linc Q1 FY27 operating income rose 1.4% to INR13,895 lakhs, but EBITDA margin fell 89 bps to 8.7% on polymer costs; no guidance given.
531241|2026-06.overview: Linc delivered a stable Q1 FY27 with operating income of INR13,895 lakhs (+1.4% YoY) despite geopolitical uncertainty and elevated input costs. Corporate sales fell 14% against a high base, exports fell 3%, general trade grew 8% and e-commerce grew 32%. Operating EBITDA was INR1,209 lakhs (8.7% margin, down 89 bps YoY) and PAT was INR581 lakhs (4.2% margin, down 93 bps YoY), both hit by polymer price increases from supply constraints and higher crude. Management said polymer prices are easing, but deferred formal guidance to the Q2 call.

qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the price increase has been passed to the trade, with the remainder not yet passed on. Management will decide on another hike after observing raw material prices for another quarter.

539336|2026-06.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
539336|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR9,670 crores (up 63% YoY), EBITDA INR1,482 crores (up 65%) and PAT INR998 crores (up 78%), with total sales volume of 15.66 mmscmd. Gas trading EBT rose 206% to INR726 crores, helped by Brent-linked long-term contracts and a Morbi industrial volume surge during the Middle East-driven propane shortage. Management kept FY27 gas trading profit guidance at about INR1,100 crores (reiterated as INR1,100-1,200 crores in one answer) and CGD EBITDA guidance at INR5.5-6.5/scm, while saying Morbi volumes will likely settle near 3 mmscmd as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources.

A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.

532528|2026-06.headline: Datamatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore, with EBITDA margin up 343 bps to 19.7%.
532528|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR 101.1 crore at a 19.7% margin, with the margin gain attributed to cost discipline and operational excellence.
