544679|2026-06.headline: Amagi Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 437 crore, a record, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 11.5% versus 5% a year ago.
544679|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR 437 crore, up 32% reported and 21% in constant currency, and almost 10% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA rose from INR 17 crore to INR 50 crore, with margin expanding to 11.5% despite the seasonally weak Q1 from annual increments. PAT rose to INR 34 crore (7.5% margin), and would have been about INR 40 crore excluding a one-time non-cash FX charge. Management reiterated operating leverage, highlighted AI product wins, and said gross margin will be kept in a 67% to 69% range for this year.

segments.name: Streaming Unification
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 249 crore, +39% YoY, driven by existing customer expansion, ~10,000 channel deliveries and 451 distributors (+21%).

segments.name: Monetization and Marketplace
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 crore, +30% YoY, volume-driven; monetized ad impressions a record 13.6 billion, +59% YoY and +21% QoQ.

segments.name: Cloud Modernization
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 17% reported; management said ~32% excluding the prior-year rev rec benefit from a large deal.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin to be kept in a 67% to 69% range for this year, with Q3 seasonally strong; management described it as not structural deterioration.

Management is focused on full-year profitability rather than quarterly margins; H1 was ~47% of FY26 revenue and ~37% of FY26 adjusted EBITDA, indicating back-half EBITDA weighting (historical context, not guidance).
Q2 YoY comparison carries ~600 bps headwind from prior-year rev rec timing benefit; management said Q2 may not be the best marker for growth.
Broader AI product suite to be announced at flagship industry conferences in Q2 FY27; AI revenue contribution expected more visibly in late FY27.
Aspiration to maintain growth rates through the year, without explicit guidance.
capex_capacity: Cloud cost optimisation delivered ~USD 282,000 monthly run-rate gross margin savings in Q1, reinvested into AI initiatives.
Live event delivery supported 104 FIFA World Cup matches on Amagi infrastructure for key customers; one US broadcaster received 100% on-air availability across 325 events and 450 hours.
Q1 is the weakest cash quarter each year due to incentive payouts, increments and software renewals.
Since January, 33 M&A opportunities evaluated, 23 passed on, 10 under active evaluation; management said this is not a signal of an imminent deal.
demand_pricing: Content processed reached 959,000 hours, +43% YoY; deliveries reached 9,900+ endpoints; distributors ~451, +21%.
Ad impressions 13.6 billion in the quarter, +59% YoY; management said FIFA did not add ad insertion upside and growth is organic (CTV penetration).

AI: 10+ active pilots; a major US news network selected Newspulse (agentic newsroom platform) after an earlier first paying customer; AI credit model introduced for some media operations, with outcome-based pricing possible later.
Pricing: one customer received a price adjustment but volume run-rate is >30% growth, a net revenue tailwind; management sees no material AI-driven deflation to revenue or pipeline yet.
Customer base: 400+ content providers, 400+ distributors, 80+ advertisers; logo churn in low single digits; top 10 customer average vintage ~5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the sequential gross margin improvement and will it recover to 69%? What is AI's impact on gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided gross margin to 67% to 69% for this year, citing mix, live events, pricing and AI costs. AI is a small base with no substantial margin impact yet; a 2 to 3 year S-curve with a possible initial dip is expected. Gross margin was ~64% three to four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Do distribution platform additions drive customer growth, and is in-sourcing a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Several distribution platforms (Vodafone, Kogan TV, Virgin UK) became customers, but it is not a prerequisite. Management sees platforms outsourcing rather than in-sourcing and is not aware of in-sourcing impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross retention (GRR) disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: GRR is not disclosed; management pointed to logo churn in low single digits and top 10 customer vintage of ~5 years as stickiness indicators.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI being priced and how is cost inflation protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Early stage; AI credits model mirrors a cost-plus approach for agentic media operations, with telemetry built with Newspulse customer to measure cost and revenue benefit. Business model not yet settled; a few more quarters needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is NRR constant currency and what is the growth impact of last year's one-time item?
qa_highlights.answer: NRR is in reported currency on a TTM basis, as in the DRHP; full-year NRR to be disclosed at Q4. The prior-year rev rec benefit affected growth by ~450 bps. Management aspires to sustain growth but Q2 will still lap the base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Can channel deliveries be split between new channels and additional deliveries on existing channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Not tracked internally; directionally growth is from existing channels going to more deliveries. Net revenue retention contributed ~26 points of the ~31% growth from existing customers.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from live event mix, customer pricing and AI costs; guided to 67% to 69%.
Cash burn remains negative in Q1 (operating outflow INR 65 crore reported), with DSO improvement of ~8 days QoQ still needed.
Q2 FY27 faces a ~600 bps headwind from the prior-year rev rec base; growth optics may be weaker.
Monetisation of AI products (Newspulse and broader Q2 suite) is still early; revenue contribution expected late FY27.
Capital deployment: active M&A pipeline (10 opportunities under evaluation) against INR 1,616 crore cash.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 17 crore (5% margin) YoY; margin +1.2 pp QoQ
from INR 4 crore (1.1% margin) YoY; ~INR 40 crore excluding one-time non-cash FX charge
from INR 141 crore YoY; excluding one-time items INR 41 crore vs INR 84 crore

540047|2026-06.headline: DBL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue Rs 1,930 crore and EBITDA margin 10.32%; consolidated PAT fell to Rs 128 crore from Rs 271 crore.
540047|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue was Rs 1,930 crore with EBITDA of Rs 199 crore (10.32% margin, up from 10.11%), and standalone PBT rose about 26% YoY to Rs 72 crore. Standalone PAT fell to Rs 39 crore from Rs 123 crore, but the base quarter included a Rs 98 crore divestment gain. Consolidated revenue dipped to Rs 2,378 crore from Rs 2,620 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 429 crore (18.05% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance (revenue growth 30-40%, EBITDA margin 10-12%, debt reduction Rs 600-800 crore) and announced a stake sale in under-construction transmission and solar projects (about Rs 8,400 crore project cost) to Alpha Alternatives.

financial_highlights.change: margin up from 10.11% in Q1 FY26
vs Rs 123 crore in Q1 FY26, which included ~Rs 98 crore exceptional divestment gain
vs Rs 2,620 crore in Q1 FY26
vs Rs 271 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Completed three HAM packages worth Rs 1,700 crore on Bengaluru-Vijayawada Expressway (AP), all ahead of COD. Management says revenue from large new projects (transmission, roads, solar, water) has not yet started and will ramp from Q2-Q3.

segments.name: MDO (Mining)
segments.commentary: Q1 coal production 4.79 MT; MDO revenue about Rs 362 crore in the quarter per analyst calculation. Siarmal planned 27 MT and Pachhwara 7 MT for FY27; FY29 target 57 MT retained. Pottangi Bauxite production not yet started.

segments.name: Multi-asset platform (InvIT/HAM)
segments.commentary: Holds units worth about Rs 1,521 crore (Rs 1,314 crore Anantam Highway Trust plus Rs 207 crore Shrem InvIT). Next tranche of 11 HAM assets to be transferred to Anantam InvIT by March 2027, expected to yield about Rs 1,700-1,800 crore of units for <Rs 81 crore incremental equity.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 10-12% (reconfirmed; analyst noted 11-12%).
Revenue growth guidance of 30-40% for FY27 reiterated; ramp-up expected from Q3, stronger in Q4 and into Q1 FY28.
Standalone debt reduction guidance of Rs 600-800 crore for FY27 reiterated; standalone net-debt-positive target by FY28 reaffirmed.
FY27 order inflow guidance of Rs 10,000-12,000 crore reiterated; bids worth Rs 15,000-20,000 crore pending opening.
Working capital days expected to reach about 120 by year-end and about 90 next year; from 131-133 days currently.
Finance cost for FY27 targeted at about Rs 350 crore.
Standalone capex guided at under Rs 100 crore for FY27, unchanged.
Coal production target of 57 MT by FY29; coal handling plant (CHP) expected to take about 1.5 years, with Siarmal at 27 MT (FY27), 35 MT (FY28), 50 MT after CHP.
capex_capacity: Siarmal total original capex Rs 2,730 crore, about 40-45% spent; more than 50% of equity already invested; around Rs 300 crore cash sitting at Siarmal SPV; Rs 235 crore residual equity to be funded from SPV accruals.
Siarmal debt sanction Rs 2,000 crore, Rs 60 crore drawn as of 30 June; around Rs 300 crore remaining to draw.

Transmission and solar stake sale to Alpha Alternatives: total equity requirement about Rs 1,600-1,650 crore; Alpha to co-invest 49% during construction; about Rs 900 crore structured equity already raised.

Anantam InvIT: 11 HAM assets, 4 to be flipped in August; 4 CODs done and 3 more by September; all 18 assets targeted for transfer by FY27 end or Q1 FY28, subject to NHAI NOC after six months of first annuity.
Other pipeline: 1977 MW solar mandate, Mekhali interstate transmission (Karnataka), water HAM, oil and gas portfolio to be considered for a future InvIT structure.
demand_pricing: NHAI FY27 pipeline: 54 highway/expressway projects, 2,442 km, about Rs 1.80 lakh crore (26 EPC, 21 HAM, 7 BOT). Awarding in Q1 was soft, particularly in national highways.
NHAI monetisation: 17 stretches (~1,693 km) targeted for FY27 via TOT/InvIT, expected proceeds Rs 30,000-35,000 crore.
Bid pipeline about Rs 1.5 lakh crore per Rohan; management later cited Rs 2.5-3 lakh crore across sectors, of which roads about Rs 1.25 lakh crore.
Declared L1 for Sikasar to Kodar Reservoir Link Canal Pipeline (Chhattisgarh), lump sum about Rs 2,524 crore.
Mining balance contract value about Rs 1.03 lakh crore; MDO reported order book about Rs 5,224 crore (3-year rolling).
Coal MDO pricing: Siarmal about Rs 550-600/t; Pachhwara about Rs 1,150-1,200/t; Siarmal coal fee currently 78%, moving to 100% after CHP.
Input costs: diesel bought at about Rs 140 and bitumen prices roughly doubled during the recent disruption; government reimburses 60-65% of fuel and bitumen cost increase.

544587|2026-06.headline: Midwest Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY and PAT 27%, with granite carrying results and quartz Phase 1 still ramping (~5,000 t sold, ~INR5 crore revenue).
544587|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 35% YoY, EBITDA up 25% and PAT up 27%, with most of the earnings from granite despite diesel cost pressure. Quartz Phase 1 has begun commercial operations with roughly INR5 crore revenue and about 5,000 tonnes sold in the quarter, and management is targeting a 10,000 t/month run rate by end-Q2 and 15,000 t/month by Q4. FY27 guidance is about INR840 crore revenue (granite INR720 crore, quartz INR100-120 crore), with quartz EBITDA expected to be low this year. Management also flagged an Indonesia MoU with PERMINAS for rare earth oxides and an imminent Sri Lanka licence step, while Kerala remains stalled on government transition.

financial_highlights.value: ~10% in both Absolute Black and Black Galaxy

financial_highlights.metric: Blended EBITDA margin impact from diesel (Q1 FY27)
financial_highlights.change: Diesel ~13% of cost; diesel rose from ~INR85 to INR125-130/litre

segments.name: Granite (natural stone)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth above 30% excluding quartz; volumes up ~10% in both Absolute Black and Black Galaxy, with better realisations and a price hike of about 3-5%. Electrified fleet and solar backing cut diesel sensitivity.

segments.name: Quartz (engineered stone, Phase 1, Kerala-linked plant)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR5 crore on ~5,000 t sold; realisation about INR10,000/t. Mix about 65% engineered stone and 35% solar. Break-even targeted around 10,000 t/month, with plant capacity up to 18,000 t/month.

segments.name: Rare earth / Midwest Advanced Materials
segments.commentary: Sister concern Midwest Advanced Materials focuses on rare earth oxide to permanent magnet. Parent scope is ore-to-oxide via a JV with PERMINAS; no revenue yet, with cash flows expected FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue estimated at ~INR840 crore vs INR645 crore in FY26; management called this conservative and said Q1 run-rate suggests beating it.
Quartz: ~120,000 t production target for FY27 (revised down from 150,000 t); quartz EBITDA this year to be below expectations; break-even around 10,000 t/month, with some profit expected by year-end.
Granite EBITDA margin in line with prior years, with 50-100 bps diesel-related variance; blended EBITDA margin expected in the 26-27% range for FY27.

FY28: quartz Phase 1 revenue INR180-200 crore plus Phase 2 contribution of about INR40-50 crore (around 4 months of production); granite growth 10-12%; blended EBITDA ~29-30%, with quartz EBITDA slightly above 30%.
Sri Lanka: policy finalised; land/licence documentation expected this quarter, groundbreaking around October, 12-15 months build-out; cash flows now expected FY29.
Indonesia (PERMINAS): MoU to be converted to an agreement this quarter and a JV formed next quarter; project report due in 45-60 days; capex to be given next call.
capex_capacity: Quartz Phase 2: total capex ~INR125 crore, with ~INR60-70 crore in Q2-Q3 and the balance in Q4 or early FY28; commissioning now 10-12 months out after machinery was resourced away from China; funded by fresh equity raised.
Quartz Phase 1 capacity can reach 18,000 t/month; 15,000 t/month is the planned stable run rate; ramp to 10,000-12,000 t/month in Q2 and above 15,000 t/month by Q4.
Sri Lanka plant capex ~INR120 crore (internal accruals); Kerala (KMML) pilot plant described as low cost, with no activity pending new government and MD appointment.
Indonesia capex to be higher than Kerala given overseas mining; figure to be given next call.
Electrification of the granite fleet mostly completed this year; regular granite replacement capex funded from operating cash flow.
demand_pricing: Quartz volumes are mostly exported to China; management said Q4 typically carries 30-40% of annual revenue due to Chinese New Year restocking.
Granite pricing improved; a further price increase of about 3-5% was taken to offset fuel costs. Management said no further price action is planned this year unless fuel moves again.
Fuel prices eased slightly from Q1 peaks but remain well above prior-year levels; management expects margin recovery in Q2.
Q3 monsoon risk noted: production is typically lower in Q3 due to rains.
Freight is generally on FOB terms, so freight costs are borne by customers and are not in Midwest's cost base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 quartz volume and the ramp-up timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5,000 t sold in Q1; management guided ~20,000 t this quarter (likely a typo for run rate), 10,000-12,000 t next quarter and above 15,000 t in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will quartz reach EBITDA break-even and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even expected around Q3 FY27 at about 10,000 t/month, with some profit by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 150,000 t FY27 quartz production target still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management revised the target to about 120,000 t after a technical production issue that has since been resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue look lower than Q4 and how does the quartz capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is seasonally the peak (30-40% of annual revenue) due to Chinese New Year restocking; Phase 2 capex is INR125 crore spread over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 see higher margins with quartz?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Blended EBITDA expected at 29-30% in FY28, with quartz EBITDA slightly above 30%, given Phase 1 revenue of INR180-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Which granite mine has the AP government revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Black Galaxy; the arrangement is a revenue-share payment to a state-owned lessor that also holds equity.

509930|2026-06.headline: Supreme Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4% to INR2,718 crore on 14% volume decline, with standalone PAT up 17% to INR208 crore; FY27 guidance held.
509930|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volumes fell about 14% to 1,57,536 tons, but revenue grew 4% to INR2,718 crore as value-added products rose 22% to INR1,142 crore. Standalone operating profit rose 25% to INR398 crore and PAT rose 17% to INR208 crore, helped by lower-margin agri pipe volumes falling sharply. Management attributed the weakness to April 2026 polymer price volatility and channel destocking, and said volumes recovered in May-July. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 12-13% overall volume growth, 15-17% piping volume growth and 14-14.5% EBITDA margin, plus about INR1,000 crore capex.

financial_highlights.change: Derived: 398/2,718; not stated on call as a figure
vs 8.8% in June 2025 quarter (as cited by analyst, not disputed)

segments.name: Plastic piping systems
segments.commentary: Volume fell about 15% YoY with value flat; April 2026 volume reportedly down more than 50%, with May-July showing growth. Agri pipe and polythene pipe saw the sharpest declines; PVC pipe demand also fell.

segments.name: Packaging
segments.commentary: Volume down about 10% YoY, value up 9%. Management attributed the value gain to customised, higher-realisation solutions.

segments.name: Industrial products
segments.commentary: Volume down about 6% YoY, value up 24%; OEM demand tied to end-market (e.g., air conditioners), priced on cost-plus. Value gain attributed to product mix (pellets, dustbins).

segments.name: Consumer products
segments.commentary: Volume down about 22% YoY, value down 11%.

segments.name: Composite cylinders
segments.commentary: Capacity 9-10 lakh cylinders per annum; utilisation 25-35%. HPCL tender of 2 lakh pieces; LOI for 60,000 pieces, supply from next month.

segments.name: Wavin (acquired) and Gas piping
segments.commentary: Wavin capacity about 70,000 tons, 50-60% utilised in Q1; management targets about 70% for the year. Gas piping (pipe and fitting) business seen at about INR600 crore this year; orders already supplied.

guidance_outlook: Overall volume growth 12-13% for FY27 (maintained from April 2026 guidance).
Piping volume growth 15-17% for FY27, maintained; management said it refers to the full year, not the balance nine months.
EBITDA margin 14-14.5% for FY27, maintained; management said FY28-29 not discussed.
Capex of about INR1,000 crore for FY27 maintained; INR500 crore committed so far, depending on machine arrival.
Management expects growth in H1 FY27 and in Q2 FY27, which it said would be visible in October.
Exports: target USD150 million in 6-7 years from USD26 million last year.
capex_capacity: Windows and doors (uPVC) business: INR220 crore invested; revenue potential INR300-350 crore at normal utilisation; capacity 5,000 tons per year; production started and market sales begun, with better utilisation expected next year.
New plants planned at Bihar (21 acres) and Jammu (13 acres) to together exceed 50,000 tons in about two years, built in small phases.
Malanpur facility to make material handling products (crates, pallets).
Pondicherry: existing factory product for Whirlpool to be shifted; capacity to be added for furniture exports. Erode land acquisition in progress.
OPVC: new machine for Eastern India; some machines running in Western India. CPVC market share said to have risen.
Composite cylinders: 9-10 lakh per annum capacity, utilisation 25-35%.
demand_pricing: April 2026 polymer price volatility caused channel destocking; management said inventory is now being refilled and demand is coming in, with PVC up INR9/kg recently.
Management said agri demand restarts from mid-September, with robust demand expected through to March as reservoirs fill.

PVC prices stabilised after about 20 April; MIP (minimum import price) for suspension-grade PVC resin set at USD766 per ton, with management noting it sets a floor, not a ceiling. MIP reportedly for six months.
Management said no inventory gain or loss to quantify; said pipe is low-margin and its volume fall lifted blended margin.
Pricing: management said prices track raw material costs, and the company is focused on return on capital employed rather than margin expansion.
Industry-wide plastic de-growth; management had no industry volume data.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15-17% piping volume guidance for the full year, given a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it refers to the full year and is maintained; it cited excellent July growth and expected good Q2 growth, to be seen in October. April volume was down more than 50%, with May-July showing growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA guidance 14-14.5% when Q1 margin was 14.6% and earlier guidance was higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not guiding lower; Q1 margin rose because pipe demand fell. It called the guidance conservative and said it does not want to present a rosy picture.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any inventory gain in Q1, or any in Q2 from the July PVC price rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify or confirm either inventory gains or losses, saying it would discuss at year-end if anything happens.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 14% margin improvement from mix persist, and what is the outlook for Wavin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Wavin is running at about 70% utilisation, with margins in the same range as Supreme; it said the 14-14.5% margin guidance holds.

qa_highlights.question: How big can gas piping be, and what is the status of uPVC windows?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas piping (pipe and fitting) was estimated at about INR600 crore this year, with orders supplied. Windows: INR220 crore invested, revenue potential INR300-350 crore at normal utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will lost volumes be recovered, and is there a restocking effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lost volume will be recovered, with growth in H1 FY27; it said channel is refilling inventory now and there is no destocking.

544045|2026-06.headline: DOMS Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 19.2% to INR670 crore, but EBITDA fell 16.4% to INR82.6 crore as margin dropped to 12.3% on raw material inflation.
544045|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue grew 19.2% YoY to INR670 crore on volume growth, with only a calibrated price increase of about 4-5%. EBITDA margin compressed to 12.3% from 17.6%, mainly from roughly 400 bps gross margin decline due to West Asia-linked raw material inflation (about 20% average RM price rise in Q1), plus ESOP, new-facility and channel partner event costs. PAT fell to INR45.3 crore from INR59.1 crore, with PAT margin at 6.8% versus 10.5%. Management chose volume and market share over near-term margin, calls the margin dip temporary, and gave limited visibility on margins given fluctuating raw material costs.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR59.1 crore in Q1 FY26 (-23% YoY)
Against about 10-11% consumption cost increase; about 500 bps left to pass on

segments.name: Scholastic stationery, scholastic art material and paper stationery
segments.commentary: Growth led by back-to-school season, new launches and recent capacity additions; no segment-level figures disclosed.

segments.name: Office supplies (pens, mechanical pencils, erasers, pencil boxes, school bags and kits)
segments.commentary: Described as high positive traction with strong acceptance of new launches; no revenue figure disclosed.

segments.name: Baby hygiene (Uniclan diapers)
segments.commentary: Drove high growth in modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce; EBITDA margin held up in Q1, but raw material (SAP, non-woven fabric) costs are expected to hit from Q2, partly offset by seasonal fixed-cost absorption.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Flattish in Q1 due to EU demand softness and West Asia logistics disruption; West Asia is about 2% of sales. Exports are about 12% of total revenue; full-year export share guided at 13-15%.

segments.name: West India region
segments.commentary: Revenue declined YoY from about INR186 crore to close to INR140 crore, mainly due to lower merchant export sales routed via western India customers.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated revenue growth guidance of 18-20% for FY27 reaffirmed, with the second-half contribution expected from the 50-plus acre greenfield plant.

Gross/EBITDA margin: management reiterated the long-term EBITDA target of about 16-17%, but gave limited visibility on margins; at current spot raw material prices, a further 4-5% price increase may be needed to return to 16-odd % margin in FY28.
Management indicated FY26 gross and EBITDA margins as the sweet spot to maintain going forward (FY28 framing), while also saying Q1 may be the margin bottom.
No further price hikes planned in Q1 FY27; decision to wait for raw material volatility to settle.
ESOP cost for FY27 from the Oct-24 and Feb-26 tranches expected at about INR10 crore for the full year; FY28 ESOP cost to rise as further grants are made.
Reynolds brand expected to contribute close to 10% of group revenue by FY29; management declined to guide FY28 revenue growth yet, saying it will do so in later calls.
Export share of revenue guided at 13-15% for full FY27.
capex_capacity: About 300,000 sq ft of operational area expected to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY27 at the 50-plus acre greenfield project in Umbergaon; first building possession already taken.
Adjoining land of about 11-plus acres acquired near existing facilities in Umbergaon and Jammu, to be developed.
Capex economics: target sales-to-capex ratio of about 3x; FY26 achieved about 2.7x. Facilities take 18-24 months to reach full utilisation.
Capex of about INR200-250 crore per year cited by an analyst; management did not confirm this figure.
Reynolds: asset purchase complete, Reynolds team integrated and assets moved to the Umbergaon facility. Reynolds production to start in the first phase of the new plant, targeted for end Q2 FY27.
Swiss-imported tip manufacturing machine installation under way; targets 30-40% in-house tip requirements over the current and next calendar year.
demand_pricing: Volume-led growth with domestic demand robust; strong back-to-school season.
Average price increase of 4-5% taken; industry reportedly took a similar calibrated step.
Raw material prices eased toward end-June, then rose again in the last few weeks on renewed West Asia tensions; management expects prices to cool over time.
Management chose not to take larger price hikes to protect market share and shelf space, arguing peers and unorganised players gain breathing room when leaders delay pricing.

Reynolds brand: FY26 sales about INR130-140 crore under Newell; positioned in INR10-100 pen price band, targeted at serious and professional users; may lift ASPs but not volumes, as it substitutes DOMS capacity.
Export demand soft in certain EU economies; West Asia disruptions causing longer transit, higher freight and shipment deferrals.

530305|2026-06.headline: Piccadily Q1 FY27 revenue rose 8.1% to Rs 270 crore (distillery +26.3%), while branded alco-bev grew 47.3% to Rs 82.3 crore.
530305|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose to about Rs 270.5 crore and EBITDA to Rs 47.2 crore, with margin up 30 bps to 18.5%. PAT grew 15.4% to about Rs 22 crore and EPS to Rs 2.21. Premium, super premium and luxury brands reached 43.5% of distillery revenue versus 37.8% a year earlier. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 60% company revenue growth, 60-70% branded alco-bev growth and a 23-24% EBITDA margin, with most revenue expected in H2. Chhattisgarh distillery contributed only about Rs 5 crore from roughly 15 days of production.

financial_highlights.change: +8.1% YoY as stated in prepared remarks (CFO said 18.1%)

financial_highlights.metric: Branded alco-bev (premium, super premium, luxury) revenue
Share of branded in distillery revenue

financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 87 lakh last quarter; mainly FX gain and scrap sale

segments.name: Distillery (total)
segments.commentary: Rs 205.7 crore revenue, 76% of total revenue (71% a year earlier). Segment margin fell YoY, which management attributed to cost pressure on grain and fuel and to mix shift toward lower-margin Whistler.

segments.name: Branded alco-bev (IMFL)
segments.commentary: Rs 82.3 crore, +47.3% YoY. Indri grew high double digits; Whistler grew more than 60% in the quarter; Camikara entered CSD and began contributing.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh distillery
segments.commentary: Commissioned, with about 15 days of production in Q1 and roughly Rs 5 crore revenue. Capacity is 210 KLPD; utilisation targeted at about 50% by year-end.

segments.name: Sugar division
segments.commentary: Demerger scheme filed with exchanges on 28 April 2026; process ongoing. Management expects the hive-off by year-end; company-level margin guidance includes sugar.

guidance_outlook: Branded alco-bev revenue to grow about 60-70% in FY27; H2 expected to contribute about 60-65% of annual branded revenue.
Company-level revenue growth target of about 60% YoY for FY27.
Company-level EBITDA margin of 23-24% for FY27 (includes sugar); management said full-year margin should be similar to or slightly better than FY26's 23%.
Chhattisgarh revenue guidance of Rs 300-400 crore for FY27 reiterated; Indri incremental sales guidance of Rs 250-300 crore reiterated.
Barrel inventory expected at 1.15-1.20 lakh barrels by March 2027, above the 1 lakh target.
No large capex planned for FY27 beyond ordinary-course upgrades; company does not plan to increase debt this year.
capex_capacity: Chhattisgarh distillery commissioned; about 15 days of production in Q1 and first revenue in June 2026. Capacity 210 KLPD; utilisation targeted at about 50% by March 2027.
Indri distillery expansion running at about 60% utilisation.
Malt capacity added last year (30 KL) running at about 80%.
Barrel inventory of 87,000 filled barrels (200-500 litre sizes); about 60-70 lakh litres added each year.
Management stated the company is not planning large capex this year; most heavy capex is complete.
demand_pricing: Indri growing 18-20% YoY, which management described as the only single malt growing at that pace; global single malts are growing 2-3%.
Whistler grew almost 100% last year and more than 60% this quarter; Camikara and Cashmir expected to grow in triple digits this year from a small base.
Management says it will not disclose individual brand margins and speaks only at portfolio level.
Ethanol margin about 10%; country liquor margin about 15-18%; management said branded margins are not under pressure, while distillery ex-branded faces price pressure from grain and fuel costs.
Receivables: branded receivables about Rs 170 crore (incl. excise), receivable days about 100 versus higher in March after a Rs 100 crore March sales spike.
Exports about 25% of sales; management targets a long-term 70% export / 30% domestic mix; North America is the largest export market; exports to 31 countries.
A court order in Chennai halted ethanol plants; management expects orders to resume in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 47.3% branded growth and what is the Chhattisgarh contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Indri grew high double digits, Whistler more than 60%, and Camikara began contributing via CSD. Chhattisgarh contributed about Rs 5 crore from roughly 15 days of production.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin rise only 30 bps and how are costs trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to mix, with Indri the highest-margin product. Cost pressure from grain and fuel hit the distillery segment. Employee, distribution and brand investment costs rose ahead of H2 revenue, and management expects margins to recover as revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough aged malt to support Indri growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. The company holds 87,000 filled barrels, which management called the largest in India, and sees no supply constraint for 18-20% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indri scale ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to reach top-five single malt volumes of about 0.5 million cases in 4-5 years, implying about Rs 1,200 crore Indri revenue at current prices. Current capacity supports about 8-8.5 lakh cases if all malt went to Indri.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Chhattisgarh ethanol exposure a guidance risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 300-400 crore guidance is intact and that ethanol is a stopgap; the company plans branded products from Chhattisgarh. It declined to split ethanol and alco-bev revenue until Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt fall and what is the working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 10 crore of debt was repaid in Q1. Management plans no net debt increase this year, with larger reductions from FY28 after investment in liquid and barrels. Receivable days fell to about 100.

544279|2026-06.headline: Godavari Biorefineries Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR2.6 crores (0.5% margin) as sugar-ethanol losses offset a 53% jump in bio-based chemicals EBITDA.
544279|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 4.6% YoY to INR557.9 crores and total income rose 4.9% to INR559.9 crores, but EBITDA dropped to INR2.6 crores from INR6.5 crores. Bio-based chemicals grew revenue 19.4% to INR168.7 crores with EBITDA up 53% to INR19.2 crores, while the integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol segment's EBITDA loss widened to INR14.6 crores. The company commissioned a 200 KLPD grain-based distillery at Sameerwadi, taking total distillery capacity to 800 KLPD, and announced a further INR25 crores debottlenecking investment in bio-based specialty chemicals. Consolidated net loss widened to INR19.3 crores from INR16 crores.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR6.5 crores in Q1 FY26
vs INR16 crores loss in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol revenue
financial_highlights.change: vs INR382.8 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol EBITDA
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR4.5 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Bio-based chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168.7 crores (+19.4% YoY) and EBITDA INR19.2 crores (+53%), margin 11.4% vs 8.9%, attributed to product mix and debottlenecking benefits. Management guides to about INR190 crores revenue next quarter.

segments.name: Integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR377.9 crores, flat YoY, with EBITDA loss of INR14.6 crores vs INR4.5 crores loss a year ago. Management cited feedstock conditions, higher manufacturing cost and ethanol tender allotments; better sugar realisations provided partial support.

guidance_outlook: Bio-based chemicals revenue expected at about INR190 crores in Q2 FY27, sustained thereafter.
INR25 crores debottlenecking in bio-based specialty chemicals, expected to complete by early FY28, targeting about INR240 crores quarterly revenue at full penetration.
Evaluating 160 KLPD fungible capacity addition within the existing 800 KLPD, mainly a maize grain-preparation front end; no firm timeline or return numbers given.
Debt levels expected broadly similar, with no major change in debt-equity structure.
DME pilot trial results expected by March 2027.

Triple-negative breast cancer molecule: CDSCO permission for preliminary efficacy trials hoped for by end of Q3 FY27; about INR20 crores spend over the next 2 to 3 years to reach preliminary efficacy.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 200 KLPD grain-based distillery at Sameerwadi in Q1 FY27; total distillery capacity now 800 KLPD.
Additional INR25 crores investment in debottlenecking bio-based specialty chemicals, completion expected early FY28.
Evaluating a 160 KLPD maize grain-preparation front end to use idle fermentation and distillation capacity if sugar diversion rises.
Bio-butanol: MoU with Synthomer for use as chemical intermediate; engaging on a government call for butanol pathways.
DME in pilot trials, progressing as planned.
demand_pricing: Management sees rising customer interest in bio-based specialty chemicals in India and overseas, driven by supply-chain reliability and a narrower fossil-to-green price gap.
Sugar prices have risen in recent weeks; ethanol prices from sugarcane juice unchanged for several years.
Management expects ethanol demand growth from E20 rollout and draft E85/E100 guidelines; gave no numeric volume outlook.
Grain/maize ethanol featured prominently in the current ethanol tender, per management.
Closing sugar inventory about 65,000 tonnes; management estimated 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes under long-term contracts, not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Commercialisation timeline for DME and bio-butanol?
qa_highlights.answer: DME pilot results expected by March 2027, with commercial discussion only after success. Bio-butanol has a Synthomer MoU as chemical intermediate, and the company is engaging on a government butanol initiative.

qa_highlights.question: Next milestones and out-licensing for the TNBC molecule?
qa_highlights.answer: CDSCO application filed; next milestone is permission for preliminary efficacy trials, hoped by end of Q3 FY27. Company plans to out-license after efficacy data.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of chemical margins and steady-state potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed gains to debottlenecking reaching the market; quarterly business to rise from INR169 crores to about INR190 crores next quarter and about INR240 crores after the INR25 crores debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Sugar vs ethanol prioritisation and feedstock flexibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Company will monitor sugar and juice-ethanol prices and policy allotments. If juice diverts to sugar, idle distillation capacity would be used via a 160 KLPD maize preparation front end, keeping total ethanol capacity at 800 KLPD.

qa_highlights.question: Sugar inventory monetisation and inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some stock is under long-term contracts and some is open; higher sugar prices should improve sector economics, with timing dependent on the coming season.

qa_highlights.question: Leverage, finance cost and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-equity to stay broadly similar. Priorities are the INR25 crores chemicals debottlenecking, front-end maize preparation, and INR20 crores over 30 to 33 months for drug discovery, with no fundraising planned.

risks_watch: Sugar-ethanol segment EBITDA loss widened to INR14.6 crores; feedstock cost and manufacturing cost pressure persists.
Monsoon and dam levels: management said rainfall improved recently, but El Niño risk is still being monitored.
Consolidated net loss widened to INR19.3 crores as depreciation rose.
Timing of CDSCO approval for TNBC trials and DME pilot outcomes by March 2027.
Whether the chemicals run-rate reaches about INR190 crores next quarter and INR240 crores after expansion.
Sugar-ethanol capacity diversion decisions and the 160 KLPD maize front-end investment size and returns, not yet disclosed.

544470|2026-06.headline: M&B Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.5% to INR291 crores; order book INR1,053 crores, but management withholds FY27 margin guidance for one more quarter.
544470|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew about 22.5% YoY to INR291 crores, with PAT up 22% to INR22 crores. Operating EBITDA was INR33 crores (11.4% margin) against reported EBITDA of INR36 crores. Order on hand stood at INR1,053 crores (up about 25% YoY), though Q1 order inflow of about INR260 crores was softer, which management attributed to large inquiries slipping into Q2. Freight costs (US-bound, roughly 2x to 2.5x since March) and steel prices (up 10-12%) are compressing margins, so management reiterated the 25%+ FY27 revenue growth target but declined to give a margin guide until Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Export ~1,400 MT vs ~INR3 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR1,053 crores (Phenix INR837 crores, Proflex INR216 crores)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.19 lakh YoY; vs INR1.38 lakh QoQ

segments.name: Phenix (PEB and heavy structural steel)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR214 crores, up 22% YoY; order book INR837 crores including export orders of INR278 crores to be executed mostly in FY27, about 28% dispatched to date. Sanand running at 75-80% utilisation.

segments.name: Proflex (self-supported steel roofing)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR77 crores, up 25% YoY; order book INR216 crores. Installed capacity raised to 21 lakh sq m per annum after commissioning two mobile manufacturing units.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue INR28 crores (about 1,400 MT); management guides about 15% sustainable export EBITDA at current freight, 16-18% in normal freight, versus about 11% domestic. More than 8,000 MT expected in the remaining three quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of over 25% in FY27, implying about INR1,600 crores top line.
No specific FY27 margin guidance; management targets improvement over the current 11-11.5% operating EBITDA margin but will guide at Q2 results (next quarter).
Sanand 20,000 TPA brownfield expansion (PEB capacity 72,000 to 92,000 TPA) commissioning in October 2026, benefits in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion of 20,000 TPA to start this fiscal, completion Q3 FY28; total capacity about 1,54,000-1,55,000 TPA.
Over 20% CAGR over the next three to four years in the medium-term plan, with progressive profitability improvement.
Targeted PEB volume of 85,000-90,000 MT in FY27 versus 72,000 MT last year.
capex_capacity: Sanand PEB brownfield: +20,000 TPA, commissioning October 2026; PEB capacity to 92,000 TPA.

INR30 crores fully automated heavy structural steel processing line at Sanand, adding 10,000 tons to existing 12,000 tons; operational by Q1 FY28. Board approved an additional heavy structural expansion at Sanand.

Cheyyar (South India) is AISC certified, enabling exports to US West Coast via Pacific route from next fiscal; brownfield expansion of 20,000 TPA to complete in Q3 FY28; utilisation targeted at about 60% this fiscal.
Proflex installed capacity 21 lakh sq m per annum after two mobile manufacturing units.
2.5 MW ground-mounted captive solar plant in Gujarat under development.
Third plant site under evaluation in North India; to be announced once finalised.
demand_pricing: Q1 order inflow about INR260 crores; management says large inquiries have rubber-banded into Q2. Management cites an INR4,000 crore Phenix inquiry pipeline and about INR200 crores in Proflex.
Hit rate of 12-15% over the last five years, with a stated policy of protecting margins over chasing volume; peers reportedly near 20%.
60-70% of customers are repeat customers.
Freight costs to US roughly 2-2.5x March levels (USD10,000-12,000 per 40ft container); US Section 232 duty cut from 50% to 25%; US steel up about 10-12% since March; domestic freight up 2-5%.
Roughly 80-85% of raw material is booked at order booking; 15-20% is left open to price variation. Domestic PEB margins down 1-2% due to inflation.
Management says domestic market share is about 10-12%, targeting 15% over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 order inflow weak at about INR260 crores versus the INR100 crore/month run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Malav Patel said inflow was up 25% YoY; large inquiries took longer on design freeze and have rubber-banded into Q2. Management says the run rate of about INR100 crores of PEB per month is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export margin and how much does freight affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Majmudar said the balance INR278 crores export order book yields about 15% EBITDA at peak freight, 16-17% in a better scenario; domestic is about 11%, so the gap has narrowed to about 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Phenix realisation per MT fall QoQ to INR1.25 lakh from INR1.38 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah attributed it to export mix (under 10%) and project-specific bought-out items, not price cuts; management expects full-year comparability.

qa_highlights.question: Why was domestic PEB realisation flat despite higher steel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah said domestic tonnage rose about 6.6% and revenue 7.6%; raw material cost was about 0.5% lower YoY and product mix (primary vs sheeting) drove the gap. Higher steel costs will show in orders booked at current prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will Cheyyar capacity come in Q1/Q2 FY28 or Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Malav Patel said the Cheyyar 20,000 TPA expansion comes in Q3 FY28, giving two effective quarters in FY28; Sanand's additional capacity arrives in Q3-Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a specific range, saying it will give guidance after one more quarter; the target is to improve over the current 11-11.5% operating margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the win rate on bids?
qa_highlights.answer: Chirag Patel said the win rate is 10-12%, up to 12-15% depending on order; large customers take longer to finalise engineering.

537259|2026-06.headline: Suyog Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR710 mn (+6.1% YoY on electricity-inclusive basis), net profit INR145 mn; Vodafone Idea rollout began mid-June with 150 tenancies converted.
537259|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR710 mn, up 6.1% YoY against INR668 mn restated for electricity, with EBITDA of INR420 mn (59.3% margin) and PBT of INR195 mn. From 1 April the company began including electricity reimbursement in revenue after a GST-related guidance change, which lowered the reported EBITDA margin from about 70% to 59.3%. Vodafone Idea orders started flowing around 15-16 June; 95 towers (150 tenancies) were converted in June. Management said most growth will show from Q2 onwards, with the full benefit in FY28. Net profit margin was about 20% against 25% a year ago, which management attributed to a vendor-provision reversal in the prior-year quarter.

segments.name: Tower / IP1 infrastructure (India)
segments.commentary: Exit Q1 FY27 with 6,103 towers and 7,468 tenancies; tenancy ratio about 1.2x. Q1 additions were mainly macro sites, with a few kilometres of fibre laid.

segments.name: Fibre
segments.commentary: Management expects fibre at 5-8% of total revenue in FY27, with no major jump this year.

guidance_outlook: Target of 3,000 Vodafone Idea tenancies in FY27 (described as conservative); about 35-40% expected in H1 and 60% in H2. Management also cited ~850 tenancies in hand (150 done plus 700+ open).
Revenue per tower to be about INR31,000 ex-electricity; about INR50,000 per site with electricity per management's arithmetic.
EBITDA margin (with electricity) guided at around 59%, to be maintained in coming quarters; PAT margin to stay around 20%.

Management aims for INR100 crore quarterly revenue (INR400 crore annualised) from Q4 and PAT growth from ~22% to 24%, per the MD. The CFO flagged that Ind AS rent accounting mutes EBITDA margin in early years.
Tenancy ratio target of 1.8x by end FY28 or early FY29.
Vodafone Idea FY28 target of about 5,000 further sites; Vodafone share of revenue targeted at 30-32% once the 3,000 sites are delivered.
capex_capacity: Zinc battery: sourced from GBB Batteries (Kerala plant) rather than manufactured in-house; first batch of 10-15 sites expected by mid-September, with a 100H unit at about INR33,000 vs INR48,000 for lithium (up ~50% in about 2.5 months).
Zinc battery expected to lower CapEx and some operating costs; management said it would be the first IP company in telecom to deploy it on sites.
Funding: management said internal accruals and bank funds cover the planned rollout. No fundraise decided; may come in Q2/Q3 if orders exceed plan.

BSNL: about 186 sites with pending billing from a prior ~1,000-site batch; expected to resume revenue in Q2 if Tejas equipment issues are resolved. No new BSNL projects booked until billing is confirmed.
demand_pricing: Vodafone Idea: about 45,000-site rollout plan over 18-24 months (3,000-3,500 per month); INR6,400 cr secured from SBI, with a further INR25,000-30,000 cr under discussion. Vodafone currently plans about 12,000 sites through September, and management expects roughly 30,000 in FY27.
Airtel and Jio not doing major rollouts per management. BSNL announced INR77,000 cr capex for 2 lakh sites over 5 years, but no new BSNL work is being taken until billing is confirmed.
Revenue share (per management): Airtel 48.1%, Vi 27%, Jio 22.6%, BSNL 2.3%.
MSAs with all operators are blanket frameworks with no fixed volume commitment; a 10-year lock-in with Vodafone was cited.
Sharing mix: 80% anchor and 20% shared on new Vodafone sites; macro sites carry tenancy ratios of 2-3x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the zinc battery project, its cost, and its margin and revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Zinc battery is bought from GBB Batteries, not manufactured in-house. Management said it cuts CapEx (100H unit at INR33,000 vs INR48,000 lithium) with no quantified EBITDA impact given.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence and breakdown of the 3,000 Vodafone tenancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident. It sees 850 tenancies in hand (150 done, 700+ open), expects 35-40% in H1 and 60% in H2, and says 80% will be on new towers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BSNL no longer being pushed in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not commit BSNL volumes until billing is confirmed. Tejas equipment issues have delayed BSNL rollouts by 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin fall from 25% to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year quarter included a vendor-provision reversal from Vi; management says the underlying margin is about 20-21% with electricity included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Vodafone target fall from 12,000 to about 10,500 tenancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 3,000 figure is conservative and tied to funds already secured; the target will rise as Vodafone confirms more funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tenancy ratio path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ratio is about 1.2x; target is 1.8x by end FY28 or early FY29, since macro sites carry 2-3 tenancies with recovery in 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are fibre's share and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Fibre is 5-8% of revenue and stays at that level in FY27; management says it is 100% recurring and carries a similar EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 189/186-site BSNL billing status?
qa_highlights.answer: 186 sites are still pending billing; management expects revenue from them to start in Q2.

risks_watch: Vodafone Idea funding: the 3,000-tenancy target depends on further SBI and consortium funds of INR25,000-30,000 cr; management says it will only raise its own targets once those are confirmed.
BSNL: 186 sites billing pending, Tejas equipment issues unresolved, and no firm rollout date.
Monsoon season may slow Q2 conversions.
Lithium battery costs up ~50% in 2.5 months; zinc battery first batch due mid-September and not yet proven on sites.
Funding: management is not ruling out a fundraise; the earlier call suggested one could come, and the analyst flagged this as an open question.
Margin optics: electricity reimbursement now in revenue, so margins are not comparable with prior periods, and the CFO flagged Ind AS rent accounting as muting EBITDA in early years.

financial_highlights.value: INR420 mn (59.3% margin, incl. electricity in revenue)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR418 mn in Q4 FY26 and INR411 mn in Q1 FY26
