500870|2026-06.headline: Castrol India Q2 CY26 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR1,871 crore and EBITDA 41% YoY to INR494 crore, helped by inventory benefits and pricing.
500870|2026-06.overview: Castrol India reported strong Q2 (April–June 2026) with revenue from operations of INR1,871 crore (+25% YoY, +21% QoQ), EBITDA of INR494 crore (+41% YoY and QoQ) and PAT of INR348 crore (+43% YoY). Growth was described as broad-based across consumer, industrial and institutional businesses, with two price increases in January–June 2026 and some benefit from older, lower-cost inventory. Management said cost inflation from supply disruptions and commodity volatility began to hit late in the quarter and will be more visible in Q3. The company declared an interim dividend of INR6.25 per share.

segments.name: Consumer (B2C, retail/auto care)
segments.commentary: Broad-based volume growth driven by rural operations and urban premiumisation; POWER1 (premium motorcycle) grew ahead of rest of business. Rural business growing at double digits; rural outlets ~45,000.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Growing at high double digits over last couple of years; about 15% of overall business per CFO. Growth from advanced solutions and expanded customer base.

segments.name: Institutional / B2B (OEMs)
segments.commentary: Works with OEMs such as Tata Motors and Maruti; growth tied to OEM volumes. No separate figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin management framework remains 21%–24%; pricing actions are set to keep margins within this band.
Commodity and feedstock inflation expected to become more visible in Q3 FY27, with some raw material increases expected to spill over into Q3.
Management says price actions taken so far are sufficient to offset raw material increases from Q2, but will take further pricing if base oil or FX move adversely.
Lubricant industry expected to grow 3%–4%; company aims to grow at about 2x market.
Capex of about INR100 crore per year, roughly half in manufacturing and half in market (dealer/workshop visibility).
Sourcing guidance of ~55% domestic / ~45% imported broadly unchanged, with quarterly tactical variation.
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR100 crore, split roughly equally between manufacturing (health, safety, capacity) and in-market investments.
Silvassa plant was shut for a few days in July 2026 due to heavy rain; fully back up with operating levels at Q2 peak per management.
Paharpur and Silvassa plants completed 9 years and 3 years respectively without significant recordable incident.

National footprint of ~160,000 outlets; auto care range in 40,000 outlets; 34,000 independent motorcycle workshops and 16,000 car workshops; 850 Castrol Auto Service (CAS) outlets; 950 rural service express units.
Building capabilities for specialised EV fluids and data-centre cooling fluids; data-centre business not yet material.
demand_pricing: Two price increases taken in January–June 2026 (late Q1 and Q2), in the low double-digit percentage range; pricing aimed at offsetting supply chain volatility and inflation.
Volume growth described as broad-based across consumer and industrial; company declined to disclose absolute volume (million litres) for the quarter, departing from past practice of sharing it.
Competitor reportedly took around 4 price increases between March and July 2026; management said it will not follow competitor pricing blindly and is guided by RM outlook and margin band.
Group III base oil prices elevated, impacted by Middle East crisis.
Inventory: about half of raw materials bought locally and half from international suppliers; company says it runs lean inventory and that Q2 benefited from older, cheaper inventory being consumed.
E20 fuel: most passenger car brands already compliant; impact on lubricants seen as limited to engine-level fuel-choice issues.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the open offer linked to the BP/Stonepeak Castrol global divestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the deal is progressing but is large and multi-country; open offer timing depends on deal closure, after which SEBI and shareholder notifications and prescribed timelines apply. No timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs pricing split and Silvassa flood impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is broad-based but no specific figures given; price increases were in low double digits. Silvassa plant was halted briefly in July for safety and is now at peak operating levels, with no impact.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said older inventory bought at softer prices was consumed in the quarter, benefiting margins; it declined to quantify and said profitability grew healthily even excluding this.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No fixed payout percentage; dividend yield usually around 5% including interim and final; special dividends given occasionally. Interim window was advanced this year. Past three years' payout has been in the 80%–90% range per the questioner, which management did not confirm as policy.

qa_highlights.question: Why are price hikes not enough to offset Q3 raw material cost, given diesel prices fell after June?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing was modelled on inventory and FX scenarios for Q2 and H2; current pricing is seen as broadly reflecting Q3 costs, but the environment is volatile and further price action is possible. Structural cost reductions are also underway.

qa_highlights.question: OCI loss of ~INR66 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a fair-value revaluation of the Ki Mobility investment made about 4 years ago, using listed comparable companies, reviewed every six months; expected to move up and down with peers.

risks_watch: Commodity and base oil (Group III) cost inflation expected to hit Q3 margins more visibly; margin band 21%–24%.
Foreign exchange movements affecting input costs.
Possible volume trade-off or downtrading from the price increases, especially with competitor pricing reportedly higher.
Dependence on Silvassa plant and monsoon/weather disruptions.
Pending BP/Stonepeak divestment of Castrol global, with open offer timing uncertain.
Lack of volume disclosure reduces visibility into volume vs price split.
500870|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and the broad-based growth story, but cautious on the outlook, citing inflation, volatility and monsoon conditions. Management was evasive on volume figures, inventory gain quantification, the open offer timeline and data-centre revenue.
key_quotes: And this is in context of a very volatile operating environment marked by supply disruptions and commodity cost inflation.
We, therefore, expect the impact of commodity and feedstock inflation to become more visible in the third quarter.
I think we pride ourselves on a very lean inventory profile.

519552|2026-09.headline: Heritage Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% to INR13,196 million, with EBITDA margin at 5.6%, up 98 bps QoQ despite milk procurement cost up 11% YoY.
519552|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 revenue grew 19% YoY to INR13,196 million and H1 grew 18% to INR26,577 million. EBITDA was INR740 million (5.6% margin), up 98 bps sequentially, while PAT was INR309 million. Landed milk procurement cost rose 11% YoY to INR47.73/litre, and management passed through about 8% weighted average price increase, with a larger hike taken in September that benefits Q3. Management expects further procurement inflation in Q3 and is watching the post-Diwali buffalo flush.

financial_highlights.change: Margin +98 bps QoQ vs Q1; ~4.6% to 5.6% per management

financial_highlights.metric: VAP share of revenue (ex ghee & butter)
Broader VAP incl. consumer ghee & butter

segments.name: Core milk
segments.commentary: Milk sales volume +2% YoY to 12.35 lakh litres/day in Q2 (H1 +1% to 11.99 lakh L/day). Price up ~6% in Q2, with milk alone taken up ~6%.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Lassi volumes +89%, buttermilk +56%, ice cream +44%, paneer +21%, curd +15% in Q2. Curd daily sales crossed 500 tonnes; Nourish+ paneer >15% of paneer portfolio.

segments.name: Ice cream / Get-A-Way
segments.commentary: New ice cream facility commissioned; Heritage supplies 3,272 litres/day to Get-A-Way (71% stake). Own ice cream revenue expected at INR170-180 crore this year vs ~INR110 crore last year.

segments.name: Heritage Novandie (LIVO yogurt)
segments.commentary: Now wholly owned; management says LIVO is among top 5 yogurt brands in India. No financials given.

segments.name: Heritage Nutrivet (Animal Nutrition)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR853 million (+47%) and PBT INR37 million; H1 revenue INR1,581 million (+42%) and PBT INR56 million. Cattle feed sales up 47% YoY in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Q3 price benefit expected: September price hikes were well above the 8% Q2 weighted average and will accrue in Q3; October opened at higher consumer price levels than Q2.
Management expects procurement prices to rise in Q3 at around 11% YoY, though it hopes for post-Diwali cooling as buffalo flush arrives; no firm view on raw milk direction.
Operating leverage expected to improve in Q3 over Q2, which was better than Q1; depreciation from recently capitalised projects weighing on PBT/PAT.
Value-added product share expected to keep expanding in Q3; first 15 days of Q3 showed continuing trend and ghee volume growth expected to be strong in Q3 on festive timing.
Management indicated a Rs 0.5/litre fall in procurement price would add about 0.7% to bottom line (~INR3 crore per month).
Ice cream target of INR500 crore revenue in 6-7 years from commissioning.
capex_capacity: New ice cream facility commissioned in the quarter, supporting Alpenvie and Get-A-Way volumes.
Several large projects capitalised at start of FY27; higher depreciation is weighing on PBT and PAT.
Procurement base ~1.8 million litres/day per management; procurement volume 17.28 lakh L/day in Q2 (+7% YoY).
Company operates a wind farm of 6.3 MW (3 turbines), which won an Indian Wind Power Association award for FY26.
demand_pricing: Weighted average price increase ~8% in Q2 (milk ~6%, VAP ~9-10%), staggered across July-September; curd premium variants taken up 15%+, and the 1 kg curd pack is the fastest-growing curd segment.
Core dairy revenue growth ~17%, of which ~49 percentage points from price and ~51 from volume.
Ghee revenue up close to 20%; ghee volumes flat in Q2 due to festive timing. Ghee, paneer and curd are 90%+ of VAP sales per management.

Competition: new large conglomerate entering drinkable dairy after ice cream; management sees organised dairy at INR5-5.5 lakh crore with Amul at INR75-80k crore and Heritage at ~INR5,000 crore, and argues more organised players expand the category.
Karnataka government (Nandini/KMF) to raise consumer price INR8/litre from 1 November, passing INR6 to farmers; Heritage has meaningful Bangalore volumes and expects pricing upside there.
Aavin raised farm-gate procurement price from INR38 to INR44/litre in steps, roughly INR6/litre, which management described as unprecedented.
Cow milk procurement inflation outpacing buffalo as producers switch to cow milk; buffalo supply constrained by monsoon/El Nino.

544647|2026-06.headline: Nephrocare Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.7% YoY to INR282 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 30.7% to INR65 crore and margin at 23.1%.
544647|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 23.7% YoY to INR282 crore on 13% higher guest count (38,262) and 13.3% more treatments (10.3 lakh). Adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to INR65.1 crore, with margin up about 120-125 bps, mainly from a 175 bps lower COGS-to-revenue ratio that management attributed to procurement scale. Adjusted PAT rose 41.7% to INR37 crore. Management reiterated 15-20% medium-term growth guidance, while the Saudi tender remains an investment-phase drag of roughly INR3 crore per quarter on the JV line.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (after ESOP and Saudi JV add-backs)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR43 crore in Q1 FY26
down 133 bps QoQ, up YoY; includes ECL provision of 2-2.5% of revenue

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: 19 clinics added in Q1 (mix of PPP in Bihar, four private, and one or two greenfield); India RPT about $22-23. Management said it will not pursue PPP contracts below return thresholds and exited two Uttarakhand PPP clinics as value dilutive. Tamil Nadu PPP contract signed.

segments.name: Philippines
segments.commentary: 7 clinics added in Q1 (7 acquisitions, towards quarter end), taking the count to 50 clinics across 39 cities; management says it is the second-largest network with about 6-7% share of about 900 standalone clinics. Average centre size is 10-12 beds.

segments.name: International (overall)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 45% of revenue, up from about 30% a year and a half earlier. Uzbekistan is the only private operator, servicing about 1,800 of roughly 9,000 patients.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia
segments.commentary: First clinic at Riyadh Hospital operational in July; home dialysis started; medical operator licence obtained; tender RFI response submitted. Still in investment phase with JV losses of about INR3 crore cited by analysts; no tender documents issued yet.

segments.name: Kazakhstan
segments.commentary: Subsidiary incorporated in Q1 to evaluate Kazakhstan and Central Asia; no revenue or timeline yet. Price points around $75 noted in the market.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth guidance of 15-20% over the next three to five years maintained.
Expansion plan: 40-50 clinics a year in India, 10-15 clinics a year in the Philippines, and a new international market every 12-18 months; management does not give capex guidance.
Saudi tender formal process expected to begin in a couple of months; management sees three to four quarters before benefits or clear visibility; no guidance on JV losses.
Tax rate of about 20% offered as a proxy for the year (India and Philippines at 25%, Uzbekistan at 0% if healthcare revenue exceeds 90%).
NIDA renal nurse academy first batch to begin training in Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of INR44 crore towards centre acquisitions and growth, vs INR43 crore a year earlier.

Depreciation life for machines is 7-10 years depending on country and regulation; RFID asset tracking reduced India depreciation, and about 50 machines a month of replacement activity was paused in the last three months.
Philippines acquisitions generate goodwill split into intangibles amortised over 5-7 years, adding to D&A.

Dialysis is a fixed-capacity business: about three cycles per machine per day; management says network growth comes from adding capacity, and clinics at about 85% utilisation need spare capacity for unplanned guests.
Management says the Philippines greenfield cost about 4 million per bed (referenced by an analyst) and declined to give acquisition cost per bed.
demand_pricing: India is still early in its dialysis market life cycle; management puts the organised (pure-play) share at about 20-22%, with 78-80% still hospital-run.
More than 300 private hospitals partner with NephroPlus on a built-own-operate model, where hospitals provide space and utilities and NephroPlus funds equipment.
Price increases are lumpy: CGHS raised rates about 35% in October 2025 after roughly 10-11 years; PhilHealth raised rates by 55-60% in October 2024.
RPT growth of about 11% CAGR was driven mainly by the international mix; management cautioned that the CAGR will not persist.
Management declined to split revenue or same-centre growth by country, saying it reports at platform level only.
75%+ of clinics are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities; India operates in 300+ cities across 25 states.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from international mix versus cost efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said COGS fell 175 bps as a share of revenue, driven by taking India procurement scale to other markets and by utilisation and supplier terms, not only reuse counts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise YoY, and how did they move QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell 133 bps QoQ. Drivers were ECL provisions of 2-2.5% of revenue (KPMG-assisted model), public-company costs such as audit and legal fees, and upfront business development spend for new international markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did D&A decline QoQ despite Philippines acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited RFID-based asset tracking that cut machine replacements (about 50 a month previously) and a one-time benefit, partly offset by goodwill amortisation from seven Philippines acquisitions late in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi breakeven path and cost exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi is a binary tender market with four clusters; management does not give clinic-count breakeven and said further investment will depend on tender terms. Tender timelines are uncertain, and the company may not win.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose country-level or same-centre growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined, saying it manages capital at platform level and that dialysis growth comes from adding capacity rather than same-store price and volume.

534600|2026-06.headline: JTL Industries Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR722 crore with EBITDA INR59 crore (8.1% margin) and volumes up 17.8% YoY to 118,513 MT.
534600|2026-06.overview: JTL Industries reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA in Q1 FY27, with revenue of INR722 crore, EBITDA of INR59 crore and PAT of INR35 crore (4.9% margin). PAT absorbed INR2.8 crore of extra non-cash depreciation from the March 2026 revaluation at JTL Defence. Operational EBITDA per ton excluding other income was INR4,954, which management attributed to product mix and efficiency; it said JTL Defence added about INR200 per ton to consolidated figures. Management reiterated FY27 volume growth of at least 30%, with Mangaon capacity expansion of about 1 million tons targeted by end H1 and capex of about INR100 crore left to reach 2 million tons.

financial_highlights.change: Margin 4.9%; after INR2.8 crore extra depreciation from JTL Defence revaluation

financial_highlights.metric: Operational EBITDA per ton (ex other income)

segments.name: JTL Industries (steel tubes and pipes)
segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton about INR4,750 excluding JTL Defence; DFT structural pipes now running at 20,000-25,000 tons per quarter, roughly double the prior ~10,000 tons. Mangaon facility utilisation about 42%.

segments.name: JTL Defence (ex-RCI Industries & Technologies)
segments.commentary: Run rate about 100 MT/month in Q1, with about 120 MT in the first month of Q2. Q1 EBITDA margin about 12%, versus about 20% in Q4 which included inventory gains. Management targets 500 MT/month by Q4 FY27 and INR150 crore top line this year.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA per ton: JTL Steel tube and pipe segment ~INR4,750 seen as sustainable; management confident of reaching INR5,000 consolidated in coming quarters; FY27 target had been ~INR4,500.
FY27 volume growth of at least 30% reiterated; H2 expected stronger than H1, and management aims to exceed 30%.
Company utilisation ~55% now, targeted ~65% by year-end FY27; Mangaon utilisation to rise toward ~60%.

Capacity: ~7 lakh tons to be commissioned by end H1 FY27; remaining 3 lakh tons (API pipes) by about the same time next year. Full utilisation by FY29; utilisation 50-60% in FY29; peak ~70% possibly FY29-FY30.
Peak revenue potential on the current capex cycle: ~1.4 million tons at ~INR65,000/ton, about INR9,100 crore (management's arithmetic).
Value-added share target of 50-60% of products once the 2 million ton capacity is complete.
Export target of 10% of total sales for coming quarters; export order book of about INR75 crore.
Capex: ~INR100 crore in FY27 to complete the expansion, then maintenance capex of INR30-40 crore a year; JTL Defence capex about INR15 crore this year and similar next year.
FY28 working capital cycle target of 35-40 days.
JTL Defence EBITDA margin long-term 15%; 10-15% band expected over time, with near-term wavering likely.
capex_capacity: Current capacity about 1 million tons; expansion to 2 million tons planned, with about 7 lakh tons commissioning by end H1 FY27.
Mangaon facility utilisation about 42%; producing about 7,000-10,000 tons of DFT a quarter there, with room to double.
Remaining INR100 crore of capex in FY27 completes the expansion; maintenance capex INR30-40 crore a year after that.
JTL Defence: capacity about 1,000 tons/month on the hot plant; INR15 crore capex in FY27 for coin and bullet shell lines, which changes product mix rather than capacity.
demand_pricing: Secondary demand described as record-breaking; primary-secondary spread ranged INR8-12/kg in Q1 (versus a normal INR4-5/kg), and management says it remains at that level.
Company has about 45-50% capacity allocated to the secondary market; dealer network contributes 50-60% of sales, with 7-8 day dealer payment cycles.
Government share of sales fell to under 5% last year from over 25% earlier; company deliberately shifting to dealers and exports, with DFT sold direct to bodies such as MMRDA and airport authorities.
Exports affected by Hormuz-related container and logistics shortages; company received ACRS certification (mainly Australia) and has started shipments to the US, Mexico and Canada.
July 2026 described as an all-time high month; management expects another record quarter.
Gaining share in DFT, specialised high-diameter/high-thickness products, and seamless-pipe replacement for hydraulic and automotive OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR5,000 per ton EBITDA a one-off or structural, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said JTL Defence added about INR200/ton; ex-Defence EBITDA was about INR4,750/ton, and INR5,000 consolidated is expected in coming quarters on the back of product mix and normalised HRC.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% volume growth guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said H2 will be stronger and it expects to exceed 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity ramp and utilisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: 7 lakh tons by end H1; the remaining 3 lakh tons (API pipes) by about the same time next year. Utilisation 50-60% in FY29; peak about 70%, possibly FY29 or FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential at peak utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1.4 million tons at INR65,000-66,000/ton, roughly INR9,100 crore on the current capex cycle.

qa_highlights.question: JTL Defence guidance and run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Run rate about 100 MT/month in Q1, about 120 MT in the first month of Q2; target 500 MT/month by Q4 FY27. Long-term margin 15%, with 10-15% expected over time.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Cycle down to about 75 days from 90; target 35-40 days by FY28, helped by dealer financing and a shift away from government receivables.

540403|2026-06.headline: CL Educate Q1 FY27: revenue fell about ₹17.5 crore QoQ-type decline offset by ₹18 crore cost cuts, lifting EBITDA margin ~218 bps to 16.6%, though still loss-making after tax.
540403|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 revenue was weak, with a decline of about ₹17.5 crore on a full-quarter basis, but operational and overhead cost cuts of about ₹18 crore (₹9.3 crore service delivery, ₹8.7 crore fixed overheads) kept EBITDA marginally above Q1 FY26 and margin at about 16.6%. After-tax profit remained negative due to interest and depreciation. Test prep (EdTech L&D) revenue fell about 15% to ₹45 crore from ₹53 crore amid MBA market churn, while DEX digital assessments revenue fell about 17% on a base effect and ₹4.7 crore of deferred revenue. Management framed Q1 as the seasonally weakest quarter and guided to Q2 and Q3 recovery for MarTech and DEX.

financial_highlights.change: up about 218 bps YoY (call also cites ~340 bps in EdTech context)

financial_highlights.value: about ₹18 crore (₹9.3 crore service delivery + ₹8.7 crore fixed overheads)

financial_highlights.change: down ~15% from ₹53 crore; EBITDA down ~13%, margin up ~60 bps

segments.name: EdTech – Test Prep (L&D)
segments.commentary: Revenue down ~15% to about ₹45 crore from ₹53 crore; EBITDA down ~13% with margin up ~60 bps. Volume decline from market churn not offset by price; franchise mix rising.

segments.name: DEX – Digital Assessments
segments.commentary: Revenue down ~17% YoY; EBITDA down ~4.3%. Drivers: ~₹6 crore rollover exams in Q1 FY26 and ₹4.7 crore revenue pending customer result declarations, expected in Q2. Won nine contracts worth ~₹34 crore TCV, ~₹22 crore to execute this year.

segments.name: MarTech
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~₹7 crore (about 3.8%-7% cited); EBITDA up ~32-35%; margin up ~180 bps. Technology business ~10% of revenue last year, targeted at 13-15% this year. Q2 is largest season.

segments.name: EasyApply (platform monetisation)
segments.commentary: Adoption widened to most management institutes and exams except IIMs; new admission cycle started with 'extremely positive' traction in first 15 days. Q1 is seasonally slow.

guidance_outlook: Management expects significant change in parameters across Q2 and Q3 as seasonally heavy quarters for MarTech and DEX.
VIRSA revenue growth targeted at 45-50% for FY27.
Target to return to near-zero net debt within 36 months; strategic discussions with global and Indian players may surface in next two quarters.
Preference share redemption (DEX acquisition RPS) expected to complete within August 2026 after NCLT approval in July.
Overhead cost rationalisation to continue reflecting in Q2 and Q3 before tapering.
Management aims to expand EBITDA margin YoY on a quarterly basis; MarTech and DEX operate at 25-30% EBITDA margin per management.
capex_capacity: Depreciation rose ~28% after fixed-asset additions toward end of Q4 FY26.
DEX technology roadmap: 60-70% of FY27 technology projects complete (examination engine, cyber/IT security, network layer, node expansion).
BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) and on-device app-based testing being rolled out to expand DEX business modes.
Centralised monitoring (NOC/SOC plus a Mumbai surveillance layer) for remote proctoring at DEX.
demand_pricing: DEX pricing is per seat/candidate; 60-65% of DEX business is government tenders (techno-commercial, L1 pricing risk), 30-35% non-tender.
DEX revenue recognised per exam/contract, typically at exam conduct and/or results declaration; generally no advance payments.

Test prep: MBA segment in significant market churn; BBA/IPM described as growth segment; free online resources and AI adoption cited as headwinds. Franchise share rising, supporting average realisation.
MarTech pipeline described as robust for Q2 and Q3; VIRSA pilots with Salesforce, Dell and Infosys moving to scaled deployment; Singapore/US empanelment expected by end Q2 or early Q3 (90-150 days).
Management sees exam rationalisation and digitisation (CBT, multiple slots) as potential opportunities for DEX and consolidation across assessment and test prep over 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How will exam rationalisation and the NTA/Nilekani task force affect DEX, and what is its near and medium term growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects exam digitisation and consolidation (possibly into SAT/GMAT/GRE-like exams) with some opportunities emerging and others disappearing; timing is 12-24 months and too early to quantify. Management sees enrolment growth of ~60% over nine years as expanding the addressable market.

qa_highlights.question: Could NTA build in-house proctoring software to mitigate malpractice, and how does DEX compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued few players have DEX-level secure, AI-enabled, real-time remote proctoring with control-room monitoring, and sees tighter scrutiny as an opportunity for credible providers.

qa_highlights.question: How is BBA/IPM performing in test prep, and what is the impact of PhysicsWallah's AI content?
qa_highlights.answer: Gautam Puri said BBA/IPM is a growth segment with more five-year programmes, and that AI content generation has been in use for 1.5-2 years; PhysicsWallah targets the lower end while CL focuses on mid-to-upper segments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Target to be near net-zero debt within 36 months; scheduled repayments on track; acquisition loan reduced from ₹210 crore to ₹174 crore. Accelerated repayment possible if surplus cash arises, but MarTech and DEX need cash for expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How does DEX pricing work and how sensitive is it to price changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is per seat/candidate; over 60% of business is government tenders awarded on techno-commercial basis, where CL usually wins on technology (T1) but can lose on lowest price (L1).

qa_highlights.question: How is VIRSA progressing in Singapore and North America?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilots with Salesforce and Dell moved to recurring campaigns; Infosys scaling from pilot to multi-division in India; Singapore/US empanelment underway; pilots with Deloitte, PwC, Elastic and AWS; management targets 45-50% VIRSA revenue growth for FY27.

544262|2026-06.headline: Manba Finance Q1 FY27: NII up 36% YoY to INR42 crore, PAT up 36% to INR13 crore, AUM up 22% YoY to INR1,731 crore.
544262|2026-06.overview: Manba Finance reported Q1 FY27 NII of INR42 crore (+36% YoY) and PAT of INR13 crore (+36% YoY), with AUM of INR1,731 crore (+22% YoY) and disbursements of INR226 crore (+37% YoY). Asset quality was stated as stable, with GNPA at 3.41% and NNPA at 2.52%, and ECL provisions of INR25 crore against an IRAC requirement of INR7.57 crore. Management reiterated 35-40% AUM growth guidance for FY27, entered South India via Namma Loan (Sreesastha) in Karnataka, and launched LAP for MSMEs and battery replacement finance for e-3W. Capital adequacy stood at 24.40%, with management planning to raise INR100 crore of preference capital by September or October.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited decline from ~29.81% in FY25; not disputed by management

financial_highlights.value: INR25 crore vs IRAC requirement INR7.57 crore
INR0.25 per share (face value INR10) for FY27

segments.name: Product mix (AUM)
segments.commentary: Two-wheeler 84.1%, top-up loans 5.1%, three-wheeler 3.1%, used vehicle loans 1.5%; management says over 95% of portfolio is secured. Management targets two-wheeler share falling to 75-77% by end FY27 and ~65% within three years.

segments.name: Asset quality (Stage-wise)
segments.commentary: Stage 1 assets INR1,619 crore (93.55%), Stage 2 INR53 crore (3.4%), gross Stage 3 INR59 crore (3.41%); Stage 2 reported lower QoQ.

segments.name: Namma Loan (Sreesastha) South entry
segments.commentary: Partnership operating as BC partner with 100% Manba funding; disbursements started in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu to follow within FY27; FY27 AUM target INR60-75 crore; breakeven expected in 9-12 months.

segments.name: MSME LAP
segments.commentary: Disbursement started in Q1 FY27; ticket size INR8-20 lakh; expected ~2-3% of AUM by FY27 end.

segments.name: Battery replacement finance (e-3W)
segments.commentary: Launched for existing e-3W customers, ticket size ~INR60,000, offered with OEM tie-ups; to be opened to wider market later.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth of 35-40% for FY27, reiterated by management.
ROA target around 3.5% for FY27, supported by higher-yield personal loan, top-up and used two-wheeler mix (~30% of further lending at higher IRR).
NIM expected in the 13-14% range.
PAT growth expected to remain similar to historical performance; no explicit quarterly numbers given.
Raise INR100 crore of preference capital by September or latest October 2026.
No new northern states planned in FY27; focus on UP, MP, part of Rajasthan and South expansion.
Seasonality: AUM expected to jump in Q2 (festivals) and especially Q3 (Dussehra, Diwali).
capex_capacity: Operating in 130 locations across seven states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, and Karnataka just started); 1,700+ dealers; ~1,950 employees, 1,000+ in sales.
Proprietary tech (LOS, LMS, LAS) claimed at ~90% of tech and software; MSME LAP uses vendor-owned software (first such).
Planning considerably higher tech spend this year on personal loan software; management said overall tech spend as a share of expenses to stay in a similar range.
Wants to reach 15% market share in new states within four years; claims 12-14% share in mature states.
Collection: ~600 people, 85% of collections in-house.
demand_pricing: Disbursement up 37% YoY to INR226 crore; management said disbursement growth of ~35% continuing in the current quarter.
Sanction speed: over 60% of loans sanctioned in one minute; 92% same-day sanctions.
Funding: cost of borrowing 10.86%, borrowing mix ~60% term loans, ~25% NCDs, balance PTC and cash credit.
Liquidity was ~INR350 crore at 31 March 2026; company raised INR100-150 crore in Q1 and held ~INR200 crore liquidity, which management linked to higher borrowing cost.

qa_highlights.question: Capital adequacy has fallen from ~29.81% to ~25-26%; will capital be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it anticipated the need and will raise INR100 crore by September or October, in the form of preference shares, to fund growth.

qa_highlights.question: What share of AUM will LAP/MSME reach by FY27 end, and what are ticket size and customer profile?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP expected at 2-3% of AUM by FY27 end; ticket size INR8-20 lakh targeting shop-owning businessmen.

qa_highlights.question: Which products will reduce two-wheeler dependence?
qa_highlights.answer: Personal loans, top-up loans (after vintage maturity), used two-wheeler loans, three-wheeler loans via TVS all-India tie-up, and small business loans (~INR6-7 crore disbursed monthly) and MSME LAP.

qa_highlights.question: Technology: proprietary vs outsourced and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About 90% of tech is proprietary; personal loan software spend increasing this year; overall tech cost share expected to stay similar. No capex-to-revenue percentage given.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on profitability for coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly guidance but expects growth in line with history, AUM growth 35-40%, and similar PAT performance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowing decline QoQ and what is the cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing reduced because of ~INR350 crore liquidity at March-end; higher cost in the quarter came from carrying extra liquidity. No forward cost trajectory given beyond NIM commentary.

qa_highlights.question: Why was QoQ AUM growth only ~1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality: run-down in April-June with few festivals; expects a large jump in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Namma Loan AUM targets and breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 AUM target INR60-75 crore; breakeven in 9-12 months, possibly 6-7 months given early response; senior hire from TVS Motor and TVS Credit.

543214|2026-06.headline: NDR Auto Q1 FY27 revenue INR221.45 crore with EBITDA margin 11.88% and PAT INR16.40 crore; management guides 11-12% margin ahead.
543214|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR221.45 crore with EBITDA of INR26.44 crore (11.88% margin) and PAT of INR16.40 crore, despite sector commodity and supply-chain pressure. The company commenced NDR Hayashi sunshade operations in Bangalore in June 2026 and inaugurated the NDR Auto South seat-trim plant at Anantapur, with SOP guided for Q2 FY27. Management reiterated an INR3,000 crore revenue endeavour by 2030 (INR2,000 crore organic plus INR1,000 crore inorganic) and guided Bharat Seats to about INR3,500 crore by 2030. Order book is about INR650 crore, unchanged from last quarter per the call, and management said it is bidding for much more business.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue growth of 19.5% as cited by analyst (YoY); not restated by management

financial_highlights.metric: Share of profit from JV (Bharat Seats, net of Hayashi loss)
Consolidated JV loss for the quarter

financial_highlights.change: Similar to last quarter per analyst

segments.name: NDR Auto Components (seat frames, seat covers, non-seat)
segments.commentary: Seat frames and covers make up most of the order book; new ambient lighting orders for Maruti Suzuki are a smaller part, with start in 2028. Management says non-seat margins will be similar to seating, though new-product ROCEs will be slightly lower.

segments.name: Bharat Seats (JV)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 35% in Q1 FY27, which management said exceeded expectations; revenue target raised to about INR3,500 crore by 2030 from INR3,000-3,500 crore earlier. Premiumisation (ventilated/AC seats) flows to Bharat Seats as final assembler.

segments.name: NDR Auto South (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Anantapur seat-trim and frame plant inaugurated; production starts in Q2 FY27 with revenue potential of INR70-80 crore at full run-rate, subject to model performance. Debt funding converted into equity.

segments.name: NDR Hayashi (JV)
segments.commentary: Sunshade production began in Bangalore in June 2026; JV is loss-making and expected to break even at about INR100-150 crore revenue. Original 5-6 year potential was INR200-300 crore.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected at about 11% to 12%, with commodities indexed to pass-through costs.
ROCE and margins expected to remain at similar levels as the business expands.
