segments.commentary: Revenue ₹26.2 cr (vs ₹23.2 cr YoY), ARPOB ₹91,326, ALOS 3.8 days. Achieved first EBITDA break-even since acquisition, reported at about 7% EBITDA margin; occupancy about 24% per analyst question.

segments.name: MedTech – SMTL India
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹36 cr per call (+29% QoQ, +98% YoY); management also cited India revenue growth of over 100% in volumes. Figures in the call are inconsistent (₹22.9 cr cited elsewhere).

segments.name: MedTech – US (SATUS)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹38.8 cr with about 9% sequential growth; standalone EBITDA marginally negative. US volumes flat YoY; FX headwind cited.

segments.name: MedTech – Singapore (SGTPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹9.9 million, lower sequentially; EBITDA about ₹5.8 million, a significant improvement vs prior quarters.

guidance_outlook: Hospital EBITDA margin: management is 'strongly confident' of reaching up to 20% for the full year FY27.
Gross margin expected to rise 100–200 bps each quarter going forward.

MedTech: double-digit EBITDA margin expected after US cost initiatives; half of progress made, remainder expected over the next 6 months. Monthly cash burn to fall ~₹3 cr/month from initiatives done in Q1 and a further ~₹3 cr/month once a project is implemented by Q4 FY27.
Shalby International occupancy expected to reach ~30% from Q3 or Q4 FY27; PBT break-even targeted around Q3–Q4 FY27 (6–9 months).
Group ROCE, currently ~7% (standalone ~9.5%), expected to reach 11–13% in 1–2 years.
Gurgaon unit to pay no tax for next 2–3 years due to carried-forward losses. Hospital tax rate moved to ~26% from 35%.
Inventory holding days expected to improve about 30%.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of about ₹160 cr in recent years, including bunker facility, robotics and MedTech investments; management expects minimal capex in the current and next year.
Bunkers (radiation facilities) installed in units last year; activation in Q1 with further uptick expected in Q2, including government-scheme coverage for bunker treatments.

Mumbai expansion: 200-bed greenfield Asha Parekh Hospital project; discussions ongoing with trustees, no approval yet. Funding by debt or internal accruals to be decided; no further debt for hospitals or MedTech expected.
47 transplants in Q1 (41 kidney, 5 liver, 1 bone marrow); liver transplant and KTP doctors recently replaced, full effect expected from Q2.
demand_pricing: Government share of payer mix rose to 32% from 24% a year ago; mix now 30% self-pay, 38% insurance, 32% government. Management cited a super-specialty rate win at Krishna unit.
TPA renewals underway, with management expecting a 5–7% revenue uplift from renewals and tie-ups in discussion.
Units Krishna, Mohali and Naroda grew ~30% YoY; Surat and Indore underperformed and are recruiting doctors.
International revenue ~42% of Shalby International operating revenue; group international business ~₹13 cr (₹2 cr Gurgaon, ₹11 cr other units).
Consolidated revenue of ₹923 mn in FY25, ₹1.3 bn in FY26, ₹472 mn in Q1 FY27 (MedTech-related, as stated).

512529|2026-06.headline: Viyash Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs 946 crore, EBITDA margin expanded to 21.6% (up ~530 bps) and PAT more than doubled to Rs 79 crore.
512529|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 946 crore (up 19.5% YoY, 2.9% QoQ), with EBITDA of Rs 205 crore and margin of 21.6% versus 16.2% a year earlier. PAT of Rs 79 crore is after about Rs 19 crore of incremental ESOP cost tied to the post-amalgamation grant. Net debt fell to Rs 86 crore (0.1x EBITDA), and management said the Sequent-Viyash integration is complete. Human API revenue was flat QoQ due to customer deferrals during raw material price volatility, which management expects to reverse in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: vs 51.9% in Q1 FY26 (~+220 bps YoY)
vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26 (~+530 bps YoY)
vs Rs 20.4 crore in Q1 FY26
Net debt/EBITDA 0.1x vs 0.24x last quarter, ~1x a year ago

financial_highlights.value: Rs 25 crore total, of which Rs 19 crore incremental
financial_highlights.change: Grant of 1.3 crore options, 2.8% of post-amalgamation paid-up capital

segments.name: US (Human formulation)
segments.commentary: Grew about 60% per management (about 45% YoY and 6% QoQ in USD per analyst); Rs 126 crore of Q1 revenue is Human formulation. Management said 60% growth will not repeat, but growth is stable, with a 50-55% US market share.

segments.name: Europe (Animal Health)
segments.commentary: Reported roughly 13% growth; analyst computed EUR 16.8 million flat YoY in constant currency. Management guided full-year Europe growth of 18-20% INR, citing phasing across quarters.

segments.name: Emerging markets (Animal Health)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% (about 23% in USD per analyst); volume growth was 25%, led by Turkey, Brazil and Mexico. Management said 25% volume growth will not be sustained every quarter.

segments.name: Animal Health India domestic
segments.commentary: Grew about 60%; management plans to expand field force and portfolio.

segments.name: API (Human and Animal)
segments.commentary: Broadly flat QoQ due to customer deferrals during raw material volatility. Animal API run-rate about Rs 100 crore, with Vizag capacity commercialised from July. API is about 40-45% of total revenue, roughly two-thirds Human and one-third Animal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 to be the best quarter in company history for API, citing a rebound in orders after customers delayed purchases in June.
FY27 double-digit growth, with management citing 13-15% overall (Human API 13-14%, Animal Health 20%+).
Europe growth of 18-20% INR for the full year; Europe double-digit growth in FY27 excluding FX.
ESOP cost of about Rs 150 crore for FY27 (Rs 25 crore in Q1, about Rs 40 crore per quarter thereafter), falling to Rs 25-30 crore in FY28.
Depreciation plus goodwill amortisation of Rs 25 crore per quarter; drops to about Rs 10-11 crore in Q2, and management expects about Rs 15 crore benefit per quarter from Q3 onward.
Minority interest expected at about 16-17% of total profit; minority stakes in the US and Spain to be fully acquired within 1-2 years.
Capex of Rs 250-300 crore per year; companion animal tablet capacity targeted to be ready by January-February 2027.
Bio For Life (Italy) acquisition SPA signed; closing expected in the next few months and within FY27. Bigger revenue expected after 18-24 months.

Human high-potent oncology first product expected in 2029; majority of new product revenue after 2030. Management targets Rs 1 billion (~Rs 10,000 crore?) aspiration by 2032 implying 18% CAGR from FY27 base.
capex_capacity: Companion animal tablet manufacturing: design finalised, construction to start within weeks, target completion January-February 2027 for exhibit batches.
High-potent formulation development lab completed last week; three high-potent API modules built over last 18-24 months.
Albendazole capacity expanded; US approval received for Vizag site, commercialisation started from July 2026.
R&D ramped up for companion animal products; equipment ordered and people hired.
Annual capex of Rs 250-300 crore, described as modest relative to existing business.
demand_pricing: Human API demand deferred in June as customers waited for raw material/solvent prices to stabilise; management says orders are returning after July.
Management noted it raised prices when raw material costs rose and may reduce them if solvent prices fall.
Human high-potent and oncology products expected to face 50-60% price erosion at generic entry versus 95% for general APIs, per management.
Target market share for new products: 10-15% on average, with 25-30% in best cases.
Europe: Spain performing strongly; Benelux and other countries lagging in tenders. Europe volume and pricing are the main growth drivers.
Animal Health portfolio focus shifted to differentiated products; the company has stopped developing mature commodity products.

532915|2026-06.headline: Religare Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% YoY to INR2,358 crores, but PBT swung to a loss of INR76.7 crores as RBI declined the demerger approval.
532915|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income reached INR2,358 crores against INR1,876 crores a year earlier, while total expenses of INR2,435 crores drove a PBT loss of INR76.73 crores versus a profit of INR5.73 crores. Care Health Insurance grew GWP 37% YoY on a full-premium basis and raised INR150 crores of equity, but its combined ratio stayed above 100% at 102.6% under Ind AS. RBI did not accede to the demerger application, and management said it is engaging with the regulator with no timeline. Broking profit rebounded, while RFL and Religare Housing reported lower income and losses as they rebuild.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR5.73 crores in Q1 FY26
Income INR4.38 crores, expense INR14 crores
vs INR19.3 crores in Q1 FY26
vs INR17.9 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Care Health Insurance
segments.commentary: GWP +37% YoY to INR3,247 crores (full premium); retail new business up over 50%; retail market share 12.6% of industry and 21.6% in SAHI. Ind AS PBT INR163 crores; investment book up over INR800 crores QoQ with leverage at 4.3x.

segments.name: Religare Broking
segments.commentary: Total income INR99.5 crores (+7% YoY), brokerage 47% of revenue, interest income 30%, e-governance 16%. Client debit book +78% YoY; cash ADTO INR375 crores vs INR334 crores; AUC INR47,946 crores.

segments.name: Religare Finvest (RFL)
segments.commentary: Core SME book about INR53 crores; net worth about INR915 crores; cash over INR600 crores; CRAR 238%; NNPA about 0.8%; collection efficiency 98%. Income fell on smaller loan book and lower GNPA recoveries.

segments.name: Religare Housing Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR247 crores (66% home loans, 34% LAP); about 15 branches in eight states; GNPA 4.4%, NNPA 3.3%; yield 14.6%; net worth about INR180 crores, CRAR above 121%.

guidance_outlook: Care targets a 100% combined ratio within two years, reiterated from last call; management declined full-year growth guidance but aims to beat the market.
Care year-end leverage expected to fall to about 3.7x after capital infusion.
Care to maintain solvency at about 1.7x; solvency was 1.58x at June 2026 against a 1.5x requirement.
RFL expects to start new lending business in roughly four months, and management ambitions a INR10,000-15,000 crore book on INR1,500-2,000 crores of capital.
Demerger timeline (previously targeted Q1 FY28) likely to slip; management gave no timeline for resolution with RBI.
capex_capacity: Care raised INR150 crores equity via rights issue in Q1 and INR200 crores subordinated debt in August 2026; of the INR600 crore earmarked, over INR376 crores infused so far.
Next Care capital raise likely via rights issue, per management.
Religare Housing to receive about INR250 crores further capital over the next few years against INR180 crores current net worth.
RFL: INR618 crores of INR1,500 crores warrant proceeds converted; INR881 crores remains due for conversion by March 2027.
Legacy written-off pool of INR350-400 crores under recovery; Q1 recoveries about INR20 crores.
demand_pricing: Care attributes growth to a 'land grab' in the market post-GST relaxation; growth driven by Tier 2/3 geographies and fresh business.
Industry health insurance grew 22.4% overall and 32% in retail; Care grew 18% above industry in retail.
Care's Q1 skews to corporate employee wellness business with upfront claims, which the company says inflates the combined ratio.
Broking: management attributes the revenue softness to market conditions and attrition; unique traded clients broadly stable.
RBI letter: no reasons attached; management says RBI did not object on capital structure grounds as stated in the letter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the demerger rejected and is a partial demerger or stake sale of Care under consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Lamba said the RBI letter gives no reasoning; the company is engaging with the regulator and is not pursuing other options for now. No timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Care's CISR 102.7% when insurance service result is only about -INR3 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambrish Jindal said CISR includes non-attributable expenses; an INR66 crore item after net finance result is added in CISR computation, which explains the gap.

qa_highlights.question: Why does consolidated Care show a loss when standalone Ind AS shows profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambrish Jindal said Care took a one-year forbearance on Ind AS 117 at consolidation, so the impact is not in consolidated accounts; this aligns from next year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RFL/Housing growth plans and why is cash so high at RFL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RFL was under PCA/CAP and lacked market funding for 7-8 years, so disbursements stopped; it expects to start business in about four months, with capital of INR1,500-2,000 crores targeting INR10,000-15,000 crores book.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the written-off book can be recovered and at what pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Srinivasan Karthik said the pool is INR350-400 crores of secured legacy loans facing litigation and repossession; recoveries are expected to decline each quarter and happen over about two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the RBI approval tied to merging the Burman-held private NBFCs?
qa_highlights.answer: Pratul Gupta said RBI's observation does not relate to merging the two sets of NBFCs; Arjun Lamba said the company is not aware of any such condition in the letter.

532923|2026-06.headline: Renaissance Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT jumped 288% to INR26 crores, but management guided revenue down as low-return customers are exited.
532923|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 30% YoY to INR690 crores (ex-bullion) and EBITDA rose 22% to INR50 crores, with PAT up sharply to about INR26 crores helped by a weak prior-year restructuring charge. Owned-brand revenue grew 29% to INR89 crores and owned-brand EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% from 10%. Working capital days fell to 220 from 253 YoY. Management said it will exit low-return customer businesses in the customer brands segment, which lowers revenue run-rate by INR400 crores by year-end, while it targets bottom-line growth above 30% for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from 7.7% a year ago (management's comparison, ex-bullion)

segments.name: Owned brands (D2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR89 crores, up 29% YoY; EBITDA margin 11.5% vs 10%. Focus on Jean Dousset and WithClarity, which together make up the bulk of owned-brand revenue. WithClarity run-rate about INR220 crores, growing about 20%.

segments.name: Licensed brands
segments.commentary: Management is rationalising licences (exiting NFL, Netflix, Harry Potter and others) to focus on Disney, where it is exclusive licensee for fine jewellery. Management said licensed-brand margin fell from 15.5% in FY24 to 10.9% in Q1 FY27 and expects a return to 14-15%.

segments.name: Customer brands (B2B/OEM)
segments.commentary: Where the planned exits sit. Management expects INR300-400 crores of annualised revenue to be removed, with the revenue run-rate down INR400 crores by year-end. Sequential revenue declines expected from Q2.

guidance_outlook: Bottom line expected to grow more than 30% in FY27, with revenue growth muted by customer exits.
Working capital release of about INR250 crores and operating cash flow above INR300 crores in FY27, to be realised by year-end.

Target of INR1,000 crores direct-to-consumer revenue by FY29 with at least 15% operating margin on that segment; FY27 D2C base is about INR500 crores (INR375 crores owned brands, INR125 crores licensed).
Jean Dousset: 7 stores by end FY27 (3 operating today, 4 more planned), then 6 more in FY28; management says each store should add INR25-35 crores of sales and pay back in under 1 year.
Management expects a minor margin dip during the year from exit costs, with margins comparable like-for-like.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity was reduced to match lab-grown diamond realities, with 24 months of restructuring cutting operating expenses by about INR45 crores annually.
Jean Dousset: company owns 65% after exercising an option up from 38.7%; a further stake increase is possible only if more funding is needed and has not yet been discussed at board level.
Tariff mitigation: some manufacturing subcontracted in the US and Middle East, which generates bullion sales.
Possible tariff refunds under application; amount not yet quantified and customers may share in refunds.
demand_pricing: Customer brands exits: management said the exited customers are low-return, with working capital costs above EBITDA generated; inventory exit cost is negligible because gold and silver prices have risen.
Average order values by tier: licensed brands about USD400, WithClarity about USD3,000, Jean Dousset about USD8,000. Customer brands range from USD50 to USD3,000.
Jean Dousset and WithClarity gross margins are 60-65%; WithClarity EBITDA margin is 11-13%.
Forex loss of about INR13 crores in Q1 (rupee appreciation); a large share of working capital is dollar-denominated, giving a natural hedge.
Metal price exposure hedged, with no inventory loss reported in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth continue at Q1's pace, and what about US tariff refunds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects bottom-line momentum to continue but revenue growth may not hold as low-return verticals are exited. Tariff refunds are being applied for; the amount was not disclosed and management asked investors to wait one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment will the INR250 crore working-capital release come from, and how big is the revenue hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Release comes from inventory and receivables, mainly in customer brands. Exits remove INR300-400 crores of annualised revenue, and the revenue run-rate falls INR400 crores by year-end; the company expects no meaningful bottom-line impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why are licensed-brand revenue and margins declining?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rationalised a wide licence portfolio, exiting NFL, Netflix, Harry Potter and others, with exit costs taken. It expects growth and margin recovery to 14-15% from focusing on Disney.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Jean Dousset's revenue is reported, and what is store economics?
qa_highlights.answer: The company consolidates Jean Dousset in full with a 65% stake, and minority interest is shown in the P&L. Brand revenue grew about 30% after acquisition in FY26; each store should add INR25-35 crores of sales and pay back in under 1 year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline and will B2B revenue keep rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Bullion sales are a continuing feature because of tariff-mitigation subcontracting. Ex-bullion margin fell from 7.7% to 7.2% due to exit costs. Sequential revenue should decline from Q2, tapering through Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 finance cost trajectory and forex loss outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give quarterly finance cost guidance but expects meaningfully lower net debt YoY by year-end. The forex loss should ease if the currency stabilises at current levels; other income of INR8-9 crores was described as normal course.

risks_watch: Revenue run-rate falls by INR400 crores by year-end from customer exits; revenue growth may turn negative sequentially from Q2.
Achieving INR250 crores working-capital release and INR300 crores operating cash flow in FY27.
Quality of PAT: the 288% jump is partly base effect from prior-year restructuring costs; Q1 forex loss of about INR13 crores.
Jean Dousset store ramp: 4 new stores in FY27 and 6 in FY28 need funding; a further stake increase or third-party investor is not yet discussed.
Tariff refund amount and how much will be passed to customers remain unquantified.
Licensed-brand margin recovery (10.9% to 14-15%) and rising Disney revenue are not yet shown in numbers.

538268|2026-06.headline: Wonderla Q1 FY27 income rose 41% YoY to INR252 crore and EBITDA 39% to INR122 crore, with Chennai Park adding INR45 crore revenue in its first year.
538268|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as one of its best quarters, with income of INR252 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA of INR122 crore (+39%) and PAT of INR72.79 crore (29% margin). Existing parks grew revenue about 15% on 7% footfall growth and 8% ARPU growth. Chennai Park, in its first year, contributed INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors, and management said it is tracking like a mature park for a Q1-type quarter. Management kept the new-park pipeline vague, saying an announcement on at least one park is expected before FY-end.

financial_highlights.value: INR252 crore (income); INR243 crore (revenue from operations)
INR9.47 crore (mainly interest and investment gains)

segments.name: Existing parks (Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 15% on 7% footfall growth and 8% ARPU growth; contributed INR15.93 crore (46%) of EBITDA growth. Footfall: Bengaluru 3.43 lakh (+6%), Kochi 2.5 lakh (+6%), Hyderabad 2.9 lakh (+11%), Bhubaneswar 1 lakh (+4%).

segments.name: Chennai Park (new, first year)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors; EBITDA contribution INR21.86 crore, 64% of EBITDA growth. Management said about 40-50% of land is developed (around 30 of 61.87 acres).

segments.name: Resorts (THE ISLE, Terrea, Wonderla resort)
segments.commentary: Added about INR3.19 crore EBITDA (9% of growth); best-ever quarter for both resorts along with Hyderabad park. Resort EBITDA is not disclosed; resort-related 'other' segment revenue was about INR63-64 crore per the segment data queried.

segments.name: Corporate overhead
segments.commentary: Overheads rose INR6.5 crore YoY, mainly investments to strengthen the organisation; about INR1.5 crore incremental digital transformation (new POS from July) and about INR5 crore higher marketing YoY.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance given; management said the year has started strongly and it hopes the trend continues, but footfall is unpredictable quarter to quarter.
Chennai margins expected to converge with other parks over time; management said Q1 margins are tracking similar to larger parks, but a full year is needed.
Chennai will not reach 1 million visitors in year one; management said a couple of years are needed.
Mature-park growth model unchanged: low-single-digit footfall growth with most growth from ARPU; non-ticket mix to rise toward 40-50% (currently about 30%).
Management expects to announce at least one new park before FY-end (by March 2027); advanced talks with 3-4 state governments.
July footfall described as good so far, but management cautioned that it is only one month.
capex_capacity: Chennai Park capex about INR570-600 crore for 40-plus rides; Bhubaneswar park capex about INR190 crore.
Payback guidance: large parks 6-8 years; small-format parks 4-5 years (ballpark).
Capex allocation: about 10% of top line for expansion and new attractions; about 6-7% of top line for maintenance capex.

Structural capacity: large park can handle about 1.2-1.3 million visitors per year; small park (Bhubaneswar) about 5-5.5 lakh; management said capacity was about 1.1 million two-three years ago and is rising as rides are added.
Land: parks are 70-80 acres for large format; excess land is retained for resorts, extensions and rides.
Chennai and Bangalore share about 50-70% of rides; 30-50% are unique to each park.
demand_pricing: Footfall growth at existing parks was 7% in Q1, but management would not commit to sustaining it; May (highest-footfall month) had no unseasonal rain, and management said weaker monsoon was not a major factor.
ARPU growth is driven by non-ticket spend (+20% YoY); management said the 8% ARPU CAGR over 4 years leaves a high base, so similar growth may not repeat.
Hyderabad growth attributed to marketing and brand investment; trailing-12-month footfall was about 895,000 vs 893,000 a year earlier per an analyst's calculation, which management did not dispute.
Management cited headwinds: state elections in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, Gulf conflict, and F&B inflation.
Q1 and Q3 are the largest quarters; Q2 is the weakest.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7% ex-Chennai footfall growth sustainable, and what margin path should Chennai follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Footfall is unpredictable, but the year has started strongly. Chennai margins should converge to other parks over time, and Q1 is tracking similarly to larger parks.

qa_highlights.question: Will Chennai reach 1 million visitors this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it would take a couple of years to reach 1 million visitors.

qa_highlights.question: How many parks will be added over the next 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans about 1-2 large parks and 1-2 small ones, with an update expected before FY-end. Parks will be picked based on land and government offers, and no closures were named.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU growth at Bangalore and Hyderabad a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium cohorts and in-park experiences drove non-ticket spend, which is the main ARPU driver. Management said the base is now high, so similar growth may not repeat each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Monsoon effect on Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon had little effect because June is weak and May had no unseasonal rain. Management also cited the Kerala and Tamil Nadu elections and inflation in F&B as factors.

qa_highlights.question: Will the resort model be replicated and is timeshare planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to take the resort model to other cities, including standalone resorts such as Goa, but will wait a full year before deciding. Timeshare was ruled out in favour of retail.

risks_watch: Footfall volatility: management declined to predict sustainability of the 7% growth.
Chennai ramp-up and margin convergence remain unproven beyond one quarter; Q2 is seasonally weaker.
Hyderabad trailing-12-month footfall flat YoY, which management attributes to a lagged marketing investment.
Overhead growth (+INR6.5 crore) and marketing spend, which may recur; management did not call them one-off.
Monsoon and regional rain or disruption risk, including Kerala heavy rain and drought.
Timing and terms of new park announcements, which were not named and remain uncertain.

526829|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 117% YoY to INR2,408 crore and PAT more than tripled to about INR62.6 crore, driven mainly by LPG volumes.
526829|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue (about INR2,408 crore), EBITDA (about INR147 crore) and PAT (about INR62.6 crore) for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, with basic EPS of INR1.86. Management attributed the top-line jump largely to higher LPG prices during supply disruption from West Asia, while saying volumes also rose sharply (about doubled YoY) and that a portion of the growth came from new bulk and institutional customers on short- to medium-term contracts. Auto LPG volumes slowed temporarily on higher prices and have since recovered per management. Most company-specific numbers (segment revenue split, FY26 capex, LPG import volumes, Type 4 cylinder margins) were deferred to follow-up emails.

financial_highlights.change: +117% YoY (from INR1,112 crore); +98% QoQ (from INR1,216 crore)

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR62.6 crore (management also cited exceeding INR66 crore in one remark)
financial_highlights.change: More than tripled YoY (from INR20.5 crore); +82% QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: PAT margin (analyst-cited, not confirmed by management)
financial_highlights.change: Management said margins are 'intact' and that the drop is due to higher LPG prices

segments.name: Packed LPG (GoGas)
segments.commentary: Packed LPG sales of about 18,000-20,000 MT per month; management said it is more commercial than domestic and price-competitive on commercial. Packed LPG and Auto LPG were named as the highest-EBITDA-margin segments, but no margin figures were given.

segments.name: Bulk LPG / industrial
segments.commentary: About 300 industrial customers served; new accounts added in FMCG, food processing, glass and ceramics. Management said a meaningful part of Q1 was volume-led from new bulk and institutional customers.

segments.name: Auto LPG (ALDS)
segments.commentary: 315+ dispensing stations, all operational. Demand slowed temporarily in the quarter on higher LPG prices, and management said volumes have since recovered. Payback on a new station is said to be under 18 months.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: 50+ CNG stations completed, with a further 50 targeted in Bengaluru. Average station volume was said to be about 6,000-6,200 kg per day, and total volume about 3 lakh kg per day.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to 10-15% QoQ growth in revenue, PAT and EBITDA in coming quarters; it did not give a multi-year revenue number.
Auto LPG network target: 500 stations, with about 75 added in FY27 and about 100 in FY28, then a further evaluation toward 500.
CNG target to increase from 50 to 100 stations; talks with other CGD players for Mumbai, Hyderabad and Indore, not finalised.
Management expects margins to rise as volumes grow and once prices normalise; no bps or percentage target was given.
Backward integration is under evaluation, including small coastal storage terminals (not finalised) and a 100% Dubai subsidiary for LPG import ease.
Type 4 high-pressure cylinder unit at Butibori (Nagpur): capex complete and machinery installed; production expected in 1-2 months, subject to order book. Margin not disclosed.
capex_capacity: Type 4 high-pressure cylinder plant (Butibori): capex complete and machinery installed; start awaits order book, with production expected in 1-2 months. Target customers are CGD players, car fleet owners and OEMs.
CNG: 50+ stations operational; 50 more planned in Bengaluru.
Auto LPG: 315+ stations; target 500 (75 in FY27, 100 in FY28).

Fleet and infrastructure as stated: ships on time charter, 68+ bottling/blending plants, 478+ LPG road tankers, 225+ HCVs/LCVs, 82 CNG road vehicles, 15 cylinder plants and 3 high-pressure cylinder plants.
Total capacity was cited by an analyst as 608 TMT or 685 TMT; management did not confirm or answer on utilisation.
demand_pricing: India LPG market about 35.04 MMT, projected at about 40-42 MMT by FY2030; OMCs hold about 94% of sales and private marketers about 6%, with CPIL holding about 33% of the private segment (management claim).
During the West Asia disruption, the company diversified sourcing to North America, Africa and the Middle East, and said several marquee customers moved to longer-term contracts.
Management said Q1 revenue growth was mainly price-driven, but also volume-driven (volumes about doubled YoY per management).
Management said it is price-competitive against PSUs in industrial, HoReCa and commercial segments.
Gin Kar Lo, Gin Kar Do scheme (pay-for-actual-consumption cylinder weighing) introduced; direct financial impact not a stated objective.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Type 4 cylinder plant operational, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is complete and machinery is installed at Butibori. Production is expected within 1-2 months, but the start depends on receiving the order book. Management declined to give margin numbers until the first deliveries.

qa_highlights.question: Which cities are in CNG network talks?
qa_highlights.answer: Mumbai, Hyderabad and Indore were named, but none is finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue, EBITDA and PAT will grow QoQ, though revenue will move with LPG prices. It later quantified 10-15% QoQ growth.

qa_highlights.question: How is the PAT margin trending and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are intact and rising, and that the lower percentage reflects higher LPG prices. It gave no quantified margin target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 growth came from the West Asia disruption, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company had inventory when PSUs faced constraints, and that new customers signed longer-term agreements. Management said volumes are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation priority (organic, M&A, debt, dividends)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of new stations, JVs and acquiring infrastructure, plus bottling expansion and backward integration. No allocation split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging of LPG import currency exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payments are made on time and spot contracts are used, so no hedge is currently required; it would hedge in future if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BW exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BW, a strategic investor from 2023-24, exited in the secondary market to focus on its shipping business, with no impact on the company.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Income Tax search?
qa_highlights.answer: The search began 7 October 2025 and closed within 7 days. Assessment is open, no final demand has been received, and management does not expect a large payable.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of revenue by segment, FY26 capex, and LPG import data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred these to follow-up emails and gave no figures on the call.

544356|2026-06.headline: AJAX Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.7% to INR475 crores and EBITDA margin fell 70 bps to 12.5%, with SLCM market share at 75.1%.
544356|2026-06.overview: Total revenue grew 1.7% YoY to INR475 crores while EBITDA fell to INR59 crores from INR61 crores, compressing margin by 70 bps to 12.5%. Profit after tax rose 5% to INR55.6 crores. Management said industry SLCM registrations fell 27% and AJAX's fell 21%, yet SLCM and retail market share rose to 75.1% from about 69% a year earlier. Management guided Q2 as seasonally soft and margins as challenging, with input cost pressure from steel and fuel and a further calibrated price increase under evaluation.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR61 crores in Q1 FY26
vs about 69% in Q1 FY26 and 73.5% in FY26

financial_highlights.value: exceeding INR1,100 crores as of June 2026

segments.name: SLCM
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR388 crores, marginally up YoY on favourable mix and Q4 FY26 price increase of about 2%. Machine volumes down; UDAAN sold 121 units in Q1 versus 202 in all of last year, with about 35-40 in July.

segments.name: Non-SLCM (concrete pumps, batching plants, boom pumps/placers)
segments.commentary: Revenue around INR48 crores, up 6.4% YoY led by pumps. Business volume about 129 machines in Q1 FY27 versus about 153 in Q1 FY26, with rain-related deferrals expected to recover in August-September.

segments.name: Spares and services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR39 crores, up 6.2% YoY; management is prioritising a higher AMC share from the installed base, but gave no quantified target.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share about 9% of Q1 revenue on first slip-form paver shipment. Algeria, Morocco and Nigeria about 38% of shipments; management targets about 30% CAGR over next three years, if not more.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be seasonally soft and a fairly challenging quarter for EBITDA; 12.5% margin looks challenging in Q2.
Margins expected to return to about 12.5% corridor from Q3 FY27 if volumes improve.
Full-year EBITDA margin of 12% described as challenging; management said too early to call full-year numbers.
Non-SLCM growth target of about 10-15% YoY on a lower base; H2 expected to be better than H1.
Long-term EBITDA margin corridor of 13-15% reiterated; Q4 FY26 cited as about 15%.
Another calibrated price increase under evaluation, with some action targeted within Q2 FY27; about 60% of revenue typically comes in H2.
capex_capacity: ARGO 4000 launch planned in Q2 FY27 to fill a portfolio gap.
Manufacturing consolidated under one leader; Obadenahalli plant head now oversees procurement and supply chain.
Strategic inventory built in first few months for products with imported components; no large strategic steel purchase made at current prices.
Cash above INR1,100 crores; management actively pursuing inorganic opportunities with guardrails, no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Industry SLCM registrations down 27% YoY in Q1; AJAX down 21%. Second-ranked player lost about 0.7% share; Conmat and Venus gained share.

State-wise: Maharashtra and MP volumes declined (MP about 50%) but share rose; Gujarat volumes up about 40% with share 71% to 82%; Rajasthan volumes down 21% with share 66% to 86%; Odisha share 61% to 88% with volume up 13%; UP down about 7%.
Application mix: roads about 40-43%, urban infra 15-20% and buildings 10-15% (now about 35-40% combined per management, up from 15-20%).
Contractors facing payment delays from some state governments; government infrastructure spending below budget.
Steel E250 and E350 prices have risen; fuel prices also up. Price increase of about 2% taken in Q4 FY26.
Management said it is not playing the price game and prefers installation over discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Is non-SLCM growth targeted at 20-30% for the year given the low base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be happy with 10-15% growth in non-SLCM on a lower base, with H2 expected better than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 17% on flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to higher outward freight from diesel prices and export mix, plus about INR16 million of cost for the SAP ECC 6 to HANA migration this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did a peer grow volume about 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the peer grows in pick-and-carry cranes, not SLCM; AJAX's SLCM decline was in line with industry registrations being down 27%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for Q2, Q3 and full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 12.5% margin looks challenging; margins to return to about 12.5% from Q3 if volumes improve; 12% for full year also looks challenging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel and pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel prices rose; management hopes for softening after US primaries in September-November; a calibrated price increase is planned, likely starting within Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are inorganic opportunities being pursued aggressively given the cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is aggressively pursuing inorganic opportunities within guardrails and will update when clear.

risks_watch: Continued SLCM volume decline (industry -27%, AJAX -21%) and weak Maharashtra and MP volumes.
Steel and fuel cost inflation with unclear timing of price increases and possible competitive pushback.
Government payment delays to contractors and under-spending on infrastructure.
Recovery of deferred non-SLCM volumes expected August-September; need to verify.
Export revenue recognition timing and country/currency risk.
Investor-call audio quality issues reported by several participants during the call.
544356|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and market share, but cautious on the near term: management repeatedly deferred to H2 and called Q2 margins challenging. Evasive on specifics for non-SLCM growth, the full-year margin, and cost initiatives.
key_quotes: Our SLCM and retail market share expanded to 75.1% during Q1 FY27, increasing from about 69% in Q1 FY26 and 73.5% during the full year FY26.
Definitely 12.5%, looks challenging at this point in time from a second quarter perspective.
For the longer term, the 13% to 15% corridor is something that we are very clear about that we will endeavor to make sure that as demand comes back to the economy, that should play.

544061|2026-06.headline: Azad Engineering Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 26.8% YoY to INR170.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 37.6% and PAT of INR36.4 crore.
544061|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 26.8% YoY and 8.3% QoQ to INR170.5 crore, with reported EBITDA of INR64 crore (37.6% margin, up 150 bps YoY). PAT rose 21.2% YoY to INR36.4 crore (21.3% margin, EPS INR5.63), held back by other income falling to INR4 crore from INR17 crore in Q4 FY26 on forex swings. Management highlighted delivery of India's first indigenous expendable turbojet engine to GTRE/DRDO and a new Baker Hughes dedicated facility, while stating that substantial revenue from new capacity begins in H2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +26.8% YoY (from INR134.5 crore); +8.3% QoQ (from INR157.4 crore)
+32.1% YoY (from INR48.5 crore); margin +150 bps YoY, +90 bps QoQ (from 36.7%)

financial_highlights.value: INR36.4 crore; PAT margin 21.3%; EPS INR5.63
financial_highlights.change: +21.2% YoY (from INR30 crore); +3.5% QoQ per CFO (Q4 FY26 cited as INR35.1 crore)
vs INR9.1 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR17 crore in Q4 FY26; attributed to forex movements
+25.9% YoY (CFO initially misspoke as INR122.6 crore, corrected on call)
targeted ~200 days in H1 FY27, 160-180 days in H2 FY27 via bill discounting

segments.name: Aerospace and Defense (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth stated as 24.7% YoY after management first said ~38.4%, corrected on call; attributed to higher share of wallet with global aviation majors and early defence/propulsion deliveries.

segments.name: Energy and Oil & Gas (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth stated as 26.7% YoY after first being said as 21.6%, corrected on call; driven by gas turbine components and launch of new customer-dedicated lines.

guidance_outlook: Long-term annual revenue growth guidance of over 25% reiterated; Chairman said the guidance will change once the company moves to the next level.

Management says it has met Q1 guidance; manufacturing infrastructure 'running at full throttle', with substantive revenue contributions from new capacity expected from H2 FY27 and acceleration from Q3-Q4.
EBITDA margin guidance framed as 32%-35% for calculation purposes, though company has delivered above 35% consistently.
Other income expected to moderate as treasury cash is deployed into factory infrastructure.
Remaining FY26 expansion initiatives: ~80% stabilised in Q1; major remaining activities due mid-Q2 and full closure by Q3 FY27.
Working-capital targets: debtor days ~200 in H1 and 160-180 in H2 FY27; natural hedge for export receivables expected by Q4 FY27 via bill discounting.
capex_capacity: Tuniki Bollaram Industrial Park: 8 customer-dedicated plants planned; each plant said to generate INR150-180 crore revenue at full utilisation, implying ~INR1,200 crore from newer plants.

Fourth dedicated facility (7,600 sq m, for Baker Hughes) inaugurated April 2026 and commenced operations in Q1; dedicated lines already running for Mitsubishi, GE Power Systems/GE Steam Power and Siemens Energy.
Civil construction at Azad Center of Excellence remaining units to finish within FY27; machine installations in modular phases aligned to customer roadmaps.
Management estimates ~1 year of capex-driven capacity for the next couple of years; capex plans beyond FY29 are being sketched, with quantum and timing to be disclosed in the next quarter.
Hot-section facility (modelled on the Mitsubishi plant) expected to be set up in roughly 7-8 months, also usable for aviation engines.
FY26 capex was roughly INR900 crore over two years per analyst; no new capex number was given by management.
demand_pricing: Turbojet engine: first indigenous expendable turbojet engine delivered to GTRE, DRDO and MoD; next step is weapon testing expected in 4-6 weeks per management (not formally communicated), followed by certification and production scale-up. Management says volumes are unknown (2-, 3- or 4-digit) and existing capacity is fungible for 2-digit volumes.
First 20 engines produced so far; management will share costing after 5-6 engines in a row (about 8-12 weeks away).
Rolls-Royce civil aircraft engine: first batch of qualification parts expected to be delivered within the current quarter.

Cost indigenisation: local suppliers Sunflag and Star Wire qualified for critical raw-material grades; import freight of ~4-5% avoided. Raw material cost fell to ~5% of sales from ~12% a year earlier, per analyst.
Employee cost rose to ~INR42 crore from ~INR29 crore per analyst; management attributed it to inventory build for H2 sales and hiring of ~150-200 people per month into 90-day training.
Management said rupee depreciation can add roughly 5-6% to revenue but is not a planning lever; FX on exports is below EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline from first turbojet engine delivery to orders and capacity planning beyond FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said next steps are weapon testing in 4-6 weeks and then certification and production; capacity is fungible for 2-digit volumes, and capex quantum/timing for next 5-6 years will be clarified in about a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Growth thesis for aerospace hot-section and peers' margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hot-section demand is a multi-billion market, OEMs are already asking when the facility is ready, and margin potential is referenced to high-cost-country peers; no growth number given.

qa_highlights.question: When will working capital days plateau?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO targeted ~200 debtor days in H1 and 160-180 in H2 FY27, mainly via bill discounting that will move ~170-180 day debtors toward ~90 days; finance cost will continue to rise on discounting charges.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 32-35% EBITDA margin when delivering 37-38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 32-35% is used for guidance and calculation purposes, while margins have been running above 35% due to shop-floor skills and continuous improvement, from ~18-19% at inception.

qa_highlights.question: Is revenue growth above 25% achievable given 3-year potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 25%+ is guided given current situation and the guidance will change on moving to the next level; no 3-year target given.

qa_highlights.question: Does rupee depreciation benefit revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is natural hedging, with imports offsetting exports; CFO said FX benefit is below EBITDA and not built into the margin.

532652|2026-06.headline: Karnataka Bank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 43% YoY to INR418.95 crores, NIM widened to 3.20%, and Gross NPA fell to 2.58%.
532652|2026-06.overview: Karnataka Bank reported a strong Q1 FY27 with PAT of INR418.95 crores (up 3% QoQ, 43% YoY), NII up 11% QoQ to INR938.29 crores, and NIM at 3.20% versus 3.07% in Q4 FY26. Asset quality improved on both gross and net NPA, with credit cost at 0.03%. Business reached a record INR1,97,007 crores, with gross advances up 4% QoQ and 17% YoY, and CASA and CD ratio both improving. Management guided to around 15% overall business growth in FY27 and an ROA of 1.35% to 1.40%, but gave limited detail on SMA-2 rise, mid-corporate growth and the ECL transition.

financial_highlights.change: +3% QoQ (vs INR408.19 crores Q4 FY26); +43% YoY (vs INR292.40 crores Q1 FY26)
+11% QoQ (vs INR842.95 crores); +24% YoY (vs INR755.60 crores)

segments.commentary: INR69,410 crores, +3% QoQ (from INR67,648 crores) and +6% YoY.

544868|2026-06.headline: Milky Mist Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR973.45 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9% and gross margin up about 270 bps to 34.2%.
544868|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR973.45 crore, up 44% YoY, led by paneer, cheese, curd, ice cream and yogurt. Gross profit was about INR333 crore (34.2% margin, up ~270 bps), EBITDA INR144.89 crore (14.9% margin vs 12.24% a year earlier) and PAT INR64.67 crore (6.6% margin). Management attributed margin gains to product mix, a ~10.5% price increase taken in Q4 FY26, and scale. The call was the company's first earnings call after listing; several figures were corrected on the call during the prepared remarks.

segments.name: Paneer
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at INR248.29 crore, up 34% in both volume and revenue; management linked this to zero GST on paneer from September 2025 and FSSAI/state bans on analogue paneer. Company claims ~20% share of the organised paneer market.

segments.name: Yogurt (incl. protein range)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR84.5 crore, up 153%; management calls it a key margin driver, with Greek yogurt and Skyr in the protein range.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Volume +45%, revenue +60% YoY, aided by extended summer; management expects demand to stay robust around the year in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

segments.name: Cheese
segments.commentary: Revenue +38% YoY; new natural cheddar plant commissioned in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day capacity. Company says cheese sales come from retail, modern trade and quick-commerce, not QSRs.

segments.name: Curd
segments.commentary: Revenue +27% YoY.

segments.name: Regional mix
segments.commentary: South ~69% of revenue, growing ~44% YoY; non-South ~31%, growing ~50% YoY. Management expects a drift toward 60:40 over time.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to add INR150-200 crore of incremental revenue versus H1 (as stated on the call).
Operating margin: management guided to about 0.5% leverage benefit from scale; asked whether 18% EBITDA margin is achievable in 3-4 years, CFO said 'you can expect that' but CEO declined to quantify.
Maharashtra plant: at drawing-board stage, about three years out; the company aims for 40% utilisation from day one at break-even.
Revenue potential from Perundurai at current MRP: 3x to 3.5x FY26 revenue (as stated on the call).
Plans to deploy more than 50,000 visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers over the next three fiscal years.
Whey protein concentrate plant expected to be operational in about 15-18 months from the call.
capex_capacity: Commissioned new natural cheddar cheese plant in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day installed capacity.

Capex in the RHP: about INR500 crore plus INR150 crore, about INR650-700 crore in total; another ~INR380 crore WIP carried from last year. CFO said capex is funded through IPO proceeds and bank funding, with no cash-flow pressure this year.
Planned expansion covers whey protein concentrate, lactose, natural cheese, processed cheese and yogurt capacity.
Capacity utilisation: CEO said more than 12 product categories have spare capacity; paneer utilisation is about 50%.

Milk procurement averaged 13.2 lakh litres per day in Q1 FY27, up 28% YoY. Third-party share is about 10-12% of volume, and the company is expanding direct procurement in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 10.5% taken in Q4 FY26 (stated as ~11% in one answer); management said this offset milk and input inflation and produced a 2.7% margin expansion net.
Trade spend: about 4.5-5% trade discount from MRP to billing and another 4.5-5% on marketing/promotion.
Milk costs are about 50-55% of input cost; landed cost is INR45/litre (farmer price INR41-42). Aavin raised farmgate prices by INR3 twice recently; management is still studying pass-through.
Pricing is set after a 2-3 month lag following input cost increases, per CFO.
Management said the company has no B2B or QSR sales other than whey powder from cheese and paneer making.

qa_highlights.question: Third-party milk procurement strategy and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party share is about 10-12% through a five-year exclusive contract with MilkLane (linked to a PE-owned entity). Management says payments go directly to farmers and that quality premiums are about 50 paise/litre, with no financial dilution.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin resilience amid milk price inflation and further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credits product mix (paneer +34%, cheese +38%, yogurt +150%, ice cream +60%) and pricing. Price hikes follow a 2-3 month lag after input costs. About 10.5% price increase taken last year.

qa_highlights.question: Freight and logistics model with a single plant serving distant cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-owned fleet of about 375 vehicles with return-load logistics saves ~18-20% on logistics cost. Shelf life of 30+ days (vs 24-48 hours for pouch milk) makes one plant viable.

qa_highlights.question: Low base in Q1 FY26 and seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 weakness was price-driven (GST and milk rationalisation), not volume-driven. Ice cream is strong in summer and robust year-round in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

qa_highlights.question: Whey protein plans and high-protein B2C products?
qa_highlights.answer: The company generates about 1 million litres of cheese whey daily and currently sells whey powder B2B. A whey protein concentrate plant is due in 15-18 months; high-protein RTD products are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Yield per animal and farmer support?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement volume is up 28% YoY. Initiatives include bank credit via Kisan Credit Cards, herd-size expansion, AI/breeding, feed and health camps.

531859|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.7% YoY to INR137.6 crore, with EBITDA up 43.7% to INR20.9 crore and margin at 15.2%.
531859|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR137.6 crore against INR117.9 crore a year earlier, up 16.7% YoY. EBITDA rose 43.7% to INR20.9 crore, with margin expanding 286 bps to 15.2%, and PAT rose 83% to INR10.7 crore (7.8% margin). Management attributed the sequential revenue moderation to the US-Iran war and a fuel and gas supply crisis in March-April, which it says is now largely resolved. The consolidated order book stood at about INR1,692 crore as of August 11, 2026, with INR1,526 crore at OFPL wagons and INR166 crore in coach interiors. Management also laid out smart wagon, next-gen wagon, wagon leasing and JV initiatives.

segments.name: Freight wagons (Oriental Foundry Pvt Ltd, OFPL)
segments.commentary: About 75% of consolidated revenue and about INR106 crore in Q1; management guides wagon volumes up more than 45-50% YoY on better capacity utilisation. Installed capacity is 2,400 wagons per annum, with FY26 utilisation around 50%.

segments.name: Seats and berths (rolling stock interiors, ORIL)
segments.commentary: About 16% of revenue; the business holds over 30% market share with installed capacity of about 3,600 coaches per annum. Management expects other businesses to grow 8-10%.

segments.name: Rexine upholstery (ORVIN)
segments.commentary: About 5% of revenue; in-house capacity is 36 lakh meters per annum serving railway and non-railway users.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 wagon dispatches of about 500 vs roughly 300 plus in Q1; FY27 turnover expected at around INR700 crore.
Order book execution at about 200 wagons per month from Q3 FY27 (October-December), which management says fully uses the 2,400-wagon capacity.
Medium-term EBITDA margin targets: 15-17% for freight wagons and 13-15% for rolling stock interiors; consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 15-17%.
Capacity expansion: application by Q1 FY28; target of 3,600 then 4,800 wagons over 12-18 months from FY28; capex of about INR60-70 crore for the 2,400 to 3,600 step.
No order inflow targeted in FY27; order inflow of about INR600 crore expected in Q1 FY28 (management said FY27 in the call, then corrected to FY28).
capex_capacity: Wagon capacity 2,400 per annum at OFPL, around 50% utilised in FY26; more than 4,000 wagons delivered to date.
Expansion to 3,600 wagons (capex INR60-70 crore), then 4,800 wagons over 12-18 months from FY28, with capacity applications starting Q1 FY28.
Dedicated smart wagon component facility planned in North India by end FY28.
Four manufacturing facilities across 100 acres; in-house bogies, draft gears, springs, couplers and side bearers. Spring plant became operational in FY26.
AAR certification application in progress.
demand_pricing: Wagon realisation about INR40 lakh per wagon (plus or minus 5%).
Wagon price escalation clause linked to steel WPI, labour index and other commodity indices; management says it does not cover vendor-driven component price hikes.
Management says FY26 and FY25 weakness was due to railway wheel shortages and reliance on external component suppliers, which squeezed margins.
Smart wagon monitoring system priced at about INR2.5-3 lakh per unit; target 30,000 units per annum, implying about INR750 crore revenue (management estimates a INR10,000 crore market).
Freight wagon market expected to nearly double to INR25,000-30,000 crore by 2031; National Rail Plan 2030 targets wagon fleet growth from about 4 lakh to 6 lakh.
Management expects 'at least two or three players' in smart wagons and says competition is anticipated.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for sequential revenue moderation and Q2 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 to the US-Iran war and the fuel and gas supply crisis in March-April, now largely resolved. Q2 is running faster, with about 500 wagons expected versus roughly 300 plus in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How many wagons does the INR1,526 crore OFPL order book represent and what is the execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3,800 wagons, executed at about 200 wagons per month from Q3 FY27 (October-December).

qa_highlights.question: Capacity expansion plans and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is to go from 2,400 to 3,600 (capex INR60-70 crore), then 4,800 over 12-18 months from FY28; the capacity application is planned for Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight revenue not grow in FY25-FY26 (INR458 crore to INR409 crore), and what changed?

504973|2026-06.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 combined ratio rose to 120.4% with GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore and motor OD loss ratio still elevated.
504973|2026-06.overview: Chola MS (general insurance arm of Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), below management's expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% (vs 81.3%) and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss (Rs 12.4 crore net). Profit before tax was Rs 116 crore on operating profit of Rs 71 crore. Management said the OD loss ratio is unacceptable and targets a high-70s level first, while the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment remains unprovided pending review.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Largest line (~70% of book per management); portfolio grew ~5.7% in Q1, mainly commercial vehicles. Mix: private cars 48%, two-wheelers ~9.5%, commercial vehicles ~42.5%. Motor combined ratio 128% in FY26 vs 123% in FY25; OD loss ratio now 80-86% range per analyst framing, not disputed by management.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 vs industry fire decline of ~28%; Chola MS fire decline limited to 15.5%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Growth moderate; decline driven by pricing corrections in PSU bank group platform and migration of business to retail platform. Claims settled within 30 days for 99%; NPS 73. Health is being rebuilt from the ground up.

guidance_outlook: OD loss ratio near-term target: bring it to high-70s, then progressively to mid-70s; management said it expects below 80% over time, with a couple of quarters needed for measures to show results.

Corrective measures across motor (new vs renewal mix, NCB focus, ACS control, repair vs replacement analysis) and health (product redesign, pricing revisions, SME push) expected to become visible over coming quarters.
Expects greater property pricing discipline after June NATCAT events; reinsurance market correction more likely at next renewal cycle.
Ind AS / IFRS transition effective April 1, 2027 (one-year IRDAI forbearance granted); no profitability impact estimate yet, preliminary observations possibly next quarter.
Industry CAT loss estimate of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore from multiple events in Gujarat, Assam, Jamshedpur and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity for fire and engineering secured at start of FY27, described as comparable to leading private players.
Motor issuance platform rolled out across bank channel; workflow enhancements under way in motor claims.
Health network exceeds 13,000 hospitals via PSU bank retail health partnerships.
Readiness work ongoing for Ind AS, Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework and DPDP requirements.
demand_pricing: Industry GI premium growth ~8.3% in Q1 vs 8.9% a year earlier; motor and health led growth, fire under severe pricing pressure.
Industry combined ratio ~117.8% in FY26 vs 112.6% FY25; Chola MS 115.2% FY26 vs 110% FY25.
Motor TP is tariff-based; premiums do not keep pace with claims inflation and court award trends.
Inward reinsurance growth cited as a driver of GWP outpacing GDPI; sources are commercial-lines participation and group health.
GIFT City reinsurers cited as contributing to soft commercial-lines pricing; management expects limited sustainable lead-line capacity from them.

qa_highlights.question: Has any additional motor TP provision been made for the Supreme Court homemaker judgment, and what is the path for motor OD loss ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No provision taken in Q1 for the Supreme Court judgment; review petition pending. OD loss ratio not accepted as the new normal; immediate target is high-70s, then mid-70s over time. Management said the 84.4% motor figure cited by analyst was not confirmed in the call, and said OD loss ratio below 80% is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retail and group health decline when the industry is growing strongly?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health decline reflects virtually no gross-subsidy business left, standalone accounts required to be individually profitable, and PSU bank group platform pricing corrections with migration to retail platform. Focus shifts to multinational single-mandate clients, SME and GPA cross-sell.

qa_highlights.question: Is the claims ratio rise from new book or from reserve provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase reflects claims inflation assumptions in reserving (expected ULR), not pure reserve strengthening; motor TP is tariff-based so pricing lags claims cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is motor two-wheeler reduced and how does the Supreme Court ruling affect claims?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler reduction was deliberate given profitability; courts have not uniformly applied the Rs 30,000 threshold and evaluate cases individually. Solvency impact of an adverse outcome not quantified; reserves said to include margin for adverse deviation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IFRS/Ind AS profitability and ROE impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Implementation effective April 1, 2027 after one-year forbearance; no reliable estimate yet, special-purpose financial statements not yet filed with IRDAI. Preliminary observations possibly next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is inward reinsurance growth sustainable and what is the CAT and reinsurance renewal outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inward reinsurance comes from commercial lines participation and selective group health; sustainable only as underwriting appetite allows. Hours-clause structure means separate deductibles per event, so P&L impact could be larger, supporting pricing discipline; reinsurance softness more visible at next renewal.

risks_watch: Motor OD loss ratio (80-86% range) and whether it moves toward high-70s as guided.
Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment: review outcome and possible retrospective provisioning; solvency at 1.93x.
Reinsurance renewal terms after soft market and GIFT City capacity; loss of commissions or higher retention risk.
Health portfolio profitability and rebuilding of retail health capabilities; combined ratio of group health was flagged as a concern.
Ind AS transition from April 1, 2027, with impact on profitability and ROE still unquantified.

522101|2026-06.headline: Kilburn Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to about INR117 crores with 20.1% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance of INR700 crores kept, H2-weighted.

Management kept FY27 guidance of about INR700 crores revenue at 20% EBITDA margin and said the year is expected to be significantly second-half weighted. Order inflow was about INR134-135 crores in the quarter and about INR190 crores year-to-date, against an internal group target of INR800 crores for FY27. Management also said the equity fundraise is complete and the balance sheet is net debt-free.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in reaching INR800 crore order inflow with 9 months left, and Middle East exposure?

Many forward figures (GScale revenue, margins, FY28) were left unquantified and deferred to future guidance.

guidance_outlook: Jonnagiri FY27 production 500-600 kg (earlier guidance retained); FY28 750-800 kg. Management will confirm after next quarter.
Altyn Tor: about 150-160 kg in FY27 and 300-350 kg thereafter, per management comments.
Jonnagiri EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at 65-70% within one to two quarters; Q1 margins were significantly lower.
Altyn Tor revised mine design and life-of-mine plan by October 2026; underground resource above 5 Mt could extend mine life by 6-7 years.
Dividend from Geomysore unlikely in FY27 per management; may come next year, not guaranteed.
Capex: about Rs400-500 Cr per 1,000 tpd plant; Bhalukona 3,000 tpd about Rs650-700 Cr; Altyn Tor underground Rs150-200 Cr in 3-4 years; Jonnagiri shaft work possibly above Rs400 Cr in 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Jonnagiri processing approvals of 1,010 tpd, with expansion to 2,500 tpd being sought; Bhumi Puja done for expansion.
Altyn Tor leach circuit and new tailings dam (10-year life) under construction; commissioning date to be announced after Chairman-level visit next week.
Finland: about 1,500 m drilling from mid-September; Kuikka pit targets about 70 kg gold; underground mines planned.
Chhattisgarh: 15th drill hole under way; plan 3,000 tpd plant; process flow sheet by mid-next-year.
Spain: Dehesa first-phase drilling complete; Maria drilling from end of this month; 40 sq km Maria licence plus 30 sq km pending.
Mozambique: 1,500-2,000 m drilling from September; 200 tpd concentrator by end-2027.
demand_pricing: Management said gold price in Q1 was about Rs1,50,000 per 10 grams and improved in the current quarter, supporting holding inventory.
Tungsten prices up 622% and tantalum up 196% over the last year; lithium up 108%; graphite up 5% (management figures).
Management plans to sell Jonnagiri stock in the coming quarter; Q1 sales lagged production because the inauguration was on June 24.
Dore from Jonnagiri is refined in-house at a small refinery (cost about Rs4-5 Cr); Altyn Tor dore must go to a government refinery at LBMA price.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Jonnagiri profit margin well below the expected ~65% EBITDA, and what is the outlook for Jonnagiri and Kyrgyzstan revenue and profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low Q1 sales (59 kg) and initial expenses explain the low margin; 65-70% EBITDA margin expected in one to two quarters. Further clarity expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex estimate and funding plan for the project pipeline (about Rs2,000 Cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than Rs1,000 Cr is needed for the next two or three projects; funding via offtake arrangements for critical minerals, combined debt and equity; gold projects possibly 50:50 or 40:60 equity to debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhalukona be funded by a rights issue like the earlier Rs80 per share issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm a specific route; said the Rs137 Cr raise is a bridge and a larger QIP may follow once drilling outcomes are clearer.

qa_highlights.question: Will Hutti Gold and Ganajur progress, and what is the legal position?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganajur is a mining lease with court proceedings pending; management cited recent judgments on restoring pre-2015 rights. Hutti is a prospecting licence, so it is more tedious; focus remains on Ganajur.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be dividends from Jonnagiri, and is a strategic promoter being sought?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend depends on Geomysore board; management doubts dividends this financial year. No decision yet on a large strategic promoter; the company remains professionally run.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not refine dore in Kyrgyzstan?
qa_highlights.answer: Kyrgyz law requires dore to be sent to a government refinery, which settles at LBMA price; no in-house refinery is possible there.

541967|2026-06.headline: Sky Gold Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 78% YoY to INR2,013 crores, with gross margin at 9.3% and operating cash flow of about INR30 crores.
541967|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 was INR2,013 crores, up 78% YoY, implying an annualised run rate near the FY27 guidance of INR8,100 crores. Gross margin rose to 9.3% from 9.1% in Q4 FY26, driven by a higher share of non-22KT jewellery and studded products. EBITDA was INR157 crores (7.8% margin) and operating PAT crossed INR100 crores for the first time. Operating cash flow turned positive at about INR30 crores, and working capital days edged up to 60 from 59 in March. Management said it will revise FY27 guidance only after Diwali.

financial_highlights.value: Crossed INR100 crores for the first time

financial_highlights.change: Positive vs negative operating cash flow through FY26
QoQ/as stated by CFO; company no longer gives volume guidance

segments.commentary: Advance Gold share of sales reached 17% in Q1 vs 20% in Q4 FY26 (management says volumes flat, share diluted by higher total volume); contributes about 90-100 bps to revenue and gross margin. Internal FY27 target was 15%.

segments.commentary: Share rose to 14% of volume from 10.5% in Q4 FY26, contributing about 1.4-1.5% to gross margin.

segments.commentary: Share rose to 2.1% of revenue from 1.65% in Q4 FY26, contributing about 0.3% to gross margin. Natural diamonds are about 2% of business.

segments.commentary: Gross margin about 6-6.5%; roughly 70% of this is CZ-studded (margin not stated separately), with plain gold at 5-5.5% margin.

segments.commentary: Export share rose to close to 18% from about 14.5% in Q4 FY26. UAE 6%, Singapore 2%, Malaysia 2% of sales; UK/Europe pipeline of INR30-45 crores, initial UK order of 25-30 kg.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR8,100 crores; management to revise after Diwali (after one more quarter).
FY30 revenue aspiration of INR18,000-19,000 crores, excluding Advance Gold business revenue; PAT target of INR1,000 crores over time.
Gross margin guidance of 8.5-9% blended; PAT margin long-term guidance of about 5.25%.
Operating cash flow to PAT conversion target of close to 20%; revenue growth of 30-35% per year cited for the Sky Gold 3.0 horizon.
Net working capital cycle: reduce by about 2 days YoY, target 52 days by 2030; net debt-free by 2030.
Advance Gold targets: 15% average in FY27, 20% in FY28, 25% in FY29, 30% by 2030. Exports targeted at 20% of sales in coming years.
Zero-salary promoter compensation from FY27; promoter pay linked to dividends paid from operating cash flow, after debt reduction.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation about 60% (stated range 55-57% earlier in the call), against 1.2 tons capacity; management expects utilisation to rise 7-8% QoQ.
Asset-light model: capacity sufficient until 2028. Post-2028 expansion planned on a leased basis, with 120-day lead time to take capacity from 1.2 to 1.10-2.4 tons.
Expansion capex of INR75-100 crores (machinery, furniture and fixtures), about 12-20% of PAT; rent-free period of around 120 days typically available.
Company has 4 facilities; no acquisitions on the table.
demand_pricing: Shift to lower-karat jewellery driven by customer preference and high gold prices; 18KT, 14KT and 9KT gaining share.
Management says gold price volatility has squeezed margins across peers, but Sky Gold maintained margin via back-to-back hedging.
Gen Z brands (CaratLane, Candere, GIVA) growing; 4 large corporates onboarded in 15-18 months, faster than the 24-36 months expected.
Industry organisation: B2C about 40% organised; B2B about 20% organised; management expects 75% organised by 2030.
Seasonality: Q2 (Navratri-Diwali) above Q1; Q3 (wedding season) above Q2; Q4 (March, Akshaya Tritiya deliveries) strongest per management.

qa_highlights.question: Given the Q1 run rate, should FY27 guidance be revised upward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will revise guidance after Diwali; revenue upgrades depend on a greater share of studded and Advance Gold business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory/working capital days rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days moved from 59 to 60. Cash is being redeployed into higher-margin studded jewellery, which needs slightly more working capital; exports rose to about 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in payable days sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold credit is nearly nil while diamond purchases get market-standard credit, so the higher payables are sustainable. Each 1-day change in operating cycle is worth about INR95 crores of operating cash.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt was INR540 crores at quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 60% (55-65% range across standalone and subsidiaries); capacity lasts until 2028, then leased expansion with capex of INR80-100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 growth guidance be given?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 30-35% sales growth under Sky Gold 3.0 and plans to give FY27/FY28 estimates after September.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide PAT margin at 5.25% and gross margin at 8.5-9% when mix is improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was set at end-2025 for a five-year horizon; volume discounts of 0.25-0.5% on large 22KT orders dilute margins. Management said guidance may be improved.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the July 2026 fraud disclosure on Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: INR10.7 crores involved; about INR3.5 crores recovered, legal proceedings initiated and a favourable order obtained. Management declined further comment as the matter is under legal and investigative process.

534425|2026-06.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q1 FY27 same-store sales grew 11.35% and gross margin rose 1.2pp to 71.1%, with management declining to give a INR600 crore revenue target.
534425|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 as the company's 20th consecutive profitable quarter, with same-store sales growth of 11.35% on a like-for-like basis versus Q1 FY26. Gross margin improved to 71.1% from 69.9%, attributed to portion control, reduced inefficiencies and vendor negotiations, despite inflation. Management said July was extremely good versus last July and early August trends were good across dine-in and delivery. Management declined to commit to a INR600 crore revenue figure but said Q3 would be a good quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Grew over last year per presentation

financial_highlights.value: 8-9% from existing food-driven stores; 40% in wetland restaurant

financial_highlights.change: Management expects to maintain by year end

segments.name: Italian (Siciliana)
segments.commentary: Positioned as a growth engine; liquor is about 25% of sales at Siciliana. Paired with Asia Kitchen in mall deals to improve revenue-to-effort ratio.

segments.name: QSR (Walters Burgers, Sweet Bengal)
segments.commentary: Walters has 3 principal stores and 2 cloud kitchens; management says revenue grew about 300% from the prior quarter with one new store added. Plans 10-15 Walters stores this year and 5 new stores by year-end. Sweet Bengal's hero product is Kheer Kadam; shelf life extended to 30 days.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to confirm whether the company would cross INR600 crore in revenue, but said it is working for good percentage growth, with Q3 expected to be a good quarter.

Cash expected to be maintained at around the INR162 crore level by year-end, with capex funded from internal cash generation.
Gross margin historically held within plus or minus 50bps; price increases are used tactically to offset raw-material pressure.
Joint development of the Odisha F&B plot (Speciality Hotels India Pvt Ltd) expected to complete by FY27 year-end; company to hold about 34% of the demerged entity.
capex_capacity: Plan of 8-10 restaurant openings per financial year plus Walters smaller-format QSR units (10-15 this year); 5 new Walters stores by end of this year.
Gong openings planned in Vasant Kunj (Delhi) and a second Pune outlet; Gong currently in Pune and Bandra (Mumbai).
Mainland China renovation programme ongoing ('Mainland China 2'); at least five renovated units have added visible bars.
Kitchen conversion from gas ranges to induction for a hybrid gas/electric setup, after gas shortages; 11 cloud kitchens in portfolio.
