Service charge was withdrawn from 7 June; a price increase was taken to offset it.

Delivery growth was attributed to new formats (Walters, Sweet Bengal, Haka), marketing, tactical discounts and in-house delivery staff; management said delivery is lower-margin but gives operating leverage above revenue thresholds.
Shravan and Ganpati cyclicality was described as having limited impact overall, with a slight Western India impact during Ganpati.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cross INR600 crore in revenue with about 15 new stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a revenue target, citing a positive trend and a focus on good percentage growth, with Q3 expected to be strong.

qa_highlights.question: How was margin expanded despite cost pressure, including gas shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Rate contracts for six months or a full year, pipe-gas supply in Mumbai, and a shift from gas to induction helped; portion-size efficiencies offset inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the delivery mix growth deliberate, and does it hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is driven by consumer demand and new formats, not a deliberate push. Dine-in grew from INR 71 crore to INR 81 crore; AOV is claimed to be among the highest in dine-in brands.

qa_highlights.question: How many stores are planned, and what are the constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: 8-10 restaurants per year plus 10-15 Walters; trained manpower is the main constraint, not locations or capital.

qa_highlights.question: Will price increases be used to protect gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically gross margin held within plus or minus 50bps; tactical price increases are used to offset raw-material and other cost inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Speciality Hotels (Odisha plot) status?
qa_highlights.answer: Joint development is progressing and expected to complete by FY27 year-end; the company will hold about 34% of the demerged entity post completion.

risks_watch: Gross margin sustainability under rising input, staff, power and licensing costs; price increases may be needed.
Trained manpower shortage may limit the pace of restaurant and Walters expansion.
Shift toward delivery (29% of revenue), which carries higher variable costs and tactical discounting.
Brand rationalisation: older brands to be phased out; Bizarre Asia format's future is unclear.
Liquor sales ramp-up targets (8-9% of revenue from food-driven stores) depend on renovations and contracts.
Cash balance guidance (about INR162 crore maintained) relies on internal cash generation for capex.
534425|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins, same-store sales and near-term demand, but evasive on the INR600 crore revenue question and on store-count numbers. Management was also defensive when challenged on delivery mix and the brand portfolio.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,505.6 Cr and gross contribution Rs 78.5 Cr (+14.5% YoY). SMC and corporate software business grew ~82% YoY. DSO rose to 65 days from 47 days, which management attributed to seasonality.

Domestic: some customers in the probable direct-billing list were retained through contract renewals after an OEM moved to direct billing with large customers.

500085|2026-06.headline: Chambal Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 12% to INR 851 crore on 17% margin despite revenue falling 12% to INR 5,000 crore.
500085|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations fell about 12% YoY to INR 5,000 crore as urea volumes dropped on the bunched Gadepan-1 and extended Gadepan-2 shutdowns and complex fertilizer placement was measured. EBITDA rose 12% to INR 851 crore with margin expanding about 350 bps to 17%, and PAT grew 10% to INR 703 crore. Management attributed margin gains to Gadepan-3 urea economics, a currency tailwind, some ammonia sales and advance NPK purchases. Management said the company is preparing for a possible fourth urea plant under the National Investment Policy for Urea 2026, with a Board decision pending.

financial_highlights.change: market debtors INR 841 crore; subsidy receivables INR 2,460 crore

financial_highlights.value: USD 17.25 per unit for the quarter

segments.name: Urea
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,860 crore vs INR 3,109 crore, down 8% on lower production and sales from shutdowns; management said profitability remained healthy. Gadepan-3 was the main margin driver.

segments.name: Complex fertilizers (NPK)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,737 crore vs INR 2,131 crore, down 18% on measured placement during delayed sowing; segment EBIT rose 67% to ~INR 239 crore, helped by earlier advance NPK purchases.

segments.name: Crop protection, specialty nutrients and seeds
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR 430 crore vs INR 458 crore, down 6% on deferred farmer purchases; segment EBIT rose 13% to INR 108 crore with margin ~25%.

NPK margins expected to decline as purchase prices average out, though a certain level will be maintained.

New urea plant (~1.27 million t G3-type capacity discussed): financial bids expected by about mid-October, then Board approval; commissioning indicatively within 2030.
IMACID phosphoric acid capacity expansion from 500,000 t to 700,000 t expected operational around April-June 2027.
Dividend to be maintained at about 25% payout; buyback not on the horizon unless no project visibility.
capex_capacity: Potential fourth urea plant under National Investment Policy for Urea 2026, estimated near INR 10,000 crore (management cited INR 9,000 crore brownfield case in Q&A); Board approval pending.
Management cited EBITDA of around INR 12,000 per tonne for the new urea plant at steady state, against ~INR 13,500 per tonne product price assumption.

TAN project: weak nitric acid and ammonium nitrate solution production started; ammonium nitrate melt trial production from ~15 June; high-density AN nearing commissioning. Sales made but not booked in P&L; proceeds decapitalised the project until commissioning is formally complete.
Q1 AN sales split: G1 ~96,000 t, G2 ~1.85 lakh t, G3 ~3.29 lakh t.
CFCL-TERI Centre of Excellence lab operational; new products expected from FY28-29.
demand_pricing: Industry offtake was subdued early in Kharif: summer crop sowing ~183 lakh ha at end-June, ~23% lower YoY; acreage reportedly caught up by late July after July monsoon revival.
Raw material costs (ammonia, sulphur, phosphatic intermediates) rose sharply on West Asia disruption; prices eased toward quarter-end but remained above historical levels.
Kharif NBS subsidy revised up ~10% but set before the price spike; NPK subsidy announcement delayed, and management expects action around October.
Chambal holds ~8.5-9 lakh t of NPK tied up with vendors for the season; mgmt said it bought advance inventory from January.
Consumption ~404-405 lakh t vs production ~305-306 lakh t, per management.
TAN realisations currently above budgeted margins per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is a fresh application needed for the new urea plant, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the application window is open and a bank guarantee process follows government approval; financial bids should be available by around mid-October, after which Board approval is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Can full G3 capacity be utilised by November?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the plant's maximum run rate is about 9.5-10 lakh t, so the policy-period quantity cannot be completed in time.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the complex fertilizer margin jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Advance NPK purchases made earlier, flagged in the previous call, allowed placement at better margins; management expects margins to decline as prices average out.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new policy return-dilutive versus NUP-2012, and what is the gain-sharing structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the policy is dilutive versus the prior one, citing scale and single-site benefits. The 12%-16% ROE band is indicative with a gas price range of USD 6.5-14; efficiency gains beyond it are not capped, and no gain sharing applies up to eight years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for TAN utilisation and oversupply risk, including Reliance's entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees a possible slight oversupply for about a year, then demand exceeding supply again; it sees no utilisation problem and said Reliance's plans are too speculative to assess.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend and buyback policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend to be maintained at about 25% payout; buyback not planned unless project visibility is lacking.

risks_watch: Subsidy disbursement and NPK subsidy revision timing; receivables of INR 3,300 crore including INR 2,460 crore subsidy receivables.
Gadepan-1 and Gadepan-2 shutdown durations and urea volume recovery.
Sulphur supply and price for IMACID; the JV resumed production in July after a temporary shutdown.
Gas price (provisional USD 17.25 in Q1) and currency movement, which management cited as margin drivers.
Urea policy classification for the existing NIP-2012 plants, which expires by December; government data review is ongoing.
TAN market oversupply risk and potential entry by Reliance; capex cost discipline on the proposed urea plant.
Tape and e-token distribution restrictions; a state suspended its e-token system after agitation.
500085|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operations and the long-term urea opportunity, but cautious on subsidy timing and raw material costs. Management was direct on margin tailwinds and policy dilution, and gave concrete numbers on monsoon-led offtake. Answers on the new urea plant's cost and timing were more qualitative and deferred to Board approval.

Operating (EBITDA) margins guided at 35-40% across segments; management said dredging margins will expand with volumes and it does not expect ~48-63% margins to persist.
FY29 revenue mix target: dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, charter ~5%.
capex_capacity: Capex of close to INR1,000 crore over roughly the next 1.5 years: ~INR250 crore for Green Tugs and green vessels, ~INR450 crore for dredging, balance for shipyard and shipbuilding.
Adding larger TSHDs, CSDs, backhoe dredgers and water injection dredgers; new dredgers of 5,000-7,000 cubic metre capacity cited for deep-sea (Samudra Manthan) work.
Saphale shipyard: Phase 1 to Phase 3 build-out to ~18 vessels per annum; Phase 1 alone 14 vessels.
Portfolio under construction: 10 accommodation boats, 10 work boats, 4 CSD vessels, 2 60-ton bollard pull Green Tugs, 10 hybrid electric passenger ferries.
demand_pricing: Management said dredging faces very little to no competition; it is selective, requiring entry barriers to be met, and targets EBITDA margins of 35-40%.

Bid pipeline results expected in 30-45 days; dredging bids to be executed over 3 years. Maintenance dredging additions of INR100-120 crore in FY27, rising to more than INR250 crore from next year; capital dredging additions ~INR70 crore in FY27 and ~INR150 crore next year.
Historical bid hit rate above 50% over the last 11 years; management said it cannot assume this will continue.
Management attributed peer DCI's margin trend to older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW's fleet is more efficiently utilised.
Green Tug contracts are with Visakhapatnam and V.O. Chidambaranar ports, 15-year fixed charter regardless of utilisation; EBITDA margin cited at 75% for Green Tug.
Export shipbuilding inquiries from Europe for ~3,000 DWT vessels under evaluation; payment terms still being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 growth guidance including the INR60 crore revenue shift from last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier guidance was 30-40% YoY; management now sees potential northwards of 60% for FY27 on order book momentum.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~INR1,300 crore order book executes in FY27 and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging book is expected in FY27. Management said margins will expand, not contract, though not at the 63% operating margin seen in Q1, which it described as not guidance (35-40% stays the guide).

qa_highlights.question: Why are KMEW's dredging margins rising while DCI's are falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCI has older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW is better sweating its assets for efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Subcontracting expense trend?
qa_highlights.answer: FY23-24 subcontracting was high because of a JV structure where KMEW was lead partner. Now projects are executed individually; FY26 subcontracting expected at 5-6% of turnover, mainly shipbuilding and ancillary boats.

qa_highlights.question: Dredging vs shipbuilding mix in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, chartering ~5%. Shipbuilding pre-subsidy margins 15-20%, post-subsidy expected to go beyond 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Is shipbuilding captive or third party, and how is working capital funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 5 captive vessels (3 tugs, 2 boats) and ~42 third-party vessels. Working capital funded from stage payments (every 10-50% milestone), with no further loans needed; shipbuilding subsidy of 15-20% comes on delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Is dredging a moat given privatisation of ports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disagreed, citing perpetual government demand, DCI's 50-year role and tender structure (domestic below INR250 crore, international above).

544131|2026-06.headline: GPT Healthcare Q1 FY27: revenue INR126.2 crore, EBITDA margin 20.4%, PAT up 66% YoY to INR12.7 crore; targets ~21% FY27 EBITDA margin.
544131|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 18.2% YoY and PAT rose 66% in Q1 FY27, with network occupancy at 45.5% and ARPOB at INR42,350. Mature-hospital occupancy excluding Raipur was 58.07%, and ~90% of revenue came from cash and insurance patients. Growth was attributed mainly to case-mix shift toward cardiology, oncology and neurosciences rather than tariff hikes, which come each October. Raipur losses were INR3 crore in Q1, and Jamshedpur (155 beds) is slated for Q4 FY27 commissioning, with a seventh hospital under evaluation to take capacity above 1,000 beds in two years.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26 also INR3 crore loss

segments.name: ILS Hospital Salt Lake
segments.commentary: Occupancy 62% (vs 60% YoY), ARPOB INR45,300 on higher-contribution surgeries; robotic procedures cumulatively above 800.

segments.name: ILS Hospitals Dumdum
segments.commentary: Occupancy 65% (vs 60% last year), ARPOB INR43,041; cardiac surgery started with ~200 surgeries in 5 months; renal transplants above 700.

segments.name: ILS Hospital Agartala
segments.commentary: Occupancy dipped slightly (ALOS cut from ~3.38 to 3 days, plus Tripura tribal-election movement curbs); ARPOB up 70% to INR41,573. Management cited last month's occupancy at ~51%.

segments.name: ILS Hospital Howrah
segments.commentary: Revenue up 31% YoY and occupancy up 16%; MAKO robotic knee replacement programme driving higher-complexity ARPOB.

segments.name: ILS Hospital Raipur
segments.commentary: Occupancy 17% vs 7% a year ago; ARPOB fell from ~INR44,500 in Q4 to INR42,300 due to Ayushman Bharat patient mix. Q1 loss INR3 crore; expected operational breakeven around 20 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected at ~21% vs 19% in FY26 (+200 bps); management put FY27 EBITDA at roughly INR110-115 crore, including other income.
Raipur loss expected to taper through the year; year-end occupancy target ~30%.

Jamshedpur (155 beds) to be commissioned in late Q4 FY27, subject to approvals; could slip to early next year. Expected ARPOB INR38,000-40,000 initially, converging toward Kolkata's ~INR42,000-43,000.
Jamshedpur breakeven in ~24 months; Dumdum and Howrah historically broke even within 12 months.
Dumdum expected to reach optimum occupancy this year and normalise around 70% by Q3 FY27.
Agartala expected to return to pre-disruption international patient levels in about 6 months; year-end occupancy target reaffirmed.
Long-term ROE and ROCE target of around 25%. Annual tariff increase each October, inflation-linked, a small contributor to ARPOB growth.
Management declined to give medium-term occupancy or mature-hospital revenue guidance for now; deferred to MUFG.
capex_capacity: Jamshedpur: 155-bed tertiary hospital under construction, on schedule for Q4 FY27; developer-built asset-light model on long-term rent (rent in the mid-30s INR crore, per management).
Raipur: asset-light model (developer-built building on long-term rent, same as Jamshedpur); ~10 liver transplants per year expected in first year.
Incoming debt of ~INR25 crore for Jamshedpur in FY27; overall debt unchanged YoY.

Seventh hospital under evaluation in Tier 1/Tier 2 eastern and central cities (Cuttack, Ranchi, Patna, Varanasi, Prayagraj), via greenfield or acquisition; target network capacity above 1,000 beds within 2 years.
Recently added: Dumdum cardiothoracic and vascular surgery unit; Howrah MAKO robotic knee programme; Agartala PET-CT and linear accelerator cancer centre (700+ radiation procedures).
demand_pricing: No tariff increase in Q1; ARPOB gains attributed to case-mix and specialty-mix shift. Management said 50-60% of ARPOB increase comes from mix.
Raipur ARPOB dip reflects limited Ayushman Bharat patient intake; management expects ARPOB to hold or rise now that most insurance empanelment is complete.
Government/scheme patients deliberately not pursued in Kolkata due to delayed payments and lower ARPOB.
Attrition: doctors ~6-7% in Calcutta, ~10% in Agartala and Raipur.
Bangladesh medical inflows at Agartala improved on targeted visa policy changes but still below pre-disruption levels.
Howrah: first corporate hospital in its micro-market; growth driven by awareness and consultant additions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Agartala occupancy fall, and is the year-end target intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy fell due to shorter ALOS (3.38 to 3 days, deliberate) and Tripura tribal-election movement curbs in May. Management said last month occupancy was ~51%, and the year-end target is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Raipur loss and ARPOB trajectory on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 loss was INR3 crore, expected to taper. ARPOB fell to INR42,300 from ~INR44,500 on Ayushman Bharat mix; exit occupancy target ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ARPOB rise sustainable, and is it price-led?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff hike in Q1; gains from case mix toward high-end tertiary care. Management hopes it continues and expects Dumdum and Salt Lake ARPOB to rise or hold.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company guide medium-term on occupancy and revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred this to MUFG (IR) with no specific guidance given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 EBITDA run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~21% FY27 EBITDA margin (vs 19% FY26), implying INR110-115 crore including other income.

risks_watch: Jamshedpur commissioning depends on approvals; slippage risk to early FY28.
Raipur ARPOB dilution from Ayushman Bharat volumes, and breakeven timing (~20 months).
Agartala dependence on Bangladesh inflows and regional disruptions; occupancy dipped in Q1.
Doctor attrition at 10% in Agartala and Raipur versus 6-7% in Calcutta.
Lease-based asset-light model implies rent of mid-30s INR crore per hospital, a fixed cost to monitor against ROCE.
Seventh hospital timing and deal terms (greenfield or acquisition) remain undisclosed.

544227|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.3% YoY to INR51.4 crores, but adjusted EBITDA fell 14.5% to INR8.1 crores as growth investments were front-loaded into H1.
544227|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 14.3% YoY to INR51.4 crores, with Uniware up 12.8% and Shipway up 16.8%. Adjusted EBITDA declined 14.5% YoY to INR8.1 crores on planned investments in AI-led product, talent and sales and marketing. PAT rose 20.2% to INR4.7 crores, helped by tax benefits recognised in the quarter. Management guided that investments are front-loaded into H1 FY27, with profitability improvement from H2 FY27, Uniware growth above 15% and Shipway growth above 20% from Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: ~15.8% (as cited by analyst, not disputed by management)
~10.6% (as cited by analyst; ESOP cost ~5% of sales)

financial_highlights.change: +20.2% YoY from INR3.9 crores; attributed to tax benefits recognised in the quarter
expected INR2.5-4 crores per quarter over the next year
up from INR9.1 crores in Q1 FY26
fourth consecutive quarter of improving growth; above 15% excluding exited top-10 client

segments.name: Uniware (OMS/WMS)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 12.8% YoY; stand-alone adjusted EBITDA rose to INR11 crores from INR9.1 crores. Added 115 enterprise customers (vs 88 a year ago, +30.7%). Growth ex-exited top-10 client was above 15%.

segments.name: Shipway (courier aggregation)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 16.8% YoY. Management is raising investment after running near breakeven in part of FY26, targeting 20%+ growth from Q4 FY27 and breakeven in Q3 FY27. Management estimates a INR4,000 crore addressable market where it holds a single-digit share.

segments.name: ConvertWay
segments.commentary: Described as performing steadily; product being extended to wider use cases and larger enterprises. No figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Uniware growth expected to exceed 15% from Q4 FY27 onwards, as Q4 FY27 is the first like-for-like quarter after the top-10 client exit in Q3 FY26.
Shipway growth expected to reach 20%+ YoY from Q4 FY27; Shipway to operate below adjusted EBITDA breakeven in H1 FY27 and at breakeven from Q3 FY27.
Investment front-loaded in H1 FY27 and expected to continue through the current quarter; profitability improvement expected from H2 FY27. Investment amount described only as 'a few crores'.
Uniware adjusted EBITDA margin expected to stay in a similar ballpark to the ~40% level of last year (management cited a move from 32% to 35% on run-rate basis).
Long-term aspiration for Uniware growth to move to late teens and beyond 20%.
capex_capacity: No capex figures or capacity disclosures were given. An analyst noted capex under INR20 crores over two years; management did not dispute this.
Growth investments focused on three areas: AI-led product development (agentic systems), talent and capability additions, and sales and marketing capacity expansion.
Management has launched three modules over the last 12-18 months (UniCapture, UniReco, UniBot) and cited upcoming AI-led launches.
Checkout product being evaluated; launch timing not given.
demand_pricing: Enterprise customer additions: 115 in Q1 FY27 vs 88 a year ago; Q4 FY26 had nearly 149. Management says acquisition is 30-50% above the listing-time run rate of 85-90 per quarter.
Marquee adds in the quarter: Amul, Haldiram's, STUDDS, Pigeon, Mahindra Logistics, The Sleep Company, Snoonu and Namshi (international). Opptra onboarded as a customer for SE Asia and D2C operations.
Module adoption: 40-45% of Uniware enterprise customers use quick commerce and B2B modules; 6-7% use UniReco; 3-4% use UniCapture within two quarters of launch.
Uniware enterprise base is 1,100+ customers. Average realisation is about INR1 lakh per month, broadly stable.
Management said NRR has been 100%+ for several years and expects it to stay there in FY27, but did not give a current quarter figure. Logo churn is mainly small brands shutting down.
Shipway-Uniware customer overlap is 10%+ and has been stable for a couple of quarters while absolute overlap grows.
On competition, management says it is the premium market leader in Uniware and sees a large opportunity against the market leader in courier aggregation.

qa_highlights.question: When will Shipway synergies and acquisition amortisation be absorbed, and when will EBITDA margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investments are front-loaded in H1, with results visible in H2 FY27 and growth improving from Q4 FY27. No quantified margin or amortisation timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ESOP expense so high, and when does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOPs are amortised over four years from grant. About INR2.5 crores was booked this quarter, and the quarterly run-rate is expected at INR2.5-4 crores over the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Shipway revenue been flat near INR20 crores, and when does it ramp up and reach breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 15%+ growth for two quarters, targeting 20%+ from Q4 FY27 and breakeven in Q3 FY27. Shipway is to be run at breakeven, reinvesting profits.

qa_highlights.question: Why do large clients prefer the market-leading aggregator over Shipway, and how many Uniware top-10 clients use Shipway?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the competitor is the aggregation leader and some overlap is natural. Shipway-Uniware overlap is 10%+ and rising in absolute terms.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI-enabled self-built software (vibe coding) displace Uniware?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that Uniware's relationships with ecosystem players, switching costs, maintenance needs and audit-grade data make it resilient; it sees AI as strengthening the system of record.

qa_highlights.question: What are the steady-state margin targets for Uniware and Shipway?
qa_highlights.answer: Uniware adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to stay near last year's ~40% level. Shipway is to operate at breakeven, with profits reinvested for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an M&A pipeline, and is a fund raise planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating start-ups in exploratory stage, with criteria of existing-customer fit, good product and team, reasonable valuation, and profitability or a path to it. No fund raise is planned because cash is building.

517385|2026-06.headline: Symphony Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 8% to ₹378 crore; adjusted PAT up 23% to ₹43 crore, with management warning of near-term margin pressure from input costs.
517385|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 8% YoY to ₹378 crore and EBITDA reported was ₹48 crore (up 26%), but management said June 2026 included a ₹5 crore one-time non-cash charge while June 2025 had ₹9 crore of exceptional income; on that basis EBITDA was ₹53 crore vs ₹38 crore and PAT ₹43 crore vs ₹35 crore. Domestic India revenue grew 15% and modern trade grew over 100%, which management attributed largely to general trade channel inventory being cleared last year. Gross margin was 49.8% and EBITDA margin 12.6%, but management guided to short-term margin pressure from elevated commodity and plastic costs, with only partial price pass-through. Australia (CTPL) remains weak, with management committing to no further capital deployment.

financial_highlights.change: ex ₹5 crore non-cash charge in Jun-26 and ₹9 crore exceptional income in Jun-25
vs ₹37 crore reported; adjusted ₹24 crore in Jun-25
core capital employed ₹73 crore vs ₹136 crore
vs ₹363 crore; after ~₹225 crore repaid to Australia and loans

segments.name: Bonaire USA
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹36 crore vs ₹27 crore (up 35%); EBITDA ₹18 crore vs ₹7 crore; PAT ₹17 crore. Growth driven by scale-up of air cooler models, sold as rebranded Indian SKUs to Home Depot and Lowe's.

segments.name: IMPCO Mexico
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹54 crore vs ₹66 crore; EBITDA ₹3 crore vs ₹7 crore; PAT ₹1 crore. Management cited two consecutive mild summers (2025 and 2026).

segments.name: GSK China
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹34 crore vs ₹24 crore (up 43%); EBITDA ₹6 crore vs ₹2 crore; PAT ₹5 crore. Standalone entity now debt-free after repaying debt and interest to Symphony India.

segments.name: CTPL Australia
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹27 crore vs ₹31 crore; EBITDA negative ₹4 crore vs negative ₹2 crore. Reported PAT of ₹36 crore includes ~₹42 crore one-time gain from sale of Bonaire USA shareholding and IPRs, excluded at consol level.

segments.name: BISP (Beyond India Summer Products)
segments.commentary: Consol TTM sales about ₹560 crore (~48% of consol revenue); standalone TTM ₹179 crore (~23%), with EBITDA near double-digit margin. Mix includes large-space ventilated air coolers, tabletop fans, water heaters and exports.

segments.name: Symphony Brazil
segments.commentary: Not a season in the quarter; no material update given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects short-term margin pressure from elevated input costs (plastic, commodities); quantum not quantifiable yet and depends on how long the war lasts.
Price hikes of 7% to 10% taken outside household coolers; no hike yet in household cooler segment; further hikes planned but extent uncertain.
Management expects Mexico and USA sales to grow significantly in summer 2027 if summer is normal or robust; no numeric target given.
Bonaire USA and GSK China expected to perform well in the current quarter (Q2 FY27), then more muted; Bonaire USA little revenue in the following two quarters.
No inventory overhang at trade or company level as of June 30, 2026; primary off-season buying by channel partners expected in current and subsequent quarters.
capex_capacity: No further capital allocation to CTPL Australia; management said Australia turnaround to be done without deploying additional capital.
Interim dividend of ₹1 per share (face value ₹2) declared for the quarter, total payout about ₹7 crore.
Impairment and write-off at CTPL Australia recorded in FY26; management said it is behind the company.
GSK China and Bonaire USA sell through company-owned or retail warehouses in the US; no new capacity commissioning details given.
demand_pricing: India revenue grew 15% despite pre-summer channel inventory overhang; modern trade (including e-commerce, D2C, large formats) grew over 100%, and modern trade is over one-third of India revenue, with profitability close to general trade.
General trade carried elevated channel inventory from the prior year, which depressed company sales to them; management does not expect 100% modern trade growth to continue.
Standalone exports from India declined due to geopolitical and shipping disruptions; Middle East remains affected and buyer sentiment muted by higher landed costs.
Q1 demand was patchy in North and East India due to uneven weather; no secondary sales expected in the coming quarter, only primary off-season buying.
Coolers in the US are used outdoors and as whole-house or window-mounted units, sold through Home Depot and Lowe's; management said US and Mexico sales were helped by a hot Southwest summer.

544176|2026-06.headline: Aadhar Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 19% YoY to INR282 crores on AUM of INR31,364 crores (+18%), with disbursements hit by a switch to cheque-clearance recognition.
544176|2026-06.overview: AUM reached INR31,364 crores, up 18% YoY, and exit spread held at 5.8% despite a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026. Disbursement was INR2,036 crores on the new cheque-clearance basis, against INR2,359 crores (+19% YoY) on the old cheque-handover basis, as the company moved recognition to clearance from Q1 FY27. Asset quality was stable YoY, with GNPA at 1.31% (down 3 bps) and Stage 2 at 3.3% (down 40 bps), though Q1 credit cost rose seasonally. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth and 17-18% disbursement growth, with the next three quarters targeted above 20%.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: 73% of AUM; non-home loans 27%. Incremental disbursement mix currently 76:24 home vs non-home, versus a historical 70:30.

segments.name: Non-home loans
segments.commentary: Disbursement growth slowed to about 22% in the quarter by the analyst's read; management called the slowdown a deliberate choice linked to the West Asia situation and the riskier profile of these loans.

segments.name: Emerging vs urban branches
segments.commentary: About 450 of 628 branches are in emerging locations. Emerging yields are 14-14.8% versus 11.5-12% in urban; average ticket size rose only from INR10.4 lakh to INR11 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance held: 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth, 17-18% disbursement growth for the full year.
Disbursement growth above 20% targeted for each of the next three quarters; management expects Q2 to close the Q1 shortfall, with Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more.
July 2026 disbursement close to INR900 crores, per management.
Spread floor of 5.5% reiterated; over 2-3 years spreads expected to end near 5.5%, ROA 4.3-4.4% steady state, and ROE around 17% in a couple of years.
Cost-to-income expected to fall 30-40 bps a year; cost-to-AUM about 6-7 bps a year.
Credit cost expected to settle at 23-25 bps for the full year, with GNPA targeted at about 1.1% at year end.
Branch openings of 45-50 planned for Q3; Q1 had only 2 openings versus a 40-50 annual pace.
capex_capacity: Network at 628 branches across 22 states and 550+ districts as of June 2026.
New branches target productivity within 9-15 months; Q1 opened only 2 branches, with 5-7 planned and pushed into July.
Capital adequacy of 42.9% Tier 1 gives room for growth; the IPO's INR1,000 crores primary raise is meant to fund growth for the next 3-4 years. No plan to return capital.
Operational-risk capital set aside at about 6-7% of capital; balance-sheet risk weight about 45%.
demand_pricing: Demand described as healthy and end-user, first-time-buyer driven, particularly in emerging markets; management reports no demand-side issues in urban locations.
Spreads held at 5.8% after a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026; management says it protects spreads over chasing yields.
Management expects 5-7% overlap with new affordable-segment entrants; Aadhar sits one notch below in low-income housing.
Incremental yields flat QoQ; management expects no decline if the urban/emerging mix moves toward 50:50.
NRI-linked exposure described as minimal; state-level rule caps any state at 15% of AUM, incremental disbursement or distribution.
Delhi's share rose slightly, a lower-yield state, yet yields held.

financial_highlights.change: includes ~INR14 crores quarterly ESOP cost; ~33-34% excluding it

543669|2026-06.headline: Keystone Realtors Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72% YoY to INR 470 crores, with EBITDA margin at 21.3% and PAT of INR 52.4 crores, its highest-ever Q1 PAT.
543669|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 pre-sales were INR 617 crores with no new launches, and collections rose 4% YoY to INR 599 crores at 97% collection efficiency. Revenue, EBITDA and PAT all grew sharply, helped by the shift to percentage-of-completion recognition and a richer product mix. Two projects were added (Igatpuri plotted development of about 62 acres and a Dindoshi cluster addition, together about INR 547 crores GDV), and the company reiterated its launch pipeline of about INR 8,000 crores-plus GDV for the year. Operating cash flow was INR 68 crores, which management said will pick up from Q2 and more visibly in Q3 and Q4, while the INR 1,000 crore OCF guidance was reaffirmed.

segments.name: Mass market (Virar JDAs)
segments.commentary: Virar FSI given out via JDAs; about 60% margin net of approval costs, with the unsold portion of about INR 181 crores (32% of INR 570 crores unsold revenue) expected to drive the higher embedded margin of the mass segment (~30% EBITDA margin on unsold). Sold share so far is only about 8%.

segments.name: Luxury / super premium
segments.commentary: Five luxury projects (Panorama, Ocean Vista, Cliff Tower, Bandstand, Parishram-completed) with unsold inventory in four; about INR 12 billion of unrecognised luxury revenue cited. Management is tilting the future pipeline toward premium and super premium.

guidance_outlook: Pre-sales guidance of INR 10,000 crores in FY30 referenced; analyst's implied run-rate for remaining three quarters is INR 4,300-4,400 crores.

Launch pipeline for FY27 of about INR 8,000 crores-plus GDV: Urban Woods (2 towers, INR 300-plus crores), Avinash Towers (Versova), Urbania Thane (2 towers), GTB Nagar Phase 1, Dindoshi cluster, Om Nagar (Andheri East); 28 HQ and Ozone Skye already launched (about INR 2,000-plus crores).
OCF guidance of INR 1,000 crores for FY27 reaffirmed; OCF to pick up from Q2, more visible in Q3 and Q4.
Gross D/E guidance raised to 0.75:1 earlier this year; current 0.3:1. Management does not intend to remain net cash over time.
Unrecognised sold revenue to be recognised over about 2 to 2.5 years on average (up to 3 years for early-stage projects).
Legacy completed-project-method revenue expected to be about 15% of FY27 revenue; about 95% of the legacy portion to be recognised in FY27. From FY28 about 98% of revenue to be on POC.
Plotted development target: INR 500-750 crores annual pre-sales and INR 150-200 crores margin per year, as stated minimum expectation.
capex_capacity: Land and approval investment of INR 232 crores in Q1 FY27 vs INR 151 crores in Q1 FY26, indicating more launches ahead.
About 12 million sq ft under development across 17 ongoing projects.
Igatpuri plotted development of about 62 acres added; plotted projects to be launched only at about 70% readiness.
GTB Nagar (MHADA C&DA): HPC cleared, final signatures pending; launch expected in Q1 or early Q2 FY28 per management. Dindoshi (MHADA): next HPC hearing, then about 2.5-3 months to launch.
Ozone Skye (Goregaon West): RERA approved, work started in July 2026, ready for launch. 28 HQ (Prabhadevi, commercial): construction commenced July 2026.
Investment before go-live targeted at about 10% of GDV under asset-light model; target gross margin around 35%.
demand_pricing: Management says luxury and premium demand is at equivalent levels; mid-mass and aspirational walk-ins are strong depending on location, with Thane and Dombivli performing to plan.
Pre-sales of INR 617 crores achieved without launches, described as resilient sustained sales on a high base.
Bank-backed 10:90 payment plans offered for about 85% of schemes; no more than 30% of buyers opt for them, per management.
Management says interest-rate sensitivity is limited for luxury buyers; the sub-INR 1 crore segment is more rate-sensitive and its share in the pipeline is falling.
Current-year revenue mix: about 40% from completed-project method projects and 60% from POC projects. Gross margin on current projects about 35% and PBT about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt outlook for FY27 and FY28, given the company now reports net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross D/E guidance was raised to 0.75:1 and is at 0.3:1, net debt will likely turn positive over time, and the company does not intend to stay net cash; more than INR 800 crores of cash is held.

qa_highlights.question: Is OCF guidance of INR 1,000 crores intact, and when does OCF pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, INR 1,000 crores guidance remains intact; OCF should begin improving from Q2, with a more noticeable difference in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the mass-market embedded EBITDA margin near 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly product mix: the Virar JDA revenue share carries about 60% margin, and about INR 181 crores of unsold revenue from these JDAs is yet to be recognised, versus only 8% sold so far.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will the INR 63 billion of sold but unrecognised revenue be recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: Average of about 2 to 2.5 years; early-stage projects up to 3 years, late-stage 1 to 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How big will plotted development be in FY30 presales?

qa_highlights.question: Will the GTB and Dindoshi launches slip beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects GTB this quarter or early next quarter and Dindoshi in this financial year, with maybe one quarter's slippage at most.

544288|2026-06.headline: BlackBuck Q1 FY27: total income up ~38% YoY, adjusted EBITDA up 16% to ₹55 crore, with reported PAT at ₹42 crore after a deferred-tax effect.
544288|2026-06.overview: Management said the business recovered through late May and June after a weak April caused by macro logistics headwinds. Revenue from operations grew ~42% YoY and ~10% QoQ, while net revenue grew 25% YoY and contribution margin held at ~93%. Adjusted EBITDA rose from ₹47 crore to ₹55 crore, and reported PAT of ₹42 crore fell sequentially from ₹66 crore because of a deferred tax item recognised in Q4 FY26. Growth businesses (Super Loads and vehicle finance) grew ~44% QoQ after ~20% QoQ last quarter.

segments.name: Core businesses (payments/tolling, telematics)
segments.commentary: Core revenue grew ~21% YoY and delivered a record quarter for profitability and cash flow. Telematics recorded its highest-ever quarterly new device sales, across AI, non-AI and specialised devices.

segments.name: Super Loads and vehicle finance (growth businesses)
segments.commentary: Growth businesses revenue is up ~2.5x YoY and grew ~44% QoQ, up from ~20% QoQ last quarter. Super Loads now operates in 14 cities. Vehicle finance is expected to reach profitability by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: Tolling demand has normalised after April; management says it is back to its normal modelling framework (road growth, toll fare inflation, truck growth).
Fuel business is still uncertain. Management gave no timeline for full recovery in fuel loyalty margins.
Super Loads will keep investing aggressively; investment is stepping up each quarter.
Vehicle finance expected to converge to profitability by end of FY27 (reaffirmed).
Effective tax: for the next two quarters, deferred tax is expected to offset current tax; the loss-utilisation view will be reassessed in Q4.
Super Loads segment-level disclosure expected in about three to four quarters, once the business is large enough.
capex_capacity: Super Loads present in 14 cities (4 initial cities plus 10 launched by March/April 2026); live in under 5% of India's industrial hubs.

First Super Loads hub is close to the ~250 loads/day (about 5,000/month) milestone; management says it is about 60-70% there on playbook building, and 70-80% of newer cities are growing faster than the first four.
Telematics device depreciation is front-loaded over two years, which raised depreciation this quarter.
About 40-50% of Super Loads loads are AI-enabled on a given day.
demand_pricing: Tolling GTV grew 16% YoY, which management says is only a low single-digit rise at NETC level and a higher single-digit rise against the CV market.

Renewal rates for telematics: first renewal around 80% for GPS products (early 70s by some accounts), stabilising in the 80s for second and third renewals; higher-end products run 5-10 percentage points better.
Fuelling is a small share of revenue. Management said loyalty margin spend is discretionary and fuel recovery is only partial.
On Delhivery's possible entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance, management sees it as positive for the industry and does not expect near-term threat.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra (Axis Capital): Which hubs is Super Loads present in, daily load volumes, and outlook for the next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Present in 14 cities; the first four are Bangalore, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Chennai. Super Loads sequential growth was ~50%, up from ~23-24% a quarter earlier. Detailed volume disclosure is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Atul Borse (JM Financial): Will the macro headwinds in tolling and fuelling taper in Q2 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Tolling caution has gone away and BAU is restored after a sharp April contraction in normalised swipe metrics. Fuel is only partially recovered, and management gave no timeline for a full recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Atul Borse: Is Delhivery's entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance a medium-term threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees it as a positive for the industry since there is little qualified competition. It sees no near-term threat and will watch market share closely.

qa_highlights.question: Abhisek Banerjee (ICICI Securities): What drives the 13% growth in transacting users, and what share of users use Super Loads?
qa_highlights.answer: User growth is driven by tolling, telematics and marketplace acquisition, which have been secular for 10-12 quarters. Super Loads is a low-frequency use case and too early to move usage minutes (under 5% of hubs covered).

qa_highlights.question: Monica Joshi: What learnings from earlier cities are being applied to new ones, and how are Bangalore like-for-like numbers trending?
qa_highlights.answer: New cities are layered and run with several parallel experiments; AI-first, less people-dependent workflows are used. Management declined to give like-for-like Bangalore numbers until the segment is large enough to report separately.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra: What is the effective tax rate this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: For the next two quarters, deferred tax is expected to offset current tax. The loss-utilisation position will be reassessed at the end of the year (Q4).

qa_highlights.question: Lokesh Manik (Vallum Capital): Why did depreciation rise, and why did GTV fall from ₹6,800 crore to ₹6,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Telematics devices are depreciated over two years, so depreciation is front-loaded with the device investment. GTV now reports tolling only, with fuelling removed because of fuel price uncertainty.

risks_watch: Fuel business recovery: no timeline given, and fuel loyalty spend is discretionary.
Tolling volume: tolling transactions fell 3% QoQ, and tolling GTV growth (16%) lags NETC and the CV market.
Super Loads investment: spending rises each quarter, and segment-level disclosure is not expected for 3-4 quarters.
Reported PAT volatility from deferred tax; the Q4 loss-utilisation reassessment could move reported earnings.
Potential competition from Delhivery in tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance.
544288|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on telematics, tolling recovery and Super Loads momentum, but cautious on fuel recovery, with no timeline given. Management deflected granular Super Loads metrics and unit economics, citing limited disclosure.

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY; down from ₹66 crore in Q4 FY26 due to deferred tax

544488|2026-06.headline: Vikram Solar Q1 FY27: record 1,006 MW volume (+32% YoY) and revenue ~INR1,563 cr, but EBITDA fell to INR126 cr (8.06% margin) as costs outran pass-through.
544488|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose about 8% QoQ and 38% YoY to roughly INR1,563 crore on 1.06 GW dispatched, with per-watt realisation up 8% QoQ to INR15.02/Wp on DCR mix. EBITDA was INR126 crore (8.06% margin) and PAT INR19.78 crore, as unit COGS rose INR1.86/Wp from metals, EVA, and cell costs that were only partly passed through. Management attributed the squeeze to ALMM-2 uncertainty, Gulf-conflict input inflation, and industry oversupply. It declined to give fresh FY27 guidance, deferring the update to H1 results, and the Gangaikondan module plant (first module 29 June) and cell plant (Q4 FY27) remain on schedule.

financial_highlights.value: 76 MW (cited as ~75 MW later on call)

segments.name: Module – DCR
segments.commentary: 76 MW sold in Q1 at materially higher realisation (DCR ~INR22+/Wp per management). Cell supply is from external domestic partners until own cell line starts; DCR volume expected to grow 2–2.5x each quarter.

segments.name: Distribution channel
segments.commentary: Monthly run rate roughly doubled from ~40 MW last year; network of 119+ distributors and 757+ dealers across 24 states. Management says distribution pricing is spot-linked and realises INR1–1.5/Wp above key accounts.

segments.name: BESS (VSL PowerHive)
segments.commentary: 7.5 GWh BESS assembly plant in Chennai: equipment ordered ~3 months ago, delivery Nov 2026, installation Jan 2027, COD from March 2027. guidance_outlook: No updated FY27 guidance; management will revisit at H1 results. Prior FY27 outlook (given 8 May) referenced as including EBITDA of INR1,500–1,600 crore per an analyst's citation; management did not reaffirm it.
Q2 margins expected to remain under some pressure from unabsorbed prices, partly offset by DCR and channel mix; management declined to say whether 16% margin returns.
Gangaikondan cell line (9 GW) on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27, with ramp possibly spilling into Q1 FY28; FY28 cell utilisation targeted at 40–50% (six-month ramp).
Wafer-ingot capacity resized to 9 GW (from 6 GW, part of the 12 GW plan), project cost ~INR5,600 crore; ground-breaking announced for next month.
Capex of ~INR5,000 crore planned for FY27 and similar in FY28; funding targeted at 75:25 debt-equity, ~70:30 once scheme is in place.
capex_capacity: Gangaikondan: 6 GW module (commissioned 29 June 2026, fully funded); module capacity cited as 15.5 GW total across sites, with 9–9.5 GW expected to be deliverable in FY27.
Gangaikondan 9 GW cell plant: civil/PEB advanced, first cell targeted Q4 FY27; ~70% backward integration once live.

Earlier 3 GW cell phase kept for FY28 on upgraded (non-TOPCon) technology.
Module portfolio transitioned from M10R to G12R; manpower down ~40% on new automated lines. Production volume in Q1 about 1,085 MW.
demand_pricing: Management attributes weak Q1 order flow to ALMM-2 enforcement uncertainty (C&I 15 GW/yr demand waited); ALMM-2 deferred to December 2026 after the 18 July operating memorandum.
Pricing power in non-DCR is under pressure from oversupply (~210 GW cited); cell oversupply limited pass-through of cost escalation.

Chinese landed cell price cited at ~4 cents/W before 27.5% BCD.
Tender pipeline: ~35–40 GW of fresh utility tenders post-August 2025; FY27 AC market estimated at 30–35 GW utility, ~15 GW C&I, 14–15 GW PM Surya Ghar plus KUSUM.

Nature's Basket saw a management change about 45 days before the call and a reset plan focused on inventory, assortment and execution.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about the growth trajectory across Spencer's, Jiffy and Nature's Basket over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give segment targets. Online is guided to ~25% full-year growth, Spencer's offline to mid-to-high single digits, and Nature's Basket to early double digits from Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What KPIs track the Nature's Basket turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Three KPIs: sales per sq ft, rupee gross margin (not percentage), and cost control. Cost cuts are limited in NB's premium format; support overheads were optimised once.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any store expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: No new Nature's Basket stores. Spencer's has no additions this fiscal beyond relocations and cluster tests; a calibrated expansion may come in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Could membership reach 50% of business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management focuses on absolute numbers: target 200,000 members shopping at least 5 times a month, contributing 39-42% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Spencer's growth, volume or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% from more bills and 30% from higher ABV; category mix stable, with member special pricing cited as a driver of basket-wide buying.

qa_highlights.question: Update on quick commerce for Nature's Basket and debt status?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce was not pursued; the tech platform is ready but customer acquisition waits on inventory fixes. Consolidated debt Rs 1,266 crore, with refinancing under way and some expected this month.

risks_watch: Nature's Basket remains loss-making at EBITDA level (negative Rs 2.5 crore) with revenue still down YoY; reset success depends on the new management team.
Q1 EBITDA improvement partly reflects a Rs 10 crore non-operating income gap versus last year; underlying gains need confirmation in Q2.
Debt of Rs 1,266 crore with a large portion due for refinancing this year; closure timing is not yet confirmed.
Spencer's gross margin fell to 18.2% from 19.1% YoY on reported basis; management attributes this to membership accounting.
Online growth relies on order volume with unit economics positive at about Rs 18 per order, and the target is limited customer acquisition spend.

qa_highlights.question: Where would an incremental crane go, India or KSA, and what drives the decision?

qa_highlights.question: Will the blended margin fall as renewables reach one-third of revenue?

qa_highlights.question: Does the 0.72x debt-to-equity imply debt of Rs 1,000-1,100 crore?

qa_highlights.question: Is the ECL provision one-time and is it India-only?

qa_highlights.question: What is the E&C margin outlook, and is 18% wind E&C margin sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Why is GCC DSO 201 days, and when will it fall?

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for GCC capex and is supply delayed by West Asia conflict?

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost and currency terms of new borrowings?

qa_highlights.question: Walter Pack and export revenue have been flat for four quarters; when will they ramp?

qa_highlights.question: What is the TAM and margin profile of the cover glass and display business?
qa_highlights.answer: Display TAM in India is Rs 500–1,000 crore now, rising to Rs 5,000–7,000 crore. Margins not yet quantified; management said it would be 10–20% and expects a clearer answer in Q2 FY28.
