532668|2026-06.headline: Aurionpro Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.3% YoY to Rs 358 crore, EBITDA margin about 17%, with management declining full-year guidance.
532668|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 358 crore, up 6.3% YoY, with Banking and FinTech up about 5% to over Rs 200 crore and TIG up 8.4% to Rs 157 crore. EBITDA was Rs 61 crore (about 17% margin) and PAT was Rs 45 crore. Management attributed the below-trajectory quarter to MEA disruption, project go-live timing, data center milestones, supply chain pressure and capacity diverted to banking product build-outs. Management said demand is not the issue, pointed to a record 23 new logos and the largest-ever US order, and declined to give full-year revenue or margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +8.4% YoY; sequential decline per analyst question
expected to remain similar this year

segments.name: Banking and FinTech
segments.commentary: Revenue above Rs 200 crore, up about 5% YoY. Large share of capacity diverted to banking product build-outs (transaction banking, trade finance), which management said depresses near-term revenue and margin; expected to normalise over one to two quarters.

segments.name: TIG (Transit, Infrastructure, Governance)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 157 crore, up 8.4% YoY, but down sequentially. Data center is about one-third of TIG; management expects it to rise to about 40% of TIG by year-end with 50-100% growth. Data center margin is 4-5 points below enterprise margin.

segments.name: Data center
segments.commentary: Execution started on one of the largest projects; management expects Q2 pickup and more significant acceleration in Q3 and Q4. Growth had run at 40-50%, now expected to exceed that. Not disclosed separately.

guidance_outlook: No full-year revenue or margin guidance; management said too many uncertain factors.
Management expects acceleration through the year, mainly in H2, citing H2 typically larger than H1 and large project execution in Q3-Q4.
Banking to stay a few points above 50% of mix and TIG a few points below 50% for FY27; mix shift more likely next year.
Middle East impact expected to be gone by Q3 on a year-on-year basis; some Middle East wins hoped for in the next one to two quarters.
Operating cash flow: H1 likely negative or close to zero; management intends to show progress through the year and will update at mid-H1.
No significant acquisitions planned for the next few quarters; R&D expense not to increase meaningfully.
capex_capacity: Capacity is being built in advance for data center demand, which is currently weighing on the cost structure.
Banking capacity diverted to product build-outs (transaction banking, trade finance, AI-native stack); management expects this to normalise over one to two quarters.
Data center business consumes very little capital, according to management.
Workforce expansion is being paced gradually; management said there is no fundamental capacity shortfall and productivity gains from AI tools will offset some capacity diversion.
Management described the business as about 13-14 P&Ls, mostly product P&Ls.
demand_pricing: Record 23 new customer logos in Q1; largest-ever US order; a large transaction banking mandate; Mumbai Metro and Delhi Metro transit mandates.
Order book described as strong and pipeline as the busiest management has seen; management said it would not discuss deals before closing.
Middle East revenue fell to zero from double-digit share last year; management said it lacks a good handle on the timing of recovery.
Transaction banking win rates upwards of 50% on products once built out, per management.
Management said conversion is slowed by long project duration (large deals versus typical 12-month projects) and capacity ramp-up needs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TIG decline sequentially despite data center execution starting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the large data center deal takes time to ramp; Q2 will see a pickup and Q3 and Q4 a more significant one.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin drop given banking grew faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin fell due to revenue, business mix and capacity converting order book to revenue; R&D expensed on product build-outs temporarily lowers EBITDA. Banking margins expected to strengthen over three to five years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company provide full-year guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it sees acceleration through the year, especially H2, but will not give revenue or margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Data center margin and full-year margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Data center margin is four to five points below enterprise margin for now; management expects volume to offset this and margins to improve over a multi-year period.

qa_highlights.question: Will data center be disclosed as a separate segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will consider sub-segment disclosure internally, without commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 cash conversion target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 operating cash flow is likely negative or close to zero due to payment cycles; progress expected in H2 with an update at mid-H1.

risks_watch: Middle East: no deal closures yet; revenue from the region fell to zero from double-digit share last year.

Execution: sequential TIG decline and conversion below normal trajectory; H2 acceleration depends on large projects keeping to schedule, with management warning that a slip from Q4 to Q1 could be material.
Margin: EBITDA margin about 17% versus a 20-22% earlier reference; R&D at about 10.5-11% and data center mix are headwinds.
Cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow likely negative; management to update at mid-H1.
Employee cost growth versus flat-to-slow revenue growth, as raised by an analyst; management attributes this to capacity build and productivity gains.
532668|2026-06.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic but evasive on forward numbers: management declined full-year guidance and sub-segment disclosure, and repeatedly deferred H2 acceleration claims. It was candid about execution shortfalls in the Middle East, banking conversion and capacity.
key_quotes: This is not really a demand issue. Our order book is strong. The pipeline is healthy.
I don't want to get into giving guidance right now. I don't think we can do a very accurate job at it right now.

519183|2026-06.headline: ADF Foods Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, but EBITDA margin of 17.7% was flattered by INR19.69 crore tariff refund; freight cost ~3% of revenue.
519183|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with consolidated EBITDA up 26% to INR29.7 crore (17.7% margin) and PAT up 13.4% to INR17.3 crore. Management said the figures include tariff-refund benefit, and that adjusting for freight (~3% of revenue) the margin would be about 13.4% to 16.4% depending on the basis quoted on the call. Standalone revenue rose 20.5% to INR120.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 22.8%. Shipments were constrained by container and vessel shortages, with about 30% of ready goods unshipped in June, and management reiterated FY27 revenue above INR900 crore with high-teens EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Processed foods
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore, up 28.5% YoY, with segment EBITDA of INR31.2 crore (21.6%). Management attributed the margin to product mix and frozen foods momentum.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.2 crore at 11.5% margin. Management said quarterly segment margins are seasonal and full-year margins will track historical ranges.

segments.name: Brands (Ashoka, Truly Indian, Soul)
segments.commentary: Ashoka growing above 30% in the latest quarter, with a 5-year revenue CAGR above 20%. Truly Indian is in 3,000+ US stores, with about 60% of growth from existing stores and 40% from new listings. Soul relaunch is still slow.

segments.name: B2B / private label
segments.commentary: Management put the sales split at about 75% own brands and 25% B2B and private label.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue upwards of INR900 crore, conditional on geopolitical and shipping conditions easing.
High-teens EBITDA margin guided for FY27 and beyond, excluding tariff refunds; management expects a return to 16-17% over about nine months as freight pass-through takes effect.
Freight pass-through began in Q1 FY27: about 75% in the US and 65-70% of total business overall, with some markets deliberately not passed on.
Surat revenue of about INR40-50 crore expected in FY27, with management saying the number is intact.
Surat full-scale utilisation expected in 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation this year and full utilisation around FY30.
Depreciation to rise by INR25-30 crore as Surat Phase 2 lines come in around Q3, with a further INR20-25 crore capex in FY27.
PLI scheme (about INR16 crore in FY26, about 2% of revenue) is in its final year; management hopes for an extension.
Q2 shipments expected to carry forward from Q1, but the carry-forward could slip into Q3 if container constraints persist.
Management said there are no further US tariff refunds expected; a USD2.8 million court award is under recovery discussion.
capex_capacity: Surat greenfield facility (frozen foods) began commercial deliveries and initial container shipments after commencing trial production in late March 2026; about 15 containers shipped in early Q1.
Surat at full capacity is expected to deliver a little under INR300 crore in revenue. Combined with brownfield capacity, total potential is about INR1,250 crore ex-agency at full ramp.
Phase 2 lines at Surat are expected in Q3, with residual capex of INR20-25 crore for FY27.
Management expects full utilisation of the combined capacity around FY30.
demand_pricing: Order book described as the strongest in company history for June, July and August, but about 30% of ready goods could not be shipped in June because of container and vessel shortages.
Management said consumer demand for ready-to-eat, frozen and shelf-stable Indian foods remains healthy across markets.
Pricing: freight costs passed through to customers from Q1 FY27 (about 3% of revenue impact). Tariff benefits will be passed back selectively by category to support market share.
Competition in Truly Indian is mainly from local US manufacturers of Indian-style foods, not Indian brands.
Management said the UK and Europe region should grow at high double digits, supported by a planned Ireland step-down subsidiary and FTAs.
West Asia disruption: March was very weak with no shipments; shipments resumed from end-April and are back near the 15% share of business previously affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and when will it reach the INR275 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full capacity will take 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight impact on margin and what is sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight impact about 3% of consolidated revenue; margin ex-freight was about 16.4% and about 13.4% after adjusting for tariff refund. Guidance is high-teens, with freight pass-through supporting recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR900 crore revenue target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it remains cautiously optimistic, conditional on easing geopolitical and shipping conditions; the order book and demand support it.

qa_highlights.question: Treatment of the remaining tariff refund balance in the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance will be evaluated against customer arrangements and recognised over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI contribution and its impact after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: PLI was about INR16 crore in FY26 (about 2% of margin). Final year is FY27; management expects brand investment as a % of sales to fall as brands scale.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 see catch-up from Q1 shipment shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Some carry-forward is expected in Q2, but it could slip into Q3 if container availability does not improve.

risks_watch: Container and vessel availability; a carry-forward of unshipped goods could push revenue from Q2 into Q3.
Freight costs and whether pass-through holds in the US, where roughly 75% of freight increase is being passed on.
Tariff: the 10% rate is still applicable, with no certainty on the future rate.
Margin dependence on the one-time tariff refund and on PLI, which ends after FY27.
Surat ramp-up is slow (about 30% utilisation this year), which limits near-term operating leverage.
Soul domestic brand is growing slowly, while brand investments in Truly Indian and Soul continue.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR24 crore a year earlier per analyst

financial_highlights.value: USD2.08 million = INR19.69 crore received; USD0.77 million (~INR7 crore) booked in P&L in Q1

544405|2026-06.headline: Belrise Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR25,465 million, EBITDA margin 11.5%, PAT up 9% to INR1,217 million.
544405|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY, led by manufacturing revenue up 20% to INR21,979 million, while trading revenue fell about 19% on Middle East disruption. EBITDA rose 5% to INR2,933 million, with margin down to 11.5%, and manufacturing EBITDA margin at 12.7%. Management reported a INR17,000 million QIP and the Hyva India tipper acquisition (completion expected Q3 FY27), and a run of new order wins across two-wheeler, renewable energy, and commercial vehicles. Management said cost pressures from steel, polymer, staff and energy have peaked and FY27 EBITDA margins should stay broadly stable versus FY26.

segments.name: Two- and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed about 81.4% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; management said segment revenue grew about 18% YoY, below industry growth of roughly 20-25%, attributed to customer mix.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 4.6% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; H-One high-tensile steel capability up to 1470 MPa cited as a differentiator.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.5% of manufacturing revenue; four-wheeler and CV revenue grew about 18% YoY per management opening remarks; Hyva India tipper acquisition announced 4 August 2026.

segments.name: Others (incl. aerospace, defence, renewables, trading)
segments.commentary: About 5.5% of manufacturing revenue. Trading business fell about 19% YoY due to Middle East crisis and logistics; management expects mid-teens group revenue growth. Aerospace and defence target is at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margins broadly stable versus FY26, with no material margin impact from input costs given back-to-back pricing.
Group revenue growth guided at mid-teens with stable EBITDA margins.
Majority of INR17,000 million QIP proceeds to be deployed within FY27, mainly for inorganic opportunities in aerospace and four-wheeler/CV, plus some organic growth.
Hyva India tipper business acquisition expected to complete in Q3 FY27; deal to be EPS and ROCE accretive from day one per management's stated threshold.
Aerospace and defence to reach at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

New programs (chassis for fast-growing 2W OEM, US solar tracker assemblies, Sambhajinagar 2W chassis, brake assemblies) to start production in Q4 FY27; margin pressure expected to ease in coming quarters as pass-through takes effect.
capex_capacity: Four new facilities coming up, including brownfield facilities; fixed costs ramping ahead of revenue, per management.
Bangalore brownfield facility to host new 2W chassis program (annual revenue above INR650 million), SOP expected Q4 FY27.
US solar tracker sheet-metal assembly setup to support about 2.5 GW annual supplies; peak annual revenue above INR1,500 million; production from Q4 FY27.
Expansion at existing Maharashtra facilities to support a 59-assembly EV localisation program for a large Indian CV OEM.
Hyva acquisition includes three manufacturing facilities in Pune, Jamshedpur and Bangalore.
Management declined to disclose utilisation or ramp-up details for specific facilities such as Bangalore and Haridwar.
demand_pricing: Order wins: 2W/3W chassis for fast-growing OEM (above INR650 million annual revenue, on top of about INR900 million fuel tank and exhaust win last quarter); cumulative about INR1,550 million with that OEM, about INR2,000 million including suspension and braking wins.
Suspension systems now supplied to five 2W/3W OEMs, including a new Vietnamese 2W entrant in India, with suspension and braking.
Two-wheeler chassis order for an existing model at a large 2W OEM's Sambhajinagar plant, potential annual revenue of about INR500 million.
Management attributed slower 2W/3W growth to a customer mix gap with faster-growing OEMs, with new OEM ramps expected in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Trading business decline was due to Middle East crisis hitting African, Asian and Middle Eastern demand and logistics; management says the worst is behind it.
Input cost pressure (steel, polymer, energy, logistics, minimum wage hike) persisted in Q1; management expects pass-through in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new chassis order additional to earlier two-wheeler wins from South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it is over and above the exhaust and fuel tank win from last quarter (about INR900 million), making about INR1,550 million cumulative annual run-rate with that one OEM.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure remains from commodities, staff costs and energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity, staff and energy/transport cost pressures have largely peaked, with staff cost rise tied to the annual increment cycle and pre-hiring for four new facilities; pass-through expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can management quantify the benefit from raw-material pass-through and the trading decline's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify either on the call and offered to respond offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did 2W/3W growth (about 18%) lag industry growth (about 20-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a customer mix issue, as some faster-growing OEMs it does not work with closely gained share; newly penetrated OEMs should add volumes in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aerospace and defence revenue outlook and the Plasan Sasa defence opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 10% of manufacturing revenue from aerospace and defence in the short-to-medium term; Belrise already exports parts to Plasan Sasa in Israel, with progress described as gradual given geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: Can H-One and Mag Filters revenue be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said it manages the business as one group and will not disclose segment-level numbers for H-One or Mag Filters.

523716|2026-06.headline: Ashiana Housing Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR107 crores from INR293 crores as handovers slipped; management reiterates INR2,200 crores FY27 presales target.
523716|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 bookings were INR358 crores across 234 units (3.6 lakh sq ft), down from the strong prior quarter, while collections rose 6% YoY to INR409 crores. Average realisation rose 37% YoY to INR9,923 per sq ft on product mix. Reported revenue was INR107 crores, driven by Phase 1 handover at Ashiana Nitara, Jaipur; management attributed the shortfall to handover timing, with OC for Anmol Phase 3 and Amarah Phase 1 (about INR532 crores of revenue) arriving mid-July and shifting into Q2. The company bought 28.55 acres at Vadgaon, Maval, Pune, its largest Senior Living land deal (about 20 lakh sq ft, potential sales value around INR1,800 crores).

financial_highlights.change: Moderated vs exceptionally strong preceding quarter
Analyst noted units were 407 a year earlier
vs INR293 crores in Q1 FY26
vs INR108 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Senior Living
segments.commentary: About 23% of the business per management, up from about 10% five to six years ago. Presales were about INR570 crores last year; management targets about INR1,500 crores by FY29-30 and about 25% CAGR long term. Five projects are deployed, and the company aims for about INR10,000 crores GDV in Senior Living.

segments.name: Regular housing (Gurugram, Jaipur, Bhiwadi)
segments.commentary: Management flagged a near-term lack of inventory to sell in these key markets, which is expected to dampen presales in the next year or two. Ashiana Aaroham Phase 3 (Gurugram) is the big H2 launch.

segments.name: Elite and Premium homes
segments.commentary: Ongoing portfolio mix at 36%, per the analyst's figure. Management said the mix shift is toward Senior Living, not a pivot to premium homes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales target of about INR2,200 crores, which management says is on track; July 2026 cumulative sales were about INR859 crores.
Expected H1 FY27 presales exit of about INR1,050-1,100 crores by 30 September 2026.
FY27 reported revenue indication of about INR2,000 crores.
Target ROE floor of 15% on a long-term basis; management expects about 20% ROE in FY27 on a reported basis.
FY27 deployment budget of about INR800 crores for new land and deals, including about INR180 crores deployed in Q1.
Vadgaon (Pune) underwriting: about 20 lakh sq ft, INR9,000-10,000 per sq ft realisation, around 2 lakh sq ft sold per year, launch in H2 of next financial year.
capex_capacity: Vadgaon, Maval, Pune: 28.55 acres acquired in Q1 FY27 for about 20 lakh sq ft saleable area, about 10-year development at base case (about 7 years at 3 lakh sq ft per year). Funded through a debenture structure with landowners holding 25% of purchase value and a 6% revenue share.
Ashiana Aaroham Phase 3 (Gurugram) launch expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27.
Bengaluru (Kanakapura Road) Senior Living project: documentation pending; two team members deployed to prepare launch.
Ashiana Nitara Phase 1 (Jaipur) handover commenced in Q1 FY27.
Business development active in Jamshedpur (small deal expected soon), Chennai, Mumbai, Pune and NCR; further Bengaluru transactions targeted for Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management described residential demand as softer in the quarter on global uncertainty and wait-and-watch buyers, with prices resilient across most markets.
Senior Living is seen as insulated from cyclicality; management says organised supply is limited.
Sales-and-marketing costs fall as a location matures: Ashiana Shubham (Chennai) fell from about 8% to 4-5% of sales.
Gurugram resale control: management says resale stock should not exceed about 20% of Amarah Phase 1, versus 80-90% trading at peers.
Anmol Phase 3 and Amarah Phase 1 gross margins are in the mid-20s blended; Amarah Phase 3 onward margins are expected to be substantially better.

qa_highlights.question: What drives H2 bookings and confidence in FY27 guidance after a soft Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said July 2026 sales beat all of Q1; cumulative FY27 sales were about INR859 crores by 31 July. The big H2 launch is Aaroham Phase 3 (Gurugram) in Q3 or Q4, and H1 is expected to exit at INR1,050-1,100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable presales trajectory over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a dip in presales for a year or two due to thin inventory in Gurugram, Jaipur and Bhiwadi, with recovery in FY28-29 or FY29-30. Capital is shifting to Senior Living, with a target of about INR1,500 crores of Senior Living presales by FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Why ROE expectations changed from 20%+ to 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15% has been the long-term goal and was reached on a reported basis last year. It expects about 20% in FY27 and says 15% should be the floor. The margin framework is about 30% gross, 12% SG&A, 18% PBT and 12-13% PAT margin, which should give teens ROE and about 20% with further improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue so low, and is it a steady-state run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was not normal. Anmol Phase 3 and Amarah Phase 1 OCs came in mid-July, so about INR532 crores of revenue shifts into Q2. Management asked investors to judge on a year-on-year basis and pointed to the FY27 revenue indication of about INR2,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Units sold fell from 407 to 234 YoY. Deliberate or volume slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not entirely deliberate, citing lower inventory in some markets. It pointed to the July launch and reiterated the INR2,200 crores presales target.

qa_highlights.question: Vadgaon payback and underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Underwriting assumes INR9,000-10,000 per sq ft on 20 lakh sq ft, or INR1,800-2,000 crores of revenue. Sales are planned at about 2 lakh sq ft per year, with a launch in about 18 months. The NCD was issued by the landowners, who keep a 25% stake plus a 6% revenue share.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for the deals in pipeline and IFC partnership status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 deployment budget is about INR800 crores, including Q1 deals and deals in active discussion. The IFC platform is exhausted or lapsed because of ticket-size caps. There is no active agreement, though discussions on future capital are ongoing.

544226|2026-06.headline: Brainbees Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to ₹2,106 crore, but India multi-channel gross margin fell ~260 bps YoY, holding adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.24%.
544226|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to ₹2,106 crore, with GMV up 12% to ₹2,807 crore and AUTC up 10% to 11.8 million. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 4.24% from 4.98%, and gross margin dropped to 36.5% from 38.5%, mainly from India multi-channel diapering competition and manufacturing cost pass-through lag. Management said diapering competition is easing and that the crude/rupee cost pass-through completes by end-Q2, but gave no firm timeline for margin recovery. Growth drivers cited were RocketBees (over 50% of online shipments), FC Qwik (125,000 shipments in June across 12 cities) and offline GMV growth of 15%.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY, best in seven quarters; GMV +12%, orders +12%, AUTC +10%. Non-diapering is ~85% of GMV; gross margin down ~260 bps YoY and EBITDA margin down ~290 bps YoY on diapering competition and manufacturing input costs. Remains PAT positive.

segments.name: International (Middle East)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12% YoY, AUTC +7%, GMV +9%. Adjusted EBITDA loss reduced 22% YoY; loss-to-revenue improved from 10% to 7%. Management targets EBITDA neutrality but gave no timeline.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat due to a planned warehouse and inventory transition for one core brand, expected to complete in Q2 with growth recovering from Q3. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% from 1%.

segments.name: Preschool (FirstCry Intellitots)
segments.commentary: Revenue +47% to ₹19 crore and adjusted EBITDA +65% to ₹5 crore. Over 500 preschools; management targets at least 1,000 over the next couple of years, organically, with no M&A being evaluated.

guidance_outlook: Management expects India multi-channel growth to stay elevated for subsequent FY27 quarters, citing RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline store expansion.
Crude/rupee-linked price increases in manufacturing expected to be fully passed on by end-Q2 FY27, with full margin normalisation for that component from Q3.
Diapering margin recovery expected over four to six quarters, with competitive intensity easing in July and August per management.
Adding around 100 net offline stores in FY27 (management said 90-100); FY28 expansion expected to be larger.
Management declined to give a timeline for International EBITDA breakeven, pointing to input metrics instead.
Management said the 280 bps gross margin gap should 'dramatically' reduce, but gave no quantified target for the full year.
capex_capacity: Offline store expansion was paused for two quarters to realign the product portfolio; now resuming with ~100 net new stores targeted in FY27.
RocketBees expanded from 62 to 72 cities and now handles over 50% of online shipments, a target set two quarters ago and met by June 2026. Delivery turnaround time improved ~20%.
FC Qwik (2-hour quick delivery) grew from ~60,000 shipments in five cities in March to 125,000 in 12 cities in June. Management targets 10% of total shipments on FC Qwik and 20% in specific pincodes.
Manufacturing business is passing crude-linked raw material and rupee-depreciation cost increases to customers.
demand_pricing: Diapering faces heightened competition from quick commerce discounting and new entrants. Management says branded diapering has started improving in Q1 and competitive intensity is softer in July and August.
Non-diapering categories (~85% of GMV, fashion >50% of GMV, home brands >50% of business) are performing well; management said gross margin is expected to improve through home brand and fashion mix.
GMV growth (12%) trails India revenue growth (18%) because the revenue line includes manufacturing and the GMV is at MRP, with GST 2.0 reducing MRP from Q2.
Management said non-diapering consumables are about 15% of India GMV, with healthy margins and no challenge from quick commerce.
Offline GMV grew 15% in Q1 after the width-to-depth assortment change, which added lower price points without a material gross margin impact.

financial_highlights.value: Down ~260 bps YoY (~20 bps recovered vs Q4's 280 bps drop)

financial_highlights.metric: International adjusted EBITDA loss as % of revenue
GlobalBees adjusted EBITDA margin (post corporate expenses)

532927|2026-06.headline: eClerx Q1FY27 operating revenue rose 15.2% YoY to USD 125.9M with 2.8% QoQ growth, its 12th straight sequential increase; EBITDA margin 23%.
532927|2026-06.overview: Q1FY27 operating revenue was USD 125.9M (up 15.2% YoY, 2.8% QoQ) and INR 11,524M (up 23% YoY), the 12th consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Operating EBITDA was INR 2,652M at 23% margin, down 260 bps QoQ mainly on wage increments, and PAT was INR 1,643M (14% margin). New deal wins were USD 41M (up 25% YoY). BFSI was roughly flat QoQ and Media/Retail/Fashion remained soft, while Analytics and Automation crossed a USD 100M annual run rate. 532457|2026-06.headline: Gulshan Polyols Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR646 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA rose 135% to INR91 crore, a 14.2% margin.
532457|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of about INR646 crore was the highest quarterly turnover in company history, up 8% YoY. EBITDA of INR91 crore grew 135% YoY, with margin at 14.2% versus 6.5% a year earlier, and PAT of INR54 crore rose about 307% YoY. Ethanol was the main driver with an 18% segment EBITDA margin, while grain processing improved from weak levels and mineral chemicals stayed steady. Management called Q1 exceptional on favourable raw material prices and high DDGS prices, and kept FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling a conservative stance.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR426 crore and EBITDA INR81 crore (18% margin); largest contributor to revenue and profit. Installed capacity about 26 crore litres per annum; order book about 19 crore litres.

segments.name: Grain processing (starch, sorbitol, derivatives)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR170 crore and EBITDA INR8 crore in Q1. FY27 guidance is revenue about INR800 crore at about 5% EBITDA margin; no capacity expansion this year.

segments.name: Mineral chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR24 crore and EBITDA INR5 crore (23% margin). Described as stable; no significant capacity expansion planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of about INR2,600 crore, unchanged.
Ethanol revenue about INR1,700-1,800 crore on supplies of about 22 crore litres (Q&A cited 21-22 crore litres generating about INR1,800 crore).
Grain processing revenue about INR800 crore; mineral processing about INR100 crore.
Consolidated EBITDA margin about 10-11% and PAT margin about 5-6%; management said it expects to end the year above these margins but is guiding conservatively.
Ethanol debottlenecking to lift utilisation to 100-110% of existing capacity by FY28, with capacity up about 15-20%.
On-site plant at Trident expected to be operational by end of FY27, adding some revenue.
capex_capacity: Majority of recent capex is complete; FY27 focus is on utilisation and cash flow, with only ethanol debottlenecking planned.
Major expansion into specialty and import-substitute chemicals, grain-based derivatives, expected from FY28; products still under evaluation and not yet named.
Starch capacity to be ramped to 100% utilisation by end of FY27; no starch expansion this year.
Capital subsidy of INR5 crore received from Madhya Pradesh in Q2, adjusted against plant and machinery capex.
Ethanol plants at Assam and Madhya Pradesh; four plants in total grinding about 3,000 tonnes of grain per day.
demand_pricing: Government support for ethanol: E20 achieved; E30 targeted by 2030. Management said higher blending beyond 20% may slip 6-12 months because of protests, but E20 will not be rolled back.
Ethanol feedstock mix: about 40% FCI rice, about 50% maize, about 10% broken rice/DDGS.

Maize prices currently INR23-25/kg across plants (Assam 23, Muzaffarnagar 23, Gujarat 24, MP 25); Q1 raw-material costs were favourable and Q2 is seasonally pressured until the Kharif harvest in October-November.
Maize DDGS priced at about INR20-22; stable for about two quarters. DDGS contributes about INR10 per litre of ethanol cost.
Grain processing: domestic starch and derivative prices improved as exports began from Gujarat; sorbitol exported to more than 40 countries. Management expects a sharp YoY improvement in the segment.
Inventory cap of 30-45 days of grain because of storage and working-capital limits, so raw-material volatility is only partly hedged.
Talks on opening ethanol exports to neighbouring countries (Japan, Indonesia mentioned in press); not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong Q1 ethanol margin a one-off, given FY guidance of about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was exceptional on favourable raw material prices and record DDGS prices. Q2 is seasonally weak, and H2 (Q3-Q4) is usually stronger; guidance is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Will E30 timelines slip given protests?
qa_highlights.answer: E20 will not be rolled back. E30 is set for 2030, and blending beyond 20% may be delayed by 6-12 months. Steady-state ethanol demand is not expected to be affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ethanol order book and how confident is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: About 19 crore litres already received, with about 2 crore litres more expected. Management is confident of 21-22 crore litres for FY27, generating about INR1,800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw-material price volatility managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocking is capped at 30-45 days of grain. Management will stock up during the April and October harvests, and the full-year margin is expected to average out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term ethanol growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity to rise 15-20% through debottlenecking, targeting 100-110% utilisation of existing capacity by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the grain processing underperformance and what is the recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recovery has started with a big YoY margin improvement. Starch capacity is to reach 100% by year-end, with FY27 grain processing EBITDA margin about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export exposure and hedging approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about INR18 crore, or 5-6% of quarterly turnover. The company does not hedge FX and relies on a natural hedge from equivalent imports.

qa_highlights.question: Were any government subsidies recognised in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Grants and incentives are accounted for on a receipt basis, and nothing was received in Q1. INR5 crore MP capital subsidy was received in Q2 and adjusted against capex.

risks_watch: Q2 seasonal pressure on maize and grain costs before the Kharif harvest; margins may fall short of Q1 levels.
Possible 6-12 month delay to blending beyond E20 because of protests, which could slow incremental ethanol allocations.
Grain processing (starch) remains low-margin, around 5% EBITDA guided, with a recovery still to be proven.
Specialty chemical expansion from FY28 has no named products or capex figure yet.
Ethanol export opening is still at talk stage; timing is uncertain.
Reliance on OMC purchase orders for the 2 crore litre balance not yet received.

544580|2026-09.headline: Canara Robeco AMC Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 17% YoY to INR 121.6 crores and PAT rose 21% to INR 59.2 crores.
544580|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 17% YoY to INR 121.6 crores and PAT grew 21% to INR 59.2 crores, with H1 PAT up 23% to INR 134.8 crores. Closing AUM was INR 1.17 lakh crores, with September quarterly average AUM up 4% YoY, while management described the quarter as challenged by a roughly 6% Nifty fall in September. The company declared an interim dividend of INR 2 per share. Management did not disclose net flows, and analysts questioned SIP book and folio trends, which management attributed to ELSS tax-law changes, vintage SIP maturities, and market-driven closures.

531595|2026-06.headline: Capri Global posted record Q1 FY27 PAT of INR353 crore (+102% YoY) on AUM of INR40,112 crore (+62% YoY) and cost-to-income of 44.2%.
531595|2026-06.overview: Capri Global reported record quarterly profit after tax of INR353 crore, up 102% YoY, with consolidated AUM of INR40,112 crore, up 62% YoY and 10% QoQ. Gold loans (48% of AUM) drove growth, with AUM of INR19,179 crore (+111% YoY, +13% QoQ), while cost-to-income improved to 44.2% from 49.4% in Q4 FY26. Asset quality weakened at the margin: gross Stage 2 ratio rose to 3.8% from 2.8%, mostly on gold loans, and gross Stage 3 rose to 1.1%, largely from one construction finance account. Management revised its FY28 AUM target to INR65,000 crore and reiterated medium-term ROE of 19-21% and ROA of 4.2-4.7%.

financial_highlights.metric: Blended yield / spread on net advances

financial_highlights.change: Gross Stage 3 up INR74 crore QoQ

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR19,179 crore, +13% QoQ and +111% YoY; gross NPA 0.3%; 1,000 branches with productivity of INR19 crore per branch (from INR17 crore); disbursal LTV about 71%. Gold yield about 18.5%, management expects 50-75 bps more improvement.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: AUM INR6,779 crore, +24% YoY; disbursements INR616 crore, +32% YoY. Micro-LAP AUM INR876 crore. Share of AUM has declined as capital was prioritised to gold loans.

segments.name: Housing finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR7,815 crore, +42% YoY; self-employed customers about 75% of AUM; new South India branches disbursing about INR65 crore per month.

segments.name: Construction finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR6,332 crore, +40% YoY across 291 active projects; PCR raised to 70%; Stage 3 up INR31 crore QoQ on one account, with about INR30 crore recovered from an old NPA account.

segments.name: Co-lending and DA
segments.commentary: AUM INR8,126 crore, +74% YoY and +4% QoQ (20% of AUM); income INR65 crore, -8% YoY. 6 of 11 partner banks moved to CLM1 model.

segments.name: Car loan distribution and insurance
segments.commentary: Car loan origination INR3,282 crore, +43% YoY across 13 partner banks; insurance net fee income INR42 crore; 14 new insurance products launched via Capri Care.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM target of about INR50,000 crore; FY28 target raised to INR65,000 crore (30%+ CAGR), up from INR47,000 crore FY27 target previously cited by analysts.
Quarterly AUM additions of about INR3,000-3,500 crore, with the back half expected to be stronger.
Medium-term ROE 19-21% and ROA 4.2-4.7%, targeted by FY28 on a sustained basis.
Gold loan share of AUM to reach about 55% medium term; spreads expected to stabilise near 7.8%, possibly about 8% once gold loans exceed 50-53% of AUM.
Cost-to-income expected to hold at 44-45% over the next 12-18 months.
Cost of funds expected to remain broadly stable for the rest of FY27.
Branch rollout: 400 new gold loan branches to be operational by December 2026 (about 150 by Q2, the rest by Q3), revised up from 350.
capex_capacity: Gold loan branch network steady at 1,000 branches; 196 added in FY26 and 89 in Q4 FY26; total branch network 1,433 locations.
Plan to open about 400 branches in FY27, with 150-plus by end Q2 and the balance by Q3; longer-term plan of 400-500 openings a year.
16 MSME branches in Telangana and Karnataka to become operational from Q3 FY27.
Employee count up only 156 QoQ; AUM per employee INR3.4 crore vs INR1.8 crore a year earlier.
demand_pricing: Gold loan growth of about 25% is achievable from existing branches, with new branches adding further growth; a weak monsoon could raise gold loan demand from microfinance and marginal farmers.
Gold price fell about 4% QoQ; management says the 85% LTV trigger for auction notices and automated margin-call alerts limit risk.
Gold loan yields rose to about 18.5% from shift to smaller ticket sizes, with incentive plans changed accordingly.
Car loan origination growth moderated in the quarter; management is limiting volume to profitable unit economics, not cash-burn growth, with a used car loan pilot planned.
Co-lending volume growth slowed to 4% QoQ due to new co-lending guidelines and partner banks moving to CLM1.

544021|2026-06.headline: Protean Q1FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to INR251 crore, but EBITDA fell 38% to INR28 crore (10% margin) on an INR18 crore upfront RFP cost.
544021|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 19% YoY to INR251 crore, driven by core businesses and new initiatives. EBITDA fell to INR28 crore from INR45 crore, with margin at 10% versus 18.7% a year ago, mainly due to about INR18 crore of upfront implementation costs on RFP mandates plus geopolitical-driven hardware and technology price inflation. Management says normalised EBITDA would have been INR46 crore (17.2%). PAT was INR6 crore (2.2% margin), and the company remains debt-free with over INR800 crore in cash and marketable securities. This was the first earnings call for new MD and CEO Ajay Rajan, who set out a shift from volume-led growth to solution-led, higher-margin DPI offerings.

segments.name: Tax Services (PAN)
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable YoY despite a 12% industry-wide decline in PAN issuances; Protean issued over 1 crore PANs and market share rose ~275 bps from 59% in FY26 to 62% in Q1FY27.

segments.name: CRA Services (NPS/APY/UPS)
segments.commentary: Onboarded ~3.9 million new subscribers and captured 95% of incremental additions; 97% share across NPS, APY and UPS. Record 1,000+ new corporates onboarded in a quarter; NPS Vatsalya added 78,000 subscribers.

segments.name: Identity Services
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 16% YoY on 20% combined volume growth; eSign Pro positioned as a key monetisation opportunity.

segments.name: New initiatives (CERSAI, CKYC, Bima Sugam, ASK, AgriStack)
segments.commentary: Contributed 17% of quarterly revenue versus 10% in FY26. Management did not quantify sub-segments; analyst data placed the line at INR42 crore.

segments.name: Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK)
segments.commentary: 75 ASKs rolled out across 24 states and UTs as of July 2026; completion expected by Q3FY27. Initial estimates in line with RFP expectations; margins not yet disclosed and not expected to be substantially low. Employee costs rising with hiring.

guidance_outlook: Management expects RFP mandate investments to contribute meaningfully to revenue in coming quarters, improving operating leverage and margin recovery.
CFO expects no further one-time costs beyond ASK-related impact; margin to stabilise from Q2 or Q3FY27.
CFO expects margins to improve substantially over the next 2 to 3 years; ASK not EBITDA-accretive initially but expected to generate sustainable, stable margins.
Cost per employee to remain flat ex-ASK; some cost reduction at year-end expected to be offset by increments.
Management intends to pursue inorganic opportunities (BFSI-focused, to add top line, bottom line or cut cost via automation); no specifics shared.
Shift from per-API-call pricing to per-journey/per-outcome pricing expected to lift margins; no quantified target given.
capex_capacity: 75 Aadhaar Seva Kendras live across 24 states and UTs as of July 2026; full implementation targeted by Q3FY27; some centres yet to be operational and hiring ongoing.
ASK working capital needs described as light (mainly furniture and office set-up), billed monthly by government; no capex quantum disclosed.
DPI-in-a-box modular stack being packaged for state governments and international markets; implementation timelines not specified.
MeitY-certified sovereign cloud and account aggregator described as small businesses; partnerships or investments being explored.
demand_pricing: PAN issuance market fell 12% due to a change requiring additional date-of-birth documents after the Supreme Court ruling on Aadhaar; assisted-mode volumes continue to grow.
Enterprise traction described as strong with a good pipeline; government wins expected through RFP and mandate processes.
Management says the CKYC registry migration covers 1 billion-plus records and on-ramps are a recurring opportunity across thousands of regulated entities.
Management says pricing is moving from per API call to per journey or per outcome, which it expects to lift margins.
PAN 2.0 is still away; no platform changes needed yet, and the company is confident of staying relevant.

qa_highlights.question: Which areas are being explored for inorganic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is looking at a couple of BFSI-focused acquisitions that either add to top line or bottom line or cut cost through automation; no specifics given.

qa_highlights.question: Is employee cost for Aadhaar Seva Kendra baked into Q1, and what is the cost trajectory to Q3FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs rose for most ASKs, but several centres go live in Q2 or Q3. Management would not quantify the employee-cost trajectory or ASK cost; ex-ASK costs to stay flat.

qa_highlights.question: Are ASK revenues in line with the RFP expectations and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early, given 3 to 4 months of operations; initial estimates are in line with RFP assumptions and ramp-up was always planned. Margins not substantially low, but ASKs are not EBITDA-accretive yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be additional costs in Q2 and the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said none to his knowledge beyond ASK-related temporary impact; margins expected to stabilise from Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE and working capital need for ASK?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital light, as it is a managed monthly-billed operation; only initial furniture and office set-up are upfront. Government payments have been timely. No ROCE figure given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in the 'other' new-initiatives revenue line from INR11 crore to INR42 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Three drivers: one RFP mandate revenue recognised, ASK revenue starting, and early traction in RISE with Protean and eSign Pro. No further breakdown given.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR11 crore in prior-year line per analyst question; mgmt cited RFP, Aadhaar Seva Kendra and new products

543533|2026-06.headline: eMudhra Q1 FY27 total income rose 28% YoY to INR 1,925 million, with EBITDA up 40% to INR 504 million at a 26.2% margin.
543533|2026-06.overview: Total income grew 27.8% YoY to INR 1,925 million, of which about 13 points came from the Cryptas acquisition (about INR 200 million revenue). Enterprise Solutions grew about 50% YoY and made up 65% of income, while Trust Services declined temporarily as legacy token demand fell ahead of a September security-standard transition. PAT rose 28% to INR 320 million (16.6% margin), and management kept its FY27 guidance of 18% organic growth and 25% PAT growth unchanged.

segments.name: Enterprise Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,623 million, about 50% YoY growth and 65% of total income; organic product growth about 25% after Cryptas contribution, per management. Management cited higher margin mix from lower token sales.

segments.name: Trust Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 284 million with a temporary decline as partners destocked legacy tokens before a September transition. Management estimated INR 5-7 crore of token volume was lost; token gross margin is about 10%.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Growth of about 5% YoY, supported by new US customers; margins are roughly 18-20%, similar to historical levels.

segments.name: Cryptas (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 20 crore in a seasonally weak quarter; first CertiNext sale to a German data center operator and first mSigner/PrimeSign deployment for an Austrian municipality. Management expects Cryptas to turn profitable in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 18% organic growth in total income and 25% PAT growth.
Management expects EBITDA margin around 25% and PAT margin around 16-16.5% going forward, as added sales hires weigh on costs.
Trust Service revenue likely stays lower in Q2 FY27 as legacy token demand remains weak; bottom-line impact described as limited given low token margins.
Three-year target (FY27-FY29) of doubling PAT, with about 18-20% organic revenue growth per year; Enterprise Solutions expected at 20-25% growth per year and Trust Services 15-20%.
UAE Trust Service (QTSP) licence expected around end of Q1 or start of Q2 FY27, after which launch is planned.
Expects the Cryptas loss to end in FY27 and the European subsidiary (BV) to be profitable this year; ROE expected to be maintained at about 14.5-15%.
capex_capacity: Token supply constrained: ePass token recertification by CCA submitted and largely complete, pending CCA action; management expects ePass certification by about September, after which volumes should recover.
New Innate token is certified but volumes are low because capacity is limited.

Cryptas integration of eMudhra's own CA and CLM IP replacing third-party products (such as Keyfactor) developed over the last six to seven months; this is intended to reduce cost and shift transfer pricing to India.
Added senior sales hires across geographies (USD 200,000-300,000 per person), which will weigh on near-term margins.
No capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Trust Services: partners destocked legacy tokens ahead of the September global transition to FIPS 140-3, which reduced volumes.

SecurePass in India: large bank or government deals typically start at INR 4-6 crore and can exceed INR 10 crore per bank for full PIM/PAM suites; compliance mandates from RBI-type regulators and SEBI-type regulators are cited as drivers.
US products: university federation (Common) onboarding is live, with about 1,000-1,500 certificates issued daily; IoT/PKI and SSL-expiry (47-day) demand are cited as pipeline drivers.
Agentic AI identity and signing is described as an early-stage opportunity; management said quantification is not possible yet and pilots are expected within about a year.
PrivaTrust consent-management modules are being piloted; a broader data discovery and classification suite is planned, with focus on India under the DPDP Act.

financial_highlights.change: About 13 points of 28% total income growth

532929|2026-06.headline: Brigade Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 36% (from 28%) on real estate margin recovery, though net sales fell 5% to INR1,061 crore.
532929|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR1,179 crore with EBITDA of INR425 crore, and PAT of INR217 crore (up 37% YoY). Real estate EBITDA margin recovered to 21% from 12%, driven by recognition of higher-margin projects, while realisation rose 21% YoY to INR14,256 per sq ft. Q1 had no launches; the Morgan Heights relaunch was stalled after SEIAA revoked its environmental clearance, and management cut that project from the launch schedule. FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore was reiterated, with launches back-ended and the launch pipeline trimmed to about 9.36 million sq ft for the rest of FY27.

segments.name: Real Estate
segments.commentary: Net sales INR707 crore and EBITDA INR150 crore (21% margin vs 12%); realisation INR14,256 per sq ft (+21% YoY) on price increases and mix shift to higher-value homes. Q1 had no new launches; Q1 presales were about INR1,050 crore per analyst question.

segments.name: Leasing (commercial office)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR328 crore (+9% YoY), EBITDA INR230 crore at 70% margin; operational GLA 8 million sq ft, occupancy 88%, gross leasing 0.22 million sq ft in Q1, rental collections 99%. Office revenue cited as INR200 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality (BHVL)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR144 crore, EBITDA INR45 crore; ADR +7%, occupancy 76% (from 74.5%), RevPAR and EBITDA up about 9%. West Asia conflict cut event/MICE business by about 10%.

segments.name: Retail (Orion Mall)
segments.commentary: Footfalls +11% YoY, retail sales +35% YoY, anchor retailer sales +64%, F&B +46%, electronics +33%, cinema admissions +20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance of INR9,000 crore reiterated; management says sales run-rate per quarter should rise as launches start from Q2.
Launch pipeline for the rolling four quarters is 12.36 million sq ft (residential 12.4 million sq ft at about INR13,400 crore GDV; commercial about 4.03 million sq ft), excluding Morgan Heights.
Within this, about 9.36 million sq ft is planned for the rest of FY27 (Q2 about 2.36 million sq ft, H2 about 7 million sq ft) and about 3 million sq ft slips into Q1 FY28.
Hyderabad Neopolis 2 (about 2 million sq ft) is now expected in Q2; Whitefield-Hoskote is now a Q3 launch; Hyderabad launch pulled forward to Q3 or earlier.
Commercial leasing revenue expected to grow at about 20% CAGR over the next 5 to 6 years; about 6 million sq ft of commercial space to come into the market mainly in FY30.
Operating contribution margin improvement of 5% to 6% expected to be largely retained through FY27; management expects margins to move into the 20s, from late teens at year end last year.
Debt-equity to stay well under 1x, with capex and BD funded first from internal accruals.
BHVL to add 1,700 keys in pipeline, targeting 3,300 keys by FY31; Courtyard by Marriott Chennai WTC (45 keys) to launch in FY27.
capex_capacity: Launch pipeline: Q1 had none; Morgan Heights (about 0.7 million sq ft unsold, attributable value about INR650 crore) removed from launch schedule pending High Court and SEIAA resolution.

Commercial pipeline launched in Q1 about 4 million sq ft across Bengaluru and Hyderabad (Brigade HRC Atrium, an industrial block, Brigade United, Cauvery, Orion Mall Hyderabad), all to be held, none for sale.
WTC Bengaluru: about 1.13 million sq ft building, Brigade holds 0.71 million sq ft, about 50% leased, about 375,000 sq ft vacant.
Upcoming commercial: 2.6 million sq ft Bengaluru (about 65%), 1.3 million sq ft Chennai (about 31%), 0.2 million sq ft Kochi.
Capex for commercial projects to be spent over the next 4 to 5 years; per sq ft capex quoted at INR4,000 to INR10,000 (construction cost, excluding land).

Land bank about 56 to 57 million sq ft, which includes the launch pipeline. Kengeri land parcel in litigation; KIADB 75-acre Devanahalli parcel residential component reduced to about 3 to 4 lakh sq ft.
demand_pricing: Pan-India residential sales down 6% YoY in April-June (Anarock); Bengaluru and Hyderabad among the only major cities with sales growth.
Q1 business development: INR2,400 crore GDV across 2.7 million sq ft, mainly Hyderabad.
Office leasing demand led by industrial and manufacturing, flexible workspace and life sciences; GCCs 58% of gross leasing; IT/ITES 26% of portfolio.
WTC Bengaluru: large-occupier RFPs (1-2 lakh sq ft) postponed due to West Asia crisis; leasing shifting to 20,000 to 40,000 sq ft deals; mark-to-market rent increase of 10% to 15%.

Hospitality: domestic corporate, weddings and social demand offset weaker international travel; Kochi (Four Points rebranded to Courtyard by Marriott) occupancy back in the 70s in Q2, ADR uplift expected at 15% to 20%.

financial_highlights.change: includes INR36.6 crore exceptional gain (Bain Capital-related reclassification)

financial_highlights.value: INR144 crore / INR45 crore / INR17 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt / Brigade share of net debt
financial_highlights.change: about 86% of debt is leasing-segment debt

543317|2026-06.headline: G R Infra Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 32.71% YoY to ~INR2,423 crores, but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 11.02% from 12.65%.
543317|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 32.71% YoY to about INR2,423 crores, while consolidated revenue rose 40% to INR2,784 crores. Margins compressed on higher construction and material costs, with standalone EBITDA margin at 11.02% versus 12.65% a year earlier and group EBITDA margin at 16.8% versus 20%. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 15-20% despite the 30%+ first-quarter run-rate, citing appointed-date timing for new projects. Order book stands at about INR25,300 crores as of 1 July 2026, with about INR32,000 crores of bids yet to be opened.

segments.name: Transport (highways and surface transport)
segments.commentary: Main growth driver in Q1 per management; the INR28,000 crore 'road' pipeline bid-out figure includes metro and other surface transport.

segments.name: Power transmission and distribution (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR110 crores versus about INR75 crores in the prior quarter; company is setting up tower manufacturing and expanding that facility.

segments.name: Oil and gas
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR270 crores; FY27 target above INR1,000 crores. Two projects currently in the books, with external receivables elevated until completion around May 2027.

segments.name: Warehousing
segments.commentary: Capital deployed to date about INR130 crores; FY27 plan INR450-500 crores.

segments.name: BharatNet
segments.commentary: FY27 expected revenue about INR400 crores, of which about INR300 crores is capex (cabling, starting second half) and the balance O&M. Order book about INR1,000 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at 15-20%; management said 25% is possible if appointed dates arrive by October-December.
FY28 revenue target about INR11,000-12,000 crores assuming about 20% growth, with margins in a similar range.
Standalone EBITDA margin guided at 10-11% for the current scenario.
FY27 order inflow target about INR20,000-22,000 crores (plus-minus 10%), with road about INR14,000 crores.
FY27 capex about INR300 crores; FY28 capex INR200-250 crores.
Other income expected to continue at the Q1 run rate for the next three quarters.
Around three to four assets targeted for transfer to the InvIT in FY27.
Equity contribution to HAM/BoT projects: INR900-1,000 crores in FY27; about INR3,300 crores over the next three years.
capex_capacity: Standalone net block of PP&E INR1,019 crores at June 2026; Q1 additions INR22 crores.
Investments in subsidiaries INR2,445 crores (loans and equity) at June 2026; balance HAM/BoT equity commitment INR3,346 crores.
Appointed dates awaited for three projects worth INR7,250 crores. Agra-Gwalior expected October-November 2026; two other HAM projects targeted for December 2026.
BharatNet capex awaiting right-of-way; capex expected to start around October 2026.
BESS work under way; battery procurement pending a move in FX and geopolitical conditions, expected within about three months.
Railway project in MP already started; management said no more than about 15% execution in year one.
Tower manufacturing facility being expanded to address tower supply delays.
demand_pricing: Pipeline cited at about INR3.85 lakh crores in transport (78% highway, 16% railway, 6% metro); government proposes a toll-cum-annuity model with 10-25% upfront support and a 20-year concession.
Government approved multi-tracking projects worth about INR48,000 crores in the quarter.
Bitumen cost spike is compensated by a government circular over and above escalation clauses; diesel and energy cost increases are not compensated, hitting margins.
Power transmission contracts have no escalation; aluminium and copper price spikes hit margins, expected to normalise over 3-6 months and spread over about two years.

Order inflow to date has lagged government pipeline claims for about two years, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance still 15% revenue growth after 32% in Q1, and what about FY28 margins?

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of the INR32,000 crore bids yet to open, and is INR20,000-25,000 crore inflow achievable?

qa_highlights.question: Why was other income low in Q1 and what is the InvIT distribution?

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise and when will they unwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly oil and gas receivables; collection expected as projects complete, with the current project finishing around May 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Bitumen is compensated by government circular over escalation. Diesel is not, and power transmission has no escalation, so margins are impacted in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company pursuing international or Middle East opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: No international focus for the next 1-2 years; domestic credentials first, with international possibly after about one year.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large equity and InvIT value be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans BOT projects, transmission and logistics to deploy accrued cash at meaningful returns; said it is waiting for suitable opportunities.

500219|2026-06.headline: Jain Irrigation Q1 FY27 revenue fell about 2.5% to Rs 1,500 crore; adjusted PAT dropped to Rs 3 crore from Rs 30 crore, with Rs 680 crore NCDs due this fiscal.

EBITDA fell because standalone India volumes were lower and fixed costs went unabsorbed; Hi-Tech margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6%. Management said April was weak, May-June improved, and July was positive, and it expects a stronger second half. Working capital days improved (consolidated net working capital 183 days vs 210 a year ago) and about 78% of EBITDA converted to cash.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (after non-cash NCD interest unwinding)

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat YoY; overseas plastics revenue grew about 40%, and segment EBITDA margin rose to about 11% from 10%.

segments.name: Agro-Processing (food)
segments.commentary: Grew significantly on new beverage business (about Rs 60 crore in April-June) and overseas sales, but EBITDA fell about 3 points on seasonality.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA lost in Q1 to be recovered in H2 FY27 and full-year PAT to beat FY26.
Hi-Tech: double-digit revenue growth targeted for FY27; solar pump sales expected to pick up from September.
FY27 margin guidance: about 14% standalone and about 12-13% consolidated.

capex_capacity: Biochar plant recently started (mango stones, corn cob, cotton stalk feedstock); management expects financial impact from next fiscal, with carbon credits taking 6-9 months.

Remaining project billing outside Pune is about Rs 40-50 crore; the large Pune water-supply project still has triple-digit crore billing left; Q2 project billing could be below Rs 24 crore.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose about 50%; most increases were passed to customers, and some customers postponed purchases until prices fall.
Delayed monsoon onset in June pushed drip sales into the current quarter; July was positive and August-September are expected to be good.
Government-linked and subsidy-driven micro-irrigation sales were deliberately not pursued because of cash flow and long receivables; management estimated Rs 50-60 crore of sales were forgone.
Dam storage was about 67% of capacity; management expects about 85% by monsoon-end, supportive of the rabi season and next summer.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy government receivables were recovered and how much project work is left?

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 674-680 crore of debt due this fiscal be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited internal accruals first, then legacy receivable collections, asset monetisation (surplus land) and refinancing; it said Rs 1,300 crore of bank debt was repaid over three and a half years and that the company has never missed a payment in four years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Hi-Tech down about 22% and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail fell about 17% and projects about 63%; management called the drip decline a one-off from the delayed monsoon and polymer-driven postponements. Hi-Tech margin was 14.4% vs 16.6%, and management expects margins to recover to typical levels through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of write-offs on project receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said provisions were made in FY21-22 after a project review and it does not expect material write-offs; net receivables of Rs 1,975 crore in June are largely good, with about 55% linked to government-related items.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital requirements higher than listed peers?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of refinancing and the food-business IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no pushback from lenders, a couple of term sheets are in hand, and talks are ongoing. The food-business IPO (about Rs 1,000 crore including PE exit) has been deferred due to weak valuations; the company will revisit it from September.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT negative when revenue is flat, and what are the coffee and biochar updates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the loss to higher raw-material costs and lower standalone India volumes, and expects a full-year PAT improvement. First coffee orders have come from the Coffee Board; the biochar business has started, with impact on numbers from next fiscal.

risks_watch: Refinancing of about Rs 230 crore NCD due in September 2026 and about Rs 450 crore due in March 2027 has not yet been completed; management relies on term sheets and internal cash flows.
Legacy government receivables of about Rs 800-900 crore and about Rs 500 crore of agency receivables above 180 days; collection pace against the Rs 380 crore minimum target is key.
Polymer price volatility and geopolitical oil-price movements may keep customers postponing purchases.
Weak Q1 adjusted PAT (Rs 3 crore) and reliance on H2 recovery; Q2 is seasonally muted.
Food-business IPO and Tamil Nadu land monetisation timelines have slipped repeatedly.
500219|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on debt repayment and H2 recovery, but cautious on near-term volumes: Q1 is described as muted and beyond management's control. Answers on receivables and monetisation timelines were broad, and several timelines (Tamil Nadu land, IPO) were pushed out.

500135|2026-06.headline: EPL Q1 FY27 revenue grew 25.3% (20% underlying ex pass-through) with EBITDA margin at 18.8%; revenue guidance raised to high teens.
500135|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue growth of 25.3%, or 20% underlying excluding pass-through of higher raw material prices, with EBITDA up 15.2% and margin at 18.8% (19.6% underlying). Reported PAT fell 1.4% while PBT rose 10%, which management attributed to a low base-year effective tax rate and phasing. Working capital rose roughly INR 180 crore in the quarter, mainly inventory, which management linked to raw material price inflation and safety stock. Revenue growth guidance was raised from early double digits to high teens for the next few quarters, with the 20% underlying EBITDA margin target held. Europe margins contracted on operational issues and transitional costs, and the Indovida merger received CCI approval but is still pending final approval.

financial_highlights.change: Management says in line with plan; FY PAT expected to grow double digits

financial_highlights.change: FY26 full-year increase cited as about INR 170 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Personal Care & Beyond share of portfolio

segments.commentary: Growth exceeded 20% in the quarter. Management cites current global market share of 8%, with a target of up to 16% over the next few years.

Thailand plant set up and ramping up.
Americas investments in Brazil and US capabilities.

Oral Care gains attributed to service and quality retention during the crisis, with wallet and market share gains across regions.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly INR 180 crore rise in working capital, and did receivables jump?

qa_highlights.question: What are the Europe transitional costs and is manufacturing footprint changing again?

qa_highlights.question: Does the upgrade to high-teens growth also lift PBT growth, given FX and depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed high-teens revenue and EBITDA growth for the year, with PBT translating to a similar trajectory; PAT was held back by ETR and phasing, with a double-digit FY PAT still expected.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain from sharp price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said old inventory did affect consumption costs, but the company recovered the entire cost impact in Q1 and expects to continue doing so.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Americas EBITDA and EBIT fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue includes pass-through pricing, which distorts sequential comparisons, and that investments in Brazil and the US capabilities weigh on margins; underlying margin is higher than reported.

Working capital and net debt rising on inventory build and capex; watch receivables ageing and inventory levels next quarter.
Oral Care growth of 24% described as exceptional and unlikely to repeat; normal mid-to-high single digits expected.
Indovida merger still awaiting final approvals; management cannot share underlying information until then.
Americas margin pressure from ahead-of-curve investments in Brazil and US.
Effective tax rate variability (18-22% range) can keep PAT growth lagging PBT growth.

543412|2026-06.headline: Star Health Q1 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 111 crore from Rs 16 crore, with CISR improving to 97% and normalised PAT up 44% to Rs 386 crore.
543412|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed a fourth successive quarter of improving core underwriting profitability, with underwriting result at Rs 111 crore versus Rs 16 crore a year earlier. Reported PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 550 crore, while normalised PAT (8% investment yield basis) rose 44% to Rs 386 crore, giving annualised ROE of 15.6% versus 12.2%. Fresh retail GWP grew 37% YoY to Rs 730 crore on a 1/N basis, but retail market share slipped to 29% from 31%, which management attributed to long-term policy accounting and deliberate avoidance of riskier pools. Management guided insurance revenue growth to rise towards 15-16% and expense ratio to fall 30-40 bps a year, while declining to give loss ratio guidance.

segments.name: Retail health
segments.commentary: Retail market share 29% vs 31% a year earlier; new-to-insurance mix in fresh retail 94% vs 90%. Proprietary channels (agency and D2C) are 90%+ of retail business.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Group share of GWP is now roughly 2.5%, down from about 5% a year earlier; management said group contributed part of the loss ratio improvement but retail also improved.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C fresh business grew 142% YoY, with 98% of customers new to insurance; D2C is 74% of digital fresh business.

guidance_outlook: Insurance revenue growth is expected to rise from 13.4% towards 15-16% as the quarters progress, and to increase further in FY28.
Expense ratio expected to improve 30-40 bps consistently each year from technology and productivity investments.

Reinsurance cost expected to fall: the voluntary quota share treaty (2023-24 and 2024-25, three-year) is fading out, and obligatory treaty renegotiation with GICRE may bring benefits; FY28 net reinsurance benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%.
Q2 is seasonally higher for loss ratio; management expects the same trend this year. No loss ratio guidance given.
Steady-state ROE target is mid-to-high teens on an Ind AS basis; no specific number given.
Fresh-business growth expected to moderate in H2 FY27 and into H1 FY28 as the post-GST-waiver base effect builds; management agreed this framing.
capex_capacity: Agency network added about 20,000 agents in the quarter to 8.5 lakh; agent productivity up 19% YoY.
Non-metro fresh business growth is 3.5x metro growth.
Customer app has about 16 million downloads and 1.5 million+ monthly active users.
97% of new applications are digitally sourced; generative AI being layered on existing AI/ML claims analytics.
Long-term policies are about 40% of retail fresh business; fresh-to-renewal share about 20:80 in insurance revenue.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is partly driven by the GST waiver; majority of fresh business comes from first-time buyers. Management expects moderation of optical growth rates.

Pricing is annual and product-by-product on a calendar; most pricing actions have been taken in Q4 over the last couple of years, with earned impact flowing through subsequent quarters. Management described upcoming pricing as maintenance-level rather than step-up, with some discounts for non-claimants.
Retail claim settlement ratio 91%; over 9.5 lakh claims settled in the quarter, over 80% cashless.
Senior citizens are under 5% of the book; focus remains on younger cohorts.
Management is watching dengue, malaria and fever outbreaks; telemedicine and home healthcare used to manage these cases.

qa_highlights.question: How will GWP growth of 19% convert into insurance revenue growth, and when will they converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance revenue grew 13.4%; management expects 15-16% through the year as long-term policy earnings build, and higher growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers for loss ratio improvement and how many claims are settled via telemedicine?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combined approach: repricing, portfolio selection, claims fraud control, network management, wellness and teleconsultation. No telemedicine claim count was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the expense ratio improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects 30-40 bps annual expense ratio improvement from tech, digitisation and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What share of acquisition cost is employee expense and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is split three ways: claims-related in claims, sales-related in acquisition cost, and support costs in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reinsurance impact on the expense ratio and what is the full-year benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Reinsurance cost is falling as the quota share treaty fades; FY28 benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%, though management said this was hard to pin down.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth slow in H2 as the GST-driven base builds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that H2 FY27 and early FY28 growth could be lower on the high base, and said it will not chase growth for its own sake.

risks_watch: Seasonal Q2 loss ratio pressure from vector-borne and infectious diseases.
Regulatory changes to commissions and claims reforms; management declined to comment until rules are final.
Retail market share fell to 29% from 31%; clean like-for-like comparison not expected until FY28.
Fresh growth may moderate in H2 FY27 as the post-GST-waiver base effect builds.
Other expenses rose about 23% YoY to Rs 283 crore, driven by loss of GST input credit and annual rate hikes.
Accounting questions open: finance income under PAA on long-term contracts (Rs 38.8 crore) and DAC balance were not fully explained.

544283|2026-06.headline: ACME Solar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to INR954 crore and EBITDA 56% to INR831 crore, with BESS contributing INR226 crore.
