Management sees the peak-power market growing toward 300-500 GWh, potentially 1 TWh in a positive case, driven by rooftop and KUSUM solar (duck-curve effect).
Competition from other BESS entrants (including Adani) is rising, but management argues merchant supply will remain limited and that the market is still new to state buyers.

qa_highlights.question: How much open or early BESS capacity will there be in FY27 and the next couple of years, and what are realisations on the INR1,400 crore short-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is contracting well above 10 GWh and realisations are INR8-10 per unit, depending on month and volume. Only ~600 MWh is open today, with a target of zero open capacity outside PPAs by end-2026. Management plans for 10-12 GWh to remain available for short-term markets each year over the next five years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the curtailment impact and what drove EBITDA growth ex-BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment was about 1% of revenue, only on state-based projects. EBITDA growth was attributed to CUF (30.9% vs 28.5%) and repowering of existing plants. Management is considering adding batteries to state projects to absorb surplus generation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,400 crore revenue sustainable for 2-3 years, given El Nino-driven pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the 10 GWh base supporting INR1,400 crore-plus for the next 2-3 years based on PPA and GNA timelines. Beyond that, it depends on market pricing and new PPAs. It said the market is still untapped by most discoms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core (ex-BESS) EBITDA margin and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-BESS margin was ~91% in Q1, with a seasonal range of 88-91%. Management expects FDRE projects may lift margins because their realisations are healthier than plain solar.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 6.28 INR/kWh PPA and the hybrid configuration changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The hybrid project was offered with 1 hour of battery, a change from the standard configuration. The other project at INR6.28 per unit has no change in configuration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for C&I and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has started hiring for data-centre opportunities but is focused on profitability. It intends to target CTU-connected C&I customers and will not dilute mid-to-high teen return targets.

517035|2026-06.headline: RIR Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.3% YoY to Rs 27.16 crore, EBITDA Rs 3.98 crore, with Odisha epi-wafer output targeted from Q3 FY27.
517035|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 27.16 crore (up 29.3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 3.98 crore and EPS of 39 paisa. Margin improvement was attributed to passing on raw-material (copper, gold, silver) cost increases to customers, with about 80-85% pass-through, plus procurement and vendor negotiation gains. The Odisha epitaxy facility is nearing commissioning: power connection is nearly done, and epi operations are expected by end-Q2 FY27, with epi-wafer revenue from Q3. Bank loan of Rs 70 crore is at in-principle approval stage, with final sanction expected the following week.

financial_highlights.change: Margin improved vs Q4 FY26 per management; no exact YoY figure stated
Spent so far: ~Rs 58 crore govt subsidy plus ~Rs 70 crore company contribution; Rs 8-10 crore non-capex spend extra

segments.name: Halol facility (silicon power semiconductors: HPD, LPD, equipment)
segments.commentary: Management sees LPD at saturation; growth to come from HPD in India and new equipment-division products. Management aims to grow top line 3-4x FY26 this year; quarterly run-rate of Rs 30+ crore targeted during FY27 excluding Odisha.

segments.name: Odisha facility (SiC epi wafers)
segments.commentary: Epitaxy phase targets epi-wafer sales from Q3 FY27; FY27 second-half epi-wafer revenue target Rs 12-15 crore. Packaging (phase 2 first step) revenue expected from Q2 FY28. Two reactors can deliver 4-, 6- and 8-inch epi; 8-inch mainly for export, 4/6-inch for domestic.

guidance_outlook: Quarterly revenue of Rs 30+ crore achievable within FY27 (excluding Odisha); Rs 50 crore per quarter expected in 6-9 months, per management, though 'it may take some more time'.
Odisha epitaxy operations to commence by end-Q2 FY27; qualification expected to take ~30 days; official inauguration targeted September 2026.
Epi-wafer revenue from Odisha from Q3 FY27; FY27 second-half epi revenue target Rs 12-15 crore.
Management targets at least 3-4x FY26 top-line growth this year, and faster bottom-line growth.
Long-term EBITDA margin aim of 15-17%, but sustainability depends on geopolitical conditions; no firm commitment given.
Epi-wafer expected yield ~85%, with a goal above 90%.
capex_capacity: Odisha power supply via 33 kV line completed; transformer charged; plant and machinery installation expected to finish end-August or mid-September 2026.
Epitaxy clean room completed; two epi reactors installed.
Phase 2 (fabrication) capex of Rs 395-400 crore still under discussion; update expected in next couple of months.
Bank term loan application of Rs 70 crore; in-principle approval received, final sanction meeting pushed a week.
Depreciation: straight-line, 15 years for plant and machinery, consistent with Halol.
demand_pricing: Price increases taken in Q1; about 80-85% of input cost increase passed on to customers, with older accepted orders lagging. New schedules carry new prices.
Further value-addition price increases seen as difficult while West Asia disruption persists.
First overseas order: 120 units of 125 mm 5 kV SCR thyristors.
Epi-wafer prospects: international customers in US and Taiwan approached; Indian government labs also interested.
Richardson Electronics: ~20,000 SiC chips supplied, under customer review; no update from customer.

qa_highlights.question: Can the core business reach Rs 50 crore quarterly revenue excluding Odisha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes so but said it may take time; Rs 30+ crore per quarter is achievable this year, with Rs 50 crore possibly in 6-9 months after supply chain and productivity work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Odisha project status and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Power resolved and transformer charged; epi operations to begin in about 30 days after installation; inauguration targeted September 2026. Government subsidy of Rs 58 crore received to date; company has contributed an equal amount.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Odisha phase 1 capex funding gap and bank loan size?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 130 crore spent (Rs 70 crore company plus Rs 58 crore subsidy), leaving ~Rs 100 crore; application made for Rs 70 crore bank loan.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is sustainable and what drove Q1 margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain came from price pass-through, procurement savings and redeployed staff; management aims for 15-17% but cannot confirm sustainability given geopolitical factors.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin does epi wafer carry?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected EBITDA 20-25% on epi-wafer sales; SiC devices expected to be higher margin than epi.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 8-10% of revenue has been the long-term R&D spend norm; products in development include optically triggered thyristors (5 kV now, targeting 8 kV).

qa_highlights.question: Will RIR enter GaN?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said focus remains on SiC; sees SiC capturing power share of GaN market in about three years.

risks_watch: Bank loan final sanction (Rs 70 crore) expected next week; delay would stall phase 1 funding.
Odisha commissioning timeline: slippage from end-Q2 FY27 epi start and Q3 revenue.
Margin sustainability amid West Asia-driven input cost volatility; only 80-85% of cost increases passed through.
Phase 2 capex (Rs 395-400 crore) funding and timing not yet finalised.
Epi-wafer yield (target 85%, goal above 90%) and customer qualification in US, Taiwan and India.
Richardson Electronics SiC chip review outcome unknown.
Management declined to name products under development, citing competition; limited visibility on new product revenue.
517035|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Odisha timelines and margins, with hedges on sustainability (margins depend on geopolitics). Evasive on long-term targets and product names, repeatedly declining forward-looking commitments. Some answers were loose or inconsistent (for example, the 3-4x growth reference and the Rs 30 crore vs Rs 50 crore run-rate), so treat guidance with caution.
key_quotes: I think this year, we will be able to easily cross about Rs. 30 plus crores per quarter.
We expect to commence epitaxy operations in the end of second quarter FY'27.
So, we expect an EBITDA somewhere in the range of 20%-25% on sale of epi wafers.
So, generally we don't give any forward -looking statements or commitments.

540293|2026-06.headline: Pricol Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23.5% YoY to Rs 1,083.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.41% on West Asia-driven cost headwinds.
540293|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 1,083.58 crore, up 23.46% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 123.69 crore (11.41% margin) and PAT of Rs 67.02 crore (6.19% margin). Management said EBITDA grew only about 21% YoY because of polymer, LPG, freight, rupee and minimum-wage cost increases, which it expects to recover through quarterly and half-yearly indexation over Q2 and Q3. The call also covered a proposed demerger of the DIS/DICVS business from the ACFMS and polymer businesses, a Rs 700 crore capex cycle, and a one-year pause on M&A.

segments.name: DIS / DICVS (driver information systems, two-wheeler, CV, PV)
segments.commentary: Growth about 25% YoY in Q1 per CEO, equal to ACFMS. Two-wheeler revenue grew 28% vs industry 23%. Targets growth at least 5% above market; two-wheeler DIS volume share 30-35%, CV share about two-thirds, PV share 8-9% (Tata Motors dependent).

segments.name: ACFMS (auto components, fluid management and switches)
segments.commentary: Growth about 25% YoY in Q1 per CEO. Target is 10% growth above market; first switches business won from Suzuki; disc brake production started for a major Indian OEM, with meaningful revenue from FY28.

segments.name: Polymer (plastics)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 249 crore at 7.8% EBITDA margin; most affected by polymer and LPG price spikes. Capacity about Rs 1,000 crore turnover today, targeted at about Rs 2,000 crore post capex; management targets 2.5x FY25 base, and sees ROCE muted during capex cycle before 16-18% steady state.

guidance_outlook: Q2 and Q3 FY27 expected to recover delayed earnings via indexation: about 75% of revenue indexed from Q2, balance from Q3 (half-yearly indexation).
EBITDA expected under pressure for next couple of quarters until West Asia-related costs normalise; management said Q1 costs were delayed, not lost.
Minimum wage increases in three states add about Rs 21 crore per annum; customer pass-through still under negotiation.
Steady-state blended EBITDA margin target 12.5-13%; management estimates about 1.5% EBITDA lost in Q1 and about another half of that still recoverable via price increases and indexation.
FY30 (CY30/FY31) revenue ambition of Rs 8,000 crore for DICVS retained; FY30 targets unchanged despite M&A pause.
Demerger expected to take at least 4 quarters, management hopes for 12 months; businesses to operate as separate entities from October and fully by December.
Disc brake and switches revenue to become meaningful only from FY28.
capex_capacity: Rs 700 crore capex cycle over 18-24 months: about Rs 400 crore for polymer (including relocating out of TVS campuses under lock-in), Rs 150-180 crore for DICVS, about Rs 120 crore for ACFMS.
Five new factories being brought on stream: Hosur (state-of-the-art), Mysore, Aurangabad (greenfield), Sanand Gujarat (for Honda), and Bhiwadi/NCR under construction.
Polymer Centre of Excellence to be fully operational by May 2027; in-house tool room being built.
Partnership with BOE for backlight modules for screens in progress.
Polymer capacity expected to support about Rs 2,000 crore turnover from about Rs 1,000 crore today; plants on schedule barring a month or two of delay.
demand_pricing: Industry growth in Q1 about 22-23% weighted average; company grew about 26% overall, outperforming by about 4 points.
Q1 sequentially flat versus Q4, which management said is seasonal; no share loss claimed.
Raw material costs rising sharply for memory-controlled devices due to AI-driven demand; polymer, LPG, crude, freight and rupee all adverse.
Two-wheeler TFT penetration about 7-8% of two-wheelers produced; management expects this to double in 2-3 years.
Polymer customer wins include Ather, River, Simple Energy, Raptee, Honda, Royal Enfield, Suzuki (switches) and Yamaha (final stage); Mahindra engagement started for PV and DICVS.
E-cockpit: proof of concept shown to customers; global competitors have volume advantage of 40-50x, so cost competitiveness limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why demerge the DIS/connected vehicles business from the rest of the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the board debated it for over two years; the DIS business needs large investment and technology partners, which investors find hard to back inside a multi-business company. Demerger is intended to allow a debt and equity mix and partner onboarding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 margin outlook and steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state blended EBITDA margin of 12.5-13% is the target; Q1 lost about 1.5% of margin; Q2 and Q3 expected to recover through indexation, with about half of the lost margin still recoverable if prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 700 crore over 18-24 months: Rs 400 crore polymer, Rs 150-180 crore DICVS, about Rs 120 crore ACFMS.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: At least 4 quarters per advisers; management hopes for 12 months. Internal operation as separate entities from October, fully by December.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A still on the cards?
qa_highlights.answer: M&A paused for about one year after due diligence found asset quality issues; FY30 targets unchanged. Will consider only attractive quality assets.

qa_highlights.question: Disc brake revenue and ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: No material revenue yet; meaningful revenue expected only from FY28, consistent with prior guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Polymer business performance in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue Rs 249 crore with EBITDA margin of 7.8%; polymer and LPG cost spikes expected to correct in Q2 and Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Gross margin down ~160 bps (per analyst question, not disputed)

540774|2026-06.headline: IFGL Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA fell 17% YoY to INR31 crore on raw material and LPG cost spikes, while consolidated PAT rose 58% to INR17 crore.
540774|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR297 crore, with domestic up 7% and exports up 9%, but gross margin fell to 43% from 47% on higher raw material prices. Standalone EBITDA dropped 17% YoY to INR31 crore as input costs and LPG availability constraints outpaced price increases, which management says will pass through with a lag. Consolidated total income rose 13% YoY to INR515 crore and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to INR40 crore, with PAT up 58% to INR17 crore. The Europe segment was weak because British Steel's low output cut offtake at Sheffield Refractories, while US operations grew double digits with improving margins.

financial_highlights.change: Management says base has grown; target double-digit for year-end

segments.name: Standalone India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR297 crore (+8% YoY); EBITDA INR31 crore (-17% YoY) hit by raw material costs and LPG/fuel price surge. Price increases were implemented but are only partly offsetting costs.

segments.name: Europe (Monocon UK + Sheffield Refractories)
segments.commentary: Management attributed the weak quarter mainly to Sheffield Refractories' low sales due to British Steel's blast furnace problems, with losses rising to about INR7 crore from INR3 crore QoQ (per analyst). Monocon UK losses reportedly fell QoQ and it is approaching breakeven.

segments.name: US subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue grew double digits YoY with improved margins from cost optimization; management described margins as more than double-digit and robust.

segments.name: Monocon and Sheffield Refractories (overall)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue grew double digits YoY despite headwinds; Monocon has opened offices in Australia and Saudi Arabia and is entering iron and steel and foundry refractories.

segments.name: Hofmann Ceramic
segments.commentary: Order book held at similar levels YoY; management targets reducing losses and breakeven by end FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects price increases to flow through progressively over coming quarters, but says they are temporary and offset only input cost rises, with no additional margin expected from them.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target is double digit, dependent on geopolitics and overseas demand; earlier 12% margin reference was not reaffirmed explicitly.
British Steel expected to restart blast furnace and normalize offtake in Q2 FY27; Sheffield Refractories expected back to normal.
Speciality Steel (ex-Liberty Rotherham) melt shops are expected to restart around November-December 2026 per market sources.
Management says staff cost is at about 10% of revenue and is not expected to go beyond this level.
Management believes the worst is behind on profitability, but cautioned that conditions can change quickly.
capex_capacity: Sheffield Refractories Phase 1 plastic ramming mass production has started at IFGL Vizag facility; marketing trials underway, with full customer trials and accreditation still needed.
Adding mag carbon brick and casting flux new lines could add INR150-200 crore of revenue at peak capacity for these two products.

Chinese JV: government appropriate authority approval sought; authorities advised changing location and reapplying, so the project is on hold. Investment so far is only in land (Gujarat), with some spend.

R&D facility in Odisha: management said spend is around INR20 crore, disputing an analyst's INR100-150 crore figure. R&D is developing foundry materials, thin slab caster tundish SEN for the US, and recycled material use.
demand_pricing: India steel demand forecast to grow 7.4% in 2026 and 9.2% in 2027 (management citation).
US steel production up 6% YoY; US business revenue up double digits, with new product introductions (thin slab caster tundish SEN) made in the US.
UK: British Steel now in public ownership; British Steel produced at very low levels in Q1 due to blast furnace problems.
Ocean freight spikes due to geopolitical situation hit UK and China operations.
Price increases were negotiated per contract and are temporary, tied to input costs from geopolitical tension.
Management said there was no market share loss in domestic business; the base has grown, which lowered the percentage growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove overseas subsidiary growth and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Rakhecha said the Americas drove top-line growth with robust margins. Management expects momentum to continue across subsidiaries and aims to turn loss-making units (UK, Europe, America, Germany) back to profit. Company-wise margins were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall 17% if there was no competitive pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said raw material and LPG/fuel costs rose sharply due to geopolitics, and price increases from customers were not enough to offset them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Europe EBITDA turn negative (-8%) after nearing breakeven in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe comprises Monocon UK and Sheffield Refractories. Sheffield's sales were low because British Steel's output was minimal; Monocon UK is near breakeven. Q2 expected to normalize; no orders lost, just timing.

qa_highlights.question: Will staff costs stay near 10% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Agarwal said standalone staff cost of INR28.7 crore is up from INR24 crore in Q4 but level with Q1 FY26; management aims to contain it. Consolidated employee cost rose partly due to a provision reversal last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is 12% consolidated EBITDA margin still the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aiming for double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin, dependent on geopolitics and overseas demand, and expects to return to that level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Chinese JV and R&D investment?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chinese JV is on hold pending government approval; the company must change location and reapply. Only land in Gujarat has been bought so far. R&D spend is about INR20 crore per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind for profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Rakhecha agreed with that view for today but cautioned that conditions can change quickly; he cited early green shoots in European steel.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No overall peak revenue figure given; the two new lines (mag carbon brick and casting flux) could add INR150-200 crore at peak.

505010|2026-06.headline: Automotive Axles Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin rose to 13.6% (from 12.4% QoQ) on revenue of Rs 5,168 mn and PAT of Rs 455 mn.
505010|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 5,168 million, EBITDA of Rs 702 million (about 13.6%), and profit for the year of Rs 455 million (about 8.7%, EPS about Rs 30). Management described EBITDA as one of the highest margins the company has achieved, helped by mix, a one-off, and lower employee costs versus the high-volume Q4. Management now sees the FY27 M&HCV industry down 5-10% versus last year, against an earlier 15-20% decline assumption, with Q4 expected to be a peak quarter. Capacity expansion (Phase-1 and Phase-1(a)) is about 40% complete.

segments.name: M&HCV on-highway axles (India)
segments.commentary: Management says demand is driven by replacement cycle and the shift from 6x2 to 10x2 or 4x2 tractor-trailers; heavy-duty (40 t and above) is the core focus. Overlap with American Axle described as minimal.

segments.name: Exports (to Meritor/CDBS global plants)
segments.commentary: Exports were about 13% of the quarter's revenue, versus a traditional 8-12% range; management guides to 8-12% for the year, with sea freight the main logistics challenge.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Defence contributes about 5-10% of revenue depending on tender timing; long gestation of 3-10 years from RFQ to SOP.

segments.name: Bus axles and new products
segments.commentary: Low-floor bus axle launch is still in validation, and is being reworked for upcoming pass-by noise norms. A 160 tandem axle is entering production with a large customer.

guidance_outlook: Management's FY27 industry view is a 5-10% decline versus last year (about 480,000 M&HCV units), against an earlier 15-20% decline assumption; best case is flat with last year.
Q2 expected to be reasonable, Q3 to see increasing demand, and Q4 to be another peak quarter, subject to geopolitical and monsoon risks.
Management guides to a steady-state PAT margin of 7.5-8.5% for the coming quarters and frames it as an overall band.
Capacity additions of roughly 25-30% are planned to cover the next two to three years of market growth, with Phase-1 and Phase-1(a) about 40% complete.
Management says it will not give specific volume guidance but expects better conversion and margins if volumes exceed the prior year.
capex_capacity: Phase-1 and Phase-1(a) of the capex programme are about 40% complete, with some production started.
Capacity improvement of roughly 25-30% is planned, depending on product mix (called a Rs 120 crore programme by the analyst).
Capex is aimed at upgrading or replacing lines with more automated equipment, to cover peak-month volumes and export opportunities.
A furnace was electrified, which helped production despite lower LPG availability.
Management says capacity must also be matched by supply chain readiness.
demand_pricing: Q1 M&HCV industry volume was about 110,000 units, down about 30% QoQ from the Q4 peak but among the highest Q1s in several years.
Steel and other commodity cost increases are fully passed through to customers on a back-to-back basis.
Conversion cost increases (LPG, tooling, consumables) were absorbed in Q1 with price negotiations ongoing with customers.
Management says the delayed monsoon is supporting freight and replacement demand.
Management says share of business with Ashok Leyland was maintained; the company confirmed it is a single source for some new products, with dual sourcing common at OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex breakup and growth versus replacement components of the Rs 120 crore programme?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the split is hard to separate. Capex is for upgrades, automation and capacity for the next 2-3 years, roughly 25-30% capacity improvement.

qa_highlights.question: How are exports and OEM opportunities split between Automotive Axles and American Axle (Bharat Forge)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two are competitors, that it cannot comment on the competitor's plans, and that exports go mainly to CDBS global entities.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company lost market share at Ashok Leyland?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a loss of share; the gap reflects product mix and seasonal/segment shifts. Confirmed Ashok Leyland share was maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How was the cost of steel and gas handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel and other commodities are passed through fully. Conversion cost increases were absorbed in Q1 with recovery from customers being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised industry outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry down 5-10% versus the earlier 15-20%; best case is flat with last year, Q4 a peak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the regulatory outlook for bus axles and new product launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Bus axle product launch is in validation and is being reworked for pass-by noise regulations; a 160 tandem axle is entering production.

risks_watch: Geopolitical tension and freight/LPG cost increases, with conversion cost recovery from customers still under negotiation.
Monsoon timing: a weak monsoon could push the industry toward the lower end of the 5-10% decline.
Pass-by noise and HPFE Phase-1B regulations could require design iteration and delay bus axle launch.
Competitive overlap with American Axle (now Bharat Forge-owned) in larger truck axles.
Sea freight rate volatility affecting export logistics.
Defence revenue lumpy with tender timing (5-10% of revenue).
505010|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Q1 margins and on the Q4 peak outlook, but cautious on FY27 volumes, with several answers deflecting share-of-business and competitor questions. Management avoided quantitative volume guidance and framed the margin range loosely.
key_quotes: If I can recall, this is probably one of the highest EBITDA percentage we ever achieved.
Overall, the EBITDA stood at Rs. 702 million, which is at about 13.6%.
We do see minimum impact on our product lines because of those recent changes.
Otherwise, in this industry, if you don't put the capacity, you cannot even go after any potential new opportunities.

544419|2026-06.headline: ArisInfra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR 291 crore, EBITDA up 68% to INR 31 crore, margin 10.49%, PAT INR 20 crore.

PAT was INR 20 crore versus INR 5 crore a year earlier. Management attributed margin expansion to a mix shift toward contract manufacturing and DaaS, whose combined share rose from about 46% to 63%. Net working capital days fell to 56 from 66 at March 2026 (about 97 in the prior quarter per an analyst exchange), and management reiterated 35-40% annual growth guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Contract manufacturing

segments.name: DaaS (Developer as a Service)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 28 crore, roughly 10% of top line, in Q1. New INR 650 crore mandate from Wadhwa Group (Mumbai); GDV under execution rose to over INR 1,800 crore from INR 1,250 crore at Q4 FY26. Management cited 60-65% EBITDA margin for DaaS.

segments.name: Asphalt (within contract manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR 53 crore from INR 30 crore in Q4 FY26; customers transacted rose to 38 from 28.

531548|2026-06.headline: Somany Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin up 3.6 pts YoY to 11.6% on standalone utilisation of 83% (vs 72%), with volume growth only ~3%.

segments.commentary: Standalone utilisation rose to 83% from 72%, with two lines under maintenance in the quarter. JV profit of INR3 crore vs a INR10 crore loss a year ago.

segments.name: Bathware / sanitaryware
segments.commentary: Management said Bathware margins run about 1% better than normal tile margins, and tile margins have now caught up. Bathware is growing healthily, with more sanitaryware balancing equipment planned.

segments.name: Construction chemicals (building materials)
segments.commentary: Large capacity added in the South, and a very large North capacity went on stream in July 2026; impact seen partly in Q1 and mostly in Q2.

segments.name: Somany Max
segments.commentary: EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR1.x crore from INR7 crore YoY. Management targets a loss of INR10 crore or less.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided at single-digit to mid-single-digit for FY27; management says it will not promise high single-digit or low double-digit growth.
EBITDA margin of 11%+ maintained for the year, with an aspiration to reach 12% and above; management said it is trying to improve margins in Q3 and Q4 as balancing equipment comes on stream.
Balancing equipment and debottlenecking (about 3-4 million sq m, some reported as 4-5 million) to be largely done by end-Q3 and fully in place in Q4 FY27; no new line in FY27.
Total capex to end-FY27 about INR275 crore (INR220 crore South plant plus balancing equipment), 65-70% funded by internal accruals; JV debt is non-recourse to Somany (60:40 JV).
9-plus million sq m South plant expected to add about INR350 crore revenue, ready in 12-15 months (end-Q3/start-Q4 FY28).
Management said maximum revenue at current capacity and prices is about INR3,700 crore; debottlenecking could add about INR300 crore partly by year-end.
Gas prices rose 16-18% in the current period; management said the company has passed through increases to date, and July and August gas prices are marginally higher.
capex_capacity: South plant: 9-plus million sq m greenfield, about INR220 crore outlay, operational around end-Q3 / start-Q4 FY28.
Balancing equipment in own plants and JVs (Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, South) to add about 3-4 million sq m (also cited as 4-5 million) by Q4 FY27; no new line in FY27.
Standalone utilisation at 83% in Q1 FY27 vs 72% a year ago; management expects slight further improvement in Q2.
Construction chemicals capacity added in South, and a very large North capacity commissioned in July 2026.
Bathware: additional balancing equipment planned at the sanitaryware plant.
demand_pricing: Price hike of about 16-17% taken in Q1 FY27; management said margins come from efficiency, with pricing being a pass-through.
Morbi was shut for about 1.5 months, with a 20-day ramp-up to full output from May. Management said about 15-17% of Morbi capacity has not restarted and will not restart.
Morbi exports are down 50-60% from peak due to geopolitical issues and freight; this may persist until freight stabilises.
Channel inventory was built up in March ahead of the April shutdown, is now back to normal but lean, as dealers wait for gas-price cuts.
Retail project share is about 7-8% and government about 10-11%; management expects this to rise by 3-4 percentage points.
Management said July demand was affected by rain but sales were still pushed; it said demand was 'perfectly fine' overall.

Management said that in the Q1 volume growth shortfall versus the industry leader, the leader benefited from in-house Morbi production in polished vitrified tiles (PVT), which Somany is fully exposed to via outsourcing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion and will it sustain from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to standalone utilisation rising to 83% from 72% and JV profit of INR3 crore vs a loss of INR10 crore YoY. It said margins are driven by efficiency rather than pricing and expects them to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Gas pricing across Morbi, North and South?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended natural gas cost is about INR68/unit. South and Morbi are around mid-INR70s (South partly on spot), and North is about INR68-69. Management did not give a blended fuel cost incl. biofuel.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth outlook and why guidance is only mid-single-digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is currently mid-single-digit. It said the leader's higher growth came from in-house PVT production. It has been cautious after missed high-single-digit targets in the past.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price premium over Morbi narrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Morbi raised prices by roughly double Somany's 16-17%, narrowing the gap. Morbi units are now on GEL gas, and their accounting is being rectified, which narrows landed-cost differences.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 capex and funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR275 crore to end-FY27 including the INR220 crore South plant and balancing equipment, with 65-70% from internal accruals. JV loan is without corporate guarantee from Somany.

qa_highlights.question: Is 2%-3% volume growth affected by outsourcing from Morbi, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Morbi outsourcing is not needed beyond a point because of freight. Own plants are targeted at 100% utilisation, with capacity located in North, South and West.

530759|2026-06.headline: Sterling Tools standalone fasteners grew total income 23.7% to INR201.9 crore with PAT up 48.4%, while EV subsidiaries remain loss-making until FY28 breakeven.
530759|2026-06.overview: Standalone fasteners delivered Q1 FY27 total income of INR201.9 crore (+23.7% YoY), EBITDA of INR31.1 crore (+26.9%, margin 15.4% vs 15%) and PAT of INR16.4 crore (+48.4%, margin 8.1%). Management flagged steel and broader inflation (chemicals, tungsten, wages up to 35% in some areas) as cost pressures, with pass-through price negotiations at a mature stage and expected to hit P&L after a 2-4 month lag. Subsidiaries SEM and STML continue to lose money; both are guided to break even in FY28 at combined revenue of about INR225-250 crore. Capacity utilisation is 90-95% and an INR88 crore fasteners capex (misstated as INR80 crore on the call) is mostly expected to commission in H2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA margin up only ~40 bps per analyst

segments.name: Standalone fasteners
segments.commentary: Total income INR201.9 crore (+23.7%), EBITDA INR31.1 crore (15.4% margin), PAT INR16.4 crore (8.1% margin); management says growth is outpacing the auto industry, with 20%+ growth in Q1 and similar near-term run-rate expected.

segments.name: Sterling E-Mobility (SEM)
segments.commentary: Loss-making; FY25 revenue was about INR380 crore on one anchor customer that in-sourced, a drop of about INR280 crore. Breakeven guided at about INR175 crore revenue in FY28; current capacity over INR300 crore; 33 active programs and 4 OEM business confirmations. Revenue mix planned at 30-35% two/three-wheeler and about 65% commercial vehicles.

segments.name: Sterling Tech-Mobility (STML)
segments.commentary: Pre-commercial; HV DC contactors and relays. Seven customer programs secured; commercial supplies to start Q2 FY27. Breakeven guided at about INR70 crore revenue in FY28; current capacity about INR140 crore on 3-shift basis. Testing/validation takes 8-16 months per customer.

guidance_outlook: Fasteners: management expects to hold margin structures on a full-year basis despite steel and inflation, citing customer price increases at an advanced stage.
Fasteners: near-term growth expected similar to Q1's 20%+ pace, unless the auto industry slows.
EV businesses (SEM and STML) revenue growth guided at 20-30% in FY27 and 30-40% in FY28.
SEM and STML both expected to break even in FY28; both will lose money in FY27.
Long-term EBITDA/operating margin for SEM and STML targeted at about 10%, plus or minus 2%, at breakeven scale.
Fasteners capex: INR88 crore in FY27, with a further INR25-30 crore next year to support about INR1,000 crore potential revenue, if markets support.
capex_capacity: Fasteners capex INR88 crore (stated as INR80 crore in the call, corrected by management), purely expansion of existing facilities in Bangalore and two NCR plants; some capacity kicked in marginally in Q1, bulk in H2 FY27.

SEM onboard charger and multifunction unit lines to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY27; samples then need about 4 months of on-road trials (around 50,000 km), so supplies expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
STML fully automated facility in Bangalore; current capacity about INR140 crore on 3-shift basis; commercial supplies from Q2 FY27.
SEM current capacity over INR300 crore without further investment.
Total invested capital in subsidiaries about INR100 crore (STML about INR50 crore, SEM about INR48-49 crore).
demand_pricing: Steel price increases in Q1 created cost pressure; lower-cost inventory largely consumed, so impact expected to be more visible in the coming quarter.
Steel pass-through negotiations typically take 2-4 months; management says customers are positive on compensating for inflation this year.
Industry: PV sales +25.9% to 1.27 million, 2W +20.3% to 5.63 million, CV +18.3%, 3W +29.7% YoY in Q1 FY27 per management.
SEM: LCV, HCV and public transport bus programs gaining traction; EV demand supported by high oil prices.
Integrated units for heavy bus and truck platforms priced at about INR3-3.5 lakh per unit.
Two new 2-wheeler programs at advanced stage with one OEM response expected in coming months; management sees second-sourcing opportunity at incumbents.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin rise about 270 bps while EBITDA margin rose only about 40 bps in standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited steel price increases plus broad inflation (chemicals, tungsten, minimum wages up to 35% in some areas), partly offset by shop-floor efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fasteners capacity utilisation and when will new capex be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 90-95%, described as fully utilised given product mix; most of the INR88 crore capex expected to commission in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How should standalone EBITDA margin be considered for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect EBITDA to weaken further and expects to hold full-year margin structures, based on price increases at an advanced stage.

qa_highlights.question: What are breakeven levels and timeline for SEM and STML?
qa_highlights.answer: Both expected to break even in FY28; SEM at about INR175 crore revenue and STML at about INR70 crore, combined about INR225-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue capacity of the subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: SEM over INR300 crore and STML about INR140 crore on current capacity, total about INR440 crore (corrected from INR400 crore plus).

qa_highlights.question: Will the fasteners capex take capacity to INR1,000 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, if markets support it, with a further INR25-30 crore of investment next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new SEM onboard charger and multifunction line contributing soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Lines commissioned by end of Q2; customer trials of about 4 months mean supplies around December 2026 or January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SEM loss-making and what is the R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss due to revenue collapse after anchor customer in-sourcing (FY25 revenue of about INR380 crore falling by about INR280 crore) and continuing R&D; about 130 people, more than half in product or application engineering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ADAS regulatory opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulation for medium and heavy CVs, about 0.5 million units a year, from October 2027, possibly pushed to January 2028; a Chinese partner signed.

544210|2026-06.headline: Emcure Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, with EBITDA of INR 508 crore (19.7% margin) and PAT up 35-36%.
544210|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, led by international markets (up 34.2% to INR 1,485 crore) while India grew 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore. EBITDA rose 25.8% to INR 508 crore with margin up 50 bps to 19.7%, and PAT grew about 36% to INR 292 crore. Gross margin fell to 58.4% on geographic and product mix, and net debt rose to INR 1,103 crore. Management reiterated low-to-mid teens FY27 revenue growth (now toward the higher end) and 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Board changes were announced: Chairman Berjis Desai retires at AGM and CEO Satish Mehta becomes Chairman; Samit Mehta becomes COO and CEO of Gennova, which is now 100% owned.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,095 crore, +10.2% YoY. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche in-licensed brands, growth was about 6-7%. Price contributed about 4-5%, new launches 1-2%. Management says no channel filling in the quarter.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 537 crore, +32.8% YoY, driven by base business and liposomal amphotericin B (Ampho). Ampho is introduced in pretty much all countries, but tender-based procurement means lumpy orders.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 427 crore, +24.6% YoY, on new launches and share gains. Semaglutide filing expected in the next few months; Quebec launch via Dr. Reddy's is uncertain.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 522 crore, +44.8% YoY, led by ARV. About two-thirds of ROW was ARV this quarter; management expects ARV at about 50-55% of ROW for the full year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid teens, with management now more comfortable at the higher end of that range, driven by ARV order book visibility.
EBITDA margin expansion of 70-100 bps for FY27 reiterated.
FY27 gross margin guided at about 59% (earlier 60-61% framing), as higher international and ARV mix dilutes gross margin while EBITDA is accretive.
R&D for FY27 guided at 4-5% of revenue; spend expected to pick up in the rest of the year.
India growth expected in line with industry in Q2 FY27 and faster than industry in H2 FY27 as the Zuventus base effect eases.
Net debt expected to rise to about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 FY27 after the Mantra and Gennova payouts (INR 450-500 crore), then turn net cash by end-FY28.
Management expects sequential improvement each quarter.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were given on the call.
Gennova consolidated to 100% after acquiring a 12.05% minority stake; Mantra acquisition payout completed in July 2026.
demand_pricing: International constant-currency growth about 12% (about 12-13% per later answer), against about 6-7% FX tailwind at company level.
India price growth about 4-5% YoY; new launches 1-2%; the remainder is volume.

Poviztra (semaglutide biosimilar with Novo Nordisk) is growing month on month, but management says 40-50 brands have launched in the market and it is hard to separate channel stocking from consumption. Pricing was set very competitively.
Gross margin pressure reflects B2B-type international businesses (lower gross margin, higher EBITDA contribution), with Europe and ARV growing faster.
Management says Zuventus is stabilised and consolidated, now moving to acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: Is India's double-digit growth clean, or is there channel filling after Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no channel filling this quarter; growth is normalised and expected to improve further in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What share of ROW is ARV, and does FY27 base make FY28 harder?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds of ROW is ARV this quarter; full-year ARV share is expected at about 50-55% of ROW, with growth in both ARV and non-ARV.

qa_highlights.question: When will domestic growth be back in line with the market, and what is organic growth ex-in-licensed brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 FY27 is expected to be in line with industry and H2 faster. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche, growth was about 6-7%. Poviztra is a new launch; OAD moves into the base next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is constant-currency international growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-level FX impact was about 6-7%; international growth would have been about 12% in constant currency (12-13% in later answer).

qa_highlights.question: Why is Canada semaglutide a second-wave filing, and what is the Quebec launch timing with Dr. Reddy's?
qa_highlights.answer: Filing expected in the next few months, delayed because semaglutide was pursued as a global development. Quebec timing depends on Dr. Reddy's supply; management will defer to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix from Europe and ARV growth; FY27 gross margin guided at about 59%. Management says B2B international businesses are EBITDA-accretive despite lower gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: When will net debt turn to net cash and how does it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt expected at about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 after acquisition payouts; net cash by about end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is guided at 4-5% of revenue for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 99 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,103 crore (CFO also cited INR 1,560 crore in Q&A)

500672|2026-06.headline: Novartis India targets doubling revenue in 4-5 years; run-rate ~INR650 crore for FY27, with incremental quarterly costs of INR40-50 crore from next quarter.
500672|2026-06.overview: Management held its first investor meet after the ChrysCapital-led takeover, presenting a commercial reset: bringing promotion in-house, building a ~900-MR field force targeting ~150,000 HCPs, and focusing on six therapy areas. Two bolt-on deals were closed in the first ~45 days: the Minipress XL trademark from Pfizer (cardiology, MAT July 2026 sales INR228 crore) and the in-licensing of ophthalmology brands Pagenax and Accentrix from NHPL. Near-term costs rise sharply, with margin expected to dip before recovering to above 20% in two to three years. Historical revenue was flat over the last four years. Management gave no quantified Dr. Reddy's termination-fee impact and no specifics on fund-raising for the Minipress debt.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR100 crore+ total portfolio; INR10 crore upfront fee

financial_highlights.metric: Annualised organic run-rate revenue (incl. acquisitions) for FY27

financial_highlights.change: Expected to dip, return to upwards of 20% in 2-3 years
Open offer price INR860.64; minimal tendering

segments.name: Cardiology (Minipress XL)
segments.commentary: Alpha-blocker trademark acquired from Pfizer; claimed >50% category share, 55-60% market share cited; MAT July 2026 sales INR228 crore growing ~6.5% CAGR vs market ~9-10%.

segments.name: Ophthalmology (Pagenax, Accentrix)
segments.commentary: In-licensed from NHPL for an upfront INR10 crore; Pagenax described as the only brand in its category (DME/wet AMD); Accentrix faces genericisation and Intas competition.

segments.name: Core anchor brands (Voveran, Methergin, Calcium Sandoz, Tegretal)
segments.commentary: Voveran sales cited at ~INR240 crore; other anchor brands cited at ~INR50 crore each. Trademarks now assigned to the company; no future royalties per management.

guidance_outlook: Organic revenue aspiration to at least double in four to five years from the current base.
Incremental cost of INR40-50 crore per quarter from the next quarter; full costs reflected from Q4 FY27 per management.
Sales team to be fully operational by around December 2026 (end Q3).
Margin to dip in the short to medium term; return to upwards of 20% in two to three years.
Plans to repay a significant portion of Minipress acquisition debt before FY end; capital-raising options to be announced in about a month.
capex_capacity: No manufacturing investment planned; products to be sourced via existing supply chain.
Distribution network expanding from ~4 C&Fs to ~25; 4,000-5,000 distributors targeted, to be set up within 45 days.
MR force of ~900 being built up de novo; hiring underway, with the sales engine fully on board by end Q3.
Minipress XL: bridging stock in place after Pfizer discontinued manufacturing; new sales force to be hired, none inherited.
demand_pricing: Management characterises India as a branded-generic market growing ~9-10%; six anchor therapy areas cited as 40-50% of incremental market value.
Minipress XL is a two-to-three player market; Intas biosimilar cited as a competitor in ophthalmology, with management expecting a four-to-five player market.
Management said brand-level sales projections will not be given.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term numbers and whether doubling includes M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to at least double the business in four to five years, measured organically; the annualised run-rate of ~INR650 crore for FY27 includes acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: M&A criteria and IRR expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Discount rate ~12-12.5%; Minipress assessed on payback rather than IRR, targeted at 8-9 years post-synergies on INR1,250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify legacy costs and the reset
qa_highlights.answer: Historical cost of INR10-15 crore per quarter as a listed entity, now rising by INR40-50 crore per quarter for team and marketing investment.

qa_highlights.question: Dr. Reddy's termination fee impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Still being worked on; no financials to be given until after Q2 close.

qa_highlights.question: Contingent liabilities (NPPA pricing dispute on Voveran and Tegretal) and INR300-odd crore income tax matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said these litigations have run 10-15 years with no recent hearings; tax risks already provided in the books, with no further detail given.

qa_highlights.question: Funding of Minipress acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Board has given exploratory approval; debt to be significantly repaid before FY end through capital-raising options, with details expected in about a month.

risks_watch: Margin compression: operating margin cited at 27% last year, expected to dip before recovering above 20% in two to three years.
Execution risk: de novo build of ~900 MRs and 25 C&Fs, with full operation targeted by December 2026.
Acquisition debt for Minipress XL; repayment and capital-raise plan to be announced.
Pending Dr. Reddy's termination financial impact and unquantified contingent liabilities (NPPA pricing dispute, ~INR300 crore income-tax matter).
Minipress supply continuity after Pfizer discontinuation; bridging stock held, long-term source not detailed.
Competition in ophthalmology (Accentrix vs Intas biosimilar) and in alpha-blockers.
500672|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and strategic on the long-term aspiration, but cautious and deliberately vague on numbers: management repeatedly deferred specifics on Dr. Reddy's impact, litigation, funding and brand-level sales, while openly flagging a near-term margin dip.
key_quotes: From this base, I clearly see ourselves at least doubling up in next four to five years.
In the near term, there will be some costs which are going to start getting incurred from now.
So, we will have a dip for sure as a part of doing this commercial reset.
We are bringing back the control of promotion into our hands.

543638|2026-06.headline: Tracxn Q1 FY27 revenue from operations ₹21.1 crore, up 2.9% QoQ; EBITDA negative ₹4.2 crore as company keeps investing in growth.
543638|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 2.9% QoQ to ₹21.1 crore, with management saying annualised ARR-type growth re-accelerated to around 19% QoQ-annualised, versus 14% in FY26. Profitability was weak: EBITDA was negative ₹4.2 crore and PAT negative ₹3 crore (including non-cash ESOP costs), and expenses rose 18% to ₹25.4 crore as sales headcount and product investment expanded. Management highlighted deferred revenue at an all-time high of ₹38.8 crore (+6% QoQ), paying accounts up 16% to 2,350, and new vertical/BU playbook launches that it said are lifting win rates. Management said margins should expand non-linearly once growth re-accelerates, but gave no timeline for positive EBITDA.

financial_highlights.value: adjusted figure not stated in call
negative ₹2.2 crore (net of buyback utilisation; buyback completed in Q2 FY26)

financial_highlights.change: reduced slightly on mix, now stabilising

segments.name: Investment banking (IB) vertical
segments.commentary: Used as the proof-point for the three-phase specialised-BU playbook; IB revenue growth reached about 30% QoQ (about 30% annualised) versus about 20% for FY26. New IB clients rose from about 9 to 13 per month to about 20 per month after dataset and product upgrades.

segments.name: VC (venture capital) segment
segments.commentary: Historically about one-third of revenue at peak; now lower than that, with management not disclosing exact share. Deal volumes at a 10-year low hurt this segment, which was flat QoQ.

segments.name: Corporates (M&A, innovation, strategy)
segments.commentary: About 45% of paying customers; corporate BU serves business-development use cases. Management said it wants corporates to be a sizeable part of the business over the long run.

segments.name: Universities BU
segments.commentary: Management said it grew about 45% in the period and is used by many top institutions, including IIMs, IITs, ISB and XLRI.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: About 50% of Q1 revenue from outside India; international revenue turned positive QoQ. US and UK are the top markets, followed by Singapore and Germany.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth guided at 15–20% for the year, likely toward the higher end, per management; management also said the current QoQ pace annualises to about 12.5%, implying roughly 10% for the year as its own estimate.

No specific timeline for positive EBITDA; management said margins will expand non-linearly once growth re-accelerates to historical levels, citing about 80% incremental EBITDA conversion historically.
Plans to double the closing-sales team from 34 (end-Dec 2025) to 60 by Dec 2026.
Expects more international launches to go live and show impact in the next quarter; management said they hope to demonstrate international improvement in Q2.
capex_capacity: Sales and marketing now about 30% of headcount, up from 27% previously; the team is now more sales-led.
Headcount has been held roughly flat while data coverage grew; the company says automation and AI infrastructure allow data expansion without significant headcount additions.
Company said that about 87% of expenses are employee cost; all workforce is in-house with no outsourced or contract staff; no paid-marketing line item.
Resellers and distribution partners being added in smaller geographies (TMX closed as key partner in Canada).
demand_pricing: Quarterly contract prices up about 7% YoY per the Q&A; management said quarterly billing and deferred revenue both increased.
Net new paying accounts were about 60 QoQ, with more than 300 users added QoQ; new-client wins include UBS, Kotak, Mizuho, Google, OpenAI, HSBC, Siemens and Bain Capital (names as cited on the call).
Record volume adds of 61 versus 43 in Q4.
Competition: management said only about three to four global players are encountered; standard offering covers 80–90% of need and the company builds the rest.
Management said Bloomberg is not used by its target private-market buyers, which are different from public-market users.
Americas revenue declined; management attributed this to VC deal volumes at a 10-year low hitting upgrades and new logos.

qa_highlights.question: Roadmap to positive EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin expansion is predictable once growth re-accelerates, citing an example where ₹20 crore of incremental revenue drove ₹15 crore of incremental EBITDA in one year. No timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been flat since March 2023 and when will the recovery show?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the slowdown to VC deal activity at a 10-year low; the company prioritised IB and other segments, which now grow at 20–30% QoQ, and the blended rate has improved to about 19% QoQ-annualised from 14%.

qa_highlights.question: How is competition evaluated, given Bloomberg?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bloomberg serves public-market users and is rarely used by private-market investors; the global competitive set is about three to four players.

qa_highlights.question: What drives IB success and what else is working?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the three-phase playbook (specialised BU, product augmentation, scale-up) lifted IB to about 30% QoQ growth and is being replicated across about five or six verticals in the UK, US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: How big is VC now as a share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: VC was about one-third of revenue at peak; it is now lower, but management did not disclose the exact percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Americas declining and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is cyclical (VC deal volumes), not structural, and that US/UK specialised teams are now being replicated internationally with QoQ growth turning positive.

qa_highlights.question: Net adds and realisation trend?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60 net new paying accounts QoQ; ASP of ₹3.6 lakh per account per year has slightly declined on mix but is now stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 6,534 user count include Lite freemium users?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the reported user count excludes Lite freemium users, which are a top-of-funnel marketing channel that had 300,000 signups since launch.

543980|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income INR411 crores, EBITDA INR79.3 crores at 19.3% margin, PAT INR37.5 crores; Dombivli drag INR9.5 crores.
543980|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter of operations for Dombivli Hospital, which contributed a INR9.5 crore EBITDA drag, in line with management's expectations. Consolidated total income was INR411 crores, EBITDA INR79.3 crores (19.3% margin) and PAT INR37.5 crores. ARPOB rose to INR73,500 and ALOS was 3.76 days, with average occupancy at 59.6% diluted by the expanded Dombivli bed base. 543330|2026-06.headline: Devyani Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore, with record Operating EBITDA of INR 151 crore (9.6% margin).

segments.commentary: Biryani By Kilo SSSG +7.2%, Vaango +7.1%; combined revenue INR 98 crore, gross margin 65.9%, brand contribution ~INR 10 crore (10.2%). 218 stores including 23 BBK Express; BBK target INR 1,000 crore brand in next few years.

capex_capacity: Store opening pace in line with prior guidance; 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in India in Q1.

BBK Express small-box format (23 stores) being tested in food courts; BBK dine-in and airport formats being piloted.

demand_pricing: KFC SSSG +3.3%; management reports demand 'stable' and July trends positive, but macro (LPG, rupee, crude) remains a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Pizza Hut?

Pizza Hut remains loss-making at brand contribution level with ADS well below peers.
Merger completion by end FY27 and the technology build-out being ready before merger approval.

543330|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on profitability and KFC momentum, but cautious on macro, SSSG outlook and Pizza Hut; management repeatedly said it is too early to call Q2 and that a bullish view requires macro stability.

540595|2026-06.headline: Tejas Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 20% QoQ to INR402 crore, with PBT still negative at INR271 crore and BSNL expansion order awaited.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY (as stated in opening remarks); +6% QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in INR; margin 29.1% (analyst-computed from Q1 FY26 33.6%)
Negative INR14 crore (-5.2% margin per analyst)

financial_highlights.change: from migration to new tax regime (25.17% vs 34.9%)

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (CPVC, SIOP)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR177 crore, up 38% YoY with CPVC volumes up 59% and SIOP volumes up about 3%. EBITDA grew about 20% YoY and 35% QoQ; margin about 29% vs 33.6% a year ago, which management linked to PVC-CPVC spread volatility.

segments.name: Basic Chemicals (PVC, caustic soda, soda ash, Synthetic Rutile)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore, down 18% QoQ on Q4 Synthetic Rutile inventory liquidation. EBITDA negative INR14 crore; management estimated a sequential PVC contribution swing of INR50-55 crore, with caustic soda and Synthetic Rutile margins improving.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Basic Chemicals' loss came from PVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only a directional estimate: a sequential contribution swing of INR50-55 crore in PVC. It confirmed PVC was the only loss-making Basic Chemicals product, with caustic soda, soda ash and Synthetic Rutile profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR400 crore EBITDA target still stand?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It was set when CPVC margins were about 40%. Management now sees steady-state EBITDA of about INR300 crore, subject to the spread holding.

qa_highlights.question: How is VCM sourced, and can it be derisked or backward integrated?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply moved from a single Qatar producer to a global distributor sourcing across Asia. Management ruled out backward integration at current scale; storage expansion would add only about 10-15 days of inventory.

538920|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58.4% YoY to INR161 crore and PAT 46.1% to INR20.8 crore, with 1,856 MT sold against 2,402 MT produced.
538920|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR161 crore (+58.4% YoY), EBITDA INR31.6 crore (+75.2%) and PAT INR20.8 crore (+46.1%), with a 12.9% PAT margin. The 4,500 MT capacity added at end-FY26 ran at about 90-95% utilisation, taking installed capacity to 11,000 MT. Management said the NCLT approved the merger of two wholly owned subsidiaries effective 21 July 2026, and freeze-dried coffee (FDC) capacity of 5,500 MT is under construction for start in Q2 FY28. Q1 was a seasonal lean quarter, with production exceeding sales and inventory building ahead of Q2 deliveries.

financial_highlights.change: +58.4% YoY vs INR101.6 crore in Q1 FY26
Management figure; analyst calculation of INR172 included chicory

financial_highlights.metric: Capex spent on FDC project to date

segments.name: Spray-dried / agglomerated coffee (core)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 11,000 MT after 4,500 MT added at end-FY26; packing capacity 5,000 MT; Q1 packing mix 45% bulk and 55% consumer packs. Management guided FY27 volume of about 10,500 MT at 95% utilisation.

segments.name: Chicory (Delecto Foods, wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Capacity 2,000 MT per annum; revenue INR42-45 crore per annum; described as profitable and at optimum utilisation with no expansion planned. Management put chicory's Q1 EBITDA at about INR2-2.2 crore and FY27 chicory sales at INR40-45 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue ballpark INR850-900 crore at Q1 average realisation on about 10,500 MT volume (CEO confirmed on call).
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to improve 0.5-1% from Q1 levels; management cited a 23-24% consolidated EBITDA margin in the business plan for the next two years.
FDC 5,500 MT line to start production in Q2 FY28 after June 2027 trials; FY28 volume from FDC about 2,400 MT at 60-65% utilisation over 8-9 months.
Peak debt capped at INR450 crore; FY28 debt in line with INR400 crore plan. Phase 2 FDC to be funded from incremental FY28 cash flow, with no further equity dilution currently planned.
Management said FY27 operating cash flow would be positive and working capital cycle around 120-125 days.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity: 6,500 MT (January 2025 addition of 2,000 MT) plus 4,500 MT at end-FY26 = 11,000 MT; expansion funded entirely from internal accruals.

FDC expansion of 5,500 MT on land from Telangana Government Food Processing Zone; total capacity to rise to 16,500 MT. Construction started and advance paid to equipment suppliers.
Another FDC line is likely soon after the first 5,500 MT line is completed.
FDC capex about INR550 crore; INR150 crore spent to date, of which INR25 crore in Q1.
demand_pricing: Green coffee prices stable at about 3,500-3,800 per MT; management expects them to stay in this range through the year, with a healthy Brazil crop offset by weather risk.
Pricing is reset quarterly on a cost-plus basis; management said margin per kg is fixed, so bulk sales lower realisation and EBITDA per kg.
Geography mix: West Africa about 30%, Russia/CIS about 22%, Southeast Asia about 20%, Central America about 15%, Europe about 10%, India about 5%.

FDC: management cited LOIs for 70-80% of FDC capacity from Russia, Europe, the US and Southeast Asia (subject to quality and price). Two of these customers are new and five are existing. Global FDC market is about 2,50,000 MT, so 5,500 MT is about 2.2% share.
FDC realisation expected to be 28-32% above spray-dried, which management said is equivalent to a 20-30% EBITDA per kg premium in later exchanges.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4,500 MT capacity contributing revenue in Q1, and what is its utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioned in March 2026 and running at about 90-95% utilisation in Q1; Q1 is seasonally lean, with Q2-Q4 expected to improve.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins keep rising, and what is the FDC start timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expected to rise 0.5-1% from Q1 levels. FDC trials by June 2027 with production from Q2 FY28; 60-65% utilisation over 8-9 months, adding about 2,400 MT in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue potential and the chicory contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 revenue ballpark is INR850-900 crore on 10,500 MT. Chicory revenue is INR40-45 crore a year, and EBITDA from chicory in Q1 was about INR2.1 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt and capex plans for FDC?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt capped at INR450 crore; phase 2 to be funded from FY28 incremental cash flow; no equity dilution planned at present.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital days high at 120-130 and when does cash flow improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth inventory is the main reason; CFO said FY27 operating cash flow will be positive, with working capital days around 125 and the FY27 cash-generation capacity estimated at about INR79 crore if growth inventory was not needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any hedging or inventory loss risk given production above sales in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said beans are bought back-to-back, with 40-45 days of stock held; surplus Q1 production is expected to be picked up by customers in Q2.

540404|2026-06.headline: Prime Fresh Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.7% to INR81.71 crore and EBITDA jumped 51% to INR6 crore (9.83% margin), which management says is not fully sustainable.
540404|2026-06.overview: Prime Fresh reported Q1 FY27 sales of INR81.71 crore (vs INR53.34 crore), EBITDA of INR6 crore (9.83% margin vs 7.53%) and PAT of INR4.35 crore (vs INR2.89 crore). Management attributed part of the jump to one-off recoveries of pending service-business billings, inventory gains from rising F&V and onion prices, and strong service volumes, and guided that margins may not be sustained. Forward guidance is EBITDA margin of 7% to 7.5% and volume growth of 15% to 25%, with value growth of 25% to 30%. The company is pursuing the Nashik cluster development project under the National Horticulture Board, expected to be awarded in August 2026, and a Bank of Baroda working capital limit increase to INR20 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: Bank of Baroda cash credit limit
financial_highlights.change: Raised from INR7.8 crore at 8.5% cost

segments.name: F&V business (B2B)
segments.commentary: Management stated FY23 sales of about INR275 crore, of which about INR245 crore plus came from F&V and the balance from service business. B2C is 1% to 2% of business; exports stopped post-COVID.

segments.name: Service business
segments.commentary: Q1 saw good volume growth and strong margins, plus recovery of old pending billings that aided the quarter. Management said this contribution is not expected to recur at the same level.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Florens Farming Ltd is the key focus for own farming and land tie-ups; management said it contributes about 10% of F&V and could pay off from next year. Prime Fresh Retail India Pvt Ltd is held for strategic partners; B2C entry deferred.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 7% to 7.5%; net profit margin guidance stated as 5.5% to 5% (as transcribed, likely a typo).
Volume growth of 15% to 20% minimum in one answer and 15% to 25% in closing remarks; value growth of 25% to 30%.
Internal aspiration of 9.5% to 11% EBITDA margin in 2 to 2.5 years (around 2029) and a vision of INR2,000 crore revenue by 2031; longer-term EBITDA margin of 14% to 16% in 4 to 5 years.
Operating margin expected to rise slowly from mid-FY28.
Debtor target of 88 to 94 days of sales, debtors below 25% of sales, and no single rupee of working capital or equity needed for an incremental INR60 crore sale by FY29.
Product portfolio to add three to four more categories within a year (currently 9 to 12 F&V products).
capex_capacity: Nashik (Sinnar) cluster development programme under National Horticulture Board: company as implementing agency; expected award in August 2026; INR75 crore investment (excluding INR5-6 crore preoperative spend), of which INR50-52 crore eligible for 40-50% grant (about INR24 crore grant expected on milestones).
Capex to start around end-October to end-November 2026 over 18 to 20 months; Phase 1 INR6-9 crore, Phase 2 INR12-15 crore, balance in Phase 3, funded from own balance sheet including debt.
Project debt peak about INR35 crore against INR42 crore sanctioned, falling to INR18-20 crore after grants.
Farmer component of about INR60 crore with around 35% government subsidy; target of 15,000 farmers and 15,000 tons incremental sourcing in year 1, scaling to 2 lakh tons in six years.
Sourcing capacity close to 2.5 lakh tons vs FY sales of about 65,000 tons.
demand_pricing: Customer mix: about 20 large modern trade and e-commerce accounts, around 90 APMC partners, 10 to 15 food processors, 20 to 30 exporters; added four to five food processing customers in Q1.
Price pass-through of 4 to 8 days on procurement changes for most business; HoReCa about one month; 5-star and tender business up to 3 months, which is under 4% of business.
Pomegranate: about 13,000 farmers and 40 plus local area aggregators; onion prices rising sharply, benefiting inventory gains.
Procurement advantage of direct farm sourcing stated at 3% to 15% on price, with 10% to 15% operational cost initially; long-term advantage 5% to 8% over supplier purchase.
Company is positioned as a pan-India supplier to modern trade and e-commerce across 10 cities for onion, pomegranate and orange.

qa_highlights.question: Can receivables (about one-third of revenue) be reduced and can trade payables be extended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a client credit exposure system, stricter onboarding with PDCs and security cheques, and about INR12 crore debtor reduction in Q1. It aims at 88-94 debtor days and a 25% of sales cap; a BoB limit rise to INR20 crore plus INR20 crore for Nashik was cited; payables to farmers are expected to rise to INR10-15 crore on credit by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Nashik Sinnar project add beyond the asset-light model?
qa_highlights.answer: Prime Fresh is implementing agency for a farmer component (subsidy-led) and an IA component of INR75 crore with 40-50% grant on eligible capex; it aims at order-book model, farm-gate packhouse and cold chain, and a separate call was offered.

qa_highlights.question: Cumulative capex, revenue/tonnage and margin impact, and replication to other cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex over about 18-20 months with phased balance-sheet spend; quantified margin uplift not given. Replication via subsidiary or SPV route is open, with full equity payback in up to 5 years targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Lag between procurement price changes and customer price resets?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 4 to 8 days; HoReCa up to one month; tender business up to three months, under 4% of business.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q1 trading and direct expenses up faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the numbers and said it would respond by mail.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter B2C given the city footprint?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C needs heavy upfront investment; an earlier franchise attempt cost INR55-75 lakh in 2021-2023. Management decided not to pursue it now, with B2C at 1-2% of business.

544179|2026-06.headline: Go Digit's Q1 FY27 GDPI fell 8% and loss ratio rose to 73.3%, with management choosing profitability over growth.
544179|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a deliberately soft quarter, with gross written premium down 8% (about -2% excluding inward reinsurance in group health and crop). Motor own damage, mainly private car, drove the loss ratio up from 70.3% to 73.3%, and management said it had made the wrong call on the stand-alone OD renewals. On its internal KPI basis (NEP with DAC, excluding MTM and discounting), PAT was INR190 crore versus INR200 crore a year ago and combined ratio was 107.2%. Under Indian Accounting Standards (IFRS-style prescribed format), PAT rose to INR372 crore from INR325 crore, helped by unrealised gains and discounting.

financial_highlights.change: About -2% excluding inward reinsurance exits in group health and crop

segments.commentary: CV share of motor fell to about 23-24% from roughly 65% four to five years ago, as the company deliberately exited the segment.

segments.commentary: GDPI down 37% against an industry decline of about 27-28%. Gross fire loss ratio was 67% in Q1 despite one large claim; retention is about 20%.

Own damage loss ratio expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.
Management said that, excluding the drop in fire, the fourth quarter could see a base effect on growth.
Dividend: management said IGAAP solvency (about 242%) supports a dividend, to be considered by the Board in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms.
Underwriting and claims-settlement actions on TP were planned for around the third week of August 2026.
capex_capacity: Investment mix: 9.5% of AUM in equity, REITs and InvITs (AT1 bonds shown separately); management said it could take equity to 13-14% if markets fall, or to 15-18% in its stated framework.
Fixed income duration moved from 4.5 to 4.9 in Q1; reinvestment yield rose to 7.8% from 7.5%. Management said it would extend duration to about 5.2 if the 30-year yield moves above about 7.75%.
Reinsurance commission increased across all lines and reinsurance capacity increased, per management.
Management said it is waiting for RBC norms, expected possibly within FY27, to know whether solvency will be measured on RBC, IFRS or IGAAP.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing across most lines has fallen and is now down across the board. It cited EOM rules, which pushed commissions up, and low-priced crop, group health, and fire business written to meet EOM.
Claims inflation: no third-party motor rate increase for about five years, while minimum wages, parts, paint and labour costs have risen.
Fire rates were said to be down about 40-45%.
Management said Digit has not chased growth; it gave up fire and commercial business it judged underpriced, and said the 2W and bancassurance/digital channels were growing well.

Supreme Court (June 11, 2026) TP ruling: management said it is comfortable with reserves and will not take a bet on judgment interpretation; two High Court rulings (July 2 Allahabad, July 16 Karnataka) were cited as narrowing the ruling.

570004|2026-06.headline: Jain Irrigation Q1 FY27 revenue fell ~2.5% to about Rs 1,500 crore, EBITDA margin dropped ~2 pts, and adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore versus Rs 30 crore a year ago.
570004|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 1,500 crore, down roughly 2.5% YoY, with Hi-Tech degrowing, plastics flat and Agro-Processing growing on beverages and overseas sales. EBITDA fell on lower standalone India fixed-cost absorption, weaker Hi-Tech volumes and negative forex, while plastics margin improved. Management said April was weak but May, June and July improved, and it expects a stronger second half. Rs 164 crore of EBITDA was converted to cash at about 78%, and net working capital days fell to 183 from 210 a year ago. Rs 680-690 crore of NCDs fall due in September (about Rs 230 crore) and March; management says these will be met from internal cash flow with refinancing and other options in progress.

segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat YoY, with overseas plastics revenue up about 40%. EBITDA margin improved to about 11% from 10%.

capex_capacity: Biochar plant recently started, using agri-waste (corn cob, cotton stalk, mango stones); impact on numbers expected from next fiscal.
