Large Pune water-supply project still needs triple-digit billing; other projects about 98-99% complete with about Rs 40-50 crore billing left.
About 10-12 of 72 projects carry O&M over the next two to three years; management says O&M spend is light.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose about 50%; management says most increases were passed on to customers, and customers deferred purchases until prices ease.
Delayed monsoon onset in June hit farm purchases; July rainfall was good and July revenue grew versus April-June.
Dam levels at about 67% of capacity; management hopes for 85% by monsoon end, which it sees as positive for Rabi and next summer.
Company chose not to pursue government-subsidy micro-irrigation business that would have needed longer receivables; management says about Rs 50-60 crore more sales were possible.
Institutional demand for larger-diameter pipes is being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt falls due and what are the repayment options?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NCDs of about Rs 680-690 crore fall due (about Rs 230 crore in September, rest in March). Options listed: internal accruals (primary), legacy receivable collection, surplus land monetisation and refinancing; term sheets are in hand.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy government receivable will be collected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about Rs 422 crore for FY27, with Rs 60 crore received in Q1 and at least Rs 380 crore expected in the remaining nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any risk of write-offs on project receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no material write-offs are expected; provisions were made in earlier review and the remaining good receivables will be collected.

qa_highlights.question: Why are standalone working capital requirements higher than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to long-tail legacy project receivables and state-government orders on behalf of farmers, which are paid in six months to one year. Expects improvement from FY28 once project receivables clear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the delay in the food business IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Market valuations fell over the past year, so merchant bankers advised waiting; the total issue, including PE exit and primary funds, was expected at about Rs 1,000 crore. Management expects action from September if markets improve.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Hi-Tech margin down and what is the full-year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6% on lower volumes. Management said a full-year standalone margin of about 14% and consolidated 12-13% is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the receivables are over 180 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 1,100 crore is above 180 days (about Rs 300 crore of farmer-order receivables plus Rs 800-900 crore of government receivables), roughly 55% of the Rs 1,975 crore net receivables.

risks_watch: Debt service: about Rs 230 crore of NCDs due in September; refinancing and asset monetisation timelines remain unconfirmed.
Recovery of Rs 380 crore of legacy government receivables in nine months; about 55% of net receivables (about Rs 1,100 crore) are above 180 days.
Polymer price volatility and oil/geopolitical risk could delay customer purchases.
Monsoon progress in August-September, which management says is critical for H2 volumes.
Food business IPO and PE exit timing with no confirmed date; Tamil Nadu land sale repeatedly delayed.
Whether the H2 margin catch-up materialises; Q1 adjusted PAT was about Rs 3 crore.

544320|2026-06.headline: Carraro India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR5,447 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.4% on pass-through lag from commodity and freight inflation.
544320|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR5,447 million, driven by domestic growth of about 26% that offset a roughly 14% fall in exports. EBITDA rose 6% YoY to INR579 million, but margin was 10.4% as higher energy, raw material and freight costs, plus supplier-side labour shortages, were not yet recovered from customers. Total income included a one-time INR88 million provision write-back linked to a customs reassessment, which flatters other income and PAT. Management expects the price pass-through gap to close over about 12 months and targets full recovery of price increments for the full year.

demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as resilient across agriculture, construction and off-highway; Carraro's backhoe loader sales to Indian OEMs grew ~18% vs ~14% for the market; driveline sales to OEMs up ~18% YoY.
Volume growth was about 8-10% per management (not verified in numbers); the rest of the 10% revenue growth is said to be little price impact because pass-through lags at least four months.
Export demand: Turkey volatile due to inflation with order flow weaker this quarter; Europe agri subdued; US decisions delayed by inflation; Latin America showing modest positive signs.
Export tele boom handler and backhoe loader demand said to be stable and rising; a major export customer's trend was described as step-by-step higher.
Customers have agreed in principle to pass-through of commodity costs, but several are in wait-and-watch mode. Transport cost pass-through is not contractually fixed, but OEMs are taking positions.
Management expects possible OEM price hikes of 3-6% in construction vehicles, citing cost pressures.
Carraro supplies all Indian backhoe loader OEMs except JCB; 36 customers in total.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue growth split between metal price increase and organic volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price pass-through is at least a four-month lag, so the price component is small; volume growth is estimated at about 8-10%, with exact numbers to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic agri and construction revenue, and YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic agri INR2,135 million (+32% YoY Q1-on-Q1); domestic construction INR1,393 million (+20% YoY); other domestic sales INR267 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EBITDA margin reach 10.5-11% for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO declined to give a range: if the price gap is fully bridged, EBITDA could be about half a point above last year, with more guidance next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is China a meaningful market for Carraro India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said China exposure is hardly 1% of revenue, with only occasional small orders (50-100 axles); the product range differs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the labour availability constraint and does it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Carraro India said it had no internal manpower constraint; shortages are at Tier-3 suppliers (migrant casual labour), which added overtime and conversion costs that are being passed to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why do exports fall and how predictable are they?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 was hit by logistics issues (container and vessel shortages) and is unrepresentative; exports should return to FY25-FY26 levels from Q2.

Supplier-side labour and material shortages, with overtime and ad hoc supplier payments adding costs.
Localisation at 74% against 86-88% target; reliance on imports for some higher-technology components.
Monsoon and El Niño risks; government subsidy and contractor cash-flow issues affecting construction demand.
Working capital and funding of capex while maintaining profitability.

Management was candid that Q1 margins are depressed by a pass-through lag, and gave no firm full-year EBITDA range. Some answers were evasive, notably on non-farm split, customer count and China exposure. Management said the worst is over.

PAT rose 26% to INR56.5 crore, helped by lower finance costs and operating leverage; management said the INR433.5 crore preferential equity raise came in late July/early August and did not benefit Q1. Order book closed at a record above INR9,200 crore and Q1 inflows were about INR1,674 crore (call also cites INR1,600 crore). Management reiterated 15% FY27 revenue growth and said the year is H2-weighted, with Engineering (export-heavy) soft in Q1.

segments.commentary: Q1 revenue muted versus last year's above INR500 crore run-rate due to commodity price volatility and trade destocking; management guides about 20% top-line growth for FY27 with some margin improvement.

segments.name: Infra (EPC services)
segments.commentary: Strong growth in Q1 and past two quarters; revenue of about INR250 crore over two quarters cited. Management expects higher growth in this segment for FY27. Order book of about INR1,800 crore is infra, roughly 25% of order inflow.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15%, reiterated despite Q1 growth of about 5%; management expects H2 weighting.
FY27 order inflow target of INR7,000 crore-plus, implying closing order book of INR10,000 crore-plus; about INR1,100 crore from exports.
Expects about INR5,000 crore of the INR9,200 crore order book to execute in FY27; orders typically execute over 2 to 2.5 years.
FY27 finance cost expected at 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue after the fundraise.
Long-term aspirational EBITDA margin 12%; export share of order inflow targeted at 50% long term (about 15% in FY27, 20-25% next year per management).
Capacity expansion of 75,000 tonnes expected to commission by end of Q2 FY27 (a few months' deferment), taking total capacity to 450,000 tpa.
Indian transmission bids expected at INR90,000-100,000 crore in FY27 vs INR50,000-60,000 crore TBCB bidding in FY26.
capex_capacity: 75,000 tonne capacity expansion to commission by end of Q2 FY27 (slight delay), taking total capacity to 450,000 tpa; bulk of this capacity is export-focused.
Fundraise of INR433.5 crore via preferential equity; entire proceeds used for debt repayment per management.
Subsidiaries established in Brazil and UAE; US entity expected to become operational shortly.
Two 765 kV projects secured in Maharashtra from a reputed developer in Q1.
Legacy low-margin contracts now under 5% of order book, largely executing out this year.
demand_pricing: Steel spiked in Q1 but normalised to pre-February levels by May; aluminium also eased. Management said firm-price contracts carry buffers, variable-price contracts adjust monthly, and inventory build-up and partial hedging are used.

Export inflow hit by tariffs and Middle East geopolitics last year; management says export ordering has rebounded, with advanced talks in the US, Australia, and other developed markets; Europe slower pending approvals.
Export shipments being deferred by customers due to elevated shipping costs.
Order book by segment: about 75% T&D-related infra/EPC services versus 25% of total order book; Q1 inflow almost entirely T&D.
Biggest challenge cited: quality technical manpower; company takes about 200-250 graduate trainees annually.

qa_highlights.question: Is ordering picking up versus FY26, and what is the outlook for the Indian transmission market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ordering has picked up, bids are being finalised, and inflows should translate from Q2. It expects INR90,000-1,00,000 crore of Indian transmission bids in FY27 and said about 40% of the INR9 lakh crore pipeline has been bid so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is the finance cost decline due to the fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Fundraise funds arrived late July or early August, so Q1 had no benefit; the decline came from working capital management and operating leverage. FY27 finance cost guided at 3.2%-3.5% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is export revenue lost or delayed, and which segment drives 15% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export ordering has not stopped and export order inflow should rise more than 50% YoY. The 15% growth is expected from all three segments, with Infra growing fastest; Q1 and Q2 are seasonally slow due to monsoon, West Bengal elections, and freight disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR9,200 crore order book executes by FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately INR5,000 crore is expected to execute in FY27, with short-term orders adding to this. Orders typically execute over 2 to 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Polymer revenue muted and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to commodity price volatility and trade destocking. It expects about 20% Polymer top-line growth in FY27 with margin improvement, and says growth will come from both volume and value.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited legacy low-margin contracts rolling off, better new-contract quality, operating leverage, and commodity mitigation through firm/variable price mix, inventory and hedging. It called the expansion structural and aimed toward 12% long-term margin.

qa_highlights.question: Does the delay in capacity expansion affect the 15% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said commissioning is deferred only by a few months to end of Q2, with no impact on the 15% target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Engineering soften while Infra jumped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Engineering is affected by weak FY26 export and domestic order intake plus shipment deferrals due to high freight costs; it called this temporary. Infra growth is from TBCB transmission EPC services, with no change in scope of work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 order inflow target, and what is the export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR7,000 crore-plus of FY27 order inflow, with about INR1,100 crore from exports (about 15% of inflow).

543390|2026-06.headline: PB Fintech Q1 FY27: consolidated operating revenue up 40% to ₹1,888 Cr and PAT up 92% to ₹163 Cr, with insurance premium up 41% to ₹8,372 Cr.
543390|2026-06.overview: Management reported broad-based growth in Q1 FY27, with insurance premium up 41% YoY to ₹8,372 Cr and new health and term premium up 53%. Consolidated operating revenue grew 40% to ₹1,888 Cr, core insurance revenue rose 46% and core credit revenue rose 25%, while PAT margin improved from 6% to 9%. Management repeatedly stated that growth, not margin expansion, remains the priority, with acquisition spend being increased. Management also said Q1 is seasonally weak and flagged that the GST-related health and term demand tailwind is already fading.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating expenses excluding contribution, % of revenue

segments.name: Insurance (Policybazaar)
segments.commentary: Core new insurance premium incl. savings grew 39%, excluding savings 48%. New health grew 59% and new health and term grew 53%. Management says 82% of business is from customers new to insurance.

segments.name: Credit (Paisabazaar)
segments.commentary: Core revenue grew 25% and core disbursals 33%, with total disbursals at ₹4,366 Cr. Operating EBITDA broke even in Q1 and contribution margin was 41%; management expects FY27 EBITDA about half of the ~₹100 Cr previously discussed.

segments.name: PB Partners (POSP)
segments.commentary: Active partners rose 55% YoY to 1.13 lakh and 78% of GWP comes from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Top 100 partners account for 16% of premium; POSP premium is about ₹1,600 Cr and corporate about ₹500 Cr.

segments.name: UAE / Dubai
segments.commentary: UAE insurance premium grew 31% YoY, about ₹500 Cr in the quarter, mainly health and life.

segments.name: PB Health
segments.commentary: Quarterly loss about ₹7 Cr. Second hospital got billing approval; internal target is ~₹500 Cr annual run rate and break-even by March 2027.

segments.name: PB Connect
segments.commentary: Revenue about ₹12 Cr from retail. Wholesale consolidation business was discontinued, so the line is down 73% YoY and was zero from wholesale in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects renewal growth to exceed fresh growth over the next 12 months, with renewal growth upwards of 50% for some time.
Management says long-term target of about 30% growth remains; margin efficiency is deferred in favour of growth, with efficiency expected later.
Management says the GST-driven insurance demand tailwind is fading in Q1 and it may be lucky if it persists in Q2.
PB Health targets ~₹500 Cr annual run rate and break-even by March 2027.
Paisabazaar FY27 EBITDA expected at roughly half of the previously discussed ~₹100 Cr; Q1 at break-even.
Several launches planned for end-August 2026, including bonds via PB Money entity and daily SIP platform on Paisabazaar.

Call-centre talk time for health transactions reduced from about 2 hours at IPO to 35-40 minutes now.
AI touches 30-40% of about 10 crore monthly customer interactions; 20-30% of service interactions are automated.
Second PB Health hospital received billing approval; more hospitals in pipeline.
demand_pricing: Health and term growth is attributed to demand creation spend, product features like monthly mode (over 30% of health business) and a 3-month maternity waiting period, and claims service (CSAT above 90%, ~70,000 health claims supported in the quarter).
Tier 2 and Tier 3 account for 65-70% of direct online business and are growing faster than metros; South has grown faster than North and West over three years.
Motor plus two-wheeler direct grew over 30%; motor POSP grew close to 50%. Retail direct TP is about 25% of premium value; POSP motor is about half TP.
Waiver of Premium (WOP) share in domestic savings has crossed 60% in some centres in July; savings fresh business grew over 20%.
Management views the Supreme Court TP-extension judgement as a potential upside via enforcement, but says it is too early to quantify.
Management said Q3 FY26 was an above-trend quarter, making the H2 base high, and said the goal is above-market growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where is health and term growth coming from (Tier 2/3 vs urban) and is the user base different from peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed outgrowth to demand investment, relevant tailored products, and claims service; 82% of business is from customers without prior insurance, and port-in is a small share.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins evolve as renewals grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renewal growth will beat fresh growth for ~12 months but will keep reinvesting in acquisition for lifetime value; margin improvement is secondary to fresh growth.

qa_highlights.question: Regulatory commission changes and the worst-case manufacturer scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not anticipate changes, pointed to legal effort requirements on brokers, and said insurance requires heavy enquiry and conversion spend, with platform cost the smallest part.

qa_highlights.question: Paisabazaar EBITDA and Tier 2/3 mix in online business?
qa_highlights.answer: Paisabazaar broke even on an operating basis in Q1 and is expected to be about half of the earlier ~₹100 Cr full-year number. Tier 2 and Tier 3 are 65-70% of direct business.

qa_highlights.question: Dark patterns and H2 growth base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denies deception in phone-number collection and said Q3 FY26 was above trend; aims to keep above-market growth. On AI, management said productivity gains may mean hiring less for the same business, while growth remains the goal.

qa_highlights.question: Expense ratio decline and call-centre cost classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Expenses excluding contribution fell to 58% of revenue from 61%; management said costs grew about 35% against 40% revenue growth and that efficiency drives have not started. All call-centre employee costs sit in employee benefit expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Savings business softness and reputation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says fresh savings grew over 20% and persistency is about 100 bps below its best; it said ULIPs are sold through verification calls and are low-cost.

544046|2026-06.headline: INOX India Q1 FY27 order inflow hit a record ~INR532 crore, lifting order book to ~INR1,686 crore; revenue of INR382 crore grew ~8.3% YoY, below management's own INR410-415 crore target.
544046|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 total income was INR382 crore (+8.3% YoY) and EBITDA INR90 crore (+1.4% YoY, 23.5% margin), with PAT flat at INR61 crore. Management attributed the revenue shortfall to INR32-35 crore of equipment ready for dispatch but held back due to freight rate spikes and ship availability issues. Order inflow was a record ~INR532 crore, driven by a large US space-sector cryogenic tank order, with the order book at INR1,686 crore, of which over INR1,140 crore is export. Management reiterated 18-20% FY27 revenue growth guidance and a 21-24% EBITDA margin range.

segments.name: Industrial Gas Solutions
segments.commentary: Won 8 large 1,500 cubic metre cryogenic storage tanks for a global space exploration customer plus 6 repeat tanks; also disposable cylinder repeat orders (crossed 2 million cylinders in FY26) and Cryoseal/liquid cylinder traction with capacity expansion. Semiconductor orders from Dholera were modest (~INR30 crore+ per management in Q&A).

segments.name: LNG Solutions
segments.commentary: Orders from Sabarmati Gas, Ultra Gas and BPCL for LNG fuelling stations and healthy LNG semi-trailer orders. Bahamas mini LNG terminal: first large tanks reached site, installation underway; two more orders for Eleuthera and Great Abaco. Cochin Shipyard marine LNG fuel tank execution continues.

segments.name: Cryo-Scientific Division
segments.commentary: Secured a CERN order for specialised cryogenic modules and another order from ITER France. Management said big LNG and CSD projects are delayed by customer issues and regulatory approvals, expected to materialise in one to two quarters.

segments.name: Beverage Kegs
segments.commentary: Orders from Heineken India, Hartwall Finland, ORBEN Germany and a UK brewery; RFQs from Asahi and CCU Chile. Keg capacity is 300,000 units and is under-utilised; management guides utilisation from ~30% to 50-60% by year-end.

segments.name: Aerospace (new)
segments.commentary: Received AS9100D certification, enabling onboard flight components beyond ground support equipment. Overall US private space order exposure is over INR1,000 crore; management said about INR400 crore of the current order book is aerospace.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20%; management reiterated this on the call, expecting dispatch delays to recover over Q2.
EBITDA margin guided at 21-24%; Q1 at 23.5% is within range.
Q1 revenue was targeted at INR410-415 crore; INR32-35 crore of ready equipment slipped out of the quarter.
Order inflow guidance of INR450-500 crore per quarter; management said it may be revised slightly upward given lumpy orders.
Kandla plant expected to start operations by December end or mid-January. Aerospace order execution to start in Q3/Q4 FY27, mainly completing in FY28.
Industrial gas non-aerospace growth expected around 15-18%. Domestic/export order mix to remain around 60:40.
US market entry not possible before 2028 due to non-compete agreement; preparation underway.

Kandla facility: civil work underway, PEB structures and major machines ordered; operations targeted for December end or mid-January.

Wayout water microfactory: first module design complete, 6-8 months of construction and testing planned.

Export order book over INR1,140 crore out of INR1,686 crore total order book.

Transformer tank business (GE orders) may be discontinued because it is carbon steel fabrication, outside core capability, despite better margins.
LNG demand improving as lower LNG prices widen the gap with diesel; PSU RFQs for about 20-25 fuelling stations.

qa_highlights.question: How much TAM does the new AS9100D certification add in aerospace, and what products?
qa_highlights.answer: Previously qualified only for ground equipment; now eligible to bid on flight projects. Targets include propellant tanks for rockets and an EoI for LVM3 manufacturing; the certification is the first eligibility criterion for flight equipment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18-20% growth guidance intact and is order inflow guidance being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth guidance of 18-20% is intact; order inflow guidance may move up slightly from INR450-500 crore given lumpy orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue below the 18-20% growth guided?
qa_highlights.answer: INR32-35 crore of ready equipment was held back due to logistics and freight issues; management said dispatches should stabilise over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the US private space order exposure and its execution profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall order from this customer is over INR1,000 crore; delivery target is end FY28, with percentage-of-completion revenue recognition in FY27 and dispatch-based in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: When will US market entry happen and what is the timeline for LNG and Cryo-Scientific bids?
qa_highlights.answer: US entry not possible before 2028 under the non-compete. Large LNG and CSD projects are delayed by customer and regulatory approvals; management expects them in one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the keg utilisation and breakeven status?
qa_highlights.answer: Keg plant has 300,000-unit capacity and is under-utilised; utilisation expected to rise from ~30% to 50-60% by year-end. No breakeven figure given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial timeline for the data centre cooling prototype?
qa_highlights.answer: Production line frozen; prototype development to start after consultant review. Commercialisation at least 1-1.5 years away.

financial_highlights.change: slightly below previous quarter; within 21-24% guided range

544862|2026-06.headline: Solex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.8% YoY to INR265.6 crore while PAT fell to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin) on higher depreciation and finance costs.
544862|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR265.6 crore, up 1.8% YoY from INR261 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR33.8 crore (12.7% margin vs 16.4%). Depreciation rose to INR10.2 crore and finance cost to INR12.5 crore, taking PAT to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin). Management attributed the weak quarter to seasonality, ALMM-2 (ALCM) timing shifts that delayed module off-take, and full-quarter costs of the 4 GW capacity, and reiterated FY27 guidance of a 5-6% PAT margin with an H2-weighted year. Management also flagged progress on a 2.2 GW cell line, with funding and land still pending.

543442|2026-06.headline: Brand Concepts Q1 FY27 revenue grew ~11% and EBITDA rose, but PBT loss widened; management expects growth to resume from October.
543442|2026-06.overview: Management said revenue grew almost 11% YoY and EBITDA grew on lower overheads, while the PBT loss widened marginally on higher depreciation, interest and operating investments. Primary billing took a dent from an e-commerce SKU realignment and channel consolidation, though secondary sales were said to be strong and market share was claimed to be intact. Retail tail-clipping continued: about 75-80% of the store consolidation is done, with completion targeted by September. The new hard-luggage and PP plants are ramping, with the PC unit at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption only.

segments.commentary: Management said luggage grew low single digits YoY in Q1; travel care overall was negative, driven by backpack SKU consolidation. Pricing pressure from new D2C entrants persists.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Primary billing hit by high-volume SKU realignment; management expects e-commerce to be back on track from August 2026. Secondary sales described as strong.

segments.name: Modern trade / EBO retail
segments.commentary: EBO business was about 10% of overall business. Multiple BAGLINE stores closed as unprofitable; nine further stores on notice per analyst question. Shoppers Stop secondary growth upwards of 12% per management.

segments.name: Tommy Hilfiger
segments.commentary: Overall flattish; volume down low single digits but ASP up. Licence renewal from international counterparty is pending paperwork; 10-year business plan and royalty terms said to be closed, royalty 'same'.

segments.name: Benetton
segments.commentary: Primary de-growth; earlier strategies failed. Management pivoting to a sharp-price e-commerce line and new offline styles launching next month, with CSD entry planned.

segments.name: New brands (Off-White, Superdry, Juicy)
segments.commentary: Off-White launched about April 2026 with Bangalore and Delhi stores; plan of five stores in total, four done. Superdry luggage not yet launched; Juicy FY26 revenue INR12 crore, FY27 target INR20-22 crore.

Management is not planning new Off-White stores beyond the five planned; Juicy to add a couple of stores then slow down over the next year.
capex_capacity: PC unit ~25,000 pieces/month capacity, at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption only; no external clients yet.
PP plant (one machine) trials complete, targeting 75-80% utilisation within about two months; moulds to arrive by end-September with production from October.
Combined ~50,000 pieces/month capacity; ~20,000 running now, ~40,000 targeted by October or November.

Management claims no market share lost at company level; some volume decline at Tommy Hilfiger offset by higher ASP.

Management said premium-end consumers remain resilient, citing top-selling INR27,000-32,000 luggage sets at Tommy Hilfiger.

qa_highlights.question: Tommy Hilfiger licence status and terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the international licence renewal is delayed but paperwork-only; the 10-year business plan, royalty and figures are closed, with royalty unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Manufacturing utilisation, benefit and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: PC at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption; PP ramping. Management said most of the plant margin benefit is being passed to consumers via pricing to stay relevant.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow, funding and capital plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is not a constraint; inventory fell ~INR5 crore, Q1 negative is temporary and INR20 crore promoter capital was committed (INR15 crore in). No new debt planned.

qa_highlights.question: When does consolidation end and when does growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation about 75-80% done; stores to exit by September, e-commerce reset this month, and growth expected back from October.

qa_highlights.question: Store closure impact and INR1,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reported figures are post-closures, EBO is ~10% of business, and the INR1,000 crore target over 4-5 years remains on track.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days and Benetton plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory INR123 crore at June-end, about 130 days per management. Benetton had failed strategies; pivoted to e-commerce price-led line and new offline styles next month.

532175|2026-06.headline: Cyient Q1 FY27: DET revenue $162.5M, down 0.5% QoQ in constant currency, while DET EBIT margin rose to 13.2% and the 15% target slipped to H1 FY28.
532175|2026-06.overview: DET revenue was flat-to-down in constant currency (-0.5% QoQ, -0.9% YoY) but rose 2.7% QoQ and 10.6% YoY in rupee terms. Normalized DET EBIT margin expanded to 13.2% (+79 bps QoQ, +114 bps YoY) on cost optimisation and a stronger USD. Management pushed out its 15% EBIT target from Q4 FY27 to around H1 FY28 because revenue ramp-up is lagging, and it said mid-single-digit FY27 growth is now hard to achieve. Group revenue was $219M (+4.5% QoQ, +9.1% YoY in constant currency), with Kinetic Technologies consolidated for the first time.

segments.commentary: Revenue $162.5M, -0.5% QoQ cc, with normalized EBIT margin of 13.2% (+79 bps QoQ). Transportation & mobility grew 3% QoQ and 14.8% YoY cc, while strategic units fell 8.2% QoQ on energy weakness.

segments.name: Cyient DLM
segments.commentary: Management said the quarter closed with its highest-ever order book and book-to-bill above 1.5, with double-digit EBITDA margins for four consecutive quarters. No DLM financial figures were given on the call.

segments.name: Semiconductor

qa_highlights.answer: Devices have not needed replacement; early 2017–18 installations are still running. The system is closed, so only Molbio cartridges and chips are used; each test consumes one cartridge or chip.

qa_highlights.question: What R&D and capex are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D at 5–6% of revenue; ₹72 crore automation and ~₹105 crore Bangalore R&D centre are the major capex items; no other major capex planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split and subsidiary profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Molbio standalone ~₹399 crore, Prognosys ~₹11 crore, OptraScan minimal. FY26 Prognosys revenue ₹154 crore, PAT ~₹12 crore; OptraScan loss ~₹9 crore in the period.

qa_highlights.question: Is device volume growing and how will the TB/other-disease mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Device sales expected in the 2,200–2,600 range, in line with history; kit volumes in Q1 were well above Q4 FY26. Non-TB assays such as HPV and hepatitis expected to contribute meaningfully over 2–3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TB market share sustainable and what is the realisation trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Truenat is the only WHO-endorsed battery-operated point-of-care TB test; remaining centres use microscopy. Pricing is contract-based; realisation moves reflect device mix and FX, with gross margin of 60–63%.

risks_watch: Quarterly lumpiness: management asks investors to track annually; Q1 was helped by export catch-up of Q4 FY26 deferrals linked to the Gulf situation.
OptraScan loss-making in FY27 and ramp dependent on US lab and hospital adoption after July 2026 FDA clearance.
HPV national-programme volumes and timing not yet quantified; next guidance deferred to next quarter.
Inventory days still high at 230 (trailing 12M), though down from 280 in March.
Export ramp slower than expected; past export volumes have been uneven.
Dependence on public-health TB programme for the bulk of domestic revenue under a two-year rate contract.

543308|2026-06.headline: KIMS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 1,180 crore, with EBITDA pre-Ind AS at INR 222 crore and debt cut to INR 2,570 crore.
543308|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total revenue of INR 1,196 crore (+36.1% YoY, +10.3% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 240 crore at a 20.1% margin, with PAT of INR 37 crore versus INR 85 crore a year earlier. Growth was driven by IP volumes (+26.6% YoY) and OP volumes (+28.5% YoY), with the Kondapur hospital commissioned in June and Palakkad (Kerala) opened. The QIP raised INR 1,500 crore, of which INR 1,100-1,125 crore repaid debt, and a INR 600 crore promoter preferential allotment is partly pending. Management guided Telangana to 30-35% margins over time, Kerala to 20-22% in two to three years, and Bengaluru to break-even for the full year, while several new units are still ramping up.

financial_highlights.change: +20.1% YoY, +10.9% QoQ; margin vs 20.27% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA pre-Ind AS excluding other income

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 85 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR 33 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,570 crore as of 30 June 2026; about INR 2,400 crore after early July repayments

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and equivalents (incl. liquid MF and deposits <12m)

segments.name: Telangana cluster (incl. Kondapur, Secunderabad)
segments.commentary: Management said revenue and EBITDA grew strongly YoY in Telangana and Andhra; Kondapur did INR 45 crore in July (first full month) against INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Telangana occupancy is about 61% on the adjusted bed base excluding Kondapur and 200 Secunderabad beds under renovation.

segments.name: Bengaluru cluster (Mahadevapura, Electronic City)
segments.commentary: Mahadevapura reached EBITDA break-even in June and did about INR 20 crore revenue in July; Electronic City expected to break even in about one to two quarters. Management aims for zero EBITDA for the cluster for FY27. Census-bed occupancy at Mahadevapura is about 40%.

segments.name: Maharashtra (Thane, Nashik, Nagpur)
segments.commentary: Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly revenue in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% EBITDA margin. Nashik reached EBITDA break-even in Q1; Nagpur did INR 30 crore revenue in July. Empanelment delays of four to five months weighed on Q1.

segments.name: Kerala
segments.commentary: Kerala margins are in the single digits currently, with management expecting mid-teens in FY28 and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Palakkad opened, taking Kerala to three units; one more hospital (Thrissur) is due in three to four months.

segments.name: Andhra Pradesh
segments.commentary: Management said AP remains strong. Q1 ARPOB growth slowed from prior quarters (Q4 FY26 about INR 27,000), which management attributed to seasonal case mix. Cancer services were added to most AP hospitals in the last two to three months.

guidance_outlook: Telangana EBITDA margin expected to return to 30-35% over time as new Kondapur and Secunderabad beds ramp up; management said 30% is achievable by FY30 without new beds, and 70% occupancy is targeted in three to four years.
Bengaluru cluster targeted at zero EBITDA for full FY27; Bengaluru ARPOB expected to settle at INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, versus about INR 90,000+ recently.
Kondapur full potential of about INR 100 crore revenue per month (about INR 1,200 crore a year) within four to five years; model margin around 30%, with 30-32% suggested for the next two years.
ARPOB growth guidance of 4-5% per year; management called 15-16% historical growth too aggressive to model.
Maintenance capex about INR 100 crore per year for three to four years; about INR 100-125 crore growth capex over the next nine months, including Rajahmundry construction (INR 60-75 crore in FY27).
Debt-equity intended to be kept around 2.5:1; surplus cash to go to greenfield and brownfield growth in core states. Minority interest about 10.5% currently, 10-15% longer term.
Empanelment with the remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, expected by end-August to mid-September 2026.
capex_capacity: Kondapur hospital commissioned in June 2026 (first patient 20 June); about 450-500 operational beds added in the last 10 days of Q1, and the old Kondapur hospital will run for about six more months with rent of about INR 90 lakh per month plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year of operating cost.

Palakkad (Kerala) opened in Q1; Thrissur to commence in three to four months; Electronic City and other Bengaluru beds added at Mahadevapura (operational beds up from about 170 to 210, total cluster 280 to 340).
Secunderabad: old 250-bed facility demolished; replacement facility expected by end of next year.

Two O&M agreements (Golden Lan Solutions, Sarvottam Healthcare) approved in draft: a 300-bed Telangana hospital near Kondapur with INR 90-95 crore monthly revenue potential, and a Kakinada hospital currently at INR 7-8 crore a month, targeting INR 15-20 crore. O&M means no losses borne by KIMS.
Future pipeline: greenfield in Karnataka (300-350 beds, expandable by about 100) and acquisitions in Maharashtra, Kerala, Telangana and Andhra; timing and bed count not committed.

538730|2026-06.headline: PDS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to ₹3,444 crore, EBITDA up 90% to ₹96 crore, and net debt fell 73% to ₹29 crore.
538730|2026-06.overview: PDS reported Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹3,444 crore (+15% YoY), with gross margin up 63 bps to 20% and EBITDA of ₹96 crore (margin 2.8%, +111 bps). PAT rose 43% YoY to ₹29 crore, though other income fell to ₹9 crore from ₹40 crore that included a ₹22 crore FX gain last year. Order book grew 23% YoY to ₹6,095 crore, and management announced new mandates with annual potential of about US$330 million. Net working capital fell to 1 day and net debt to ₹29 crore, with management stating a commitment to low single-digit working capital days.

financial_highlights.change: +8% YoY in INR; -2.4% YoY and -6.2% QoQ in USD
vs ₹40 crore in Q1 FY26 (which included ~₹22 crore FX gain)
+11% YoY in INR; flat in USD
down 73% from ₹105 crore at Mar-26; net debt/equity 0.02x, net debt/EBITDA 0.07x

segments.name: Sourcing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹3,272 crore (+16% YoY), EBIT ₹58 crore, EBIT margin 1.8%; the key contributor to the quarter.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹227 crore (+4% YoY), EBIT ₹15 crore, EBIT margin 6.5%; management aims to upgrade customer mix toward fashion customers via the Busana partnership.

segments.name: New verticals investment
segments.commentary: Investment of ₹37 crore in Q1 vs ₹41 crore last year (-8%); brand management investment down 38%, design-led sourcing down 5%, North America investment up on GSCL scale-up.

segments.name: Americas / Europe
segments.commentary: Americas revenue grew 48% YoY; Europe revenue grew 21%.

guidance_outlook: Management asked analysts to focus on Q2 repeating Q1 trend; will revisit guidance after mid-year.
Interest cost guided flat-to-down in USD terms, with early payment discounts (EPD) offsetting lower interest cost; more disclosure on EPD vs gross margin planned from Q2.
Working capital expected to stay at low single-digit days, possibly 0-1 days in some quarters.
Ted Baker losses for FY27 expected not to exceed US$2-3 million; Q1 loss approx US$2 million PBT.
Venture investment capped at under ₹10 crore a year (US$1-1.5 million).
Expect new sourcing-as-a-service contracts to ramp over 12-24 months; the French retailer contract has option value of US$300-400 million GMV within 2 years.
Management said the 555 target is still a long-term goal, with focus on sequential EBITDA margin and PAT improvement each quarter.
capex_capacity: Asset-light sourcing model used to add capacity; management said it could onboard 4-5 third-party factories within ~6 months for a large account, versus a US$50-60 million manufacturing investment otherwise.
Depreciation increase reflects Knit Gallery acquisition and capitalisation of UK office property.
Ongoing SAP upgrade to S/4HANA and AI/digital investment across sourcing, pricing, supply management and operations.
Sourcing-as-a-service GMV under execution in Q1 was ~₹1,700 crore; 600 partner factories cited across the platform.
Sourcing geography: >50% of sourcing from Bangladesh; expanding India (Knit Gallery) and exploring Egypt.
demand_pricing: New mandates from marquee customers with annual business potential ~US$330 million, with 3-4 year contract horizons.
Sourcing-as-a-service GMV of ~₹1,700 crore in Q1 generated ~₹42 crore revenue (~2.5% of GMV) and ~₹10 crore PBT (~25% of revenue).
US accounts reopened or added: Coles, Walmart, Fashion Nova, T.J. Maxx, PBS, American Eagle; management says 70-80% of key US accounts are now opened.
Europe: growth from Mango (Spain), CCC (Poland); Gerry Weber's bankruptcy replaced by new German accounts.
Marks & Spencer reportedly exploring a 50/50 in-house vs third-party sourcing split; opportunity cited at US$100 million (not yet confirmed as a contract).
Matalan account fell from ~US$140 million to ~US$70 million business, and Gerry Weber went bankrupt, creating a revenue hole management says is now being rebuilt.
New Lobster (brand management) revenue ~₹100 crore in Q1; other licensed brands ~₹350 crore annually (~₹90 crore per quarter) and profitable.

500148|2026-06.headline: UFlex Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 53,972 million and EBITDA rose 92% to Rs 9,198 million, with margin at 17%.
500148|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38% YoY to Rs 53,972 million and reported EBITDA rose 92% to Rs 9,198 million, with margin up 480 bps to 17%. Normalized EBITDA (after Rs 825 million forex derivative adjustment) was Rs 8,373 million, up 78%, at a 15.5% margin. Overseas operations (Egypt, Mexico, Nigeria) contributed about 91% of the Rs 4,410 million incremental EBITDA, while India volumes and Aseptic softened. Management guided to 35% growth in FY27 revenue and EBITDA over FY26, while saying Q2 would see some normalization from exceptional Q1 realizations.

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized EBITDA (post Rs 825 mn forex derivative adjustment)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 580 million, 1.5% margin in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Packaging Films (India)
segments.commentary: Volume 29,323 MT, up 9.1% QoQ but declined YoY against a high Q1 FY26 base affected by industry supply shortage. Converters resumed buying after May-June price normalization.

segments.name: Americas
segments.commentary: Volume 31,724 MT, up 18% YoY, supported by US onshoring push and constrained West Asia/India imports.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Volume 35,653 MT, flat YoY; low-priced imports pressured CPP, CIS BOPET steady. Demand expected to moderate next quarter on seasonal holidays.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa
segments.commentary: Volume 39,486 MT, up 14.9% YoY and 16.5% QoQ; Egypt led growth and Nigeria benefited from export opportunities as customers derisked supply chains.

segments.name: Packaging (Aseptic and flexible)
segments.commentary: Volume down 8.4% YoY to 37,285 MT due to shift to high-margin products in India, Aseptic softness from duty-free Indonesian imports, larger pack-size mix overseas and West Asia consignment delays.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of about 35% over FY26 (management also cited 30%-plus in places); management said it normally avoids guidance.
Q2 expected to see some normalization from exceptionally strong Q1 realizations; management asked investors to benchmark YoY, not QoQ.
Expects FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14%-plus; said margins could be better if geopolitical conditions hold.
Debt-EBITDA targeted at about 3x in FY28 and below 3x by FY29; interest cost expected to fall by about 1% over the next year.
Volume to roughly double over three years to FY29 as Egypt Aseptic, Noida recycling and Mexico WPP ramp; FY26-FY29 CAGR indicated at least 10%, to be confirmed by IR.

Egypt Aseptic (12 billion packs) expected commissioning in H1 FY27, targeting around 30% utilization in year one annualized (about 2 billion packs in FY27 if started 1 October) and 60-70% in year two.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex Rs 4,782 million: Egypt Aseptic Rs 1,236 mn, Mexico WPP bags Rs 205 mn, Noida Sector 155 recycling Rs 320 mn, Dharwad BOPP line Rs 215 mn.
Noida Sector 155 recycling plant (39,000 MT per annum) commissioned 30 April 2026; capex about USD 30-32 million, no further capex planned.
Mexico 80-million-unit WPP bags plant commissioned 31 July 2026; capex about USD 54 million.
Egypt Aseptic greenfield (12 billion packs): over USD 100 million spent, about USD 15 million remaining; commissioning H1 FY27.
Dharwad BOPP brownfield: USD 10 million spent, about USD 50+ million planned over FY27-FY28. Remaining new capex about USD 80-100 million; management says FY27 capex cycle about 75% complete.
Domestic utilization about 70-73%; specialty films (metallizer, ultra-high barrier) utilized about 30-40%. India Aseptic installed capacity about 24 billion packs.
demand_pricing: BOPP prices up about 25-32% and BOPET up about 30-35% from February 2026 (pre West Asia war) levels, per management.
Management said raw material prices rose but less than finished goods, and prices now appear to be normalizing; prices described as stable at current levels while the West Asia crisis persists.
Overseas selling prices said to be about 2.5x India prices; overseas margins higher because pass-through is easier.
Aseptic faces duty-free imports from Indonesia under India trade treaty at aggressive prices; management says value realization improved via shift to value-added films.
Management said it carries little inventory, so Q1 realizations were passed through to customers; customers prefer UFlex's integrated, local supply for security of supply.

qa_highlights.question: How are price realizations and raw material trends shaping up in India and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: BOPP prices up 25-32% and BOPET up 30-35% since February 2026; raw material costs rose less than finished goods prices, which are normalizing.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 margin and growth sustainable for full-year FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing 2-3 years of capex; FY27 guided to about 35% revenue and EBITDA growth over FY26, with FY27 EBITDA margin about 14%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalization expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined QoQ benchmarking; said Q2 will normalize from exceptional Q1 realization but growth remains about 35% YoY, with shipment timing risk around West Asia.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.5% normalized margin sustainable and how much currency impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex impact about Rs 70 crore in the quarter (Rs 825 mn per the prepared remarks); management said margins are sustainable over next 3 years, not just FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for surplus cash: debt reduction vs capex vs shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash to go to debt reduction; leverage to fall to about 3x in FY28. No buyback planned; management prefers wealth creation via growth. 60-70% of future capex to value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Interest rate and rating outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Rated AA by CRISIL and India Ratings; interest cost fell 0.3-0.4% this quarter and management targets a further 1% reduction in the next year.

532749|2026-06.headline: Allcargo Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.2% YoY to INR546 crores and PAT turned to a INR14 crore profit from a Q1 FY26 loss.
532749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR546 crores, up 11.2% YoY and 6.2% QoQ, with gross profit of INR163 crores (+11.6% YoY) and EBITDA of INR71 crores (+39.2% YoY). Express volumes grew 6.7% YoY to 312,000 tonnes and realisation per tonne rose 6.4%, with management attributing much of the yield gain to natural escalation from service-quality improvement and only about 20% to diesel pass-through. Consultative Logistics revenue grew 6.1% YoY on a stable 7.5 million sq ft of warehouse space under management. Management reiterated a 3-year plan targeting Express EBITDA margin of 10% and a company-level EBITDA margin of about 13% this year.

financial_highlights.change: Within 28%-29% range over Q4 and Q1 per CFO
Includes about INR8 crores one-off from lease closure; normal run-rate about INR5 crores

segments.name: Express Logistics
segments.commentary: Volumes up 6.7% YoY to 312,000 tonnes; realisation per tonne up 6.4%; revenue up 13.5% YoY. Gross margin 26.3% and EBITDA margin about 6.2%, against a 10% three-year target.

segments.name: Consultative Logistics
segments.commentary: Warehouse space under management stable at 7.5 million sq ft; revenue up 6.1% YoY and 6.3% QoQ. Revenue per sq ft up 3%; EBITDA margin about 29.56%; customer retention 98%.

guidance_outlook: Company-level EBITDA margin expected around 13% for FY27, implying about 1 percentage point annual improvement over three years (confirmed by CFO).
Express EBITDA margin trajectory: 7.5% targeted this year and 10% in the three-year plan; management said it is 'inching up' from 6.2%.
Pre-Ind AS operating PBT margin guided to 5%-6% this year and to improve thereafter.
Growth ambition: grow 1 percentage point above logistics industry growth; industry estimated at low double digits (1.2x-1.5x GDP of 6%-7%).
Price realisation actions expected to continue into Q2 FY27, with diesel pass-through impact seen fully from Q2.
Consultative Logistics revenue to grow slightly faster than Express, per management.
Capex: INR10-15 crores for Express infrastructure improvements; about INR20 crores additional capex for Consultative Logistics this year.
capex_capacity: Express: constant infrastructure improvements of INR10-15 crores; hubs described as well capitalised.
Consultative Logistics: about INR20 crores additional capex this year, tied to new business and warehouse additions.
Warehouse space under management at 7.5 million sq ft in Q1 FY27 (about 8 million sq ft earlier in the year per Q&A); two large warehouses were consolidated to reduce white space.
Express fleet and network: about 95% road and 5% air; capacity utilisation and lane planning cited as cost levers.
demand_pricing: Express realisation up 6.4% YoY; management attributes most (about 80%) to natural escalation from service-level improvement and about 20% to diesel pass-through, with DPH mechanism passed through since June.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage hikes is passed through in CL and Express contracts; annual GPI exercise applied.
Express KEA share about 60%-63% of revenue, retail about 20%, strategic balance; reclassification prevents direct comparison with earlier 80:20 split.
E-commerce and quick commerce: CL runs sort and fulfilment centres for majors; Express does not do last-mile for e-commerce.
Industry view: Express industry growth low double digits; shift from unorganised to organised players cited as a driver.
Q1 FY27 macro indicators cited: June e-way bills about 137 million (+14.5% YoY), GST collections near INR2 lakh crores (+14%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Express EBITDA margin and what are the levers to expand it?
qa_highlights.answer: Express EBITDA margin about 6.2% vs CL at 29.56%, giving the blended 13%. Yield enhancement is the main lever; cost and operating efficiency add further. Three-year target is 10%, with 7.5% targeted this year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 24-month priorities and capital allocation policy after the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth 1 percentage point above industry, with margin improvement across gross, EBITDA and PAT. Express is well capitalised (INR10-15 crores capex); CL needs about INR20 crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Express gross margin base change versus earlier disclosures?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 figures reflected pre-merger Allcargo Gati numbers. Post the merger effective 1 November, prior quarters were recast to include CL aggregation, so the margin trajectory is around 30% from Q3 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation increase is diesel versus natural escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split the 6.3%-6.4% number precisely; roughly 80% natural escalation and 20% diesel pass-through. Diesel pass-through effective June, with full impact in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why has CL warehouse space declined over the last three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes are not impacted; two large warehouses were actioned to reduce white space, lowering cost without affecting revenue capability.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company focus more on CL given its margin and EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both businesses get focus; CL revenue growth will be slightly faster than Express while balancing profitability of both.

risks_watch: Diesel and labour cost inflation: pass-through lags may compress margins in Q2 before full recovery.
Express EBITDA margin at about 6.2% remains far below the 10% three-year target; progress must be tracked quarterly.
Q1 PAT of INR14 crores includes about INR8 crores of one-off lease-closure income; underlying profit is lower.
CL warehouse area under management fell from about 8.4 million sq ft three quarters ago to 7.5 million sq ft; monitor volume impact.
Pre-Ind AS operating PBT margin of about 2.7% (per analyst) needs to reach 5%-6% this year.
Segment disclosure: analysts requested air/surface split and pre- vs post-Ind AS EBITDA bridge; not provided on the call. KEA classification changed, so historic comparisons are limited.
532749|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on volume, pricing and CL retention, with a clear 3-year margin plan. Evasive on the KEA/strategic reclassification and on the exact diesel versus natural-escalation split, and it did not provide a segment EBITDA bridge.

517498|2026-06.headline: Websol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 70% YoY to INR373 crore and PAT grew 16% to INR78 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 34% from 47% on module mix.
517498|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR373 crore, up 70% YoY and down about 7% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR126 crore (+21% YoY, margin 34% vs 47%) and PAT of INR78 crore (+16%). Cell output rose to 259 MW (92% utilisation) and module output to 103 MW (81% utilisation), with module volume doubling and driving the margin dilution. The company repaid the INR110 crore IREDA term loan on 4 August from internal accruals, with promoter pledge set to fall from 80% to 16% of promoter holding once released. Phase 3 expansion is being relocated from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, with land approval awaited; management says capex, cost and timelines are unchanged.

segments.name: Solar cells
segments.commentary: Production 259 MW vs 126 MW in Q1 FY26, utilisation 92%; average cell efficiency 23.3%. About 153 MW sold externally in Q1, with the rest consumed captively for modules.

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: Production 103 MW vs 50 MW, utilisation 81% vs 39%. Module margins are lower than cell margins, and module-led mix is the main driver of the margin decline.

guidance_outlook: Cell utilisation of about 92% to be held; management expects close to full run-rate utilisation across lines except TOPCon upgrade downtime.

TOPCon upgrade of 600 MW mono PERC line to 750 MW TOPCon, lifting total cell capacity to 1.3 GW (about 55% TOPCon), expected by March 2027 at about INR270 crore, funded from internal accruals with possible debt.
Management expects payback of 2 to 3 years on the TOPCon capex; cell efficiency expected around 25% post-upgrade.

Phase 3 (4 GW total, cell and module, two phases of 2 GW each): land approval expected in August; construction targeted mid-September; equipment lead time 4 to 6 months; trial run after about 2 months post installation; management says no change in timelines or capex.
Margins: management expects cell margins to fall somewhat but not aggressively, and believes current margin levels can hold for a year or two.
Silver consumption cut 20% in FY26, with a further 10% reduction target for cells.
capex_capacity: Current capacity: cells about 1.2 GW pre-upgrade, rising to 1.35 GW (per management, with 750 MW TOPCon) after the TOPCon upgrade; the upgrade adds about 150 MW of cell capacity.

Phase 3: 4 GW of additional cell and 4 GW of module capacity in two 2 GW phases; location moved from Andhra Pradesh (Naidupeta) to West Bengal (land shortlisted near Falta facility, approval pending).
Expected timeline: land approval in August 2026, construction from mid-September, equipment ordered around December, arrival April to May 2027, about 9 months to complete, then 2 months of trials.
Module utilisation of 81% described as close to full effective utilisation; industry comfort range cited at 70-75%.
demand_pricing: Prices softened in the previous quarter; management says prices rose in the current quarter on ALMM-related expectations, but the ALMM cell mandate was deferred from June to December 2026.
Current cell price quoted at about USD0.13 per Wp and module at about INR21 per watt, against Q1 levels of about USD0.125 and INR20.50.

Demand is mainly DCR (PM-Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM); management sees no decline. Inventory rose about 7% QoQ and management attributes it to monsoon-season offtake slowdown and captive cell blocking in modules.
Input costs: silver prices have eased but imported paste carries a lag; wafer prices are flat. The West Asia conflict has raised BOM costs for modules, not cells.
Management said Q1 margin decline reflects lower cell prices and higher silver and BOM cost, alongside mix shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company moving Phase 3 from Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal, and does it change timelines and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited synergies in skilled manpower, supply chain and infrastructure, with no change to capex, project cost, funding or timelines; no financial outflow had occurred on the AP land.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trend and is margin pressure expected to persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to module-heavy mix plus lower cell prices and higher silver/BOM costs; it expects cell margins to fall but not aggressively and to hold current levels for a year or two.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory rising, and what were Q1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose about 7% QoQ, which management attributed to monsoon-led offtake slowdown and cell cost blocked in modules; Q1 realisations were about USD0.125/Wp for cells and INR20.50/W for modules.

qa_highlights.question: What returns does the TOPCon upgrade generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects incremental revenue from higher Wp per cell (7.6-7.7 Wp for PERC to about 9.5 Wp for TOPCon), higher capacity (600 MW to 750 MW) and a price premium; it expects a 2-3 year payback on the INR270 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company targeting a larger order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book reports only firm purchase orders and repeat business, and the company is not targeting a higher order book; it sees regular DCR-market inquiries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ability to execute and ramp Phase 3 at the same pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TOPCon conversion will serve as practical training before the greenfield expansion; it cited the mono PERC installation timeline as precedent.

risks_watch: Margin compression as module mix rises: EBITDA margin fell 13 percentage points YoY to 34%, and management expects further cell margin softening.
Phase 3 execution: relocation to West Bengal depends on pending land approval (targeted August 2026); no incentive terms disclosed yet.
Inventory build (about 7% QoQ) and monsoon-season offtake; watch whether it clears in Q2.
ALMM cell mandate deferred to December 2026 and dependence on domestic cell capacity; price direction after that date.
Investor-communication concerns raised by several participants (valuation, share-price moves, lack of disclosure). The company said it is increasing investor interactions.

544240|2026-06.headline: Raymond Lifestyle Q1 FY27 total income rose 6% to INR1,560 crore, EBITDA up 11% to INR135 crore at 8.6% margin, net cash surplus INR154 crore.
544240|2026-06.overview: Total income grew 6% YoY to INR1,560 crore and EBITDA rose 11% to INR135 crore, with margin up 40 bps to 8.6%. Garmenting was the standout, with revenue up 50% to INR296 crore and EBITDA turning positive at INR22 crore. Branded Apparel grew only 4% and Branded Textiles fell about 2%, mainly on base effects and adverse channel and product mix. Management called FY27 a year of consolidation, with net store closures continuing for two to three more quarters, and said Q1 was ahead of budget.

-15 days vs 90 days in Q1 FY26
Attributed to business mix shift toward lower-margin garmenting

segments.name: Branded Textiles

segments.name: Branded Apparel (four core brands)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR349 crore, +4% YoY, with LFS and e-commerce growing high double digits (LFS above 25%); EBITDA INR18 crore, margin 5.1% on adverse channel mix.

segments.name: Garmenting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR296 crore vs INR197 crore, +50% YoY on US tariff rationalisation and new UK/EU clients; EBITDA INR22 crore vs negative INR8 crore, margin 7.3% vs -4.1%.

segments.name: High Value Cotton Shirting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR195 crore vs INR205 crore YoY on base effect; EBITDA steady at INR19 crore, margin 9.7% vs 9.1%.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR79 crore, +9% YoY; now reported as a standalone segment after reclassification. Ethnix net stores down 17 in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management is bullish on FY27 and said Q1 is ahead of budget phasing and ahead of last year; Q2 described as decent.
Garmenting capacity is full through December; orders booked from January onwards. Management said no risk to margins on cost-plus contracts, though changes in Sep-Oct could affect pricing.
Price hikes to start in Q2: management estimates 5-7% in apparel and 7-9% in fabric, calibrated against volumes.

Medium term: aim to at least double turnover in five years and grow EBITDA faster than revenue, before any Kearney-led transformation outcomes. Mid-teens ROCE described as the endeavour, not a target. Garmenting EBITDA double-digit described as an endeavour with no firm timeline.
Net branded EBO openings to be negative in FY27; EBO closures expected to take another 2-3 quarters.
capex_capacity: Garmenting: five factories (three in Karnataka, one new in Andhra Pradesh, one in Ethiopia); no spare capacity until December per management. Company has 11 factories in total.
Active network 1,627 stores across 600 cities. Since June 2025, 133 stores exited and 85 opened.

Ethnix plan: shift sherwanis and bandhgalas above INR50,000 to made-to-measure; basic kurtas to be sold through TRS and e-commerce; high-impact flagship stores in wedding areas.

qa_highlights.question: Input cost pressure in fabric and textiles, and how price hikes or inventory efficiency will offset it?

qa_highlights.question: Garmenting outlook and whether contracts allow pass-through of RM costs?

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation rise of about 25%?

qa_highlights.question: Store rationalisation timeline and Ethnix store additions?

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term revenue, margin and ROCE targets?

qa_highlights.question: Which brands drive casualisation, and what are the branded apparel and export order trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Branded apparel grew 4% due to EBO closures, with e-commerce and LFS growing high double digits. Order books span Europe, US, Japan, Korea and Asia. Management said FY28 is not being looked at closely.

543415|2026-06.headline: Anand Rathi Wealth Q1 FY27 underlying PAT rose 24% YoY to INR116 crore, with AUM up 21% to INR1,06,300 crore.
543415|2026-06.overview: Management reported its 19th consecutive quarter of profit growth, with underlying consolidated revenue (excluding fair value gains, ESOP and related tax) up 18% YoY to INR336 crore and PAT up 24% to INR116 crore, a 34.4% margin. Reported revenue and PAT including fair value gains were INR430 crore and INR163 crore, with INR96 crore of the other income being mark-to-market gain on the Anand Rathi Global Finance (ARGFL) holding. Net flows were INR2,743 crore in the quarter, and client attrition was 0.09% of AUM with zero RM attrition. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,415 crore revenue and INR460 crore PAT, with Q1 delivering 24% and 25% of these respectively. The call also covered a Board approval to apply for an AMC licence, a UK subsidiary, and a GIFT City licence in progress.

segments.name: Flagship wealth management (ARWL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,06,300 crore, 13,941 client families after net addition of 1,600+ in last 12 months; client AUM attrition 0.09% in Q1 and zero RM attrition. AUM per RM described as rising, with 33 clients per RM.

segments.name: Digital wealth (B2B2C subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,526 crore, up 23% YoY; clients up 16% to 7,320.

segments.name: OFA (SaaS platform subsidiary)
segments.commentary: 6,890 subscribers and platform assets of INR1.66 lakh crore as of 30 June 2026.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Net equity MF sales of INR1,900 crore in Q1. Management cites FY26 market share of net flows at 2.3% (presented as 2.47%), up from 0.18% in FY19-20; distributor yield about 1.09% post-GST, with 1-3 bps possible pressure from TER changes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,415 crore and PAT guidance of INR460 crore reiterated; Q1 achieved 24% and 25% respectively.
Management modelled AUM growth of 20-25% p.a. over next 3 years: 10-12% from mark-to-market plus net sales of INR1,100-1,200 crore per month (about 1% of AUM per month).
Long-term target of about 4% share of AMFI Category II assets (around INR6 lakh crore in ~8-10 years), requiring 22-23% asset growth.
Board approved applying for an AMC licence; GIFT City licence in process (second stage underway).
capex_capacity: Board approved AMC licence application; first stage of licensing done, second stage in process per management.
UK subsidiary operations started in Q1; management said it would be built brick-by-brick, not scaled quickly.
Management cites capacity for about 6,500 new client families with existing RMs (33 clients per RM against capacity of ~50), plus 490 trained RMs and 100 more RMs about 60% ready.
Fund of funds in UK with 11 schemes listed there for UK participants.
demand_pricing: Net flows of INR2,743 crore in Q1 despite volatile markets; equity MF net sales INR1,900 crore.

Platinum families (INR50 crore+ bucket) about 230 vs 211 earlier; target 450-500 in two years. Upgrade rate from sub-INR5 crore to INR50 crore cohort guided at roughly 10-20% per quarter (management estimate).
Model portfolio of 14 mutual fund schemes beat Nifty by about 6% in Q1 (Nifty about 7%, portfolio about 7% after costs per management; figures as stated).

Structured products: management says ARGFL products dominate the mix; third-party share kept low for credit risk. Q1 MLD primary issuance INR2,187 crore (INR1,875 crore to group companies, INR312 crore third party), up from INR1,704 crore; secondary INR968 crore vs INR755 crore.
Client retention on three RM departures to a competitor: about 90% of INR758 crore assets retained as of June end (INR658.5 crore), excluding market movement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 update on Platinum families and how fast will the INR5-50 crore bucket upgrade?
qa_highlights.answer: Platinum families are about 230 vs 211 earlier, from 40-45 at launch about 2.5 years ago; upgrade rate estimated at 10-20% a quarter; management expects four-digit client counts in a few years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cap on AUM per RM?
qa_highlights.answer: No cap; management says AUM per RM should keep rising while client attrition stays low (0.09%), and some RMs have reached INR500-1,500 crore. The figure was INR100 crore at listing.

qa_highlights.question: How is asset allocation managed in volatile markets and why not recommend gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the highest portfolio beta is 0.6-0.65 and it sells products it buys; it does not recommend gold given household gold holdings of about 28% of savings. Overall mix is about INR55,000 crore equity and INR4,500 crore debt plus structured products.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the other income of INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: INR96 crore is mark-to-market gain on ARGFL holding, revalued semi-annually by a third-party investment banker; the rest is interest on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is there yield pressure from TER changes in mutual funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through is limited to 1-3 bps of its roughly 1.09% post-GST yield, and scale gives bargaining power; it has no plans to recommend stocks, PMS or long-only AIFs currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARWL enter investment banking or other capital market businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will pursue only an AMC licence and no investment banking, focusing on intergenerational wealth rather than transaction-driven capital management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM growth plan and how is it sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% AUM growth from embedded client returns, capacity in existing RMs, new RMs and penetration, citing 90-95% confidence; the 4% Category II target implies 22-23% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI bank guarantee circular on derivatives volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views the circular as positive, expecting reduced high-frequency trading volumes, and sees negligible or positive impact on ARWL.

503101|2026-06.headline: Marathon Nextgen Q1 FY27 total income hit INR 217 crores, a multi-quarter high, with PAT of INR 52 crores and INR 900 crores of new redevelopment GDV added.
503101|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 217 crores (multi-quarter high), EBITDA of INR 66 crores and PAT of INR 52 crores. Sales on the existing portfolio were 38,000 sq ft with booking value of INR 86 crores and collections of INR 118 crores (MNRL's 40% share of Monte South); including the merged portfolio, sales were 46,000 sq ft, booking value INR 108 crores and collections INR 146 crores. Two redevelopment projects (Versova and Sewri, INR 450 crores GDV each) were added, and the company says it is debt-free with about INR 200 crores of acquisition capital after a INR 900 crore QIP. The merger with group entities is awaiting NCLT shareholder and creditor meetings in early September 2026.

segments.name: Monte South (Byculla, JV, 40% stake)

segments.name: Marathon Nexzone (Panvel)

segments.commentary: Futurex combined sales ~4,000 sq ft, booking INR 19 crores, collections INR 23 crores; Futurex has OC. Millennium sold over 1,000 sq ft, booking INR 3 crores, collections INR 1 crore; under construction.

segments.commentary: Started after Kanjurmarg land acquisition in Q4 FY26, focused on Bhandup; no presales yet, but management expects some in coming quarters.

Collections this year expected to be on the heavier side, supported by ready-to-move inventory (about 3-month TAT on sales at Futurex and Monte South) and percentage-completion receipts.
Surplus capital of about INR 200 crores expected to be fully deployed into new projects this FY27.
Target EBITDA margin of 30-35% for project acquisitions.

Merger: shareholder and creditor meetings planned for first week of September 2026, followed by a second NCLT hearing; completion timing uncertain, dependent on NCLT dates (management said it was not sure whether it would complete by December).
