Existing portfolio estimated unsold GDV ~INR 8,000 crores.
Redevelopment additions: Versova (via subsidiary Sunset Spaces, ~1.5 acres, GDV >INR 450 crores, first society redevelopment) and Sewri (cluster redevelopment JDA, ~7,500 sq m, GDV ~INR 450 crores).
Merger to bring over 400 acres of land, several ongoing projects and ready inventory at Futurex into the listed entity.
Panvel-Karjat corridor deadline cited as December 2026; Monte South commercial to launch ~5 minutes from Futurex.
demand_pricing: Management cited strong demand at Monte South (footfalls up sharply), commercial space (limited Grade A supply near Futurex), and newly launched Bhandup and Panvel phases.
Ready-to-move inventory at Monte South Towers A and B is sold at a premium, per management.
Redevelopment selection: prime locations and strict financial metrics; management said it avoids high-premium deals that may get stuck.
PTC demand from neighbouring redevelopment projects in Bhandup; area serves western suburbs (around Malad, P-South ward), Mulund, Ghatkopar and parts of Chembur.

qa_highlights.question: What are the launch timelines for the INR 900 crore redevelopment GDV, and how much more can be added in 12-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two new projects (Sewri and Versova, INR 450 crores each) add INR 900 crores in the quarter; no launch timeline or further 12-24 month addition was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 business outlook and which projects will drive acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers but said the outlook is positive and better than last year, citing Monte South, commercial, and new Bhandup and Panvel phases, with bookings flowing in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections trend over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ready-to-move sales at Futurex and Monte South convert to collections in about 3 months; Monte South Tower C is at the 28th slab, with about 40% collection on that basis. Collections expected to be heavier this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A Futurex investment-property floor was not sold in the quarter, so no rental/sale income was recognised from it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the amalgamation complete by December 2026 or slip into 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder and stakeholder meetings are planned for early September, followed by a second NCLT hearing; management said it is not sure of the timeline because NCLT benches are heavily loaded.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the redevelopment pipeline beyond INR 900 crores, and how are deals selected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Mumbai redevelopment opportunity is very large; selection focuses on prime locations and strict margin thresholds, and it avoids over-priced deals that can stall.

qa_highlights.question: How much capital will be deployed in FY27 and what return thresholds apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Target EBITDA margin 30-35% on acquisitions; about INR 200 crores of surplus capital to be fully deployed this FY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PTC vertical's pipeline and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PTC business started after the Q4 FY26 Kanjurmarg land acquisition; strong demand from neighbouring redevelopments; presales may start in next few quarters.

financial_highlights.change: Futurex investment-property floor not sold in quarter

539400|2026-06.headline: Mallcom Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 25% QoQ to Rs 110 crore, while EBITDA margin rose 317 bps to 12.51% on pricing and raw material relief.
539400|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was Rs 110 crore, down 25% QoQ, driven by weaker international sales and West Asia disruption. EBITDA held flat QoQ at Rs 14 crore, with margin up to 12.51%, and PAT rose 5% QoQ to Rs 7 crore (6.03% margin). Domestic revenue of Rs 64 crore grew 10% QoQ and was the highest-ever Q1 domestic number; international revenue was Rs 46 crore. Management said port congestion and weak Western demand cost the company a targeted double-digit export growth.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 64 crore, up 10% QoQ and the highest Q1 domestic revenue to date; brand recall and the SMILE reseller programme (over 1,000 resellers) cited as drivers.

segments.name: International / Export
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 46 crore, down sharply QoQ on weak Western demand and port congestion; management says exports are about 55% of the mix. Europe is down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1 against about Rs 170 crore for last year.

segments.name: Sanand plant
segments.commentary: Three lines now operating (helmets, foam caps, nasal caps); FY26 revenue about Rs 5 crore (Q4 only); FY27 minimum target Rs 40 crore, described as on track.

guidance_outlook: Management will not revise the Rs 1,000 crore revenue ambition for FY28, calling it a stretch but still a goal.
Top-line guidance of about 10-12% growth maintained; management hopes to reach the Rs 600 crore level for the year.
Export and domestic mix expected to approach 50:50 by year end, which management called realistic.
Aim to return to the regular margin profile, helped by price pass-through and Sanand efficiency.
Europe expected to grow YoY this year, with a target to recover the lost sales over the next three quarters; the India-EU FTA effect is seen mainly from next year.
Working capital borrowings expected flat through the year; term loans taken for Sanand capex and incentives.
capex_capacity: Sanand plant: three lines operating; helmet, foam cap and nasal cap production underway; management looking to add further capacity.
New EN812 certified bump cap mould launched and manufacturing started at Sanand.
Ongoing machinery capex to add capacity (no new building or land spend), per CFO.
Newer Gujarat investments aimed mainly at domestic and branded markets, with some export; large export contracts not expected quickly.
demand_pricing: Export demand weak in the West; management attributes part of the export shortfall to port congestion and containers stuck at sea.
Roughly 60-70% of export sales are planned and 30% spot/L1-priced (about 30% of export is commoditised).
Raw material prices remain elevated vs pre-West Asia levels for crude-linked products; some easing seen versus March-April.
Price pass-through: own-brand pricing adjusted from the start of the crisis; white-label contracts lag and will be recovered over the rest of the year.
No FX gain in the quarter; the company says costs are largely hedged.
New FR workwear (EN/US certified) launched for own brand and white label; value-added products cited at about 60-70% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Are raw material prices trending and how should margins move?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude-linked products remain at escalated levels versus pre-war; overall RM costs are higher than at start of calendar year, with some easing. Pass-through is gradual because of long-term fixed-price contracts.

qa_highlights.question: How much export growth was lost and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both weak Western demand and port congestion. The company had targeted at least double-digit export growth, which it missed this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a margin base now and what about under-recovery and FX?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a base and the aim is to grow from here. CFO said there is no under-recovery after the price increases taken at the start of the quarter, and no FX gain as costs are hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its Rs 1,000 crore target for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not revise the target now, calling it a stretch, and levers include capacity, distribution, new geographies, FTAs and larger contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Sanand revenue target and new lines?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: minimum FY27 target of Rs 40 crore, on track after Q1. FY26 was about Rs 5 crore. Three lines are operating; more capacity is being considered.

qa_highlights.question: Have any large LATAM or US export contracts been won?
qa_highlights.answer: Some long-term contracts exist for workwear and footwear. Large new contracts are not expected quickly; US demand is uncertain due to tariffs.

risks_watch: Export demand in Europe and LATAM remains weak; Europe was down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1.
White-label price pass-through lags, so margin recovery depends on contract renewals within the year.
US tariff uncertainty and importer hesitation; no large US contract yet.
Port congestion and container availability disrupting shipments and Middle East supply.
Revenue must rise to earn back the fixed-cost absorption lost in Q1 (lower turnover).
539400|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and domestic execution, but cautious and somewhat defensive on exports, US and the Rs 1,000 crore target. Management stressed that volatility and logistics, not strategy, drove the export shortfall.
key_quotes: Despite the challenging and volatile market environment during the quarter, we delivered a meaningful improvement in profitability supported by lower raw material cost, improved operational efficiency at our Sanand plant, and our continued ability to pass on cost increases to our customers.
So, there is no FOREX gain because in our case, mostly we are hedged.
So, whatever cost increase was there, we have been able to pass on this to the customer, and we took this exercise at the beginning of the quarter itself.

Direct clients' share of revenue fell to 65.2% from 73.9% in FY26, which management attributed to the agency/reseller route used for international expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +56.9% YoY; +16.3% QoQ (Q1 FY26 Rs 464 mn; Q4 FY26 Rs 626 mn)
+77% YoY (from Rs 87 mn); +15.8% QoQ (from Rs 133 mn)

segments.commentary: Contributed 65.2% of Q1 revenue, down from 73.9% in FY26. Management said the decline reflects the agency/reseller route used for international entry and expects the direct share to recover over the long term.

segments.name: Agency, reseller and platform channels
segments.commentary: Make up the remaining ~34.8% of revenue. Management cited agency and reseller models as an accelerator for international growth.

segments.commentary: Contributed 20.7% of revenue, with India as the anchor. Markets referenced include UK (first entered, ramping fastest), Latin America, Philippines, Singapore and US; management expects international share to build gradually over coming years.

segments.commentary: Newly launched in Q1 for Apple Search Ads, custom product pages and ASO; management said revenue contribution is negligible today and it will start in India.

Expects growth drivers from new geographies and products (US, UK, Apple ecosystem, emerging markets) to become meaningful in the next 12 to 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What moat protects the Neural Engine from global platforms replicating it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it owns the full stack across all three P3 layers and that proprietary consented signals feed a closed feedback loop, with pricing linked to outcomes. It pointed to rising revenue per outcome as evidence.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is 56.9% growth, and what would normalise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it optimises for full-year performance and targets 30% growth and 20% EBITDA margin over the long term. It said quarter-to-quarter variation is expected as international markets scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 56.9% growth: market or share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said general market growth cannot explain 56.9%. It attributed growth to international markets (UK first, then LatAm, Philippines, US, Singapore) and premium inventory such as streaming, CTV, Apple ecosystem and DOOH.

qa_highlights.question: What is PiiX's revenue contribution and size of opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PiiX revenue is negligible today. It cited Apple's Indian reach at about 6% growing to 8-10%, and said the product will start in India before going international.

qa_highlights.question: How will the preferential raise proceeds be allocated, and what are the key risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are mainly for strategic acquisitions with disciplined selection, plus technology investment. Named risks were regulation, currency (revenue balanced between INR and USD), AI disruption and inflation; no near-term inflation impact was seen.

risks_watch: Shift in revenue mix toward agency/reseller channels (direct share down to 65.2% from 73.9%) and its effect on margins.
International execution in US, UK, Singapore and Philippines, which management says drives a large share of growth but is still early.
Regulatory risk, which management named as the primary risk; also currency risk and AI disruption.
Client concentration: top-5 sectors contribute about 70-80% of revenue, and top-5/top-10 client shares were not disclosed.
Deployment of the FY26 preferential raise into acquisitions, which management has not yet named.
539682|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability; the tone was more qualitative when answering questions on client concentration, the scale of PiiX revenue and the acquisition pipeline, where few figures were given.

544256|2026-06.headline: PNG Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, with EBITDA up 57% to INR192.4 crore and PAT up 52% to INR105.3 crore.
544256|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, driven by retail (up 56%, with 46% SSSG), franchise (up 8%) and e-commerce (up 20%). EBITDA margin expanded 80 bps to 8.0% and PAT margin rose 40 bps to 4.4%, with gross margin flat at 13.2% reported. Management kept FY27 guidance (around 25 store additions to 103 stores, about 7% EBITDA margin, about INR400 crore other expenses) and flagged that Q1 other expenses were low due to cuts in marketing and no store launches. Hedging gains and lower other income were discussed in detail, and the promoter stake and franchise economics drew scrutiny.

financial_highlights.change: Reported gross margin flat YoY; adjusted ex-hedging up ~40-50 bps per CFO
vs ~INR12 crore in Q4 FY26 (analyst cited INR31 crore, CFO disputed); lower FD balances on mortgage

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Grew 56% with 46% SSSG; now about 78% of total revenue, with jewellery about 78-79% of retail and bars/coins about 20-21%. Newer North and Central India stores run 15-18% studded ratios.

segments.name: Franchise
segments.commentary: Grew 8% YoY; management attributed the slowdown to B2B billing timing and stock replenishment, with franchise openings expected to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle planned).

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Grew 20% YoY; company is deliberately shifting mix towards jewellery and away from bars/coins, so management expects better margins but slower total sales growth.

segments.name: Litestyle by PNG
segments.commentary: Studded ratio 32.9% in Q1; current litestyle gross margin of about 18-20%, with management targeting about 50% studded ratio in two years and 30-35% margin later.

guidance_outlook: Open around 25 stores in FY27, taking network to about 103 by March 2027 (63 COCO, balance FOCO); a few launches in Q2, bulk in Q3-Q4.
Network targets: about 140 stores by March 2028 and about 177 by March 2029 (about 113 legacy and 64 litestyle; about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO by March 2029).
EBITDA margin guidance of about 7% for full year FY27; other expenses about 3% of sales or roughly INR400 crore for FY27.
PAT margin underlying (ex-hedging gains) targeted at 4.1-4.25% in FY27 per CFO, versus 4.2% per CEO; 4.5-4.7% by FY29.
Hedging coverage to reach about 80% around Q3 FY27 (Q2 around 80% per CEO), and fully hedged in FY28; currently 70%+.
Gold metal loan of INR1,500-1,550 crore to be reduced by INR500-600 crore by FY29, non-GML borrowing about INR1,200 crore; targeted debt-free in four to five years.
Gross margin guidance for retail mix of 13-14% (CFO: 12.5-13.5% at 10-11% studded ratio), including hedging gains shown separately.
capex_capacity: Store count 78 at end-Q1 FY27 (57 COCO, 21 FOCO).
FY27 plan: 25 new stores, bulk in Q3 and Q4, franchise-led; deepening Maharashtra and expanding UP, Bihar, Central India and NCR.
UP stores running 18%+ studded versus 15% projection; 8-10 UP franchise openings planned in FY27; Ayodhya store opening soon.
Capital allocation focused on store expansion, franchise network, digital and operational excellence, funded from internal accruals.
Management plans a QIP at a suitable time to reduce promoter holding (above 75%); board enabling resolution already in place.
demand_pricing: Management said demand held up through April-June despite record gold prices, supported by weddings and Akshaya Tritiya; Adhik Maas was muted due to high silver prices.
Weddings postponed by Adhik Maas expected to benefit Q2 and a large part of Q3.
Customers shifting towards lightweight jewellery, studded products and old gold exchange, favouring organised players.
Hedging gains: Q3 FY26 about INR45 crore, Q4 FY26 about INR20 crore, Q2 FY26 about INR5.5-6 crore; gains shrinking as hedging coverage rises.
Marketing kept within 1.5% of sales; 250-300 hoardings cut versus last year. FY26 other expenses included about INR40-50 crore for UP launch and one-time campaigns that are not expected to recur.
Inventory turns stabilised at about 3.5-4x after refinery and B2B sales wound down (previously about 7x).

541167|2026-06.headline: Yasho Q1 FY27 revenue hit record Rs 308 crore (volume +42% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 24.2%; management guides to sustain margins.
541167|2026-06.overview:
Consolidated revenue reached a record Rs 308 crore, driven by 42% YoY volume growth from customer approvals and additional offtake in industrial chemicals. EBITDA rose to Rs 74.42 crore (24.2% margin, vs 17% previously cited), with PAT of Rs 36 crore (11.7% margin). Net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.86x from 3.75x at Q4 FY26, bank loan ratings were upgraded to A- by CRISIL and ICRA, and working capital cycle shortened from 190 to 143 days. Management raised FY27 capex from Rs 125 crore to Rs 250 crore for two new buildings at Pakhajan and set a FY28 revenue target above Rs 1,600 crore.</overview>

532782|2026-06.headline: Sutlej Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (6.7% margin) from INR5 crore, with PBT of INR4.2 crore versus a loss a year ago.
532782|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 17% YoY to INR704 crore, marginally ahead of Q4 FY26. Gross margin expanded about 370 bps to 46.8%, with raw material cost falling to 53.2% of revenue from 56.9%. EBITDA margin has now expanded for five consecutive quarters (0.8%, 2.7%, 3.9%, 5.3%, 6.7%). Management said the quarter was clean with no exceptional items and that all three business clusters and six manufacturing units delivered positive EBITDA. Value-added yarn share is still only about 10-15% against a 30-35% target.

financial_highlights.change: +17% YoY; marginally ahead of Q4 FY26
from 17.7% a year ago; includes annual wage revision
vs INR5 crore (0.8%) in Q1 FY26 and 5.3% in Q4 FY26
vs INR17 crore in Q4 FY26
vs loss of INR38.6 crore in Q1 FY26; no exceptional items (FY26 had INR22.5 crore)
vs loss of INR25.7 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Segment revenue INR640 crore, up 16% YoY; segment EBITDA INR34.4 crore vs INR6.5 crore a year ago. Management attributes about 60% of the 2.5% raw-material-to-sales improvement to moving up product categories and the balance to operational efficiency.

segments.name: Sutlej Green Fibre (recycled PET)
segments.commentary: Gross sales roughly INR400 crore; about 70-75% is consumed internally by the group's own units. Management is adding performance properties to recycled polyester and discussing collaborations with brands.

segments.name: Home textiles
segments.commentary: Revenue up 22% YoY and profitability held versus a loss a year ago. Sequentially softer on order phasing, not demand. Management targets doubling the business in about two years.

guidance_outlook: No formal quarterly guidance. Management said it will maintain or better Q1 numbers in Q2 and Q3, but declined to give a clear outlook.
Long-term aim is a double-digit EBITDA margin, described as the near-term benchmark; no timeline was given.
Finance cost in absolute terms expected to rise to about INR75 crore this year from about INR67 crore last year, due to capex, even though the cost-of-borrowing percentage is down about 40 bps.
Rationalization programme is not complete; remaining cost benefits expected through the balance of FY27.
Employee cost expected to decline in coming quarters, per management, with no quantified target.
Southeast Asia and Latin America market entries are expected this financial year.
Technical textiles (Protech) and protective textiles are expected to contribute in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Capex is mainly upgrading existing assets rather than new capacity; funded from internal accruals and existing facilities with no additional equity, per management.
Maintenance capex is proceeding as planned.
Protech technical textiles has moved from qualification into sampling and trials; some protective textile products have qualified.
Home textile growth plans are underway, with the business in investment mode for technical and protective textiles.
demand_pricing: Global demand described as relatively stable; management said legacy yarn makers benefited from China-driven demand in cotton-grade yarn, which Sutlej does not directly target.

Export markets: Far East and Africa, opened last year, have moved from trial volumes to repeat orders. Core markets Latin America and Europe are steady; Bangladesh demand is stable but below levels of two years ago. Exports go to about 60 destinations.
Customers are rebuilding inventories cautiously from very low levels.

Raw material outlook: cotton expected flat to slightly higher, with parity emerging between international and Indian prices; polyester/synthetics expected to ease over the long term, but a return to pre-war levels is uncertain.
Cotton is about 30% of fibre consumption by quantity; synthetics about 70%, of which about 30% of the total is recycled.
Value-added yarn is about 10-15% of yarn products against a 30-35% target. Customer trials take 3-6 months, and first containers of new specialty SKUs have shipped for testing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the yarn portfolio is value-added now, and what EBITDA margin can the business reach at 30-35% value-added?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added share is about 10-15% of yarn products, with a pipeline and new SKUs under customer evaluation. Management would not give a margin number for the steady state but said double-digit EBITDA is the minimum target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the yarn EBITDA gain came from spread expansion versus mix and integration?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% of the raw material-to-sales improvement (about 2.5 percentage points) came from moving up product categories; the rest came from operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost (15-17% of revenue) so far above peers, and will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ratio is not at target and will fall in coming quarters. It attributed the gap to melange and dyeing layers, job processing in home textiles, and low realisations, and said absolute costs have not risen.

qa_highlights.question: What will the interest outflow be this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost is expected to rise to about INR75 crore from about INR67 crore last year, because of capex, even though the cost-of-borrowing percentage is down about 40 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and EBITDA potential of Green Fibre and home textiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Green Fibre gross sales are about INR400 crore, of which 70-75% is consumed internally. Home textiles are to be doubled in about two years, with no margin target given.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt be structured, and how do raw material prices affect working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital borrowing will rise for the same number of days because of higher raw material prices. Long-term debt is mainly for capex, which is secured. Credit lines will be rebalanced as results move.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Q2 and Q3 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance. Management said it will try to maintain or better the Q1 numbers.

506879|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.1% YoY to INR43.8 crore and EBITDA margin hit 47.5%, while the company pursues a debt- and equity-funded acquisition of MicroBiopharm Japan and Sanofi brands.
506879|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR43.8 crore (up 22.1% YoY) on higher sales volumes, with EBITDA up 49.4% to INR20.8 crore at a 47.5% margin and PAT of INR11.1 crore (up 22.1%). Management described the business as sold out in capacity for years and said the expanded fermentation capacity (about 540 KL, roughly doubling capacity) starts full operation by end-August 2026. The call focused mostly on the strategic pivot to a fermentation-based CDMO, the MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) acquisition, and the Sanofi brand portfolio, with funding (up to INR1,000 crore equity, debt mix undecided) and deal timing left open.

financial_highlights.change: from about INR62 crore in FY23; about INR370 crore added in 3 years

segments.name: Standalone GTBL - fermentation and API (Rifamycin-S, Rifapentine, Rifaximin)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue has been stuck around the historic INR40 crore run rate; API block bookings are in Rifapentine, Rifaximin and Rifamycin-S. Management said API output began only recently because intermediate capacity was the constraint.

segments.name: MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) - to be acquired
segments.commentary: MBJ is about 100% API CDMO, with roughly 4-5% formulations; 60% of its business is CDMO, and revenue is 60% Japan and 40% outside Japan. Revenue by vertical was not disclosed. ADCs are patented but have no CDMO project yet; other platforms are commercialised.

segments.name: Sanofi brands (13 anti-TB and anti-infective brands)
segments.commentary: Branded generics sold in 55 countries across Europe, Middle East and Africa. Revenue and margin figures were not disclosed. Manufacturing will move to CMOs over a 3-year transition services agreement.

guidance_outlook: Expanded fermentation capacity to be fully operational by end-August 2026; output to start partly in Q2 and fully in H2 FY27.
Base-case growth target of high-teens percentage per annum over the next 3-5 years; no revenue number given.
Base-business capex for FY27 about INR20 crore including maintenance, with INR10-15 crore of last-mile capex.
MBJ closing targeted around end-August 2026 with funding largely secured; Sanofi closing long-stop date June 2027, needing approvals in over 50 countries.
Hybrid power Phase 1 expected to go live in September 2026, Phase 2 about two months later; management expects EBITDA margin improvement.
Management expects some synergy projects with MBJ within the first year.
capex_capacity: Fermentation capacity has been roughly doubled (additional 540 KL); some capacity is for R&D and cGMP pilot facilities. Management said utilisation is effectively 0 or 100 and all output must be commercialised.
API block output started only recently, with fermentation constraints having delayed it by about two years versus the November 2023 guidance of FY25.
Gross block incremental INR370 crore over three years, of which about INR200 crore is fermentation and API facilities (asset turn 1.4-1.5x).
Hybrid power project is in progress and expected to lower power costs.
demand_pricing: Management said FY26 was stable and that the company was sold out on capacity; one year saw a dip due to excessive rains and power fluctuations.
Rifampicin to Rifapentine market shift is slower than hoped; management said Rifa-S demand is unaffected because GTBL is ready with both APIs.
A dispute with Optimus Drugs, a major customer, has been resolved and business is restarting; management said other buyers were available and capacity was sold out during the suspension.
Management said the company aims to sell intermediates to other Indian and global API makers to reduce customer concentration.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there nearly a three-year gap in earnings calls, and why was the API block revenue delayed from FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business was flat but sold out; capex was late by about a year. API could not start because intermediate capacity was fully contracted to long-term customers.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR3,000 crore acquisition make sense given interest costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sanofi deal is expected to close later, with long-stop June 2027, and that interest rates in the target geographies are much lower than 10%. It said the business is cash-flow positive from the start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding structure for the MBJ and Sanofi deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity raise of up to INR1,000 crore is planned; the debt component is undecided and will depend on the optimal mix, with options kept open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the base business in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10-15 crore of last-mile capex remains, and total base-business capex including maintenance is about INR20 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path from Sanofi brands to manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: A 3-year transition services agreement will move marketing authorisations country by country, with manufacturing moved to CMOs; management hopes for faster transfer, with tech transfer complete in year 1.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Themis Medicare merger withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an external strategy review led it to focus on a fermentation-based CDMO and avoid diluting focus with predominantly domestic businesses.

risks_watch: Funding and leverage: INR1,000 crore equity planned; debt amount undecided. Interest and dilution implications are open.
Integration and bandwidth risk from two acquisitions across different geographies, plus a promoter pledge that management said should fall significantly within 12-15 months.
Sanofi closing timing depends on approvals in more than 50 countries, with long-stop June 2027. MBJ closing around end-August 2026 still needs final approvals.
ADCs have no CDMO project yet; MBJ revenue by vertical is undisclosed.
Sanofi margin uplift depends on integrating GTBL's own API; management said margins would return to current levels after stabilisation.
Customer concentration and the Optimus Drugs dispute; the settlement terms were not disclosed.
506879|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and strategic on the long-term CDMO vision, but evasive on specifics: MBJ and Sanofi revenue, debt quantum, Optimus dispute details and promoter pledge data were withheld or left vague. Management also sounded defensive about the three-year gap in calls and the earlier API delays.
key_quotes: from a fermentation perspective, it's 0 or 100. So basically, we will be running capacity at full scale.
So MicroBiopharm is 100% API CDMO.
We are simply bringing in the synergies in both the places, which can add value, whereby 1 plus 1 is equal to more -- significantly more than 2.

544537|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~76% YoY to ~Rs 2,725 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to ~4% (from 5.8%), with EBITDA ~Rs 110 crore.
544537|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 2,725 crore, up ~76% YoY, with EBITDA of about Rs 110 crore (+22% YoY) and PAT of about Rs 69 crore (+23% YoY). EBITDA margin compressed to ~4% from 5.8% a year earlier, though up ~48 bps from Q4 FY26's 3.5%, which management attributed to product mix and the ramp-up of value-added copper. The copper anode line was fully commissioned, with ~600 tonnes sold since commissioning, and Unit-2 restarted on 27 July 2026 after a furnace accident on 14 July. Management gave no quantitative volume or margin guidance beyond directional statements that FY27 margins and EBITDA per tonne should improve.

financial_highlights.change: ~+76% YoY vs Rs 1,549 crore in Q1 FY26
vs 5.8% in Q1 FY26 and 3.5% in Q4 FY26 (+~48 bps QoQ)
~+23% YoY vs ~Rs 56 crore; continuing operations Rs 69 crore vs Rs 57 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Copper and copper products share of revenue
Lead and lead alloy ingots share of revenue
Aluminium and alloys share of revenue

segments.name: Copper and copper products
segments.commentary: Now ~67% of revenue. Anode line runs at 1,600 MT/month installed capacity after both furnaces started; ~600 MT anode sold in the quarter. Management cited copper EBITDA of ~Rs 31,000-32,000/tonne in Q1 vs ~Rs 36,000/tonne FY26 average and ~Rs 13,000 in Q4 FY26 (as stated in Q&A).

segments.name: Lead and lead alloy
segments.commentary: ~29% of revenue. Management said margins fell from ~7-7.5% toward lower levels due to expensive raw material from West Asia disruption; capacity expansion of 15-20% over ~1,85,000 tonnes (FY26 volume) is awaiting approval.

segments.name: Aluminium and alloys
segments.commentary: ~3% of revenue; no further commentary in the call.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 copper EBITDA/tonne and overall margins to improve as value-added products ramp up; it cited an average uplift of ~2% (around Rs 25/tonne per Q&A) on value-added volumes at steady state.
Copper cathode Phase-1 (1,500 MT/month installed) targeted for Q2 FY27; a 750 MT cathode facility to begin volumes about a month after readiness.
Copper wire rod (600 MT/month) and copper busbar and profiles (1,500 MT/month) targeted for Q3 FY27.
Antimony project (1,000 MT lead antimony bullion, ~100 MT/month output) on schedule for Q3 FY27; Ahmedabad JV trial production started, stabilisation expected in Q2 FY27.
Plastic recycling facility (~Rs 15 crore, ~6 acres) targeted for Q3 FY27; Kuwait investment expected to contribute from Q3 FY27 subject to shipping normalisation.
FY27 capex outlay of ~Rs 87 crore, mainly copper value-added, antimony and plastic recycling.
No quantitative revenue, volume or EBITDA guidance given; management declined to guide FY27/FY28 volume growth percentages.
capex_capacity: Copper anode line commissioned in Q1 FY27; installed capacity 1,600 MT/month with both furnaces operational.
Copper cathode: civil construction complete; Phase-1 of 1,500 MT/month installed capacity for Q2 FY27.
Copper wire rod 600 MT/month and busbar/profiles 1,500 MT/month, both for Q3 FY27.
Ahmedabad JV with C&Y Group: designed for ~72,000 tonnes/year copper-bearing scrap and ~25,000 tonnes/year copper products at full ramp-up; trial production started.

Unit-2 (Gummidipoondi) furnace shed resumed operations after approval on 27 July 2026 following the 14 July furnace accident (one contract worker died, others injured); insurance claim under settlement. Management said the one-week closure would not affect annual production.
demand_pricing: Management said the West Asia conflict caused raw material shortages, forcing purchases of expensive local and imported material, which pressured lead margins.
Around Rs 20-30 crore of raw material remains stuck on a vessel at Dubai port; management said it is insured against war risk.

Regulatory tailwind: amended hazardous waste rules require manufacturers of cables, conductors and similar products to collect end-of-life items and use recycled copper/aluminium/zinc at 5% from FY28, rising to 10% later. Management said the volume impact is hard to quantify.
Most new copper value-added customers are expected to be new to the company, with in-principle go-aheads received from many.
Management said competition is welcome and the regulation applies to all players.

qa_highlights.question: How will lead and copper EBITDA margins move over the next three quarters and full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain attributed lead margin pressure to West Asia raw material costs and said copper value-added products should offset it; he expects a better FY27 margin but gave no figures. Hemant Jain said EBITDA per tonne, not percentage margin, is the right metric.

qa_highlights.question: What volume guidance is there for lead and copper in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there would be some volume growth in later FY27 but declined to give percentages, calling it premature. Lead capacity expansion of 15-20% is pending approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the furnace incident on volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-week closure and maintenance shutdown would have no material impact on production, given spare capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 FY26 copper EBITDA/tonne so low (~Rs 13,000), and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business should be viewed on a two-quarter average because of hedging and the procurement-to-sale cycle; Q1 copper margin was back to normal. Value-added copper is expected to add ~Rs 25/tonne at stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is raw material still 100% hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain said the 100% hedging policy is unchanged, that hedging is a cost centre and not a speculative position, and that broker limits exceed $30 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategic rationale for the telecom infrastructure diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Mayank Pareek said the company already removes redundant copper cables for telecom firms and has added a new object clause to lay optical fibre cable as an incidental activity. No revenue or margin numbers were given.

543419|2026-06.headline: Shriram Properties posted record Q1 FY27 sales of INR484 crores (+10% YoY) but revenue of INR271 crores (+4%) and PAT of INR11 crores lag, with growth back-ended.
543419|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 sales value rose 10% YoY to INR484 crores on 0.85 million sq ft, the company's highest-ever Q1, driven by launches at Shriram Stellar (Chennai), Shriram Southbrook (Kolkata) and Green Meadows phase (Chennai). Revenue of INR271 crores, EBITDA of INR42 crores and PAT of INR11 crores were steady, with margins diluted by low-margin legacy Kolkata handovers. Management reiterated full-year FY27 guidance, pointing to Q2 and H2 OCs (about 2,900 units, INR1,560 crores revenue potential) and a back-ended launch calendar. Net debt to equity stood at 0.29x, with gearing expected to rise in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Free cash flow before new project investment
Closing cash / gross external debt / net debt
financial_highlights.value: INR219 crores / INR651 crores / INR432 crores

segments.name: Chennai
segments.commentary: Shriram Stellar, a premium launch late June, sold about 20% on launch weekend; Green Meadows new phase (0.2 million sq ft) also launched.

segments.name: Kolkata
segments.commentary: Shriram Southbrook (0.4 million sq ft) launched; branded plotted development had about 55% of inventory sold within 30 days. Legacy Grand One and Sunshine One handovers carry thin margins.

segments.name: Bengaluru / Pune
segments.commentary: Doddagubbi JDA (about 0.7 million sq ft saleable) added in Q1, expected on board end-Q3/early Q4; Manjari (Pune, 2.3 million sq ft via FSI purchase) expected to launch after plan approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: sales value INR3,300-3,500 crores (40-50% growth) and collections INR2,100-2,200 crores (26-30% growth), per Q&A.
Revenue recognition expected to grow at least 20% in FY27; PAT growth guided at 20-25%; FY27 PBT margin about 8-9%.
FY28 mission reiterated: sales value about INR5,000 crores, revenue INR2,500 crores, PBT about INR250 crores (around 10% margin); FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.

Handover pipeline: 410+ units of pent-up handovers, 2 projects (400+ units, INR160 crores) for OC in Q2, and 5+ projects (2,100+ units, INR1,000 crores) for H2; total 2,900+ units, INR1,560 crores revenue potential for balance of FY27.
Management expects gearing to rise temporarily in FY27, with long-term comfort at 0.5x-1.0x net debt to equity.
Management reiterated FY27 sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores; launch GDV of about INR6,000 crores from 7.23 million sq ft targeted supply.
capex_capacity: FY27 launch calendar: about 6 million sq ft planned out of 7 million sq ft potential across Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata; 2 projects (0.7 million sq ft) launched in Q1.

Current pipeline 33.7 million sq ft (16 million ongoing, 17.7 million upcoming) with GDV potential about INR13,530 crores; 7.3 million sq ft (GDV above INR6,000 crores) at advanced stage for addition in 3-6 months.
Kolkata: about 110 acres of land; 2.3 million sq ft apartment approval obtained pre-election, to be released in phases of 750,000-800,000 sq ft, with only one phase possible in FY27.
Management targets nearly doubling the upcoming pipeline over 18-24 months.
Cash flow: INR88 crores invested in new projects in Q1.
demand_pricing: Sustenance sales prices rising about 4-5% annually, versus 10-15% in the post-COVID period; launch prices set by competition in each micro-market.
Average mid-market selling price about INR7,600-7,700 per sq ft, versus about INR5,000 pre-COVID; Sunshine 2 and 3 realising about INR7,600-7,700 per sq ft.
Management sees no material slowdown in conversion or housing loan application momentum; Bengaluru launches described as slow, upper-end investment demand flagged as softer.
Legacy Shankari (Chennai) and Grand One (Kolkata) realise about INR4,500-5,000 and INR18-24 lakh tickets, dragging margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 mission (INR5,000 crores sales, INR2,500 crores revenue, INR250 crores PBT) still intact and how credible is a 10% PBT margin versus historic EBITDA of 7-8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the targets. EBITDA margin was 22.5% (FY23), 22.6% (FY24), 18.4% (FY25) and about 13.5% (FY26), with PBT of 8.8%, 7.7%, 9% and about 5.3%. It guided FY28 EBITDA margin of 22-24% and PBT around 10%, based on project-level build-up and not land sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why is sales value growing 40-50% while collections grow only 26-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections follow project progress: 10% on booking, 20% after agreement, then construction-linked. Launches are back-ended to Q3-Q4, so collections ramp in later quarters and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of FY27 launch GDV versus sustenance sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores look right; the balance comes from new launches off about 7.23 million sq ft supply worth about INR6,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata land plan and value?
qa_highlights.answer: About 104-106 acres approved for apartments, villas and plots, with a 3-year build and 5-year handover target. Management estimates INR6.5-7.5 crores net contribution per acre and INR1,200-1,400 crores free cash over about five years; bulk sale at INR3.5-4 crores per acre was rejected as uneconomic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 PBT margin 10% and what drives the margin recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PBT margin guided at 8-9%. Margins are product-mix driven: Grand One, Shankari and Sunshine One handovers are low-margin, with Sunshine 2 and 3 and post-2019 launches expected to restore mid-20s EBITDA margin and 9-10% PBT, mainly in H2 FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will tax write-backs boost PAT in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tax write-backs cannot be predicted; they arise only from loss-making subsidiaries recognising deferred tax assets. PAT growth guided at 20-25% without a write-back assumption.

534076|2026-06.headline: RHI Magnesita India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR1,014 crore and EBITDA rose 42% to INR147 crore, a 14.5% margin; management keeps the 13% FY27 margin guidance.
534076|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,014 crore, up 9% QoQ and 6% YoY, led by the steel business on favourable realizations and healthy demand. EBITDA grew 42% YoY to INR147 crore and margin expanded to 14.5% from 10.8%, which management attributed to steelmaking execution, price realisation and operating leverage. PAT nearly doubled to INR65 crore from INR35 crore. Management said price increases were largely war surcharges, and it kept FY27 guidance of 13% EBITDA margin and 7-8% volume growth, while stating 9% is a stretch. A leadership change was announced with Pankaj Malhan as MD and CEO, and Parmod Sagar continues as Chairman.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Main driver of Q1 revenue growth on favourable realisations and healthy demand; flow control business cited as the growth engine, with one large group's market share up almost twofold in about 6 months. Management said Dalmia business is flat and growth came from RHIM India.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Recovered in Q1 on seasonal maintenance demand; management said cement season is almost over by end-September.

segments.name: Industrial (non-ferrous, glass)
segments.commentary: Described as weak in Q1 with few projects in H1; silica and glass project orders expected in Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Coke oven project (PSU)
segments.commentary: Final-stage negotiation with pricing adjustment pending; production to start next month, with a 14-16 month project life.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 13% for FY27 reaffirmed; management said upside possible only if raw material costs ease.
Volume growth guidance of 7-8% for FY27 (management said 9% is a stretch); long-term volume guidance of steel/cement market growth plus 1-2%.
Management said the EUR45 million group pricing and mix benefit is already reflected in Q1 and that India will contribute proportionately.
Capex guidance of INR80-100 crore per year maintained, covering Dalmia plant modernisation, 4PRO machinery, robotics and maintenance.
MINPRO JV (51% RHIM, 49% Khemka) targeted to start production around Q4 FY27; initial investment about INR35 crore over two years, EBITDA 8-10%, payback under 3 years after production.
Quartzite mines (Chiraipani and Bhikampali) expected to open by end of Q1 FY27, with cost benefits from Q2.
Magnesite prices up 6-8% over the last two months; company is working on recipe optimisation and price pass-through.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR8 crore in Q1 vs INR150 crore guidance cited by an analyst; management kept the INR80-100 crore annual run-rate.
MINPRO greenfield mineral processing facility in Odisha, via JV with Khemka Refractories; roughly INR35 crore initial investment over two years.
Quartzite mines Chiraipani and Bhikampali came with the Dalmia deal; all licences received.
SAIL SMS4 expansion (about 6-6.5 million tonnes) expected to open refractory tenders in about 6-8 months.
Four or five products being transferred to India production within about one year (investor deck pages 21-22).
demand_pricing: Management cited steel production growth, high capacity utilisation and blast furnace/steelmaking investments as demand support; Indian steel grew 7-8% in H1 and steel capex of INR50,000-60,000 crore is expected this financial year.
Cement demand strong, but cement margins under pressure from fuel, energy and raw material costs.
Competitive pressure from domestic and multinational players, with greenfield and brownfield capacity additions and some excess capacity.
Exports reduced QoQ in Q1 per CFO; management expects isostatic flow control export growth over a year.
Alumina prices stable over the last six months; magnesite up 6-8% recently.
Realisation rise attributed mostly to war surcharges and product mix; no price/mix/FX split disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Split of ~12% realisation growth into price, mix and currency; sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: No split given. CFO said most price increases were war surcharges, so growth is primarily product-mix driven.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 capex only INR8 crore vs INR150 crore guidance; will guidance change?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term capex of INR80-100 crore a year unchanged; covers Dalmia modernisation, 4PRO robotics and maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Can volume growth of about 9% be achieved for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 7-8% is achievable but 9% is a stretch unless large high-volume orders come in.

qa_highlights.question: How should medium-term margins be viewed; split between Dalmia and RHIM India?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalmia flat; growth from RHIM India (flow control heavy, Bhiwadi and Jamshedpur). Medium-term margin supported by MINPRO and captive mines; no numeric range given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EUR45 million group pricing benefit flow into India?
qa_highlights.answer: Benefit is group-wide across six regions; India contributes proportionately and it is already in Q1 numbers. FY27 margin guidance held at 13%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q1 numbers affected by project orders, and what is the H2 project pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: No project revenue in Q1. Coke oven project to start next month; glass and silica projects expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the quartzite mine and MINPRO JV deliver quantified savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantification still in progress by FP&A; management will share later. Mine opening expected by end-Q1 with benefits from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Auditor resignation and goodwill impairment?
qa_highlights.answer: Auditor change aligned with group auditor rotation; Dalmia goodwill fully written off, non-cash and below EBITDA, with headroom. No reversal planned.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (magnesite up 6-8%) and geopolitical risk (war surcharge dependence) could limit the 13% margin.
Volume guidance gap: H1 volume growth is below the 7-9% range, requiring a strong H2 for 7-8% growth.
Weak industrial segment until Q3-Q4 project orders (glass, silica) materialise.
Export volumes declined QoQ in Q1 and management has no near-term recovery timeline.
Capex run-rate far below the INR150 crore guidance cited by an analyst; check whether it catches up.
Execution on MINPRO (Q4 FY27 start) and quartzite mine (cost benefit from Q2).
CEO transition to Pankaj Malhan and auditor change at the AGM.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR35 crore in Q1 FY26 (nearly doubled)
Company described balance sheet as net cash positive
Not confirmed by management; no price/mix/FX split given
Against INR150 crore guidance per analyst; management did not dispute

500380|2026-06.headline: JK Lakshmi Q1 FY27: realisation up ~8-9% QoQ on geo-mix and non-trade price gains, but management guides to a sharp Q2 cost squeeze from fuel and packaging.
500380|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 demand was reasonable, with industry growth around 8%, and the company's realisation rose roughly 9% sequentially, driven mainly by a 20 km reduction in lead distance (to 368 km from 388 km) and higher non-trade prices in Gujarat, Mumbai, East and North. Fuel cost per Kcal rose to INR1.65 from INR1.54 in Q4, and management expects Q2 fuel cost of 1.8-1.85 plus packaging inflation of INR3.5-4 per bag, with July-September demand cyclicality compounding the pressure. Management reiterated 30 MTPA by FY30 and a net debt/EBITDA ceiling of 2.5x, stretching to 2.75x at peak. Management also described the proxy-advisor-driven AGM voting outcome and an Assam PIL affecting the Northeast project.

financial_highlights.value: INR185 crore (RMC INR93 cr, AAC INR60 cr, POP INR23 cr)

financial_highlights.change: Trade share rose to 59% from prior level

segments.name: Cement (core)
segments.commentary: Realisation rose ~9% QoQ, helped by non-trade price increases in Gujarat, Mumbai, East and North and a 20 km lead reduction worth about INR60-70/tonne. Roughly 90% of sales came from Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Haryana and western UP.

segments.name: Non-cement (RMC, AAC, POP)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR185 crore in Q1 with 5% EBITDA margin. Management expects FY27 non-cement revenue near INR800 crore vs INR613 crore last year.

segments.name: Renewable energy / power
segments.commentary: 49% of power from renewables. Installed: solar 129 MW, WHRS 45 MW, wind 4 MW, thermal 74 MW. A 42 MW solar captive SPV (INR20 crore investment) at INR4.10 tariff against grid INR7.50 is expected to be live in 8-9 months.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 fuel cost per Kcal expected to rise from INR1.65 to about INR1.8-1.85, with management saying the cost impact is larger than Q1.
Packaging granule cost up, adding about INR3.5-4 per bag versus Q1 as per initial calculation.
Management expects some pass-through of cost, but says the extent is uncertain given July-September demand cyclicality and maintenance.
Installed/operational capacity targeted at 18 MTPA by end FY27; 30 MTPA by FY30 reiterated.

FY27 capex about INR1,500 crore, FY28 about INR2,000 crore, FY29 about INR1,500 crore (including Northeast; excluding Kutch and Nagaur land acquisition). Durg has about INR400 crore spent to date out of about INR3,000 crore.
Lead distance expected to rise during monsoon/lean months (July-September) but management aims to contain it.
capex_capacity: Durg expansion: about INR400 crore spent to date, INR300 crore in Q1; equipment ordering for Durg clinker and grinding, plus Prayagraj and Madhubani grinding, largely complete.

Northeast: two mines won via auction at various approval stages; initial 1.5 MTPA planned with grinding station sites still being identified; management says project is back on track with milestone updates next quarter.
Overhead conveyor belt approval from SAIL is granted and agreement is with SAIL for execution; railway siding phase 2 is contingent on SAIL and state road collaboration.
Assam PIL filed in Guwahati High Court involving land for the Mahabal Cement (subsidiary) grinding plant; JK Lakshmi has been named as a recipient of the notice.
BESS of 28 MW planned as part of Rajasthan solar setup to store excess captive generation.
demand_pricing: Industry demand grew ~8% in Q1; industry capacity added about 11 MT in the quarter, about 52 MT expected for the year, taking national capacity to about 725 MT; industry utilisation about 73-74%.
Non-trade prices rose in several markets; trade was flat in North, up in West and East; trade prices in July and early August have not fallen and have seen little upward movement.
Management believes North has pricing headroom because it was most impacted by imported coal/pet coke costs; East/Chhattisgarh prices are seen as lowest in India with room to rise.
Management said trade is the focus going forward because blended cement sells in trade and offers better equivalent realisation, though non-trade margins can be higher in absolute terms.
Far-off markets were reduced in Q1 to concentrate on core states; management says demand months are used to expand channel reach and lean months to spread wider.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ~9% sequential realisation increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited non-trade price increases in Gujarat, Mumbai, East and North, trade gains in West and East, and a 20 km lead reduction worth about INR60-70/tonne; the rest was price and geo-mix. Non-trade is 41% of volume.

qa_highlights.question: Fuel cost trajectory into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 fuel cost INR1.65/Kcal vs INR1.54 in Q4. Q2 is expected to exceed 1.65, potentially reaching 1.8-1.85. Imported coal is about USD130-135/t and pet coke has risen above USD140-145/t.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 margin outlook given cost increases and cyclical demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full pass-through is uncertain due to July-September seasonal weakness and maintenance; it expects to pass costs on but cannot quantify how much.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan and whether Northeast is included?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 about INR1,500 crore, FY28 about INR2,000 crore, FY29 about INR1,500 crore; this includes Northeast (INR1,500 crore) and Durg (about INR3,000 crore total); Kutch and Nagaur land is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Leverage ceiling and the 30 MTPA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not cross 2.5x net debt/EBITDA, and at most 2.75x near the end of the expansion plan; 30 MTPA by 2030 is reaffirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material cost inflation QoQ and YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Cited kiln shutdowns requiring fly ash from L2 sources at higher cost, gypsum availability, diesel, and higher SBS/non-cement raw material use. Trade share rising to 59% and blended share rising also drove cementitious material cost.

544081|2026-06.headline: Jyoti CNC Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37% to INR509 crore, but consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 23.4% on Huron revenue deferral.
544081|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 37% YoY to INR509 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin of 28.4% and PAT of INR88 crore (17.2% margin). Consolidated revenue was INR508.5 crore (+24% YoY), but Huron revenue was deferred because the company moved from percentage-of-completion to recognising revenue only on dispatch, citing end-user certificate and export licence delays. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR119 crore (23.4%) after a INR10 crore unrealised forex loss; reported EBITDA was INR109 crore (21.4%). Management guided to 25-30% top-line growth and about 25% EBITDA margin for FY27, with the 10,000-machine expansion due by end-September.

segments.name: Standalone (Jyoti India)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR509 crore (+37% YoY), adjusted EBITDA margin 28.4%, PAT INR88 crore. Management says standalone margin was about 27.5% after Huron effect. Demand from general engineering, automotive, EMS, defence and precision engineering.

segments.name: Huron (Germany, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Produced about EUR6.5 million of machines in Q1 but billed about EUR3 million; roughly INR35 crore of revenue deferred versus Q1 FY26 (about INR70 crore). Management says costs are fully booked, so the gap hits margin. Recognition moved from percentage-of-completion to dispatch-based.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 25-30%; EBITDA margin guided around 25%, which management says it is committed to.
Huron FY27 revenue expected at INR300-325 crore, with Huron EBITDA margin of 8-10%; management says Huron will be PAT positive this year.
Standalone FY27 capex about INR200-225 crore against a total expansion target of about INR450 crore for the new capacity; management said capex will not touch INR300 crore.
Debt to stay at about March 2026 levels; management targets net debt not above 2x EBITDA. OCF for FY27 expected at about 50% of EBITDA.
Order book expected to reach INR2,500-3,000 crore by year-end; FY27 machine volume expected above 8,000 units.
capex_capacity: New 10,000-machine-per-year facility targeted to commence operations by end-September 2026; machine shop, sheet metal and paint shop buildings ready or near completion, with foundry about one month late (October).
Current capacity 6,000 machines per year; 5,550 machines built in FY26; Q1 FY27 utilisation 86%.
Management cites a targeted INR450 crore capex for the new capacity and says it is on track.
CNC controller: HMI ready; commercialisation expected in about two years; PLI application filed with capital subsidy about 25% central plus matching state support (about 50% total).
Raw material and inventory built up over the past nine months to support the ramp-up; management expects working capital and inventory to improve after the new facility is operational.
demand_pricing: Order book INR4,848 crore; mix: aerospace and defence 38%, general engineering 20%, automotive 19%, EMS 13%, die and mould 4%.
Q1 revenue mix: aerospace and defence 37%, automotive 35%, general engineering 17%, EMS 6%, other 5%.
Blended realisation about INR34.56 lakh per machine in Q1 FY27 vs INR34.41 lakh in Q1 FY26; management expects the range to hold.
Management says the Rajkot unit booked more than 250 machines in July and that the company crossed 1,000 machines in one month in the domestic market.

India imports about 60-62% of machine tool demand, mainly from Japan, Europe and South Korea. New NX double-column machine targets railway, commercial vehicles, infra, power and heavy engineering, with 6m model launched and 8m and 10m in development.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Huron's accounting change and what drove the revenue gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says end-user certificates (EUC) and export licences now take longer, and auditors apply a conservative dispatch-based approach. Revenue will return to POCM once EUC is received; the company says it can book POCM if EUC arrives within 3 months of order. Around 7-8 machines across multiple orders are pending, and management expects clearance in one batch.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an impairment risk if the Huron investigation drags on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no impairment risk ("Not at all").

qa_highlights.question: Will the Huron revenue shortfall reverse in the coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 dispatches to improve, but says large machines have long lead times, so the bulk should come in Q3 and Q4. Management said the company should be judged on an annual basis, not quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex and debt plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone capex of INR200-225 crore for FY27 against a INR450 crore expansion total. Debt is expected to stay flat versus March; management targets net debt not above 2x EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise and why was it not capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs were booked to P&L because the new capacity has already been put to use (building and components), so capitalisation was not applied.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 Huron margin and does it reach PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Huron FY27 revenue expected at INR300-325 crore with EBITDA margin of 8-10%; management said Huron is PAT positive this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sequential margin decline explained by Huron alone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes; it pointed to the same standalone business at about 27.5% margin in Q1.

EBITDA was about ₹12.4 crore versus ₹11.3 crore QoQ and ₹8.8 crore YoY (the slide labelled the YoY figure incorrectly).
