group capex plan ~₹15 crore for FY27

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Sales ₹103 crore, up from ₹78 crore YoY and ₹86 crore QoQ; growth led by tubeless (~25% volume YoY), TPMS (~75-80% YoY) and EV components (~103% YoY). Tube valves ex-motorcycle segment grew ~20%. Tubeless, TPMS and EV lines running above 85-90% utilisation.

segments.name: Metals (Triton Valves Future Tech, brass mill)
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹79 crore, up from ~₹50-52 crore YoY and ₹68 crore QoQ; capacity utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, implying ~30% headroom. Current ROCE above 16%, with management targeting 20%+ and possibly 25%. Scrap sales now netted off under Ind AS, reducing reported standalone top line without affecting EBITDA.

segments.name: Climate control
segments.commentary: Sales ~₹3.9 crore, down YoY and QoQ. Management cited Chinese dumping, copper costs and a weak AC season; it is lobbying for QCO and minimum import price. Q2 expected to be quiet, with recovery from Oct-Nov.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of a 'reasonably good' Q2 if the second half of the quarter holds, and says FY27 will be much better than FY26.
Annualised Q1 group EBITDA ~₹50 crore vs ~₹40 crore in FY26; PBT, EBITDA and revenue expected to run slightly above annualised Q1 levels.
Group ROCE expected to rise from ~12.5% to 13-14% this year and ~15% by mid-next year; new investments targeted at 20-25% internal ROCE.
Ambition of a ₹1,000 crore revenue target by about FY30; management says it has a plan that does not depend on climate control recovery.
EV component vertical targeted at ~₹100 crore over the next few quarters, with climate control also scaling to ~₹100 crore if trade remediation happens.
Double-digit EBITDA margin is not expected until commodity prices stabilise; management said it would take a long time.
Tax credit of ~₹4.75 crore already availed, plus a further ~₹0.3-0.4 crore claimed, subject to assessment; no advance tax outflow expected for ~14-15 months.
capex_capacity: FY27 group capex planned at ~₹15 crore: ~₹10 crore for automotive (tubeless, TPMS, EV components) and ~₹5 crore for metals (special alloy foundry, extrusion and drawing equipment).
About 50-60% of the ₹15 crore is expected to be commercialised in FY27, with the balance in FY28.
Automotive tubeless, TPMS and EV lines are at 85-90%+ utilisation; management said capacity will run out during the year without investment.
Metals utilisation ~65-70% post expansion, leaving ~30% volume headroom.
Climate control has spare capacity; management said it only needs orders.
demand_pricing: Automotive growth described as ~80% vehicle production growth and ~20% share gain; passenger car and two-wheeler production grew ~12-15% YoY in Q1 (per management).
Management expects automotive growth to moderate in Q3-Q4 but remain positive; new programmes cited with AUMOVIO, SENSATA and Bosch (LOIs from AUMOVIO and SENSATA in TPMS).

Metals: Q1 started slowly from Middle East raw material disruption; ~₹10 crore of metals sales were not delivered on time due to Hormuz issues. Demand strong into Q2; management expects Q3 seasonal traction in metals and climate control.
Prices pass through to automotive and climate control customers every three months. Brass selling price to external customers now above ₹1,000/kg vs ~₹500-550/kg last July-August.
Management expects metals to reach 60%+ of group revenue over 2-3 years; special alloys (naval brass, marine grades) being developed as import substitutes.
Climate control faces Chinese dumping; management is refusing to cut margins to win volume.

533293|2026-06.headline: KOEL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 16% to INR1,461 crore, but EBITDA fell 4% and margin contracted to 11.2% on commodity costs and export weakness.
533293|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 16% YoY to INR1,461 crore, led by domestic power gen (+18%), industrial (+19%) and distribution & aftermarket (+20%), while international fell 11% to INR106 crore. Standalone EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR165 crore and margin compressed to 11.2% from 13.5%, which management attributed to lower export volumes, elevated commodity costs and a lag between cost inflation and price realisation. Standalone net profit fell 9% to INR99 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR2,000 crore, with consolidated net profit down 17% to INR111 crore. Management said pricing actions have been taken across most businesses and expects profitability to improve as they flow through over coming quarters.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone net cash (net of debt, incl. treasury investments)

segments.name: Standalone power generation
segments.commentary: Revenue INR720 crore, +18% YoY; management cites sub-30 kVA portfolio redesign and domestic share gains, mainly below 750 kVA.

segments.name: Standalone industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue INR368 crore, +19% YoY; construction up double digits, marine up 125%, railways up 62%, plus first natural gas genset order from oil and gas (ONGC) up to 500 kVA.

segments.name: Standalone distribution & aftermarket
segments.commentary: Revenue INR268 crore, +20% YoY; growth across all channels led by service; 12 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth cited.

segments.name: Standalone international
segments.commentary: Revenue INR106 crore, -11% YoY; Middle East below normal levels due to West Asia conflict and logistics disruption.

segments.name: Consolidated B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,488 crore, +17% YoY; PBIT INR115 crore, -18% YoY.

segments.name: Consolidated B2C (KOEL Fluid Dynamics)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR301 crore, +3% YoY; PBIT INR26 crore, -7% YoY. Fluid Dynamics business broadly flat at INR294 crore; domestic up, exports down; channel pumps more than doubled.

segments.name: Financial services (Arka)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR210 crore, +9% YoY; PBT INR9 crore, -31% YoY; AUM INR7,651 crore; around 136 branches and over 1,800 employees.

guidance_outlook: Management says it remains committed to EBITDA delivery for the full year despite international headwinds.
Pricing actions taken across most businesses; realisation staged over different timeframes, expected to flow through over coming quarters.
Management views 3 to 6 months as a reasonable horizon for supply-chain queues and input-cost normalisation.
Long-term aspiration of a $2 billion revenue enterprise by FY30, roughly INR16,600 crore per management; no year-wise breakup given.
Management aims for a higher double-digit EBITDA margin by FY30 but declined to give a specific range; says margins have improved more than 400 bps over three years.
Data center order (~192 MW hyperscale): genset revenue to be recognised in FY27; O&M contract runs at least 5 to 6 years.
capex_capacity: First hyperscale data center order of approximately 192 MW secured in Q1, composite genset supply plus O&M contract.
NPCIL order is milestone-based; execution has started and some revenue expected this financial year; no NPCIL contribution in Q1.
Completed first end-to-end turnkey repowering of a 1,010 kVA high horsepower installation won in direct competition.
Optiprime modular power platform for data centers and mission-critical infrastructure; hybrid architectures up to 2 MW cited.
Largest range of CPCB IV compliant gas gensets claimed; new energy vertical is at programme-management stage (ethanol, methanol, isobutanol, natural gas, hydrogen).
Defense subsidiary Kirloskar Advanced Systems Limited established last quarter; no revenue contribution discussed.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand broad-based; management says market share gains are mostly below 750 kVA and only marginal above 750 kVA.
Pricing realisation varies by segment: power gen and distribution can pass on price readily, industrial and tenders are contract-specific, and fluid dynamics differs; realisation has lagged in Q1.
Middle East, a key export market, operated below normal levels due to West Asia conflict and choked logistics routes.
Management declined to split Power Gen growth between price and volume.
Employee cost rose about INR31 crore YoY (~40%), attributed to annual increments, ESOP expense, and capability additions; management says some costs are structural and some timing-related.
Inventory days rose slightly to 264 to support business expansion; cash conversion cycle at 25 days.

qa_highlights.question: Customer profile and further pipeline for the hyperscaler data center order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order is a reference point, not an endpoint, with one customer materialised through purchase orders after checks; further orders are proprietary and not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost jump roughly 40% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited a bridge of about INR31 crore YoY from increments, ESOP expense, and capability investments; some costs structural, some timing, not characterised as one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Has NPCIL or defence/marine revenue started?
qa_highlights.answer: No NPCIL contribution in Q1; execution milestone-based, revenue to start this FY. Defence and marine opportunities being pursued without specific Q1 contribution.

qa_highlights.question: Reasons for gross margin decline and pass-through of price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin contraction mainly from global commodity prices; price increases taken, with realisation lagging. Management says KOEL was among the first to start price conversations with customers.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for international business and normalisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Weakness mainly Middle East due to logistics disruption; management sees 3 to 6 months as a reasonable normalisation horizon as queues open.

qa_highlights.question: Is Arka being hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Arka CFO said a hive-off is the long-term plan, to be pursued in stepwise options, with updates to be shared when available.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin recovery depends on price realisation lagging cost inflation; watch Q2 margin trend.
Export and Middle East recovery timing; international revenue down 11% and operating leverage hit.
Employee cost run-rate (~40% YoY rise) against revenue; management promised fixed-cost absorption but gave no target.
Data center order execution, further order visibility, and customer experience in hyperscale segment; management declined to disclose pipeline.
Arka hive-off and segment PBT down 31% YoY; Fluid Dynamics export recovery.
Marine and railway growth described as partly execution and billing timing; sustainability uncertain.

533259|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR440 crores, but EBITDA was still a negative INR15 crores (-3.4% margin) and PAT was INR2 crores.
533259|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew over 58% YoY to INR440 crores and about 16% QoQ from INR378 crores, with gross profit up 64% YoY to INR34 crores. Gross margin improved to 7.8% from 7.3% in Q4 FY26, and EBITDA loss narrowed to INR15 crores from INR20 crores. PAT of INR2 crores compared with a loss of INR13 crores in Q4 FY26 but remained below the INR26 crores reported in Q1 FY26. Management said July revenue was about INR150 crores (subject to audit) and that it does not expect EBITDA positivity for the next two to three years at group level.

financial_highlights.change: from loss of INR20 crores (-5.5%) in Q4 FY26
from loss of INR13 crores in Q4 FY26; below INR26 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: July FY27 revenue (monthly ARR, subject to audit)

segments.name: RetailerShakti
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 48% YoY and remains the principal growth engine; gross margin about 7.8% and EBITDA close to break-even, with management targeting positive EBITDA in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: SastaSundar (B2C via Health Buddy franchisees)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 44% YoY; management attributes about 90% of its EBITDA loss to technology build-up and says the model spends about 15% of revenue on building it. Segment P&L is not disclosed.

segments.name: JITO private label
segments.commentary: Sales rose from about INR25 lakhs in Q4 FY26 to about INR79 lakhs in Q1 FY27 (about 200% growth), with gross margin said to be above 50%; still a very small share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Entire FY27 gross margin to be maintained at 8% plus; medium-term industry gross margin of about 12% cited as target.
RetailerShakti expected to reach positive EBITDA in Q3 FY27.
Management described FY27 as possibly the best year in company history, with Q1 as the best quarter ever; no formal annual revenue guidance given.
Company not expected to be EBITDA positive for the next two to three years; focus stated as cash flow and capital efficiency.
RetailAir AI-monitored SaaS for retailers scheduled to launch in Q2 FY27.
Existing plus side-extension fulfilment capacity said to support revenue up to about INR3,000 crores; existing capacity described as running at about 90%.
capex_capacity: New warehouses: Noida operational (new facility starting 17 August); West Bengal partly done; Guwahati 75,000 sq ft rented, owned construction to start in about 6 months.
Udaipur construction started; Patna and Lucknow to start in about 2-3 months; Ranchi warehouse planned in Jharkhand.
Management says it intends to own fulfilment infrastructure rather than rely on third-party warehouses; no capex quantum disclosed.
JITO conversions: 19 Health Buddies converted to JITO, 25 in pipeline; about 50% of Health Buddies expected to convert within 3 months.
demand_pricing: Customer base: about 75,000 retail pharmacies served, 40,000 active in last 30 days; average wallet share about 2%.
Order-size mix: 69.4% of RetailerShakti business from orders above INR2,500 and 42.4% above INR5,000; 69.2% of SastaSundar orders above INR1,000.

Geography: about 67% of RetailerShakti and 78% of SastaSundar business from tier 2 and tier 3 markets; West Bengal share about 70% per analyst question, with management citing about 30% now from West Bengal in the call.
Expansion into Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan; Northeast cited as the fastest-growing region.
Sourcing: over 95% of purchases direct from pharma companies; purchase returns below 1%; more than 50,000 SKUs from over 1,000 vendors.
Management estimates current market share in Kolkata and West Bengal at about 3-4%, with a target of about 7% in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are gross and EBITDA margins for RetailerShakti in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin about 7.8%; EBITDA close to break-even, with positive EBITDA expected in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 revenue aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not give annual projections; July revenue was above INR150 crores (subject to audit), which it said investors can extrapolate.

qa_highlights.question: How will gross margin ramp, and what is the JITO contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects blended B2B and B2C gross margin to move toward about 12%, driven by volume, wallet share and private label; it declined to give a JITO share target but said internal projections exceed analyst scenarios of 5-6% of revenue within three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SastaSundar burn and its split?
qa_highlights.answer: Lokesh Agarwal put the burn at about 25-30% marketing and advertising and 40-45% technology; management said segment P&L is not yet separable because procurement, fulfilment and tech are integrated.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the EBITDA break-even timeline moved from one or two years to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied any postponement, saying RetailerShakti is near break-even and that break-even at group level was never promised for the current year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warehouse and fulfilment capacity status?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing infrastructure can handle about 100% growth from current levels (INR2,500-3,000 crores), with existing plus side extensions sufficient up to about INR3,000 crores revenue; company operates last-mile riders on its own payroll.

risks_watch: SastaSundar burn (technology and marketing) continues with no segment disclosure; management said segment P&L carve-out is in progress with no timeline.
PAT of INR2 crores is below Q1 FY26 INR26 crores; EBITDA still negative at INR15 crores.
Gross margin of 7.8% is below management's 8%-plus full-year target and far below the 12% industry benchmark it cited.
Treasury income cited as a source of 7-8% of revenue; in response to a question, management confirmed it as treasury income, so core operating revenue quality is a question.
Pending SEBI approval for the merger and demerger scheme; management said it is on track and that stock exchange queries are being answered.
Check RetailAir launch in Q2 FY27 and whether the claimed working-capital and inventory benefits materialise.
533259|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, JITO and the long-term model, but evasive on specifics such as segment burn, SastaSundar losses, and quantitative JITO targets. Management repeatedly deflected EBITDA questions toward cash flow and capital efficiency.

511196|2026-06.headline: Can Fin Homes Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 29% YoY to INR 2,609 crores, but rundown of INR 1,857 crores absorbed the AUM gain.
511196|2026-06.overview: Disbursements of INR 2,609 crores beat the INR 2,500 crore internal plan and grew 29% YoY across all six zones. Book rundown rose to INR 1,857 crores (from INR 1,730 crores in Q4), mainly from part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crores after the annual-to-quarterly reset, so net AUM growth was about 10.8% YoY. Yield held at 9.81% and cost of borrowing fell to 6.98%, lifting spread to 2.83% and NIM to 3.81%. Management reaffirmed 14% AUM growth and a 10 bps credit cost for FY27, while ROA slipped to 2.39% on higher opex and an IT project rollout is underway across 250 branches.

segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 1,650 crores, up 28% YoY; accounted for about 63% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Non-housing / LAP
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 958 crores, up 32% YoY; about 37% of Q1 disbursements.

segments.name: Self-employed (SENP)
segments.commentary: Disbursements up 44% YoY; current NPA around 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% in salaried, per management.

segments.name: Karnataka / Telangana
segments.commentary: All six zones grew; Karnataka grew 18% YoY (lowest zone), Telangana slightly higher. IT-sector exposure about 6% of customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crores with 14% AUM growth; management may push to INR 13,200-13,400 crores if needed to offset higher rundown.
Q2 FY27 disbursement target INR 3,000 crores; quarterly path then steps up to INR 3,500 crores and INR 4,000 crores in Q3 and Q4 per prior plan.
NIM to be maintained at 3.81% plus; Q2 incremental bank borrowing at 7.25-7.5% expected to add only marginal cost, on new loans only.
Credit cost guided at 10 bps for FY27; management sees no challenge to this.
Cost-to-income ratio around 19.5% for FY27, trending back toward 18% over about three years.
Remaining 245 branches to move to new IT platform by end of Q2, in tranches at month-end (July, August, September); update expected around September.
Opex: about INR 40 crores of further IT-related costs yet to come; no other major surprises expected.
capex_capacity: New LOS/LMS/report-generation platform live in 5 pilot branches from 8 July 2026, with sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS collections and closures processed.
Rollout to remaining 245 branches (250 total) planned within Q2 FY27, migrating month-end data in tranches.
Management expects about six months for new branches to stabilise on the new system; staffing benefits expected this year with sales additions from existing headcount.
APF (apartment finance) approvals up to 331 projects; per-project exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.
demand_pricing: No demand slowdown seen across geographies; partner banks willing to sanction, including a couple of large sanctions.
Bank borrowing rates for new loans now 7.25-7.5% vs about 6.95% last year; existing loans unchanged.
Special-rate threshold raised from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh loans, to offset higher incremental borrowing costs.
Customer pricing range about 8.4% (best, salaried, CIBIL above 725, INR 25 lakh+) to about 12.5% (non-salaried, non-housing, S3); blended yield 9.81%.
Competition: LIC and Bajaj Housing are the main rivals in branches; Bajaj growing around 25-30% per analyst comment, with its technology edge cited.
Best rate gap to banks widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps after repo cuts; management says it cannot close the gap cheaply.
82% of loans now have CIBIL score above 700 (vs about 75% earlier); 80% of business sourced via DSA.

511196|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
511196|2026-09.overview: Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.

segments.name: Branches live on new system (Project Tejas)
segments.commentary: Rollout in phases: 11 branches in July (5 old, 6 new), 89 in August (75 old, 14 new), 77 old in September and 98 in October (93 old plus 5 new). Disbursements at branches during their go-live month dropped about 70-75%, recovering to 80-90% of prior run-rate the following month.

segments.name: Branches not yet migrated (93-branch cohort)
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement was INR435 crore in Q1 and rose to INR454, INR458, INR424 and INR481 crore in the months of July-September per management's slide 20 data (management's figures; not independently verified).

segments.name: Sales team channel
segments.commentary: Sales team headcount about 90 now, targeted at 150 by year-end and 250 in FY28; management expects INR1,500-1,600 crore from sales in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Disbursement has stabilised at INR230-250 crore per period, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement guidance held at INR13,000 crore (20%+ growth over INR10,500 crore in FY26); Q3 target about INR3,500 crore with the shortfall to be recovered in Q4.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 13-14%, closer to 14%; management said the 15% AUM growth figure for FY28 is a resultant of disbursement and rundown.
FY28 disbursement internal target INR16,000 crore (about 22% growth), implying 15%+ AUM growth, closer to 15.5%.

Spread and NIM guidance of 2.75% and 3.75% maintained; management said it will pass through rate hikes, with about 12-13 bps of liability cost increase on the full book from the 25 bps repo hike and 10 bps passed on so far.
FY27 credit cost guidance of 10 bps maintained; gross NPA expected to fall in H2.
Plans to draw NHB refinance earlier, from Q3 if sanctions are higher, to benefit from lower rates; exploring an additional refinance limit.
capex_capacity: Project Tejas fully live: LOS and LMS live across all branches as of 1 October 2026; modules including risk, ALM, borrowings (by September 2025 onward) and deposits/DMS (January) implemented per management.
25 of 28 branches planned for FY27 are already operational with staff; these are expected to contribute in Q3 and Q4.
Branch expansion: about 12 branches added in UP in the last year, per management.
About 129 staff who were deployed on the IT project are being redeployed to branches and departments, with some support retained for 1-2 months.
demand_pricing: Management said underlying demand is robust with no change, and attributed the Q2 shortfall to process changes (about 8-10 additional OTPs per borrower and co-borrower), a 5-day post-month data handover lag, and a new Telangana Section 22 sub-registrar verification requirement.
Housing loan rate raised by 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 (new customers from 12 October); about 87% of floating book is on quarterly reset, about 12-13% on annual reset.
Management expects a 25 bps repo hike to translate into about 12-13 bps on the book, with plans to pass on about 15 bps next time.

Prepayment rate was about 15.5-16% historically and about 17-17.5% recently; management said a 100 bps rise could narrow the rate gap by around 60 bps, reducing prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.
Higher-ticket (INR30 lakh+) loans have grown, and the company is also looking at AHF-linked INR15-25 lakh loans as NHB AHF share rises.
PMAY 2.0 uptake described as slow relative to CLSS-1, with limited presence in the high-need states (Odisha, Bengal, Bihar, UP).
Management said the sales team contributed INR560 crore in H1 FY27 and targets about 20% of disbursement from sales in FY28.

544466|2026-06.headline: Aditya Infotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 89.5% YoY to INR1,402 crore; EBITDA margin 14.8%, adjusted PAT INR142.2 crore.
544466|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR1,402 crore grew 89.5% YoY, with CP PLUS contributing about 87% of revenue and IP products about 79% of the CP PLUS portfolio. EBITDA rose 20% YoY to INR208 crore, with margin up 604 bps to 14.8%, helped by product and brand mix and operating efficiencies. Gross margin was 30.8%, up 8-10 bps YoY but moderated from Q4 as lower-cost inventory was exhausted. Adjusted PAT of INR142.2 crore rose 332.5% YoY, aided by a 59% fall in finance costs; management reiterated its FY27 EBITDA guidance of 14-15%.

segments.name: CP PLUS (brand)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 87% of Q1 revenue; IP products were about 79% of the CP PLUS portfolio, reflecting shift to higher-value AI surveillance.

segments.name: Nexivue (second brand)
segments.commentary: Rollout being accelerated in coming months with a wider portfolio to extend channel coverage; no revenue disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 14-15% reiterated; Q1 at 14.8%; management will stick to guidance and revisit after H1 results.
FY27 revenue guidance cited by an analyst as INR60-65 billion; management did not dispute it on the call.
Price increases of 10-20% taken so far by product; expected 15-20% cumulative by end of H1 and about 25% for FY27 overall.
Backward-integration plants (housing and enclosures) operational by Q3 FY27; in-house scale manufacturing to kick off in Q3-Q4 FY27.
CP PLUS Pro series and Home IoT products targeted to go live by end-Q3/beginning-Q4 FY27; exports expected to be significant in 18-24 months.
Corelink Cable JV (with Orient Cables) to start commercial production by end of FY27.
capex_capacity: Current capacity about 2.5 million units per month at Kadapa; utilisation about 85-90%.
Plan to roughly double capacity in the next three years via Kadapa expansion (land acquisition in final stages) and a second cluster in Greater Noida (land identified, allocation applied).
Adding three FA lines and one MI line in August; total 42 FA, 4 MI and 12 SMT lines by end-August.
Corelink Cable JV plant in Rajasthan of about 1 lakh sq ft, expected commercial production by end of FY27.
New corporate office and R&D centre inaugurated 2 August 2026; three R&D centres operating (Noida, Ahmedabad, Taiwan), Bengaluru opening shortly.
Lens backward-integration: trial automatic line being set up; fully automated plant planned.
demand_pricing: Market share 43.3% in Indian video surveillance in FY26 (Frost & Sullivan), roughly doubled over the period shown.
Price hikes of 10-20% by product, taken monthly, bi-monthly or quarterly, to pass through DDR and SOC cost inflation; management says no major consumption impact seen so far.
STQC norms bar Chinese semiconductors and memory; about 40+ brands now certified, so competition is rising, though management says scale helps it secure components.
Management is moving to top-down demand generation targeting enterprise, government and AI projects through SIs and channel.
Imported BOM: about 35% from Taiwan (semiconductors), 15-20% passives (Taiwan and China); current mix about 55-60% imported and 40% domestic, targeted over the next two quarters.
No impact from the Middle East crisis on supply chain so far; some forex impact noted, which is hedged.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes were taken this quarter, and is there a gap between current market prices and inventory cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Hikes ranged 10-20% by product, passed gradually to avoid a shock to consumers; management expects to keep passing costs through in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What margin improvement can be expected from backward integration in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify; said housing, enclosures, cable connectors, lenses and later bare PCBs add basis points, and semiconductors and passives will not be localised.

qa_highlights.question: Can new categories add INR5,000-10,000 crore of TAM?

544882|2026-06.headline: Shankesh Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR424 crore and PAT to INR43 crore, but management gave few numbers to explain the margin jump.
544882|2026-06.overview: Maiden earnings call after the August 2026 listing on NSE and BSE. Revenue from operations was INR424 crore (up 55% YoY from INR273 crore), gross profit INR66 crore, EBITDA INR61 crore and PAT INR43 crore. Management attributed growth to customer relationships and product mix, while stating volumes were roughly flat YoY. Analysts repeatedly pressed for quantified margin bridges, volume data and gold-inventory gains; management mostly answered qualitatively and offered to provide more detail later.

financial_highlights.change: +55% YoY from INR273 crore; QoQ not stated
+323 bps YoY and +323 bps QoQ as stated on the call

INR1,631 crore / INR158 crore / INR107 crore
financial_highlights.change: FY23 to FY26 3-yr revenue CAGR ~21.5%; EBITDA CAGR ~90.1%; PAT CAGR ~120%

segments.name: Corporate customers
segments.commentary: Contributed 66% of Q1 FY27 revenue, up from 55% in FY24 and 64% in FY26. Corporate clients select from company designs, and co-creation designs are billed through sales invoices, with advances given only sometimes.

segments.name: Non-corporate (single-store retail)
segments.commentary: Contributed 34% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management says the company serves around 800+ customers across India.

segments.name: 22-karat jewellery

segments.name: 18-karat jewellery
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q1 FY27 mix. Revenue grew from INR18 crore in FY24 to INR221 crore in FY26. Management says it earns a 'bit higher' margin than 22-karat, not a dramatically higher one.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue share)
segments.commentary: West India 32%, East India 28%, South India 21%, North India 18%. Core markets are Maharashtra, Bihar, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 55% YoY growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were approximately the same YoY, so growth came from product mix and customer relationships. No quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin, given EBITDA of about 14% in Q1 after 9.5% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins move quarter to quarter with product mix and that the company focuses on profit amount rather than percentage. It did not commit to a sustainable margin range.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: The company buys gold equal to what it sells on the same day at market price. Inventory is carried at a weighted-average cost that management says is below market, so no hedging is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion comes from product mix and how much from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix was one factor and gold-price gains add 1-3 percentage points YoY. Analysts disputed that Q1 had gold gains, and management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: How is growth funded and what is the working-capital cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Profits are reinvested, and the bank lines are open. The IPO raised equity to about INR450 crore to fund working capital. Management said the business needs more working capital as it grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers moving karigar work in-house, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said handcrafted, co-created bridal designs and long-standing relationships protect the business. It gave no figures to show the moat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did job-worker count fall and employee cost drop QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers larger, organised contract manufacturers. Employee cost fell because Q4 included an ex-gratia payment to directors, which will not recur.

543689|2026-06.headline: Uniparts Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR347 crore and EBITDA 55% to INR90 crore, with management guiding FY27 growth a few points above FY26's 21%.
543689|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR347 crore (+27% YoY), with EBITDA of INR90 crore (+55% YoY, +10% QoQ) and PAT of INR57 crore (+64% YoY, +11% QoQ). Management said the quarter was in line with its quarterly guidance and above its annual guidance. Construction equipment is now 45% of revenue and drove growth, while large ag is at its cyclical trough and growth there comes from new wins. Aftermarket was flat YoY in absolute terms but fell to about 12% of revenue as OEM business grew faster. Net cash is about INR190 crore and the company is debt-free, with about half a dozen acquisition targets under review.

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Now 45% of total revenue and the main growth driver in Q1 FY27; momentum that began in 2H CY2025 has continued, supported by US and European infrastructure spend.

segments.name: Large agricultural equipment
segments.commentary: Conditions subdued; management expects about a 15-16% decline in CY2026 after about 30% in CY2025. Growth is from new wins, particularly in Europe, not market recovery.

segments.name: Small agricultural equipment
segments.commentary: India performing well on government subsidies and mid-to-high HP adoption, with strong new wins. Western small ag still soft but volumes have started recovering after three years of decline.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: About 12% of Q1 FY27 revenue (vs 15% in FY26 and 20% in FY25), flat YoY in absolute terms; tariff-driven price volatility deferred channel purchases.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth to be a couple of percentage points above FY26's 21% growth, per management; Q2 FY27 expected to be in line with Q1.
Management expects FY27 EBITDA margin comfortably above 20%; long-run cycle margin guidance remains about 20% (peak to trough).
Second half expected to be better than first half, linked to the ag recovery.
Mexico facility: first customer deliveries from the warehouse expected in Q3 FY27; FY27 Mexico revenue in mid-single-digit USD million.
Warehouse sales expected to stay in a 52-56% range over the next 12-18 months.
Material cost range of 34-37% of revenue is considered sustainable; fabrication vertical expected to become meaningful in 18-24 months.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of INR12 crore; organic capex (fresh equipment plus repairs and maintenance) guided at 2.5-3.5% of revenue.
Fabrication facility for small and medium-sized fabrication set up about 2.5 years ago; now in deep discussions with OEMs to supply fabrications.
Restoration of the Ludhiana finishing shop is on schedule; customer supply uninterrupted.
Mexico operations on track; Phase 2 may add manufacturing in Mexico.
demand_pricing: Channel mix: warehouse sales about 56% of Q1 FY27 revenue (vs 50-52% in Q1 FY26); locally made and locally sold about 22% (vs about 25%); the balance is direct exports.
Margin hierarchy by channel: locally made and sold is lowest; direct exports are the base (about 20% margin); warehouse sales are highest.
Product margins stated as broadly similar across three-point linkage, precision machined parts and fabrication; material consumption differs by product mix.
New business order book over INR225 crore on a trailing 12-month basis; new wins split roughly equally between Europe and US, with the majority of wins in ag and construction.
Above-70 HP three-point linkage is a single-digit market share with a major European OEM win in FY26; below-70 HP is dominant share globally.

qa_highlights.question: Will the construction share of revenue structurally rise and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said construction is 45% of revenue; drivers (new wins, industry recovery, wallet expansion) are multi-quarter. Mix will rebalance as ag recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Is construction higher margin than tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Product margins are fairly similar; differences come from channel. Warehouse sales are highest margin, direct exports about 20% base, and locally made/sold lowest.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on acquisitions and their revenue timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About a dozen targets evaluated since IPO in hydraulics, fabrication and PTO; about half a dozen currently under close review. Targets must be ROCE/ROE accretive within 18-30 months, manageable, and not deeply distressed.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 33.3% material cost and the gross margin level?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly product mix (three-point linkage, precision machined parts, fabrication have different material consumption), plus channel mix; inventory gain only about INR1 crore. Material cost range 34-37% is typical.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the aftermarket?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat in absolute terms YoY; demand deferred by tariffs and inflation. Management expects normalisation over the next 12 months as tariffs have come down.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to gain share in large ag?
qa_highlights.answer: Share is lower due to OEM validation and testing cycles; FY26 wins are now flowing into P&L, and deep discussions are ongoing on several opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2.5-3.5% capex guidance inclusive of acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It covers organic capex (fresh equipment and R&M). Acquisitions would use the INR190 crore cash and could involve debt; the balance sheet is strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 expected to be in line with Q1 and robust; H2 expected to be better than H1, tied to the ag recovery.

risks_watch: Large ag remains at cyclical trough in CY2026 (about 15-16% decline expected); recovery is only expected through CY2027.
Western small ag recovery is early and consumer buying for big-ticket items remains deferred due to economic uncertainty.
Aftermarket softness: tariffs and West Asia-driven inflation; management expects normalisation over the next 12 months.
Input cost and supply chain pressure from the West Asia situation.
Margin sensitivity to warehouse sales mix, currency movements and industry recovery pace.
Acquisition execution: no deal yet despite about a dozen targets evaluated since IPO; timing and value accretion uncertain.
Mexico warehouse ramp: first deliveries expected Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: About 25% in Q1 FY27; about 24% in Q4 FY26 (as stated on call)
33.3% of revenue (includes about INR1 crore inventory gain)

524372|2026-06.headline: Orchid Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 15% YoY to INR304 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR25 crore, on a merged Dhanuka basis.
524372|2026-06.overview: Orchid Pharma reported Q1 FY27 on a combined basis after the Dhanuka Laboratories merger (effective 10 July 2026, appointed date 1 April 2024), with FY25 and FY26 restated. Revenue from operations rose to INR304 crore from INR263 crore, and gross margin improved about 3 percentage points to 33%. EBITDA rose to INR25 crore from INR10 crore a year earlier. Management described the quarter as mediocre and said recovery would be gradual, with cephalosporin pricing still under pressure from overcapacity. Project milestones for 7-ACA (March 2027) and cefiderocol (commissioning December 2026) were reiterated.

up ~3 percentage points from ~30% in Q1 FY26
up from INR10 crore in Q1 FY26
down from INR1,398 crore in FY25
down ~4 percentage points from ~36% in FY25
EBITDA loss ~INR50 lakh, much better than prior quarter

segments.name: Cephalosporin API / core business
segments.commentary: FY26 volumes and pricing fell 15-20% by product in a difficult cephalosporin year. Cefixime faces the most margin pressure, mainly in rest-of-world markets. 7-ACA pricing has been stable for about a year.

segments.name: Exblifep (Cefepime-Enmetazobactam)
segments.commentary: Europe volumes grew about 300% QoQ in Q3 FY26, about 170-175% in Q4 FY26 and about 50% in Q1 FY27. The Russia licence has an estimated 10-year value of about USD178 million, not current revenue. South Africa registration is done and GCC coverage is in place, but Middle East rollout is delayed by regional conflict.

segments.name: AMS (Antimicrobial Stewardship)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR5 crore in Q1 FY27 from Orblicef and other brands. Quarterly EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR50 lakh.

segments.name: NP-NC (Dhanuka Laboratories)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21 crore in Q1 FY27, against an earlier quarterly run-rate of INR20-25 crore. Management said it would not reach 25% of revenue in 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give FY27 YoY revenue growth guidance; it said it hopes for better QoQ sales in H2, when regulated demand is seasonally stronger.
Merger synergies are expected to show initial benefits from FY28.

Cefiderocol: facility commissioning targeted for December 2026, then validation and initial batches in January-March 2027. Indian approval expected 6-9 months after that, subject to a DCGI trial waiver, so around Q3 FY28.
7-ACA (Jammu): first commercial batch targeted by March 2027. Ramp-up to 80-100% utilisation within the first year, with long-term split of 80% captive and 20% third-party sales.

US formulations strategy: guidance still 2030, with annual updates only. Generic ANDA filings from the cefiderocol facility take a few years; some new molecules may be filed by end of next year, with nothing commercial before 2028.
capex_capacity: 7-ACA project capex about INR750 crore, with commissioning and first commercial batch targeted by March 2027.
Cefiderocol project capex about USD20-25 million; facility commissioning by December 2026.
Management said FY27 capex is not significantly large beyond completing the 7-ACA and cefiderocol projects.
Equipment originally sourced from China was rerouted through Italy, adding execution complexity without changing timelines.

Jammu site chosen for low power costs, abundant water and cheap steam from agricultural waste, plus GST benefit. PLI incentive expected for 2 years, with extension to be sought after the plant starts.
demand_pricing: Management said the industry still has overcapacity and cutthroat competition in non-regulated markets.

7-ACA weighted average price about USD60/kg per management, stable over 10-12 years. 7-ACA supply is concentrated among 3-4 Chinese producers (Sinopharm Weiqida, Zhuhai United, Yili Pharmaceutical, Livzon named).
Cefixime is under the most margin stress, driven by rest-of-world volumes.
Management expects regulated-market demand to improve over the next 2-3 quarters, with H2 seasonally stronger.
Ceftriaxone non-sterile supply from the new 7-ACA-linked capacity is planned for other Indian sterile manufacturers, which currently import from China.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover in H2 FY27 or only in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-regulated competition will persist and is hard to predict. It hopes regulated demand improves over the next two to three quarters, and called Q1 mediocre.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 7-ACA ramp-up and captive vs third-party split?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up to 80-100% by the end of year one, starting slowly. Long-term guidance is 80% in-house and 20% third-party. All output goes in-house until customer GMP approvals are obtained.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is budgeted for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant new capex beyond completing 7-ACA (INR750 crore) and cefiderocol (USD20-25 million).

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth reach about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not be prudent to give an annual growth number at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Exblifep partner pipeline and FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Advanced talks for South America, Mexico, Philippines, Thailand, Morocco and Australia. Management does not guide yearly numbers; the USD1-2 billion is lifetime potential. Management hopes for three or four more agreements by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk of Chinese 7-ACA price cuts once the plant is running?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese producers have stable pricing and no cartel-like Pen G situation, so it sees little room for drastic cuts. It also acknowledged that Chinese pricing is unpredictable and that the company is working on yield and tighter concentration as its plan A.

501455|2026-06.headline: Greaves Cotton Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% YoY to INR975 crores, but margins fell 2-2.5 percentage points on investments and commodity costs.
501455|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 31% YoY to INR975 crores and core businesses grew 16% to INR710 crores (19% like-for-like after portfolio exits). Margins came under pressure by 2 to 2.5 percentage points, which management attributed to about 1.5 points of deliberate Greaves.Next investments and commodity inflation (platinum, aluminium, steel, fuel) that pricing has only partly offset. Management said Q2 will be marginally better than Q1 and H2 better than H1, and that it remains committed to full-year FY27 margin targets. GEML revenue was about INR270 crores, roughly double last year, with market share reported at 5.6% in June.

segments.name: Energy Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 21% YoY; medium-horsepower gensets grew 32% YoY. A pilot BESS facility was commissioned and a large institutional order covering supply, installation, commissioning and aftersales was executed.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY; automotive engines grew 36% YoY. Retail aftermarket pruning is complete (2-wheeler spares, lead-acid batteries, multi-brand EV retail, farm equipment exited). Excel grew 14% YoY.

segments.name: Industrial Solutions
segments.commentary: Reported revenue flat YoY and 9% growth after portfolio rationalisation. FM-UL compliant firefighting engine exports started and a large defence order was completed.

segments.name: Greaves Electric Mobility (GEML)
segments.commentary: Record Q1 volume growth of 101% YoY vs industry 75%. Market share rose to 5.6% in June from 4.5% exit FY26; 2-wheeler revenue up ~120% and 3-wheeler up ~80% YoY. Dealer network expanded from ~300 to 600.

segments.name: Greaves Finance (GFL)
segments.commentary: AUM at INR560 crores, growing; Board approved an additional ~INR50 crores investment.

guidance_outlook: Greaves.Next target of 16-20% revenue CAGR for the next few years reiterated; management says it is on track for the 16% growth guided for the current period.
Price increases and cost-avoidance measures expected to show from Q2, with full benefit in H2 FY27.
Q2 margin expected marginally better than Q1; H2 expected to make up any H1 shortfall; full-year FY27 margin target reiterated.
GEML expected to move into positive EBITDA in 4 to 6 quarters; management declined to give specifics.
GEML double-digit national market share targeted in 4 to 8 quarters, based on roughly 1-1.5 points of share gain every 3 to 4 quarters.
Current capital infusion expected to fund GEML for about 2 years including capex, with burn rates now in single digits.
capex_capacity: GEML invested INR331 crores via rights issue (total INR530 crore issue, fully subscribed by GCL and Abdul Latif Jameel in proportion to holding).
GEML 2-wheeler production capacity is about 480,000 units.
Robotic gantry cell commissioned at CSN facility; Excel debottlenecking added 10-15% output; Excel pushpull cable utilisation at 70-75%, rubber line just starting.
Pilot Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) facility commissioned; commercial launch targeted in subsequent quarters.
Core business capex stated as on track; 650 kVA own engine launched last quarter.
demand_pricing: GEML 2-wheeler run rate roughly 9,000-10,000 units in the latest quarter; growing ~2,000 units per quarter.
Raw material price indexing for OEM contracts applies with a lag; aftermarket pricing passed through via distributors.

Strong demand for medium-horsepower gensets in industrial and commercial applications; AI data-centre demand described as strong, with a strategic supply agreement with a large global engine maker for larger sizes.
Excel: business restarted from Europe and expected from the US after a Russia-Ukraine-related export setback last year.
International business is about 13% of core revenue; Greaves International Trading FZE set up in Dubai for Middle East and Africa.

qa_highlights.question: How has margin erosion split between OEM and aftermarket/retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity costs hit all products. OEM contracts have indexing with a lag, while aftermarket pricing is easier to pass on; price increases have been taken in both.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin drop is investment versus commodity cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar attributed about 1.5 percentage points to additional investments; the rest is the inflation-price lag, which should narrow in Q2 and fully in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is GEML's growth sustainable and when does it turn EBITDA-positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said per-unit losses have fallen sharply and EBITDA could turn positive in 4 to 6 quarters, without committing to timing or scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why does GFL, an EV financing NBFC, exist in a pruned portfolio, and is it brand-agnostic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GFL is part of the EV ecosystem; its share of GEML financing is near double digits and rising. Vikas Singh said financing partners are brand-agnostic by nature.

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough cash for the investee investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar said standalone liquidity as of March 2026 covers the INR50 crore GFL and INR331 crore GEML investments plus Q1-Q2 capex and dividends, and that the core business generates enough cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is motorcycle entry planned for GEML?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said motorcycle prototypes are underway; the scooter opportunity is also large and prioritisation is under leadership review with no timing decided.

risks_watch: Margins: Q1 margin down 2-2.5 pts; recovery depends on Q2-H2 pricing and cost savings, and the full-year target is contingent on H2 catch-up.
Commodity and geopolitical cost pressure (West Asia developments) may outlast the pricing actions.
GEML is still loss-making with a 4-6 quarter timeline to positive EBITDA; management gave no firm timing.
Excel revenue of about INR66-70 crores and export-led recovery depend on new Europe and US customers.
Greaves Technologies had earlier slippages; management said it is still stabilising and cited one pilot design-work order.
Unallocable expenses of INR25.82 crores in segment results; the company said these are now folded into core business P&L (slide 27).

539141|2026-06.headline: UFO Moviez Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹1,118 mn (vs ₹1,090 mn YoY) and advertisement revenue grew 33% YoY, helped by Dhurandhar spillover.
539141|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose about 3% YoY to ₹1,118 mn, while EBITDA was flat at ₹189 mn versus ₹193 mn a year earlier and PAT fell to ₹56 mn from ₹65 mn. Management credited a 33% YoY jump in advertisement revenue to the spillover from "Dhurandhar" and to annual advertisers onboarded around it. Product sales declined YoY, driven by roughly ₹7 crore lower international sales because Dubai imports were delayed by the regional war; management says these orders remain in hand. Releases fell to 399 titles in the quarter from 456 in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Advertisement revenue grew 33% YoY, with spillover from Dhurandhar and new annual advertisers. Advertising footprint is 3,891 screens (2,565 multiplex, 1,326 single).

segments.name: Product sales
segments.commentary: Declined YoY mainly due to international product sales falling about ₹7 crore on Dubai import delays. Indian product sales rose marginally. International sales were over 80% of product sales until last year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects delayed international product orders to be executed in Q2 FY27, or at the latest Q3 FY27.
Q2 FY27 started with releases 'Alpha', 'Dhamaal 4' and 'Jana Nayagan'; upcoming slate includes 'Batwara 1947', 'Toxic', 'Haiwan' and 'Awarapan 2'.
Management sees a consistent content pipeline with no significant gaps this year and expects advertising growth confidence over coming quarters, without quantifying it.
Historically 30-40% of advertising revenue comes from annual advertisers; the mix may evolve with the content pipeline.
capex_capacity: Advertising footprint at 3,891 screens (2,565 multiplex, 1,326 single). No capex or screen addition plans were discussed.
Off-screen (lobby) digital advertising is an unexplored opportunity; it would require a new arrangement with theatres and separate infrastructure investment, with no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Releases in Q1 FY27 were 399 (including versions/languages) vs 456 in Q1 FY26 and 459 in Q4 FY26.

Quarter drivers: Dhurandhar: The Revenge (carried over from Q4), Malayalam 'Drishyam 3', Marathi 'Raja Shivaji', and June titles 'Welcome to the Jungle', 'Main Vaapas Aaunga' and 'Cocktail 2'. Southern regional cinema stayed subdued.
Management says tactical advertising spikes last 1-4 weeks around major releases; Dhurandhar was described as an outlier with no precedent for that level of tactical spend.
Management did not quantify the share of the 33% advertising growth attributable to Dhurandhar.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 33% advertising growth came from Dhurandhar, and will growth normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a part of the growth is attributable to Dhurandhar spillover, plus new annual advertisers. It declined to give a percentage split.

qa_highlights.question: Trade receivables: how have they moved since March 31 and what was cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: India net debtors fell to ₹89.4 crore from ₹93.5 crore; consolidated net debtors fell to ₹148.1 crore from ₹152.4 crore. Management said receivables are within historical ageing and anything over one year is fully provided.

qa_highlights.question: Is the drop in product sales a concern or seasonality?
