qa_highlights.question: Given the raw material situation, are further price increases needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is happy with the current price increases. It passes on only 50-60% of inflation, managing the rest through efficiencies, and may absorb the impact in restaurant EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is KFC's growth divergence from aggregator growth likely to persist?
qa_highlights.answer: KFC is back at 17% growth as SSSG recovers. With 5-6% SSSG, management sees KFC matching 15-20% growth, while Pizza Hut needs a unified strategy before it can expand.

qa_highlights.question: Is Sri Lanka's FY27 high single-digit growth guidance changing given inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sri Lanka guidance remains high single-digit. A single weak profitability quarter will not change the store-opening plan for the year.

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.
Medium-term growth of 20-25% CAGR referenced, with EBITDA margins above 18% (management answered 'yes').
Dossiers to reach 400+ additions, taking the total from 2,100 to about 2,500 by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: About ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over roughly 2 to 2.5 years across a new warehouse, capacity enhancement at the existing facility, and the Jammu facility (EU-GMP/PIC/S audit under way).
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.
demand_pricing: CDMO economics: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders.
Selection criteria for new products include a minimum 50-55% gross margin and customer confidence in R&D delivery. Candidate molecules include Rosuvastatin, Mirabegron, Sitagliptin and Empagliflozin.
Tiffen-Becker arrangement: transfer-priced supply with about 43% of the customer's margin shared with Ind-Swift.
Management expects no dearth of capacity for the planned growth; new partnerships under discussion with 3-4 existing overseas customers, not expected to contribute this year.

500003|2026-06.headline: Aegis Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose 212% YoY to INR545 crore and normalized EBITDA 184% to INR727 crore, driven by a record LPG distribution quarter.
500003|2026-06.overview: Management reported record Q1 FY27 results, with PAT of INR545 crore (up 212% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR727 crore (up 184%). The Gas division posted its highest-ever EBITDA of INR591 crore (up 296% YoY), with distribution volumes of 2.77 lakh MT (up 91% YoY, up 19% QoQ). Liquids EBITDA rose 28% to INR136 crore on INR178 crore revenue. Management announced several port and capacity milestones, including commissioning of a 36,000 MT ammonia terminal at Pipavav and a Board-approved 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA.

segments.name: Gas (LPG) – Logistics
segments.commentary: Throughput held steady at 1.124 million MT. Sourcing volumes rose marginally 1% YoY to 1.21 lakh MT.

segments.name: Gas (LPG) – Distribution
segments.commentary: Record 2.77 lakh MT volume. Management cites a distribution margin of INR7,000+ per MT as sustainable, versus INR4,000 historically.

segments.name: Liquids
segments.commentary: Highest-ever Q1 EBITDA of INR136 crore, with five consecutive quarters of EBITDA growth. Mangalore liquid capacity of 193,000 CBM is fully utilized after a 75,000 CBM addition.

guidance_outlook: Cumulative capex of about $1.2 billion targeted in FY27.
Capex pipeline of about $5 billion through FY2030-31; funding via equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting gearing of about 0.6.
Distribution volume: management aims for 2 million MT, now expected to cross 1 million MT this year and possibly 1.5 million MT next year; growth rate closer to 50% per management.
Logistics throughput: worst-case growth of about 25% a year, with step-up growth possible as Pipavav and KGPL enablers are used.
Mumbai 64,000 CBM liquid storage (INR125 crore) targeted for commissioning in H1 FY27.
JNPA first phase of about 100,000 CBM liquid storage targeted for Q3 FY27; Kochi additional 49,577 CBM expected early next fiscal year; Kandla CRL 4 (94,148 CBM) targeted next year.
capex_capacity: Mumbai: 334,000 CBM liquid and 21,000 MT static LPG; 64,000 CBM expansion under way.
JNPA: 101,900 CBM liquid today; about 318,100 CBM liquid, 77,236 MT LPG and a 35,000 MT bottling plant under a roughly INR1,675 crore program. Board also approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank.

Pipavav: LPG capacity now 70,800 MT after a 48,000 MT terminal commissioned June 2025; 36,000 MT ammonia terminal commissioned; VLGC-compliant jetty due this year; liquid rail gantry with 0.5 million MT/yr take-or-pay due by year-end; Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline connection expected in H1 FY27. Jamnagar-Loni LPG pipeline complete.
Kandla: 952,000 CBM liquid and 48,000 MT LPG; VLGC-compliant; CRL 4 expansion targeted next year.
Kochi: 82,545 CBM liquid today, rising to 132,122 CBM after a 49,577 CBM addition.
Mangalore: 82,000 MT LPG terminal commissioned June 2025; LPG rail gantry and bottling plant at INR52.5 crore; liquid capacity 193,000 CBM; evaluating 60,000 CBM more.
Haldia: about 25,000 MT LPG terminal under HPCL terminaling agreement to 2038; 226,890 CBM liquid storage; 3 acres of land acquired for expansion.
Vadhavan port: non-binding MoU for a potential INR20,000 crore investment, subject to approvals.
demand_pricing: Management says distribution volume growth reflects new customers, wider geography and ullage added from Pipavav and Mangalore cryogenic terminals, not only the war.

Blended distribution margin was about INR7,000/MT in FY26 and Q1 FY27. Management says the margin should be INR7,000+ going forward, supported by shipping savings from VLGC carriers (freight of about $15 vs $50 on MGCs).
Management states margins were not INR5,000 in Q4 or Q1 and said blended FY margin matters more than quarterly figures.
Ammonia: distribution to industrial customers starts within weeks of commissioning; no cylinders or gas stations. Margins not disclosed.
Management says it is a distributor, not a trader, and does not take inventory or price positions.
Morbi demand has partly restarted; management says Morbi is no longer the core of the business.
Logistics tariffs are uniform across ports; no port-wise split given.

qa_highlights.question: Is distribution volume growth ahead of expectations, and are the customer contracts sticky?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2 million MT aim predates the war and reflects infrastructure build-out; new cryogenic terminals at Pipavav and Mangalore have added ullage and geography.

qa_highlights.question: How should EBITDA per ton be viewed near term and structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR7,000+ per MT is sustainable. It expects the margin not to fall back to INR4,000, citing procurement gains from VLGC shipping as volumes rise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the per-unit margins for sourcing, logistics and distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquids EBITDA is divided by capacity (about 2 million CBM). Logistics throughput gives close to INR1,000/MT EBITDA. Sourcing is a low contributor, at about $85-90/MT.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth outlook beyond 25% CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: 25% is the benchmark for logistics; anything above depends on the enablers. Distribution growth is expected to be higher, closer to 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why not fill more storage given the ITOCHU partnership and the LPG supply deficit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not take inventory or price positions and will distribute on a monthly basis, rather than act as a trader.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash across subsidiaries fund the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: AVTL is self-funded through equity, and ITOCHU is planned to rise to 25% over three years. Standalone cash is around INR2,700 crore, and consolidated liquidity exceeds INR5,940 crore. Management will hold cash until it finds opportunities.

544008|2026-06.headline: Max Estates Q1 FY27 pre-sales of about Rs 1,100 crore (5x YoY), with consol PAT of Rs 8 crore on Rs 52 crore revenue.
544008|2026-06.overview: Pre-sales rose 5x YoY to about Rs 1,100 crore, anchored by the full sellout of Phase-1 of the Terraces at Estate 361 (about Rs 500 crore) plus Rs 600 crore of sustenance sales. Collections were about Rs 575 crore, and management said these fund construction without incremental debt on residential projects. Consolidated revenue was Rs 52 crore, EBITDA Rs 8 crore, PBT Rs 11 crore and PAT Rs 8 crore, with the P&L reflecting only a fraction of the contracted portfolio. ICRA assigned a first-time A+ (stable) issuer rating on a consolidated basis. Management declined to give FY27 sales guidance, though it did guide collections and deployment figures.

financial_highlights.metric: Lease rental income (Max Towers, Max House, Max Square)
Gross debt (incl. LRD borrowings of Rs 934 crore)

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Pre-sales about Rs 1,100 crore, with Estate 361 Terraces Phase-1 (GDV Rs 500 crore) fully sold out and sustenance sales of Rs 600 crore. Management said about 50% of sales came from new launches and 50% from sustenance.

segments.name: Commercial annuity (Max Towers, Max House, Max Square)
segments.commentary: 100% occupancy across three operating assets; lease rental income Rs 40 crore, up 5% YoY. Latest Max Towers lease at Rs 156/sq ft/month vs weighted average Rs 132, a mark-to-market upside of over 50%.

segments.name: Max Asset Services
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 15 crore in Q1, up 16% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 collections guided to Rs 2,500-2,700 crore (earlier call: Rs 2,500-3,000 crore), with about half from already-sold projects reaching construction milestones and half from fresh sales.
FY27 project deployment of about Rs 1,500-1,800 crore, leaving OCF of about Rs 750-1,000 crore for business development.
H2 FY27 new launches of about Rs 5,000-5,500 crore, plus Rs 3,000-4,000 crore of already-launched unsold inventory for sustenance sales.
Sector 59 (Golf Course Extension Road, GDV above Rs 3,500 crore) expected to launch in Q3 FY27; management has not decided whether to launch it in phases.

Max Square 2 (1 mn sq ft) OC expected by Q2 FY28, adding about Rs 125 crore to annuity; Max District (1.6 mn sq ft) OC in Q3 FY28 and Q3 FY29, adding about Rs 200 crore; combined annual rental of about Rs 700 crore at peak occupancy.
Management is not giving pre-sales guidance for FY27, citing volatile micro-economic conditions.
capex_capacity: Remaining equity and debt capex on commercial assets is Rs 1,500-1,800 crore, described as fully tied up; financial closure achieved on all commercial assets with SBI and ICICI debt sanctioned.
Long-term strategy is about 40% equity and the rest debt on commercial projects; construction finance converts to lease rental discounting on commissioning.
Under-construction commercial assets: Max Square 2, Max District and Max One.
Annual target of 2 mn sq ft of residential development additions.
Estate 105 (Noida) GDV revised up to Rs 6,000 crore on a residential mix; Phase-2 to launch in FY27.
Max One (Delhi One redevelopment): 2.5 mn sq ft, GDV about Rs 3,200 crore, annuity Rs 145 crore; sold at Rs 37,000/sq ft ex-GST, described as the highest in Noida.
demand_pricing: Delhi NCR recorded about 8,800 residential launches in Q2 CY26 (Gurgaon about 70%); about 18,500 units in H1 CY26.
Residential weighted average prices broadly stable QoQ; sales volumes across the sector moderated through the quarter.
Delhi NCR office leasing of 4.1 mn sq ft in Q2 CY26.

Pre-leasing at Max District (about 200,000 sq ft) and Max One (about 100,000 sq ft) at 25-30% premium; pipeline above 3 mn sq ft under discussion. Max Square 2 LOI for about 90,000 sq ft at 25% premium; Max District LOI for 200,000 sq ft at 35% premium.

Antara-branded senior living units sell at about a 7-10% (management also cited ~10%) premium to Max Estates units; development management fee to Antara is about 9.5% of topline on the Antara portion.
Embedded value: Rs 17,500 crore total revenue potential on launched portfolio, of which Rs 13,500 crore sold and contracted (Rs 3,500 crore collected); embedded PBT Rs 4,500-5,500 crore.

544886|2026-06.headline: Tempsens Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR118 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on higher employee cost.
544886|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 33% YoY to INR118 crores, led by Electrical Heating (+148.8% to INR25 crores) and Temperature Sensing (+42% to INR60 crores), while Specialized Cables fell 8.8% to INR32.5 crores on export order timing. EBITDA rose 15.7% to INR26.6 crores, but margin compressed about 330 bps to 22%, driven by a roughly 140 bps hit from employee cost (up 45% to INR20.4 crores) and a high prior-year gross margin base. Management guided FY27 revenue growth in line with the three-year blended growth rate and said margins should recover in H2 FY27. Four capacity projects with aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores are slated to commission between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Temperature Sensing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR60 crores, up 42%, led by thermal power and OEMs including CVD equipment makers; EDGE pyrometer series (with Micro-Epsilon) to start dispatch in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Electrical Heating
segments.commentary: Revenue INR25 crores, up 148.8% on oil and gas dispatches in India, Southeast Asia and Middle East; 5-year standard furnace supply contract signed with a life sciences OEM.

segments.name: Specialized Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crores, down 8.8% on export order timing; cable harness line launched with UL certification; Unit 8 greenfield under construction, completion by Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected in line with blended three-year growth; management pointed to about 25% in analyst's framing but said visibility improves in H2.
EBITDA margin to remain broadly similar to FY26 profile; margin recovery visible in H2 FY27 as employee cost is absorbed by revenue.
Management expects profit growth to be in line with revenue growth by end of FY27.
Lower finance cost to be visible from the coming quarter after INR55 crores of IPO proceeds used for debt repayment.
OEM and new products expected to contribute more than 25% of revenue starting FY28.
capex_capacity: Brownfield 50,000 sq ft plant in Unit 1 for OEM contact sensors, commissioning by Q3 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

50,000 sq ft plant in Unit 6 for medium-voltage heaters, completion by Q1 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR200 crores; heaters tested to 7.2 kV, explosion-proof certification targeted by Q4 FY27.
Unit 8 greenfield cable plant, completion by Q2 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR60 crores; capacity can be ramped quickly.
Victura JV to acquire 80,000 sq ft facility with existing shed; production to start by Q4 FY27, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

Aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores across four projects versus FY26 revenue of INR445 crores; existing capacity running at about 80%. Additional 25,000 sq ft planned for custom furnaces this year; land acquired for about INR25 crores in Q1 for cable expansion.
demand_pricing: Pipeline healthy across thermal and nuclear power in India and steel and glass globally; quoted pipeline in Middle East has increased but firm orders still awaited.
OEM order visibility of 9-12 months versus about 4-4.5 months order book for heavy-industry customers; furnace contract is 5 years.
Inventory of INR110-120 crores, 65-70% in raw material; raw materials booked at order receipt and price fluctuations passed through to customers.
Management says Chinese competition is limited for engineered make-to-order products; some customers shifting sourcing to India.
Export share rose to about 34%; new subsidiaries in Mexico, Poland and South Korea; Korean JV supplying battery manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: How has the fuel cell OEM order trajectory evolved and what run-rate exit FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said field trials and run-up are advanced and focus is now on scaling execution; it declined to quantify exit run-rate, calling it a work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from critical, high-barrier industries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated roughly 75-90% of revenue from critical applications, with 10-20% from regular, more competitive industries; vendor approvals can take 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the new-age industry TAM and its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify TAM; said new-age products could grow in the high 20s or 30s percent over 2-3 years. Newer products segment addressable market is about INR3,000 crores with less than 1% currently addressed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin recovery bridge and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost increase reflects headcount added for future projects; margin recovery expected to start in H2 FY27, not FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East/Africa and political situation a risk to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no negative impact seen in the next few quarters; electrification trend could be positive mid-term.

qa_highlights.question: When will the INR500 crore incremental capacity reach full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity comes online from Q1 FY28 with construction largely done by Q3 FY28; full utilisation expected around FY29-FY30, with plants typically run at about 80% maximum.

financial_highlights.change: +148.8% YoY, low base as heater facility commissioned end of Q1 FY26
+45% YoY, about 140 bps margin impact; includes INR57 lakh ESOP charge in prior-year quarter

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (excl. amortisation of acquisition and intangibles)

544613|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn; EBITDA margin 18.9%, normalized PAT Rs 1,652 mn after Bawal fire exceptional loss of Rs 1,436 mn.
544613|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 125.3% YoY to Rs 13,457 mn and EBITDA rose 140.6% to Rs 2,548 mn, with margin up to 18.9% from 17.7%. A Rs 1,436 mn provisional exceptional loss from the Bawal facility fire brought reported PAT to Rs 578 mn (4.3% margin), while normalized PAT was Rs 1,652 mn (12.3%). Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, kept the margin guidance at "sustainable to improve," and added distributors, dealers and two states. Ratlam capacity additions (2 GW solar panel, 2 GW power electronics, 2 GW battery due Q2 FY27) and stake increases in Zayo entities were the main capex and integration moves.

financial_highlights.change: expected to be fully recovered via insurance

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized PAT (ex post-tax fire provision Rs 1,074 mn)

segments.name: Residential rooftop / B2C
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% of revenue comes from the B2C channel. Sales are sold as a package of panels, inverters and batteries; no segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Off-grid vs on-grid vs hybrid
segments.commentary: Management said on-grid growth was the main driver this quarter, enabled by in-house DCR cells; off-grid is still growing but more slowly. No split was disclosed.

segments.name: Tubular batteries
segments.commentary: Tubular battery output (about 10% of revenue) was lost in the Bawal fire; management estimated the gross margin impact at below 0.5% as batteries are now bought from outside vendors.

guidance_outlook: Full-year revenue growth guidance raised to about 70% from the earlier 50%, with a stated intent to trail it upward in later quarters.
EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 'sustainable to improve' (Q1 at 18.9%).
Insurance claim on the Bawal fire (net carrying value about Rs 1,436 mn) expected to settle by end of FY27; management expects full recovery.
Ratlam 2 GW lithium-ion battery plant on track for commissioning by Q2 FY27.
FY27 gross block (incl. CWIP) expected at about Rs 1,300 cr, up from about Rs 800 cr at start of year.
Channel partner target of more than 15,000 (distributors, dealers, shoppes) by end FY28.
Zayo Energy plant expected to add Rs 400-500 cr top-line in the next financial year; Fujiyama's share of Zayo capex about Rs 50 cr.
capex_capacity: Solar panel capacity: 2 GW added at Ratlam (capitalized 14 May 2026), taking total to 3.5 GW; Ratlam running one shift and ramping in phases.
Power electronics: 2 GW facility at Ratlam commissioned in August 2026, taking total to 4 GW; initial utilization of Ratlam capacity guided at 40-50%.
Solar cell (DCR) plant at 1 GW (some reports say 1.2 GW) running at 80%+ utilization; non-Ratlam panel plants at 70-80% utilization.
TOPCon line: building complete and machine orders placed; target commissioning in about 9 months (within the next financial year per the call).
Zayo Energy/Zayo Cables: stake raised from 19% to 50% each; Zayo Energy capex about Rs 180-200 cr total, with land acquisition under way and production targeted within about one year.
demand_pricing: Management cited current PM Surya Ghar installation run rate of about 1 GW per month; about 50 lakh of the 1 crore household target covered.
Industry rooftop capacity installed to date put at over 30 GW, with about 15 GW under PM Surya Ghar; government target 90-100 GW rooftop of 300 GW solar by 2030.
System pricing quoted at Rs 26-30 per watt (BOM with panel, inverter, battery) at distributor billing level, including GST.
Industry growth rate cited at about 40%; Fujiyama estimates about 10% share of the on-grid market (not officially confirmed).
Distributors rose from 950+ to 1,150+ in the quarter; channel partners rose from about 8,900 to over 10,100 with Odisha and Uttarakhand newly moved to covered states.
Management said DCR pricing and higher realization on Mono PERC DCR panels drove the higher average realization.

qa_highlights.question: How should full-year revenue and profit be modelled after a strong Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to about 70% from 50%, citing demand and Ratlam capacity, and said it will trail the guidance upward as the year progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Will backward integration lift margins or be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCR cell capacity supports margins but raw material price volatility is a factor, and it will pass on part of the gains; margin guidance remains 'sustainable to improve'.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Bawal fire loss is recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the damaged assets with net carrying value about Rs 143 cr are fully insured, the survey is done, the full loss was booked in Q1, and claim settlement is expected by year end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 26-30 per watt figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an average distributor BOM (roughly Rs 15 panel, Rs 5 inverter, Rs 5 battery), varying with DCR/non-DCR, battery type and system type, with GST included.

qa_highlights.question: Capex funding for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution this year; about Rs 200 cr of the Rs 500 cr additional capex will be debt-funded, with Rs 100 cr from IPO proceeds and Rs 200 cr from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the TOPCon line and the lead-acid plant after the fire?
qa_highlights.answer: TOPCon commissioning is targeted within about 9 months. The fire-hit lead-acid plant will not restart until insurance work is done; the company is in talks to lease an operating plant.

risks_watch: Bawal insurance claim settlement (management targets end FY27); any delay or shortfall versus Rs 1,436 mn would hit reported earnings.
Margin sustainability as market share is pushed with price cuts and as module prices fall; non-DCR margins are under pressure.
PM Surya Ghar 2.0 is not yet notified; loan sanction and DCR supply constraints are slowing installations.
Ratlam battery plant (2 GW) commissioning in Q2 FY27 and new power electronics ramp-up at 40-50% utilization.
BIS compliance: 15 of about 500 SKUs were flagged by the authority; management says these are now certified and represent under 1% of stock value.
Revenue is not disclosed by segment, which limits visibility into on-grid, off-grid and hybrid mix.
Zayo Energy stake commitments and capex (Rs 180-200 cr total) plus the lead-acid plant lease.

544612|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.2% YoY to INR15,448 million; VAR up 18.4% to INR13,816 million, EBITDA margin 17.9% of VAR.
544612|2026-06.overview: Tenneco Clean Air India reported Q1 FY27 value added revenue (VAR) of INR13,816 million, up 18.4% YoY, with ART growing 27.9% and Clean Air and Powertrain growing 9.6%. EBITDA rose 7.9% YoY to INR2,469 million, with margin at 17.9% of VAR, down about 170 bps YoY and 43 bps QoQ as commodity inflation, rupee depreciation, Middle East-related costs and listed-company costs weighed. PAT was INR1,652 million, with management stating PAT growth tracked EBITDA growth once the prior-year Motocare one-time gain is excluded. Management said it had partially recovered non-indexed commodity costs from customers, with recovery still under discussion for the remainder.

financial_highlights.change: +7.9% YoY; margin down ~170 bps YoY and 43 bps QoQ (per analyst)
Prior-year quarter included one-time Motocare sale gain and other one-off income; PAT growth stated as similar to EBITDA growth excluding this

financial_highlights.metric: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions VAR

segments.name: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions
segments.commentary: VAR of INR6,626 million, up 9.6% YoY. Management attributes gap versus ~mid-to-high-teens industry growth to EV exclusion, a leading Japanese PV OEM where Tenneco has no business, and GST-driven demand concentrated at that OEM.

segments.name: Advanced Ride Technologies (suspension)
segments.commentary: VAR of INR7,190 million, up 27.9% YoY, now the larger segment by VAR. Capacity utilisation above 90%; new western India plant planned at about INR70 crore.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle Clean Air Solutions
segments.commentary: Value market share rose from 57% to 58% in FY2026 per management.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle shock absorbers and struts
segments.commentary: Value market share rose from 52% to 55% in FY2026 per management.

segments.name: Off-highway Clean Air Solutions
segments.commentary: Market share of 68% stated; later referred to as 60%+ in answers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex indicated at INR350-450 crore, funded through internal accruals; includes about INR140 crore for two already-announced plants and export-oriented investment; management said it may pull in or pull out based on demand and figures are indicative, not precise guidance.
Management expects demand to remain good through Q2 FY27 for Indian OEMs; margins expected to follow prior-year seasonal pattern.

Order book to be reported half-yearly; H1 order book, including domestic and export split, to be disclosed with Q2 results. Management said order book growth is unchanged from the earlier mid-teens outlook but gave no number.

Middle East conflict duration and its effect on input costs and demand; management flagged potential Q3 impact if it deteriorates.
Export headwinds from Section 232 tariffs and weak Europe/Americas macro.
BS-VII specification and timing unclear; CAFE 3 entry at a large PV OEM expected 2028-29.
Order book, export split and H1 capex to be disclosed with Q2 results.
Management flagged possible pull-in or pull-out of capex based on demand.

506655|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs.2,642 Cr and business EBITDA Rs.247 Cr for One Sudarshan; FY27 guidance held pending Q2 review.
506655|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong Q1 FY27 for One Sudarshan, with revenue from operations of Rs.2,642 Cr, business EBITDA of Rs.247 Cr and reported EBITDA of Rs.266 Cr, cited as roughly 60%+ YoY EBITDA growth and about 5% revenue growth. financial_highlights.change: from Rs.78 Cr; inventory overhead impact Rs.18 Cr

management: movement of ~2% QoQ, sustained at 50%+

segments.commentary: Business EBITDA Rs.128 Cr vs Rs.65 Cr YoY; reported EBITDA Rs.146 Cr after Rs.18 Cr inventory overhead impact. Management says business margin has been consistently double-digit historically, and sees a 6-7% level as a stepping stone to high single or low double digits.

segments.name: RIECO
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.38 Cr, with EBITDA down on execution delays (customer readiness, subcontractor manpower shortages). Management expects normalisation from Q2 and a positive EBITDA before year end.

Project Integra (One SAP) go-live and value capture delivery within FY27.

500336|2026-06.headline: Surya Roshni Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR2,046 crore and PAT 77% to INR60 crore, but steel EBITDA/ton of INR4,006 sits well below the FY27 INR4,600-4,700 guidance.

Lighting FY27: revenue about INR2,200 crore (vs INR1,809 crore FY26), value growth 19-22%, volume growth about 25%, EBITDA about INR200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income of ₹4.4 crore from power sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No; likely FX-related or export incentives. Management has not sold power; solar lapsed units were lost under the MSEDCL policy change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the ₹600-700 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Renamed the executable order book; ₹500 crore set for FY27 given hurdles, with ₹600 crore possible next year on higher capacity.

qa_highlights.question: When will the next capex and fundraising happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three good quarters needed first; land by December or March; project start by Q3 next year; fundraising ideally Q1/Q2 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Will Vestas concentration stay the same at ~₹600 crore revenue in two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Vestas wants more allocation but capacity is going to new OEMs (Nordex, Adani) each allocating ₹100-150 crore; wind is ~₹400 crore of revenue, non-wind and gearboxes ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is offshore wind or Adani 5 MW participation viable?
qa_highlights.answer: Adani 5 MW parts often exceed 30 MT, so imported from China; Adani 5.2 MW bearing (6-7 ton casting) supplied. Offshore volumes not expected for 5-10 years; company focuses on 3-4 MW onshore.

financial_highlights.change: Marginal decline in exports YoY; total YoY change not stated
Moderated in Q1; prior-year figure not stated

financial_highlights.value: ~66% utilisation of 45,000 tpa capacity (~7,400 MT implied)

financial_highlights.change: Management attributed to FX or export incentives, not power sales

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material inflation impact on PBDIT
financial_highlights.change: Recoverable via indexation with one-quarter lag

543720|2026-06.headline: KFin Q1 FY27 revenue grew 30% YoY to consolidate Ascent (ex-Ascent ~10%), while PAT was flat-to-down and EBITDA margin fell to 34.2% with Ascent.
543720|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 30% YoY, with about 9.6% growth excluding Ascent, and 2.7% QoQ including Ascent (1.6% excluding). EBITDA grew about 7.1% YoY, but consolidated EBITDA margin was 34.2% with Ascent versus 39.4% without it. PAT margin was 21% including Ascent and 26.6% excluding it, and PAT was broadly flat to marginally down YoY. Management raised its FY27 growth outlook to EBITDA growth of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, while a yield decline of about 2% QoQ in mutual funds was attributed to debt-to-liquid mix shift and provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

financial_highlights.change: About INR 200 crore to go to dividend already declared

financial_highlights.value: About 51% of EBITDA converted to free cash flow

financial_highlights.change: from US$5.7 million in Q4; US$4.4 million in Q1 FY26 (pre-consolidation), +32% YoY

segments.name: Domestic mutual fund (RTA/fund admin)
segments.commentary: Industry AUM grew about 15% YoY versus KFin about 16%; KFin's equity AUM market share rose about 80 bps QoQ. Yield fell about 2% QoQ, of which about 30% was debt-to-liquid mix and the rest mainly provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

segments.name: Issuer solutions
segments.commentary: Managed about 80% of main-board IPO issue size in Q1 and holds about 50% of NSE 500 market share (versus ~52% earlier). Corporate actions are about 30% of issuer revenue; the company guided to tepid corporate actions in Q2 due to IT services dividend deferrals.

segments.name: International (Ascent and global fund solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 200% YoY with Ascent and about 32% organically. Ascent EBITDA margin was about 8%; management targets double-digit margin within 12 months. Sequential decline ex-Ascent was attributed to pipeline timing, with growth expected above 25%.

segments.name: Alternatives (XAlt, GIFT City)
segments.commentary: About 731 funds with about 37.3% market share, targeting close to 40% with pending launches. 15 new AIF wins in Q1; the AIF business has compounded above 60% over four years and management expects at least 40% growth going forward.

segments.name: Pensions (NPS)
segments.commentary: Reached break-even last quarter and now contributes about 15%+ EBITDA margin. Manages about 2.5 million pensioners and is the second-largest CRA in India.

segments.name: Wealth management (mPower Wealth) and technology
segments.commentary: Three wealth platform mandates won. An INR 25 crore+ big-data mandate runs over about 18 months, with INR 40 crore of signed bolt-on deals across 3-15 month durations.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR guided at 18-20%, unchanged from prior guidance.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 40-45%; management aims to hold 40% threshold including Ascent by end of FY27.
FY27 visibility of EBITDA growth of about 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, ahead of the earlier high-single to low-double-digit indication.
Ascent to become EBITDA accretive by end-FY27 or early FY28; double-digit margin targeted within the next 12 months; KFin-level EBITDA margin expansion to take three to five years.
Cost optimisation benefits expected from Q2 FY27 onwards; mutual fund yield expected to stabilise, with management unwilling to guide a yield number.
Target of at least 20% of revenue from controllable (non-market) businesses; currently about 6% from VAS plus 5-6% from other non-market businesses.
capex_capacity: Ascent cost base is being rationalised through shared support functions, consolidated office space and better vendor contracts (AWS, Oracle, Microsoft); contract renewals roll into KFin structures in October and January.

Mutual fund platform transformation under FinEx: SIP processing now completes within three working days for 99.7% of transactions (versus about 21 days industry); next launch by end-calendar 2026 to automate non-commercial and purchase transactions.
Cayman Islands facility being set up to meet regulatory substance requirements, a near-term cost already in the plan.
Infrastructure cost pressure (servers, routers, laptops) noted; management will be harder on client discount negotiations.
demand_pricing: Mutual fund yield fell about 2% QoQ: debt-to-liquid shift (debt yields 2-2.5x liquid) contributed about 30% of the decline, and provisioning for a large-contract renewal this year accounted for the rest. Management guides against a fixed yield number, citing asset-mix and AMC-growth effects.
Ascent revenue hit by digital-asset fund markdowns, offset by six new fund managers with over US$100 million each (transitions taking 3-5 months) and fund launches.

Retail participation is still weak, with Demat net additions slowing despite IPOs; IPO pipeline includes PhonePe, Zepto, Jio, Manipal Health and Razorpay, plus Razorpay, Garuda and Pushp Brand mandates won.
Management expects strong corporate actions outside IT services; IT services firms have deferred dividends, which could weigh on Q2.
Pending Philippines government contract: KFin is reported as highest bidder on technical and commercial scores, but no award has been announced.

532349|2026-06.headline: TCI Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew ~9% (24th straight quarter of growth) while standalone profit turned slightly negative on lower JV dividends and bunker costs.
532349|2026-06.overview: Management reported 9% consolidated top-line growth and 7% standalone growth for Q1 FY27, with the freight business up 10-11%. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 1.6% and PAT slightly negative, largely because JV dividend income was lower; consolidated EBITDA was about 5%. Seaways margins were flat as bunker prices rose to around Rs 86,000/ton, partly offset by rate increases; the Concor JV grew about 88% and Cold Chain about 48%. Management guided supply chain to 12-15% growth and freight to 10-12%, with capex of Rs 550-600 crore for FY27 (Rs 167 crore spent in Q1).

segments.name: Supply chain (standalone)
segments.commentary: Growth moderate against a high base; EBITDA margin slightly improved but EBIT flat. Management expects 12-15% top-line growth for FY27, pick-up in H2 from new contracts and diesel pass-through bills.

segments.name: Freight
segments.commentary: Top line up ~10-11% with slight margin improvement; 10 of planned 30 new branches opened in Q1. FY27 guidance 10-12% growth with higher profitability.

segments.name: Seaways
segments.commentary: Revenue up on pricing with similar voyages (one ship dry-docked); margins flat. Bunker prices at ~Rs 86,000/ton; Q2 EBITDA guided at 25-30%, and new ships expected Sept-Oct and Oct-Nov.

segments.name: Concor JV
segments.commentary: Grew ~88% per management; revenue moderated vs last quarter per Q&A. Rail shift from road limited due to lean season and rail congestion.

segments.name: Cold Chain JV
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~48% from contracts won in Q3-Q4 FY26; still small in quantum.

segments.name: Trans System JV (Toyota-linked, Mitsui partner)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~11.5%, but margin fell to ~9% from 14-15% on pricing pressure and production cuts; profit run-rate down to ~Rs 30 crore from Rs 40-42 crore. Management sees ~10% margin as reasonable.

guidance_outlook: Supply chain revenue growth 12-15% for FY27, with pick-up expected from Q2 onwards.
Freight revenue growth 10-12% for FY27 with higher profitability year on year.
Seaways Q2 EBITDA margin guided at 25-30%; FY27 Seaways EBITDA may rise on higher depreciation from new ships, but profitability may subdue for one or two quarters after induction.

FY27 capex budget Rs 550-600 crore (management estimate Rs 500-600 crore): ~Rs 237 crore on ships, ~Rs 100 crore warehouses, ~Rs 120 crore trucks and rakes, ~Rs 100 crore warehousing equipment and IT.
JV dividend payout expected similar to last year; not expected to rise in the next year or two due to capex.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex Rs 167 crore against FY26 total of ~Rs 370 crore.
Two new ships expected in Sept-end and Oct-Nov 2026; a third ship under exploration with advance payment possible.
Dry dock: one ship completed already; one scheduled for late March 2027; dry-dock duration 25-35 days.
Freight network: 30 new branches planned for FY27, 10 opened in Q1.
Supply chain: 'trucks being added based on new contracts'; 624 rakes handled in Q1, flat YoY; 67 yards managed; three owned rakes.
demand_pricing: Auto sector accounts for ~75-80% of supply chain business; management says auto demand robust but some customers slowed in Q1 as Q4 pipeline inventory was delivered.
Bunker prices rose sharply from late Feb-March 2026 on Middle East crisis; ranged ~Rs 72,000-1,05,000/ton in recent weeks; fuel discounts no longer available.
Diesel price up ~6-7%; management estimates pass-through impact of 1-2% of revenue, with contract customers lagging.
Rail congestion and monsoon/lean season limited shift from road to rail; containers backlog ~10,000-12,000 at JNPT.
Trans System pricing pressure and production cuts at Japanese OEM clients; some low-priced business not renewed.

qa_highlights.question: Can supply chain reach 12-15% growth in H2 and how much diesel-linked price growth came in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites pipeline and new contracts from H2, plus supplementary diesel bills from mid-May; Q1 diesel-linked benefit was minimal, mostly volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Seaways profitability with bunker volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Bunker prices are volatile; Q2 EBITDA expected at 25-30%. New ships take 4-6 months to reach full utilisation; breakeven timing not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why is freight profit not improving despite the auto recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Some customers were served from Q4 pipeline inventory; longer-haul replenishment expected in subsequent quarters; mix shift and 30 new branches to drive margin, a slow process.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days ~55-56; some pressure expected from rate hikes but credit policies in place. FY27 capex mainly ships, trucks/rakes, warehouses.

qa_highlights.question: Margin impact of LTL mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: LTL gross margin ~20% vs FTL ~10%; mix shift from ~35-37% to ~40% is gradual, adding a few basis points per 1% shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Trans System margins fall and what is the JV earnings outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment in expansion, pricing pressure and lost low-priced business; ~10% margin seen as reasonable. JV profitability guided similar to last year; Toyota plant at Aurangabad to need investment next fiscal.

risks_watch: Bunker price volatility tied to Middle East hostilities could compress Seaways margins in Q2.
Supply chain growth must accelerate to 12-15% in H2 from a moderate Q1; auto customer demand timing uncertain.
Standalone PAT turned slightly negative; JV dividend income lower, affecting profit visibility.
Trans System margin decline (to ~9%) and falling profit contribution.
Working capital pressure from rate hikes; receivable days ~55-56.
Labour shortages and cost pressure in warehousing after LPG disruption; possible shutdown of gas-hit customers.

544880|2026-06.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR200 crores, with EBITDA of INR161 crores (80% margin) and a net loss of INR12 crores.
544880|2026-06.overview: Management's first earnings call after the August IPO, which raised INR4,250 crores of primary capital used for deleveraging to a proforma net debt of about INR2,500 crores at 30 June. Revenue was INR200 crores (+23% YoY) and EBITDA INR161 crores (+36% YoY). Management steered attention to a proforma cash PAT of INR116 crores, arguing the reported net loss is distorted by non-cash depreciation and pre-deleveraging interest. Leasing was 1.9 million sq ft across 13 transactions, with contracted revenue run rate at about INR967-970 crores.

financial_highlights.change: expected to fall 40-50 bps post deleveraging

segments.name: Large-format industrial and warehousing parks
segments.commentary: 29.5 million sq ft operational across 46 assets in 9 states and 10 markets; 26.9 mn sq ft on operational area, plus 2.4 mn sq ft pre-leased under construction. Yield on cost about 11-12%.

segments.name: In-city (urban mid-mile/last-mile) assets
segments.commentary: 17 assets across 7 cities, about 6-7 mn sq ft; rentals about 2.5-3x big-format; yield on cost 13-14% after CWC revenue share. Three mid-mile assets fully leased at INR65-70 per sq ft (as stated). First Pune (Pimpri) delivery targeted Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Value-added services (rooftop solar, worker accommodation, hospitality, skill centre)
segments.commentary: Rooftop solar about 38 MW, of which about 20 MW operational and 17-18 MW being operationalised. Worker accommodation of 6,000-7,000 beds under construction; target 5-10% of revenue in 4-5 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 leasing target of 6.5 mn sq ft (about 30% growth vs last fiscal), with 4-4.5 mn sq ft of incremental leasing expected over the next 9 months.
FY27 completion target of 6 mn sq ft, taking operational area to about 34-35 mn sq ft by year-end at high-90s occupancy.
Net loss expected to turn to profit from Q2 or Q3 FY27 (management guidance on reported P&L).
Capex of INR1,500-2,000 crores over next 3 years, roughly one-third internal accruals and two-thirds incremental debt.
Target to double large-format park capacity over 4-5 years; in-city 6 mn sq ft over next 3 years.
Incremental capex yield on cost guided at 13-14%; in-city construction cost about INR4,500 per sq ft with rents guided at INR70-75 per sq ft (as stated).
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 30 mn sq ft is fully paid, with approvals and financing largely in place; 25 mn sq ft of large-park development remaining.
Build cycles are 9-12 months; 20-30% of development pre-leased, with a stock-in-trade of 1.6 mn sq ft across the operational network.

Pimpri (Pune) in-city multi-storey asset targeted for Q4 FY27 delivery; a Delhi High Court case challenging the tender for 13 in-city warehouses is sub judice, with management expecting large part delivery in 12-24 months.
Approximately 1 mn sq ft delivered in Q1; 5 mn sq ft of buildings to be delivered over the next 9 months.
demand_pricing: Re-leasing spreads of 12% in Q1 (on about 300,000 sq ft expiries), versus 12-15% historically, above the 5% contractual annual escalation; WALE about 7.1 years.
Industrial-segment leases at about INR29+ per sq ft versus about INR24 for bare-bone warehousing; blended in-place rent plus CAM about INR27.20 per sq ft.
High single-digit market rent growth in deeper markets (as stated).
Expiries of about 1.4 mn sq ft in the next 9 months and 2.2 mn sq ft next fiscal (about 13% of portfolio over 21 months).
Three-fourths of Q1 leasing came from industrial customers; industrial and manufacturing customers are close to half the portfolio. Over 120 customers; nine new customers onboarded in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Does 25% volume growth plus 5% escalation imply about 30% revenue CAGR over 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described four growth engines: contractual escalations plus re-leasing spreads on 29.5 mn sq ft, 6 mn sq ft of large-park development, in-city expansion of about 2 mn sq ft a year, and value-added services at 5-10% of revenue. It did not confirm a 30% CAGR figure.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR967 crore contracted run rate translate into reported EBITDA and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-85% sits on existing assets with nearly full 12-month revenue flow expected; the 2.4 mn sq ft pre-leased, under-construction area should contribute within 9-12 months. Further 4-4.5 mn sq ft of leases are expected over 9 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for leverage, capex and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of INR1,500-2,000 crores over 3 years, funded one-third internally and two-thirds by debt. Cost of debt (about 8.2%) expected to fall 40-50 bps as ratings improve.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand beyond its 10 markets and pursue acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will explore Tier 1-minus/Tier 2 markets opportunistically (cited Nagpur, Goa, Nashik), focus on share gains in existing Tier 1 markets, and keep acquisitions (land parcels and consolidation of sub-scale platforms) central. No quantified annual addition target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive intensity in institutional supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market can absorb many more Horizon-scale players; Grade-A stock is under 500 mn sq ft nationally, and more than 90% of stock is fragmented or non-compliant.

qa_highlights.question: When will the reported P&L turn profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided that the P&L should turn black from Q2 or Q3 FY27 onwards.

544595|2026-06.headline: Orkla India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.5% to ~INR659 crore with EBITDA of INR115 crore at 17.5% margin, helped by 11.4% price-led growth.
544595|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 10.4% YoY to INR659 crore (product sales up 11.5%), ending eight quarters of deflation-hit single-digit growth. Volume growth was 1.7% reported and 4.4% excluding Kerala, where a distribution restructuring is underway. EBITDA rose 3% YoY to INR115 crore at a 17.5% margin, up 150 bps QoQ, but the base included a PLI benefit and the quarter absorbed Project Bolt digital investments. Spice inflation of about 33% YoY was passed through, with price-led contribution rising from 6.5% in Q4 to 11.4% in Q1.

financial_highlights.change: +3% YoY; +150 bps QoQ; underlying +7.2% ex-PLI base; +12.7% ex-Bolt and PLI, margin +40 bps
Base quarter aided by deflation and PLI

segments.name: Spices
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.3% YoY; ex-Kerala domestic spices NSV +16% with volume +5.2%. Pure spices (~26% of business) priced off chilli mandi rates at 10% premium; masalas (~39-40% of revenue) priced calibrated to margin threshold and competitor index.

segments.name: Convenience Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.9% YoY, growth split roughly equally between volume and price; meals grew double digit. Digital commerce mix for convenience is ~60:40 vs spices.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.8% YoY; ex-Kerala +12.8% with volume +6.3%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue +10.1% YoY; GCC +18.1%. US back to positive value growth after prior volume pressure.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give forward-looking guidance; reiterated double-digit growth as the ambition.
Further price increases 'very difficult to say'; most needed increases taken, some Q2 impact from current pricing expected.
PLI: eligibility for FY27 (last year of the scheme) uncertain; no accrual assumed yet.
Kerala restructuring to take several quarters to mature; food program substantially complete June 2026, spices and standalone modern trade still in pilot/planning.
Willing to increase A&P spend behind growth and volume.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed in the call.
Project Bolt (digital commerce capability: people, technology, analytics) underway with strategic investments booked in Q1.
Six new Gen Z innovations launched, including protein-rich breakfast and palm-oil-free products; 23 launches/re-launches in the quarter.
Non-dairy reformulation of paneer ready meals planned for UK and EU markets.
demand_pricing: Spice inflation of ~33% YoY in Q1; pricing passed through, with price-led contribution at 11.4% vs 6.5% in Q4.
Market share: +30-50 bps in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh; about -30 bps in Kerala.
Digital commerce and modern trade growing fastest; breakfast expanded in top 28 metros and wet batter into Hyderabad.
International volumes pressured in the US (unbranded/price-competitive shelves), though US value growth turned positive; GCC shelves kept fully stocked despite West Asia disruption.
Management argues spices are ~2.5% of household consumption basket, so a 30% spice inflation is a modest wallet impact; branded share tends to rise when prices spike as small brands exit.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 6.5% and Q1 11.4% price figures correct, and what are ex-Kerala consolidated revenue and volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed price-led growth moved from 6.5% to 11.4%. Ex-Kerala consolidated revenue growth 12.1% and volume growth 4.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Given spice inflation of ~30%, why are margins holding with price hikes of ~18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Pure spices (~26% of business) mirror mandi prices; masalas (~39-40%) priced calibrated to margin threshold and relative price index. Approaches differ by segment.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q1 FY26 margin inflated by one-offs, and are there IPO expenses not repeating?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 margin ~18.7% driven by ~45.6% gross margin, deflation and some PLI recognition. No material IPO expenses; a small transaction bonus was booked and the OFS costs were borne by selling shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Is mid-single-digit volume growth a safe expectation in inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume moderates with high inflation but cited 12.8% ex-Kerala domestic growth and 6.3% volume as a good trajectory; masala pricing errs on volume over margin.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for PLI benefit in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to confirm eligibility; will accrue only if eligible; FY27 is the last year of the PLI scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Profitability of digital commerce versus general trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital margins described as extremely strong, driven by a convenience-heavy mix (~60:40 convenience to spices, with blended spices outselling pure).

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Kerala restructuring not done before the IPO, and what is the market share impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Kerala learning curve, CEO change in January 2025, and project start in February 2026; Kerala share down ~30 bps, Karnataka and AP up 30-50 bps.

risks_watch: Spice input inflation (chilli +78%, coriander +40%) and West Asia freight/commodity pressure on margins into Q2.
Volume sustainability post-price hikes; ex-Kerala volume 4.4% consolidated and 6.3% domestic.
Kerala restructuring execution and share loss (~30 bps); benefits still several quarters away.
PLI eligibility for FY27, the final year of the scheme, is uncertain.
Continued US export pressure from multiple-priced products on shelves.
Digital commerce investment (Project Bolt) weighing on margins; monitor EBITDA margin trajectory against Q1 FY26 base of ~18.7%.
544595|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on top-line recovery and brand strength, but cautious on margins and inflation, and evasive on forward targets (no guidance given, repeatedly declined growth multiples). Acknowledged the Kerala issue defensively when challenged by minority shareholders.

539150|2026-06.headline: PNC Infratech Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs 1,518 crore and PAT to Rs 271 crore, while management kept FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 6,000 crore.
539150|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs 1,518 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 375 crore (24.7% margin) and PAT of Rs 271 crore (17.8% margin). Consolidated revenue was Rs 1,688 crore (+19% YoY) and consolidated EBITDA Rs 524 crore (31% margin). Management kept FY27 and FY28 revenue guidance and new-business targets unchanged. The call was dominated by the Kanpur-Lucknow expressway issue, where NHAI has issued a show cause notice to the SPV and management declined to discuss the possible non-performer or bidding-ban outcome.

financial_highlights.value: Net worth Rs 6,084 crore; bank debt Rs 428 crore (D/E 0.07x excl. ICD); cash and investments Rs 1,046 crore; net cash surplus Rs 133 crore
Net worth Rs 7,147 crore; total debt Rs 5,448 crore (D/E 0.76x); cash and bank Rs 2,870 crore
About Rs 20 crore in Q1, guided run-rate about Rs 20 crore/quarter
financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 30 crore in Q4

segments.name: Highways (EPC/HAM/BOT)
segments.commentary: Highway contracts are 64% of the Rs 19,100 crore unexecuted order book. Management says the road unexecuted order book is slightly above 60%. Fund-based portfolio is 17 projects: 1 BOT-Toll, 2 BOT-Annuity, 14 HAM.

segments.name: Water (Jal Jeevan Mission and irrigation)
segments.commentary: Opening water order book was Rs 2,310 crore; Rs 136 crore executed in Q1, leaving about Rs 2,180 crore. About Rs 741 crore (ex-GST) is due from government. Andhra Pradesh irrigation: Rs 416 crore invoiced, Rs 263 crore received, Rs 153 crore receivable.

segments.name: Coal mining
segments.commentary: Mining EPC targeted at about Rs 500 crore revenue in FY27 and similar in FY28; Q1 execution was low due to land-access problems, and two new surface miners were deployed.

segments.name: Pune Ring Road
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about Rs 75 crore. Billing is milestone-linked to precasting and erection, so it is lumpy; management did not give FY27/FY28 revenue numbers.

segments.name: Solar (MP, NHPC PSA route)
segments.commentary: EPC component about Rs 2,000 crore on more than 300 acres leased in Madhya Pradesh. Work to start in Q4 FY27; more than Rs 1,000 crore revenue targeted in FY28, balance in FY29. Equity requirement about Rs 400 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about Rs 6,000 crore and FY28 of Rs 7,500 crore, with about 12% margin, maintained unchanged.
New business target of Rs 12,000-15,000 crore for FY27 maintained; management said about Rs 5,900 crore has been secured so far.
JJM revenue targeted at Rs 700-800 crore in FY27 and about Rs 1,000 crore in FY28; project to complete by December 2028.
Andhra Pradesh irrigation: Rs 150 crore targeted in FY27, balance about Rs 600 crore in FY28, subject to timely payment.
Effective tax rate guided at 25-27% for FY27. Capex guided at about Rs 150 crore for standalone FY27 and FY28 (Q1 spend about Rs 70 crore), plus about Rs 350 crore on the mining project.
Equity: Rs 436 crore remaining for existing HAMs over two years (about Rs 226 crore in FY27); about Rs 400 crore for the two new HAMs, mainly in FY28-29.
Pantnagar airport expected before end-September 2026; Bhopal bypass AD pushed to Q3 CY26 due to scope change.
capex_capacity: Standalone capex guided at about Rs 150 crore for FY27 and about Rs 150 crore for FY28; Rs 70 crore spent on machinery in Q1.
Coal mining project total capex about Rs 350 crore (management corrected from Rs 150 crore), front-loaded in the initial years.

Two new HAM SPVs (Barabanki-Mustafabad and Mustafabad-Biswariya) signed concession agreements with NHAI on 16 July 2026; 150 days allowed for financial closure, and appointed date depends on NHAI handing over 90% of land.
HAM portfolio: 6 projects at COD/PCOD, 5 under construction, 1 (MPRDC) with financial closure documents submitted, 2 new projects in financial closure.
Rs 1,187 crore of HAM equity infused to June 2026 out of Rs 1,623 crore requirement (excluding the two new HAMs).
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order book about Rs 19,100 crore (mgmt said Rs 19,600 crore earlier in call, then Rs 19,100 crore per prepared remarks). It is 64% highways, about 21% water/canal/railway/airport, about 15% coal mining.

Bids submitted: 24 projects worth about Rs 32,000 crore (16 EPC, 8 HAM), including 10 HAM, 8 railway, 2 coalfield. A further about 78 projects (about Rs 1.7 lakh crore) are to be bid in the next 2-3 months.
NHAI's Q1 FY27 awards were 107 km and execution about 640 km; NHAI plans to bid out 54 projects worth about Rs 1.8 lakh crore over 2-3 months.
Management targets a non-road share of about 40-45% over time, versus about 60% road order book today.
Management did not comment on pricing or competition.

544890|2026-06.headline: Skyways Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores, with consolidated PAT margin at 2.2% versus 1.72%.

FMEG revenue grew about 28% to INR288 crore and reached operational breakeven versus a loss of about INR7 crore a year earlier. Management reiterated its FY28 Wires & Cables margin guidance of 10.5% and ~18% volume growth, and cautioned that the quarter is early in the year.

544917|2026-06.headline: Karamtara Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72% YoY to INR1,581 crore, EBITDA INR174 crore (~11% margin), PAT INR87 crore; FY27 growth target 60-65%.

Transmission was flagged as the next major growth driver, with new Bhachau capacity ramping and a Saudi Arabia plant targeted for trials around December. qa_highlights.question: Why has performance deteriorated since demerger and what verticals offer good margin growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management framed the period as Chapter 3 of the company, with strategy unchanged but execution, accountability and walking away from weak accounts emphasised. Tech and Digital tracks are payroll, insurance and collections platforms, AI and cloud services, and AI within BPM.

qa_highlights.question: Should Alldigi be merged, and will margins return to pre-demerger levels?
qa_highlights.answer: The board will decide on any legal merger at an appropriate time with no timeline. Management said Digitide's central costs and capabilities are interlocked with Alldigi and that the group should be viewed on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-led revenue incremental or cannibalised, and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue of about INR15 crore is net new from new and existing clients; the pipeline is INR100-150 crore across stages. Management is building dedicated AI sales and solutioning teams.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not reaffirm it. Its priority is margin improvement, and it asked investors to track profitability and ROE rather than revenue.

505196|2026-06.headline: TIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 86% YoY to INR117.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.2% (vs 1.5%) and PAT at negative INR5.5 crore.
505196|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR117.1 crore included Tulip Compression (TCPL) only from 8 May to 30 June 2026, so the quarter is a partial-period read. Standalone revenue grew 25% YoY to INR78.6 crore, with EBITDA up to INR3.4 crore (4.3% margin vs 1.5%), but standalone PAT was negative INR7.2 crore. Management flagged that blended margins will stay volatile for the next six to eight quarters because of product mix and supply-chain localisation, and gave no near-term margin guidance. The company delivered nine ReachStackers and reported a current order book of INR211 crore against a pipeline of about INR373 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.1 crore (1.5%) in Q1 FY26; 9.6% in Q4 FY26 per analyst
+223% YoY vs INR1.1 crore; margin up from 1.5%

segments.name: Standalone TIL (cranes, material handling, defence)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78.6 crore (+25% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.3%. Management said FY26 turnover was about 50% defence. Nine ReachStackers delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: Tulip Compression (TCPL)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from 8 May 2026 (part period). Order book INR328 crore, pipeline INR117 crore. FY26 revenue about INR278 crore per management. Management's medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin view is 14-15%.

segments.name: Aftermarket / services
segments.commentary: FY26 aftermarket about INR56 crore. Management's long-term aim is 40-45% of revenue; parts margins 25-35%, service margins slightly better.

Five-to-seven-year ambition to roughly triple turnover; no significant capex needed up to about INR700-750 crore turnover, beyond bridging capex of INR5-10 crore.
Debtor days target 60-75 days maximum; long-term aftermarket share target 40-45% of revenue.
Board approved up to INR50 crore equity infusion into Tulip; commitment to raise stake to 74% over a few years.
CarryKing 515 launch hoped for Q4 FY27, worst case Q1 FY28.

Bridging capex of INR5-10 crore per instance, mainly for the old Kamarhati plant.
Target to localise 75-80% in every product and above 90% overall, with Cummins engines for ReachStacker a key dependency.
Pick and carry crane (CarryKing 515) launch targeted Q4 FY27 with 520 configuration to follow.
demand_pricing: ReachStacker market share 38-40% after a comeback; CONCOR order described as one-time, first such order since 2014-15.
Rough terrain crane market share about 50%+; truck crane share now below 5% from over 95% a decade ago, lost to Chinese competition.
Order delivery timelines range from 60-90 days (retail ReachStacker) to 6-9 months (defence), with the bulk of the order book typically exhausted within nine months.
Chinese competitors have pricing and credit advantages; management said TIL will not compete on extended credit terms.
Tulip's market share is about one-third in India in a three-player market; clients include city gas distributors such as IGL, MNGL and IGL-type CGD operators.

qa_highlights.question: ReachStacker market share, competitors and whether the Q1 order is CONCOR.
qa_highlights.answer: Share is 38-40%, and the CONCOR order is one-time. Management expects ReachStacker sales to scale to a sizable number this year via retail and niche buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book deliver more than INR200 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figure. It said the order book is exhausted over about nine months and new orders will add to it, and expects a significant jump in turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall from Q4 to Q1, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product mix and localisation drive volatility; Q4 had Air Force cranes and ReachStackers. No harmonised margin for six to eight quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Tulip's business, revenue, margin, and plans to raise stake.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 14-15% medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin, equity infusion up to INR50 crore, and a 74% stake target over a few years. Export to Nigeria has just begun.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtor days.
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors rose at end-FY26 due to a large IAF missile crane order in late March. Target is 60-75 days; TIL is now an MSME, which should speed customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese competition and pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TIL competes on reliability, durability, and aftermarket uptime commitments, not on credit terms.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt: management called the working capital cycle stressed; debtor days and debt reduction are the key items to track.
Margin volatility: EBITDA margins depend on product mix, and management gave no margin guidance for six to eight quarters.

Execution: converting the INR211 crore standalone order book and the INR328 crore TCPL order book on time; the FY26 shortfall was attributed to geopolitics and logistics.
Governance and bandwidth: the Chairman plans to devote 40-50% of his time to TIL from next quarter, versus about 60% needed, and the Gainwell merger question was left open.
Tulip integration and TCPL full-quarter contribution in Q2 FY27.

key_quotes: Hence, we are looking at a few more quarters before we are really able to fix the margins.
You're right, working capital cycle at this stage in TIL looks stressed.

533552|2026-06.headline: Rupa Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.1% YoY to Rs 202.4 crore, EBITDA margin 7.8% (+120 bps) and PAT up 50.2% to Rs 8.3 crore.

EBITDA rose 29.1% to Rs 15.7 crore at a 7.8% margin, and PAT rose 50.2% to Rs 8.3 crore. Management said a price hike taken in April was largely passed on to trade through extra schemes, so realisations did not capture it. Management guided to 10-12% revenue growth and a 9-10% EBITDA margin for the coming quarter, with a further price hike planned for August.

segments.name: Athleisure
segments.commentary: Q1 declined 5-7% YoY after a strong Q4; management targets at least double-digit growth from Q2 and more than double-digit for the full year.

segments.name: Thermal (winterwear)
segments.commentary: Management described the order book as sound and expects FY27 thermal sales to be better than last year, but this depends on how the winter unfolds.

Athleisure expected to grow at least double digits from Q2 and more than double digits for the full year; e-commerce targeted at 20-25% growth.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed on the call.
Management said a DMS (distributor management system) is being rolled out state by state, with a hands-on presence expected in a year or two; ARS is described as in place but dependent on DMS.
demand_pricing: Q1 price hike of 4-5% was largely passed to trade through extra schemes because of intense competition, so realisations did not reflect it; growth was volume-led.
Gross margin slipped 30 bps YoY to 37.4%.
Yarn prices are rising, which management sees as a favourable pricing environment, but competitors are offering extra discounts and extended sale periods to gain share.
Old inventory across the industry is described as now largely exhausted, with fresh stock at higher prices, which management expects will allow the new rate to stick from August.
Management said competition is mainly from organised players and that Rupa is taking share, but via higher discounts.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said advertising and marketing spend was about 10.5% of revenue in Q1 and would be rationalised to 6-7%, which should help achieve the desired EBITDA level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the April price hike not show up in realisations, and when will it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intense competition led to extra schemes that passed the hike on to trade. A new rate is expected from August, and it is yet to be implemented.

qa_highlights.question: What is the thermal order book outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sound and healthy order book; management expects thermal to contribute better than last year, but this depends on how the winter season unfolds.

qa_highlights.question: Will further price hikes be taken to offset yarn cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a further hike is planned, but it depends on how competitors behave.

qa_highlights.question: What were the athleisure and women's trends, and what is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Athleisure fell 5-7% YoY in Q1 and is targeted at double-digit growth from Q2. Women's share is about 8%, and Softline is being rebranded and gets a new team and fabrics.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ROCE/ROE decline structural, and is there room to cut costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the returns are not desirable and blamed the tough competitive environment. It cited the shift from wholesale to secondary-led sales, LFS, e-commerce and other channels. Cost efficiency is an ongoing process with no fixed target.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity from organised players continues to drive extra schemes, so price hikes may not stick (the April hike was largely passed on).
Whether the planned August price hike is implemented and reflected in realisations.
Thermal sales depend on the timing and severity of the winter season.
Women's wear and athleisure both declined or underperformed in Q1; the recovery is not yet proven.
Management guided 9-10% EBITDA margin last quarter but reported 7.8%; the cut in ad spend to 6-7% of revenue needs to show up next quarter.

When there is a scope of 2%, there is a scope of another 2%, we have to do it.

531179|2026-06.headline: Arman Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT rose to INR45 crore from a loss of INR15 crore a year ago, with AUM at a record INR2,925 crore (+36% YoY).
531179|2026-06.overview: Consolidated disbursements of INR686 crore were up 76% YoY, the highest ever Q1, while cost-to-income improved to 44.3% from 51.7% in Q4 FY26. GNPA fell to 2.76% and NNPA to 0.84%, with collection efficiency at 96.6% for the quarter. Management repeatedly said the sector has not fully normalised and that volumes were below expectations, with a stated focus on quality over quantity. Namra Finance (microfinance) drove most of the profit improvement, and the individual loan book rose to 33% of the book.

vs loss of INR15 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR41 crore in Q4 FY26

segments.commentary: AUM INR2,167 crore (+39% YoY, +8% QoQ); disbursements INR530 crore; GTI INR138 crore (+35% YoY); PPOP INR52 crore (+64% YoY); PAT INR30 crore vs loss of INR28 crore a year ago; NIM 15.37%; GNPA 2.59% from a peak of 3.8%.

guidance_outlook: Opex-to-AUM target of about 7% by end of FY27; management said the ratio was about 8% this quarter (vs about 9% last quarter) and expects further decline.

capex_capacity: Management said current infrastructure can support disbursements of INR750 crore per quarter; Q4 FY26 consolidated disbursements were cited at INR700 crore-plus, and microfinance alone at INR738 crore per the presentation.

CGFMU coverage: about 94% of eligible microfinance portfolio covered as of 30 June 2026.

demand_pricing: Q1 volumes were below management's expectations; rejection rates remain relatively high by design.

LAP (loan against property) disbursement is well below the analyst's expected INR40-50 crore per quarter; management cited secured-lending competition from MFIs, SFBs, banks and fintechs.

qa_highlights.question: Why remain cautious given favourable collection and delinquency data?
qa_highlights.answer: Aalok Patel said the data is favourable but rural income growth and jobs quality are concerning on the ground; he called it a little PTSD and said he has no reason to be pessimistic.

qa_highlights.question: Recoveries on written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi said about INR185 crore of pool written off over 24 months was sold to an ARC in March 2025; recovery on it this year is about 10%, and overall write-off recoveries are about 3-4%, with 12-18 months still to run.

qa_highlights.question: When will liquidity fall and disbursements pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquidity is already sufficiently low, averaging about INR300 crore, and described the current level as a 'Goldilocks' position; the team has been in collection mode for two years and volumes should recover over the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Yield, funding cost and opex outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is expected to fall toward 7% of AUM; funding cost of about 11.7% is expected to fall 20-30 bps on rating upgrades; on yields, management said it will reduce rates only if earnings become excessive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MSME 31-90 PAR and LAP GNPA rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi attributed about 10-15 bps of upward movement in MSME PAR to higher stress in Telangana, with other states stable; Aalok Patel said there were other reasons too.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost guidance and July collections?
qa_highlights.answer: July repayment rates were marginally lower than June, about 3 bps on zero DPD, attributed to rain in Gujarat, UP and Bihar; credit cost guided at about 3-3.5% by Vivek Modi, with management saying 2-3% is possible including CGFMU costs.

qa_highlights.question: ROA and individual loan economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it gives no formal ROA guidance; historically about 4.5% on a fully levered basis, and about 3.5-4% at 20% CAR on current opex. Individual loans are preferred but the product is still new.
