544022|2026-06.headline: ASK Automotive Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 52.1% and EBITDA reached Rs. 164 crore (12% margin), with a record PAT of Rs. 85 crore.
544022|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with consolidated revenue up 52.1% YoY (33.4% excluding alloy pass-through, and down 6.6% from the wheel assembly exit). EBITDA rose 32.7% YoY to Rs. 164 crore but the margin of 12% was diluted by the pass-through of a sharp aluminium alloy price spike. PAT grew 28.8% to Rs. 85 crore and EPS was Rs. 4.32 versus Rs. 3.35. Management raised FY27 growth guidance to high-teens from mid-teens and lifted the capex plan to about Rs. 700 crore from Rs. 450-500 crore, to be funded partly by term loans and higher working capital debt.

segments.name: Advanced braking system
segments.commentary: Revenue up 48% YoY in Q1; management says it sustains market leadership in this segment.

segments.name: Aluminium lightweighting precision solutions (alloy wheels)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 75% YoY in Q1; HPDC alloy wheel first supply started to a Japanese customer via Kyushu Yanagawa collaboration at Karoli. Wheel assembly revenue is nil from 1 April 2026 after strategic exit.

segments.name: Safety control cable
segments.commentary: Revenue up 20% YoY in Q1; sunroof cable initial supplies expected from H2 FY27, with substantial growth next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guidance revised to high-teens (previously mid-teens); management expects the Q1 momentum to continue through the year.
Capex for FY27 revised to about Rs. 700 crore from earlier Rs. 450-500 crore, driven by a new South India (Bangalore) plant targeted to be operational before March 2027.
Confirmed alloy wheel orders of Rs. 70-90 crore for FY27 depending on customer ramp-up, and Rs. 250 crore confirmed for FY28.
Ford export business expected at Rs. 40-45 crore in FY27, rising to about Rs. 60 crore in FY28.
Export growth guidance of 20% for FY27, which management says it remains confident of achieving.
Management expects EBITDA margin to recover to about 13.5-14% as aluminium prices cool, though conditional on geopolitics; aluminium has fallen more than 10% from peak of about Rs. 365.
AISIN JV expected to turn marginally profitable by end of Q1 FY28 quarter (not significant); revenue guidance for the JV to be given with Q4 call for FY28.
Debt-to-equity to remain below 0.5 per management; current debt levels to be disclosed with Q2 results.
capex_capacity: New South India plant in Bangalore (18th plant) to be operational before March 2027 to serve new orders.
Karoli plant utilisation rose to about 75% from 60-65% last quarter; management expects about 80% by Q4 FY27. Karoli has about 20% more land scope; Rs. 750 crore already invested there.
Captive solar: 9.9 MW Sirsa (Haryana) plant fully operational; 11.55 MW Bikaner (Rajasthan) plant ready, commissioning expected Q2 FY27. Payback 5-5.5 years.
Capex funding: internal accruals plus term loans for machines and working capital borrowing.
Workforce rose to over 9,000 from over 7,000 in February, with 500 more to be recruited soon at Karoli; management expects more than 10,000 next year.
demand_pricing: Industry: two-wheeler production 72.5 lakh units in Q1 FY27 vs 59.5 lakh, +22.8% YoY (per SIAM as cited); total vehicle production +22.1%.
Management attributes industry strength to GST 2.0 rate cut, income tax changes, RBI rate cuts, and a favourable base.
Alloy price pass-through is 100% back-to-back with customers and hedged, so absolute EBITDA is protected; margin % moves inversely with aluminium prices.
Management says no pass-through lag is pending; all alloy cost increases have been received from customers.
New orders are broad-based across ICE and EV, with EV substantial and concentrated in ALPS. One major EV customer has underperformed for some time, distorting EV growth.
Honda (largest customer) plans 10 new models; management says content per vehicle is highest for this customer.
Export negotiations ongoing with 2-3 players; a big export order to be announced only on materialisation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 33% revenue inflation is alloy pass-through in the braking division, and what are FY27/FY28 alloy wheel and Ford order sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management had not calculated the braking-division share; Kuldip Rathee estimated about 28% impact if prices rose about 48%. Confirmed alloy wheel orders are Rs. 70-90 crore for FY27 and Rs. 250 crore for FY28; Ford exports Rs. 40-45 crore in FY27 and about Rs. 60 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is a new South plant needed, and what are capex and utilisation levels?
qa_highlights.answer: New orders from an existing customer require a Bangalore plant to be operational before March 2027. Capex guidance rose from Rs. 450-500 crore to about Rs. 700 crore; Karoli utilisation is about 75%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AISIN JV still loss-making and when will it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramping up with more products; profitability expected by end of the current quarter, but not significant as it is mainly trading. Revenue guidance for FY28 to come with the Q4 call.

qa_highlights.question: Is any commodity pass-through still pending with a lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No lag pending; customers have passed through everything. Absolute EBITDA is unaffected; only percentage margin moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.7% adjusted margin (analyst's calculation) sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Analyst's math was described as nearly right, but management said 15% is not sustainable; overall margin expected at about 13.5-14%.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded and how has debt moved?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals plus term loans for machines; debt rose in Q1 due to working capital needs from higher aluminium prices. Debt-to-equity to stay below 0.5; exact debt to be disclosed in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EV growth in two-wheelers similar to ICE, given faster EV industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: ASK is growing in EV with all top customers, but one major EV customer with large revenue has underperformed for some time, distorting the percentage.

segments.commentary: US and UK grew over 40% YoY and China 20.3%; US is about INR30 crore last year with INR45 crore targeted this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years on an organic basis. Management says these remain on a small base.

segments.commentary: Single-phase iUNO (up to 5 kW) reached operational profitability; 3-phase iNEO launched up to 12 kW this quarter, with up to 50 kW due by end FY27 and hybrid inverters in development. FY27 solar target is INR24-25 crore, rising to INR250-300 crore next year per management.

US organic revenue target INR45 crore this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years.

capex_capacity: New Nashik manufacturing facility partially commissioned; both buildings complete, with full completion expected in about 1-2 months.
Current transformer capacity being raised from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day (near-doubling), with added machinery already ordered.
Three SMT lines in PCB/EMS operations; latest is high-end and an older line is being upgraded. A fourth line will be added once the three run on three shifts.
Dedicated automated floor for solar inverter manufacturing in the new facility.
Lumel Alucast capacity is underutilised; management is filling it with higher-value orders.
demand_pricing: Domestic order bookings in Q1 were about 20% above last year, but billing lagged, leaving a backlog to be worked off.
Data-centre wins: first win announced, then 3-4 more; about 10 more quotes outstanding.

Lumel S.A. growth comes from product spread, German grid upgrades (EUR5 mn order executed; EUR3 mn follow-on running to year-end) and radiation-detection gates, with Poland security demand after the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Lumel Alucast: RFQs in advanced stages of commercial negotiation and customer approval; ramp-up takes about 6 months after award. Management is prioritising value over volume.
Solar inverter pricing is competitive with Chinese imports; EPC contractors are moving away from Chinese-sourced units over after-sales and warranty concerns.
Contribution margin is about 45% on average; solar and EMS run at 15-20%, while other products run at 40-75%.

539450|2026-06.headline: S H Kelkar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore, with EBITDA up 21% to Rs 89 crore and margin at 13.4%.
539450|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore and EBITDA rose 21% to Rs 89 crore, with margin expanding to 13.4% from 12.6%. Flavours was the standout, at Rs 112 crore, which management says includes about Rs 15 crore of one-off pre-ordering and stock build; the normalised run-rate is about Rs 95-96 crore. segments.commentary: Like-to-like growth of 24.8%. Comfort Click carries much higher margins and is EPS accretive; launched WeightWorld D2C in the US, Walmart marketplace, and noon UAE with a physical UAE base.

Comfort Click: management expects continued EPS accretion and margin improvement if the current momentum holds, despite the seasonally weak September and December quarters.
Effective tax rate: Q1 ETR near 27% due to UK thin-cap disallowances (about 25% underlying). For FY27, about 12-15 points of the 25% are cash; from FY28 the full 25% is expected to be cash.
Finance cost: lower after switching the GBP loan to a euro loan at a much lower rate; the run-rate is expected to hold unless euro benchmark rates move significantly.
Seasonal brands: management expects a positive trajectory for the rest of the year; trade inventory is said to be no higher than last year and the product shelf life is three years.
capex_capacity: Comfort Click costs: an analyst cited about INR 80-85 crore a quarter of interest and depreciation, which management did not dispute.

New launches: Complan Power Play RTD milkshake (vanilla and chocolate, no added sugar), VieMax Diabetes Care, and additional RiteBite Max Protein range (millet wafer bar, Roots, Korean chips, RTDs, cookies).
Comfort Click support and service teams remain in India even as operations expand into the US and Middle East.
Management said more launches are coming in the next few quarters, with a long-term pipeline described as robust for two to three years.
demand_pricing: Consumer demand held up, with spending shifting towards premium products; quick commerce and e-commerce remain the primary growth engines with strong double-digit growth.
Pricing discipline, mix improvement and premium offerings offset input cost volatility, which management described as manageable.
Core gross margin expansion stayed strong, with additional margin support from Comfort Click.
Geopolitical disruption: management said the company's impact was limited to mitigation measures.
Nycil faced channel destocking and slower uptake because of high retailer inventory from the prior year; management said it expects a more positive finish to the year.

qa_highlights.question: Was international growth constrained by stock availability or supply chain issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no specific constraints; 25% is a good growth rate, but it will keep guiding to double-digit growth and does not give forward-looking numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective tax rate outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ETR was near 27% (about 25% underlying, distorted by UK thin-cap disallowances). For FY27, 12-15 points of the 25% are cash; from FY28 it is expected to be fully cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: The GBP loan was refinanced into a euro loan at a much lower rate; the finance cost run-rate should hold unless the euro benchmark moves materially.

qa_highlights.question: What was the 12% seasonal decline by geography?
qa_highlights.answer: East (continuous April-May rain) and North were the main drags. Glucon-D's gains in North, West and South were offset by East. Nycil was hit by North and East plus retailer stock. Growth recovered in the second half of the quarter but not enough to offset the full-quarter drag.

qa_highlights.question: Will Comfort Click be EBITDA-positive in the seasonally weak September and December quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Comfort Click has been EPS accretive since Q4 FY26 and expects net margin, EBITDA and PBT to rise if momentum continues. Comfort Click's US presence is 'very small' but growing well and is too early to judge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Complan's growth despite category degrowth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from the core kids segment (better nutrition, advertising, distribution), celebrity endorsement, toddler (NutriGro), adult nutrition (VieMax, VieMax Diabetes Care) and RTD entry (Complan Power Play). Kids nutrition is the core driver.

qa_highlights.question: What were A&P spends and digital mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported A&P was 18.2% of total sales, including Comfort Click, which spends heavily on advertising. Like-for-like core A&P was similar to last year. Digital's share of spend is rising.

500780|2026-06.headline: Zuari Q1 FY27 standalone loss widened to INR9.5 crore PAT on sugar margin squeeze; Dubai St. Regis repatriation of INR142.58 crore received so far against INR900 crore FY27 target.

Management attributed margin pressure to an 8% rise in UP cane SAP (INR370 to INR400 per quintal). Consolidated PAT was a marginal INR0.05 crore, supported by associate income, mainly Zuari Agro Chemicals. Management reiterated the INR900 crore Dubai repatriation target for FY27 and said that sugar prices are at record highs, which it expects to support the next quarters.

segments.commentary: Production up 1% to 10,138 KL and sales up 5% to 10,248 KL; realisation INR60.70/litre, described as static. Molasses-route recovery was lower, and outsourced molasses was not economical, so no extra purchases were made.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Power sales of 62.8 lakh units vs 7.7 lakh units in Q1 FY26; R&M is in progress ahead of the crushing season.

segments.name: Real estate (Zuari Infraworld)

Zuari Agro Chemicals loan of about INR258 crore expected to be repaid in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).

capex_capacity: Sugar facility operating at 100% capacity utilisation; R&M under way for the 2026-27 crushing season.

Gangothri Tribhuja (Hyderabad) saleable area 2.8 million sq ft; sales office complete, marketing under way. DM agreement for 14.8-acre plotted development in Bengaluru with RERA approval; cycle time about 15-18 months.

demand_pricing: Indian sugar prices up 10% in the past month to record highs; global raw sugar about 16.6 cents/lb, near 1-year highs. Management attributes this to lower FY26 closing stocks (4.3 MMT vs 5.3 MMT).

Cane SAP in UP up 8% (INR370 to INR400/quintal), the main driver of margin compression.
Simon India orders slowed by West Asia-related capex deferrals across sectors.
Zuari Finserv and insurance broking volumes declined as the market weakened (gross return premium down about 38% YoY).

544140|2026-06.headline: Gopal Snacks Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR 422.3 cr (+31.1% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 7.4%; FY27 EBITDA guided at 8-9%.
544140|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue from operations of INR 422.3 crore, up 31.1% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, with the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA more than doubled YoY to INR 31.5 crore (7.4% margin vs 4.7%), and PAT was INR 12.8 crore. Rajkot main facility restarted after the Gondal consolidation, though April saw about 5-6 working days of disruption (gas shortage and plant shift) that cost INR 12-13 crore of revenue in core markets. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ growth (INR 1,800-1,900 crore revenue) and 8-9% EBITDA margin with exit near double digits.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5.3 crore in Q1 FY26
No exceptional items in Q1; prior quarter had insurance gain, so QoQ not comparable

segments.name: Core market (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Flat sequentially in Q1 due to April disruption that cost INR 12-13 crore; management targets INR 100-plus crore per month from here. Gathiya is the leading product, followed by namkeen, snack pellets and potato wafers; wafers grew 15% YoY in core markets. About 65% of Gujarat Gathiya market is still unorganised.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41% YoY; 100% of UP top line comes from two SKUs, Champakali Gathiya and Papdi Gathiya.

segments.commentary: Focus-state distributors rose from 440 (Q1 FY26) to 530 (Q4 FY26) to 567 (Q1 FY27); other states rose from 110 to 129. Maharashtra distributors went 194 to 205 to 198, with focus on Marathwada and the Nagpur belt.

segments.name: Other snack products
segments.commentary: Revenue in the other snacks bucket went from about INR 10 crore last year to about INR 23-24 crore per quarter, including Shot Go noodles, rusks, wafer biscuits, wafer rolls, jeera biscuits and washing bar.

segments.name: Alternate channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce was INR 2.79 crore in Q1 FY27 vs INR 2 crore in Q4 FY26. Modern trade was flat at INR 1.85 crore.

segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation is below 30%; 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, of which about 60 have moved to Modasa for logistics reasons. Third-party units at Kashipur (about INR 2 crore per month) and Manendragarh support other regions.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 1,800-1,900 crore (20%+ growth), reaffirmed; management says it has held the stance on 20%+ growth.
FY27 EBITDA margin 8-9% for the full year, with exit run rate near double digits.
FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 10-11% with exit near 11%; sustainable target 11-11.5%; average reaching that level around mid-FY28-29.
FY28 PAT margin around 7-7.5%; minimum 20% revenue CAGR over the medium term.
Insurance claim of about INR 30-40 crore on the fire loss expected in Q2 FY27; management says documents are submitted.
Seven NPIs planned across Q2 and Q3, five of them non-palm-oil with better margins; 6 lakh outlets targeted by end of CY2026 (from 5.25-5.5 lakh).
capex_capacity: Rajkot main facility restarted; production consolidated from Gondal to Rajkot, with expected savings in power, fuel, logistics and operating costs as utilisation improves.
Modasa and Nagpur plants contribute to the network; Nagpur utilisation is below 30%.
Double-service coverage now reaches 38% of outlets; run rate up 14-25% where it has been rolled out. Pilot of ARS (auto replenishment) started; DMS covers most of the distributor network.
Retail touchpoints on DMS at 4.24 lakh; another 60-70k outlets are served but not on DMS.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation was 5% in Q1; 4.2% passed on through price hikes and grammage cuts, 0.8% absorbed in P&L. Another 0.2-0.3% hit is pending and will be passed through.
Q2 inflation is slightly lower than 100 bps additional, per management.
Management says the company now runs at par or lower grammage than competitors and relies on distribution automation rather than grammage to drive volume.
Management expects roughly 75-80% of growth from volume and about 20% from price in the rest of FY27.
Chana stored till Q3-end; potato stored; palm oil and laminate are bought from the market with no major near-term increase foreseen.
INR 5 price point remains about 60% of sales (down from ~80% in FY22); management says no visible industry shift.
Regional brands in core states (Balaji, Gokul, Shri Hari) remain present; Miraj and Star brands shut, and Miraj has restarted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 330-350 crore FY27 incremental revenue guidance still intact, and what is the festive run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the run rate is INR 150 crore+ per month, April was lower due to the Gondal to Rajkot shift, and 20%+ growth guidance stands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and when will it ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable target is 11-11.5%. FY27 exit near double digits, FY28 exit near 11%, and an average of that level around mid-FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core market run rate target and how is the Gujarat business growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of INR 100-plus crore per month in core markets. Double service is being scaled up, and more products are planned to lift margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the A&P and trade spend trends?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P was about 1% of sales in Q1 against a 2.2% annualised budget; trade discount is 2.5% of sales versus about 3.5% earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Nagpur utilisation below 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, about 60 were moved to Modasa for logistics, and the 250-distributor-a-year addition is below plan for the 300-400 km catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an FMCG business with no order book, and daily run rate is steady with no month-end billing.

544521|2026-06.headline: VMS TMT Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.16% YoY to ₹247.88 crore, but EBITDA fell about 41% and PAT dropped to ₹2.45 crore on imported scrap costs.
544521|2026-06.overview: Total income for Q1 FY27 was ₹247.88 crore versus ₹213.39 crore a year earlier, up 16.16% YoY, with TMT sales volume and average realisation both stated as higher. Management attributed the margin squeeze to a sharp rise in imported scrap prices linked to the Iran conflict, plus a rupee depreciation effect on cargo bought earlier at lower dollar rates; PAT fell to ₹2.45 crore and EBITDA declined about 41% per the analyst's figures. Billet capacity commissioning and the 15 MW captive solar plant (12 MW live from 7 August) were highlighted as cost levers. Management guided margin recovery from Q3 FY27, with the proposed Aditya Ultra Steel amalgamation presented as a further scale driver.

qa_highlights.answer: 12 MW of 15 MW is live since 7 August with the rest in about 1.5 months; ~30% of power needs covered. Savings of about ₹4/unit after EMI, ~2.7 crore units/yr, giving about ₹10 crore annual savings. Capex and funding structure were not stated.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise to ₹228.35 crore?

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported scrap prices rose sharply due to the Iran conflict, and TMT prices did not rise as much. Rupee depreciation also raised the cost of cargo bought at earlier dollar rates. Management expects improvement in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is imported scrap still economically viable versus local scrap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said imports are preferred for bulk buying, GST simplicity and consistent quality; large players continue to rely mainly on imports, with 50-60% of input imported.

KNR-2 (acquired): 4 furnaces switched on in March 2026, but loading restricted; 2 sets of transformers plus a spare ordered, to replace doubtful transformers in Q2-Q3 FY27.
Power constraint at KNR-2 cited as ~6-7 MW lower loading plus ~15 MVA load limit; gas cleaning plant work pending to meet emission norms.
Renewable power contract with JSW Energy: corridor available since June, power flow expected August; ~INR1 crore per month benefit indicated.
KNR-2 furnace of 50,000 t awaiting environmental clearance; expected operational around mid-2027, with clarity in next 3-4 months.
Board approved an additional INR15-20 crore budget for KNR-2 environmental and related work.
demand_pricing: Ferrochrome prices at recent highs; management expects Q2 prices broadly similar with slight correction; no Q3/Q4 price guidance.
Met coke prices up a little (currency depreciation in Colombia, high ferrochrome prices); impact expected in Q3 rather than Q2.
Chinese/South African supply: Eskom special tariff ($0.62/unit cited) lifting South African output; management expects chrome ore reallocation to offset, but flagged possible glut risk.
Global stainless steel production growth ~2.5-3% per management.
Domestic demand: management expects Indian ferrochrome demand to grow; duty protection only ~2-3%, so domestic and export pricing near parity.
FACOR capacity expansion (145,000 t to 500,000 t by FY28) noted by analyst; management declined to comment on FACOR plans.
West Asia crisis: no direct impact (no imports or sales to West Asia); freight costs up modestly but offset by prices.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Q2 volume, at least 90,000 t given KNR-2 running at optimum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers; output to rise further, but some ferrochrome stock build (17,000-18,000 t needed at higher output) will limit the increase. Q2 volume increase expected to be marginal.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 EBITDA a base for the coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: No definitive statement. Prices similar in Q2 with slight correction, offset by a slightly higher tonnage; Q3 and Q4 to see much larger tonnage.

qa_highlights.question: Has the KNR-1 and KNR-2 benefit reached EBITDA per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Not much yet; ramp-up inefficiencies (power consumed without output). Full benefit expected from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Per-ton EBITDA trajectory and whether FY27 volume will be 360-380k t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 380,000 t for FY27; per-ton EBITDA guidance not given, with margin uplift of INR1,500-2,000/t expected once 500,000 t is reached smoothly.

qa_highlights.question: Met coke and cost per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Chrome ore cost is insulated via captive mines; met coke has risen modestly, with the impact seen in Q3. Royalty increases a potential risk.

qa_highlights.question: Coke and ore consumption per ton of ferrochrome?
qa_highlights.answer: About 0.65 kg of coke and about 2.5 t of chrome ore per ton of ferrochrome.

risks_watch: KNR-2 transformer replacement (Q2-Q3) and GCP work; any further load restrictions would cut the 380,000 t FY27 target.
KNR-2 50,000 t furnace environmental clearance timing, expected mid-2027.
Ferrochrome price correction in Q3-Q4 as South African supply recovers; management would not give visibility.
Possible domestic supply additions (FACOR expansion) and domestic pricing pressure.
Met coke price rise and currency movements (Colombia) feeding into costs from Q3.
Forex MTM volatility on export hedges (Q4 FY26 precedent of INR32 crore hit).

543992|2026-06.headline: Yatra Q1 FY27 gross bookings rose 17% to INR21,007 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell 39% to INR151 million on MICE disruption and Kanoo build-out costs.
543992|2026-06.overview: Gross bookings grew about 17% YoY to INR21,007 million and gross margin rose 6.1% to INR1,227 million, while revenue from operations fell 10.4% to INR1,879 million as MICE top line dropped about INR300 million. Adjusted EBITDA declined 39.4% to INR151 million (12.29% of gross margin) and PAT was INR3.4 million. Management attributed the margin squeeze to temporary MICE disruption, air margin pressure from delayed Middle East airline PLB deals, and pre-revenue people and platform costs for the Kanoo partnership. No FY27 guidance was issued; management said it expects to provide guidance next quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and cash equivalents plus term deposits

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: Gross bookings INR16,579 million (+17.6%) and gross margin INR699 million (+8%), with take rate down from 4.6% to 4.2%. Passenger volume grew 4.8% to 1.264 million, about twice industry growth.

segments.name: Hotels and Packages
segments.commentary: Gross bookings INR3,876 million (+13%) and gross margin INR386 million (+24%), margin up to 9.95%. Standalone hotels: gross bookings +34%, revenue +62%, room nights +30%.

segments.name: MICE
segments.commentary: Top line about INR300 million lower YoY due to international group travel disruption; about INR60 million gross margin hit (INR30 million from lower TTV, INR30 million from domestic competition). Management says Q2 MICE volumes are about 50% above Q1.

segments.name: Corporate and Travel Pro
segments.commentary: 53 new corporate customers with expected annual billable potential of about INR2,223 million; 30-plus logos (about INR800 million, per CEO; INR80 crore of INR140 crore per the Q&A answer) came via Travel Pro. Corporate net retention cited at 97%.

segments.name: RECAP (expense management)
segments.commentary: More than 20 customers added since launch; no financials disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 guidance given; management expects to issue guidance next quarter once the market stabilises.
Second half of FY27: air margins expected to recover as Middle East airline PLB deals close and capacity returns; management expects adjusted EBITDA margin close to 20% in H2 before scaling again.
Q2 FY27: MICE pipeline stronger and margins healthier; margins expected to be range-bound with marginal improvement, Kanoo contribution-positive from Q2.
Medium term: adjusted EBITDA margin back to 20%-plus, then 30% range over time.
Air-to-hotel gross margin mix about 60:40 today; 50:50 target over the next 2-3 years reiterated.
capex_capacity: Kanoo Travel partnership extends corporate platform into the Middle East; revenue began around 1 July or mid-July 2026, with people hiring, training, infrastructure and GCP cloud hosting costs incurred in Q1.
Management said people costs will stay at Q1 absolute levels in Q2 while Kanoo revenue ramps.
Technology investments in platform stability and response times said to have lifted B2C performance.
Hotel supply expansion described as a strategic priority, supporting standalone hotel growth.
Management said capacity was built ahead of expected revenue across Travel Pro, RECAP and Kanoo.
demand_pricing: Domestic travel resilient; air passenger traffic in India grew about 2.3% YoY in the period per management.
International and MICE hit by West Asia conflict; industry inquiries for some international destinations down roughly 10% to 15%.
Airfares elevated: ATPs 20% to 30% higher on some routes due to European transit and rerouting.
Share of international business fell to under 30% of mix, from late 30s to near 40% previously.
B2C share rose and travel agency volumes grew; corporate share fell slightly. B2B mix moved from late 60s to mid-60s percent.
Customer promotion as a percentage of gross bookings at about a five-quarter high, attributed to B2C mix and discounting.
Middle East as an endpoint under 20% of business; including transit, 30%-plus of international travel transits the region.

qa_highlights.question: Will air margins stay subdued for FY27 given supply cuts and incentive timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East carriers have not closed annual PLB deals, so revenue is recognised at lower rates; capacity is normalising and margins are expected to improve in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is MICE revenue loss recoverable in the next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MICE restructuring from international to domestic group travel is over; Q2 volumes are about 50% above Q1 with better margin profile.

qa_highlights.question: Can Travel Pro bookings run at about INR200 crore and are contracts multi-year?
qa_highlights.answer: Travel Pro projects are mostly annual contracts versus two to three years for Elite; Travel Pro Q2 trend 20-30% higher; corporate net retention 97%.

qa_highlights.question: How is MICE contribution to profit and what is the long-run profit mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MICE carries about 9-10% gross margin and 40-plus% operating margin; it should account for about 20-25% of profit, not 50%. Q1 MICE impact estimated at INR4-5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise as a share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Hiring, training and infrastructure for Kanoo were incurred in Q1 before revenue; absolute people costs stay at these levels, with revenue contribution from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate restructuring (Yatra India merger with parent) timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said work has continued for about six quarters across India, Singapore, Cyprus, Cayman and SEC; no timeline given as regulator timing is hard to predict.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate card product and working capital plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Working with banks on a product that balances MDR of about 165 bps against shorter credit cycles; also working with Amex, HDFC/Citi and SBI on card platforms, targeting airlines and hotels to bear card cost. Long lead time.

544642|2026-06.headline: Wakefit Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.6% YoY to Rs 404.9 cr; reported EBITDA margin 13.9% and gross margin 57.1%, with ~100 bps raw-material hit guided for H1.
544642|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 16.6% YoY to Rs 404.9 cr, with mattresses up 27.3% and about two-thirds of growth attributed to volume. Gross margin expanded to 57.1% (from 55.8%) and reported EBITDA rose 25.2% to Rs 56 cr (13.9% margin), while PAT rose 19.2% to Rs 23.3 cr but was hit by a Rs 7.3 cr deferred tax charge versus a Rs 98 cr deferred tax credit in Q4. Management flagged that polyol/TDI cost inflation from Middle East disruption will fully flow through in H1 FY27, and that furniture growth slowed due to deliberate pauses in furniture-first store openings.

financial_highlights.change: +19.2% YoY; includes Rs 7.3 cr deferred tax charge

segments.name: Mattress
segments.commentary: 65.9% of Q1 revenue, growing 27.3% YoY; about two-thirds volume and one-third price. Premium share of sales rose ~20-30% relative, but management says price hikes did not drive premiumisation.

segments.name: Furniture
segments.commentary: About 28% of revenue; growth slowed from ~30% last year due to machine breakdowns, workforce shortage, delivery-date backlog and a pause in furniture-first stores. Management guides mid-to-late teens growth over the next two quarters.

segments.name: Furnishing
segments.commentary: 6.3% of revenue in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: Own channels (COCO + D2C web/app) 72.3% of revenue, +20.5% YoY; external marketplaces/MBOs 27.7%, +7.6% YoY after two quarters of 15-20% decline.

guidance_outlook: Raw-material cost impact to fully reflect in H1 FY27; overall H1 gross margin compression of about 100-120 bps versus H1 last year, and about 100 bps lower than Q1 level (could be below 100 bps if prices stabilise).

Furniture category growth to return to mid-to-late teens over next two quarters; step-jump of more than 25-30% expected when Jumbo stores open (first Bangalore store targeted June-July 2027, second Aug-Sep 2027).
Add about 80 COCO stores in FY27 (27 added in Q1; 42 in all of FY26); similar number targeted next year.
FY27 capex of Rs 100-120 cr, ~80% for retail expansion (Jumbo stores), ~20% for manufacturing automation and upgrades.
Rental outgo for FY27 around Rs 80-90 cr; A&P at 7-8% of revenue for FY27; ESOP expense Rs 10-12 cr versus earlier Rs 12 cr guidance.
Long-term aspiration: operating EBITDA around 9% this year, steady state 2-3 years out; management seeks 20-25% revenue growth focus and 4-5 pp organised market share gain over 3-5 years.
capex_capacity: 165 COCO stores across 100 cities as of June 30, 2026 (about 105-106 mega stores with furniture; about 60 mini mattress-first stores).
MBO network about 2,250 outlets across 701 cities.
First Jumbo store: excavation nearly complete, civil work underway; second Jumbo store location under negotiation and approvals (both Bangalore).
Mini-store payback about 10-11 months; catchment revenue up ~2.7-3x after store opening; mini-store inventory about Rs 4-5 lakh.
Raw material buffer: about 3-4 weeks of inventory acquired at lower prices; blended cost still below spot.
demand_pricing: Raw-material spot prices rose 140-160% for some inputs and 70-80% for others; effective net inflation on acquisitions about 30-40%. Passed through via two price increases of about 5% each.

Price hikes first taken late March 2026; June began with a nominal price cut; July saw a modest further cut; management says prices broadly held since and no further hikes planned barring unforeseen increases.
Own channel growth 20.5% YoY; total online 52.7% of revenue, offline 47.3%; repeat customers about 36% of revenue; about two products per cart.
Organised mattress market share estimated at close to 10% (internal estimate, no industry report). B2B finished goods 2-3% of revenue.
Competitive intensity in mattresses described as stable; no new major entrants, with A&P raised from ~5% to ~7.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs value split of mattress growth and outlook for furniture growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds volume and one-third price for Q1; furniture to return to mid-to-late teens over next two quarters, with a step-up of 25-30% once Jumbo stores open. Full-year furniture growth not commented.

qa_highlights.question: Is further cost escalation expected and will more price hikes be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Conflict flares intermittently; supply shortages have pushed suppliers to higher prices. Management is monitoring weekly/monthly and says there is no visibility beyond a few weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin compression expected for H1 and why not pass through earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Full impact of costs bought in March-May lands in July-September. H1 margin compression about 100-120 bps; management says it absorbs short disruptions and adjusts price within 4-6 weeks of sustained moves.

qa_highlights.question: Own-channel versus marketplace growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Own channel up 20% YoY (website/app plus COCO); total online sales up 7% YoY. External channels recovered on platforms prioritising growth and a sale event, with a July sale also expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: Operating leverage, corporate overhead and EBITDA trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate overhead about 7-8% of revenue; absolute spend rising as senior hires join, but percentage expected to fall. Operating EBITDA about 9% this quarter, targeted near 7.5%-9% this year, with steady-state margins two to three years away.

qa_highlights.question: Store payback and expansion economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Mini-store payback around 10-11 months, about 2-3 months longer than mega stores; plan of at least 80 COCO stores this year and a similar number next year, with no guidance beyond that.

532953|2026-06.headline: V-Guard Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.4%.
532953|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore, with about 14% price and 9% volume contribution per management's blended split. EBITDA excluding other income rose 54.5% to INR191 crore, and PAT rose 76% to INR130 crore. Gross margin held at 36.9%, flat YoY, as management says roughly 75-80% of input cost inflation has been passed through. Management raised FY27 growth expectations to above 15% and reaffirmed a 9-10% EBITDA margin, while noting wires volumes were nearly flat under a large price increase.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR155 crore a year ago

segments.name: Electronics (stabilizers, UPS, solar)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY with all major categories contributing; solar is growing fastest on a small base, and solar pumps for Maharashtra government are only a couple of crore so far.

segments.name: Electricals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 27.7% YoY, aided by higher copper prices; wires saw very high price growth with near-flat volumes, while ex-wires grew at high double digits and switchgear, modular switches and pumps grew volumes robustly.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (fans, water heaters, kitchen, air coolers)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.2% YoY; induction cooktops spiked, other kitchen categories grew healthily, fans grew reasonably (pedestal fans short on inventory), and air coolers lost share due to weak North demand and competitor price delays.

segments.name: Sunflame
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18.3% YoY on a low base; management says integration is complete and a sales acceleration programme has started, with margin recovery expected to be more gradual than top-line recovery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 15%, with management saying it may be 'a bit more than 15%' given price growth; no specific number given.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 9-10% ('we should be okay this year in terms of margins').
Long-term target of 15% growth, with normal-year mix of 10-12% volume and 2-3% price growth.
Capex to average INR150-170 crore per year over the next two years, below the earlier INR200-250 crore range.
Advertising spend to reach about 2.5% of revenue for FY27, with spending resumed from around May 15.
Pricing actions about 80-85% complete; some smaller categories still need price increases in the current quarter, and management does not expect large further hikes.
Wires competitive intensity expected to slow growth for some unorganised-sector players by 1-2% vs market, with no major impact in the first one to two years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance revised: INR150-170 crore per year on average for the next two years, versus the earlier INR200-250 crore range referenced by the analyst.
Own manufacturing now above 65% of products (previously sourced), a key driver of gross margin improvement.
Investment phase in capability (technology, systems, R&D, renewables, lighting) expected to last another two to three years before plateauing.
Lighting launch planned in FY27; solar rooftop next-generation battery (BESS) launch planned in the next two to three months.
Gegadyne (battery start-up) has moved from R&D to commercial supply to small customers; V-Guard may source batteries from it.
demand_pricing: Pricing: management cited a blended split of about 14% price and 9% volume within 22-23% revenue growth; category price increases range from 5% to 18%, with some categories cited up to 30%.
Wires: very large price increases led to near-zero volume growth as customers deferred purchases; value growth held up and margins were maintained.
Copper purchase mix shifted to roughly 95% domestic from 70-80% earlier, which helped working capital through supplier credit.
Management described the 12-14% price increase over four months as unprecedented since 2006 and said consumers have accepted it so far.
Air coolers lost share as some competitors delayed price increases and the North zone was weak.
Solar rooftop: focus is B2C residential and small SMEs; BESS seen as the next large opportunity at about INR1.5-2 lakh per home.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 22-23% growth is price vs volume, and how much of the input inflation has been passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended growth split is about 14% price and 9% volume; about 80-85% of pricing actions are complete and roughly 75-80% of inflation has been passed through, with the gross margin expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why is South growing faster than non-South for the fourth quarter in a row?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it mainly to weather: South had a good summer while North was disrupted by rain. It also said it took pricing ahead of competitors in non-South markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capex guidance still INR2-2.5 billion a year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Capex is expected to average INR150-170 crore a year over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth and margins be higher than the medium-term guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth is expected to be more than 15%, with the 15% figure kept as the long-term aim. EBITDA margin is expected at 9-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is payables so high on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a one-off: copper purchases shifted to domestic suppliers who give credit, instead of imports paid by LC, and payables are expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Why not gain share in wires by passing on less price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wires are a commoditised, utilitarian product with low margins, so a price war would be lose-lose and hard to end.

risks_watch: Wires price war from new entrants and a possible festive-season launch; wire volumes near zero and customer deferment.
Sustainability of working capital gains, as the high payables are described as one-off and net cash of INR670 crore may normalise.
Sunflame margin recovery is expected to be slow given pricing transmission lags in CSD and non-South general trade.
Further commodity volatility from the West Asia conflict and shipping constraints; management says a few smaller categories still need price action.
Ad spend at 2.5% for FY27 vs 2.2% in Q1, and the budget was set on January prices, not current input costs.
Cost base has risen sharply over five years; management expects extended investment for two to three more years.
532953|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and margins, with the word 'shock' used for price inflation. Cautious and evasive on categories, state-level data and wire-category volumes, which were not disclosed. Management is wary of predicting the FY27 growth rate given volatile commodity prices.
key_quotes: We have delivered double-digit EBITDA margin this quarter.
So in a normal environment, yes, we should grow at 10% to 12% volume growth and 2% to 3% price growth.
So the problem with this price war is that you will start it, but you won't be able to end it.

543514|2026-06.headline: Veranda Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR150 crore and PAT to INR34 crore, with commerce demerger listing guided for September 2026.
543514|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 42% YoY to about INR150 crore and enrollments rose 35% to about 1.03 lakh students. EBITDA was about INR54 crore with a margin near 36% as stated, but management acknowledged the reported EBITDA growth of 10% was flattered by a INR17 crore one-time other income in Q1 FY26; excluding it, EBITDA grew about 30%. PAT rose to INR34 crore from INR5.9 crore, helped by a INR7.35 crore tax reversal tied to an intra-group merger. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR670 crore revenue, INR260 crore EBITDA and INR144 crore PAT, and said the Commerce demerger NCLT order is expected shortly with listing before end-September 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +10% YoY reported; ~30% excluding Q1 FY26 one-time other income of INR17 crore
+472% YoY from INR5.9 crore; sixth consecutive PAT-positive quarter
+53% YoY; EBITDA INR42.7 crore (+58% YoY), margin ~40%
+41% YoY; EBITDA nearly INR4 crore vs near breakeven prior quarter
Post refinancing; debt cost ~9-9.5% vs 17.5% last year

financial_highlights.value: Commerce INR125 crore; non-commerce INR145 crore

segments.name: Commerce Test Prep
segments.commentary: Revenue INR108.6 crore (+53% YoY), EBITDA INR42.7 crore (~40% margin). Offline revenue about INR330 crore and online about INR120 crore annualised, offline margin ~35% and online ~45-48%. Managed commerce colleges at about 17 now, to add 15 more this year.

segments.name: Government test prep
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA nearly INR4 crore vs near breakeven last quarter. Target of INR95-100 crore EBITDA over four to five years; Karnataka expansion planned in FY27.

segments.name: Academic / K-12
segments.commentary: Revenue INR12.2 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR9.2 crore (+53% YoY). Manages six schools with over 5,400 students; preschool managed operations to be entered in FY27.

segments.name: SNVA Veranda (associate stake)
segments.commentary: Vocational/higher-ed businesses (Edureka, Six Phrase) were moved into SNVA Veranda; management expects value unlock, with the stake to sit in the non-commerce entity post demerger. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: revenue about INR670 crore (FY26: INR482 crore), EBITDA about INR260 crore (FY26: INR204 crore), PAT about INR144 crore (FY26: INR130 crore).
Commerce FY27: revenue about INR450 crore, EBITDA about INR215 crore, PAT about INR110 crore.
Non-commerce FY27: revenue about INR220 crore, EBITDA INR46 crore, PAT INR34 crore.
Management cited EBITDA margin of about 38.8% for FY27 (per analyst reading of guidance); expects margins to recover in Q2 and Q3 as college and marketing spends mature.

Commerce demerger: NCLT order expected imminently after July 20 hearing (orders reserved); next NCLT hearing 17 August 2026; listing targeted by end-September 2026. Shareholders receive 1 JK Shah Commerce Education share per Veranda share.
Commerce long-term aspiration: revenue above INR1,000 crore by FY30.
capex_capacity: Offline commerce network at over 105 centres; 50 new commerce colleges under management in pipeline; plan to add 15 managed commerce colleges in FY27 (doubling from about 17).
Commerce Virtuals (live and recorded digital format for Class 11-12) recently launched for pan-India reach without physical infrastructure.
Government test prep: Group 1 offline programmes, junior IAS, subscription magazines; expansion into Karnataka in FY27.
Planned offline presence in UP, Bihar, Rajasthan and Gujarat to reduce regional concentration.
Managed schools: six schools, 5,400+ students; preschool managed operations to start in FY27.
demand_pricing: Enrollments +35% YoY vs collections +27%; management attributed gap to subject-wise commerce classes, which raise enrollment counts with lower per-enrollment billing.
Q1 collections INR165 crore vs revenue INR150 crore; about INR15 crore of advances deferred under Ind AS 11 to later quarters.
Managed school revenue jump attributed to ~10% student growth plus start-of-year book and service sales (~20% uplift in Q1).
Guided ARPU increase of 7-8% a year and 10% student growth in FY27 as EBITDA drivers, plus 15 new colleges.
Commerce positioned as number one across CA, CS, CMA, ACCA; management claims undisputed leadership in pedigree, alumni, centres and ranks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable quarterly finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohasin Khan guided INR7.5-8 crore per quarter after refinancing; EBITDA excludes finance cost, so no finance savings sit in the EBITDA bridge.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tax swing to a credit of about INR3 crore from about INR8 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Following an intra-group merger of a subsidiary into the parent, management reversed INR7.35 crore of tax related to earlier years; described as current tax, not a DTA write-off.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline QoQ and how will FY27 38.8% margin be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited doubled college expansion spend, pre-demerger advertising for the commerce brand, and initial work on 15 new colleges, all expensed in Q1; expects benefit in next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timing of the NCLT approval and listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders were reserved at the 20 July hearing; affidavit filed on the appointed date query; next hearing 17 August. Management expects order within about a week, then ROC filing in 3-4 days, a record date one week later, and listing before end-September.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-commerce be valued lower because it carries all the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the commerce entity to command the highest sector multiple as the leader; government test prep should earn a good multiple, K-12 less so. No numbers provided on valuation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offline/online split and margins in commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline about INR330 crore and online about INR120 crore (roughly 3:1 offline to online per management); offline margin ~35%, online ~45-48%.

532811|2026-06.headline: Ahluwalia Q1 FY27 PAT fell 77.65% to INR11.42 crore on 4.29% EBITDA margin, as AIIMS Jammu bill cut and NCR labour cost spike hit margins; FY27 double-digit margin ruled out.
532811|2026-06.overview: Turnover rose 12.03% YoY to INR1,125.81 crore, but PAT fell to INR11.42 crore from INR51.11 crore, with EBITDA margin at 4.29% versus 8.59%. Management attributed the drop to a INR29 crore AIIMS Jammu bill reduction (2.6 percentage points), labour cost increases of roughly 35-40% in NCR (about 50% of the order book), higher staff costs, and SIR/election-related disruption in West Bengal and Assam. Net order book stands at INR20,663.52 crore, with only INR512.81 crore of inflow in FY27 to date. Management guided to 12-15% top-line growth but ruled out double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, and did not give a firm date for margin recovery.

financial_highlights.value: Sharp increase YoY; mgmt expects similar ~INR15-16 crore per quarter
financial_highlights.change: due to mobilisation advance for Central Vista

segments.name: NCR projects (about 50% of order book)
segments.commentary: Labour minimum wages rose about 35-40% for skilled and unskilled categories in Haryana and UP, with projects running at 40-50% labour strength. Management estimated a company-level EBITDA hit of about 1.5% this quarter, up to 5% of turnover on some projects where material is client-issued.

segments.name: AIIMS Jammu
segments.commentary: Final bill reduced by INR29 crore after finalisation; the matter is going to arbitration. Impact is 2.6 percentage points on EBITDA. Management says the project is closed and no further hit is expected.

segments.name: Central Vista (Ministry of Housing/CPWD-type govt project)
segments.commentary: Management targets about INR700 crore billing in FY27 and about INR1,000 crore in FY28, with Nirman Bhawan demolition complete and Udyog Bhawan 90% demolished. Full project completes in FY29.

segments.name: CST (Mumbai railway station project)
segments.commentary: Q1 billing about INR70 crore; management targets about INR400-450 crore for FY27 (hoping to cross INR500 crore total) and about INR700 crore in FY28. Earlier target was about INR600 crore.

segments.name: Gems and Jewellery Park
segments.commentary: Work on ground delayed by client design changes; expected to start in Q3 FY27. Targets INR100 crore billing in FY27 and about INR450 crore in FY28; 3.5-year completion.

guidance_outlook: Top-line growth guidance of 12-15% for FY27 retained, with the low end attributed to NGT uncertainty.
No double-digit EBITDA margin in FY27; management hopes to return to Q1 FY26-level margins over the next three quarters, but gave no firm timeline.
Expects some client compensation for labour cost increases to flow over the next two quarters; NGT impact on Q3 unquantified.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR4,000-5,000 crore versus earlier INR8,000 crore guidance; bidding to be less aggressive.
FY27 capex cut to INR220-250 crore (from about INR300 crore); Q1 capex about INR60 crore.
Working capital expected to improve from current level (119 days), with Assam receivables collection resuming.
Expects double-digit margin aspiration for FY28 but said it is hard to predict.
capex_capacity: Capex guided at INR220-250 crore for FY27, down from about INR300 crore earlier; Q1 capex about INR60 crore.
Depreciation is elevated and expected to recur given higher capex over the last 2-3 years.
Machinery investment planned to offset labour shortages, and digitisation is in progress.

Central Vista: Nirman Bhawan fully demolished, foundation casting begun, structural steel work from September; Udyog Bhawan handed over about 3 weeks ago with excavation started. About 50% of the job to be commissioned by end of next year.
Dahlias (DLF) and DLF Downtown (about INR1,600-1,700 crore) projects delayed by design changes; billing targets INR30-35 crore/month from Dahlias and INR25-30 crore/month from DLF Downtown.
demand_pricing: Net order book INR20,663.52 crore; private sector about 62% of order book; fixed-price contracts about 10.34%.

Order inflow only INR512.81 crore in FY27 to date; RML (about INR500 crore) is L1 but not converted. Odisha government university bid (about INR1,620 crore L1 hospital/university) lapsed after the company refused a bid validity extension on a fixed-price contract.

Management is deliberately less aggressive in bidding given material and labour volatility; bid prices now factor in labour, doubled shuttering and steel rates, and staff costs above 5% (up from 3.5-4.5%).

Materials: cement and steel are pass-through (about 30-day lag on private contracts); government contracts use quarterly WPI-based escalation. Switchgear delivery lead times have stretched from 4-6 weeks to 3-4 months due to the war.

Payments: central government payments not an issue, except a Central University project in Himachal unpaid for 5 months. Assam receipts resumed after elections, with major chunks received in the last 15 days.

524669|2026-06.headline: Hester Q1 FY27 standalone PAT up 88% and gross margin up to 78%, while consolidated revenue fell 8% on Nepal and Africa weakness.
524669|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 14% YoY and EBITDA rose 95%, with gross margin improving from 69% to 78% on product mix and operational efficiencies. Consolidated revenue declined 8%, mainly on lower Nepal and Africa revenues. Consolidated profit included an exceptional gain from the Gates Foundation amendment that cut the Hester Africa soft loan from USD 12 million to USD 5 million, waived accrued interest and made the loan interest-free. Poultry grew 48% on institutional business and deeper penetration, while Animal Healthcare was held back by delayed government immunisation programmes (PPR, Lumpy Skin Disease / Goat Pox).

financial_highlights.metric: Hester Africa Gates Foundation soft loan
financial_highlights.value: Reduced from USD 12 million to USD 5 million, interest-free
financial_highlights.change: Exceptional accounting gain in consolidated profit

segments.name: Poultry Healthcare Division
segments.commentary: Grew 48% YoY on higher institutional business and deeper market penetration. Management said the low pathogenic avian influenza vaccine, approved in March 2026, contributed to the jump. Management also cited early traction in poultry health products (feed supplements, disinfectants).

segments.name: Animal Healthcare Division
segments.commentary: Impacted by timing of government immunisation programmes (PPR eradication, Lumpy Skin Disease Control Initiative, Goat Pox vaccine supply). Management described this as timing-related rather than a demand issue.

segments.name: International (Nepal and Africa)
segments.commentary: Revenues were low in the quarter and drove the consolidated decline. Management said strategic direction is unchanged, focused on registration, market development and commercial presence.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: Emerging, not reported separately and included within animal health. Product categories are antibiotics, anti-parasites and grooming products sold under the Hester brand.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give directional guidance on Africa demand or when it would turn profitable, describing the region as a formative period.
Management said the delayed government vaccine tender business is expected to come through in the next quarter.
No numerical guidance was given on revenue, margins or capacity utilisation targets.
Management said it is not providing guidance on the capacity utilisation trajectory.
capex_capacity: Average plant capacity utilisation is around 60% to 65%, covering the whole manufacturing set-up (poultry, large animal, and the newly added fill-and-finish and BSL3 facilities).
New fill-and-finish and BSL3 facilities came online a couple of quarters ago. Management did not give a utilisation figure for these specifically.
Fixed assets rose by around Rs. 200 crore in FY26 (per analyst), with the new facilities cited as the driver. Management did not dispute the figure.
Pipeline products under development at the new facilities were not disclosed. Recombinant Brucella vaccine development is said to be progressing on timeline.
Regulatory dossiers were submitted in animal health during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Poultry growth came mainly from higher market share and deeper penetration; management said vaccine prices have only marginally increased.
Government tender timing caused animal vaccine sales to slip from Q1, with management expecting them to come in the next quarter.
Management said the poultry vaccine business is shared across India, Nepal and Africa; poultry exports from India are part of the consolidated poultry top line.
Management said the poultry distribution network is the same for vaccines and health products, with cross-selling of feed supplements and medicines under way.
Management said there was no material impact on the industry from the H5N1 culling compensation delay.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ministry's recent decision on HPAI vaccine imports for testing, and how does Hester benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Priya Gandhi said it is premature to comment: the government still has to decide whether the vaccine will be imported or made in India.

qa_highlights.question: How does the poultry business's sharp growth compare with its historical track record? Is it cyclical or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said the division pushed sales where opportunities arose, while animal health sales slipped due to tender delays. No value or volume split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation, and can sales grow without new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said average utilisation is about 60% to 65%, but noted that this is subjective given the mix of batch sizes.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the step-up in poultry revenue from about Rs. 45-48 crore to over Rs. 60 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi attributed it to better placement and more aggressive market penetration, with price increases contributing little.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash conversion weak, given that receivables are higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Desai said operating cash flow is positive and conversion has improved. Rajiv Gandhi said higher receivables are seasonal and not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Africa operation's slow scale-up a natural gestation period or a tendering problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said it is a formative period in a new continent with economic and political strain. He declined to give directional guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Africa tax holiday timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Desai said the tax-free status runs until 2030.

risks_watch: Africa and Nepal revenue weakness, with no profitability timeline given and geopolitical constraints acknowledged by management.
Animal Healthcare dependence on government tender timing, with the next quarter expected to see catch-up sales.
Receivables rising, which management attributes to seasonality. Analysts questioned cash conversion.
Low utilisation (about 65%) despite the recent fill-and-finish and BSL3 capacity additions, with fixed assets up about Rs. 200 crore in FY26.
Regulatory and policy uncertainty on HPAI vaccine import or domestic manufacturing pathway.
Gates Foundation loan reduction, which boosted consolidated profit through a one-time exceptional gain rather than operations.
524669|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on standalone profitability and poultry growth, but evasive on Africa, Nepal, pet vaccines, utilisation numbers, pipeline products and HPAI policy, repeatedly declining to quantify or guide. Management dismissed the receivables and cash conversion concern as seasonal.
key_quotes: As we have consistently maintained, this remains a timing-related issue rather than a reflection of any underlying demand issue.
We would not want to get into any directional guidance or anything.

523676|2026-06.headline: Golkunda Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.7% YoY to INR85.2 crore and EBITDA rose 69% to INR8.64 crore, with margin up to 10.14%.
523676|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR85.2 crore versus INR69.4 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 69% to INR8.64 crore and EBITDA margin expanding from 7.35% to 10.14%. Net profit rose about 64% to INR5.14 crore (margin 6.03% vs 4.2%). Management framed the quarter as the start of a domestic diversification phase, anchored by a newly operational Andheri (Mumbai) manufacturing facility outside the SEZ. This was the company's first formal earnings call, and management said near-term volumes from the domestic facility will be small.

financial_highlights.change: +22.7% YoY vs INR69.44 crore in Q1 FY26
up from INR230 crore two years earlier
up from INR16.9 crore two years earlier (about 35%)

segments.name: Export (Middle East, USA, Europe)
segments.commentary: Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain) contributes about 85-90% of total business; USA share has fallen to below 10% from 20-30% a year earlier due to tariffs. Management pegs current export run-rate at about INR280 crore.

segments.name: Domestic (Andheri, Mumbai facility)
segments.commentary: Facility covers about 5,360 sq ft with estimated capacity of 125-150 kg jewellery per annum, expected to lift overall capacity by 50-60%. Currently producing sample lines; management expects only INR15-20 crore revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Lab-grown diamond jewellery
segments.commentary: Management put lab-grown at less than 5-7% of current revenue, mainly from the US market. Domestic B2C lab-grown retail launch is targeted around Diwali (Sept-Oct 2026).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of around 15-20%, predominantly from exports.
Domestic business targeted at about 50% of total revenue by 2030; implied revenue of INR550-600 crore on current export base.
Andheri facility peak revenue potential of around INR250-300 crore in about three years; revenue mix depends on gold carat mix (shift from 18k to 14k, 10k, 9k).
Five-year target of revenue more than double the current level.
Domestic EBITDA margin expected to be tighter initially, converging to export levels over time; B2C expected to be better margin than B2B but insignificant in FY27.
capex_capacity: Andheri, Mumbai facility (approx. 5,360 sq ft, three-storey; two storeys operational, third storey being built as a retail lounge for B2C) is up and running with 125-150 kg per annum estimated capacity.
Existing two facilities are in an SEZ and export-focused; the Andheri unit is the first outside SEZ for domestic operations.
Preferential allotment of convertible warrants (about INR27 crore) to fund facility expansion and working capital.
Inventory days cited at roughly 10-11 times for exports, with management expecting domestic to be similar or better.
demand_pricing: Retail customers are shifting from 18k to 14k, and in some cases 9k-10k gold jewellery, following gold price increases.
Top 10 customers account for approximately 60-65% of revenue (management could not give top-5 split).
Diamonds are hedged via forward contracts covering 4-6 months of receivables; gold has a natural hedge through matched import/export pricing.
Management said the Middle East revenue was not materially affected by the Hormuz disruption beyond roughly a month of air-freight stoppage from late February to March 2026.
Competition in domestic lab-grown is nascent; management named no specific head-to-head competitor and cited branded retailers and traditional jewellers as entrants.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic expansion strategy given competition from organised players?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-pronged: manufacture for major Indian retail chains already served in the Middle East, and pursue B2C retail, especially lab-grown, over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US business exported or through a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: No subsidiary; sales are to wholesalers, distributors and retailers in Middle East, USA and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can the new capacity generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates INR250-300 crore of incremental revenue potential, subject to gold carat mix.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and 2030 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth of 15-20%, mainly exports; domestic to reach 50% of business by 2030, implying INR550-600 crore total on current export base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the lab-grown contribution and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab-grown is under 5-7% of revenue, mostly US; management hopes it will be a significant domestic contributor but gave no numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 revenue from the Mumbai facility and when does B2C start?
qa_highlights.answer: INR15-20 crore in FY27; B2C launch targeted around Diwali (Sept-Oct 2026), with B2C insignificant in FY27.

risks_watch: Domestic ramp is unproven: FY27 facility revenue guided at only INR15-20 crore against a 2030 target of about 50% domestic mix.
Heavy concentration: top 10 customers are about 60-65% of revenue, and Middle East is 85-90% of business.
Domestic EBITDA is expected to be thinner initially, which could dilute the 10.14% margin as B2B and B2C scale.
Gold price shifts toward lower carat jewellery and the 250-300 crore capacity estimate depend on mix assumptions.
Management said the company is still building a brand and retail experience for B2C; it gave no B2C target beyond the Diwali launch.
523676|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term domestic and lab-grown ambitions, but vague or deferential on specifics; several answers lacked numbers (e.g., competitors, B2C mix, margins) and the CEO had to look up top-10 customer share. Clear and specific on near-term FY27 guidance and the Middle East share.
key_quotes: This is expected to increase our overall manufacturing capacity by approximately 50% to 60%.
So right now for the current year, our target is to have a growth of around 15 % to 20%.

543336|2026-06.headline: Chemplast Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA loss of INR115 crores on INR1,125 crores revenue; net loss INR176 crores on VCM high-cost inventory.
543336|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose to INR1,125 crores from INR1,100 crores a year earlier, but input cost spikes from the Middle East disruption drove an EBITDA loss of INR115 crores and a net loss of INR176 crores. Management attributed the loss mainly to high-priced VCM inventory booked around March-April, which it says will be consumed by July-August. Specialty chemicals (CMCD) volumes grew 21% YoY and the segment is described as recovering, while Suspension PVC and caustic/chloromethane remained under price pressure. Management expects spreads near $160/t from September onward, with the Karaikal PVC plant offline after a 17 July fire.

segments.name: Suspension PVC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR569 crores vs INR608 crores YoY; prices fell in April after duty exemption let Chinese imports surge, and demand softened seasonally. Management guides spread to ~$160/t (India, replacement basis) from September.

segments.name: Paste PVC
segments.commentary: Realisations about $200/t above Suspension PVC per management; Cuddalore 7,000 t debottlenecking on track for October 2026 commissioning.

segments.name: Specialty / CMCD
segments.commentary: Volumes up 21% YoY on revenue of INR427 crores; 14 molecules commercial out of ~50 in pipeline; INR1,000 crore revenue target reiterated as on track. MPB-3 Phase 3 and pilot Phase 3 commissioned; utilisation ex-new assets ~60-70%.

segments.name: Refrigerant gas (R32)
segments.commentary: Commercial production started May 2026 from swing plant; full 14,000 t capacity expected online by end of FY27 per management, with ramp-up in Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Value-added chemicals (caustic, chloromethane, H2O2)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR129 crores vs INR138 crores; lower output due to planned caustic membrane changeover; caustic pricing under pressure from weak demand and excess supply.

guidance_outlook: Management expects VCM high-cost inventory to be consumed by July and part of August, with normal-price VCM from September and better Q3 performance.
Targeted spread of ~$160/t between PVC and VCM; management says ~$120-130/t needed for EBITDA neutral and a further ~$20-30/t for PBT positive.
Management declined to give a numerical guidance but said 'reasonable performance' expected from Q3 FY27.
Onerous contract net provisions of ~INR90 crores (CCVL) and ~INR30 crores (Chemplast) expected to be reversed in Q2 FY27.
R32 full capacity expected online by end of FY27; management says margin contribution is healthy but too early to forecast sustainability.
Debottlenecking of 7,000 t at Cuddalore Paste PVC due October 2026.
capex_capacity: Karaikal PVC plant manually shut after a fire on 17 July 2026; no injuries or spillage reported; restoration timeline not disclosed on the call.
Cuddalore Paste PVC 7,000 t debottlenecking on track for October 2026.
CMCD: MPB-3 Phase 3 and pilot Phase 3 commissioned in Q1 FY27; CMCD capacity expanded from ~1,100 t to ~5,400 t per analyst question (not contested).
R32: 14,000 t capacity targeted online by end of FY27; swing plant commercial production from May 2026.
Caustic soda capacity 120,000 t, operating range 100-120k t given electrolyser ageing.
demand_pricing: Paste PVC demand recovered to 70-80% downstream operating rates in June as Middle East situation eased; Europe and Asia supplies turned aggressive from mid-June.
Suspension PVC prices fell in April; customs duty on PVC resin exempted 2 April-30 June 2026 and reinstated 16 July 2026; minimum import price (MIP) imposed for six months.
Anti-dumping recommendation on EU and Japan Paste PVC imports lapsed; Madras High Court ordered provisional assessment and importer bonds for retrospective ADD recovery.
Agchem market subdued with generic competition from China; management says demand on commercialised molecules remains healthy but some ramp-ups delayed by a quarter.
Caustic soda and chloromethane prices under pressure from weak regional demand and excess supply; hydrogen peroxide volumes up sequentially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM sourcing situation and would the company partially shut the plant given negative economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement VCM ~$700/t delivered vs PVC ~$900+/t, a $150-160 spread; management is evaluating alternate VCM sources and expects VCM prices to soften further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 PVC-VCM spread and what spread is needed for EBITDA and PBT breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 spread was negative (VCM ~$1,000+/t landed vs realisation ~$700-750/t). EBITDA neutral needs ~$120-130/t; PBT positive needs another $20-30/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company locked into fixed-price PVC contracts with floating raw material costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are formula/market-linked on both PVC and VCM; the Q1 loss came from VCM parcels booked at March peak prices when PVC prices later fell.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is CMCD revenue across the 14 commercial molecules and is the INR1,000 crore target agchem-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is mostly agchem and spread across multiple customers and innovators; management declined to give product or customer concentration. The INR1,000 crore target is reflective of agchem molecules already commercialised; pharma and other specialty projects are not included.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CMCD utilisation and ROCE trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding the newly commissioned MPB-3 Phase 3, utilisation is ~60-70%; management expects returns to reach industry levels this year as costs optimise.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to service debt with ~INR235 crores annual interest and negative FCF from growth capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said conserved cash and current accruals will cover debt servicing; liquidity is sufficient and no equity dilution flagged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spread for Paste vs Suspension PVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Paste realisations are ~$200/t above Suspension PVC per management.

543288|2026-06.headline: Deep Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR278.92 crores, EBITDA margin 43.6%, net profit INR89.14 crores (+44.5%), order book INR3,047 crores.
543288|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 40% YoY to INR278.92 crores and EBITDA rose 38.7% to INR131.8 crores at a 43.6% margin, with net profit up 44.5% to INR89.14 crores. Growth drivers cited were offshore (Dolphin), the ONGC production enhancement contract (PEC), and Dubai subsidiaries, with the standalone business guided to grow only 18-20% in FY27. Management reiterated FY28 PAT ambition of about INR500 crores and said there are no further Kandla legacy write-offs this year.

financial_highlights.metric: Dubai subsidiaries plus Indian subsidiary other revenue

financial_highlights.value: 75-80% historically; Q1 said to be on similar lines

segments.name: Gas processing
segments.commentary: Charter Hire model for gas processing plants; operating from 3 fields (2 ONGC, 1 Cairn). Management says capacity can be increased as opportunities arise.

segments.name: Gas compression and dehydration
segments.commentary: Management says Deep has executed about 85% of outsourced gas compression work in India and owns more than 80 compressor units. Standalone revenue has been flat at around INR175 crores for 5 quarters.

segments.name: Onshore drilling and workover rigs
segments.commentary: Fleet of 20 rigs (14 workover, 6 drilling of 1,000 HP) at 100% utilisation. Management is evaluating 2,000-3,000 HP rigs with bids expected in the next few months.

segments.name: Production enhancement (ONGC contract)
segments.commentary: INR1,402 crore, 15-year contract. Incremental production delayed 5-6 months by a well incident at Mori-5; incremental output expected from around September-October 2026. FY28 revenue guided at more than INR150 crores.

segments.name: Offshore (Dolphin Offshore)
segments.commentary: Two assets fully deployed: DP2 barge Prabha (3-year contract, expected to contribute more than INR150 crores a year) and AHTS V, which has no long-term contract. Further tugs and barges planned over 3-5 years, capex only after firm orders.

guidance_outlook: FY28 PAT target of almost INR500 crores; management said FY27 PAT expected to be about INR350 crores.
Standalone revenue growth of 18-20% in FY27 and consolidated growth above 25%; standalone revenue expected to improve from Q2 as 4-5 gas compression and processing contracts start.
Blended EBITDA expected to improve in FY28 as offshore and PEC contribute at higher margins; offshore margins expected to exceed onshore.
Kandla hydrocarbon fluids unit expected to contribute from later in FY27, adding about 1.5% to EBITDA margin with INR10-15 crores of capex and no debt.
Capex of around INR250-300 crores in FY27 for higher-capacity rigs, contingent on firm orders; PEC capex of about INR150 crores by March 2027.
