capex_capacity: PEC incremental production expected from around September-October 2026; new wells to contribute in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; PEC capex of about INR150 crores by March 2027.
Higher-capacity (2,000-3,000 HP) drilling rig bids expected in the next few months; funding via debt and internal accruals once awarded.
Offshore fleet expansion planned over 3-5 years (tugs, barges, 1-2 support vessels), capex only after firm contracts.
Kandla facility revival requires INR10-15 crores, no debt planned.
Management does not foresee an equity raise; net debt-free position.
demand_pricing: Order intake has been roughly equal to execution over the last 4-5 quarters; management expects a similar run rate and some larger contracts.
Contracts are largely fixed-price, tender-driven L1 bidding; the company bears no exploration success risk.
PEC block is under a free-price mechanism; spot gas prices quoted at USD 8-15/MMBtu, with management not expecting a fall below USD 8.
Onshore rig market estimated at 215-220 rigs (about 120-125 outsourced); outsourced share rising.
Bidding pipeline about INR700-800 crores; none of the three strategic priorities (PEC tender, DSV/PSV, higher-HP rig) yet in the pipeline.
Inquiries from Vedanta, ONGC and Oil India increased, which management attributed to both pre-existing demand and the current geopolitical situation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kandla facility a margin lever and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says reviving Kandla to make a chemical used in drilling and integrated project management improves EBITDA margin by about 1.5%, with INR10-15 crores of capex and no debt; no further write-offs expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY28 PAT of INR450-500 crores achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is gunning for almost INR500 crores PAT in FY28 and expects about INR350 crores in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much does the Mori PEC well and incremental production matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mori was beyond expectations with high-pressure gas, but Mori-5 is not operating after the incident; other wells around it may be explored. Incremental output expected from around September-October 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for standalone business given flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects standalone growth of 18-20% in FY27 as new gas compression and processing contracts start from late Q1/Q2, with consolidated growth above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Offshore pipeline and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Two assets (Prabha DP2 barge and AHTS V) fully deployed; no current bid pipeline, though several tenders are being evaluated; offshore contracts would be fixed-price charter hire.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Dolphin contribution sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Prabha barge contract of 3 years expected to contribute more than INR150 crores a year; further growth in FY28 expected with fleet additions.

risks_watch: Mori-5 well incident delayed PEC incremental production by 5-6 months; restart timing (Sept-Oct 2026) and new well contribution (Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28) to monitor.
Standalone revenue flat at around INR175 crores for 5 quarters; 18-20% FY27 growth depends on new contract starts from Q2.
Offshore growth depends on winning firm tenders; AHTS V not on long-term contract and contributing little.
Green hydrogen tender outcome pending; geothermal and hydrogen remain at evaluation stage with partners.
Order book conversion: about INR800 crores expected to execute in FY27 of INR3,047 crores.

Executable order book stands at about Rs 8,450 crore over 2026-2031.

about 124 tonnes above prior-year Q1 per management; FY26 tonnage 34,000 tonnes

533655|2026-06.headline: Triveni Turbine Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.2% to ₹4.43 bn, but EBITDA margin fell to 18% from 25.8% on export deferrals and low-margin legacy orders.
533655|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 19.2% YoY to ₹4.43 bn, with domestic sales up 27.4% to ₹2.4 bn and exports up to ₹2.03 bn. Management attributed the margin fall to a higher domestic mix, export deliveries deferred by freight costs rising 3-4x, a near-zero-margin NTPC CO2 energy storage project, and legacy orders priced before commodity inflation. Consolidated volumes grew 5% YoY, with India up 11% and Rest of World up 6%, while AMET volumes fell 4% YoY but rose 19% QoQ after West Asia logistics disruptions cut April–May supply. Management attributed the margin jump to reformulation-led volume recovery, a richer specialty mix, commercial execution and feedstock volatility, and said some of these gains may not persist. FY27 volume guidance of 6–8% was maintained, while EBITDA/MT guidance was raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000; management implied roughly INR 21,000–22,000 per MT for the remaining three quarters.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volumes up 11% YoY, led by double-digit growth in performance surfactants and high single-digit growth in specialty products; non-Tier 1 and direct-to-consumer volumes grew near double digit.

segments.name: Rest of World (Americas, APAC, Europe)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 6% YoY; Americas led on tariff clarity and TRI-K premium specialties; APAC grew double-digit. Specialty mix improved, lifting EBITDA/MT.

segments.name: AMET (incl. Egypt)
segments.commentary: Volumes down 4% YoY but up 19% QoQ; about seven weeks of Q1 at the Egypt site were effectively lost because raw materials were stuck at Jebel Ali, Jeddah and Port Said/Suez ports; management called this supply-led, not demand-led.

segments.name: EPC service income (Mexico project)
segments.commentary: Separate business model, not part of performance segment; income recognised in Q1 with amount not disclosed (management said not significant to overall numbers); recognition to complete by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance maintained at 6–8%.
FY27 EBITDA per MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000.
Management indicated INR 21,000–22,000/MT for the next three quarters, implying the INR 35,458 Q1 level is not sustainable.
Fatty alcohol expected to trade sideways at INR 2,600–2,800/MT (ex-Indonesia-type range), with no major expected jumps or corrections.
Annual capex around INR 150–200 crore; management referenced about INR 150 crore for this year.
Specialty products targeted to contribute more than 5% of total revenue by 2030 (per management).
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR 150–200 crore, with some capacity already front-loaded and commissioned; some more to be commissioned this year.
Capacity in place for petrochemical derivative-based products, but supplies were constrained because the derivative was not available; oleochemical use was prioritised.
No acquisition planned in AMET; any AMET capex will be debottlenecking.
Inorganic growth in Beauty and Wellness under evaluation; management hopes to announce something in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Reformulation tailwind: oleochemical-based solutions became more attractive as petrochemical availability and cost worsened after West Asia developments; management expects this to persist for some time.
Feedstock: crude averaged above USD 100/bbl in Q1; oleochemical feedstock ranged USD 2,800 to 3,300/MT, then fell below USD 2,500/MT by late June.
Freight rates on exports more than doubled, feeding into CIF-linked pricing; rupee moved from INR 88 to INR 95 per USD (per management).
Price pass-through: management said customers accept increases when transparently justified; contractual business has a cost pass-through methodology; decreases passed on at the first opportunity.
BASF announced closure of its sulfation plant in Dahej; management said it is too early to quantify any demand upside.
Customer restocking was seen ahead of festive and summer demand, plus some extra buying on fears of feedstock availability; management did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA/kg at INR 35,000 in Q1, and how much came from inventory gains or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited reformulation-led volume recovery and operating leverage, specialty mix improvement, and commercial opportunities; some may not persist. It did not quantify inventory gains, but said mix and freight also contributed. Without these, it said EBITDA/MT would have been about INR 21,000.

qa_highlights.question: Is the specialty share decline from about 40% to 34% a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said specialty absolute revenue grew strongly; the share fell because performance products grew faster, enlarging the denominator.

qa_highlights.question: Will AMET return to positive volume growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was supply-led, not demand-led, with Egypt effectively washed out for about seven weeks; sequential growth of 18–19% and June momentum support a recovery, and it sees AMET returning to growth this year absent a new shock.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of reformulation reversing in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reformulation remains favourable while petrochemical and oleochemical balance holds; it does not see a big risk currently but will monitor coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 22–23/kg gross margin or INR 25/kg EBITDA a steady-state base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the structure has improved but said it wants at least one more quarter before changing long-term guidance, to avoid overpromising.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pricing gain is from finished-goods inventory spikes or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said freight costs, mix shift toward dry (100%/95% active) products, and the reformulation mix all lifted realisations; it declined to quantify the ASP increase excluding these.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for fatty alcohol prices and Indonesia's biodiesel mandate?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil is around USD 1,100–1,200/MT and the mandate is largely priced in; fatty alcohol expected to hold at INR 2,600–2,800 on a sideways basis, with El Nino a possible supply-side risk for next year.

vs about INR 20,009/MT in Q1 FY26
performance segment double-digit, specialty high single-digit

544054|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income rose 10% YoY to INR146 crores and PAT 7% to INR23 crores, while net debt climbed to INR614 crores.
544054|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR146 crores (up 10% YoY) and EBITDA of INR55 crores (up 9%, margin near 37.5%). Sales value rose 74% YoY to INR141 crores on 28,834 sq ft sold, but collections fell to INR86 crores from INR115 crores. Net debt rose to INR614 crores, which management attributed to Bandra land, the Dadar West acquisition and project investments. Management guided to a FY27 launch pipeline of about INR1,600 crores and presales of about INR700 crores.

segments.name: Suraj One Business Bay (Mahim, commercial)
segments.commentary: About 33% of inventory sold since launch; management says it is the largest contributor to sales and collections over the next 2-3 quarters. Average realisation about INR50,000 per sq ft, per Q&A.

segments.name: Residential (Suraj Nova / Lobo Villa, Mahim)
segments.commentary: Expected launch in Q2 with about INR180 crores top line; CC and RERA expected soon. Residential unsold inventory is about 22,000 sq ft, GDV about INR109 crores.

segments.name: Ongoing portfolio overall
segments.commentary: Cumulative sold area 5.95 lakh sq ft at average realisation about INR45,922 per sq ft; cumulative collections INR1,672 crores; balance receivable about INR1,060 crores.

segments.name: Commercial unsold inventory
segments.commentary: About 1.4 lakh sq ft unsold, estimated top line INR841 crores. Total unsold inventory across ongoing projects about INR950 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 launch pipeline about INR1,600 crores: about INR240 crores in Q2, INR800-880 crores in Q3, about INR480 crores in Q4.
FY27 presales target about INR700 crores across residential and commercial; at least 1 lakh sq ft more to be sold in One Business Bay.
Accounting revenue growth of about 10-15% over FY26, subject to launch timing.
EBITDA margin guided at 35-37% for the next two years.

Bandra project: two balance conveyances pending; launch in FY28. Premiums estimated at INR300-350 crores for the entire land parcel, funded initially from internal accruals; construction debt facility to be arranged later.
Debt expected to rise temporarily with launches, then decline on a sustainable basis; no quantified de-leveraging target given.
capex_capacity: Suraj One Business Bay Phase 2 (amalgamated into current phase, INR800 crores top line) expected Q3 FY27, pending RERA amendment; concession plan for amalgamated portion already approved.
Shivteerth (Shivaji Park, INR80 crores top line) expected Q3 FY27; Madonna (Dadar, INR60 crores top line) expected in FY27.
Three further projects with about INR480 crores top line expected in Q4 FY27.
Bandra: adjoining third land parcel amalgamation pending; management targets completion before FY27 end but gave no firm timeline. Amalgamation depends on BMC process.
Dadar West land parcel acquired for about INR18 crores; about 18,000 sq ft saleable, GDV about INR100 crores.
demand_pricing: Residential sales growth in Q1 described as low-inventory driven rather than market slowdown, per management.
Management says no increase in redevelopment acquisition costs yet, though competition is rising; deal terms described as standard with limited additional area to societies.
Luxury segment has little ongoing inventory; the Value Luxury and commercial segments are seeing traction.
Management expects pricing appreciation in One Business Bay once the project reaches RCC stage; current focus is on velocity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 launch pipeline, and which projects drive sales and collections over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,600 crores of launches (INR240 crores Q2, INR800-880 crores Q3, INR480 crores Q4). Commercial (One Business Bay) is the largest near-term contributor, with Suraj Nova also expected to generate cash flows soon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding plan and capital need for the Bandra project?
qa_highlights.answer: Premiums estimated at INR300-350 crores for the entire parcel, funded initially from internal accruals. A construction finance limit is separate and will be arranged closer to launch once basic IOD is in place.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 revenue and EBITDA margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of close to 10-15% over FY26 is expected, subject to launch timing. EBITDA margin is guided at 35-37%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 presales guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR700 crores in total across residential and commercial, with at least 1 lakh sq ft more to be sold in One Business Bay.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unsold inventory breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Residential about 22,000 sq ft (GDV about INR109 crores). Commercial about 1.4 lakh sq ft (top line about INR841 crores). Total about INR950 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the Bandra third plot amalgamation?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm timeline. Conveyances for the two balance plots come first; management targets completion before FY27 end but says this is not assured.

risks_watch: Collections fell 25% YoY to INR86 crores while sales value rose 74%, widening the gap between booked sales and cash received.
Net debt of INR614 crores, with further increases expected before any de-leveraging; management gave no target.
Launch timing depends on RERA amendment for One Business Bay Phase 2 and Suraj Nova CC and RERA approval.
Bandra third land parcel amalgamation has no firm timeline and depends on BMC process and conveyances.
Management declined to give operating cash flow or collections targets on the call.
544054|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and pipeline, with specific launch and presales targets. Cautious and evasive on cash flow and debt: deferred OCF and collections targets offline and gave no quantified de-leveraging path. Timelines for the Bandra third plot were left open.
key_quotes: Our ongoing projects continue to witness healthy momentum with a total sold area reaching 5.95 lakh square feet with an average realization of approximately INR45,922 per square foot.
it's mainly because of low inventory.
So close to 10%- 15% growth we will achieve as compared to the last financial year.

543965|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 3,335.2 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 34% to Rs 232.2 crore, but ISCS margin fell to 8.1%.
543965|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 28.7% YoY and 10% QoQ, with both ISCS and GFS posting double-digit growth. Adjusted EBITDA margin was about 7%, up 30 bps YoY. ISCS margin slipped to 8.1% from 9.3% in Q4 on onboarding costs for new contracts and no Q4-style price corrections, while GFS margin rose to 4.1%. New business wins of Rs 543 crore were an all-time quarterly high and the pipeline reached over Rs 7,500 crore.

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,417 crore (+21.9% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA Rs 196.3 crore at 8.1% margin, down from 9.3% in Q4 FY26 due to implementation costs on new contracts. Management targets a return to above 9% in Q2.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 918 crore (+50.6% YoY), driven by ocean freight volumes in India and higher freight rates. Adjusted EBITDA Rs 38 crore at 4.1% margin, versus 2.1% a year ago; management said it wants at least 5% over time.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration of mid-teen percentage revenue growth for FY27; management expects profit to grow faster than revenue.
Target of about 4% PBT margin; management called FY27 an aspiration and said FY28 will definitely reach 4%.
ISCS EBITDA margin expected to return to about 9% in Q2 FY27 and reach 9.5% to 10% by Q4 FY27.
GFS EBITDA margin expected at 4.5% to 5%, with management wanting at least 5%.
Early-teens EBITDA margin target referenced by an analyst; management said first 45 days of Q2 are on similar lines to Q1.
ALA JV expected to contribute revenue in H2 FY27, targeting about Rs 2,000 crore in year 5 of operations; H2 expected to be stronger than H1.
capex_capacity: Warehousing footprint about 25 million sq ft per analyst; utilisation around 85%, with room to improve through racking and automation investment.
Warehouses are largely project-driven and backed by customer contracts; depreciation on right-of-use assets rose to Rs 114 crore from Rs 93 crore YoY due to additional space for new wins.
Acquired Swamy & Sons 3PL; its results were included for 40 days of Q1 and integration is on track.
Joint venture with ALA Group for defence and aerospace: warehouse finalised, staff being trained in Italy, and warehouse certification pending before business can start in India.
Oracle ERP implemented for the India ISCS business.
demand_pricing: New business wins of Rs 543 crore in Q1 (Rs 524 crore in Q4); about two-thirds from existing customers and one-third from new logos.
Order pipeline above Rs 7,500 crore, up from Rs 6,100 crore; management expects 20-25% conversion over 12-18 months, in line with track record.
Fuel and freight cost increases are passed through to customers under contracts with some time lag; container and air cost increases also passed on.
Management expects ISCS steady-state EBITDA margin of about 8.5-9% on new contracts.
India geography revenue grew 44% YoY on record new business wins and freight volumes.
Management sees recession and geopolitical disruption as the main risk, but said it has not yet seen this playing out in customer volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ISCS EBITDA margin decline despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited transition and implementation costs on new contracts onboarded in Q4 and Q1, plus the absence of the Q4 customer price corrections. Management called it a one-time effect and expects margins to recover.

qa_highlights.question: How long do new ISCS contracts take to reach stable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 to 2 quarters, depending on the contract: about 2 quarters for implant and sub-assembly work and about 1 quarter for aftermarket or finished-goods work.

qa_highlights.question: Was the GFS margin improvement due to one-offs linked to the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth came from new wins and cost optimisation through vendor consolidation, and it expects margins to stay around current levels with high double-digit growth ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ALA JV revenue potential and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to about Rs 2,000 crore revenue in year 5, with first revenue in H2 FY27. It expects the JV to be margin accretive given high entry barriers and a regulated sector.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FIT 3PL merger going ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FIT 3PL will remain a separate legal entity due to GST mechanisms for certain FMCG customers. It said the entity was never part of the announced merger.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East and Africa be entered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in discussions with Middle East companies and prefers a partnership route. It said it will announce once something crystallises and is taking extra precautions due to the war.

risks_watch: ISCS margin recovery to about 9% in Q2 FY27 is the key test; management has committed to this.
Recession, geopolitical events and supply-chain disruption, with the war cited as a factor.
Container and air capacity constraints and freight rate volatility; management said costs are passed through, though with time lags.
Manpower availability across geographies.
Warehouse depreciation and lease costs rising with new space (other expenses up on short-term rentals).

+70.7% YoY (vs Rs 18.8 crore); Q4 FY26 Rs 30.9 crore

500620|2026-06.headline: GE Shipping posted record Q1 FY27 consolidated profit of INR 1,309 crore (standalone INR 1,157 crore), with ~INR 91-92/share EPS and a INR 14.40 interim dividend.
500620|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the company's most profitable quarter ever by a significant margin, driven by Strait of Hormuz disruption that pushed tanker freight rates and asset prices to record levels. Standalone NAV rose about INR 100/share to ~INR 1,512 and consolidated NAV is just under INR 1,900/share, with the stock trading at about a 25% discount. The company announced its 18th consecutive interim dividend of INR 14.40/share, its highest quarterly payout. Management said it remains predominantly on the spot market (about 25-26% of capacity on time charter), is net cash, and is holding most cash rather than buying ships at peak prices.

financial_highlights.change: Most profitable quarter ever, per management

financial_highlights.value: ~USD 700 million gross, ~USD 600 million net of debt

segments.name: Crude tankers
segments.commentary: All crude tankers are on spot. Management said 46% of Q2 operating days are fixed; crude TC coverage is about $90,000/day. Suezmax rates are flat to slightly lower and Aframax rates significantly lower than in Q1.

segments.name: Product tankers (MR/LR2)
segments.commentary: MR spot earnings were close to $50,000/day in the last quarter. Product tanker TC coverage is about $45,000/day; product rates are significantly lower than in Q1. Some LR2s switched to dirty Aframax trades because of the earnings gap.

segments.name: LPG (VLGC)
segments.commentary: Fleet is on fixed-rate time charters. One vessel has profit-sharing upside. Repricing of one time charter came in 25-30% above the prior charter rate; another VLGC comes off charter in Q1 CY2027 at about $15,000-20,000/day above its current rate.

segments.name: Dry bulk
segments.commentary: Bulk earnings were marginally better than a year ago. Coal demand rose as LNG disruption pushed power plants to coal, and grain trade was strong. Bulk carrier rates are marginally higher than in Q1.

segments.name: Offshore (OSV and jack-up rigs)
segments.commentary: Fleet has 19 offshore vessels and 4 rigs; OSV cover for Q2 is about 90%. One rig was idle from April and is pending short-term work after monsoon. A letter of award for a 3-year contract was received on another rig, and ONGC tender was won for a rig, with management not disclosing rates.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give earnings guidance and does not forecast the market.
Fleet strategy is to replace, not expand; capacity expansion awaits prices that offer good long-term returns.
Repricing: two rigs require repricing in 2026 after the new 3-year award; OSV rates largely covered for FY27.
Debt is being paid down over the next 2 years, with the last debt maturing in November 2028.
Buyback is treated as one capital allocation option; no policy, target multiple or price band, and not yet announced.
capex_capacity: Fleet fleet of 40 ships, average age 14.5 years, plus 19 offshore vessels and 4 rigs; 2 chartered-in vessels.
Q1 FY27 transactions: sold 2 MR tankers and bought 1 MR; bought a Kamsarmax bulk carrier; in July sold LR2 Jag Lokesh and bought Jag Lakshya (6 years younger, eco-ship).
Last month alone, capex of about INR 250-300 crore already invested in fleet changes.
No annual capex budget; decisions are ship-specific and age-driven (tradability), with sales possibly ahead of the theoretical age limit if a good replacement is found.
Order book share: crude tankers ~27%, VLGC ~35%, product tankers ~20-21%, bulk carriers ~14%. Next-year deliveries about 7% of product tanker and 4% of bulk order book, per management.
demand_pricing: MR spot earnings near $50,000/day last quarter (all-time high); LPG freight rates above $100,000/day; asset prices up ~5-10% in the quarter.
Trade pattern shifts after Hormuz disruption (US and Brazil supplying Asia) raised ton-mile demand; Venezuelan crude now long-haul East; Russian product exports diverted.
Management views the shift as temporary, depending on Hormuz, Russia-Ukraine and sanctions outcomes; pipelines bypassing Hormuz have security and Red Sea risks.
Panama Canal water levels falling, restricting transits; mainly affects LPG.
Asset price cycle risk: management cited a ~20% drawdown in 2025 impairments on ships bought in 2023-24.

qa_highlights.question: Will product-to-crude switching by LR2s be permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Sheth said LR2s switched to Aframax because of the earnings gap and lack of Gulf cargoes; the switch can reverse if LR2 earnings recover.

qa_highlights.question: Buyback framework and whether a buyback is feasible at current valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: G. Shivakumar said there is no price or multiple target; buyback will be assessed by the Board like other capital allocation. The tax disadvantage on buybacks has gone, lowering the premium needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy incremental cash into ships given strong freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers to hold most cash and invest only at the margin (1-2 ships), citing the risk that ships bought at peak prices write down; it said it cannot make a market call with this uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: What fuel and earnings savings come from newer ships?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Sheth said 2020s-built ships can save up to 20-25% fuel versus pre-2013 ships, worth about $1,000-2,500/day in earnings depending on size. Switching will continue over the next few quarters, timing depending on deals.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Hormuz-exposed ships and the idle rig?
qa_highlights.answer: All ships that had to exit the Strait have exited; one ship remains there on time charter to ADNOC, trading within the Strait. The idle rig came off in April and is in talks for short-term work after the monsoon; nothing has been finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue spillover from Q4 and the 46% crude operating-days figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4-to-Q1 spillover was about INR 50 crore last quarter and is not significant this quarter. The 46% refers to fixed days for the quarter, not utilisation, since crude tankers are fully spot.

544626|2026-06.headline: Exato Q1 FY27: revenue up 50% YoY, PAT up 104% YoY, order book raised to Rs 660 crore from Rs 600 crore.
544626|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 50% YoY, EBITDA up about 82%, PBT up 102% and PAT up 104%, with margin gains attributed mainly to international business and order execution. Order book rose to Rs 660 crore after about Rs 60 crore of fresh bookings, mostly from international customers including iQor. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of at least 60-70% and profit growth of 70-80%, with ARR targeted at Rs 180-200 crore by FY27-end. The company is adding an AI infrastructure vertical, a US sales push, a potential acquisition, and an IP/platform product expected to start contributing earlier than the Q3 FY27 commitment. Absolute financial values (revenue, EBITDA, PAT in rupees) were not stated in the call.

financial_highlights.value: Up 50% YoY (absolute figure not stated in call)
Up about 82% YoY; margin expanded significantly
About Rs 30 crore executed from order book; Rs 221 crore executed up to Q4; cumulative Rs 251 crore
Rs 660 crore (Rs 600 crore at Q4); about Rs 410 crore unexecuted
About Rs 140 crore (Rs 118 crore at last call)
About 30% from maintenance, implementation and consulting

segments.name: CX and analytics / CX as a service
segments.commentary: Described as the growth engine; managed services across contact centre, workforce management, interaction analytics; BPO and IT/ITES above 70% of revenue. Management expects this vertical to remain the largest contributor.

segments.name: AI infrastructure (new vertical)
segments.commentary: Built over the last two months with HPE partnership (about two months old); not yet contributing revenue. Management expects 25-30% of FY27 contribution and margins of about 10-12% initially. Expected to start clicking within about a quarter.

segments.name: Unified communications
segments.commentary: Steady vertical; new logos include Kotak Life Insurance and Kotak Mutual Fund. Margin also expected at 10-12% in early years.

segments.name: Cloud ERP
segments.commentary: Growing at close to 20% CAGR per management; new sales team hired and a good pipeline with closures expected this quarter and later.

segments.name: IP / product (ExatoIQ, own platform)
segments.commentary: Revenue expected from this month or next; margins guided at 40-50%; two deals said to be near signing with new customers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected at least 60-70%, or more; profitability growth expected above 70-80% (organic; inorganic on top).
ARR targeted at Rs 180-200 crore by end FY27, potentially more.
AI infrastructure expected to contribute 25-30% of FY27 business at 10-12% initial margins.
IP/product revenue to start this month or next, earlier than prior Q3 FY27 commitment; margins 40-50%.
Customer target of 300-500 additions in 2-3 years (organic and inorganic); longer-term aim of 400-500 customers.
Management aims for 500 crore revenue ambition and mentions 1,000 crore in three years as a wish list, not guidance.
Revenue mix for AI infrastructure deals: about 60-70% one-time and 30-40% recurring.
capex_capacity: AI-ready infrastructure practice built over two months; includes private AI, LLM in a Box, networking, observability and secure infrastructure; part of go-to-market for next three to four quarters.
24x7 delivery team already built; management plans to add manpower in the US as Chief Revenue Officer is based there.
Acquisition under evaluation to add geographic presence in APAC, UK, Middle East or US; a big-four firm is conducting due diligence; funding may be cash, equity or a mix.
Platform readiness had been expected by March 2027; now pulled forward given BPO agreements.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs 660 crore; new bookings of about Rs 60 crore mainly from international customers, including iQor (Rs 60-65 crore) as a new logo; expansion at TaskUs and Diligenta.
Two UK customers, one of which (Diligenta) contributed significantly; US, Singapore and UK named as key international contributors.
Client retention cited at 97-98%; over 150 clients; 20-plus contracts of three to five years with large customers.
Management cites TAM of USD 500-600 million for Exato currently, growing 18-20% CAGR; CX as a service plus AI as a service combined growth of 35-40% cited.
Competition: TTEC Digital in US; Big Four and large SIs (Wipro, TCS, Accenture, Infosys) seen as not competing directly in BPO-focused CX.
Partnerships: NiCE remains largest revenue contributor; upgraded to Platinum with Mitel (APAC); Acumatica upgraded to Gold; HPE and AWS added; Fortinet and amplifAI partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 growth expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects revenue growth of at least 60-70% and profit growth of 70-80% or more, citing international deals and AI infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: Customer count and inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 300-500 customers to be added in 2-3 years, organic and inorganic; four or five large customers added in Q1; five verticals planned from four; acquisition could add one or two verticals, though later said acquisition is limited to existing verticals.

qa_highlights.question: Contribution and margins of IP revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: IP revenue expected to start this month or next, with two deals close to signing; margins guided at 40-50%, from new clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is HPE partnership recurring or one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 60-70% one-time and 30-40% recurring revenue from these contracts; commercial terms say Exato owns the customer and the product comes from HPE.

qa_highlights.question: Top-five client concentration and retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Top five clients about 60% of revenue; management says contracts are non-cancellable and renewable, and client retention is 97-98%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ARR and order book be on a cumulative basis, and what is executable balance?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 251 crore executed cumulatively, leaving about Rs 410 crore unexecuted; order book up about Rs 150-180 crore since last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company tilt to services-led revenue and what headcount is planned?

542651|2026-06.headline: KPIT Q1 FY27: constant-currency revenue grew only 0.1% YoY and fell 3.6% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 17.2% and PAT at INR 1.17 billion.

segments.name: Consumer durables

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursement ~₹104 crores at June end; channel partners up to 1,100+ from 900; 70+ locations across 30 states.

segments.name: Education loans

segments.name: Business loans / shopkeeper loans
segments.commentary: Business loans growing ~15-16%; shopkeeper loans deliberately not being accelerated given credit cost and ROA considerations.

guidance_outlook: Management guides to a June 2028 exit ROA of 3% to 3.5%, versus 1.98% today.
Opex to AUM may fluctuate 10-25 bps QoQ due to investment and clustered gold branch openings; internal benchmark trends lower over FY27.
Management expects disbursement yield gains to offset any cost of borrowing uptick; no NIM pressure seen at current trajectory.
Gold branch addition of ~400 in FY27, similar to last year's pace; 60 branches already opened this financial year.
Write-offs expected to stay around ₹275-280 crores per quarter run-rate, with no material legacy-book write-offs left.
Management is comfortable on capital for the next 4-5 quarters after the ₹2,500 crore QIP; no further raise indicated.
Provision coverage expected to remain range-bound, with rising gold and education loan share lowering overall PCR over time.
capex_capacity: 460 gold loan branches; plan to add ~400 in FY27, targeting new states including Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Madhya Pradesh.
Consumer durables capacity to process ~50,000 customers a month, per management.
Education loan origination footprint expanded from 25 to 50 locations; consultant network of 600+ partners.
AI estate: 101 AI projects across 21 departments (50 deployed, 51 in pipeline); ~130 smart agents live in production.
demand_pricing: Disbursement yield up ~50 bps QoQ on product mix; portfolio yield up ~17-19 bps; management cites pricing power in prime PL and digital channels.
New products accounted for 26% of disbursements in Q1 vs 24% in Q4 and 20% in the quarter before.
Management says it will slow growth in products where calibration needs it; business loans being grown only to 10-16% levels versus over 40% in used cars.
Retail loan exposure industry-wide grew over 16% YoY as of March 2026; Q1 FY27 cumulative GST collections up 8.4% YoY.
6 MoB 30+ on Q1 sourcing at 0.64%, vs 1.05% in Q4 and 1.66% in Q3FY25 (as stated by management).

524000|2026-09.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q2 FY27: PAT up 22% QoQ to ₹375 crore, ROA 2.18%, credit cost down to 2.19%, AUM ₹74,008 crore.
524000|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as an inflection point, with AUM up about 10.4% QoQ to ₹74,008 crore and PAT of ₹375 crore (up 21.8% QoQ). NIM plus fees rose 16 bps QoQ to 9.26%, while credit cost fell to 2.19% from 2.40-2.41% and GNPA fell to 1.20% from 1.37%. Opex-to-average AUM rose to 4.15% on frontloaded investments in collections, AI and gold branches, which management said sits within the 10-25 bps guided range. New products contributed 28% of disbursements, and the company is still building cross-sell.

segments.name: Prime Personal Loans (digital)
segments.commentary: Now 42% of PL disbursements (38% in Q1); average monthly disbursement about ₹577 crore, up 8% QoQ.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Quarterly disbursements ₹1,066 crore vs ₹875 crore in Q1; network rose to 550 branches from 460, with 90 added in the quarter and about 200 planned for FY27.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement ₹127 crore; channel partners up to 1,250 from 1,100, across 90+ locations in 13 states.

segments.name: Education loans
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement ₹218 crore; consultant network at 700 partners; about 35% of sanctions fully digital.

segments.name: Consumer durables
segments.commentary: Quarterly disbursement ₹606 crore vs ₹433 crore in Q1; 20,000 dealers across 360 locations.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost expected to keep sloping down and gradually stabilise; management said it is tracking better than plan, with a visible path over the next one to two years.
Opex-to-AUM expected to move on plan, with 300-400 branches invested in per year and gold branches breaking even in about 13 months.
Management targets a sustainable ROA with a 'peak' expected in about 2.5-3 years; a commitment on ROA by June 2028 was referenced.
A 25 bps lending rate increase was already passed through about a week before the call; pass-through of further hikes is expected to depend on product and market.
AUM CAGR target of 35-40% over the next couple of years was referenced by an analyst; management did not restate it.
Management aims for consumer durable customer franchise to roughly double this year.
capex_capacity: Gold loan network at 550 branches, targeting about 200 new branches in FY27.
AI portfolio at 143 projects (up from 101), of which 84 are live in production and 59 underway; 34 delivered in Q2, a record quarter.
Collections capacity expanded with product-segmented expert teams and AI-led predictive analytics.
Commercial vehicle channel partners at 1,250; education consultant network at 700; consumer durable dealers at 20,000.
demand_pricing: Portfolio yield 14.08%, up about 45 bps QoQ; disbursement yield up about 20 bps QoQ after roughly 50 bps rise last quarter.
New products contributed 28% of disbursements (26% in Q1, 24% before that).
Management cites a gap of about 200 bps between portfolio yield and disbursement yield.
Digital-led AI campaigns reported 1.5-2x higher click-through rates, with outreach to more than 15 lakh leads per month at 60%+ lower cost than agencies.
Management flagged possible fee compression from a proposed insurance commission regulation but said earnings could absorb it.

qa_highlights.question: How far has cross-sell progressed (products per customer now vs a year or two ago), and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a products-per-customer figure; said cross-sell has only just started and the metric will be more relevant in about a year, with improvement each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How many new products are profitable, and what blended ROA is possible once they mature?
qa_highlights.answer: No product-level count given. Management said gold branches break even in about 13 months, new businesses are not yet at full ROA, and peak ROA is expected in about 2.5-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Where will credit cost settle, and how will product mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 2.19% a first milestone that looks structural. CRO said 12 MoB 90-plus for origination post September 2024 improved by over 53% versus the book 12 months earlier, and credit cost is tracking better than plan.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of borrowing cost to a 50 bps repo hike and fixed vs floating mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost of borrowing rose minimally during the tightening; NCDs are about 30% of borrowings and fixed-rate; pricing power allows pass-through. A 25 bps increase was already passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Trade-off between growth and profitability; sustainable ROA and the split of ROA gains between operating leverage and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all three levers (spread, opex-to-AUM, credit cost) contribute over the next two years. Quarterly opex may fluctuate because of AI investment; no specific split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is asset quality improvement from underwriting or benign credit conditions? Are AI/ML models reducing loss rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to proprietary models (30-35 models) and calibration. It cited bureau data showing consumer durable borrowers completing 9-month loans are about 40% better credit than industry.

qa_highlights.question: With most of the book under 12 months seasoned, why are write-offs still high, and what is the impact of the insurance commission regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: CRO said slippages were contained across stages and GNPA and write-offs are falling; core credit cost impairment is stable in absolute terms despite over 10% QoQ book growth. On insurance commissions, management said fee compression could be absorbed by lending spreads and operating leverage.

financial_highlights.metric: Net interest income incl. fees and other income

financial_highlights.change: +16 bps QoQ, +86 bps YoY (NIM alone per CFO)

532934|2026-06.headline: PPAP Automotive Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34.1% YoY to INR156.4 crores, with EBITDA up 33.3% to INR12.4 crores.
532934|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 34.1% YoY to INR156.4 crores and EBITDA rose 33.3% YoY to INR12.4 crores, driven by higher volumes, better fixed-cost absorption and capacity utilisation. Management said raw material inflation (about 4% of raw material cost increase, only about 2% passed through so far) is holding back margin expansion, with the rest under negotiation and expected to settle by end-Q2 or early Q3. Restructuring continues: tooling is to be hived into Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited by Q3 FY27, and Avinya Batteries is to merge into the parent by Q4 FY27. Battery losses remain a concern despite 4x revenue growth off a low base.

financial_highlights.metric: EV programme share of lifetime orders
financial_highlights.change: vs roughly INR11 crores in year-ago period (per analyst)
sales moderated QoQ/seasonally; about 30% of quarter revenue from exports

financial_highlights.metric: Sale proceeds from Japanese JV exit
financial_highlights.change: INR8 crores used for tax; 25% of balance to working capital, rest to strategic capex

segments.name: Automotive parts
segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor; growth from higher OEM production schedules, better utilisation and new programme ramp-ups. Lifetime orders INR131 crores, of which EV about INR64 crores.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Revenue up 30% YoY, about 6% of total revenue. Launched 345 SKUs (portfolio 1,312 vs 1,264 at FY26 end); distributors expanded to 155. Management targets about 10% of revenue over time.

segments.name: Tooling
segments.commentary: Utilisation 84%; 30 mold orders received in quarter, pipeline of 124 molds. Plans 20% higher output than the 148 molds developed in FY26. Being moved to Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Moderated in Q1 on seasonal demand after 38% growth in FY26; about 30% of quarter revenue from exports. Under 1% of revenue; medium-term aspiration about 10%.

segments.name: Battery (Avinya)
segments.commentary: Revenue about 4x YoY on a low base, but Q1 contribution weak amid raw material cost increases, pricing pressure and shorter customer delivery timelines. Management expects improvement from Q2 but calls it a continuing concern.

guidance_outlook: Sales expected to rise sequentially each quarter; Q2 to date reportedly shows continued strong YoY growth.
EBITDA margin expected to improve gradually in Q2–Q3 as raw material price settlements with customers conclude by end-Q2/early Q3.
Target of about 12–13% sustainable margin for automotive ancillaries on OEM business (management view, versus about 19% cited by analyst as current).
Targeted to be net debt free within 3 years.
Aftermarket expected to keep growing around 30%; new distribution warehouse in West India planned this quarter.
Tooling output to increase 20% in FY27 versus 148 molds in FY26.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex focused on EPDM capability: one new line operational in Q2 FY27 and two further lines planned in FY27.
Tooling toolroom expansion and land acquisition in west area near Sambhaji Nagar planned in FY27.
Hutchinson-linked technology investment in machines and equipment for new product development (no JV; amount not given).
Industrial product business needs no major capex (low-value tooling made in-house).
Capacity utilisation at 73% in Q1; tooling at 84%.
demand_pricing: Industry posted record Q1 sales: passenger vehicles +25% YoY to 1.27 million units; two-wheelers +20.3%; commercial vehicles +18.3%; three-wheelers +29.7%; vehicle exports record Q1.
Raw material cost up about 4%; about 2% passed to customers so far, with the remaining about 50% of the increase still under negotiation.

Technology partnership with Hutchinson (sealing systems) signed; initial focus on glass run channel products for Indian market. Management expects clarity on revenue by end-2026; no revenue figure given. Named competitors: SFC, Anand Nishikawa, Toyota Bussei.
Mahindra: Tier 1 sealing products SOP scheduled for Q3 FY27; Tier 2 injection moulding tooling and sunroof sealing in development.
Management said pre-COVID margins are very difficult to regain given changed raw material prices and competitive pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is expected from the Hutchinson partnership over the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical estimate; products are being co-developed for all customers with focus on India, and clarity on timing expected by end-2026. Focus product is glass run channel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating margin plan and when will margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4% raw material inflation with about 2% passed through; the rest expected to be settled by end-Q2 or early Q3. Internal margin targets exist but were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the JV exit proceeds be used?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR100 crores received; INR8 crores for tax; 25% of the remainder for working capital; the rest for strategic capex in EPDM, tooling expansion and western land.

qa_highlights.question: When does the battery business reach breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 contribution was weak; management hopes for improvement from Q2 but acknowledged it remains a concern without giving a breakeven figure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth momentum continue through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 to date shows strong growth and expects sequential sales increases; not a one-off from low base or deferred orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin level and why has top-line growth been muted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 12–13% sustainable margin for OEM ancillaries; attributed past slow growth to actions taken over 2–3 years and to electrical content gains not reaching the company's sealing and moulded parts portfolio.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: about 50% of the 4% cost increase still unrecovered from customers; settlement timing (end-Q2/early Q3) is a key watch item.
Battery segment losses continuing; Q1 contribution described as weak.
Industrial Products sales moderation in Q1; seasonality versus trend.
Geopolitical developments, commodity price volatility and global supply chain dynamics flagged by management.
Hutchinson partnership revenue remains unquantified; timing clarity only by end-2026.
Debt: net debt-free target within 3 years; finance cost trajectory not quantified.
Restructuring execution: tooling hive-off by Q3 FY27 and Avinya merger by Q4 FY27.

539787|2026-06.headline: HCG Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~13% YoY to INR6,951 million on 11% volume growth; adjusted EBITDA up 20% to INR1,339 million, margin 19.4%.
539787|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR6,951 million, up about 13% YoY, with volumes up 11% and ARPP up 2%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 20% YoY to INR1,339 million, with margin expanding to 19.4% from 18.2%, helped by a payor mix shift toward non-institutional business (69% vs 67%). The North Bangalore hospital, opened in May 2026, contributed INR67 million revenue and management says peak EBITDA loss was reached this quarter. A chemo drug discontinuation cost about 1.5% of top line but was margin-accretive.

segments.name: South cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue grew ~16% YoY on volume and realization growth, including North Bangalore's INR67 million; cash and TPA mix improving in Bangalore CoE and Vizag.

segments.name: West cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 9% YoY; Maharashtra grew over 14%, Gujarat moderate. Institutional business fell over 4% as low-margin scheme immunotherapy was cut; ARPP broadly stable.

segments.name: East cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22% YoY on volume growth, despite temporary ARPP moderation.

segments.name: Hospital size buckets
segments.commentary: Hospitals above INR10 crore per month rose from 4 to 7; INR5-10 crore bucket fell from 14 to 11; below INR5 crore rose from 6 to 7 (including North Bangalore).

guidance_outlook: Mid-teens revenue growth outlook maintained for existing and new centres combined.
Long-term EBITDA margin: 21-22% within about 2 years; 24-25% over the next 4-5 years (management clarified 25% timeline in Q&A).

North Bangalore: peak EBITDA loss reached in Q1 FY27; losses expected to fall over the next few quarters; monthly breakeven expected this year; optimal 60-65% utilisation in 3rd-4th year of operation.
Chemo drug discontinuation to keep ~1.5% top-line impact for the next few quarters, may marginally decline.
ARPP growth expected in line with inflation.
Marketing spend to settle at 2.5-2.6% of revenue long term (2.9% currently).
Maintenance capex ~INR100 crore for FY27.
ESOP charge to be quantified and reported in Q2 once policy is finalised.
Interest cost expected to moderate versus last year after INR170 crore debt repayment.
capex_capacity: 121 beds added in Q1 (South 61, West 27, East 26, Kenya 7).
Planned additions: 65 beds in FY27, 520 beds across FY28-FY29, 230 beds in FY30; ~60% brownfield.
Three greenfield projects in pipeline; two (~180 beds, Whitefield in South and a Maharashtra site in West) expected to operationalise around end-FY28 and the following year.
Commissioned a new LINAC in Rajkot (now a Comprehensive Cancer Centre); added two surgical robots (Nashik and Bangalore CoE replacement).
North Bangalore MR-LINAC commissioned in July 2026.
Existing facilities can run at 75-80% utilisation; Southern cluster was 68% in FY26.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of 11% drove the top line; ARPP up 2% helped by payor mix, offset by case mix shift away from high-value low-margin therapies.
Government/CGHS price capping cost about 1.5% of top line; margin impact not quantified.
Discontinued some high-value, low-margin chemo drugs (about 1.5% of Q1 revenue), which management says was margin-accretive.
Institutional business reduced about 200 bps of revenue mix; ~50% of centres are at 20%+ EBITDA margin.
North Bangalore: 550+ new patient registrations and 300+ admissions in its first quarter; onboarded about 20 oncologists in the last 4-5 months.
Sales and marketing spend up more than 20% YoY to about 2.9% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Growth in hospital revenue buckets and like-to-like growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Hospitals above INR10 crore/month rose from 4 to 7; like-to-like growth not disclosed and to be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for North Bangalore losses and ESOP charge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes peak EBITDA loss was reached in Q1; losses to fall over coming quarters. ESOP charge to be assessed and reported in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of drug discontinuation on FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1.5% top-line impact in Q1, expected to stay in the same range for next few quarters; margin-accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Capex in Q1 and maintenance capex for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 capex about INR750 million (growth ~INR350 million, maintenance ~INR400 million per the call); FY27 maintenance capex about INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term EBITDA margin target and levers?
qa_highlights.answer: 21-22% in about 2 years, 24-25% in 4-5 years, driven by payor mix, clinical complexity, operating leverage and North Bangalore losses declining.

qa_highlights.question: Cash and use of rights issue proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Used INR170 crore for debt repayment, about INR150 crore to raise Vizag stake from 51% to 85%, and about INR95 crore for general corporate purposes per the call (figures as transcribed).

risks_watch: North Bangalore ramp-up: utilisation, insurance empanelment and loss trajectory; first-year losses still weigh on EBITDA.
Pricing pressure from CGHS/government price capping; ARPP up only 2% and management says top line could have been better.
Institutional business decline in West (over 4%) and Gujarat slowdown; watch replacement by cash/non-institutional patients.
ESOP charge impact on P&L, to be disclosed in Q2.
Margin target credibility: 24-25% EBITDA ambition depends on payor mix shift and operating leverage.
Management did not disclose cluster-level utilisation or like-to-like growth; disclosure limited to annual reporting.
539787|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and volume momentum, but candid that top-line growth could have been better given price capping. Management was guarded on specifics, deferring cluster utilisation, like-to-like growth, CGHS margin impact and ARPP drivers to annual disclosure or offline follow-up.
