539524|2026-06.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.1% to Rs 798 crore, with EBITDA margin of 31.0%, and guidance may move toward mid-teens growth.
539524|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 798 crore grew 19.1% YoY, described as the highest quarterly growth in four years, led by patient volume growth of 8.2% and sample volume growth of 10.7%. EBITDA rose 28.7% to Rs 247 crore (31.0% margin) and PAT rose 27.2% to Rs 170 crore. Management said the CGHS/ECHS price revision adds 2-3% to realisations, and it may be more towards mid-teens revenue growth than early teens. Management will not revise the 27-28% margin guidance until after Q2, and leans towards reinvesting any upside.

segments.name: Swasthfit (bundled wellness packages)
segments.commentary: Growing about 20% YoY, but its share of revenue is flat at about 27% because total revenue grew at a similar pace. Management expects this growth to be sustained.

segments.name: B2C vs B2B
segments.commentary: B2C is about 75% of the mix and B2B about 25%, which management considers a good balance and intends to keep.

segments.name: Genomics
segments.commentary: Contributes less than 5% of the portfolio and is not yet moving significantly; management does not disclose it separately.

segments.name: West India (Suburban)
segments.commentary: Growth is close to double digits after LIMS integration. Suburban profitability is no longer tracked separately after its voluntary liquidation and back-end merger.

segments.name: Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: Management aims to grow it at double digits, in line with or close to overall revenue, and says it is achieving this.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth now seen towards mid-teens rather than early teens for FY27, versus the earlier guidance; the Q1 beat was slightly ahead of expectations.
EBITDA margin guidance of 27-28% is unchanged for now; management will reassess after Q2 and leans towards reinvesting any upside into growth.
Patient volume growth guidance of 6-7% for FY27 is unchanged; management said Q1 came in slightly ahead and that it is too early to call the full year.
CGHS/ECHS price uplift of about 2-3% at company level is expected to flow through for at least another 2-3 quarters and to support margins for one or two more quarters.
General price increase is not planned for H1; it will be reassessed towards the end of the year based on competitor pricing and cost pressures.
Capex of about Rs 140-150 crore per year; 12-15 lab additions planned for FY27 and 3-4 radiology centres (Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns).
International business is a 3-5 year project; management has not set a contribution target and says it will remain below 5% for at least the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance of about Rs 140-150 crore for the year, covering maintenance capex plus high-end radiology centres in Delhi NCR and Tier 2 North India.
Plans to add 12-15 labs in FY27, similar to last year; network addition numbers are disclosed once a year.
Plans to add 3-4 radiology centres this year, mainly Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns outside Delhi NCR.
Capacity utilisation is not disclosed; management says capacity is never a constraint in pathology.
Sovaaka premium wellness centre: only the first centre is launched and is in the learning and stabilisation phase; no scale-up yet.
demand_pricing: Patient volume growth of 8.2% was spread across geographies; management said it is too early to call a sustained shift from the 5.5-6% levels of two quarters ago, because the fever season has not yet started.
CGHS/ECHS price revision is worth about 2-3% of realisations; the rest of the 10% rise in revenue per patient came from test and geography mix, per management.
Industry growth acceleration is described as structural and broad-based across geographies, with no single trigger identified yet.
Competitive intensity is seen as staying high; management sees no structural price change in recent quarters.
Gross margin is near 81%. Management says higher-realisation tests carry higher COGS, so margin is unlikely to improve significantly.
Weather in Q1 was unusual (more heat, some showers), and its effect on diagnostics volume is not yet known.
Tier 3 and below is about 39% of FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation growth comes from CGHS/ECHS, and will it continue for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: CGHS/ECHS price increase adds about 2-3% at company level and should continue for at least another 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guidance be upgraded from 27-28% margin and mid-teens growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is more likely to be mid-teens than early teens; margin guidance will be reviewed after Q2, with a lean towards reinvestment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Swasthfit growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Swasthfit grew about 20% in Q1 and management expects this rate to be sustained, with traction in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Neuome and international plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Neuome (30% stake, up to Rs 3.5 crore) is a diagnostic supply-chain innovation play with operational benefit, not a new business. International is a long-term project: Ghana (80% of Sunshine Healthcare, up to GHS 45.6 million) and a Dubai subsidiary, with focus on Africa, Middle East, CIS and Southeast Asia; no target set.

qa_highlights.question: How should the cash of about Rs 1,700 crore be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily M&A to build presence in the West and South, plus high-end radiology centres as capex on top of maintenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost as a percentage of revenue fall to 16.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a reclassification of logistics and courier costs out of manpower cost into other costs, applied like-to-like in the previous quarter too, not a structural change.

500330|2026-06.headline: Raymond Q1 FY27 consolidated total income rose 13% to INR628 crores, with EBITDA up 14% to INR100 crores at a 15.9% margin.
500330|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR628 crores (up 13% YoY) and EBITDA reached INR100 crores (up 14% YoY) at a 15.9% margin, versus 15.7% a year earlier. Aerospace (JKMGAL) revenue grew 40% to INR123 crores, but its EBITDA margin fell to 21.2% from 23.7% because R&D for new programmes was expensed in the quarter. Precision Technology and Auto Components (JKMPTL) revenue grew 11% to INR444 crores, with EBITDA up 46% to INR61 crores and margin expanding to 13.8% from 10.6%, driven by export ramp-up and operating leverage. Management reiterated a 25% organic growth commitment for aerospace and plans for an aftermarket business launching in Q2 FY27 and a greenfield facility in Andhra Pradesh targeting commercial production in late 2027.

financial_highlights.change: +13% YoY (vs INR555 crores in Q1 FY26)
+14% YoY (vs INR87 crores in Q1 FY26)
Company stated it remains net debt-free

segments.name: Aerospace & Defence (JKMGAL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR123 crores (+40% YoY) and EBITDA INR26 crores at 21.2% margin, down from 23.7%, due to expensed R&D for new programmes. Order book of INR5,960 crores over 10 years and RFQ pipeline of INR1,632 crores; mass production of precision defence components has commenced.

segments.name: Precision Technology & Auto Components (JKMPTL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR444 crores (+11% YoY), led by export ramp-up, with EBITDA INR61 crores at 13.8% margin (vs 10.6%). Automotive aftermarket product line scheduled for launch in Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Aerospace: committed 25% organic growth for the year; management said it is slightly ahead of that in Q1.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to follow the current trend, per management's answer on FY27 margins (analyst had cited a 12-13% range).
Aerospace mature EBITDA margin target around 25%; precision manufacturing around 12-13% in the near and medium term.
Andhra Pradesh greenfield facility (Gudipalli, near Bangalore Airport) targeted for commercial production in late 2027; up to 6 months of approvals, so meaningful revenue from FY28.
Existing aerospace facility now expected to exceed the earlier INR600 crore revenue estimate, per the Parivartan improvement programme.
Asset turns on new business: aerospace about 1.8-2.2x, automotive about 2-2.5x; ROCE expected to be broadly maintained.
Aftermarket business for automotive components and white-label products to roll out in Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: INR1,000 crore five-year capex plan: INR510 crores for aerospace and INR430 crores for auto; management says it is progressing on schedule.
Greenfield Andhra Pradesh facility (Gudipalli, near Bangalore Airport) groundwork on track; commercial production targeted for late 2027.
Setting up an advanced training and production facility near the greenfield site ahead of schedule for pre-launch readiness.
Plans to add special processes such as heat treatment at the Andhra facility to increase vertical integration.
Current aerospace order book relates only to the existing facility; new capacity is over a year away.
demand_pricing: Aerospace demand described as well ahead of supply; management said supply chain constraints (titanium, alloys) eased in Q1 but cited a large backlog.
Export revival for auto components helped by the India-UK CETA (in force 15 July 2026) and the rollback of US tariffs; Tier 1 buyers rebuilding inventory.
Aerospace customer concentration: over 25 global customers, with top 3 at about 40-45% of the business. Management aims to widen this to 8-10 high-value customers.
Input costs rising: logistics, carbide and HSS tooling, and minimum wage increases. Some costs are being passed to customers; management expects some quarterly pressure.
Management said it had N4 self-certification and that engine-critical parts are the core; it is not yet in N1 (rotating parts).

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity for inorganic deals after the warrant issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it keeps evaluating inorganic opportunities across aerospace, auto components and defence; the warrants give flexibility, and it will update only when deals are close.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company exposed to aerospace casting and forging supply bottlenecks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not exposed as much because critical-part programmes have not yet transferred; the constraint is seen as an execution advantage.

qa_highlights.question: Will consolidated EBITDA margins stay around 12-13% in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the same trend as shown in Q1 at consolidated level, with margins better than last year.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the 10-year aerospace order book versus the earlier 5-year figure?
qa_highlights.answer: The change was made to give longer visibility; the 5-year breakup summed to about INR2,765 crores versus INR2,350 crores last quarter, which an analyst computed as about 17% QoQ growth, and management confirmed this. The INR5,960 crore book covers only the existing facility.

qa_highlights.question: How much can the existing facility produce, and what is the timeline for the new facility revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing facility is expected to exceed the earlier INR600 crore estimate under the Parivartan programme. New facility revenue starts in FY28 after up to 6 months of approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What are asset turns and long-term margin targets by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Aerospace new business asset turns of 1.8-2.2x and auto 2-2.5x. Long-term EBITDA margin targets are about 25% for aerospace and 12-13% for precision manufacturing.

risks_watch: Aerospace margin (21.2%, down 2.5 pp YoY) depends on R&D write-offs and product maturity; management expects stabilisation as programmes move to steady state.
Rising input costs (tooling, logistics, wages) may compress margins for a quarter before pass-through or efficiency offsets.
Customer concentration: top 3 aerospace customers at about 40-45%.
Greenfield ramp depends on customer approvals (up to 6 months); late 2027 start with FY28 revenue impact.
Inorganic deals are not yet identified, and the warrant issue means possible dilution if deals close.
Medical certification obtained, but no business plan yet; defence strategy under development after hiring a former BEL executive.

531768|2026-06.headline: Poly Medicure Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 30.3% to INR525 crore (12.4% organic), with consolidated EBITDA margin at 24.1% and standalone at 28%.
531768|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 30.3% to INR525 crore, of which INR72.3 crore came from acquisitions, leaving organic growth at 12.4% to INR453.1 crore. Standalone revenue rose 12.3% to INR431 crore and standalone EBITDA was INR120.8 crore (28% margin), above the 25-27% FY27 guidance, helped by price hikes and inventory gains. Middle East sales fell 32% due to West Asia logistics disruption, while renal degrew 3.8% amid Chinese pricing pressure. Management maintained FY27 guidance and launched a "PolyMed 3.0" target to double revenue by FY30.

financial_highlights.change: +12.3% YoY; domestic INR146 crore (+16.2%), international INR281.8 crore (+10%)
Flagged as above historic 68-69% trend; partly price hikes and inventory gain
From INR2.9 crore a year ago, led by PendraCare plus domestic scale-up

financial_highlights.value: Standalone working capital debt about INR250 crore (revolver); Citieffe loan about EUR 9 million, EUR 1.5-2 million repaid annually

segments.name: Infusion therapy
segments.commentary: Revenue INR259.2 crore, +11.1%, led by domestic growth of 20%+ from higher value-added products and price increases.

segments.name: Orthopedics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR49.2 crore, largely reflecting consolidation of Citieffe.

segments.name: Cardiology
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28.6 crore versus INR2.9 crore a year ago, driven by PendraCare acquisition and domestic scale-up.

segments.name: Renal
segments.commentary: Revenue INR43.2 crore, -3.8%; pressure from Chinese dialyzer imports, with company choosing price hikes over volume defence. Anti-dumping probe on China and Malaysia dialyzers initiated, 20% injury margin claimed.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Revenue INR141.9 crore, +18.5%, forming the balance of the consolidated mix.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated FY27 revenue guidance INR2,300-2,400 crore including full-year PendraCare and Citieffe; maintained after Q1.
Standalone FY27 revenue guidance INR1,900-2,000 crore; domestic expected to grow over 20%, international over 15%.
Standalone EBITDA margin guided at 25-27% for FY27, with management expecting to close near the upper end; standalone gross margin guided at 67-69% going forward.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 23-25%; consolidated gross margin expected at 71-72%.
FY27 capex INR200-225 crore; asset turns 1.2-1.4x.
Renal FY27 growth targeted at 15-18%, possibly close to 20%, contingent on anti-dumping outcome expected by year-end.
Long-term aspiration to double consolidated revenue by FY30 (PolyMed 3.0, 'Ascent'), roughly 80% organic and 20% inorganic; margins expected to be held at similar levels rather than expanded.
Faridabad (Palwal) plant expected online by March 2027, focused on orthopedics, transfusion and extra infusion capacity; Noida plant commercial from Q1 FY28, focused on cardiology.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR200-225 crore, with cash earmarked partly for two plants under construction.
Faridabad (Palwal) facility targeted online by March 2027 for orthopedics, transfusion and infusion capacity expansion.
Noida facility targeted for commercial operation in Q1 FY28, for cardiology expansion.
Asset turns of 1.2-1.4x expected to continue on the balance sheet.
PendraCare and Citieffe manufacturing shifts to India are in progress and at regulatory approval stage.
demand_pricing: Middle East: 32% decline due to West Asia crisis; orders are piling up at ports as ships are not calling and containers are hard to find. Management expects 20-25%+ growth once normalised.
Europe: +17.6% organic growth, back to the 17-18% planned rate after adding new customers; Southeast Asia also growing well.
US: exports expected at USD 3.5-4 million for FY27; current duty 10%.
Price hikes taken at start of FY27 to offset raw material increases; management sees raw material peak as past, with only minor further changes.
Renal faces pricing pressure from Chinese players importing duty-free via ASEAN FTA; company raised prices rather than defend volume.
PendraCare had about 20% Middle East exposure and is currently not growing; Citieffe growing in mid-to-high single digits.

qa_highlights.question: How will standalone revenue reach INR350-400 crore incremental growth, given about 12% growth in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally the lowest and early-year price hikes slowed sales, with recovery later in the quarter; momentum should lift Q2 onwards to meet guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What will the INR850 crore cash be used for?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic and inorganic expansion, including Brazil direct sales, technology in cardiology, oncology and orthopedics, adjacent technologies, and capex at two plants under construction.

qa_highlights.question: Will Middle East exports resume and will Q2 gross margin be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipping remains disrupted and orders are stuck at ports. Standalone gross margin is guided at 68-69%, so some correction from Q1's 71.5% is likely, with EBITDA broadly held by higher revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the 2x revenue goal and the implied gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated 2x is the target and standalone will grow faster than the subsidiaries; did not provide a precise breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt and repayments?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone has only about INR250 crore working capital revolver; PendraCare has no long-term loan; Citieffe has about EUR 9 million loan with EUR 1.5-2 million repaid annually.

qa_highlights.question: Will the working capital cycle improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash conversion cycle remains around 140 days, same as March; management declined to give forward guidance given geopolitical delays.

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
539334|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.
K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.
Dye utilisation has decreased due to the global scenario, per management.
Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume weakness mitigating, and is the company on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is optimistic, citing 40 days of data, and expects Q2 to beat Q1; volumes should be met while protecting value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 not reflect the upside from orders held back from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

risks_watch: Volumes are down about 17% in fertiliser and about 39% in chemicals YoY, and management has prioritised pricing over volume.
Unit 6 start-up timing depends on long-term raw material contracts, due by August or September 2026; ammonia and sulphur supply and price remain volatile with Hormuz still closed.
Working-capital strain from advance sulphur payments; acid plants at low load.
Management guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, and its PAT target is 8.5-9% versus a remark of up to about 10%.
Inconsistent figures in the call: revenue of Rs 280.1 crore vs Rs 281.1 crore; EBITDA of Rs 31.9 crore vs Rs 31 crore; PAT growth of 9.4% vs 9%. Verify against the filing.
Capex of Rs 303 crore remains to be spent against the Rs 512 crore plan.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 280.1 crore (CEO remarks) / Rs 281.1 crore (CFO remarks)
Rs 31.9 crore (11.4% margin); CFO quoted Rs 31 crore

544914|2026-06.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.
544914|2026-06.overview: Steamhouse reported record quarterly steam volumes of about 3,05,816 tons, up 16.7% YoY and 11.52% QoQ, with revenue from operations up 13.35% to INR128.62 crore. EBITDA rose 60.08% to INR30.93 crore, lifting margin to 24.05% (up 702 bps), while PAT rose 80.25% to INR18.34 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher volumes, utilisation (41.40% vs 36.06% YoY) and operating leverage, and noted the exit from low-margin coal trading. Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore at FY26 end, with IPO proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and capacity expansion.

segments.name: Steam generation and distribution (own boilers)
segments.commentary: Own-generated steam was 73.7% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said it will be the source of future growth, with waste-to-energy boilers at Vapi supporting realisation.

segments.name: Steam trading (purchased and resold)
segments.commentary: Traded steam was 22.2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Coal trading has been discontinued as low-margin; two trading agreements (Dahej SEZ, Haldia) are signed and management declined to split margins between generation and trading.

segments.name: Industrial gases / nitrogen
segments.commentary: PSA-based nitrogen plant of 350 Nm3/hr commissioned at Ankleshwar. Management described it as currently small and plans air separation units for LIN/LOX and other gases.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to take utilisation to 60%-65%; newer boilers expected at about 50% in initial months after commissioning.
Steam volume growth of 5%-10% expected at existing locations; company-level 20%-25% volume growth described as 'very comfortably' achievable with new capacity and demand revival.

EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 expected to be maintained for next few quarters; Q2 seasonally weaker due to monsoon; full-year performance expected to be at par with or better than Q1 run-rate (management said 'we will try' to sustain growth).
Finance costs expected to moderate in FY27 as IPO proceeds repay high-cost borrowings.
Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive.

Capacity to rise from 345 TPH to approx. 705 TPH; four under-construction projects (Jhagadia, Vapi, Nandesari, AMC Pirana) targeted to go live in FY27; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28; IPO-funded Dahej, Ankleshwar and Panoli by Q1 FY29.
Una (Himachal Pradesh) 300 TPH EPC project: expected 8%-10% clear margin per ton, pass-through to customers, no capex; agreement not yet signed.
capex_capacity: Installed steam capacity 345 TPH, about 70% contracted; expansion to approx. 705 TPH.
Around INR60 crore further capex needed to complete the four under-construction projects; another INR170 crore planned over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects.
Ankleshwar nitrogen PSA plant of 350 Nm3/hr commenced; ASU for LIN/LOX under evaluation with build-own-operate partners as an option.
Una EPC: 300 TPH community boiler, project value approx. INR311 crore incl. GST, funded by Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd; 9% revenue share to be recovered from end customers.
Pipeline network above 60 km across seven industrial areas; management estimates adding pipelines costs 10%-20% of existing infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Management attributed volume growth to revival in chemical and pharma demand after weak FY24-FY26; tyre and food processing (Haldia agreement) added as new segments.
Customer contracts tenor 1-10 years with non-exit clauses; fuel cost pass-through predominantly monthly, some quarterly; newer contracts include minimum guaranteed off-take.
Management claims 25%-35% cost saving versus captive boilers using furnace oil, LDO or natural gas; less beneficial for large coal-fired textile users, which may be at par.
Monsoon disrupts operations because fuel is wet and industrial clusters flood; Q2 seasonally weaker.
Realisation per ton improved due to better utilisation and higher waste-to-energy mix at Vapi.

financial_highlights.metric: Clean EBITDA (adj. for operating lease expenses)

financial_highlights.change: +80.25% YoY (vs INR10.18 crore); PAT margin 14.26%, +529 bps
vs 36.06% in Q1 FY26 and 38.32% in Q4 FY26
vs INR281.62 crore at FY26 end

541195|2026-06.headline: MIDHANI Q1 FY27 turnover rose 40.46% to Rs 239.49 crore, but LPG and raw-material costs compressed EBITDA margin to about 20%.
541195|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover was Rs 239.49 crore (up 40.46% YoY) and value of production Rs 260.36 crore (up 7.9%). PBT rose 25.89% to Rs 23.92 crore and PAT rose 27.42% to Rs 16.31 crore. EBITDA was Rs 46.6 crore (up 12.89%), with margin about 20% versus roughly 23% expected, pressured by LPG price spikes and adverse raw-material price variance of about Rs 13-14 crore. Order book stood at about Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026, now won entirely through competitive bidding.

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 2,329 crore as of 1 July 2026

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Defense about 66%, space (ISRO) about 21%, energy about 9%, others about 4%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Current-year export sales Rs 33 crore to date with open export order book of about Rs 25 crore; target about 10% of turnover (about Rs 100-120 crore).

segments.name: Titanium
segments.commentary: Melted about 750 tonnes last year after new melting facility; titanium orders worth about Rs 600 crore cited. Management says titanium and super alloys carry higher margins than special steel.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 margins expected to be hit somewhat; management expects normalisation from Q3 FY27, with EBITDA margin returning toward 20-21%.
FY27 growth expected to exceed FY26 growth, though management said sustaining Q1's 40% growth through the year is not practicable.
FY27 normal capex about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance; Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex over 2-3 years, with returns from year 4 and proposal still awaiting Board and ministry approval.
Metal bank: procurement under way for one customer; further clarity expected by end of Q2 FY27, with implementation targeted next quarter.
Aluminium JV plant at Nellore (with NALCO) being closed; a separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied 7000-series aluminium billets has been done as first commercial order.
Export expectation: at least 15-20% increase on the 10% export base over the next 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex proposed for replacing ageing equipment; sent to ministry for evaluation, management declined to give timeline.
Isothermal forging completed in 6,000-tonne press for nickel-based super alloy for fighter aircraft engine; orders for four super alloy grades and three titanium grades to be executed this year.
New titanium melting facility commissioned last year; about 750 tonnes melted last year, with expected growth.
Spring plant in campus started; sample order received from BEML. Preliminary BAFA licence obtained for metal powder equipment, expected on campus by next year.
Bulletproof jacket (ABHED, from DRDO/IIT Delhi) fabricated; testing expected to complete this quarter, with test certificates by next quarter.
demand_pricing: Raw-material prices of nickel, molybdenum, tungsten rose sharply; cobalt also higher. Adverse price variance of about Rs 13 crore (or Rs 14 crore per later remark) in Q1.
LPG price nearly doubled due to Middle East conflict; furnaces are LPG-fired, affecting Q1 and possibly Q2.
Freight cost mostly booked at fixed terms; management said it sometimes absorbs freight increases on fixed-price contracts.
No nomination-based orders now; all orders won through competitive bidding.
Titanium sourced by import from Eastern Europe (former Russian Federation); management reports no import constraints currently.
Scrap usage in melt typically 50-60% for normal aerospace grades; virgin material mandated for human spaceflight and critical engine parts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin compress in Q1 and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Madhubala Kalluri cited raw-material prices and LPG prices, which nearly doubled. She said Q2 may be hit, with normalisation expected in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin return to 20-21% from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD S.V.S. Narayana Murty said yes, and that the Q1 shortfall was due to the raw-material and LPG issues.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,000 crore capex yielding EBITDA, and what is FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex takes 2-3 years, with returns from year 4. FY27 capex will be about Rs 50-60 crore, mostly maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the aluminium plant still on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Nellore aluminium JV plant is being closed, pending ministry approval. The separate wide-plate rolling of customer-supplied aluminium billets is an alternative route.

qa_highlights.question: Will the S400 certification generate meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is testing-only revenue, conservatively estimated at about 10% of export base, with clarity in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin recovery to 20-21% in Q3 depends on LPG and raw-material prices easing; Q2 margin likely lower.
Fixed-price defence contracts leave the company exposed to raw-material and freight cost increases.
Rs 1,000 crore modernisation capex is not yet Board- or ministry-approved; no timeline given.
Metal bank benefits are customer-owned and not on company balance sheet; implementation and utilisation are still to be confirmed.
Scrap inventory policy and sales of titanium scrap; management says scrap is a strategic asset rather than surplus.
541195|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and certifications, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, capex timelines and the scale of new orders. Management repeatedly attributed Q1 margin pressure to temporary LPG and raw-material factors and declined to quantify the Rs 1,000 crore capex return or the S400 revenue.
key_quotes: Q2 may be little bit hit will be there, but Q3 we have hope that we will be coming to normal state.
Only because of these little raw material and LPG issues only that was little lower bottom line.
So, we reduced our scrap inventory by Rs. 75 crores.
We are not going ahead with that plant.

543463|2026-06.headline: Vedant Fashions Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 7.2% to INR3,014 mn, with PAT up 14.7% to about INR81 crore and domestic SSG at 3.8%.
543463|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 retail sales (customer sales) of INR4,195 mn, up 3.4% YoY, with domestic SSG ex-SIS of about 3.8%. Revenue from operations was about INR3,014 mn (INR301 crore), up 7.2%, with gross margin of 65.7% and EBITDA margin of 44.6%. EBITDA grew 10.8% and PAT margin was 26.7%. Store closures were elevated in Q1 by design, with openings pushed to H2, and management said closures and competitor exits are reducing industry store count in about 8 top states.

financial_highlights.change: vs 65.0% in Q4 FY26; YoY decline attributed partly to GST

financial_highlights.metric: Cash conversion (TTM June 2026, OCF/PAT excl. finance income)

segments.name: Manyavar / Mohey (core and non-bridal push)
segments.commentary: Mohey is growing faster than company average; push into stitched suits, sarees and crop-top lehengas. Manyavar's mega campaign with Rashmika Mandanna and Vijay Deverakonda reportedly exceeded 1 billion views.

segments.name: Twamev (premium)
segments.commentary: Management said Twamev outperformed the company in overall growth in Q1.

segments.name: Diwas
segments.commentary: Launched about a year ago; Q1 not reflective of its progress. Majority of MBO/SIS bookings for Q2 done; e-commerce deals signed with Myntra, Amazon, Blinkit and Zepto.

segments.name: MBO + SIS + e-commerce
segments.commentary: Together about 5% of revenue today; new leadership team built and growth targets described as aggressive. SIS is a few hundred sq ft versus EBO average of about 3,000 sq ft.

segments.name: International (UAE, North America)
segments.commentary: Under pressure: UAE affected by war, North America by tariffs. No growth figures given.

guidance_outlook: Core goal is a strong SSG in FY27; management said a net positive store count for the year is expected despite closures.
Gross openings to be concentrated in H2 (end of Q2 and early Q3), with openings at about 3-4% of store base as a typical annual tail; openings to accelerate as rental pressure eases.
Revenue growth target for FY27 relies on SSG, productivity uplift from new versus closed stores, net openings and MBO/SIS/e-commerce growth.
Asked about high-single-digit SSG for the remaining nine months: management called it a fair understanding and said FY27 will still be net positive.
ASP growth ambition slightly above plan; expected to start materialising from mid-Q2. Q1 SSG was split roughly half volume and half price.
Wedding calendar: November to March expected to be fantastic; October may be weaker YoY because Navratri was pushed by Adhik maas; January has wedding dates this year versus none last year.
capex_capacity: Q1 closures were deliberately front-loaded; management avoids carrying loss-making stores into the Q2 off-season, with openings aimed at H2.
Closure reasons cited: market shifted to newer locations, cannibalisation by a larger store in a nearby bigger town, and early new-store mistakes. Competition was not cited as a reason.
Franchisee capex: about INR2,100-2,150 per sq ft in Tier 2/3 cities and about INR2,500 per sq ft in Tier 1.
Franchisee revenue break-even benchmarks per sq ft: about INR7,000 (Tier 3), INR8,500 (Tier 2), INR10,000-10,500 (Tier 1). Management said franchisee ROI is currently good.
Internal research covers about 8 top states; net closures now seen in many states versus last quarter.
demand_pricing: Q1 SSG of about 3.8% split roughly evenly between volume and price.
Management said competitors that entered 3-4 years ago are closing large stores while new players add, and that industry store count was not rising.
Celebration wear dead stock is hard to liquidate at a discount, so management expects weaker players to exit, mainly regional and local ones.
Management said it is too early to link competitor closures to its own growth and wants 2-3 more quarters of data.
Retention: YoY retention improved; a separate task force targets repeat business; plans to be announced in the next call if finalised this month.
Marketing will shift from top-of-mind branding to consideration and conversion-led social campaigns for Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are franchisee revenue-per-sq-ft benchmarks, and is franchisee margin under pressure after GST changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even-type benchmarks: about INR7,000/sq ft (Tier 3), INR8,500 (Tier 2), INR10,000-10,500 (Tier 1). Management said franchisee ROI is good and there is no pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Why close stores at an accelerated pace if competition is the issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition has never been a closure reason. Closures were from market shifts, cannibalisation by larger nearby stores, and early mistakes. Q1 was front-loaded to avoid off-season rentals.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin trend YoY: will it stabilise at 65-65.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: GM was 65.7% in Q1 FY27 versus 65.0% in Q4 FY26, so it improved sequentially. GST was not in the base in Q1 and entered the base from Q3, which explains YoY comparisons.

qa_highlights.question: Primary vs secondary sales gap despite Adhik maas impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Replenishment is auto-driven, so quarterly gaps vary. Management asked analysts to review primary and secondary at full-year level, where directions align.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days?
qa_highlights.answer: 34 days for TTM June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for revenue growth of low-to-mid teens, and how to fund square footage addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Majority from SSG, plus closed-vs-new store productivity delta, net openings, and aggressive MBO/SIS/e-commerce targets. No specific square footage number given.

qa_highlights.question: Is Mohey scaling and what are the steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohey performing better than company average; doubling down on non-bridal categories (stitched suits, sarees, crop-top lehengas) and digital marketing for them.

qa_highlights.question: Share of MBO, SIS and e-commerce in revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5% combined today, with aggressive growth targets.

544744|2026-06.headline: Powerica Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR780 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 13.6% on commodity inflation; DC order book hit INR900 crore (INR1,100 crore by Aug 7).
544744|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 26.7% YoY to INR780 crore, with EBITDA of INR106 crore (13.6% margin) and PAT of INR64 crore (8.3% margin). Management said elevated commodity and energy prices, a lag in passing costs to customers, and an adverse revenue mix compressed genset margins, with recovery expected from Q2-Q3 after two-phase price hikes. Order book as of July 31, 2026 was INR1,700 crore, of which data center orders were INR900 crore. Wind IPP portfolio visibility rose to about 638 MW after new awards, and FY27 double-digit revenue growth guidance was reiterated.

segments.name: DG sets (Cummins-powered)
segments.commentary: Order book of INR1,700 crore as of July 31, 2026, with data center orders at INR900 crore; genset EBITDA margin fell to 5.6% in Q1 on commodity costs and mix. Capacity utilisation 75-80% on one shift.

segments.name: Wind / IPP and EPC-BOP
segments.commentary: Wind is 18.6% of revenue, growing 28.8% YoY at a 48.6% EBITDA margin, helped by 51.3 MW added in Feb 2026. Owned IPP capacity is 330 MW, with a roadmap to about 638 MW.

segments.name: MSLG (defence/large projects)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell on slower order booking because international inquiries were put on hold by the geopolitical situation. Won a INR41 crore tender to be executed in 12-15 months and has a large PSU order executable by Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Allied business
segments.commentary: Contributed 9% of revenue; management attributed the slowdown to milestone-based project revenue recognition and defence product approval cycles of 1-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit revenue growth guidance reiterated.
Genset margins expected to stay subdued in Q1 and part of Q2 and improve from Q3 onward, per management; no formal margin guidance given for the DG business this year.
Order book up 15-19% YoY as of July 31, 2026, depending on product mix.
Data center order book expected to execute over 12-18 months; management expects data center at 20%+ of revenue on an annualised basis.
Wind pipeline: 50 MW to go live in Q4 FY27, 150 MW in FY28, and 100 MW the year after.
Management expects 250-300 MW of EPC/BOP execution per year, at about INR400 crore of top line.
capex_capacity: DG set capacity: one shift in operation, utilisation 75-80%; management says capacity is sufficient for current demand and can be expanded if needed.
IPP portfolio: 330 MW operating, targeting about 638 MW (management corrected 633.55 MW). 50 MW added this FY, 150 MW in FY28, 100 MW later.
New wind projects: 100 MW GUVNL PPA signed and under construction; 50 MW GUVNL LOA awaited, with PPA expected Nov-Dec 2026; 100 MW SECI LOA received, PPA pending SECI call.
Two wholly-owned subsidiaries, Windfusion Renewable and Whisper Wind Renewable, set up for transmission connectivity; 49% stake acquired in Fuji-Kailash Energy.
Net cash of about INR193 crore is earmarked for the 300 MW under construction and pipeline wind projects.
demand_pricing: Data center order book rose from INR400-500 crore to INR900 crore as of July 31, 2026, and INR1,100 crore as of Aug 7, including a single order of over INR200 crore.

Price hikes taken in two phases: a small increase mid-Q1 and the balance at start of Q2. Quantum not disclosed; management cited a 10-15% range as not accurate. Old orders executed at pre-hike prices, new orders quoted at new prices.
Management expects one or two quarters for price pass-through, citing CPCB IV+ precedent of ~33% price increase over 9 months.
Manufacturing is the largest end market by share, followed by real estate; rentals and commercial are among the faster-growing segments.
Management said competition in data centers is rising, but it cites execution reputation; no market share data available.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow and order book comparison vs March 2025/2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book as of July 31, 2026 is up 15-19% YoY versus the same quarter last year, depending on product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Genset margin outlook and whether the order book is fixed-price?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are impacted by the West Asia crisis for Q1 and part of Q2, improving from Q3. Older orders have fixed prices, with some price hikes obtained; new orders carry new prices.

qa_highlights.question: Data center BOP share and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: BOP execution is about 30% of data center project value. Margins vary order to order by volume, delivery timeline, engine requirement and customisation; no fixed margin given.

qa_highlights.question: DG capacity utilisation and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-80% on one shift; current capacity is sufficient, with expansion planned if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Wind PPA timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: 100 MW GUVNL PPA signed and under construction. The 50 MW GUVNL PPA is expected by Nov-Dec 2026 after LOA and about 90 days. The 100 MW SECI PPA is pending SECI's call.

qa_highlights.question: Wind EBITDA margins by project type?
qa_highlights.answer: New projects earn 82-83% EBITDA per management, old 330 MW projects 62-63%, EPC 10-11%. Analysts noted these figures as stated by management.

risks_watch: Genset margin (5.6% in Q1) recovery depends on whether price hikes stick over one or two quarters amid high commodity and energy prices.
Old data center orders were priced before the hikes, so margin may stay below the new-order level until they execute.
MSLG order inflow slowed because international inquiries were paused by the geopolitical situation; the pipeline is not yet quantified.
Wind PPAs for the 50 MW GUVNL and 100 MW SECI projects are still pending, and commissioning depends on them.
Competition in data centers is rising, and management said it lost two direct data center projects to Cummins in the past (per analyst).

financial_highlights.change: Tax rate ~25.168% vs one-time deferred tax benefit last year

financial_highlights.metric: EPC and O&M for BOP share

financial_highlights.value: ~INR193 crore (as cited by analyst, not disputed)

financial_highlights.change: Lower; demand deferred by crisis and GRAP

533344|2026-06.headline: PFS Q1 FY27 disbursements fell to INR 117 crores with PAT of INR 40.24 crores; management says Q2 sanctions exceed INR 1,200 crores in month one.
533344|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a muted quarter for PTC India Financial Services, with disbursements of about INR 117 crores and loan assets of INR 2,946 crores. Profit after tax was INR 40.24 crores on net interest income of INR 48.71 crores, with NIM at 4.46%. Management attributed the weak origination to a leadership transition and to delayed construction at some borrowers, and said it is pausing the FI and SME books to focus on infrastructure lending. Management guided to an AUM of about INR 5,000 crores by end-FY27, though no dividend timing was given. The call was dominated by retail shareholder complaints about performance and dividends.

segments.name: Infrastructure lending
segments.commentary: Named as the core growth engine; management wants a balanced book across private sector and PSU borrowers across large, medium and small tickets. Q2 sanctions in month one were above INR 1,200 crores, described as a 13-quarter high.

segments.name: FI and SME books
segments.commentary: Management is pausing new lending in these books to concentrate on infrastructure financing.

guidance_outlook: AUM target of about INR 5,000 crores by end of FY27, per Director Operations Sanjeev Kumar.

Q1 disbursements of about INR 1,000 crores were expected but slipped; management says the delayed amounts will convert to disbursement in Q2 once borrowers complete their own contribution and construction.
Management expects momentum to continue into stronger disbursements and performance over the coming quarters, citing a good pipeline.
Dividend timing: CEO said he cannot answer on dividends today; asked shareholders to be patient for the next 2-3 quarters.
Borrowing costs: some new sanctions for additional facilities are expected by end of next quarter; management is working to reduce existing borrowing costs and keep future costs low.
capex_capacity: Not applicable; PFS is a lender, and the call gave no capacity or capex metrics.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 sanctions exceeded INR 1,200 crores in the first month, which management called the highest in 13 quarters.
Q1 disbursements were held back by delayed construction at some borrowers in gas and oil-producing projects in international markets, plus a leadership transition.
Management says sufficient liquidity exists in the system, and talks with institutions for new facilities are positive, though no sanctions are yet in hand.
Management did not give a specific pricing or cost-of-funds figure; it said it is chasing existing lenders to cut borrowing costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the loan book shrunk and profits declined over several years, and what is management delivering for investors?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO acknowledged the weak track record and said there is no lack of intent to grow shareholder value; he asked investors to stay invested and watch the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: When will dividends be paid, and how will the company grow returns given its cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO declined to give a dividend timeline and said the cash will be deployed into infrastructure projects; he asked for patience over the next 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company been unable to raise funds at competitive rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Dilip Srivastava said liquidity is sufficient and talks with lenders are positive, with sanctions for new facilities expected before end of next quarter; cost reduction with existing lenders is under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the remaining NPA account?
qa_highlights.answer: Kalur Srinivas said the single NPA account (INR 187 crores of the INR 190 crores gross Stage III) has an NCLT application pending admission; IBC resolution starts after admission, expected during the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q1 disbursements so low against the expected INR 1,000 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Kumar said some disbursements slipped because borrowers' construction was delayed, and a leadership change added to the delay; he said about INR 1,000 crores is sanctioned and will be disbursed in Q2.

risks_watch: Single account of INR 187 crores pending NCLT admission makes up most of the INR 190 crores gross Stage III; resolution timing depends on admission.
Disbursement timing is dependent on borrowers' construction progress, so Q2 conversion of the delayed INR 1,000 crores is unproven.
Borrowing cost and new sanctions remain unconfirmed; management has no sanctions in hand yet.
Management transition: the CEO is new, and the previous MD has left.
Dividend policy remains undetermined; shareholders are pressing for returns.
Check Q2 disbursement and AUM progress against the INR 5,000 crore target.
533344|2026-06.management_tone: Defensive and reassuring on the outlook but cautious on specifics. Management admitted Q1 was weak, attributing it to a leadership transition and delayed borrower construction, and offered no dividend timeline or cost-of-funds figures, relying on the promise of Q2 momentum.
key_quotes: So this month's sanction has reached the record sanction of last 13 quarters, reflecting a significant acceleration in business activities.
We expect our book size or you can say our asset under management, AUM, to be something around INR5,000 crores by the end of this financial year.
The answer is, I cannot answer the dividend question today.

523405|2026-06.headline: JM Financial Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 13% YoY to INR883 crores, with Private Markets doubling to INR462 crores offsetting weak capital markets.
523405|2026-06.overview: Consolidated net revenue grew 13% YoY to INR883 crores and pre-provision operating profit rose 21% to INR469 crores. PAT ex-provisions before minorities rose 24% to INR379 crores, but after minorities it was flat at INR302 crores; reported PAT was INR292 crores (annualised ROE about 11%). Private Markets, led by a large distressed-credit resolution, carried the quarter while Corporate Advisory & Capital Markets and Wealth were weak on lack of primary issuance. Management said July revenues on the transaction side already exceeded June.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated net worth / book value per share

segments.name: Corporate Advisory & Capital Markets
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR115 crores vs INR182 crores a year ago; PAT INR32 crores. Closed 9 capital markets transactions worth about INR22,000 crores; filed for 60 IPOs aggregating about INR150,000 crores, excluding Jio Platforms and NSE.

segments.name: Wealth Management
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR185 crores vs INR211 crores; PAT INR19 crores. Wealth loan book up 43% YoY to INR2,417 crores; recurring AUM about INR33,400 crores, now 30% of total AUM; 1,000+ RMs, 71 branches.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: Mutual fund management fees up 62% YoY to INR13 crores; loss after minorities flat at INR5 crores. Non-liquid AUM about INR10,900 crores, up 16% QoQ; employees up 10% YoY to 222.

segments.name: Private Markets
segments.commentary: Net revenue doubled YoY to INR462 crores; pre-provision operating profit about 2.3x to INR375 crores; segment PAT after minorities INR228 crores. Gross ARC resolutions over INR2,000 crores, group share of cash flows over INR1,200 crores.

segments.name: Affordable Home Loans
segments.commentary: AUM up 28% YoY to INR3,715 crores; disbursements up 87% YoY; revenue up 22% to INR123 crores; PAT after minorities up 16% to INR17 crores. 151 branches, about 36,000 customers.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Private Markets to meet its guidance; bespoke credit book targeted to grow 15-20% YoY, with about half of that already achieved in Q1.
Capital markets pipeline of about INR150,000 crores excluding Jio and NSE; management hopes to execute a majority of it in the rest of FY27.
Net flows in Wealth expected at minimum about INR6,000 crores for the year vs about INR2,000 crores in Q1.
ROE for FY27 guided in a similar range to last year (about 11.5%) or better; management aims to push Wealth and Asset Management ROE into the mid-to-high teens over time.
Asset Management to get INR150 crores further investment over next 2 years; management targets AMC AUM of INR25,000 crores.
Debt-to-equity expected to rise from 0.8x to about 2x within 3 years as syndication ramps; ARC expected to become debt-free within about 6 months.
capex_capacity: Affordable Home Loans: 151 branches; plan to list the business separately in 2 to 3 years.
Asset Management: INR150 crores further investment over next 2 years.
Wealth: recruitment of 100+ RMs over last 18 months; 2 to 3 year profitability gestation; 5-year plan approved by Board last year.
ARC distressed credit book INR3,114 crores at Q1 (down from INR3,665 crores in Q4 FY26) after about INR1,200 crores recovery and INR600 crores new deployment.
demand_pricing: ARC returns: wholesale 18-22% IRR, retail 15-18%; new-book ARC transactions show IRRs of 18%+ and blended 16-18%.
Equity allocation INR970 crores (flat for 5 quarters); alternatives allocation about INR500 crores vs INR300 crores earlier; cash about INR3,000 crores earning about 6%.
Margin trade financing book about INR2,500 crores with combined yield about 13.5%; management sees 15% annual growth.
Credit syndication income about INR20 crores in Q1.
Industry wealth AUM growth expected at early to mid-teens; management targets above-industry growth.
Mutual fund equity AUM about INR10,500 crores, up from under INR500 crores three years ago; SIP book down about 30% per analyst question, management expects stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cyclicality break in wealth and private credit, and when does organic credit growth start?
qa_highlights.answer: Bespoke book reached about INR3,000 crores, a 5-quarter high, and is about halfway to the 15-20% annual growth guided in Q4. Wealth is a 2-3 year build-out, with FY27 and FY28 expected to be productivity-led.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wealth profitability drop sharply, and will employee costs as a share of revenue fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower transactional revenue and gestation of 100+ RMs hired in 18 months, who take 2.5-3 years to turn profitable. Management said headcount has likely peaked, with hiring now selective.

qa_highlights.question: Asset management SIP book down about 30% and AUM flat; what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-liquid AUM rose 16% QoQ; decline was linked to small/mid-cap concentration. Management engaged more distributors and expects SIP and AUM to recover over the next couple of quarters. Quantitative targets to be shared separately.

qa_highlights.question: What steady-state ROE is achievable excluding market peaks?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 ROE was about 11.5%, constrained by the 50% NBFC payout cap. Management expects a similar or better range this year, with stronger ROE from Wealth and AMC operating leverage in about 2 years; CACM is about 15% ROE in a weak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Private Markets carries 60-65% of capital and drags ROE; will capital mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-to-equity is at a low of 0.8x and will rise toward 2x in about 3 years as syndication grows, lifting ROE into the teens. Dividends constrained to 50% of NBFC profits.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 Private Markets revenue came from the single large ARC transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARC income is lumpy and largely booked on resolution; the June quarter included a big resolution, while book value fell by about INR1,200 crores of recovery and about INR600 crores was redeployed.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for demerger or listing of wealth and asset management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wealth and AM are still small; it will evaluate a listing or demerger at scale, subject to no tax leakage. Affordable housing listing is planned in 2-3 years.

533326|2026-06.headline: Texmaco Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR753 crore but PAT rose 85.9% YoY to INR52 crore; order book INR9,923 crore.
533326|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR753 crore, hit by lower freight car and Rail & Green execution, while Bright Power electrical revenue grew 76.8% YoY to INR175 crore. EBITDA was INR81 crore (10.8% margin), flat YoY, and PAT rose 85.9% YoY to INR52 crore (6.9% margin) on lower finance costs. Management said the order book stood at INR9,923 crore at June 30, 2026, with private and export orders at 96.4% of freight car orders in Q1 FY27. Strategic updates covered the leasing JV with Trinity (Texmaco stake to fall from 50% to 34%), the Wabtec air brake JV, a South Africa order of about INR4,100 crore, and a 2030 vision of doubling the top line.

segments.name: Freight Cars (FCD)
segments.commentary: 1,054 freight cars delivered in Q1 FY27; execution lower on supply-chain stress tied to oil and gas prices. Private and export share of orders rose from 21% in FY25 to 79% in FY26 and 96.4% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Rail Infra & Green (formerly Kalindee)
segments.commentary: Revenue lower YoY; EBIT margin turned positive at 1.4% versus an EBIT loss in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Bright Power (Electrical infra)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR175 crore, +76.8% YoY; EBIT margin 10.8%, up 150 bps YoY.

segments.name: Foundry
segments.commentary: Production of 5,148 tonnes in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Core business EBITDA margin target of 1.2% to 3% over the next 1 to 3 years (as stated by management; the figure is ambiguous in the transcript).
Vision 2030: core rolling stock revenue of INR5,000-6,000 crore; aim to double the top line to about 2x by 2030 with a steady bottom line in the mid-teens.
New businesses could add 20% to 50% top-line growth in some years; management would not give absolute FY27 or FY28 numbers.

South Africa order (about INR4,100 crore, wagons plus 15-year maintenance, which is 30-35% of value): about 50-60% expected to execute in FY28; locomotive value to be additional and not yet finalised.
Management expects freight car output and supply-chain normalisation to improve from coming quarters; no volume target given.
capex_capacity: Leasing: about 35 rakes operating today; near-term readiness to invest in about 100 more rakes. Leasing JV with Trinity: Texmaco stake falls from 50% to 34%; capital allocation to be modest in percentage terms.
Capacity described as elastic (15,000-16,000 commodity wagons possible), but management is prioritising specialised wagons over volume.
South Africa: considering a locomotive plant and a wagon manufacturing plant; management declined to confirm the INR200-300 crore reported investment figure.
Wheelset supply from Rail Wheel Factory: enough stock for current export and private orders.
demand_pricing: Order book INR9,923 crore at June 30, 2026, with more than 6,000 wagons in hand (per CFO).
Q1 FY27 order wins include about INR5,200 crore, of which the South Africa order is about INR4,100 crore; some export orders are under execution.
Management expects no Indian Railways wagon tender near term; it expects orders to come from private and export customers.
Other expenses rose because export freight charges are booked there while the related income is in revenue (CFO).

qa_highlights.question: Wagon leasing: is the report of about INR1,800 crore investment for about 100 rakes over 3-5 years correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm figures; it said the leasing JV is separate from Texmaco, with Trinity entry cutting Texmaco's stake to 34%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the South Africa order exposure correct: a locomotive and wagon plant costing INR200-300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not confirm the numbers; it said it is open to facilities for localisation and that footprint matters more than investment amount.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timeline for the INR5,200 crore order and the maintenance share?
qa_highlights.answer: The South Africa order is about INR4,100 crore, not INR5,200 crore, and is executable mainly in FY28; maintenance is 15 years and about 30-35% of value.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No absolute guidance; management pointed to a core EBITDA margin target of 1.2% to 3% and possible 20-50% top-line growth from new businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight car output fall, and is there a 2030 roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed oil and gas-driven supply-chain stress and said order book is healthy; it reiterated Vision 2030 (2x top line, mid-teens bottom line).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook as the mix moves to private and export orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin is hard to predict and that it expects to sustain and improve margins, without giving a number.

Dependence on the South Africa order, which is lumpy and where the locomotive component is not yet finalised or partnered.
No Indian Railways wagon tender yet; management says it is insulated for now.
Leasing and new-business capital needs, and the reduced JV stake after the Trinity entry.
Freight car volumes fell YoY; watch Q2 deliveries and whether the margin gain holds as execution resumes.
Management declined to give FY27 and FY28 revenue or margin numbers; a call for clearer guidance.
533326|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and the order mix, and expansive on the strategic vision. Evasive on numbers: it declined to confirm reported investment figures, locomotive values and absolute FY27 or FY28 targets, and it repeatedly deferred to future announcements.
key_quotes: So, this order is executable in the next financial year.
We want to have at least a 50% share in terms of the business from a jump from 15% to 50%.
The share of private sector and export orders increased from 21% in FY25 to 79% in FY26 and further to 96.4% in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Lower freight car and Rail & Green execution (YoY change not stated)
Turnaround from EBIT loss in Q1 FY26

543534|2026-06.headline: Aether Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 27% YoY to INR3,266 million, with EBITDA up 31% to INR1,028 million and margin at 31%.
543534|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 27% YoY to INR3,266 million and EBITDA rose 31% to INR1,028 million, with EBITDA margin at 31% versus 30% a year ago. PAT grew 33% YoY to INR627 million, a 19% margin. segments.name: CEM (Contract Exclusive Manufacturing)

segments.name: CRAMS

segments.name: LSM (Large-scale manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Volume fell 22.5% YoY as some lines at Site 3 moved to CEM; management said pricing rose 22.5% and demand is intact. LSM expected to be about 35% of top line in coming years.

segments.name: Oil and Gas

Site 5 (Magnum) LSM products expected to contribute revenue from Q2 FY27; first three LSM products priced around $30-40/kg.

Oil and gas: management states the segment grew from zero to about 20% of business over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Are there orders in hand for semiconductor products, and which chemistries are involved?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dow collaboration scope, timeline, and commercialisation path?
