financial_highlights.value: Rs. 10 crore (incl. ZeroTouch hardware, ZeroTouch software, AI engines)

500403|2026-06.headline: Sundram Fasteners Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose 20% to INR1,618 crores from INR1,367 crores; standalone profit up ~10% to INR150 crores.
500403|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a very good start, with consolidated turnover up 20% YoY to INR1,618 crores and growth across OE, aftermarket and exports. Standalone profit rose from INR138 crores to INR150 crores, which management attributed to tighter control of fixed costs. Input cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict was a pressure, with direct materials passed through to domestic OEMs and indirect/energy costs under negotiation. Management guided to margin expansion in Q2 once indirect cost recoveries are accounted for, and said the 20% run rate should hold through the festive period.

financial_highlights.change: management expects close to 16.5% by year end

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material inflation contribution to top line

financial_highlights.change: back up from earlier levels, peaked near one-third
elevated over last two years vs 110-130 days earlier; management guides to stay around current levels

segments.name: Standalone exports
segments.commentary: Standalone exports grew upwards of 20% YoY in dollar terms; North American passenger car ICE volumes recovered and Class 8 truck primary orders were 20-25% above last year, with backlogs at a 38-month high as of June.

segments.name: Domestic auto (M&HCV, PV, tractor)
segments.commentary: Management said M&HCV industry grew ~20% in Q1 and SFL growth almost matched it; PV industry grew ~23% with SFL matching; tractors grew ~14-15%, roughly in line. Two-wheeler/three-wheeler (5-6% of mix) is an under-indexed area.

segments.name: Non-auto: wind energy, aerospace
segments.commentary: Wind energy fasteners moved from INR25 crores to INR30 crores per month after an expansion; a further ~INR100 crores capex is planned to lift annualised run rate from INR350 crores to INR500 crores. Aerospace revenue was ~INR50 crores, targeted at INR100 crores+ this year and INR500 crores in 2-3 years.

segments.name: EV (General Motors, Stellantis)
segments.commentary: EV revenue from General Motors was under INR50 crores in FY26 and is planned at INR200-250 crores in FY27 (combined with Stellantis), on track per Q1. EV overall is 4-5% of revenue.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Sundram Fasteners China expected to grow close to 20% this year; UK subsidiary tracking European truck market; TVS Upasana (two-wheeler) growing well. Management expects all subsidiaries to grow broadly in line with standalone.

guidance_outlook: Q2 and Q3 export outlook described as strong; run rate of ~20% growth expected to continue given festivals and customer schedules.
EBITDA margin expected to rise from 16.1% toward ~16.5% and expand further in Q2 as indirect material negotiations are accounted.
Retains FY27 growth assumptions of CV 8%, PV 10%, tractor 7% (vs industry CV 4%, tractor flat to 2%) but flagged high H2 FY26 base; may recalibrate in a quarter or so.
Capex this year quoted at around INR400 crores, of which ~30% is replacement and the balance growth; earlier guidance was ~INR250 crores.
Hyundai and Kia fasteners entry targeted at INR100 crores+ over 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Wind energy fasteners: further expansion of close to INR100 crores to lift annualised capacity from INR350 crores to INR500 crores.
Project lead times run about 12-18 months; management is looking at asset purchases to shorten them, but said no advanced inorganic deal is in pipeline.
Imported machinery is being monitored case by case due to the West Asia crisis to protect commissioning timelines.
Digital: IoT deployed across all plants, delivering 5-10% productivity gain with 0.2-0.5% margin benefit; AS/RS systems being added.
Powder metallurgy capacity being expanded to serve passenger car, shock absorber and consumer durable customers.
demand_pricing: Direct raw materials (steel) are passed through to OEMs under contract; indirect/energy costs (e.g., LPG) are being negotiated, with recovery expected to lift Q2 margins.
Aftermarket pricing is adjusted to reflect cost inflation; exports are partly protected by rupee depreciation.
Europe is sub-20% of exports; Garrett Motion business won in two divisions (turbocharger machined parts) and ZF work at Sri City; more RFQs pending.
Standard fastener share with each OEM is 30-40% (50-60% share of business where supplied); specials are single-sourced.
New OEM entries via BIS/QCO norms at Hyundai and Kia; Cummins fasteners business growing; new pipeline of over INR1,000 crores with an equal amount under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 20% growth came from raw material inflation, and what was volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew about 13% in tonnage; raw material inflation contributed roughly INR20-25 crores to the top line.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing domestic market share given industry growth of 20%+ vs SFL's 16% domestic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth matched industry in M&HCV (~20%), PV (~23%) and tractors (~14-15%); the gap is mainly 2W/3W, which is only 5-6% of revenue and where SFL is not present.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GM and Stellantis EV revenue expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: GM EV revenue was under INR50 crores in FY26 and is planned at INR200-250 crores this year, including Stellantis; management will take it one year at a time, with INR750 crores cited as a past peak projection.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the cash conversion cycle stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it should stay around current levels, around 140-150 days, as higher export share lengthens the operating cycle; DSO has come down and the spike is mainly inventory timing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited around INR400 crores, about 30% for replacement and the rest growth, and said investment will continue as an industry norm.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 20% growth pace hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the current run rate to hold, supported by festivals and indicative customer schedules.

risks_watch: Indirect material and energy cost inflation (West Asia conflict) still under negotiation; margin recovery depends on Q2 settlements.
Working capital: cash conversion cycle elevated at 150+ days; inventory days spiked and need to normalise toward 140-150 days.
High H2 FY26 base may compress percentage growth; management may recalibrate FY27 segment growth rates in a quarter or so.
Imported machinery delays from the West Asia crisis could affect capex commissioning.
Defence business is at an early startup stage with long validation cycles; EV revenue ramp depends on GM and Stellantis schedules.

532867|2026-06.headline: V2 Retail Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR997 crore, with PAT up 70% to INR41.9 crore and store count at 381.
532867|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR997 crore (+58% YoY), with reported EBITDA of INR139.5 crore (+60%, 14.0% margin) and PAT of INR41.9 crore (+70%). Pre-Ind AS EBITDA was about INR79 crore (~8% margin, +51%) and PAT INR50 crore (+64%). Gross margin eased to 28.6% from 29.5%, which management attributed to Adhik Maas reducing full-price sell-through to 90% from 92%. Store count reached 381 at June 30, 2026 (56 net adds), and management says it has since crossed 400 stores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of at least 50% revenue growth, 8-10% SSSG, 170-200 new stores and 29-30% gross margin.

financial_highlights.change: vs 92% in prior-year Q1 per Q&A

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 381 stores at June 30, 2026 covering ~40.7 lakh sq ft; 57 opened and 1 closed in Q1, net +56. Crossed 400 stores after quarter-end. Stores are mostly standalone, 10,000-12,000 sq ft, in 26 states.

segments.name: New vs mature stores
segments.commentary: New stores run ~34% lower sales per sq ft than mature stores (>2 years old at ~INR1,070-1,100/sq ft); new stores at ~INR730-740/sq ft. New-store SSSG is ~2.3 pts above old stores in Q1. Cohort SPSF cited at 886 vs 925 earlier.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance at least 50% for FY27, unchanged.
SSSG guidance 8-10% for the full year, retained despite Q1 at ~7.5%.
Gross margin guided at 29-30% (earlier 28-30% range), dependent on sell-through.
170-200 store openings planned for FY27; no change in plan despite capex inflation.
Targeting ~50% CAGR growth for the next 2-3 years, per CEO.
Price increase of 4-5% in garment MRPs from Q3 FY27 to offset raw material inflation.
EBITDA margin to be maintained despite the new-store expansion; new stores pay back in 2.5-3 years and break even from their first month.
Funding via internal accruals, release of ~INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases; no QIP planned.
capex_capacity: New store capex has risen ~10% to INR1.22 crore from INR1.1 crore, due to input inflation.
Inventory held ~100 days (earlier 90-100 days target) and creditors ~45-50 days; safety stock raised due to geopolitical tension and to be reduced later.
Inventory for new stores is staged ~2 months ahead, with ~INR100-150 crore tied up per quarter of 50-55 openings.
MOU signed for the next 100 stores; ~15-20 store locations finalised each month based on regional data.
Store-level replenishment cut to 2-3 days of sales cover from 10-12 days, with store back-room space converted into selling area.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is inelastic; kids' wear is ~25% of sales. July-August trends described as in line with plan, but too early to judge given festive shift into Q3.
Adhik Maas (30 days in Q1) and fewer wedding dates weakened Tier 2/3 demand and cut full-price sales to 90%.
Price increase of 4-5% on garment cost from Q3; management says past increases reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.
Repeat customers within first year rose from ~40% to ~55% over three years, per management.
80% of stores face 3-4 other value fashion retailers in the same catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Will price increases be passed on, and what is the volume impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation to hit from Q3 as H1 orders were placed earlier; a 4-5% rise in garment cost will be passed to consumers. Past price hikes reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.

qa_highlights.question: Will the store addition pace slow or need new equity?
qa_highlights.answer: 170-200 openings remain on track with no capex slowdown. Internal accruals, INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases will fund it; no QIP planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhik Maas cut full-price sales to 90% from 92%. Guidance remains 29-30% gross margin, dependent on season sell-through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new-store productivity gap closing?
qa_highlights.answer: New stores run ~34% below mature stores on SPSF; 10-12 stores are below INR600/sq ft, which management says is too early to judge. Management expects maturity in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are stores appearing in Tier 1 cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said V2 has long operated in Tier 1 (about 11 stores in Delhi NCR) and that Tier 1 is part of the target market.

qa_highlights.question: Customer experience: are NPS or other KPIs tracked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not focus on Google reviews; an NPS link is sent after billing to ~40% of customers as a pilot, with store incentives linked to NPS. AI on CCTV flags long checkout queues.

risks_watch: Gross margin at 28.6% is below the 29-30% guided range; the recovery depends on full-price sell-through in the festive season (Q2-Q3).
New-store productivity is ~34% below mature stores, with 10-12 stores below INR600/sq ft; RK Retail acquisition will consolidate from Q2.
Working capital is inflated by vendor prepayments; cash release depends on creditor days normalising to 45-50 days.
Capex inflation (~10%) and rising rent escalation (12-15% every 3 years) could pressure store economics.
Geopolitical risk is driving higher safety stock and raw-material inflation; the timing of 4-5% price pass-through is a watch item.
Customer experience issues (store-level reviews and checkout queues) could weigh on repeat rates and SSSG.
532867|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and store expansion; cautious and deflective on near-term demand, saying it is too early to call July-August trends ahead of the festive quarters. Management gave few numbers on the post-quarter trend and deferred several questions to the next call.
key_quotes: We delivered an amazing 58% year -on-year revenue growth in the first quarter while maintaining healthy returns.
So we need to have that inventory at least 2 months prior to the opening of the store.

544292|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR4,490 million and EBITDA to INR1,233 million (+39% YoY); FY28 guidance of $400M revenue and 40% margin reiterated.
544292|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR4,490 million grew 37% YoY, driven by the semaglutide commercial launch, new MSA contracts and new customer wins. EBITDA of INR1,233 million rose 39% YoY and 34% QoQ, with management attributing the margin step-up mainly to a higher drug-device combination (DDC) contribution. Management said capacity is full, with the second cartridge line commissioning this quarter and a third line due within FY27. FY28 guidance of $400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margin was reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Each new line doubles sterile days

segments.name: Drug-device combination (DDC)
segments.commentary: Main driver of the margin improvement; second cartridge line commissioning this quarter, third line within FY27, and a fourth later in FY28. Management says existing cartridge capacity is fully utilised while pre-filled syringe capacity is largely available.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: Added Formycon (biosimilars) and an animal-health contract; RFP funnel is almost 4x what it was just over a year ago. Commercial revenue expected from FY29 onward, with mammalian and microbial capacity expansion under consideration.

segments.name: Soft gelatin
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded from 800 million to 2.4 billion units; the business is shifting from captive Strides IP to CDMO. Management expects the added capacity to be fully taken up over 12-15 months and has started a greenfield site process.

segments.name: Injectables (Steri-Science)
segments.commentary: Focused portfolio built around penicillin and FDA-shortage products. A sterile injectable site shutdown starts in Q2 and runs into Q3 to add pre-filled syringe and lyophilisation capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance reiterated: US$400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margin; Q&A cites US$160 million EBITDA.
EBITDA trajectory expected to keep rising beyond FY28, with Europe and US (FTF) volumes opening from FY29-30.
Revenue and EBITDA expected to grow sequentially QoQ through FY27, with H2 weighted by new-line ramp-up and soft gel seasonality.
Opex already upfronted, so the full contribution from new lines is expected once all lines are in place.
Capex beyond the US$100 million programme for biologics expected to be significantly lower than DDC spend.
capex_capacity: Second cartridge line to commission in Q1 FY27; batch sizes moving from ~200 L to ~500 L on lines to increase output per sterile day.
Third line to be ready within FY27; fourth line later in FY28. Management expects three lines fully available for FY28 (675 sterile days in total).
Soft gelatin is at its current site capacity limit; a greenfield site is being initiated, with an update expected in about one quarter.
Injectables shutdown in Q2-Q3 FY27 for pre-filled syringe and lyophilisation additions; benefit expected in FY28.
Around 80% of the US$100 million capex is committed; the remaining ~20% is the balance.
demand_pricing: Management says all current capacity is full, and demand is pulled forward to offset temporary supply disruption at Dr. Reddy's, with no supply impact expected.

Semaglutide generics: all three Canadian approvals held; two partners launched; over 40% of India's generic pen market is made at the site. Indian generic pen volumes rose from under 2,000 a month to 150,000-160,000.
Management says the mix will shift toward commercial supply (CSA) over MSAs as the new lines come online.
Six new logos and nine launches added in the quarter; a new GLP customer was onboarded last quarter.
First oncology soft gel NDA secured with a top-10 US generic; management described the market as small with no significant near-term revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why has soft gel revenue not grown faster after capacity went from 800 million to 2.4 billion units?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business was captive under Strides and is now shifting to CDMO, with tech transfers taking time. It expects the added capacity to be fully taken over 12-15 months and has started a greenfield site process.

qa_highlights.question: Did the injectable shutdown affect Q1, and what drove the sequential margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: The injectable shutdown starts this quarter and runs into Q2. The margin rise was attributed mainly to higher DDC contribution plus soft gel and injectable seasonality, which is H2-weighted.

qa_highlights.question: Is there order book visibility to achieve the $400 million FY28 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing DDC order book, biologics new contracts and funnel, soft gel customer additions and new injectable capabilities.

qa_highlights.question: Can the new lines be used for any customer, and will batch-size changes need regulatory approval?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is fungible across lines and customers; customers will be served from both lines. Batch size increases from 200 L to 500 L should be possible in most geographies with a quick approval, depending on the market.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q1 capture the full EBITDA contribution from line one?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue from line one reached full per-line contribution in Q1, but profitability will improve only once all lines are installed, because most opex has already been upfronted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook beyond the US$100 million programme?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of the US$100 million is committed. Biologics capacity expansion will need additional capex, expected to be significantly lower than DDC spend.

risks_watch: Dr. Reddy's temporary supply disruption: whether its supplies resume on the publicly stated timeline, and how it affects the pulled-forward demand.
Soft gel ramp-up pace versus the 12-15 month takeover estimate, plus the greenfield site decision and cost (update due in about one quarter).
Execution of line 2 (Q1) and line 3 (within FY27) commissioning, batch-size approvals, and whether opex leverage follows.
Geopolitical freight disruption (Suez and Strait of Hormuz) and new US tariff announcements on generics; management says CDMO exposure is limited because contracts are ex-works.
Biologics commercial revenue is largely expected only from FY29 onward, so FY28 depends on DDC, soft gel and injectables.
544292|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and assertive on demand, capacity and FY28 targets, with management repeatedly stressing that capacity is full. Less specific on soft gel timelines, the greenfield site, and the injectable shutdown impact. Several answers deflected on capacity utilisation and CSA counts.
key_quotes: With all this, we really remain confident and are happy to reiterate our FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue as well as, EBITDA margins of 40%.
The constraint in this market has been supply, not demand.

544454|2026-06.headline: Indiqube Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR428 crore (+37% YoY) and PAT rose 91% to INR35 crore, with PAT margin at 8%.
544454|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR428 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA of INR87 crore (+34%), EBIT of INR55 crore (+59%) and PAT of INR35 crore (+91%). Margins expanded, with EBIT margin at 13% (11% a year ago) and PAT margin at 8% (6%). Rent-paying area was flat QoQ, which management attributed to the timing of building handovers, with about 2 million sq ft of annual additions still guided. Q&A centred on VAS revenue (INR39 crore one-time in the quarter), solar capex, a large new Noida centre, and occupancy and margin ranges. Management declined to give quarterly OCF or capex figures ahead of the H1 audit.

segments.name: Client mix (revenue)
segments.commentary: GCCs ~52-53% of revenue, startups and unicorns ~23%, Indian enterprises ~28% (of which GCCs ~10-12%). Multi-center clients ~41% of revenue; top five clients 12% of revenue; 855 clients as of June 2026.

segments.name: VAS (DesignQube, IndiCare, Eco)
segments.commentary: VAS is ~17% of revenue and management expects it to rise by about 2-4 percentage points. VAS EBIT margin is guided at ~15% for the next one to two years, as growth takes priority over margin.

segments.name: Solar / sustainability
segments.commentary: About 30 MW of solar capacity is operational. Plan to add 25-30 MW this year at INR100-120 crore capex; solar IRR stated at 18-22%.

guidance_outlook: Annual additions of close to 2 million sq ft (about 44,000 seats) reiterated; about 3.9 million sq ft (about 97,000 seats) of headroom already signed.
Corporate occupancy guided at 80-85% (stated later as 82-86%); mature centres (over 12 months) at 85-90% (stated as 86-90%/88-90%).
Margin ranges guided at EBITDA 19-21%, EBIT 11-13%, PAT 8-10% on a annual basis.
Operational break-even for new centres is 5-6 months at about 52-57% occupancy; steady state around 12 months (9-12 months to reach ~90%).
Around 2.8 million sq ft of area under management not yet rent-paying is expected to become operational in 12-16 months (most signed supply to deliver in 12-18 months).
Large Noida centre expected to go live around mid-2027 (Q2 or Q3 FY28).
Management expects to sign larger spaces in Hyderabad and Mumbai during this financial year.
capex_capacity: Solar: 30 MW operational; plan to add 25-30 MW this year at INR100-120 crore capex.
Capex and OCF for Q1 not disclosed; management said figures would be provided with H1 results after audit and review. Capex is driven by interiors, design-and-build, solar and vendor payment cycles.
Debt increase is attributed to solar investment, not the leasing business (per Vikas Agarwal).
New Noida centre is a large single building; live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28).
demand_pricing: Institutional supply share rose to ~20% of portfolio from ~12% a couple of years ago; institutional buildings carry higher rents and CAM costs but management says margins are consistent across supply types.
Tier-2 centres: real estate cost INR50-70 per sq ft; seat pricing INR6,500-7,500 per seat; unit economics said to be similar to Tier-1.
Bangalore is ~60-64% of area; Chennai ~10%. Management expects Bangalore share to fall as NCR, Hyderabad, Mumbai and West India grow.
Attrition is negative (net expansion); client renewal rate ~90%; client notice periods 60-90 days; leases are straight leases with landlords (no back-to-back).
Tech parks are ~20% of portfolio. North Bangalore exposure is under 0.5 million sq ft of ~6.5 million sq ft in Bangalore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no QoQ rise in rent-paying area despite 2 million sq ft annual guidance, and is supply slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said additions are lumpy and tracked annually; H2 FY26 added ~1.14 million sq ft. No slowdown is seen, and ~3.9 million sq ft of signed headroom is available.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR39 crore one-time VAS revenue and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue came across DesignQube, IndiCare and Eco. Management said it is non-recurring in quarters but will keep recurring over time, with VAS share rising 2-4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How much solar capex is planned and what IRR is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25-30 MW more at INR100-120 crore; solar IRR 18-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the large Noida centre and is it demand-backed?
qa_highlights.answer: Live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28). Management said it was largely proactive supply, not pre-leased, based on NCR micro-market research.

qa_highlights.question: Will new centres dilute margins given slow break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational break-even takes 5-6 months at 52-57% occupancy and steady state ~12 months, so no margin pressure expected. The 36 months referred to full capex recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What margin will VAS deliver and will it drive group margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: VAS margin ~15% for the next one to two years; management prioritises scale. Group-level margins are expected to stay within the stated ranges.

risks_watch: Rent-paying area was flat QoQ; the ~2 million sq ft annual addition depends on H2-weighted handovers in Jan-Feb.
Revenue concentration: Bangalore ~60% of area; the Noida site is a large non-institutional asset held by an HNI family group.
Capex and OCF not disclosed for Q1; H1 numbers due after audit.
One-time VAS revenue (INR39 crore) inflates the quarter; the underlying run-rate needs checking.
Interest cost rising with solar-linked debt; watch debt quantum and cost in H1 disclosures.
Occupancy guidance has been stated in different ranges during the call (corporate 80-85% vs 82-86%); clarify the official range.
544454|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, pipeline and margin stability, with specific ranges given. Evasive on quarterly capex, OCF and city-wise revenue-to-rent ratio, deferring these to H1 audited numbers.

+91% YoY; PAT margin 8% vs 6% in Q1 FY26
up from ~12% earlier and ~15% at a later point

513349|2026-06.headline: Ajmera Realty Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR320 crores, PAT up 14% to INR45 crores, debt cut to INR680 crores.
513349|2026-06.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was about INR320 crores, up 23% YoY from INR265 crores, with EBITDA of INR94 crores (about 29% margin) and PAT of INR45 crores (14% margin). Ajmera Solis entered revenue recognition for the first time this quarter. Debt fell by INR57 crores to INR680 crores, taking debt-equity to 0.47x. segments.name: Residential (Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Manhattan 1 ~93% sold; Greenfinity A&B 94% sold, nearing OC; Vihara Bhandup 81% sold; Solis 86% absorbed and first to enter revenue recognition this quarter.

segments.name: Commercial (Bandra 33Fifteen)
segments.commentary: 19% of inventory sold; piling and shoring in progress; management aims to speed up execution.

segments.name: Luxury collective (Ajmera One, Versova)
segments.commentary: 3% of inventory sold as of the call date; excavation stage, subdued sales expected this year.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Iris 90% sold, finishing work toward OC; Marina 69% sold, second slab in progress.

segments.name: Wadala (Manhattan 2 and others)
segments.commentary: Over 50% of inventory sold, excavation in progress; boutique office Phase 1 part of ~INR18,000 crore Wadala GDV.

guidance_outlook: Revenue visibility of INR3,846 crores (INR1,661 crores committed sales plus INR2,185 crores unsold inventory), rising to INR10,000-plus crores with the upcoming launch pipeline of about INR6,500 crores.

FY27 launch pipeline of about INR3,000 crores (call mentions INR6,500 crores for launches in another part of the call); Wadala boutique office launch in a single phase of about INR3,600 crores, targeted for Q3.
Estimated cash flow potential, pre-tax and post-debt, from ongoing projects, upcoming projects and other revenue of about INR3,380 crores over project life cycles.
Remaining INR241 crores of the INR330 crores asset monetisation target; a further stake sale in a JV was signed in early July 2026 and will be reported in Q2.

Bangalore SV Concrete project removed from pipeline and replaced by Whitefield (INR389 crores GDV, asset-light, Q4 FY27 target) against a INR1,800 crore BD guidance; a further ~INR400 crore asset-light Bangalore project was added during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Management described the sector as seasonally softer in Q1 with sequential moderation in presales and collections after a strong Q4 FY26, but attributes this to seasonality rather than a structural slowdown.
Demand is strongest in lifestyle and premium segments; Wadala commercial demand is linked to the new airport and BKC connectivity and GCC growth.
Ajmera One (Versova) demand is for larger apartments; management expects subdued sales this year until superstructure progresses.
Mid and luxury segments are seeing an uptick per management, though overall sales were subdued due to fewer large launches this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Kanjurmarg land conversion and tie-up for the 7-acre plot?
qa_highlights.answer: Conversion targeted in 2-3 months, before the December deadline; tie-up talks are active but will only conclude after conversion. Deal is a single transaction, with a mix of outright and JV bids.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in the INR3,600 crore single-phase Wadala boutique office launch and why it was scaled up?
qa_highlights.answer: Approval changes added ~1 million sq ft FSI and ~INR3,000 crores GDV. Office launch scaled from 4-5 lakh sq ft to 8-8.5 lakh sq ft, supported by GCC and connectivity-driven demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why have Pune and Borivali launch timelines moved?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly regulatory reasons; management is choosing to launch at plinth level for better demand and pricing, not at excavation stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sales weak at Ajmera One (Versova)?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand for larger units appears only after RCC level; the project is at excavation, so management will not push desperate sales and expects a year before traction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated finance cost rise from ~INR21 crores to ~INR30 crores QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Solis entered revenue recognition, so accumulated interest on its high-cost PE-funded debt was charged to P&L. Cost is expected to normalise to about INR20 crores from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any P&L impact from the INR89 crores monetisation, and why was SV Concrete dropped?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR89 crores is a balance-sheet financial asset realisation with no P&L impact. SV Concrete was swapped for Whitefield (INR389 crores GDV, Q4 FY27 target).

risks_watch: Debt-equity may stay above 0.47x for a quarter or two due to pre-RERA working capital needs before reaching the 1x target.
Kanjurmarg conversion timing (December deadline) and the strategic tie-up structure are unresolved.
Large Wadala boutique office launch (~INR3,600 crores single phase) is unprecedented for the company and depends on commercial demand.
Launch slippage: Pune and Borivali were moved to Q4 FY27; Ajmera One sales are subdued until superstructure starts.
Weighted average cost of debt and finance cost normalisation to ~INR20 crores per quarter needs to be confirmed in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: down INR57 crores from INR737 crores at 31 Mar 2026
stated as Q1FY26 in transcript, likely Q1FY27; described as down
up from ~INR21 crores QoQ, due to Solis revenue recognition and high-cost PE debt servicing

509496|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 operating income rose 6% YoY to Rs 2,721 crore, EBITDA margin 10.5%, while order inflow nearly tripled to Rs 8,519 crore.
509496|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 6% YoY to Rs 2,721 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs 285 crore, with margin up to 10.5% from 10.1%. PAT rose 3% to Rs 141 crore. Management said Q1 revenue was held back by Vadhvan port execution not starting, and by four newly won jobs (Munger, Pune Metro, Delhi Metro, Morsagar; about Rs 10,000-12,000 crore) that had not yet begun production. Management maintained FY27 revenue growth guidance of 25%, with the bulk of catch-up expected from Q3. A Rs 5,000 crore QIP enabling resolution was approved, but management said the timing and amount depend on future orders and market conditions.

financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 2,900 crore in Q1 FY26 (about 3x)

financial_highlights.value: about 120 days (inventory about 30 days, WIP about 107 days)

segments.name: Marine
segments.commentary: About Rs 15,000 crore of marine jobs in the tender pipeline, including Vadhvan port (execution not started), overseas jobs in Oman and UAE, and Bangladesh work. Tuticorin Outer Harbour and Vizag port also mentioned.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Five Navi Mumbai projects (three of 140 MW, one of 130 MW and two of 30 MW) are under way; a Vizag civil job has also been secured. Total work is about 320-400 MW, with electromechanical work possibly later.

segments.name: Bangladesh transmission project
segments.commentary: Execution is under control. Completion is now guided for September/October 2026 (earlier June 2026 timing was cited by an analyst). Receivables are about Rs 178 crore plus retention.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 25% (management also said 20-25% growth is achievable for a few years).
FY27 order inflow target of about Rs 25,000 crore; Rs 8,519 crore secured in Q1 and about Rs 1,247 crore added in July, with L1 positions of about Rs 900-1,000 crore.
Q3 and Q4 expected to be much better than Q1; Q2 seen as weak because of monsoon. Management cited last year's Q1 of Rs 2,500 crore, Q2 Rs 2,100 crore and Q4 Rs 3,000 crore as the pattern.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 350-400 crore, barring exceptional plant purchases such as TBMs for large road tunnels.
Working capital expected to stay at 110-120 days; gross debt expected to rise about 10-20% and at least 20-25% if top line grows 25%.

Rs 5,000 crore QIP is an enabling resolution. Management said part is for capex (Rs 4,000-5,000 crore range cited for capex needs) and part for working capital and possibly inorganic growth, with timing dependent on orders and markets.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex additions were Rs 81 crore; FY27 capex guided at Rs 350-400 crore.
Large diameter road tunnel jobs would need tunnel boring machines, raising capex well above the normal run-rate.
Management said plant older than five years is not permitted on many projects, which raises replacement capex needs.
Data centre capacity is about 320-400 MW in progress; Navi Mumbai civil works already in place.
Management said current operating capacity allows about Rs 5,000 crore of quarterly revenue, which the analyst asked about and management confirmed.
demand_pricing: Work-in-hand is about Rs 31,000 crore versus Rs 18,000-20,000 crore earlier; about Rs 12,000 crore of it had no progress yet (Munger, DMRC, Pune Metro, Morsagar).

Adani group makes up about 50% of the order book (Rs 6,000 crore of Q1 orders from the group and Rs 2,500 crore from outside). Group work is competitively bid with no fixed price, and some material is supplied free by the client.

Bid pipeline is about Rs 90,000 crore, with a hit ratio of about 15% (earlier about 20%). Six segments each carry about Rs 15,000-20,000 crore: marine, underground metro, airports, data centre, highways and bridges, and water.
Export share of order book is about 2-3%.
Management expects margin to hold in double digits, with contingency built into estimates for geopolitical and commodity risk. A government agency cut performance guarantees from 10% to 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise Rs 5,000 crore via QIP when the company is net-cash and the order book is already Rs 31,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the money is for growth, with part for plant and equipment, part for inorganic growth, and part for working capital. It also said timing depends on market conditions and near-term visibility, and that little of it would be used this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected revenue trajectory and why is growth lagging order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Vadhvan (zero production so far), about Rs 10,000-12,000 crore of newly won jobs that need 6-7 months of design and mobilisation, and Abu Dhabi work that has only just picked up. It guided for 25% FY27 growth, with Q3 and Q4 stronger.

qa_highlights.question: What is Vadhvan port execution status?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution has not started. Management said pending issues are outside its control, with no timeline set; it hopes work will resume soon.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Bangladesh project timeline moved and what is its status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution remains on plan for September/October 2026. Monsoon-driven river conditions and deep-water foundation work are the constraints, and a different technology is being used. Receivables are about Rs 178 crore plus retention.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth sustainable, and what capex does it need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20-25% growth is possible over coming years. Normal segments (marine, road, industrial, airport) need about Rs 300-400 crore capex a year, but a Rs 10,000 crore road tunnel would need much more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the marine and overall competitive landscape?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are about three major marine players, with about five including others. Competition is intense and price-driven, and the hit ratio is about 15%.

530655|2026-06.headline: Goodluck India Q1 FY27 standalone revenue up ~23% to INR1,205.9 cr, EBITDA up 15% to INR110.5 cr; Defence expansion delayed 6-9 months.
530655|2026-06.overview: Standalone income from operations rose to INR1,205.94 crore from INR983.29 crore YoY, while standalone EBITDA rose 15% to INR110.53 crore and PAT rose to INR49.66 crore from INR40.14 crore. Management cited 31% consolidated revenue growth, 46% consolidated EBITDA growth and 67% consolidated PAT growth, with EBITDA margin above 10%. Defence (Goodluck Defence & Aerospace) won orders of INR255 crore and INR52 crore for 155 mm shells, but its capacity expansion has slipped 6-9 months due to financial closure. A preferential issue at the Defence subsidiary (about 75 lakh shares at INR375, about INR285 crore) drew heavy shareholder criticism over valuation and the choice over a rights issue at parent level.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR983.29 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +23%)
vs INR40.14 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA margin

segments.name: Defence (Goodluck Defence & Aerospace)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA margin. Orders of INR255 crore (about 50,000 shells of 155 mm long-range RTF empty shells, 10-month execution) and INR52 crore (20,000 shells, 3-month execution). DGQA certificate received for 107 RTF artillery shells.

segments.name: Precision tubes / auto tubes
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 12-13%. Hydraulic tube utilisation rose to 60-65% in Q1 from about 50%.

segments.name: Pipes and CR sheet
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 3-5%.

segments.name: Solar structures
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 7-8%.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 10-11%. Transmission tower capacity about 50,000 tons per year.

segments.name: Forging
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margin of 12-13%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated revenue growth guidance maintained at 15-20% for FY27 (versus 14-15% in the prior call, per an analyst).
Defence FY27 revenue target INR300-350 crore at 30-35% EBITDA margin; management reiterated 30-35% margin range, saying it is conservative.
Defence expansion (250,000 shells capacity) delayed 6-9 months; management hopes expansion starts by Q4 FY27, with commercialisation about one year later (around Q4 FY28).
Post-expansion Defence plant capacity 400,000 shells, achievable about 350,000 shells per annum.
Earlier Defence FY28 target of INR1,000 crore (INR800 crore shells, INR200 crore aerospace) to move out by 6-9 months; management declined to give a new FY28 number.
Capex: Defence about INR400 crore; standalone INR100-150 crore.
Debt repayment for FY27 stated as INR62 crore (INR25 crore repaid in Q1), per CFO; analyst had noted a lower figure earlier.
Management said Defence subsidiary IPO could be in about 18 months, subject to approvals.

Value-added products about 60% of business; GI tube and front fork tube capacity expected in about 6 months; 40,000-45,000 metric tons of capacity addition announced for FY27 (large-diameter pipe ramp delayed by West Asia crisis).
capex_capacity: Defence shell capacity currently 150,000 shells per annum; expansion (plant capacity 400,000) delayed 6-9 months due to financial closure.
Defence capex about INR400 crore; standalone capex INR100-150 crore.
Hydraulic tube capacity utilisation 60-65% in Q1 (about 50% earlier).
Standalone capacity utilisation annualised at 98%.
Plans for aerospace rolling mill to supply outer bodies for space rockets and an aerospace supplier ecosystem; Goodluck Astra land allotted, licence applied for.
Large-diameter pipe and precision tube capacity additions (40,000-45,000 MT) ramping slower due to West Asia crisis.
demand_pricing: Standalone volume 1,22,718 MT, up 8.8% YoY.
Overall realisation about INR7,000/ton in Q4; target INR9,000/ton within 3 years; management said it has not increased much in Q1 due to West Asia crisis.
Defence realisation roughly doubled between the 107 (18 km range) and ERFB (38 km range) shell orders; EBITDA per ton about INR9,000 in Q1.
Exports to more than 100 countries; growth coming from US and Europe; export order pipeline described as healthy; first-quarter export growth about 53% per management.
Solar: 30%+ market share. Transmission demand supported by solar evacuation from Rajasthan and Gujarat.
Input cost risk high due to petroleum-linked inputs and logistics costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Defence subsidiary being listed separately rather than demerged, and how does that create value for current shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said financial advisers recommended a separate listing; the listing will be based on future numbers. Parent shareholders benefit as a subsidiary's value accrues to the group.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the subsidiary stake sold through a preferential issue instead of a rights issue at Goodluck India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said financial advisers preferred this route and that the company needs funds for growth. Management acknowledged a differing view and said it would consider feedback.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidiary's implied valuation from the INR285 crore issue at INR375/share?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-issue outstanding shares about 4.91 crore; post-issue about 5.66 crore shares (about 75 lakh new shares). Implied valuation not explicitly stated; dilution cited as about 10.5% (an investor said 15%).

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Defence expansion slipped and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay is due to financial closure of the project and approvals; expansion now expected to start by Q4 FY27, with commercialisation around a year later.

qa_highlights.question: What are Defence margins and revenue in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Defence revenue about INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA; management is guiding 30-35% sustainable margin, stating it is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company maintaining its FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 15-20% revenue growth guidance; volume up 9% in Q1 and expected to improve if geopolitical conditions ease.

544870|2026-06.headline: Behari Lal Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR29.7 crore (19.6% margin) and high-value share at 60.4%.
544870|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's first earnings call as a listed entity, following its IPO (INR301 crore issue, listed 19 August 2026). Revenue from operations grew 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore and PAT rose 24.5% to INR19.2 crore, though both EBITDA and PAT fell sequentially against Q4 FY26, which carried INR5.9 crore of one-off state incentives. Mix improved: high-value products (rolls, castings, specialty alloys) reached 60.4% of revenue and EBITDA per ton rose to about INR13,500. Management guided to about INR80 crore of FY27 capex, with Unit 3 (centrifugal/foundry for ICDP and HSS rolls) targeted to start in Q1 FY28, while defense revenue is expected to become meaningful from FY28.

segments.name: Alloy steel products (bars 6-230 mm, valve/tool/die steel)
segments.commentary: 47.7% of Q1 revenue (FY26 share ~46%); includes recently introduced valve, tool and die steel grades.

segments.name: Metal rolls
segments.commentary: 25.8% of Q1 revenue (FY26 ~26%); supplied to steel majors such as SAIL, JSW, Tata Steel and Vizag.

segments.name: Engineering castings (500 kg to 25 t single pieces)
segments.commentary: 19.8% of Q1 revenue (FY26 ~20%); demand from power sector, crusher OEMs; recent 22-23 t single-piece casting for a thermal power customer.

segments.name: Forging ingots and shafts
segments.commentary: 1.9% of Q1 revenue, down from 4.4%, as management deliberately shifts steel into finished high-value grades.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex target of about INR80 crore; INR5 crore spent in Q1 and INR75 crore planned over the next three quarters. Funding split: IPO proceeds plus internal accruals.
Unit 3 (foundry, centrifugal casting for ICDP/HSS rolls) targeted to commence in Q1 FY28; exact capex amount not yet disclosed pending exchange filing.
High-value product share targeted at about 70% in the near future (currently ~60%).
Operating EBITDA margin expected to grow 20-25% over the next two to three years per management; prior-year operating EBITDA margin cited as around 25%.
Inventory days to be held at 90-100 days as high-value mix grows.
Defense revenue expected to become meaningful from FY28; no quantified mix target given.
capex_capacity: Melting capacity is 1.5x FY24 levels; last melting addition was in FY24, and management plans a considerable melting addition next year with Unit 3.
Unit 3 shed under construction and most machinery ordered; centrifugal casting (vertical and horizontal) planned to make ICDP and HSS rolls; commencement targeted Q1 FY28.

IPO net proceeds of INR93 crore fresh capital: INR56 crore for equipment and civil work at both facilities, ~INR7 crore for rooftop solar, small debt repayment and ~INR19 crore general corporate purposes. Management said part of GCP was already used for working capital within 15 days of receipt.
Planned investments in CNC machining, shot blasting, painting, NDT, finish machining and a NABL-accredited lab to make castings ready-to-use.
Solar power project funded from internal accruals to lower power cost.
demand_pricing: High-value share rose from ~47% (two-three years ago) to 57% in FY26 and 60.4% in Q1 FY27; EBITDA per ton rose from ~INR9,100 (FY25) to ~INR11,500 (FY26) and INR13,457 in Q1.
Order book INR162 crore / 13,138 t at 30 June (over one quarter of revenue), skewed to high-value products.
Thermal power sector demand is rising; management cites customer visibility to 2035 and orders for CNC machines to support castings.
Defense: orders from Bharat Dynamics and Nuclear Power Corporation of India plus private suppliers to defense customers; prototype revenue started; long approval cycles.
Automotive share fell to 33% (from 38.7% in FY26) as low-margin commodity alloy bars for forging customers are being redirected; infrastructure rose to 26.4% from 20.7%.
Imports of ICDP and HSS rolls about 3.5 lakh tons in FY26 per management; management says it is the first domestic player to add capacity for these grades.
Management attributed the export decline to timing of casting shipments and order phasing, and said the trend is not changed.

524208|2026-06.headline: Aarti Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 2,627 crore and EBITDA 79% to Rs 385 crore, with management refusing to guarantee the run rate.
524208|2026-06.overview: Revenue of Rs 2,627 crore (+41% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 385 crore (+79% YoY) were lifted by raw-material price pass-through, product mix, and inventory and FX gains, which management sized at roughly Rs 50-60 crore. Volumes fell sequentially (energy -17% QoQ, non-energy -7%, overall about -12%) amid West Asia disruption and high raw-material prices. Zone IV commissioning is delayed by 3-6 months due to labour shortages, and management declined to commit to a forward EBITDA run rate. The Augene JV is near commissioning, and FY27 capex remains on track at Rs 700-800 crore.

segments.name: Energy (Fuel Additives)
segments.commentary: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; West Asia share fell to about 2% from about 15%, and volumes were redirected to US, Africa, Europe and India. Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged about $15-18/bbl, and management expects the capacity to reach high utilisation in Q1 itself.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Polymers
segments.commentary: Demand was soft in Q1 on weak downstream US and China demand, and low shipments followed heavy Q4 FY26 bulk shipments to the US. Management expects recovery in Q2 and full-year growth.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Dyes & Pigments
segments.commentary: Demand remained subdued amid high raw-material prices and seasonality. Price increases in dyes and pigments and pharma were partly linked to China's VAT removal on the NCB chain.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Pharma and Agro
segments.commentary: Pharma demand was stable. Agrochemical volumes were marginally lower as customers resisted elevated raw-material-linked prices; recovery is expected in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY28 EBITDA target of Rs 1,800 crore retained; the Augene JV is included in this guidance, but management said Zone IV ramp-up may be slower than originally assumed.
Management declined to guide to a sustainable quarterly EBITDA run rate, citing plus/minus 15-20% monthly price volatility; it expects volume growth to offset lost inventory gains.
Augene JV (50:50, consolidated at PAT level) expected to start operations in Q2 FY27, with steady-state revenue retained at Rs 300-400 crore.
FY27 capex on track at Rs 700-800 crore; capex intensity expected to fall significantly from FY28.

Zone IV commissioning is delayed 3-6 months; the MPP is expected to produce first product in August 2026 and commissioning will be announced thereafter. Management expects 5-10 products in FY27 and 25-30 by FY28.
Sabic-linked backward-integration project commissioning expected around Sep-Oct 2027.
capex_capacity: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; management said there is no fixed limit on further expansion, and it will first demonstrate utilisation over the next 12 months.
Zone IV: 97% of equipment erected and 85% of piping complete across the five chemistry blocks; full manpower restored, with commissioning expected in FY27 and ramp-up over FY28-FY29.
PEDA project in market seeding and expected to commercialise soon; DCB debottlenecking to 140 KTPA under evaluation.
NCB chain debottlenecking is being evaluated within existing assets given demand in India.
Aarti Circularity plastic recycling plant with Re Sustainability slated for commissioning in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Raw-material inflation (benzene, sulphur, methanol, aniline) was passed through to customers; high prices reduced purchasing power in dyes, selected agro and polymer compounds.
Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged $15-18/bbl, which management described as healthy, while the energy business remains volatile.
Exports were 59% of revenue; US-bound DAP shipments carry 2-3 month voyage times that delay revenue recognition.
China's suspension of export tax rebates is creating opportunities for the NCB value chain.
Non-energy volumes fell on delayed purchasing in a high-price environment, with some supply-chain effects; management said Middle East exposure in non-energy is low.

qa_highlights.question: What were the FX and inventory gains in Q1, and what is the impact on the EBITDA base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a Rs 50-60 crore impact but said it is hard to quantify because of intra-quarter volatility; the CFO said FX gains came from squaring off import positions as the rupee moved in a Rs 92-97 range, and management advised treating this as operating profit with no forward commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin lower sequentially despite the inventory and FX benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly gross margin is not a reliable steady-state indicator, citing timing of raw-material purchases and product placement, freight, lower volumes raising operating costs, and the chemical business running on absolute rupee deltas rather than percentage margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Zone IV delay affect FY28 EBITDA visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MPP and calcium chloride unit are on track, but the five chemistry blocks face slower ramp-up than originally planned, and it will share ramp-up details once the blocks commission.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Augene JV affect reported EBITDA, and is it in the Rs 1,800 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that the Rs 1,800 crore FY28 guidance includes Augene EBITDA, while the Re Aarti JV is not expected to contribute meaningfully before FY28; reporting treatment for JVs is yet to be finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the energy business's volume, capacity and market share sustainable once West Asia normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business remains in a market-development phase; the portfolio is diversified across US, Africa, Europe, Middle East and India (Southeast Asia not yet penetrated), and it expects utilisation gains rather than volume shifts when West Asia reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company stop disclosing absolute sales volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it removed absolute sales numbers from slides because they were being used in an unfavourable way, and now gives energy/non-energy volume growth plus value-chain utilisation ranges.

532734|2026-06.headline: GPIL Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin 19.1%, PAT margin 12.7%, both flat YoY but softer QoQ on costlier merchant iron ore and imported coal.
532734|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew both YoY and QoQ on higher volumes and better realisations, while EBITDA and PAT were broadly flat YoY and down sequentially on input costs. Iron ore mining volume fell because dumping space was constrained by pending tree-cutting approval on additional land, forcing market ore purchases for pellets. One of the new 2 mtpa pellet plants was shut from around mid-June/July on gas price and iron ore economics, with Q2 pellet output guided to roughly 500 kt. Management shelved the 1 mtpa integrated steel project over water allocation delays and moved the 0.7 mtpa CRM complex to Maharashtra, with commissioning now targeted December 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Stable YoY; softer QoQ due to input costs

financial_highlights.metric: Pellet plant (4.7 mtpa expanded capacity) utilisation

financial_highlights.value: About INR13,000/t now vs about INR10,500/t in Q4 FY26 and early Q1
Up about 40-45% under new PNGRB guidelines
About INR10,000/t currently; low of about INR8,700/t in early July

financial_highlights.change: Broadly stable QoQ and YoY; target 2.4920

segments.name: Iron ore mining (Ari Dongri)
segments.commentary: Mining volume declined YoY and QoQ, constrained by overburden dumping space pending government land approval. Captive mining guidance of 3.4 mt for FY27 is said to be unchanged; management expects mining cost to fall below INR2,700/t from FY28 vs INR3,000-3,500/t now.

segments.name: Pellets (4.7 mtpa expanded capacity)
segments.commentary: Ran at 77% utilisation in Q1 with all three plants operating, and pellet sales jumped in Q1 as surplus pellets went to the merchant market. One 2 mtpa plant has been shut since about mid-2026; FY27 pellet guidance of 4.0 mt is under review and expected to be lower.

segments.name: Sponge iron, billet, rolled products (value-added)
segments.commentary: Management cited healthy YoY growth in value-added production led by sponge iron, billets and rolled products. No segment volumes or revenues were given on the call.

segments.name: Galvanized products
segments.commentary: Volumes declined YoY, attributed to monsoon-season delays in project deliveries. Management described this as seasonal.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage, Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: About INR500 crore spent. Machine delivery starts December 2026 and first container is targeted for Q1 FY28. Containers are being quoted from August 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance is said to be on track, with Q1 at 16-29% of full-year guidance. Management said FY27 pellet output will be slightly lower, and a revised figure will come later.

Q2 FY27 pellet production is expected at about 500 kt if the plant stays shut for the whole quarter. Q3 is expected at full pellet capacity, with merchant ore purchases at 25-30%, falling below 10% in Q4 and to zero (fully captive) in FY28.

Mining ramp-up is expected from Q3 FY27 once government land approval comes through (targeted end-September), reaching full capacity by end Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Beneficiation plant commissioning is expected by Q3 FY27.

Margin improvement is expected from Q4 FY27 once the beneficiation plant enables higher captive pellet use. Management said CRM incentives can add 2-3% to CRM margins, taking them to 10-11% from the earlier 7-8%.
Vision 2030 target (4x revenue, 3x EBITDA and PAT) was restated without the steel plant. Management said the steel plant is on hold and no timeline is set.
capex_capacity: CRM complex (0.7 mtpa, relocated to Maharashtra near Sambhajinagar): capex raised to INR1,100 crore from earlier INR900-950 crore, including working capital margin money; INR80 crore spent so far; land about INR50 crore for 35 acres; construction from October 2026; commissioning December 2027; funded by INR550 crore debt and internal accruals. Land allotment approval is expected by end-August 2026.
BESS (20 GW... as stated in transcript, battery storage project in Maharashtra): about INR500 crore spent; remaining INR700-800 crore to be spent over FY27 and FY28; commissioning targeted Q1 FY28.
Mining and other capex: about INR2,000 crore for the remaining FY27 and the whole of FY28. No FY29 projection has been given.
Ari Dongri beneficiation plant: INR218 crore spent till June 2026; ramp-up from Q3 FY27 and full-scale operation from FY28.

Captive solar: 25 MW commissioned in May 2026; 100 MW under construction, targeted September 2026; 150 MW project in abeyance. Solar storage of 45 MW targeted for Q3 FY27 (management corrected 'Q3 27' to 'Q3 26' and then said Q3 FY27 was intended). Captive solar would reach 290 MW.

543258|2026-06.headline: Indigo Paints Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.7% to INR350 crore with EBITDA margin up to 17.7%, its best Q1 margin in four years.

segments.commentary: Actual production began in May/June 2026 after prototyping and trials. Management says it is aligned with five industry-leading aftermarket LED brands. FY27 contribution is expected to be small.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance kept at 18-20%, as given in Q4; management will revisit by end-Q2 or Q3 if needed.
Group EBITDA margin guided at about 13-14% for FY27; management said it would be 14% or slightly better without the war.
ODM home lighting EBITDA margin expected to stay near 8.4%, give or take 0.5%, if raw material prices stay stable or fall.
Long-term feasible EBITDA margin cited at 17-18%, not the earlier 20-23%. Management targets asset turns of 4.5-5x in about 3-3.5 years.
Management expects raw material and wage pressure to normalise in coming quarters as revenue scale and operating leverage build.
Automotive OEM onboarding targeted by FY28, after aftermarket traction.
Honeywell SKUs expected to rise 3-4x by year-end.
capex_capacity: Block 1 (about 2 lakh sq ft) is operational; Block 2 (Tower-2) partially commercialised in Q2 FY27, with hearables and wearables using two floors.
Block 3 construction is on schedule; about Rs 20 crore of remaining capex is earmarked for Tower-3.
FY27 capex guided at about Rs 20-25 crore, with little left after Tower-2.
Depreciation from Tower-2 expected to start from Q2 FY27; management pointed to cash PAT for comparability.
demand_pricing: Semiconductor prices have roughly doubled in some cases, and lead times have risen from about 4-6 weeks to over a year for some electronic components, forcing spot buying and design changes.
Metals (MS, aluminium, copper) prices have been volatile over the past 4-5 months.
Management is in talks with customers on pricing to offset cost pressure.
Middle East/UAE business declined YoY due to the war, though management says IKIO is outperforming peers there and is entering the developer segment.
About 50% of hearables/wearables products are now IKIO-designed ODM products, up from job work.
Honeywell: amplifiers, PA systems and fire alarm panels are in production, with more products in the pipeline.
Solar inverter/BESS: one sizeable order completed; new products in development.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory given geopolitical and manpower headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are in line with annual guidance. Gross margin was hit by component lead times and metal and semiconductor costs, and the company is negotiating with customers. Long-term feasible EBITDA margin is 17-18%, not 20-23%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall from 44-45% to 41%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed metal price volatility and semiconductor shortages and price spikes. It redesigned products to keep specs while avoiding shortages, and said 41% is sustainable at current raw material prices unless the war escalates.

qa_highlights.question: Was the other business QoQ dip due to seasonality or the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is seasonally the leanest quarter. YoY, Q1 FY27 Rs 124 crore matched the full Q1 FY26 base of about Rs 120 crore, and the war cost an estimated Rs 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 40% growth in the home lighting ODM business and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New customers were added and the customer base diversified from one customer to 3-4. Management expects FY27 at around Rs 170 crore, plus or minus Rs 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hearables and wearables production visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: H&W is about 15-16% of revenue now and is guided at 16-18% for FY27. Customers plan 3-6 months ahead, with 10-12 month pipeline discussions with larger customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of automotive lighting and the OEM path?
qa_highlights.answer: Aftermarket production began in May/June 2026 with five leading brands. OEM onboarding is planned for Phase 2, targeted by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be raised given stronger growth in the other business?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management kept the 18-20% FY27 growth guidance, citing volatility, and will revisit at end-Q2 or Q3.

517569|2026-06.headline: KEI Industries Q1 FY27 net sales rose 23% to INR3,185 crore and operating margin reached 12.43%, with EBITDA up 39.5%.
517569|2026-06.overview: Net sales grew 23% YoY to INR3,185 crore, while domestic wire and cable sales rose 29% to INR2,784 crore. Operating (EBITDA) margin expanded to 13.04% from 11.49%, and PAT rose 40% to INR274 crore, helped by product mix (EHV, retail/dealer channel) and operating leverage. Exports fell to INR341 crore from INR375 crore because Middle East orders were not executed and US custom duty issues persisted. Management reiterated a 20%+ growth target, though it declined to raise guidance above that, and said the Sanand plant is ramping up slowly.

financial_highlights.value: INR3,185 crore total (domestic INR2,784 crore; export INR341 crore)
financial_highlights.change: Total wire and cable +24.4% YoY; domestic +29%; export down from INR375 crore
Improved YoY; management guides 11-12% operating margin going forward
+40% YoY (vs INR195 crore); PAT margin 8.61% vs 7.56%

financial_highlights.value: INR1,054 crore (incl. INR303 crore unutilised QIP)

segments.name: Domestic wire and cable
segments.commentary: Sales INR2,784 crore, up 29% YoY. Retail/dealer channel share rose to 59% from about 51%; 2,128 active dealers as of 30 June.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Sales INR341 crore vs INR375 crore last year, hit by unexecuted Middle East orders and US customs duty issues. Management expects exports to recover for full year.

segments.name: Extra high-voltage (EHV) cable
segments.commentary: Sales INR186 crore, up 47% YoY. Management cites EHV operating margin of about 15%, vs about 10.5% for institutional LV/MV power cable, 11% retail and above 11% export.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Sales INR43 crore vs INR61 crore last year; PHV EPC execution sales INR18 crore. Management says EPC is no longer a large share, supporting gross margin.

guidance_outlook: Management targets value growth of 20%+ CAGR; in Q&A it said full-year growth would be around 24-25%, and the CMD said FY27 revenue growth would exceed 25%.
Operating margin guided at 11-12% for coming year after crossing the earlier 11% hurdle; management says quarterly fluctuation of 0.25-0.5% is normal.

Sanand revenue expected at INR1,500-2,000 crore in FY27 (CMD corrected a media figure of about INR3,000 crore); long-run Sanand capacity about INR6,000 crore, rising to about INR7,000 crore within 2 years after balancing equipment.
Export share target of 17-18% of revenue for FY27 (FY26 about 16%); management expects exports to grow about 50% in the remaining nine months.
Capex of INR600-700 crore per year for the next 3-4 years; new INR700 crore Salarpur (Bhiwadi) plant for LV/MV cable to be built over about 2 years. Sanand balance of about INR300 crore in FY27.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex payment INR191 crore, of which Sanand INR180 crore; cumulative Sanand spend INR1,722 crore against a INR2,000 crore project cost, with the balance to be spent over about the next 6 months.
Capacity utilisation in Q1: cable 72%, house wire 61%, stainless steel wire 91%, communication cable 45%. Sanand Phase 1 at about 50% utilisation as of the call.
Sanand EHV line (152-metre tower) to be commissioned by March 2027; INR1,300 crore of Sanand capacity is for EHV cable, and EHV is expected to contribute about 9-10% of added capacity revenue.
Salarpur (Bhiwadi) plant of about INR700 crore announced for LV/MV power cable; management said greenfield projects take about 2 years to build plus about 1 year to ramp.
Management expects Sanand to run at 70-75% utilisation next year; the INR100-200 crore balancing equipment will add INR1,000+ crore turnover.
demand_pricing: Order book INR4,292 crore: domestic cable INR2,400 crore, export INR822 crore, EHV INR793 crore, EPC INR271 crore.
Price pass-through is formula-based on copper content, not a fixed percentage; management confirmed cost inflation has been passed on.
Management attributes margin gains to product mix, export margin orders, retail mix and lower fixed cost as a share of sales, not to market share gains.
Management cited strong demand from data centres, power T&D, renewables, EV, railways, urban infrastructure, housing and thermal power construction.
Inventory build reflects Sanand ramp-up and about INR60-100 crore of finished goods reversed under Ind AS because export goods had not yet reached customers at quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex grow slowly and what drove the sharp wire and cable margin rise from 12.4% to 13.6% quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said fixed costs did not rise with incremental sales, and product mix and export margin orders helped. He said the company has crossed its earlier sub-11% operating margin hurdle and expects 11-12% going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing market share given industry volume growth near 33-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied losing share, citing strong demand and capacity constraints. It reiterated a 20%+ CAGR target and said it is not chasing 35-40% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sanand revenue guidance for FY27 and the capacity potential?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said FY27 Sanand revenue of INR1,500-2,000 crore, correcting a media figure of about INR3,000 crore. Management said the long-run potential is INR6,000 crore, rising to about INR7,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 20%+ guidance not raised given industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited capital allocation discipline, the need to fund capex for future capacity, and working capital limits. It said actual growth could exceed guidance but it would not give higher numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports fall and can they grow about 50% over the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said Middle East shipments were blocked and US orders stalled; shipments have resumed at high freight cost. He expects exports to grow to meet the 17-18% share target.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the house wire breakup dropped and what is the outlook for retail share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give product-wise sales because competitors use the data. It said retail is favoured for lower working capital needs, and the mix may shift with export orders.

544457|2026-06.headline: Brigade Hotel Ventures Q1 FY27 PAT rose 140% to INR17 crores on 9% RevPAR growth and lower finance cost, despite a ~INR14 crore West Asia-linked MICE cancellation hit.
544457|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 5% YoY to INR131 crores and EBITDA rose 9% to INR46 crores at a 34.8% margin, with GST 2.0 weighing 1.6 points on margin. PAT more than doubled to INR17 crores from INR7 crores, mainly because finance cost fell over 50% to INR8.7 crores after post-IPO debt repayment. Operationally, ARR rose 7% to INR7,241 and occupancy rose 2% to 75.7%, with management calling the RevPAR growth rate-led. F&B was the weak spot as large MICE events were cancelled or postponed across the city, and management expects a stronger Q2 and H2.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR18.9 crores in Q1 FY26 (over 50%)
no institutional debt after INR468.1 crores repaid from IPO proceeds

segments.name: Bangalore hotels
segments.commentary: ARR grew about 3% and occupancy rose 8%, giving RevPAR growth of about 10%; management is holding occupancy and will push ADR over the next three quarters.

segments.name: Sheraton Grand (F&B-heavy)
segments.commentary: Roughly 50-50 room and F&B revenue mix; it took the largest F&B hit from MICE cancellations, and its ADR was about INR500 lower YoY.

segments.name: Courtyard by Marriott Kochi Infopark (ex Four Points)
segments.commentary: ARR rose to INR4,650 from INR4,200, but occupancy fell sharply (71% in Q1 FY26) due to lost crew business and GDS changes during rebranding; management sees occupancy in the high 60s in Q2 and expects at least 10% ADR growth this year.

segments.name: ibis Styles
segments.commentary: Occupancy was about 40% in its first half-year of operations and is now in the 70s in its second year.

guidance_outlook: Management is trying to hold mid-teens like-to-like revenue growth for FY27, with the Q1 shortfall (about INR14 crores, roughly 10% of top line) expected to be recouped in H2.
July performance described as better and September as very buoyant; management expects Q2 to be much stronger than Q1.
Q4 FY27 expected to be strong on large-scale MICE events, which recur every alternate year (Aero Show year).
ADR target of above INR7,500 for the portfolio and each hotel, to offset GST impact; Q1 FY26 ADR was INR6,761.
Management says the 1,700 upcoming keys take the portfolio from 1,600 to 3,300 keys by FY30/FY31; luxury and upper-upscale mix to reach 31% by FY29 and 38% by FY31.
Internal accruals expected to contribute over INR1,000 crores over the coming years, with the rest from borrowing (about 60:40 mix).
Hotel acquisition from IPO proceeds under discussion, with a transaction targeted in FY27 subject to due diligence.
capex_capacity: Total development capex of about INR3,600 crores; about INR400 crores spent in FY26 and INR500 crores planned for FY27. Q1 FY27 spend was about INR53 crores (INR45 crores CWIP, INR3.5 crores renovation, INR4 crores for the new restaurant Project Grain), with about INR350 crores to be spent over the remaining three quarters.
Courtyard by Marriott Chennai at World Trade Center, 45 keys, launch planned for October / Q3 FY27.

Two Fairfield hotels under construction; Ritz-Carlton Vaikom well underway with designs finalised; JW Marriott Chennai excavation to start soon; InterContinental at Brigade Gateway dependent on the mixed-use township.
Grand Hyatt slightly delayed from FY28 because of pending approvals; Tumkur Road (Bangalore) project waiting for approvals.
JW Marriott Chennai under approval and Thiruvananthapuram still in planning; management expects both to open by 2030.
Renewable energy at 61% of total energy needs; several hotels above 90%.
demand_pricing: Management attributes Q1 weakness to West Asia conflict, which cut foreign travellers (FTAs) from about 40% to about 30% of room arrivals and raised fares and fuel costs.
Cancellations and postponements of large MICE events hit the whole city; the INR14 crore impact was about 60% F&B and 40% rooms. MICE is about 15-18% of room bookings.
Domestic corporate business, locally negotiated rates, staycations, and social events were used to backfill room revenue.
Management says RevPAR growth was rate-led rather than occupancy-led, though occupancy rose in Bangalore and in most hotels.
F&B is about 32% of overall top line.
WTC Chennai expected to open at a minimum starting ADR of INR9,000 with stabilised occupancy of about 80%, backed by captive demand from tenants.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex was spent in Q1 and how will the INR500 crore FY27 plan be phased?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR53 crores was spent in Q1; about INR350 crores is expected in the remaining three quarters, mainly H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the F&B and MICE trend improving for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites July pickup, very healthy September, and larger MICE inquiries, and expects the lost Q1 revenue to be partly recovered in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mid-teens growth target for FY27 hold given the slow start and high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management still aims for mid-teens like-to-like growth, citing the INR14 crore cancellation hit as the main gap; no revised number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is Bangalore strength driven by domestic demand or business recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic accounts, locally negotiated rates, and staycations replaced lost foreign travellers; management says the portfolio occupancy is about 76% with five of nine hotels above 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Are there delays on live projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly on track; the Grand Hyatt is slightly delayed pending approvals, and the Tumkur Road project awaits approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Should ADR be prioritised over occupancy in Bangalore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to hold occupancy and grow ADR; it aims for the portfolio and each hotel to cross INR7,500 ADR.

532493|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue was modest at INR182 crore, while a INR2,205 crore HAL Uttam Radar order lifted the total order book to about INR4,300 crore.
532493|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 as modest on revenue and profitability, blaming customer approval delays and last-stage technical issues that it expects to normalise in coming quarters. Q1 order inflow was INR185 crore, in line with guidance. The July receipt of the INR2,205 crore HAL Uttam Radar subsystem order (about INR1,870 crore ex-GST) roughly doubled the order book. Management reiterated FY27 revenue of about INR1,350 crore (guided as more than 15-20% growth) and flagged a planned demerger of the Space and Weather divisions from April 1, 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Described as modest; no YoY figure given in call

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone order book at quarter end
Consolidated order book at quarter end
financial_highlights.change: Includes about INR244 crore of service orders

financial_highlights.metric: Order book after July HAL Uttam Radar win (as stated)
financial_highlights.change: Uttam order roughly doubled the book

segments.name: Defence (Uttam Radar, HAL)
segments.commentary: Largest order in company history: about INR2,205 crore from HAL for critical subsystems for Uttam Radar, with a 5-year execution window. Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027, about 14 months from order date.

segments.name: Space, Metrology and Hydrology
segments.commentary: About 34% of the standalone order book. Management guided INR120-150 crore of FY27 revenue from space. Space and Weather is to be demerged as a separate listed entity, with first-year standalone revenue guided at INR300-plus crore and at least 18-20% PBT margin.

segments.name: Joint venture (Astra Rafael Comsys)
segments.commentary: Order book INR836 crore; FY27 booking target INR360 crore. Management expects INR500-750 crore of further ARC orders over the forecast period.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target about INR1,350 crore, plus or minus INR25 crore; growth stated as more than 15%, with 15-20% given in Q&A.
FY28 revenue about INR1,600 crore, plus or minus INR50 crore, with growth of 15-18%.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR1,600 crore, excluding the Uttam order; management said it may be improved over the next few quarters.
Over 5 years, management expects at least 6-7x FY26 revenue. It sees order intake of INR8,000-9,000 crore over 3-4 years, excluding chip sales, counter-UAV, EM wall, exports and BrahMos NG.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be similar to FY26, with a positive delta increase; no long-term margin guidance given.
Management said it expects the Q3 and Q4 working capital position to be broadly similar to FY26, and it has no plan to dilute equity for working capital.
capex_capacity: Uttam Radar: Phase 1 of 12 numbers due by September 2027; roughly 25+ numbers per year thereafter; management said total quantity could be executed by FY31.
Own satellite to be launched within the first 6 months after the Space and Weather entity lists; part of a planned satellite constellation.
Management said production lines and teams are fully ready for large-scale execution; investment in automated process engineering and infrastructure is ongoing.
Migration to SAP/HANA completed; standalone accounting for the space business has run from the start of the year.
Two complete radars of own IP and one drone-mounted electronic intelligence product are targeted for around Diwali 2026.
