demand_pricing: AMCA AAAU: company is L1 and BEL is L2 for the active antenna array unit development, with a contract expected in about a month. Management did not disclose the quantum; the AMCA radar DcPP RFP has 3 shortlisted consortium partners.

Tejas Mk1A EW: AATRU subsystem already qualified; the EW suite is in final qualification, after which production orders follow. Management expects about INR500-600 crore of additional orders from these programmes.
Su-30 upgrades (Virupaksha, Angad): Tier 1 radar and Tier 2 EW role; management expects about INR3,000 crore of orders over the forecast period.
QRSAM: expects INR700-800 crore of orders for the first 3 regiments; part of the existing INR4,300 crore book is expected before year-end.
Shatrughat and Samaghat (P-75I): management expects INR100-120 crore of production orders from BEL for the two programmes combined.
BrahMos: supplies gimbal-based RF seeker components and telemetry products; a new-generation (NG) seeker is in development. Upside from NG is not in the order inflow projections.
Exports: a couple of BTS orders executed and prototypes given for qualification; MMIC component leads from US and Europe, with sizable orders possibly taking about 2 more years.

qa_highlights.question: Which top-line growth target is correct: 10-15% (press release) or 15-20% (presentation)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the correct target is in excess of 15%, i.e. 15-20% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the year-end order book target?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding Uttam, management reiterated order booking of about INR1,600 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is EW (Tejas, Su-30) and LCH content in the order inflow projections?
qa_highlights.answer: Angad and some LCH subsystems are included in the 4-year projections. Tejas Mk1A is additional, around INR500-600 crore. Management said none of the EM wall or counter-UAV revenue is in its numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to positive cash at the end of FY26, which kept overdraft utilisation in Q1 minimal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uttam execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall execution is about 5 years, with total completion before FY32 and possibly by FY31; Phase 1 of 12 numbers is due by September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What margin guidance is available for new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to margins, citing product mix and lifecycle economics. It expects margins to be as healthy as the current business, or nearly so.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 6-7x five-year revenue target based on the defence business only?
qa_highlights.answer: The order visibility excludes space, apart from the existing book. Management said the 6-7x is against the combined FY26 base of INR1,057 crore, since the demerger has not yet happened.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue decline and was there deferred revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited inspection and specification-proof delays, development-cycle issues and supply-chain issues that pushed some programmes out of Q1. It expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger and said quarterly numbers are internal estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital moderate further in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant change versus FY26 is expected; Q1 and early Q2 are seasonally better and pressure rises in Q3 and Q4. Management ruled out equity dilution for working capital.

526247|2026-06.headline: Premier Explosives Q1 FY27 revenue fell 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore, EBIT margin 4.7%, order book INR1,393 crore (94% defence).
526247|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined 28% YoY to INR102.6 crore as dispatches and project execution slipped, mainly on export deliveries held up by maritime disruption and imported countermeasure components. EBIT fell 80% YoY to INR4.8 crore (4.7% margin) and PAT fell 80% to INR3 crore (3% margin), with raw material costs squeezing margins. Management said the export licence backlog is largely cleared and expects the delayed execution to complete in Q2 and Q3. Order book stands at INR1,393 crore, and FY27 revenue target is retained at about INR600 crore. Apollo Micro Systems' acquisition of promoter stake was discussed, with synergy details deferred to next quarter.

segments.name: Defence and Space
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 35% YoY per analyst question; management attributed delays to export licences and component imports, not customer acceptance. Defence is 94% of the order book.

segments.name: Industrial explosives / bulk
segments.commentary: About 6% of order book. Singareni execution of about INR25-30 crore remains for FY27; margins described as very thin, with some contracts negative. Coal India work withdrawn.

segments.name: Services (O&M)
segments.commentary: INR42 crore of order book (3%), no separate commentary on quarterly performance.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target retained at about INR600 crore (analyst-reported INR600-700 crore earlier); management said Q1 revenue of about INR103 crore leaves 9 months to deliver INR500-600 crore.
EBITDA margin target of 15-20% for the year, reiterated; management said the gap in Q1 would be made up in coming quarters.
FY27 order inflow expected at INR200-300 crore; management said run rate of INR1,000 crore-plus per year over the next two years.
Export execution targeted at INR150-200 crore in Q2 FY27, with prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear in the quarter.
Order of INR430 crore (Oct 2025) to be fully executed in FY27 per management, versus earlier guidance of about two-thirds; Q1 execution was about INR21 crore.
Other expenses run-rate of INR9-10 crore per quarter cited as sustainable.
Katepally RDX/HMX water trials expected in September 2026 (about one month); mixing plant dummy trials expected by end September after imported mixer components are airlifted.
capex_capacity: Katepally: RDX and HMX plant integration and erection almost complete; water trials expected September 2026, lasting about one month before production.
Katepally mixing plant: 2.5 tonne planetary mixer installed; imported components delayed by shipping, now being airlifted; dummy trials targeted end-September 2026.
Andhra Pradesh expansion: land pricing unresolved; company has asked the state government to revise price. Management said Apollo would continue the expansion, with a decision after presentation.
Flares produced in own plant; production has started on the July 2023 flares order, with backlog of about INR75 crore to complete in 4-5 months. Chaff payload depends on imports, now executed.
Drones: company builds payloads and partners with drone makers as a partner, not a standalone supplier.
demand_pricing: Export licences: several received in the past week, with some in pipeline; material moving out of factories. Export of INR150-200 crore targeted in Q2.

INR350 crore international defence order (April 2026): export licence still in process; management said licence processing takes at least 3-4 months after importing-country import licence; some dispatches expected in the last quarter of the year.
Bulk explosives: pricing tied to raw material costs; more than 40 players in the segment; management declined to predict FY28.
RDX/HMX: international demand good, but licences difficult; management said war-driven demand has lifted prices for now.
Alternate raw material for mines/loitering munitions under DRDO, ARDE and HEMRL testing; management expects about 6 more months.
Naval opportunity linked to Apollo association; potential to be clearer by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall from INR20 crore to INR11 crore, and is INR11 crore sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier quarters had expected credit loss provisions and forex losses that did not recur; a sustainable run rate of about INR9-10 crore per quarter was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin improve from the 35% level, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve as the product mix and dispatches improve; it reiterated the 15-20% EBITDA target and did not quantify a gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the roughly INR400 crore of export licences, and what export revenue is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Several licences received in the past week, with material moving; INR150-200 crore of export is targeted in Q2, and prior-quarter export backlogs expected to clear this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR430 crore October 2025 order on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 execution was about INR21 crore, the order will be fully executed in FY27 (not two-thirds), and capacity is available with chaff imports already executed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Defence revenue fall 35%, and was it procurement or acceptance delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to export licence and component import delays, and said customer procurement and acceptance were not a cause; completion expected in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook if raw material prices normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material prices are not normalising yet; contracts already signed must be executed first, then prices will be raised. The 15-20% EBITDA target is for this financial year.

risks_watch: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to about 6% (per analyst calculation) from about 15% in the prior year, with raw material cost and under-absorption cited; recovery to 15-20% depends on contracts and price pass-through.
FY27 revenue of INR600 crore needs INR500-600 crore in 9 months after INR103 crore in Q1; Chaff imports remain dependent on conditions abroad.
Export licence timing (3-4 months processing plus importing-country licence) could delay the INR350 crore April 2026 order.
Katepally commissioning relies on water trials in September and imported mixer parts; any slippage pushes production later.
Andhra Pradesh expansion land pricing unresolved; Apollo's stance on expansion not yet confirmed.
Pending LD (liquidated damages) reversal of about INR30 crore on the July 2023 flares order, expected by October-November 2026.
Unclear Apollo synergy details; management said more to come next quarter.

544425|2026-06.headline: AJC Jewel Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 124.69% YoY to Rs 101.38 crore; EBITDA margin 4.58% and PAT margin 2.35%.
544425|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached Rs 101.38 crore versus Rs 45.12 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of Rs 4.64 crore (from Rs 1.58 crore) and PAT of Rs 2.38 crore (from Rs 0.57 crore). Margins expanded, with EBITDA margin at 4.58% (from 3.5%) and PAT margin at 2.35% (from 1.26%). Management announced a proposed 80% stake acquisition in AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC, Sharjah, via a non-cash share swap valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore, though the Sharjah entity is not consolidated in Q1. Management guided FY27 standalone India revenue of Rs 450 crore and 50% CAGR for three years, on a volume basis. Many answers on utilisation, Esthara economics and FY28 targets were deferred to H1 results.

segments.name: India gold jewellery (core B2B, casting)
segments.commentary: Capacity 5 kg/day; utilisation about 25% (about 1.2 kg/day). Kerala accounts for 90-95% of revenue. Top 10 customers are about 50% of revenue; about 200 other customers make up the rest.

segments.name: Sharjah UAE (AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC)
segments.commentary: Gold jewellery capacity 3 kg/day at about 800 g/day (about 27% utilisation). Management cited PAT margin of about 4% and EBITDA margin of about 5%, in a tax-exempt free zone. Not consolidated in Q1; expected consolidation from Q3.

segments.name: Esthara Jewels (silver DTC)
segments.commentary: Three stores operational in Kerala; two more under fit-out, expected to open by end of next month. Silver capacity 8 kg/day with about 1 kg/day production. Management targets about Rs 20 lakh revenue per store per month; first store reportedly about Rs 15 lakh per month. Capex about Rs 4,000 per sq ft; opex about Rs 5-6 lakh per store; breakeven targeted within one year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone India revenue target of Rs 450 crore (management reiterated it is standalone India only; Sharjah additional).
Revenue growth of about 50% CAGR for the next three years, stated as based on volume growth; management said price effects would be added only if gold prices rise.
Current PAT margin of about 2.5% cited for the year.
Sharjah full-year contribution to be updated after H1 results; acquisition completion expected in 3-6 months subject to BSE and regulatory approvals.
Dilution to existing shareholders from the share swap estimated at about 7-8%, per management (uncertain).
Store count and three-year store plans to be updated post H1 results.
Q1 and Q2 seasonally moderate; Q3 and Q4 stronger on festivals and weddings.
capex_capacity: India: 5 kg/day gold casting capacity, upgraded from IPO proceeds to 120% expansion (cited as 5 kg Kerala, 8 kg silver), with about 25% utilisation today.
Silver jewellery production started in India; capacity up to 8 kg/day, currently about 1 kg/day.
Sharjah: 3 kg/day installed gold capacity at about 800 g/day.
At 100% utilisation management cited India about Rs 7 crore/day (about Rs 2,500 crore/yr at 5 kg/day) and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day; these are indicative and not guidance.
Additional working capital needed to reach peak utilisation; to be funded via internal accruals, debt and possibly equity, gradually.
Design and innovation centre set up; about 20 in-house design staff; library of about 2.5 lakh designs on B2B portal.
demand_pricing: Added 12 independent jewellers in Q1, mainly mid and small Kerala retailers; no new corporate clients after Kalyan.
Management is targeting expansion beyond Kerala, with a marketing team in Chennai; international orders to be served via Sharjah.
Management said gold price moves will not affect margins because it hedges with suppliers and on MCX.
Launched 9-karat and 18-karat products; 18-karat is served to some customers for higher margin at lower caratage. Early response described as encouraging.
Management said no gold metal loan or advance gold loan business; no bullion trading in consolidated revenue.
Receivables growth well ahead of sales (3-year receivables CAGR about 51% vs sales 16%), attributed to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total value and rationale of the Sharjah acquisition, and what margins does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: 80% stake via share swap, valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore; Sharjah earns about 4% PAT and about 5% EBITDA, aided by free-zone tax exemption. Completion expected in 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 50% growth guidance based on, volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume only; price changes would be added only if gold prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation for FY27/FY28 and revenue at 100% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No utilisation guidance given. Indicative values at 100%: India about Rs 7 crore/day and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day. FY27 India target is Rs 450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables growth far ahead of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods, and said it will try to reduce debtors.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow from operations has been negative for six years; when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to make it positive in coming years, without a specific timeline; focus is on sales volume and growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a demand impact from the duty change talk and what is the Q2/Q3 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty changes have not affected the business historically; Q1 and Q2 are moderate, Q3 and Q4 stronger. No specific Q3 numbers given.

540212|2026-06.headline: TCI Express Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR 312 crore, with PAT up 6% to INR 22.4 crore and volumes up 7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes.
540212|2026-06.overview: Income from operations grew about 9% YoY to INR 312 crore and EBITDA rose 11% to INR 37 crore, with margin at 11.7% versus 11.5%. PAT rose 6% to INR 22.4 crore (7.1% margin). Management said the fuel price hike taken in mid-May was only partly reflected in Q1 (June only), so benefits should show from Q2. The company stated it is debt-free with net cash of about INR 118 crore.

financial_highlights.change: up ~6% YoY from INR 21 crore; margin 7.1%

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; grew 9% YoY on existing customers, new accounts and industrial growth. Management targets accelerating to double-digit growth.

segments.name: Domestic Air Express
segments.commentary: Grew 29% YoY per opening remarks (CEO-level figure); later cited ~28% on enterprise account wins and airline partnerships.

segments.name: International Express
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY on new customers, win-backs and expanded global carrier partnerships.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: Grew 63% YoY, the fastest-growing vertical, but only ~2-2.5% of revenue; target small-merchant, D2C and e-commerce B2B segments at 16-18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Rail Express / C2C Express
segments.commentary: Rail added operational branches; C2C added clients, regional branch coverage and a larger dedicated vehicle fleet. No growth figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 11-12%, with net price realisation of about 3%, implying 13-15% overall revenue growth.
FY27 PAT growth guided at 20-25%.
EBITDA margin expansion of 100-150 bps targeted for FY27; margin benefit from fuel pass-through expected from Q2.
Multimodal share of revenue targeted at 17-18% to 19% in FY27 and 22-25% by 2030.
FY27 capex guided at INR 125-140 crore; management said it expects to cross INR 125 crore, with about INR 20 crore spent so far.
Kolkata hub automation expected by March 2027 or June 2027 at latest; Ahmedabad around mid-2027, taking automated hubs to four by 2027.
capex_capacity: Two hubs automated so far: Tajnagar (North India) and Chakan (Pune); Kolkata and Ahmedabad under construction.
Ongoing construction at four sites: Ahmedabad, Kolkata, corporate office and Lucknow.
Management said it is close to finalising a land purchase in one of Mumbai, Chennai or Bangalore.
Regional branch expansion ongoing across Surface, Air, Rail and C2C; e-commerce regional branches being opened and bikers hired for sub-5 kg deliveries.
demand_pricing: Volume grew ~7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes, but management said price hikes were held back until fuel increased in mid-May; diesel and annual hikes together gave a 'handsome' increase, with ~90%+ of customers passed through in June.
Analyst noted peers are taking 3-5% price hikes; management did not give a specific Q1 price-hike percentage.
SME to B2B mix returned to 50:50 in Q1 from 48:52 in FY26.
Management cited pipeline visibility, manufacturing demand and SME recovery; growth expected from both existing customers and new industries.
Analyst raised competitive pricing in certain segments and elevated operating costs industry-wide; management said its service quality and tech investment keep it ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q1 volumes and price hikes versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was 2.5 lakh tonnes, up ~7.5%. Management said fuel-linked pass-through came in mid-May, with the full price increase reflected mainly in June; the company deferred hikes ahead of expected fuel increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategic rationale for expanding e-commerce given lower margins historically?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is ~2-2.5% of revenue. Management said D2C margins are 16-18% and it is targeting small merchants, D2C and e-commerce B2B, with regional teams and branches to support Surface.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to drive consistent double-digit EBITDA growth and volume acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it strengthened vertical-wise regional teams and built regional structures across Air, International, Rail and C2C. Air grew ~28% on new customers, and a clear pipeline supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the volume, pricing and PAT targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 11-12%, net price hikes of about 3%, total growth of 13-15%, and PAT growth of 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of hub automation and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Two hubs are automated (Tajnagar, Chakan); Kolkata is expected by March or June 2027 and Ahmedabad around mid-2027. FY27 capex is INR 125-140 crore, with about INR 20 crore spent so far.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins improve in Q2 as fuel pass-through takes full effect, and what is the multimodal share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fuel increase was passed on to 90%+ of customers in June, so margins should improve from Q2. Multimodal share is about 17-18% now, targeted at 17-19% this year and 22-25% by 2030.

risks_watch: Realisation: management said price hikes were deferred and partly reflected only in June, so Q2 pricing and margin uplift need to be verified.
Net price hike guidance of ~3% is below the 3-5% peers were said to be taking; the analyst questioned this.
E-commerce last-mile economics: management cited 16-18% EBITDA margin, but the analyst questioned profitability in last-mile delivery.
Capex of INR 125-140 crore against INR 20 crore spent so far; land purchase timing is uncertain.
Management's 11-12% volume and 20-25% PAT growth guidance is ambitious against 7.5% volume growth and 6% PAT growth in Q1.
Domestic Air growth figure inconsistency: 29% in prepared remarks versus ~28% in Q&A.
540212|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, pipeline and margin recovery, but vague on specifics such as the Q1 price-hike percentage and the e-commerce economics. Answers were often loosely structured and repetitive.

532859|2026-06.headline: HGS Q1 FY27 revenue flat at Rs 1,050.4 crore (-0.6% YoY) while EBITDA margin fell to 9.7% from 15.7% QoQ, with a PAT loss of Rs 66.3 crore.
532859|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 1,050.4 crore, down 3.2% QoQ and 0.6% YoY, as a large client engagement is being phased out. EBITDA fell to Rs 116.3 crore (9.7% margin) from 15.7% in Q4, which management attributed to one-time phase-out costs, ramp and training costs on new wins, and front-loaded investment in sales, domain hiring and AI (Agent X). Net loss was Rs 66.3 crore against a Rs 13.6 crore loss in the previous quarter. Management said the new business carries more technology content and outcome-linked pricing, with margin benefits expected ahead of revenue growth in later quarters.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs +14.1 crore QoQ; Rs -26.5 crore YoY
vs Rs -13.6 crore QoQ; Rs +11.2 crore YoY (prior year incl. Rs 57.5 crore discontinued ops)
vs Rs 48.1 crore QoQ; Rs 57.9 crore YoY
vs Rs 5,346 crore at March 2026; borrowings Rs 1,279 crore

segments.name: CX services
segments.commentary: 54% of Q1 operating revenue. Vertical mix shows Tech, Media and Telecom at 46% of total revenue, with CG and Retail 19%, BFSI 17%, Public Sector 12%, Health and Life Sciences 3%, others 4%.

segments.name: Digital and Media services
segments.commentary: 46% of Q1 operating revenue. Broadband (ONEOTT/CelerityX) growing; high-speed (above 100 Mbps) share of subscribers rose to 15% from 11% a year ago. Digital television (linear TV) faces structural headwinds, mitigated via broadband bundling, IPTV and cost optimisation.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth and margins to pick up before the end of FY27, as the planned ramp-downs conclude within the current fiscal year.
Management views the Q1 margin hit as one-time investment absorption, not a structural change in earning power, and expects operating leverage to return as volume normalises.
Management expects AI and platform services to be medium-term margin accretive rather than dilutive.
Management is cautiously optimistic; macro uncertainty and client prudence may persist near term, with gradual improvement in growth and margins expected through the year.
Project Ganga is expected to enter operational mode in Q2 FY27; management said reporting will be in a different position at end of Q2.
Management expects the largest growth driver in FY27 to be AI and digital, with existing clients as the main source of growth.
capex_capacity: Project Ganga (launched 9 June 2026 in Uttar Pradesh) targets enabling 8,000 to 10,000 Nyaya Panchayat entrepreneurs as digital service providers, 50% women, and connecting over 2 million households over 2 to 3 years; about 2,000 applications and about 500 applicants trained as of 4 August 2026.

Project Ganga is funded primarily through internal accruals; management said it is run on a no-profit, no-loss basis for the network rollout, with ISP pricing in line with competition in Uttar Pradesh.
New subsidiary HGS MENA IT Consulting LLC incorporated in Dubai to build technology and consulting capabilities in the MENA region.
Investments in domain hiring, fractional advisors, solutions build-out, Agent X and the 90-day proof-of-value model were front-loaded in Q1.
demand_pricing: Added 19 new logos across CX and digital services and 8 clients in HRO and payroll processing in Q1; approximately 78 to 79 new logos were added in FY26.
New engagements start at about $150,000 to $300,000 in annual work and take 6 to 8 months to reach meaningful scale; initial 3 months carry training and ramp-up costs.
New AI-linked deals are smaller in revenue size but carry higher margins; AI share of work in new deals is expected to scale from 20-30% to 60-70%.
Pricing is shifting toward outcome-linked and non-headcount commercial structures; clients are moving from AI pilots to production but many are not yet ready on data and governance.
Broadband: customers choosing higher base plans; 10-30 Mbps entry plan share fell to 18% from 22%; 31-100 Mbps stable at about 67%.
Lost contracts were largely labour-priced; new contracts carry technology content and offshore-weighted delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Ankit Jain asked what margins HGS expects on Project Ganga, and whether it is subsidised.
qa_highlights.answer: Vynsley Fernandes said HGS acts as enabler and knowledge partner; pricing is in line with Uttar Pradesh competition, the no-profit-no-loss framing relates to supporting network rollout, and it is not a negative cash flow play.

qa_highlights.question: Aniruddha Sharma asked how quickly the new logos will contribute to revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Venkatesh Korla said benefits typically take 6 to 8 months, with margin pressure in the first months; he expects growth and margin-attractive revenue before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Aniruddha Sharma asked what limits faster revenue growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combination of ramp-up time and planned ramp-downs of legacy contracts, which should conclude before FY27 ends; new deals are smaller in revenue size but higher margin.

qa_highlights.question: Prisha Shah asked whether clients are moving from Agentic AI pilots to production.
qa_highlights.answer: Korla said demand for production deployments is strong but many customers lack data and governance readiness; he expects deployments to grow larger through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Prisha Shah asked where HGS has a sustainable AI edge as foundation models commoditise.
qa_highlights.answer: Korla said the edge lies in applying models to industry-specific process re-engineering, which benefits HGS as model costs fall.

qa_highlights.question: Prisha Shah asked how to measure Agent X success over 12 to 18 months.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will track number of customers and contracts with AI embedded and may look at measuring the share of revenue influenced by AI.

qa_highlights.question: Aniruddha Sharma asked whether the intelligent experiences positioning is producing larger, multi-towered deals.
qa_highlights.answer: Korla said every recent new deal has AI components and that deals are becoming multi-towered, which he expects to lift revenue and margins over time.

540749|2026-06.headline: MAS Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated AUM up 21% to INR16,100 crores and PAT up 27% to INR110 crores; credit cost guided 1.25%-1.75%.
540749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated AUM grew about 21% YoY to INR16,100 crores and PAT rose about 27% to INR110 crores, with standalone PAT up 25% to INR105 crores. Asset quality was stable, with standalone GNPA at 2.58% and NNPA at 1.70%, flat QoQ, and a management overlay of INR17.60 crores held. Borrowing cost fell 55 bps YoY to 9.25%, while credit cost rose to about 1.6% of AUM, which management attributed to higher on-book mix, a 5 bps rise in Stage 1/2 provisioning and prudent write-offs. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth guidance, with the call leaning toward the upper end for FY27.

segments.name: MEL (Micro/MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Book grew 23% from INR5,009 crores to INR6,153 crores; MEL is about 77% of loan book combined with SME.

segments.name: SME loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR4,526 crores to INR5,485 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: Grew 19% from INR872 crores to INR1,039 crores; management said Q1 is seasonally muted, with festive Q3/Q4 stronger.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle (used CV)
segments.commentary: Grew 13% from INR967 crores to INR1,096 crores; eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening, with growth push deferred 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Salaried personal loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR1,131 crores to INR1,374 crores; about 9% of the loan book.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM INR976 crores, GS3 0.98% and NS3 0.68%; PBT up 62% to INR5.70 crores; average yield about 14%, credit cost about 0.5%. Expansion into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka starts this quarter.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance maintained at 20-25%, with management saying the full year is very likely to be at the higher end of the range.
Credit cost to stay in a 1.25%-1.75% range, depending on product mix; management pointed to commercial vehicles as high-yield, high-loss.
ROA target of 2.75%-3.25%, with an aspiration of 3%+.
Net interest margin target of 8%-8.5% on a 7%-7.5% spread; incremental borrowing cost 9.2%-9.25%, expected to stay stable (9.2%-9.3% per Q&A).
Direct distribution share (currently 66%-67%) expected to reach 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years; off-book target kept at 20-25% of AUM.
Used CV growth expected to pick up only after 1-2 quarters; housing finance AUM expected to inch up in the next few quarters.
Credit rating upgrade being pursued, timing not given; sub-9% borrowing cost called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Distribution of 16,500 centres through 209 branches, with more than 200 NBFC partners providing about 33% of originations; direct share 67%.
Employee count reduced by 380 in Q1 due to technology adoption; no quantified headcount target given.
In-house tech team of close to 100 people; LOS live for all products, with BRE added and straight-through processing improving.
Branches opened after March 2024 expected to mature (sweat) by 2027-28 or earlier.
demand_pricing: Standalone MSME/SME demand stable across manufacturing and trading; eligible demand fell in Q1 due to tighter credit screens on energy-dependent sectors (restaurants, gas-dependent manufacturing, export businesses).
Used CV demand robust, but eligible demand lower because of fuel-cost tightening.
Two-wheeler Q1 degrowth QoQ attributed to seasonality; monsoon and Gujarat floods flagged as temporary and not expected to cause major stress.
Working capital demand rising for some businesses on higher input costs; underwriting parameters also tightened.
Write-offs were INR29 crores in March and INR19 crores in June, offset by higher ECL provisioning, keeping impairment cost flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise from about 1.2-1.3% to about 1.6% of AUM despite the microfinance impact and Q4 write-offs last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher on-book assets (on-book up 8.25% QoQ vs AUM up 5.5%), which added INR6-7 crores of Stage 1/2 provisioning from a 5 bps rise to 0.7%. Prudent write-offs and mix shift toward higher-yield commercial vehicles also contributed; ROA not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth guidance at risk given the West Asia conflict and energy-linked stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said energy-dependent segments were tightened early and stress was limited; eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 but normalised, and guidance is expected to hold with the upper end targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Will borrowing cost fall further from 9.25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict and depends on RBI and liquidity; the target is to stabilise at 9.2%-9.3%, with a credit rating upgrade being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the Stage 1/2 provisioning increase and whether there are macro-related buffers?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 1/2 provisioning rose to 0.7% from 0.65%, adding INR6-7 crores; management described it as a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR10 crore OCPS redemption in the subsidiary MRHMFL?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCPS was refunded to the parent because the housing subsidiary's CRAR exceeded 37% and it did not need the capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why did off-book share fall and what is the housing finance growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-book is dynamic and chosen by price; target stays at 20-25%. Housing finance plans to expand into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka from Q1, with results expected in Q3-Q4.

544410|2026-06.headline: Prostarm Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR 76 crore, PAT up 156% to INR 5 crore, with a 25% minimum FY27 growth target reiterated.
544410|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 76 crore, up 38% YoY but down 27% QoQ from INR 104 crore in Q4, which management attributed to seasonality and deferred execution. EBITDA was INR 7 crore at an 8.55% margin (up 126 bps YoY) and PAT was INR 5 crore at a 6.05% margin. Management said the 12-13% margin guidance still holds on a full-year basis, while also guiding FY27 PAT margin to 8.5-9%. Order book stood at about INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1, and working capital days fell from 185 to 168.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY; -27% QoQ vs INR 104 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: approx INR 1,085 crore plus INR 5 crore L1 (about INR 1,090 crore total)

financial_highlights.change: from INR -49 crore in Q4 FY26
from about INR 254 crore as of March 2026

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage) developer projects
segments.commentary: Order book includes about INR 855-857 crore of developer business (Bihar and Karnataka/KPTCL). Management said no revenue recognition from these in FY27, only EPC billing on the standalone books; Karnataka dispute was resolved in KPTCL's favour and the company is targeting a sale of that project.

segments.name: Solar EPC and EPC orders
segments.commentary: Solar EPC order of about INR 165 crore from Solarium Green Energy, which management expects to execute fully in FY27. Adani EPC billing was largely completed in Q1 (INR 36 crore of deferred work executed); a further solar EPC order of about INR 12 crore (8.36 MWh) was won.

segments.name: Utility vs C&I BESS
segments.commentary: Company has stopped bidding for utility-scale BESS for about 10 months and is shifting to C&I BESS (200-500 kWh installations), where management says margins are better. Adani project gave about 26% gross margin in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target: minimum 25%.
Margin guidance of 12-13% EBITDA is maintained on a full-year basis, with H2 expected to be stronger; Q1 margin is affected by low turnover and high fixed-cost ratio.
FY27 PAT margin expected at about 8.5-9%, not 10%, due to higher costs from new plants, import costs and hiring.
Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant and Gujarat UPS plant both expected operational in Q2 FY27; SAP and Salesforce expected operational by end of H1 FY27.
Working capital days targeted at about 120-150 by March 2027; management aims for positive operating cash flow by year-end FY27.
Jhajjar BESS utilisation: not more than 20-25% in FY27, 40-50% in FY28 (around INR 500 crore revenue targeted in FY28); steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%.
capex_capacity: Jhajjar, Haryana: 1.2 GWh BESS manufacturing facility in final stage of commissioning; earlier delayed, management cited cost and logistics movements and a strategy shift to C&I. Commercial operation now expected by end of H1 FY27.
Gujarat: new UPS manufacturing facility progressing as planned, expected to start commercial operations in Q2 FY27.
Existing manufacturing in Pune and Navi Mumbai.

Bihar BESS (developer/rental model): yearly cash flow of about INR 16 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of INR 32.40 crore; SBI facility tied up in SPV, LC-backed by Bihar DISCOM, no corporate guarantee.
Karnataka BESS (KPTCL): annual cash flow of about INR 45.72 crore over 12 years plus capital subsidy of about INR 81 crore; management prioritising a sale post-COD.
demand_pricing: Order book approx INR 1,090 crore including L1. Excluding developer orders (about INR 855 crore), in-hand orders are about INR 236 crore, plus dealer business of about INR 10 crore per month, giving about INR 306-307 crore additional order in hand.
Bids under evaluation of about INR 2,000+ crore, including two large orders of about INR 1,800 crore.
Utility BESS margins under pressure: management said bidders quoted below cost assuming Chinese supply negotiations; cited China export restrictions and a 2% battery tax from 1 September.
Q1 FY27 order wins included an INR 11 crore BESS project from a corporate customer and a INR 165 crore solar EPC order.

Trade receivables: about INR 46 crore realised from the CCTNS (Pune) project in Q1, with a large further amount expected by end-August; management said most of the INR 231 crore is government-funded with no realisation risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the deferred Q4 orders (Adani INR 43 crore, SAIL INR 7 crore, South Eastern Railway INR 13 crore) was executed in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 36 crore has been executed. Adani is almost fully billed; SAIL and South Eastern Railway are to be billed mainly in Q2, with some South Eastern Railway work spilling into Q3 pending site clearance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 revenue fall 27% QoQ, and is the margin guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally low and that the Adani billing was the major Q4 item. It said the 12-13% margin is a full-year target, with H2 stronger, and that Q1 fixed-cost absorption is weak at INR 76 crore turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital days targets and cash flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days fell to 168 from 185; target about 120-150 by March 2027. Operating cash flow improved to about INR -16 crore from INR -49 crore, with a goal of turning positive by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin should be expected from the Jhajjar plant, and what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 utilisation not above 20-25%; FY28 40-50% with around INR 500 crore revenue targeted. Steady-state EBITDA margin 14-15%, with C&I focus preferred over utility BESS.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further equity dilution or significant borrowing over the next 1.5-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity dilution is planned for at least the next year; the Bihar debt sits in an SPV, and the INR 43 crore warrant issue is for working capital. Any future dilution would be tied to a major expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables position and realisation timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables fell from INR 254 crore (March) to INR 231 crore (June) and dropped further by mid-August. Management expects about half to be collected by end-Q2, with most of the Solarium EPC realised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on order inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited INR 1,090 crore order book and bids of INR 2,000+ crore under evaluation, and expects the non-developer order book to grow over the next year as qualifications and bid participation increase.

509079|2026-06.headline: Gufic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR260.8 crore and PAT rose 86% to INR22.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18.09%.
509079|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR260.8 crore versus INR226.9 crore a year earlier and INR252.1 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (18.09% margin) from INR33.2 crore (14.6%), and PAT reached INR22.46 crore (8.61% margin) versus INR12.1 crore. Management said Indore is running to plan, with capacity utilisation expected to reach 40-45% by year-end and the GLP-1 CMO ramp expected to build from Q2 and more in Q3. Management reiterated 15-20% annual growth as a minimum commitment, with EU and US certifications for Indore still pending.

financial_highlights.change: +15% YoY vs INR226.9 crore; +3% QoQ vs INR252.1 crore
+42% YoY vs INR33.2 crore; +6% QoQ vs INR44.7 crore
+349 bps YoY vs 14.6%; +35 bps QoQ vs 17.74%
+85% YoY vs INR16.3 crore; +9% QoQ vs INR27.6 crore
+86% YoY vs INR12.1 crore; +9% QoQ vs INR20.6 crore

segments.name: Critical Care
segments.commentary: Launched monobactam and beta-lactamase inhibitor combination on innovator patent expiry; Sparsh completed a full quarter on the rebuilt channel with outstanding days within trade terms. Focus is on own-manufactured brands and depth within existing hospital groups.

segments.name: Women's health / IVF (Puregraf, Ferticare, Zenova)
segments.commentary: Ferticare retains leadership in recurrent implantation failure; Puregraf entered major corporate IVF chains. Zenova is shifting from injectables to prescription chronic therapies, with two first-mover launches (osteoarthritis, metabolic ovarian) due ahead.

segments.name: Aesthetics (botulinum toxin and fillers)
segments.commentary: Claims to be number 2 in toxin type A in India, made from its own strain. Filler partnership with Revanesse (Prollenium, Canada) expected to launch in India around December-January, subject to registration in Q2 or mid-Q3.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Shifted to a model that earns fee income alongside supply revenue. Licensing progressed in Europe, a contract manufacturing and licensing arrangement was signed with a North American partner, and first CMO orders were received in Australia. Approvals were secured in 8 countries in the quarter.

segments.name: GLP-1 (semaglutide, via Hetero)
segments.commentary: Operates purely as a CMO for Hetero, which received permission in May 2026; Q1 revenue contribution was residual. A 10-15 day plant shutdown in Q1 was for a new machine. Management expects traction from Q2 and the main contribution in Q3, with 70% of capacity targeted for international use.

guidance_outlook: Management commits to 15-20% year-on-year company growth as a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond that.
Indore capacity utilisation expected to rise from about 30-35% now to around 40-45% by year-end, with the Indore liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within three years.
Margin expansion from Indore expected once EU certification is in place. Management says the 18% operating margin is the start of an improvement trend, not a new normal.
Management expects operating leverage to start around mid-FY28.

Indore revenue potential is INR800-1,200 crore from current capex (about INR300 crore), so combined with Navsari the maximum is about INR1,600-2,000 crore; management also cited INR1,600-1,800 crore with no further capex.
Botulinum toxin and biostimulator in-licensed products are to launch this financial year with no significant capex. Stunnox and Zarbot registrations in SE Asia and Africa take 12-18 months.
capex_capacity: Indore has about 6 lyophilisers (4 at 100,000-vial capacity and 2 at 44,000-vial capacity). Depot and liposomal lines are in installation and qualification, with both targeted to be operational this year.
Indore has four lines: two lyophilisation lines, one suspension/liquid vial line, and one ampoule line. Target mix is roughly 20% liquid, 50-60% lyophilisation, and 20-30% complex injectables.
Indore is fully operational as a unit; new product lines are being added within the existing capex of about INR300 crore, with no major new infrastructure.
Indore utilisation has risen from 18-22% last year, to 20-25%, to close to 30-35% this year.
Navsari is largely capped at about INR800 crore revenue, with toxin and penem blocks not yet saturated.
Toxin plant is WHO Phase 1 with limited capacity; global registrations are deferred until after next year pending cash flow.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per vial is about INR80-100 on current product mix (pantoprazole 10 ml vial at about INR60-80). Management aims to move to INR300-400 and eventually an average of INR500 per vial with depot, liposomal and complex injectables.
Fillers market in India is estimated at about INR200 crore. Management aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

International: aims to raise margins from 40-50% under distributor models to 15-20% higher with its own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia. Recruitment of a regional team happened in Q1.
CHAI partnership for liposomal amphotericin B gives access to more than 100 markets; bioequivalence study due by August-September, followed by WHO PQ filing.

Employee additions are mainly at Indore (around 50-60 for domestic expansion), with international headcount capped at 20-25. Management says the previous-year contract-to-payroll conversion was one-time.

532522|2026-06.headline: Petronet Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 33% to INR 1,133 crore despite company LNG volumes falling to 207 TBTU, aided by trading and inventory gains.
532522|2026-06.overview: Standalone PBT rose 33% YoY to INR 1,514 crore and PAT to INR 1,133 crore, with consolidated PBT of INR 1,491 crore described as the highest ever Q1. Volumes fell: company LNG processed was 207 TBTU versus 220 TBTU a year earlier, and company utilisation was 58% versus 76%. Management attributed the profit resilience to trading gains of INR 301 crore and inventory gains of INR 193 crore, as Qatar supplies remained under force majeure and tolling cargoes from other sources replaced most of the gap. Dahej's nameplate capacity was raised from 17.5 to 22.5 MMTPA on 31 March 2026, which lowers reported utilisation.

segments.name: Dahej terminal
segments.commentary: Processed 192 TBTU in Q1 FY27 versus 207 TBTU a year ago and 201 TBTU in Q4; utilisation 66% on 22.5 MMTPA expanded capacity (65.6% per call) versus 92% a year ago.

segments.name: Kochi terminal
segments.commentary: Utilisation 23.27% in Q1 FY27 as stated on the call; pipeline connectivity expected to be mechanically complete by end of the quarter.

segments.name: Company overall
segments.commentary: Processed 207 TBTU (vs 220 TBTU YoY, 219 TBTU QoQ); utilisation 58% vs 76% in both prior periods.

guidance_outlook: Capex budgeted at INR 9,064 crore for FY27, with similar levels expected for FY28.
Utilisation expected to improve slightly: April was low, May and June ran at the rate that continues into the quarter, and recovery depends on reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Contract talks with offtakers on tariffs or renewal expected to close in the next 2 to 3 quarters; no tariff revision discussion currently.
New Qatar contract to start in 2028; it will be on DES basis, with a formula-driven price that includes shipping.
Petchem project is on schedule, about 40% complete on physical progress; propane contract signing expected in 2027.
capex_capacity: Dahej nameplate capacity increased from 17.5 MMTPA to 22.5 MMTPA on 31 March 2026; Dahej utilisation 66% on the expanded base.
Kochi utilisation 23.27% in Q1; Kochi pipeline connectivity expected to be mechanically complete by end of Q1 FY27 (end-June quarter per management).
Petchem project about 40% complete physically; capex INR 472 crore in the quarter, cumulative INR 679 crore.
FY27 capex budget INR 9,064 crore; FY28 expected at a similar level.
Petchem: 600 KTPA ethane handling contract and a Deepak Phenolics contract signed; equity IRR not disclosed for now as commercial contracts are still being finalised.
demand_pricing: Term volumes fell sharply; third-party regas and tolling volumes filled the gap, and management said more than two-thirds of the missing Middle East volume is being replaced by these customers.
Qatar force majeure is declared month by month, and was declared for end-August at the time of the call; offtakers are booking volumes on a month-to-month basis.
Spot trading was small (about 6 TBTU in the quarter per management), yet produced material trading gains when spot prices were well above long-term prices.
Deepak Fertilizers contract (about 0.5 MTPA expected at Dahej) began May 2026 with 2 cargoes brought so far; ExxonMobil volume increase at Kochi also started.
Tariffs at Dahej around INR 69 and at Kochi around INR 98 for the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Has the term-versus-third-party volume mix persisted into Q2, and should it hold until the Gulf conflict resolves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pattern continued into Q2 so far; it hopes Qatar volumes resume soon.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the margin improvement come from; is there an inventory gain and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Trading gains INR 301 crore and inventory gains INR 193 crore; management described trading gains during spot-price spikes as the established business model over the past 5-6 years, without committing to a Q2 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation by terminal and the FY27/FY28 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej 65.6%, Kochi 23.27%; recovery depends on Hormuz reopening, and May-June run-rate is slightly better than April.

qa_highlights.question: Use-or-pay treatment of tolling cargoes?
qa_highlights.answer: Tolling cargoes from non-GAIL offtakers can offset use-or-pay after current-year commitments are met; GAIL has no use-or-pay, and the long-term take-or-pay contract is separate.

qa_highlights.question: Ind AS impacts for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin impact positive INR 14 crore, forex loss INR 5 crore, other expenses positive INR 8 crore, depreciation INR 66 crore, finance cost INR 48 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are time-charter vessel costs being paid during force majeure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said time-charter vessel operations have been suspended under clauses other than force majeure, so charter costs are not being paid.

risks_watch: Strait of Hormuz closure and Qatar supply: no timing given; FM declared month-to-month.
Dependence on spot-price spreads for trading and inventory gains, which management did not say would persist into Q2.
Utilisation at Dahej (66%) and company level (58%) against the enlarged capacity base.
Tariff renewal with offtakers, expected in 2 to 3 quarters.
Petchem project economics: IRR not disclosed; commercial contracts still pending.
Ongoing time-charter cost treatment and the contracted vessel fleet after DES shift.
532522|2026-06.management_tone: ["Confident on earnings resilience and the trading business model, with the Q1 PAT and PBT growth framed as a strong start.","Cautious and non-committal on volumes: Hormuz timing is unknown, and management repeatedly said recovery depends on geopolitics. Evasive on petchem IRR and the Q2 margin outlook."]
key_quotes: Overall, I would say it has been a strong start to the year, while volumes were somewhat lower, we have delivered a healthy financial performance supported by commercial and operational efficiencies.
Inventory gains are at INR193 crores and trading gains are at INR301 crores.

financial_highlights.value: INR 472 crore (about INR 470 crore stated in same answer)
financial_highlights.change: Cumulative petchem capex to date INR 679 crore per management

539221|2026-06.headline: Sportking Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin reached about 18.8% on yarn spreads of INR133/kg versus INR107 last quarter, with management guiding 18-20% margins to be hard to sustain.
539221|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong start, with healthy revenue growth and a significant profitability improvement driven by better cotton yarn realisations, strong export demand and disciplined raw material buying. The overall spread rose to INR133/kg from INR107 in the prior quarter, and the EBITDA margin was cited at about 18.8%. Management said the margin is elevated, expects the next two quarters to stay around these levels, and expects longer-term margins near 15% after the Odisha plant. The solar project started commercial operations late in the prior quarter (about 10 days of contribution) and is guided to save about INR15 crore a year, with the full 90 days flowing from the current month.

segments.name: Cotton yarn
segments.commentary: Better realisations cited as main driver of margin expansion; spread rose to INR133/kg from INR107/kg. Management said the Odisha plant will add to revenue from Q4.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Management targets a 55:45 export-to-domestic split. China and Bangladesh together account for about 60-70% of Sportking's exports; China's incremental yarn demand was the main driver of the recent uptick.

segments.name: Fabric and garments (proposed acquisitions)
segments.commentary: Proposed acquisitions of Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales are expected to add 8-10% to top line and similar EBITDA share from next year, with about INR250 crore impact from next financial year once the deal completes.

capex_capacity: Greenfield 150,000-spindle expansion in Odisha: first-phase production expected in Q3 FY27, full project targeted within FY27; announced cost about INR975-1,000 crore.
Management expects 30-40% of potential revenue from the new plant in Q4 FY27 and targets 90% plant utilisation by March 2027 and 96-97% by the start of FY28; ramp-up expected to take 5-6 months.
Odisha margins expected at least 300-400 bps above existing plants, per management.
Odisha incentives: INR2.50/unit power subsidy, 30% capital subsidy with no cap, land subsidy tied to employment, and about INR7,000 per employee employment subsidy.
Land is available to triple Odisha capacity; further capex depends on balance sheet and leverage comfort.
Solar project commissioned and operating; expected to cut annual power cost by 12-15%.
demand_pricing: Management said demand from all markets remains healthy and expects festive-season support domestically.

Global cotton yarn demand improved as China became a large buyer, pushing Indian yarn prices higher; management said China imports about 20,000 tonnes against India's roughly 400,000 tonnes monthly output.
Order book kept at 70-90 days, similar to end of last quarter.
Cotton prices rose about 10-11% over the last quarter; management says most purchases were made about 3 months earlier and that Q2 should be similar to or better than Q1.
India-UK FTA signed last month, but no orders yet; management expects 6-9 months for orders to reflect in the order book.

Management expects China to remain a buyer because Chinese cotton prices are above international levels. Bangladesh's spinning sector is under strain from gas and capital costs, which helps Indian yarn demand.
Exports to the US are indirect via downstream vendors whose offtake has roughly doubled in the last 6 months.
guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected around 18-19% for the next two quarters; longer-term margin guided around 15% after Odisha, with 12-14% described as the comfortable range.
FY27 revenue target about INR3,000 crore (around 20% growth); FY28 target above INR4,000 crore with Odisha.
Solar savings about INR15 crore annually; full 90-day contribution expected from the current month.
Absolute EBITDA expected to keep rising in FY28 even if percentage margins moderate.
Cotton import duty waiver runs to 31 October; management is lobbying the government to extend it and says FY27 inventory is already covered for two quarters.
Acquisition completion expected in about one more quarter, with full impact from next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin sustainability and what drove the 18.8% margin, including the import duty effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cotton import duty made no contribution to Q1 because raw material was already bought; margins should stay around current levels for two quarters, with absolute EBITDA expected to keep trending higher.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread of INR133/kg sustainable for a year or two?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict precisely, expects cotton prices to ease after the new crop, and said the inventory effect will be larger in the next two quarters because Q1 realisations lagged cotton prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Odisha plant reach high utilisation and what is the revenue run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 96-97% utilisation by start of FY28; no Q3 revenue assumed, with 30-40% of potential revenue from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the merger financing and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly preferential shares, with cash outflow of about INR25-30 crore and no meaningful incremental debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity beyond Odisha Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Land exists to triple Odisha capacity; further capex depends on the balance sheet and leverage comfort.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term product mix shift toward value-added products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value-added fabric and garment share would be about 10% in the next year; longer-term plans to be announced once there is more visibility.

risks_watch: Cyclicality: management itself flagged 18-20% margins as likely not sustainable long term and cited FY22 peaks as an aberration.
Cotton input cost: prices up 10-11% in the last quarter; management expects a moderation after October, but the import duty waiver ends on 31 October unless extended.
Capacity additions: spread strength may attract new spindle capacity; management says it has not seen announced projects.
Odisha ramp-up: 5-6 month ramp, targeted 90% utilisation by March 2027, and margin accretion (300-400 bps) depend on execution.
Acquisitions of Marvel Dyers and Sobhagia Sales: completion timing has slipped and the contribution is still under progress.
Export concentration: China and Bangladesh make up 60-70% of exports; the China-driven demand could reverse.
539221|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, margins and the Odisha plant, but guarded on forward cotton and spread outlook, with repeated statements that it is difficult to predict. Evasive on pricing details, declining to share cotton cost or realisation numbers.
key_quotes: So the overall spread was INR133 vis-a-vis INR107 last quarter.
And the 18%, 19%, 20% might not be sustainable in the long-term, but we expect them to be healthier than where they were in last 2, 3 years going forward next year.
So I won't take it as a benchmark for the volatility of margins. Otherwise, they stay between 12% to 14%, which is where we are comfortable actually.

500710|2026-06.headline: JSW Dulux Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.8% to ₹965 crore on ~25% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% with PAT lifted by one-offs.
500710|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% like-to-like to ₹965 crore, with volume up about 25% (about 18-19% after price). Gross margin was 37.4%, which management says was depressed by roughly 2 points of high-cost inventory and about 2.5 points from reclassifying promotional spends to gross revenue; underlying gross margin was put at 39.5-40%. EBITDA rose 14.7% to ₹115.1 crore but margin diluted about 50 bps to 11.9% after headcount additions (~160 people) and R&D investment. Reported PAT of ₹135.5 crore includes one-offs: ₹55.9 crore dividend from ICICI R&T and ₹108 crore income tax refund (incl. ₹21.5 crore interest) for AY 2013-14.

financial_highlights.change: Management: underlying ~39.5-40% before inventory and reclassification effects
Other income; linked to real estate monetisation

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Grew double digits (management cites ~20% volume growth) and is ~60% of business; premium is ~45% of decorative and led growth, with premium and luxury growing high double digits. Mass and economy grew lower.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: All sub-segments grew upwards of 25%; automotive grew strongly with premium OEM and refinish wins (Porsche, Mahindra, MG via JSW group, Sikkens body shops).

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected in 13-15% range going forward, as reinvestment costs normalise and input prices ease.
Management expects Q2 growth in a similar band to Q1 despite a weaker July due to late rains; target is double-digit volume and value growth.
Strategic ambition: become number two in decorative and number one in industrial coatings, with a 2030-31 vision; decorative aim is market share gains while protecting absolute EBITDA.
Project Akshaya cost programme targets synergies with JSW Paints; ₹2.4 crore savings realised in Q1 and a 3-year roadmap set.
ERP migration from AkzoNobel systems planned by end of calendar year; TSA period is limited.
capex_capacity: Active towns about 3,400-3,500 out of 5,000+ presence; target to lift to about 4,500 this year, focusing on towns above 20,000 population.
Shift to direct/hybrid model in about the top 20 high-share towns; distributor model retained elsewhere.
Cross-manufacturing: JSW Paints made at Gwalior; JSW Dulux products made in JSW Paints plants; some JSW Paints products made in Mohali.
Headquarters moved from Delhi to JSW Centre, Mumbai during Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth ~25%, with price contributing ~6-7 points; growth driven by value per outlet from existing outlets, broadly secular across outlet types.
Gross-to-net reclassification of promotional spends (~2.5% of blended revenue) reduced reported gross margin; management says this aligns with industry presentation.
Management says decorative pricing has stabilised but competition from new entrants, with discounting, will persist for 1-2 years.

Discount ratio includes distributor commission (~4.5-4.7% of revenue), which management says makes dealer commissions otherwise modest; company benchmarks pricing to the market leader, not new entrants.
Benefit expected as high-priced inventory bought at end-March is consumed; lower-cost stock now entering August.

qa_highlights.question: What execution changes are driving better decorative performance, beyond headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-market segmentation by share tiers; reinforced Velvet Touch and WeatherShield; focus on undercoats such as primers in weak states; digital lead management, AI/analytics and an architect/painter programme. Hybrid direct model being tested in top 20 towns.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume-value gap reconcile with mix improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three factors: high-cost inventory, ~2.5% gross-to-net reclassification, and faster growth in lower-margin industrial and other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Target for top-three position and inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined JSW Paints and JSW Dulux revenue is about ₹6,000 crore. Aim is to become number two; industrial to be number one in 1-1.5 years and wider ambition by 2030-31. No explicit M&A mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and discounting vs. new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition to remain intense for 1-2 years; company does not match new entrant discounts and benchmarks against the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Decorative outperformance vs Asian Paints and Berger (8-9% volume growth)?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to premium-led growth, distribution expansion, digital tools and recovery in smaller dealers after new-entrant pressure; no single driver cited.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for July-August?
qa_highlights.answer: July was weaker due to late rains, but management expects Q2 in a similar band and targets double-digit growth in volume and value.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery to the 39.5-40% underlying level as high-cost inventory is consumed; crude-linked raw material costs.
EBITDA margin trajectory versus the 13-15% guidance as headcount and R&D costs continue.
Persistent discounting by new entrants in decorative; mass and economy segment growth lagging.
One-off income (₹55.9 crore dividend, ₹108 crore tax refund) inflates Q1 PAT; underlying profit is lower.
Execution risk in Project Akshaya, ERP migration and exit from AkzoNobel TSA; related-party governance with JSW Paints.
500710|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume growth and market share ambitions, while openly explaining margin shortfall via inventory, reclassification and reinvestment. Somewhat evasive on specific M&A and the precise timeline for top-three positioning; cautious on competitive intensity.
key_quotes: we have decided to reinvest in the growth.
But given the crude prices, I have said that the EBITDA margin would be in the range of 13% to 15%.
Unless you grow 20% in decorative and volume, you can't get a 25% volume growth.

532976|2026-06.headline: Jai Balaji Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore; adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore, PAT up 21% to INR85 crore.
532976|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore (about 9% margin) and PAT up 21% to INR85 crore (about 5% margin), attributed to price normalisation and operational efficiency. Ferroalloy and pig iron realisations rose sharply YoY, while DI pipe demand stayed subdued on slow government ordering and fund releases. Management declined to give volume or EBITDA guidance, citing uncertainty, but said pipe prices are at the bottom and cannot fall further. Expansion capex was revised up to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, with completion expected by Q3 FY27 and the balance by end-2026.

financial_highlights.change: Net term debt was INR3,408 crore in FY21

segments.name: Ductile iron pipes (DI)
segments.commentary: About 15% of Q1 turnover; utilisation about 30% of the enhanced 5.5 lakh tpa capacity. Order book about four months at current dispatch rate. Management said pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins in Q1.

segments.name: Specialised ferroalloys
segments.commentary: About 27% of revenue; utilisation above 80% in the last quarter. Ferroalloy prices up 46% YoY. Management guided a long-term margin of 15-20%, and exports go to more than 42 countries.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: About 19% of revenue; realisations up 16% YoY.

segments.name: TMT bars
segments.commentary: About 14.8% of revenue. Management expects West Bengal sales to rise to 50-70% of TMT volume from 15-20% previously.

segments.name: Commodity mix (sponge iron, billets, coke, scrap, fines)
segments.commentary: Sponge iron 7.4%, billets 3.5%, coke about 7%, scrap and fines about 1% of revenue. Sponge iron and billet realisations were broadly stable.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance for DI pipes or ferroalloys for FY27; management said demand visibility is too uncertain.
No EBITDA-per-tonne guidance for pipes; management said prices are 25-30% below levels of a year and a half ago and 'cannot get worse'.
Ferroalloy utilisation expected at 80-90% once the new module is commissioned around December-January.
Management indicated revenue of INR7,000-7,500 crore in a normal market once expanded capacity is complete by end-2026; no FY28 or FY30 targets were given beyond this.
Post-monsoon recovery in DI dispatches and payments expected, with improvement from Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: DI pipe capacity raised from 5 lakh tpa to 5.5 lakh tpa.

Specialised ferroalloy capacity rising to 1.9 lakh tpa from 1.66 lakh tpa; blast furnace to 7.5 lakh tpa from 6.3 lakh tpa; sinter to 12.08 lakh tpa from 9.08 lakh tpa. All expected commissioned by Q3 FY27.

Expansion outlay revised to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore (cause: equipment shipment delays, inflation, rupee depreciation, technical upgrades). About INR1,076 crore already spent, mostly from internal accruals; INR35-40 crore balance by end-2026.
Three railway sidings in operation; about 400 acres of land largely occupied for new capacity.
Management said the INR20 crore trial plastic-alternative pipe plant has sold no pipes and is in abeyance.
demand_pricing: Government DI pipe ordering is slow. Management said INR10,344 crore has been released by the Centre this year, and a FY26 backlog (only INR1,560 crore released in the budget) remains the constraint.
Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 extended to December 2028 with outlay of INR8.69 lakh crore (including INR3.5 lakh crore central assistance); AMRUT 2.0 also cited as a driver.
Competition intense while pipe utilisation stays at 25-35% industry-wide; management said intensity eases above 65-70% utilisation.
Jal Jeevan Mission receivables: management estimated 25-35% of outstanding dues collected, with the rest expected over the next 2-4 months.
Ferroalloy demand described as strong with repeat orders; management said 80-85% capacity is utilised.

qa_highlights.question: When will increased government spending translate into DI pipe dispatches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a post-monsoon recovery in dispatches and payments, with improvement from Q3 FY27, after central fund releases and state matching shares.

qa_highlights.question: Will pricing pressure persist given competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition will persist until industry utilisation reaches 65-70%. Management said pipe prices are at rock bottom and Q1 pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give DI pipe EBITDA per tonne guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management called pipe EBITDA guidance speculative given the 25-30% price fall and said it would reassess next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of specialised ferroalloys versus conventional steel?
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional steel margins are 5-7%, specialised ferroalloys 15-18%. Long-term ferroalloy margin guidance is 15-20%, with a 1-2% swing from raw materials or freight.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex rise to about INR1,100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase was about 7-8%, from delayed equipment shipments from China, inflation, higher freight, rupee depreciation, and technical upgrades.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DI pipe order book?
qa_highlights.answer: About four months at current dispatch rates. Q1 DI production was 41,000 tonnes, about 30-33% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is current debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayable term debt is INR188 crore. Working capital is INR375-400 crore, sanctioned limits about INR525-550 crore, and net utilisation stays below INR500 crore with INR70-80 crore cash or unutilised limits.

risks_watch: Government fund releases and state payments: DI demand depends on clearing the FY26 backlog and recovering dues.
Pipe pricing at 25-30% below a year and a half ago, with management saying no further downside yet giving no guidance.
Capex overrun risk: budget rose to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, and commissioning by Q3 FY27 depends on imported equipment.

qa_highlights.question: How many new projects in FY27 and what is the pipeline?

qa_highlights.question: Are Square and Signature margins tracking underwriting?

qa_highlights.question: How will capital employed and leverage be managed?

risks_watch: Margin recovery: Q1 EBITDA margin compression from war-related costs; watch whether Q2 margins return to the 20-30% range management cited.

543539|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, with a clear focus on delivery timelines. Evasive or non-committal on pipeline count, leverage and capital planning, which management said have not been set. Acknowledged war-related margin pressure as a one-off that has eased.
key_quotes: Rashmi Square has completed 22 slabs.
Because war situation happened, the cost of materials and everything increased.

The projects are starting from now.

543322|2026-06.headline: Alivus Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.4% YoY to INR640 crores as non-GPL grew 26.5%, offsetting a 52.6% GPL drop; EBITDA margin 36.6%.

532527|2026-06.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 1,217 crore (+19.8% YoY), PAT Rs 46.9 crore (~4x YoY), EBITDA margin 17.96%.

financial_highlights.change: from 17.11% in previous quarter (+85 bps QoQ)

543276|2026-06.headline: Craftsman guides standalone capex above INR 1,000 crore and consolidated about INR 1,500 crore for FY27, with heavy-HP stationary engine revenue targeted at USD 100 million by FY29-30.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Margins rose on higher demand in material handling and storage; management says orders are rising quarter on quarter and the uptick is not a one-off spike. Contract manufacturing described as steady.

segments.name: Sunbeam

segments.name: DR Axion (subsidiary)

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Industrial segment's step-up this quarter?

qa_highlights.question: When will balance sheet and gearing improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose on working capital for ~33% growth in a 60-day debt industry. Cash flows go to debt repayment, with no large capex planned. Target is long-term debt within 1x EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is it possible to give MDF FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance has been stopped due to volatility. The objective is 15%+ MDF margins and a good growth trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Will particle board capacity increase by minor capex to ~3 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The line was pre-designed in two parts. Efficiency gains are possible but a 20%+ increase is unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for UP and Odisha greenfield projects?
qa_highlights.answer: UP land is not yet secured; target is to acquire by year-end, with the plywood plant by April 2028. Odisha is still in government talks with no land selected. UP MDF timing is not finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable ROCE for MDF and particle board, given particle board capex and realisation differences?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the analyst's numbers do not match its capacity basis. The target for both segments is 20% ROCE, which it believes is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the logistics business and its structure?
qa_highlights.answer: The business is EBITDA- and cash-flow-positive and not core. A strategic partner may come in at an accretive valuation. Only half of phase 1 of the new port is operating, and CFS is expected to grow double digits.

540048|2026-06.headline: S.P. Apparels Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR 61.4 crore on revenue flat at INR 401 crore; FY27 guidance of INR 2,000 crore reiterated.
540048|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was broadly flat year-on-year at INR 401 crore (vs INR 403 crore), while EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR 61.4 crore and margin expanded to 15.3% from 13.1%. PAT grew 20.4% to INR 24.9 crore. Management attributed the soft top line to U.S. tariff-related order holding in March-May and customer-requested shipment deferrals, and said growth will be back-end weighted into H2 FY27. The company reiterated its INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue guidance, and announced a INR 3 per share dividend and a proposed stock split from INR 10 to INR 2 face value.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 403 crore in Q1 FY26 (broadly flat)
vs INR 287.7 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)
