financial_highlights.value: INR 258 crore / INR 46.6 crore / INR 211 crore

segments.name: Garment division (SPAL + Young Brand, adjusted)
segments.commentary: Adjusted revenue INR 337.3 crore with adjusted EBITDA INR 59.2 crore, a 17.6% margin; management attributed the margin to efficiency and product mix, not one-offs.

segments.name: Young Brand Apparel (YBA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 72.7 crore, adjusted EBITDA INR 12.6 crore (17.7% margin), PAT INR 6.3 crore; revenue fell YoY on U.S. tariff after-effects. Export volume 5 million pieces, vs 5.2 million in the prior quarter per the analyst exchange.

segments.name: SPUK (UK trading)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 33.3 crore, up 125.2% YoY, but EBITDA was negative INR 1.0 crore due to small air shipments and shipments slipping into Q2.

segments.name: SP Retail Ventures
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 18.8 crore, up 26.7% YoY, with EBITDA of INR 0.41 crore; the business is at EBITDA breakeven and moving toward sustainable profit. Angel & Rocket India is the key brand.

segments.name: Yarn division
segments.commentary: EBITDA of about INR 7.5 crore in Q1 FY27 as stated on the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 2,000 crore reiterated; management expects H2 to be stronger and to recover the Q1 shortfall, though Q1 delivered only INR 400 crore.
Q2 FY27 revenue expected to be better than Q1 on the top line.
Garment division (incl. YBA and Sri Lanka) EBITDA margin guided above 15% for the full year.
Young Brand revenue guided to INR 340-350 crore for FY27 (FY26: about INR 300 crore).
Infant export value guided to INR 1,300-1,400 crore for FY27 (FY26: about INR 1,100 crore; call also cited INR 955 crore for the prior year).
Consolidated interest cost guided to INR 30-35 crore for the full year, excluding exchange loss; Q1 interest of about INR 15 crore included a INR 1.75 crore forex hit.
SPUK guidance of GBP 13 million+ in about 3 years and GBP 50 million in about 5 years; a later answer cited GBP 50-60 million in 3-5 years.
Sri Lanka revenue expected at INR 150-200 crore by end of March 2027, per CFO.
Sri Lanka stabilisation expected by about March 2027; job-work route could add 500-600 machines within a year.
capex_capacity: About 750 machines added in India in FY27 so far; utilisation fell YoY because of order slowness from U.S. tariff uncertainty in March-May.
Sri Lanka has about 1,650 machines (about 1,300 used for exports); management says it can go up to 2,000. Factories are fully running except one at 85-90%.
Salem facility started trial production last month; full Phase 1 capacity expected about three months after Diwali.
Sivakasi factory started; plan to add about 400 machines over two years.

Young Brand: Palladum facility in production; all planned units in commercial production by October; new bra line with about INR 10 crore investment, investment from September-October, full revenue next fiscal, orders for about 200 machines.
Total sewing capacity cited at about 10,000 machines (about 6,000 India, 2,000 Sri Lanka, 1,750 YBA).
demand_pricing: Order book about INR 570-600 crore in total: SPAL about INR 430 crore, YBA about INR 100 crore (figure stated as INR 72 crore in one answer), SPUK about INR 60-70 crore. The call gave inconsistent figures.
SPAL booked until October and open for November onwards; YBA orders booked until January per management.
SPUK added three UK customers (two UK, one EU) and is adding three more; Marks & Spencer named as one of them.
UK-India FTA recently effective; UK customer engagement improving. The EU-India FTA is expected to be signed by end of FY27.
Management says customers are cautious about possible new U.S. legislation but are not currently expecting a negative impact.

543401|2026-06.headline: Go Fashion Q1 FY27: EBITDA before exceptionals down 2% to INR67.4 crores on marketing spend, while EBO SSSG turned positive at 0.6%.
543401|2026-06.overview: Revenue was flat YoY at about INR223 crores with gross margin of 62.9%, and EBITDA before exceptional items was INR67.4 crores (30.3% margin), down 2%. Management attributed the EBITDA moderation mainly to higher marketing spend, including the brand ambassador partnership. A one-off exceptional charge of INR6.5 crores was booked for write-off of capex on 66 closed stores, and PAT was about INR16 crores. Management presented the quarter as early progress against five FY27 priorities but repeatedly cautioned that one quarter does not make a trend.

segments.name: EBO (company-operated stores)
segments.commentary: SSSG +0.6% and same cluster sales growth +1.2%; footfall up about 1-1.5% YoY per bill cuts. Stores above 700 sq ft delivered SSSG of roughly 2.5%-3%, over 130 such stores.

segments.name: LFS (large format stores, Reliance Trends channel)
segments.commentary: Grew 2% YoY to INR50 crores after a difficult FY26; management says supply-chain disruption with a key LFS partner in Q3-Q4 FY26 has largely normalised.

segments.name: Everyday wear (daily wear concept)
segments.commentary: 15 stores live; 12-13 stated as profitable, with about 12 double-digit EBITDA positive. Sales around INR1,000 per sq ft per month. Target of 25-30 stores by end FY27. Size requirement 1,500-2,000 sq ft.

guidance_outlook: Store footprint: square feet to rise about 8%-10% on a year-through basis in FY27, back-ended; closures expected to be much lower than in recent quarters, though no store-count guidance given.
Advertising spend to stay within 2%-3% of revenue in FY27.
Everyday wear stores targeted at 25-30 by end FY27, from 15 today; 10-12 new product refreshes planned for FY27.
Company-level inventory days expected at 90-100 by year-end, including daily wear; working capital days have room to improve by a few days.
Capex to be funded through internal accruals; new large stores assumed 15-20 month payback and 45-60 days inventory on sales.
Fabric costs up 7%-10%; management is not taking price hikes now and expects gross margin pressure in coming quarters, magnitude not quantified.
capex_capacity: Store network: 66 stores closed in Q1, reducing retail space by 7,000 sq ft; further larger-format stores to be added in catchments where small stores are closed.
Plan to expand footprint over five years with potential to double square feet deployed, across Tier 1, 2 and 3 cities.
New store unit economics: payback 15-20 months, inventory turns 45-60 days on sales for larger stores.
Exceptional INR6.5 crores capex write-off linked to store closures in Q1.
Lingerie and ladies innerwear under evaluation as an addition to the daily wear concept.
demand_pricing: EBO SSSG +0.6% in Q1; management attributes it to possibly a weak base, transfer of sales from closed stores, and better Q1 footfalls, and says it is too early to call a trend.
Full price sales 94%; ASP about INR863.
Fabric cost inflation of 7%-10% linked to Middle East disruption; no price hikes taken yet.
Brand ambassador Shraddha Kapoor onboarded from July 2026 to target a younger audience.
Management said malls and high streets show no real outlier in SSSG, and older 700+ sq ft stores show a similar trend.

qa_highlights.question: What net retail area growth is expected in FY27, and is it back-ended?
qa_highlights.answer: Square feet deployed to rise about 8%-10% on a 12-month basis; the quarter alone saw a 7,000 sq ft reduction, and the increase will come over the year.

qa_highlights.question: What would SSSG look like excluding closed or to-be-closed stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported SSSG excludes stores closed in Q1 but not future closures. 700+ sq ft stores grew about 2.5%-3%; management could not give a clean ex-closures figure and attributed the 0.6% to base effects, transfers and footfall.

qa_highlights.question: How many more store closures in FY27 and how far through is the process?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance; closures depend on large-store opportunities but are expected to be much lower than in recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much have raw material costs risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric costs up 7%-10%; no price hike currently, and gross margin impact is hard to quantify given older inventory, though it is expected to hit coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are SSSG trends by store vintage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no clean vintage correlation; some FY18 stores grew about 10% while some FY24 stores declined. Detailed bucket data to be sent later through SGA.

qa_highlights.question: How are everyday wear stores performing?
qa_highlights.answer: 15 stores live; about 12-13 profitable and 12 double-digit EBITDA positive; INR1,000 per sq ft monthly sales; actual size requirement 1,500-2,000 sq ft.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from fabric inflation of 7%-10%, with no price hikes yet and timing of pass-through uncertain.
SSSG sustainability: management explicitly said 0.6% is not a trend and the drivers are not clearly separated.
LFS dependence on Reliance Trends; speculation about partner format conversion to AZORTE, which management could not assess.
Marketing spend elevated (2.3% of revenue, with brand ambassador) with EBITDA already down 2%.
Management said it would clarify the earlier 10%-12% SSSG statement on ~275 stores via SGA; this is unresolved and a credibility question.
Inventory of INR245 crores and 139 working capital days; target to reduce inventory days to 90-100.

financial_highlights.change: revenue and gross margin stable vs Q1 last year
one-off write-off of capex on store closures

532443|2026-06.headline: Cera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.5% (volume-led) to INR 486 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.1% on one-time factors management says reverse from Q3.
532443|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 19.5% YoY to INR 486 crore, with Sanitaryware up 14%, Faucetware up 25% and growth mainly volume-driven. EBITDA excluding other income fell to INR 49.2 crore (10.1% margin vs 13.1% a year ago), which management attributed to a wage settlement, under-absorption from single-kiln operation in April-May, project-order foreclosures and delayed price pass-through. PAT was INR 45 crore vs INR 47 crore. Turnover discounts were reclassified from expenses into revenue deductions, lowering reported revenue by about 2.5-3% with no absolute profit impact. FY27 guidance of 18-20% revenue growth and 13.5-14% EBITDA margin was maintained.

segments.name: Sanitaryware
segments.commentary: 47% of revenue; grew 14% YoY (volume ~10%, price ~2%, mix ~2%). Capacity utilisation 61% in Q1, roughly 80% across both plants from June.

segments.name: Faucetware
segments.commentary: 40% of revenue; grew 25% YoY (volume 18%, price 4%, mix 3%). Utilisation 96%; gross margin severely hit by brass cost inflation.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: 11% of revenue; grew 22% YoY.

segments.name: Wellness
segments.commentary: 2% of revenue; declined 7% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 18-20% reiterated.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 13.5-14% maintained; management says it will be met on a full-year basis, implying a recovery after Q2.
Q2 expected to carry some residual impact as project orders still at old prices; project price revisions to flow from Q3.
Gross margin expected to return to ~51% from Q3 if brass and gas prices hold; Q1 gross margin was ~46%.
FY27 wage cost add-on of INR 18.3 crore (INR 6.3 crore one-time arrears plus INR 12 crore for the year); FY27 staff cost guided at ~INR 300 crore.
FY27 capex outlay ~INR 43 crore, mainly Faucetware brownfield expansion (capacity expected from Q4 FY27), efficiency, digital and infrastructure.
FY27 brand-building and marketing budget ~INR 85 crore, which management says can be increased.
Management declined to guide FY28 margins; said it would revisit at year end. Long-term margin of 16% not committed to a timeline.
capex_capacity: Sanitaryware utilisation 61% in Q1 FY27 (one kiln run in April-May; second kiln started June); both plants running from June at ~80% of total capacity.
Faucetware utilisation 96% in Q1; management says it can go beyond 100% via in-house and outsourced supply until brownfield expansion comes in from Q4 FY27.
Greenfield sanitaryware project (earlier INR 130-150 crore, deferred) to be reviewed by year-end; would take ~18 months to build once decided.
Internalising higher-selling SKUs from Morbi outsourcing partners; incremental casting-line investment of INR 2-3 crore.
Long-term in-house/outsourced split about 50:50; Sanitaryware skewed more towards outsourcing recently due to bought-out parts.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price increases (March and May 2026): ~12% in Sanitaryware, ~16% in Faucetware; management says absorbed well by the market.
Price hikes reflected mainly in retail; project contracts (43% of Q1 revenue vs 39% in Q4) to move to revised pricing from Q3.
Brass prices rose from INR 665 (Dec) to ~INR 880 (June) and ~INR 900 (July) per management; further hike possible if prices go to INR 950-1,000.
Product mix: premium 44%, mid 37%, entry 19%. Tier 1 and Tier 3 at 38% each, Tier 2 at 24%.
Management described growth as volume-driven and broad-based across retail and project, with Sanitaryware demand up from ~10% growth in prior quarters to 14%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 19.5% growth was volume vs price, and what was the Senator/Polipluz contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanitaryware: volume ~10%, price ~2%, mix ~2%. Faucetware: volume 18%, price 4%, mix 3%. Management would not split out Senator and Polipluz numbers, saying they are in build-up phase and FY27 targets are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-time wage settlement and what is the staff cost run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 6.3 crore arrears for Sept 2025-Mar 2026 booked in Q1, plus INR 3 crore for the current quarter. Full-year wage impact INR 18.3 crore. Staff cost expected ~INR 300 crore for FY27 excluding the one-off.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the margin drop, and how much is one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 4.35 percentage point one-time impact: wage arrears 1.3%, under-absorption from single kiln 0.75% (INR 3.7 crore), accelerated project order closures 0.8% (INR 4 crore), and delayed retail price pass-through 1.5%. Ex-these items EBITDA would be ~14.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Morbi and SKU internalisation need capex, and how many flagship stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Internalisation needs only INR 2-3 crore of casting-line changes. Senator stores to rise from 35 to ~50 by year end, on track.

qa_highlights.question: Who leads Senator and Polipluz after Mr. Baliga's resignation?
qa_highlights.answer: The existing national head under the succession plan will lead them. Baliga stays until 30 September. Management says targets are unchanged and no execution impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Should the greenfield sanitaryware plant be revived?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand improving (Sanitaryware growth 14% vs ~10% earlier). Review by year end; if approved the plant takes ~18 months. Some capacity remains available.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further price hikes and where does gross margin go?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin ~46% in Q1 (Faucetware hit hardest); expected ~51% from Q3 if brass and gas hold. Further hike to be evaluated if brass goes beyond INR 900-950.

543600|2026-06.headline: Harsha Engineers Q1 FY27 consolidated Engineering supply up 25% YoY to Rs 421 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed on a 6-7% raw material spike pending pass-through.
543600|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Engineering supply rose to Rs 421 crore from Rs 382 crore QoQ and Rs 349 crore YoY, with India Engineering growing about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ. Consolidated Engineering EBITDA was Rs 69.8 crore versus Rs 77 crore QoQ and Rs 65.3 crore YoY, so margin fell QoQ. Management attributed the squeeze to an ~8% rise in average raw material cost (lagged pass-through of one to two quarters), about Rs 4 crore of FX hedge accounting loss, and about Rs 3 crore of higher indirect material costs after the West Asia conflict. Management kept FY27 guidance of high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth, with India Engineering EBITDA margin of 22-24%.

-9% QoQ vs Rs 77 crore; +7% YoY vs Rs 65.3 crore

financial_highlights.change: Figures inconsistent in call; CEO cited +31% YoY

segments.name: India Engineering (HEIL + Harsha Advantek)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 21% YoY and 6% QoQ; EBITDA and PAT up YoY but margin down QoQ on material pass-through lag and FX loss. Management guides high-teens India growth for FY27.

segments.name: Harsha Advantek (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q1 sales about Rs 30 crore (+7% QoQ), EBITDA margin about 9%. FY27 target Rs 140 crore plus vs Rs 43 crore in FY26; expected PAT positive by end-FY27.

segments.name: Harsha China
segments.commentary: Stable and profitable; FY27 revenue growth about 10% on FY26 base of about Rs 120 crore, EBITDA margin 12-14%, PAT about 6%. Brownfield steel cage expansion to commission by Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Harsha Romania
segments.commentary: Still loss-making; slight top-line growth but one-time FX loss of about Rs 2 crore in Q1. Management expects some losses in FY27, aiming for break-even; new top management in place.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 36.3 crore, EBITDA Rs 2.82 crore; management guides about Rs 200 crore FY27 revenue at 7-8% EBITDA margin, project-driven and seasonal.

segments.name: Large-size cages
segments.commentary: Q1 sales only about Rs 10 crore on capacity ramp-up constraints at new facility; management still targets about 50% growth on FY26 base of Rs 49 crore (the call also cites about 30%, so the target is unclear).

guidance_outlook: India Engineering: high-teens growth in FY27 (volume-led, with some price pass-through); India Engineering EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%, with management noting the 24% Q1 standalone figure may be high due to lag cycles.
Consolidated FY27: low-to-mid-teens sales growth; management called 20% a very tough stretch.
Bushing: about 30% growth in FY27 vs Rs 127 crore in FY26.
Stamping: about 30% growth in FY27 vs Rs 60 crore in FY26.
Japanese customers: about 10% growth to about Rs 72-80 crore (management also said Rs 80 crore or thereabouts).
Consolidated EBITDA margin could recover to about 18% (FY26 level 18.7%) if metal prices stabilise; management had no view on RM price normalisation.
Subsidiaries: China plus Romania revenue growth below 10%; combined FY27 loss about Rs 2-3 crore, with Romania possibly profitable next year.
CapEx: Rs 50-80 crore per year, with Rs 180-200 crore combined over 1.5-2 years for Bhayla Phase-2 and China expansion.
capex_capacity: Bhayla (India) Phase-2 expansion: building construction delayed by heavy rain in Ahmedabad, expected to start this month; third building targeted for completion by end-2026 or Q4 FY27.
Bhayla total target: about Rs 300-400 crore revenue by year three across both phases; Phase-1 and Phase-2 demand visibility expected to absorb capacity within about one year.
China Brownfield steel cage expansion: funded with debt at attractive rate; construction under way; commissioning around Q3 FY28; full impact from FY29.
Large-size cage capacity at new facility still ramping up, constraining Q1 volumes.
Advantek Phase-2 expansion (bushings, stampings, large cages) announced earlier; Advantek FY27 target Rs 140 crore plus.
demand_pricing: Cage demand strong in India from bearing majors and MNC customers' new plants; exports from India Rs 139 crore, +22% YoY.
Europe and US demand improving alongside industrial demand; management described growth as broad-based.
Raw material cost up about 8% in Q1 across brass, copper, zinc, steel and polymer; pass-through lag of one to two quarters (about four months per CFO).
Management estimated the raw material increase would lift prices by about 3-4% (CFO said 40-50% of a 6-7% increase), though the CEO declined to quantify the price impact.
Top 10 customers about 80% of revenue; top customers (SKF, Schaeffler, Timken, NBC, ZF, Flender) rank in a shifting order; management claims 80-90% wallet share with major Indian customers.
Management cited wind bushing upgrades, rail stampings and defence/aerospace stamping developments as future growth areas.

542649|2026-06.headline: RVNL Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA nearly doubled to INR 171 crore (margin 3.99% vs 2.08%) on turnover up 9.62% to INR 4,300 crore.
542649|2026-06.overview: Standalone turnover rose 9.62% YoY to INR 4,300 crore and consolidated turnover rose 10.55% to INR 4,321 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR 171 crore, with PAT up 21.72% to INR 155 crore. Order inflow in the quarter was INR 5,417 crore, taking the total order book to INR 93,492 crore as on 30 June 2026. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% top-line growth and 15-20% bottom-line growth, and flagged labour shortages, client payment delays and geopolitics as challenges.

vs INR 64.91 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.commentary: Order book of about INR 12,000 crore.

segments.commentary: Order book of about INR 4,000 crore.

segments.commentary: Subsidiaries contributed INR 126 crore to consolidated revenue and INR 12.70 crore to PAT; share of JV/associate profit was INR 6.16 crore; dividend income from JVs/subsidiaries was INR 12.07 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at about 15%, and bottom-line growth at about 15-20%; management said it expects to maintain this after Q1 (Q1 PAT growth 19% cited).
Order inflow target for FY27 of about INR 20,000 crore (with one answer citing INR 20,000-25,000 crore), in addition to existing order book; about INR 5,000-5,500 crore already received or entrusted.
Three-year vision: EBITDA margin of 5-7% and ROE of about 12-13%.
Over the next three years, order book targeted to split about 50:50 between railway management works and bidding works; overseas share expected to rise.
Margin expectations: management works 8-10%, PMC work about 7%, domestic bidding works 5-6%, overseas works 15-20% targeted.
Dividend policy follows DIPAM guidelines: 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher.
No new external borrowing planned for the next two to three quarters; working capital lines available at about 5.5-5.9%.
capex_capacity: BharatNet (INR 13,000 crore, BSNL, 82,000 km OFC, DB-1 model): infrastructure implementation timeline three years, with about six to eight months of extension expected due to ground-level issues; 10-year maintenance follows.

Vande Bharat sleeper (INR 14,400 crore, executed by SPV Kinet Railway Solutions): first prototype trainset targeted for December 2026; 120 sets to be delivered over five years; 35-year maintenance contract.
Rishikesh-Karnaprayag rail project (INR 37,000 crore, 125 km): 78% overall progress, about 97% tunnel excavation complete; completion targeted December 2029.
Hardware for BharatNet was procured at pre-crisis tender prices, per management.
demand_pricing: Management says about 40-42% of the order book is fixed-price-like railway management-fee work; most contracts have price variation clauses covering inflation, so impact is limited.
Q1 revenue mix: about 63% from management (nomination) work and remainder from bidding and PMC work.
NMDC PMC award of about INR 6,500 crore cited as a nomination-basis win; talks ongoing with other PSUs and state governments for similar fixed-margin PMC work.

Overseas pursuits: bids in Africa (power transmission and roads), Nepal (hydro), Israel (Tel Aviv Metro EOI), Georgia and Serbia (rail reconstruction); management names Central Asia, Middle East, Eastern Europe and Southeast Asia as targets.
Management flagged labour availability shortages and client payment delays as key execution challenges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the L1 size and where is business development focused?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR 20,000-25,000 crore of order inflow this year, with about INR 5,500 crore already entrusted; focus on ports, hydro, highways and green energy.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is fixed-price and how is inflation handled?
qa_highlights.answer: About 42% is railway work on management-fee basis; contracts generally have price variation clauses, so inflation impact is not very big.

qa_highlights.question: How is BharatNet progressing and how are payments?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution was initially challenged but has improved; work is in full swing in UP West and UP East; some BSNL payments received and others in pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth guidance maintained after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management says it expects about 15% top-line and 15-20% bottom-line growth, with Q1 bottom-line growth at 19%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from overseas projects in volatile regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says risk assessment is done before bidding and risk premium is built in; it expects margins of 15-20% overseas and cites government support.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further losses on onerous contracts? What is outstanding from Railways?
qa_highlights.answer: Onerous contract provisions are already made and no further provisions are anticipated; railway receivables are about INR 2,500 crore, with bills typically paid within 30 days.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: standalone EBITDA margin of 3.99% remains thin; management says margins remain a focus area.
Client payment delays, notably BharatNet payments from BSNL, and railway receivables of about INR 2,500 crore.
Labour availability shortages and geopolitical situation affecting execution and overseas projects (Middle East, Israel).
Order inflow must reach the INR 20,000 crore target; the number was given as both INR 20,000 crore and INR 20,000-25,000 crore.
Inconsistent figures on call: order book split by segment, and order book mix (40% vs 42% railway); verify against filings.
Vande Bharat prototype timing (December 2026) and BharatNet extension of six to eight months.

520008|2026-06.headline: Rico Auto Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~39% to INR755 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.6% and PAT turned to a INR3.4 crore loss.
520008|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record INR755 crore against INR543 crore a year earlier, with aluminium casting at 89% of revenue and exports near 15%. Profitability was hit by about INR24 crore of higher other operating expenses (including air freight and sorting costs of about INR13 crore), plus an estimated INR10 crore raw-material settlement lag. Management reiterated full-year revenue of about INR3,250 crore and said margins should recover from Q3 as air freight ceases and customer price revisions flow through. Q2 margins are expected to be better than Q1 but still in between the Q1 level and the targeted trajectory.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR543 crore in Q1 FY26, ~39% growth
vs profit of INR16.7 crore in Q1 FY26
primarily air freight and sorting; air freight and sorting ~INR12.8-13 crore
standalone lag impact INR3.3 crore vs INR12 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR349/kg vs INR222/kg in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Aluminium casting
segments.commentary: Principal contributor at 89% of consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue; supports Toyota, Ford and BMW long-term programmes.

segments.name: Ferrous casting
segments.commentary: Contributed the remaining 11% of consolidated revenue in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Revenue contribution in Q1 stated at roughly INR5-7 crore (verbal estimate, exact figure to be shared later); RDSO approvals in progress and supplies started.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Building computerised shooting/practice ranges in containers; management said 200 ranges to be supplied this year, plus baffle range consultancy.

July 2026 turnover stated at about INR300 crore.
Full-year EBITDA margin target around 10%; management said it expects to exit the year near targeted full-year margins; Q2 margin to be between Q1 and Q3 levels.
Air freight expected to peak in Q2 and cease from Q3, with shipments returning to sea freight; progressive profitability improvement from Q3 onwards.
Management said the company will achieve its previously stated 12% margin target over time; Hosur commercial production expected September 2026.
Long-term target of about INR7,500 crore revenue by 2030 referenced by an analyst; management said about INR4,000 crore is achievable with current asset base.
capex_capacity: Hosur plant expected to start commercial production in September 2026, supporting hybrid and EV programmes; production ramp from October.
54 projects in hand; management is curbing investment and expects to invest only where absolutely necessary for about one year, then stabilise assets before larger projects.
Company has about 7-8 high-tonnage die-casting machines (1,000-2,700 ton); a 2,700-ton machine costs about INR25 crore landed plus INR10-15 crore infrastructure.
Capex guidance for FY27 and FY28 (including maintenance capex) not given; management said it will share later.
Land held for sale in Haridwar (about 2 acres, about INR10 crore) expected to be paid in full by 30 December; further land bank under discussion.
demand_pricing: Around 55 new programmes in launch phase, of which 28 launched and in ramp-up; customers include Toyota, Ford and BMW with 7-8 year programme life; company is single-source supplier on these.

Air freight incurred because ocean transit rose from 5 weeks to 9 weeks (sometimes 10 or 8) due to the West Asia conflict; customers in US and Europe; one customer agreed to pay roughly 50% of air freight cost, not yet booked.
Price increases sought from domestic and overseas customers for rupee-driven import inflation, manpower, power, fuel, gas and carbide inserts; Haryana labour cost increase of about 40% cited.
About 75% of customers (by management's statement) moved to real-time raw-material settlement; remaining 25% being onboarded.
Company does not hedge aluminium; customers announce prices. Management said aluminium prices eased slightly in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance of ~10% EBITDA margin given in June if air freight pressures were already visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transit times rose from 7 weeks assumed to 9-10 weeks; most air freight was incurred after the early-June call as the situation escalated in late June.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 39% growth came from higher metal prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR100-200 crore of revenue was due to higher metal prices on a consolidated basis; standalone raw-material impact about INR100 crore, with consolidated possibly INR10-15 crore higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and full-year margin outlook and what is the path to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 margin would be between Q1 and H2 levels, with margins improving from Q3 as freight normalises and price revisions are realised; it expects to be confident of the trajectory if conditions hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aluminium price assumption behind FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the ruling price around INR320/kg (approximately INR32,000 per tonne); raw-material impact estimated at INR200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can the business reach INR4,000 crore revenue without major capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR4,000 crore plus is achievable with the current setup, with die investments largely recovered upfront from customers except for Maruti and Hero, which pay via piece price.

qa_highlights.question: Will hedging be used to manage aluminium volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company does not bank on commodities; the focus is on passing through raw-material cost via real-time settlements to eliminate the lag.

risks_watch: Air freight and sorting costs (INR12.8-13 crore in Q1) may persist into Q2; recovery from one customer (about 50% of freight) is not yet booked.
Customer settlement timing: 25% of customers not yet on real-time settlement; overseas customers may take longer to accept inflation-related price revisions.
Aluminium price volatility (about 57% higher YoY for a grade) and reliance on customer-led pricing; geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) could extend shipping times.
Quality correlation issue with a major customer put some parts on hold; rust issues from prolonged sea transit required repacking.
Margin recovery to ~10% for FY27 requires about 12-13% in H2 per analyst's arithmetic; management has not given a quarterly margin figure.
Capex, land monetisation and railway/defence revenue numbers were not fully quantified on the call.

544480|2026-06.headline: JSW Cement Q1 FY27 volume rose 15% YoY to 3.81 Mt, but consolidated operating EBITDA fell 7.5% YoY to INR299 crore on North start-up costs and fuel.
544480|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volumes grew 15% YoY to 3.81 million tons, with cement up 27% to 2.34 Mt; ex-North cement volume grew 8%. Consolidated revenue was INR1,896 crore (+22% YoY, flat QoQ) while operating EBITDA fell 7.5% YoY to INR299 crore (INR784/t), as blended fuel cost rose to INR1.80/Mcal from INR1.49 and North marketing spend was about INR33 crore. Management kept high-teens company-wide volume growth guidance for FY27 but cut GGBS growth expectations to high single digits. North breakeven is targeted at EBITDA level in Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt / Net debt to EBITDA

segments.name: North region (new)
segments.commentary: First full quarter of sales; operating loss about INR40 crore including ~INR33 crore marketing; average utilisation ~55% in Q1 and ~68% in June 2026.

segments.commentary: Volume 2.34 Mt (+27% YoY); trade mix stable at 51%; clinker-to-cement factor rose to 55% with North launch; lead distance stable.

capex_capacity: Nagaur integrated unit: WHRS, OLBC and AFR co-processing being installed, expected to commission in the next few weeks.
Nagaur 1 Mt additional grinding on track for end Q2 FY27; capacity 2.5 Mt operating, rising to 3.5 Mt by late Sep/early Oct 2026.
Nagaur project total capex ~INR3,500 crore, of which ~INR2,400–2,500 crore spent to date.
Added 56 MW wind capacity at Dolvi and Vijayanagar in Q1; RE share reached 30%. Management said 60%+ RE share targeted from Q3 FY27, with delays linked to land.
Clinker utilisation 61% including Nagaur (Nandyal, Shiva, Nagaur); 87% excluding Nagaur. Overall cement utilisation 61% in Q1.
Punjab plant: ~INR50–60 crore spent, mainly land; awaiting environmental clearance before work begins; included in capex plan.

532626|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56% YoY to INR931 crore and PAT 32% to INR36 crore, while lead volumes fell on supply-chain disruption.
532626|2026-06.overview: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 56%, 30% and 32% YoY to INR931 crore, INR56 crore and INR36 crore, with EBITDA margin about 6%. Copper volumes more than tripled YoY to record levels and copper EBITDA per ton rose 66% to INR48,488. Lead volumes moderated as shipping delays via the Strait of Hormuz constrained scrap imports, and management chose to prioritise value-added products (85% of lead revenue), giving a record lead EBITDA of INR21,595 per ton. Management says demand is intact and the constraint is supply, not demand.

segments.name: Lead

segments.name: Copper
segments.commentary: Production and sales volumes each rose more than 3x YoY to record levels (about 4,000 tonnes in the quarter per analyst); export mix 25%. Copper expected to be about 45% of FY27 revenue. Existing capacity about 75% utilised.

segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q1 with net profit of about INR15 lakh on about 800 tonnes of volume.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Small production of about 200 metric tonnes in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Lead value-added mix for FY27 targeted at 65-70% (FY26 about 63%).
Lead EBITDA sustainable at INR18,000-20,000 per ton as volumes rise; Q1 INR21,595 was driven by 85% value-added mix.
Copper EBITDA per ton before value-addition guided above INR40,000 (earlier guidance INR35,000-40,000); cathode blended EBITDA guided INR60,000-65,000 per ton.

Phase 1 (18,000 tpa) on track for commissioning in December 2026, trial runs in Q4 FY27; machine installation from end-September, Phase 2 (18,000 tpa) targeted for Q3 FY28.
Incremental 6,000 tpa copper recycling capacity commissioned in Q4 FY26 (copper recycling total about 12,000 tpa, in Andhra Pradesh); about 75% utilised. Target utilisation about 75% through FY27.
New 72,000 tpa lead (TKD) capacity utilisation below 50% because of the focus on value-added pure lead.
CRISIL upgraded outlook to A positive from A stable, rating reaffirmed.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand softness; the constraint is delayed shipments and supply-chain disruption.
Lead exports go mainly to Southeast Asia, not Europe; Middle East procurement below 5% of sourcing, with the main issue being shipping routes via the Strait of Hormuz.
Lead sourcing about 97% international in Q1; domestic prices were too high for profitable domestic buying, though management has started looking at domestic procurement.
Copper pricing was supported by tight availability, enabling a premium on copper sales.
Copper sourcing: mostly imports, with plans for 25-30% domestic sourcing going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Can lead volumes reach the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance given the current run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of closing up to the committed numbers but will see how supply chains evolve over the next 1-2 months; no revision given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there demand softness in lead, given exposure to Western and Middle East markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No demand softness; exports are mainly Southeast Asia. Only supply delays are affecting volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 16% YoY and 44% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Logistics is a small part; the major driver is fuel prices and some additive prices that rose over the last three months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the record lead EBITDA per ton one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a sustainable level is INR18,000-20,000 per ton; Q1 was high because of the 85% value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split for FY27 of about INR175 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance INR20-25 crore; the balance of INR140-150 crore is for the new copper plant.

qa_highlights.question: Copper EBITDA per ton outlook before value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects above INR40,000 per ton going forward, aided by capacity efficiencies and a premium in the current tight market.

qa_highlights.question: EPR credits and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: EPR benefit minimal this quarter as most purchases were imports; unmonetised EPR credits remain on the books. Working capital not stretched because payments are made about a week before arrival at port.

risks_watch: Lead volume shortfall from shipping disruption (Strait of Hormuz) could put the 1.25-1.3 lakh tonne FY27 guidance at risk; monthly production fell in May and early June.
Cost inflation from fuel and additive prices, with other expenses up 44% QoQ.
Copper cathode commissioning slipping beyond December 2026 would delay margin uplift; the cathode blended EBITDA of INR60,000-65,000 per ton is not yet proven.
Copper scrap security as global supply tightens and more countries retain scrap; reliance on imports for most copper sourcing.
Lead EBITDA per ton could normalise toward INR18,000-20,000 as the value-added mix falls from 85%.
Lead volumes fell sharply YoY, with analysts noting a much steeper decline than a competitor; management declined to comment.
532626|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the copper ramp-up and margins, but noticeably cautious and vague on lead volumes, where it repeatedly said it would wait 1-2 months before giving a firm view. Several answers were defensive or repetitive when pressed on FY28 copper volumes and recycling capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why stay in premium bottomwear, and why were margins hit by tariffs despite premium positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premium bottomwear was chosen for quota-era history and competition from Turkey/Tunisia/Eastern Europe rather than mass-market countries; it claimed tariff burden sharing was lower than mass-market peers.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and timing for the incremental 20 lakh pieces?
qa_highlights.answer: Two factories of about Rs 20 crore each: first around FY28 (may slip a couple of months), second around FY30; total about Rs 40-50 crore, described as ballpark.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 utilisation and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Target about 70% utilisation in FY27 and move towards FY25 EBITDA margins; about 17% margin targeted by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why the Sri Lanka contract manufacturing and overseas plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Sri Lanka MOU is a contingency for US tariff changes (country-of-origin flexibility), not yet used; Nepal, Vietnam and Sri Lanka being evaluated for the next plant. Management said Europe/UK demand is not being moved out of India.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY30 projection of Rs 500 crore revenue and Rs 65 crore PAT conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, conservative given FTAs not yet operational; includes Sri Lanka contract volumes but no quantified share was given.

qa_highlights.question: D2C plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Test marketing started, put on hold due to a patent issue with the SHORTSTOP brand; not much invested in the brand.

qa_highlights.question: Athleisure and women's wear plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Women's wear is an easy extension of men's bottomwear; athleisure needs supplier base development (mainly cotton with some man-made fibre), using similar machines; no separate plant planned.

qa_highlights.question: FY25 base and exceptional income?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 revenue about Rs 155 crore (operational) and Rs 191 crore gross; EBITDA Rs 51 crore including Rs 12.5 crore exceptional gain from sale of agricultural land; PAT Rs 40 crore including exceptional item.

qa_highlights.question: Will BTS revenue recognition accelerate given the order book has nearly doubled since FY24 and project cycles exceed 2.5 years?

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor equipment: who are the customers, and what are the margins?

qa_highlights.question: Will BTS revenue mix move sustainably beyond 70:30 in favour of BTS?

qa_highlights.question: Will India revenue growth stay at the medium-term target of 25%-plus this year?

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27/FY28 guidance for revenue, margins and export mix?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the KIADB Aerospace Park facility and the capex plan?

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the export BTS opportunity and its margin?

Monitor SBS and EW order conversion, and first deliveries for UHM, Virupaksha and TACAN programmes.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated profit from continuing operations after tax
Consolidated PAT incl. one-time deconsolidation gain

532875|2026-06.headline: Allied Digital Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs. 260 crore, but PAT fell to Rs. 12 crore from Rs. 14 crore on higher tax and margin pressure.
532875|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 19% YoY to Rs. 260 crore and PBT rose 19% to about Rs. 17 crore, while EBITDA was Rs. 25 crore at a 10% margin. Trailing 12-month revenue crossed Rs. 1,000 crore (Rs. 1,009 crore). Management said the audit report is now unmodified, with all earlier auditor qualifications resolved. Management acknowledged competitive pricing pressure in the US and India hardware-linked deals, and said margins are under pressure across the industry. Management also said revenue declined quarter-on-quarter, which it attributed to cautious deal-making and delayed large government and hardware-linked orders.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY26 had net tax benefit of Rs. 0.3 crore
vs Rs. 14 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration of 10x growth over 10 years, about 20% CAGR, with some quarters varying with macroeconomic conditions.
Management expects EBITDA margin of 10-11% currently, and says margins could reach 12-13% once large deals kick in over a couple of quarters.
Management expects new deal announcements from the pipeline in the next one to two quarters (Q2 or Q3 FY27), once hardware prices bottom out and RFPs are issued.
No specific FY28 guidance given; management said timing of margin recovery is uncertain.
capex_capacity: Management says it is investing in AI, people, mid-level leadership and governance, which weighed on margins.
Finance costs rose modestly due to higher working capital deployment as large projects moved into execution.
demand_pricing: Order book: orders of Rs. 120-plus crore booked in the quarter, including new wins and multiyear renewals.

Key wins included a US NYSE-listed electronics company (application maintenance on ServiceNow, Jitterbit and Boomi, entry into US Enterprise Application Services), an Australian mutual bank (workspace services), a Punjab government command and control centre, a Ministry of Commerce body (managed services), an international property consultant (IT asset management) and an Indian FMCG company (IT infrastructure support).
Management said customers are more measured, procurement cycles are longer, and it sees a timing shift rather than weaker underlying demand.
Railway orders of Rs. 180-200 crore were lost after product (hardware) prices rose 25-30% during bidding; the company withdrew to avoid losses.
Competitive pressure in the US market with margin-reduction demands from clients over the last 4-8 quarters; customers seeking discounts in anticipation of automation.
Management said it stayed away from low-margin customer acquisition in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 due to hardware price volatility, and that revenue declined quarter-on-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why have EBITDA and PAT margins been declining for 3-4 years, and how can they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited competitive pressure over the last 4-8 quarters, especially in the US, and investments in hiring, leadership and AI. It expects margins to improve in the next few quarters as automation is rolled out to clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI a threat or benefit, and is it causing revenue deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called AI an opportunity and a boon. It said revenue pressure comes from two causes: hardware price increases in India and the company's choice to avoid low-margin deals. Exact AI impact will be clear only once automation is implemented at client level.

qa_highlights.question: When will margin pressure bottom out, and what is the FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot give a timeline because the market is in flux, and that margins are under pressure across the industry as customers seek discounts. It pointed to 10x growth in 10 years (about 20% a year) as the guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What constraints are delaying revenue conversion, and when will growth inflect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that a hardware price spike of 25-30% led it to exit Rs. 180-200 crore of railway orders. It became cautious on elongated government bids. Pricing from OEMs has now stabilised, and it expects good announcements in the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin is currently 10-11%, and it expects 12-13% once large deals kick in over a couple of quarters, with AI investment continuing.

risks_watch: PAT declined YoY to Rs. 12 crore from Rs. 14 crore despite PBT growth, as tax provision rose to about Rs. 4.5 crore.
Other income fell due to the absence of FX revaluation gains after the US subsidiary funding was reclassified from debt to equity.
Quarter-on-quarter revenue decline, which management attributed to delayed large deals.
Margin pressure from US pricing competition and customer discount demands; recovery to 12-13% EBITDA is conditional on large deals and AI deployment.
Hardware price volatility in India affecting bidding on government projects.
Management tone is confident on long-term direction but gave no timeline for margin recovery; delivery on the promised 2-3 quarter order recovery is the key test.
532875|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and the governance clean-up, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins and timing of order wins. Management repeatedly framed the slowdown as timing-related and gave no firm date for margin recovery.
key_quotes: We see this as a shift in the timing of decisions rather than underlying demand.
So, the margin trajectory right now, we are anywhere between 10% to 11% EBITDA.
For the first time since the comprehensive review commenced, the audit report carries no qualifications or observations.
So, we are seeing 10x growth in 10 years, which turns out to be about 20% a year is what we are looking at.

543918|2026-06.headline: GHCL Textiles Q1 FY27 revenue rose 52% YoY to Rs.410 crores, with EBITDA of Rs.70 crores (~17% margin) helped by cotton inventory gains.
543918|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs.410 crores (up 52% YoY), EBITDA Rs.70 crores and PAT Rs.39 crores. Management said the spread widened to about Rs.155/kg (with packing) from Rs.138/kg in Q4 FY26, helped by cotton bought earlier at lower prices. Fabric reached 16% of sales (vs 9% a year ago) as the first 15 of 40 planned knitting machines ran. Management guided a normalised EBITDA margin of 14-15% for FY27 and 16-18% once ready-to-cut fabric capacity is in place, and set a target of Rs.2,000 crores revenue by FY29.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA margin ~17% (vs ~12% last year, per management)

financial_highlights.value: ~10-12% of sales price increase attributed to inventory gain (sales prices up ~20-24%)

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: 89% of yarn production sold as yarn; 11% converted to fabric. Spinning utilisation ~99% per management, and 98%+ per the CEO's answer on volume. No new yarn capacity planned beyond knitting.

segments.name: Fabric (woven and knitted)
segments.commentary: Fabric is ~16% of sales, split roughly 50:50 woven and knitted. The 15 knitting machines run at 80-85% utilisation, with Q1 the first full quarter. Greige fabric contributed about Rs.65 crores this quarter.

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin of 14-15% for FY27; Q1's inventory gain will not recur. Q2 spread expected slightly below Q1 but similar to the current level.
Ready-to-cut fabric integration expected to lift normalised EBITDA margin to 16-18%.
Revenue target of Rs.2,000 crores by FY29, from about Rs.1,350 crores in FY26 (14% growth); management expects FY27 at about Rs.1,500 crores.
FY27 capex of about Rs.100-120 crores including modernisation; about Rs.350-400 crores earmarked for ready-to-cut fabric facilities, subject to shareholder approval.
Remaining 25 knitting machines to be received in Q2 and Q3 FY27, bringing the total to 40 by Q3-end.
11 MW ground solar commissioning now expected December 2026 (~Rs.6 crores/year savings, full benefit next year); 3 MW rooftop solar live since January (~Rs.2 crores/year).
capex_capacity: Total installed renewable capacity ~65 MW, with an additional 11 MW ground solar in progress (commissioning slipped to December 2026 due to MNRE/ALMM list changes).
First 50 knitting machines installed and commercial production stabilised; 15 knitting machines received so far and 25 more to follow in phases through Q3 FY27.

PM MITRA Park (Tamil Nadu): land allotted in Q4 FY26; park completion targeted December 2027; GHCL must complete within three years of allotment. Fabric/processing plant planned for CY28, with part work possibly earlier.
In-house knitting capacity expected to be about 12-15% of total yarn production once all 40 machines are running.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices (domestic): Rs.62,000/candy in April, Rs.67,000 in May, Rs.64,000 in June, and back to about Rs.68,000-70,000 by the call. NY futures reached 80 cents/lb at end-June.

Order book healthy with 1.5-2 months of forward booking maintained. Exports to Europe (Germany, Italy and others) were strong in Q1; GHCL has no direct US/UK exposure and sells through process houses and garmenters.
Chinese yarn demand from India has risen since December 2025 (partly on lower Chinese cotton output); GHCL itself exports little to China. Q1 saw some slowdown in that demand.
Management says domestic textile demand is growing 6-8% YoY. Cotton is now at parity with imported cotton, supporting export competitiveness.
Cotton stock is held till November-December; further inventory plans depend on the monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cotton inventory position and the current spread?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is covered until the new season (Nov-Dec). Current spread is ~Rs.160/kg before packing (~Rs.155 after), up from ~Rs.138/kg in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin sustainable, and what does fabric contribution look like over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads should stay better than last year and similar in Q2, then depend on the market. Fabric to reach 30-40% of revenue after about three years as a ready-to-cut supplier, up from 15-16% now.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 EBITDA came from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales prices rose ~20-24%, but inventory gain accounted for only ~10-12%. The rest came from better pricing, customer mix and strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the Q1 spread given rising cotton prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread can be held at current cotton levels of Rs.68,000-69,000/candy, but may compress if yarn prices lag. Q2 expected slightly below Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any capacity expansion on the yarn side besides knitting?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Only knitting machines are in the pipeline, plus about Rs.350 crores of capex for ready-to-cut fabric.

qa_highlights.question: How is the order book for H2 FY27, and are there US/UK/EU orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book healthy at 1.5-2 months forward. Strong European demand in Q1; no direct US/UK orders since GHCL supplies yarn and greige fabric as a tier-two vendor.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected once ready-to-cut is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Normalised margin 14-15% for FY27; 16-18% after vertical integration (ready-to-cut fabric).

qa_highlights.question: What incentives come with the PM MITRA Park project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited capital subsidy of about Rs.100-125 crores on a ~Rs.1,000 crore total investment under TN incentive schemes. The first inspection is done and the file is moving. The CEO said debt concessions were not a main factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the roadmap to double revenue to Rs.2,000 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue grows about 14% a year from ~Rs.1,350 crores in FY26 to reach Rs.2,000 crores by FY29. Growth comes from greige fabric and ready-to-cut fabric (Rs.350-400 crores of turnover at 1:1 or 1:0.8 asset turnover).

500086|2026-06.headline: Exide Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew 17.6% and EBITDA rose 19.5% to INR655 crores, with margin at 12.4%.
500086|2026-06.overview: Management reported broad-based double-digit growth across automotive OEM, replacement, home inverter, solar, industrial and exports, helped by a strong summer and a low base. EBITDA margin expanded 20 bps YoY and about 70 bps QoQ despite higher input costs from West Asia disruption and rupee weakness. Price increases of 4-6% YoY across categories were taken, with further hikes to be decided case by case. In lithium-ion, all four Bangalore lines are installed, the NCM cylindrical and LFP prismatic lines have started customer samples, and revenue is expected to start during FY27. Management declined to give full-year guidance.

segments.name: Automotive OEM
segments.commentary: Grew about 25% YoY for a third straight quarter; 4W OEM volume up 21% and 2W OEM up 20%, on a low base. Management expects percentage growth to slow in H2 against a strong Q3/Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Replacement (2W/4W)
segments.commentary: 4-wheeler replacement volume grew about 10%; all replacement businesses reported double-digit revenue growth.

segments.name: Home inverters and solar
segments.commentary: Both grew over 20% YoY on summer demand; solar volume grew about 12-14% and solar posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR400+ crores. Inverters are 15-25% of revenue depending on season.

segments.name: Industrial infrastructure (ex-telecom)
segments.commentary: Maintained double-digit growth, supported by industrial UPS and traction. Government tenders were muted in the quarter, with an H2 pick-up expected.

segments.name: Lithium-ion (Exide Energy Solutions)
segments.commentary: Bangalore plant: 4 lines installed; NCM cylindrical and LFP prismatic lines are shipping samples. Lithium pack business is small (INR100-200 crores in FY26 per management) and management does not expect it to be profitable with imported cells.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 revenue guidance; management cited poor visibility on market and H2 base effects, though Q2 benefits from a low base.
Bangalore plant revenue expected to commence during FY27 shortly; utilisation of 25-30% of the factory in the first year, which management reaffirmed.
FY27 lithium-ion capex approved by Board at INR1,400 crores, with INR100 crores spent in July; may be reviewed.
Phase 1 (6 GWh) has no PLI support; Phase 2 capex is lower than Phase 1 as land and utilities for 12 GWh are already built, but total could exceed the earlier INR7,000 crore plan.
Target of 50-60% localisation of lithium-ion bill of materials in 2-3 years.
Q2 price increases not yet decided; will be taken in small steps as input costs move.
capex_capacity: Bangalore giga factory: equipment for all 4 lines delivered and installed; utilities fully operational.

First NCM cylindrical line began customer sample deliveries in Q1; LFP prismatic line has started samples for 3W and telecom. Lines 1 and 3 are the first to be run; Line 4 (LFP, for 4W OEMs) is to be commissioned around end of FY27.
Phase 1 capacity is 6 GWh, with provision to expand to 12 GWh in the next few years. Pack capacity in-house is 1.5 GWh.

Lead-acid: INR500 crores is set aside every year for the core business, for bottleneck debottlenecking, automation and capacity expansion, mainly in 4W. Exide has 5 SLI plants with brownfield headroom.
Pilot line for R&D expected at end of calendar 2026; more than 100 R&D engineers are in Bangalore.
demand_pricing: Volume growth was double-digit in most businesses: 4W replacement about 10%, 4W OEM 21%, 2W OEM 20%, solar 12-14%.
Price increases of 4-6% YoY were taken across categories. Management expects to take further 1-2% steps as needed.
Input costs were elevated due to West Asia disruption and rupee weakness, while LME lead in USD was range-bound.
Management said 2W/3W/telecom lithium demand is a switch from imported cells, not new demand, and that the 3W market is about 70-75% aftermarket retrofits.

Chinese export VAT rebate on cells fell from 9% to 6%, and management expects the removal from 1 January 2027 to affect imported-cell landed costs. China export controls on raw materials are deferred to around November.

qa_highlights.question: Split of volume vs pricing growth, and whether any new contracts contributed?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was double-digit in most businesses (4W OEM 21%, 2W OEM 20%, 4W replacement 10%, solar 12-14%). Price correction added to top-line growth. No new contract wins contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Can full-year FY27 growth of 15-16% be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no full-year guidance. It flagged H2 percentage slowdown in auto OEM due to the high base from Q3/Q4 FY26, though absolute volumes remain high (passenger vehicles up from 1.2 to 1.4 million).

qa_highlights.question: Cell yields and early learnings from the giga factory?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields are improving, but the real yield will only be visible at 3-shift operation. Management did not disclose yield numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Are there PLI and pricing views for the imported-cell competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating the 10 GWh PLI re-application. It declined to comment on early-phase margins, citing the China VAT rebate removal from 1 January as a watch item.

qa_highlights.question: Inverter share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Home inverters are 15-25% of revenue, depending on the season.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of 2W EV OEM and 4W OEM engagement?
qa_highlights.answer: Talks are under way with about 3 major 2W OEMs (about 80% of EV volume) and homologation is in progress. For 4W, 1-2 major OEMs are in talks, with Line 4 expected to be commissioned around end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 lithium-ion capex and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: INR1,400 crores is approved for FY27 (INR100 crores spent in July). Phase 1 is 6 GWh, expandable to 12 GWh; management declined to give rupee revenue figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% utilisation target achievable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 25-30% factory utilisation for the first year and declined to forecast FY27 revenue, citing contractual BESS delivery dates and start-up timing.

financial_highlights.metric: Cumulative equity in Exide Energy Solutions

544644|2026-06.headline: Corona Remedies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with EBITDA margin up ~190 bps to 22%.
544644|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with India business up 22.7% against IPM growth of 11.6%, and organic growth of 21.4%. EBITDA rose 33.5% to INR93 crore and PAT rose 30.1% to INR60 crore, with PAT margin at 14.2%. Management kept FY27 guidance of 15% organic revenue growth and 20% PAT growth, but flagged raw material and geopolitical cost risk and said it is premature to extrapolate the Q1 margin. The Europe-GMP hormonal facility was capitalised on 30 June 2026 and export filings are targeted for FY28-29.

financial_highlights.change: +21.9% YoY (vs INR347 crore in Q1 FY26)
+33.5% YoY; margin up ~190 bps (from INR70 crore)
vs INR10 crore in Q1 FY26; mainly amortisation of Wokadine and Bayer brands

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 97% of revenue and grew 22.7% YoY, roughly twice the IPM growth of 11.6%.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 3% of revenue and did not grow in Q1; management says it will stay in the low-single-digit share for the next few years.

segments.name: Therapy areas (PharmaTrac, per management)
segments.commentary: Women's Healthcare grew about 23.3% vs IPM 9.4%; Urology grew 27.6% vs IPM 14.9%; Cardio-metabolic and Pain Management outperformed IPM by 1.7x and 1.4x respectively.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 15% organic revenue growth plus about 1.5-2% inorganic growth, for about 17% total revenue growth and 20% PAT growth.
Management says it aims to maintain margins 'within a similar range' but will not commit to sustaining Q1 levels given cost volatility.

Raw material: about 70-90 days of stock held at quarter end; new stocks began arriving in June 2026. Management sees possible 100 bps margin hit in coming quarters and is offsetting via other cost cuts.
Hormonal facility asset turnover expected below 1x in FY27, rising to 2-3x over about three years; depreciation on the INR130 crore capex is about INR6.5 crore a year.
Export ramp: dossiers ready by Nov-Dec 2026, then 12-18 months for registration; international launch targeted FY28-29.
Medical representative additions guided at 6-8% per year (about 200-250 MRs), with no MR additions planned in FY27 after about 400 were added in Q4 FY26.
capex_capacity: Europe-GMP hormonal (women's healthcare) facility commercialised on 30 June 2026, after INR130 crore capex; it handles tablets, soft gelatin capsules, ointments and gels.
Ahmedabad oral solid dosage facility Europe-GMP certification renewed.
Manufacturing mix is about 60% in-house and 40% outsourced, expected to stay similar through FY27.
API sourcing: about 60-65% of API needs are met by La Chandra Pharma Lab, in which the company holds a 31% stake (via Remedies Private Limited). La Chandra has EU GMP and a recent US DMF approval.
Hormonal plant to serve the domestic market initially; international dossier filings are in preparation.
demand_pricing: MAT June 2026 PharmaTrac split: volume growth 6.3% vs IPM 1.3%; price-led growth about 8.7% vs IPM 5.6%; new product contribution 3.4% vs IPM 2.9%.
Management says the Q1 India growth split is broadly in line with the MAT split.
Company ranks 26th in IPM (up from 29th a year ago). It is 5th in Women's Healthcare and Pain Management, 9th in Urology, and 20th in Cardio-diabeto (top 10 in new consolidated business).
Two brands now exceed INR100 crore annual revenue (one in MAT June 2023), and more than 40 brands exceed INR10 crore (from 32). Two new INR10 crore entrants are both organic.
Management expects IPM growth of about 9-11%, sustained since December 2025.
Semaglutide: management expects a INR1,500-1,800 crore market and targets a top-10 position, but says focus remains on engine brands.

qa_highlights.question: Is there scope for margin expansion if 20% growth continues, or will incremental growth be reinvested?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited favourable mix and operating leverage in Q1 but would not extrapolate. It said it aims to keep margins in a similar range and cited Southeast Asia and geopolitical cost risk.

qa_highlights.question: Did raw material inflation affect Q1, and will Q2 see more of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was largely unaffected due to 70-90 days of inventory. Management sees a possible 100 bps hit and is trying to offset it with other cost reductions to keep the 20% PAT guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the acquired Bayer-Zydus molecule (Dr. Reddy's-sourced, per the analyst) seem to decline YoY, and what is the path to 25% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: External revenue was INR28-30 crore, plus INR20 crore internal. Management called Q1 the launch quarter and said supply-chain integration took priority; it is targeting INR20-40 crore over the coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth by volume, price and new launches, and IVF traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is in line with MAT: volume 6.3%, price 8.7%, new launches 3.4%. The IVF task force started in April 2026; management says it is too early to comment and will update in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the employee and other expense ratios vs peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is high because about 1,000 MRs (35% of the 3,111 total) were added in three years and productivity per MR is lower; operating leverage should bring it down. Other expenses are mainly UCPMP-governed promotion costs, which are variable.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and amortisation impact from the Wokadine and Bayer acquisitions, and from the hormonal plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Wokadine (INR97 crore plus GST) and Bayer (INR7 crore) are amortised over 10 years. The hormonal plant is depreciated over 20 years (about INR6.5 crore a year).

risks_watch: Raw material and geopolitical (Southeast Asia) cost pressure could cut gross margin by about 100 bps in coming quarters.
Hormonal facility under-recoveries until asset turnover rises from below 1x in FY27 toward 2-3x.
International revenue was flat in Q1; export ramp depends on dossier approvals (FY28-29).
Wokadine and Bayer-Zydus brand ramp is early; management guides to 25% inorganic growth over 2-3 years.
Dependence on La Chandra for about 60-65% of API needs.
Next quarter: whether margin holds near 22% EBITDA and the India growth rate stays about twice the IPM.

500038|2026-06.headline: Balrampur Chini guided ~40% average PLA capacity utilisation for Jan-Mar 2027 and held 45.67 lakh quintals of sugar stock at INR 37.19/kg carrying cost.
500038|2026-06.overview: Management described FY26 as a tighter-than-expected season with lower production, healthy domestic consumption and ethanol diversion drawing down inventory, which firmed sugar prices to roughly INR 48-49 per kg. Q1 is an off-season quarter with almost no sugar production, so results reflect carrying cost and realisation of inventory from the prior season. The 80,000-tonne PLA plant is on track, with lactic acid commissioning expected in October and PLA in December, and about INR 2,180 crore spent by end-July. Management said it sees no B-heavy or juice diversion next season as a reasonable working assumption, but did not give quantified Q1 financials on the call.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Q1 is off-season with largely no production; 45.67 lakh quintals inventory at INR 37.19/kg carrying cost is seen as a favourable base for upcoming quarters. Some Maizapur distillery costs were retained in sugar, not distillery, in Q1.

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: Q1 margins described as resilient, driven by B-heavy and maize-based ethanol with hardly any juice-based sales. Management said distillery costs are not comparable apples-to-apples due to cost allocation to sugar.

segments.name: PLA (new, 80,000 t)
segments.commentary: Lactic acid commissioning targeted October 2026 and PLA December 2026; ~40% average utilisation guided for Jan-Mar 2027, described as a safe expectation with target higher.

guidance_outlook: PLA: lactic acid commissioning around October 2026 and PLA around December 2026, subject to production, quality and timing.
PLA: safe expectation of ~40% average capacity utilisation for January-March 2027; internal target is higher.

FY28 ethanol: management assumes no B-heavy or juice diversion allowed next season and only C-heavy permitted; company has not yet finalised numbers. Expects crushing may reduce slightly in some units but overall targets intact.

Sugar price: management expects a cane price hike and ban on diversion, and believes the net effect will be positive; said closing-stock tightness could normalise by around 1 October 2027, with prices above current levels in coming years.
Clarity on 2026-27 sugar season production expected around end-September 2026.
capex_capacity: 80,000-tonne PLA plant on track; civil work, equipment arrivals and erection underway.
Maizapur distillery equipped for grain-based ethanol (~10 crore litres per analyst's cited figure), and now ready to make sugar as well.
Management said C-heavy-based distillery volumes are fully equipped across all units.
Cane development and varietal balancing identified as key focus areas.
demand_pricing: Domestic sugar prices firmed on tighter inventory; management says the market is assuming closing stock lower than reality.
Management view: 2025-26 closing stock could be meaningfully higher than market assumes; rejected external estimates of a 20 lakh tonne spread as not credible.
Illustrative balance: 31 mt gross production, 29 mt consumption, ~3 mt closing stock; 45-50 lakh tonnes consumption could take stock to normal by 1 October 2027 if diversion is banned.
PLA demand: management cites pan masala/gutka packaging shift after FSSAI-related moves; technical trials positive; outcome expected within 2-3 months; no verified market size given.
Cane sowing area described as flat YoY with better yields expected; Q1 rainfall described as ideal for cane in the company's area.

qa_highlights.question: What distillery volumes are achievable next season if B-heavy and juice diversion are restricted (C-heavy ~10 crore litres, grain ~9-10 crore litres)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no B-heavy or juice diversion is a reasonable assumption and only C-heavy would be allowed; the analyst's C-heavy estimate was 'not too much off the mark', with numbers still being reworked. Grain availability depends on government broken-rice policy expected around September-October.

qa_highlights.question: When will PLA be commissioned and what first-year utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Lactic acid targeted for October and PLA for December 2026; management asked investors not to judge Q1 on PLA and said 3-6 months at best to see the trend. Jan-Mar 2027 guided at ~40% average utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a parallel Balrampur opportunity from the INR 3,000-3,200 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 'definitely yes' if things go right, but described this as a first attempt requiring patience.

qa_highlights.question: Why did distillery margins hold up despite higher transfer pricing, and will they continue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 used mainly B-heavy and maize ethanol with hardly any juice sales. Maizapur costs were retained in sugar, so the comparison is not like-for-like. Management said less B-heavy means more sugar, which should be net positive.

qa_highlights.question: How long before the sugar stock tightness normalises, and what price levels are sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said about one year, around 1 October 2027, if diversion is not allowed; he expected prices to stay above current levels in upcoming years.

qa_highlights.question: Would PLA qualify under the proposed rule that pan masala packaging be free of plastic and synthetic polymers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is dynamic and the answer is 'yes and no' pending government clarification.

risks_watch: Government policy on B-heavy/juice diversion and grain-based ethanol, which will drive FY28 distillery volumes.
Cane price hike ahead of the state elections, which could offset higher sugar realisations.
PLA commissioning (October), production start (December) and utilisation against 40% guidance for Jan-Mar 2027; PLA regulatory treatment under pan masala packaging rules.
Sugar production outlook for 2026-27, with the first clarity expected around end-September 2026; El Nino and monsoon risk.
Management's sugar balance-sheet view (closing stock) differs from market estimates; verify once ISMA and government data firm up.
